# Widgets, surfaces and shapes

How a widget is defined, where it can be shown, and what decides its size.
This is the target architecture: the code does not look like this yet, and
§6 says in what order it gets there.

> **Grid folders and grid widgets are gone (2026-10-09, §70).** A widget is a taskbar entry or a
> list folder's line, and nothing moves between the two. Where an older section below still speaks
> of a grid, its cards, spans, the titles toggle or three types, it records what was built then;
> §70 is what holds now.

## 1. What went wrong with the current shape

A widget kind is a value of the `Section` enum, and everything about that kind
is decided by switching on it somewhere else:

| Where | Section references |
|---|---|
| `Karpo.Core\Config.cs` | 182 |
| `Karpo.Settings\IslandOptions.cs` | 71 |
| `Karpo.Dock\Layout.cs` | 59 |
| `Karpo.Settings\Controls\Previews.cs` | 26 |
| `Karpo.Dock\Islands\Island.cs` | 18 |
| plus `Dock.Pins.cs`, `EditMode.cs`, `LayoutEntries.cs`, `Dock.cs`, `Switches.cs` | 9-16 each |

Adding a kind means editing eight files that each hold one more `case`, and
nothing fails when one of them is forgotten — the kind silently has no preview,
no options page, no folder tile, or no flyout. Four concrete failures this
caused, all of them real bugs we have paid for:

1. **Two renderers per kind.** `IIsland` draws the bar cell, `ITile` draws the
   folder card, and they drift. The user's rule that a row folder *is* the
   taskbar can only be guaranteed if there is one renderer, not two that agree
   by hand.
2. **Size depending on live state.** `IIsland.Measure(IslandStyle)` takes only
   the style, but an island reads its own state inside it, so the notifications
   badge widened the widget and the bar jumped. We fixed it by sweeping every
   kind and writing a test per kind. The sweep is a patch; the contract is the
   fix.
3. **Capability by interface sniffing.** `is ISliderIsland`, `is ITile`, a
   virtual `ShowsTooltip` defaulting to true. A new kind inherits an answer it
   never gave — which is how a null `Tooltip` still showed "Weather".
4. **Three copies of the same knowledge.** The dock knows a kind's glyph and
   title, the settings app knows its preview and its options page, the
   catalogue knows its category. Each is a separate switch.

The user's folder model makes this urgent rather than merely untidy: with three
folder shapes, every kind now has to answer *where it can be shown*, and an
enum switched in eight files has nowhere to put that answer.

## 2. The model

Four **locations** were planned, which reduce to three **surfaces**; the grid folder went on
2026-10-09 (§70), and so did its surface:

| Location | Surface | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| taskbar | `Bar` | cells along the bar |
| row folder | `Bar` | the same renderer, inside a flyout |
| ~~grid folder~~ | ~~`Grid`~~ | removed (§70) |
| list folder | `List` | one row, name always shown beside the content |

Row and taskbar are the same surface, not two surfaces that look alike. That is
what makes "every widget on the bar works in a row" true by construction, and
it is why `ITile`'s row path is deleted rather than kept in step.

**What that bought, in defects that were live.** Doing it (stage 4) turned the
surface into an argument of one paint method, and `PaintOn`/`TargetOn` handle
the bar themselves and are not virtual, so no kind can answer for a row. Two
things fell out that nobody had gone looking for:

- **A row folder drew the bar's cells and hit-tested them as a card.** The
  drawing switch chose the bar's cells for a row; the click path asked the
  tile's `TileTarget` *first, whatever the view*. So in a row folder a click was
  mapped by the card's geometry — onto buttons that were never drawn there. The
  now-playing widget is where it bites: its card carries three transport buttons
  in places its bar cells do not, so a click near the title could pause the
  music. Two code paths, each correct about its own half, disagreeing about
  which half they were in.
- **A tile that was not a `CellIsland` would have drawn its card in a row**,
  through a third arm below the `CellIsland` one. Nothing reached it yet.

Neither was found by reading for bugs. They were found by making the surface a
parameter and seeing what no longer type-checked — which is the argument for
this section, now with evidence rather than only first principles.

**A grid card smaller than a card, a component's card, a card told its cells, a control's least
span, a slider's short form** — the rules this section held for a grid folder's cards — went with
the grid folder (2026-10-09, §70). A list's line is laid out by its own rules (§9, "List forms").

A **widget kind** is a descriptor: one object, in one file, that answers every
question anyone can ask about that kind. A **widget instance** is an entry in
the config: id, kind, group, width, and the kind's own options.

## 3. The descriptor

```csharp
public sealed record WidgetKind
{
    public required string Id { get; init; }            // "clock", stable, in JSON
    public required string Title { get; init; }
    public required string Glyph { get; init; }
    public required WidgetCategory Category { get; init; }

    // Where it may be placed. Bar is implied and not declarable: everything
    // that exists on the bar works in a row folder.
    public required Surfaces Surfaces { get; init; }    // Grid | List | None

    public required WidgetSize Size { get; init; }      // default width, min/max cells, fixed?
    public required bool Tooltip { get; init; }
    public required Interaction Interaction { get; init; } // Click | Slider | Buttons

    public required Func<WidgetOptions> Defaults { get; init; }
    public required Func<WidgetContext, IWidget> Create { get; init; }
    public Action<PreviewContext>? Preview { get; init; }      // catalogue and edit overlay
    public Func<OptionsContext, IReadOnlyList<Card>>? Options { get; init; } // settings page
    public IReadOnlyList<Migration> From { get; init; } = [];  // legacy ids and shapes
}
```

Everything is `required`. A new kind cannot compile without saying whether it
works as a grid card and as a list row, what its default width is, and whether
it wants a tooltip. That is the whole point: the questions that used to be
answered by omission are now answered by the type system.

An entry whose click opens a flyout of Karpo's own (`BarClick.Flyout`) answers no:
the mail, the desktop and layout switchers, and the rest. So do the parts of an
entry that open one — the apps' "…" and the tray's chevron (`IslandTooltips.ForPart`)
— while the tray's icons keep the apps' own. The one exception is a lone layout's
switcher, whose click opens nothing and whose tooltip says why.
`IslandTooltipsTests` walks every kind and fails if one drifts back.
(§367: no widget or folder on the bar has a tooltip any more; the field and the table went.)

The registry is a single list in `Karpo.Core`, shared by the dock and the
settings app. `Section` disappears; the config stores `Id`.

**As built (the split, S5).** The one descriptor became a record per subject
(`WidgetInfo`, in `WidgetInfos`) and one registry per place a widget can stand —
`BarEntries` (`BarKind`), `GridWidgets` (`GridKind`) and `ListWidgets` (`ListKind`),
with `Partners` saying which members of the three are one subject. A placed widget
is a taskbar's entry (`BarItem`) or a folder's widget (`CellItem`, a card or a line
in its folder's view). `Section` is gone, and the file still stores the id.

## 4. Shape and content are separate objects

**One function answers, and everyone asks it.** A number that is measured in one place and drawn
in another will drift the day either place changes. It has been the same fault four times in one
day: the folder's name, measured by one set of numbers and drawn by another; the resize ghost,
which kept its own copy of the grid's placement arithmetic and was left behind when the grid began
to be centred; the notification rows, laid out in one space and drawn in another; and the
performance graph, measured one way and drawn another at a single folder cell. Each was fixed the
same way — one function, read by both sides — and that is the rule, not the folder's rule.

**Its twin: two places each politely adding room.** The same fault inverted, and it has now
happened twice in a day as well. A folder insets every card by its own pad, and a component then
laid the panel's own gutter out inside that card, so every row was indented twice and the user
read "way too much spacing" off a screenshot. In the card painters, a shared helper centred what
every caller was already left-aligning. Neither is a drift between a measurement and a drawing;
both are two parties being generous about the same space because neither was told the other had
it. The fix is the same shape as the one above — one place owns the space, and the other asks it
what is left — and the question to ask of any inset is *who else is already adding this?*


The rule the user gave — a widget's size follows its settings, never its state
— becomes impossible to break rather than tested for:

```csharp
// Pure. Options and metrics only: no clock, no network, no disk, no state.
WidgetShape Shape(WidgetOptions options, SurfaceMetrics metrics);

// Live. Receives the shape it must draw within and cannot change it.
void Paint(in PaintContext context, in WidgetShape shape);
```

`Shape` has no access to the instance's live data, because it is not a method
on the instance: it is a function on the descriptor, called with options. The
content object is created afterwards and is handed the shape. A widget that
wants to say something longer than its shape allows must shorten it — the
ellipsis is the only outcome available.

**The worked example, found by the conversion and not by any test.** The clock
tile measured the time it was showing. Its measuring helper normalises digits —
`TextLine.Template` reads every figure as an eight, so only the *shape* of the
text counts — and that looks like enough. It is not: normalising keeps the
digit *count*. In a region that writes 12-hour time, "1:05 PM" is one figure
narrower than "11:05 PM", so the tile was narrower all morning and jumped a
figure wider at ten o'clock. Every state test passed. Every picture on the
machine we develop on was identical, because that machine writes 24-hour time,
where the hour is always two figures.

So this is a widget that changes size with its state, passes every check we can
see, and is broken only for somebody else. No sweep finds that, because the
sweep is done by the person who cannot see it. The contract does: `Shape` is
handed the options and the metrics, the clock is not among them, and the only
answer left is to measure the longest the time can ever read in that region's
format. The guard is a test over all twenty-four hours rather than over the
clock, so it means the same thing in every region.

State-driven *appearance* stays free: colours, glyphs, badges, values. Only the
box is fixed.

**The other half, and the one that was silently wrong.** A shape is a function
of the options, so it has to be given the options — and in the tree today that
means the `Island` an island holds in `CellIsland.Settings`. The base class sets
it once, in the constructor. **`Configure` must put the new one there**, or the
widget draws its new settings at the size of its old ones. Thirteen of the
converted kinds did not, so *every* settings change that should have resized a
widget silently did nothing: only a folder switched to show its name was ever
noticed, because that is the one where the difference is a whole cell. The rule
is one line at the top of `Configure`:

```csharp
Settings = island;   // the shape is measured from this
```

The guard is `Karpo.Tests\Sizing\SettingsFollowTests.cs`, which walks every kind
the catalogue offers, reconfigures it with a different `Island`, and asserts it
then measures what a freshly built widget of those settings measures — so a kind
added later that forgets fails without anyone remembering to add it.

Appearing and disappearing remains a separate, allowed thing (a folder with no
drives, media with nothing playing) and belongs to the container, not the
shape.

## 5. What the dock and the settings app become

**Dock.** A widget is made by its registry's factory — `Islands.Create` for a taskbar entry,
`CreateCard` and `CreateLine` for a folder's — each reading which drawing its descriptor
names. `IslandView` and the dock's flyout switch are
replaced by a `Flyout` the descriptor hands back, so the dock only knows "open
this at this anchor". `Layout` asks the descriptor for shapes and no longer
switches on kinds. `EditMode` asks the descriptor which surfaces accept a drop.

**Settings.** The catalogue, the previews and the per-kind options pages are all
generated from the registry: `IslandOptions.cs` and the per-kind XAML blocks go
away. A kind's options page is the `Options` delegate in its own file, next to
its behaviour, instead of 71 `Section.` references in another project.

**Config.** An instance is `{ id, kind, group, width, options }` with `kind` a
string from the registry. The accumulated migration chain (`Repair`'s legacy
branches, `PinMigration`, `DriveMigration`, the clock's `showDate`, the old
`Drives` aggregate, `Display` on folders) is gone, and with it every reader of
an older shape (config shape 17): a config.json in an older shape is kept aside
as `config.shape<N>.json`, never over a name already taken, and the defaults
take its place; an import from one is refused with a sentence. The user
accepted breaking backwards compatibility, so it was taken once, here, rather
than carrying every past shape forever.

**Unknown because the file is older is not the same as unknown because someone
forgot, and only the second should be loud.** Both arrive as "this build has no
answer for that value", and the reflex is to write one default arm covering
them. That is wrong in both directions: it either makes an old file fail, or it
hands a new kind some other kind's answer and says nothing. So the boundary is
the only place that tolerates an unknown value: a word the file has that this
build does not know reads as the sentinel, and `Repair` drops it or maps it
forward. Everywhere inside the boundary, a value nobody has answered for throws
— inside, every value came from this build's own enum, so a missing answer is a
mistake and not an old file.

`Folders.KindOf` is the worked example. A `FolderView` outside the enum (an
older file's `"carousel"`) is the migration's own case and reads as the plain
grid folder; a *defined* view that no kind opens in throws. Written as one
`_ =>` arm, a fourth view would quietly have become a grid folder — which is
what the catalogue's preview, `Islands.Create` and the one-button sentences each
did before somebody happened to notice (§7a, and §6's first two stages).

## 6. Getting there

Each stage keeps the suite green and is useful on its own. Stages 3-5 are
per-kind, so they land incrementally rather than as one commit.

1. **Registry as data.** Descriptors exist and hold what is already knowable
   (id, title, glyph, category, surfaces, default width). Existing code reads
   them instead of its own switch. No behaviour change.
2. **Settings from the registry.** Catalogue, previews and options pages come
   from descriptors; the per-kind switches in the settings project are deleted.
3. **Shape split.** `Shape(options, metrics)` becomes the only sizing path,
   kind by kind, behind an adapter for the ones not yet converted. The
   state-sizing tests become redundant and are deleted when the last kind lands.
4. **One renderer.** `ITile`'s row path and the `*.Tile.cs` files go; grid and
   list are surface parameters of the same paint method. The catalogue's preview
   becomes a call to that same method (§7a), so `Karpo.Settings\Controls\
   Previews.cs` — a hand-drawn imitation of every kind — is deleted rather than
   kept in step.
5. **Flyouts by descriptor.** `IslandView` and the dock's switch go.
6. **Config rewrite.** String kinds, one legacy boundary, the migration chain
   deleted.

**Testing changes shape too.** Today a new kind needs someone to remember to
write its tests. With a registry, the suite enumerates it: every kind must
declare its surfaces, round-trip its options through JSON, produce a stable
shape for a given options/metrics pair, and render in each surface it claims.
A kind that forgets something fails a table test the day it is added.

## 7. The catalogue

There are about forty kinds and the number keeps growing, so the catalogue has
to be **browsable** and **dense** at the same time. It is shown in one place:
the add list every "+" of the bar opens (§7b). The settings app had a "Widget
library" page as well, a gallery with a tab per type; the person asked for
**no widget gallery any more** (backlog item 40), and the standing rule is that
Settings shows only settings, so the page, its side-menu row, its search and its
deep links (`--page catalogue`, `--add`, `--add-to`) are gone (2026-10-03). What
stays is the data both used, in Core (`Karpo.Core\Catalogue.cs`): the three
types' rows (`Catalogue.On`), their groups and order, and why a row can't be
added (`Catalogue.WhyNot`).

**One list with group headings**, not tabs and not pages. Tabs hide most of the
catalogue behind a click and make "what else is there?" expensive; one list can
be scanned end to end.

- **Each entry is a row, not a tile**: the kind's icon on the left and its name
  on the right, as a menu's row, left-aligned so the icons line up down each
  column and every name starts at the same x. A long name is cut with an
  ellipsis at its column's edge rather than widening the column. (This replaced
  square tiles with a caption under the glyph: the person found them harder to
  scan.)
- **Columns, read down and then across** (§7b), as many as keep it within a
  panel's most and the screen's width allow.
- **There is no detail panel and no preview.** The place was chosen before the
  list opened - the "+" that was pressed - so **a click on a row adds that kind
  there at once**. No selecting, no second button: that decision was already
  made. Enter does what a click does.
- **No rule under a group's heading.** The heading's weight and the room around
  it are the separation.
- **Groups, in this order**, each a heading in the same list:
  `Taskbar` (Start, Search, Task view, Widgets, Show desktop, Apps,
  Tray, Desktops, Separator) · `Time and information` (Clock, Calendar,
  Weather, Notifications) · `Network` (Network, Bluetooth, Airplane mode, Hotspot, VPN,
  Nearby sharing, Cast, Project) · `System` (Battery and power, Power button,
  Energy saver, Live captions, Accessibility, Keyboard, Pen menu, Touch keyboard,
  Virtual touchpad, Quick settings) · `Display` (Brightness, Night light, Rotation
  lock: Windows keeps the three on its Display page) · `Sound and media`
  (Volume, Volume slider, Spatial sound, Media controls) ·
  `Files and links` (Pin, Drive, Network drive, Removable devices,
  Snipping Tool, Clipboard history; Settings is under `System`) ·
  `Folders` (Grid, List, Row).
- **Availability is shown, never hidden.** A kind that cannot go where the
  list was opened (rotation lock on a PC whose screen doesn't turn, a card too
  big for its grid folder) is greyed, still in its place, and **says why in the
  row**: a second line under its name, in a few words ("This screen doesn't
  turn", "Needs 2 × 2 cells"). Hiding it makes the person wonder whether it
  exists at all, and a reason only on hover is one nobody sees.

This falls out of the registry: `Category`, `Blurb` and `Keywords` are
`required` fields on the descriptor, so a new kind cannot be added without
saying where it belongs. The grouping is data, not a hand-kept list.

**One calendar** (2026-09-27). The calendar and the date were two taskbar
entries whose click opened the same flyout, and the person asked for one. The
one is the calendar, beside the clock, and on the bar it shows the date — the
person's own format, in a time zone where they set one — with a click that opens
the calendar in the view it is set to. The calendar's badge and next event went
from the bar with it; the calendar's card and its line in a folder are what they
were. So the library lists one entry. The date's zone is the taskbar entry's
alone: a calendar carried into a folder takes its own options and leaves it
behind (`Partners`). A file with a `date` entry reads it as the calendar with the
date's zone and view, and a bar that had both keeps one, in the date's place,
with the calendar's options (`Karpo.Core\ConfigWords.cs`); no file is reset for it.

**The calendar's settings are its view, and its zone on the bar** (2026-10-05).
The person: "show events for shoudl not be a configuration option. it should list
all of them if the view shows the date for it", "there should not be a label
setting for the calendar", "there should not be a calendar size option". So three
cards went from the calendar's page in Settings, with their options in the file:

- **Show events for** (`daysAhead`, a day to a month, a week unless chosen; the agenda's is back as Days ahead,
  §496). The
  calendar lists every event of every day its view shows: the month's dots on all
  of its six weeks and the selected day's every event under them, the week's seven
  days and the day's one at every hour (below), and the card and the line in a
  folder every event of the days they name, today, tomorrow and the weekdays after:
  a week of them, so no two share a name (`CalendarIsland.AgendaDays`), as many as
  the room holds and the rest counted.
- **Label** (`label`, on the calendar's entry): words such as a city that stood for
  the day's name on the bar. The date shows the day's name and the date, as
  Windows' own does. The clock keeps its own **Label**, which names its place
  ("Tokyo") in its panel and its tile, and the card is shown for a clock alone.
- **Calendar size** (`size`: Normal, Large, Larger). The panel has one size, as
  Windows 11's calendar flyout has: the normal one, the island flyouts' width for
  the day and the month, 640 DIP for the week and the year, at most 70 % of the
  work area tall.

A file that still has `daysAhead`, `label` or `size` in a calendar's record reads
as every other: the keys are read past and not written back, and nothing counts as
a change for them (`OneCalendarTests`, `RepairTests`, `CalendarAgendaTests`). A
date entry's label from before the one calendar is not carried over either.

**The day and week views show the whole day, and slide through the days**
(2026-10-04, the whole day 2026-10-05). The person: "scrolling should basically
scroll in the day direction", and then "the calendar height changes when i scroll
in week view. in week view it should show the whole day from 0-24 all the time, not
only when there is a entry there". The hours had been only those the events needed
(never less than 8 to 18), the rest folded into thin strips, and sized to fit the
panel; as the days slid, other events opened other hours and the panel grew and
shrank under the pointer. Now the hours are always midnight to midnight
(`DayStrip.Hours`): an hour is 48 DIP at the least (Caption's two lines and their
air, so a half-hour event says its title and an hour its time), more where the
room holds the whole day at more, and the hours scroll in a window that takes all
the panel has under its most (70 % of the work area). The room is the panel's, not
the events': the same hours whatever days are shown, and the window gives the
all-day lanes their room as they come and go, so the panel is one height whatever
the days and wherever the hours are scrolled. It opens with the hour before now at
the top of the hours, as Outlook opens on the time it is (`DayStrip.OpenBefore`).
The largest text on a small screen, whose head alone takes most of the 70 %, keeps a
window of hours and may go past the most while it stays on the screen; there "Date
and time" goes under "Open Calendar" where the two no longer fit side by side.

Up and down scroll the hours, as Outlook's do: the wheel over them, gliding an hour
a notch on the slide's curve, a touchpad's small moves following the fingers, and
the up and down arrows an hour. Sideways moves the days: a tilt of the wheel, Shift
with it, a touchpad's sideways moves and the wheel anywhere off the hours (the
headings, the title), the left and right arrows, Page Up/Down and the arrow buttons;
a day at a time, a week with Ctrl or Shift, the week view a continuous strip that
follows a touchpad's small moves and rests on a whole day when they stop, the
selection going along. The strip is painted once with a week spare on either side
(three days in the day view) and glided by the compositor, the head band with its
weekdays and all-day row in step with the hours; the events of the days beyond it
are asked for ahead (`Karpo.Dock\Calendar\DayStrip.cs`, `CalendarFlyout`). "Today"
and Home bring today back.

**What a block says** (2026-10-04). On a busy week at 100 % the fitted hours came to
some 19 px and the events' titles were cut to two or three letters ("Sta…"). The
events' blocks step their type down from Caption as the hours get short (12, 11,
then 10 DIP at the text size, the floor), one size for the whole view, and say the
title first: over as many lines as the block holds, broken between words, the time
and then the place only on the lines the whole title leaves
(`Karpo.Dock\Calendar\EventText.cs`). At the whole day's 48 DIP an hour they are
Caption.

**Windows' own buttons** (2026-09-27). The person: "implement all… orient
yourself on how windows11 does it". Five taskbar entries that Windows 11 has and
Karpo did not, each where Windows keeps it and each the taskbar's alone:

- **Widgets**, first on the bar, opens Windows' widgets board as Win+W does. A
  new bar put Karpo's weather where Windows keeps this button until 2026-10-14, and now neither (§167)
  (`Sections.DefaultLayout`); both are in the add list for whoever wants them.
- **Pen menu, Touch keyboard, Virtual touchpad**, after the tray's icons, open
  Windows' own pen menu, touch keyboard and virtual touchpad. The pen menu and
  the touchpad show where Windows would show them — the pen menu on a PC with a
  pen, the virtual touchpad on a touch screen — or always, where the person
  chose that, as Windows' "System tray icons" settings let them (`InputButtons`,
  `InputButtonOptions`). The touch keyboard has no such option and always shows
  where it is placed (2026-10-08: "it should always show"); a choice an older
  file kept for it is dropped as the file is read. One that would
  not show takes no room on the bar, and edit mode keeps its placeholder so it
  can still be moved or set to Always. A new bar has the pen menu on a PC with a
  pen and the touch keyboard on one with a touch screen, never the touchpad,
  which Windows leaves off; the bar follows the PC as a pen or a keyboard comes
  and goes.

All four are drawn as Start, search and task view are: one glyph in a button's
well, drawn by the bar (`BarEntries.IsWindowsButton`, `HitKind.WindowsButton`),
and each has a tooltip, because its click opens nothing of Karpo's own. What a
click opens is a question with no side effects (`Karpo.Dock\WindowsButtons.cs`,
`WindowsButtons.Target`): Win+W, the
addresses Windows registers for the pen menu and the touchpad
(`ms-penworkspace:`, `ms-virtualtouchpad:`), and the touch keyboard's own switch
(ITipInvocation), which shows it and hides it again as Windows' button does.

Copilot had a button here too, after task view, opening the Copilot app or Copilot on the web, until
the person asked for it gone (2026-10-09: "remove the copilot widget."). It is in no registry, page,
add list or language now; `copilot` is a word this build does not know, so a file that still has one
drops it as it is read (`TolerantEnumConverter`), as it drops an entry from a newer Karpo, and the
bar never shows it as a broken widget. Where Windows pinned the Copilot app, that pin is a pin.

**Shortcuts to Windows' apps** (the backlog, items 10 and 18). Two one-icon
widgets in the design of Task view and Search, on the bar, as a grid's card and as a
list's line alike (`Partners`), drawn on the bar as Windows' buttons are and in a
folder by `ShortcutTile`; a click opens the same thing wherever it stands
(`WindowsButtons.Target`, carried out by `WindowsButtons.Press` in a folder):

- **Snipping Tool** starts a snip straight away, as Win+Shift+S does. Microsoft's
  documented way in (`ms-screenclip://capture/…`, 2025) answers a packaged app only —
  it needs a `redirect-uri` only a package can receive, and without one the Snipping
  Tool shows nothing — so Karpo uses the address the Snipping Tool has always answered,
  bare `ms-screenclip:`, which opens the overlay as the Print Screen key does. The
  installed app still reads the older parameters (its own buttons build them), and they
  are its menu: "Open Snipping Tool" (the app itself), "Snip in 3 seconds" and "Snip in
  10 seconds" (`?delayInSeconds=`) and "Record screen" (`?type=recording`, Snipping Tool
  11.2307 and later). A row the installed Snipping Tool cannot do is greyed. In a folder
  the snip waits for the folder: the click closes every open folder, and the dock starts
  the snip once they are off the screen (destroyed, and `DwmFlush` twice), so no folder is
  in the picture — and so do the menu's snips in 3 and 10 seconds and "Record screen"
  (`PicturesTheScreen`), the folder the menu stood over and any it stood in. Where the Snipping Tool is not installed it says so as a pin to an app
  that is not here does: faint with the warning badge, its name in the faint ink; a click on
  the bar says "This app isn't installed on this PC" in a menu with "Get Snipping Tool from
  Microsoft Store", which its right click offers too, and a click in a folder — which opens
  no popup — opens that Store page. Its button then has no tooltip: a click opens Karpo's own
  menu, which says it (as a broken pin's does). Win+Shift+S is its own overlay, so pressing
  that instead would do nothing.
- **Settings** opens Windows Settings (`ms-settings:`), as Win+I.

Each opens an app, an `Action`, so each has a tooltip on the bar, the Snipping Tool only while
it is installed. The library groups the Snipping Tool under Files (what a click opens) and
Settings under System.

**Phone Link** was a third shortcut (item 23) and was **removed at the person's asking**
(2026-10-04: "it can just be replaced by a user by a pin"). A pin to the app does what it did.
A file that still holds one — on the bar, as a grid's card or as a list's line — reads with
exactly that pin in its place: the same id, size and cell, its target
`shell:AppsFolder\Microsoft.YourPhone_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App`, its name and icon left to Windows
(`ConfigWords`, read before the file is parsed, and written back once). Turning it into a pin
rather than dropping it keeps the person's bar as it was.

**Clipboard history** (the backlog, item 13; since 2026-10-10 a preset folder holding the clipboard's line, §101). A taskbar entry alone — its face is only a
way into its flyout (§15.2) — at the end of the bar before the status icons and the tray,
whose click opens what was copied lately in a flyout modelled on Windows' own Win+V panel
(`Karpo.Dock\Clipboard`): "Clipboard history" over a card per item, the newest first —
text in its first three lines, a picture as its thumbnail — with "Clear all" at the top,
and on each card its delete and, where the history can be pinned, its pin. A click on a
card does what Win+V's does: the item goes on the clipboard, the flyout closes and gives
the focus back to the window that had it, and the dock pastes it there with Ctrl+V
(`ClipboardPaste`) — only where that window is still there and in front again, is not
Karpo's (its process, `Karpo.exe`, the settings app's `settings\Karpo.exe`), not the shell's (the desktop, a
taskbar, Start, Search), not a console's (conhost, Windows Terminal, mintty, PuTTY, ConEmu:
there Ctrl+V is as often the program's own key — vim's block select, a shell's quoted insert —
as a paste, so it would type ^V), not an elevated program's (above Karpo's integrity, where
Windows drops Karpo's keys without a word, so the paste would do nothing and seem done) and
not focused on an edit control's password box (`ES_PASSWORD`); anywhere else the item is left
on the clipboard. The window puts its focus back on its own control a moment after it is given
the front, so the dock reads it again every 25 ms (`PasteWait`) and pastes only once two reads
in a row find it in front with the same control focused — the password box that takes the focus
a moment later is seen — and gives up after twelve. A Store app (Calculator, Settings) is a
frame in front with the app's CoreWindow inside it on another thread, and the frame's thread reads
no focus at all: its focus is read on the CoreWindow's thread, else is the CoreWindow itself while
it or its frame is in front, where XAML keeps its controls' focus (`ClipboardPaste.FocusOf`), so
it settles and pastes like any other window. Chosen with Enter or Space, the flyout keeps
the keyboard until the key is let go, so its repeats and its release never reach the window the
item is pasted into. A browser's or a XAML app's password box
does not say so to user32, and asking UI Automation would turn on the app's accessibility
tree for one paste, so it is not asked. Pin, delete and "Clear all" (which keeps the
pinned) leave the flyout open. No tooltip: the flyout says it all.

Whose history it shows (`ClipboardStore`): **Windows' own** while the person has it on and
Windows gives it — `Clipboard.GetHistoryItemsAsync` answers an unpackaged program — read
afresh each time the flyout opens; an item is put back with `SetHistoryItemAsContent`,
deleted with `DeleteItemFromHistory`, and "Clear all" is `ClearHistory`. Windows gives a
program no way to pin, so Windows' items have no pin. Otherwise **Karpo's own**: what the
clipboard heard (`AddClipboardFormatListener`) while a clipboard widget stood on a bar, in
memory only, never on disk — text up to a million characters (a longer text is not kept,
as one cut short would paste something else), and pictures whole up to 40 MB each, which
covers a 4K screenshot (about 33 MB as a DIB), all of them under a budget of 160 MB past
which the oldest unpinned pictures go; 25 at most with the pinned kept, the same content
once — and a line under the cards says why, with a link to Windows' clipboard settings.
Karpo keeps its own only while Windows' cannot be had: reading Windows' is given 5 seconds
for `GetHistoryItemsAsync` and 8 in all, past which Karpo's own shows, saying Windows'
could not be read. A card is made from the first few thousand characters of a text alone,
and that is all of a Windows item's text Karpo holds.

**A secret is never kept or shown.** Content a program marks for it is not even read:
`ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing` present, `CanIncludeInClipboardHistory` 0,
`CanUploadToCloudClipboard` 0 (which Windows still keeps locally; Karpo, at the person's
word, nowhere), or the older "Clipboard Viewer Ignore"; a marker whose value cannot be read
counts as a no (`ClipboardRules`). What Karpo asks of Windows is one seam
(`IClipboardSystem`), so the tests bring a fake and never touch the person's clipboard.

### 7a. The previews are gone

This section used to argue that the catalogue's previews should stop being a
second drawing of every widget and become the widget's own paint method, once
stage 4 made `Paint(surface, box, state)` callable from outside the dock.

That plan never ran, and it does not need to. The person looked at the catalogue
and asked for the previews to be **removed everywhere** - from the catalogue and
from the top of a widget's own settings page. So the second drawing is deleted
rather than unified: `Karpo.Settings\Controls\Previews.cs`, `Controls\KindPreview.cs`,
`Logic\PreviewMetrics.cs`, `Logic\DrivePreview.cs`, their coverage and picture
tests, and the preview-versus-widget sheets that existed to prove the two agreed.

What is left in their place is the kind's **icon and name** in the catalogue's
rows and - the point - the real widget on the bar a moment after it is clicked. `WidgetKind.Preview` had no reader after that, and it went from
the registry with the first step of the split (S5).

The lesson worth keeping is the one that made the section: a drawing whose only
job is to look like another drawing will drift, and the choice is to unify them
or to have only one. We now have only one.

### 7b. Adding from the bar: the add list (2026-10-03)

Backlog items 39, 40, 3, 24, 1 and 5. The bar no longer opens the settings app to add a widget:
there is no gallery to go to. Every add opens **one list, right where it was pressed**, and a pick
adds the widget there at once.

- **Where the adds are: "Add a widget" on every display** (the person, 2026-10-07, round 3, and
  round 6; `EditDeck`, `EditDeckPlan`, Dock.EditDeck.cs). In edit mode, and only then, every display
  has an **"Add a widget"** button, the first of its edit bar by the layout's first bar (§50). It
  opens the add list for that display, away from the bar. A list folder and a separator are not at
  the top of the list any more (§50), nor buttons of their own beside "Add a widget" (2026-10-08, gone
  again in §304): they stand among the widgets, in Popular. **A pick places nothing** (`AddSpot.Follows`,
  Dock.EditFollow.cs): the widget goes into the list at the place of that display nearest the pointer,
  so a bar can draw it as it really is, and is carried from there as a drag carries a block, with no
  button held — the widget at the pointer, the blue ghost where it would land. A left click puts it
  down there (its settings page opens then); Escape or a right click calls it off and it comes out of
  the list again. The click, the right click and Escape are heard by low-level hooks wherever they
  land (`EditFollowHook`), and kept from what is under the pointer: the add list, a menu, hands the
  foreground to another app as it closes, which takes the mouse from the bar, and with no button held
  a bar hears no click outside Karpo's windows. Losing the mouse does not drop a following widget, and
  a click while one follows only puts it down. A widget goes into the list of the display it was added
  on, and is put down on any display, as every carried block is (§519; it stayed on its own display
  until then). The bar carries no "+", and no button for the settings or for leaving: the
  edit bar's "Open settings" opens the settings app, which stays in front while edit mode is on,
  and its "Close edit mode" (§42, §43), or Escape wherever the keys are, ends it (§7, "Edit mode and
  the settings app"); a click away leaves it on.
  - *The sections' edit bars hold only what they cannot show* (`EditRail`, `EditRailPlan`,
    Dock.EditRail.cs). Their "+" and direct adds are gone; a section with a widget it has no room for
    has an edit bar of one button beside it on its inner side, one row or one column, never a square,
    which names the widget (or warns of several) and opens its menu; a section showing everything has
    none. They keep clear of the surfaces' bars, of each other and of the display's edit bar
    (`EditRails.Clear`). The button is a warning and looks like one (2026-10-11: "it should be
    more visible. it should be red or orange"): solid in Windows' warning orange (#FC9A03, the
    orange of Windows Update's warning shield, the same on light and dark), its glyph black on it,
    lighter under the pointer and darker pressed; the system's highlight with its highlight text in
    high contrast (`EditRail.Warning`).
  - *An empty section is room of its own* (2026-10-07: "empty sections show with a sensible size in
    edit mode"; `Layout.EmptyRooms`, `Layout.EmptyCells`): three cells of the widget grid and the
    gaps between them, an empty edit block in the blocks' wash and outline, where that section would
    grow from — the bar's start, its centre, its end — and where a block carried onto it is dropped
    (`DropSlotTests`, `SectionLayoutTests`). At rest an empty section takes no room. A full bar makes
    that room as it makes room for anything: placeholders go first, then its app buttons get smaller
    and go behind "…", and only then the last widget gives way, which the bar lists (`NotShown`) and
    the section's edit bar says (`AddButtonProbeTests` walks two thousand bars).
  - *Keys and Narrator.* Tab walks the blocks of the bar with the keys, in their order along it
    (`EditStops`), then every edit bar's button, and back; Enter does not place a following widget —
    a click does. The display's edit bar is the pointer's.
- **What the list is** (`AddList`, `FlyoutLayout.Library`; since 2026-10-11 the add tree, §136). A
  Karpo flyout, not a window: the heading says where the widget will go ("Add to taskbar", "Add to
  <folder>"), the search field, then two columns under their headings — **Popular**, a fixed handful
  and what a bar or folder is arranged with, and **Browse**, a row per subject ("Time and calendar",
  "Connections", …) opening its submenu, as Windows' "New ›" is. Each row the icon and the name.
  - *Columns* (`Flyout.HeadingFlow`). Each heading stands at the top of a column of its own, 240
    DIPs wide, its rows down it: the list is two columns, about twelve rows tall, on every screen.
    (Until 2026-10-11 the rows were the library's groups, run down as many as six columns as a
    newspaper's, `Flyout.LibraryFlow`, which the search's results still use.) The arrows follow the
    columns: Up and Down stay in one, Left and Right go to the nearest row of the other; Right,
    Enter or Space on a subject open its submenu with the keys in it, Left and Escape close it. A
    submenu opens beside its row's column after the system's menu delay under the pointer, and a
    folder in it opens another the same way.
  - A pick closes it, as a menu's pick does, and the new widget has edit mode's focus; the "+" is
    still there for the next. It light-dismisses as a menu (`Topic.Library`).
  - *A search field* (2026-10-04: "the add widget dialog should have a search field where you can
    search for widgets"; `Flyout.Search.cs`). Under the heading, over the rows and staying there as
    they scroll: Windows 11's text box as Karpo's other flyout fields are (`TextField`), 32 DIPs,
    "Search widgets" while empty, the accent line along its bottom while it has the keys, inset as
    the content is (16 DIPs, under the title's start). Typing **lists what matches** in place of the
    tree (`AddList.Results`; until 2026-10-11 it dimmed what didn't match where it stood, which a
    tree of submenus can't show): one column of rows, each its icon, its name and under it where it
    is, the folders it is in ("Connections › Wi-Fi") or at the top its column's heading, a greyed
    row's reason after that. Each widget once, however often the tree shows it. The panel keeps the
    tree's size and place while the person types, the results scrolling in it where there are more;
    nothing matching is one greyed row, "No widgets match". A widget matches by its name, its
    description, its search words (`WidgetInfo.Keywords`) and the names of the folders it is in, every
    word typed found somewhere inside one of them, whatever the capitals and the accents
    (`CatalogueSearch`, which folds accents by a table of its own: the dock runs in invariant
    globalization, where `string.Normalize` does nothing). What is called what was typed comes first,
    then what has it in its name, then in its words, then in its folders'. An empty field is the tree.
    The keys: the field has them as the list opens, so typing searches at once, and typing in a
    submenu closes it and goes on in the field; Down, Tab or Enter go to the first result; Enter adds
    the one result where there is one and it can be added; Escape empties the field, from a row too,
    and an empty field's Escape closes the list. Up from the first row, Backspace and anything typed
    on a row go back to the field. Narrator finds the field first, an edit named "Search widgets" with
    the focus while it has the keys, and hears how many widgets match as the search changes, "3
    widgets match" (`AddList.Said`, a UI Automation notification: `Uia.Announce`).
    `AddListSearchTests`, `AddListSearchPictures`.
- **Three libraries, one rule** (item 3). The place decides the library (`AddList.TypeOf`): a place
  on the bar lists the taskbar entries, a grid folder the grid widgets, a list folder the list
  widgets — `Catalogue.On(type)`, in its groups and order. A widget of another library is not in
  the list at all: the list is about this place. What can't be added here is greyed in its place —
  rotation lock where the screen doesn't turn, a card too big for the grid — and says why under
  its name, in a few words (`Catalogue.WhyNot`), the row two lines tall and its column flowing
  round it. A pick adds through `IslandEdits.Add` on the bar and `Folders.AddNew` in a folder (at
  the cell of the "+" that was pressed, as much of the card's usual span as fits there, else the
  first free place; after the last line in a list).
- **Ready-made groups** (2026-10-05: "in the add widget menu there should also be another
  additional section where you can add precompiled groups of stuff. for example a list folder which
  contains all the system widgets already, or a list folder which shows a list of stocks already";
  `Karpo.Core\Presets.cs`). A row each in its subject of the add tree (§136; until 2026-10-11 under
  a heading of their own after the widgets), its icon and its name as a widget's row is; the search
  field finds a group by its name, its line, its words and the names of the widgets in it ("cpu"
  finds System). A pick adds the group's one folder at the "+" that was pressed.
  - *One folder, always* (2026-10-05: "the ready made widgets should only ever add one folder with
    multiple widgets inside"). Every group is a folder, a grid or a list, and adding one adds exactly
    that one entry to the bar, its widgets inside. Connectivity was loose taskbar entries and put four
    buttons on the bar; it is a list folder now (below).
    `PresetsTests.EveryGroupAddsExactlyOneFolderWithItsWidgetsInside` holds every group at every "+"
    of the bar.
  - *Data, once, in Core.* A group is a `Preset` record in `Presets.All`: the folder it makes (a grid
    or a list folder), its name and glyph, its grid's columns, and its widgets — each its word, a grid
    card's place and span, a list line's height, a share's symbol, what this PC must have
    (`PresetNeed.Battery`), or one per fixed drive. The act that makes widgets of it
    (`Presets.Folder`, `Presets.AddToBar`) is Core's too, so the settings app can offer the same
    groups later and make the same thing. A group is never stored: what it makes is an ordinary
    folder of ordinary widgets, every one with an id nobody else on the bar has.
  - *Where they fit* (`Presets.On`): **the bar alone**, every group, its folder in the section of
    the "+" at its index. A folder's add list has none: folders do not nest, so a
    group there could only be its widgets loose, which is not one folder. (Until 2026-10-05 a folder
    offered the groups of its own view and took their widgets loose.)
  - *All of them at once* (2026-10-11: "make a layout with all the premade groups, then i will
    rearrange them"). `Karpo.exe --add-preset-layout` (`PresetLayout`) writes a layout "All
    ready-made folders" (id `allPresets`) into config.json through the ordinary load and save, so a
    running dock merges it in on its reload; it opens no window and touches no taskbar, and exits 0,
    or 1 with the reason on stderr. The layout is a new bar's (`Config.FirstLayout`) without its
    groups: its type, size, show and own buttons, then every group in `Presets.All` made by
    `Presets.AddToBar`, in library order, where the person arranged them (2026-10-11, below): the
    clock to the power button after the open apps, the mail to the network drive in the middle,
    the notifications to the notes at the end, a separator, the system icons, the keyboard, now
    playing and show desktop; no search box, Task view, tray or brightness (`PresetLayout.SectionOf`,
    a preset added later falling where its library place puts it); the battery's only on a PC with one. No
    display is switched to it and no other layout changes; run again, it replaces the one before
    (by id, else by name) in its place, under that one's id.
  - *One layout made new* (2026-10-11). `Karpo.exe --renew-layout <layoutId>` (`LayoutRenewal`)
    puts what a first install makes (`Config.FirstLayout`, read on this PC as a new install reads
    it, its folders the presets') in the place of that layout, under its id, name and icon, so the
    displays showing it still do; its own pins stay, as they are and in their order, before the
    open apps, instead of Windows' pins read again. Nothing else in the file changes. It first
    copies config.json to `config.before-renew-<id>.json` beside it (a later run to the same name
    with the time after the id, never over the first copy), then saves through the ordinary load
    and save; exits 0 saying what it did, 1 with the reason (an unknown id lists the layouts), 2
    without an id.
  - *Its icon* (2026-10-05: "the ready made folders should also get an icon per default and not
    show the multiple icon ones"). A group's folder shows its own glyph on the bar
    (the Icon face, `FolderFaces.Icon`, §67), not its first four widgets' icons in a 2×2; its settings can switch it to
    what is inside, as any folder's. System the diagnostic glyph (E9D9), Stocks the area chart
    (E9D2), Quick settings the sliders (E9E9), Widgets board the dashboard (F246), Notification
    center the bell (EA8F), Focus F272, Media the speaker (E8D6), Storage the drive (EDA2),
    Connectivity the network (E968).
  - *The groups.* **Clock** (list, the clock face): the bar's clock made of widgets (§73), as the
    person arranged it (2026-10-11, below). **System** (list): processor, memory, disk, network and graphics, each its
    two-row compact line, and the battery where the PC has one. **Stocks** (list): MSFT, AAPL,
    NVDA and ^GSPC as "S&P 500", Windows' Watchlist, each a two-row line. **Quick settings** (grid,
    nine columns, 364 DIP, the width of Windows' own): Windows 11's tiles three across at three by
    two (118 × 77 DIP, wider than tall, as Windows' buttons are) — airplane mode, energy saver,
    accessibility, night light, do not disturb, mobile hotspot — and the brightness and the volume a
    row each across the foot, brightness first, as Windows has them; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, Windows'
    first two tiles, are the taskbar's alone and have no card. **Widgets board** (grid, twelve by
    eleven, two of Windows' card columns): its cards Windows' medium and large, never small — the
    weather and the calendar at six by five (241 × 200 DIP: the weather's hours, the calendar's
    month), MSFT and the S&P 500 at six by three (wide cards, the chart beside the price), what's
    playing twelve by three across the foot; 511 × 518 DIP with the panel's pads and footer, inside
    70 % of a 1080p screen at 100 %, scrolling its last row at 150 % there. (Quick settings was six
    columns at two by two, the board eight columns with the weather and the calendar at four by
    four: 2026-10-05, "make the ready made widgets board widgets bigger. same for quick settings".)
    **Notification center** (list): the notifications, the calendar and a focus session, the flyout
    Windows' clock opens. **Focus** (list): the clock, a timer, a focus session, do not disturb and
    the calendar. **Media** (list): what's playing, the volume and the output device. **Storage**
    (list): a line for each fixed drive, read as the group is picked, and the removable devices.
    **Connectivity** (list): the network's activity (a two-row line), airplane mode, the VPN, the
    mobile hotspot and nearby sharing. The network and Bluetooth buttons are not in it: they are the
    taskbar's alone and no folder holds them.
  - *Its dividers* (2026-10-08: "add proper dividers for the ready made widget groups"). A list
    group parts its lines with the list's own divider (`PresetItem.Divider`, §9, "A divider") where
    they are two things, as Windows parts them. A divider splits the list into cards since
    2026-10-09 (§78), so it stands only where a split clearly helps (the person, the same day):
    **Focus** the Clock app's three and do not disturb from the calendar; **Storage** the fixed

    **System** (the battery is one more reading) and **Stocks** (one Watchlist) have none.
  - *One card, the person's clock* (2026-10-11: "the clock layout i already changed on the given
    list, get it from there, design the other ones in a similar fashion"). The person arranged the
    Clock folder of their "All ready-made folders" layout by hand: the time over its date, the

    (no fixed drive read) it goes too, so none is ever first, last or next to another

  - *The person's own, every one* (2026-10-11: "ah and yes i changed the layouts on the layout page
    already. so take them over to the presets"). Their "All ready-made folders" layout, arranged by
    hand, is now what every preset makes, line for line, and their "Default" what a new bar is.

    order, lists, widths, heights, options, footers, face, name, glyph), the preset layout's
    arrangement, and a new left-aligned bar's entries. What changed: **Calendar** the date, the

    fixed; **Wi-Fi** and **Bluetooth** their page ten rows fixed; **Sound** two lists side by side,

    `PresetItem.NewList`, and a preset name its lists' widths, `Preset.Widths`); **Timer** and
    **Focus time** two rows fixed, **Stopwatch** five; **Power** the commands alone; **System** a
    Task Manager footer; the **Task Manager** and **Clipboard** footers' one link on the right
    (`PremadeWidgets`); **Stocks** a wide list; **Stock** six rows fixed (its age and refresh come
    from eight); **Drive** automatic up to ten; **Clipboard history**, **To-do** and **Notes** ten
    rows fixed; **Media** a divider again between what's playing and its volume and output, as they

    their "Default" as it stands later that day ("the default taskbar that i have right now should
    become the new template for the new installations. (the templates for the folders of course

    the weather, a separator, the tray, a separator, the system icons and the keyboard, a

    of their layout only because their PC has none, and is unchanged.
  - *Its settings.* As every add opens the new widget's page, a group opens the page of the one of
    its widgets that needs setting up — the widgets board's weather, with no place yet, at its
    place field — else the folder's own page (`AddList.SettingsPath`). The edit mode's focus goes to

  - `PresetsTests`, `AddListPresetsTests`; pictures in `AddListPresetPictures`
    (`add-list-groups-bar-*.png`), `PresetFolderPictures` (`preset-<id>-*.png`) and
    `SceneTreeTests.PresetBarSheets` (`preset-bar-<id>-*.png`).
- **What went.** The dock's `--page catalogue --add-to …` launches, the marker that waited for the
  settings app to save, and `karpo.addcancel`; then (2026-10-03) the settings app's "Widget
  library" page itself, with its side-menu row, its search (the settings app's `CatalogueSearch`,
  whose rule the add list's field took up in Core, 2026-10-04), its
  `--add`/`--add-to` deep links (`AddPlace`, `CatalogueTarget`), `KarpoProcess.AddCancelled` and
  the test hooks that pictured it. Nothing in the settings app adds a widget any more; its test
  hooks' "add" and "add-to-folder" still make an edit to picture a page after it.
- **No buttons in a folder's footer** (2026-10-05: "remove the edit button and close button from
  the folder views again"). The edit button item 5 put in a resting folder's footer, and the close
  control an arranged folder had in the same corner, are gone: the footer carries the folder's
  glyph and name, and while a grid is arranged its steppers and titles toggle on a second line.
  The way into a folder's contents is the bar's edit mode ("Edit taskbar" on the bar, or a widget
  dragged): a click on the folder there opens it arranged in place. The ways out are its own
  button on the bar (a click on a folder standing open closes it), Escape with the folder's keys,
  and edit mode ending (Escape, "Close edit mode" on the edit bar, the bar menu's
  Done), which closes every folder standing open; a click on another app's window no longer does.
- **A widget's menu at rest** (item 1; **superseded by §129**: Duplicate, Settings and Remove are a
  row of icon buttons in every widget's menu, at rest and arranged). Duplicate, Ungroup and Remove arrange the bar, so they are
  a widget's menu only while the bar is arranged, on the bar and in a folder alike
  (`WidgetRowsFor`). At rest a widget's menu is its kind's own actions — the clock's date and time,
  the desktops' rows, the sound, network and battery icons' rows, a status icon's rows, a card's or
  a line's acts — then, last, under a separator, its **"Settings"** (`RestRows`), which opens its
  page in Karpo's settings exactly as a click on it in edit mode does (`OpenWidgetSettings`: an open
  settings window goes there, a closed one starts on it). Item 1 had moved Settings to edit mode
  too; the person brought it back (2026-10-05: "when i right click a widget it should show the
  settings action again"). The row reads "Settings" everywhere, the same row and command as edit
  mode's: not "<Widget> settings", which is how a row naming a page of Windows' reads ("Sound
  settings", "Power & battery settings"), and some widgets' own rows are those. A widget with
  nothing of its own — Search, Task view, show desktop, the tray's chevron, Settings — shows
  **"Settings" alone**, with no separator, on the bar as in a folder; that reverses G17, where it
  showed no menu at rest. Only a widget the file has lost shows none (`Dock.RestMenuFor`). A pin's
  jump list has its "Settings" at rest again, after pinning and before closing its windows, and a
  broken pin's flyout after "Locate…" and "Remove this pin" (`Dock.BrokenRows`), on the bar and in a
  folder; it read "Pin settings…", and reads "Settings" now. Not affected: a tray icon's menu, which
  is its app's, the Start button's quick links, and the bar's own menu. "Edit
  taskbar" and "Taskbar settings", the bar's own menu, open only on the bar where it is not a
  widget: the room between and around the widgets and the sections, the grip band (2026-10-04: "edit
  taskbar and taskbar settings should only appear when right clicking on the taskbar area that is
  not a widget"). That reverses two earlier turns (F1/G5): such a widget fell back to the bar's
  menu, as a right click on Windows' own search button gives the taskbar's, and a bar covered end
  to end added "Edit taskbar" under a widget's own rows (`Layout.AnyBare`, gone with it); the grip
  band, which runs the bar's whole length, is the bar on every bar. In edit mode the rows are as
  they were.
- **A widget's menu has no title** (2026-10-10: "in the right click context menu for all taskbar
  widgets you should remove their title, e.g. Folder - Calendar"). The bold "Clock · Tokyo" or
  "<folder kind> · Calendar" line over the rows is gone from every widget's menu — at rest and while
  arranged, on the bar and for a widget in a folder, and a broken pin's menu in a folder; the first
  row is the first act (or "Settings"). The name is still the menu's accessible name, for a screen
  reader (`Dock.WidgetMenuName`, `Flyout.SpokenName`). Section headings inside the rows stay: the
  sound panel's "Output"/"Input", a removable device's name, a media line's position. Not a menu,
  so kept: the title of the flyout a click on a broken pin or a missing app's shortcut opens.
- **A new widget opens its settings at once** (superseded 2026-10-12, §149: adding opens nothing) (item 24; 2026-10-04: "when a widget was added it
  should immediately open its settings in the settings window"). Every pick from the add list —
  on the bar, in a grid folder, in a list folder — opens the new widget's own page in Karpo's
  settings straight away: an open settings window goes there, a closed one starts on it
  (`Dock.AddedArgs`, `--page layout --owner … --island <path> --added <stamp>`). The app reads the
  file before it looks for the widget (`SettingsModel.CatchUp`), since the dock saved it a moment
  ago and an open window would not have it yet. A widget with nothing of its own to set still
  opens its own page, which says what it is and where it stands, and its size where that varies:
  the page is where the next thing about it is done.
  - **One that needs setting up opens at its field.** A pin with no target, a stock with no
    symbol, a weather kind with neither a place nor this PC's location, a folder's contents with
    no folder, a heading with no words, a feed with no address and a drive widget with no drive
    show nothing until somebody sets them; their page opens with the keyboard in the box that sets
    it up — "What it opens", the symbol's and the place's search boxes, the folder's path, the
    heading's words, the feed's address, the list of drives — scrolled into view (`WidgetSetup.Needs`
    in Core, `--setup <field>`, `MainWindow.Arrive`, `Logic\SetupFocus.cs`).
  - **Every other one opens at the top of its page**, its settings first, with the keyboard in no
    box: a kind's options page is kept between widgets, so it is scrolled back up, and a box an
    earlier widget left the keyboard in lets go of it.
  - **Several added quickly are one window, showing the last.** Each add starts
    the settings app, and every start after the first hands its arguments to the one running
    (`SingleInstance`; one whose window has closed lets go of its claim before it exits,
    `SingleInstance.Release`, so a start just after starts a window of its own rather than handing
    over to a process that is ending); starts made while the first is still coming up can hand over out of
    order, so the window goes by the stamp of each add, and an add overtaken by a later one is
    passed over (`Logic\AddedArrival.cs`). An earlier add's focusing or scrolling still under way
    gives way to the next start (`MainWindow.StopArrival`).
  - **Never a second window** (2026-10-11: "sometimes it opens two or more, sometimes the window
    crashes, other times it just freezes"). The first process owns the claim (a mutex it holds, not
    merely made) and listens from the first moment of `Main`, before WinUI starts; what is handed to
    it while it is still starting waits in a queue and is shown in order once the window can show it,
    each hand-off on its own, so one that fails is logged and costs neither the window nor the rest
    (`Logic\SingleStart.cs`, `HandOffQueue`). A later start hands over, or takes the claim the moment
    the first lets go of it; it never starts a window while another process holds the claim — what
    used to happen when the first took more than 3–5 s to answer. The crashes and freezes were the
    alarm's time picker: its setter raised on every set, the binding gave the picker its time back,
    and the page recursed until the stack ran out (nine WER dumps, all the same frames); it raises
    only on a change now (`AlarmTimes.Picked`). An error XAML reports is logged with XAML's own
    words for it and the window stays.
  - The page rather than a flyout of Karpo's, because those boxes (the suggestion boxes that
    search as you type, a pin's file and folder choosers) are the settings app's and are not
    repeated in the dock.
  - **Not for drops.** A pin made by dropping a file, folder or app onto the bar is a drag, not
    a pick from the add list: it already has its target, and the person is arranging, so nothing
    opens.
- **A widget that is not set up says so, with "Set up in Settings"** (2026-10-08: "rss feed flyout
  should show shortcut to settings if it is not fully configured to show a source, this should also
  be done for all the other widgets. in the same fashion"; `Karpo.Dock\SetupPrompt.cs`). Every
  widget that shows nothing until it is set up — a feed with no address, a stock with no symbol, a
  weather kind with neither a place nor this PC's location, a drive or network drive with no drive,
  a pin with nothing to open, a heading with no words (`WidgetSetup.Needs`, which now names the
  drives' `volume` too, so adding one opens its page at the list of drives), and the mail, the
  calendar and the contacts while no account gives them anything — carries one component, in one
  style:
  - *Its flyout* says what it needs in a sentence, with the accent button **"Set up in Settings"**
    under it where the stock's and the weather's "Try again" stand (`SetupPrompt`): the feed's, the
    stock's, the weather's, the drive's, the mail's and the contacts' panels, and the calendar
    widget's agenda (a clock's calendar, which has no agenda of its own without an account, shows
    none). The button is the one thing the keys reach. A press closes the flyout and opens the
    widget's own page with the keyboard in the box that sets it up (`SetupLink`, `--setup
    <field>`, as an add opens it), or, for the three that need an account, the Accounts page
    (`--page accounts`). This is the one way into the settings a flyout has: one with something to
    show still has none, and its widget's right-click "Settings" stays the route.
  - *Its card and its line* are the same: the kind's glyph, a short line ("No feed yet", "No
    symbol yet", "No location yet", "No drive chosen", "Nothing pinned yet", "No words yet", "No mail
    account", "No contacts account") and the button, as much of it as the room holds and nothing
    cut (`SetupFace`), **centred in the box across and down** (2026-10-10: "when the widget first
    has to be configured it should show it in the center center"; `SetupFace.Lay`, one plan for
    every kind and height): where the box is tall enough an empty state as Windows draws one — the
    glyph half as large again, the words under it on up to two centred rows, the button under them
    — else, or without the glyph where only that is short of room, one centred row of glyph, words
    and button, leaving out the glyph and then the words where they do not fit; the button's words
    shorten to "Set up", then to the gear alone, and where not even the gear fits (a tile) the
    kind's own drawing stays. A heading has no glyph.
  - *Its taskbar entry* (`CellIsland.PaintBar`, `SetupFace.OnBar`): the kind's glyph and the short
    line, centred in the cell, with no button (a click opens its flyout, which has it); the glyph
    alone where the words do not fit beside it, and down a bar on its side. The cell keeps the
    size its settings give it, so nothing moves once it is set up. The weather face before a place
    is set is the pin and "Set location", centred as the face always is.
  - *In a folder the whole card or line is the button*: a left click, or Enter or Space on it,
    opens the settings directly (`FolderFlyoutAction.Setup`) and the folder closes, as a folder
    opens no flyout (§15) and such a widget has nothing else a click could do. It takes no pointer
    and lights no part of itself.
  - *A pin on the bar* has no card: its menu says why it cannot open and ends with "Set up in
    Settings" in place of "Settings" (`Dock.SetupItem`).
- **A click on a widget opens its settings** (2026-10-04: "when clicking on a widget in edit mode
  it should open its settings"; `Karpo.Dock\EditClicks.cs`). While the bar is arranged, a press
  and release on a widget's block that never leaves the system's drag threshold (`SM_CXDRAG`,
  `SM_CYDRAG`, `EditClicks.IsClick`, the same side of it as every other drag) opens that widget's
  own page in Karpo's settings, where it used to open the block's menu: an open settings window
  goes there, a closed one starts on it. The arguments are the ones its menu's "Settings" sends,
  then `--clicked <stamp>` (`EditClicks.SettingsArgs`), which the settings app orders with the adds
  on one clock, so of several clicked quickly the window shows the last (`Logic\AddedArrival.cs`),
  and reads the file first (`SettingsModel.CatchUp`), as the widget may have moved a moment ago.
  The page opens as "Settings" opens it, with no box focused for it.
  - *Dragging still moves it.* Past the threshold the block is carried, and a release lands it;
    nothing opens. The press still gives the block edit mode's focus.
  - *A drag at rest turns edit mode on*, on the bar and in a folder standing open alike. On the bar
    a widget pressed outside edit mode and carried past the same threshold turns edit mode on, and
    **the same widget goes on being carried** into edit mode (`Dock.Pins.cs` `HandOverToEditMode`,
    `Dock.BeginEditFromDrag`, `DockWindow.AdoptDrag`; the person, 2026-10-08): its ghost follows the
    pointer, where it would land shows, and the release places it, nothing opening. It was let go
    for a while (2026-10-07), when edit mode shrank the screen and moved the bar from under the
    pointer; edit mode is edited where the bars stand now, so nothing shifts as it comes. Where the
    pointer holds the block is measured again as edit mode arrives (`PinDrags.GrabOffset`), as its
    build may give a widget with nothing to show room, or a section its "+". In a folder, grid or list, it is the same (2026-10-05: "when a widget is dragged
    in the grid or list view it should also automatically switch into edit mode";
    `FolderFlyout.HandOver`, `Dock.BeginEditFromFolderDrag`). At the threshold the folder asks the
    dock (`FolderFlyout.ArrangeFromDrag`), and the dock turns edit mode on for the folder's bar. The
    folder holds itself open first, then is arranged where it stands (`FolderFlyout.Arrange`: laid
    out again in edit mode's dress, its "+" places and a grid's steppers), and carries on with the
    card that was pressed, by edit mode's rules: its landing where the pointer is, placed on the
    release, dragged out onto the bar where it is let go off the folder; the folder stays open
    after it.
    Edit mode stays on once the drag is over, as on the bar; Escape, "Close edit mode" beside the add
    button and the bar menu's Done end it, and every folder standing open closes with it.
    - At the threshold, not at the press: a click at rest is what it always was (a folder's card
      opens no flyout, §15), and no edit mode flashes up for it.
    - A widget's own control keeps its drag: a slider in a card takes its press first
      (`FolderFlyout.TakePointer`, `CellIsland.PressOn`) and has the moves and the release, as the
      bar's slider has them before a move can start (`Dock.TakesDragItself`). Only a press the
      widget did not take, on the rest of its card or on its line, can turn edit mode on.
    - Refused while another bar is arranged, because ending that would close this folder under
      the pointer. The drag then carries the widget out of the folder, as every drag at rest did
      before.
  - *The widget clicked is selected* (2026-10-05: "it should also show the widget as selected";
    `Dock.EditPick`, `EditView.Selected`, `FolderFlyout.Picked`). Its block on the bar, or its
    card or line in a folder standing open, wears the accent's ring, 2 px — on the block's edge on
    the bar, just outside the card or line in a folder, so it reads on a switch whose card is the
    accent — as Windows 11 rings a selected item. It stays until another widget is clicked, on the
    bar or in a folder, or edit mode ends; it goes by the widget's key, so it keeps to the widget
    through every rebuild (`EditClicks.SelectedPart`, `FolderFlyout.PickedCard`). A folder clicked
    on the bar is selected as its block. The keyboard's focus rectangle is the keys' alone and
    goes over the ring where both are on one widget. In a folder the ring stands in the layer
    outside the panels, on whole pixels, so it is never clipped by the panel's rounded edge at a
    first or last line or by a line as wide as its list (2026-10-11: "often clipped by the edge,
    clipped by other widgets, behind other stuff"); only a "+" standing on its edge is over it.
    With the settings window already open, the
    same click moves the window to the widget's page and the ring to the widget.
  - *Which blocks* (`EditClicks.OnBlock`). Every widget, separators included — a separator has a
    width, so it has a page. The "+" buttons,
    the resize grip and a folder's own chrome (its "+", steppers and titles toggle) keep their own
    clicks.
  - *A folder does both* (2026-10-04: "it should do both"). A folder of either type on the bar
    opens itself, arranged in place, as before (the way to its widgets), and then its own page
    opens in Karpo's settings, with the arguments its menu's "Settings" sends and the click's stamp,
    so the last of several clicks wins as for any widget. The folder opens first, so the settings
    window is the one that ends in front; the folder stays open and arranged behind it, because a
    folder shown while its bar is arranged holds itself open through another window taking the
    focus (`FolderFlyout.Show` sets `FlyoutHost.StaysOpen`, the same hold that keeps it open
    through the presses on the bar). A click on a folder already standing open only closes it, as
    its button does: putting it away asks for no page, and the settings window stays as it was.
  - *In a folder standing open*, the same for its cards and its lines (`FolderFlyoutAction.Settings`;
    the folder stays open). A card carried past the threshold is moving, even let go back on its
    own cells, and a press on a card's corner grip is a resize, never a click.
  - *A double-click is one click* (`EditClickGuard`): its second half on the same widget, within
    the double-click time and rectangle Windows uses (`GetDoubleClickTime`, `SM_CXDOUBLECLK`), does
    nothing, so the settings app is not started twice and a folder does not open and close again
    (nor open its page twice).
  - *Keys and Narrator* (`EditClicks.OnKey`, `EditClicks.ByAutomation`). Enter and Space on the
    block with the keyboard's focus do what a click does, on the bar and in a folder, once however
    long they are held; the menu key and Shift+F10 open the block's menu, as a right click does.
    UI Automation's Invoke and Toggle on a widget of a bar being arranged (Narrator's primary
    action) are the click too, and never the widget's own act: a switch is not switched then. On a
    folder that is both again: it opens and its page opens, and the keyboard's focus ends in the
    settings window, with the folder standing open behind it.
- **Left for item 4** (the editing redesign): typing to find a widget in the list (the flyout has
  no search), and keeping the list open to add several in one visit.

## 8. What this does not solve

- **Accessibility, since 2026-09-27, in part.** Each bar, every menu and every
  panel of controls answers UI Automation (`Karpo.Dock\Accessibility`): a bar
  is a tool bar of its entries along it — Start, search, the app buttons (their
  windows and `TileSignal.Spoken` as their status), "…", each widget's cells (a
  switch a toggle, the volume a slider, the rest buttons named by their
  tooltip's first line), the tray's icons and chevron, the clock —, a menu is
  its rows, a panel its controls. Pressing, switching, setting a slider, the
  focus and the menu are done as the pointer or the keys would. The keyboard's
  place is the focused element (Win+T, Win+B, Tab in a panel, the arrows in a
  menu), so Narrator follows it. The calendar, the clock's lines, the
  notification list, the desktops' flyout and a folder's cells draw their own
  content and have no tree yet, and the tooltips are still composition visuals.
- **Per-kind behaviour is still per-kind.** This removes the scatter, not the
  work: a drive widget still has to know about volumes.

## 9. Flyouts become folders

A widget and the panel it opens are two things glued together today. They come
apart: **only folders have panels, and no widget owns a flyout.** What exists now
as "the clock widget, which opens a calendar" becomes **a grid folder whose face
is the clock widget, holding calendar components** — and the clock is a leaf that
draws the time, knowing nothing about where it is drawn.

This is the user's own framing, and it is better than the one it replaced (a kind
that "is a container") for one reason: **no kind is ever a container**, so nothing
is ever evicted from a folder. The rule stays "folders do not nest", every widget
remains placeable everywhere, and a grid can still hold a clock and the weather —
which matters, because those two are what every picture of a folder uses to show
what a folder is *for*.

**What is left of the conversions (2026-09-26).** The person took some of these out as widgets:
*"weather hours, weather days, screen time, screen time graph, screen time app list, should be
removed as widgets."* Screen time is gone whole — its taskbar entry, its flyout, its three pieces,
its idle-time setting and its `screenTime` key in config.json; the files it counted the days into
(`screentime.json`, `screentime-history.json` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo`) are left where they are,
and nothing reads or deletes them. The weather's list form is its conditions alone
(`weatherNow`); the hours and the week are the bar's flyout's only. The notes below are the record
of how the conversions were built, screen time's included. (Screen time came back on 2026-10-09 as
two lines of a list and a ready-made folder, reading those same files: §69.)

In the same ruling the desktop and layout switchers, the keyboard layout, the date and the
notification bell left grids, and the date left lists: they are the taskbar's alone
(*"widgets to remove from grid display: virtual desktop, taskbar layout, keyboard layout, date"*,
*"widgets to remove from list display: day switcher, date"*, *"notifications bell should not be
shown in grid view"*). A file that still names one in a folder of that view loses it where the
file is read.

**Shells.** Then: *"go ahead and implement just the shells for these even if there is no
functionality yet."* A kind in its registry before its drawing is built is a **shell**
(`WidgetSource.Shell`, `ShellIsland`): the kind's glyph and its title, centred in the room it is
given — beside each other where the title fits whole, the glyph alone and larger where it does
not — on the list's one gutter in a line, and a click that does nothing. No kind is a shell now.
The notification list's card, where the bell's card stood, was one and is built: the panel's list
at every span (§16). The removable devices' card and line are built, drawn by the button's own
island (`RemovableIsland.Cards.cs`, §16), and the output device's card is drawn by its own island
(`SoundPartTile`), where it is being built. Building a shell's kind is one word of its registry
record (its `Drawing`) and its class.

The timer and the focus time were shells on the taskbar and in a list, and are built now: one
widget (`CountdownTile`) in all three places. On the taskbar it is one row, its glyph and the
