  (`WindowsTaskbar` keeps `LeftAligned`, `Seconds` and `Battery`). §23.5's table holds otherwise.
- **Conditional in Windows, decided for Karpo:** the input indicator is on every new bar, since
  Karpo's always shows the layout in use (§23.3) and the person asked for it; the battery stays only
  on a PC with one, since Windows shows no icon without and Karpo's would stand there as a power
  button. The alignment (`TaskbarAl`) and the clock's seconds are still the person's: they say where
  and how, not what. Copilot has no entry (removed in Karpo) and Chat is gone from Windows.
- **Separators** (no line by default, §78; a card each side on an islands bar, §54; two docks in a
  Dock, §81) only between groups Windows sets apart: one between the tray and system icons (the tray
  through the battery) and the time, the date, the bell and show desktop — Windows' clock button and
  its corner. Left-aligned, one more after the weather, which then stands before the tray and would
  otherwise share its card. None among Start, search, Task view and the apps, which Windows sets
  flush; none around show desktop, a sliver that as a card of its own would be a stub.
- **Existing configs are not changed** (no shape bump): the new default reaches a new install, a
  config with no layout left, and a layout made with "Add layout" on Settings' Layouts page, which
  is `Config.FirstLayout` (`SettingsModel.AddLayout`). There is no "reset layout" command.
- `DefaultBarTests` (the full set and order, every button whatever Windows' settings, the separators'
  places, left-aligned, no battery, the pen and touch buttons in the tray's group),
  `DefaultsTests.EveryNewBarHasTheIndicator`. Pictures `default-bar-*.png` and
  `default-bar-dock-<theme>-<scale>.png` (the same entries as a Dock layout's four docks).

### 23.6 The connected look is the default (2026-10-05)

*Gone (2026-10-08, §41): the looks are no choice any more — a dock floats, a bar wears islands — and
the connected look is gone. What follows is how it stood.*

The person's decision: the bar's flat look, **Connected**, is the default rather than **Islands**,
because Windows 11's taskbar is one flat band. Since the same day the look is **one choice of three**
(`Config.Style`, §23.7), where it was two looks and an "Island backgrounds" switch beside them:

- **Connected**: the bar is one flat band across the edge, its widgets square and flush, no gap
  between two widgets or two sections, no card, and no line unless somebody placed a separator.
- **Islands**: a card behind every widget, always, a gap between them, rounded corners.
- **Floating**: each section a rounded panel of its own off the screen's edge (§23.7).

**Which one a bar wears.** The one its config chose; where it chose none, `Config.DefaultStyle`,
Connected, at every height (`Config.StyleOrDefault`). The height used to decide it (connected under
`Config.ThinHeight`, islands above), so a new install wore islands at 48 DIP. Now the height decides
only the room (`Layout.Thin`: text sizes, the cell, the grip, the desktop buttons), never the look.
The first read writes the answer down (`Config.Repair`), so a config that chose islands keeps them
and a new one says `"style": "connected"`. The settings app's Appearance page has the choice
("Style": three pictures, Connected, Islands, Floating), with the look a file wears shown as chosen.

**The cards are the look's** (2026-10-05: "the connected style (with island background disabled),
the island style (with island background enabled, you cannot choose this anymore)"). `Layout.Cards`
is the islands look and no other; there is no switch. A file of the build before keeps its look,
whatever its `"islandCards"` said — connected with or without backgrounds is connected, islands with
or without is islands, its cards back on — and the word is read past and gone the next time the file
is saved (ConfigWords' note). The band a connected bar with backgrounds wore behind its widgets
(`Scene.BandParts`) went with the switch: a connected bar is the bar's own material and nothing on it.

**What reads differently without cards** (Connected, and the widgets inside a floating bar's panels),
each from the one predicate `Layout.Connected`:

- **Gaps and corners**: none (`Layout.PartGap`, `CardRadius`): between widgets, between the
  sections, between app buttons, between tray icons (`TrayStep` is the cell), between the status
  icons (`Layout.CellsApart`) and between the cells of a widget more than one cell long. A
  separator stands flush and its Automatic line is doubled (`SeparatorInk.ForPlaced`), as nothing
  else keeps two widgets apart.
- **Cards**: none, per widget, per tray icon, per status icon, per app button or for "…"
  (`Scene.WearsCard`, `TrayCard`, `AppCard` draw only where `Layout.Cards`).
- **Hover, press and the keyboard's focus**: no card to light, so each lights what Windows' flat
  taskbar lights, the button's own plate with rounded corners (4 DIP): an app button's and Start's
  the taskbar's highlight, a tray icon's and the clock's the small highlight, a widget's its cell.
  They were square, edge to edge, which cut a hole in the band.
- **A graph or a chart on the bar** runs into its neighbour square-cornered (`IslandStyle.Square`,
  `GraphBackdrop.BarRadius`).
- **Search** keeps its box in every look, its corners a control's 4 DIPs; on a connected bar it
  sits on the band, as Windows' box sits on the taskbar.
- **Edit mode** (shading, outlines, empty sections, the ghost of a carried block) is the same in
  every look: the blocks keep the edit corners (`Scene.EditRadius`) (§13).

Tests: `BarStyleTests` (no style is connected at every height, a choice of islands is kept, a new
install's bar is connected); `IslandCardsTests.TheCardsAreTheLooks`; `BarStyleConfigTests` (every
old combination of style and switch, the round trip, the merge); `DefaultBarPictures` draws the
default bar in the connected look. Tests about the islands look ask for it (`Style = BarStyle.Islands`).

### 23.7 Floating: each section a dock of its own (2026-10-05)

*Since §41 (2026-10-08) the floating look is a Dock layout's; since §71 (2026-10-09) all three of its
sections, each a dock of its own, and a press between two is the desktop's.*

*"additionally a style where each of the three sections is displayed floating / on their own. like a
floating dock."* `BarStyle.Floating`, `"style": "floating"`.

- **The panels** (`Layout.SectionPanels`): every section that holds a widget is a panel of the bar's
  material — Mica, Acrylic, the tint, at the same opacity, as `Scene.Panel` dresses the whole bar —
  as long as its widgets and the room it keeps inside either end (the room across the bar between a
  cell and the panel's edge, 4 DIPs at least), and the bar's thickness
  across. Windows 11's floating surfaces' values: corners of 8 DIPs (`Layout.PanelRadius`), a
  hairline round it in the bar's border colour, and a soft shadow under it (16 DIPs of blur, 2 down,
  30 % dark and 14 % light, `Scene.FloatingPanels`) — only where the panel covers it, Acrylic and
  Opaque: under a see-through tint it would show through, so a Translucent panel has its hairline
  alone, and a Clear bar no panels at all. An empty section has no panel: at rest it takes no room,
  and in edit mode its empty room stands on its own.
- **Where they stand**: 8 DIPs off the screen's edge (`Layout.Lift`), the first and the last 8 DIPs
  off the screen's ends, and 8 DIPs at least between two panels; the start's from the start, the
  end's to the end, the middle's centred, by the same rules as every bar (§13). On every edge: the
  panels run down a bar on the left or the right as they run along one at the bottom or the top.
- **The desktop shows** between and around the panels: the window draws nothing there.
- **Inside a panel the widgets stand as on a connected bar**: flush, square, no card each
  (`Layout.Connected` is true, `Layout.Cards` false). Decided by eye: with a card per widget inside
  each panel (`bar-style-floating-cards-*.png`, drawn once for the comparison) the panel is a frame
  round a row of frames and reads as clutter; flat, it reads as a dock.
- **The work area**: the bar keeps the strip it covers, its thickness and the room under it
  (`Layout.Reserve` = thickness + lift, `Dock.Reserve`), so no window goes under a panel or into the
  gap below it. The window is that much deeper too (`Layout.WindowFor` takes the reserve).
- **A press between or around the panels** is the bar's own, as anywhere the bar has nothing
  (`Hit.Panel`): its menu opens there. The window's
  region is the strip and the room under it, as before. A press between a widget and the screen's
  edge is that widget's, so the screen's edge stays a target as Windows' taskbar's does.
- **Edit mode**: the sections, their edit bars and the empty rooms work as on every bar; an empty
  room lies on the desktop between the panels, a widgets' inset clear of each.
  While a block is carried the panels glide with the sections as they open and close
  (`Layout.SectionPanels(moving, slot)`, `Scene.ShowPanels`), and one whose last widget is carried
  away goes.
- **Autohide**: the reveal strip stays at the screen's edge itself (`Layout.HotStrip`), and a hidden
  bar slides past the edge with the room under it and its shadow (`Layout.HiddenOffset`).

Tests: `FloatingBarTests` (the panels per section, an empty section's none, the margins and the gaps,
all four edges at 100 % and 150 %, the strip kept, the presses between and under the panels, an
empty section's room in edit mode, a carried block), `SceneTreeTests.AFloatingBar*` (the scene shows the
layout's panels, and follows a drag). Pictures, over a wallpaper of the tests' own:
`bar-style-{connected,islands,floating}-{bottom,left}-{dark,light}-{100,150}.png`,
`bar-style-floating-edit-{bottom,left}-*.png` and `bar-style-floating-drag-bottom-*.png`
(`SceneTreeTests.BarStyleSheets`).
## 24. A graph behind its words

*"Graphs across the whole widget. Processor, memory, graphics and the other graphs, and stock, span
the whole width and fade behind the text"* (backlog 11). A graph was a strip of its widget: beside
the reading on the bar, under the words on a card and a line, and the widget's room was split
between the two. It is the widget's ground now, as Windows 11's Task Manager draws its small graphs
and its Widgets board a share's card: one picture, the words written on it.

- **Across the whole widget, at every size and on every surface.** On the bar the graph is the whole
  entry — its width and its height, on its card's corners (`GraphBackdrop.BarRadius`), square on a
  connected bar (§23.6); on a grid
  card the whole card, on its rounded corners; on a list's line the whole line. A share's chart is
  the same, on the bar as well, where it had none. The standing rule holds: a graph runs edge to
  edge, with nothing behind it but its own fill.
  *Amended 2026-10-09 (§55): the five performance readings show no graph on the bar any more; their
  graph is in the flyout a click opens. The cards and lines keep theirs.*
- **A soft fade under the words.** Where the words stand the graph shows at a fraction of its
  strength (`GraphBackdrop.UnderWords`, 0.28), and past them it comes back to full over a ramp of
  12 to 28 DIP: across the entry on the bar and on a row, down the card or the line where the words
  are at its top, and on a list's one-row line under the name at its start and the figure at its
  end, full between. The fade is an opacity mask on the graph alone (a layer whose opacity is a
  gradient), never a band of a colour over it, because what is under a widget is the bar's glass, a
  folder's card or a list's flyout, in either theme. A share's entry on the bar is all words, so its
  chart is faded across the whole of it: a tint of the day behind the ticker.
- **The fill under the line is a gradient** (`GraphBackdrop.Fill`): strongest at the graph's top,
  thinning to a breath at its foot, as Windows' own small charts fill theirs, so a tall card is not
  one block of colour and the ground under the words stays light.
- **The layout of the words is what it was.** The bar's entry keeps its width, its glyph and its
  figure where they stood, and the graph's old room past the figure is where it shows unfaded; a
  card keeps the value's share of its height; a line keeps its tiers. The history and its sampling
  are the sources' as before (`Sources\PerformanceData.cs`).

**A disk's read and write stay put** (backlog 12). They came and went: whether they were drawn, and
where, was measured on the figures showing, so "R 0K  W 8.8M" fitted a card or a line where
"R 88K  W 8.8M" did not, and the W walked along as the R changed. Now every figure is measured on the
widest it can be (`Units.RateShape` "8.8M", `Units.LongRateShape` "888 MB/s", `Units.SizeShape`,
`Units.OfShape`) and right-aligned in that room, as figures in a column are (`TilePaint.Fields`, a
card's `CardReading.SecondParts`): the line is there whatever the figures, or not at all the same way
for every figure, and nothing after a figure moves. A disk not read yet says "–" in the same room
rather than leaving its line out. On a grid card from two by two up they are always there: kept
before the graph's room, and read over write where one line will not fit (§16, "What gives way").
The whole widget's detail is a small table — its labels in a
column, its figures right-aligned — for every graph: in use and available, down and up, read and
write, peak and average.

`GraphBackdropTests` holds the fade, the disk's read and write on a compact and a whole line and on
cards from two by two to four by four, at 100 and 150 % and the largest text — present for every
figure from nothing to gigabytes a second and not read yet, each label and each figure's end in one
place — and the shapes being the widest figures. It draws every graph and a share on a history that
runs through the figures, on the bar at 28, 48 and 72 DIP, as cards from one tile to four by four and
as lines one to five rows tall, light and dark, at 100 and 150 % and at the largest text
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR\graphs-behind-*.png`). The list's gutter test reads a line's words with the graphs
behind them left out (`PaintWatch.NoBackdrops`) and the graph from the drawing with them.

**The disk widget is the disk's activity, a disk at a time** (2026-10-04). *"disk widget should show
diskio as graph not the storage space"*. The widget the person meant was the one a new bar came
with: a Drive widget for the drive Windows is on, which says "Local Disk C:" beside a bar of how full
it is. The Disk widget (`WidgetInfos.Disk`, "Disk" in the add list) already graphed activity, but no
bar had one. So:

- **A new bar gets the Disk widget** where it got the drive (`Sections.DefaultLayout`), in the run
  the performance graphs stand in. A bar that has a Drive widget keeps it: nothing in a person's file
  is changed for them, and the drive is a widget of its own in the add list (Files).
- **What it plots is the disk's active time**, the main graph of Task Manager's Performance › Disk,
  over the history its source has gathered from the dock's start, one read of the disks a pass for
  every graph (`PerformanceData`, `SharedSamplers.Disk`). The read and write figures stay where they
  were — on the card's second line, under a line's name, in a whole line's table — as Task Manager
  puts them under its graph. Never storage space: that is the Drive widget's.
- **One disk, or all of them** (`PerformanceOptions.Disk`, the card's Disk list). "All disks" is the
  default — the busiest disk's active time and what every disk reads and writes together, which on a
  PC with one disk is that disk — and "Disk 0 (C:)", "Disk 1 (E:)" follow one, as Task Manager's Disk
  0 and Disk 1 do. The file keeps the number ("Disk 1"), never the letters, which move; a disk that
  is not attached is kept in the list and shows "–" until it is back. Each disk followed is a source
  of its own with a history of its own (`Disk/1s/Disk 1`); the disks are still read once a pass, and
  each widget takes its disk from that one read (`DiskSampler.Pick`).
- **Its name says which disk**: "Disk 1" on its card and its line where one disk is followed, "Disk"
  where that does not fit and for all of them. Its tooltip is the disk as Task Manager names it, its
  active time, its read and write, and how full each volume on it is ("C: 419 GB free of 931 GB"):
  the storage space the drive showed, a hover away.

`DiskActivityTests` holds the picking (one disk, all of them, one not attached), the source keys and
their histories from the start, the settings card's list, the file's form and the new bar; it draws
the widget following one disk on the bar at 28, 41 and 72 DIP, as cards from one tile to four by
four and as lines one to six rows tall, at 100 and 150 %, dark and light
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR\disk-activity-*.png`).

## 25. How far back a share's chart goes

*"Each stock widget can be set how far back its chart goes, including 'the last X years'"*
(backlog 32). A per-widget setting, Chart range (`StockOptions.Range`, `RangeYears`): 1 day, 5 days,
1 month, 6 months, year to date, 1 year, 5 years, max, and a custom number of years, 1 to 50, whole:
a fraction typed in the Years field is the whole number it rounds to, and the field shows that
number (`StockRanges.YearsFrom`). **Five years is the default** (`StockRanges.Default`), the
person's: *"default chart range should be 5 years"*. A new widget, one a ready-made group adds and
a file with no range or one this build does not know all show five years. A range somebody picked
is kept, a day included: since ranges came every widget's range is written out, so a widget saved
at a day since then stays at a day until it is changed in its settings.

- **What is asked.** Yahoo's chart endpoint offers the ranges 1d, 5d, 1mo, 3mo, 6mo, 1y, 2y, 5y, 10y,
  ytd and max, and keeps minutes only so far back (a minute for a week, up to thirty minutes for
  sixty days, an hour for two years). Each range asks for the finest interval that reaches that far
  and still draws a few hundred points (`StockAsk.Interval`): 5 minutes for a day, 15 for five days,
  an hour for a month, a day for six months, the year to date and a year, a week for five years, a
  month for max (which the endpoint answers at three months for a long history). The last N years is
  no range of the endpoint's, so it is asked as two moments, `period1` and `period2`, at a day up to
  two years, a week up to ten and a month past that. A widget's range is part of what its price is
  fetched and kept for (`StockAsk.Key`): a day keeps the plain symbol as its key, so a price kept
  before ranges existed is still found, and two widgets of one share over two ranges are two fetches.
- **The change follows the range**, as Yahoo's page and Windows' stock card have it: over a day, the
  price against the previous close (the answer's own `regularMarketChangePercent`); over any other
  range, from the close before the range began (`chartPreviousClose`) to the price now, or from the
  range's first price where the answer gives none (`StockReading.ChangeOver`). The colour follows the
  same change. The panel's note says what it is over ("Past 5 years · At Friday's close"), a
  card's third line says it where there is room ("Past year"), and so does a list line of five rows
  and more, which is the panel's header. The bar's entry has no tooltip to say it in — its click
  opens the panel, which says it — and a shorter line has no room beside its symbol, company,
  price and change.
- **The range is written beside the change**, small and in the quiet ink, as Windows' stock card
  and Yahoo Finance write their range buttons: "1D", "5D", "1M", "6M", "YTD", "1Y", "5Y", "Max",
  and "3Y" for the last three years (`StockRanges.Label`). A card of two by two and up writes it
  after its change ("-1.24% 5Y", `CardReading.SecondNote`) where the line has the room; a list
  line of two to four rows after its change on the row, the first of the figures to give way; a
  line of five rows and up says it in its header's note ("Past 5 years"). A single tile, a row, a
  column and a line of one row leave it out.
- **A range is drawn in trading time**, one step a point, as Yahoo draws one: five sessions side by
  side, not five sessions and four nights. The panel writes the first point of each day, week, month
  or year under the graph, whichever the range is long enough to want (`StockReading.TicksOf`), at the
  densest rhythm of them that stands apart (`DayGraph.Ticks`), and marks the last trade at the line's
  end. A day is drawn as it was: its session from bell to bell, its hours.

`StockRangeTests` holds the request for every range and the custom years, the keys, two ranges of
one share being two fetches, the change over a day and over a range with and without the close
before it, the series and its ticks, a long answer keeping its newest points, and the setting's
words in the file. `StockOffscreenTests` pictures the panel over five days, a year, five years and
three years (`stock-range-*.png`).

### 25.1 The currency, and an amount owned

*"it should also show the currency. you should also be able to add a holding amount, very simple,
just an amount you own, it should then show the amount you hold."*

- **The currency** is the provider's own code after the price, quiet: "412.34 USD", as the panel
  has always written it and as MSN Money writes a quote. Karpo guesses no symbol for it. A card of
  two by two and up writes it after the price where the words have the room at the price's size
  (`CardReading.ValueNote`); where they have not, at the label row's end, unless a holding stands
  there; it never makes the price smaller. A list line of two to four rows writes it after the
  price, giving way before the change does; a line of five rows and up is the panel's header,
  which has it. In the header the change stands after the price and its code; where it does not
  fit there (the largest text and a move of two figures, "+42.63%") it takes a line of its own under
  the price rather than drawing over it, and the code stays after the price where it fits
  (`StockHeader.ChangeBelow`; `StockOffscreenTests`, `stock-bigtext-5y-*.png`). Numbers are
  written as the price is, in the dock's one number format (grouped with commas, a point for
  decimals): the dock runs with invariant globalization.
- **The holding** is a per-widget setting, "Amount you own" (`StockOptions.Holding`): an amount,
  decimals allowed, kept to eight places; empty, 0 or less is none, and none is not written to the
  file (`StockHoldings.From`). What it is worth is the amount times the price now, in the price's
  currency, to the cent — "4,123.40 USD" — a currency's hundredths (pence "GBp", cents "ZAc", agorot
  "ILA") counted in the currency itself (`StockHoldings.Worth`). With room the amount comes first,
  "10 shares · 4,123.40 USD"; a crypto pair or a currency pair is counted in its first currency
  ("0.5 BTC", "1,000 EUR") (`StockHoldings.Said`). Where it shows:
  - a card of two by two and up: as its third line where the card has the height and the width for
    it (the long form or the worth alone), else at the label row's end where the worth stands
    whole (`CardReading.Corner`); on a wide card (4x2) the chart then keeps under the label row;
  - a list line of two to four rows: on a row of its own under the figures where the line has the
    height, else in the company's place after the symbol, the currency giving way first for it;
  - a line of five rows and up, and the stock panel: a line of the header, under the note;
  - a single tile, a row, a column, a line of one row and the bar's entry: not at all.

`StockHoldingTests` holds what a typed amount is kept as, how amounts and sums are written, what a
holding is worth and said as, a reading's and the header's holding, the file's round trip and the
three-way merge, the holding going with a widget to its card and line, and the field's card on a
stock widget's page, which "Find a setting" does not search (§31,
`SettingsIndexTests.NothingOfOneWidgetFolderOrPinIsFound`). `StockRangeTests` holds the default
and the labels. `GridReadingsTests` pictures a five-year share with and without a holding at every span (`grid-stock-5y-*.png`,
`grid-stock-5y-holding-*.png`), `ListLineReadingsTests` its line at every height
(`list-stock-holding.png`), and `StockOffscreenTests` the panel with a holding
(`stock-holding-*.png`).

## 26. Start is Windows' Start

Karpo had its own Start menu for a day (backlog 38); the person asked for it to go again: the
Start button, a lone press of the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc always open **Windows' own Start**. There
is no setting for it. The button opens it through Explorer's launcher (below), or presses the
Windows key where that can't be asked (`Desktops.StartMenu`), and is named "Start" in its tooltip,
as on the taskbar. A config that still holds the old `"startMenu"` key loads as before; the key is
ignored, and the next save leaves it out.

**It opens on the clicked button's display, where Windows puts it there** (the person, 2026-10-08:
"the Start button just opens Start"; 2026-10-28, §373: "sometimes ... the start just appears no the
wrong screen"). Karpo steered more of it for a while — `TaskbarAl` set to the place nearer the button
(§45 before 2026-10-08) — and that is gone for good; what came back is only the display: Explorer's
launcher is connected to the button's display and opens Start there (`StartLauncher`, §373), as that
display's own taskbar button does. A click on the button while Start is open closes it, as on Windows' taskbar:
what showed as the button went down decides, as for Search (`SearchToggle` over `WindowsPanel.Start`;
§28) — including a Start the press itself sent away before the dock read it, which went after the
press's time (`PanelWatch`) and so is not opened again (the person, 2026-10-10: "when i click the
start button when the start is already opened it should close it again"). The bar never takes the
activation on a press (`MA_NOACTIVATE`), so the press alone does not dismiss Start through Karpo.
The Windows key itself is Windows' own (below): it toggles Start without Karpo. Where an earlier build kept the person's own `TaskbarAl` aside in `taskbar-alignment`, it is
put back once, from the places that put the taskbar back (Dispose, the guard, a crash;
`TaskbarAlignment.Restore`), and the file goes; nothing sets the alignment any more.

**The keys.** The keyboard hook (`TaskbarKeys`) is in only while Karpo's bars are the taskbar, and
takes only the taskbar's chords (Win+1..9 and Win+0, Win+T, Win+B). It never keeps the Windows key,
nor Ctrl+Esc: every shortcut of Windows', and Start, reaches Windows as it came. The hook hears
nothing while another desktop has the input (Win+L's lock screen, UAC's prompt, Ctrl+Alt+Del) or
while Windows has taken it away for a slow answer, so before each key it lets go of every modifier
the keyboard itself no longer holds (`KeyChords.IsDown`, GetAsyncKeyState): a release it never
heard leaves no Windows key held for good, which would keep a plain 1, T or B as Win+1, Win+T or
Win+B. The keys Karpo presses itself carry Karpo's mark (`TaskbarKeys.Ours`), so the hook lets
them by.

`TaskbarKeysTests` holds which keys are taken and which go to Windows, the lone Windows key and
Ctrl+Esc among the latter, and the releases the hook never hears; `LoadSaveTests` and
`ConfigMergeTests` a file with the old `"startMenu"` key, loaded, saved and merged.

## 27. The taskbar's own menu is the person's (2026-10-04) — removed again (2026-10-12)

**Removed (2026-10-12).** "taskbar menu customization should not be possible anymore." The settings
app's "Taskbar menu" page, its model and its strings (`settings.barMenu.*`, the built-in rows'
"about" lines, the Add menu's groups, the way back's reason) are gone, and so are `Config.BarMenu`,
`Config.EditBarMenu`, `BarMenus.Repair` and the row's migration (`BarMenus.MigrateToRow`, below in
§137). The menu is fixed, `BarMenus.Fixed`. **Since 2026-10-12, later** ("task manager is the most
bottom entry. the taskbar settings button should be a settings cog and open the settings. there
should also be an add button which opens the edit mode and the add window"): the row's buttons on
top are "Add" (+, tooltip "Add a widget", `BarMenuAction.Add`), "Edit taskbar" (the pen) and "Taskbar
settings" (the gear now, not the palette; it opens Karpo's settings in front at the bar's layout card,
as before); then the layouts (with two or more); then Task Manager behind a rule, the very last. With
one layout, the buttons and Task Manager alone. "Add" is the same command as edit mode's "Add to
taskbar…" (`CMD_GALLERY`, `Dock.AddFromMenu`): edit mode on where it was off, then the add list for
the place the menu was opened at. A widget's menu keeps the bar's first two buttons at its row's far
end ("Add a widget", "Edit taskbar"); not the gear, since the widget's own "Settings" is one. No
reset: a file that still has `"barMenu"` loads with everything else in it as it was, the list is not
read (it is no property of `Config` any more, and an unknown key is skipped whatever it holds), and it
drops out of the file at the next write; a `"menuButtonRow"` mark in `"migrated"` stays, harmless.
The model keeps its kinds (built-in rows, shortcuts, dividers, headings) and the drawing below
(`BarMenus.Lines`, `Dock.BarMenu.cs`), which is how the fixed list is drawn and picked from.
`BarMenuModelTests` hold the order and the tolerant read (a current file with the old list, a junk
one, a mark), `BarMenuRowsTests` the drawn menu, `BarMenuPictures` draws it with one layout and two.
What follows is the record of what was.

The person's words: "you should be able to reorder and remove / add shortcuts to the right click
menu on the taskbar. it should get its own configuration page for it. (the dividers / groups should
also be configurable.)" The menu is the one a right click on the bar itself opens, and the one a
taskbar entry with nothing of its own falls back to (Dock.Menus.cs). Edit mode's own bar menu ("Add
to taskbar…", "Done editing", "Taskbar settings") stays as it is.

**The model** (`Karpo.Core\BarMenus.cs`). `Config.BarMenu` is an ordered list; each entry has an
`id` (so the three-way merge takes it entry by entry) and a `kind`:

- `action`, a built-in row: Karpo's own (Task Manager, Layouts, Edit taskbar, Taskbar settings,
  Show desktop) and Windows' places, named and pictured as the Start button's quick links name them
  (File Explorer, Run, Terminal and Terminal (Admin) — Windows PowerShell where Windows Terminal
  isn't installed —, Device Manager, Disk Management, Computer Management, Event Viewer, Settings,
  System, Display, Sound, Network Connections, Power Options, Installed apps). Each once.
- `shortcut`: a `target` written as a pin's is (a program, a shortcut, a file, a folder, an app as
  `shell:AppsFolder\<ID>`, a link), with optional `arguments`, `name` and `icon` (a glyph, or a file
  whose icon is taken).
- `divider`, and `heading` with its `name`: a group's title, as a jump list titles its groups.

Null — the key not in the file — is the default list, `BarMenus.Default`: Task Manager, a divider,
Layouts, a divider, Edit taskbar, Taskbar settings, which draws exactly the menu there was. A file
without the key reads and writes back as it was; the first change writes the default down
(`Config.EditBarMenu`, fixed ids, so two writers writing it at once write the same entries), and
"Reset to default" takes the key out again. `BarMenus.Repair` (from `Config.Repair`) drops kinds and
actions this build doesn't know, a built-in row's second showing and a shortcut with nothing to
open; trims the words; makes every id present and unique; cuts the list at 100 entries.

**The way back.** "Edit taskbar" and "Taskbar settings" are always in the menu: they move, sit under
a heading or between dividers, but cannot be taken out — the page greys their Remove with the
reason, and a list typed into the file without them gets them back at its end under a divider. The
settings app is where the menu is changed and edit mode is the other way in; a menu without both
would leave no way back to either.

**Drawing** (`BarMenus.Lines`, `Dock.BarMenu.cs`). The list is kept as the person left it and tidied
as it is drawn: a heading with no row under it before the next heading, divider or the end goes ("no
empty groups"), then a divider at either end or beside another. Layouts is a row per layout with two
or more, none with one. A heading is a `FlyoutItem` header, drawn as a jump list's group title; a
divider a separator. A shortcut is named by its own name, else the shell's, else its target
(`BarMenus.FallbackName`); it has its shell icon (a network path is not asked, and has the link
glyph); and where `PinTargets.Check` finds its target missing it is greyed with the pins' own
sentence under it. Karpo's own rows keep the commands they always had wherever they are moved;
every other row is `CMD_BAR_ENTRY` + n, remembered with the menu (`Pending.BarMenu`), and does what
the quick links do for the same place — Run is Win+R, Show desktop the Show desktop button, a
shortcut opens as a pin opens, with its arguments.

**The page** (`Pages\BarMenuPage`, "Taskbar menu" in the side menu, `--page barmenu`). The
"Entries" heading, with "Add to menu" at the far end of its row as Windows
Settings puts "Add device" beside its list's heading: a drop-down button offering a built-in action
(by group, greyed where the menu has it), a custom shortcut, a heading and a divider. Under it the
entries as cards in order, each with a handle — a drag anywhere on the card moves it, by mouse or a
held finger, to any place, the first and the last included, the page scrolling under a row held at
the window's edge — Edit for a shortcut or a heading, and Remove; "Reset to default" last. A row has
no up and down arrows ("taskbar menu, the reorder arrows should go away"): from the keyboard, Alt+Up
and Alt+Down move the focused row, as in Windows' Preferred languages list. There is no preview of the menu ("taskbar
menu should not show a preview"): a right click on the bar shows it. A shortcut's dialog has what it
opens, typed, browsed for (a file or a folder, in the one dialog of §29) or chosen from the apps (an
`App` button: Start's shortcuts and the packaged apps, searched by name, `AppList`,
`Logic\AppChoices.cs`), its arguments, its name and its icon (the
pins' icon gallery). What each control does is `Logic\BarMenuEdits.cs`.

The Start button's quick links (`QuickLinks.Items`) are built the same fixed way the bar's menu was;
they are Windows' Win+X menu and stay so.

`BarMenuModelTests` and `BarMenuLinesTests` hold the model, the default, the round trip, the merge,
the repair and the tidying; `BarMenuRowsTests` the dock's rows and commands; `BarMenuEditsTests` the
page's edits, its dialog, its app list, its place in the side menu and "Add to menu" in the
"Entries" heading's row. `BarMenuPictures` draws the
default menu (with one layout and with two) and the sample (`BarMenuEdits.Sample`) at 100 and 150 %,
dark and light (`KARPO_PNG_DIR\bar-menu-*.png`); the page itself is pictured by hand with
`Karpo.Settings.exe --page barmenu --test bar-menu sample --shot bar-menu-page` and
`KARPO_SETTINGS_SHOTS` set.

## 28. Search is Windows 11's search box

*"Search and Search Google in Windows 11's style"*, *"Search closes on a second click"*, *"Karpo's
flyouts close Windows Search"*.

- **The web-search box is gone (2026-10-11).** *"remove the web search widget alltogether. from
  everywhere"*: the `webSearch` entry, its card in a folder, its flyout (`SearchFlyout`, its
  suggestions and its recent searches), its Settings cards and its add-list row went. A file still
  holding one loses it where it is read, everything around it untouched (`ConfigWords.WebSearchGone`),
  and its engine became the app's one search engine (§80, `Config.SearchEngine`). What follows is
  Windows' own Search button.
- **The box.** Windows' own Search button (`search`) has a switch, "Show the search box": the box, or
  the magnifier alone. Off is no options at all (`WindowsSearchOptions`, null), so a bar from before
  keeps its icon; a new bar takes the box where Windows' taskbar shows the box
  (`SearchboxTaskbarMode` 2). The box is Windows 11's (`Islands\SearchPill.cs`), with Windows' own numbers read from the taskbar's resources
  (`SearchBoxButton` and its `_SearchBox_Wave3` states in `MicrosoftWindows.Client.Core`'s
  `resources.pri`, 25H2, and the WinUI 2.8 colours they name): 220 DIPs long, 32 tall on the
  48-DIP bar and 8 down it, the magnifier 11 DIPs in, the words 37 DIPs in and 16 from the far end,
  in Segoe UI Variable Text 14. Its corners are not Windows' pill (radius 16): the person asked for
  "less rounded corners ... the same roundness as the other parts in the design language", so they
  are a control's 4 DIPs (`PopupPaint.ControlRadiusDip`: WinUI's ControlCornerRadius, the bar's
  highlights' own), growing with the cell as the box does (`SearchPill.Radius`). Every search box
  Karpo draws takes that one number: the plate, its highlight and the keyboard's ring on the bar,
  the contacts' field, the add list's field and the other flyout fields, and Settings' "Find a setting" (ControlCornerRadius). It is a text box, not a
  taskbar button:

  | State | Fill | Edge | Words |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | rest | ControlFillColorDefault `#B3FFFFFF` / `#0FFFFFFF` | ControlElevationBorderBrush: `#0F000000` / `#12FFFFFF`, its bottom 3 DIPs shading to `#29000000` / `#18FFFFFF` | TextFillColorSecondary `#9E000000` / `#C5FFFFFF` |
  | pointer over | ControlFillColorSecondary `#80F9F9F9` / `#15FFFFFF` | the same | the same |
  | pressed | ControlFillColorInputActive `#FFFFFFFF` / `#B31E1E1E` | ControlStrokeColorDefault, flat | TextFillColorTertiary `#72000000` / `#87FFFFFF` |

  (light / dark). The magnifier is TextFillColorPrimary. Windows keeps the pressed look while its
  Search is open; Karpo's bar does not follow Search's state, so its box rests then. On the bar the
  fill and edge are the scene's (`Scene.SearchPlate`, under the words), so they change as Windows'
  do instead of a shade lighting up under the box, over Windows' 83 ms brush transition; the button
  also dims its words while pressed. It does not shrink under a press.
  They grow with the bar's cell as every widget's content does; along the bar the box is Windows'
  220 DIPs on the 48-DIP bar, in proportion on any other. Only a
  horizontal bar of 40 DIPs and more shows it, as Windows' small taskbar shows the icon. The
  keyboard's ring goes round the box, its corners the box's (`Layout.SearchBoxRect`). The one width a person sets for
  Windows' button is the icon's, so its card goes while the box is on (`SizeRange.Shows`).
- **On the bar the box is its slot (2026-10-11).** *"the search widgets should take up the full
  height of the widget space, right now there is a faint edge on the top and bottom and left and
  right"*. The box stood inside its part's card, Windows' 32 DIPs of the card's 38.4 and 2 DIPs in
  at each end (`SearchPill.In`), and the card (CardBackgroundFillColorDefault with its
  CardStrokeColorDefault edge) showed in that room all round it as a second, fainter edge. Now the
  box is the whole slot: the card's height and
  the part's whole length (`Layout.SearchBoxed`, `Layout.SearchBoxRect`), at every bar height,
  scale, and on top and bottom bars (a vertical bar shows the icon). It is the part's card, so the
  part wears no other under it (`Scene`'s cards skip it) and its corners are the card's
  (`Layout.SearchBoxRadius`; a control's 4 DIPs on a floating bar, which has no cards), on the plate,
  the highlight and the keyboard's ring, so no corner of anything peeks out past it. A box is a field,
  not a button: it stands in no group (`Layout.Groupable`), a gap either side as Windows keeps its
  box apart from its buttons, so the default run's Start and Task view get their own rounded card
  ends next to it instead of a card running on under it. The magnifier and the words keep their
  numbers from the box's ends and stay centred across; `SearchPill.In` and the margins are for a box
  drawn off the bar (the contacts' field, `TextField.SearchBox`).
- **A second click closes Windows Search.** What Search was as the Search button went down decides
  the click (`SearchToggle`): closed, the click opens it (Win+S); open and still open, the click
  closes it; open and closed by that very press, the click does nothing, so it does not come back.
  A click without a press (the keyboard's, Narrator's) reads Search as it is. The shell may send a
  panel away as the pointer goes down outside it, before the dock has read the press, so the press
  is not only read then: WinEvent hooks (foreground, cloaked) note when each panel last went
  (`PanelWatch`, `WindowsPanels.Watch`), and a panel that went at or after the press's own message
  time (less 50 ms for the two stamps) was open at the press and is gone or going — the click does
  nothing, and never hands the foreground back to a panel on its way out. The Start button is the
  same toggle over Start (§26); it was the one the person saw open again (2026-10-10).
- **Every flyout of Karpo's closes Windows Search and Start** as it opens: one hook in the place every
  popup that takes the focus opens through (`FlyoutHost.Opening`, `WindowsPanels.CloseFor`). Not a
  hover's popup, which opening by pointing would make hostile, nor the edit strip.
- **How Windows' panels are read and closed** (`WindowsPanels.cs`): each is a
  `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow` of its own process — `SearchHost.exe` (`SearchApp.exe`,
  `SearchUI.exe` before it), `StartMenuExperienceHost.exe` — open while visible and not cloaked; the
  title ("Search", "Start") is not read, being English only. Closing is Escape, sent only while the
  panel is the foreground window, as a person closes it; the dock waits up to 150 ms for the panel
  to take it, so it never lands on the flyout opening after it.
- **Start on Windows 11 26xxx (2026-10-11).** The person: "clicking the start menu button again does
  not close the start menu. is this even possible to implement?" It is. Read on 26300: an open Start
  is two windows uncloaked, Start's own host (a CoreWindow the size of the screen) and Search's host
  over it, which is Start's search box and holds the foreground the whole time; a press on the bar
  (no activation) leaves both be; Start is cloaked some 30 ms after it closes. So the press read
  Start open and the click chose to close it, but the close was Escape with Start's window made the
  foreground first, and that window was never in front: the foreground had to be taken from the
  search box, which the shell does not always allow, and where it did not nothing happened. Now
  Start is closed with the Windows key, as Windows' own Start button closes it, wherever the
  foreground is; the dock waits up to 150 ms for it to go. And Search is open only where its window
  shows and Start's does not (`PanelRules.Open`): over Start it is Start's search box, so a click on
  Search with Start open opens Search, and a flyout over Start closes Start alone and does not hand
  the focus back to the search box (`IWindowsPanels.Owns`). Tests: `WindowsSearchTests`
  (`WhichPanelIsOpen`, `AClickClosesStartWithItsSearchBoxInFront`,
  `AFlyoutOverStartsSearchBoxClosesStart`).
- **Windows' Start** (§26) is one of Windows' panels here, closed as Search is when a flyout of
  Karpo's opens. Opening Start itself is Windows' business, which closes its own Search. It costs a
  flyout nothing that can be felt: with nothing of Windows' open, the look is a walk over the
  handful of CoreWindows, under a millisecond for both panels, and nothing is waited for; the wait
  is only for a panel that shows, and ends as soon as it has taken its Escape.

`WindowsSearchTests` holds the click's rule, the flyouts' rule with a fake Search and Start, which
window is which panel, the option as the file keeps it, and the box on the bar: 220 DIPs, its whole
slot, at 100 and 150 %, none on a vertical or thin bar, growing with a tall one.
`SceneTreeTests.TheSearchBoxCoversItsSlot` looks at the pixels: just inside each of the slot's four
edges the box's own fill, at rest and under the pointer, dark and light, top and
bottom bars, 40/48/64 DIPs, 100 and 150 % (`search-slot-*.png`).
`SearchPillTests` holds Windows' numbers and every state's colours, light, dark and high contrast,
the box 8 DIPs down the 48-DIP bar, ; `SceneTreeTests` that the
button's box lays its plate and does not shrink under a press, and that the plate, the highlight
and the keyboard's ring take the box's corners (the card's on an islands bar, a control's 4 DIPs on
a floating one) on the 40-, 48- and 64-DIP bars (`TheSearchBoxHasItsSlotsCorners`, `SearchPillTests.TheBoxHasAControlsCornersNotAPills`).
`DismissOffscreenTests.Opening_a_flyout_closes_Windows_Search_first` holds the hook. The pictures:
`KARPO_PNG_DIR\search-box-*.png` (Windows' button on the real scene: the box at rest, under the
pointer and pressed, and the icon, on 48-, 40- and 64-DIP bars), dark and light, 100 and 150 %.

## 29. One "Browse…" for a file or a folder (2026-10-04)

*"for the pins, there should not be a difference between picking a file or a folder. there should
not be multiple options if that is possible to do."*

Wherever a pin's or a shortcut's target is chosen there is one **Browse…**, and its dialog picks a
file or a folder alike: the pin's page (Browse… beside "What it opens", and Locate… on its "This PC
doesn't have it" bar), the taskbar menu page's shortcut dialog, and "Locate…" / "Choose what to
pin…" on a pin's menu on the bar. Typing a path or an address in the box works as before.

- **The dialog** (`Karpo.Dock\TargetDialog.cs`, compiled into the settings app as well) is Windows'
  own open dialog (`IFileOpenDialog`) with one button added through `IFileDialogCustomize`,
  **Select folder**, beside Open — the words of Windows' own folder dialog. Open takes the file
  chosen, as it always does. Select folder takes the folder selected in the list or, with none
  selected (or a file selected), the folder the dialog is in. It is grey where there is no folder
  on disk to take: This PC, Quick access, a library. Open on a folder still goes into it: the
  dialog can't tell that Open from a double click, which must go in, and `FOS_PICKFOLDERS` would
  hide the files. A shortcut chosen is pinned as the shortcut (`FOS_NODEREFERENCELINKS`), so its
  arguments go with it. The dialog starts beside what the box holds — a file's folder, a folder's
  parent, or the nearest folder above a target that moved — and where it last was for anything
  else (`TargetPicks.StartIn`).
- **The rules** are plain values in `Karpo.Core\TargetPicks.cs`: what each way of closing the
  dialog picks (Open, Select folder, cancel) and where it starts; whether a path is a folder is
  handed in.
- **The apps stay a choice of their own** in the shortcut dialog (the `App` button): they are a
  list of Start's apps, not files, and the open dialog can't show them. The pin's page offers no
  app list; a pin to an app comes from "Pin to taskbar" or a drag out of Start.
- The **folder widget** that picked its folder with Windows' folder picker is gone into the pin
  (§32): a pin to a folder picks it with this one "Browse…", whose "Select folder" takes it.

`TargetPickTests` holds the rules: Open on a file, Select folder on a selected folder, on the folder
the dialog is in and with nothing to take, a cancel, and where the dialog starts.

## 30. Tray icons are reordered, hidden and shown as on Windows 11 (2026-10-04)

The person: "reordering tray icons, hiding them, moving them, does not properly work."

- **Along the bar** an icon held by its middle takes the slot its middle is over, the others closing
  up around it (`TrayDrags.SlotAt`); the nearest boundary (`IndexAt`) counted the held icon's own
  place as still there, so a drop past a cell's middle landed one place too far either way. An icon
  coming from the overflow still takes the nearest boundary. A `TrayDrop`'s index counts the area's
  icons without the dragged one, which is how `TrayLayout.Apply` always read it.
- **Within the overflow** a drop was never a drop: `TrayTargetAt` asked for a flyout in any mode but
  `Menu`, and the overflow is one. Its rows are now a target, the dragged row counted out of them
  (`TrayDrags.InOverflow(…, from)`), and the overflow shows its new order at once.
- **An icon keeps its place** when its app adds it again or restarts, and across Karpo's starts
  (`TrayArrivals`, Karpo.Core): icons nobody placed followed the order their adds came in, so one
  re-added jumped to the end (or past the maximum into the overflow) and every start, which asks
  every app to add its icon again, shuffled the bar. The first arrival stands for the session, and
  `tray-icons.json` seeds the next one.
- **Identity**: a GUID icon whose executable sits in a version folder is named by its app's family
  and `|guid` (`TrayIdentity.Of`): WhatsApp gives every build a new GUID, so its choice and place
  were lost at each update. Its Windows promotion follows the same family (`Promotions.Decide`).
- **Windows' own choice** (`NotifyIconSettings\<icon>\IsPromoted`): a choice made in Karpo — a drag,
  or a state picked in the settings app (§34) — is written into the icon's own record, as Windows writes it
  (`Tray.Promote`, only an existing record, only the build that runs); a change made in Windows'
  Settings while Karpo runs becomes Karpo's choice (`WindowsChoices`, `TrayLayout.FollowWindows`).
  The newest word wins, wherever it was said.

### What was left, done as Windows 11 does it

- **The chevron while dragging**: it stands on every bar's tray for as long as an icon is dragged,
  even with nothing behind it yet (`Content.TrayOverflow` while `trayDrag`), so the first icon can be
  hidden by a drop onto it; the bars are laid out with it as the drag starts and without it after.
  That layout is a new scene in the middle of the drag: it takes every icon up where the last scene
  had it, mid-glide (`Scene.TrayNow`, `CarryTray`, `TrayGlide.Settling`), and the dock shows the drag
  on it at once (`Dock.TrayDragRebuilt`). Before, the new scene started each icon at its place: the
  held one jumped home and back to the pointer, and the others restarted their slides, once per drag
  — the "shift" at the start of every drag. The tray's neighbours still move a cell for the chevron,
  gliding.
- **The overflow opens mid-drag**: an icon held on the chevron for Windows' hover time
  (SPI_GETMOUSEHOVERTIME) opens the overflow from that bar (`TrayOverflowHover`), and its icons make
  room where the icon would land: those after the place slide a cell on (`Flyout.DropGap`,
  `GapPlaces`, 167 ms on the compositor), as Windows 11's overflow opens a gap. (It was an accent line
  between two icons, with nothing moving.) An icon dragged within the overflow leaves its place closed
  up behind it and follows the pointer, a little see-through, while it is over the panel; off it, it
  waits in its place, faint. Where the drop lands is `Flyout.DropAt`: the nearest line, then the
  nearest icon on it and which half; for an icon taken from the overflow the icon it is over (a slot,
  as `TrayDrags.SlotAt` on the bar). The place it has holds until the pointer is a fifth of a cell
  past the line it was given at (`Flyout.DropHysteresis`, as `TrayDrags.Hysteresis` on the bar), so a
  pointer resting on a boundary doesn't flick the gap. A gap past a full last line wraps the last icon
  onto a line the panel has no room for until the drop lays it out again. Opened that way, it closes again once the icon has been away from both the chevron
  and the overflow for the hover time (not at once: the way up crosses the gap between them), and
  when the icon is let go anywhere but inside it, or the drag is called off. A drop inside it keeps
  it open, showing the new order. An overflow that was open before the drag is left alone.
  *(2026-10-14, §172: the overflow now opens as a drag from the bar starts, empty or not, stays open
  for the whole drag and closes with it; the dragged icon follows the pointer in both directions in
  a window of its own, and its place in the overflow stands empty rather than the icon moving there.
  `TrayOverflowHover` is `TrayDragOverflow`.)*
- **Two icons of one name** (two windows of one app, each with uID 1; two GUIDs of one app's
  version-folder family) get a name each (`TrayNames`, Karpo.Core): the first keeps the plain one,
  the next `#2`, `#3`…, so a drag of one no longer moves the other and each keeps its own choice. A
  name stays with its live icon (one window closing hands nothing over) and a freed one goes to the
  next icon that needs it. `TrayIdentity.Of` is unchanged, so a lone icon's name, and G20's names
  that last across updates, stay as they were. Windows' record for two icons of one path and one uID
  is one record, so their IsPromoted is shared, as on Windows.
- **A tray of a set size** with more icons to show than room: the chevron stands there
  (`Layout.TraySpills`), and the icons without room go into the overflow, at its start, before the
  hidden ones (`TrayDrags.Overflow`, `Dock.TrayOverflowOf`) — before, they showed nowhere. A drop
  among the overflow's hidden icons counts after them (`TrayDrags.InOverflow(…, spilled)`); dragged
  out onto the bar one is shown where it lands, dragged within the overflow it becomes hidden.
- **A drop lands where the gap was shown** (the person: "when releasing the icons it moves to
  another spot than the one i put it to"). The release read the place again from the point of the
  release after the drag had been forgotten (`Dock.EndTrayDrag` cleared it first): without its own
  place an icon moved along the bar went by the overflow's rule (`TrayDrags.IndexAt`, itself counted
  among the others) — a place too far whenever the pointer was past a cell's middle —, one moved
  down the overflow a row too far, and the hysteresis holding the gap was gone. Now the drop commits
  the place the last move showed (`TrayDragging.Drop`, refreshed too when the chevron's layout comes
  mid-drag, `TrayDragRebuilt`), never a fresh reading: the drag's timer reads the cursor as it is now,
  the release where the button came up. And it lands beside the neighbours it was shown beside
  (`TrayLayout.Apply(…, seen)`), should the tray have changed under the drag. `TrayDropCommitTests`
  plays thousands of drags — orders, states (hidden completely among them), paths resting on the
  lines, bar and overflow, with and without the chevron — and checks the order written is the order
  shown.

`TrayOverflowDragTests` holds the names, the set-size chevron and overflow, the drop places with icons
without room, the hover's opening and closing, and where a drop lands in the overflow, its hysteresis and
the room the icons make there. The pictures
(`TrayDragSheets`): `KARPO_PNG_DIR\tray-drag-rest-*.png` (no chevron with nothing hidden),
`tray-drag-chevron-*.png` (an icon held over the lit chevron mid-drag), `tray-drag-along-*.png` (the
chevron shown while an icon moves along the tray) and `tray-overflow-drag-*.png` (the overflow opened
mid-drag, its icons moved aside for the third place), dark and light, 100 and 150 %.

## 31. The settings window is Windows 11's Settings (2026-10-04)

*"Make sure that the settings part of the app is designed in exactly the same system as the settings
app from Windows 11 … remove the bottom bar … add a find a setting search field on the topbar …
take the same colors."*

- **One surface.** Mica from the title bar down (`MicaBackdrop`), the side menu and the pages lying
  on it alike: the NavigationView's content layer, its stroke and its rounded corner are gone
  (`NavigationViewContentBackground` and its border made transparent in `MainWindow.xaml`), as in
  Settings, where only the cards stand on the Mica. Every colour is a theme resource; none is
  written out (`SettingsChromeTests.NoColourIsKarposOwn`), so light, dark and high contrast are the
  theme's own.
- **The title bar** (WinUI's `TitleBar`): the back arrow first, "Karpo" with no logo before it (the
  logo is the taskbar's and Alt+Tab's), "Find a setting" in the middle, and the caption buttons. With
  the box in it the bar is the tall one, 48, while the caption buttons stay the standard 46 by 32 at
  its top (`TitleBarHeightOption.Standard`), as Settings' do. The back arrow is always there and
  greyed while there is nowhere to go back to; it goes back one place at a time, whichever way the
  window got there, as do Alt+Left and the mouse's back button (`MainWindow`, "Back"). With the
  window in the background only the caption buttons grey; the name, the arrow and the box stay as
  they are, as in Settings (`TitleBarDeactivatedOpacity` 1).
- **The side menu** is Settings' list of categories: an icon and a name each, the selected one with
  the accent pill, 300 wide, its rows 16 in from the window's edge. Wide (799 and more), it stands
  open with no button; narrower, it folds away entirely and the title bar's pane button opens it
  over the page, and the title over the page stands higher, nearer the title bar, as Settings' does.
  Settings has no icons-only rail, so neither does this (`CompactModeThresholdWidth` =
  `ExpandedModeThresholdWidth`). The title over the page is the breadcrumb in Settings' title size
  (28, semibold).
- **The side menu's icons** (2026-10-04, *"design the icons of the sidebar in the same way that win11
  settings icons in the sidebar are designed"*) are small full-colour pictures, as Settings' are,
  drawn from SVG at the screen's scale (`MainWindow.Icons.cs`), and as big as Settings' stand: these
  drawings keep a margin inside their square that Settings' don't, so they are drawn 25 square, the
  row's icon box made as big, where Settings draws its own 20. They are not
  Microsoft's Settings icons but the same design language's open set, Microsoft's Fluent UI System
  Icons, "Color" style, MIT (`assets\settings-icons`, with the licence and a table of which row
  wears which and why): General the gear, Appearance the paint brush, Localization the globe,
  Displays the laptop, Layouts the board, Accounts the person (Taskbar menu's list went with its page, §27), About the
  question circle. Each row names its file in `MainWindow.xaml` (`karpo:SideMenu.Picture`). The
  picture stays in colour on hover, press and selection, and the accent pill marks the selected
  row, as in Settings. In high contrast every row shows the glyph its markup gives it instead, in
  the theme's text colour, as Settings turns its pictures one-coloured; Windows says when high
  contrast comes on or goes off (`UISettings.ColorValuesChanged`; whether it is on is
  `SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST`) and the rows follow at once. Never `AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged`:
  an unpackaged WinUI 3 app is refused it with `CLASS_E_CLASSNOTAVAILABLE`, and thrown from the
  window's constructor that ended every start of the settings app before its window showed
  (2026-10-05: a click on a widget in edit mode opened nothing with the settings app closed). The
  subscription goes through `NavIcon.Watch`, so a refusal costs the live follow and nothing more
  (`SettingsStartTests`). The breadcrumb, the page titles and the cards keep no picture or their monochrome glyph,
  as in Settings. "Find a setting" lists a page with its row's picture, and a card with its glyph.
  `SideMenuIconsTests` holds it.
- **No status bar.** The line along the foot ("Karpo is running", the start link, the count of
  layouts, displays and widgets) is gone with its code (`Logic\StatusLine.cs`,
  `SettingsModel.SetupSummary`). Whether the dock runs, and the way to start it, were already on the
  About page under "The dock", where Settings keeps what is about the app; the counts are what the
  Layouts page shows by being that list.
- **"Find a setting".** Windows 11 25H2 keeps the box at the top of the side menu on most PCs, and
  in the middle of the title bar on PCs with the agent in Settings (as the Store has it). The person
  asked for it "on the topbar", so it is in the title bar, drawn as Settings draws its own there: a
  box at most 516 wide, its corners a control's (ControlCornerRadius) rather than a pill, centred on the window (moved off the centre only as far as the room between
  the name and the caption buttons makes it, `Logic\SearchPlacement.cs`), 8 from the window's top,
  its magnifier at its start. With the menu folded away there is no room for it: the magnifier
  alone stands after the name, and opens the box under the title bar, as Settings' does. Ctrl+E and
  Ctrl+F put the keyboard in it, opening it first when folded. It finds, ranked as Settings ranks (`Logic\SettingsSearch.cs`: the
  name typed, then a name starting with it, then each word typed starting a word of the name, then
  the name holding it, then the page, the choices and keywords, and last the description):
  - every side-menu page, by its name and the words its row names (`Findable.Keywords`);
  - every card of those pages, read from the pages' own markup, which is embedded in the app for
    that (`Logic\SettingsIndex.cs`, `Karpo.Settings.csproj`): no second list of the settings. A card
    under `Visibility="{x:Bind Model.X}"` is offered only while the model says it shows.

  Only the app's own settings (2026-10-05, *"when i search the settings of the individual folder /
  widgets should not be searched"*). The settings of one widget, folder, pin or layout are never
  found: not their cards, not the item by its name. Which pages are read is decided by kind, not by
  card (`SettingsIndex.Searched`): the side menu's pages (General, Appearance, Localization,
  Displays, Layouts, Accounts, About), and never `WidgetPage` or a page it holds
  (`WidgetPage.Hosts`: the widgets', the tray's, a folder's, a pin's), so a card added to any of
  those later stays out of the search with no change here. Layouts is found as a page; the layouts
  it lists, and what each holds, are not. Until then the search also listed every layout and widget
  by its name and every card of a widget's page once per widget it showed for ("Show seconds" on
  each clock).

  Each suggestion is the setting's icon, its name and the page it is on ("Displays > Position").
  Choosing one, or Enter for the best, opens the page, opens the expander it is in, brings the card
  into view with the accent around it for 1.6 s, and puts the keyboard on its control. Cards built
  in code (the Layouts page's list) are not read; the page is found by the words its side-menu row
  names.
- **The pages.** Links to Windows' own settings stand last, under "Related settings", with the
  open-elsewhere icon, as Settings has them (Appearance's Colors, Localization's region, the tray's
  taskbar settings). The cards are the Community Toolkit's `SettingsCard` and `SettingsExpander`,
  3 apart; a page's column at most 1000 wide, 26 in from the menu and 24 from the window's edge, and
  centred under its title when the window is wider (`PageColumnStyle`, `Controls\PageColumn.cs`:
  a bare `MaxWidth` inside a `ScrollViewer` stood off centre, further right the wider the window).
  The measures are Settings' own, read off it side by side at 150 % with UI Automation (2026-10-05).

`SettingsSearchTests` holds the ranking; `SettingsIndexTests` the reading of a page's markup, that
the index has every card every page writes, that each goes to a page the window shows, what a
few searches find first, and that the pages read are exactly the side menu's: words only a
widget's, folder's or pin's settings have ("show seconds", "symbol", "columns", "how to show") find
nothing there; `SettingsChromeTests` that the status bar is gone and the window is built as
above. The pictures are taken by hand, with `KARPO_SETTINGS_SHOTS` set (and `KARPO_SETTINGS_THEME`
light or dark): start the settings app's `Karpo.exe --page general`, then hand it
`--test find "taskbar" --shot settings-find`, `--test go "hide dock" --shot settings-go`,
`--test size 760 640 --shot settings-narrow` and the like; what stands open over the window (the
search's list) is pictured beside it as `<shot>-popup.png`. The side menu's look in high contrast
is pictured without turning Windows' own on: `KARPO_SETTINGS_CONTRAST=high` at the start, or
`--test contrast high --shot settings-contrast` (and `standard` or `system` back).

### The pages' shared controls (2026-10-05)

*"the windows settings dont just show everything in the same style, they think about how to show
the information in an appropriate way … sometimes thy also use images to illustrate stuff for the
selectors."* The redesign (G58's survey and plan) is built from a few shared pieces, each documented
at the top of its file, so every page uses them the same way:

- **Pictures** (`Controls\PictureChoice.cs`): a choice of one by pictures, as Windows' "Taskbar
  position". A `GridView` with single selection (a list with list items to UI Automation, the
  arrow keys move the choice), `SelectedIndex` two-way. Each `PictureOption` is a drawing (its
  content), a `Caption` under it and an `AutomationName` when the caption is not what to say. The
  picture is 108 x 81 with its frame, the chosen one ringed 2 in the accent with 1 between, 18
  between pictures, the caption 6 under, as measured off Windows at 150 %. One is always chosen
  (`Logic\PictureIndex.Keep`; `PictureIndex.Of` and `ValueAt` map pictures to values). Only for
  spatial or visual choices; an abstract choice stays a dropdown. In an expander's body it stands
  in a row with no header (`ContentAlignment="Left"`), or under a header and description
  (`ContentAlignment="Vertical"`).
- **The drawings** (`Controls\Art`): made at run time from rounded rectangles on a canvas, each
  painted with an ink of `App.xaml` (`ArtDesktopStyle`, `ArtBarStyle`, `ArtCardStyle`,
  `ArtBlockStyle`, `ArtAccentStyle`, `ArtLineStyle`, `ArtInkStyle`): styles of theme resources, so
  they follow dark, light, high contrast and the accent live, and have no words in them.
  `BarStyleArt` (connected, islands with their cards, or floating panels), `EdgeArt` (a bar on one edge),
  `FolderButtonArt` (a folder's button: what's inside, or its own glyph), `CalendarViewArt` (day,
  week, month, year), `SliderEnds` (a thin and a thick bar; a hollow and a filled square),
  `WindowPreviewArt` (an app's button with the pointer resting on it and its window list above, or
  clicking it and its window brought to the front), `WidgetFlyoutArt` (a widget's flyout open above
  it, the pointer resting on the widget or clicking it). The pointer is `Ink.Pointer`, an arrow in
  `ArtPointerStyle` (the text's colour, outlined in the page's), with a click a ring of the accent
  (`ArtClickStyle`) round its tip. No
  picture files: they would go stale, couldn't follow the accent, and would need a test run to
  make again. The desktop is a plain fill, not the wallpaper (the person, 2026-10-05).
- **A slider with ends** (`Controls\EndsSlider.cs`): the value, a picture for less, the slider, a
  picture for more, as Windows' Text size. `Ends` picks a pair of drawings, or `SmallEnd` and
  `LargeEnd` any other; `ValueWidth` holds the value's room still. The value is written back only
  when the person moves the thumb, never when a range or a value given to it moves it.
- **The (i) line** (`Controls\InfoLine.cs`): under an option that can't be used, why, in one
  line, shown only then; it keeps its colour while the card greys.
- **Check rows**: a sub-option in an expander is a checkbox, not a switch, in a row with no icon
  and no header (`<controls:SettingsCard ContentAlignment="Left"><CheckBox Content="…" />`), as
  Windows' Taskbar behaviours. Not a style: a style set on a row replaces the toolkit's own style
  for an expander's rows, which can't be named from `App.xaml`.
- **Styles** (`App.xaml`): `ExpanderSummaryTextStyle`, the current value in an expander's header
  ("Islands"); `PageIntroTextStyle`, one secondary sentence under a title; `SourceFooterStyle` and
  `SourceFooterGlyphStyle`, a quiet footer line where data comes from; `PictureTileStyle`, the
  pictures' list items.
- **"Find a setting"** reads them (`Logic\SettingsIndex.cs`): a check row is a setting by its
  checkbox's words (`CheckOf`), and is found and opened inside a collapsed expander; pictures'
  captions are words (`Caption`); a row with no name (a row of pictures) gives its words to its
  expander, so "islands" and "floating" find Style. The window focuses a picture row on the picture
  chosen.

**Appearance** is the first page built from them, as G58's plan has it: Style is an expander with
the look in its header ("Floating"), open from the start, holding three pictures, Connected, Islands
and Floating (`PictureIndex.Styles`, the model's `StyleIndex`, §23.6–23.7); Material has its dropdown
in its header and the opacity in its body, greyed with "Only with Acrylic and Translucent" under it
for the other three; the height has a slider with ends; Colors stays under Related settings. The
"Island backgrounds" checkbox that stood under the pictures is gone with the switch (2026-10-05): the
islands look always wears its cards, and a search for "island backgrounds" finds Style. Its words are
all Karpo's (`settings.appearance.*`, `settings.related.header`), in the five languages.

**Localization, Accounts, About and Taskbar menu** follow (G58's plan, chunk 3), each with every
word in the strings table (`settings.localization.*`, `settings.accounts.*`, `settings.about.*`,
`settings.barMenu.*`, and `settings.common.*` for Add, Save, Cancel, Remove, OK). Nothing was removed:

- **Localization**: the display language first, under "Language", as it was; then "Formats": the
  four date and time formats in one closed expander, "Date and time formats", whose header says what
  Karpo writes now ("22/09/2026 · 14:40:07", the lists' own sample, `Logic\FormatsSummary.cs`, held
  by `FormatsSummaryTests`); its rows have no icons. Temperature and File sizes stand as cards,
  "Follow Windows for everything" last of the settings, the region's link under Related settings.
  The "Dates and times" and "Units" headers are gone.
- **Accounts**: one line under the title, then each account as a card: its provider's glyph, its
  address, and under it what Karpo shows of it and where it comes from ("Calendars, contacts, mail ·
  Microsoft account", `Logic\AccountRows.cs`, `AccountRowsTests`), with Remove in its "…" menu. With
  none, "No account yet" as one secondary line. Both forms ask for the address, then the password,
  then "Set the server myself", a check row that shows the Server and User name rows; unticked, what
  they hold is left out and the server is found from the address. Whether each is ticked is the
  model's (`SettingsModel.ImapOwnServer`, `DavOwnServer`, never saved), so "Find a setting" offers the
  rows only while they show.
- **About**: the name card as it was; Lometics and Quit Karpo (or Start Karpo) as cards with no
  header over them; Export, Import and Open config file in one closed expander, "Settings file".
- **Taskbar menu**: one line under the title, then "Entries" with Add to menu, then the rows, then
  "Reset to default" last, as Windows puts its resets. A row has Windows' six-dot gripper (drawn:
  Segoe Fluent Icons has none), its icon, its title, and under it only what the title doesn't say: a
  shortcut's target, a heading's role, a built-in row's "what it opens" where that isn't its name
  again; a divider has none. The two rows that always stay wear a lock, with the reason as its
  tooltip, in place of the sentence. No arrows ("the reorder arrows should go away"): a row moves
  by a drag, from anywhere on it, or by Alt+Up and Alt+Down, as in Windows' language list. Edit and
  remove stay visible buttons on every row, each in a column of its own down the list, not folded
  into a "…" menu (the person: "no stay as visible", G58's Q5).

`--test` edits come one after another in one start: `--test size 800 1000 --test go "short date"`.
`--test own-server` shows both account forms' server rows.
`--test open-choice <name|#n>` opens a dropdown on the page shown (after `--test expand` for one in
an expander's body) and traces where its list stands against the box. A dropdown is as wide as the
entry it shows, and keeps that width while its list is open (`Controls\ChoiceBox.cs`): WinUI
empties the box as it opens, and a box that fell to its 130 floor jumped right at the card's edge
and took its list far to the right with it (the person, 2026-10-05: *"the anchor of the dropdown
showing is way off to the right"*).

**General** (G58's spec §2.1) starts as Windows' pages do, with no section header: Start with
Windows, Hide the Windows taskbar and **Automatically hide the taskbar**, each a switch.
"Automatically hide the taskbar" is Windows' own words for what was "Hide the dock: When away /
Never" (the person, 2026-10-05): a switch over the same setting, so the file says what it always
said, `"hide": "auto"` on and `"never"` off (`Logic\AutoHide.cs`). The setting has only those two
values since hiding partly was dropped (a word no build knows is repaired to never), so the switch
reaches all of it.

Then **Combine taskbar buttons and hide labels**, in Windows' words, a card with its dropdown. It
is every taskbar's (the person, 2026-10-05: *"combine taskbar buttons and hide labels on other
taskbars should not be a setting. it should follow the default one for the main taskbar"*): the
main display's bar and every other lay their buttons out by it, through the same `AppButtons.Lay`,
so "When taskbar is full" combines on each exactly when its own buttons stop fitting
(`Layout.ButtonRoom`, `Layout.EvenCut`, §40). The other taskbars' card, its strings and the config's
`combineOther` are gone, with Windows' `MMTaskbarGlomLevel` read into a new config; a file that
still says `combineOther` loads whole and is read past it quietly, nothing saved for it, and the
word is gone at the next save (`TaskbarApps.cs`). With "Show my taskbar apps on" gone too, the
**Taskbar apps** expander held one setting, so it is gone; "taskbar apps" and "other taskbars" are
the card's keywords.

Then **Window previews** and **Open widget flyouts**, laid out as Appearance's Style (the person,
2026-10-05: *"window previews on hover should be layouted like the style setting. same for the open
widget flyouts on hover, these two should not just be a toggle button but a selector"*): each an
expander, open from the start, its header and a short description, the choice in words in its
header, and its pictures in its body. Each is still the one switch in the file (`previews`,
`hoverFlyouts`; `PictureIndex.Previews` and `PictureIndex.HoverFlyouts`, the hover picture first):

- Window previews: **On hover**, the pointer resting on an app's button with the window list
  above it; **Off**, the pointer clicking the button with its window brought to the front. Off is
  not "on click": with previews off nothing opens a list, and a click on an app's button switches
  to its windows as it does either way (`AppClicks`), so the caption says what is so.
- Open widget flyouts: **On hover**, the pointer resting on a widget with its flyout open above
  it; **On click**, the pointer clicking it, as the taskbar's own buttons open theirs (the default).
  On hover a click still opens one (`WidgetHover`).

The captions are words "Find a setting" finds the expander by, as Style's are: "previews",
"thumbnails" and "hover" land on them. The "Behavior", "Apps" and "Widgets" headers are gone; no
setting is. How often what is online updates stands last, a section of its own under "Online", as
Windows heads a page's later sections.

**Displays** (§2.4) starts with a line saying what to do and a **map of the displays**
(`Controls\DisplayMap.cs`), as Windows' Display page: each display a numbered rectangle at its real
size and place among the others (`Logic\DisplayMapLayout.cs`: one scale for all, as big as fits,
centred, two that touch a hairline apart), Karpo's bar a band along the edge it stands on (none
where Karpo is off), and the display whose card is open in the accent. A click, or Enter, opens that
display's card and closes the others. Read-only: Karpo doesn't move Windows' displays, so nothing is
dragged (the person, 2026-10-05). Each display is a button a screen reader names by its number,
its name and what Karpo does there ("1, LU28R55, Karpo at the bottom"). Then Same layout on every
display, then **one card per display**: its name and the "Main display" tag, the line under it the
display alone ("Display 1 · 3840 × 2160 · 150%"; the edge moved out, to the map and the pictures),
**Show Karpo on this display** as the switch in its header, as Windows puts a card's main switch,
and in its body **Position as Windows' Taskbar position pictures** (`EdgeArt`, greyed while Karpo
is off there) and Identify this display. What a new display gets, which matters once, is last, in a
closed **New displays** expander whose header says both answers ("Bottom · Default"), its Position
and Layout dropdowns inside. Still no page-wide Identify, and the cards still don't say which
layout a display shows.

"Find a setting" finds a display's card by its header's switch: an expander whose header is not
written out (the display's name) and whose one content is a switch with written-out words is that
setting (`SettingsIndex.SwitchOf`), its rows still the first display's. Both pages' words are
Karpo's (`settings.general.*`, `settings.displays.*`), in the five languages.

(Since §41 a display's card has no Position, no Same layout on every display and no New displays:
it has a card per edge instead. Since §42 the Displays page is gone altogether: each edge has a page
of its own, opened from edit mode, and General has the displays' switches and Identify.)

Pictures, by hand: `--new-window --page general --test size 1100 1100 --test expand --shot general`
(every expander of the page open) and `--new-window --page displays --test size 1100 1100 --test
displays 2 0 --shot displays` (two cards, the first open). `AutoHideTests`, `DisplayCardTests` and
`DisplayMapLayoutTests` hold the logic; `SettingsIndexTests` where both pages' cards stand, the
switch in a header, and the searches the General page's pictures answer; `PictureIndexTests` the two
switches' pictures; `TaskbarAppsTests` the one combine setting and the file that still says
`combineOther`.

**Layouts and the pages of one widget, folder, pin and the tray** (§2.5, §2.9–§2.13, chunk 4), with
every word in the strings table (`settings.widget.*`, `settings.folder.*`, `settings.pin.*`,
`settings.layouts.*`, `settings.tray.*`). Nothing was removed:

- **Layouts**: a layout's Duplicate and Delete stand in one row with no name, as Windows puts the
  actions on one thing (Contrast themes); Delete asks first in a flyout saying what happens to the
  displays that show it, as the Taskbar menu's Reset does; the last layout's Delete is greyed with
  "There is always one layout" under it (`InfoLine`). Duplicate's sentence is its tooltip. A new
  layout and a copy are named in the language shown ("New layout 2", "Default copy").
- **The frame** (`WidgetPage`, `IWidgetHost`): the line under the title, "Taskbar entry · in the
