  right section of Default", is one secondary sentence (`PageIntroTextStyle`) in the kind's page's
  own scroll, not a bold header; a whole sentence per section, so a language orders its words
  (`WidgetHeading`). Then the kind's own settings, most used first; then the **size, last and
  closed**: "Height in the list" or "Size in the folder", its header saying the size ("1 to 2
  rows", "2 × 1", `SizeRange.Summary`, `SpanChoice.Summary`), each field a row of its body. A
  taskbar entry has none since 2026-10-08: "Width on the taskbar" is gone with its strings (§12.6). **The same control on every page** (2026-10-06: *"the width on the
  taskbar setting should be homogenized so it looks the same way everywhere in each widget
  configuration page"*): a kind with nothing else to set (`WidgetSettings.NothingElse`: Apps, Start,
  the sound) used to get a plain card instead, its fields side by side under their own names and
  no line under its title; it has the same expander now, started open (`SizeRange.StartsOpen`) so
  the page isn't one closed card. G72 opened every kind's page (bar, grid and list, 146 pages) and
  the size differed only there, on 31 pages: 17 taskbar entries (Apps, Start, Task View, the sound,
the network, Bluetooth and the other one-glyph kinds), 7 grid cards and 7 list lines (the battery,
mail, the notifications, the sound's). The separator
  has no size card (it is outside cells: its line width and its space are its footprint), nor do
  the indicators, show desktop, the tray, and a list's divider, Task View and Snipping Tool lines,
  whose one-line row has nothing to choose. Then Windows' own page for the widget under **Related settings**, with the open-elsewhere
  arrow, and last a quiet line where online data comes from ("Weather data from Open-Meteo.com",
  "Price data from Yahoo Finance", `SourceFooterStyle`), no longer a card. Each kind's page keeps
  an empty place at its top and one after its settings, and the widget page hands its line and its
  size card into them, so everything scrolls together.
- **Per kind** (§2.10): the clock's seconds first, then "Time zone" (its header the zone's city or
  "This PC's time zone"; the zone and the label in its body) and "Timer and focus" ("5 min · 25 min";
  the two lengths, and do not disturb as a check row; the label is the clock's alone). The calendar
  on the bar: "When it opens" ("Week": the view as four pictures, `CalendarViewArt`), then Time zone.
  The weather is Windows' "Set the time zone automatically": the device's location
  as the switch in the header, the place beside it while it is off, the place search greyed with
  its (i) line while it is on, and Location settings as a link row. Stock as it was, its price
  source the footer; RSS's address and headline cards after it. Performance: the adapter or disk first, then "Show a graph" with its switch in
  the header and the pace in its body. (Web search had its engine here until the widget went,
  2026-10-11: the engine is the General page's now, §80.) The other kinds keep their cards; their links to Windows moved under Related settings.
  The weather's own scale and every widget's own interval stay gone (G61).
- **A folder** (§2.11): Name; "Face", a section with the face dropdown in its header and the face's
  own rows in its body (§86; §67 before; until 2026-10-09 the choice was two pictures,
  `FolderButtonArt`, "What's inside" and "Its icon"; the icon and "Show the name beside it" stood
  in a "Button on the taskbar" card after it until §86 moved them into the face's body); the grid's
  titles switch, or the list's "Panel" ("360 wide · automatic height": width, height, and the fixed
  height as a row of its own only while fixed, `FolderRows.PanelSummary`) — gone with the width
  every list shared (2026-10-10, §74: each list's own is chosen in the open folder); its width last.
  No list of its widgets (the person, Q4).
- **A pin** (§2.12): "What it opens", its header the target's name, its path and Browse… in its
  body, open while nothing is pinned; Name; Icon; a folder's two settings; the width last.
- **The tray** (§2.13): one sentence under the title, then the icons as one open block with
  hairlines, as Windows' "Other system tray icons", each row the icon's picture, its app's name and
  its three-way choice (G45).

A widget's, folder's, pin's or layout's settings are still never searched (§31 above): these pages
add nothing to the index. `SizeRangeTests`, `SizePlacementTests` (one form, one set of words per
place and the size last on every page, read off the registries and the pages' source),
`WidgetStandTests` (the heading, the "nothing else" rule, the span's header), `FolderRowsTests` (the button and panel headers), `TrayRowsTests` and
`ShortDescriptionsTests` (descriptions from the strings table too) hold the logic. Pictures, by
hand: `--new-window --island <id> --owner layout:<id> --test size 1100 1100 --test expand --shot
<name>`; `--test add Brightness end 0` for a kind the config has none of.

Pictures, by hand: `KARPO_SETTINGS_SHOTS` (and `KARPO_SETTINGS_THEME`, and
`KARPO_SETTINGS_SHOT_DELAY` in ms for a page still settling), then
`settings\Karpo.exe --new-window --page appearance --test size 1100 900 --shot appearance`, or
`--test gallery 1100 1500 --shot gallery` for every shared control on one page. A window started
apart takes its `--test` edit at its start too. XAML's renderer leaves out what composition
animates: a checkbox can come out with a dash and a closed expander's chevron pointing up in the
picture though neither is on screen. `PictureIndexTests` holds the mapping; `SettingsIndexTests`
the check rows, the captions, the rows with no name and where Appearance's cards stand.

## 32. One way to pin a folder (2026-10-04)

**Undone on 2026-10-28** (§380): a pin opens what it points at, and a folder's contents are a widget of their own
again, with the navigation and the titles; "How to show" went.

The person: "there should only be one way to pin/show a folder. the pin should be that way. when a
folder is selected as a pin all the folder content and navigation options should be available to
the user … also dont show open in file explorer and dont show folder title. these options should be
available for all three locations where you can show folders." The "Folder contents" widget
(backlog 14) and the folder pin's click modes (backlog 28) are one thing now: a pin to a folder.

**Two settings, only for a folder** (`PinOptions.Show`, `ShowTitles`, `Navigation`; the rules in
`Karpo.Core\PinFolders.cs`). The pin's page in the settings shows them only while its target is a
folder this PC has (`PinPage.ShowFolder`); a pin to an app, a file or a site keeps the settings it
had.

- **How to show.** *Just the folder* — the pin's icon and its name, as every pin — the default; or
  *its contents*, the folder's items inline. *Show titles*, shown under it while the pin shows its
  contents, puts each item's name beside its icon on the taskbar; a grid and a list say the names in
  their own layouts either way.
- **Navigation**, what a click on a folder does: on the pinned folder itself where the pin shows
  just the folder, and on each subfolder shown where it shows its contents. *Open in File Explorer*
  (the default), *Show its contents* (one level), or *all levels deep*, each subfolder a list of its
  own beside its row (§15.1). A file always just opens.

The defaults are what a pin to a folder always did, and none is written to the file while it stands.
The same two settings hold on the taskbar, in a grid folder and in a list folder; nothing asks where
the pin stands.

**Its contents, in each place.**

- **The taskbar: a row of buttons** (`Dock.FolderRows.cs`). The folder's items stand in the pin's
  place, a button each, in the drive flyout's order, each an app button like a pin's: the item's own
  icon and name, resolved as a pin to it would be, and its name beside the icon where "Show titles"
  is on, in two to four whole cells and shortened as an app button's label is. Where the bar runs
  short they fold as app buttons do: the labels give up cells first, then the last buttons go behind
  "…", in the pin's place (`AppButtons`, `Layout.FitTiles`). A file's button opens it; a folder's
  does what the navigation says, its list opening from that button. A right click is the pin's own
  menu. The row follows the folder: a watcher, and a read once it has settled; a read that finds the
  same items in the same order changes nothing on the bar (`FolderRows.Same`). Until the first read
  is back, and while there is nothing to list, the pin stands as its own button, so it never leaves
  the bar. Each folder is read once whichever bars show it (`FolderRows`), and let go of when none
  does.
- **A grid's card and a list's line** are the folder widget's layouts, unchanged (`PinContents`, drawn
  by `PinTile` while the pin shows its contents; §9 "A folder on this PC", §16): its sizes, the row
  lit under the pointer and never the card or the line (`LightsItsRows`), the items' icons, "+N".
  Its line in a list is as tall as its items, held inside the pin's range.

**The cascade, as deep as the folders go, from every place.** A navigation of all levels opens the
same lists (`PinFolderFlyout`) wherever the first one opens — from the pin's button or a row's
button on the bar, from the pin's card or line in a folder, from a subfolder's row of a pin showing
its contents — and each subfolder's list cascades further, on a click only. It was one level deep
from the folder widget, whose subfolders only ever opened File Explorer: the person's "it only works
one level deep. it should work x levels deep". Out of a folder of Karpo's the lists stand beside the
folder, level with the card, the line or the row clicked (`FolderFlyout.RowOnScreen`), which stays
lit (`FolderFlyout.Hold`, `PinContents.Hold`). G16's rules hold everywhere: click to open, the
parent row stays lit, the lists turn left at the screen's edge, Escape closes the deepest, a press
outside closes all, a click on another subfolder replaces the deeper lists.

**No title and no footer.** A list is the folder's items and nothing else. Opening a folder in File
Explorer from a list is a folder row's right click: a menu of Karpo's at the pointer with "Open in
File Explorer" (`Dock.FolderRowRows`, `Topic.FolderRow`), over the lists, which it holds open
(`PinFolderFlyout.MenuClosed`; a folder they stand out of is held as a widget's menu holds it).

**What a file from before reads as** (`ConfigWords`).

- A "Folder contents" widget ("fileFolder"), a grid's card or a list's line, is a pin to its folder
  showing its contents, in its cell, with its id and its size; its name and icon left to Windows. Its
  navigation is *Open in File Explorer*, which is what the widget did with a subfolder, and is not
  written. One with no folder chosen is a pin with nothing chosen, which asks for its target as the
  widget asked for its folder.
- A pin's click mode ("folderClick") is its navigation ("navigation"): "contents" and "cascade" are
  the same words, "open" is the default and is dropped. A grid folder's pin never had a mode in force
  — its click always opened File Explorer — so a word one carried is dropped and it opens File
  Explorer still.

Both are read once, and the file is written back in today's words (`Config.Repair` says it
changed). The widget is out of the registries, `Partners`, `WidgetInfos`, the add list and the menus
table; the words that found it ("folder", "folder contents", "files", "directory", "explorer") find
the pin.

**Proof.** `PinFolderSettingsTests`: the model, its defaults, the file's words, the settings going with the
pin, the cascade's stack and how a folder under it answers. `FolderContentsRemovedTests`: the widget
gone from every list, the migration of a card, a line, an unset widget and every `folderClick`, and
a file of today's words left alone, each round-tripped. `FolderRowTests`: the row's order, nothing to
list, a file opening and a folder going where its navigation says, the row following the folder, and
the row on a real layout with and without titles, folding as apps do, with pictures
(`folder-row-<icons|titles>-<roomy|short>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`). `FolderPinContentsTests`: the
card and the line, what a click opens and the navigation applying to the folder clicked, the watcher,
nothing past the box, with pictures (`folder-pin-spans-…`, `folder-pin-lines-…`, `list-headings-…`).
`PinFolderFlyoutTests`: no title and no footer, the row's menu, and four lists deep from the bar and
out of a grid's card, a list's line and a pin showing just the folder
(`pin-folder-cascade-four-<bar|grid|list>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`).

## 33. Tray icons are Windows' size (2026-10-05)

**Undone on 2026-10-08** (§48): the tray's icons are the size of every other icon on the bar again, in
the bar's square.

The person: *"can you show the tray icons a little smaller than the pins / other icons."* Windows 11
draws its app buttons' icons at 24 DIP and every icon of its notification area — the apps' tray icons,
the network, the sound, the battery — at 16 DIP, in 32-DIP buttons; its overflow is a grid of 40-DIP
squares, five to a row. Karpo drew a tray icon an app icon's size (24 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, as large
as the pins and half as large again as the network glyph beside it), in the bar's 44-DIP square, and
its overflow at 16 DIP in 36-DIP squares four to a row.

- **The picture** (`Layout.TrayIconPx`) is the taskbar's own icons' size, the one formula the network,
  the sound and the status icons use (`Fit.SystemIconFor`, `Fit.SystemIcon`): 16 DIP on the 48-DIP
  bar, at every DPI. It is always a step under the pins (`Fit.StepUnder`): from 64 DIP up the system
  glyphs grow past the pins, which stopped at 24 DIP until §538, and the tray stays at 20 there. It is never under
  Windows' small icon, 16 DIP, which on a bar of 32 DIP or less is the pins' own size, so there the two
  are one size: there is no smaller icon to draw from. 16 DIP from 28 to 53 DIP, 20 from 54 up.
- **The capture** is the same size (`Tray.IconSize`), which is the small icon an app gives NIM_ADD
  for the display's DPI, so most icons are not scaled at all. One of another size is first looked for
  at the bar's size in its app's own icon group, where the app loaded it from one (`Tray.Matched`: the
  file and resource the icon carries, opened as data only), rather than scaled down from a large one.
- **The cell** (`Layout.TrayCell`, `TrayCellPx`) is twice the icon along the bar, 32 DIP on the 48-DIP
  bar, and as thick across it (§38: it was as thick as every small widget, which was no square);
  never larger than the bar's cell, so on a bar of 36 DIP or less it is that square. The chevron's is the same. The hover, the press, a drag's gap,
  the overflow's opening over the chevron, the places apps are told (`PublishTrayRects`, NIN_*) and
  Narrator's rectangles all read `ItemRect`, `TrayStep` and `TrayIconRect`, so they follow.
- **The overflow** (`Dock.ShowFlyout`): its icons the tray's size, the size they were captured at,
  in squares of two and a half times it, Windows' 40 DIP (`Layout.TrayOverflowCell`), five to a row
  (`Layout.TrayOverflowColumns`, `Flyout.StripCell`, `Flyout.GridColumns`). The apps' "…" keeps its
  own grid.

Not changed: the status icons (§21) keep a square cell each; Windows shows them in its tray's 32-DIP
buttons, which is theirs to follow.

Tests (written 2026-10-05, not yet run): `TrayCellsTests` holds the picture at 16 DIP on the 48-DIP
bar at every DPI, the network glyph's size and smaller than a pin at every height and DPI (one size
with the pins where those are 16 DIP), the cell Windows' 32 DIP and narrower than an app button's
where the bar has the room, and the overflow's 40-DIP squares and five columns;
`NarratorTests.ATrayIconsElementIsItsNarrowCell` the elements' rectangles; `TrayRenderTests` a large
icon from an app's group taken from the group at the bar's size; `TrayOverflowDragTests`
a tray of a set size holding more of the narrower cells. Pictures: `TraySizeSheets` draws the default
bar with apps and tray icons on the real scene and the overflow as the dock opens it
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR\tray-scene-*.png`, `tray-overflow-grid-*.png`), and `TraySizePictures` the tray beside
pins and the network glyph at 32, 48, 64 and 96 DIP (`tray-size-{dark|light}-{100|150}.png`), dark and
light, 100 and 150 %.

## 34. Three places for a tray icon, and the way out of the overflow (2026-10-05)

The person: *"dragging and dropping system tray icons from the hidden view into the shown view is not
currently possible"*, *"you should also be able to completely hide a system tray icon so that it does
not even show up behind the arrow"*, *"there should basically just be three different configuration
options per tray icon, show on taskbar, show in extended or something like that, and hide
completely"*, *"most icons shown should not be a configuration option"*, *"icons on the taskbar should
also be removed as it is not needed anymore"*, *"remove the related settings section"* and *"the
icons should properly show in the settings as well, right now the settings just shows a generic
icon."*

- **One state per icon** (`Config.TrayStates`, `TrayState`), by the identity §30 gives it: **Show on
  taskbar** (`Taskbar`), **Show in hidden icon menu** (`Overflow` — "Hidden icon menu" is Windows 11's
  own name for the overflow, in Settings, Personalization, Taskbar) and **Hide completely**
  (`Hidden`): on neither, its app and its icon going on for Windows as before. An icon with no state
  goes where Windows' own choice puts it (IsPromoted: the taskbar or the hidden icon menu), as a new
  icon does on Windows 11, never hidden completely (`TrayLayout.State`, `Split`, `Off`).
- **Gone**: the "Icons on the taskbar" card (As Windows shows them / All icons / Only the ones set to
  Show: `trayShowAll`, `traySelectedOnly`), the "Most icons shown" card (`trayMaximum`), the per-icon
  Automatic/Show/Hide (`trayVisibility`) and the tray page's "Related settings" (the link to Windows'
  taskbar settings). A file holding them reads in today's words (`ConfigWords.TrayStates`): Show is
  Show on taskbar, Hide is the hidden icon menu, and the mode keeps what the bar showed — with "All
  icons", every file's default, each icon the dock last saw (`tray-icons.json`) with no choice of its
  own is written on the taskbar; with "Only the ones set to Show" in the hidden icon menu; "As Windows
  shows them" writes nothing. Icons only the maximum kept behind the chevron are on the bar again.
- **Windows' record** (§30) is told what it has a word for: Show on taskbar is promoted, the hidden
  icon menu not promoted, and Hide completely not promoted too, Karpo's own state keeping it hidden
  (`TrayLayout.Promoted`, `NewChoices`). Windows' word read back never brings an icon hidden
  completely back (`TrayLayout.FollowWindows`): only the settings app does, and its page says so.
- **The tray page** is one row per icon, as Windows 11's "Other system tray icons" is: the icon's own
  picture, its app's name and a ComboBox of the three. Settings runs in its own process, so it shows
  each icon as Windows' page does, from what the dock writes for it (`TrayCatalogue`: identity,
  tooltip, executable, the key of its NotifyIconSettings record, Windows' choice): the picture is the
  record's IconSnapshot (a PNG), else the executable's icon, else Windows' generic app icon (see
  below); the name is the executable's description or product name, else the record's InitialTooltip,
  else the tooltip, which stands under the name where it says more (`TrayRows`). The registry and the
  files are only read.

### Icons missing from the tray, and the page without pictures (2026-10-05)

The person: *"not all of the tray icons show in the tray icons widget. in the tray icons settings it
also does not yet show the tray icons icon. just their name."* On the person's machine Explorer's own
tray had WhatsApp, Spotify, the new Outlook and Windows' update icon besides the four Karpo showed
(Synology Drive, Windows Security, Claude, Bitwarden); `tray-icons.json` had only those four, so the
icons were never in Karpo's tray at all — not a state, the migration or the update icon's rule hiding
them (no icon was "Hidden", and the update rule takes MoNotificationUx.exe alone).

- **A GUID icon changed without its window was dropped.** WhatsApp's packaged app draws its icon with
  H.NotifyIcon: it adds the icon with its window, its GUID and NIS_HIDDEN, then sets its version,
  makes it visible and changes its picture and tooltip by the GUID alone, the window left 0, which
  Windows allows. `Tray.Apply` took that 0 for the icon's new window, and `Tray.Icons` drops an icon
  whose window is gone: the icon went the moment it was made visible. Only a call that names another
  window moves an icon now (`Tray.OwnerChanged`).
- **The spy lost its first place.** Apps find the tray by the first `Shell_TrayWnd` in z-order, and
  Explorer's taskbar raises itself above the spy when it is shown or activated (seen live: Explorer's
  was first a few minutes after Karpo started). From then on every icon added or changed went to
  Explorer alone; the spy was put first again only when a bar was revealed, which a bar that never
  hides is only at its start. It is checked now after every arrange (hiding Explorer's taskbar is in
  it) and whenever a window comes to the front (`Tray.EnsureFirst`: one FindWindow; where the spy was
  not first it is raised and every app asked for its icons again).
- **Not fixed: an app that never adds its icon again.** Karpo learns of an icon added before it
  started only from the TaskbarCreated it announces. Spotify (its own tray code on its main window,
  with no TaskbarCreated in it) does not answer it: its icon stays Explorer's alone until Spotify
  adds it again (restarted after Karpo), and Windows has no call that lists another tray's icons with
  what clicking them needs. The new Outlook and Windows' update icon are GUID icons that did not show
  when asked again either; whether they fell to the GUID rule above or never answer could not be told
  from outside Karpo.
- **The page's pictures.** The row's header held an `IconSourceElement`, which drew nothing in the
  card's header — not the snapshot, not the app's icon, not even the glyph it was given — so every row
  was its name alone. It is an `ImageIcon` now, as the About page's logo is, bound to
  `TrayIconRule.Picture`, and the picture is looked for in order (`TrayRows.PicturesFrom`):
  Windows' snapshot, read from its PNG in plain code (`TrayPng`), unless the page's background
  swallows it (`TrayPng.Faint`: Claude's white icon for a dark taskbar on a light page); the app's own
  icon through the shell (`Shell.Describe`), a packaged app's as Start lists it
  (`shell:AppsFolder\<family>!<app>`, from its AppxManifest.xml: `TrayRows.AppOf`), whose name is then
  the row's too (WhatsApp, not WhatsApp.Root); else its executable's; and last Windows' generic app
  icon (SIID_APPLICATION, `Shell.Generic`), which always draws.
- **One folder.** The dock writes the list and the settings app reads it through `TrayCatalogue.Write`
  and `Read`, both in `Config.Folder` (which KARPO_CONFIG_DIR moves).

`TrayGuidOwnerTests` (H.NotifyIcon's calls; every icon listed but the ones hidden completely and the
update icon the status icons take; Windows' "not promoted" never hidden completely) and
`TrayPictureTests` (the PNG reader, each filter; the faint snapshot; the order of the pictures; the
packaged app; the list in one folder) hold the rules.

### The drag out of the overflow

Three things stopped an icon dragged out of the overflow from landing on the bar:

- **The overflow closed under it.** Its icons hear the left button as it goes down (§30), and the app
  is allowed the foreground with it; an app that answers the press by coming forward (Chromium and
  Electron apps act on the button's down) took the foreground, and the overflow, a menu, closed. Its
  rows went with it but the drag did not (`Flyout.Close` kept `dragRow` and `dragging`), so nothing
  more was told — no move, no drop — and the dock's drag stayed half begun; the next showing took a
  plain move for a drag of whatever icon stood in the old row. Now a held row keeps the overflow open
  until the button comes up (`Flyout.Hold`, `LetGo`: closed then where another window took the
  foreground meanwhile), a closing flyout forgets its drag and lets the pointer go, and the dock calls
  a drag from an overflow that closes off (`FlyoutClosed`).
- **The bar had no room for it.** The tray block ends on its last cell, so "after the last icon" was
  that cell's right half, and on a bar showing no icon the block was the chevron alone — every drop on
  it went back into the overflow. An icon from the overflow now also takes the cell after the last
  icon, and on an empty tray the cell after the chevron (`TrayDrags.OnBar`).
- **The overflow's window reached over the bar.** A drop counted as one in the overflow anywhere in
  its window, whose room for the shadow reaches down to the chevron's cell, over the top of the icons
  beside it; it is the panel now (`Flyout.OnPanel`).

`TrayLayoutTests` holds the three states, Windows' choice for an icon with none, hide completely
showing nowhere, the IsPromoted mapping and Windows' word never bringing back a hidden icon;
`TrayStatesTests` the old files' words and the list for the settings app; `TrayDragsTests` the drop
after the last icon and on an empty tray, pointer to state; `TrayRowsTests` the rows' picture and name
and the page as written; `FlyoutOffscreenTests` the overflow held open through an app coming forward
and forgetting a drag when it closes.

## 35. The brightness is one slider (2026-10-05)

The person: "the brightness widget shows brightness sliders for both screens, this should not be, it
should dimm the screens brigness together with one slider. optionally you can set it so that it only
dimms the brigtness of the current screen the widget is onl."

- **One slider, everywhere.** The bar's entry, its flyout, a grid card at every span and a list line
  each have exactly one brightness slider, and no display's name. The card no longer lists the
  displays from three by three, and the line no longer grows a row for each (`BrightnessIsland` is no
  `IListContent` now: a line is its kind's rows, the slider in the middle of them).
- **Every display together, by default.** The slider sets every display whose brightness Karpo can
  set — the built-in panel through WMI, a monitor over DDC/CI — to its level; a display neither way
  reaches is skipped (`Brightness.Dimmed`, `Brightness.Set(monitor, screens, level)`).
- **What it shows.** The level of the display the widget is on: its bar's, and in a folder the one
  the folder opened on, which stands in its bar's work area and so is its bar's display. Where that
  display has no brightness, the first display that has one (`Brightness.Shown`). With no display to
  set at all it is what it was: the sun quiet and no track on the bar, "No brightness to set" on a
  line and a card, and the flyout's notice.
- **"Screens it dims".** The widget's Settings page has the one choice, "All screens" (the default)
  or "Only the screen it's on", which sets the display the widget is on alone, and has no slider to
  offer where that display has no brightness. It is `BrightnessOptions` (`"brightness": { "screens":
  "own" }`), carried by the widget's three kinds and across a move between the bar and a folder
  (`Partners`); every display is no options at all and is never written, so a file from before reads
  and writes as it did. "Find a setting" does not offer it, as it offers no one widget's settings
  (§31, only the app's own settings).
- **The flyout is Windows' row.** The sun and the slider, and nothing else: no title, no number, no
  names, no footer (`BrightnessPage`, `BrightnessRows.Line`, which gives the level's room to the
  slider). The page with no display to set keeps its title, its notice and "Display settings".
- **A slow monitor is never flooded.** A drag asks every display at every move; the worker keeps only
  each display's newest level and writes it, one display after another, as it did for one. A display
  written after a slow one is written at the drag's newest level when its turn comes, never at the
  level the round began with (`Brightness.Step`), so the last value always wins and nothing queues.

`BrightnessTests` holds every display set and the one with none skipped, its own alone, which
display's level the slider shows, and a drag over a slow monitor written as each display's newest;
`BrightnessOptionsTests` the file (nothing written by default, "own" read and written back, "all"
dropped, another kind dropping it), the move into a folder and back, and the three-way merge;
`BrightnessWidgetTests` one slider on every surface whatever the displays, and draws
`brightness-widget-{100,150}-{dark,light}.png`; `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests` the flyout's one row,
both choices, and the page with none.

## 36. Karpo's words: one table, five languages (2026-10-05)

*"make the app multilingual. add german, french, spanish, chinese simplified"*

Karpo speaks English, German, French, Spanish and Simplified Chinese. Every word Karpo writes
itself is a key in `Karpo.Core\Strings\en.json`, with its translation under the same key in
`de.json`, `fr.json`, `es.json` and `zh-Hans.json`. A source generator
(`Karpo.Strings.Generator`, referenced by Karpo.Core as an analyzer; nothing of it ships) turns
them into the class `S` at build time: one array per language, read by index, so the dock's native
AOT build needs no reflection, no resx and no CultureInfo. A key missing from a language, a
translation that lost a place, a brace left open or a key written twice is a **build error** at its
line in the JSON (KS001–KS010).

### Adding a string

1. Add the key and its English to `en.json`, in its prefix's block:
   `"dock.volume.level": "Volume: {level:int}%"`.
2. Add the same key, translated, to every other language's file (the rules are below). The build fails
   until every one has it.
3. Use it: `S.DockVolumeLevel(level)` in C#; `Header="{x:Bind s:S.SettingsShortDateHeader}"`, with
   `xmlns:s="using:Karpo"`, in XAML.

**Keys.** Dot-separated words of letters and digits, the first word one of four prefixes, each
owned by one part of the app, so two people translating never edit the same block:

| Prefix | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `settings.*` | the settings app: its pages, cards, dialogs and side menu (`settings.localization.shortDate.header`) |
| `dock.*` | the bar's menus, flyouts, quick settings and UIA names (`dock.menu.newDesktop`) |
| `core.*` | the registries both apps read: WidgetInfos, BarMenus, Presets, the catalogue (`core.widget.clock.title`) |
| `widget.*` | what a widget's face says on the bar or in a folder (`widget.weather.feelsLike`) |

`S`'s member is the key's words joined, each with a capital: `settings.language.header` is
`S.SettingsLanguageHeader`. `S` lives in the namespace `Karpo`, not `Karpo.Core`: TerraFX has an `S`
of its own (`S.S_OK`), and a type of the namespace `Karpo` is found from every `Karpo.*` namespace
before anything a using brings in, so `S.X` needs no using and is never ambiguous. TerraFX's is
written `S_OK`, with `using static TerraFX.Interop.Windows.S;`.

**Places.** A value goes into a text as a named place: `{name}`. Its type is written once, in
`en.json`, after a colon (`{count:int}`, `{count:long}`, `{ratio:double}`) and is `string` where
none is written; a translation writes `{count}`, or the same type. `S` makes a method with one
parameter per place, in the order English first uses them: `S.DockVolumeLevel(int level)`. A text
with **two or more places of one type is called with named arguments**, `S.X(name: n, app: a)`, so
a reworded English can never swap them. A number with a format of its own (a date, a size, a
temperature) is written by Nls first and passed as a string. A brace meant as a brace is doubled:
`{{` and `}}`.

**Counts.** Two keys `x.one` and `x.other`, each with `{count:int}`, also give `S.X(int count)`,
which picks one by the language's own rule (`Strings.IsOne`, `Languages.Plural`: one in English,
German and Spanish; nought and one in French; never in Chinese, which writes both alike).

**Lists of choices.** `<x:String>` choices become a model list of `S` texts, or `ComboBoxItem
Content="{x:Bind s:S.…}"`. `Findable.Keywords` is one key whose text is a comma list in each
language; the search reads `{x:Bind s:S.Name}` through `S.Lookup` (`SettingsIndex.Literal`), and in
another language than English keeps the card's English name, words and section as keywords
besides (`SettingsIndex.English`), so "short date" still finds "Kurzes Datum". A side-menu row's
name and words are keyed by its tag, `settings.nav.<tag>` and `settings.nav.<tag>.keywords`, and
are found in English the same way (`SettingsIndex.RowWords`). The window's own words (the title
bar, the search box, the breadcrumb, the undo bar) are `settings.chrome.*`; at a language change
`MainWindow.RetranslateChrome` runs `Bindings.Update()` and names the title bar's back and pane
buttons, whose tips TitleBar's template writes in English.

**Never cache a text.** A language change swaps the table (`Strings.Use`); whatever read it before
keeps the old words. A `static readonly string[] Names = [S.X, …]`, a field set in a constructor, a
width measured once and kept across rebuilds: each becomes a getter, or is made again at the
rebuild.

### What is not translated

- Logs: `Troubles.*`, `Console.*`, `Trace.*`, `Debug.*`, `appbarTrace`, `--smoke`'s report.
- The config: keys, ids, `JsonStringEnumMemberName` values.
- Interop names: window classes, `ms-settings:` links, UIA automation ids, property names. Such a
  literal that looks like words is marked `// not-ui` on its line.
- Text Windows or another app gives: app names, their jump lists and tray tips, notification
  content, device, network and endpoint names, time-zone names, keyboard layouts, the shell's menus.
  In the dock it stays in Windows' language; the settings app asks WinUI for Karpo's
  (`Languages.SetPreferred`), so its built-in controls match the page.
- Day and month names: they follow the Windows region format (Nls), which is a setting of its own.
- English search keywords stay; the translated ones are added beside them.

### Which language

`Config.Language`: null, and left out of the file, follows Windows' display language; otherwise a
code of `Languages.All` (below, "Forty languages" and "Thirty languages"), or the hidden `qps-ploc`. A code this build has
no table for is kept and reads as following Windows. `Languages.Resolve` walks Windows' preferred
list (`GetUserPreferredUILanguages`) and takes the first language Karpo has: `de-CH` is German;
`zh-CN`, `zh-SG` and `zh-Hans-*` are Simplified Chinese, `zh-TW` and `zh-HK` Traditional; one Karpo
has no file for passes on to the next in the list, else English.

- **Settings**: the Localization page's first card, "Display language": Windows default, then each
  language written in itself. `Program.Main` reads the language from the file before WinUI starts
  (`Languages.Peek`). A change rebuilds the window in place, on the page it showed, with a new frame
  (the old one keeps its cached pages in the old words), and the search reads the pages again
  (`MainWindow.Relocalize`).
- **Dock**: `Dock.Apply` compares the language; a new one swaps the table, closes an open flyout,
  and `Arrange` rebuilds every bar, which re-measures every widget, as a region format change does.
  Menus are made when they open, so they follow by themselves. DirectWrite lays text out in the
  language's locale (`Languages.TextLocale`), so Chinese falls back to Microsoft YaHei UI rather
  than Japanese's Yu Gothic UI.
- **The dock's menus and flyouts** (`dock.*`): every row, heading, empty line, reason under a
  greyed row, tooltip and screen-reader name of the bar's menu, an app's menu, a widget's menu, the
  Win+X menu, the add list, quick settings, the calendar, notifications, the clipboard, folders,
  drives, mail and contacts. A flyout that is kept between openings and names its controls once
  (the clipboard, the drives, the contacts' search box) remembers the language it was made in and
  is made again at its next opening after a change. What a screen reader hears of several things
  at once is joined as the language writes a list (`Dock.Listed`: "Pinned, wants attention", in
  Chinese with its own comma). Words measured once to keep room (the desktop switcher's "Desktop
  88", the countdown's action words) are measured in the language shown, so German's longer words
  get their room.

`qps-ploc` is English made foreign at build time: every letter accented, about 40 % longer, in
brackets (`[Đíšþĺáý ĺáñĝúáĝé·····]`). A plain English word in a picture under it is a string still
written in the code; a cut word is a width measured from English.

### Translating

Agents translate now; a native speaker reads every language later. Until then:

- **Natural and short.** Say it as that language's Windows 11 says it, not word for word. A label is
  as short as the English, or shorter where the language allows: German runs about a third longer,
  so take the shorter of two good words.
- **Windows 11's own terms**, exactly:

  | English | Deutsch | Français | Español | 简体中文 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Taskbar | Taskleiste | Barre des tâches | Barra de tareas | 任务栏 |
  | Settings | Einstellungen | Paramètres | Configuración | 设置 |
  | Start | Start | Démarrer | Inicio | 开始 |
  | Search | Suche | Rechercher | Búsqueda | 搜索 |
  | Notifications | Benachrichtigungen | Notifications | Notificaciones | 通知 |
  | Quick settings | Schnelleinstellungen | Paramètres rapides | Configuración rápida | 快速设置 |
  | Widgets | Widgets | Widgets | Widgets | 小组件 |
  | Pin to taskbar | An Taskleiste anheften | Épingler à la barre des tâches | Anclar a la barra de tareas | 固定到任务栏 |
  | Do not disturb | Nicht stören | Ne pas déranger | No molestar | 请勿打扰 |
  | Wi-Fi | WLAN | Wi-Fi | Wi-Fi | WLAN |
  | Volume | Lautstärke | Volume | Volumen | 音量 |

- **Address the person** as Windows does: German *Sie*, French *vous*, Spanish *tú*, Chinese *你*.
- **Typography**: sentence case, as English has it; no full stop after a label; in French, ’ for the
  apostrophe and a no-break space (U+00A0) before `:` `;` `?` `!`; in Chinese, full-width punctuation
  (（），、：) and a space between Chinese and Latin words.
- Places stay as they are, by name; their order may change to suit the sentence.

### A widget's words

A widget's title, blurb and search words are not written in its `WidgetInfo`: they are keyed by its
id, `core.widget.<id>.title`, `.blurb` and `.keywords` (a comma list, small letters), and
`Title`, `Blurb` and `Keywords` read them each time they are asked for (`Strings.Text`,
`Strings.List`). A ready-made group's are keyed the same way (`core.preset.<id>.*`), and a link to
Windows' settings names its key (`WindowsLink.TitleKey`, `core.link.*`). So no record holds a
text, and a language change reaches every title with nothing to rebuild. The build cannot check a
key made from an id; `RegistryWordsTests` does: every widget, preset and link has its words.

The other registries' words are S's members, read in getters, never kept: the bar menu's rows
(`BarMenus.Actions` is made each time it is asked for), the catalogue's groups and pages, a
drive's kind, a pin's check, the stock ranges, and the faces' words (`widget.*`). A width template
is made of the same member as the text it measures (`Units.SizeShape` is "88.8 MB" in English and
"88.8 Mo" in French), and `TextLine.Template`'s cache is keyed by the language as well, since
DirectWrite lays a text out in the language's locale.

**Search in two languages.** In another language than English, a widget is found by its English
words as well as its own: `Keywords` is the language's list, then English's, and a catalogue row
carries the English title and blurb besides (`CatalogueEntry.English`), so "clock" still finds
"Uhr" in German. A preset's words (`Presets.WordsOf`) do the same.

### Forty languages (2026-11-09)

*"add a new language to all the applications and also websites. greek. and then also add 10 more
languages that are next in popularity."* And: *"the apps should get the same languages as the website is
in. i want to homogenize that accross all the apps and websites."*

Every Lometics app and site now has the same forty. After the thirty below come the next ten by how
many people speak them: Kiswahili `sw` (`sw-KE`), Hausa `ha` (`ha-NG`), ਪੰਜਾਬੀ `pa` (`pa-IN`,
Gurmukhi; Shahmukhi `pa-Arab` is not this table and passes on to the next preference), Filipino `fil`
(`fil-PH`; Tagalog's older `tl` maps to it), ગુજરાતી `gu` (`gu-IN`), ಕನ್ನಡ `kn` (`kn-IN`), മലയാളം
`ml` (`ml-IN`), አማርኛ `am` (`am-ET`), Yorùbá `yo` (`yo-NG`) and မြန်မာ `my` (`my-MM`). None reads
right to left. Punjabi, Gujarati, Kannada and Amharic take the singular for nought too (CLDR);
Yoruba and Burmese write both alike. Windows has no Yoruba or Burmese display language, so their
Windows words are the ones their readers use; Burmese and Filipino keep the English names of the
tools Windows names in English (`UntranslatedTests.Same`). All ten are machine-written and want a
native reader.

### Thirty languages (2026-10-12)

*"translate the app for 10 more languages, start from the most to the least common ones." —
"make sure that every text is actually translated and not just in english"* — and then *"implement
the languages that themia has translated but karpo has not here as well."*

After the first five come, by how many people use them: Português (Brasil) `pt-BR`, 日本語 `ja`,
Русский `ru`, 한국어 `ko`, Italiano `it`, 繁體中文 `zh-Hant`, Polski `pl`, Türkçe `tr`,
Nederlands `nl`, Bahasa Indonesia `id`; then Themia's six, in the same order: हिन्दी `hi`
(`hi-IN`), العربية `ar` (`ar-SA`), বাংলা `bn` (`bn-IN`; `bn-BD` maps to it too), اردو `ur`
(`ur-PK`), मराठी `mr` (`mr-IN`) and Tiếng Việt `vi` (`vi-VN`). Bengali is laid out as India's, as
Themia's is: Bangladesh's default digits are Bengali ones, wider than the Latin figures every
width here is measured on. Then nine more, by how many people use them: తెలుగు `te` (`te-IN`),
தமிழ் `ta` (`ta-IN`), فارسی `fa` (`fa-IR`; `fa-AF` and Dari's `prs-AF` map to it), Bahasa Melayu
`ms` (`ms-MY`; `ms-BN`, `ms-SG` too), ไทย `th` (`th-TH`), Українська `uk` (`uk-UA`), Română `ro`
(`ro-RO`), Ελληνικά `el` (`el-GR`) and Čeština `cs` (`cs-CZ`). Arabic, Urdu and Persian read right
to left ("Right to left", below); Hebrew is not translated.

All thirty files are there, each with every key of `en.json` in its order and layout
(`StringFileTests.EveryLanguageKarpoKnowsHasItsFile`). A text its Windows writes as English does
(Dutch's Timer, Indonesian's File Explorer, Italian's Desktop) is listed by key in
`UntranslatedTests.Same`; Japanese, Russian, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali,
Urdu, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Persian, Ukrainian and Greek need no list.

**One list, the files decide.** `Languages.All` is every language Karpo knows: its code (the file's
name), its name in itself, the tag Windows knows it by (`Tag`: `zh-Hant` is `zh-TW`, `ja` is
`ja-JP`) and its plural rule. A language is *offered* — in Settings' list, and to Windows' list —
once `Karpo.Core\Strings\<code>.json` exists (`Languages.Offered`, `Map`: `Strings.Has`); the
generator already makes a table of every file there is. So adding a translation is adding its file,
and a file whose code `All` lacks fails `StringFileTests`. Windows' tags map by `Languages.Code`:
the language subtag, with Chinese told apart by script or region (`zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-MO`,
`zh-Hant-*` Traditional; the rest Simplified), every Portuguese to `pt-BR`, `in` (Indonesian's
old code) to `id`, and `prs` (Dari) to `fa`.

**Counts.** `Languages.IsOne` by the language's rule: one alone (en, de, es, it, nl, pl, tr, ar, ur,
mr, te, ta, ro, el, cs), nought and one (fr, pt-BR, hi, bn, fa), 1, 21, 31 … but not 11 (ru, uk),
never (zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ko, id, vi, ms, th, which write both alike). Russian's, Ukrainian's,
Polish's and Czech's "few" (2–4), Czech's many, Romanian's few, and Arabic's dual, few and many,
have no key of their own and take `.other`; a translator words `.other` so that it reads for
all of them where the language allows.

**Fonts.** Nothing is bundled: DirectWrite falls back from Segoe UI Variable by the text's locale,
and Chinese, Japanese and Korean share code points, so the locale is what picks Microsoft YaHei UI
(zh-CN), Microsoft JhengHei UI (zh-TW), Yu Gothic UI (ja-JP) or Malgun Gothic (ko-KR). The dock
gives every text format `Languages.TextLocale`; the settings window sets `Root.Language` to it
(`MainWindow.SpeakLanguage`), at its start and at each language change, or 繁體中文 would be drawn
in a Japanese font on an English Windows. Widths are measured, never assumed: `TextLine.Template`'s
cache is keyed by the language. Devanagari (hi, mr), Bengali, Tamil and Telugu fall back to Nirmala
UI, Thai to Leelawadee UI, Arabic, Urdu and Persian to Segoe UI's own Arabic; Vietnamese, Greek,
Cyrillic and the Latin languages stay in Segoe UI Variable. Urdu is not asked for a
Nastaliq face: Windows installs "Urdu Typesetting" only with its language pack, and its tall lines
would overflow every height the rows are measured for. Devanagari's and Bengali's marks above and
below the line fit the menus' rows and a folder's lines as they are, uncut (`RightToLeftPictures`'
Hindi sheets; Thai's and Tamil's folder sheets), so no line height changed for them.

**Keyword lists.** A comma list (`.keywords`, the icon gallery's words) is split at whichever comma
the language writes (`Strings.Words`): the Latin one, Arabic's `،` (Arabic and Urdu write it between
keywords, and Persian in the icon gallery), and Chinese's and Japanese's `、` and `，`. Until then
Arabic's and Urdu's keywords were read as one long word, so only the first found a widget, and an
icon's Arabic name was its whole list.

### Right to left (2026-10-12)

Arabic, Urdu and Persian (`Languages.Known.RightToLeft`, `Languages.RightToLeft`) are read from the right,
and so is what Karpo draws in them — as far as this goes:

- **Settings** flows right to left: `MainWindow.SpeakLanguage` sets `Root.FlowDirection` with the
  language, so the side menu stands at the right and every card's control at its left, and WinUI
  turns its own controls, chevrons and sliders. The title bar's TitleBar swaps the caption
  buttons' room by its own FlowDirection, which is set on it too. A dialog is not under the root
  and takes the direction where every dialog passes (`MainWindow.FollowPresses`); "Find a setting"
  folded into its popup opens at the window's right. What pictures the bar or the screens stays
  left to right (the Art pictures, `DisplayMap`): the bar does, and a screen at the left is at the
  left in every language. "Open in a new window" glyphs turn (`MirroredWhenRightToLeft`).
- **Every line of text the dock draws** (`Gfx.TextLayout`) is laid out right to left where
  `Languages.ReadsRightToLeft` says: in Arabic, Urdu or Persian, a line with any Arabic letter in it, so
  "Wi-Fi" and the Arabic after it read in Arabic's order; in any language, a line whose first letter
  is Arabic (a window's title). Numbers, times, sizes and Latin words alone stay left to right. The
  line is trailing-aligned, which puts it at its box's left exactly as a left-to-right line, so no
  caller's box or place changes; an ellipsis stands at its left end.
- **Menus and the add list** (`Flyout`) are mirrored once, after they are laid out: each row's
  visuals and its box are turned across the panel (`Mirror.Across`), so the icon stands at a row's
  right, the check mark further out, the shortcut, the tag and a submenu's chevron at its left —
  the chevron pointing left — and the icon buttons' row from the right. The title and the scroll
  indicator change sides, a submenu opens to the left (`ShowBeside(leftward)`), Left opens it and
  Right closes it, and the add list's columns read from the right. The search field's words stand
  at its right while they fit. Tooltips are a line of text and need nothing more. A grid of tiles
  (the tray's overflow, a Start-like folder) keeps its order.
- **A folder's lines** are Direct2D drawings, and each is painted under a mirror (`Mirror.Begin`,
  `FolderFlyout.DrawCard`): every fill, bar, plate and slider lands mirrored — a slider fills from
  the right, a graph runs from the right — while every piece of text and every picture is drawn
  through `Mirror.Text` and `Gfx.DrawPixels`, which turn it back about its own middle, so it reads.
  A glyph that points along the line (chevrons, back and forward, undo, send, open in a new window:
  `Mirror.Turns`) is left mirrored, as Windows turns it. What reads left to right in every language
  is kept upright whole (`Mirror.Keep`): a clock's face, the media's previous, play and next, and a
  text box being typed in (its caret and selection are DirectWrite's, from the left). The pointer
  is mirrored back into the line before the widget hears of it (`FolderFlyout.CardSpace`), and
  turned back again inside a part kept upright, so a press lands on what is drawn there; a part's
  tooltip is placed the same way.

**Not mirrored, on purpose or not yet.** The **bar** keeps its sections where the person put
them: Windows mirrors its taskbar in Arabic (Start at the right), but Karpo's sections are the
person's own arrangement, and the layout's drop slots, edit mode and carries reckon along the bar
from its left in many places with no start/end seam to turn them at once; a vertical bar has no
right to left anyway. Its text is laid out right to left all the same. The **quick settings,
calendar, notifications, clipboard, drives and mail flyouts** are laid out left to right, their
words right to left; mirroring them is a pass of its own per flyout. A typed line in a folder's text
box starts at the box's left. The IME's composition window is placed by the unmirrored caret.

`RightToLeftPictures` speaks Arabic, Urdu and Persian from their files: a menu with a submenu, a
check, a shortcut, a greyed row and the icon buttons; their tooltip; the add list and its search in
each; a folder of a heading, switches, the brightness, a clock, the battery, the processor and the
media in each; and the same menu and folder in Hindi, and the folder in Thai and Tamil, for their
letters' height.

**Nothing left in English.** `UntranslatedTests` fails on any text a translation writes exactly as
English does, unless it is a name (Karpo, Wi-Fi, Windows Update, Microsoft Store), a unit (GB,
GHz, and the SI's s, min, h, d and px, which "{minutes} min" keeps in every language), an address, only places and signs (`{first}, {next}`), or listed for that language by key
(`UntranslatedTests.Same`): a word its Windows writes the same, German's "System", French's
"Notifications". A new language lands with every such text translated or listed after a check.
`HardCodedEnglishTests` now also counts any words put straight into a control (`Text = "…"`,
`SetToolTip(…, "…")`, a TextBlock's own text), whatever their case, and both baselines are 0.

The audit that came with them moved the last English out of the code: the icon gallery's names and
search words (`settings.iconPicker.icon.<id>`, a comma list, its name first; found in the language
and in English), the import summary's lines (each setting by its card's own header; a key this
version has no card for by its name in the file), and the settings app's save, import and export
messages.

### Tests

`Karpo.Tests\Localization`: every file has English's keys and places, balanced braces and the four
prefixes, and the tables say what the files say (`StringFileTests`); switching, places, counts,
lookups, the pseudo-locale and the text locale (`StringsTests`); Windows' tags, the list walk, a
choice over Windows, the settings list and the peek (`LanguageTests`); the setting through the file
and the three-way merge (`ConfigLanguageTests`); the search reading `{x:Bind s:S.…}` in English and
in German (`SearchWordsTests`). Every test reads English: `Isolation.cs` pins it
(`Strings.Use("en")`, and `KARPO_LANGUAGE=en` for every Karpo a test starts, which an isolated run
reads instead of Windows' list). A test that switches the language is in the `InLanguage` collection
and takes it with `InLanguage.Use`, which puts English back.

`HardCodedEnglishTests` is the ratchet. It counts the English still written in Karpo's C# (a
capitalised literal with a space; logs, exceptions, attributes and `// not-ui` lines aside) and in
the settings app's XAML (a written-out Header, Description, Text, Content, PlaceholderText,
AutomationProperties.Name or `<x:String>`), and holds each count to its baseline. More fails; fewer
fails too, saying what to lower the baseline to, so English that has gone stays gone. Both are 0
since the i18n audit (2026-10-12). `UntranslatedTests` is its other half, for the files: no
translation leaves a text in English ("Thirty languages", above).

## 37. One interval for everything online (2026-10-05)

*"no remove the own setting completely for this. also there should be only one counter for online
updates, e.g. the stock widgets should follow it, weather should update in that duration, and other
online stuff should also just update in that intervall."*

Everything Karpo fetches from the internet on a timer is fetched again at **one interval**,
`Config.OnlineUpdateMinutes`: General → Online → "Update online widgets", every 5, 15 or 30
minutes, every hour, or every 2 or 3 hours — the weather's and the stocks' own choices together.
A new config says **15 minutes**: it was the stocks' default, it sits between the accounts' old
5 and 10 minutes and the weather's old 30, and it is the weather's own floor. No widget has an
interval of its own any more, and the weather has no scale of its own either.

**What follows it.** Each service asks the interval when it decides what is due, held to its
provider's floor where it has one:

| Service | Floor | Before | How a change reaches it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weather (Open-Meteo; the widget, its rows and its sources) | 15 min: Open-Meteo's current conditions move in quarter-hour steps | the widget's own, 15–180, default 30 | `WeatherStore.Every`, asked at every poll |
| Stocks (Yahoo's chart endpoint) | 5 min: an unkeyed endpoint, asked as an ordinary client would | the widget's own, 5–180, default 15 | `StockStore.Every`, asked at every poll |
| Calendars (Microsoft, CalDAV) | none | every 10 minutes | the store's timer is re-armed (`OnlineUpdates.Changed`) |
| Mail (Microsoft, IMAP) | none | every 5 minutes | the store's timer is re-armed |
| Contacts (Microsoft, CardDAV) | none | fresh for 5 minutes | asked each time the panel opens |

None of the accounts is push-based: Karpo holds no IMAP IDLE connection and no Graph subscription,
so a poll is all there is, and they follow the interval with the rest. What is *not* on it, because
it is fetched only when somebody asks: a pinned site's icon (`FaviconStore`), the search box's
suggestions, and the settings app's place and symbol searches.

**What stays as it was.** A failure rests its own minute (the accounts) or five (the weather, the
stocks), and a stock the endpoint told to slow down waits its half hour, whatever the interval. The
person's own **Refresh** — the weather's and a share's panel, a folder's card, a widget's menu —
fetches at once, at any interval. The mail panel reads again on opening when the last read is more
than a minute old, as it did. A reading is called stale after three intervals (`WeatherAge`), now
the one interval held to its kind's floor (`WeatherReading.Refresh`, `StockReading.Refresh`).

**Live.** The dock sets `OnlineUpdates.Shared` from the config at its start and in every `Apply`,
before the bars are arranged again, so the islands' ticks (`IntervalMs`) are read afresh; the
weather and the stocks ask the interval at each poll, so a shorter one makes a reading due at the
next tick; the calendars and the mail re-arm their timers from their last read the moment it
changes. Nothing restarts.

**For a new online widget** (a feed, a rate): take an `OnlineUpdates` in the store's constructor,
defaulting to `OnlineUpdates.Shared`; ask `Every(floor)` whenever deciding whether a fetch is due,
with the provider's floor declared beside it and why; a store with a timer of its own listens to
`Changed` and re-arms it. `Karpo.Core\OnlineUpdates.cs` says this at its top.

**The scale.** The weather shows Localization's temperature scale (`Nls.Fahrenheit`): the one
somebody set, else the region's measurement system (`LOCALE_IMEASURE`: US units are Fahrenheit).
The widget's own Temperature row, which that setting already overrode once set, is gone.

**Files from before.** The weather's `refreshMinutes` and `fahrenheit` and the stocks'
`refreshMinutes` are read past quietly, as any word Karpo no longer knows is, and are gone from
the file the next time it is saved; reading past them is not a change to save. The interval is
carried over only without guessing (`ConfigWords.OnlineMinutes`): a file with no
`onlineUpdateMinutes` whose weather and stock widgets — on any bar, in any folder — were every one
of them set to the same interval, none of them left at the default it came with, takes that
interval. Widgets that disagreed, one left at its default, or none at all: 15 minutes. The scale is
not carried: Localization's follows Windows until somebody sets it. The calendar's retired
`refreshMinutes` was never read and carries nothing.

**Tests.** `OnlineUpdatesTests` (each service takes the interval, its floors, a change applied at
once, Refresh by hand), `OnlineUpdateConfigTests` (the file, the clamp, the carry-over, the merge),
`OnlineUpdateRowTests` (the row's choices and words), `SettingsIndexTests` (the card on General is
found; no widget page has an Update or a Temperature row), and `WeatherReadingTests` (the scale is
Localization's).

## 38. A tray icon's cell is square (2026-10-05)

Since 2026-10-08 (§48) the square is the bar's own again, 44 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, and the picture
the pins' size; the cell stays square.

The person: *"i just saw right now that the tray icons dont have the 1x1 aspect ratio anymore, they
should have it."* §33 made a tray cell Windows' 32 DIP along the bar but left it as thick across it as
a small widget (`Layout.Locate` asked for `SmallWell` across): 32 by 44 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, 32 by 33
at 37 DIP, the same on a vertical bar turned round. Its card in the islands look and its hover and
press plate in the connected one are that rectangle, so they stood taller than wide.

- **The cell is `TrayCell` both ways**, centred across the bar (`Layout.Locate`, `HitKind.Tray` and
  `HitKind.TrayOverflow`): 32 by 32 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, the bar's own square on a bar too thin for
  32 DIP, 40 by 40 from 54 DIP up where the icon is 20; at every DPI, on every edge and in every look,
  as each reads `ItemRect`. The chevron's cell is the same square.
- **The picture** stays the system icons' size (16 DIP on the 48-DIP bar) in the middle of its square
  (`TrayIconRect`).
- **The card and the plate** are the square: the islands look's card (`Scene` `TrayCard`) and a lit
  card keep the cards' corner (`CardRadius`); the connected look's plate keeps Windows' 4-DIP corner
  (`Scene.Highlight`, `SoftPx(HighlightRadiusDip)`). Narrator's rectangles and the places apps are told
  (`PublishTrayRects`) are the square as well.
- **Along the bar nothing moved**: the step from one cell to the next (`TrayStep`), the block's length,
  the hit test (anywhere across the bar still reaches the icon, as on Windows) and a drag's places
  (`TrayDrags.OnBar`, which reads the bar along it only) are as §33 and §34 left them.
- **Not changed**: the status icons (§21) and the network, sound and battery keep their own cells;
  Windows draws those as one wider group, not as squares, and they are their widgets' to follow.

Tests: `TrayCellsTests.EveryTrayCellIsSquare` (every icon's and the chevron's cell square and centred
across, every look, every height from 32 to 64 DIP, 100, 125, 150 and 200 %, all four edges),
`ThePictureIsCentredInItsSquare` and `TheDropCellsAreTheSquares` (each square's middle is that icon's
drop place, the chevron's the overflow); `EveryTrayCellIsWindowsTrayButton` and
`NarratorTests.ATrayIconsElementIsItsNarrowCell` hold the 32-by-32 square. Pictures:
`TraySquareSheets` draws three icons and the chevron with the second under the pointer
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR	ray-square-<style>-<32|48|64>-<bottom|left>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`).

## 39. A news feed, in all three places (2026-10-05)

*"add rss widget as well, for all three positions"*

The RSS widget (`rss`, in the add list's Time group beside the weather and the stocks) follows one
news feed, RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0's RDF or Atom, and is a taskbar entry, a grid card and a list line, one
subject in all three (`Partners`), its feed going with it from one to another. Windows 11's widgets
board and MSN's news cards are the look.

**The feed.** One address per widget (`RssOptions.Address`), set on the widget's own page in the
settings, "Feed address". The address is read once there, through the reader the bar uses, and
only an address that reads as a feed is kept, with the name the feed gives itself
(`RssOptions.Title`), as a stock's symbol is proved against the price service before it is saved.
One that is not a feed is refused with words ("That address isn't an RSS or Atom feed"); one that
could not be asked says so, which is not the same thing. A bare host gets "https://", and `feed:`
is the address behind it (`Feeds.Address`). A new widget opens its page at that box
(`SetupField.Feed`).

**The reader** (`Karpo.Core\Feeds.cs`) is shared by both apps, so an address the card accepts is
one the widget reads. A feed is somebody else's XML and is read as data, never as instructions:

- System.Xml with the DTD ignored and no resolver, so no entity of the feed's own is expanded and
  nothing it names is fetched; a document that needs either is refused (the billion laughs and an
  external entity are both tests). No serializer: the reader walks the elements it knows by name,
  which is what keeps it trim- and NativeAOT-safe.
- Every text ends as plain words: the tags of any HTML taken out, entities decoded (twice where a
  feed encoded them twice), white space folded, a headline cut at 300 characters, a feed's name at
  120. At most 30 items, newest first where every item says when, else in the feed's order, and a
  document of at most 4 MB.
- A link, a site and a picture are kept only as absolute http or https addresses, relative ones read
  against the feed (and Atom's `xml:base`). Everything else a feed names is dropped, so a click can
  only ever open a web page: `Feeds.Opens` is asked again by every place that opens one — the panel,
  a folder, the menu's "Open website" — whatever it was handed.
- Dates in RSS's RFC 822 (numeric, named and missing zones, two-figure years) and Atom's ISO 8601.
- A picture is the item's `media:thumbnail`, an image of its `media:content` (or a `media:group`'s),
  an image enclosure (Atom's `rel="enclosure"` link), and as a last resort the first `<img>` in its
  words.

**The store** (`Karpo.Dock\Rss\RssStore.cs`) reads each feed once however many widgets show it, off
the dock's thread through the islands' one HTTP client (no cookies, a timeout), sends the site's
ETag and Last-Modified back so an unchanged feed is a 304, and keeps the last read in `rss.json`, so
a widget shows its headlines at the start rather than after the first answer. A failed read keeps
what was read before and says why beside it ("The feed can't be reached"); a site that says it is
busy is left alone for half an hour. A feed is read again at **the one online interval** every
online widget keeps (§37, `OnlineUpdates`), asked at each poll so a change applies at once, with no
interval of the widget's own (`RssStore.Every`, never sooner than five minutes); the panel's
Refresh and the menu's read at once, whatever the interval. A data source (`RssData`) keeps every feed in the config read from the dock's start, drawn or not, as
a share's price is.

**New since the panel was opened.** The store remembers which items the panel showed when it was
last opened (in `rss.json`); a headline that came after wears the accent's dot — on the bar's glyph,
before the headline on a card and a line, and in the panel — until the panel is opened again. A
feed's first read has nothing new in it.

**On the bar**: the news glyph and, where the widget says so (`RssOptions.ShowHeadline`, on unless
switched off, the taskbar entry's alone), the newest headline beside it in a room of its own
(`WidgetShapes.Rss`: about twenty-six letters of the bar's text), never the headline itself — a feed
read again would move the bar. What does not fit ends in "…", and down a bar on its side it is the
glyph alone. A click opens Karpo's own headlines panel, so the
entry has no tooltip.

**The panel** (`RssFlyout`) is the feed's name with a refresh, then its newest stories (fifteen at
most), each its headline on up to three lines, "Example News · 2 h" under it, the accent's dot while
it is new, and its picture on the right — a quiet square where the feed names one that has not
arrived, so nothing moves when it does. Pictures are fetched only when something is about to show
them, from the feed's own http or https addresses, capped in size, decoded off the dock's thread and
cropped square; they are kept in memory only. A story's click closes the panel and opens it in the
browser; the footer's link opens the feed's site. Escape and a click elsewhere close it.

**As a grid card** at every span (§16): at a tile, the glyph, in the accent while something is new;
in a row, the glyph, the newest headline on one line and how old it is; in a column, the newest
headline under the glyph on as many lines as the column holds, or the glyph alone where not even its
first word fits the column's width; from two by two, the feed's name over its newest headlines, each
over where it is from and how old it is — the first on up to three lines with its picture beside it
where the card is wide enough, the rest on up to two — as many as the card holds whole. The name is
left out where a headline of two lines would not fit under it (a two-by-two card is its headline),
and the first headline gives up its third line where that lets a second one in, so the card fills its
box. A headline is the one thing a card shortens: its last line ends in "…" after its last whole
word, as a news card's does, and no word is ever broken across two lines; the feed's name and a
byline are whole or left out, as every card's words are. At the largest text the headlines' size
gives way to the card (never under 11 DIP), as a row's does, so a small card still says a headline.

(F18, 2026-10-05: the picture tests (`RssPictureTests`) and the feed rules' tests
(`FeedRulesTests`) did not land with the widget; restored, they found the cards of two rows drawing
no headline — the name's room was counted with one gap and laid out with one and a half — words
broken mid-word in a column, and a two-by-two card left empty at the largest text. Fixed as above.)

**As a list line** at every height (§9), laid out as the mail's: on one row the newest headline and
its age; the compact line, the feed's name over its newest headlines a line each with their ages;
the whole widget, each headline over where it is from and how old it is, and how many more there
are. A new line asks for room for eight.

**Clicks in a folder** (§15). A headline on a card or a line is a target of its own
(`RssIsland.CardTarget`, one layout for the drawing and the click) and lights under the pointer as a
list's row does (`LightsItsRows`). Its click is an app opening (`CellAct.Action`, `IslandView.App`):
the folder carries it out as it carries out a pin's, closing as the browser comes
(`Dock.FolderForward`). A click anywhere else asks for the panel, which a folder refuses. The right
click (`Dock.WidgetMenus.cs`) has "Refresh" and "Open website", the feed's site, greyed until the
feed names one; the bar's entry has neither, its panel having both.

**Words.** `core.widget.rss.*`, `widget.rss.*` (the faces: why there is no headline, the ages "5 m",
"2 h", "3 d", "2 w", "1 y" and the byline, each in the language's own units), `dock.rss.*` (the panel
and why a read failed), `dock.widgetMenu.openWebsite` and `settings.rss.*`, in all five languages.

**Tests.** `Karpo.Tests\Rss`: the reader (RSS 2.0, Atom, RDF, a document's own encoding, malformed
input, an entity bomb, an external entity, HTML and entities in titles, thumbnails, dates, the
limits), the ages in five languages, which links open, a typed address, the menu's website row, the
file (round trip, a hand-edited address, the three-way merge, the partners), the registries, the
store (the pace, ETag and 304, a failure, the dots, rss.json, a picture's crop), and, with
`KARPO_UI_TESTS=1`, the pictures: the entry, every card span, every line height and the panel, at
100 % and 150 %, dark and light (`rss-*.png`), the entry's width against the headline, every card in
its box, every line in its line, and a headline's click.

## 40. The open apps: every window on every bar, and "…" only when the bar is full (2026-10-05)

The person: *"'show my taskbar apps on', should not be a setting. if the apps widget is on a layout it
should always behave the same way."* And: *"when i have combine taskbar button... set to never it
shows me the three ... even though there is plenty of space. fix that."*

- **No "Show my taskbar apps on".** Its card is gone from Settings › General's "Taskbar apps"
  expander, with its five strings in every language, the config's `showAppsOn`, Windows'
  `MMTaskbarMode` read into a new config, and the bar's question of which display a window is on.
  Wherever a layout holds the Apps widget, it shows every open window, the same on every bar and
  display: Windows' "All taskbars", which is what the person had chosen (`Dock.TilesFor`). A file
  that still says `showAppsOn` loads whole and is read past it quietly, as any word Karpo no longer
  knows is; nothing is saved for it, and the word is gone at the next save (`TaskbarApps.cs`).
- **Why "…" stood on a roomy bar.** With "Never", a pinned app with windows open stands as a labelled
  button per window in its own place, and the pin's own range, one cell (`WidgetSize.OneCell`), held
  them all inside that cell: none fit, so all of them went behind "…" whatever room the bar had. The
  open apps were held the same way to their most, 32 cells (1408 DIP), which a wide bar of labelled
  buttons passes long before it is full. "When taskbar is full" hid the same thing by combining.
  Neither holds app buttons now (`Layout.ButtonRoom`): a pin's most never does — its width is its
  icon's —, and the open apps' only where the person narrowed it below the most there is. The fewest
  of either is still kept whole.
- **How they give way, as Windows 11's do.** A labelled button is the whole cells its title asks, up
  to four (176 DIP at 100 %). Where the bar runs short the labelled buttons narrow **alike**: the
  longest are cut to one length, to the whole px, before a shorter one is touched
  (`Layout.EvenCut`), down to two cells (88 DIP). Only once every one of them is that short does the
  last button go behind "…" — still before any widget gives way (`Layout.FitTiles`). "When taskbar
  is full" combines exactly then: a window each for as long as they fit at their least, an app each
  from there (`AppButtons.Lay`). "Always" is unchanged.

- **One setting for every bar** (later the same day). "Combine taskbar buttons and hide labels on
  other taskbars" is gone (§31, General): every bar combines by the one setting, through the same
  `AppButtons.Lay`, so all of the above holds on the main display's bar and on every other.

Tests: `NeverCombineTests` (the pin's window not held to its cell; twenty windows past the open
apps' 32 cells on a 3840 px bar; a narrowed most still holding; Never with 3, 8 and 20 windows on
every bar length beside the weather, Start, search, Task view, two pins, the battery and the clock,
at 100 and 150 %, both looks: no "…" while they fit at their least, one length for every button cut,
"…" only past that; "When taskbar is full" combining at exactly that length; "Always"; the cut
itself), `TaskbarAppsTests` (an old file with the word loads and drops it; nothing is left that
could choose a bar), `SettingsIndexTests.GeneralsCardsStandWhereTheyMoved` (no card, no "All
taskbars" to find). Pictures: `NeverCombinePictures` draws Never with 3, 8 and 20 windows on a wide
bar (`KARPO_PNG_DIR\never-<3|8|20>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`).

## 41. Named layouts, each of a type (2026-10-08)

The person found one configuration — every display its own widgets on twelve places, every edge its
own layout, size, show and look, Start placed per display, a shrunk screen in edit mode — too
complicated, and decided (one configuration, 2026-10-07, and §44 and §45's per-edge settings are gone):

- **Named layouts are back** (`TaskbarLayout`, `Config.Layouts`, TaskbarLayouts.cs): several layouts,
  a default one for new displays (`DefaultLayoutId`), one shown on each display
  (`Screen.ActiveLayoutId`), switched from the bar's own menu (its "Layouts" rows, `Dock.LayoutRows`,
  `ChooseLayout`) and from the **layout switcher** widget (`BarKind.LayoutSwitcher`, `"layout"`), and
  named, iconed, duplicated, deleted and set up on the settings app's **Layouts** page. Two displays
  showing one layout show the same widgets. A widget's list is its layout's: the dock keys it by the
  display it stands on (`display:<id>`, the list of the layout that display shows), the settings app
  by its layout (`layout:<id>`); `Config.LayoutOf` reads either.
- **Each layout has a type** (`LayoutType`, JSON `"type"`), part of the layout, and its widgets live
  in **six fixed slots**: two rows (`BarRow`, JSON `"row"`: `main`, `top`) of three sections each
  (`BarItem.Row`, `BarItem.Section`; a slot is a `BarPlace`). The type only picks which slots are
  **shown** (`LayoutTypes.Places`, `TaskbarLayout.Shows`):
  - **Taskbar**: the main row's start, middle and end, one bar;
  - **Dock**: the main row's start, middle and end, each a floating dock of its own (§71; until
    2026-10-09 the middle only);
  - **Top and bottom**: the main row as the bottom bar and the top row as the top bar. *Gone since §488*, and with
    it the rows: a layout is one bar's three sections.
  - *Gone since §438:* **Dock, two rows** (`"dockRows"`, §130).

  **Nothing moves or goes when the type changes** (`TaskbarLayout.Become` only sets the type): a
  widget in a slot the type does not show stays in the file, unseen (`Dock.Shows` leaves it out of
  every window), and shows again when a type with its slot comes back, so Taskbar to Dock to Taskbar
  restores the layout exactly. Only a widget nobody placed (a new one) is given a shown slot
  (`TaskbarLayout.Home`). `Config.Repair` reads an unknown row as the main row and nothing else.
- **Where a one-bar layout stands is the display's** (`Screen.Edge`, JSON `"edge"` on the display:
  bottom, top, left or right since §145, default bottom; an unknown word reads as the bottom). A
  Taskbar or a Dock stands on its display's edge, a taskbar at the top still shows the main row; Top
  and bottom only asks whether it is a side (`TaskbarLayout.EdgeOf`, `RowAt`, `Edges(screen)`;
  `Config.EdgeOfScreen`, `EdgesOf`). So one layout can stand at the bottom of one display and down
  the left of another.
- **The looks are fixed** (`EdgeLayouts.Style`): a dock floats, a bar wears islands. The style
  setting, the Connected look and its pictures are gone (`BarStyle` is Islands and Floating).
- **How each bar shows** — *Always, reserve space* (`reserve`), *Always, over windows* (`float`) or
  *When the pointer comes near* (`hover`) — is set per bar: a Taskbar's and a Dock's one bar
  (`"show"`), a Top and bottom's bottom (`"show"`) and top (`"topShow"`). **A size per bar**:
  `"size"` for the main bar (the dock, the one taskbar, a Top and bottom's bottom) and `"topSize"`
  for a Top and bottom's top bar, both 28–160 DIPs; dragging a bar's inner edge sizes that bar's
  (`TaskbarLayout.SetSizeOf`). The dock reads a
  display's four edges from its layout (`Config.EdgesOf`, `TaskbarLayout.Edges`) and makes them as
  before: a bar window per bar shown all the time, the reserving ones first, hover places for a bar on
  hover — only the places its type has (`ScreenEdges.Has(edge, section)`: since §71 all three of a
  dock's edge, as of a taskbar's).
- **The Layouts page** (settings app, `LayoutsPage`, SettingsModel.Layouts.cs): a card per layout —
  its name, its icon, its **Type** as
  pictures (`LayoutTypeArt`), its **Size** (a Top and bottom's **Top bar size** and **Bottom bar size**),
  its **Show** (a Top and bottom's **Top bar** and **Bottom bar**), and Duplicate and Delete (the last
  layout can't go; its displays go to the default). The bar's "Taskbar settings" opens it at the card
  of the layout its display shows (`EditClicks.LayoutsArgs`, `--page layouts --owner layout:<id>`).
- **Per display: a layout or None, on the Displays page** (the person, 2026-10-08: "bring back the
  Displays page"; `Pages\DisplaysPage`, a side-menu row after Layouts, searched as every row's page
  is). Laid out as before §42 and as Windows' Display page: the **map** of the displays where Windows
  put them, numbered, a band on each edge where a bar of the layout a display shows stands all the
  time (`Controls\DisplayMap`, `Logic\DisplayMapLayout`), the open card's display in the accent, a
  click on one opening its card alone; then **Connected displays** with Refresh, a card per display
  attached — its name, the "Main display" tag, the line saying which display it is, and in its header
  a dropdown, **Layout on this display**: every layout, then **None**, which hides Karpo there
  (`Screen.Enabled` false); in its body **Position**: the display's edge, bottom or top
  (`DisplayEntry.EdgeIndex`, `SettingsModel.SetDisplayEdge`). At least one display attached shows Karpo: the last one is never offered
  None, and None chosen there anyway is refused (`Config.CanHide`, `Logic\DisplayLayoutChoice`); should
  a file say None for every display attached the dock shows the primary one's layout all the same.
  There is no "Windows taskbar" choice. In the card's body, **Identify this display** (greyed with no
  dock, its line saying why). Last, **New displays show**: the default layout. General has none of it
  any more. "Find a setting" finds a display's card by its dropdown (`SettingsIndex.SwitchOf` reads a
  ComboBox in an expander's header as it reads a switch), as the first display's.
- **A new display** shows the default layout (`Config.AddDisplay`); nothing is copied.
- **Reset** (shape 19, then 20, 21 and 22): a file of shape 17 or 18 was read in place with its layouts
  replaced (`Config.LayoutsReset`, `Config.ResetLayouts`). That in-place read went with shape 20
  (2026-10-09, §70): every older shape, 19 included, is now kept aside as `config.shape<N>.json` and
