  the defaults take its place, as §5 says; shape 21 (§73, the clock a folder) and shape 22 (§9, a
  folder's lists, §74) do the same.
- **Merges** stay three-way and plain JSON (`ConfigMerge`): layouts and displays are lists of objects
  told apart by their ids, so one app's type change and the other's widget edit, a display switched in
  one and a layout sized and renamed in the other, all stay.

Tests: `NamedLayoutsTests` (each type's slots; a type change moving and deleting nothing, every round trip
of types; a display's own edge and a layout on two displays; a size per bar and its clamps; a layout
through the file; each display
its layout, a new display the default; None and at least one display; deleting; three merges),
`ResetTests` (every older shape kept aside, §70), `EdgeModesTests`, `BarStyleTests`, `PlacesTests`, `RepairTests`,
`WindowsPinSyncTests`, `SwitcherTests`, `BarMenuRowsTests`, `DisplayCardTests` (the map's words),
`DisplayLayoutChoiceTests` (a display's dropdown, None refused on the last display that shows Karpo,
the map's bands), `DisplayMapLayoutTests`, `SettingsIndexTests` (the Displays page's cards, "display"
landing on the page, General without them).

## 42. Edit mode: its own buttons, an edge's page, several widgets at once (2026-10-07)

The person: the settings app's "Edit" switch goes; edit mode gets "Open settings" and "Close edit
mode" beside "Add a widget"; the Displays page goes, each edge's settings on a page of its own; and
widgets are selected, dragged, removed, copied and pasted several at once.

- **The buttons.** "Add a widget", "Open settings" and "Close edit mode" stand in one row, every
  display's edit bar (`EditDeckPlan.For`, `EditDeck`; since round 6 a compact command bar in the
  display's top right corner, §43). "Open settings" brings the settings app up, over
  everything as it stays while edit mode is on; "Close edit mode" ends it as Escape does. The side
  menu's "Edit" switch is gone, and with it the settings app's way to end edit mode
  (`MainWindow.Edit.cs` keeps only the window on top; the dock still answers "karpo.editing" 0 for
  an older app, Dock.EditSettings.cs).
- **An edge's page** (gone since §44: an edge is set by its strip in edit mode). The Displays page is gone, its map, its search words, its side-menu row and
  icon, and its strings in five languages. Each edge's mode, style and size are its own page
  (`Pages\EdgePage`), as a widget has one: not in the side menu, its title the display and the
  edge ("LU28R55 › Bottom edge"), the line under it which display that is ("Bottom edge of LU28R55 ·
  Display 1 · 3840 × 2160 · 150%"). It opens from edit mode: **a label per edge in the frame** — a
  pill with a gear and the edge's name, each in the middle of its edge (round 6), just outside its
  places, the sides' turned to run along their side (`EditFrame.LabelArea`, `ShadeLabels`; the frame
  keeps them room, `EditFrame.LabelDip`) —
  and a click on a bar's or a place's empty room opens its edge's page too. The bar's "Taskbar
  settings" opens the page of its own edge (`--owner display:<id> --edge <bottom|top|left|right>`,
  `EditClicks.EdgeArgs`, `StartRequest.Edge`). A display not attached has no page: General instead.
- **What else the Displays page held.** Karpo on or off per display, and Identify, are General's
  now: a **Displays** expander, a row per display attached — its name, the "Main display" tag, the
  line that says which display it is, Identify (greyed with no dock, its tip saying why) and its
  switch. It carries the edges' search words, so "auto hide" or "taskbar height" finds it, and says
  where those settings are. A display Karpo is off on has no frame in edit mode, so its switch has to
  be outside it. The edge page is never searched (an item's page, as a widget's is).
- **Selecting several** (`EditSelection`, Dock.EditSelect.cs). A click selects a widget alone, as
  before, and opens its page. Ctrl+click adds one or takes it out; Shift+click selects the run from
  the one last clicked in its display's order; neither opens a page. A drag on the frame's empty room
  draws Windows' selection rectangle (`EditBand`, a window of its own over everything) and selects
  every widget of that display it runs over as it goes, what was selected kept with Ctrl or Shift; a
  click there clears the selection and leaves edit mode on. Every selected widget wears the selected ring
  (`EditView.AlsoSelected`). A right click on a widget not selected selects it alone; on one of
  several, they stay selected and its menu acts on them all.
- **Dragging several.** A press on one of several selected widgets of a display and a drag carry all
  of that display's selected widgets (`Dock.GroupFor`). Each is drawn at the pointer in the carry
  window, side by side in their order, the one taken hold of under the pointer (`EditCarryPlan`);
  every surface they came from closes up behind them (`Layout.Without`, `Layout.Remaining`); the
  surface nearest the pointer opens the room for all of them and shows one blue landing round them
  all (`Layout.Landing` with a group, `Dock.GroupOffer`). Let go, they land there side by side in
  their order (`IslandEdits.MoveGroup`, `DockWindow.ListSlotGroup`). Escape or a right press puts
  them back. They do not go into an open folder or make one.
- **Removing several.** Delete removes every selected widget where the one with the keys' focus is
  one of them (or none has it), else the focused one; a selected widget's "Remove" removes them all
  (`Dock.RemoveSelected`).
  - *A folder's lines too* (2026-10-09, the person: "i cannot remove widgets from the list view").
    A line clicked in an arranged folder is selected, and what is selected was read through the
    displays' orders alone, which hold the bars' widgets and no folder's line: its "Remove" and
    Delete came to nothing. The selection is now every selected widget, the displays' in their
    order and then the lines in the order they were selected (`EditSelection.All`,
    `EditSelection.ActedOn`). And Delete reaches the dock from an arranged folder, which has the
    keys: the folder says `FolderFlyoutAction.Remove`, with the line the keys are on or none (what
    is selected), and stays open. At rest Delete removes nothing. The settings app has no way to
    remove a widget (the bar arranges), and a line dragged out over nothing was always a cancel.
    `FolderLineRemoveTests` (every kind of line, the toggles, actions, month, time header and screen
    time among them: "Remove" clicked first or not, Delete selected or focused, the open folder
    losing the line). A line removed alone in its list takes the list with it, as one dragged out
    does (`Folders.Remove` goes through `Folders.Take`, §9): only a folder's one list stays empty.
- **Copy and paste.** Ctrl+C, or "Copy" in a widget's menu, copies the selected widgets — or the one
  whose menu it is, where it is not selected — into Karpo's own clipboard, never Windows'. Ctrl+V,
  or "Paste" (greyed while nothing was copied, `Dock.CopyPasteRows`), puts copies of them into the
  display under the pointer, at its place nearest the pointer, each a deep copy with a new id
  (`IslandEdits.Paste`), and lets them follow the pointer drawn as they are, as a widget from "Add a
  widget" does (`EditFollowHook`): a left click puts them down where the landing shows, Escape or a
  right click takes them out again. The copies are the selection then.

Tests: `EditSelectTests` (the selection's rules, landing together, pasting with new ids, the group's
landing and the bars closing up, the carry window's row, the menu's rows), `EditFrameTests` (the row
of three buttons, every edge's label in the frame), `DisplayCardTests` (an edge page's words, its
arguments), `SettingsIndexTests` (General's Displays card, no Displays or edge page searched), and
the tests of the settings app's arguments. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): every `edit-places-*` and
`edit-displays-*` sheet shows the buttons and the labels; `edit-select-<dark|light>-<150|100>.png`
three widgets of two places selected, the selection rectangle over the top's;
`edit-select-group-dark-<150|100>.png` the three carried together into the top's start place. A
carry window drawn from a light surface comes back black on the hidden desktop, one widget carried
as well as several, so the group's pictures are dark only.

## 43. Edit mode, round 6: no "Parked" tray, a compact edit bar, Escape anywhere (2026-10-07)

The person's round 6 on edit mode:

- **"Parked" is gone**: the tray, the model's flag (`BarItem.Parked`, `BarPlace.Parked`,
  `Sections.ParkedIn`), dragging onto it and out of it, the settings app's "Parked, not shown", and
  its strings in five languages. A file that still has a widget `"parked": true` loads: the word is
  read once (`BarItem.OldParked`, never written again) and `Config.Unpark`, part of `Repair`, puts
  the widget at the end of the end section of its display's first edge shown all the time
  (`ScreenEdges.Standing`, in bottom, top, left, right order), or of its bottom edge where none is;
  its options go with it, and the file is written back without the word. It stays on the display
  whose list it is in: a widget never moves from one display's list to another's, and on the
  primary display that is the edge the person named.
- **The edit bar** ("Add a widget", "Open settings", "Close edit mode") stands in every display's
  **top right corner**, 8 DIPs from its top and its right side, as a compact Windows 11 command bar
  (`EditDeck`, `EditDeckPlan`): 40 DIPs tall, its buttons 32 inside a 4 DIP padding with 4 between
  them, each a 16 DIP glyph and its words at 14 DIPs, 12 DIPs inside either side, on the flyouts'
  background (acrylic, 8 DIP corners, their shadow); the buttons have no fill at rest and the subtle
  fills under the pointer and pressed, "Add a widget"'s "+" in the accent. The frame keeps its row
  clear over the top's places (`EditDeckPlan.TallDip`, `EditFrame.For`).
- **Each edge's label** sits in the middle of its edge in the frame, just outside its places — or
  the small screen where that edge's bar stands in it (`EditFrame.LabelArea`).
- **The settings app does not open with edit mode** (`Dock.EditingChanged`); opened, it stays on top
  while edit mode is on, as before.
- **Escape leaves edit mode wherever the keys are**. The bar heard it only while it held the keys,
  and the frame and the edit bars take no activation, so the keys were often with the settings app
  or with nothing. All edit mode long a low-level keyboard hook is in (`EditFollowHook.Edit`, on the
  desktop with the person's input only), and Escape is taken from whatever has the keys and posted
  to the dock (`FollowInput.Leave`, `Dock.EscapeHeard`): a block being dragged goes back, else edit
  mode ends. While a widget follows the pointer (added or pasted) Escape calls it off first, and its
  repeats held down mean nothing more; the next Escape leaves edit mode (`FollowGesture.Key`). A popup
  of the dock's own with the keys — a menu, the add list, an open folder — keeps its Escape and
  closes on it first (`Dock.EscapeIsTheirs`).

Tests: `PlacesTests` (a parked widget back at the end of the first edge shown all the time, or the
bottom, on its own display, through a merge; no "parked" ever written), `EditFrameTests` (the
compact command bar, a button's width, the labels in the middle of their edges, the top's label and
the edit bar apart), `EdgeModesTests`, `EditStaysOnTests` (the tray gone; Escape leaves, a following
widget first, a popup keeps its own), `EditFollowHookTests` (Escape in edit mode posted as its end),
`EveryDisplayKeepsItsEditBarInFrontOfItsFrame` (two 4K displays at 150 %, the edit bar in each top
right corner, in front of its frame). Pictures: `edit-displays-4k-<dark|light>-150.png`,
`edit-displays-follow-drag-dark-150.png` and every `edit-places-*`, `edit-select-*` and
`edit-motion-*` sheet.

## 45. A section grows into the free room (2026-10-08)

*Start's place per display, set on the bottom edge's strip in edit mode, was here until the same day:
it is gone (§26), with the strips (§44).*

The person: "the sections dont properly expand when there is enougth space for it. my center bottom
dock bar for example shrinks its apps even though there is enough space on the left and right
side"; and Windows' Start's place a setting of each display, set inline in edit mode.

- **A bar shown all the time** never held a section to a third: its sections lay out along the
  whole bar (§13, `Layout.SectionStarts`), the middle centred while it fits, then moved as little as
  keeps it off the others, and app buttons fold only once the whole bar is full. That holds in every
  layout on every edge (`SectionGrowthTests.ABarShownAllTheTimeGrowsItsMiddleIntoTheFreeRoom`).
- **An edge on hover** was the cap: each of its three places was a window in its third of the edge
  (`HoverPlaces.Third`), so a middle dock of many apps folded them into "…" beside two empty thirds.
  The places now **share the edge as a bar's sections share the bar** (`HoverPlaces.Share`):
  - each place's window measures what it wants: its bar's length with every part at its own size,
    labelled buttons whole and none behind "…", in edit mode an empty place's room, a dock's ends
    (`Layout.Natural`; of a window each and an app each the longer), and the gap two places keep
    (`Layout.PlaceGap`: the sections' gap, none for a dock, whose places keep their ends) —
    `DockWindow.Wants`, at the DPI it was laid out at;
  - where the three fit, the start's stretch runs from the edge's start and the end's to its end,
    and the middle's content is centred on the edge, exactly while that keeps it a gap clear of the
    other two, else moved as little as does; the room nobody wants is shared too, the middle a third
    of it evenly either side (so it stays about its centre) and the start and the end the rest, so
    every place has room for what is dropped on it in edit mode;
  - only where the three want more than the edge does anything give: the room less the gaps is
    shared out, a place wanting less than an even share keeps all it wants, and the others share the
    rest evenly (`HoverPlaces.Even`), so the longest are cut first and only they fold apps or give
    widgets up;
  - the stretches meet and cover the edge, so a band runs the whole edge (§41); an empty place a
    neighbour takes all of has no window;
  - until every place of an edge has been measured, the thirds. A place whose want changes has its
    edge shared again and every place whose stretch or strip moved laid out again (`Dock.Reshare`),
    once all bars are built where a rebuild is under way; the strips follow their stretches.
- **Edit mode** edits the bars where they stand (§44): an edge's places share it there as at rest.

Tests: `SectionGrowthTests` (the share: a middle with empty neighbours using the free room, growing
evenly, moving as little as it must, the start and the end growing towards the middle, every place
some of the free room, nothing cut until the edge is full and then the longest first, thirds until
measured; the places and their strips; a middle place of many apps folding only when the whole edge
is full, the places beside keeping theirs and a bar shown all the time, each a dock's and a bar's on
all four edges; `Layout.Natural`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`section-growth-<dock|taskbar>-<before|after>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (a bottom edge on hover,
revealed: a dock of Start and 24 apps with empty sides, and a taskbar of 16 between the weather and
the clock; before in thirds with the apps in "…", after all of them, centred).

## 46. Project, Cast and Mobile hotspot get flyouts of their own (2026-10-08)

*"Give these taskbar widgets their own Karpo flyouts, in the Quick Settings flyout style the others
use."* On the bar a click on each opens a quick-settings page (`QuickKind.Project`, `Cast`,
`Hotspot`; `IslandView` of the same names; `SwitchIsland.Page`), the entry says `Flyout`, and, by
the house rule, none has a tooltip any more. In a folder nothing changes: second screen and cast are
still in none (§15), and the hotspot's card and line still switch it.

- **Project** (`ProjectPage`, `Services\Projection.cs`): Win+P's four modes as rows — PC screen only,
  Duplicate, Extend, Second screen only — the one in force marked as a list's chosen row. What is in
  force is the topology `QueryDisplayConfig(QDC_DATABASE_CURRENT)` reports; choosing one is
  `SetDisplayConfig` with `SDC_APPLY` and that `SDC_TOPOLOGY_*` flag alone, as Win+P asks, on the
  pool. The row chosen is marked at once and the panel stays up as Win+P's does; when the screens
  change the flyout goes by itself (a display change ends every Menu popup), and where Windows
  refuses, the page says so under the list. With one screen attached the four are still offered, with
  a line saying the others need a second. Footer: "More display settings".
- **Cast** (`CastPage`, `Services\Cast.cs`): the wireless displays in range, found with a
  `DeviceWatcher` on the Miracast half of `ProjectionManager.GetDeviceSelector()` (Wi-Fi Direct
  endpoints offering Miracast; the selector's other half is every wired monitor). The display cast to
  now comes first, "Connected": an active display path whose output technology is Miracast, named by
  its target. **Connecting and disconnecting are not possible unpackaged**: the one published call,
  `ProjectionManager.StartProjectingAsync`, takes application view ids only a packaged app's views
  have, `Windows.Media.Casting` casts a media stream rather than the screen, and disconnecting has no
  public call. So a display's row, and "Open Cast" at the right of the footer, close the flyout and
  open Windows' own cast panel (Win+K), where it is connected or disconnected; a line under the list
  says so. "Find other devices" opens Windows' "Add a device" dialog.
- **Mobile hotspot** (`HotspotPage`, `Services\Hotspot.cs`): the switch in the title row, then what
  Windows' hotspot page lists under Properties — the network name, the password (dots until the eye
  shows it, a Copy button beside it whose tick lasts a moment), the band ("Any available", 2.4, 5 or
  6 GHz, where Windows says one), "2 of 8" devices — then the devices on it, by the name each gave or
  its address. All of it is `NetworkOperatorTetheringManager`'s, the class the hotspot switch already
  used from the AOT dock (checked unpackaged again: capability, state, name, password, band, the
  bands the adapter takes, the client count and list all answer). Where the PC can't host one there
  is no switch and the page says why, a reason each: no connection to share, an adapter that can't,
  an administrator's policy, the connection or edition not allowing it, or Windows not saying. While
  the page is open it asks who is on it every five seconds; closed, nothing. The password is copied
  through the source, with the panel's window as the clipboard's owner. Footer: "Mobile hotspot
  settings".

Every real action is behind its source (`IProjectSource`, `ICastSource`, `IHotspotSource`), and a set
of sources defaults to the samples (`SampleProjection`, `SampleCast`, `SampleHotspot`), which record
what they were asked and change no screen, press no key, share nothing and copy nothing; only
`QuickSources.Windows` holds Windows' own. Strings `dock.quick.project.*`, `dock.quick.cast.*` and
`dock.quick.hotspot.*` in five languages; no English literal in code.

Tests: `DisplayFlyoutsTests` (the modes, their topology ids and flags, the screens counted; the cast
rows merged, the query; the hotspot's reasons, bands, hidden password, count and device names; the
entries, the pages each button asks for, the sources' defaults), `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests`
(`ChoosingAProjectModeAppliesItAndMarksIt`, `ACastRowOpensWindowsCastPanel`,
`TheHotspotPageShowsCopiesAndSwitches`, `TheThreeButtonsOpenTheirOwnPages`), and the updated
`FolderClickRuleTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`,
`DisplayPagePictures`): `quick-<project|project-one-screen|cast|cast-looking|cast-none|hotspot|hotspot-shown|hotspot-off|hotspot-cant>-<dark-150|light-150|dark-100>.png`.

## 47. A flyout keeps the room for its rows; now playing's words at the left (2026-10-08)

*"To reduce layout shift"*: each flyout that lists rows "reserves room for 5 rows even when it shows
fewer, so its height doesn't jump", configurable per widget with a min and a max; past the max, the
list scrolls. And now playing's text left-aligned, the cover right-aligned.

*The min and the max below are gone: one exact row count replaced them (§52), and a height replaced that (§53).*

- **Which flyouts**: the network's (its cables and networks are one list), Bluetooth's (the paired
  devices), VPN's (its connections; the line and "VPN settings" follow the room rather than standing
  in it) and the calendar's (the month's list of the day's events). `WidgetInfo.FlyoutRows` names
  them; a clock's calendar keeps the defaults.
- **The rule** (`FlyoutRows.Room`, `Hidden`): the flyout is as tall from no row up to the min, a
  row taller for each past it up to the max, and no taller after that. What stands in the room
  where there are fewer rows — a notice (Wi-Fi off, no networks, Bluetooth off), "No events", an
  opened network's card — takes it rather than adding to it, so turning a radio off or opening a
  short list's network does not move the flyout. Past the max the list scrolls, the next row's
  top showing at its foot. Each takes the room the way its list is laid out:
  `PageLayout.List` for the quick pages, `Flyout.Rows` (`FlyoutList`, its `Tail` the last line and
  what follows it, `SwitchIsland.Kept`) for VPN's list, `CalendarInputs.Rows` for the agenda — where
  the most a flyout may be has no room for the min under the month, the agenda keeps the whole rows
  it has, which a busy day shows before it scrolls, so a quiet day is as tall and scrolls nothing.
- **The setting** (`FlyoutRowsOptions`, the entry's `flyoutRows`: `{ "min": 5, "max": 8 }`): min 0
  to 20 (0 is as tall as what it shows), max 1 to 20, the fewest winning where they disagree, as a
  widget's size does. The defaults are no options at all, so a widget nobody set writes nothing.
  A setting of its own beside the options record; it goes with the widget into a folder and back
  (`Partners.Convert`) and merges as any property (`ConfigMerge`). On the widget's page, for an
  entry on the bar only (a folder opens no flyout): "Rows in its flyout", an expander whose header
  says "5 to 8 rows", with two number fields; one end pushes the other where they would cross
  (`Logic\FlyoutRowsRow.cs`). The network's and Bluetooth's pages are no longer "nothing else"
  (`WidgetSettings.NothingElse`). Strings `settings.widget.flyoutRows.*` in five languages.
- **Now playing**: in the media flyout the track and the artist start at the left, where the
  source line over them does, and the art is at the right (`MediaPage`); in a grid card wherever
  the words stand beside the cover (§16, `MediaIsland.ArrangeGrid`). The list's line is unchanged.

Tests: `FlyoutRowsOptionsTests` (the rule, the file, nobody set writes nothing, the ranges, the
kinds, a folder and back, the merge), `FlyoutRowsRowTests` (the card's widgets, the fields, one end
moving the other). Measured from none to eleven rows, with the defaults and with 3 to 6:
`QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheListsKeepTheRoomForTheirRows` and
`AnOpenedNetworkTakesTheKeptRoomAndALongListScrolls`, `VpnRowsPictures`,
`CalendarViewsOffscreenTests.TheDaysEventsKeepTheRoomForTheirRows`; the words at the left:
`TheMediaFlyoutsWordsAreLeftOfTheArt`, `MediaSizeTests.BesideTheCoverTheWordsAreAtTheLeft`. Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `quick-network-rows-<1|7|11|1-open>-150-dark.png`,
`quick-bluetooth-rows-<1|7>-150-dark.png`, `vpn-rows-<1|7>-150-dark.png`,
`calendar-rows-<1|7>-150-dark.png`, `quick-media-text-left-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`,
`media-cards-text-left-150-dark.png`.

## 48. Tray icons the bar's size, a drag out of the overflow that lands, the status icons' card (2026-10-08)

The person: *"tray icons show in the same size as all the other icons on the bar again"*, *"dragging
tray icons between the bar and the overflow still doesn't work"*, *"the overflow is bigger than the
icons it holds"*, *"remove the Windows Update widget"* and *"all the status icons should show with
primary background"*.

- **The size** (`Layout.TrayIconPx`): an app icon's again, 24 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, the pins' and
  every other icon's on the bar; the cell the bar's square (`TrayCell` = `CellSide`), square both ways
  as §38 asked. §33's 16 DIP in 32-DIP cells, its 40-DIP overflow squares and `Fit.StepUnder` are gone;
  `Tray.Render` still takes an icon from its app's group at the bar's size.
- **The drag, found**: a drop over a bar was read across the bar from the top of the bar's window
  and taken up to the bar's thickness (`Dock.TrayTargetAt`). The window is deeper than the bar by the
  room it keeps for tooltips (`Layout.DepthFor`), which a bottom bar keeps above it, so the bar itself
  lay past the bar's thickness from the window's top: no point on a bottom (or right) bar's tray was
  a drop. An icon dragged out of the overflow onto the bar went back, an icon moved along the bar went
  back, and the chevron never opened the overflow mid-drag; only the empty room above the bar took a
  drop. §34's fixes were right and never reached. Now the point is read against the bar's own strip
  (`Layout.AlongOnBar`: the strip and the room to the screen's edge, as the hit test reads it, per
  window, so two bars on one display each take their own), and the drop worked out by
  `TrayDrags.OnLayout`, which the dock and the tests share.
- **The overflow fits its icons** (`Flyout.FitsItsIcons`, `Flyout.FittedSize`): its icons in the bar's
  own squares (`Layout.TrayOverflowCell` = `TrayCell`), five to a row, and 4 DIP around them
  (`FittedPadDip`), the panel no larger. As any grid it was at least 120 DIP wide with 8 DIP around,
  twice one icon's square and more.
- **The Windows Update widget is gone** (§21.2): from the bar's, the grid's and the list's registries,
  `Partners`, `WidgetInfos` and so the add list, the menus table (`WidgetAct.WindowsUpdate`,
  `RestartOptions`), its data source and its strings. The status icons keep their update icon, its
  menu and its words; its name, where Windows' own icon gives none, is `dock.quick.indicator.windowsUpdate`.
  A file holding one loads without it.
- **The status icons' background**: drawn against the other widgets in each look they already stood on
  the same fill, at rest and under the pointer (pixel for pixel in `tray-bar-*.png`); what set them
  apart was the islands look's card per icon a gap from the next, where every other widget wears one
  card. They wear one card now (`Scene.WearsCard`), their icons side by side on it, each still lit on
  its own square (`Scene.LightsItsOwnCell`); `Layout.CellsApart` is gone. "Primary" could also mean
  the accent colour; that reading was not built.

Tests: `TrayCellsTests` (the square, the pins' size at every height, DPI, edge and look, the overflow's
squares), `TrayDropOnBarTests` (the window deeper than the bar; every tray icon's middle a drop on every
edge in every look, from the bar and from the overflow, the chevron hiding; the tooltips' room and
off the bar none; two bars on one display), `FlyoutOffscreenTests.AnIconIsDraggedOutOfTheOverflowOntoABottomBarAndBack`
(the overflow on a hidden desktop, pressed, moved and let go with its window's own messages onto a
bottom bar's tray, the drop written, then back onto the chevron and into the overflow) and
`TheOverflowFitsItsIcons` (1, 2, 5 and 7 icons at 100 and 150 %), `StatusIconColourTests` and
`IslandCardsTests` (one card), `WindowsUpdateRemovedTests` (no registry or library has it; a bar's, a
grid's and a list's load without it). Pictures (`TraySizeSheets`, `KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`tray-bar-<islands|floating>[-hover-<status|wifi>]-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (the bar's
end with four tray icons and three status icons) and `tray-overflow[-one]-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.

## 49. The status icons' three places (2026-10-08)

The person: *"for the status icons you should be able to set which status icons are visible and which
should be hidden / hidden behind an extend arrow, (basically the same style as it is done with the tray
icons.) as default all should show"*.

- **Three places per icon**, the tray's (`TrayState`, §34), per Status icons entry
  (`BarItem.StatusIcons`, `Karpo.Core\StatusIcons.cs`): *Show on taskbar*, every icon's where nobody
  chose; *Show behind the arrow*; *Hide completely*. The icons are the entry's ten (`StatusIcon`): the
  microphone, the camera, the location and presence sensing in use, airplane mode, the mobile hotspot,
  a metered connection, energy saver, do not disturb and Windows Update. The microphone and the
  location in use together are Windows' one icon only where both stand in one place; set apart, each
  shows alone in its own (`Indicators.Split`). Windows Update hidden takes Windows' own update icon
  with it: the tray still leaves that one to the status icons.
- **The arrow** (`IndicatorsIsland.Chevron`): a cell after the icons on the bar, the tray's chevron
  (E70E) at three quarters of the icons' size, on the status icons' one card, standing only while an
  icon behind it is so. No tooltip: its click opens Karpo's own flyout. The flyout
  (`IslandAction.Icons`) is shown as the tray's overflow is (§48): the icons' glyphs at their size on
  the bar in the bar's squares, five to a row, the panel no larger. A click on one opens its page and
  closes the flyout; a right click opens its own rows and the widget's "Settings"
  (`IWidgetMenu.MenuCellOf`), as on the bar. The arrow's own right click is the widget's menu.
- **The file**: `"statusIcons": { "states": { "camera": "Overflow", "doNotDisturb": "Hidden" } }`,
  only what is not the bar written (`StatusIconOptions.Normalized`), so an entry nobody set, and every
  file from before this, writes nothing and shows every icon. A key this build does not know stays;
  the map merges key by key (`ConfigMerge`), as the tray's states do.
- **Settings**: the entry's page has one open block, *Status icons*, a row per icon with its glyph,
  its name and the three-way choice, as the tray page's (`WidgetsPage.xaml`,
  `Logic\StatusIconChoices.cs`).
- **Not built**: dragging a status icon between the bar and its arrow's flyout. The tray's drag is the
  scene's own (`Dock.Tray.cs`, `TrayDrags`, the flyout's drag events), not an island's; the place is
  set in Settings.

Tests: `StatusIconStatesTests` (every icon on the bar unless chosen; each icon behind the arrow is
there and not on the bar; hidden never shows; the microphone and the location; the settings' glyphs
the bar's; the map kept, read tolerantly, round-tripped, absent in an old file, dropped from other
kinds, merged), `StatusIconArrowTests` (the arrow only while something is behind it; a hidden icon
takes no cell; the flyout's icons open their pages and their right clicks their rows; new options
move the icons), `StatusIconChoicesTests` (the rows and the page's markup). Pictures
(`StatusIconArrowSheets`, `KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `status-arrow-bar[-hover]-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`
and `status-arrow-flyout-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`. The Settings page by hand:
`--new-window --island <id> --owner layout:<id> --test size 1100 1100 --test expand --shot status-icons`
with `KARPO_SETTINGS_SHOTS` and `KARPO_SETTINGS_THEME=dark`, at 150 %.

## 50. The edit bar by the bar, with its own folder and separator buttons (2026-10-08)

The person: "Grid folder", "List folder" and "Separator" each get their own button next to "Add a
widget", and starting one follows the mouse as adding a widget does; the highlighted row of them at
the top of the add list goes again; and the edit bar sits closer to the bar area, near the layout's
first bar, never over widgets or hover bars.

- **The buttons** (`EditDeckPlan.For`, `EditDeck`): "Add a widget", "Grid folder", "List folder",
  "Separator", a command bar's separator (a hairline 20 DIPs tall, `DividerStrokeColorDefault`),
  "Open settings", "Close edit mode". The three new ones carry their kind's own name and glyph
  (`BarKind.Title`, `BarKind.Glyph`), so they read as the settings app and the bar name them, in
  every language. A click on one (`EditDeckPlan.ActionAt`, `EditDeckAction.Place`) puts one of its
  kind in at the place of the display nearest the pointer (`EditDeckPlan.FollowSpot`,
  `AddList.AddQuick`) and it follows the pointer as a widget from the add list does (§7): a left
  click puts it down, Escape or a right click takes it out. A folder or a separator has no settings
  page to open.
- **The add list has no band** any more (`FlyoutItem.Quick`, `AddList.QuickRows` and
  `CMD_ADD_QUICK` are gone): its search field, then the widgets, then the ready-made groups.
- **Where the edit bar stands** (`EditDeckPlan.Place`, `Dock.DeckRoom`; the person, 2026-10-09: "move
  the edit bar to the top center, independent of the layout"), the rules:
  - always **centred at the top** of the display, whatever the layout;
  - **8 DIPs under** the deepest of what stands along the top in edit mode — a bar shown all the
    time there, or every place of a top bar on hover brought in —, each by what it takes (its panel
    and the room off its edge, `DockWindow.DropArea`); 8 DIPs under the display's top with nothing
    there. So it never covers an area a widget can be put in;
  - inside the display, 8 DIPs from its sides; it hangs as a flyout does, its window starting at
    what stands above it; the sections' edit bars keep clear of it as before;
  - "Open settings" and "Close edit mode" are icon-only, square, their words a tooltip under them
    (`EditDeckPlan.IsIcon`). They have no accessible name of their own yet: the edit bar has no UIA
    source;
  - the add list opens **under** "Add a widget" (`EditDeckPlan.ListEdge`, `EditDeck.AddAnchor`),
    away from the top: it once opened upwards, over the edit bar and a bar along the top;
  - **popups of a bar along the top** — its menus, its widgets' flyouts, a folder — open right where
    the edit bar stands: one that would stand over it opens under it instead, its gap kept
    (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`, `FlyoutHost.ClearOf`, set from `Dock.ShowDecks`); one beside it stays by
    its bar.

the edit bar centred at the top, under what stands there by 8 DIPs, inside the display, over no
