## 51. Tray icons that touch, sharp pictures, and WhatsApp's icon that came and went (2026-10-08)

The person: *"tray icons sit connected, with no gap between them"*, *"tray icons are drawn at very low
resolution"* and *"the whatsapp tray icon sometimes disappears and appears again"*.

- **Touching** (`Layout.TrayStep` = `TrayCell`): the chevron's square and every icon's stand side by
  side with no gap, in every look, as Windows 11's tray icons do; the widgets either side keep their
  gap to the tray. The squares stay the bar's (§38, §48), so an icon is still a pin's size in a square
  of the bar's thickness: what went is the widgets' gap between them. In the islands look the tray
  wears the one card every widget wears (`Scene.WearsCard`), its icons on it, each lit on its own
  square under the pointer as a status icon is; a card per icon with no gap between read as tiles
  seamed together. A tray of a set size holds whole squares of its room (`Layout.TraySpills`). With
  no gap, half a step is an icon's middle: a drop exactly there lands where that icon stands, before
  it (`TrayDrags.IndexAt`).
- **Sharp pictures** (`Tray.Capture`): most apps hand the tray their small icon for the display's DPI
  (16 DIP: 24 px at 150 %), which the bar draws at an app icon's 24 DIP (36 px). DrawIconEx made it
  36 px by copying pixels: blocky. Now, in order: an icon made at the bar's size is taken as it is;
  one loaded from its app's icon group is taken from the group at the bar's size (as before); one made
  in memory, which has one picture only, is taken at its own size and filtered to the bar's with a
  cubic filter (`TrayPictures.Resize`, Catmull-Rom, widened when it shrinks). And where that picture
  is the app's executable's own icon (`TrayPictures.Alike` with the executable's icon at the same
  size), the executable's icon at the bar's size is drawn instead (`Tray.ExeIcons`, through the shell's
  `IShellItemImageFactory`, `Items.Icon`), looked up once per executable and size, on the dock's
  thread, never while an app waits on the tray. A picture of the app's own (a badge, another state)
  is never swapped; it stays filtered. What can't be had: an app that hands over 16 px and has no
  bigger picture anywhere can only be filtered up, which is smooth, not sharp. A change of the bars'
  icon size (a display, its DPI, a bar's height) now asks every app for its icon again half a second
  later (`Tray.Resize`), so the pictures already there are taken at the new size too.
- **WhatsApp's icon**: WhatsApp's packaged app draws its icon with H.NotifyIcon, which answers every
  TaskbarCreated by deleting its icon twice, adding it hidden (NIS_HIDDEN), setting its version and
  showing it (`TaskbarIcon.OnTaskbarCreated`, `TrayIcon.Create`). Karpo announces TaskbarCreated at
  its start, after an icon size change and whenever Explorer's taskbar came in front of Karpo's tray
  (`Tray.EnsureFirst`), and the dock read the icons between those calls: the icon went and came back.
  WhatsApp's behaviour, brought about by Karpo's asking. An icon taken away (NIM_DELETE), hidden by
  its app or left by a window that went now stays where it stands for 1.5 s (`TrayPictures.GraceMs`)
  before it goes; an add within that brings it back in its place, as the same icon. A change to an
  icon taken away is refused, as one to an icon never added is, so its app adds it again. One its app
  added again from a new window (no GUID) goes at once: its successor stands for it. The spy's own
  timer wakes the dock when a grace ends. There is no tray log to read: `appbar.log` holds the bars'
  strips only.

Tests: `TrayCellsTests` (the cells touch in every look, height, DPI and edge; the block is its cells;
a tray of a set size holds whole squares), `TrayDragsTests` (a drop on an icon's middle), `TrayPicturesTests` (the filter: sizes, one colour kept,
an edge filtered and not copied, no colour above its alpha, every pixel counted when shrinking;
`Alike`; the executable's icon taken at the bar's size for 96, 120, 144 and 192 DPI, never over a
badge, once per executable and size), `TrayRenderTests` (the group's image at the bar's size per DPI;
an icon made in memory filtered up and down), `TrayGraceTests` (H.NotifyIcon's whole TaskbarCreated
answer read after every call, the icon there throughout; a delete kept for the grace and gone at its
end; a change to a deleted icon refused; hidden and shown; added hidden never shows; a window that
went; a new window's icon taking the old one's place at once; on a clock of the tests' own),
`IslandCardsTests`. Pictures (`TraySizeSheets`, `TrayDragSheets`, `TrayPictures`, `KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`tray-bar-<islands|floating>[-hover-tray]-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`,
`tray-bar-small-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (the icons handed over at 16 DIP),
`tray-drag-<rest|chevron|along>-*.png`, `tray-cells-*.png`.

## 52. One exact row count; "Open Calendar" only with a calendar app; the pin's own icon (2026-10-08)

*The row count below is gone: a flyout height, a preset or one's own in DIP, replaced it (§53).*

*The person*: the network's, Bluetooth's, VPN's and the calendar's lists get "one exact row count
(default 5)", always exactly that tall and scrolling at once past it, never growing; "Open calendar"
is not shown "when there's no calendar app that can be opened"; and a pin's "What it opens" header
"shows the pin's own icon (the target's icon, as the bar shows it) instead of the generic glyph".

- **The rows** (`FlyoutRowsOptions`, `FlyoutRows(Count)`): §47's min and max are one count, 1 to 20,
  five where nobody set it. Each list is exactly that many rows tall, whatever it lists: fewer rows,
  a notice, "No events" or an opened network's card stand in that room, and whatever is past it —
  more rows, or a card that runs past it — is a scroll away at once, the next row's top showing at
  the foot. `PageLayout.List(top, pitch, rows)` for the quick pages (what is past the room becomes
  the scroll), `Flyout.Rows` for VPN's list (the room, then the line and "VPN settings"; past the
  room the panel is the room and what follows it), `CalendarInputs.Rows` for the agenda (its window
  the rows and 8 DIP; where the most a flyout may be has no room for them, the whole rows it has,
  as before). The file: the entry's `flyoutRows` is a number (`"flyoutRows": 7`), written only where
  set; a file from §47 (`{ "min": 3, "max": 12 }`) reads as its min (`FlyoutRowsConverter`), held to
  1 to 20, so an old `{ "min": 5, ... }` is no setting at all and an old min of 0 is one row. On the
  widget's page: one card, "Rows in its flyout", its number field 1 to 20 (`Logic\FlyoutRowsRow.cs`);
  the strings `settings.widget.flyoutRows.summary`, `.min.*` and `.max.*` went.
- **Open Calendar** (`CalendarApp`): the calendar widget's footer offers it only where Windows has an
  app for `outlookcal:`, or else `ms-calendar:` — asked as Explorer asks (`AssocQueryString`,
  `ASSOCF_IS_PROTOCOL`, the "open" verb: a desktop app's command, a packaged app's id, or a
  `DelegateExecute` handler). A key with none of them (what the new Outlook leaves behind for
  `outlookcal:`) opens nothing, and the footer is then the date and time settings alone
  (`CalendarInputs.App`). The dock asks on each showing and again on the click, and opens the link it
  found. The widget's right-click "Open calendar" is unchanged.
- **The pin's header** (`Logic\PinHeaderIcon.cs`, `PinPage.ShowOpensIcon`): in the bar's order
  (`Item.Icon`) — the glyph the pin was given; the file it took its picture from, the target's icon
  behind it; the target's own, as the shell draws it (`Shell.Describe`). A site wears the globe (its
  favicon is the dock's, which the settings app does not fetch); a pin with nothing to open keeps the
  generic glyph; where the shell has no picture, the glyph of its kind (an app, a folder, a file, a
  link). Asked again only when what it comes from changes; an answer for an icon no longer shown is
  dropped.

Tests: `FlyoutRowsOptionsTests` (nothing hidden up to the count, the number in the file, the old min
and max as the min, what is no number, the range, the kinds, a folder and back, the merge),
`FlyoutRowsRowTests` (the one field), `PinHeaderIconTests` (the header's source),
`CalendarViewsOffscreenTests.TheCalendarAppIsTheFirstLinkAnAppTakes` (a fake of Windows' answer) and
`NoCalendarAppNoOpenCalendar`. One height at 0 to 11 rows, scrolling only past the count, with the
default and with 1, 3 and 9 rows, and at 1, 5 and 9 rows with the default:
`QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheListsAreExactlyTheirRows`, `VpnRowsPictures.TheListIsExactlyItsRows`,
`CalendarViewsOffscreenTests.TheDaysEventsAreExactlyTheirRows`; and
`AnOpenedNetworkTakesTheKeptRoomAndALongListScrolls`, `TheCalendarIsAsTallAsTheDayItShows`. Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `quick-network-rows-<1|5|9|11|1-open>-150-dark.png`,
`quick-bluetooth-rows-<1|5|9>-150-dark.png`, `vpn-rows-<1|5|9>-150-dark.png`,
`calendar-rows-<1|5|9>-150-dark.png`, `calendar-no-app-150-dark.png`.

## 53. A flyout height, not a count of rows (2026-10-08)

*Automatic came beside the presets as what nobody set, Custom's field takes a number, and the bar
shows the flyout while its height changes (§59).*

*The person*: "for notifications, bluetooth, network, keyboard layout, etc flyouts you should be able
to set the height actually and not the number of items, there should a few height presets and custom
should also be possible where you can enter a specific value. other widgets should have the same
behaviour if it makes sense for them."

- **The setting** (`FlyoutHeight`, `FlyoutHeightPreset`, the entry's `flyoutHeight`): Small, Medium,
  Large, or Custom with a height of its own in DIP, 48 to 1600 (`FlyoutHeights.LeastDip`,
  `MostDip`). Medium is what nobody set and is never written; a preset is written by its name
  (`"flyoutHeight": "large"`), one's own as a number (`"flyoutHeight": 320`); a name this build does
  not know, an array or true reads as Medium (`FlyoutHeightConverter`). A setting of its own beside the
  options record, it goes with the widget into a folder and back (`Partners.Convert`) and merges as any
  property (`ConfigMerge`).
- **The presets** (`WidgetInfo.FlyoutHeights`, `FlyoutHeights(Small, Medium, Large, Row)`), in DIP at a
  text size of 100 % — the list grows with the text, as its rows do, so a preset keeps its rows. Where a
  list has rows of one height, Medium is five of them (§52's default), Small three, Large eight:

  | Widget | Small | Medium | Large | What the height is |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Network (`wifi`), Bluetooth | 174 | 290 | 464 | the networks and cables, the paired devices (58 a row) |
  | VPN | 108 | 180 | 288 | the connections (36 a one-line row) |
  | Calendar | 156 | 260 | 416 | the month's list of the day's events (52 a row) |
  | Keyboard | 156 | 260 | 416 | the layouts (52 a two-line row) |
  | Sound | 126 | 210 | 336 | the volume mixer (42 an app) |
  | Mail, Contacts | 156 | 260 | 416 | the messages, the people |
  | Removable devices | 144 | 240 | 384 | the devices |
  | Notifications, Clipboard history, RSS | 240 | 400 | 600 | the cards, what was copied, the headlines |

  Not given one: the weather, a share, the clock, a timer and focus, media, battery, power,
  brightness, project, cast and the hotspot (content of a fixed length), a drive (what it holds,
  sized its own way), the switchers (two or three desktops or layouts), search, a folder and the tray (grids of their
  own sizes). Sound's output and microphone pickers hang over the page as dropdowns (`PageLayout.Over`)
  and keep their own length; the mixer under them is what the height sets.
- **The rule**: the list is exactly that tall whatever it lists — fewer rows, a notice ("No events",
  Wi-Fi off, "No apps are playing", an empty inbox, the notifications' bell) stand in that room — and
  what is past it is a scroll away at once; the flyout never grows or shrinks with its content, only
  with the setting. Where the most a flyout may be (`FlyoutPlacement.MostHeight`) has no room for it,
  the most. One mechanism per kind of panel, each fed the DIP: `PageLayout.List(top, dip)` for the quick
  pages (network, Bluetooth, the mixer), `PanelContent.Kept` for the panels of `QuickPanel` (mail,
  contacts, clipboard, RSS, removable devices: the body that tall, scrolling past it), `Flyout.Rows`
  (`FlyoutList(Dip, Tail)`) for a list of choices (VPN, the keyboard's layouts), `CalendarInputs.HeightDip`
  for the agenda and `NotificationInputs.HeightDip` for the notifications. The dock asks
  `Dock.HeightAt(window, hit, flyout)`: the widget's own setting against that flyout's presets, Medium
  where it has none — a clock's calendar, the notifications from the clock's menu.
- **The notifications** were "only as high as its contents"; with a height they are that height,
  their empty state's bell in the same room. A plan drawn without one (a folder's list, its card) is
  still as tall as its cards.
- **The old count** (§52's `flyoutRows`, and §47's `{ "min", "max" }` as its min) becomes the height
  those rows were (`FlyoutHeights.FromRows`, `Row` the DIP of one): a preset where one is exactly that
  tall (three rows Small, five Medium and so nothing written, eight Large), a height of its own
  otherwise (seven networks, 406), the count held to 1 to 20 first. Read only to become a height, never
  written again; a `flyoutHeight` beside it wins.
- **Settings**: on the widget's page, for an entry on the bar whose kind has presets, one card,
  "Flyout height": a dropdown of Small, Medium, Large and Custom, and for Custom a number field in DIP
  beside it, 48 to 1600, whole DIP; picking Custom starts it at the height the list had
  (`Logic\FlyoutHeightRow.cs`). Such an entry is no longer "nothing else" (`WidgetSettings.NothingElse`).
  Strings `settings.widget.flyoutHeight.*` in five languages; `settings.widget.flyoutRows.*` went.

Tests: `FlyoutHeightTests` (the presets and one's own, three, five and eight rows, nobody set writes
nothing, the names and the number in the file, what is no height, the range, the old count and the old
min and max becoming their height, a height beside a count, the kinds, a folder and back, the merge),
`FlyoutHeightRowTests` (the card's widgets, the dropdown, a pick, the field), `WidgetStandTests`.
One height from none to eleven rows, scrolling only past the height, at Medium, Small, Large and a
height of the tests' own: `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheListsAreExactlyTheirHeight` and
`TheMixerIsAlwaysAsTallAsItsApps`, `VpnRowsPictures.TheListIsExactlyItsHeight`,
`CalendarViewsOffscreenTests.TheDaysEventsAreExactlyTheirHeight`; the same height whatever they hold,
Small and Large by exactly the difference: `FlyoutOffscreenTests.TheNotificationPanelKeepsItsHeight`
(and the plan's in `TheNotificationPanelIsAsTallAsItsCards`), `MailFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheMailListIsExactlyItsHeight`,
`ContactsFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheContactsListIsExactlyItsHeight`,
`DrivesFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheRemovableListKeepsItsHeight`, the clipboard's and RSS's room in
`ClipboardFlyoutPictures` and `TheHeadlinesPanelIsPictured`, `KeyboardIslandTests.TheListOfLayoutsIsTheWidgetsHeight`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`), at Small and at Large, 150 %, dark:
`quick-<network|bluetooth>-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`, `quick-sound-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`,
`vpn-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`, `calendar-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`,
`notifications-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`, `mail-height-<small|large>-150-dark.png`.

## 54. Widgets with nothing between them are one group; a spacer with no line (2026-10-09) — no separator, a section's run one group, since §511 (2026-11-05); every app button its own card, not one over the open apps, since §602 (2026-11-09)

The person: "the widgets in the taskbar should be grouped together like the system tray ones or the
status ones if there is not a divider / spacer between them. you should also be able to make a
spacer now that does not have a width at all."

**The rule.** On an islands bar (the connected look has no cards and no gaps already), consecutive
widgets of one section with nothing between them are one group: no gap between them
(`Layout.Between` → `Together`), one card behind the run, each lit on its own square under the
pointer (the tray's and the status icons' way, `Scene.Dress` already lit a part's own card). A
separator ends a group, and so does the spacer below, and a section's end; a widget alone is a group
of one and looks as it did. Between groups the gap is the ordinary one (`islandGap`), and a divider
stands in it as before. `Layout.Joined(part)` says whether a part runs on into the one before and
the one after it; that is the whole rule, tested in `WidgetGroupTests`.

**Who is in a group.** Every part that wears a card over its whole block (`Scene.WearsCard`), which
is everything but a separator: Start, Search, Task View, Windows' buttons, the tray, the clock, Show
desktop, Karpo's own widgets — and the pins and the open apps (below).

**The pins and the open apps join too** (the person, later the same day: "they should join too").
They first stayed out, a card a button and one gap between buttons, because a pin and a running app
are the same button and a group would have put a shared card over per-button cards. Now:

- *No gap inside a part.* The buttons of a part — a pin's (one, or one a window where its windows are
  not combined, or a folder pin's row), the Apps widget's, and "…" after the last one shown — stand
  flush, as the tray's icons do (`Layout.TileGap`, 0, in `TileRun`, `LayTiles`, the "…" room and
  `TileAt`). So a pin next to a pin, a pin next to the open apps and two open apps all keep the same
  room: none. A pin and its running app are still the same button and take the same room, in a
  group or not (`AppButtonTests.RunningAppsKeepTheRoomPinsKeep`, now also between the last pin and
  the first open app; `WidgetGroupTests.APinAndARunningAppTakeTheSameRoomInAGroup`).
- *One card.* `Scene.WearsCard(Apps)` is true and the per-button cards are gone (`AppCard`, the "…"
  card, `Layout.ButtonsApart`): a pin or the Apps widget wears one card over its block like any
  widget, and that card is its piece of the group's (`Scene.PlaceCard`). With nothing between them,
  Start, the pins, the open apps and the widgets after them are one group; a divider or a spacer
  (also the one with no line) splits it, and a section's end ends it. The Apps widget with nothing
  open is no part of the bar at rest and leaves no seam.
- *Each button lit on its own.* The pointer over a button lights its own cell (`Layout.TileCell`, the
  "…" its `OverflowCell`) with the card's corner, on the shared card, as a tray icon lights its
  square (`Scene.Dress`); a pin alone lights the whole of its card as before, since that is its cell.
  The focused app's plate, the attention plate and the running indicator stay the taskbar's, inside
  the cell (`ItemRect`), and a press shrinks the icon as before.
- *Growing and shrinking.* When an app opens or closes the Apps piece's visual glides to its new size
  as every movable does, and now its shape glides with it (`Rounded.GrowFrom`, called from the glide
  for any card whose size changed): a card's shape is sized by itself, not by its visual, so it used
  to jump to its new length while what stood on it slid.
- *Drags.* Nothing changed in how pins are dragged or how edit mode moves parts: the pieces are the
  parts' own visuals. "Add" stands on the seam beside a pin or the open apps, as beside any member.

Tested in `WidgetGroupTests` (the app-button cases), `AppOverflowTests` (a pin's windows and "…" flush
in their group), `IslandCardsTests`, and on the real tree in `SceneTreeTests.AnAppGroupWearsOneCardAndLightsEachButtonOnIt`
(one card a part, none a button, the hover on a pin's and an open app's own cell, inside its piece).
Pictures: `SceneTreeTests.AppGroupSheets`, to KARPO_PNG_DIR as
`app-group-<40|48>-<dark|light>-<100|150>-<rest|hover-pin|hover-app|hover-more>.png` — Start, two
pins (the second running), three open apps (the first focused), a spacer with no line, then a group
of widgets; and with twenty more apps, "…" lit at the group's end. The busy bar's sheets
(`BusyBarSheets`) now open 40 apps, since 30 flush buttons no longer fill a 1920-DIP bar.

**The card.** A group is not one visual: edit mode moves, selects and carries parts one by one, and a
card spanning several would not move with them. Each member draws its piece of the card
(`Scene.PlaceCard`): the part's usual rounded card, drawn longer than the part on each side it runs
on, by more than its corner, and clipped back to the part with an inset clip. That side is square and
has no outline, so the pieces meet as one card with the group's two ends round and the outline
running along the top and bottom. Each piece stays the part's own `Movable`, so a drag takes it with
the part. While a block is carried over a group the gap that opens shows the pieces' square sides for
a moment; the scene is built again when it lands.

**The spacer with no line.** Since §78 a separator is a spacer when Appearance gives every
separator no line (`Config.Separators.Line` off, the default; `Layout.Separators`). It draws nothing and takes no room of its own: with no
space either, its width at rest is 0 and it is no part of the bar (no block, no hit). It still ends
a group, which `Layout.SpacerBetween` finds by looking in the list between two neighbours, since it is
not among the parts shown. The gap between the two groups it parts is one ordinary gap, the same a
divider stands in, and at a section's end it adds nothing. With a space chosen it is a plain spacer,
exactly that room either side and no line. Appearance's "Separators" has "Line" (a switch); the
line's width and colour cards are off while it is off.

**Edit mode.** A spacer that takes no room could never be taken hold of, so edit mode gives it a
marker: two hairlines wide, laid over the seam between its neighbours and taking no room of the
run (`Layout.markers`), so nothing moves on a bar with gaps or on a dock's flush panel; drawn as a
dashed box over its grab zone (§61), the same grab zone a separator has
(`SeparatorGrabDip`). Dragging, selecting, deleting and the Settings button work on it as on any
separator (`WidgetGroupTests.ASpacerWithNoLineCanBeTakenHoldOfInEditMode`). The "Add" marker
(`Layout.InsertionRect`) stands on the seam between two members of a group, where there is no gap,
and in the gap's middle beside anything else.

**Not changed.** The distance from a group to the bar's edges is what a widget's card always had
across the bar (the bar's margin) and none along the screen's ends, as before. A floating dock's
panel is unchanged: its widgets were flush already.

Pictures to look at (not drawn by the tests): a bar with a clock, weather and battery in a row, then
a divider, then more; dark, light and high contrast; a vertical bar; edit mode with a spacer; a pin
dragged along a group of pins and open apps; an app opening and closing at the end of a group.

## 55. The performance readings: one always-running source, a flyout of their own (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "if you click on one of the system graph widgets it should also show a flyout with
more information about that specific metric." "The graph of the system widgets should also be removed
in the taskbar view. The graph should show with the flyout again." "There should be one service in the
background that always gets the data for the graph and then all the widgets that show this data should
pull the data from this one service. This service should always run."

- **One source, always running.** `DataSources` keeps the five readings — processor, graphics, memory,
  disk and network, at one second, the main graphics card and every disk together — from the dock's start
  whether or not the config has a widget that shows them (`SourceKinds.Always`, the registry's
  `always` list, which `Want` adds to what the config names and which only `Clear` takes away). Before
  this a reading's source existed only while a widget of it was in the config, so a flyout, a card
  made later or a layout shown for the first time began with an empty history. The dock's one timer
  runs at the sources' pace with nothing in the config (`DataSources.Period`).
- **Every widget pulls from it.** A bar entry, a card, a line and the flyout hold or read the registry's
  one source (`PerformanceData`, keyed by reading and device — **never by pace**). The source reads
  every second, always; a widget set to read every 2 to 10 seconds draws the same history a step every
  so many samples (`Series`, `PerformanceData.Paced`: each step the mean of its samples, counted from
  the history's first sample so a whole step never changes, the step still filling left out) and
  repaints at its pace. So a slow graph is not a second reader of the counter and has its history from
  the dock's start like the rest. (The first version keyed the source by pace too, so a 5-second graph
  was a sixth source with a history starting at its creation: not "one service".) Only a named adapter
  or disk is a source of its own, because its reading is another device's; it is added to the five,
  never in their place. The counters under them are `SharedSamplers`', one read of each per pass
  whoever asks. **No widget samples.**
  `PerformanceIsland.Sample` used to ask its source to gather (`Catch`) when it ticked; it draws what
  the source holds now, and the dock ticks the sources before the islands (`Dock.TickIslands`) so a
  tick draws what was just read.
- **History** is a ring of one-second samples on the source (`History`, `PerformanceData.Kept`): the
  widest graph's 512 steps at the slowest pace and the step still filling, 5130 floats (20 KB) a
  source. The flyout draws its last 61 (`PerformanceModel.Samples`, Task Manager's minute).
- **Cheap per tick.** A gather is the sampler's read and a float into the ring; `DataSources.Tick`
  walks an array kept until the set of sources changes, so the once-a-second tick allocates nothing;
  the open flyout redraws only when its source gathered (`PerformanceFlyout.Update` compares what it
  last drew), not on every tick of a faster dock timer (a clock with seconds).
- **The taskbar entry has no graph.** Glyph and the reading, as the form with no room for a graph
  already was (the setting `ShowGraph` is a folder cell's: `WidgetShapes.Performance` and
  `PerformanceIsland.Configure` ignore it for a `BarItem`), and no tooltip (`BarEntry.Tooltip` false:
  the flyout says all of it). Given more room than it needs, the reading goes to the entry's end and the
  glyph stays at its start. The cards and the lines keep their graphs, and their click is still Task
  Manager.
- **The click is the entry's own flyout** (`BarClick.Flyout`, `IslandView.Performance`, the table in
  `Dock.Widgets.cs`, `Dock.Performance.cs`): `Performance\PerformanceFlyout.cs`, a Menu-mode
  `FlyoutHost` of the quick settings' chrome, 360 DIP wide, as tall as its content (`QuickPanel.Fit`).
  The title and the reading large; what the graph's top stands for over its right end ("100%", or for
  the network the minute's busiest rate rounded up to a power of two, "8.0 MB/s", which the graph is
  scaled to: `Sparkline.Round`); the last minute edge to edge as an area under a line in a box of five
  hairlines, top, quarters and foot (`HistoryGraph`, drawn by `Graphs\Sparkline` as the cards are);
  "60 seconds" and "0" under it; the facts in two columns (a long one across both); and "Open Task
  Manager". It draws the widget's own source, so the minute is there when it opens.
  **Live**: after each tick of the sources the dock calls `Update`, which sets the texts and the graph
  and paints only what changed, and lays the panel out again only when the facts are others (an
  adapter came). The hover flyout (`HoverFlyouts`) opens it too.
- **What it shows**, from the source and a few figures read once a second while it is open
  (`PerformanceFigures`, `Islands\Samplers\System.cs`) — never on the sources' tick:
  - Processor: utilization, base speed (GHz), logical processors, processes, threads, handles, up time
    (`d:hh:mm:ss`).
  - Memory: in use (of the total), available, committed (of the limit), cached.
  - Graphics: utilization, and the adapter — **one card, never all of them** (2026-10-11). The person:
    "the graphics widget should only show information / details about one graphics card not all
    installed once." A graphics widget (line, entry, face, flyout, tooltip) reads, names and graphs
    exactly one adapter (`GpuSampler.Followed`): the one its `PerformanceOptions.GpuAdapter` names
    ("GPU 1: NVIDIA …", per widget), or with none named the **main card** (`GpuSampler.MainOf`): the
    most dedicated video memory (DXGI's `DedicatedVideoMemory`, so a discrete card beats the
    integrated one even on a laptop whose panel the integrated one drives), then the one with a
    display attached (`EnumOutputs`), then DXGI's first. The Microsoft Basic Render Driver and
    compute-only adapters were never in the list. Before, an empty name meant "the busiest of them" and
    the flyout and tooltip listed every adapter's load. Backward compatible: the field is unchanged and
    an empty one (every older file) now means the main card; a named card not attached shows no reading
    and the card says so, as before. The settings card's list is "The main graphics card", then each
    attached card; with two or more its note names the main one ("Shows GPU 1: …, the card with the
    most video memory", `Adapters.Listed`, the bar's own rule). Tests: `SamplerTests`
    (`TheMainCardHas…`, `AWidgetFollows…`), `PerformanceCardTests`.
  - Disk: active time, read speed, write speed; the title is "Disk 1 (C:)" for a graph that follows one.
  - Network: send, receive, the adapter carrying the most (`NetworkSampler.AdapterName`, one row asked
    when the flyout is open; the sample only keeps its LUID). The big figure is down and up together,
    which is what the graph plots.
  Left out as not cheap or not reliable: the processor's current speed (`CallNtPowerInformation` answers
  the base clock for it), the graphics adapters' dedicated memory (a driver query that fails on some
  machines), a link speed. A figure Windows would not give is left out, never shown as 0; a reading
  not taken yet is a dash.
- **Strings**: `widget.performance.*` (utilization, activeTime, readSpeed, writeSpeed, send, receive,
  adapter, baseSpeed, logicalProcessors, processes, threads, handles, upTime, committed, cached, seconds,
  openTaskManager, notAvailable) in five languages.

Tests: `PerformanceFlyoutTests` (a source per reading with an empty config, the always list, gathering
with no widget, the timer's pace, a layout that names no graph, every widget of a reading holding the one
source and the dock's hold outliving theirs, another pace reading the one source and only another
device adding one, the paced series' means, its whole steps that never change and its wrap, the ring
keeping the widest graph at the slowest pace, the minute's samples, the graph's top, the click table and no tooltip, the words of each reading from stand-in
sources and figures, a dash before any reading, the time and the clock written),
`PerformanceFlyoutOffscreenTests` (UI: pictures of the five in dark and light, before a reading and at
larger text; a live update, the button, Escape, an adapter coming, opening under a top bar; the bar entry's length unchanged by
`ShowGraph`, a bar entry and a card holding one source, ticking them gathers nothing and the registry's
tick gathers once), `OneRowTests`, `MediaRowTests`, `GraphShapeTests.TheGraphSettingChangesNothingOnTheBar`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `performance-<cpu|gpu|memory|disk|network>-<dark|light>.png`.

## 56. A little room off the bar, forms that fill their card, widths that are what the content needs (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "the widgets themselves should have a little space to the taskbar and neighbouring widgets and should get their own background. they should then be designed in a way so that they use up the whole space that is available to them. additionally the taskbar widgets should not have configurable sizes by cells."

- **Room off the bar** (`Layout.CardInsetPx`, `CardInsetDips`, `Layout.EndRoom`). On the islands look a card keeps a tenth of the bar's height off the bar's edge across it (4 DIPs of 40, 8 of 80), never under 2 DIPs, never over 10, and never so much that the card is shorter than the bar's icon. The first and the last card of a section keep the same off the bar's ends (they were flush; `EndPadTests` says so now). The card is the bar less that, above and below (`SmallWellPx`, the grid cell, `Layout.CellPx`); `WellPx` (an app button's highlight) takes the same margin. The floating dock keeps its look: 2 DIPs of breath and its panel's own room. The gap between groups is unchanged.
- **Forms fill the card** (`Fit`, the one shared helper, in `CellIsland.cs`). Sized from the card's height: the glyph is `Fit.GlyphShare` (0.55) of it on the icon font's own steps, a step taken when the glyph is within 10 % of it (20 DIPs of the 48-DIP bar's 38.4, 16 of the 36's, 32 of the 80's); text is `Layout.CellTextDips` (12.5 DIPs of 38.4, a third of the card, 11 to 26); `Fit.Edge` (along the run) is 18 % of the card, 4 to 12 DIPs; `Fit.Side` is the old narrow room (9 %) a line keeps across a cell that is only as wide as the bar is thick (vertical bars, the input indicator, the date). Every `Glyph(0.4f)` call takes the default now. Per kind: glyph buttons, switches, the status icons (`SystemIcon`, the same size as the others: 20 not 16 DIPs on the 48 bar), folders, notifications, security, power, removable devices, Rss, contacts, desktops: the new glyph size; text kinds (calendar, timer, stock, weather, the readings): the new text; the bell's badge is measured from the bell alone (six tenths of the glyph, never from the text scale); the switch's pill is held inside the card (it was 28 px in a 22-px card at 28 DIPs, `SwitchIsland.Pill`); the drive keeps its 0.44 icon and the narrow `Side` so one cell still holds icon and bar; the input indicator uses `Side` so its code is not stepped down to nothing; the Windows search box is Windows' own geometry on the 48-DIP bar's card (`SearchPill.BaseCellDip` 38.4, length 220 DIPs, no longer five cells); now playing's column is 3 cells of the card (it was 2.4 with the slack of whole cells) and its two lines need a 44-DIP bar (a card of 35 px), not 40.
- **Widths are what the content needs** (`Layout.ExactSpan`, `AllotCells`, `CellIsland.Fill`, `CellPair.Length`). A widget is as long as its content, never under one cell, in whole pixels: not whole cells, so a date can be two cells and a bit. A range whose ends meet (a drive's two cells) and a range the content falls outside are still whole cells; a clock is exact too. A glyph with its air is still exactly one square cell (`CellPair.Length` tightens the air where the full edge would spend a second).
- **No cell sizes on the bar**: already so since 2026-10-08 (no card in Settings, `BarItem.Normalize` drops `atLeast`/`atMost`, tolerant read); `SizeRangeTests` holds it over every kind now, file included. What remains is a kind's internal range (`WidgetSize`), which Settings never shows.
- **Settings**: "Show a graph" is for a folder's card or line only (`PerformanceCard.ShowsGraphSwitch`); a bar entry's page keeps the pace alone. No new strings.

Tests: `BarFormTests` (the room present and scaling, 28 to 160 DIPs at four scales, ends and edges on every edge, the dock's look; every entry's form at 28, 36, 40, 48 and 80 DIPs at 100 % and 150 % leaves nothing outside its card, stands in the middle of it and has content at least 40 % of its height), `SceneTreeTests.BarHeightSheets` (the real scene at six heights, every card's room checked on the real layout). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `bar-forms-<28|36|40|48|80>-<dark|light>.png` and `.txt` (every kind on its card, the numbers beside), `bar-height-<height>-<look>-<scale>.png`. By hand: the 36- and 40-DIP bars (the input indicator's language is small there; now playing is one line under 44), the status icons' new size, a vertical bar.

## 57. The icons that are not an app's are Windows' 16 DIP (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "the icons that are not pins, like network, tray icons, notifications, etc in the taskbar are too big."

- **One share** (`Fit.SystemIconShare`, 5/12 of the card, taken to the font's step at or under it, with none of §56's slack upwards, so a floating dock's 44-DIP card is 16 too; `Fit.Glyph()` is `Fit.SystemIcon`). On the 48-DIP bar's 38.4-DIP card that is 16 DIP, Windows 11's size for its tray, its network, sound and battery icons and its bell, beside its 24-DIP app icons (a third and a half of the bar). On the icon font's steps: 16 DIP up to a 54-DIP bar (the 40-DIP bar too: its 32-DIP card gives 13, held at the font's 16), 20 on 64, 24 on 80. §56's 0.55 (20 DIP on 48) is gone.
- **Every kind**: the status icons and the input indicator's neighbours (`Fit.SystemIcon`), the bell and its badge (`NotificationsIsland`, the badge from the bell), a widget's glyph beside its text and a glyph-only widget (`Fit.Glyph()`), the status icons behind their arrow (`Fit.SystemIconFor`), Show desktop's glyph (`Scene.GlyphButton`, was 20), and **tray icons** (`Layout.TrayIconPx`: the same size, never more than an app's icon; was an app's 24 DIP since 2026-10-08). The tray's chevron is three quarters of it, as the status icons' arrow is. A tray icon's cell stays the bar's square card (`TrayCell`), so a 16-DIP icon has Windows' room round it; the overflow's icons follow (`Dock`, `StripIconSize`). Unchanged: Start, pins, open apps (`Config.IconDips`, 24 DIP; half the bar since §538), Windows' search and task view buttons (20 DIP glyphs on the app row), the weather's picture (as tall as its reading, at most three fifths of the card: 20 DIP on 48).

Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `bar-look-<32|40|48|64>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` and `bar-look-edit-*.png` (`SceneTreeTests.BarLookSheets`: the weather and a reading as a group, a spacer with no line, a reading alone, a divider, the timer; Start, search, task view, two pins and three apps; three tray icons, the input indicator, network, sound, battery, date, time, bell), with the sizes in `bar-look-*.txt`. Tests: `IconSizeTests`.

## 58. Bars along the top (2026-10-09)

The person: "the topbar implementation is also wrong". Everything a bar along the top does was
gone through against the bottom's — a Taskbar or a Dock on a display whose edge is the top, and a
Top and bottom's top bar —: what only worked at the bottom is fixed.

- **The edit bar's add list** opened upwards (`Edge.Bottom`, from when the edit bar stood by the
  bottom bar), over the edit bar and the top bar: it opens under "Add a widget" now (§50;
  `EditDeckPlan.ListEdge`, the tooltips' edge too).
- **Popups of a top bar in edit mode** opened onto the edit bar, which stands right under the top
  bar: they keep clear of it (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`, §50).
- **A popup never runs over the other bar** (`Dock.PopupRoom`, `DockWindow.WorkArea`): Windows' work
  area keeps no strip for a bar over the windows, so a long menu of a Top and bottom's bottom bar
  ran up over a top bar over the windows, and the top bar's down over the bottom one. What popups
  stay inside is the work area less every other bar of the display in sight. Placement keeps to the
  work area on the bar's side too (`FlyoutHost`, `Flyout`, `Preview`, `FlyoutPlacement.MostHeight`):
  a popup pushed down is never laid out from above it.
- **The keys in edit mode** were the bar's edit mode began on only: a widget focused on a Top and
  bottom's other bar, or in a place, took no Tab, arrow, Ctrl+arrow, Enter or Shift+F10. The surface
  last pressed on has them now (`Dock.Keyed`, `FocusBar`).
- **Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down** carry the focused widget to the same section of the bar above or below,
  at its end (`IslandEdits.Across`, `Dock.StepRow`): the keyboard's way between a Top and bottom's
  two bars. A Ctrl+arrow never steps a widget into a slot its layout does not show any more (a
  Dock's start or end, where it vanished; `IslandEdits.Step` with the layout's `Shows`).
- **"Pin to taskbar"** from a top bar's open app pinned before the first Apps widget in the list, the
  bottom bar's (or one in a slot not shown): it pins before the apps of the bar it was chosen on.
- **The anchor** of a display whose every bar comes in on hover stands on the display's edge
  (`Config.EdgeOfScreen`), not always the bottom.
- **The Displays page** greys **Position** while the display shows a Top and bottom, which has a bar
  on both edges (`DisplayEntry.EdgeApplies`); its line says so.
- **The sides are gone from the code too**, where nothing needed them: the hover places are the
  bottom's and the top's three, each along the whole edge (`HoverPlaces`: no corners, no side runs,
  no `BarArea`; `HoverPlaces.For` takes the edges shown all the time), `ScreenEdges` has a bottom and
  a top (a side reads as no bar), a bar stands in the whole display (`DockWindow.Area`), and the
  settings app's side words, bands and pictures went (`DisplayCard.Doing`, `WidgetHeading`,
  `DisplayMap`, `EdgeArt`). Kept: `Edge.Left`/`Right` and `Layout.Vertical` with what lays a bar out
  down a side (Layout.cs, Scene.cs, the pins and the tray drags, the appbar's ABE codes), which a
  bar can no longer be but which is woven through the layout code.
- Checked and right at the top already: the bar's window and its tooltip room under it, the
  resize grip on its inner (lower) side and the drag that sizes the top bar's `TopSize`, the
  appbar strip at the top beside one at the bottom, hover and its 1 px strip at the top, the slide
  in from above, every widget flyout, menu, jump list, window list and folder opening downwards from
  the bar's inner side, the section edit bars under a top bar, the carry window, drops onto a top
  bar or place, and a widget added on a top bar landing in its row (`DockWindow.Row`, `PlaceIn`).
  Windows' own Start and Search open where Windows puts them (§26).

Tests: `PopupRoomTests`, `IslandEditsTests.StepNeverLeavesTheSlotsTheLayoutShows`,
`AcrossTakesAWidgetToTheSameSectionOfTheOtherBar`, `HoverPlacesTests` (top and bottom only),
`EdgeModesTests.ATopOnHoverHasItsPlacesAlongTheWholeTop`, `TheEditBarsAddListOpensUnderIt`,
`EditDeckPlanTests.ItsListsDropDownFromTheTop`. Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `top-<taskbar|dock|top-bottom>-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png` (a Taskbar and a Dock on
a display whose edge is the top, a Top and bottom with a 32-DIP top bar and a 48-DIP bottom one) and
`top-<taskbar|top-bottom>-<rest|edit>-menu-dark-150.png` (a menu from the top bar, under the edit bar
in edit mode). By hand: Tab and Ctrl+Up/Down on a Top and bottom's top bar in edit mode, a long
jump list of a bottom bar with a top bar over the windows, Position greyed for a Top and bottom.

## 59. Flyout height: Automatic, a field that takes a number, a look while it changes (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "when you say custom height in the flyout you cannot enter the custom height", "when
changing the flyout height it should show the flyout so you can actually see the new height", "for
flyout height there should also be automatic now which automatically adjust the height".

- **Why Custom could not be entered.** The number field sat in the card for every choice, hidden but
  bound two ways; handed a preset's height, it handed it back, and `FlyoutHeightRow.Write` took that
  as a height of one's own. Picking Large made the widget Custom 464 behind the dropdown (the person's
  file had 464 for the network and 416 for the calendar, both Large), so picking Custom afterwards
  changed nothing and its field never showed. The field now writes only while Custom is picked
  (`FlyoutHeightRow.Write`, `HasField`), and has a card of its own under the dropdown's, shown for
  Custom alone, as the stock's custom years have: "Custom height", "In pixels at 100% scale, 48 to
  1600", whole numbers, steps of 10 (50 with Page Up/Down), anything outside put back in range.
- **Automatic** (`FlyoutHeightPreset.Automatic`), first in the dropdown and what nobody set: the list as
  tall as what it lists, up to the most a flyout may be (`FlyoutPlacement.MostHeight`, 70 % of the work
  area beside the bar), past it scrolling — the rule every panel kept before the height came, and still keeps for a list of no
  set height, and still follows its content at once (`FlyoutHost.Fit`). Never written; null in the
  model. Medium is now written (`"medium"`) like the other presets; an old count of rows still becomes
  the height it was, five rows Medium, never Automatic. A file from yesterday's build where Medium was
  chosen (and so not written) reads as Automatic now. `FlyoutHeights.Dip` is null for Automatic, and
  every flyout takes the null its own way: `PageLayout.List` keeps no room, `PanelContent.Kept` is
  null, `Flyout.Rows` is null, the calendar's agenda and the notifications' list are as tall as they
  are. `Dock.HeightAt` gives null where nothing is set — a clock's calendar, the notifications from
  the clock's menu.
- **One limit for every mode.** A preset or a height of one's own is still exactly that tall and never
  more than the most a flyout may be; on a top bar the room is measured downward from the bar, the same
  rule (`FlyoutPlacement.MostHeight`, `Edge.Top`), inside the room popups keep to (§58: the work area
  less a Top and bottom's other bar, with the anchor held to it). The look opens through the same
  `OpenWidgetFlyout`, so it keeps to that room too.
- **The look while it changes** (`Logic\FlyoutHeightPreview.cs`, `FlyoutLook.cs`, Karpo.Core
  `FlyoutPreview`, the dock's `Dock.FlyoutPreview.cs`). Each change of the height in Settings — a pick,
  a number typed or stepped — has the dock open that widget's flyout from where it stands on the bar
  (on the display the Settings window is on, where it stands there too), at the height being set,
  shown again at each change. It is asked the way a start is handed over (SettingsHandOff):
  WM_COPYDATA to the dock's window with a marker of its own ("KARF") and the text `id\0word\0`
  (`FlyoutHeight.Word`: `automatic`, `small`…, or the DIP); no text ends the look. The dock answers at
  once and opens from its host's queue (`WM_KARPO_FLYOUT_PREVIEW`), so a run of steps opens the last.
  The flyout opens for a look (`FlyoutHost.Previewing`): it takes no focus, closes nothing of Windows',
  and stays through presses in Settings and Settings having the focus. It ends when the focus leaves
  the two cards (the dropdown's own list counts as inside), the page unloads, another widget is shown,
  the window closes, or four seconds pass with no change (`FlyoutHeightPreview.Idle`); and in the dock
  after ten seconds with no word (`FLYOUT_PREVIEW`), for a Settings that went. Anything the person opens
  meanwhile is theirs (`PreviewYields`): the look's end never closes it. In edit mode it shares the one flyout with the selection (§65); a VPN
  whose click switches it rather than listing (`SwitchIsland.Lists`) is never clicked for a look.

Tests: `FlyoutHeightTests` (Automatic as no height and never written, Medium written, `"automatic"` and
unknown words read as Automatic, the old counts becoming Medium, a height's word read back,
`FlyoutPreview` read back and its marker), `FlyoutHeightRowTests` (the dropdown, Automatic first and
the default, the field for Custom alone, the regression of the hidden field's number, the look shown on
each change, closed once on leaving, ended by another widget, nothing without a card or a dock),
`QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.AFlyoutOpenedForALookTakesNoFocusAndStays`; Automatic a row taller for each
row and held to the most on a short screen in `TheListsAreExactlyTheirHeight`, `TheMixerIsAlwaysAsTallAsItsApps`,
`TheDaysEventsAreExactlyTheirHeight`, `TheNotificationPanelKeepsItsHeight`,
`TheRemovableListKeepsItsHeight`, `TheContactsListIsExactlyItsHeight`, `TheMailListIsExactlyItsHeight`,
`ACablePluggedInOrPulledOutShowsAtOnce`, `KeyboardIslandTests.TheListOfLayoutsIsTheWidgetsHeight`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `quick-<network|bluetooth>-automatic-<1|5|9|most>-150-dark.png`,
`quick-sound-automatic-5-150-dark.png`, `calendar-automatic-<1|5>-150-dark.png`,
`calendar-automatic-most-100-dark.png`, `notifications-automatic-3-dark.png`,
`removable-automatic-2-150-dark.png`. By hand: pick Custom and type a height, the flyout showing on
the bar at once without Settings losing the keyboard; step with the spin buttons; tab away and see it
close.

## 60. Colours of one's own (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "in appearance you should be able to customize individual colors like island background, taskbar background, with color pickers".

- **What can be chosen** (`ColorSlot`, `Karpo.Core\BarColors.cs`): the taskbar's background, the widgets' cards, the cards' outline, the highlight (under the pointer, and the open app's button), the separators' line, the flyouts' background, and the folders' dividers (since §78; the separators' and the dividers' swatches stand in their own groups). Large and plainly seen; the rest (text, icons, the accent's indicators, tooltips, edit mode) keeps following Windows. Text was left out on purpose: the widgets draw their own text in many places from the mode, and a text colour that reached some of them and not others would look broken.
- **Per mode**: every colour is kept for the light mode and the dark mode apart (`config.colors.light` / `.dark`, `"#AARRGGBB"` each, nothing written while Automatic). The automatic colours come in pairs with the text over them, and Windows can switch the mode on a schedule; one colour for both would be right in one mode and unreadable in the other. A value that does not read (a typo, a number) is Automatic and stays in the file as written (`ColorTextConverter`).
- **One place**: the dock resolves every one in `Scene.Theme` (the bar: Windows' own `Automatic` tokens, then the chosen ones over them) and `FlyoutTheme.For` (the flyouts); `Look.Colors` carries the mode's palette, read in `Dock.ReadLook`. **High contrast** carries none: Windows' system colours win, as Windows asks of every app.
- **Material**: Opaque draws the bar's colour without its alpha. Follow Windows is Acrylic with transparency effects on; with them off it is Opaque, as Windows' taskbar is, unless the chosen bar colour is see-through (alpha under 255): then it is Translucent, so "#00000000" shows the desktop rather than a black bar (the person, 2026-10-09: "when the taskbar is transparent it does not actually show the background"; Scene.Settle). Acrylic and Translucent lay the colour over the blur or the desktop with **its own alpha in place of the Opacity slider** (the row says so). Clear draws no bar, chosen or not. A chosen flyout colour is the tint over the blur, and solid without transparency effects.
- **Live, nothing rebuilt**: the settings app saves a colour once the picker rests (150 ms, as a slider). A config whose colours alone changed (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`) is applied by `Dock.Recolour`: every brush that draws a chosen colour (the ground, every part's card and outline, the pins' and open apps' one card over their buttons among them, the edit wash where a part has none, the open app's fill, the separators) was made through `Scene.Swatch` and is set again in place (`Scene.Recolour`), the lit highlight with them; nothing is laid out, built or redrawn. `IslandStyle.Look` drops the palette, so no widget's surfaces are redrawn either. If Windows' own look changed meanwhile the bars are built again, as before. An open flyout takes the new colour when it opens next.
- **Settings** (Appearance, `SettingsModel.Colors.cs`, `Controls\ColorSwatch.cs`, `Logic\ColorRows.cs`): an expander "Custom colors" with "Reset all" in its header and a row per colour; each row has two swatches, light (sun) and dark (moon), each a fixed-width button showing the colour over a checkerboard and its value ("Automatic", "#1E3A5F, 80%"). A click opens WinUI's `ColorPicker` with alpha and hex input, and "Use automatic". While Automatic, the picker starts at about what Windows shows (`ColorRows.Start`). The "Colors" link to Windows' settings stays under Related settings, for the mode and the accent.

Tests: `BarColorsTests` (the file: nothing while Automatic, per mode, tolerant, emptied modes go), `BarColorThemeTests` (resolution: unchosen is Windows' own, a chosen one replaces only itself, Opaque against see-through alpha, the highlight's steps, high contrast ignores all, the flyout's tint, widget styles unaffected, a colours-only change and a mixed one), `ColorRowsTests` (writes, Automatic, Reset all, words), `SceneTreeTests.RecolouringShowsWhatABuildInTheColorsShows` (a recoloured bar's brushes and pixels match a bar built in those colours). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `bar-colors-<automatic|navy|warm|see-through>-<dark|light>.png` (the clock lit), `bar-colors-recoloured-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: the picker in the settings app (its flyout's size, a drag recolouring the bar live), Acrylic with a chosen bar colour over a real desktop, switching Windows between light and dark with colours set for both.

## 61. The input indicator at the bar's text size; edit mode's divider and spacer told apart (2026-10-09)

*The person*: the input indicator on a thin bar may be wider than square — its text at the bar's
normal widget text size, never shrunk to fit a square; and in edit mode a spacer with no line must
look clearly different from a divider, the divider's box "filled ... in the primary colour".

- **Input indicator** (`KeyboardIsland.Room`, `WidgetShapes.Keyboard`). Across a horizontal bar the
  codes are `Fit.Primary`, the clock's size, at every height. The entry is the widest code the PC's
  installed layouts show (`KeyboardIsland.Installed`, `GetKeyboardLayoutList`, read again only when the
  list changes; "WWW" with none) and `Fit.Edge` at each end, never narrower than the square. So it is
  square where the codes fit one (48 DIP and up at 100 %) and a few px wider on a thin bar (30 px for
  a 22 px cell at 28 DIP); switching layout never moves the bar, adding a language in Windows can.
  Two lines (language over region) where two lines of that size fit the cell's height, else the
  language alone. Down a vertical bar unchanged.
- **Divider in edit mode** (`Scene.MarkFor`; superseded by §121, a plain line): its grab zone a box filled with the accent
  (`Tokens.EditMarker`: the accent, the highlight in high contrast), its line on it in the accent's
  text colour, no outline. Under the pointer that colour washes over it with a hairline ring; selected,
  a 2-px ring of it a hairline inside the edge (the accent ring other blocks wear would vanish on it).
  At rest, out of edit mode, the divider is drawn exactly as before.
- **Spacer with no line in edit mode** (superseded by §121, a plain line): an empty box over its grab zone with a dashed outline in the
  secondary text colour, the text colour under the pointer (the highlight in high contrast), the
  accent ring selected. No line. Its marker is laid over the seam its neighbours meet at and takes no
  room of the run, which also ends the 2-px shift a dock's flush panel had on entering edit mode.
- Colours somebody chose (§60) never reach edit mode's marks.

Tests: `KeyboardSquareTests` (the bar's text size at every height, width = text and ends and never
under square, wider at 28 DIP, the same for every layout, the widest installed code),
`SeparatorMarkTests` (filled accent vs dashed and empty, high contrast's highlight, chosen colours
change nothing), `WidgetGroupTests.EnteringEditModeMovesNothing` (both looks, both edges, three scales).
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `keyboard-square-<dpi>-<look>.png`, `edit-marks-<style>-<dark|light|contrast>-<scale>-<state>.png`
(`SceneTreeTests.EditMarkSheets`), `bar-look-edit-*.png`. By hand: the indicator on a 28-40 DIP bar
with two languages installed; hover and select a divider and a spacer in edit mode.

## 62. The sound panel keeps no height (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "sound flyout: sound should not have a flyout height as configuration option, always automatic".

- **Per kind, not a case in Settings.** A kind with no `WidgetInfo.FlyoutHeights` has no height to
  choose: no "Flyout height" card (`FlyoutHeightRow.Shows`), no look from Settings, and a height in a
  file — a preset, one's own, an old `flyoutRows` — reads as Automatic and is never written again
  (`WidgetItem.Normalize`). Sound now keeps none; another kind opts out the same way. The dock opens
  the sound panel with no height and `SoundPage` lays the mixer out with none: as tall as the apps
  playing, up to the most a flyout may be, scrolling past it, as Windows' own panel. §53's table row
  for Sound is history.
- **Others looked at, left as they are**: the keyboard's layouts and the VPN connections are short
  lists for most people, but somebody with many layouts or a work VPN list can have more than fit,
  and a set height is what keeps those from growing to the screen's edge; the network's and
  Bluetooth's pages are the same kind of quick-settings panel as sound, but their lists (networks
  around, paired devices) run long where the mixer rarely does. Each could opt out the same way.

Tests: `FlyoutHeightTests.SoundKeepsNoHeight` (a preset, one's own, an old count: read as Automatic,
never written), `OnlyTheKindsWithAListKeepIt`, `FlyoutHeightRowTests.TheCardIsTheKindsOwnDeclaration`
(the card is the kind's `FlyoutHeights` and nothing else), `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheMixerIsAlwaysAsTallAsItsApps`
(a height handed to the sound flyout changes nothing). Picture: `quick-sound-automatic-5-150-dark.png`.

## 63. Colour pickers as Windows has them, with presets (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "generally the color pickers should follow windows style, they should also have preset
colors for example." §60's swatch opened WinUI's bare `ColorPicker`; it now opens what Windows 11's
Settings > Personalization > Colors shows (`Controls\ColorSwatch.cs`, `Logic\ColorPresets.cs`).

- **The flyout**, under the swatch: the colour's name and the mode; **Automatic** as a row of its own
  first (a 40 DIP tile of Windows' own colour, `ColorRows.Start`, "Automatic / Follows Windows", the
  tick on it while nothing is chosen); **Recent colors**, one row, only when there are some; the
  **grid**, eight 40 x 40 rounded tiles a row with 4 between (a `GridView`, arrow keys and selection
  for free), each the colour over a checkerboard, the chosen one ticked with a check in white or
  black, whichever stands out (`ColorPresets.InkOn`), and named by its colour in words for a screen
  reader; and **Custom colors** with a "View colors" button. A tile is the colour at once and saved at
  once, the flyout staying open so colours can be tried one after another on the bar.
- **View colors** opens a `ContentDialog`, "Pick a custom color", as Windows' own: the `ColorPicker`
  with the box spectrum, its slider, the alpha slider and box, the hex box and "More" for the
  channels, starting at the colour chosen or at Windows' own. Live on the bar as it moves (saved once
  it rests, as before); **Done** keeps it and makes it the first recent colour, **Cancel** or Esc puts
  back what was there, Automatic included.
- **Which presets** (`ColorPresets.For`): the backgrounds (taskbar, cards, flyouts) get 24
  backgrounds — eight neutrals, eight deep tints, eight richer ones, a hue a column (blue, teal,
  green, olive, brown, red, plum, purple) — dark for the dark mode and pale for the light one, so the
  mode's own text stays readable on every one; with the automatic colour's alpha (the bar's 70 %,
  the flyout's 90 % dark and 85 % light; the cards 70 %, their automatic dark 5 % would hide any
  colour), so a pick over Acrylic still lets the blur through. Windows' accent colours were left out
  there: as a whole bar they shout and fight the white or black text. The lines (card outline,
  separators) and the highlight get **Windows' 48 accent colours** in its order (6 rows of 8): the
  lines opaque, the highlight at 35 %, since it lies under text and the open app's icon. Anything
  else is "View colors" away.
- **Recent colors** (`BarColors.Recent`, `"colors": { "recent": ["#AARRGGBB", ...] }`): the colours
  the dialog was left with by Done, newest first, each once (picked again it moves to the front), at
  most a row (8), shared by every colour and both modes as Windows shares its own. A preset or
  Automatic is never added: it is a click away already. Read tolerantly (`ColorListConverter`: an
  entry that is not text is left out, anything but a list is none; an entry that is not a colour is
  skipped); kept when a colour goes back to Automatic and by "Reset all", as Windows keeps its own.
  The dock draws none of them, and a change of them alone is a colours-only change
  (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`), so nothing is built again.
- "Use automatic" in the flyout went (the Automatic row is it); "Reset all" stays in the expander's
  header. Strings `settings.appearance.custom.{recent,windowsColors,backgrounds,viewColors,pickTitle,done,automaticDescription,selected}`
  in five languages.

rows after it for every colour and mode, each colour's kind of presets and their alpha, the tick on
Automatic, on exactly a preset and on none for one's own, the recent colours leading, once, one

all", the tick's colour), `BarColorThemeTests.RecentColorsAloneAreNoRebuild`. Picture:

## 64. Choosing another desktop switches to it (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "desktop switching does not work".

- **Not the interface.** On 26200.9457 the shell's `IVirtualDesktopManagerInternal` is still the 24H2
  one `DesktopControl` uses: `QueryService` hands out 53F5CA0B, `GetCount`, `GetCurrentDesktop`
  and `FindDesktop` answer at their slots, and a found desktop answers to IVirtualDesktop 3F07F4BE
  (checked read-only, nothing switched). Karpo's windows are on every desktop.
- **The foreground was.** Choosing a row closed the list the way every popup closes, giving the
  foreground back to the window that had it, then switched. That window is on the desktop being
  left, and a window of another desktop activated as the switch goes makes Windows switch straight
  back to it: nothing seemed to happen. A desktop's row now closes the list leaving the foreground
  with Karpo (`QuickFlyout.GivesFocusBack`), and `Desktops.Go` hands it on in the right order:
  straight through the shell, then to the window in front on the desktop arrived at (the first of
  the z-order that is on it, cloaked or not, since the switch is still uncloaking it; none: the
  desktop itself, `GetShellWindow`), as Windows' own Ctrl+Win+arrow leaves it. Where the interface
  can't be used, the foreground goes back to the desktop showing first and the keys follow, as
  typed. The row of the desktop showing just gives its foreground back. "New desktop" (Ctrl+Win+D)
  and the layouts' rows close as before.

Tests: `DesktopSwitchTests` (the order of a straight switch and of the keys, the desktop showing, a
desktop not there, ids the registry has not written yet, the window chosen for the foreground, which
rows keep it from the window they came from), with a stand-in for the shell. By hand: two or more
desktops with windows open on each; choose another desktop in the switcher's list (the desktop
changes and stays, its last window has the keyboard, the widget names it); one with nothing open;
the current row (nothing moves, the keyboard goes back to the window you were in); "New desktop".

## 65. The selected widget's flyout stands open in edit mode (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "when clicking on a widget it should actually also open its flyout when it is selected as
individual widget", and of the clock: "when clicking on it is should open the settings but it should
also open the flyout. the flyout should basically be kept open as long as the widget is selected."

- **The rule** (`SelectedFlyout`, apart from any window): one widget selected alone in edit mode, on a
  bar or a place, whose kind has a flyout of Karpo's own (the dock's table, `Dock.HasFlyout`, or the
  list of choices the keyboard's and a listing switch's click hand back) has its flyout open, from
  where it stands. Another selected alone: that one's instead, or none. Several, none, a block
  carried, a selection rectangle being drawn, or edit mode ending: none. It follows every way the
  selection changes (`ShowSelection`): a click, Enter, Ctrl/Shift+click, the rectangle once let go,
  Delete, a paste. The settings app cannot select a widget on the bar, so there is nothing to follow
  from that side.
- **Never**: Windows' own panels (Start, Search, task view, the widgets board...) and acts (a pin, a
  switch that flips) — no flyout of Karpo's; and `SelectedFlyout.Never`: the notification
  list, whose opening marks everything seen; a folder (grid or list), whose click in edit mode opens
  the folder itself, arranged (`EditClicks`); the tray, whose click is one of its icons'.
- **Opened as a look** (`OpenLook`, `FlyoutHost.Previewing`, the same as §59's): no focus taken, nothing
  of Windows' closed, standing through the settings app the click brought up having the keys, through
  presses on it and on the dim, and through presses on the bar (`Dock.PressedOn` leaves a look alone
  in edit mode; the press on another widget selects it, and its flyout takes the place). The settings
  app stands over everything in edit mode, so when a window comes to the front the look is brought
  over it again (`FlyoutHost.RaiseLooks`). It opens like the click outside edit mode, beside its bar,
  never over it nor over the edit bar (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`, §58).
- **Live**: opened again where the widget's settings in the file change (a change in Settings, read
  back by `Apply`) or where it stands now (a Ctrl+arrow, a rebuild). Closed while a block is carried
  (it would hang off where the widget stood) and opened again once it lands (`SELECTED_FLYOUT`, after
  the landing is applied).
- **One flyout, one owner.** While Settings has a look at a height (§59), the look has the flyout: the
  selected widget's own at the height being set, or another widget's; a selection changed to another
  widget ends it. When the look ends, the selection's comes back at the height the file keeps.
- Outside edit mode nothing changes.

Tests: `SelectedFlyoutTests` (one alone opens, another switches or has none, several, none, carried
and out of edit mode have none, the kinds that open, no panel of Windows' nor an act, the kinds wrong
to open), `FlyoutOffscreenTests.TheSelectedClocksFlyoutStandsClearOfTheEditBarAndThroughTheSettingsApp`
(the clock from a top bar right under the edit bar: under the edit bar and off its bar, no focus, open
through another window's focus and a press elsewhere, where a click's closes). By hand: edit mode, click
the clock — Settings on its page and the clock's flyout both open, the flyout staying while you work in
Settings; change the clock's options and see the flyout follow; click the weather (its flyout instead),
a separator (none), Ctrl+click a second (none); drag the clock (closed, back where it lands); a top bar
(under the edit bar); Escape (gone).

## 66. The tray and the open apps, twice on a bar (2026-10-09)

The person: "if i place the tray icons widget twice they only show once. (in the first one)", and the
same of the apps. A layout may hold a kind more than once (two in one bar, the Main and Top rows, two
displays), and both kinds were written as one of a kind on a bar: the layout gave the second tray its
room but the scene drew the first's icons only (`Layout.GetPart(BarKind.Tray)`, one set of sprites,
one `Hit.Tray(i)` that names the first tray), and the open apps were counted into the first Apps
widget alone (`Layout.Measure`: "the Apps part is one of a kind on a bar") — the second got none and
the first got both copies' buttons.

- **The tray, twice, is the whole tray twice**: the same icons in the same order, each tray with its
  own chevron where *it* needs one (`Layout.TrayChevronOf`: a tray of a set size too short for the
  icons has one, an Automatic one beside it has none), its own hover, click, menu and popups (the
  icon rects an app asks for are those of the tray it was pressed or rested in,
  `PublishTrayRects(window, at)`), and the overflow opens from the chevron clicked
  (`Dock.ChevronOf`, kept on the open overflow's `Pending.Hit`, so it follows that tray when it
  shows again). A drag reads the tray under the pointer (`TrayDrags.OnTrays`: the one the pointer is
  in before one whose room past its last icon takes a new one); that tray opens the gap, the one the
  icon was taken from keeps its place open, and the drop writes the one shared order, which both
  trays then show. The scene keeps each tray's sprites and glides under its own key
  (`tray:<tray key>|<icon>`). The keyboard (Win+B) and a screen reader reach every icon of both; a
  bar with one tray keeps the bare hits and ids it had (`Layout.InTray`). Taking one of two trays off
  the bar in edit mode leaves the other its icons.
- **The open apps, twice, are every open app in each Apps widget**: `Dock.TilesFor` makes each Apps
  widget its own buttons (`Tile.Apps`, the widget's key), and `Layout.TileCountsOf` counts each button
  into the part it names (one that names none is the first Apps widget's). Every bar still shows every
  window (§40), so on other bars and displays each Apps widget follows that same rule. Each copy is a
  button of its own for previews, the jump list, attention (both bounce), progress and badges, and a
  drag of a running app moves the widget it stands in. "Pin to taskbar" puts the pin before the Apps
  widget it was chosen from. Win+N counts an app once on a bar: the copy takes no number
  (`AppNumbers.Numbered`). A bar too short for both copies gives up the second's buttons first, and
  "…" stands where they went, at the end of the Apps widget that lost the last of them (`Home` in the
  layout's `FitTiles`); its list names each app or window once (`Dock.OverflowedTiles`).
- **An app pinned in one place and open**: its windows are its pin's, merged with it, and no Apps
  widget of that display's layout shows it again — not a second one on the same bar, nor one on the
  other row. A display whose layout does not pin it shows it among its open apps like any other. The
  pin is where the person said the app goes; showing it again as an unpinned button would be two
  buttons for one app on one bar.

Tests: `TwiceOverTests` (both trays whole, hit and drawn in their own room; each tray's own chevron;
the overflow from the tray clicked; a drop read in the tray under the pointer; one tray taken off
leaves the other its icons; the keyboard's stops and the screen reader's elements in both; each
button counted into the part it names; both Apps widgets showing the open apps, hit in their own
widget; the second copy giving way first with "…" in it; one Apps widget keeping "…" at its end;
Win+N counting an app once). Pictures: `twice-over-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (Start, the open apps
twice, the tray twice with both chevrons) and `twice-over-lit-…` (the second tray's second icon lit).
By hand: two trays — hover, click, right-click and double-click an icon in the second (its app's popup
or menu opens by that icon), open the overflow from each chevron, drag an icon within and between the
two and into each overflow; two Apps widgets — click, preview, jump list and Win+1… in both, an app
asking for attention, a bar narrowed until "…" appears.

## 67. A folder's face (2026-10-09, branch folder-faces)

The person: *"for a folder you should be able to select the 'face' which could be a clock or a
bluetooth icon, or just a fixed icon etc. lets start with just what we have at the moment + the
clock and calendar face"*, and *"when you select a face there should basically spawn more options
for the face style, face look etc."*. A folder's button on the bar is its **face** and, where it
shows one, its name beside it. "Icon or content" (`FolderButton`) is folded into it: those are two
faces now, beside the clock and the calendar.

- **A face is a descriptor** (`Karpo.Core\FolderFaces.cs`): `FaceInfo` — an id the file stores and
  its options, each a `FaceOption` of a key, a kind (switch, choice, text, time zone), a default, a
  choice's words and, where it applies only sometimes, the option and value it follows (`When`).
  Its words are found by its ids (`core.face.<face>.title`, `.blurb`, `core.face.<face>.<option>.title`,
  `.description`, `core.face.<face>.<option>.<choice>`), so a record holds no text. The faces, in
  the order offered: **What's inside** (the default), **Its icon**, **Clock**, **Calendar**, and
  since §80 **Weather**, since §88 **Wi-Fi** and **Bluetooth**, since §90 **Sound**.
- **The file**: `FolderOptions.Face` is `{ "kind": "clock", "options": { "seconds": true, "hours":
  "twentyFour", "label": "Tokyo" } }` — JSON's own values, only what somebody set. Read through the
  descriptor (`FolderFace.Switch`, `.Text`, `ClockFace.Read`): a face this build does not know is
  kept and read as What's inside, and an option it does not know, a value of the wrong kind or a
  choice that is not one of its words is kept and read as the default, so a file goes through an
  older build unharmed. No migration: the old `"button"` key is read past (configs on this branch
  are reset anyway).
- **The bar** (`Karpo.Dock\Islands\FaceDrawings.cs`): each face is an `IFaceDrawing` found by the
  same id — `Measure` (its length along the bar from the settings and templates alone, and whether
  it is a glyph's square), `Paint`, `Reading` (what it shows now), `Seconds`, `Tooltip`.
  `FolderIsland` lays the face and the name out (`Parts`, shared with `WidgetShapes.Folder`, so the
  size and the drawing cannot disagree): a square face with no name is one square cell, as a folder
  always was; a face of text is as long as its widest reading with the text widgets' room at its
  ends — content-sized, never whole cells.
- **Ticking without a rebuild**: the dock's clock tick (`Dock.TickClock`, on the minute, or every
  second while a face shows seconds or a countdown runs — `SecondsTick` counts `FaceSeconds`) and a
  countdown changing (`TimersChanged`) call `FolderIsland.FaceTick` on every folder on the bar: the
  face's `Reading` is compared with what was last painted and the cell is painted again in place
  where it changed (`CellIsland.Redraw`), and nothing else happens. A face is measured on its
  widest, so the redraw never finds another size, and the bar is never built again for a minute
  (the trap `ClockSizes` fixed for the scene's clock, a485e3d, cannot arise: there is no measuring
  of what is shown at all). Windows' clock being set (`WM_TIMECHANGE`) ticks it too.
- **Clock** — the time as the clock entry drew it (§12.5), and only the clock (§76): *Show seconds*, *Clock* (as the region writes it, 12-hour, 24-hour: the
  region's own pattern, or the one set in Karpo's formats, with its hours changed —
  `ClockFace.Pattern`), *Time zone*, *Label* ("Tokyo"), and *Show what a timer has left* (on). Across
  a horizontal bar one row at every height: the time, its colons the taskbar's U+2236, then "· label" and what a timer or focus session **in the folder** has left (the clock
  entry's own countdown, now the folder's widgets'), the running one first. Its room is the widest
  morning and evening of its format and — only where the folder
  holds a timer or a focus widget and the switch is on — five figures for the countdown, so a
  countdown starting moves nothing. Down a vertical bar the time over its second line where both
  fit, else the time, else the time turned bottom-to-top (§12.4). The tooltip is the long date (and
  the zone). The clock entry (`BarKind.Clock`, drawn by the scene) went with the clock preset
  (§73); the face does everything it did, and `ClockSizes` went with it.
- **Calendar** — two looks: *The date as text* (with a *Date* choice: the short date as under
  Windows' clock, "09.10.2026", or the day and the date, "Fri, 09.10.", as the calendar entry has
  it), measured over the 28th of every month and every weekday; and *A calendar page with the day*:
  an outline with rounded corners, a band of the accent along its top and the day's number in
  semibold, 70 % of the cell (larger than a glyph, so the number reads at 32 DIP), its outline
  thickening with the page. Down a vertical bar the text is the calendar entry's stacked pair. The
  date is read on the minute's tick, so it turns over at midnight; the tooltip is the long date.
- **Settings** (`FolderPage`, `FolderRows`): the **Face** section (since §86 a section of its own,
  the dropdown in its header) has a row per option of the face, made from the descriptor (a
  toggle, a dropdown, a text box, the time zones), shown while its `When` holds (the calendar's
  *Date* only for text). Switching faces and back keeps what was set on the page
  (`FolderRows.FaceFor`, remembered for as long as the page is open). The icon face's body has
  the icon; what is inside and the icon have "Show the name beside it" as their last row, and the
  bar draws a name beside those two alone (`FaceInfo.Named`, `FolderOptions.NameShown`; §86).
- **Adding a face** (a Bluetooth icon, say): a `FaceInfo` in `FolderFaces.All`; an `IFaceDrawing` in
  `FaceDrawings.All` (`FolderFaceTests.EveryFaceHasADrawing` holds the two registries together); its
  words in the five languages. Nothing else names a face. A face that reads live state draws it in
  `Paint`, says it in `Reading`, and is measured from its settings.

Tests: `FolderFaceTests` (the file's words and values round-trip; what is not known is kept and read
as the default; each face's options and defaults; every face has a drawing; the hours patterns; the
size the same at every time and day; every face and look inside its cell, centred, at 32–64 DIP, 100
and 150 %, dark, light and high contrast, across and down the bar; a clock painted again in place on
its minute or second and not otherwise, never asking for a rebuild; the calendar turning over at
midnight; the room for a timer in the folder), `FolderRowsTests` (the dropdown, the rows per face,
switching back, every word in every language), `FolderPreviewTests` (unknown faces). Pictures:
`folder-faces-<40|48>-<dark|light>.png` and `folder-faces-more.png` (32 and 64 DIP, 150 %, high
contrast, a vertical bar). By hand: a folder switched through the four faces in Settings and the bar
following at once; a clock face with seconds ticking smoothly and the bar not flickering; a timer in a
clock folder counting down on the face; the calendar at midnight; a vertical bar; a custom bar colour.

## 68. A flyout made of widgets: toggles, actions, the month, the time (2026-10-09)

Four list widgets, so a folder can be what a flyout was (the folder-faces branch; the clock preset is
built from them). Each is a `ListKind` with its own island, its words in the five languages, and,
where it has options, its Settings page.

- **Toggles** (`toggles`, `TogglesTile`, `Karpo.Core\Toggles.cs`). The person: "one list line holding
  several toggle icons … The user picks which toggles and their order. Icon-only row (wraps to more rows
  if many). No details/arrow: pure on/off." Each toggle is a button of Windows 11's quick settings
