  without its words: the control fill and outline while off, the accent with the on-accent glyph while
  on, the disabled ink where this PC has not got it. The buttons stand on the list's gutters on one grid
  — as many to a row as fit at 48 DIP, sharing the row evenly, the rest wrapped in the same columns
  (`TogglesTile.Lay`). A click switches that toggle and the folder stays open; the button under the
  pointer lights; its tooltip says its name and state ("Wi-Fi: on"); Left and Right walk the buttons and
  Enter or Space switches the one ringed. The toggles are Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (their radios, as their
  flyouts switch them: `RadioToggle`) and every one-button widget whose click switches it (airplane
  mode, the hotspot, energy saver, night light, do not disturb, the VPN, rotation lock, spatial sound),
  read from the one-button widgets' own data sources (`SwitchData`), so a row and a button on the bar
  read one switch. Not there: live captions, nearby sharing, accessibility, project and cast, whose
  state Windows tells no app; location and mobile data, for which Karpo has no switch yet. Settings: the
  toggles shown, each with its gripper and Remove, dragged into their order (§157), and "Add a toggle"
  with the ones not shown. The buttons stand in the middle of a line taller than they are (§157).
- **Actions** (`actions`, `ActionsTile`, `Karpo.Core\SettingsActions.cs`): a flyout's footer — the left
  action's name as a hyperlink button on the gutter, the right action's glyph as a subtle icon button
  against the other gutter, its name in its tooltip. An action is a page of Windows' Settings from a
  curated list (its `ms-settings:` address, Settings' glyph for it and its name in Settings' words);
  either slot may be empty. Each opens its page at once, which takes the focus and so closes the folder.
  Settings: two lists, "Link" and "Button", "None" first. A new line opens Date & time.

  **Reworked 2026-10-10.** The person: "the actions widget should show both actions as text … in
  normal color and not primary color … it should not even have a resizing option as it should be one
  row height all the time." So both slots are subtle text buttons: each action's name in the text
  colour (`QuickTheme.Text`, not the link's accent), the subtle fill under the pointer and high
  contrast's on-hover ink, as `ButtonStyle.Subtle` draws. The left's words stand on the gutter, the
  right's end on the other, 8 DIP between the two buttons. Where both names do not fit, the shorter
  keeps every word if it takes no more than half the room and the other is cut with an ellipsis, else
  each has half (`ActionsTile.Split`); a name cut short says itself whole in its tooltip, a whole one
  has none. Keys as before (Left/Right walk the two, Enter/Space open). No pressed fill: a line that
  takes the press itself has to declare a drag of its own (`InteractionTests`), which is not worth it
  for a click that opens Settings and closes the folder at once. The line is always one row of the list
  (§76, `ListWidget.FixedHeight`), so no height card. Settings calls the two lists "Left" and "Right"
  ("The text button at the start/end of the line"). Presets that hold an actions line (§73, §80) are
  unchanged: their slots are page ids, as before. Tests: `ActionsLineTests` (the split, the kind's fixed
  height in the file, the plan and Settings, both names in the text colour dark and light, cut names'
  tooltips), `FlyoutLinesTests.BothButtonsSayAndOpenTheirPages`.

  **Inside the card (2026-10-11).** The person: "the action buttons are not properly spaced from the
  widget borders, they directly touch it." The words stood on the gutter, so the button's fill (11 DIP
  of padding round them) began 1 px from the card's edge and ran 4 DIP from its top and bottom. Now the
  buttons are the card's controls, as the toggles' boxes and the month's arrows are: the left button
  stands on the gutter, the right ends on the other, each 28 DIP tall (at 100 % text) in the 40 DIP row,
  so 6 DIP of card above and below; the words 11 DIP inside their button, 8 DIP between the buttons.
  `ActionsLineTests.TheButtonsKeepTheCardsPadding` holds it at five widths, 100/150 % scale and
  100/150/225 % text; the sheet `list-form-actions-*.png` shows each button under the pointer.

  **Windows' footer band (2026-10-16).** The person: "the action buttons just look a little off." They
  were words floating on the body. Windows' quick settings end in a band, measured (dark, 150 %): a
  1 DIP hairline (#191919) over a darker band (#1C1C1C on the body's #242424) across the flyout, the
  flyout's rounded corners its own; subtle buttons 12 DIP in from the flyout's sides and 6 DIP from the
  band's top and bottom, a 16 DIP glyph in each, lit #0F white (#292929 on the band). The calendar's
  footer is the body's colour under the same hairline, its header the darker band. So the line is that
  band, always, wherever it stands: it is a flyout's footer, and the presets put it last, where it is
  the folder's bottom edge as Windows' is (the card's clip rounds its corners). The band and the
  hairline are shades of black over the body (`QuickTheme.Footer`, `FooterLine`: 22 % and 31 % dark,
  4 % and 8 % light, the light ones Windows' #EEEEEE and a hairline a step darker on #F9F9F9,
  unmeasured), so a chosen flyout colour or the glass darkens alike; a quick settings page's footer
  band (`Backdrop`, `BackdropKind.Footer`) wears the same. The row stays one row (40 DIP; Windows' band
  is 48) at the person's 2026-10-10 asking, so the 28 DIP buttons keep Windows' 6 DIP above and below.
  Each button is now Settings' glyph for its page (16 DIP, 11 DIP in) and its name 8 DIP after it —
  Windows' are glyph only; the names stay, as asked on 2026-10-10. Where a name would keep fewer than
  about two letters, every button is its glyph alone in a 28 DIP square, its name in its tooltip
  (`ActionsPlan.Bare`). Tests: `ActionsLineTests.TheLineIsAFooterBand`, `TheButtonsKeepTheCardsPadding`
  (the glyphs), `FlyoutSurfaceTests.TheFooterIsWindowsOwn`, `AButtonLitOnTheBandIsWindowsOwn`.

  **Premade actions (2026-10-10, §85).** The add list offers an actions line set up already under
  "Actions", in its submenu: Clock, Calendar, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Sound and Notification actions. Two more targets in
  the curated list for them: "Add device" (Settings' Add a device dialog, the address Bluetooth's
  quick settings page opens) and "Volume mixer" (`ms-settings:apps-volume`).
- **Month calendar** (`month`, `MonthTile`): the calendar of Windows 11's clock flyout — the month and
  year with the two arrows that step it, the weekdays from the region's first day (`Nls.FirstDayOfWeek`),
  six weeks always (the days either side quieter), today ringed in the accent, the day picked filled with
  it. A click on a day publishes it as the folder's day (§9, "Channels"); the wheel steps the month; the
  arrows, Page Up/Down and Home move the day picked and publish it.
- **Time and date** (`timeHeader`, `TimeHeaderTile`): the top of the clock's flyout — the time at 34 DIP
  with its seconds, in tabular figures sized once for the widest the format reads (`TimeFit`), over the
  long date in the longest form that fits; no glyph, on the list's gutter, quiet under the pointer. The
  clock's own line (`ClockTile`) stays the clock widget's list form; this is the flyout's header, which
  the list did not have. The folder ticks every second while it holds one.
- **The agenda follows the day.** The calendar's line, where a month beside it has a day picked, is
  that day's: its page that day, headed Today, Tomorrow, Yesterday or its weekday, and every event of
  the day under it; with no day picked, today picked, or its switch off, today and what is coming, as
  before. Its data is the same store.

**Tooltips in a folder** (`FolderFlyout.Tips.cs`). A widget whose parts are icons names them:
`CellIsland.CardTip` (none by default) answers the part under the pointer and its text, and the folder
shows the edit rail's kind of tip above it after Windows' hover time, moving at once from part to part.
A folder has no screen-reader tree yet (`FlyoutUia.cs`), so the tooltips and the keys are what these
lines offer beyond the pointer.

Tests: `TogglesAndActionsTests` (defaults, the order and an emptied row round-tripping, unknown and
repeated toggles dropped, moving, every toggle described, an emptied action slot staying empty, unknown
pages emptied, every curated page a valid `ms-settings:` address with a Fluent glyph and a name in every
language), `FlyoutLinesTests` (a click and the keys switch a toggle, the grid wraps on the gutters, the
link and the button open their pages, the month's first weekday per region, the channels in §9).
Pictures: `list-form-toggles-<dark|light>.png`, `list-form-actions-…`, `list-form-month-…` (the clock's
flyout as widgets; a day picked; a day with nothing), `list-form-month-<monday|sunday|saturday>.png`.
By hand: switch each toggle from a folder (Wi-Fi and Bluetooth may ask Windows' permission the first
time); hover them for the tooltips; open a page from each slot; pick days in a month beside an agenda,
step months with the arrows and the wheel, walk the days with the keys; close and reopen the folder.

## 69. Screen time is back, as lines of a list (2026-10-09)

Screen time was deleted whole on 2026-09-26 (the person's ruling then, §9 "What is left of the
conversions"); the day before they had said of its pieces in a folder that it "just does not feel as
good as before" — the app list drew nothing (its rows were lifted a panel's height off the card) and
nothing lit under the pointer. It comes back on the folder-faces branch the way that branch builds
everything: list widgets, and a ready-made folder of them on the bar instead of an entry with its
own flyout.

- **One source, always counting** (`ScreenTime\ScreenTimeTracker.cs`, as the readings' §55): the dock
  starts it with itself (never on an isolated config: a test or `--smoke` reads and writes nobody's
  files) and stops it with itself, whether or not a line shows it, so a line added in the afternoon has
  the morning. The counting is `ScreenTimeCount`, pure and handed the time and the last input: time
  counts while the session is unlocked, a display on, the PC awake and somebody's input within five
  minutes (`IdleMinutes`, one for the PC now — the old per-widget "idle after" is gone), for the app
  whose window is in front (a WinEvent hook; a Store app in its frame is the app inside, a packaged
  app its AUMID), cut at each local midnight. **What the messages miss, the minute's look puts
  right**: the lock and unlock, sleep and wake and the display going dark arrive as messages, now
  heard at the top of the window procedure whatever the dock is doing (a menu's loop used to swallow
  them); and each look asks Windows whether the session is locked, and takes input after the PC slept
  or went dark as being back — a lost message used to stop the count for the rest of the day.
- **The same files, read as they are** (`ScreenTime\ScreenTimeHistory.cs`, restored from c8a9db1^
  unchanged in what it reads and writes): `screentime.json` (today, the shape since revision 8 and the
  top-level fields from before it) and `screentime-history.json` (every other day, 90 kept, the file
  it replaces kept as `.bak` and read when the file is broken). Days counted under another idle time
  (an island once set to ten minutes) go on as the five minutes' where the five has none, and every
  idle time a file has is written back.
- **Two lines** (`ScreenTime\ScreenTimeLine.cs`, `ListKind.ScreenTime`, `ScreenTimeApps`, list only,
  under "System": "Time and information" would have run past the catalogue's twelve), each drawn for its height (§9, "A line at every height"):
  - *Screen time* (`screenTime`): one row, the widget's name — or the day, where the folder shows
    another — and the day's total, the last two weeks behind the row as the readings' graph is; two
    rows, the daily average (the week ending at the day, over the days used) under it; from three, the
    day's name with ‹ › on the trailing gutter, the total large with the daily average beside it, and
    the fortnight as an area under a line edge to edge under them (§24's `Sparkline` and
    `GraphBackdrop`), the shown day marked with a dot, a day lit under the pointer and shown by a click.
    The fortnight ends today, or at the day shown where that is older, so a click inside it moves the
    dot and not the graph.
  - *App usage* (`screenTimeApps`): a row per app of the day, most used first, a list row each: the
    app's logo in the list's icon column (the Start menu's name and logo, `ScreenTimeNames`, looked up
    once per app), its name over a bar of its share of the top app's time, its time on the trailing
    gutter; the last slot saying how many more (`WidgetFill`, "3 other apps"); one row, the top app.
    The row under the pointer lights (`LightsItsRows`: the line as a whole does not), and a click
    picks the app (see "The folder's app" below; it opened the app until 2026-10-10). It is as tall as
    the day has apps where nobody set a height.
- **The folder's day** (folder-faces item 6; §9, "Channels"). Both lines follow the Day channel
  (`ListWidget.Follows`), and the total publishes it (`Publishes`): ‹ ›, the day's name (back to
  today) and a day of the graph publish the day shown, so the apps follow the total, and a month
  calendar or an agenda in the same folder follows it as the total follows theirs. Stepping stays
  between the first day counted and today; a day set from outside the record (the calendar's next
  week, a month before the history) is shown as it is, "No apps" and a zero, not moved. Each line has
  the follower's switch, "Follow the folder's day": switched off it shows today, or — the total — the
  day it stepped to itself, which it still publishes, as a month switched off does. The folder forgets
  the day when it closes.
- **On the bar: a ready-made folder** (`Presets`, `screenTimeGroup`, "Screen time"): a list folder
  with the screen-time glyph as its button, the total four rows over the apps, eight rows Fixed
  (2026-10-10, below) — an ordinary folder
  anybody could have made, editable afterwards — not a taskbar kind with a flyout of its own. Glyph:
  Segoe Fluent's screen with a clock (U+F182); the font has no hourglass.
- **Strings**: `core.widget.screenTime*`, `core.preset.screenTimeGroup.*`, `widget.screenTime.*`
  (today, yesterday, the average, the durations, "No apps", how many more) in five languages.

Tests: `ScreenTimeCountTests` (each app while in front, away after the idle time, the lock, the sleep,
a dark display, a lost unlock, a lost lock, a lost wake, midnight, a clock set back, the day from the
logon, the snapshot, the days past the kept ones, another idle time's files; the files Karpo wrote, read
from a made-up copy of their shape, written back in it, read from the backup, a day after the live
file's), `ScreenTimeHistoryTests` (restored: summer time, midnights that jump, merging, pruning, the
files' migrations), `ScreenTimeLinesTests` (UI: every height of both lines at three scales and both
text sizes inside its line with nothing on anything; one row says the total and the top app; the
folder's day followed, stepped, chosen on the graph and forgotten on closing; a month's click followed;
a step published to a month and an agenda; a line switched off from the day; the step's bounds; the
graph's fortnight and the average; rows and steps lit under the pointer, a row opening its app; the
lines' own heights). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `screentime-total[-light].png`,
`screentime-apps[-light].png` (every height at 150 %), `screentime-folder-<dark|light>.png` (the
ready-made folder at 100 % and 225 % text, an app's row lit). By hand: the counting over a real day
(lock, sleep, a display timing out, midnight), an app's logo and its click (a Store app, a desktop
app), and the folder on the bar with a month calendar added to it.

**Bars by app (2026-10-10).** The person: "screen time widget should show a bar chart with the
different apps as well". From three rows the total's fortnight is now a bar a day, each split by app,
as Screen Time and Digital Wellbeing draw a week (`ScreenTime\ScreenTimeChart.cs`, drawn by
`ScreenTimeLine`):

- **What is split**: the period's top four apps by their time over the days shown (an app under a
  minute never), most used at a bar's foot; the rest of the day — smaller apps and time counted for
  no app — on top as *Other*, neutral. The data was there: the history has kept each day's apps since
  revision 8. A day an older Karpo kept as a total only (the live file's `earlier`, a history day
  without `apps`) still loads and is one neutral bar. No change to either file.
- **Colours**: a chart palette of eight hues in two sets — Tailwind's 400s for light text, its 600s
  for dark text — chosen by the theme's text, so a flyout colour of one's own (§60) gets the set its
  text is readable on. An app takes the free colour nearest its logo's most common saturated hue
  (its icon's pixels are on the CPU already, 48 × 48 counted per look); a grey logo takes the first
  free one from its key's FNV hash. So no two apps of a chart share a colour, and an app keeps its
  colour on every day and from look to look while the top apps stay the same. High contrast: every
  piece the text's colour, the shown day the highlight's, pieces told apart by a 1-px gap; no legend.
- **The shown day**: full colour with an accent tick under it; every other day at half opacity (one
  layer per bar, so pieces never show a seam). The day under the pointer lights as before, its
  click publishes the day (Channels.Day, §9) as the area's did. Tooltip (`CardTip`): over a piece
  "Browser — 1 h 12 min" (or "Other — …"), elsewhere in the column — or on an unsplit day — the day
  and its total.
- **Room**: the bars stand under the words, not behind them (a stacked bar faded under text reads as
  noise), between the list's gutters, fourteen columns with the last day at the trailing end. The
  legend (swatch and name, the top apps then Other, as many as fit on one line) only where the bars
  keep their least height (36 DIP) beside it; the bars themselves only where they have 12 px. One
  and two rows keep the area behind the row — a stacked bar a few px tall says nothing. The line's
  own height (Automatic, §76) adds the legend's line.
- **Option** (`ScreenTimeOptions`, `"screenTime": { "graph": "area" }` on the line; Settings:
  "Graph", Bars by app / Area): the bars are the default and no options at all, so every existing
  line draws them and writes nothing; the area is the old drawing. An unknown word reads as the bars.

Tests (`ScreenTimeLinesTests`): the top apps and Other (ties, case, the minute, a total under its apps),
old days unsplit (read through `ScreenTimeFiles.Read`), colours (logo hue, grey logos, distinct,
deterministic, the hash, the two sets), a piece's and a column's tooltip and a bar's click publishing
its day, the bars inside their chart and under the words at 1–6 rows × three scales × two text sizes,
the area as an option, the option's file words. Pictures: `screentime-total[-light].png` (now bars),
`screentime-total-area[-light].png`, `screentime-bars-<dark|light|contrast>.png` (older days, a day
picked, a bar lit). By hand: real logos' colours (several blue apps), the tooltip's delay over the
bars, and switching Graph in Settings with the folder open.

**The apps' bars in the chart's colours (2026-10-10, later).** Each app row's share bar was the accent
while the bars over it gave the same app a colour of its own. Now the apps' line colours each bar as
the chart does: both lines take one ranking, the fortnight's chart for the day shown
(`ScreenTimeLine.ChartOf`, the same days as the total's graph, so the same top four), and one
assignment of colours (`SlotsOf`) and one ink (`PartInk`), so the two lines of a folder cannot
disagree. An app outside the chart's top four — the line shows every app of the day, the chart four —
is *Other*'s grey, which is where the chart counts its time: the next free palette colour would be a
colour the chart never shows for it, and one a top app may take on another fortnight. The colours
are the data's, not the total line's look: the apps' line keeps them where the total draws the area,
has no room for bars, or is not in the folder. High contrast: the shown day's highlight, as the
shown day's bar is (so as before, the accent). Tests: `TheAppsBarsAreTheChartsColours` (parts and
inks equal to the chart's for the same app, today and another day, with and without the total;
Other one grey, the top four apart, never the accent; the drawn bar read back off the pixels, dark,
light and high contrast). Picture: `screentime-folder-<dark|light>.png`.

**The folder's app (2026-10-10, later).** The person: "for the screen time widgets, when you click on
an application it should not open it but select it, also when you hover over it should show the hover
state, now, this does not get shared with other widgets yet but it should. both states, hover and
selected." Both lines publish and follow the folder's **App** and **App hover** (§9, "Channels"):

- **A click picks, never opens.** An app's row, or a top app's piece of a bar, picks that app; a
  second click on it lets it go, Escape too (the first Escape; the second closes the folder). A piece
  of another day's bar picks its app *and* shows that day, so a click on a bar still moves the day as
  it did; on the day shown a second click lets the app go. "Other" and the bar's empty part are the
  day's, as before. The apps' line asks nothing of the dock any more (`CellAct.Nothing`;
  `Dock.FolderForward` has no screen-time case). **Opening** is the right click's: both lines' menus
  have "Open *app*" (`WidgetAct.OpenApp`: the app under the pointer, else the one picked; no row for
  no app or one with no pin to open), which the dock carries out by the pins' one rule — its windows
  forward, else started — never the shell's open of the path, which would start a second copy.
- **The pointer on an app** — a row, or its piece of a bar — is App hover while it is there, taken
  back as it leaves (`ScreenTimeLine.Point`): the bars light that app's pieces on every day and dim the
  rest a little; the apps' line lights its row even when the pointer is in the bars.
- **The app picked**: the bars draw its pieces whole on every day and the rest dimmed more (one layer
  per bar as before, the pieces' own alpha inside it, `Emphasis`); its legend entry in the text's
  colour, the others' swatches dimmed. The total is the app's: its time on the day shown, large; beside
  it the app's name over "of 6 h 48 min" (the day's total) where the daily average stood — the name
  cut to the room, the figure measured at its widest shape so nothing moves as the minutes change; one
  row, the app's name and its time; two rows, "of …" under them. The apps' line marks its row as a
  Windows list marks its selection: the selected fill and the accent's 3-px pill at the row's leading
  edge, a lighter fill with the pointer on it too (`RowState`); the rows' plates reach to 4 DIP short of
  the line's edges so the pill clears the logo. An app inside "Other" lights "Other" in the bars,
  where its time is; an older day's unsplit bar is no app's and dims.
- **High contrast**: the app's pieces the highlight, the rest grey (`TextDisabled`); the bar column
  under the pointer ringed in the highlight rather than filled (the fill was the highlight, which hid
  the highlighted pieces); the row picked filled with the highlight, its words, glyph and bar in the
  highlight's text; the row pointed at ringed.
- **Opt-out** per line and channel ("Follow the folder's app", "Light the app pointed at"): a line
  switched off keeps a pick of its own and lights only its own pointer, and still publishes both.

Tests (`ScreenTimeLinesTests`): a row's click picks, a second lets go, another row moves the pick, the
click asks the dock for nothing, Escape takes the pick back then nothing, closing forgets it; the
pointer on a row and on a piece publishes and takes back App hover, "Other" and a bar's empty part are
no app, the other line lights it (the bars' emphasis, the row's state); a piece's click picks and shows
its day, a second lets go; the total's words for a pick at full height and one row; the emphasis'
alphas and inks, high contrast's; the row picked and pointed at; a line switched off. `ChannelsTests`:
the two channels, `AppId`'s case, taking back, Escape taking back only the pick, the records.
`WidgetMenuTests`: the menus' "Open", which never goes to the shell. Pictures:
`screentime-app-<dark|light|contrast>.png` (nothing, the pointer on a row, an app picked, an app picked
and another pointed at in the bars). By hand: Escape in the open folder (first lets go, second closes),
the right click's "Open" on a running and a closed app, the hover moving between the two lines with no
flicker, and the two switches in Settings.

### The apps keep their rows' height (2026-10-10)

The person: in the ready-made folder "the app usage should have a default fixed height of 8 rows",
and it "is now trying to stretch its items a bit when there is enough space, this should not be done".

- **The preset's apps line is Fixed, 8 rows** (`Presets`, `screenTimeGroup`; `"height": {"fixed":
  true, "rows": 8}`, §76), so the folder is the same size whatever the day's count; only the preset's
  default — the line's height is edited as any other's afterwards.
- **An app's row is always a list row** (`RowHeight`, 40 DIP at 100 %), whatever the line's height.
  `AppsPlan` shared a taller line's height between the slots, up to a quarter more than a row each;
  now `WidgetFill` counts slots of one row each, more apps where there is room, and what is left under
  the last stays empty. "3 other apps", words alone, takes a folder cell (36 DIP), so a line two rows
  tall still says the top app and how many more. The total's line had no such stretch: its rows keep their heights and the room
  goes to the chart (and the large figure's tier, as every tiered widget's, §9), which is its purpose.

Tests (`ScreenTimeLinesTests`): the preset makes a Fixed 8; the apps' row is the same height at 4 to 12
rows and a taller line shows more apps. Pictures: `screentime-folder-<dark|light>.png` (the ready-made
folder, now with its Fixed 8) and `screentime-apps[-light].png` (every height).
## 70. Grid folders and grid widgets are gone; nothing moves between the taskbar and a folder (2026-10-09)

The person: the grid folders and every grid widget "should be deleted completely", and of moving a
widget between the taskbar and a folder: "even though it would technically be possible ... it does
not work for every widget so i would rather disable it completely".

**What is gone.** The grid folder (`BarKind.Folder`, "Grid folder") and its view (`FolderView.Grid`);
the grid widget registry (`GridKind`, `GridWidgets`, `CellItem.Grid`) and every card drawing
(`GridCard`, `CardFrame`, `SliderCard`, `SoundOutputCard`, `CountdownPlace.Card`, the card halves of the
islands, `CellIsland.CardAtEverySpan`, `TileStyle.ShowTitles`); the grid folder's flyout (spans,
grips, resizing, the column and row steppers, the titles toggle, scrolling across); the library's
Grid page and its rows; the "Grid folder" button of the edit bar; the two grid presets (Quick
settings, Widgets board); the settings app's span card and folder resize (`SpanCard`, `SpanChoice`,
`FolderMoves`, `SettingsModel.ResizeFolder`, `PlaceInFolder`) and the folder page's titles switch;
`WidgetType.Grid` and `WidgetSurface.Grid`; their words in all five languages. §16 is marked removed.

**Two types, and each stays its own.** `WidgetType` is `Bar` or `List`, the type of the place a
widget stands in. `Partners` is no longer a table of one subject's three forms but the gate: a widget
may go to a place of its own type and nowhere else (`Partners.CanBe`, `Partners.Move`). So:

- **Along the bar, between bars and between list folders** a widget moves as before (`Layout.Arrange`,
  `Dock.BetweenFolders` — a line moved as it is, its height and options with it).
- **From the bar into an open folder:** the folder lights no place, and letting go changes nothing;
  the folder says why in its footer, one sentence naming the widget — "Clock can't be moved from the
  taskbar into a folder. Moving widgets between the taskbar and folders isn't supported."
  (`FolderFlyout.Offer`, `Dock.DropIntoOpenFolder`, `Partners.WhyNot`).
- **Out of a folder onto the bar:** the bar opens no gap, and the folder says the other sentence —
  "… can't be moved from a folder onto the taskbar. …" — while it is carried there and when it is let
  go (`Dock.FolderDragged`).
- **Onto a closed folder's button** on the bar: the button is a block like any other; the widget moves
  along the bar past it (no drop target, no spring-loading open).
- **Gone with it:** two widgets dropped on each other no longer make a folder, a folder's "Ungroup" is
  gone, and the settings app has no command that carries a widget across (its folder resize, which
  pushed widgets out onto the bar, went with the grid).
- **The add list** offers only the type of the place it adds to: taskbar entries on the bar, list
  widgets in a list folder (`AddList.Rows`, `Catalogue.On`); a row of the other type adds nothing.
- Files dropped from Explorer onto an open folder still become pin lines.

**Config shape 20.** A file of any older shape — 19, with its grid folders, included — is kept aside
whole as `config.shape<N>.json` and the defaults take its place, as every reset has been (§5); the
in-place read of shapes 17 and 18 (`Config.LayoutsReset`) is gone. A file of shape 20 that still
names a grid folder (written by hand) reads with it dropped as a kind this build does not know.

Kept for the other agents' work in flight: `FolderView` and `WidgetSurface` keep their one member
(`List`) and the parameters that carry them, rather than being removed with every signature that
names them.

Tests: `GridRemovedTests` (no grid type in any assembly, no enum member, no library page or preset, a
grid folder in a file dropped, no grid words), `PartnersTests` (both refusals, every kind of either
registry; a move within a type is the widget itself; the sentences in every language),
`PartnerMoveTests` (list to list keeping height, options and id; refusals leave the file as it was;
the dock has no edit across), `FolderDockTests` (a block over a folder's button moves past it),
`AddListTests` (only the place's type), `ResetTests` (a shape 19 file with a grid folder kept aside,
the folder gone), `EditDeckPlanTests` (five buttons).


## 71. A dock in three: start, middle and end (2026-10-09, branch folder-faces)

*"dock mode should get the left and right slot as well"* — as three separate floating docks, one at
the left end of the display's edge, one centred, one at the right end; switching a Taskbar to a Dock
now shows all three of its main sections (nothing hidden; it just floats).

- **The model** (`LayoutTypes.Places`, `ScreenEdges.Has`): a Dock shows the main row's start, middle
  and end, as a Taskbar does; only the look differs (`EdgeLayouts.Style`: floating). A new widget
  keeps its kind's section (`LayoutTypes.Home`). Taskbar ↔ Dock moves and hides nothing.
- **The docks** are the floating look's section panels (§23.7, `Layout.SectionPanels`), drawn by the
  bar's one window along the edge: the start's 8 DIPs from the left end, the end's 8 from the right,
  the middle's centred, each as long as what it holds, 8 DIPs off the edge. The bar window no longer
  lays a dock out with `Layout.Only` = middle; a hover place still has its one section. Since §81 a
  separator splits a section's dock into two (`Layout.Panels`), the gap between them as between two
  sections' docks.
- **One window, three docks.** A dock's bar stays one window per edge (its appbar, keys, rails and
  accessibility tree are a bar's), and at rest its region is the panels and the room under them
  alone (`DockWindow.Region`, `PanelsRegion`), as a hover place's already was: a press between two
  docks is the desktop's, the pointer passes through, and a dock with nothing in it takes no press.
  In edit mode, or while something is dragged, the region is the whole strip, so a block can be
  dropped anywhere along the edge, into an empty section's room too. Before, a press between the
  panels opened the bar's menu.
- **The strip held** (*Always, reserve space*): one along the whole edge, a dock's thickness and its
  lift (`Layout.Reserve`), whichever sections hold something — the three are one thickness.
- **On hover each dock comes in by itself**: the edge's three places are the docks
  (`HoverPlaces.For`, `Share`), each a window of its own sliding in when the pointer reaches its
  stretch of the edge — not one strip that brings all three. A floating edge has no band
  (`HoverPlaces.Banded`), so a place with nothing in it has no window at rest.
- **An empty section** is no dock at rest and takes no room; in edit mode it shows its empty room
  (three cells, `Layout.EmptyRooms`) where a widget dropped there would stand, as on a taskbar —
  the start's at the left end, the end's at the right.
- **Unchanged and per part, so nothing assumed one dock**: drags across docks (`Layout.SectionAt`,
  `DropSlot`), Ctrl+arrow from one dock to the next (`IslandEdits.Step`), the keyboard's arrows
  through every widget of the bar from one dock to the next and Tab between the apps and the tray
  as on a taskbar (one window; in edit mode Tab rings the blocks and the edit bars), flyouts
  anchored to their widget, the edit bar's top depth (the strip's),
  the accessibility tree (one "Taskbar" element per window, its widgets inside).
- **Settings**: the Layouts page's Dock picture shows three panels, the start's at the left, the
  middle's centred, the end's at the right (`LayoutTypeArt`).

Tests: `DockSectionsTests` (a Dock shows all three; the three docks left, centred and right at the
bottom and the top, 100 % and 150 %; an empty section no dock at rest and its empty room in edit
mode; the strip held; one place per dock on hover; Taskbar → Dock → Taskbar keeps everything);
`NamedLayoutsTests`, `EdgeModesTests`, `IslandEditsTests`, `EditDeckPlanTests` and the edit-in-place
pictures updated. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `dock-three-<bottom|top>-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-150.png`,
`dock-three-empty-start-edit-<dark|light>-150.png`. By hand: a click between two docks reaches the
window under it; on hover each dock comes in alone.

## 72. "Folder", not "List folder" (2026-10-09)

With the grid gone there is one kind of folder, and the person: it should be called just "Folder"
everywhere it is seen. So, in all five languages (Ordner, dossier, carpeta, 文件夹): the edit bar's
button, the add list's title for an unnamed folder ("Add to Folder") and the library's page are
"Folder"; a widget that stands in one is a **folder widget** ("Folder widget · in the folder Today"), as
one on the bar is a **taskbar entry**; the page's line says "Widgets that stand in a folder"; a
widget's height card is "Height in the folder", and the refusals and blurbs that said "a list" or
"a list view" say "a folder". Only words changed: `BarKind.FolderList`, `ListKind`,
`WidgetType.List`, the string keys and the files' `"folderList"` stay. Tests: `FolderWordTests` (no
text in any language says the old names; the folder, the library page and an unnamed folder say
the one word).

## 73. The clock is a preset (2026-10-09, branch folder-faces)

The person: *"the clock taskbar widget is actually just a premade widget that is actually a list
folder with a face and correct widgets inside the folder"*, *"basically the same way that the
current clock/date widget is structured, but all made with widgets"*, and it is *"nothing special"*.

- **The preset** (`Presets.ClockId`, "Clock", first in the add list's Popular and in Time and calendar): a list
  folder wearing the clock face (`ClockFace.New()`, the time only since §76), holding, top to bottom, what a click on the clock and on the date gave: the
  clock flyout's time over its long date (`timeHeader`), the calendar flyout's month (`month`) and
  the day's agenda under it (`calendar`), the clock flyout's timer and focus session (`timer`,
  `focus`) and its footer (`actions`: Date & time as the link, as the clock flyout's own; Focus as
  the button — an action is a Settings page, and the focus session above it is the one thing in
  the folder with a page of its own; the notifications are not in this folder). Dividers split it
  into four cards: the time over its month, the agenda, the timer and focus, the footer (§78). The month publishes the folder's Day and the agenda
  follows it (§9, "Channels"), so a click on a day shows that day's events with nothing set up.
  *Since 2026-10-11 it is the person's own arrangement*: the time, the timer, the stopwatch, the
  focus session and the footer, one card; the month and the agenda are the calendar's (the presets
  section, "One card, the person's clock").
  A preset can now say its folder's face (`Preset.Face`, copied for each folder made) and an
  actions line's pages (`PresetItem.Actions`); every other group still wears its icon.
- **Nothing special.** What it adds is an ordinary folder of ordinary widgets: lines added, taken
  out and moved, its face changed, its lists' width set, as any folder's. Two clocks are two
  folders, faces and countdowns their own.
- **The default bar** (`Sections.DefaultLayout`) has the clock preset where the date and the clock
  stood, its seconds where Windows' clock shows them (`ShowSecondsInSystemClock`). Configs are
  reset for it: shape 21 (22 since §74); a file of shape 20 or before is kept aside whole as
  config.shape<N>.json and the defaults take its place, as §70's reset does.
- **What went.** The clock taskbar entry (`BarKind.Clock`) and everything that was only its: the
  scene's drawing and measuring of it (`HitKind.Clock`, `Content.Clock(s)`, `Scene.MeasureClock`,
  `Layout.ClockTextRect`, `ClockSizes`, `Dock.RefreshClocks`/`ClocksFit`), Karpo's clock flyout
  (the face, the other clocks, the two lines and their menu, the footer; `ClockLayout`,
  `ClockPainter`, `ClockLineMenu`), the clock's own two countdowns (`Countdowns.ClockKey`,
  `ClockOptions.TimerMinutes`/`FocusMinutes`/`FocusDoNotDisturb` and their Settings card), the
  clock's right-click menu (Adjust date and time, Notifications) and its Narrator entry, and
  `CalendarOrigin` (the calendar opened "from a clock" had no agenda; nothing opens it so now).
  Their words went from the five languages. The clock's line in a list folder stays
  (`ListKind.Clock`), a list widget like any other. `SecondsTick` is
  a running countdown or a folder face showing seconds. The bell stays the bell: Windows opens the
  notification center from the clock, Karpo from the bell beside it, as before.
- **What stays, renamed to what it is.** A timer's or a focus session's own panel — what its entry
  on the bar opens — was a mode of the clock flyout; it is `CountdownFlyout` now: its card at full
  size (`CountdownPanel`), the steppers, the start and stop buttons, the wheel, Tab and Enter, its
  own second while open. `Dock.Clock.cs` is `Dock.Countdowns.cs`.
- **The calendar entry stayed** — until the same day, when it became a preset too (§80). It was not a date-only duplicate: its flyout has the day, week,
  month and year views (`CalendarView`), and it is the calendar's taskbar form beside its agenda
  line. It is only no longer on a new bar, whose date is the clock's face.
- **Made generic for it.** The clock flyout's timer and focus lines were one-liners ("for the time
  widget flyout make the focus time and timer one liners"): a countdown's line one row tall in any
  list folder is that line now (`CountdownTile.Inline`, `CountdownLine.Arrange(…, ListForm, …)` on
  the list's edges): the glyph in the list's icon column, the name, the minus, the length, the plus
  and the start button, the stop button in the plus's place and a bar along the foot while it
  runs, as tall as the clock flyout's line was (`ListHeight`). Taller, it is the compact line or the
  whole widget as before. Its menu is the folder's right-click.

Tests: `ClockPresetTests` (the folder, its face and its lines in order; two clocks apart; an
ordinary folder after — lines added, removed and moved and the face changed, read back as written;
no clock entry, a file's clock entry dropped and the clock line kept), `ClockPresetFolderTests` (a
click on a day in the clock's month and the agenda shows it; closing forgets it; pictures),
`DefaultBarTests.TheClockIsTheClockPreset`, `PresetsTests` (the clock's dividers),
`CountdownPanelTests` (the panel is its card; one countdown on the entry, the panel and the
line; Tab; the one-liner in a list). Pictures: `clock-preset-<dark|light>.png`,
`preset-clockGroup-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`. By hand: a new install's bar (or a reset one) shows
the clock folder with the time where Windows' clock is; open it, pick a day, start a
timer from its line and watch the face count down; open Date & time and Focus from the footer;
remove a line and change the face in Settings; a timer on the bar still opens its own panel.

## 74. Several lists in a folder, one folder open (2026-10-09, branch folder-faces)

The person: "only one folder can be open at a time", "a list folder holds 1..n lists shown side by
side", "folder height = automatic only", and edit mode's add buttons placed so nothing shifts. The
record is in §9 (lists side by side, a width per list, no height, each list scrolling on its own,
the "+" buttons, `OneFolder`, the pair of folders gone); this section says how it stands beside the
sections that came with it on the branch.

- **Config shape 22** (`Config.Shape`): a folder is `"lists": [[…], …]` (`FolderOptions.Lists`),
  where shape 21 had its lines at columns and rows and a height. A file of 21 or before is kept
  aside as `config.shape<N>.json` and the defaults take its place, as §70's and §73's resets did.
- **Presets** (`Presets.Folder`) make one list of their lines; the clock preset (§73) is that one
  list, wearing its own face (`Preset.Face`).
- **Removing a line** (§42, `Dock.RemoveFrom`) goes through `Folders.Take`: a list it was alone in
  goes with it.
- **Words** (§72): the folder page's "Panel" card says how wide its lists are; the height card, the
  fixed height and the "widgets hidden" line went with the height, in all five languages.

Tests: `FolderModelTests` (places, `Take`, `Move`, `Tidy`), `FolderLineRemoveTests` (a list goes
with its last line), `ResetTests` (a shape-21 folder of places is kept aside), `ClockPresetTests`
(the clock is one list).

### Lists apart, the title a row of its own, no "+" between widgets (2026-10-09, later)

Seen live, the person asked for three changes: "there is an add button between every widget in the
list folder, it should only be one at the top and in between the list views themselves"; "the
different columns are shown together with a divider between them, but they should actually be
shown separately, also have their separate heights"; and the title kept, as a row of its own
between the lists and the bar, as wide as all of them, its own panel, never touching the lists.

- **Each list is a panel of its own** (`FolderPlan.Lists[i].Box`): its own material, rounded
  corners, rim and shadow, as tall as its own widgets up to the most (70 % of the work area, less
  the title's row and its gap), scrolling on its own past that. The lists stand side by side 12 DIP
  apart (`FolderPlan.ListGap`, the gap a flyout keeps from its bar), lined up on the bar's side —
  bottoms level over a bottom bar, tops level under a top bar, the far ends ragged. Nothing is drawn
  between two lists: the hairline that parted them in one panel is gone.
- **The title** (`FolderPlan.Title`, `FolderFlyout.PaintTitle`) — the folder's glyph and its name,
  and the moment's note while it is arranged (`Say`) — is one more panel, between the lists and the
  bar (under them for a bottom bar or a side bar, over them for a top bar), as wide as the lists
  together, the same gap from them. It was the footer: the same row's height, no shade or hairline
  of its own now it is a panel apart.
- **One window holds them all.** The host draws each piece's chrome (`FlyoutHost.Pieces`,
  `MakePieces`), the window being the box round them and the room round that, so focus, Escape,
  the one-folder rule, the capture of a drag from one list to another and the "+" outside are what
  they were with one panel. Only a piece is the folder for a press (`FlyoutHost.Contains`): a
  press in a gap or over a shorter list is a press elsewhere, which closes a folder at rest. A
  carried line, though, is still being arranged there (`FolderFlyout.Message`), so it crosses a gap
  to the next list rather than leaving the folder. One window per list was weighed and not taken:
  a drag between lists would cross windows and the capture, and the one-folder and Escape rules
  would need a group of windows to keep.
- **The "+" buttons**: at each list's own end, outside its panel and following its height; in
  every gap between two lists and outside the outer two, for a new list there
  (`FolderAddKind.NewList`, `FolderPlace.NewList(i)`); none between two widgets — a widget goes in
  between two others by a drag. `FolderAddKind.Seam` is gone.
- **Settings**: the folder's name "is shown on a row of its own when the folder opens", and the
  card for the width is "Lists" rather than "Panel", in all five languages.
- **Where the group stands**: the box round the lists and the title is the panel the host places,
  so the group is centred on the folder's bar widget and kept inside the work area as every flyout
  is (`FlyoutPlacement.Along`); the "+" buttons outside it come in over its edge where the screen
  ends (`KeepIn`).
- **A list's dividers split it further** (§78): each run of lines between two dividers is a card
  of its own (`FolderListPlan.Runs`), the pieces the host draws are the cards and the title
  (`FolderPlan.PiecesAt`), and each card clips its lines to its rounded shape (`runViews`). A list
  that scrolls moves its cards with it: the host is handed them again, cut to what the list shows,
  on every scroll (`FlyoutHost.SetPieces`), and a press is the folder's only on a card.

Nothing moves between edit mode and rest: the panels, the lines and the title are the same, only
the "+" buttons come and go (`ListFolderTests.ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing`).

Tests: `ListFolderTests` (panels of their own heights, lined up on the bar's side; the "+" at each
list's own end and in the gaps, none on a line), `FolderTitleTests` (the title's row between the
lists and the bar, a gap apart), `FolderAddTests`, `FolderDragEditTests.ALineIsCarriedAcrossTheGapBetweenTwoPanels`;
pictures `MultiListPictures` (`folder-lists-<edge>-<look>-<scale>.png`: one, two and three lists,
at rest over arranged, with a divider in two of them).

By hand: open a folder of two or three lists on a bottom and a top bar, arranged and not; drag a
widget from one list to another across the gap; a long list with dividers scrolled with the wheel
(its cards follow); a folder against the screen's edge.

### No title, the lists the divider gap apart, a day picked repaints in place (2026-10-10)

*The person*: "remove the folder names completely. they just dont look good."; "the spacing between
list views should be the same as the divider spacing."; and "sometimes when changing the day in the
calendar view the whole folder where i am currently in refreshes so that it disappears very briefly
less than 0.1 seconds probably, and then appears again."

- **No title.** The title's panel (above, "the title a row of its own") is gone: `FolderPlan.Title`,
  `Name`, `Glyph` and `FolderFlyout.PaintTitle` with it, and no room is kept for it — the folder is
  as tall as its tallest list, which may now take all of the 70 % (`Build`), and the lists stand
  next to the bar at the flyout's own gap from it. The name stays the folder's: its button's tooltip
  (`FolderIsland.Tooltip`), Settings (the folder page's "Name", now "Shown in the folder's tooltip
  on the taskbar", in all five languages) and the face's name where it shows one.
- **The note** a folder says while it is arranged (`Say`: a widget carried over it that may not
  stand there, a drop the dock refused) stood on the title's row. It is a tip now, the folder tips'
  look (`FolderFlyout.Tips.cs`, `ShowNote`, `Pop`), centred over the folder on its side away from the
  bar and past the "+" buttons there (`OutsideRoomDip`); a refusal while the widget is over the
  folder stays for as long as it is, anything else for `NoteMs` (4 s); it goes with the folder.
- **The gap between two lists is the divider gap** (`FolderPlan.ListGap` = `DividerGap(Config.Dividers)`,
  6 DIP by default, 2..48), so two lists stand exactly as far apart as two cards of one list, and
  follow Appearance's slider live (the gap is in the open folder's `Signature`). The "+" for a new
  list between two lists keeps its place, centred on the gap and level with what the two lists have
  in common; at a gap narrower than the button it lies over both lists' edges by at most half its
  width (over a line's edge, never its middle), drawn over them, as it already did at 12 DIP.
- **The blink.** A day picked in the month (or a view, the date's header, a screen time bar —
  `Channels.Day`) whose agenda is another length makes the agenda's line another height, and the
  open folder is laid out again (`FolderChanged` → `LayOut`). That laid-out-again did two things
  that the compositor shows a frame late: it made *every* visual of the folder again
  (`RemakeVisuals`), and the host made every panel's chrome again — a new backdrop brush, a new
  shadow and its visual surface, a new rim per card (`FlyoutHost.MakePieces`, on every `Arrange`
  and every scroll). Not the config, not the window: the publish never reaches the file, and the
  window was never hidden. Now:
  - the host's panels are made once each and only moved and sized after (`FlyoutHost.PlacePieces`,
    `PieceVisuals`): a card more is one more set, a card fewer one closed;
  - the folder's visuals are made again only for another *shape* (`FolderFlyout.ShapeOf`: the
    lists and their cards, each line's list and card, the "+" count) — a widget come, gone or moved
    to another card, edit mode's "+" — and are otherwise placed and repainted in place (the lists'
    clips are placed by `DrawNow` now, not when made);
  - the window is not put anywhere when it would stand where it stands, as large
    (`FlyoutHost.Arrange`, `WindowMoves`).
  What else lays a folder out again goes the same way: a timer started, a notification come, a line
  of the media or screen time that changed height. The month stepping (‹ ›, the wheel) lays out
  nothing — six weeks always — and only repaints.
  Still not one atomic step: where the folder's height changes, the window is moved and sized
  (`SetWindowPos`) and its content follows in the compositor's next frame, so on a slow frame the
  lists may stand a frame off by the height's change; nothing disappears.

Tests: `FolderRepaintTests` (a day picked whose agenda is shorter and back: same window, shown,
no visuals or panels made; the month stepped and two days of one agenda length: nothing made and
the window moved at most once; edit mode makes the "+" and keeps the panels; `ShapeOf`),
`FolderTitleTests` (the folder is its lists alone, all of the 70 % a list's), `ListFolderTests`
(`TwoListsStandTheDividerGapApart`, `TheAddBetweenTwoListsSitsOnTheGapWhateverItsWidth`,
`ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing` at gaps 2, 6 and 24), `FolderOfferTests` (the note's tip), and the
pictures `folder-lists-<edge>-gap<6|24>-<look>-<scale>.png` (`MultiListPictures`, one, two and
three lists, at rest over arranged).

By hand: the calendar folder open, days with many and with no events clicked in turn, glass on and
off — no blink; Appearance's divider gap dragged with a folder of two lists open; a widget from the
bar carried over an arranged folder (the note's tip over it).

### A width per list, chosen beside its "+" (2026-10-10)

*The person*: "you should be able to change the width of individual columns in the folder view, the
width change configuration should show up next to the add button and should have three presets or
so. the global width configuration should be removed."

- **Three presets** (`FolderListWidth`, `FolderListWidths`): narrow **280**, medium **360**, wide
  **480** DIP. Medium is every panel's width (`Flyout.PanelWidthDip`) and a list's until somebody
  chooses. 280 is the narrowest the lines' own designs keep whole: the month's seven columns at
  36 DIP with the card's inset, a row of switches (four to a row there, six at medium), screen
  time's bars, legend and app rows (the legend drops what does not fit, a long name is cut), a
  note's text wrapping. 480 is a third wider than medium: room for a long agenda line, a note, a
  week. 240 (the old least) was tighter than the month's cells want; 640 and up made a three-list
  folder wider than many screens.
- **Stored per list** (`FolderOptions.Widths`, `"widths": ["narrow", "medium", "wide"]`), beside
  `"lists"`, not inside it, so a list stays the array of lines it is in the file and no shape bump
  is needed. Null, and not written, until a list is given a width; a missing entry, a name this
  build does not know or null reads as medium (`FolderOptions.WidthOf`, `TolerantEnumConverter`).
  A list's entry moves with it in every edit that moves a list (`Folders.Take`, `Move`, `Tidy`,
  `InsertList`/`RemoveList`): a list that goes takes its width; a new list for a line is medium; a
  line that was its list alone, carried to a new list elsewhere, carries its width — the list
  moved. `Folders.SetWidth` is the one edit.
- **The old folder-wide width** (`"width"`, 240–720, 0 for 360) is read once and never written
  (`FolderOptions.OldWidth`): each list gets the preset nearest it (`FolderListWidths.Nearest`,
  medium on a tie; 300 → narrow, 640 → wide), a list with a width of its own keeps it, and 0 or 360
  leaves the widths unwritten.
- **The button**: beside each list's end "+", on its right, level with it, 4 DIP apart
  (`FolderFlyout.PairApartDip`), the same round accent button (`FolderAddKind.Width`, painted by
  `PaintAdd` with Segoe Fluent's upright resize glyph turned a quarter, ‹•›). It is one of the
  plan's `Adds`, so it is found, lit, focused with the keys and kept on the screen (`KeepIn`) as a
  "+" is, and it comes and goes with them: nothing else moves between rest and edit mode. The
  group — the "+", the width and, with more than one list, the remove — is centred on its list, not
  the "+" (2026-10-11: "the add button is always in the center but the group should be centered"):
  as much room left of the "+" as right of the last button, at every width and scale
  (`FolderAddGroupPictures`, folder-add-group-<100|150|225>.png). Three buttons are 80 DIP and the
  narrowest list 280, so a group never meets another list's buttons or the gap's "+" (which stand
  level with the lists, not past their ends). Over a top bar the group stands under the list.
- **The menu**: a press asks the dock (`FolderFlyoutAction.Width`, the list in `Place.List`, `At`
  the button's side away from the bar); the folder holds itself open as for a widget's menu and the
  button stands pressed until it ends (`MenuClosed`). The dock shows Narrow, Medium, Wide, the
  list's own ticked (`Dock.FolderWidthMenu`, `FolderWidthRows`, `Topic.FolderWidth`, a menu's
  light-dismiss); a pick sets that list (`FolderWidthChosen` → `Folders.SetWidth` → `Apply`) and
  the open folder lays itself out again in place — the widths are in its `Signature` — that list
  wider or narrower, the lists after it moved along by as much. Words in all five languages
  (`dock.folder.width.*`).
- **Lines measure from their own list** (`FolderFlyout.Natural`: each line's content at its list's
  width; `ListWidth(scale, width)`), so a month in a narrow list and one in a wide list are each
  the height their width makes them.
- **Gone**: the folder page's "Lists" card (`settings.folder.panel.*` in all five languages,
  `FolderRows.PanelSummary`, `PanelWidthNote`), `FolderOptions.Width`, `WidthDip`,
  `WidthSmallest`/`WidthLargest`/`WidthDefault`, and `FolderPlan.ListWidth` (each list's is its
  `FolderListPlan.Width`).

Tests: `FolderListWidthTests` (the presets; a width set once; widths going with their lists through
`Take`, `Move`, `Tidy` and a new list; written by name, only once given, read back; read tolerantly;
an old width to its nearest preset once; the menu's tick; arranged, the button asks for its list's
menu and the folder stays; a picked width relays the open folder in place), `ListFolderTests`
(`EachListIsAsWideAsItsOwnPreset`, `EachListsWidthButtonStandsBesideItsAdd` for one to three lists,
bottom and top, no two buttons overlapping; `ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing` with mixed widths),
`FolderAddTests`, `FolderRowsTests.TheFolderHasNoWidthOfItsOwnToSet`; pictures
`folder-list-widths-<edge>-<look>-<scale>.png` (`MultiListPictures.ListWidthSheets`: three lists,
narrow, medium and wide, each the month, the switches, screen time and a note, at rest over
arranged) and `screentime-folder-*.png` (screen time narrow and wide).

By hand: arrange a folder of three lists on a bottom and a top bar; each list's ‹•› beside its "+"
opens Narrow/Medium/Wide with its own ticked; pick each — the list resizes in place, the others
move along, nothing else shifts; Escape and a click away close the menu and leave the folder open;
a folder saved by an older build with a width set opens with each list at the nearest preset.

### Empty columns, the "+" beside the lists adds one, a column's remove (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "the add buttons on the both sides, left and right should just add another column,
there can be empty columns, then the button that is on the top of the column actually opens the
widgets to add"; "when a column is added there should also be a remove button next to the width
button. you have to confirm before removing the column"; and "when a column is empty it should not
show up at all except for space, but if you are in edit mode it should actually have some height to
it and a text about placing widgets there". This undoes two rules of the spec above: "a list
disappears when its last widget goes" and "no empty lists except the first".

- **The model** (`Folders`): an empty list is kept. `Tidy` drops only a missing (null) list and
  keeps one list at least; `Take` and `Move` leave the list a widget left, empty where it was its
  last (a line alone in its list asked to be a new list either side of itself still moves nothing,
  and `FolderFlyout.Ghost` agrees). `Folders.AddList(folder, at)` puts an empty, medium list in;
  `Folders.RemoveList(folder, list)` takes a list with its widgets and its width, never a folder's
  last. In the file an empty list is an empty array among `"lists"`, its width beside it in
  `"widths"` as any list's; no shape bump — an older build reads it as it always read a folder's one
  empty list. Repair keeps a list it empties (a widget of a kind this build has no line of).
- *(gone 2026-10-12, §148)* **The "+" beside the lists and between two** (`FolderAddKind.NewList`) adds an empty column there
  at once (`FolderFlyoutAction.AddList` → `Dock.AddFolderList` → `Apply`), no add list. They stand
  for an empty folder too. A line carried onto one is still a new list of its own there, as before.
  **A list's own "+"** at its far end (`FolderAddKind.End`) opens the add list for that list, an
  empty one's included.
- **A column's remove** (removed 2026-10-12, §149: a column cannot be deleted) (`FolderAddKind.Remove`): beside the width button, on its right, the pair's
  4 DIP apart, the same round accent button wearing Segoe Fluent's Delete (the bin). None while the
  folder has one list. A press asks the dock (`FolderFlyoutAction.RemoveList`, the button pressed and
  the folder held open meanwhile → `Dock.RemoveFolderList`): a column with no widgets goes at once;
  one with widgets asks first in Windows' own dialog (§ "Deleting a folder or a column" at the end;
  it was a menu over the button, asked for an empty column too, until 2026-10-11). The column goes
  by `Folders.RemoveList` → `Apply`, and a widget selected in it leaves the selection. Not undoable:
  the dock has no undo for a removal (the settings app's undo is for a widget it removed itself).
  The three buttons reach 68 DIP right of the list's middle; a narrow list is 140 half.
- **At rest an empty column is room** (since 2026-10-12 only between two with widgets; an outer one is none, §158): its width, in its place among the lists, and nothing drawn —
  no panel, no height (`FolderListPlan` 0 tall at the bar's side, no card in `Runs`, so the host
  draws no piece and a press there is not the folder's). The lists either side stand where they
  would with it filled. A folder with no widget at all shows its one list's panel at rest too
  (below), or opening it would show nothing.
- **Arranged, an empty column is a panel** (since 2026-10-12 a slot of its width instead, §149) `FolderFlyout.EmptyRows` (3) rows tall (118 DIP), lined up
  on the bar's side like the others, with "Add widgets here" centred on it in the secondary text
  (`PaintEmpty`, `FolderPlan.Empty`; it was a faint line where the first widget would stand). A line
  carried over it lands in it (`Aim`: the list under the pointer, at its top).
- **The zero-shift rule, relaxed for this alone**: arranging changes nothing but an empty column's
  height. Every list keeps its place and width, and a list with widgets keeps its height and its
  distance from the bar, which is where the window stands on the screen. Only where the empty
  column's panel is taller than every other list does the folder's box grow, away from the bar.
  `ListFolderTests.ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing` holds the rule for folders without an empty list;
  `FolderColumnsTests.ArrangingMovesNothingButAnEmptyColumnsHeight` holds this.
- **Words**, in all five languages: `dock.folder.column.empty`, `.removeAsk`,
  `.removeWidgets.one/.other`, `.removeNone`, `.cancel`.

Tests: `FolderModelTests` (`AListStaysWhenItsLastWidgetIsTakenOut`, `AnEmptyListIsAddedBesideOrBetweenTheOthers`,
`AListIsRemovedWithItsWidgetsButAFolderKeepsOne`, `AnEmptyListIsWrittenAndReadBack`, the carry into an empty
list, `RepairKeepsTheListsRule`), `FolderColumnsTests` (an empty column at rest and arranged; nothing but its
height moves; the remove beside the width and none for one list; the question's rows; on real windows: the side
"+" asks for a column and the end "+" for the add list, the remove asks and the folder stays, a line carried into
an empty column and that column's room at rest not the folder's), `FolderAddTests`, `ListFolderTests`; pictures
`folder-empty-lists-<edge>-<look>-<scale>.png` (`MultiListPictures.EmptyListSheets`: an empty column in the
middle, first and last, and a folder with nothing in it, at rest over arranged).

By hand: arrange a folder of two lists; the "+" left, between and right each add an empty column at
once; an empty column's own "+" opens the add list for it; drag a widget into it and out again (the
column stays); its bin asks, Cancel keeps it, Remove takes it and its widgets; a folder of one list
has no bin; leave edit mode — an empty column is a gap of its width, nothing drawn.

## 75. A network drive that is not connected, as Explorer shows it (2026-10-09)

The person: "the not connected state of a network drive widget should show up in the same style as
win11 would show not connected". It was drawn as any missing drive is — faint, Segoe's warning badge,
an empty track — which is Karpo's way of saying a widget's target has gone, and not what File
Explorer shows for a mapped drive it cannot reach. Now a Network drive widget whose share is not
connected (`DriveIsland.Disconnected`) is drawn as This PC draws one, on every surface:

- **The picture** is the shell's own disconnected network drive, the drive with the red X
  (`SIID_DRIVENETDISABLED`, `DriveIcons.Disconnected`), read from the stock icons off the dock's
  thread — never from the drive's root, which would be a question to the share that is not there.
  Until it is read, or where the shell has none, the kind's glyph with a red disc and a white cross
  drawn on at its foot. The same in every theme, high contrast included, as the shell's is.
- **The name** in the text's own ink, not faded: Explorer does not fade it.
- **No capacity bar.** On the bar the name has the bar's room (`DriveIsland.Rows`, `capacity:
  false`); the widget's size does not change (§12.2).
- **Explorer's word for it**, "Disconnected network drive" (`core.drive.type.disconnected`, the
  Type column's), in the secondary ink where there is a line for it: under the name on a tall line,
  "Disconnected" (`widget.drive.disconnected`) where only a short word fits — a one-row line's
  end — and as the kind in the list's and the flyout's header. The bar
  entry says it in its tooltip.

A local drive that is missing, and a widget with no drive chosen, keep the broken look.

**Detection** (`DriveWatch`). A network drive is read on the pool and is **never waited for** on
the dock's thread (it was, for up to 150 ms, every time a probe started — once a minute for a share
that is gone). Its first answer is **pending** (`Drive.Pending`, `DriveWatch.Pick`): the widget draws
its glyph, its name and an empty track, never the red X, so a reachable share does not flash
disconnected at start; a share asked again keeps what it showed until the answer is in. When an
answer comes that changes whether the drive is there, the widgets that asked are woken
(`DriveWatch.For(…, ready)`, the island's `Wake`), and the next read lists afresh. A connection
Windows remembers but has not made (`WNetGetConnection`'s `ERROR_CONNECTION_UNAVAIL`, Explorer's
red X) is disconnected without a question to the share (`DriveWatch.Reading`): reading it would try
to reconnect, which Explorer leaves to the person opening the drive. Anything else is there when its
space can be read.

Held by `DisconnectedDriveTests` (the answer, the pick, the cell without a bar) and
`DriveWidgetOffscreenTests` (disconnected, not pending, not for a local drive; the same size at every
bar), with `drive-disconnected-{bar,vertical,lines}-{dark,light,hc}.png` and the drawn red X in
`drive-disconnected-{bar-drawn-dark,lines-drawn-light}.png`. By hand: map a drive to a share, put a
Network drive widget on the bar and in a folder, take the share's server away (or
sign in without it) and watch the widget turn to Explorer's picture without the bar stuttering;
bring it back and open the drive.

## 76. The clock face is only the clock; a folder widget's height is Automatic or Fixed (2026-10-09)

**The clock face** — the person: "the clock face should only show the clock and not the calendar
stuff as well". Its *Shows* choice (the time, or the time and the date) went, and with it every date
it measured or drew (`ClockFaceSettings.Date`, `ClockFaceDrawing.WidestDate`): the face is the time,
then the label and what a timer in the folder has left. The date is the calendar face's. The clock
preset (§73) and a new bar's clock wear the clock face with the time alone (`ClockFace.New()`); a
file's leftover `"show"` is kept in the face's bag and read as nothing (§67's rule). The tooltip is
still the long date, as Windows' clock's is. Words: `core.face.clock.show.*` went from the five
languages.

**A folder widget's height** — the person: "either the height is automatic, then you can just set a
max height, or the height is fixed, then you just set the height", "for every widget shown in a
folder", and "the folder itself should always just grow to its contents".

- **The model** (`Karpo.Core\LineHeight.cs`): `LineHeight(Fixed, Rows)`, rows 1 to 32. Automatic
  gives the line its content's height (IListContent, else what its kind declares), from one row up
  to its rows; Fixed gives it exactly its rows (`LineHeight.Given`). It replaces the least and the
  most (`AtLeast`/`AtMost`, §12.3): two numbers for one choice, and a least other than one only ever
  added empty room under a short content. A new line starts Automatic up to its kind's most
  (`ListWidget.Range.Most`, `LineHeight.StartFor`), which is what it was given before.
- **The unit stays the row** of the folder's cells (36 + 5 DIP): lines set by hand line up across
  lists side by side, and a count says the same at every scale and text size; pixels would have
  made a number nobody can picture and two neighbours a few px apart easy.
- **Which widgets**: every line that is its own card (`Folders.HasHeight`). The list's own row of an
  icon and a name is one line and a divider its hairline, whatever anybody asks, so they carry none.
  A taskbar entry has none (§12.6). The folder has no height of its own: it is its tallest list,
  capped at 70 % of the work area, where each list scrolls (§74).
  **A kind may opt out** (2026-10-10): `ListWidget.FixedHeight` says its line is always exactly its
  `Rows`, so `HasHeight` is false — Settings shows no height card, `Normalize` drops a height a file
  holds, and `LineHeight.For`/`StartFor` answer `Exactly(Rows)` whatever it carries. The actions line
  (§68) is the first: one row, as the person asked ("one row height all the time"). Since §138 a kind of a fixed content is Fixed only, and every kind's rows have limits.
- **What does not fit**: no scrolling inside a line — the list already scrolls, and a scroller in a
  scroller catches the wheel half-way down it. A line held shorter than its content shortens itself
  as its kind does: the agenda and the apps of screen time show fewer and "N other events/apps", the
  month whole weeks, media and screen time's total a smaller tier, the toggles whole rows (and at
  one row buttons as tall as the row leaves them, `TogglesTile.Fit` — it was cut in half before).
  Every line is also clipped to its own box by the folder. Taller than its content, a Fixed line is
  the kind's to fill (a bigger tier) or to centre in.
- **The file**: `"height": { "fixed": false, "rows": 6 }` on a folder's widget. A file of this shape
  that still says `"atLeast"`/`"atMost"` is read tolerantly, once (`LineHeight.Read`): the same two
  numbers are Fixed at that count, any other pair Automatic up to its most; written back in the new
  words. No shape bump.
- **Settings** (`Controls\SizeCard.cs`, `Logic\HeightChoice.cs`): the "Height in the folder"
  expander, its header saying "Automatic, up to 6 rows" or "Fixed, 4 rows"; in it a **Height**
  dropdown (Automatic, Fixed) with a line saying what it does, and one number field of 1 to 32,
  "Maximum rows" or "Rows" as the mode says. Switching keeps the number. Same place and same rules
  on every widget's page as before.

Tests: `FolderFaceTests.TheClockFaceShowsOnlyTheClock`, `FolderRowsTests`; `ListBoundsTests` (the
rule, the file's words, old least/most mapped, a new line's start, Automatic up to its most, Fixed
exactly for every kind, the folder growing to its lines), `HeightChoiceTests` (the card's words, the
summary, switching modes, every height round-tripping), `LineHeightPicturesTests`
(`line-height-<toggles|month|agenda|media|screentime|screentime-apps>-<dark|light>.png`: each kind
Automatic, Automatic up to 2, Fixed 1, 2, 4 and 8, every line drawn inside its box). By hand: in
Settings switch a folder widget between Automatic and Fixed and change the rows with the folder
open; a toggles row at Fixed 1; a busy agenda at Fixed 2.

## 77. Events and mail offline, and a mark for what could not be refreshed (2026-10-09)

*"the event should by synchronized in the background for all the widgets, the same for the
emails. you dont have to keep everything but this is just so that you can also show events and
emails without internet connection. if the refresh was not possible just show an indicator for the
widgets that show this data is possibly stale or could not be updated or something."*

The whole design is in `docs\accounts.md`, "Offline"; in short:

- **One sync per account**, for the calendars and for the mail (`AccountCalendars`, `MailStore`),
  read side by side from the dock's start, at the online interval (§37), a minute after a failure,
  at once on Refresh or an account change.
- **Synced all the time** (*"sync all the time"*, a follow-up the same day): from the dock's start
  for every account that gives calendars or mail, whether or not any widget is placed
  (`Pim\PimSync.cs`) — the accounts decide, not the config; this replaces "while the config names
  a widget of them". With no such account a store asks nobody and its timer stops; an account
  added is read at once, one removed is not asked again and leaves the cache. Contacts waited for
  their panel (§11) until §389, which syncs them the same way.
- **A bounded cache** in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo` (`PimCache`): the events of a week back to 60 days
  ahead and the newest 30 messages an account, as the rows draw them and nothing else — no token, no
  address, no preview. Taken in on the pool before the first read, so a start without a connection
  shows them; written after every good read.
- **Encrypted for the Windows user** (the same follow-up): DPAPI, CurrentUser scope with the
  cache's own entropy, through the ProtectedData package `Karpo.Accounts\Secrets.cs` already uses
  (native-AOT clean). Atomic writes as before. A file that does not decrypt — another user's,
  tampered, or the plain JSON of the first version — is no cache and is written over by the next
  good read; nothing logged quotes a file.
- **Every widget reads the stores' memory**, never the file and never an account (§11's rule
  stands: no view waits).
- **Stale**: an account whose refresh fails keeps what it showed, and the store's `Freshness` says
  from when. `StaleMark` draws it the same everywhere — the SyncError glyph in the secondary ink at a
  list line's trailing gutter, on the mail envelope's lower corner, and the words "Last updated 14:05
  — couldn't refresh" as its tooltip (the mail's taskbar entry, which shows no tooltip otherwise,
  shows this one) and as the mail and calendar flyouts' note. An account with nothing kept says why,
  as before: a first start offline is "… could not be reached".

**The read API for new calendar and mail widgets** (the calendar views as list widgets) is in
`docs\accounts.md`, "For a new widget that shows events or mail".

**By hand:** with an account set up, let Karpo read once, then disconnect the network and press
Refresh on the calendar or mail line: the events and messages stay, with the mark and its tooltip;
restart Karpo still offline: they are there at once, marked stale after the first try; reconnect and
Refresh: the mark goes. With no calendar or mail widget anywhere, start Karpo online, then go
offline and place a mail line: the messages are there at once. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\mail-cache.json`
opened in an editor is unreadable bytes, with no subject in it.

## 78. Separators and dividers look as Appearance says (2026-10-09) — a separator is empty space, with no look, since §505 (2026-11-05)

*The person*: "the separators should not have an individual style anymore. you can set the separator
style in the global appearance settings but not individually anymore. you should be able to set the
same settings for the dividers too, also in global appearance settings" — all of it global, the line
or no line included. Defaults: separators have no line; dividers have no spacing over and under them
(written "now spacing", read as **no** spacing — to be confirmed).

- **One style each** (`LineStyle`, `Karpo.Core\Config.cs`): `Config.Separators` for every separator on
  the bars, `Config.Dividers` for every divider in the folders (`ListKind.Divider`). Each is `line`
  (on or off), `width` (hairlines, 1 to 8, absent for Automatic) and `space` (DIP either side, 0 to
  48). Written at the top of the file, always; null or a missing one reads as its default
  (`Config.Repair`). The colour is a custom colour like the others (§60): `ColorSlot.Separator` (as
  before) and the new `ColorSlot.Divider`, per mode. A separator or a divider item has no look of its
  own: `WidgetOptionsKind.Separator` and the item's `"separator": {…}` are gone, the old key read and
  dropped without a word (`SeparatorLineTests.AnItemsOwnLookIsDroppedFromTheFile`).
- **The bar** (`Layout.Separators`, copied from the config the bar is laid out with; `PartSpec` no
  longer carries a line, a width or a space). Every separator of a bar is alike: a divider where the
  style has a line, a spacer where not — except in a dock, where a separator never draws a line and
  splits the dock in two, its space widening the gap (§81). `Layout.LineSpace(style, scale)`, `SeparatorInk.Thickness(…,
  style.Hairlines)`. **Edit mode** keeps §61's two marks, now chosen by the style: with a line every
  separator's grab is the accent-filled box with its line on it; without, the dashed empty box
  (`Scene.MarkFor(spec, style, tokens)`). A spacer's marker still lies over the seam and takes no room.
- **The folders** (superseded the same day, below: a divider is no line any more).
  (`FolderIsland.Dividers` → `FolderFlyout.Build(…, dividers)`). A divider's line of the
  list is `FolderFlyout.DividerHeight`: its line (`SeparatorInk.DividerThickness`, the panel's hairline
  times the width; none without a line) and the room over and under it. With the default that is the
  hairline alone between the list's own 2-DIP gaps (it was 13 DIP of air). No line and no room is no
  height and no gap of its own: the lines either side meet as if it were not there, and it still
  splits the list. `DividerTile` draws the line in `FlyoutTheme.ChosenDivider ?? Divider`
  (`DividerTile.InkOf`); the other lines of a panel keep the divider colour. **Edit mode** moves
  nothing ("identical in edit and view mode"): a divider is taken hold of over a grab at least
  `DividerDip` (13 DIP) tall centred on it, laid over its neighbours' edges and found before them
  (`FolderPlan.Grabs`, `TargetAt`); the selection and focus rings go round the grab; a divider with
  no line wears a dashed outline there (`FolderPlan.Marks`, the strong fill colour), as a spacer does
  on the bar. The open folder plans again when the style changes (`Signature`).
- **Settings** (Appearance, `SettingsModel.Lines.cs`, `Logic\LineRows.cs`): two expanders after
  "Custom colors", "Separators" and "Dividers", each with Line (switch), Line width (slider and field,
  0 is Automatic), Line color (the two swatches, moved here from "Custom colors"), and the space
  ("Space on each side" / "Space above and below"). Width and colour are off without a line. A
  separator's widget page has only a link card, "How separators look", to Appearance.

Tests: `SeparatorLineTests` (default no line, the style round trip, ranges, the item's old look
dropped, null reads as default, merge, every separator alike), `WidgetGroupTests` (spacers and
dividers by the style, edit mode moves nothing in both), `SeparatorMarkTests` (marks by the style),
`DividerStyleTests` (default hairline, style reaches the line, no line no room takes nothing, edit
