grab and marks, the chosen colour), `LineRowsTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`separator-style-<none|line|spaced|thick>-<look>-<edge>-<theme>-<scale>.png` and `separator-style-edit-…`,
`edit-marks-<look>-<theme>-<scale>-<spacers|dividers>-<state>.png`, `divider-style-<theme>-<scale>.png`.
By hand: switch the separators' line on and off with the bar in edit mode; a divider with no line in
an open folder in edit mode, dragged; the colours in both modes.

### Dividers split the list into cards, no line (2026-10-09, later)

*The person*, confirmed: "a divider inside a list splits that list's panel background into separate
cards with a gap (like a taskbar separator splits widget groups). NO line any more"; Appearance's
"Dividers" drop the line on/off, the line width and colour and keep the gap; and the presets keep a
divider only where a split clearly helps.

- **A style of its own** (`DividerStyle`, `Karpo.Core\Config.cs`): `Config.Dividers` is a gap, in
  DIPs, 2 to 48, 6 by default — the room the bar keeps between two groups, and since 2026-10-10 the
  room between two lists of a folder too (§74, "No title, the lists the divider gap apart") — written `"dividers": { "gap": n }` and left out while it is 6. What a file kept of a
  divider's line (`line`, `width`, `space`) is read past, the gap its default.
  `LineStyle.DividerDefault` is gone; `LineStyle` is the separators' alone. `ColorSlot.Divider` and
  `ModeColors.Divider` are gone too: a `"divider"` colour a file has is read past.
- **The plan** (`FolderFlyout.Build`): a divider's line is its gap (`FolderFlyout.DividerGap`) and
  the whole room between the line over it and the line under it — the lines' own 2 DIPs give way to
  it. Each list's lines between two dividers make a card (`FolderListPlan.Runs`, `FolderPlan.CardRun`;
  -1 for a divider). A divider first, last or next to another keeps its gap — it is where it was
  put, to be taken hold of — but no empty card stands there; a list of nothing but dividers is one
  card. `ListFolderTests.ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing` holds the cards too (`FolderListPlan` compares
  them one by one).
- **Drawn** as the lists are (§74): the host gives each card its material, corners, rim and shadow
  (`FolderPlan.PiecesAt`, `FlyoutHost.Pieces`), and the folder clips each card's lines to it. A
  scrolled list's cards move with it and are cut to the list (`FlyoutHost.SetPieces`).
  `DividerTile` draws nothing; `DividerTile.LineOf`, `InkOf`, `FlyoutTheme.ChosenDivider` and
  `SeparatorInk.DividerThickness` are gone.
- **Edit mode** moves nothing: a divider is still taken hold of over its grab (at least
  `DividerDip`, 13 DIP, centred on its gap), and every divider wears the dashed box over its gap
  (`FolderPlan.Marks`), as a spacer does on the bar.
- **Settings** (Appearance): "Dividers" is one card now, not an expander — the gap's slider and
  field (`DividerChoices`, `LineRows.WriteGap`); its Line, Line width and Line color rows and the
  divider's custom colour went, in all five languages ("settings.appearance.dividerGap.*").
- **Presets** (§7b, "Its dividers"): the clock keeps three (time and month | agenda | timer and
  focus | footer), the calendar two (date and month | events | footer); System loses its one, the
  notification center and Focus one each; the weather (now | hours | week), Media, Storage and
  Connectivity keep theirs.

Tests: `DividerStyleTests` (the default gap, the gap held to its range, a card a group and none
empty, the cards following the scroll in the plan and on the host, edit grab and marks, the file),
`LineRowsTests`, `ListFolderTests.ADividerSplitsTheListWhereItWasPut`, `ListGutterTests` (a divider
draws no ink), `PresetsTests`, `ClockPresetTests`. Pictures: `divider-style-<theme>-<scale>.png`
(narrowest, default and wide gaps), `folder-lists-*.png`, `preset-<id>-*.png`. By hand: a long
clock folder scrolled; the gap slider in Appearance with a folder open.

## 79. Every settings section starts collapsed (2026-10-09)

*The person*: "generally in settings the individual sections should start collapsed and not opened.
(e.g. Window previews)". No page opens a `SettingsExpander` in its markup or as it is made (Window
previews, Flyouts, the tray's icons, the status icons, the weather's place, the toggles, a folder's button, and the size card even where it is all the page has). The pages
are kept between visits (`NavigationCacheMode`), so a page being left closes its sections
(`Visuals.CollapseSections` on `Frame.Navigating`) and is collapsed when opened again, as Windows'
Settings is. What still opens one is somebody's doing: "Find a setting" opening the section of what
it found, a layout just added, duplicated or asked for by the bar, a pin just made with nothing to
open yet, a display chosen on the map. Held by `SectionsStartCollapsedTests` (a source scan).

## 80. The weather and the calendar are presets (2026-10-10)

The person: *"now as a next step, you already moved the clock widget over to the new folder
architecture, now do the same for the weather forecast and calendar widget. make sure that their
styles are preseved as well as possible."* Done as the clock was (§73): the entries and their
flyouts went, and what a click on them gave is a ready-made folder of widgets wearing a face.

- **The weather preset** (`Presets.WeatherId`, "Weather"): a list folder wearing the **weather
  face**, holding the conditions now (`weatherNow`, the flyout's header with its refresh button and
  the reading's age), a divider, the next hours (`weatherHours`, the flyout's day graph:
  `WeatherHoursTile`), a divider, and the week (`weatherDays`, the flyout's rows of days:
  `WeatherDaysTile`). Each is drawn by the flyout's own control (`DayGraph`, `WeatherHeader`,
  `WeatherDayRow`) housed on the list's gutter. No footer: the flyout had none but the age, which is
  the conditions' line's last. The hours and the week had been lines once and were taken out as
  widgets on 2026-09-26; they are back because the flyout they stood in is gone.
- **A click on a weather line searches the weather** (2026-10-11: "when clicking on a weather widget
  it should search for the weather in the default browser"): the conditions, each hour and each day
  act (`CellAct.Action`, each its own target since §131 — no line lights as a whole) and open
  "weather <place>" (a day other than today: "weather <place> <day>") — "weather"
  alone for the device's location, which the engine places itself — in the default browser, with the
  app's search engine (`SearchUrls.Weather`, `WeatherLineTile.SearchTheWeb`).
- **One search engine for the whole app** (2026-10-11: *"you should be able to select the default
  serach engine globally for the whole application. not per widget anymore. (weather widget should
  also respect it for example.)"*): Settings → General → Online → "Search engine" (`Config.SearchEngine`,
  `SettingsModel.Search.cs`): Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Startpage, Brave Search, or Custom,
  an address with `{q}` where the words go, judged as it is typed. Every web search Karpo opens goes
  through `SearchUrls.Search(Config, …)`; the weather's click is the one today. Null, and not in the
  file, until somebody chooses: Google (2026-10-16: *"default search engine should be google"*; Bing before, and a file that chose Bing keeps it). The default browser's engine is not read: it is
  each browser's own, kept in its profile, no setting of Windows'. A custom engine with no usable
  address searches with Google. A file from before takes the first web search box's engine, in the
  file's order, where it had one (`ConfigWords.WebSearchGone`); one with none stays unset. The conditions' refresh button stays its own; a line with no place
  is its "Set up in Settings". The weather face opens its folder, as every face does.
- **Every weather widget has its own place** (2026-10-10, replacing the folder's one place: *"location
  should not actually be shared in the folder, this means you have to set it multiple times but you
  are actually able to show different places per folder which is a feature i want"*). Each weather
  line keeps its own (`WeatherOptions`), and so does the weather face (`FolderFace.Weather`, set in
  the folder's Face section, §86); nothing follows anything else, so a folder can show Bern on one
  line and Chur on another, and two folders two places. One without a place is its centred "Set up
  in Settings" (`SetupFace`), the face its pin and "Set location". `WeatherPlaces.Of`, the lines'
  `Fallback` and their quiet "No location yet" under the conditions' prompt are gone.
  - *New, it is the device's location* (2026-10-11: *"as default in weather widgets take current
    location"*). Every new weather widget starts with "Use my device's location" on
    (`WeatherOptions.New`): a line of each weather kind (`ListKind.New`), the weather face
    (`FolderFace.Of`, `WeatherFace.New`), so the preset's four pieces too. A record read from a file
    keeps what it says — one without `useDeviceLocation` is off, as it always was — so no existing
    widget changes. Where Windows gives no location (desktop apps' location access off) and no
    forecast was ever fetched for it, a line shows the same centred "Set up in Settings" as one with
    no place (`WeatherLineTile.LocationOff`), and goes on asking at its interval, so it shows the
    weather once location is switched on; the face keeps its size and draws the pin with "–".
    In the test run the shared store answers offline (`WeatherStore.SharedFetch`, set by the run's
    isolation), so no test asks Windows for the PC's location or the network.
  - *The preset asks once* — where its pieces have no place: a new one has the device's, so the
    page opens at its top. Added from the bar's add list without one, the
    settings open at the conditions' place (`--added … --setup place`, as before); the first place
    or "Use my device's location" chosen on that page is also given, as copies, to the folder's
    other weather pieces still without one, the face included (`SettingsModel.OfferPlace` /
    `PlaceChosen`, `WeatherPlaces.Spread`). Once, at that moment: after it each piece's place is
    its own and changing one changes nothing else.
  - *Files from before* load: a weather face with no `weather` of its own is from the shared days,
    and is read once into the face and into every weather line that had no place and followed the
    folder's (`WeatherPlaces.Adopt`, from `FolderOptions.Normalize`), so the folder shows what it
    showed. The face has a place after (set or not), so it never happens twice.
  One place is one fetch, whatever shows it (`WeatherStore`): the face is a user of the store like
  the lines (`FolderIsland.Weather`), ticking at every online widget's interval and painting itself
  again in place when the reading changes. The lines share `WeatherLineTile` (the place, the store,
  the look).
- **The weather face** (`FolderFaces.Weather`, `WeatherFaceDrawing`): the entry's drawing as a face,
  with its looks as the face's *Look* option — *Simple* (the glyph and the temperature, the default),
  *Detailed* (and today's high and low), *3-day forecast*. Measured from the settings and templates
  (`WeatherRow`), never from the forecast; the simple look down a bar on its side and before a place
  is set ("Set location" with the pin); a reading past due in the quiet ink. No tooltip.
- **The faces of text stand in the middle of their button (2026-10-11).** *"the taskbar weather face
  should be centerd, right now it does not appear centered but left aligned"*. The room is the widest
  reading's (so the bar never moves), and the weather was drawn from its start: "16°" in the room of
  "-88°", the forecast's days in boxes as wide as the widest pair, the room left over all at the end.
  Now what each look reads stands in the middle of that room, along the bar and across it (the loud
  figures' ink on the middle line; down a bar on its side the glyph and the figures centred by their
  ink). The same held for the ticker (its price in the room of the widest) and for the timer and the
  focus session at rest ("5m" in the room of "04:59"), which are centred the same way; a running one
  says five figures as wide as the widest, so it still does not move as it counts. Left as they are:
  the time and date, the clock, the calendar, the readings (the figure right-aligned against its
  glyph, the two spanning the room), the drives (the bar fills the room), whose ink is already in
  the middle; the now playing face and the desktops' name, which are titles and read from their
  start; and the badges on the removable devices', the hotspot's and the mail's glyphs, which stand
  on a corner by design. `FaceCentringTests` measures the ink (±1 px for the weather, ±1.5 for the
  countdowns' glyphs) at 32 to 64 DIP, 100 and 150 %, and draws `face-centring.png`.
- **The calendar preset** (`Presets.CalendarId`, "Calendar"): a list folder wearing the calendar
  face with the day and the date (the calendar entry's text, `CalendarFace.New(withDay: true)`),
  holding the flyout's header (`dateHeader`, `DateHeaderTile`: today in its longest form that fits,
  a click going back to today by publishing it as the folder's day), the month (`month`, now with a
  dot under each day with events, in its calendar's colour, as the flyout's month had), the day's
  events (`events`, `EventsTile`: the flyout's list under its month — "Today" or the day's name over
  a row per event with its calendar's bar, its time and place; whole rows only, the rest counted),
  and the footer (`actions`, `PremadeWidgets.CalendarActions`: Date & time as the link and the
  calendar app as the button — `SettingsActions.CalendarId`, the one action that is no Settings page,
  `outlookcal:` or `ms-calendar:` as Windows has an app for them, and left out where it has none). Dividers split it into three cards
  as the clock's (§78): the date over its month, the events, the footer.
- **The other views are lines** (`dayView`, `weekView`, `yearView`: `CalendarViewTile`, one class,
  its kind the view), drawn by the flyout's own layout and painter (`CalendarLayout`, now laid out for
  a line of a given width and height on the list's gutter, its header, month view and footer gone;
  `CalendarPainter`). Each follows and publishes the folder's day: a click on a day, a week's heading
  or a year's day picks it, the arrows step a day, a week (the window with it) or a year. The day and
  week show the whole day in a window as tall as the line leaves them (ten hours where nothing set
  it), opened an hour before now; the wheel scrolls it and, at either end, is the folder's again; Up
  and Down scroll an hour; the other keys move the day as the flyout's did. A target is named by what
  it is (a day by its day: `CalendarViewTile.DayTarget`), never by its place, so a layout between a
  press and its release cannot move the click. The year's months take as many columns as the width
  holds and scroll where the line is shorter.
- **The events, offline** (§77): every calendar line reads its events only through
  `CalendarLines.Store` — `CalendarStore.Shared`, or a test's own — and asks only what the flyout
  asked: whether there are calendars, whether they are being read, why not, the events in a range.
  So the offline cache behind the store reaches all of them. They have no data source of their own:
  the dock syncs the calendars from its start (§389).
- **Stale** (`StaleMark`, §77): while an account could not be refreshed and its last good read is
  shown, the day's events carry the mark at the trailing gutter of their heading, and the month
  (the clock preset's too, for its dots) and the day, week and year views before their arrows —
  the title gives up the room (`CalendarInputs.Reserve`, `CalendarPlan.TitleEnd`), so the arrows
  and the days never move. Its tooltip is the store's "Last updated … — couldn't refresh"
  (`CalendarLineTile.StaleTip`). The weather was never an account's and says its age beside its refresh button, and nowhere else (2026-10-11).
- **Catalogue.** Two new groups, *Calendar* and *Weather*, after *Time and information*: the seven
  calendar lines and three weather lines would have taken Time past the catalogue's twelve, and each
  is a family, its flyout's.
- **The default bar** has the weather preset where the weather entry stood (where Windows shows its
  Widgets button: the start, or before the tray when left-aligned), and the calendar preset right
  after the clock preset, wearing the short date (`CalendarFace.New()`): the clock face is the time
  alone since §76, so the time and the date stand side by side as Windows' clock shows them
  (2026-10-10, the person's decision). **Config shape 23**: a file of 22 or before is kept aside
  whole and the defaults take its place.
- **Dividers** only where the flyouts had a hairline between two subjects: the calendar's header,
  its month, the day's events, its footer; the weather's now, its hours, its week. Nothing between
  lines of one subject.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Weather` and `BarKind.Calendar` and everything only theirs: `WeatherIsland`
  (its forecast's types are `Weather\Forecast.cs`), `WeatherBarLooks`, `WeatherFlyout`,
  `Dock.Weather.cs`, `CalendarFlyout` (with its sliding strip and its composition visuals),
  `DateIsland` (what the calendar face measured with is `DateText`), the entries' shapes,
  `IslandView.Weather`/`.Calendar`, `WidgetSource.Weather`/`.Date`, `WidgetInfos.Weather`,
  `CalendarOptions.View` and `.TimeZone`, the calendar's flyout heights, the Settings view row and
  its pictures (`CalendarViewRow`, `CalendarViewArt`), the Look row and the looks (§12.7), and their
  words in the five languages.

**Matched against the flyouts' own pictures** (rendered before they went: `calendar-<view>-dark.png`,
`weather-dark.png`, …). The same: the weather's header, graph and rows at 150 %; the calendar's
header, agenda rows (each event in its calendar's colour) and the day, week and year views; the
weather face's three looks against the entry's (`weather-looks-*` against `weather-faces-*`).
**Different, and why:** a list's gutter is
12 px at 100 % where the flyouts kept 16; the month is the clock's month (§68) — the day picked filled
with the accent and today ringed, cells a seventh of the width — where the calendar's flyout filled
today and ringed the day picked; the footer is the actions line, a link and an icon button, where the
flyout had two text buttons; the weather's age is the conditions' line's last line, not a footer
band; a folder ends in its name's band; the week's days step without the flyout's glide; the
accent is the folder's (the system accent) where the flyouts in a dark theme took its lighter tone;
the hours and the week before a place is set say "No location yet" where the flyout had one
prompt; and a view starts Automatic up to its kind's most, so the week and the day show fewer hours
than a tall flyout did unless their height is set higher (§76).

Tests: `WeatherPlacesTests` (each piece its own place; a new one the device's location, a file's unchanged; the preset's one spread; a file of the shared place read once), `SetupLinkTests` (a weather line with no place, or for a location Windows will not give, links to its place), `WeatherCalendarPresetTests` (each folder, its face and its lines in order; each its own; an
ordinary folder after; no entries, a file's entries dropped and their lines kept), `WeatherFaceTests`
(the looks in the file, unknown words, words in every language; the face's own place; widths from the
settings in order and never the forecast's; inside the cell and centred; the days from the place's
today; a new reading paints again), `CalendarWeatherFolderTests` (the month picks the day the events
show and the header goes back; the views follow and publish, step and keep their own when switched
off; the hours scroll and stop and targets are where they are drawn; the week from the region's
first day — Monday, Sunday, Saturday; the weather set up once; pictures),
`DefaultBarTests.TheWeatherIsTheWeatherPreset`, `.TheDateIsTheCalendarPresetAfterTheClock`,
`StaleMarkPictures` (the mark on the events, the month and the views, clear of their titles and
arrows, its tooltip; `stale-<events|month|dayview|weekview|yearview>-lines.png`), `ResetTests` (a
shape 22 file kept aside),
`ChannelsTests`, `ListGutterTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `DataSourcesTests`. Pictures:
`calendar-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `calendar-views-<dark|light>.png`, `weather-preset-<dark|light>.png`,
`weather-faces-<96|144>-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: a weather folder — set a place on its
first line and watch the face and the other two lines follow; the face's three looks; the calendar
folder — pick days in the month and the events follow, the header back to today, "Open Calendar"
opening the calendar app; a week view added to it, its days clicked, stepped and scrolled.

## 81. A separator splits a dock (2026-10-10) — no separator, a section one dock, since §511 (2026-11-05)

*The person*: "the separator should also separate groups in the dock view as well. right now it
basically just adds a space and line between but it should look like they are separate
'docks'/groups so to speak." On an islands bar a separator already ends a group and the next group
wears a card of its own (§54); in a dock (§71) it drew a line, or only a seam, inside one panel.

- **Two docks** (`Layout.Panels`, `DockPanel(Section, Group, Rect)`). A section that holds a widget is
  one dock, and each separator between two of its widgets splits it: the widgets either side are two
  docks, each Windows 11's floating surface as a section's dock always was — its own material, 8-DIP
  corners, hairline and shadow, the bar's thickness, the lift off the edge — and the room between
  them is the room between two docks (8 DIP) plus each dock's own room inside its end
  (`Layout.split`). A separator at a section's start or end, or a second one beside the first,
  splits nothing. `SectionPanels()` is still each section's whole stretch, the docks inside it.
- **The separator draws nothing in a dock.** Appearance's line (§78) is read as off on a floating bar
  (`Layout.Separators.Line`): the gap is the separation, and a line in it would stand on the
  wallpaper or on whatever window is behind, with nothing to sit on, and over a stretch a press
  passes through. Windows draws nothing between its floating surfaces either. The **space**
  Appearance gives separators still counts: it widens the gap by itself either side. At rest the
  separator takes no room and is no part of the bar (no block, no hit, no line), as §54's spacer.
- **A press in the gap is the desktop's**, as between two sections' docks: the window's region at
  rest is the docks and the room under each to the edge (`Layout.PanelReach`, `DockWindow.PanelsRegion`).
- **Edit mode moves nothing.** The separator gets §61's marker, always the dashed empty box in a dock,
  laid in the middle of the gap and taking no room, so the docks and every widget stand where they
  stood at rest; it is grabbed, selected, dragged and deleted there. A marker is now found between
  its neighbours in the run being laid out rather than in the list (`Layout.Parted`), so while a
  block is carried across a separator, or the separator itself is carried, the docks split and join
  where the block will land (`Layout.Panels(moving, slot)`, the scene's panels following it). The
  same fixes an islands bar's group cards during such a drag. A section holding only a separator
  has no dock; in edit mode its marker stands at the section's start.
- **The scene** keeps one panel per (section, group), made the first time that dock shows and then
  shown, hidden and glided like the old three (`Scene.ShowPanels`); a dock that appears mid-drag gets
  its panel then.
- **Hover**: a hover place is still a section: its docks come in together, the gaps between them
  passing presses through. A group is not a place of its own; splitting a dock is about the look,
  and three sliding windows per edge are already the most §71 wanted.
- **Unchanged**: the strip held (`Reserve`), the keyboard's order, drags between sections, flyouts
  anchored to their widget, the accessibility tree.

Tests: `DockGroupsTests` (a separator makes two docks the 8-DIP room apart inside the section's
panel, both edges, 100 and 150 %; no separator one dock a section; a separator at an end or beside
another splits once; a press in the gap is nobody's; edit mode moves nothing and the marker is in
the gap and grabbed there; the line is not drawn and the space widens the gap; carrying a widget or
the separator across joins and splits the docks), `SceneTreeTests.ASeparatorSplitsADocksPanelInTheScene`,
and the floating cases of `SeparatorLineTests`, `WidgetGroupTests` and `BarLineTests` turned to the
new rule. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `dock-groups-<bottom|top>-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-<150|100>.png`
(search split from Task view and the apps, the clock from the graph) and
`dock-groups-line-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png` (Appearance's line with space: no line, a wider gap).
By hand: a click in the gap between two docks reaches the window under it; drag a widget across a
separator in edit mode and watch the docks re-form.

**Settings says so (2026-10-10, later).** Appearance's Line switch for separators read as if it drew
a line everywhere. Its description (`settings.appearance.line.separatorDescription`, five languages)
is now "Never drawn in a dock: a separator splits it into separate docks". The islands and the flat
bar are unchanged — a line there where the switch is on — so the hint names only the dock, with the
word the layout's type uses (`settings.layouts.type.dock`). What the card said before ("Off, a
separator draws nothing and only splits the widgets into groups") moved, shortened, to the group's
description, "How every separator looks; each splits the widgets into groups": a description is one
sentence of twelve words at most (`ShortDescriptionsTests`), too few for both. Test:
`LineRowsTests.TheLineSaysADockDrawsNone`.

## 82. A tray icon dragged is never clicked (2026-10-10)

The person: *"when you try to reorder the tray widgets it left clicks them immediately, this should
not be."*

- **What it was.** The dock sent an icon's app `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` as the button went down
  (`Tray.Press`, from the rewrite on, 2298bf5; in the overflow from 61bba08) and the up with
  `NIN_SELECT` as it came up. A drag only dropped the up (`pressedTray = null`), so an app that acts
  on the down opened under every drag, on the bar, in a bar's second tray and in the overflow. One
  that came forward also closed the overflow under the held icon, which `Flyout.Hold` (7e6305c)
  worked around rather than fixed. No commit ever held the press back; what looked fixed was apps
  that act on the up only.
- **As Windows does it.** A press sends nothing. The click goes whole as the button comes up on the
  icon it went down on within the drag threshold (SM_CXDRAG/SM_CYDRAG): down (a double click's for
  the second of two within the double-click time), up, and `NIN_SELECT` or `WM_CONTEXTMENU` for
  version 3 and later. Past the threshold it is a drag and stays one, back over its place or not,
  and nothing is sent. Escape or the mouse lost calls the press off.
- **One place decides** (`TrayClicks`): the bars' grabs ask it at every move whether the press is a
  drag yet (screen px, so the relayout that brings the chevron in at drag start changes nothing), the
  overflow tells it so at its first `DragMove`, and a release asks it for the click to send
  (`Tray.Click(TrayClick, bar)`, the only way left to send a click). The bar's icons and the
  overflow's share it, as they share the double-click record. Edit mode presses no tray icon at all.

Tests: `TrayClicksTests` (a drag along the bar, in a second tray and out of the overflow sends
nothing; a press called off or let go on another icon is no click; within the threshold the whole
click on the release for versions 0, 3 and 4; the double click, broken by a drag between; the right
button; and a real window standing for the app's hears the three messages only on the release).
By hand: drag a tray icon whose app opens on a press (Teams, OneDrive, the Bluetooth icon) along the
bar, onto the chevron and out of the overflow: nothing opens. A click still opens it, a double click
still double-clicks, a right click still shows the menu.

## 83. Connecting to a network never holds the pointer (2026-10-10)

The person: "when i click connect on a network the mouse freezes for a second or so". Two faults
together:

- **The Wi-Fi page asked Windows on the dock's thread.** Connect wrote the profile and called
  `WlanConnect`, then read the list again; the WLAN service answers only once it is done with what it
  is doing, a second and more while it joins. The cables' list (`WindowsWired`, the Network List
  Manager) is as slow while a network is identified, and was read on every news.
- **The menus' low-level mouse hook was the dock thread's.** Windows holds every mouse event of the
  machine until a low-level hook's thread answers, so any slow call on the dock's thread while a
  flyout was open froze the pointer, not only the flyout.

Fixes:

- `OffThread<T>` (`QuickSettings/Services/OffThread.cs`): each network source (`OffThreadWifi`,
  `OffThreadWired`) makes every call into Windows on a thread of its own, in turn, and keeps what it
  last read. The page reads that at once and hears through its `Changes` when it changed (the
  source's own news, or a read that came out different). Connect shows "Connecting…" at once — or the
  key/sign-in at once where that is plain without Windows (`WifiProfiles.Foreseen`, which
  `WindowsWifi.Connect` uses too) — and the outcome follows. Opening waits at most 250 ms for the
  first read, so the page opens with its networks rather than growing into them.
- `PressHook` (`Karpo.Dock/PressHook.cs`): the menus' mouse hook runs on a thread of its own that only
  posts a button press to each thread with a menu open (a message-only sink window), where
  `FlyoutHost.Pressed` does what the hook did before. Posted messages are read before input, so a menu
  still sees itself closed before the click that closed it.
- `WindowsSound.SetDefault` (the output/microphone pickers, the sound island's device choice) switches
  the default device on the pool, in order; the page hears the new default from Windows.

Left as they are (a brief look, 2026-10-10), all on the dock's thread from a click: `Items.Open`'s
synchronous `ShellExecuteExW` (ms-settings fallbacks, the drives flyout opening a folder — a dead
network path can take seconds), the power-mode rows (`PowerSetActiveOverlayScheme`), renaming a
desktop, and `EditFollowHook`'s keyboard/mouse hooks, which are still the dock thread's during edit
mode (whether to keep a key is decided from the dock's own windows).

Tests: `OffThreadTests` (a stand-in Wi-Fi whose connect blocks: the dock's thread is back at once
with "Connecting…", the outcome comes back through the Changes from the worker thread; a key asked
for at once; forget and dispose; `Foreseen`; reads compared by what they show), `PressHookTests`
(the hook on a thread of its own, a press posted with its point and a move not, nothing posted after
the last menu; a busy menu thread doesn't hold the hook). By hand: open the network flyout, Connect
to a network — the pointer keeps moving and "Connecting…" shows at once; menus and flyouts still close
for a click outside them, and a click on the bar still toggles its flyout.

## 84. A stopwatch, in the timer's style (2026-10-10)

The person: "add a stopwatch widget as well, in the same style as the timer and focus widget." It is
built as the timer is, in its three places, and drawn with the same pieces (the list's edges, the
quick-settings buttons, the countdown pane's sizes).

- **The value** (`Clock\Stopwatch.cs`): `StopwatchState` is what it banked, since when it runs and its
  laps (totals; a lap's length is the difference). Start, pause, resume (one button, `Act`), lap while
  running (at most 999), reset to nought. It is handed a **monotonic** time (`StopwatchClock`, the
  performance counter), never the wall clock, so setting Windows' clock or a zone change never moves
  it; it never reads below nought or what it banked, and stops at 99:59:59.9.
- **One per widget, shared by its faces.** Kept by the widget's id in the dock's store
  (`Countdowns.Stopwatches`, beside the countdowns so it travels wherever they are handed), so the
  entry, its panel and a line of it are one stopwatch, closing the panel leaves it running, and a
  widget removed takes it with it (`Countdowns.Keep`, `KeysIn`). In memory only, as a timer is: a
  restart of Karpo clears it. It has no options (`WidgetOptionsKind.None`).
- **Written**: in tenths, begun not rounded ("0:00.0", "12:34.5", "1:02:03.4"), the tenth set off by
  the region's decimal sign (`Nls.DecimalSeparator`); its room is the widest reading
  (`StopwatchText.Template`), so nothing moves as it counts. On the bar and a clock face five figures
  in whole seconds, as a countdown's (`StopwatchText.Cell`).
- **The entry** (`StopwatchTile`, `WidgetShapes.Stopwatch`): glyph and "04:59", one to four cells, the
  room "88:88" keeps; paused in the quieter ink. It ticks once a second while it runs, and its tick
  redraws it in place: it never asks for a rebuild. A click opens its own panel.
- **The panel** (`StopwatchFlyout`, `StopwatchCard.Pane`): a countdown pane with laps — glyph and
  name, the time at 34 DIP, the lap and reset buttons at the left, the start button with its word at
  the right (Start, Pause, Resume), a hairline, and its newest four laps (name, length, total), or
  "No laps yet". One height whatever it does. It ticks a tenth on its own window only while it is
  open and the stopwatch runs, and draws only when what it reads changed. Tab walks the buttons that
  do something now, Enter and Space press, Escape closes.
- **A line** (`StopwatchCard.Arrange/Build`), one row to six, natural height a timer's one-row line:
  glyph, name, the time against the buttons, then lap, reset and the accent start button at the
  gutter. Narrow, it gives way as a countdown's line does (`CountdownLineTier`): the name, then the
  lap and reset fold into the line's menu (Start/Pause, Lap, Reset — `WidgetAct.Lap/Reset`), then the
  glyph. Taller, its laps under the row, newest first, the lap's length under the time and its total
  at the end; two rows hold one at the list's text, three at larger text.
- **One row shows the lap too** (2026-10-11). The person: "for the stopwatch the flag does not do
  anything (at least when shown one row high.), it should at least show the lap time on the same row
  as well there." The flag did take laps; a one-row line had no room to list them, so nothing showed.
  Now, once a lap is taken, a line with no lap rows writes the **lap under way**
  (`StopwatchState.CurrentLap`: since the last lap ended) in the name's place, right-aligned a gap
  before the time, after a small flag, in the quieter ink: "⚑ 0:03.9  **1:23.4**". It ticks with the
  time, holds while paused, and goes on reset (with the laps). Its room is judged by the widest its
  shape can say (`StopwatchCard.Widest`, every figure an 8), so it never comes and goes as it counts;
  where even that leaves no room for the flag (narrow, past an hour) the flag goes, and with no room
  for the figures the readout does — the time and the start button always stay. At the Narrow list
  width, 100 % and 150 %, it fits with its flag. Taller lines keep listing laps and show no readout.
  Pictures: `stopwatch-one-row-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png` (Narrow, Medium, Wide × every state and a
  lap just taken); tests `TheLapUnderWayRunsFromTheLastLap`, `AtOneRowTheFlagShowsTheLapUnderWay`.
- **Greyed, not gone.** The lap and reset buttons are always there and greyed where they do nothing
  (no lap unless running, no reset when idle), as Windows' Clock has them, so the row never moves; a
  greyed button takes no click and the keyboard passes it over.
- **Tenths only while visible and running, no full redraws.** In a folder the line asks the dock for
  no tick; the open folder arms a *quick* tick of its own (`FolderFlyout.ArmQuick`, 100 ms) while a
  stopwatch in it counts, which redraws that line alone (`DrawCard`) and nothing else of the folder;
  started or stopped from the line, its menu, its panel or its entry, the dock re-arms it. A closed
  folder ticks nothing.
- **The clock face** shows a stopwatch in its folder as it shows a timer, after one: a running
  countdown, then a running stopwatch, then a paused or finished countdown, then a paused stopwatch.
  What moves beats what stands still, and a countdown, a time somebody has to meet, beats a
  stopwatch. A face over a folder holding one keeps the room for it, and the dock ticks a second
  while one runs.
- **Library**: the Time group beside the timer and the focus time, on both pages (the group stays
  under the twelve-row cap). Not in the default layout.

Tests: `StopwatchTests` (state machine, monotonic clock, store, keep, formatting, registries),
`StopwatchFormsTests` (the entry one row at every bar height and scale; ticks repaint and rebuild
nothing; the line at its own height and one row to six at three scales, three text sizes and two
widths, every state: nothing overlaps or leaves the gutters, nothing moves between states, laps
listed; greyed buttons; the panel's height, keyboard and tenth; the folder's quick tick). Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `stopwatch-<bar|line|panel>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`,
`stopwatch-<line|panel>-150-<contrast|colours>.png`. By hand: start one on the bar and open its panel
and a folder holding it; the tenths run smoothly in both and the rest of the folder stays still.

## 85. Premade widgets (2026-10-10)

The person: "you should premade widgets (which are actually just configurations of the action
widget), like bluetooth actions, wifi actions, clock action, calendar actions." The library had
presets (§73, §80), which are folders of several widgets; nothing offered one widget set up already.

A **premade widget** (`Karpo.Core\PremadeWidgets.cs`) is a list widget's kind and its options, and a
name and icon for the add list — nothing else. `Catalogue.Offered(page)` is the page's rows
(`Catalogue.On`, unchanged: still exactly the registry) with each widget's premade widgets right
under it; the add list (`AddList.Rows`) shows them as a **submenu of the widget's row**, as Windows'
"New ›" is: "Actions ›" in System opens Actions itself, a line, then the six, each its own name and
glyph (the submenu beside the row's column, `Flyout.OpenSubmenu`). They were rows of the list at first,
right under Actions: six near-identical "… actions" rows made the list a column wider, past three
quarters of a 1440p screen at 150 % (`AddListPictures`), for variants of one widget — a submenu
keeps the list to the widgets and the variants one hover away. The search still reaches them: the
row lights where one under it matches (`AddList.Matching`), the count counts them
(`AddList.Count`), and Enter adds the one that matches from under its row (`AddList.Single`,
`AddList.Picks`). Its row (`CatalogueEntry.Premade`) keeps its widget's id, group
and search words, and is found besides by the names of what it opens ("add device" finds Bluetooth
actions). A pick adds an **ordinary line** of the widget (`PremadeWidget.New`, `Folders.AddNew` for a
made island): nothing in the file says where it came from, and its settings change it as any line's.
Another kind of premade widget is another options property on the record and a line in `Apply`.

The six, each a flyout's footer as Windows ends it (link left, button right):

| Premade | Left | Right |
|---|---|---|
| Clock actions | Date & time | Focus |
| Calendar actions | Date & time | Open Calendar (the calendar app) |
| Wi-Fi actions | Wi-Fi | Network & internet |
| Bluetooth actions | Bluetooth & devices | Add device |
| Sound actions | Sound | Volume mixer |
| Notification actions | Notifications | Focus |

"Add device" is `ms-settings:bluetooth`, Settings' Bluetooth page with its "Add device" button at the
top, the same address as `BluetoothPage.AddDevice` (a test holds the two equal; §88 for why not
`ms-settings-connectabledevices:devicediscovery`, which opens Cast). Opening the calendar app was an action
already (§68). The calendar's footer is Date & time on the left and Open Calendar on the right, as
the clock's starts with Date & time (the user's call, 2026-10-11; it was the app on the left before).

**Presets use them**: a preset's line names a premade widget (`PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.ClockActions)`,
`PresetItem.Premade`) instead of its own slots, so the clock's and the calendar's footers are the
premade widgets and cannot drift. The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth presets (§88) end with
`PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.WifiActions)` / `BluetoothActions` the same way.

Tests: `PremadeWidgetsTests` (the six and their pages, words in every language, under Actions in the
add list in order with their own name and icon and none on the bar, the search, a pick is an ordinary
actions line, two made share nothing, the presets' footers are the records, Add device is the
Bluetooth page's), `TheSubmenuOpensBesideItsColumnAndEnterAddsFromIt` (on a real list: the keys open it beside its
column, Enter in the field adds the one premade widget that matches),
`AddListTests.TheRowsAreThatLibrarysOwn` (the library's rows plus the premade ones, as picked),
`TogglesAndActionsTests` (the Add device address).

## 86. A folder's face is a section of its own (2026-10-10)

The person: *"in the folder configuration the face should get an own expand section where you
choose the face in the section header and then the configurations for the face (e.g. the location
for the weather) should be shown in the section dependent on what face is shown."*

- **The section** (`FolderPage.faceCard`): "Face", *What its button on the taskbar shows*, the face
  dropdown in its header where an expander's summary stands (as Windows puts a choice in a section's
  header). Closed at the start, as every section (§79; `SectionsStartCollapsedTests`).
- **Its body is the face's rows alone** (`FolderRows.Rows`, `RowsShown`): the icon face the icon
  picker and the name; the clock its seconds, hours, zone, label and timer; the calendar its look
  and, for text, its form; the weather *Use my device's location*, *Place* and its look; what is
  inside the name (first drafted with nothing, "This face has nothing to set"; see below). A new face's
  options come with its descriptor as before. The body is made again when the face changes and only
  filled otherwise, so a row being typed in is never pulled away; values per face are kept while the
  page is open (`FolderRows.FaceFor`).
- **The weather's place** is the face's own (§80, `FolderFace.Weather`, `FolderRows.PlaceKept`):
  the rows set it there and touch no line of the folder, each of which has its own place on its
  own page (2026-10-10; before, the row wrote into a weather line and the lines followed it, and a
  folder with no weather line had its rows greyed). The box is the widget
  page's, as a control the page builds in code (`PlacePicker`: search as you type, Enter, forget,
  the status line under it).
- **No "Button on the taskbar" card.** It had the icon and the name beside it; both are rows of
  the faces that use them now (below), so it went.
- **The name beside the button only beside icons** (the person, later that day: *"showing the
  name for example should only be possible if you show its icons or its contents, but not with
  every face type."*). A clock, a date or a temperature is words already; a name beside it reads
  as one run of text. `FaceInfo.Named` says which faces take one (what is inside, the icon); their
  bodies end with the "Show the name beside it" check row, and the others have none. The bar asks
  `FolderOptions.NameShown` (`ShowName` and the face takes one), so a file set to show the name
  under a clock draws none. The stored `ShowName` is **kept**, not cleared: the file keeps what was
  chosen, an older build reads it as it did, and switching back to the icon or what is inside
  brings the name back as the faces' own options come back (`FolderRows.FaceFor`).
- **The icon is the icon face's row alone.** What the folder's glyph (`FolderOptions.Glyph`) is
  used for, looked up 2026-10-10: the icon face's drawing (`IconFace`), and nothing else. The open
  folder has no title row since 8e455a6 (and no footer glyph), its tooltip is the name, the
  Settings tree and the add list use the kind's glyph, and what is inside draws its widgets — or
  four empty squares with none — never the folder's glyph. So the icon is set where it shows. A
  folder's chosen glyph is kept under the other faces, for the icon face to wear again.

Every face's body has a row now (what is inside its name), so "This face has nothing to set" is
only for a face that has neither options nor a name: the Wi-Fi, Bluetooth (§88) and sound (§90) glyphs.

Tests: `FolderRowsTests` (every face's body from the header's pick, the name for the icon and
what is inside alone and last, the icon for the icon face alone, switching keeps each face's
values, the weather's place row and where it keeps the place), `FolderFaceTests` (`NameShown` per
face; a name set under a clock round-trips and comes back with the icon; the sheets draw a clock
and a calendar page set to show the name without it), `FolderButtonTests.AFaceOfWordsDrawsNoNameBesideIt`
(a clock, calendar or weather button as wide with the name set as without; the icon wider),
`SectionsStartCollapsedTests.TheFolderFaceSectionStartsClosed`. By hand: a folder's page, Face
section — the check row under what is inside and under the icon (after the icon), none under the
clock, the date, the weather; no "Button on the taskbar" card; a folder showing its name switched
to a clock loses the name on the bar and gets it back switched to the icon.

## 87. To-do lists and notes (2026-10-10)

The person: "add a generic todo list widget and add a notes widget. (they should have a central
store and you should be able to select which list / note they are showing.) the notes widget should
support markdown".

**The store.** One notebook for both kinds, `Karpo.Core\Notebook.cs`, in its own file,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\notebook.json` (`Config.LocalFolder`, which `KARPO_CONFIG_DIR` moves): named
to-do lists (each task its words, done, its place in the list, when it was made and when it was
ticked off) and named notes (a title, a Markdown body, when it last changed). Not config.json: what
somebody writes is theirs, and the settings file is exported, merged and edited by hand. A widget
keeps only the id of the list or note it shows (`TodoOptions.List`, `NoteOptions.Note`); none, or
one that has been deleted, shows the notebook's first.

- **Writes**: every change is a function of what the file says *now*, under a named mutex for the
  file (one per path, so the tests' folders never wait on the person's) and a lock in the process:
  read, apply, write to a temporary file, `File.Replace` it in with the version before kept as
  `notebook.json.bak`. The dock and the settings app never lose each other's change; a crash never
  leaves half a file.
- **Tolerant reads**: a file that does not parse is kept as `notebook.json.broken-<time>` and the
  backup read instead, never written over; one another program holds is not read as an empty
  notebook (a change then stands on what was last read). Inside a file that parses, `Normalize` puts
  right missing lists, ids missing or twice, names of spaces, over-long words and a finished time on
  a task not done; comments and trailing commas are allowed, unknown fields ignored.
- **Live**: `Changed` fires after this process's change and when the file changes under it
  (`Watch`, a debounced `FileSystemWatcher`: the settings app's change, a hand edit). Every line
  showing that list or note is woken (`CellIsland.Wake`) and redraws; a change made in a line is
  drawn at once (`CellIsland.Redrawn`, `IWidgetContainer.Redraw`), not a post away.
- **Not encrypted, deliberately.** The PIM cache is encrypted with DPAPI (dd11aa3) because it is a
  copy of what a server holds: losing the key costs a download. A note is the only copy there is.
  DPAPI ties it to the profile's key — an administrator's password reset, a restored profile, a copy
  to a new PC, and every note is noise for ever — and a person who opens the file to rescue their
  notes could not read it. The file is as private as the profile's folder (its ACL is the user's)
  and a BitLocker disk.

**The to-do line** (`Karpo.Dock\Notes\TodoTile.cs`), as Microsoft To Do draws a list: the list's
name, "Add a task", the tasks not done each with Windows' check box, and "Completed N" with the done
ones under it — struck through and quieter — once it is opened (closed again each time the folder
opens). Everything happens in the line:

- a press on "Add a task", or a letter typed while the line has the focus, types a task in a text
  box drawn in place (`InlineEditor`, WinUI's look: the fill, the rim, the accent along the bottom);
  Enter adds it at the top and types the next, Escape or a press elsewhere keeps what was typed;
- a box ticks (the task keeps its place among the others, so unticking puts it back); the trash at
  the end of the row under the pointer deletes; a double click or F2 renames, and words taken away
  delete, as To Do's do;
- a task pressed and dragged up or down goes where the accent line between two rows shows;
- the keys with the focus on the line: Up and Down choose a row (past the first or last, the
  folder's focus moves on), Space ticks, Enter adds or renames, Delete deletes, Alt+Up/Down moves.

Its height is §76's: Automatic up to its most (the panel's), or Fixed. **No scrolling inside**: held
shorter than the list, the name and "Add a task" stay, the tasks that fit are shown and the last row
says how many more ("6 more tasks", `WidgetFill`), the rule every list line follows.

**The note line** (`NoteTile.cs`): the note's title, and its body as **one editor that is always
live** — the person (2026-10-11): "the note widget should not switch between input and showing the
note, it should be a wysiwyg editor much like obsidian does it." It was a rendered view that a click
swapped for a raw text box; now it is one live editor. The note stays Markdown, stored as before (no
format change); every line of its text is a row on screen, every mark of it shown faint and the words
drawn as what the marks make them, at rest and wherever the caret is (§321; until then the marks hid
but where the caret was, as Obsidian's live preview does):

- `Markdown.cs` reads the text line by line (`Markdown.Lines`: headings `#`–`######`, bulleted and
  numbered items nested by two spaces, tasks, quotes holding any of these, fences and the code
  between them, rules, paragraphs' lines, blank lines) and each line's inline runs (`MdSpan`: bold,
  italic, both, struck, `code`, `[links](…)`, `<…>`, bare `https://` and `www.` addresses, escapes,
  images as their words), every one keeping where it stands in the text and which of its characters
  are marks. Not read: setext headings (a `---` line is a rule), indented code, tables, HTML,
  footnotes, reference links.
- `Markdown.Show` makes a line as shown (`MdShown`): its text, every character, and its runs — the
  marks (`#`s, a list's marker, `>`s, `**`, a link's address, fences, rules) `Mark`, a task's
  `[ ]`/`[x]` `Box`, a ticked task's words struck. A place in the note is the same place in the row.
- `NoteLayout.cs` lays each row out with the DirectWrite pipeline every line uses (type ramp 20, 18,
  16, 14 semibold for headings, their `#`s as big; code in Consolas on a plate from fence to fence;
  marks in the tertiary ink; a task's box and links in the link colour; selected text in the
  selection's own colour on the accent; since §669 a row's marks a lead of their own and its words
  wrapping in a hanging indent after it), and answers where things are: a point's place in the text
  (a task's box with a little slack), the caret's box, a wrapped line's ends, the place above or
  below. Rows that did not change keep their layouts; the caret moving lays nothing out again.
- `NoteEditor.cs` (pure) holds the text, caret and selection (`TextEditing`'s rules, multi-line) and
  the edits Markdown asks for (`NoteEdits`): Enter goes on with a list (a task unticked, a number one
  on, the indent and quote kept) and on an empty item ends it (one level out, then no marker), the
  same for a quote; Tab and Shift+Tab indent every item the caret or selection is on (off a list Tab
  leaves the note, as before, so the keyboard can get out); Backspace at an item's words takes the
  marker away (one level out first); the arrows go through marks a character at a time. Undo and redo
  (`NoteHistory`): a run of typing or deleting is a step up to a space after a word, anything else a
  step of its own, at most 200.

The keys: typing (surrogate pairs whole), the arrows (Ctrl by words), Up, Down, Page Up and Down by
the lines as they wrap, Home and End by the wrapped line (Ctrl: the note's ends), Shift with any of
them to select, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C/X/V as plain text (the Markdown as written; a paste's tabs become
four spaces), Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Enter ticks the task the caret is on (elsewhere
it ends the typing), Escape ends it. The pointer: a click puts the caret there (a double click a
word, a triple its line, Shift+click selects to it, a drag selects); the pointer over the words is
the text cursor (`CellIsland.TextOn`). A click on a task's `[ ]` ticks it (in the text being typed, so it is undone like typing, else in the note), and a
click on a link opens it by the shell on a thread of its own (STA), only http, https and mailto
(`Markdown.Opens`) — unless the caret is in that link, where the click edits it; its tooltip is
where it goes. Enter or F2 with the focus on the line gives it the keys; a press on the title, a
press elsewhere in the folder or the folder closing takes them; what was typed is kept then, and
after two seconds of rest while typing.

**IME.** There is no TSF text store: the editor is a custom one on the folder's `WM_KEYDOWN` and
`WM_CHAR`. An IME composes in its own window, which the folder puts at the caret on
`WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION` (`ImmSetCompositionWindow`, the candidates kept clear of the line;
`CellIsland.CaretOn`), and the default handling sends what was chosen as `WM_CHAR`. The composition is
not drawn inline in the note.

**Longer than its line**, the note scrolls inside it: the wheel scrolls it (and is the list's once
it can go no further either way), the caret is kept in view, and a thin bar at the line's edge says
how much more there is and where this is.

**The toolbar** (2026-10-11, *"for the note widget it should also get a little toolbar on top where
you have basic formatting helpers"*). A row of Windows 11 icon buttons under the title, fixed: the
note scrolls under it, as a command bar stands over what it acts on. In three groups with a thin
line between: a heading; bold, italic, strikethrough, code and link; bulleted list, numbered list,
task list and quote. Segoe Fluent Icons glyphs (E8DD, E8DB, EDE0, E943, E71B, E8FD, E9D5, E9B2); the
font has no numbered list, so that one is drawn ("1" and "2" before two strokes), and the heading
is a semibold "H" that reads "H1" to "H3" with the caret in one. Each tooltip says what it does and
its key: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+Shift+X, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+H (the heading in turn), Ctrl+Shift+8,
Ctrl+Shift+7, Ctrl+Shift+9 and Ctrl+Shift+. (Word's, Teams' and GitHub's, as near as they agree);
never with Alt held, since Ctrl+Alt is AltGr typing € or @ on German and Swiss keyboards.

What they do is `NoteFormat.cs`, pure and tested without a window, each one step to undo:
- *Bold, italic, struck, code* toggle round the selection: off (the run's marks taken away, its
  words kept, a `***both***` run keeping the other) where every line's selected words, or the caret,
  already stand in a run of that kind, else on, line by line over several lines, the spaces at the
  ends left outside the marks, the selection kept on the words. Nothing selected, a pair goes in with
  the caret between it (`**|**`), and the same button again takes the untouched pair away.
- *Link*: in a `[words](address)` it takes the marks away; else `[]()` with the caret in the
  brackets, `[words]()` with the caret in the parentheses, or an address selected
  `[](address)` with the caret in the brackets.
- *Heading* goes round none, 1, 2, 3, none, as the first line touched is; every line touched takes
  that level, an item's marker going.
- *Lists and quote* act on every line the selection touches (a selection ending at a line's start
  leaves that line): off where they all are that already, else each made one, another list's marker
  or a heading's #s replaced, indents and quotes kept, numbers counting on from an item just above
  and each depth on its own. A quote quotes the blank lines between too, so it stays one quote.
  Code blocks are left alone.

A button lights under the pointer and shows pressed (the subtle selected fill) where the caret's
words already are what it makes; it acts when let go on it, and a press that slides off does
nothing. A press on it is the note's own, so the typing, the caret and the selection stay — the
folder ends typing only for a press on another line. At rest a button starts the typing first, the
caret at the note's end, and the toolbar's ink is the secondary until then.

*Narrow.* Every button needs about 330 DIP at 100 % text: a medium (360) or wide list has them all in
a row; a narrow one (280), or any at large text, has the buttons that fit, in order, and "More"
(E712) at the row's end, which opens the rest in rows under it and closes them again. Rows rather
than a menu, since a folder's line has no menu of its own to open and a row keeps the buttons
where the pointer is; the line grows by the rows while it is open, which is the person's doing.
*Short.* The toolbar takes a row of 34 DIP (scaled by the text size); a line held too short for the
title, the toolbar and one line of the note has none, and the keys still work.

**How the folder hands it the keys.** A line with a text box that has the keys says so
(`CellIsland.TypingOn`). The folder then hands it every key first — Escape and Tab too, so Escape
ends the typing rather than closing the folder — and every `WM_CHAR` (`CharOn`; a character with no
line typing goes to the line with the focus, which is how a letter starts a task). A press anywhere
else in the folder ends the typing (`StopTypingOn`) before the press does anything else. The caret
blinks on the folder's tick (`IntervalMs` 500 while typing, nothing otherwise).

**Settings.** The widget's page has one card: the list (or the note) as a dropdown of the
notebook's, and New, Rename and Delete beside it, each a dialog; Delete says it deletes from every
line that shows it. The names follow the notebook as it changes (`IslandOptions.Notebook.cs`).

**Library.** A new group, "Notes and to-dos" (`WidgetCategory.Notes`), before the folders, and two
ready-made folders, "To-do" and "Notes" (`Presets`, one line each, the checklist and the note glyph).
No taskbar entry: a quick-add on the bar is for later.

Tests: `NotebookTests` (round trip, a new task's place, the first task making a list, a list that is
gone, tick, rename, move and delete, the view's order, names held to their most, two stores and
forty changes at once keeping every change, a broken file kept aside and the backup read, an odd
file put right, a held file not written over with nothing, the watcher hearing another store),
`MarkdownTests` (every line and inline form, nested emphasis, marks that are not emphasis, links
that would start a program as plain words, task boxes and toggling; every mark shown and styled, and
every place shown one for one over a set of half-written notes), `NoteEditorTests` (Enter going on
with and ending a list or a quote, Tab and Shift+Tab over a selection, Backspace taking a marker, the
arrows through the marks, undo by words and by edit, the history's most, cut and paste), `NoteFormatTests` (every
format on and off, over several lines, an empty pair in and out, what each button shows, a format
one step to undo), `TextEditingTests` (the
multi-line mode), `NotebookLinesTests` (typing, ticking, renaming, deleting and the keys; a drag
into another place; "N more tasks" inside the line; editing a note and keeping it on Escape and on
close; the marks shown on every line, Up, Down, Home, Enter and Tab in a list, a link
opened or edited; a link opening and a box ticking; a long note scrolled by the wheel and to the
caret with no ink past its line at 100 and 225 % text; which list or note a line shows, and a change
elsewhere shown; the toolbar's buttons and keys, a press sliding off, AltGr not taken, "More" in a
narrow line and no toolbar in a line too short), and the registries' tables (`TypedRegistryTests`, `ListGutterTests`,
`WidgetMenuTests`, `InteractionTests`, `CataloguePagesTests`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`notes-todo-<dark|light>.png` (at rest, completed open with a task lit, typing a task, ten tasks held
to six rows; 100 and 225 % text) and `notes-note-<dark|light>.png` (the Markdown sample at rest, the
caret in the heading, in the bold, in a task's words and in its marker, in a link with words
selected; held to five rows and scrolled; an empty note typed in) and `notes-toolbar-<dark|light>.png`
(narrow, medium and wide at 100 and 225 % text: at rest, the caret in the bold with the pointer on
italic, the caret in the heading with "More" open where there is one).

By hand: type into "Add a task" in a folder (another keyboard layout, and an IME: its candidate
window stands where Windows puts it, not at the caret); drag a task; tick a box in a note; open a
link; edit a note and press Escape; the toolbar's buttons and keys (Ctrl+B with a German or Swiss
layout, AltGr+E still typing €), "More" in a narrow list; change the list on the widget's settings page, and make, rename
and delete one in the settings app while the folder is open.

### Microsoft To Do (2026-10-16)

*"add a todo widget as well if we dont have already. it should get its tasks from microsoft office, like the
email etc."* There was one; it now has a source. The widget's page has **Tasks from**: "On this PC" (the
notebook, as above, and the default) or a Microsoft account's To Do list, listed as "Groceries
(me@outlook.com)" from what the dock last synced (`sync-report.json`; an account not read yet offers its
default "Tasks"). Kept as `TodoOptions.Account` (the account's address, which signing in again keeps) and
`TodoOptions.TaskList` (Graph's id; empty or gone is the account's default list), both left out of the file
for a line on this PC, so every config of before reads and writes as it was.

Set to To Do, the line is drawn by the same `TodoTile` from `TaskStore` (docs\accounts.md, "To Do"): the open
tasks oldest first (To Do keeps no order Graph can set, so they are not dragged and Alt+Up/Down does
nothing), each with its due day and To Do's star at its end — Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow or the date, red
once passed — the day left out first, then the star, where the words would keep fewer than five letters;
"Completed" with its count; "Add a task" at the foot. A tick, an add, a rename (F2, double click) go to To Do
at once and are shown before the account answers; the trash and Delete ask first in Windows' task dialog
("Delete this task?", the task's words, *Delete task* / *Cancel*), since the task goes from every device.
"Clear completed" stays the notebook's. Not read yet, a row under the name says "Reading the tasks…" (or
why it could not be read); read before but not refreshed, the stale mark stands at the name's end with its
tooltip (StaleMark.cs). An account that never consented to To Do ("Reconnect to sync tasks"), one gone, or
a list turned off on the Accounts page is "Set up in Settings" (SetupPrompt.cs), which opens the Accounts
page.

Tests: `Folders\ToDoLinesTests` (tick, add, rename, delete asked and answered, Alt+Down moving nothing; the
three states that open the Accounts page; a line on this PC unchanged), `Core\TodoSourceTests` (a line of
before writes no account; a list only with its account). Pictures: `todo-microsoft-<dark|light>.png` (at
rest, completed open with a starred task lit, another list, at 100 and 225 % text; the stale mark; being
read). By hand: pick a To Do list on the widget's page; tick, add, rename and delete there and see it in To
Do on the phone; go offline, change something, come back.
## 88. The network and Bluetooth are presets (2026-10-10)

The person: *"port the wifi and bluetooth flyouts to the new system as well"*, as the clock (§73),
the weather and the calendar (§80) went. And first a bug: *"when i click add bluetooth device the
cast opens, but it should open the bluetooth setttings instead"*.

- **Add device, the bug.** The Bluetooth flyout's "Add device" opened
  `ms-settings-connectabledevices:devicediscovery`. On this Windows 11 build that protocol is the
  Devices Flow's ("Devices Flow Connectable Devices Protocol", HKCR), which answers with the Cast
  panel; the Add a device dialog it meant is Windows 10's. Windows 11's own quick-settings Bluetooth
  page has no add button: its way out is "More Bluetooth settings", `ms-settings:bluetooth`, whose
  "Add device" heads the page. So Add device opens that (`SettingsActions.AddDeviceId`, a curated
  action of its own with Settings' plus, the one action sharing another's page), and Cast's "Find
  other devices" opens `ms-settings:connecteddevices` rather than itself. `DevicePairingWizard.exe`
  (the old wizard) was not taken: it is not what Windows 11 shows. Test:
  `QuickSettingsTests.AddDeviceOpensBluetoothSettingsNotCast` (no action opens a connectabledevices
  address), `QuickPageLineTests.TheFootersAddDeviceOpensBluetoothSettings`.
- **The presets** (`Presets.WifiId` "Wi-Fi", `Presets.BluetoothId` "Bluetooth"): a list folder
  wearing the **Wi-Fi face** holding the network's page (`wifi`) and, after a divider, its footer;
  and one wearing the **Bluetooth face** holding Bluetooth's page (`bluetooth`) and its footer. The
  footers are the premade widgets (§85, `PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.WifiActions)` and
  `.BluetoothActions`), no copies of their own: "Wi-Fi" | "Network & internet", and "Bluetooth &
  devices" (for "More Bluetooth settings") | "Add device". The new bar has the
  Wi-Fi preset where the network icon stood, after the input indicator and before the sound; Bluetooth
  was never on a new bar and is in the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The pages are lines** (`ListKind.Wifi`, `ListKind.Bluetooth`, the ids the widgets always had:
  `WidgetSource.QuickPage`, `QuickPageTile`). `WifiPage` and `BluetoothPage` are kept whole — the
  title with the radio's switch (and Refresh), the cables over the networks, a network opened in place
  onto Connect, its key, the hidden network's name or an enterprise sign-in, "Connecting…" at once
  while `OffThreadWifi` joins off the dock's thread (§83), Disconnect and Properties; the paired
  devices with their batteries, an audio device's Connect/Disconnect, Remove device; the three empty
  states. `QuickPageTile` is an `IQuickHost` that is a card instead of `QuickFlyout`: it builds the page
  into `PageLayout.ForLine` (the list's width, rows, words and the title's switch on the list's gutter,
  no footer, no list held to a height) and paints the controls where the page put them. One decision
  over splitting the title into a widget of its own: the switch belongs to the list it switches, and
  two widgets would read the radio twice.
  - *As tall as it shows* (`IListContent`): a network or a device opened grows the line and the folder
    follows; nothing inside scrolls, the folder does past its most. Rows above an opened one never move.
  - *Open while the folder is*: the page is made and started on `Visible(true)` (the Wi-Fi waits at
    most 250 ms for its first read) and disposed on `Visible(false)` with its watchers, as the flyout's.
  - *The pointer*: a press on a control is the card's (`CardPress`/`CardDrag`/`CardRelease`), pressed,
    focused where it takes the keyboard, clicked when the button comes up on it — a key's field takes a
    drag to select and never turns into edit mode's drag. Beside the controls the press is the folder's
    and ends the editing. Only the row under the pointer lights. An icon-only button names itself
    (`CardTip`).
  - *The keys*: a press on a card makes it the folder's focused card (`FolderFlyout.TakePointer`). The
    folder's WM_CHAR goes to it (`CellIsland.CharOn`/`CardChar`, §87's). A field being typed in takes
    every key but Tab and Escape; otherwise Up and Down walk the controls, Enter and Space click the one
    ringed, and past the ends the keys are the folder's. Keys typed straight after Connect, before a
    paint, reach the field the page asked for (`Catch`; a regression test). `TextField` reads its scale
    from a card host (`ContextNow`) and opens the clipboard for the active window where it has no panel.
  - *Time*: the page's wake (a scan that never reports, the Bluetooth batteries every 30 s), the busy
    ring and the caret's blink share one timer of the card's, armed for the soonest; its posts reach the
    dock's thread as a source's do (`Wake`).
  - *Its right click* (§49's rows): the network line has the network icon's "Diagnose network problems"
    and "Network and Internet settings"; Bluetooth's its page in Windows.
- **The faces** (`FolderFaces.Wifi`, `FolderFaces.Bluetooth`, no options and not `Named` (§86): a
  glyph of the state, no name beside it, so their Face section says "This face has nothing to set";
  `StatusFaceDrawing`): the
  network icon's and Bluetooth icon's glyphs as the taskbar shows them, painted by the sound button's
  drawing (`SystemControlIsland.Paint`, shared): the Wi-Fi's bars with the unreached arcs faded, the
  cable or no connection, a VPN's shield in Windows' corner; Bluetooth's rune dimmed while off or
  where there is none. One glyph's square, as the buttons were. Their tooltip is the icon's (the
  network and its internet, the VPN), and Narrator names the VPN in the folder's name. The dock keeps
  `SystemStatus` running while a sound button or such a face is placed, hands its state to every
  folder that shows it (`Dock.GiveStatus`, `FolderIsland.SetStatus`), and the face paints itself again
  in place when its reading changes (`FaceTick`) — no rebuild.
- **What a click on the bar opens.** The status icons entry (`Indicators`) is unchanged: its icons
  still open Windows' pages. The sound and battery stay entries with their flyouts. Clicking the
  network's or Bluetooth's glyph now opens its folder — the page, as the flyout was — rather than
  Windows' Quick Settings, which Karpo never opened from these.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Wifi` and `BarKind.Bluetooth` and what was only theirs: their entries,
  their `QuickFlyout` arms and the flyout's `height` (`IslandView.Wifi`/`.Bluetooth`, `Dock.Widgets`'
  handlers), their `FlyoutHeights` (a line has no flyout height), the pages' footers and `kept` heights,
  `SystemControlIsland`'s Wi-Fi and Bluetooth branches (`Vpn`, `Spoken`). `QuickKind.Wifi`/`.Bluetooth`
  stay as the pages' own kinds; `QuickFlyout` refuses them. **Config shape 24**: a file of 23 or before
  is kept aside whole and the defaults take its place.

**Matched against the flyouts' own pictures** (rendered before they went: `quick-wifi-*.png`,
`quick-bluetooth-*.png`, `quick-network-*.png`). The same: the title row and its switch and Refresh,
every row, an opened network's card with its key field, the error and Next/Cancel, the cables, the
notices, the devices' batteries in one column. **Different, and why:** the list's gutter (12 px at
100 %) where the flyout kept 8 for rows and 20 for words, so the title starts on the gutter with the
rows' plates; the footer is the actions line, a link and a button, in a card of its own after a
divider (the actions widget's look: two text buttons, one row); no name band or title row (folders
have none since 8e455a6); the line grows with an opened card where the flyout kept a
height of its own (FlyoutHeight); and the face before `SystemStatus` has read shows full bars.

Tests: `QuickPageLineTests` (a network joined with a key, a wrong one said; the line grows by a card
and nothing above moves; a press beside the controls ends the editing; the hidden network; an
enterprise sign-in and a network's own Properties; Refresh's ring and the wake that ends a scan; the
keys walk the controls and leave; keys straight after Connect; the cables over the networks, opened,
pulled out; no Wi-Fi; a device's battery; an audio device connected and disconnected, the radio off;
the three empty states; the page lives while the folder is open; Add device; pictures),
`FolderFaceTests` (the two faces in every sheet and size check, in a made-up state with a VPN),
`NetworkIconVpnTests` (the shield on the Wi-Fi face only, its hover, the folder's VPN for Narrator, the
icon not moving), `GlyphCentreTests.TheWifiArcsStayInsideTheFaintFullSet` (on the face's drawing),
`SystemIconMenuTests.TheNetworkLineHasTheNetworkIconsRows`, `ResetTests` (a shape 23 file kept aside,
the Wi-Fi preset in the defaults), `DefaultBarTests`, `ListGutterTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`,
`TypedRegistryTests`. Pictures: `wifi-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `bluetooth-preset-<dark|light>.png`
(150 %, and 225 % text), `folder-faces-*.png`, `default-bar-*.png`. By hand: click the network glyph
on a new bar and connect to a network with a key (type it, Enter, a wrong one, the right one); open a
network's Properties; Refresh; switch Wi-Fi off and on; add the Bluetooth preset, connect and
disconnect a headset, Add device opens Bluetooth & devices (not Cast); Tab and the arrows through a
page; watch the face follow a network change and a VPN coming up.

## 89. The bar and Task view (2026-10-10)

The user: "the taskbar vanishes on the task view mode. is that normal windows behaviour? if not,
fix." Task view is Explorer's `XamlExplorerHostIslandWindow` (Windows 10: `MultitaskingViewFrame`)
over the whole display, and it comes to the front.

- **Not a full screen app.** The bar hides for `ABN_FULLSCREENAPP` when the front window is an app's
  and covers the display (`FullscreenApps.MakesWayFor`; since §272 Karpo's own look, `FullscreenApps.Fills`, on every change of the window in front); Task view covers it, so the bar hid. The
  shell's views are never an app to make way for (`FullscreenApps.Overlays`, `IsShellOverlay`, with
  Explorer's `ForegroundStaging`, its unshown stand-in for the front while a view opens), nor is a
  front window that is not shown or that is in a band over the apps' (`FullscreenApps.IsAppBand`,
  `WindowBand.Of`: user32's undocumented `GetWindowBand`, null where missing). Kept.
- **Under it all the same.** Task view is in z-band 5 (ZBID_IMMERSIVE_APPCHROME), Karpo's bars in
  band 1 like every app's window, and no z-order puts a band-1 window over a higher band: only a
  signed `uiAccess` app under Program Files makes windows there (`CreateWindowInBand`). Windows'
  own taskbar is lifted to band 6 by Explorer while Task view is up. Re-raising the bars (§89's
  first try), a log of what happens around Task view (§105) and showing Explorer's taskbar over
  Task view (§107) were tried and are gone.

The user chose (2026-10-11): "dont actually show the windows taskbar in taskview, hide it still,
this just throws off the application otherwise". Explorer's taskbar stays hidden at all times while
Karpo hides it, Task view included, and Task view shows no taskbar. `Taskbar.Bars` still lists the
taskbars with FindWindowEx (`Taskbar.TopLevel`), in any band: EnumWindows lists band-1 windows only,
so a taskbar lifted for Task view would be missed by `Cover` (a new Explorer) and `Restore` (Karpo
ending) there.

Tests: `FullscreenTests` (`TaskViewIsNeverAFullScreenApp`, `OnlyTheShellsViewsAreOverlays`,
`ExplorersForegroundStagingIsAnOverlay`, `OnlyAnAppsBandMakesWay`), `TaskbarBarsTests`. By hand:
Win+Tab: no taskbar over Task view, Explorer's taskbar never appears; Esc: Karpo's bars as before.

## 90. The sound is a preset (2026-10-10)

The first of the remaining flyout ports, done as the network's and Bluetooth's were (§88), the clock's
(§73) and the weather's and calendar's (§80): the sound button and its flyout went; what a click on it
gave is a ready-made folder under a face of the button's glyph.

- **The preset** (`Presets.SoundId` "Sound"): a list folder wearing the **sound face**, holding the
  sound panel's regions as lines in the flyout's order — the output devices (`soundOutput`), the
  microphones with their mute (`soundInput`), the volume row (`soundVolume`), the volume mixer
  (`soundMixer`) — on one card, as the flyout kept them on one page with the mixer under its heading;
  then a divider, as the flyout's footer band stood apart, and the premade sound actions (§85,
  `PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.SoundActions)`): "Sound" | "Volume mixer" for the flyout's "More
  volume settings". The lines were there already (§9, `SoundPartTile`, drawn by the flyout's own rows,
  `SoundRows`), so nothing new draws a region. A new bar has the preset where the sound button stood,
  after the network's (`Config.FirstLayout`).
  - **One column** (2026-10-11, "take the new layout of the volume ready made folder from my main
    taskbar, i made it a one column design"; it had been two lists side by side since the presets took over their layouts): one list,
    the output over the microphone (automatic up to 12 rows each), a divider, the mixer (up to 12),
    the volume (up to 6) and the footer "Sound" | "Volume mixer" — two cards. `PersonsLayouts.json`
    holds that design in both its layouts.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Sound`, no options, not `Named`: "This face has nothing to set";
  `StatusFaceDrawing`): the volume icon's glyph as the taskbar shows it — a wave for each third, none at
  nothing, crossed out while muted or where there is no output — painted by the drawing the Wi-Fi and
  Bluetooth faces share (`SystemGlyph.Paint`, what was left of `SystemControlIsland`), one glyph's
  square. Its tooltip is the icon's ("Speakers: 45%", "Speakers: Muted"). `SystemStatus` reads the
  volume for it; the dock hands the state to the folder (`Dock.GiveStatus`) and the face paints itself
  again in place when the level or the mute changes (`FaceTick`), never a rebuild.
- **The wheel and the middle click stay.** The button stepped the volume two a notch under the wheel
  and muted on a middle click, as Windows 11's icon does; the face does the same
  (`FolderIsland.Wheel`, `MiddleClick`, through `VolumeWatch`, made the first time either is asked
  for). The folder entry declares the wheel (`Interaction.Wheel` on `folderList`) and only the sound
  face takes it; every other folder leaves it to the bar, and a middle click there is a click.
- **Its right click** keeps the volume icon's rows — Open volume mixer, Sound settings, Troubleshoot
  sound problems (`Dock.ActsOnBar`): a folder wearing the sound face has them, any other folder none.
