- **What went.** `BarKind.Sound` (config shape **25**: a file of 24 or before is kept aside whole and
  the defaults take its place), its entry and `WidgetInfos.Sound` with its words, `IslandView.Sound`,
  `QuickKind.Sound`, `QuickSources.Sound`, `SoundPage` and its `QuickFlyout` arm, the dock's handler,
  `WidgetSource.SystemControl` and `SystemControlIsland` (its painting is `SystemGlyph`). Sound had no
  flyout height since f6a2d52, so none went. The sound lines link to Settings' Sound page through the
  volume slider's record (`Dock.WindowsLinkOf`). The volume slider on the bar (`BarClick.Nothing`) is
  unchanged.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `quick-sound-*.png`). The same:
the order — the output, the microphone with its mute at the heading's end, the volume with its mute
button and level, the volume mixer under its heading with each app's icon, slider and level — the
rows' geometry and glyphs (one `SoundRows`), the footer's two words. **Different, and why:** the
pickers are lists, every device a row and the one in use marked, as the lines always were (a card has
no panel to hang a dropdown over); no "Sound" title row (folders have none since 8e455a6); the
list's gutter instead of the flyout's insets; the mixer lists the person's apps first and Windows' own
sounds last (`SoundPartTile`'s order), and grows where the flyout scrolled; the footer is the actions
line in a card of its own after a divider.

Tests: `SoundPresetTests` (the preset's lines, order, divider and premade footer; the four regions in
the open folder; the face's glyph and tooltip at each level, muted and with no output; the face painted
again in place, no rebuild, the same size; pictures), `SoundIconTests` (the wheel and the middle click
now on the face, only on the sound face), `SystemIconMenuTests.OnlyTheSoundFaceHasTheVolumeIconsRows`,
`FolderFaceTests` (the sound face in the sheets), `GlyphCentreTests` (the speaker centred at every
level, on the face), `StateSizingTests`, `ResetTests.TheSoundEntryIsGoneAfterTheReset`,
`PresetsTests`, `DefaultBarTests`, `FolderRowsTests`. Pictures: `sound-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %,
and 225 % text), `folder-faces-*.png`, `sound-widget-levels-*.png`, `default-bar-*.png`. By hand: on a
new bar click the speaker and change the output, the microphone, the volume and an app's level; turn
the wheel over the speaker and middle-click it; watch the face follow a media key; right-click it.

## 91. The removable devices are a preset (2026-10-10)

The second of the remaining flyout ports, done as the sound's (§90): the removable-devices button and
its flyout went; what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder under a face of the button's stick.

- **The preset** (`Presets.RemovableId` "Removable devices"): a list folder wearing the **removable
  face**, holding the removable devices' line (`removableDevices`, `RemovableIsland.Cards.cs`, §9)
  alone: a row per device with its picture, its name, what it holds and its Eject, or "Nothing plugged
  in". The line was there already and already showed what the flyout showed, so nothing new draws a
  device. The flyout had no footer, so there is none, and no premade was made up for one. A new bar
  never had the button, so it has no preset either; it is in the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Removable`, no options, not `Named`: "This face has nothing to set";
  `RemovableFaceDrawing`): the button's drawing, moved — the USB stick (E88E) in one glyph's square,
  drawn quiet (the disabled ink) while nothing is plugged in and never taken away (the button's own
  reasoning: a zero is noise, dimming is Windows' sign for nothing to act on), and from two devices a
  count in an accent pill on its corner, "9+" past nine, held inside the cell. Its tooltip is the
  button's ("2 removable devices" and their names, five at most; "Removable devices / Nothing plugged
  in"). The folder reads the devices for it (`FolderIsland.Devices`, `RemovableIsland.Plugged`): again
  only when Windows said a device came or went (`DriveWatch.Changes`, after the dock's `RefreshIslands`)
  and on the face's own minute tick (`IntervalMs`), the safety net the button had for a card slipped
  into a reader. Either paints the face again in place (`FaceTick`, `Redraw`), never a rebuild.
- **Hiding.** The button never hid with nothing plugged in (it dimmed, see above), so the face does
  not either; a folder has no way to hide and needs none here.
- **Its right click** was the button's "Settings" alone (`ActsFor(BarKind)` had no rows for it), and so
  is the face's. Opening, ejecting and Properties of each device stay the line's rows in the folder.
- **What went.** `BarKind.RemovableDevices` (config shape **26**: a file of 25 or before is kept aside
  whole and the defaults take its place), its entry, `IslandView.RemovableDevices`, `RemovableFlyout`
  and the dock's part of it (`Dock.Drives.cs`), its shape (`WidgetShapes`), its flyout height
  (`WidgetInfos.RemovableDevices.FlyoutHeights`; a line has none), and the badge's setting
  (`RemovableOptions`, `WidgetOptionsKind.Removable`, the "Show how many" card): the line never read it
  and the face has nothing to set. `RemovableIsland` is the line's alone (its bar drawing throws, as
  `SoundPartTile`'s does). The line's "Eject" is Karpo's word now (`S.DockDrivesEject`), no longer an
  English constant.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `removable-two-*.png`,
`removable-none-*.png`, `removable-mixed-dark.png`) and the button's (`drive-bar-48-dark.png`). The
same: a row per device with its picture, name and letter, what it holds or why it has no figures ("No
disc in the drive"), Eject at the row's end; the empty state; the stick, its dim and its count.
**Different, and why:** no "Removable devices" title row (folders have none since 8e455a6); the
empty state is the line's "Nothing plugged in" beside a quiet stick, not the flyout's sentence; a row
is the list's row with what is free beside the name (under it, with a capacity bar, where the line is
set taller), where the flyout set it under the name in a 48 DIP row; the list's gutter instead of the
flyout's insets; and the line grows with the devices, the folder scrolling past its most, where the
flyout had a height of its own.

Tests: `RemovablePresetTests` (the preset's one line and its face; the button, its flyout height and
its options gone; the line of what is plugged in; the count from two and "9+"; the hover; the face
painted again in place as devices come and go, by a refresh and by the tick, dim with none, never
another size; one square at every bar; no rows of its own; pictures), `RemovableCardTests` (a press
beside the controls does nothing), `FolderFaceTests` (the removable face in every sheet and size
check), `SystemIconMenuTests.OnlyTheSoundFaceHasTheVolumeIconsRows`,
`ResetTests.TheRemovableDevicesEntryIsGoneAfterTheReset`, `PresetsTests`, `FolderRowsTests`,
`TypedRegistryTests`, `FlyoutHeightTests`, `WidgetItemTests`. Pictures: `removable-preset-<dark|light>.png`
(150 %, and 225 % text), `removable-face-<dark|light>.png`, `folder-faces-*.png`. By hand: add the
Removable devices preset from the add list; plug a stick in and out and watch the face dim and count;
open the folder, open a device and eject one; hover the face.

**Its height (2026-10-11, the person confirming it).** The line has the height every folder widget
has (§76), and Settings shows "Height in the folder" for it: it was never `FixedHeight` and its range
is one row to `FolderOptions.MostRows`, so the card and the plan already held; this pins it. Automatic
grows a row per device (the content, `ListHeight`) up to its most, then shows what fits and "N other
devices" in the last row; Fixed is that many rows whatever is plugged in, the devices sharing them (one
device in three rows takes two with its capacity bar) and "N other devices" past them. Nothing plugged
in is now said **centred** in the line, the quiet stick and its words as one group across it and down
it, at any height — it stood in the first row at the icon column, which left a tall fixed line empty
under it. Configs load unchanged: a height already in a file reads as it was (automatic, fixed, the old
least and most, none). The face keeps showing the count from two, with no setting (§91 above).
Tests: `RemovableHeightTests` (the card; Automatic and Fixed with 0, 1 and 5 devices; the centred empty
state at 100 % and 225 % text; a file's height read tolerantly with the rest of the folder intact).
Picture: `removable-heights-<dark|light>.png`.

## 92. The timer, the focus session and the stopwatch are presets (2026-10-10)

The third of the remaining flyout ports, done as the sound's and the removable devices' (§90, §91):
the timer, focus and stopwatch entries and their own panels went; what a click on each gave is a
ready-made folder holding its line at the height of its whole card, under a face of what the entry
said.

- **The presets** (`Presets.TimerId` "Timer", `FocusId` "Focus time" — `focusTimeGroup`, since
  `focusGroup` is Getting work done's, which takes the briefcase now so no two groups share a glyph —
  and `StopwatchId` "Stopwatch"): a list folder each, holding its line alone at a fixed height. A
  countdown's at **three rows**, its whole widget (§84's `CountdownCard` tiers): the glyph and the
  name, the time large, the steppers (or the clear button while it runs) and the start button with its
  word — what the panel was. The stopwatch's at **four rows**: its row of time, lap, reset and start,
  and four laps under it, as its panel kept four. Fixed rather than Automatic: a line's own height is
  its one row (`ListHeight`), so Automatic would show the one-liner, not the card. The panels had no
  footer, so there is none. A new bar never had the entries, so it has none of the three; they are in
  the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The faces** (`FolderFaces.Timer`, `Focus`, `Stopwatch`, no options, not `Named`;
  `CountdownFaceDrawing`): the entries' drawing, moved — the kind's glyph and what it says, side by
  side across a bar and the glyph over it down one. A countdown at rest says the length it is set to
  ("5m"), running what is left in five figures ("04:59", hours and minutes from an hour up), paused
  the same in the quieter ink, over "00:00" in the accent; a name given to the line stands between
  the glyph and the figures across a bar (a setting, so the face is that much wider for good), and
  down one takes the figures' place once over. A stopwatch says what it has counted in whole seconds,
  never its tenths (those are the open folder's quick tick, §84), quieter while paused. The room is
  the widest it can say, so the face is one size whatever it reads, and the glyph never moves. **Idle
  shows the length set, not the glyph alone**: the brief asked for the glyph when idle, but a face
  can't change size without a rebuild (§67: measured from settings), so a glyph alone would sit
  centred in the room kept for the figures and jump left on start; the entry's own "5m" keeps it
  still and says what a click will start. Its tooltip: the line's name or its kind's, and the length,
  what is left, "Paused: 4:12", or "The timer is over".
- **One timer.** The face reads the first line of its kind in its folder (`FolderIsland.FaceLine`)
  and that line's countdown or stopwatch in the dock's store (`Countdowns`, one per widget id) — the
  way a clock face reads the timers in its folder (§67, `CountdownLeft`, which is unchanged), so the
  face, the line and a clock face over the same folder show one countdown, and the face keeps none of
  its own. The dock's second tick (`SecondsTick`, armed while a countdown or a stopwatch runs) and
  every change of the store (`TimersChanged`, `CountdownStepped` → `FaceTicks`) paint it again in
  place (`FaceTick`), never a rebuild.
- **Its right click** is the line's rows (`Dock.ActsOnBar`): Start/Pause/Resume, Stop, A minute
  longer, A minute shorter for a countdown; Start/Pause, Lap, Reset for the stopwatch, greyed as the
  line's buttons are — worked on the line itself (`FolderIsland.FaceWidget`, handed to `ActRows` and
  `RunAct`), so a timer starts from the bar without opening the folder. The entries had no rows of
  their own (only "Settings"); these are the line's, which the face shows.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Timer`, `Focus`, `Stopwatch` (config shape **27**: a file of 26 or before is
  kept aside whole and the defaults take its place), their entries, `IslandView.Countdown` and
  `Stopwatch`, `CountdownFlyout` and `StopwatchFlyout` with the dock's part of them
  (`Dock.Countdowns.cs` keeps the store, the ring, do not disturb and the save), their shapes
  (`WidgetShapes.Countdown`, `Stopwatch`), the tiles' bar drawing (their `PaintCell` throws, as a
  line's does), and the panes' layouts (`CountdownPlace`, `CountdownCard.NaturalHeight`/`Pane`,
  `StopwatchCard.Pane`/`PaneHeight`/`StopwatchPanePlan`). `CountdownSource` is the length's two
  conversions; `FolderFlyout` takes a window class of a test's own.
- **Fixed on the way:** at a large text the stopwatch line drew a lap's length over its total, the
  time standing near the line's end; the length now moves left before the total, and where all three
  do not fit the total gives way (`StopwatchCard.LapColumns`).

**Matched against the panels' and entries' own pictures** (rendered before they went:
`countdown-panel-*.png`, `stopwatch-panel-*.png`, `countdown-bar-*.png`, `stopwatch-bar-*.png`). The
same: the card's pieces and order — glyph and name, time, steppers or clear, the worded start button
— and the stopwatch's time, lap, reset and start, its laps newest first with length and total; the
faces' glyph, figures, inks and room are the entries'. **Different, and why:** no title band (folders
have none since 8e455a6); the countdown's time is the line's whole-widget size, a little smaller
than the panel's 34 DIP, and the stopwatch's row is the line's one-liner (time at the list's text,
square buttons) rather than the panel's large time and worded start — the lines were there and are
the one drawing of each, so nothing new draws a card; "No laps yet" stands where laps will rather
than under a rule; rows do not grow with the text size, so at 225 % text three rows hold the
countdown's one-liner, not its whole card, and four the stopwatch's row and two laps.

Tests: `TimerPresetTests` (each preset's one line, height and face; the entries gone; the face reads
the first line of its kind; what a countdown and a stopwatch face say in every state; the face, its
line and a clock face as one timer, worked from the face's menu; the stopwatch face's rows; painted
again in place each second, never another size; one size whatever it says, at every bar, across and
down, named; the hover; laps never meeting; pictures), `ResetTests.TheTimerFocusAndStopwatchEntriesAreGoneAfterTheReset`,
`CountdownFormsTests`, `StopwatchFormsTests` (lines only now), `FolderFaceTests`, `FolderRowsTests`,
`PresetsTests`, `ShellTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`, `SectionsTests`, `CountdownsTests`, `FocusQuietTests`
(countdowns in folders now). Pictures: `timer-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `stopwatch-preset-<dark|light>.png`
(150 %, and 225 % text), `time-faces-<dark|light>.png`, `folder-faces-*.png`. By hand: add the Timer
preset, right-click its face and start it; watch the face count, pause it from the line, let it ring;
add a Stopwatch, start it from the face, open the folder and take laps; hover a face.

## 93. The mobile hotspot is a preset (2026-10-10)

The fourth of the remaining flyout ports, done as the network's and Bluetooth's (§88, a page as a
line) and the sound's, the removable devices' and the timers' (§90–§92): the mobile hotspot button and
its flyout went; what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder under a face of the hotspot's state.

- **The preset** (`Presets.HotspotId` "Mobile hotspot", `hotspotGroup`): a list folder wearing the
  **hotspot face**, holding the hotspot's page as a line (`hotspot`, `ListKind.Hotspot`,
  `WidgetInfos.Hotspot` "Mobile hotspot details") and, after a divider as the flyout's band stood
  apart, its footer as a premade widget (§85, `PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.HotspotActions)`, new):
  "Mobile hotspot" (`mobileHotspot`, for the flyout's "Mobile hotspot settings") | "Network & internet"
  (`network`), where Windows keeps the hotspot. A new bar never had the button, so it has no preset
  either; it is in the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The page is a line** (`QuickPageTile`, which knew the network's and Bluetooth's pages, now knows
  `QuickKind.Hotspot` too): `HotspotPage` kept whole — the title with the switch, "Properties" with the
  network's name, its password behind the eye and Copy, its band and "2 of 8" devices, the devices on
  it while it is on, its five reasons it cannot be (no switch then), the devices asked again every 5 s
  while the folder is open. Without a footer (the actions line is it). Copy takes the active window,
  the folder's, as the clipboard's owner where there is no panel, as a field's Copy in a card does.
  Its right click is its page in Windows (`WidgetAct.WindowsSettings`), as Bluetooth's line's.
- **The switch stays a line.** `ListKind.MobileHotspot` (`mobileHotspot`, `SwitchIsland`) is unchanged:
  Connectivity and the toggles row hold it, and a click on it switches the hotspot. Only its taskbar
  form went, whose click opened the page (`SwitchIsland.Page` names Project and Cast alone now).
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Hotspot`, no options, not `Named`: "This face has nothing to set";
  `HotspotFaceDrawing`): the antenna Windows' own hotspot icon on the taskbar shows (E704, the page's
  and the status icons' glyph), drawn as the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth faces beside it are
  (`SystemGlyph.Paint`), dimmed while the hotspot is off, before Windows has answered and where this PC
  cannot host one, as the Bluetooth face is with its radio off; while it is on, how many devices are on
  it in the removable face's accent pill (`RemovableFaceDrawing.PaintCount`, shared), from one, "9+"
  past nine — on the antenna's bottom corner beside its mast, which its ink leaves empty, rather than
  over its arcs as a top corner put it, and by the antenna's own size so the ink stays centred. One glyph's square whatever it says. Its tooltip: "Mobile hotspot: on" and
  "2 of 8 devices connected", "Mobile hotspot: off", or why it cannot be.
  - *Not the button's glyph.* The button wore `WidgetInfos.MobileHotspot.Glyph` (EBC4), a tray with an
    arrow; on the face, beside the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth glyphs, it did not read as a hotspot (rendered
    side by side), so the face takes Windows' taskbar antenna. The switch line keeps EBC4.
  - *Not the button's accent tile.* The button drew Windows' quick-settings tile: the accent behind the
    glyph while on. The face is a status glyph like its neighbours, and the count's accent pill would
    vanish on an accent tile; on and off are full and dimmed ink instead.
  - *The count is new.* The button showed none. Who is on a hotspot is what a hotspot that is on is
    for, and the source reads it anyway.
- **Where the face reads it.** A source of the face's own (`FolderIsland.Hotspot`, an `IHotspotSource`
  from `QuickPageTile.SourcesNow`: a test's, the samples on an isolated run, or `WindowsHotspot`),
  made when the face is put on and let go when it is taken off. It asks off the dock's thread on every
  network change, on its own 30 s tick (`IntervalMs`: the tethering manager tells nobody when a device
  joins, nor always when the hotspot is switched in Settings), and whenever a line in the open folder
  had news (the page switching it or asking who is on it), so the face follows the line at once; its
  own news never makes it ask again. What it hears paints the face again in place (`Post` → refresh →
  `Redraw`), never a rebuild.
- **Its right click** (`Dock.ActsOnBar`): the button had no rows of its own (its "Settings" alone). The
  face has Windows' hotspot icon's "Mobile hotspot settings" (`WidgetAct.HotspotSettings`), not its
  "Turn off": a switch a slip away on the bar is the line's job, inside the folder.
- **What went.** `BarKind.MobileHotspot` (config shape **28**: a file of 27 or before is kept aside
  whole and the defaults take its place), its entry, `IslandView.Hotspot` and its `QuickKinds` arm, the
  `QuickFlyout` arm (`QuickKind.Hotspot` stays as the page's own kind; `QuickFlyout` refuses it), the
  dock's handler, the page's footer and `HotspotPage.Settings`, the smoke run's hotspot flyout.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `quick-hotspot-*.png`). The
same: the title and its switch, "Properties" and its four pairs, the eye and Copy beside the password,
the devices' rows with their addresses, the can't-notice. **Different, and why:** the footer is the
actions line in a card of its own after a divider, with Network & internet beside the hotspot's page;
no name band (folders have none since 8e455a6); the list's gutter instead of the flyout's insets; at
225 % text the line runs past the folder's most and the folder scrolls, as the Wi-Fi's does.

Tests: `HotspotPresetTests` (the preset's line, divider and premade footer, the face; the button gone
and the switch still a line; the line shows, copies to the sample, switches, hides the password again;
where it cannot be; the footer's two pages; the face's dim and count; its hover; painted again in place

(the switch line acts once), `DisplayFlyoutsTests`, `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests` (two pages now),

  (`battery`, `BatteryIsland`, §9: the level's glyph, the percentage and what it is doing, the charge

- **The power mode is a line** (`ListKind.PowerMode`, `WidgetInfos.PowerMode`, `PowerModePage` in
