  device is switched since ded0255): the row is marked at once, and the mark follows what Windows
  says — back where it was, with "Windows didn't change the power mode.", where it refused
  (`BatteryNews.Refused`). A plan that takes no overlay offers no modes, and the line says so
  ("This PC's power plan has no power modes.") rather than showing rows that do nothing. Energy
  saver, the section's other row, is the energySaver switch beside it, which switches it rather than
  linking to its page.
- **The power commands are a line** (`ListKind.PowerCommands`, `WidgetInfos.PowerCommands` "Power
  menu", `PowerCommandsPage`, what was `PowerPage`): sleep and hibernate where Windows' power menu
  shows them, shut down, restart, sign out and lock, each a row with the quick links' glyph
  (`QuickLinks.PowerLines`). A row does its command at once, as Windows' power menu does: the
  folder closes first (`WM_CANCELMODE` posted to it, so it is not taken apart under the click), and
  the command runs on the pool a moment after (`QuickPageTile.Runner`, the very `QuickLinks.Power`
  the quick links run), so a sleep that holds its caller never holds the dock's thread.
- **The battery face** (`FolderFaces.Battery`, `BatteryFaceDrawing`, not `Named`): the battery's own
  drawing, moved — the level's glyph Windows' battery icon shows (tenths, charging, energy saver) and
  the percentage, a row across a bar, the glyph over the figure down one, in the taskbar's icon ink;
  its room a full charge's "100%", so it is one size whatever the charge; on a PC without a battery
  the power bolt alone in a glyph's square (`WidgetMachine.HasBattery`, now handed to the face as
  `FaceContext.Machine`). The battery had no setting for the percentage, so the face has none:
  "This face has nothing to set". The folder reads the charge (`FolderIsland.Battery`, through
  `BatteryIsland.Probe`) on a power broadcast (the charger, the charge, energy saver, as the battery
  did) and on its minute tick, and paints the face again in place, never a rebuild. Its tooltip is
  the battery's ("76% remaining", or "Power / Energy saver and the power mode").
- **The power face** (`FolderFaces.Power`, `PowerFaceDrawing`): the button's glyph (E7E8) at its size,
  full strength; never painted again. Its tooltip names it.
- **Their right click.** The battery face keeps the battery's "Power & battery settings"
  (`Dock.ActsOnBar`); the power button had only its "Settings", and so does the face. The two new
  lines' rows are their page in Windows.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Battery` and `BarKind.Power` (config shape **29**: a file of 28 or before is
  kept aside whole and the defaults take its place), their entries, `IslandView.Battery`/`.Power`,
  `QuickKind.Battery`, `BatteryPage`, `PowerPage`, `PowerSection`, `PowerIsland`,
  `WidgetSource.Power`, `WidgetInfos.Power`, the flyouts' `QuickFlyout` arms and the dock's handlers,
  the battery's shape (`WidgetShapes.Battery`) and its bar drawing (its `PaintCell` throws, as a
  line's does). `QuickKind.Power` is the power commands' page now, and `PowerMode` new; `QuickFlyout`
  refuses both. The battery flyout's words are `BatteryText`.

**Matched against the flyouts' own pictures** (rendered before they went: `quick-battery-*.png`,
`quick-power-*.png`, `battery-battery-48-*.png`). The same: the order — charge, energy saver, the
power mode under its heading and caption, the three modes with their gauges and the marked one's
plate; the commands in Windows' order with their glyphs; the face's glyph, figure and room.
**Different, and why:** the charge is the battery's line (the percentage at the list's size, a bar,
the time left under it) rather than the flyout's display figure; energy saver is its switch, with no
"Off" under its name; no "Battery"/"Power" title row (folders have none since 8e455a6); the footer is
the actions line in a card of its own, with Energy saver beside Power & battery; the list's gutter
instead of the flyout's insets (the rows' glyphs stand inside their plates, a little in from the
lines' icon column, as the network's rows do); and the commands close the folder before they run.

Tests: `BatteryPowerPresetTests` (both presets' lines, order, divider and premade footer; the battery
line left out on the wall; the entries gone; the power mode marked, asked, asked once, refused, a plan
with none; the mode asked off the caller's thread, with a stand-in for Windows; the commands as this
PC offers them, run through a stand-in; the footer's two pages; the face's figure and hover, painted
again in place on a tick and a power broadcast, one size whatever the charge at every bar, the
square without a battery; the power face; the faces' rows; pictures),
`ResetTests.TheBatteryAndPowerEntriesAreGoneAfterTheReset`, `DefaultBarTests`, `DefaultsTests`,
`SystemIconMenuTests` (the battery face's row), `FolderFaceTests`, `FolderRowsTests`, `ListGutterTests`,
`WidgetMenuTests`, `InteractionTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`, `PremadeWidgetsTests`, `StatusIconColourTests`,
`StateSizingTests`, `CellOffscreenTests`. Pictures: `battery-preset-<dark|light>.png`,
`power-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 % text), `battery-face-<dark|light>.png`,
`folder-faces-*.png`, `islands-*.png`, `default-bar-*.png`. By hand (never from a test): on a laptop's
new bar, hover the battery face, plug the charger in and out and watch it follow; open it, change the
power mode and check Settings agrees; add the Power preset and lock from it (the folder closes first);
right-click the battery face.

## 95. The mail is a preset (2026-10-10)

The sixth of the remaining flyout ports, done as the removable devices' (§91, a line that was there
already): the mail entry and its panel went; what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder under a
face of the envelope the entry was.

- **The preset** (`Presets.MailId` "Mail", `mailGroup`): a list folder wearing the **mail face**,
  holding the inbox's line (`mail`, `MailIsland`, §16) alone at its own height (Automatic): the
  count over the newest messages, each its sender (semibold while unread) over its subject and when
  it came, up to eight and how many more; "Set up in Settings" centred with no account (SetupFace,
  the line's own since 2026-10-08); the stale mark at its trailing gutter with "Last updated 14:05 —
  couldn't refresh" over it (§77). The panel had no footer but that note, which the line's mark
  says, and no button that opened a mail app (a row opened nothing: no program can be asked to show
  one message of one account), so there is no premade footer and no mail-app action. A new bar
  never had the entry, so it has no preset either; it is in the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Mail`, no options, not `Named`: "This face has nothing to set";
  `MailFaceDrawing`): the entry's drawing, moved (`GlyphBadge`, now drawn into the face's square
  and held inside the bar's cell about it) — the envelope (E715), how many are unread in an accent
  pill on its corner ("99+" past 99), dimmed with no count while an inbox cannot be read, the stale
  mark small on its lower corner while what it shows could not be refreshed, the envelope alone with
  no account (the entry's "Set up" on a one-cell button was its glyph alone). One glyph's square
  whatever it shows. The pill stands a fifth of its height above the glyph's square, not the bell's
  third: the envelope's ink is short in its square, and the higher pill drew the face's ink off the
  cell's middle on a 40 DIP bar (`FolderFaceTests`).
- **Where the face reads it.** `MailStore.Shared`, the one store (docs\accounts.md, "Offline"): the
  folder attaches to it while it wears the face (`FolderIsland.Mail`, `FollowMail`) and lets go when
  the face is taken off or the folder goes. The store's news wakes the folder as it woke the entry;
  the refresh raises it (`Deliver`) and the face is painted again in place (`Redraw`), never a
  rebuild. Its first paint is the look that starts the first read (§11). No tick of its own: the
  store reads on its own clock (`PimSync`). Tests hand a stand-in store to the line and the face
  alike (`MailIsland.Stand`), so no account is ever reached.
- **Its tooltip** is the entry's: none over the bar (§367); to a screen reader the
  count or why an inbox cannot be read, and from when (`MailIsland.Tip`).
- **Its right click** has the line's Refresh (`Dock.ActsOnBar`, `MailFaceActs`), worked on the face's
  own store (`FolderIsland.RefreshMail`, through `FaceWidget`, which is the folder for this face): the
  entry had no rows of its own, but its panel read the inboxes again as it opened, and the line is
  not always in the folder.
- **The line says an empty inbox.** It said "All read" over nothing; it says "Your inbox is empty"
  now, as the panel did (the string kept, its full stop dropped as a head has none).
- **What went.** `BarKind.Mail` (config shape **30**: a file of 29 or before is kept aside whole and
  the defaults take its place), its entry, `IslandView.Mail`, `MailFlyout` and the dock's part of it
  (`Dock.Mail.cs`), its shape (`WidgetShapes`), its flyout height (`WidgetInfos.Mail.FlyoutHeights`; a
  line has none), the panel's words ("Inbox", "Inbox · 3 unread") and `MailFlyoutOffscreenTests`.
  `MailIsland` is the line's alone (its bar drawing throws, as `RemovableIsland`'s does); `When` moved
  to it from the panel.

**Matched against the panel's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `mailref-<inbox|stale|empty|setup>-<dark|light>.png`)
and the entry's (`stale-envelope-*.png`). The same: the messages newest first, sender over subject,
when at the end, the unread in the heavier weight; the empty state; the setup prompt's words and
button; the stale words; the envelope, its count, its dim and its mark. **Different, and why:** no
"Inbox · 3 unread" title row (folders have none since 8e455a6) — the line's own head says "3 unread"
by the envelope; no per-row open/closed envelope glyph (the weight says unread, as in the line); the
stale note is the line's mark with its tooltip rather than a footer band; the setup prompt is the
line's, its words and button side by side in one row; the line shows eight messages and says how
many more, where the panel scrolled thirty; at 225 % text the senders are cut shorter.

Tests: `MailPresetTests` (the preset's one line and face; the entry and its flyout height gone; the
line in the opened folder over the face's store; the face's count, dim, mark and no-account look; an
account that fails dims it; the hover over the bar and to a screen reader; painted again in place as
mail arrives and as a refresh fails, never another size; one square at every bar; the face's Refresh
reaches the store with and without the line; another face lets go of the store; an empty inbox says
so; pictures), `ResetTests.TheMailEntryIsGoneAfterTheReset`, `FolderFaceTests` (the mail face in
every sheet and size check), `StaleMarkPictures` (the envelope is the face now), `FolderRowsTests`,
`TypedRegistryTests`, `FlyoutHeightTests`, `FlyoutHeightRowTests`, `SectionsTests`,
`IslandTooltipsTests`, `WidgetItemTests`. Pictures: `mail-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 %
text), `mail-face-<dark|light>.png`, `stale-envelope-*.png`, `folder-faces-*.png`. By hand: add the
Mail preset from the add list with a mail account set up; watch the count follow new and read mail;
go offline and Refresh from the face's right click — the mark and its hover; remove the account —
the envelope alone, and the folder's "Set up in Settings".

## 96. Now playing is a preset (2026-10-10)

The seventh of the remaining flyout ports: the now-playing entry and its flyout (`MediaPage`) went;
what a click on it gave is the media preset, the quick settings' media group (§86's recipes) under a
face of what the entry was. Unlike the mail (§95) the line was missing parts of the flyout, so the
line gained them.

- **The preset** (`Presets.MediaId` "Media", `mediaGroup`, the id the group already had): a list
  folder wearing the **now-playing face**, holding the now-playing line (`media`, `MediaIsland`) at
  **four rows** — the whole widget: where it plays, the art, the track and the artist, the timeline,
  the transport with shuffle and repeat — then a divider and the volume and the output, which the
  flyout's "Sound settings" footer led to. At its own height (Automatic) the line was the compact
  line, the transport alone, which left out half the flyout. At 225 % text four rows hold only the
  compact line; its menu has the rest (§9, "A line keeps what it does at every height"). A new bar
  never had the entry, so it has no preset either.
- **What the line gained** (MediaLine.cs, `MediaIsland`):
  - *Shuffle and repeat*, at the two ends of the whole widget's transport, where the flyout had
    them: drawn only where the session says it lets them be set (GSMTC's `IsShuffleEnabled`,
    `IsRepeatEnabled`), in the accent while on, repeat's glyph "repeat one" for this track; a click
    sets shuffle, and steps repeat off → this track → all. Asked of the app off the dock's thread
    (`TryChangeShuffleActiveAsync`, `TryChangeAutoRepeatModeAsync` in `Task.Run`) and shown at once,
    until the app's own event says what it did. Their places are the row's (five buttons and two
    gaps, `Ends`), never the app's, so nothing moves when an app with them follows one without. To
    make the room the whole widget keeps five buttons' width beside the art, so the art is the
    flyout's size beside its words rather than the line's whole height. A shorter line's menu has
    "Shuffle" (ticked while on) and the repeat mode set ("Repeat all", ticked while on), and neither
    where the app has neither.
  - *The source app's name*, under the artist, now on the whole widget without a timeline too
    where it fits (it was only the timeline's line before); its icon is the art's corner badge, as
    before.
  - *The picker*: where two apps or more have a session, the app's name carries a chevron and is
    the picker; its click opens the line's own menu over the folder (`IslandView.Menu`, which only
    the folder answers: `FolderFlyout.Activate` makes it the right click's `Context` event), whose
    first rows are "Playing in" and each app by its icon and name, the one followed ticked
    (`WidgetAct.FollowSession`). A pick follows that app's session; the picked app picked again goes
    back to the session Windows leads with, as the flyout's list did, and so does an app that goes.
    The choice is the line's own and is never written down: a restart follows Windows. The chevron's
    room is kept whether or not two apps play, so the name does not move.
  - *The second tick only while playing*: the open line asks for a draw a second while it shows a
    timeline and the track plays; paused, it stands still.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.NowPlaying`, `nowPlaying`, not `Named`; `NowPlayingFaceDrawing`): the
  entry's drawing, moved (`MediaIsland.PaintFace`) — the art (the note where there is none) and the
  title with the artist, over each other where the bar has room for two lines at its own text size
  and on one line ("title · artist") where it has not (`TwoLines`, §12.5), turned under the art down
  a bar on its side; "Nothing playing" quietly. New: a **pause mark** on the art while the track is
  paused (the pause glyph on a dark plate in its corner); without the art the title goes quiet
  instead. Its options are the entry's, which went with it from `WidgetItem` (`MediaOptions`,
  `WidgetOptionsKind.Media`, the Settings page's two switches): **the art** (on), and **hiding while
  nothing plays** (off) — on, the folder takes no cell while nothing plays (`FolderIsland.Count`) and
  the bar is laid out again when a track starts, as the entry went. Its length is the entry's,
  without the ends the folder keeps: the art and its gap and three cells' words (`FaceLength`, from
  the settings and the bar alone, never the track).
- **Where the face reads it.** The folder's first now-playing line (`FolderIsland.NowPlaying`), so
  the face and the line follow one session — a pick on the line is the face's too — else a widget of
  the face's own, made and attached as a line is (`FollowNowPlaying`) where the folder holds no line.
  Their news posts with the folder's token; the refresh takes it and the face is painted again in
  place, never a rebuild (its `Reading`: the track, the art, playing or paused, the app). No tick: it
  shows no time.
- **Its tooltip** is the entry's: none over the bar; to a screen reader the track and where it
  plays ("Air on the G String — Johann Sebastian Bach · Spotify"), or "Nothing playing".
- **Its right click** has play or pause, previous and next (`NowPlayingFaceActs`), worked on what the
  face shows (`FaceWidget` is the now-playing widget), greyed as its buttons would be. The entry had
  no wheel or middle click to keep.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Media` (config shape **31**: a file of 30 or before is kept aside whole and
  the defaults take its place), its entry and shape (`WidgetShapes.Media`), its flyout
  (`QuickKind.Media`, `MediaPage`, `IslandView.Media` → `IslandView.Menu`), the flyout's own reading
  of the sessions (`IMediaSource`, `WindowsMedia`, `SampleMedia`, `MediaTrack`, `MediaView`; the
  line reads the sessions itself through `MediaSessions.Shared`), `MediaOptions` and its Settings
  switches, and the flyout's words (`dock.quick.media.*`; shuffle, the repeat modes and "Playing in"
  moved to `widget.media.*`). `MediaIsland` is the line's alone (its bar drawing throws).

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `quick-media-*.png`) and the
entry's (`media-bars-*.png`, `media-row-*.png`). The same: the art, the track over the artist, where
it plays, the timeline and its times, previous/play-pause/next, shuffle and repeat at the transport's
ends, the apps to pick from; the face's art and words at every bar. **Different, and why:** the art
stands left of the words, as every line's leading part does, where the flyout put it right; the
source name is under the artist, not over the title; play or pause is a glyph, not the flyout's
accent square (the line's transport is glyphs at every height); the apps to pick from are a menu off
the name rather than rows under the transport, since a line has no room for a list that comes and
goes; "This app doesn't let Karpo move the track" is gone — the timeline simply has no thumb; the
footer is the volume and output lines themselves rather than a link to Sound settings.

Tests: `MediaPresetTests` (the preset's line, its height and face; the entry, its flyout and options
gone; the face reads the folder's line, or its own, or nothing for another face; its length the
settings' alone, shorter without the art; the pause mark; painted again in place; hiding while
nothing plays; the hover; the face's play, previous and next; shuffle and repeat on the whole line
and only where the app has them; a short line's menu; the picker and following another app and back;
the second tick only while playing; pictures), `MediaSizeTests` and `MediaRowTests` (the entry's
size and row rules, held on the face now), `ResetTests.TheNowPlayingEntryIsGoneAfterTheReset`,
`FolderFaceTests` (the face in every sheet), `ListLinesControlsTests` (the line with the modes and
two apps at every height), `MediaTrackTests`, `MediaControlsRetiredTests`. Pictures:
`media-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `media-face-<dark|light>.png`, `list-media-source-modes-*.png`,
`media-row-*.png`, `media-bars-*.png`. By hand: add the Media preset; play in Spotify and a browser
at once — the chevron on the app's name, pick the browser and back, the face following; shuffle and
repeat from the line and see the app follow; pause — the face's mark; set the face's "Hide it while
nothing plays" and close the player.

## 97. The performance readings are presets (2026-10-10)

The eighth of the remaining flyout ports, the five in one step: the processor, graphics, memory,
disk and network activity entries and their flyout (`PerformanceFlyout`, Task Manager's page for the
reading in a panel) went; what a click on each gave is a ready-made folder under a face of what the
entry was. As with now playing (§96) the line was missing part of the flyout — its minute and its
facts — so the line gained them, as its tallest form.

- **The presets** (`Presets.CpuId` "Processor", `GpuId` "Graphics", `MemoryId` "Memory", `DiskId`
  "Disk", `NetworkActivityId` "Network activity" — not "networkGroup", which reads as the Wi-Fi's):
  a list folder each, wearing its reading's face, holding the reading's line at a fixed height — the
  processor's at **nine rows** for its seven facts, the other four at **seven** — then a divider, as
  the flyout's band stood apart, and the premade Task Manager footer (§85,
  `PresetItem.Of(PremadeWidgets.TaskManagerActions)`, new). **System** (`systemGroup`), the five as
  compact lines with the battery, is kept as it was: it is the overview, these are the flyouts. A
  new bar never had the entries, so it has none of the five either; they are in the add list's
  ready-made groups. The disk's group icon is a gauge (EC4A): its drive glyph is Storage's, and no
  two groups share one (`PresetsTests`); its face keeps the drive.
- **Task Manager is an action** (`SettingsActions.TaskManagerId` "taskManager", `taskmgr.exe`,
  Task Manager's glyph E9D9): an app, as the calendar app is (§80), not a page of Settings, which
  every Windows has, so its slot never stands empty. The premade footer is it alone on the left,
  nothing on the right — the flyout's one link, "Open Task Manager", in the actions line's words
  ("Task Manager"). Any actions line can take it.
- **The line at its tallest is the flyout** (`PerformanceIsland.LineFacts`, a fourth height above
  the whole widget, §9 "A line at every height"): the reading's name as the flyout titled it (the
  disk's with its letters, "Disk 1 (C:)"), the figure large (28 DIP, the flyout's own: the network's
  down and up together written out, "5.6 MB/s", where the shorter lines say "6M"), what the graph's
  top stands for at the other end of the figure's row ("100%", or the minute's busiest rate rounded
  up), the last minute edge to edge on its quarters' hairlines, "60 seconds" and "0" under it, and
  the facts in two columns, a name over its figure, one too long for its column across both
  (`PerformanceModel.For`, unchanged). The graph takes what the facts leave, at least 64 DIP; under
  that the line is the whole widget, as before. One choice over a details line of its own: the
  facts are the reading's, of the same source and device, and a second widget would be a second
  thing to set to the same disk.
  - *The minute at the line's pace*: the flyout's minute was sixty one-second steps whatever the
    entry was set to; the line draws sixty of its own steps, so at five seconds it is five minutes,
    and it says so ("300 seconds").
  - *The figures*: what the system holds, its clock and up time, the adapters' and the disk's names
    (`PerformanceFigures.Read`) are read only for a line drawn that tall, once a gather of its
    source at most (`FiguresNow`), as the flyout read them only while open.
- **The faces** (`FolderFaces.Cpu`, `Gpu`, `Memory`, `Disk`, `NetworkActivity`; `PerformanceFace`;
  `PerformanceFaceDrawing`, not `Named`): the entry's drawing, moved (`PerformanceIsland.PaintFace`)
  — the reading's glyph in the quieter ink and the figure right-aligned in the room its worst case
  keeps ("100%", "8.8M"), a row across a bar, the glyph over the figure down one, no graph (§55); a
  dash, quietly, before any reading. One size whatever it reads (`FaceLength`, from the bar alone).
  Its options are the entry's: **how often it updates** (`FaceOptionKind.Pace`, 1 to 10 seconds, the
  line's list) and, for the graphics and the disk, **which adapter** (`FaceOptionKind.Adapter`, the
  main card unless named) and **which disk** (`FaceOptionKind.Disk`, every disk unless named) — two new
  option kinds whose lists are what this PC has, listed by the settings app off its UI thread as the
  line's card lists them (`PerformanceCard.FaceDevices`). The network had no device to choose, so its
  face has the pace alone.
- **Where the face reads it.** One source per reading and device (§55, 0ddaee3, `DataSources`): the
  folder holds the source of its face's reading and device while it wears the face
  (`FolderIsland.Performance`, `FollowPerformance`, made as the line set as the face is,
  `SourceKinds.FaceLine`), and reads the folder's line of that device where there is one — the very
  same source, or a line a test fed. A face set to a disk of its own is wanted by the config from the
  dock's start (`SourceKinds.Wanted`), so its history is there before anything draws it; its pace
  adds no source. It is painted again in place on its own tick at its pace (`IntervalMs`), after the
  dock's timer has gathered the sources, never a rebuild.
- **Its tooltip** is the entry's: none over the bar (the folder takes no hover); to a screen reader
  the line's words ("Processor 42%", the adapter, the disk's volumes) — `PerformanceIsland.Tip`,
  shared with the line.
- **Its right click** has the line's Resource Monitor (`Dock.ActsOnBar`): the entries had none of
  their own (only "Settings"), and the face's click opens the folder, whose footer is Task Manager.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Cpu`, `Gpu`, `Memory`, `Disk`, `Network` (config shape **32**: a file of 31
  or before is kept aside whole and the defaults take its place), their entries and their shape
  (`WidgetShapes.Performance`), the bar drawing (`PerformanceIsland.PaintCell` throws, as a line's
  does; `Plan`, `GraphPlan`), the flyout (`PerformanceFlyout`, `HistoryGraph`, `Dock.Performance.cs`,
  `IslandView.Performance`), its "Open Task Manager" words, and the settings page's pace card for an
  entry (`PerformanceOnBar`, `ShowsGraphSwitch`): every reading on a page is a line now, which has
  the graph switch and its pace. The lines and their settings are unchanged.

**Matched against the flyouts' own pictures** (rendered before they went: `performance-<cpu|gpu|memory|disk|network>-<dark|light>.png`)
and the entries' (`perf-bar-*.png`). The same: the name, the large figure, the scale over the
graph's right end, the minute edge to edge on its hairlines, "60 seconds" and "0", the facts in two
columns with a long one across both, Task Manager at the foot; the faces' glyph, figure and room.
**Different, and why:** the glyph stands in the list's leading column beside the name, as every
line's does, where the flyout had none; no title band (folders have none since 8e455a6); the
figure is the list's semibold rather than the flyout's display weight; the footer is the actions
line in a card of its own after a divider, "Task Manager" rather than "Open Task Manager"; the
list's gutter instead of the flyout's insets; the facts' columns start at the name's edge; rows do
not grow with the text size, so at 225 % text the line is the whole widget without the facts.

Tests: `PerformancePresetTests` (each preset's line, height, divider, premade footer and face with
its options; Task Manager the action and the footer; the entries and the flyout gone; the face reads
the folder's line or its own source, lets it go for another face; its figure, a dash before any
reading, painted again in place at its pace, never another size; one size whatever it reads at every
bar, across and down, at 225 % text; its row; the line at the preset's height says every fact and
the minute, at four rows none; the figures read once a gather and only where shown; pictures),
`PerformanceReadingTests` (was `PerformanceFlyoutTests`: a face's device wanted from the start, its
pace adds nothing, no entry is a reading), `GraphShapeTests` (the faces one width whatever they
read, their options never moving the bar), `GraphOffscreenTests` and `DiskActivityTests` (the faces
on the bar), `PerformanceCardTests` (the faces' pace and device lists), `ResetTests.ThePerformanceEntriesAreGoneAfterTheReset`,
`RemovedKindsTests`, `DataSourcesTests`, `FolderRowsTests`, `PremadeWidgetsTests`,
`TogglesAndActionsTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`, `SectionsTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`. Pictures:
`performance-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, a reading not taken yet, and 225 % text),
`performance-face-<dark|light>.png`, `perf-bar-*.png`, `perf-vertical-*.png`, `disk-activity-*.png`.
By hand: add the Processor preset, watch the face follow a load, open it and read the facts against
Task Manager; set the face to five seconds; add the Disk preset and set its face and its line to a
second disk; click Task Manager in the footer; right-click a face for Resource Monitor.

## 98. The stock and the news feed are presets (2026-10-10)

The ninth of the remaining flyout ports, both in one step: the stock and RSS entries and their panels
(`StockFlyout`, `RssFlyout`) went; what a click on each gave is a ready-made folder under a face of
what the entry was. As with now playing (§96) and the readings (§97) the lines were missing parts of
the panels, so the lines gained them.

- **The stock preset** (`Presets.StockId` "Stock", `stockGroup` — not `stocksGroup`, the Watchlist,
  which is kept as it was): a list folder wearing the **stock face**, holding a stock line at
  `Presets.StockRows` (**8**) rows, its tallest form, which is the panel. It starts with no symbol, as
  the entry did; the line's "Set up in Settings" asks for one. No footer: the panel's footer was its
  age, which is the line's last row now. The panel had no range picker (the range is the widget's
  setting, §25), so there is none to carry over.
- **What the stock line gained** (`StockIsland`, a fourth height above the header with the day behind
  it, §9 "A line at every height"): *the panel* — its header (`StockHeader`, unchanged: the symbol and
  the company, the price large with its currency and the change, whether the market trades, the
  holding, the problem in the critical ink), its **refresh button** at the header's top right, the
  panel's **graph** (`DayGraph` through `StockIsland.ShowDay`, moved from the panel: the session
  shaded from bell to bell, the times under it, the mark at the last trade; a range's points with
  its days, months or years under them), and its footer's **"Updated 3 minutes ago"**, on the
  header's gutter rather than centred in a band, critical once the price is past due. The graph
  stands on the list's gutter with its times, as the weather's hours do (`ListForm.Housed`). Where a
  refresh failed and the last price stands (stocks.json keeps it), the **stale mark** (§77) stands at
  the end of that row with "Last updated 14:05 — couldn't refresh" over it (`CardTip`). A new line
  where nobody set a height asks for the panel (`ListHeight`).
  - *The ring*: the refresh button's ring turns while the fetch is on its way, as the panel's did.
    A line has no timer of the folder's to turn it, so `RefreshRing` (new, the stock's and the
    feed's) arms one of its own only while the ring turns — a fetch on its way, the button drawn
    (the panel's height), the open folder showing the line (`Visible`) — and each tick wakes the
    line (`CellIsland.Wake`), which steps the phase on the dock's thread, as a quick-settings page
    turns its ring in a folder (`QuickPageTile`). The weather's conditions line still greys its
    button instead (§80); it could take the ring the same way.
  - *The click*: the button is the line's one target (`CardTarget`), a fetch now whatever the age;
    nothing else on the line does anything. The panel's "Try again" under a failed price is the
    same button; the panel's set-up prompt is the line's own (SetupFace).
- **The stock face** (`FolderFaces.Stock`, `stock`, not `Named`; `StockFaceDrawing`): the entry's
  drawing, moved (`StockIsland.PaintFace`) — "MSFT 412.34 +1.2%" on one row across a bar, the symbol
  quiet and semibold, the change in the up or down colour, the day's chart faded behind the whole
  button; the symbol over the price down a bar on its side; quieter once the price is past due;
  **"Set up"** beside the kind's glyph until a symbol is set (`SetupFace.OnBar`, the glyph alone down
  a bar on its side). **Its share is its own** (2026-10-11, the person: the stock face "should get
  its own face, you might also have multiple stocks for one folder"; it first showed the folder's
  first stock line): `FolderFace.Stock` keeps its symbol, the service's name for the listing, its
  name for it (the label) and its range with its years — everything of a stock line's that the face
  draws; not the holding, which it never shows. A folder holds any number of stock lines, each with
  its own symbol, and **none of them is the face's** (`StockSymbols`, as `WeatherPlaces` for the
  weather face, §80). In Settings the face's section has the rows (`FolderRows`: `Symbol`,
  `StockLabel`, `StockRange`, `StockYears` while the range is the last so many, then the change):
  the symbol box is the stock line's own control, now one control for both (`SymbolPicker`: the same
  search as you type, the same proof against the price service before anything is kept, the same
  words). The price comes from the store every line reads (`StockStore`): the folder is a user of
  its own for the face's share (`FolderIsland.FollowStock`), so a face and a line of one symbol and
  range are one fetch, and its right click's Refresh asks for the face's share alone
  (`FolderIsland.RefreshStock`, `FaceWidget` is the folder). Its one option is the entry's own: **the
  change** (`StockFace.Change`, on). Its length is its settings' and the option's alone
  (`StockIsland.FaceLength`: the label or the symbol, the price's room "8,888.88", the change's
  "-88.88%"; `UnsetLength` before a symbol), never the price. Painted again in place as the store
  posts news of its share (the folder is woken and reads it) and on the stocks' interval, when a
  price may go stale (`FaceReading`).
  - *The preset* asks once, as the weather preset does: added, its page opens at the line's symbol
    ("--setup symbol"), and the first symbol chosen there is given to the face still without one
    (`StockSymbols.Spread`, through `SettingsModel.OfferSetup`/`SymbolChosen`) — the symbol, the
    listing's name and the line's label; the face keeps its own range. Never to another stock line.
    After that the two are independent.
  - *Old files*: a stock face with no share of its own (written before 2026-10-11) takes its
    folder's first stock line's symbol, label and range once as the file is read
    (`StockSymbols.Adopt`, from `FolderOptions.Normalize`), so it shows what it showed; no shape
    change.
- **The news preset** (`Presets.NewsId` "News", `newsGroup`): a list folder wearing the **news face**,
  holding a feed line at its own height (Automatic: up to eight stories and how many more, the
  footer under them). It starts with no feed, as the entry did.
- **What the RSS line gained** (`RssIsland`, its whole widget, the panel): the **refresh button** at
  the end of the feed's name, with its ring (`RefreshRing`); a **picture** at the line's end for each
  story whose feed names one, a square as tall as its headline and byline, fetched off the dock's
  thread by the store (`RssStore.Picture`, cached, as the panel fetched them) with its room kept
  quiet until it comes, so nothing moves when it does (and none where it would take more than
  three tenths of the words' room: at the largest text the headlines come first); and the panel's **footer**: "Open
  news.example.com" with the globe (a target of its own, `SiteTarget`, opened as a story is: the
  folder closes and the browser comes, `Dock.FolderForward`), and after it what kept the newest read
  from coming. A footer row rather than a header link: it is the panel's, its words say where it
  goes, and the name's row has the refresh. The **new-story dot** was the line's already; now
  **opening the folder is seeing what is new**, as opening the panel was (`Visible`): the store is
  told the stories are seen, so the face's dot goes at once, while the line keeps its dots on what
  was new for that showing (and on any story that comes while it is open).
- **The news face** (`FolderFaces.News`, `news`, not `Named`; `NewsFaceDrawing`): the entry's drawing,
  moved (`RssIsland.PaintFace`) — the news glyph, the accent's dot on it while something new has
  come, and the newest headline beside it in a room of its own (`HeadlineTemplate`), cut with "…";
  why there is none quietly; the glyph alone down a bar on its side. Its one option is the entry's
  own: **the headline** (`NewsFace.Headline`, on); off, the glyph's square. It shows the folder's
  first feed line (`FolderIsland.Feed`). Painted again in place as the feed is read.
- **Tooltips** are the entries': none over the bar (a folder's button has none); to a screen reader
  the ticker ("MSFT 512.40 +0.86%") and the feed with its newest headline.
- **Right clicks**: the stock face has a Refresh of its own share, the news face its line's Refresh and
  "Open website" (`Dock.ActsOnBar`, worked on `FolderIsland.FaceWidget`, the line): the panels had both.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Stock` and `BarKind.Rss` (config shape **33**: a file of 32 or before is kept
  aside whole and the defaults take its place), their entries, `IslandView.Stock`/`.Rss`, the panels
  (`StockFlyout`, `RssFlyout` with `RssRow`) and the dock's part of them (`Dock.Stocks.cs`,
  `Dock.Rss.cs`), the RSS entry's shape (`WidgetShapes.Rss`) and flyout height
  (`WidgetInfos.Rss.FlyoutHeights`), `StockOptions.ShowChange` and `RssOptions.ShowHeadline` and their
  Settings switches (the faces' options now), the panels' own words ("Try again", its hint, "No feed
  yet", "Getting the news…", "The feed has nothing in it right now."). `StockIsland` and `RssIsland`
  are lines alone (their bar drawings throw). The default bar never had either entry: nothing to
  mirror there.

**Matched against the panels' own pictures** (rendered before they went: `stock-<state>-<dark|light>.png`,
`rss-panel-<state>-*.png`) and the entries' (`stock-bar-*.png`, `rss-bar-*.png`). The same: the stock
header word for word, the graph, "Updated 3 minutes ago" in the critical ink when stale, the refresh
and its ring; the feed's name with its refresh, the stories newest first with their bylines, the new
ones dotted, the pictures at the right, "Open news.example.com" with the globe; the faces' ticker and
headline at every bar. **Different, and why:** no title band or hairline under the header (folders
have none since 8e455a6); the age on the gutter rather than centred in a footer band; the stale mark
beside it, the §77 mark every stale line has; the list's gutter instead of the panel's insets; a
story's headline on one line over its byline (a line's rows are even), where the panel wrapped it on
up to three beside a 64 DIP picture — the picture is the two lines' height; eight stories and how
many more, where the panel scrolled fifteen; the site's link and the problem in the line's last row
rather than a footer band; a feed still being read or that cannot be read is one row saying so, its
Refresh in the line's menu, where the panel kept its button; the accent is the folder's (the
system accent) where the panels in a dark theme took its lighter tone.

Tests: `StockPresetTests` (the preset's line, its rows and face; the entry and its switch gone; the
rows hold the whole panel at 100 % and 150 %; the refresh button asks and its ring turns only while
the fetch is on its way, shown and drawn; a stale price's mark and words; the face reads its own
share, not its line's, with its screen-reader words and its Refresh; a folder of several shares, one
fetch per symbol, the face's Refresh its own; no symbol says "Set up" and asks for nothing; one size
whatever the price does, at every bar, its option and label followed; painted again in place as its
own share's price comes, from its Refresh or a line of the same share; pictures),
`StockSymbolsTests` (a new face's share unset, the face follows no line, the preset's spread to the
face alone, an old file adopted once, the share through the file), `FolderRowsTests` (the stock
face's rows set its own share and no line's), `NewsPresetTests` (the preset, the face
and its option; the whole line is the panel: the site's link, the head, the pictures' room; opening
the folder sees what is new — the face's dot goes, the line's stay for the showing; the refresh and
its ring; the face reads the line, one width whatever the headline, the glyph alone a cell; pictures),
`RssPictureTests` (the line at every height; a headline or the site opens, the refresh does not, and
nothing else), `RssRegistryTests`, `RssConfigTests` (the feed on a folder's line),
`StockHoldingTests`, `StockRangeTests` (the share on a folder's line), `ResetTests.TheStockAndRssEntriesAreGoneAfterTheReset`,
`TypedRegistryTests`, `WidgetSetupTests`, `SectionsTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`, `FlyoutHeightTests`,
`FlyoutHeightRowTests`, `SelectedFlyoutTests`, `MediaRowTests`; the tests that stood a stock or a feed
on a bar as any widget stand the desktops or the layout switcher there instead. Pictures:
`stock-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `stock-face-<dark|light>.png`, `stock-face-own-<dark|light>.png`
(a face of MSFT over lines of AAPL and NVDA, and a face with no symbol), `news-preset-<dark|light>.png`,
`news-face-<dark|light>.png`, `rss-list-*.png`. By hand: add the Stock preset, set a symbol, open it
and press refresh — the ring; go offline and refresh — the mark and its words; set the face's change
off. Check the face took the line's first symbol; then set the face to another symbol in the folder's
Face section (the search box), add a second stock line of a third — the face follows neither. Add the News preset with a feed that has pictures; let a new story come — the face's dot — and
open the folder; click a story and the site's link.

## 99. The drive and the network drive are presets (2026-10-10)

The tenth of the remaining flyout ports, both in one step: the drive and network drive entries and
their flyout (`DrivesFlyout`) went; what a click on each gave is a ready-made folder under a face of
what the entry was.

- **First, the pin.** A pin to a drive's root set to show "Its contents" (`PinContents`, §9) draws
  the flyout's listing already: the same reader's order (folders first, names as a person reads
  them, hidden and system left out), the shell's icon per kind, the date column the rows share, the
  rest in "12 more items", a row lit under the pointer. So nothing new reads or draws a drive's top
  level. But a pin is pointed at a path of its own, and the preset starts with no drive (as the
  entry did) and has to follow the drive its line names when the letter changes or the person picks
  another: a pin that copied the drive line's drive when the preset was made would go stale, and a
  pin that read the drive line's drive would be a pin whose target means nothing. So the listing is
  the **drive line's own**, made of the pin's contents: one widget, one drive chosen in one place.
- **The line** (`DriveIsland`, `DriveTargetOptions.Contents`, "contents", not written while off; the
  card's switch "Show its contents" in Settings): set so, the line is the flyout — the flyout's
  header (`DriveHeader`, unchanged) at the line's top, its second line the kind, the file system and
  the BitLocker state as the flyout said them ("Local disk · NTFS · BitLocker On"), and under it the
  drive's top level, a row each (`PinContents` without its own head row, `head: false`). A line not
  set so draws its tiers as before. The drive line **acts** now (`CellAct.Action`): a row opens its
  item — a folder in File Explorer, a file with its own program — and anywhere else the drive in File
  Explorer, as the flyout's header and its footer did, once the folder has gone (`Dock.FolderForward`,
  `DriveIsland.Open`). While the rows show, only a row or the header lights under the pointer
  (`LightsItsRows`), as the flyout's did. A new line may grow to twelve rows (`FolderOptions.MostRows`).
  - *Off the dock's thread*: the listing is read through the folders' source (`FolderSource.Run`, a
    thread of its own), the volume's file system and BitLocker state the same way, once per root
    (`DriveReader.Facts`); both only while the open folder shows the line (`Visible`), as the flyout
    read only while open. A local drive's root is watched (`FolderWatch`), a **share's never**: a
    watcher's start waits on a share that has gone, on the dock's thread; a share's contents are read
    again on the minute while they show. The drive itself is read as ever (`DriveWatch`).
  - *Following the drive*: the contents are pointed at the drive's root as it is now, so a stick that
    was E: and comes back as F: is listed at F:; a drive not there, not chosen or not answered yet has
    no rows, its header saying why.
- **The presets** (`Presets.DriveId` "Drive", `NetworkDriveId` "Network drive", glyphs the widgets'):
  a list folder each wearing its drive face, holding the drive's line with its contents, automatic up
  to twelve rows (`PresetItem.Contents`). No footer: the flyout's "Open in File Explorer" is the line's
  click and its right click's "Open". Storage is kept as it was, its lines without contents. A new bar
  never had the entries, so it has neither preset; they are in the add list's groups.
- **The faces** (`FolderFaces.Drive`, `NetworkDrive`, not `Named`; `DriveFaceDrawing`): the entry's
  drawing, moved (`DriveIsland.PaintFace`, the cell's code made static over a `DriveLook`): two cells,
  the drive's picture, its name and the capacity bar after it, faint with the warning badge while the
  drive is not there, Explorer's red-X drive with its name and no bar for a disconnected share, "Set
  up" with no drive chosen; down a bar on its side the three stacked. It shows the folder's first line
  of its kind (`FolderIsland.DriveLine`) — the drive is chosen on the line, once, as the stock face
  reads its line (§98); a face of a drive of its own would be a second place to set the same drive,
  and the contents a third. Its one option is the entry's own: **its name** (`DriveFace.Name`, on),
  or the letter alone; `DriveTargetOptions.ShowName` and its Settings switch went. One size whatever it
  shows (`FaceLength`). Painted again in place as the drive is read: on the folder's minute
  (`IntervalMs`) and as the dock reads every drive again, the folder reading its line's drive
  whether open or not (`DriveIsland.Follow`), never the contents.
- **Tooltips** are the entries': none over the bar; to a screen reader the line's words ("Local Disk
  (C:)", how much is used and free).
- **Right clicks**: the faces have their line's Open, Eject (a drive Windows can eject) or Disconnect
  (a mapped share), and Properties (`Dock.ActsOnBar`, on `FolderIsland.FaceWidget`, the line).
- **What went.** `BarKind.Drive` and `BarKind.NetworkDrive` (config shape **34**: a file of 33 or
  before is kept aside whole and the defaults take its place), their entries, `IslandView.Drives`, the
  flyout (`DrivesFlyout`) and the dock's part of it (`Dock.Drives.cs`), the reader's flyout half
  (`DriveSource`, `DriveRequest`, `DriveContents`, `DriveListState`, `DriveReader.List`/`Icons`),
  `DriveTargetOptions.ShowName`, and the flyout's own words ("This drive is taking a while to
  answer…", "Drive"). `DriveIsland` is a line alone (its bar drawing throws). The default bar never had
  either entry: nothing to mirror there.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `drives-<state>-<dark|light>.png`)
and the entries' (`drive-bar-*.png`, `drive-vertical-*.png`, `drive-disconnected-*.png`, now drawn as
the faces and the same pixel for pixel). The same: the header word for word with its file system and
BitLocker, the bar and "512 of 931 GB used · 419 GB free" in the alarm colour when nearly full, the
rows with their icons and dates, a long name cut before its date. **Different, and why:** no hairline
under the header and no footer band (folders have none since 8e455a6; "Open in File Explorer" is the
click on the header, as it was, and the menu's Open); the list's gutter instead of the panel's insets;
an empty drive says the folder words ("This folder is empty") the pin's listing says; a drive still
being read says "Reading…" in a row, never "taking a while"; the rows show as many as twelve rows
hold and how many more, where the panel scrolled a hundred; at 225 % text that is two rows.

Tests: `DrivePresetTests` (the presets, the entries gone and the switch, the line lists the top level
under its header read only once shown, a row opens its item and the rest the drive, the contents
follow the drive's letter and a share is never watched, no rows without a drive, the face reads the
folder's line with its rows and its tooltip, painted again in place one size; pictures),
`DriveWidgetOffscreenTests` (the faces one size in every state, the label's size down a bar, the
disconnected share; pictures), `DriveRowTests` (the face's row measured from its pixels),
`DriveCellTests` (a face is two cells), `ResetTests.TheDriveEntriesAreGoneAfterTheReset`,
`DriveListingTests`, `SetupLinkTests`, `WidgetSetupTests`, `SectionsTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`,
`MediaRowTests`, `CellGridTests`, `WidgetBoundsTests`, `DiskActivityTests`; the tests that stood a
drive on a bar as any widget stand the layout switcher or a folder there instead. Pictures:
`drive-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `drive-preset-share-dark.png` (150 %), `drive-bar-*.png`,
`drive-vertical-*.png`, `drive-disconnected-*.png`, `drive-row-*.png`. By hand: add the Drive
preset, set its drive, open it and click a folder and the header; plug a stick in at another letter;
add the Network drive preset for a mapped share, open it, then disconnect the share — the red X; set
the face's name off; right-click the face for Eject or Disconnect.

*Since 2026-10-11 (§119) the line lists nothing: its contents are a folder pin under it, and a line
that listed is carried over into the two.*

## 100. The notifications are a preset (2026-10-10)

The eleventh of the remaining flyout ports, and the largest: the bell and its flyout
(`NotificationsFlyout`, 2.3k lines) went; what a click on the bell gave is a ready-made folder under
a face of the bell it was. The line (`NotificationPartTile`) drew the flyout's plan flat — every
notification newest first, nothing to expand, nothing to answer — so this is not "accept flat": the
line does what the flyout did.

- **The preset** (`Presets.NotificationsId` "Notifications", `notificationsGroup`; it replaces the
  notification center preset, `clockNotificationsGroup`, whose calendar and focus session are the
  clock preset's): the notification list's line, Automatic up to the most a line may be
  (`FolderOptions.MostRows`), a divider, and the premade notification actions (§85: Notifications |
  Focus), where the flyout's footer had "Notification settings" and "Do not disturb schedule".
- **What the line gained** (NotificationPartTile.cs):
  - *Its header*: the bell, how many there are, "Clear all" and **do not disturb's switch** at its
    end — Windows 11's bell with "zZ", on the accent while on — as the flyout's header had it (the
    old look, rather than the do not disturb line at the folder's top). An empty list with do not
    disturb on says "Do not disturb is on". Where the count and both controls do not fit (225 %
    text) the switch gives way first, then "Clear all"; both stay on the line's menu (and each app's
    ×), the count being what a glance at the line reads.
  - *Grouped by app* (`NotificationText.Groups`), from where two notifications fit so (the whole
    widget's tier): each app's heading — its icon in the list's leading column, its name where
    every name begins, a × under the pointer that clears the app — over its notifications; a group of
    more than three its newest three and "See more (2)", which "See fewer" folds again. Shorter
    lines keep the compact form: the count over the newest one line each, flat, with each app's icon.
  - *A notification* is a row, not the flyout's card: its title over two lines of body, when it came
    at the end and the × in its place under the pointer; Windows' chevron where there is more — a
    longer body, or buttons and boxes. Rows, because a line stands on the folder's card already and a
    card on a card, the look changing as notifications came and went, is what the line was moved off
    once (2026-09-27); they light under the pointer as every list row does.
  - *Expanded*, a card shows its whole body, then each input under its title — the reply box
    (`InlineEditor`, §87's: the folder hands a typing line the keys, Escape first, so Escape ends the
    typing and only a second one closes the folder), a selection that steps on a click — and the
    buttons, side by side where each fits its share, else one under another, in WinUI's shapes.
  - *Acting*, all of it the flyout's rules (ToastActivation.cs): a click on a card is the toast's
    launch, a button its own arguments and every input's value, Enter in a box the button it
    belongs to (or the one button); Windows' Dismiss clears. Each clears the notification. What
    brings an app forward is the line's click that acts (`CellAct.Action`, `IslandView.App`): the
    folder goes and the dock hands the activation on at once (`FolderForward`, `ActivatePending`)
    while the right to the foreground is Karpo's; a background one (Like, a reply sent) is handed
    on in place and the folder stays. A press is matched by what it is (`Target`: the spot, the app,
    the notification, the control), never by its place, so a card cleared above the pointer never
    turns a click into one on its neighbour.
  - *Held short*, it shows what fits whole from the top and says how many more (`WidgetFill`), never
    a heading alone at the foot. Which form a height takes is measured collapsed, so expanding a card
    or opening a group makes the list longer, never another form of it. The count's line starts at
    the line's top inset at every height; what is left over is at the foot (it was centred, which
    left a band above the header — 2026-10-11, `TheHeaderStartsAtTheLinesTop`).
  - What is opened, expanded, typed and chosen (`NotificationView`) is the showing's, gone when the
    folder closes, as Windows' own forgets it.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Notifications`, `notifications`, not `Named`; `NotificationsFaceDrawing`):
  the bell's drawing moved onto `GlyphBadge` — how many are new in an accent pill on its corner
  ("99+"), Windows' bell with "zZ" while do not disturb is on and the pill on the lower corner then,
  dimmed with no count while the notifications cannot be read. Its one option is the bell's:
  **Show how many are new** (`NotificationsFace.Count`, on). One square whatever it shows, painted
  again in place as the store or do not disturb changes (its first paint is the look at do not
  disturb, §11). The folder uses `NotificationStore.Shared` while it wears the face (tests:
  `NotificationPartTile.Stand`, the line's and the face's).
- **Seen.** Opening the folder to look at it marks everything seen (`FolderIsland.MarkSeen`, from
  `ShowFolder`), as the bell's list did as it opened; opened arranged in edit mode, nothing is — the
  rule `SelectedFlyout` kept by never opening the bell's list for a selection (folders are in
  `Never` already).
- **Its right click** has the list's Clear all, Do not disturb and Notification settings, on the
  face's own store (`INotificationActs`, which the line and the folder both are): the bell had its
  "Settings" alone, its list's header and footer had the three.
- **Its tooltip** is the bell's: none over the bar; to a screen reader how many are new, its name
  with none, or why none can be read.
- **The default bar** has the preset where the bell stood, after the date and before show desktop.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Notifications` (config shape **35**: a file of 34 or before is kept aside
  whole and the defaults take its place), its entry and shape, `NotificationOptions` and its
  Settings card, `WidgetInfos.Notifications` and its flyout height, `IslandView.Notifications`, the
  dock's flyout plumbing (`ShowNotifications`, `IslandPopupMessage`), `NotificationsIsland`,
  `NotificationsFlyout`, and the flyout's own words (its title, footer links, "Clear all", the empty
  and quiet lines). The smoke run opens the preset's folder on its made-up database instead.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went: `notifications-grouped-*.png`,
`notifications-expanded-*.png`, `notifications-quiet-*.png`; the bell's `notification-badge-*.png`
and `bell-quiet-*.png`). The same: the grouping and its order, the heading's icon, name and ×, "See
more (2)" and "See fewer", the chevron, the expanded body, the reply box with the accent along its
bottom, the selection and the stacked buttons, the times, the do not disturb switch on the accent,
the bell, its pill and its "zZ". **Different, and why:** rows rather than cards (above); two lines
of body rather than three, a list's line being shorter; no "Notifications" title (folders have none
since 8e455a6); the footer is the premade actions, Focus where "Do not disturb schedule" was; the
empty state is the count's words rather than a large dim bell; an expanded card that leaves no room
for the next is followed by "N other notifications" rather than a scroll.

Tests: `NotificationsPresetTests` (the preset, its line, divider and footer and face; the bell gone;
grouped by app and a long group folding; the chevron expanding; a card and its buttons activating —
the foreground one through the folder, a Like at once; a reply typed and sent with Enter, Escape
ending the typing before the folder; the heading's ×, a card's × and Clear all; a click the thing and
not its place; the header's switch; held short; the header at the top; the showing forgotten; opening marks seen; the face's
count, dim and words; one square painted again in place; the face's right click; pictures),
`DefaultBarTests.TheBellIsTheNotificationsPresetBesideTheDate`, `SerializationTests.TheBellShowsItsCountByDefault`,
`BadgeSizeTests`, `StateSizingTests`, `CellOffscreenTests` (the bell face), `ListLinesTests`,
`ListGutterTests`. Pictures: `notifications-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 % text),
`notifications-face-<dark|light>.png`, `list-notificationsList*.png`, `notification-badge-*.png`.
By hand: open the bell with a chat app's toast that has a reply; expand it, type a reply, Enter;
press a card of an app that brings itself forward; clear an app with the heading's ×; switch do not
disturb from the header and see the face's "zZ"; open the folder in edit mode and see the count stay.

## 101. The clipboard history is a preset (2026-10-10)

The twelfth of the remaining flyout ports: the clipboard history entry and its flyout
(`ClipboardFlyout`, Win+V's panel, §7's "Clipboard history") went; what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder
under a face of the glyph it was. No list line showed the history before, so the line is new.

- **The preset** (`Presets.ClipboardId` "Clipboard history", `clipboardGroup`): the clipboard's line,
  Automatic up to the most a line may be (`FolderOptions.MostRows`), a divider, and the premade
  **clipboard actions** (`PremadeWidgets.ClipboardActions`, new: the "clipboard" settings action alone
  on the left, as the task manager's), where the flyout's footer had "Clipboard settings". A new bar
  never had the entry, so it has no preset either; it is in the add list's groups.
- **The line** (`ListKind.Clipboard`, "clipboard", `WidgetInfos.Clipboard`, `ClipboardLine`; it takes
  the entry's info, its id `clipboardHistory` becoming `clipboard`, its words renamed with it):
  - *Its header*: the clipboard's glyph in the list's leading column, how many items ("6 items";
    "Nothing copied yet", "Reading your clipboard history…") and "Clear all" at its end — the pinned
    stay, as in Win+V; dimmed with nothing but pinned ones; at 225 % text it gives way to the count.
  - *The note*: while Karpo's own history shows, the flyout's footer sentence under the header (why:
    Windows' history is off, or would not be read) and, where it is off, **Turn on**, which opens
    Windows' clipboard settings (`ms-settings:clipboard`), where it is switched on.
  - *A row per item*, newest first, not the flyout's cards (a line stands on the folder's card
    already, as the notification line's rows, §100): text in its first three lines (`ClipText`,
    moved here), a picture as its thumbnail, up to 96 DIP tall and never larger than it was copied,
    rounded with a hairline; a pinned one wears the filled pin in the leading column. Under the
    pointer or the keys a row lights and shows its pin and its delete at its end — the pin only where
    the history can be pinned (Karpo's own; Windows gives a program no way to). Their room is kept
    whether they show or not, so nothing reflows as the pointer moves. Each names itself in a tooltip.
  - *Held short* it shows whole rows from the top and says how many more ("9 other items",
    `WidgetFill`); on one row the glyph, the count and "Clear all". Its height follows its items
    (`IListContent`).
  - *Reading*: the shared store (`ClipboardStore.Shared`); Windows' history is read afresh as the
    folder opens (`Visible`), as the flyout read it as it opened, and the line follows the store's
    news while it shows. A click is matched by the item (`Target`, by its id), never its place.
- **A click pastes, as Win+V's does.** The item goes on the clipboard (`ClipboardStore.Choose`), and
  the click is the folder's act (`CellAct.Action`, `IslandView.App`): the folder closes, which gives
  the focus back to the window in front before it opened (its host's Menu mode), and the dock — told
  where that was (`FolderFlyout.Previous`, read before the folder is let go of) and asked once whether
  a paste is due (`ClipboardLine.TakePaste`, in `FolderForward`) — pastes there once that window's
  focus has settled (`ClipboardPaste`, `PasteWait` on the dock's `PASTE` timer: read every 25 ms, never
  waited on, with every rule of §7's — not into Karpo, the shell, a console, an elevated program or a
  password box). Pin, delete, "Clear all" and "Turn on" act in place and the folder stays.
- **The keys**: Up and Down walk the rows (Up from nothing the last), past either end the folder's
  again. Enter or Space on a row is kept — its repeats too, and every other key meanwhile — and the
  row is chosen only when that key is let go, as the flyout did, so none of it reaches the window
  pasted into. The folder hands a line a key's release for this (`CellIsland.KeyUpOn`/`CardKeyUp`,
  new; on true it clicks the line with no part, `Activate(focused, null)`).
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Clipboard`, `clipboard`, not `Named`, no options;
  `ClipboardFaceDrawing`): the entry's glyph (Segoe Fluent's clipboard, U+F0E3) in a glyph's
  square, full strength, no count (the entry had none). It never changes, so nothing paints it again.
  The folder wearing it attaches to the store (`FolderIsland.FollowClipboard`), as the entry did while
  it stood on a bar: that is what starts the clipboard being heard where Karpo keeps its own, so what
  was copied before the first look is there; another face, or the folder gone, lets go. Its tooltip is
  the entry's: none over the bar, its name to a screen reader. Its right click is the folder's own
  (the entry had no rows of its own).
- **What went.** `BarKind.ClipboardHistory` (config shape **36**: a file of 35 or before is kept aside
  whole and the defaults take its place), its entry and shape, `WidgetInfos.ClipboardHistory` and its
  flyout height, `IslandView.Clipboard`, `ClipboardIsland`, `ClipboardFlyout`/`ClipCard`, the dock's
  flyout plumbing (`ShowClipboard`, `ClipboardMessage`, `ClipboardClosed`; `Dock.Clipboard.cs` keeps
  the paste), the flyout's words (its title, empty sentence, "Clipboard settings", "Item 3", "Pin 3",
  "Delete 3") and `ClipboardFlyoutOffscreenTests`. The default bar never had the entry: nothing to
  mirror there. Tests that stood it on a bar as any one-cell widget stand the touch keyboard there
  (the status icons where it had to sort before the tray; the contacts where it had a flyout height).

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went:
`clipboard-<karpo|windows|empty>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`). The same: newest first, text in its
first three lines, the picture as its thumbnail, pin and delete per item (delete alone for Windows'
own), "Clear all" keeping the pinned, the note's words and the way to the setting, a click pasting,
a key chosen only on its release. **Different, and why:** rows rather than cards (above); the pin and
delete show under the pointer or the keys, not always, the pinned item marked in the leading column
instead; no "Clipboard history" title (folders have none since 8e455a6) — the header says how many;
the note is under the header with "Turn on" rather than in a footer band, and the footer is the
premade "Clipboard" action; a picture is at most 96 DIP tall rather than 120; held short it says how
many more rather than scrolling; the empty state is the header's words.

Tests: `ClipboardPresetTests` (the preset, its line, divider, footer and face; the entry gone and the
line's act; the face hears the clipboard and lets go, one square; Karpo's own rows, note and "Turn
on"; Windows' own with delete alone; a row pastes once and the buttons act in place; a click the item
and not its place; the keys walk and choose on release; held short; opening reads Windows' history
again; pictures), `ClipboardHistoryTests` (`HistoryOff`), `FlyoutsLanguageTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`,
`FlyoutHeightTests`, `FlyoutHeightRowTests`, `SectionsTests`, `ShortcutWidgetTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`.
Pictures: `clipboard-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 % text), `clipboard-face-<dark|light>.png`.
By hand: add the Clipboard history preset; copy text and a screenshot; open it from a text editor and
click an item — the folder goes and the item is pasted there; again with Down and Enter held; pin,
delete, Clear all; with Windows' history off, "Turn on"; with it on, delete alone.

## 102. The contacts are a preset (2026-10-11)

The person: *"port contacts, keep websearch as flyout"* — the thirteenth of the remaining flyout
ports. The contacts entry and its flyout (`ContactsFlyout`, a search box over the people in the
accounts) went; what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder under a face of the glyph it was. Search
the web stayed a taskbar entry with its own flyout, until it went altogether (2026-10-11, §28). No list line showed the contacts before, so the
line is new.

- **The preset** (`Presets.ContactsId` "Contacts", `contactsGroup`): the contacts' line alone,
  Automatic up to the most a line may be (`FolderOptions.MostRows`). The flyout's footer was a count
  and no link, so the count moved into the line and there is no actions line under it. A new bar never
  had the entry, so it has no preset either; it is in the add list's groups.
- **The line** (`ListKind.Contacts`, "contacts", `WidgetInfos.Contacts`, `ContactsLine`; it takes the
  entry's info and id, its flyout heights gone; `CellAct.Nothing`, `Interaction.Click | Drag`):
  - *The search box* at its top, on both gutters: the quick settings' `TextField` drawn on the card
    as the Wi-Fi's key field is (§88), in Windows 11's search-box look (the magnifier, as the web
    search's box). It has the keys as the folder opens, so typing searches at once.
  - *Under it* what the flyout's footer said, small and quiet: "5 contacts" ("… in a@b.com" with one
    account), "1 of 5" while typing narrows ("Copied …" stood here until a person's details came, see
    below: what was copied now says so where it was copied). Where nobody is listed, why, in its place: "Reading your contacts…",
    the account's problem, "Your accounts have no contacts yet.", "Nobody matches “q”."
  - *A row per person* who answers (`ContactSearch`, unchanged: name start, word start, inside the
    name, an address or the organization, a phone's digits; accents folded): the contact glyph in the
    leading column, the name, and under it the address, else the number, else the organization. Lit
    under the pointer; the chosen one wears the keys' ring, and once copied the accept glyph at its end.
  - *Held short* it shows whole rows under the box and says how many more ("56 other contacts",
    `WidgetFill`); on one row the box alone. The box stays at the top however few answer. Its height
    follows the people listed (`IListContent`): typing shrinks the line and the folder follows.
- **A person's details** (2026-10-11, the person: *"it should actually show copy buttons for different
  things like the email, phone, etc. also a send email or call button. make sure that it does not
  overload the widget"*). Not overloading it was the rule the design was chosen by: a list of hundreds
  with buttons on every row is a toolbar, not a list. So each thing appears only where the person
  reached for it:
  - *At rest* a row is what it was: the glyph, the name, the detail under it. Nothing more.
  - *Under the pointer* (or the keys) it shows at most two glyph buttons at its end, Email and Call —
    each only where the person has an address or a number Windows can open (`ContactActs.FirstEmail`,
    `FirstPhone`); an organization alone shows none. The name and detail give way to them on that
    row only (their ellipsis moves), so no room is kept empty on the rows at rest.
  - *A click on the row opens it in place* — an accordion, one row open at a time, Windows 11's
    expander: the row becomes a small card (a control's fill and hairline), the name semibold with a
    chevron that closes it, and under it every detail on a line of its own (`ContactActs.Details`:
    each address, each number, the organization; blank ones and repeats left out), its kind's glyph
    in the leading column, Copy at its end and Email or Call before it. A click on the line copies it
    too. At a text size where the value would have no room to be read, the line keeps Copy alone (the
    menu still writes or calls). Typing that narrows the person away closes it.
  - *Copying says so where it happened*: the clipboard's chip — the accent's check and "Copied" — in
    the buttons' place for 1.5 s (`ClipboardLine.CopiedMs`), on the line copied, or at the end of a
    closed row (Ctrl+C, the menu). The folder stays: looking up the next person is what the list is for.
  - *Email and Call* hand Windows `mailto:` and `tel:` (`ContactActs.MailUri`, `TelUri`) — the default
    mail app and the default calling app (Phone Link, Teams, Skype) — once the folder has gone: the
    line's click is now the folder's act (`CellAct.Action`, `Dock.FolderForward` → `OpenChosen`), as a
    message of the mail line is. `mailto:` carries the address alone, every character not plain in a
    mailto percent-encoded as UTF-8, so a `?`, `&`, `#` or `%` in an address can never start a subject or
    a body; no address without an `@` with something on both sides, none with white space. `tel:` is
    the digits alone, a leading `+` kept, an extension ("ext. 12", "x12", "#12") as `;ext=12`; none
    without digits.
  - *Its right click on a row* (`WidgetAct.ContactEmail`, `ContactCall`, `ContactCopy`): the person's
    name as a heading, Send email, Call, Copy email, Copy phone number, Copy contact details (the name,
    the organization, every address and number, a line each), each only where they have it, then
    Refresh and Settings. Over an open row's line it is that address or number. Over no person,
    Refresh alone. A copy leaves the folder open; Send email and Call close it (`HandsAway`).
  - *Scrolled into sight*: a row opened, or chosen by the keys, past the window of a line held short is
    brought into sight as little as it takes, its ring with it (`IListScroll.ScrollReveal`,
    `ListScrolled.Revealing`, asked once by `CellIsland.Scrolled`).
  - The click that copied the first address before is the click that opens now; Ctrl+C copies it
    (`ContactActs.Primary`: the first address, else the first number). A click is matched by the
    person (`TargetOf`), never the row's place.
  - Tests: `ContactActsTests` (details, what each person is offered, mailto/tel escaping, the copy
    texts, `Revealing`), `ContactsPresetTests` (Email and Call under the pointer, an open row copying
    each detail, the right click's rows, the keys, scrolled into sight); sheets
    `contacts-details-<dark|light>.png` at 150 %: at rest, hovered, open, copied, Ctrl+C, narrow,
    held short, Compact, 225 % text.
- **The keys.** The box with the keys is a text box with the keys (`CardTyping`, §87): the folder hands
  the line every key and character first. Up and Down choose a row while the caret stays in the box,
  neither end wrapping (`ContactsLine.Move`, the flyout's rule for a list of hundreds); Enter opens or closes the row chosen; Ctrl+C copies its address unless text is selected in the box;
  Escape is the folder's and closes it, as it closed the flyout; Tab lets the box go and moves on. With
  the folder's focus on the line but not the box, Up and Down walk the rows (past either end the
  folder's), Enter or Space opens, Ctrl+C copies, and a letter gives the box the keys again and types it. A press
  on the box puts the caret there and a drag selects (`CardPress`/`CardDrag`); a press anywhere else
  in the folder lets the box go, keeping what was typed. The caret blinks on the folder's tick.
- **Reading.** The one store (`ContactStore.Shared`, a test's `ContactsLine.Stand`), synced from the
  dock's start whether or not the line is placed (§389); the folder opening starts only what is due
  (`Visible`), and the line follows the store's news while it shows. Closing it forgets what was typed,
  chosen and copied. With no account that gives
  contacts the line is "Set up in Settings" (`Unset`, the Accounts page), as the flyout's empty list
  was; that is the store's last read, so the first opening shows the box until the read answers.
- **Its right click**: over a person, theirs (above); then Refresh (`ContactStore.Reread`: the accounts asked again however fresh the last
  read, as the mail line's Refresh), then its Settings.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Contacts`, `contacts`, not `Named`, no options; `ContactsFaceDrawing`):
  the entry's glyph (U+E77B) in a glyph's square, full strength, no count. The entry dimmed itself once
  a read had failed; the face reads nothing, and the line says why. Its tooltip is the entry's: none
  over the bar, its name to a screen reader. Its right click is the folder's own.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Contacts` (config shape **37**: a file of 36 or before is kept aside whole
  and the defaults take its place), its entry, `WidgetInfos.Contacts.FlyoutHeights`,
  `IslandView.Contacts`, `ContactsIsland`, `ContactsFlyout`, `Dock.Contacts.cs` and the dock's flyout
  plumbing, the "Contacts" title string and `ContactsFlyoutOffscreenTests`. Tests that stood the entry
  on a bar as a one-cell widget stand the touch keyboard there; those that needed a flyout height take
  the keyboard's (the same 156/260/416).

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (rendered before it went:
`contacts-flyout-<list|typed|none|noaccount>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`). The same: the box first
with the keys, every row's glyph, name and detail, the search and its order, Enter and a click copying
with the folder kept, the arrows choosing with the caret in the box, the empty states' words, Set up in
Settings. **Different, and why:** the box is Windows 11's search box (magnifier, no accent underline)
rather than a plain text box — it searches; the count and "Copied …" stand under the box rather than
in a footer band (folders have no footer; the line is all there is); the chosen row wears the keys'
ring rather than the list's accent pill (every line marks the row the keys are on so, and the pill sat
on the leading glyph); held short it says how many more rather than scrolling; the copied row has the
accept glyph at its end; the flyout's "Copied" glyph, which drew as a box, is Segoe's accept.

Tests: `ContactsPresetTests` (the preset and the face; the entry gone and the line acting in place,
its Refresh; the face one square; typing narrows at once, digits and accents; the arrows choose, Enter
copies, Escape and Tab are the folder's, a letter takes the box back, a press elsewhere lets it go; a
click copies the person not the place, a press on the box is the line's; held short, one row; why
nobody is listed, Unset; opening reads and Refresh reads again; `Move`; pictures), `SetupLinkTests`,
`ResetTests` (a shape 36 file kept aside), `TypedRegistryTests`, `SectionsTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`,
`ListGutterTests`, `FlyoutHeightTests`, `FlyoutHeightRowTests`. Pictures: `contacts-preset-<dark|light>.png`
(150 %, and 225 % text), `contacts-face-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: add the Contacts preset with an
account that has contacts; type a name, a number's digits; Down, Enter, paste somewhere; click a row;
Tab and the arrows; Escape; with no account, Set up in Settings; right click, Refresh.

slider itself — the sun, the track and the thumb, dragged and turned (§35, `BrightnessIsland`)
