## 104. Cast opens Windows' Cast panel (2026-10-11)

The person, of the cast widget: *"yeah do that honestly"* — a click opens Windows' own Cast panel,
not a page of Karpo's. The page (`CastPage`) listed the wireless displays in range and the one cast
to, but could do nothing with them: no unpackaged app may connect to or disconnect from a wireless
display (the one connecting call takes a packaged app's view ids, and disconnecting has no public
call at all), so every row and its "Open Cast" button only opened Windows' panel anyway. The list
before the panel was a click in the way.

- **The click presses Win+K** (`QuickSwitch.Cast`'s `ShortcutSwitch`, `QuickSwitches.Chord`, one
  `SendInput` of the four strokes), Windows 11's own shortcut for Cast, which opens the quick
  settings' Cast panel where its button would. Chosen over
  `ms-settings-connectabledevices:devicediscovery`: that address is the Devices Flow's protocol,
  which answers with the Cast panel on this build but with Windows 10's "Add a device" elsewhere
  (§88); the shortcut is what Windows documents for Cast and is what the page's "Open Cast" already
  pressed. The entry is a Windows panel now (`BarClick.Panel`) and, as Windows' panels' buttons do,
  shows its tooltip (the switch's name and "Opens Windows' panel for wireless displays and
  speakers."). Still the bar's alone: a folder holds no cast line.
- **What went.** `CastPage`, the cast service (`Services\Cast.cs`: `ICastSource`, `WindowsCast`,
  `SampleCast`, `CastDisplays`, the Miracast watcher and the read of the display cast to),
  `QuickKind.Cast`, `IslandView.Cast`, `SwitchIsland.Page`'s cast arm, `QuickSources.Cast`, the
  dock's arm, the page's words (`dock.quick.cast.*`) and its tests and pictures
  (`quick-cast*-*.png`). What the service found out about Miracast from an unpackaged process is in
  git (`Karpo.Dock\QuickSettings\Services\Cast.cs` before this change).

Tests: `DisplayFlyoutsTests.CastOpensWindowsCastPanel` (a Windows panel with a tooltip, no flyout,
Win+K), `EachButtonAsksForItsOwnPage`, `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.ProjectOpensItsPageAndCastActs`
(the bar's click acts and asks for no page), `FolderClickRuleTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`. By hand:
click the cast widget on a bar — Windows' Cast panel opens, as Win+K opens it; connect to a display
there.

*Superseded the same day by §114: the cast button is the cast preset, whose line lists the displays
again and hands the connecting to this panel.*

## 106. An alarm (2026-10-11)

The person: *"add an alarm widget too, the alarm widget should just have one alarm that you can
configure to a certain time and then activate. (optionally also repeats on configurable days)"*. A
list line (`ListKind.Alarm`, `alarm`), in the library's Time group beside the stopwatch; no taskbar
entry and no preset folder (yet).

- **What is set** (`AlarmOptions`, `WidgetItem.Alarm`, written only for an alarm and optional, so every
  file from before reads as it was; no shape change): its time (`"HH:mm"`, 24-hour in the file, a new
  one 07:00), the days it repeats on (`"mon"` … `"sun"`, Monday first; absent rings once), whether it
  is on, and a name. Kept through a restart, unlike a timer: an alarm is a promise about tomorrow.
  Set in Settings (Time — a time picker on the clock Karpo shows, Localization's time pattern else
  Windows'; Alarm on; Repeat — a button per day in the region's week; Name). The switch on the line
  is the same "on", which the dock writes (`AlarmBook.Switched` → the countdowns' settled save).
- **When it rings** (`AlarmSchedule`, `AlarmBook`, Karpo.Core\Alarms.cs, all pure): the next coming
  of its time on a day it may ring on, reckoned on the wall clock of the zone in force and kept as an
  instant (UTC). Set at a time already past, it is tomorrow's — switching it on, Karpo starting or a
  new time never rings for a moment before. Overdue by at most five minutes (`Grace`) — asleep through
  it, the clock set forward — it rings once when seen; later, it is missed. Each ring or miss is
  remembered and the next reckoned after it, so the clock set back never rings it twice; a clock set
  back before it was switched on still lets its time come. Summer time's gap rings at the first
  minute after it; winter time's repeated hour rings at the first of the two.
- **Ringing.** No packaged identity, so no Windows toast (as the timer): Windows' alarm sound
  (`Notification.Looping.Alarm`) looped while it rings, the notification sound once where the scheme
  has none (`AlarmSound`); a shut folder holding it is marked as a timer's end marks it. It rings
  until Snoozed (ten minutes, Windows Clock's default), Dismissed, or five minutes pass (`RingFor`).
  One that does not repeat turns itself off when its ring is over — dismissed, run out or missed — in
  its options, written.
- **The dock** (`Dock.Alarms.cs`): one book (`Countdowns.Alarms`), handed the config's alarms at the
  start and on each config change (`Sync`), looked at (`Tick`) by a host timer (`ALARM`) armed for the
  next thing due and at least once a minute, and on `WM_TIMECHANGE` (zone cache cleared) and resume.
- **The line** (`AlarmTile`, `ListTiers`): one row is the glyph, the time (the region's 12/24-hour
  `Nls.Time`), the hint after it where it fits whole, and the switch at the gutter; the compact line
  (its own height when Automatic, two rows) the time at the list's figure over the hint (its name
  before it); from three rows its name over the time, large, and the hint. The hint: Off, Today,
  Tomorrow, its days ("Every day", "Weekdays", "Weekends", "Mon, Wed" in the region's week), Ringing
  (accent), Snoozed until 7:10. Ringing, Snooze and Dismiss stand where the switch was (worded, else
  glyphs); snoozed, Dismiss alone. Off, the time is the quieter ink and the glyph not in the accent.
  Only those controls take a click (`CellAct.Nothing`). A large text shrinks the time rather than
  cutting it, but for a 12-hour time ringing on the narrow list at 225 %.
- **Glyph** U+ECC5 (the clock with its arrow round): Segoe has no alarm clock, and the bell is the
  notifications'.
- **Not done:** setting the time on the line itself (wheel or steppers) — a wheel over a list that
  scrolls would move somebody's alarm; Settings sets it.

Tests: `AlarmTests` (next coming, days, summer and winter time, once and repeating, sleep, clock back
and forward, snooze and dismiss, the switch, sync, the hint and days' words, options and the file,
registry), `AlarmFormsTests` (one row to six at three scales, three text sizes, both widths, six
states: inside the gutters, nothing overlapping, controls reached; the switch and buttons; sheets
`alarm-line-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`, `-100-text225`, `-150-contrast`). By hand: add an Alarm line,
set it a minute or two ahead in Settings, switch it on on the line, hear it ring, Snooze, Dismiss; set
repeat days; sleep the PC across one.

## 107. Explorer's taskbar over Task view (2026-10-11)

Explorer's taskbar was let be shown, and put in sight from auto-hide's place, while Task view was
up, and hidden again after. The user found it threw the application off and chose to keep the
taskbar hidden (§89); removed the same day.

## 108. The rows of the item lines: a message opens, a headline on the gutter, "Copied", the field at the foot (2026-10-11)

The person: "the emails in the email widget should be individually clickable / highligtable"; "the
rss newsfeed seems to have a gap on the left side of the articles"; "when clicking on a clipboard
item it should show a copied text"; "add a task should be all the way on the bottom".

- **A message is a row** (`MailIsland`). Each message lights under the pointer and pressed, and a
  click opens it in the account's web mail: the folder closes and the dock opens it as it opens a
  headline (`CellAct.Action` on the mail line now, `Dock.FolderForward`, `MailIsland.Open`). Where:
  `MailItem.Link` (`Karpo.Accounts\Mail\MailLinks.cs`) — a Microsoft account's message is Graph's
  `webLink` (Outlook on the web, the message itself); a Gmail IMAP account's is found by its
  Message-ID (`#search/rfc822msgid:`), in its own mailbox (`u/<address>`); Outlook.com, Microsoft 365,
  Yahoo, iCloud and AOL by IMAP open their web mail's inbox; any other server gives none, and its
  messages are read, not pressed (no plate, no target). Only https is ever handed to the shell
  (`MailLinks.Web`). `mail-cache.json` keeps the link (`CachedMail.Link`, absent in a file of before,
  which reads as none: no reset). Taller than a row, the messages stand on the gutter like the
  headlines below.
- **The headlines stand on the gutter** (`RssIsland`). They began where the feed's name does, after
  the leading column, which stood empty before every headline and read as a missing picture with
  the picture at the other end. Now a headline and its byline start at the list's gutter, its
  picture at the end; the new dot leads the byline (beside the age on the compact line). The
  feed's name keeps its glyph in the leading column.
- **The pressed look** (`Islands\RowPress.cs`). A line whose rows light themselves
  (`LightsItsRows`) is never lit pressed by the folder, so each row now lights pressed itself — the
  subtle pressed fill, Windows 11's list item — while the button is down on it: the line is told of
  the press (`CardPress`, answering false so the press stays the folder's click) and lets it go at
  the click, when the pointer leaves the row, or when the folder closes. The mail and the news
  (plate 6 px past the words into the gutter, `MailIsland.Around`), the clipboard (rows, "Clear all",
  "Turn on"), the notifications, the contacts (whose rows lit pressed only while the search box was
  held, a bug), the removable devices and a folder pin's or a drive's items. The day's events open
  nothing and do not light.
- **A clipboard click copies, and says so** (`ClipboardLine`). It pasted into the window in front,
  closing the folder first, and nothing said what had happened. Now the item goes on the clipboard,
  the folder stays, and the row wears a chip — the accent's check and "Copied" (`dock.clipboard.copied`)
  on a control's fill over the flyout's solid colour, at the end of its first line where its pin and
  delete stand — for 1.5 s (`CopiedMs`; the line is woken then to be drawn again). Enter or Space on
  a row still pastes, Win+V's way, the folder gone first.
- **"Add a task" at the foot** (`TodoTile`). It stood under the list's name; it is the last row now,
  under the tasks, "Completed" and how many more, and stays there when the line is held short. A task
  typed there goes under the others (`Notebook.AddTask(..., last: true)`), just over the field, rather
  than at the top far from where it was typed; Down from nothing chooses the first task.

Tests: `MailLinksTests`, `MicrosoftReaderTests.AMessageOpensAtItsWebLink`,
`OfflineCacheTests.AMessagesLinkIsKeptAndAFileWithoutOneStillReads`,
`MailCardTests.AMessageLightsAndItsClickOpensIt`/`TheMessagesStandOnTheGutter`, `RowPressTests`,
`NewsPresetTests` (gutter, pressed), `ClipboardPresetTests.ARowCopiesAndSaysSoAndTheButtonsActInPlace`,
`NotebookLinesTests`, `NotebookTests.ATaskAddedLastGoesUnderTheOthers`; sheets `mail-preset-*`
(a message under the pointer, pressed), `news-preset-*`, `clipboard-preset-*` (a row pressed, a row
just copied), `notes-todo-*`. By hand: click a message of a Microsoft and of a Gmail account; press
and drag off a row; click a clipboard row and watch "Copied" go; add tasks from the foot.

## 109. Lines of items scroll, everything stands at the top, and items have a style (2026-10-11)

The person, three requests about the lines of a list folder:

1. *"if content is cut off by the fixed height the widgets should always be scrollable in list
   view. dont just show x more items, let the user scroll down to see all of the other items too."*
2. *"generally speaking if the widgets cannot fill the space available to them they should be top
   aligned and not center their content somehow. make sure this is done with all widgets. (e.g. one
   that violates this is the clipboard widget)"*
3. *"there should be different item styles that you should be able to select, for example the size
   of how the items are shown, if they have preview text, etc."*

**Scrolling inside a line** (`Karpo.Dock\Islands\ListScroll.cs`, `CellIsland.Scrolled`). One
mechanism for every line of items, kept in `CellIsland` so the drawing and every hit test (target,
press, drag, hover, wheel, tooltip) read one offset. A line implements `IListScroll`:
`ScrollHeight(width, height)` is its whole content — every item, nothing summarised — where at that
height it lists items at all (a line of one row keeps its one-row reading), and `ScrollHead` the band
that stays (the count over the mail, the clipboard's header and note, the notifications' "Clear all",
the contacts' search box, a to-do list's name, a day's heading, the sound heading). Given less than
its content, the line is laid out as tall as all of it (`ListScrolled.Moved`), drawn through the
window under its head, its head drawn still over it with 2 px of air; a widget never learns it is
scrolled. Items out of sight are not drawn (`CellIsland.Hidden`). Converted: mail, news, the
notifications, the clipboard, the contacts, to-do, a day's events, the calendar's agenda, the
removable devices, screen time's apps, the sound devices, microphones and mixer. Every "N more" /
"N other …" row went with it. Not converted: a folder pin's contents (its entries are capped by the
reader and the rest is the folder it opens).

- **The wheel** (`FolderFlyout.ScrollLine`, `Glide`): over a line with more than it shows, the wheel
  or the touchpad moves its items — a notch three lines of text (48 DIP at 100 %, never more than
  80 % of what shows), a touchpad's small deltas by as little — eased over ~15 ms frames (35 % of the
  way each frame), the row under the pointer re-lit as the items pass. **Nested scrolling is
  Windows' scroll chaining**: the line scrolls until its items reach their end, and the next turn
  that way scrolls the folder; turned back, the line scrolls back first. A line that takes the
  wheel itself (`Interaction.Wheel`: a stepper, the mixer's sliders) is asked by the notch first,
  and only where it did not take it do its items scroll. A folder opens with every line at its start.
- **The overlay scrollbar**: Windows 11's thin indicator — 2 DIP, rounded, at the line's trailing
  edge inside the window, as long as the share shown (24 DIP at least), in the theme's scroll
  indicator ink — drawn while the pointer is over the line.
- **Edit mode** keeps working: a line being carried takes no wheel; otherwise the wheel scrolls a
  line's items in edit mode too, as it scrolls the folder.

**Top-aligned** (`LineRows.Top`). What is shorter than its line stands at its top, the list's pad
under it; only where the room leaves less than that above and below is it in the middle. Swept for
every kind (`ListScrollTests.EveryLineStandsAtTheTopOfATallLine`: drawn ten rows tall, the first ink
is in the first row). Fixed: the clipboard, mail, news, the calendar's agenda, the clock (and its
dial), Security, the switches, Brightness, the battery, the toggles, the time header, the weather's
hours and days while they wait, the alarm, the timer and focus time, what is playing (all three
tall forms), the sound lists and the volume (its tall form keeps at most 12 DIP between its rows).
Kept in the middle by design: the removable devices' "Nothing plugged in" and "Set up in Settings",
the empty states; and a line's one-row form, which is the row's middle band at any height under the
compact line, as every one-row form is (`ListTiers.Row`).

**Item styles** (`Karpo.Core\ItemStyles.cs`, `Karpo.Dock\Islands\ItemForm.cs`). One setting for every
line of items, `"items": { "size": "compact", "preview": true, "pictures": false, "time": false }`,
every field optional; a line nobody set carries none and draws exactly as before (Standard is the
list form's own sizes); normalizing drops what equals the kind's default, a part the kind's items do
not have, and the whole record where nothing is left; an unknown size reads as Standard. Sizes:
Compact (13/11 DIP text, half the room in and between items, ¾ pictures, 32-DIP rows), Standard
(14/12, as before, 40-DIP rows), Large (16/13, 1½ the room, 1⅓ pictures, 48-DIP rows). Parts per kind
(`ItemStyles.Offer`, default in brackets): mail — preview of the message [on since 2026-10-11, *"the email widget as a default should show preview text"*; off was the default before, so no file ever wrote it off and every mail line shows it now, one turned off since writes `"preview": false`], time [on]; news —
pictures [on], time [on]; notifications — body [on], app icons and pictures [on], time [on];
clipboard — a text's further lines [on], picture thumbnails [on]; contacts — the address line [on];
events — place [on], time [on]; the agenda — time [on]; to-do, removable devices, screen time's apps —
size only. Settings (Widgets page, a line's options): "Item size" and a switch per part offered.

Tests: `ListScrollTests` (the sweep; a clipboard of twenty in three rows scrolls to every item, a
press at the end lands on the last, the head's pixels do not move; a line that fits or is one row
does not scroll; the wheel in an open folder scrolls to the end, then chains, a touchpad step moves
by little; item sizes order Compact < Standard < Large; sheets `list-scroll-<dark|light>.png`,
`list-item-styles-<dark|light>.png`), `ItemStylesTests` (offers, looks, normalizing, the file and an
older and a newer one), and the converted lines' own tests now asserting scrolling instead of "N more".
By hand: a mail or clipboard line Fixed at 3 rows — wheel and touchpad over it, the thin bar on
hover, the head still, the wheel reaching the end and then moving the folder; a click on an item
after scrolling; the item size and switches in Settings on a mail, clipboard and notifications line.

**With §108's rows** (rebased onto them the same day). Both hold: the mail's messages and the news'
headlines stand on the gutter in the item style's sizes, each a target lit under the pointer and
pressed, read through the scroll offset like every hit test (`CellIsland.CardPress` hands
`CardDown` the scrolled box). Their plates keep at most half the room between two rows above and
below their words (`MailIsland.Around(words, style, above)`), so Compact rows' plates do not meet.
The clipboard's "Copied" chip is on the copied row wherever it has scrolled to. To-do's "Add a task"
stays at the line's bottom while the tasks scroll (§119, `ScrollFoot`); held so short that nothing
scrolls, it stays at the foot and the tasks give way above it. What is playing has no centred
column any more (§9, "Now playing", the same day): its tall forms stand at the top with the words at the left edge
and the art at the right. The apps playing (`mediaSources`, new there) say "Nothing playing" in their
first row, where the first app would stand, not in the middle of a taller line.

## 110. The power menu is a button per command (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the power menu should actually be separate widgets which are just single buttons"* and
*"the battery / power thing should be separate from the power folder, the power folder / premade group
should only show the individual power buttons"*.

- **Six list widgets** (`ListKind.Sleep`, `Hibernate`, `ShutDown`, `Restart`, `SignOut`, `Lock`; ids
  `sleep`, `hibernate`, `shutDown`, `restart`, `signOut`, `lock`; `WidgetInfo.Power`, `PowerCommand`),
  in System. Each is the list's own row (`ListLine.Row`) of the quick-link menu's glyph and name, as
  Task view's is, drawn by `PowerButtonTile` (`WidgetSource.PowerButton`). A click asks the folder to
  close (`IslandView.App`); the dock closes every folder and runs the command off its thread
  (`Dock.FolderForward` → `PowerButtonTile.Act` → `QuickLinks.Power`, after the fade). Sleep and
  hibernate where Windows' power menu offers them (`QuickLinkMachine`); where it does not, the row is
  faint with the warning badge, says why in its hover (`dock.power.notOffered`) and does nothing. Right
  click: Power & battery for the four the page is about.
- **The power preset** (`Presets.PowerId`) is the buttons alone, in Windows' power menu's order and
  then its account menu's: sleep (`PresetNeed.Sleep`), hibernate (`PresetNeed.Hibernate`), shut down,
  restart, sign out, lock; `PresetMachine` carries what the power menu offers, which the dock reads as
  a preset is picked. The power mode and the power actions footer are the battery preset's only (§94).
- **Gone:** the `powerCommands` line (one line of six rows), `PowerCommandsPage` and
  `QuickKind.Power`.
- **Carried over in place** (`LineMigrations.SplitPowerCommands`, run by `Config.Repair`; no reset): a
  `powerCommands` line becomes sleep, shut down, restart, sign out and lock where it stood, the first
  keeping its id; hibernate is left out (Windows' menu shows it only where somebody turned it on), one
  pick in the add list. Everything around it is untouched.

Tests: `BatteryPowerPresetTests` (the preset per machine, the buttons' commands and order, the click
that closes first, a command not offered), `LineMigrationsTests` (a file with the line, written back
once), the registry tables. Sheets `power-preset-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: add the Power preset, try
Lock.

## 111. A reading's graph and its details are two widgets (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the graphics / cpu / network graphs and details should be separate widgets. they should
not have a divider in between them in the default group"*.

- **Five details widgets** (`cpuDetails`, `gpuDetails`, `memoryDetails`, `diskDetails`,
  `networkDetails`; `WidgetInfo.Facts`, each with its reading's `Metric` and the graphs'
  `PerformanceOptions`, so the graphics' details follow the card their own options name): the facts
  the flyout had under its minute (`PerformanceModel.Facts`) in two columns, each its name over its
  figure, a fact too long for its column across both, starting where the graph's name does over them.
  As tall as the facts (`IListContent`), up to twelve rows at the largest text; where the grid would be taller
  than the twelve rows a line has (at 225 % text most facts are too long for a column and the
  processor's up time was left out), a row each instead: the name leading and the figure trailing, or
  the name over the figure where the two do not fit beside each other. A row that would be cut
  is left out whole. Same class as the graphs (`PerformanceIsland`), same source; a click opens Task
  Manager, right click Resource Monitor. Settings shows the adapter or the disk, not the graph's pace.
- **The graph** no longer draws the facts. Its tallest form (from 160 DIP) is the top of the flyout:
  the name, the figure large with what the top stands for, the minute on its hairlines with "60
  seconds" and "0". Its catalogue name says "graph" ("Processor graph"); what it draws beside the
  figure is still the reading's word (`PerformanceIsland.Drawn`).
- **The readings' presets** are the graph at `Presets.ReadingGraphRows` (5), its details at their own
  height and the Task Manager footer: one card, no divider. System keeps its five compact graphs.
- **Carried over once** (`LineMigrations.SplitReadings`): a graph set to a fixed height tall enough to
  have shown the facts (the presets' 9 rows for the processor, 7 for the others) becomes the graph —
  same id and options, its rows less the facts' (at least 5) — and its details under it. Shorter
  graphs showed no facts and stay, and so does a graph with its details under it already. Once it
  has split one, `Config.Migrated` ("migrated") keeps `readingDetails` and it never runs again in that
  file, so a graph set tall later stays one line. A file it found nothing in is not marked (a clean
  file is not written): there, a lone graph set by hand to 9 or 7 fixed rows would get its details
  once.

Tests: `PerformancePresetTests`, `LineMigrationsTests`, `ListGutterTests`. Sheet
`performance-preset-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: open each reading's preset; an existing tall reading
folder should look as it did, now two lines.

## 112. Families in the add list (2026-10-11)

*Gone the same day: the add list is a tree of subjects (§136), whose folders are what the families
were, and more. The toggles family is its Quick settings.*

The person: *"i really like how you grouped the actions together so that they dont all appear
individually in the selector, can you do the same with other widgets where it makes sense too? (for
example for all the toggles)"*.

`WidgetFamilies` (Karpo.Core\WidgetFamilies.cs): a name, a glyph and members. `Catalogue.Offered` puts a
family's members together, in its order, where its first member on the page stands, in that member's
group (`CatalogueEntry.Family`); `AddList.Rows` shows them as one row opening a submenu, as a widget's
premade widgets are (§85). The row carries its first member's command but is never picked itself. A
family with one member on a page is that member's own row. The search finds a member by its own words
and lights the family's row; Enter adds it where it is the one match.

| Family | Members | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Toggles | the row of toggles, a line, then each widget a click flips where it stands (§117): Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode, energy saver, night light, rotation lock, do not disturb, sound, microphone, spatial sound, mono audio, color filters, game mode | Network (on the bar, from Wi-Fi) |
| Power buttons | sleep, hibernate, shut down, restart, sign out, lock | System |
| Processor, Graphics, Memory, Disk, Network activity | the reading's graph, its details | Performance |
| Calendar views | day, week, year | Calendar |
| Sound | volume, output, microphone, mixer | Sound and media |
| Windows | Start, search, Task view, Widgets, desktops, open apps, tray, status icons, input indicator, pen menu, touch keyboard, touchpad, nearby sharing, cast, projection, Snipping Tool, Settings, show desktop | Taskbar |

Windows (2026-10-11: *"make a windows group (the taskbar group actually) in the add widgets where you
put all the windows specific stuff like desktop, sharing"*) is Windows' own shell, in the order its
taskbar shows it; on the bar's page the Taskbar group is then that row, the layout switcher and the
separator (what Karpo adds). Called "Windows", not "Taskbar", which the page and the group already
are. Not the switches (Toggles has them), nor the connections, sound and battery, whose groups are
their own. Nearby sharing, cast and projection are lines on the folder page only; there the row is
Task view and those three.

Project is not a toggle (it opens something) and stays a row of its own; Cast is a preset (§114). The catalogue's
cap of twelve rows a group counts a family as one row (`CataloguePagesTests`).

## 113. An actions slot is searched, in Settings' sections (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the actions in the action widget should be searchable and shown as subsections"*.

An actions line's two slots in Settings were combo boxes of every action in one list. Each is an
`ActionPicker` (Karpo.Settings\Controls\ActionPicker.cs): a button with the action's glyph and name (or
"None"), whose flyout is a search box over the actions under their sections of Windows' Settings, in
Settings' order and words — System, Bluetooth & devices, Network & internet, Personalization, Apps,
Time & language, Accessibility, Privacy & security, Windows Update (`ActionSection`,
`SettingsActions.SectionOf`, `core.actionSection.*`). Typing narrows them by name, English name or
section name (`SettingsActions.Search`); a section with nothing found goes; Enter picks the one found;
the chosen one is on the accent. The calendar app is under Apps and Task Manager under System. Tests:
`ActionSectionsTests`. By hand: an actions line's page in Settings, type "blue", pick Add device.

## 114. Cast is a preset, its panel and Win+P's modes lines (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the cast icon opens the windows cast flyout, is it hard to implement everything from cast
properly or why dont we implement it so that it looks and behaves the same everywhere?"* and *"all the
remaining flyouts should become folders with a face now."* §104 had made the cast button press Win+K;
it is a folder now, as every other flyout's button became one.

- **The preset** (`Presets.CastId` "castGroup", "Cast"): a list folder wearing the **cast face**, holding
  Windows' Cast panel as a line (`wirelessDisplays`, `ListKind.WirelessDisplays`,
  `WidgetInfos.WirelessDisplays` "Wireless displays"), Win+P's modes as a line (`projection`,
  `ListKind.Projection`, `WidgetInfos.Projection` "Projection mode") and, in the same card, the cast
  actions (`PremadeWidgets.CastActions`, new): Display | Add device (the panel's "Find other devices").
  It is in the add list's ready-made groups.
- **The panel's line** (`CastPage`, the page §104 removed, back as a line of `QuickPageTile`,
  `QuickKind.Cast`): "Cast", the Miracast receivers in range as Windows finds them (`WindowsCast`, a
  `DeviceWatcher` on the Miracast half of `ProjectionManager.GetDeviceSelector()`), the one this PC shows
  on first, marked "Connected" and selected (read where Windows keeps it: an active Miracast path,
  `QueryDisplayConfig`); "Looking for wireless displays…" while the first pass runs; "No wireless
  displays found" after it; the line saying Windows connects and disconnects in its own panel; and
  "Open Cast". A display's row and "Open Cast" press Win+K (Windows' panel takes the focus and the
  folder goes).
- **Win+P's line** (`ProjectPage`, the project button's flyout, hosted by `QuickPageTile` as
  `QuickKind.Projection`; its footer is dropped in a line): PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend, Second
  screen only, the one in force marked, a click putting another in force through `SetDisplayConfig`
  exactly as Win+P does (`WindowsProjection`), the line saying so where only one screen is attached.
  The project button and its flyout are unchanged by this.
- **What is native and what is Windows'.** Listing the receivers, knowing which one is cast to, and the
  projection mode are Karpo's own. **Connecting and disconnecting are not, and cannot be**: the one
  connecting call Windows publishes (`ProjectionManager.StartProjectingAsync`) projects one of a
  packaged app's own `CoreWindow` views, never the desktop; `Windows.Media.Casting` casts a media
  element's stream; `Windows.Media.Miracast` is the receiving end (this PC as a display);
  `Windows.Devices.Display.Core` drives displays already attached; `WiFiDirectDevice` makes the radio
  link only, without the Miracast session and display path Windows' Connect broker sets up; and there
  is no public call to disconnect at all. So the rows hand that one step to Windows' own Cast panel,
  and say so.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Cast` "cast", `CastFaceDrawing`): Windows' cast glyph (EC15) drawn as the
  status faces are, and while this PC is cast to a display an accent dot on its bottom corner. Never
  dimmed: casting is not a switch that is off. One square. Its tooltip: "Cast" and "Casting to Living
  Room TV" or "Not casting to a display". It reads a source of its own (`FolderIsland.Cast`,
  `QuickSources.Cast(false)`) that looks for no receivers — a radio scan for as long as the bar runs
  would be a cost for a dot — and reads which display is cast to on its own 10 s tick, off the dock's
  thread (Windows tells a desktop app nothing when a Miracast session starts or ends). Painted again in
  place. Its right click is its first line's: the display settings.
- **What went, and the file.** `BarKind.Cast`, its entry, `WidgetInfos.Cast`, `QuickSwitch.Cast` and its
  Win+K switch, `core.widget.cast.*`, `dock.quick.switch.castNote`. **No reset**: a bar's `"cast"` entry
  in a file reads as the cast preset's folder in its place — its id, section and row — and nothing else
  in the file changes (`ConfigWords.CastNearbyFolders`, on the file's text before it is parsed, as the
  Phone Link pins were); the file is written back once. Config shape unchanged.

Tests: `CastNearbyPresetTests` (the preset, the button gone, the file's button as the folder where it
stood with everything else intact, the panel's line listing, marking and opening Windows' panel, Win+P's
line choosing, the face's dot and hover, the face's own source asking for no scan and ticking, the
pictures), `DisplayFlyoutsTests` (sources), `FolderClickRuleTests`, `SwitchWidgetTests`,
`SectionsTests`. Pictures: `cast-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `cast-nearby-faces-<dark|light>.png`. By hand:
add the Cast preset; with a Miracast TV or adapter on, see it listed; click it — Windows' Cast panel opens
— connect there; within ten seconds the face has its dot and the line marks the display "Connected";
choose Extend and Duplicate on the projection line; disconnect in Windows' panel and watch the dot go.

## 115. Nearby sharing is a preset, its own line, and a real switch (2026-10-11)

The person: *"sharing widget just opens the sharing settings, is it possible to actually make a proper
flyout out of this?"* Yes: what Settings > System > Nearby sharing holds is readable, and settable the
way Windows' own tile sets it.

- **Where Windows keeps it** (read on this PC, 26300, and named in Settings' handler,
  SettingsHandlers_SharedExperiences_Rome.dll): `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CDP`
  `NearShareChannelUserAuthzPolicy` (0 off, 1 my devices only, 2 everyone nearby) and
  `NearShareFileSaveLocation` (none: Downloads); `...\CDP\SettingsPage` `NearShareChannelUserAuthzPolicy`,
  the mode last on, which turning it on brings back. The key is watched (`RegistryWatch`); Windows tells
  no app otherwise. The quick action's Settings handler
  (`SystemSettings_SharedExperiences_NearShareQuickAction`) read as a switch holding a boolean that
  matched (`SettingHandler.NearbySharing`).
- **Setting it** (`WindowsNearby.Set`, `NearbyModes.Plan`, off the dock's thread): off, and on from off,
  go through that handler, as Windows' tile does — it is also what turns Bluetooth on for nearby sharing,
  with Windows' own toast; the mode is the remembered value, written before the handler turns it on,
  and the policy itself when it changes while on or where the handler is not there. A change that could
  not be written says "Windows didn't change nearby sharing." Not exercised by any test (no test may
  change the person's setting): **checked by hand only**.
- **The preset** (`Presets.NearbyId` "nearbyGroup", "Nearby sharing"): a list folder wearing the
  **nearby sharing face**, holding the line (`nearbySharing`, `ListKind.NearbySharing`,
  `WidgetInfos.NearbySharing` "Nearby sharing details") and, in the same card, the nearby actions
  (`PremadeWidgets.NearbyActions`, new: "Nearby sharing" alone on the right, `ms-settings:crossdevice`,
  a new action, `SettingsActions.NearbySharingId`).
- **The line** (`NearbyPage`, `QuickKind.Nearby`): "Nearby sharing" and what it is (Bluetooth and
  Wi-Fi); Off, My devices only and Everyone nearby, each with who it lets share, the one in force
  selected, a click marking the one asked for at once; "Save files I receive to", the folder and
  **Change**, which asks in Windows' folder dialog (`FolderDialog`, `FOS_PICKFOLDERS`, on an STA thread of
  its own, owned by nothing, as the folder goes when it takes the focus) and writes the location;
  "Discoverable as" and this PC's name.
- **The switch line** (`nearbyShare`, Connectivity's) is a real switch now (`NearbySwitch`): off, or on
  in the mode last on, as Windows' tile; while on it says who may share; before Windows has said it
  shows no state and a click opens its settings, as before.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Nearby` "nearbySharing", `NearbyFaceDrawing`): the share glyph (E72D),
  dimmed while off and while unread. Tooltip "Nearby sharing: off", or "Nearby sharing: on" and who may
  share. Its own source (`FolderIsland.Nearby`), the key's watch its only news, no tick.
- **Not done: "Share a file".** Windows' share sheet for a picked file needs `DataTransferManager`
  through `IDataTransferManagerInterop` and a `DataPackage` holding a `StorageFile` list, which is a
  managed collection crossing to WinRT — what the AOT build cannot do (Bluetooth.cs) — so it was left
  out rather than shipped untested. Explorer's own Share on a file is that sheet.
- **What went, and the file.** `BarKind.NearbyShare` and its entry. A bar's `"nearbyShare"` entry reads as
  the preset's folder in its place (`ConfigWords.CastNearbyFolders`); a folder's `"nearbyShare"` line is
  left as it is. No reset, no shape change.

Tests: `CastNearbyPresetTests` (the policy's values, the change's plan, the line's modes, Change and the
name, the switch's off and back on, the face's dim and hover, the face following its source in place,
the file's button), `DisplayFlyoutsTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`, `SwitchWidgetTests`. Pictures:
`nearby-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `cast-nearby-faces-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: add the Nearby sharing
preset; it marks what Settings shows; choose Everyone nearby and see Settings follow (and the face light);
choose Off and on again from Connectivity's switch; with Bluetooth off, turn it on and see Windows turn
Bluetooth on; Change the folder and send a file from a phone; check it lands there.

## 116. The desktop switcher is a preset; desktops are reordered by a drag (2026-10-11)

The person: *"reordering desktops should be with drag and drop, not with the up and down buttons,
there should be proper drag handles to indicate drag and drop reordering"* and *"the desktop switcher
should be made into a folder with face and widgets inside"*. The desktop switcher entry and its flyout
(the desktops' `SwitcherPage`, a row's right click Move up / Move down / Rename / Delete) went; what a
click on it gave is a ready-made folder under a face of the switcher it was. The layout switcher stays
a taskbar entry with its own list.

- **The preset** (`Presets.DesktopsId` "Virtual desktops", `desktopsGroup`, after the power button
  with the start's groups): the desktops' line, Automatic up to the most a line may be, and the premade
  **desktop actions** (`PremadeWidgets.DesktopActions`, new) in its card: Multitasking
  (`ms-settings:multitasking`, new action) on the left, **Task view** on the right — a new action that is
  no page or program but Win+Tab, as the taskbar's button presses it (`SettingsActions.TaskViewId`,
  `ActionsTile.Open`). A new bar never had the switcher, so it is in the add list's groups and in "All
  ready-made folders" with the start's (`PresetLayout.SectionOf`).
- **The line** (`ListKind.Desktops`, "desktops", `WidgetInfos.Desktops`, `DesktopsLine`; it takes the
  entry's info, id and option, `DesktopOptions.ShowApps`, whose Settings card is the line's now;
  `CellAct.Action`, `Interaction.Click | Drag`; item sizes only, `ItemStyles`):
  - *A row per desktop* in Windows' order: the **gripper** in the list's leading column — six dots, two
    by three, as Windows' reorderable lists and Settings' bar menu list draw it, at the display's scale
    whatever the text size — the name (Windows' "Desktop 3" where none was given), the one you are on
    marked as WinUI marks a list's chosen item (the subtle fill, the accent pill, the name semibold),
    and the apps open on it at its end, "+N" for the rest. Under the pointer or the keys a row lights
    and shows its **pencil** and its **cross** where its apps stood. "New desktop" at the foot.
  - *A click switches*: the folder's act, which closes it **without handing the focus back** (the window
    in front before it opened is on the desktop being left: activated as the switch goes it would
    switch Windows straight back) — `IslandView.Desktops`, `FolderFlyout.Hide(restore: false)` — and the
    dock switches (`DesktopsLine.TakeSwitch`, `Dock.SwitchDesktop`), as the switcher's row did.
  - *The pencil* (or F2) renames in place: a text box on the row (`InlineEditor`) with the name chosen;
    Enter or a press elsewhere keeps it (Task View's rule), Escape does not. *The cross* (or Delete)
    closes the desktop, its windows going to its neighbour. *"New desktop"* makes one at the end
    through the shell's `CreateDesktop` (`DesktopControl.Create`, slot 11 of the table already checked),
    which leaves you where you are; without it, Ctrl+Win+D. Each acts in place; the folder stays.
  - *What cannot be done* is dimmed and says why in its tooltip (`Switchers.ActionsFor`, now
    `CanMove`/`WhyNotMove` in place of the two moves): no shell, nothing renamed or moved and only the
    current desktop closed; one desktop, nothing closed or moved.
- **Reordering is a drag.** The pointer over a gripper is the move cursor (`CellIsland.GripOn`,
  `IDC_SIZEALL`); a press on it is the line's, and past the drag threshold the row **lifts** — a raised
  plate (the solid control fill, its rim, a soft shadow) that follows the pointer, held between the first
  and last slot — while the rows it passes **slide** out of its way, each eased to its new place in a
  fifth of a second (`DesktopsLine.Tween`, `Ms`), drawn on the folder's quick tick at a display's pace
  while anything slides (`CellIsland.Animating`, `FolderFlyout.ArmQuick`, `SlideMs`). Let go, the desktop
  is moved to the nearest slot through the shell's `MoveDesktop` (`IDesktops.Move`), once, and the row
  settles into it from where it was let go; until Windows has written the new order down the line shows
  the one it asked for (`pending`, two seconds at most), so nothing jumps back. **Escape** while a row is
  lifted puts it back (`CellIsland.EscapeOn`, before the folder's own Escape) and the folder stays.
  **Alt+Up / Alt+Down** on the row the keys are on move it a place, sliding the same way; they come as
  system keys, which the folder now hands the line with the focus (`WM_SYSKEYDOWN` — before, no line
  heard them, the to-do's Alt+Up/Down included). Up and Down walk the rows and the foot, Enter switches.
  There is no reorder in Settings: the desktops are Windows', not Karpo's config.
- **Reading.** The line reads and acts through `DesktopState.Service` (`IDesktops`), which is the dock's
  (`Dock.DesktopsService`: the apps on the display the open folder stands on, each change read back at
  once), or a test's (`DesktopsLine.Stand`). What it read is kept until the dock says the desktops
  changed (`IDesktops.Changed`, from `RefreshSwitcher`) or the folder opens again — the shell is not
  asked whether its calls can be made on every layout pass.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Desktops`, `desktops`, not `Named`, no options; `DesktopsFaceDrawing`): the
  switcher's button — its glyph and the desktop's name in the room of "Desktop 88" whatever the name
  is (`Switchers.NameRoom`), so switching never moves the bar; the glyph alone down a bar on its side.
  Its tooltip is the switcher's (the whole name and "Desktop 2 of 3"); its right click the switcher's
  own: New desktop, Rename this desktop (the rename page at the face), Delete this desktop, Task view.
- **What went.** `BarKind.Desktops`, its entry, `Switcher.Desktops`, `QuickKind.Desktops`, the
  switcher list's "New desktop" footer and row menus (`SwitchSource.Add`/`RowMenu`, `IQuickHost.Menu`,
  `QuickFlyoutAction.Menu`, `QuickChoice.Add`), the Move up / Move down commands and their words, the
  rename's way back to the list. **No reset**: a file that still has the switcher on a bar gets the
  preset's folder in its place (`ConfigWords.DesktopsFolders`) — the same id, section and row, its
  `showApps` carried to the line — and everything else in it reads as it did.

**Matched against the flyout's own pictures** (`quick-desktops-*.png`, rendered before it went). The
same: the rows' names, the chosen one's fill and pill, the apps and "+N", "New desktop", the switch on
a click. **Different, and why:** the gripper in the leading column where the switch glyph stood (it
says the row can be carried); rename and close are the row's own buttons, not a right click's menu; no
"Desktops" title (folders have none); the footer is Multitasking | Task view.

Tests: `DesktopsPresetTests` (the preset and the face; the switcher gone and the line's act; rows and
the foot; a click switches once the folder has gone; rename, Escape, a press elsewhere, close, new;
without the shell; a drag lifted, slid, dropped and shown before Windows writes it; Escape; back to its
own slot; `DropIndex`, `Shift`, `Reordered`; the keys; in a real folder window: the quick tick, Escape
keeping the folder, the drop, Alt+Down as a system key, a click closing it with the switch; the face's
fixed room; pictures), `DesktopSwitcherMigrationTests` (the person's file with a switcher: the folder in
its place, the rest word for word, written back once; several bars), `SwitcherTests`,
`DesktopSwitchTests`, `FolderClickRuleTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`, `FolderRowsTests`,
`PremadeWidgetsTests`, `TogglesAndActionsTests`, `ListGutterTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`,
`InteractionTests`, `PersonsPresetsTests` (newer presets apart). Tests that stood the switcher on a bar
as any automatic widget stand the layout switcher there. Pictures: `desktops-preset-<dark|light>.png`
(150 %: at rest, a row lit, the keys, a row lifted, renaming, no shell, held short, 225 % text),
`desktops-face-<dark|light>.png`, `quick-layouts-*.png`. By hand: add the Virtual desktops preset;
drag a desktop by its gripper (the move cursor, the rows sliding, Task View showing the new order),
Escape mid-drag; Alt+Down; rename with the pencil; New desktop (stays where you are); the cross; click
a desktop (the switch, and the window there in front); the face's right click; Task view and
Multitasking in the footer.

## 117. The toggles are toggles: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound and microphone, and spatial sound (2026-10-11)

The person: *"some of the toggles you put into toggles are not actually toggles. the ones in the
toggles group should only be the ones that you can click and click again to untoggle, directly on the
taskbar without opening a flyout or folder or anything."* — *"wifi on / off should also get an own
toggle widget, same for bluetooth, same for sound where you can mute / unmute, same for microphone."* —
*"if it makes sense try to remove the spacial sound flyout and just make the spacial sound widget into
a toggle, you can also, if needed, configure this further in the settings."*

- **What a toggle is** is a fact of the widget, `WidgetInfo.Flips`: a click flips what it stands for on
  or off where it stands — a taskbar entry whose click is `BarClick.Action` (no flyout, no panel, no
  folder) with the tooltip that says where it stands, and a folder's line whose click acts — and its
  glyph shows which (lit on the accent while on). The toggles family (§112) is the row of toggles and
  then exactly those (`WidgetFamilies.Toggles`; since §136 the add tree's Quick settings,
  `AddTree.QuickSettings`), and `QuickSettingsFolderTests` holds the two together: a
  widget that flips cannot be left out, and one that opens something cannot join.
- **Audit** of the family §112 made:

  | Widget | On the bar | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | airplane mode, energy saver, night light, rotation lock, do not disturb | a click flips it | stays |
  | spatial sound | listed its formats | a toggle now (below), stays |
  | VPN | lists the connections (a flyout) | out: Network |
  | live captions | presses Win+Ctrl+L, no state | out: System |
  | accessibility | opens its settings page | out: System |
  | mobile hotspot's switch | no bar entry: on the bar it is its preset, a folder (§93) | out: Network (a line) |
  | nearby sharing's switch | no bar entry: on the bar it is its preset, a folder (§115) | out: Network (a line) |

  The order: the row of toggles, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode, energy saver, night light, rotation
  lock, do not disturb, sound, microphone, spatial sound. On the bar the family stands in Network, from
  Wi-Fi.
- **Four new toggles**, each a taskbar entry and a line (`SwitchIsland`, the one-button widgets' drawing
  and line), tooltip "Wi-Fi: on":
  - **Wi-Fi on/off** (`wifiSwitch`, `QuickSwitch.WifiRadio`) and **Bluetooth on/off**
    (`bluetoothSwitch`, `QuickSwitch.BluetoothRadio`): the radio through Windows.Devices.Radios, as the
    Wi-Fi and Bluetooth lines switch it (`RadioToggle` over `RadioSwitch`, already in the AOT build),
    its `StateChanged` followed, so a radio switched in Windows' panel shows at once. A refusal says
    "Windows didn't let Karpo switch it." in the tooltip; the next click asks again. No radio: drawn as
    a command that cannot be used.
  - **Sound on/off** (`soundSwitch`, `QuickSwitch.Sound`) and **Microphone on/off**
    (`microphoneSwitch`, `QuickSwitch.Microphone`): the default output's and the default microphone's
    mute (`MuteSwitch` over `VolumeWatch`, which now takes the endpoint's flow), the endpoint's callback
    and the enumerator's followed, so the keyboard's mute key or a call app's mute shows at once and a
    new default endpoint is followed. On is heard: lit while unmuted, and the glyph struck through
    while muted (`IQuickSwitch.Glyph`: E74F, EC54), on the bar, as a line and in a row of toggles.
  - The row of toggles holds them too (`Toggle.Sound`, `Toggle.Microphone`, new; `Toggle.Wifi` and
    `Toggle.Bluetooth` are the new widgets' switches now, so a row and a widget read one source,
    `SwitchData` "switch:WifiRadio"), named "Wi-Fi", "Bluetooth", "Sound", "Microphone".
- **"on/off" in the add list alone** (2026-10-11: "the airplane mode is also an airplane mode on / off
  switch, so it should be properly named. all the toggle switches should be named the same in that
  regard" — "dont actually change the text of the widget to Microphone on/off, it should just show up
  like that in the add widgets lists"). Every toggle (`Flips`) is "`<title> on/off`" in the add
  list's rows and its search results (`WidgetInfo.AddTitle`, one pattern per language,
  `core.addTree.onOff`: "{name} on/off", "ein/aus", "activé/désactivé", "activado/desactivado", "开/关");
  its line, its tooltip, its page and edit mode say its title, the thing's name ("Microphone"). The
  search finds either, and the English add-list name in another language. `AddListToggleNamesTests`.
  The Bluetooth devices' list widget, which was "Bluetooth" too, is "Bluetooth devices", so no two
  widgets share a name (`WiredTests.NoTwoWidgetsShareAName`).
- **Spatial sound is a toggle.** Its list of formats went (`IQuickSwitch.Choices`, `SpatialFormats.List`
  and their words); `BarClick.Action`, with its tooltip ("Spatial sound: on" and the format). A click
  turns it off, or on in the format its Settings card names where the output offers it, else the one
  last used here, else the first offered — Windows Sonic (`SpatialFormats.Next`, `IQuickSwitch.Act(options)`).
  The card, **When on** (`SwitchOptions.SpatialFormat`, null for "The one last used"): the formats
  Windows knows by name (`SpatialSoundFormats.Known`: Windows Sonic for Headphones, Dolby Atmos for
  Headphones and for Speakers, DTS Headphone:X, DTS:X Ultra, their GUIDs as an output's list writes them,
  read on 25H2). A format that is not a GUID, or on another switch, is dropped (`WidgetItem.Normalize`).
  Where Windows refuses the switch it still says so and opens the sound settings, as before.
- **The file.** Nothing to convert: `"spatialSound"` keeps its word and its options and is a toggle;
  the new words are new kinds. No reset, no shape change (`TogglesFamilyTests.SpatialSoundInAFileLoadsAsAToggle`).

Tests: `TogglesFamilyTests`, `MuteSwitchTests`, `SpatialTests` (the card's format first), and the
registries' lists. By hand: click each new toggle on the bar and see Windows' quick settings follow;
mute with the keyboard's key and see the sound toggle strike through; switch Wi-Fi off in Windows' panel
and see the toggle go out; spatial sound with a headset: click on (Windows Sonic), off, and with
"When on" set to an installed Dolby Atmos, on again in that one.

### Game mode, color filters and mono audio (2026-10-11)

Three more toggles, each a taskbar entry and a line drawn by `SwitchIsland` like the others (glyph lit
while on, tooltip "Game mode: on", hover, followed live), in Quick settings and at home in their subject:
**Game mode**, **Color filters** and **Mono audio** — "… on/off" in the add list alone, as every toggle
(`WidgetInfo.AddTitle`): **Game mode** (`gameMode`, System), **Color filters** (`colorFilters`, Screen) and **Mono
audio on/off** (`monoAudio`, Music and sound). The row of toggles does not offer them yet: fifteen
toggles wrapped at the largest text size are more than the six rows a new line may have
(`FlyoutLinesTests`), so that waits for the row to be reconsidered.

- **Switched as Windows switches them**: through the Settings handler Windows' own switch calls
  (`SettingHandlers.cs`, `SettingToggle` in `SettingToggles.cs`) — color filters' and mono audio's
  quick-settings tiles (`SettingsHandlers_nt.dll` `SystemSettings_Accessibility_ColorFiltering_IsEnabled`,
  `SettingsHandlers_Accessibility.dll` `SystemSettings_Accessibility_IsAudioMonoMixStateEnabled`) and
  game mode's Settings page (`SettingsHandlers_Gaming.dll` `SystemSettings_Gaming_GameMode_Toggle`).
  The registry value alone is not applied live: color filters wait for Win+Ctrl+C (and need
  `HotkeyEnabled`), mono audio for the audio service to be told. The handler applies it and writes the
  value. Each was read, switched once and put back on Windows 11 26300 with a probe; all three
  handlers are type 3 (a switch) holding a boolean.
- **Followed where Windows keeps it**, a DWORD under HKCU, watched (`RegistryWatch`): `GameBar`
  `AutoGameModeEnabled` (absent is on, as on this PC), `ColorFiltering` `Active` (the key is not there
  until color filters are used once; its parent is watched for it), `Multimedia\Audio`
  `AccessibilityMonoMixState`. `SettingPlace.State` reads a value (absent is the default, a DWORD is
  on unless 0, anything else unknown).
- **Color filters' filter**: the card **Filter** (`SwitchOptions.ColorFilter`, `ColorFilter`, Windows'
  `FilterType` numbers 0–5, listed in Settings' order; grayscale by default and not written). A click
  that turns them on writes `FilterType` first, then the switch. An unknown word in a file reads as
  grayscale; on another switch it is dropped.
- **Without the handler** (an older Windows): the state still shows, nothing is switched, and a click
  opens the setting's page ("Windows doesn't let Karpo switch this here; a click opens its settings.").
- `SwitchIsland.Click` hands the switch the widget's options again (`IQuickSwitch.Act(options)`): project's preset (96e4ad1)
  rewrote the click and dropped them, so spatial sound's "When on" was ignored.
- Quick settings now has fifteen rows, the one folder past twelve (`AddTreeTests` allows it sixteen),
  in runs between lines: the radios, the sound, the screen, the PC. With color filters in it, Screen
  and sharing ran to thirteen on a folder's page, so nearby sharing is a folder of its own there
  (`nearby`: its preset, its switch, its details, its actions), as Wi-Fi's is in Connections.

Tests: `SettingToggleTests`. By hand: click each on the bar and see Windows' Settings page (Gaming >
Game mode, Accessibility > Color filters, Accessibility > Audio) follow; flip each there and see the
toggle follow; set the filter to another one and click color filters on.

## 118. A folder wears several faces; the time over the date; the clock and the calendar together (2026-10-11)

The person: *"for a folder you should be actually able to give him multiple faces, so that i can also
combine widgets as i want"* and *"create a folder face that combined time and clock together like it
is shown on the windows default taskbar. you should also make a premade group that combines both too."*

- **Several faces** (`FolderOptions.Faces`): a folder's button wears one face or more, side by side in
  their order, each any face with its own options. `FolderOptions.Face` is the first, which is all most
  folders have. On the bar (`FolderIsland.FaceSizes`, `Parts`, `PaintCell`) the faces stand one after
  another with `FolderIsland.Between` between each two — 5 DIP since §506 (it was about two fifths of a
  glyph, 10 DIP on a 48-DIP bar), closer than two buttons stand, so the faces on one button read as one —
  and the room at the ends one face of words has; a square stays a square in the
  middle of the bar, a face of words takes the bar's thickness. Down a bar on its side they stack, top
  to bottom. The button is one block of one cell: a press anywhere on it opens the folder, and its hover
  and press cover all of it. The name stands beside a button's one face only (`NameShown`).
- **Each face keeps reading.** The folder follows what every face needs — the network, Bluetooth and
  the sound for theirs, the weather's place, the stock's share, the hotspot, cast, nearby sharing, the
  mail, the bell, the clipboard, now playing, a drive's line — and a reading's source for each
  performance face (a CPU face beside a memory face holds both; `PerformanceOf`, `SourceKinds.Wanted`).
  Its tick is the quickest of its faces' paces, and a slower face's own reading waits for its pace
  (`PaceDue`). What the button shows is each face's reading in their order (`FaceShown`); a new minute,
  a new day or a face's news paints it in place. Its tooltip is each face's words on a line of its own,
  as Windows' button of the three says each; its right click the rows of its first face that has any
  (`FolderIsland.ActingFace`, `Dock.ActsOnBar`), worked on that face's widget. A now-playing face set
  to leave the bar while nothing plays takes the folder off only where it is all the folder wears.
- **Once or more** (`FaceInfo.Repeats`, `FolderFaces.CanWear`): a clock, a date, the time and date and
  a reading may stand twice — their options make each another (a zone, a disk); every other face shows
  what is the folder's one of a kind (its weather's place, its stock face's share, the Wi-Fi, its first
  drive line) and stands once. At most eight (`FolderFaces.Most`).
- **The file, backward compatible, no reset.** One face is written as it always was, `"face"`, and
  nothing more, so no file of before changes (the person's own file is read and written back with no
  `"faces"`, `FolderFacesTests`). Several are `"faces"`, in order, with the first as `"face"` too, which
  a build of one face wears. Reading, `"faces"` wins wherever it stands; an empty one is not there; nulls
  are left out; past eight the first are kept. The weather's place and the stock's share are their first
  face's wherever it stands (`WeatherPlaces.OfFace`, `StockSymbols`); a file's one-off adoptions read the
  first face, which is all a file of before has.
- **Settings** (`FolderPage`, `FolderRows`): each face is a section of its own — the face's dropdown and,
  while there are several, Remove in its header; its rows in its body, as the one face's section was. The
  sections stand in a list in the faces' order, dragged to reorder (the gripper beside each, as in
  Windows' Preferred languages list) and moved by Alt+Up and Alt+Down; "Add a face" under them, its menu
  greying a face the folder may not wear again (`FolderRows.AddFace`, `RemoveFace`, `Reorder`, `Moved`,
  `Offered`). With one face the page is what it was: one section, headed "Face". There is no face picker
  on the bar's edit mode to change.
- **The time over the date** (`FolderFaces.DateTime` "dateTime", `DateTimeFaceDrawing`): Windows 11's
  clock on the taskbar — two lines at the taskbar's text size, the time over the short date, both in
  the primary ink, right-aligned at the end of the face, the pair in the middle of the bar; the region's
  time and short date (and the formats set in Karpo, as every clock and date). Its one option, "Seconds":
  as Windows' clock shows them (`ShowSecondsInSystemClock`, read once and again on `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`,
  which rebuilds the bar where it changed: `WindowsClock`), always, or never. Measured on the widest time
  of a day and the widest short date of a year. Where the bar is too thin for two lines at any of the
  text's sizes (32 DIP), one line, the time then the date; down a bar on its side the time over the date
  without its year (or the day alone), each as large as the bar's width lets it be. Its tooltip is the
  long date. It repeats.
- **The clock and the calendar together** (`Presets.ClockCalendarId` "clockCalendarGroup", "Clock &
  calendar", the first of the combined groups below): a list folder
  wearing the time over the date. Inside, the person's own two arrangements side by side: the clock's
  list — the time over the long date, the timer, the stopwatch, the focus session, its footer (Date &
  time, Focus) — and the calendar's — the month, that day's events six rows fixed, its footer (Date &
  time, the calendar app). The calendar's date header is left out: the time header says the date. Two
  lists, not one: one would be some 21 rows, taller than a 1080-pixel screen leaves a folder; side by
  side it is as tall as the calendar alone; the timer and the focus session two rows each, the stopwatch
  three, so the clock's list stands about as tall. `PersonsPresetsTests` counts it among the presets made
  since their arrangement.

Tests: `FolderFacesTests` (one face written as before, several in order, every shape a file may hold,
the person's file unchanged, the name, once or more, adding, removing and reordering, the weather's
place wherever it stands, the right click, both readings gathered, the seconds, the preset; the
button's length, a press anywhere, each face reading, the time and date's fit and width),
`FolderRowsTests`, `FolderFaceTests`. Picture: `folder-faces-side-by-side.png`. By hand: give a folder
the weather and the time and date and see both update; give one the network, the sound and the battery
and compare with Windows' own button; drag the faces' sections in Settings, and Alt+Up/Down; switch
"Show seconds in system tray clock" in Windows and see the time and date follow; add "Clock & calendar".

## 119. Item rows edge to edge, a foot that stays, the stock over two rows (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the add task button should be aligned on the bottom of the task widget"*, *"the clipboard
items have a little unnecessary space on the left ... the same space appears on the notifications widget
as well, i dont want this anywhere"*, *"the open xyz in the rss feed list should always be shown and not
scroll with contents"* and *"the stock widget should, if there is enough space, not only be shown on one
line"*.

- **A foot that stays** (`IListScroll.ScrollFoot`, `ListScrolled.Foot`/`End`/`FootBand`). The band at the
  end of a scrolled line's content stays at the line's bottom as the head stays at its top: it is drawn
  and hit-tested in the content scrolled to its end, the items show through the window between head and
  foot, and the scrollbar runs in that window. Used by to-do ("Add a task") and the news ("Open
  news.example.com" and the read's problem). A line that does not scroll is unchanged.
- **"Add a task" on the line's bottom** (`TodoTile.Lay`): in a line taller than its tasks the field
  stands on the foot and the room is between the tasks and it; scrolled, it is the foot.
- **Item rows on the gutter.** The clipboard's items and the notifications' cards began after the list's
  leading column, which stood empty. Their words now start on the gutter, as the mail's and the news'
  do, the trailing buttons end on the trailing gutter, and the row's plate reaches 6 DIP past both
  (`MailIsland.Around`). The clipboard's pin mark moved from the leading column to the row's end, where
  its delete shows under the pointer. A notification with a picture of its own keeps it at the gutter,
  its words where the app's name begins. The audit: the contacts', the removable devices' and the apps
  playing's rows had their glyph or icon on the gutter with the plate flush against it; their plates now
  reach past it like the others'. To-do (its check box), the desktops (the gripper), screen time's apps,
  the sound lists and the events already started on the gutter with something in the column.
- **The stock over two rows** (`StockIsland.Painted`). A line whose height holds two lines of words lays
  them out as two: the symbol with the price and its currency, then the company with the change and its
  range; a third where there is room: "At yesterday's close" while the market is shut, and the holding's
  worth at its end. The chart stays at the foot, no taller than 60 DIP, reaching up behind the words
  (faded) where the line has no room of its own for it. One row is one row, as it was.

Tests: `ListScrollTests.TheFootStaysAtTheBottom`, `ListScrollTests.ItemRowsStandOnTheGutter`,
`NotificationsPresetTests.ACardsWordsStandOnTheGutter`, `NotebookLinesTests.AddATaskStaysOnTheFoot`,
`NewsPresetTests.TheSitesLinkStaysAtTheFoot`. Pictures: `stock-line-widths-100.png` and `-150.png` (the
three widths at one, two, three and six rows), `news-scroll-foot.png`, `list-scroll-*.png`,
`clipboard-preset-*.png`, `notifications-preset-*.png`, `notes-todo-*.png`.

## 120. System's readings say more, a card each; every separator is a "Separator" (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "for the widget that shows the multiple system widgets like cpu, ram etc, add more
details and also make a divider in between in the default layout", and "divider and separator should
both get a common name as they basically do the same thing just in different contexts."

**System** (`Presets.cs`, `systemGroup`). Each reading is three rows (`Presets.SystemRows`), the line's
whole widget: its name, the figure large and beside it the two facts its Task Manager page leads with,
over its graph (`PerformanceIsland.Details`): the processor's base speed and processes (threads where
the speed is not known; the busiest and the usual where neither is), the memory in use of all there is
and what is available, the disk's read and write, the network's down and up, the graphics' busiest and
usual (its dedicated memory is not read, §97). The processor's facts are the machine's figures, read
once a gather and only for a line at that tier. Not the readings' details widgets: the processor's seven
facts alone are taller than the five readings together may be. A divider between each two readings, a
card each, in **two lists side by side** — processor, memory, disk; network, graphics, battery and the
Task Manager footer in the last card. Five cards of three rows over one another are about 680 DIP,
past the 70 % of the work area a folder may stand on a 1440p screen at 150 % (638 DIP), where it would
scroll; two lists are about 370. The battery keeps its two rows, which makes the lists one height, and
its divider goes with it on a PC without one (a divider's `Needs`, `Presets.ItemsOn`). Folders made
before keep what they have.

**One name.** The bar's separator, a folder list's divider and the bar menu's divider are each called
**Separator** wherever anybody sees them — the add list, edit mode, Settings, the bar menu page — in
every language (Trennlinie, Separador, Séparateur, 分隔符), with one glyph (`WidgetInfos.SeparatorGlyph`,
Segoe Fluent Icons' rule, U+E921). "Separator" is Windows' own word for the line between groups of a
menu or a list (`MenuFlyoutSeparator`). Appearance keeps its two groups, "Separators" (the bar's) and
"Separators in folders". The file keeps its words, `separator` and `divider`, so nothing is migrated;
"divider" stays a search word for both.

## 121. Deleting a folder or a column: nothing lost, nothing asked; else Windows' dialog (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "if there is no widget in a folder there should not be a confirmation on delete. the
confirmation should be a system dialog that says that you will loose the widgets inside when you
delete and should show how many widget you loose on the delete button."

- **What counts** (`FolderDeletes`, Karpo.Core): every line of the folder but a divider, a hairline
  with nothing of its own. A heading counts (its words), and so does an actions footer (its buttons).
- **A folder** deleted in edit mode — Delete, a widget menu's "Remove", Delete in an open folder
  with the selection reaching a folder on the bar — goes through `Dock.RemoveSelected`. Where no
  folder among what goes holds a widget, it goes at once. Else the dock asks first
  (`Dock.DeleteQuestionFor` → `FolderDeletes.ForRemoving`): one folder is named, "Delete “Sound”?",
  "The 7 widgets inside it will be removed too."; several are counted, "Delete 3 folders?", "The 5
  widgets inside them will be removed too."
- **A column** (§74's remove button, `Dock.RemoveFolderList`): an empty one goes at once; else
  "Delete this column?", "The 2 widgets in it will be removed too."
- **The dialog** (`TaskDialogs`, Karpo.Dock) is Windows' task dialog, comctl32 v6 as the dock's
  manifest asks for it: the warning icon, "Karpo" in its caption, the question, what is lost, then
  "Delete 7 widgets" and "Cancel" — Cancel the default, as Windows asks of a destructive question;
  Escape and the close button cancel too. The count is plural in every language ("Delete 1 widget",
  "1 Widget löschen", "删除 1 个小组件"). It is modal to the bar (for a column: to the open folder),
  centred on its display; owned by a topmost window it is topmost, raised and given the foreground
  as it shows, so it stands over the bar, the edit dim and an open folder. Edit mode's Escape hook
  leaves it the key (`EscapeIsTheirs`: the dock's own window has the keys). The dock runs on in the
  dialog's loop; after it, nothing goes where edit mode ended under it. Without comctl32 v6 it falls
  back to a plain warning message box, Cancel the default.
- Behind `IDeleteAsk` (`Dock.DeleteAsk`), so a test answers instead of a dialog showing. The settings
  app deletes no folder (widgets are added and removed on the taskbar), so it asks nothing.
- Tests: `FolderDeleteTests` (the count, nothing asked where nothing is lost, the words, the button
  in five languages), `TaskDialogsTests` (the real dialog on a hidden desktop: owned by a topmost bar,
  topmost itself, the delete button true and Cancel false). Picture: `folder-delete-dialog.png`. By
  hand: delete an empty folder (no question) and one with widgets (the dialog over the bar, Enter
  cancels); a column with and without widgets; Escape in the dialog cancels it and stays in edit mode.

## 122. The drive line is its information; its contents are a folder pin. The person's own media, Watchlist, stock and power presets (2026-10-11)

"the drive widget should get split in two, right now it shows drive information and (optionally)
folder contents, but it should only show the drive information and then the drive contents should
just be shown by the normal folder widget inline." And: "update the second layout, i did some
changes, take mine in the: now playing widget, stocks widget, stock widget, power options widget."

- **The drive line** (`DriveIsland`) is the drive's information alone at every height: its tiers, or
  the flyout's header with the kind, the file system and the BitLocker state (read off the dock's
  thread while the open folder shows the line, now whatever height draws the header). It lists
  nothing; a click opens the drive in File Explorer. `DriveTargetOptions.Contents` and its Settings
  switch "Show its contents" went (the flag is still read, to be carried over); `PinContents` lost
  its headless mode.
- **The contents** are the folder pin's (§9, `PinTile`, `PinFolderShow.Contents`), a line of its own
  under the drive's, pointed at the drive's root (`DriveTargets.ContentsFolder`: "C:\" by the letter,
  a share's or a letterless volume's durable name otherwise). One way to show a folder, as the person
  asked before (2026-10-04). What §99 weighed against it — a pin does not follow the drive's letter —
  is the price: a stick that comes back at another letter keeps its pin at the old one until it is
  pointed again.
- **A pin on a network** (a UNC path, or a path on a mapped drive, `PinFolders.OnNetwork`, the
  redirector asked and never the share) set to show its contents is taken as a folder without asking
  the share on the dock's thread, is never watched, and is read only while the open folder shows it,
  again on the minute — what the drive line did for a share.
- **The presets** (`Presets.DriveId`, `NetworkDriveId`): the drive's line at its own height, then a
  folder pin showing its contents (`PresetItem.DriveContents`), automatic up to the rest of the
  person's height — ten rows for the drive and twelve for the share, less the drive line's three
  (`LineMigrations.DriveRows`). The preset starts with no drive; the drive chosen on the line in the
  settings page the add opens ("--setup volume") is given once to the folder's pins showing their
  contents with no folder yet (`DriveTargets.SpreadContents`, `SettingsModel.DriveChosen`), as the
  stock preset's first symbol is given to its face (§98). Storage is unchanged: its lines never listed.
- **Carried over in place** (`LineMigrations.SplitDriveContents`, no reset): a drive or network drive
  line with "contents" on becomes the line, keeping its id, its drive and its place, and under it the
  folder pin to its root; the flag is turned off, so it never runs twice. The height it had is shared
  (`SplitHeight`): fixed N, the line three rows (fewer where N is small) and the pin the rest;
  automatic up to N, the line where its kind starts (its header decides) and the pin automatic up to
  N − 3; each at least one row. The person's "All ready-made folders" is carried over this way and is
  then exactly what the presets make.
- **The person's folders** (their config of 2026-10-11, `PersonsLayouts.json`): Media is the now-playing
  line alone, four rows fixed (the apps-playing list, the divider and the volume went); the Watchlist's
  four shares three rows fixed each (`Presets.WatchlistRows`), wide; the stock one line six rows fixed
  with no symbol (unchanged); Power sign out, lock, sleep, restart, shut down — sleep only where
  Windows offers it, hibernate not at all. `PersonsPresetsTests` compares every preset again, none left
  out. The media and power blurbs and the media's search words follow.

Tests: `DrivePresetTests` (the presets, the spread, the drive line its information and the pin
listing the root, the line opening the drive, a share never watched and read only while shown, what
is on a network; pictures), `LineMigrationsTests.ADriveLineListingItsDriveBecomesTheLineAndAFolderPin`
and `TheHeightIsShared`, `PersonsPresetsTests`, `PresetsTests`, `MediaPresetTests`,
`BatteryPowerPresetTests`. Pictures: `drive-preset-<dark|light>.png`, `drive-preset-share-dark.png`,
`power-preset-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: open the Drive and Network drive folders after the update —
the line, then the folder; add a Drive preset and pick a drive, then see the folder follow; pull a
share's cable and open its folder (no hang, "This folder isn't there").

## 123. A folder named on hover; a removed folder's lists close; a thin bar is flush (2026-10-11) — flush only where the layout's Spacing is None, at any height, since §533 (2026-11-07)

The person: "when hovering over a folder / widget there should be a tooltip of the folder name if
applicable and if possible", "when deleting a folder when it is open in edit mode it deletes it but its
contents are still open and still show until i click away", and "when the taskbar shrinks to a small
size the island should basically go away … the edges of the widgets should then also be sharp without
any corner radius".

- **A folder's tooltip** (`FolderIsland.BarTip`, `Dock.TooltipFor`, `IslandTooltips.NamesFor`): its name
  on the first line — the open folder has no title, so nothing else says it — and under it what its
  faces say, each on a line, as Windows' clock says the long date and its network icon the network:
  "Agenda / Saturday, 11 October 2026". A line that only repeats one before it (a clipboard face in a
  folder named "Clipboard history") is left out; the age of data that could not be refreshed comes last
  (StaleMark.cs). No name and no words, no tooltip. The house rule (a widget whose click opens a flyout
  of Karpo's has none) stays for what a flyout says; a name is what none says, so the folder is an
  exception by `NamesFor`, not by flipping `BarEntry.Tooltip`. Same card, delay and look as every bar
  tooltip (`Scene.Tooltip`). (Undone by §367: no folder or widget on the bar has a tooltip.)
- **The room it stands in** (2026-10-11, the person: "when hovering over quick settings the tooltip is
  cutoff at the top"). A bar tooltip is drawn in the bar's own window, in the room the window keeps on
  the bar's inner side, which was three lines; Quick settings' says its name, the network's two lines,
  the volume's and the battery's, ran past the window's edge and was cut off. The room is six lines now
  (`Layout.TooltipLines`), and a tooltip taller than it (`Layout.TooltipMostHeight`: to the window's edge
  less the gap to the bar; beside a vertical bar the window's height) keeps its first lines, as many as
  fit, the last ending in "…" (`IslandTooltips.Fitted`, in `Scene.ShowTip`): never past the window,
  never over the bar. `TooltipRoomTests` (every edge, 100 and 150 %, a 35- and a 48-DIP bar).
- **The other entries named**: the keyboard (its cell abbreviates the language its tooltip writes whole,
  as Windows' input indicator does), VPN and project (a glyph each; their lists name everything but
  themselves). Not the volume and brightness sliders (a card over a control being dragged), the web
  search box (its placeholder says what it is) or the layout switcher (its button is the layout's name).
  None of these where a rest opens the flyout (`Config.HoverFlyouts`): the flyout comes in its place.
- **In an open folder** nothing changes: a line is its name, and a widget of icons names its parts
  (`CellIsland.CardTip`, "Tooltips in a folder").
- **A folder removed while its lists stand open, arranged**: its leaving posts a dismissal
  (`FolderFlyout.FolderChanged`), which edit mode's hold (`FlyoutHost.StaysOpen`) used to turn away, so
  the lists stood until a click elsewhere. A dismissal for a folder that is gone now drops the hold
  first (`FolderFlyout.Message`), whatever removed it — its badge, Delete, the menu's Remove — and the
  dock's close takes the lists cascading out of it along (`Dock.Forget`).
- **Flush** (`Layout.Flush`, `Layout.FlushFor`): an islands bar under `Config.ThinHeight` (36 DIP; of
  the sizes Settings offers, 32 only) keeps no room off the screen's edge — across the bar
  (`CardInsetPx` 0, so the cell is the bar's whole thickness) or at its ends (`EndRoom` 0) — and no
  card, plate, box or ring on it has a corner: the cards (`CardRadius` 0), the plate under the pointer
  and the press (`Scene.Dress`), the keyboard's ring, the focused app's plate, the search box
  (`SearchBoxRadius`), edit mode's blocks and drop marks (`Layout.Corner`), and the widgets' own drawing
  (`IslandStyle.Square`). The cards stay, and the gaps between groups: they keep one widget's edge from
  the next. From 36 DIP up, and on a floating dock, nothing changes. A joined card's pieces now bleed
  past the whole of the outline's stroke (`Scene.PlaceCard`), which with no corner had left a seam.
