Tests: `FolderBarTipTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests.TheEntriesWithoutATooltipThatAreNamedAllTheSame`,
`FolderOffscreenTests.AFolderRemovedWhileArrangedClosesAtOnce`, `BarStyleTests.AThinIslandsBarIsFlush`
(every edge, 100–200 %: the cards edge to edge, the first at the screen's start, the last at its end,
every corner 0) and `FromTheThinHeightUpTheIslandsAreUnchanged`, `SceneTreeTests.AFlushBarsPlatesAreSquare`,
the search box on the 32-DIP bar (`TheSearchBoxHasItsSlotsCorners`, `TheSearchBoxCoversItsSlot`).
Pictures: `bar-height-<28|32|…>-…[-top].png`, `search-box-*-32-*.png`, `search-slot-*-32-*.png`. By
hand: hover a folder, a clock folder, the Wi-Fi preset; delete an open folder in edit mode by its badge,
by Delete and by the menu; set a layout to 32 and to 40 and compare, at the bottom and the top.

## 124. The input indicator is a preset (2026-10-11)

The person: *"all the remaining flyouts should become folders with a face now."* The inventory, of
every taskbar entry whose click still opened a popup of Karpo's own that was not a folder:

| Entry | Its popup | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Input indicator (`keyboard`) | the layouts to switch to | the keyboard preset (this section) |
| VPN | its connections | the VPN preset (§125) |
| Spatial sound | the formats | **no flyout any more**: the person made it a toggle (§117), a click turns it off or on in its chosen format |
| Project | Win+P's four modes | the project preset (§126) |
| Layout switcher | the bar's layouts | the layouts preset (§127) |
| Search the web | its box, its engine, its recent searches | kept at first (*"keep websearch as flyout"*, §102), then **gone**: the person, *"remove the web search widget alltogether"*; its engine is the app's one setting (§28) |
| Desktop switcher | the desktops | the desktops preset (§116) |
| Nearby sharing, Cast | Windows' nearby sharing; Windows' Cast panel | the nearby sharing and cast presets (§114, §115) |
| The tray's "^" | the icons Windows keeps behind it | **kept**: Windows' own overflow, not a widget's flyout — its icons are other programs', each with its own click, right click, hover and drag between the bar and the overflow (§48, §82), which a folder's line has none of |
| The status icons' arrow | the icons behind it | **kept**: the same overflow, of the status icons, each opening Windows' page for it |
| A pin to a folder | its contents, cascading | **kept**: a launcher — File Explorer's folders as menus, as Start's folders are — not a widget's flyout (§70) |
| Start, Search, Task view, the widgets board, the pen menu, the touch keyboard, the touchpad | Windows' own | Windows' panels (`BarClick.Panel`), not Karpo's |
| The open apps | the windows of a group, previews | the taskbar's own app buttons, as Windows has them |

Context menus are not flyouts and stay. The first port, the most used — the indicator is on every
new bar — is the input indicator; the others follow in their own sections.

- **The preset** (`Presets.KeyboardId` "Keyboard layout", `keyboardGroup`): the keyboard's line,
  Automatic (as tall as there are layouts), and in the same card the premade **keyboard actions**
  (`PremadeWidgets.KeyboardActions`, new: Language & region alone on the right, `language`), Windows'
  input switcher's "More keyboard settings". A new bar has it where it had the entry, after the status
  icons (`Sections.DefaultLayout`); the layout of every ready-made folder (`PresetLayout`) puts it
  there too, after the status icons, before now playing.
- **The line** (`ListKind.Keyboard`, "keyboard" — the entry's word and `WidgetInfos.Keyboard`, its
  flyout heights gone; `QuickPageTile` hosting `KeyboardPage`, `QuickKind.Keyboard`): a row per layout
  installed, in Windows' order, as the flyout had them and Windows' switcher has them: the language's
  name over the indicator's codes and the layout's keyboard ("English (United States)" over "ENG US ·
  US keyboard"), each with the keyboard glyph; the one in use marked as a quick-settings list marks
  its chosen row (the fill and the accent pill) and in semibold. As tall as its rows, no title (the
  switcher has none).
  - *Which window.* A layout belongs to a thread. The one in use and the one a pick switches is the
    window the folder opened over: the window in front as the page starts — the folder has not taken
    the keys yet then — or, where that is Karpo's own, the last window in front that was not
    (`KeyboardIsland.Front`, kept by the indicator as it reads). The source (`IKeyboardSource`,
    `WindowsKeyboard`; `SampleKeyboard` for pictures and tests, through `QuickSources.Keyboard`) reads
    the layouts as the folder opens.
  - *A pick* posts `WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST` to that window and gives it the keys back, and the
    folder closes (`IQuickHost.Close`, which in a line now closes the folder as it closes a flyout,
    Windows' own cancel posted), as a pick in Windows' switcher closes it. The keys walk the rows and
    Enter picks, as in every page line.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Keyboard`, `keyboard`, not `Named`, no options; `KeyboardFaceDrawing`):
  the indicator itself — the folder holds a `KeyboardIsland` of its own (`FolderIsland.Keyboard`),
  which the dock tells when another window comes to the front or a layout changes (`Dock.Keyboards`),
  and which paints into the face's box (`KeyboardIsland.PaintFace`): the language over the region
  where two lines fit, the language alone where not, at the bar's text size. Its length is the entry's
  exactly — the widest code of this PC's layouts and a text's ends, never under a square across a
  bar — less the ends the folder puts around a face, so a bar is as long as it was
  (`KeyboardSquareTests` holds it on the folder). Painted again in place when the codes change; its
  tooltip is the entry's, the language and the keyboard.
- **A file keeps its indicator.** No reset: the entry in a file of today's shape becomes the preset's
  folder where it stood, with its id, section and row (`ConfigWords.FlyoutFolders`, run where the file
  is parsed, the file written back once); a line with the word in a folder is a line and is left
  alone. The other ports add their words to the same table (`ConfigWords.FlyoutWords`).
- **What went.** `BarKind.Keyboard` and its entry, `WidgetSource.Keyboard` and its shape
  (`WidgetShapes.Keyboard`, now the face's measure), the island's click and its list
  (`KeyboardIsland.Click`/`Invoke`), the flyout's title string, the flyout look's arm for it. Tests that
  stood the entry on a bar as any widget of the end stand night light there.

Tests: `KeyboardPresetTests` (the preset, its footer and face; the entry gone and its word the line;
the rows, the one in use marked; a click and the keys switch through the source; as tall as its
layouts; the face is the indicator, paints again as the codes change, lets go with another face;
pictures), `FlyoutFoldersTests` (a file with the entry keeps everything; a line with the word stays a
line), `KeyboardSquareTests` and `KeyboardIslandTests` (the face's size and lines), `DefaultBarTests`,
`SectionsTests`. Pictures: `keyboard-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 % text),
`keyboard-face-<dark|light>.png`, `keyboard-square-*.png`. By hand: with two layouts installed, open
the indicator over a text editor, pick the other — the folder goes and the editor types in it, the
face shows it; Win+Space — the face follows; Language & region in the footer.

## 125. VPN is a preset, and flyout heights are gone (2026-10-11)

The second of §124's ports: the VPN entry and its list of connections went; what a click on it gave
is a ready-made folder under a face of the shield it was.

- **The preset** (`Presets.VpnId` "VPN", `vpnGroup`): the connections' line, as tall as there are
  connections, and in the same card the premade **VPN actions** (`PremadeWidgets.VpnActions`, new:
  "VPN" — Windows' VPN settings, the flyout's "VPN settings" — and Network & internet, as the hotspot's
  footer). A new bar never had the entry; it is in the add list's groups, and the layout of every
  ready-made folder puts it after the contacts in the end.
- **The line** (`ListKind.VpnConnections`, `vpnConnections`, `WidgetInfos.VpnConnections` "VPN
  connections"; `QuickPageTile` hosting `ChoicesPage`, `QuickKind.Vpn`): "VPN" over a row per connection,
  as Windows' VPN page has them, by name, its shield before it, where it stands under it ("Connected",
  "Connecting…", "Can't connect: …"), the ones up marked as a quick-settings list marks its chosen row.
  One connection is a row too (the bar's click used to switch it at once, Windows' split toggle); with
  none, a quiet row that says so. A click connects or disconnects that connection through the VPN switch
  (`VpnSwitch.Choose`, RAS on the pool) and the folder stays, so "Connecting…" and then "Connected" are
  seen. `ChoicesPage` is any switch's own list (`IQuickSwitch.Choices`) under the switch's name, made
  and let go with the folder; the trailing "VPN settings" row went from the list, which the footer is.
- **The switch stays a line.** `ListKind.Vpn` (`vpn`, `SwitchIsland`) is unchanged — Connectivity and
  the toggles row hold it — and its click connects the last one used or disconnects what is up.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Vpn`, `vpn`, not `Named`, no options; `SwitchFaceDrawing`): the shield, drawn
  as the status glyphs beside it are (`SystemGlyph.Paint`), full while a connection is up and dimmed
  while none is, before Windows has answered, or where this PC has none — not the entry's accent tile,
  as the hotspot's face (§93). It reads a switch of its own (`FolderIsland.FaceSwitch`, made by
  `QuickSwitches.For` where the face is worn, `FolderFaces.SwitchOf`), whose news paints it again in
  place. Its tooltip is the switch's words: "VPN: Home" or "VPN: off".
- **A file keeps its VPN**: the entry becomes the preset's folder where it stood (§124's
  `ConfigWords.FlyoutFolders`, the word `vpn` added); the switch's line with the same word in a folder
  is left alone.
- **Flyout heights went** (§53, §59): the keyboard's layouts and VPN's connections were the last lists a
  flyout held to a height, and both are folders' lines now, as tall as what they list. Gone: `FlyoutHeight`,
  `FlyoutHeights`, `FlyoutHeightPreset` and their converters, `WidgetInfo.FlyoutHeights`,
  `WidgetItem.FlyoutHeight`/`FlyoutRows`, the settings app's flyout height cards (`FlyoutHeightRow`,
  `FlyoutHeightPreview`, `FlyoutLook`) and its look at a height (`FlyoutPreview`, the dock's
  `WM_KARPO_FLYOUT_PREVIEW`, `HeightAt`, `RowsFor`), `SwitchIsland.Kept`. A file's `flyoutHeight` and
  `flyoutRows` are read past and not written again. The selected widget's flyout in edit mode
  (`SelectedFlyout`) stays as a rule; since the web search box went no bar entry has a flyout it opens.
- **What went besides.** `BarKind.Vpn` and its entry, `VpnRowsPictures`, `FlyoutHeightRowTests`.

Tests: `VpnPresetTests` (the preset, its footer and face; the entry gone and the switch a line; the
list as the line has it; the line lists, and a click connects through the switch; the face lit while a
connection is up and following its switch, one square; pictures), `VpnTests`, `FlyoutFoldersTests`,
`FlyoutHeightTests` (a file with heights loads whole and forgets them), `PersonsPresetsTests` (presets
made after their arrangement held apart). Pictures: `vpn-preset-<dark|light>.png` (150 %, and 225 %
text), `vpn-face-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: with a VPN set up, add the VPN preset, connect from its row
and watch the face light; disconnect; "VPN" in the footer; a widget's settings page has no flyout height
card any more.

## 126. Project is a preset (2026-10-11)

The third of §124's ports: the project entry and its flyout, Win+P's four modes, went; what a click
on it gave is a ready-made folder.

- **The preset** (`Presets.ProjectId` "Project", `projectGroup`): the projection line the cast preset has
  too (§114: "Projection mode", the four modes, the one in force marked, a click putting another in
  force), and in the same card the premade **project actions** (`PremadeWidgets.ProjectActions`, new:
  Display alone on the right, the flyout's "More display settings"). In the add list's groups.
- **The face is the folder's icon** — the second screen, the entry's glyph — not a face of its own:
  Windows tells no app which mode is in force until it is asked, so the entry wore no state, and a
  face would have nothing more to say than the icon does.
- **A file keeps its entry** as the preset's folder in its place (`ConfigWords.FlyoutWords`, `project`).
- **What went.** `BarKind.Project` and its entry, `WidgetInfos.Project` and `QuickSwitch.Project` (the
  switch that only pressed Win+P, and its note), `SwitchIsland.Page` and `IslandView.Project`, and with them the last of a switch's click on the bar that opened anything — `SwitchIsland.Lists`, its list's rows (`Rows`, `ChoiceItem`, `Invoke`): VPN's connections are its preset's line (§125) and spatial sound is a toggle (§117) — the quick
  flyout's project page (`QuickKind.Project`: `ProjectPage` is the projection line's alone,
  `QuickKind.Projection`), the smoke run's project flyout, and the flyout tests of it
  (`QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.Display`); the quick flyout's own tests open the rename page instead, and
  the one that needed a page long enough to scroll on a low screen went with the last such page.

Tests: `ProjectPresetTests`, `FlyoutFoldersTests`, `CastNearbyPresetTests` (the line). By hand: add the
Project preset, pick Extend and Duplicate with a second screen attached; Display in the footer.

## 127. The layout switcher is a preset (2026-10-11)

The last of §124's ports: the layout switcher and its flyout, the bar's layouts to switch to, went;
what a click on it gave is a ready-made folder. With it every popup of a widget's own that was not a
folder is one, but for what §124's table keeps.

- **The preset** (`Presets.LayoutsId` "Taskbar layouts", `layoutsGroup`): the **layouts' line**
  (`ListKind.Layouts`, its word `layout`, the entry's; `LayoutsLine`) alone — a row per layout in the
  config's order, its own glyph and its name, the one this bar shows marked as WinUI marks a list's
  chosen item (the fill, the accent pill, its name semibold); as tall as there are layouts. The rows are
  the bar's own right-click menu's (`Dock.LayoutRows`, `Switchers.Layouts`), and with them its rule:
  below two layouts there is nothing to choose, and the line says so ("The only taskbar layout; more
  are made in Karpo's settings"). A new bar never had the switcher; the preset is in the add list's
  groups. No footer: there is no Windows page for Karpo's layouts.
- **A click switches.** A row's click (or Enter on it; Up and Down walk the rows) is the folder's act
  (`CellAct.Action`, `IslandView.Layouts`, `FolderFlyout.Forwards`): the folder closes, and then the
  dock switches this display to it (`Dock.SwitchLayout`) with the very method the bar's menu runs
  (`ChooseLayout`) — after the folder has gone, since a switch builds the bar the folder stood on
  again. A click on the one shown does nothing and leaves the folder open.
- **The face** (`FolderFaces.Layouts`, `layout`; `LayoutsFaceDrawing`): what the switcher was — the
  layout's own glyph and its name after it, in the room of ten characters whatever the name is, so a
  switch never moves the bar; dimmed while there is no other layout; the glyph alone down a bar on its
  side. Read from the folder (`FolderIsland.Shown`, `LayoutShown`), which a switch or a rename builds
  again. Its tooltip is the switcher's: the whole name, and that a click shows another, or that there
  is no other.
- **A file keeps its switcher** as the preset's folder in its place, with its id, section and row
  (`ConfigWords.FlyoutWords`, `layout`); a folder's line of the word is the layouts' line and is left
  alone.
- **What went.** `BarKind.LayoutSwitcher` and its entry, `WidgetSource.Switcher` and its shape,
  `SwitcherIsland`, the quick flyout's switcher page (`SwitcherPage`, `SwitchSource`,
  `QuickKind.Layouts`) and with it the last page that chose something for the dock to do
  (`IQuickHost.Chose`, `QuickChoice`, `QuickFlyoutAction.Chose`, `QuickKinds`): the quick flyout shows
  the rename box alone now. The tests that stood the switcher on a bar as any widget of the start
  stand the widgets board there; the flyout tests of the switcher's page went with it.

Tests: `LayoutsPresetTests`, `FlyoutFoldersTests`. Pictures: `layouts-preset-<dark|light>.png`,
`layouts-face-<dark|light>.png`. By hand: with two layouts or more, add the Taskbar layouts preset,
open it and pick another layout — the folder goes and the bar comes again in that layout, wearing its
name; rename a layout in Settings and see the face follow; with one layout the face is dimmed and the
folder says why.

## 128. In a list only what acts lights; a separator in edit mode is its line (2026-10-11) — no bar separator since §511 (2026-11-05)

*The person*: "generally speaking, the widgets in the list view should not have a hover over animation,
but all the logic subitems that have an logic/ action behind them", and "the spacers / dividers in edit
mode should just show up as a vertical bar / horizontal bar."

**Hover in a list.** See §9's "Only what acts lights" (`FolderFlyout.LightsWhole`): a line lights whole
only where the whole of it is the one thing a press does; every other line keeps still and lights only
its buttons, rows, chips and thumbs, each on its own. Added where they had none: the media line's
transport, shuffle, repeat and picker (the subtle button plate, pressed while held), the brightness
thumb (its core grows under the pointer and shrinks while held, as the panel's slider's), the weather
conditions' refresh button. Arranging is unchanged: every line lights whole.

**Separators in edit mode.** On the bar (`Scene.MarkFor`, `Scene.EditLine`) a separator is its line,
drawn as at rest — the bar's separator colour and thickness, across the bar: upright on a horizontal
bar, lying down a side — and one with no line at rest (Appearance's default, and every dock's) shows
one in edit mode all the same, as thick as a line would be, in the middle of its block or of the marker
laid over the seam. No box, no fill, no dashed outline, no glyph; under the pointer the edit wash over
its grab zone (an outline as well only in high contrast); selected, the accent ring every block wears,
round the grab zone, which stays wider than the line (`Layout.GrabRect`). The `EditMarker` tokens went
with the accent box. In a folder (`FolderFlyout`'s divider marks) a separator is a rule across its gap,
two hairlines (`DividerRule`) in the strong line colour, inset by a row's gutter; it is still taken
hold of over its 13-DIP grab and ringed when selected. Nothing in the file changes.

Tests: `LineHoverRuleTests` (every kind's rule, the real folder's lines under the pointer, the media's
play button), `BrightnessWidgetTests.ALinesSliderLightsUnderThePointer`, `SeparatorMarkTests`,
`DividerEditLookTests`. Pictures: `line-hover-*.png`, `edit-marks-<style>-<edge>-*.png`,
`divider-edit-*.png`.

## 129. A widget's menu has a row of buttons; one right click goes from one menu to the next (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "when right clicking a widget it should show the remove, settings, and duplicate entries in
the context menu as well, but they should be shown in a row like win11 does", and "when i have a context
menu open and i right click onto another widget i have to right click twice to open the context menu. is
this normal win11 behaviour? if not fix."

*Changed by §137:* the row is always on top, Duplicate is Copy (it follows the pointer), there are no
Copy and Paste rows, a pin's jump list has the row, and Remove from a menu always asks. *Changed by
§180:* the buttons are Explorer's — icon over word, across the menu, hairlines between — and the bar's
stand at the row's end without a gap.

**The row.** Every widget's menu — a bar's widget, a folder's face, a line in an open folder, the
desktops face, a status icon (also behind its arrow), at rest and while the bar is arranged — has
Duplicate, Settings and Remove as icon-only buttons in a row of their own (`Dock.WidgetButtons`,
`FlyoutItem.Primary`), as Explorer's Windows 11 menu has Cut, Copy, Rename, Share and Delete: in that
order, what copies first and what deletes last; Remove wears Explorer's Delete glyph. The row is ruled
off from the rows of text and stands at the menu's end nearest the pointer (`Flyout.WithPrimaryRow`,
`PrimaryRowFirst`): at the bottom of a bottom bar's menus, which open upward, on top of every other
bar's. The "Settings" row of text at the end of a resting menu is gone into the row, and so are edit
mode's Settings, Duplicate and Remove rows; on the bar edit mode keeps "Copy" and "Paste" as rows under
the buttons. A pin's jump list is unchanged: it is Windows' jump list, which has no such row, and its
"Unpin from taskbar" is its remove.

Each button is a row in all but its drawing (`Flyout.Primary.cs`): 40 DIP wide, a row's height and 4
DIP, 4 DIP apart from the menu's inset; the subtle hover and pressed plates; a click, Enter or Space
chooses it; greyed and skipped where it can't act. Left and Right walk the row, Down leaves it for the
rows, Up from the rows comes back onto its first button, Tab and Home and End take it in reading order.
Its word is its tooltip (12 px text, the edit rail's kind of tip), after the hover time of the pointer
or the keys resting on it, at once from one button to the next, outside the menu where there is room;
a screen reader hears a button.

**What they do.** Settings opens the widget's page (`OpenWidgetSettings`). Duplicate puts a copy right
after the original — on the bar after it, in a folder under it in its own list — with its options and a
new id; a folder's copy holds copies of its widgets, each with a new id (`Dock.DuplicateIn`,
`BarItem.Copy`, `CellItem.Copy`). It used to put a folder's line's copy at the end of the folder. It is
greyed where the copy has nowhere to go: a line whose kind its folder no longer takes, a widget the
file has lost (`CanDuplicate`). Nothing is limited to one per bar any more, so no kind is greyed for
that. Remove is edit mode's remove (`RemoveSelected`): at rest it takes the widget off at once, with no
edit mode first and no question, as Windows' "Unpin from taskbar" and edit mode's own Remove and Delete
do — but a folder with widgets in it asks first, in Windows' own dialog (§121). A folder at rest stays
open under a Duplicate or a Remove of one of its lines; Settings closes it, as it hands the screen to
the settings app.

**One right click.** A menu took every press that closed it (`LightDismiss.Consumes`), so a right click
on another widget only closed the open menu, and a second opened the next. Windows 11's taskbar goes
from one app's jump list to the next with one right click, and a click on another app's button while a
jump list is open switches to that app at once. So a menu now takes only a press on what opened it
(which closes it and does nothing else, any button); a press anywhere else on a bar goes on to what it
landed on, a right click opening that widget's menu and a click doing what its click does. In an open
folder the folder is a window of its own and always had its presses: a right click on another line
while one line's menu stands closes that menu and opens the other's, and the folder stays.

Tests: `WidgetButtonsTests` (where the row goes, no stray rules, Duplicate's ids, options, folder copies
and places), `BarMenuTests`, `FolderMenuRowsTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `EditSelectTests`,
`LightDismissTests.One_right_click_goes_from_one_widgets_menu_to_the_next`. Pictures:
`menu-<widget>-<rest|edit>-<up|down>-*.png`, `menu-sound-rest-<up|down>-keys-*.png` (the keys on the first
button) and `menu-tip-<up|down>-*.png`.

## 130. A dock with two rows (2026-10-11) — removed again (2026-10-30)

**Removed (2026-10-30, §438).** "the dock with two rows style should be removed." The type, its
windows a row, the joined panels and everything below are gone; what follows is the record.

*The person*: "for the dock add a two row layout as well" — "one panel with two rows"; "they should
have the already existing sections … the top row should be the topbar and the bottom row should be the
bottom bar slots (if you switch between layouts)"; "dock size should basically double"; the main row
(Start, pins, open apps) nearest the screen's edge, the second row on it; "it should basically behave
the same way as the current dock, just with two rows".

- **A fourth layout type**, `LayoutType.DockRows`, JSON `"dockRows"`, offered after Dock
  (`LayoutTypes.All`): the six slots shown, the **main row along the display's edge** and the **top
  row on it**, further in (`TaskbarLayout.RowsAt`, `Stacks`; at the top of the display mirrored, the
  main row still along the edge). A switch between Top and bottom and two rows moves nothing: the top
  bar's widgets are the row further in, the bottom bar's the row along the edge (`Become` sets the type
  alone). One size, each row's (`"size"`; the dock twice as thick, the room it floats over once), one
  way of showing (`"show"`); the Layouts page labels the size **Row size**. No config change beyond the
  new word: **an older build reads `"dockRows"` as a Taskbar** (`TolerantEnumConverter`, then
  `Config.Repair`), keeps every widget, row and section, and writes the layout back as a Taskbar.
- **A window a row** (`DockWindow.StackIndex`, `RowJoin`): each row is a bar of its own, as a Top and
  bottom's two are, so every widget, drop, drag between the rows, flyout, tooltip, hover, place and
  edit-mode rule is the one-row dock's. The top row stands flush on the main row
  (`Layout.Stacking`: no room of its own off the edge, `RowJoin.On`), goes out of sight past it
  (`HiddenOffset`), and holds no appbar: the main row reserves the whole dock, both rows and the room
  it floats over (`Layout.Reserve`), and tells the top row of full screen apps. The main row's window
  keeps the top row's room, so its tooltips (`Layout.TooltipAnchor`) and popups (`DockWindow.InnerSide`,
  `PointerAnchor`) open past the top row, never on it; the top row's are past it as ever. The dock's
  height is dragged on the top row's inner edge, both rows growing (`Distance` shared by the rows); the
  main row has no grip. Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down step a focused widget between the rows
  (`TaskbarLayout.Step`). On hover, each place has a window a row, sharing its stretch at the longer
  row's want (`Dock.WantsOf`); the edge comes and goes together (`EdgeReveal`), only the main row's
  place has the reveal strip, and the top row's place exists only while its row holds something
  there, or in edit mode.
- **One panel with two rows** (`RowJoin.Join`, `Scene.JoinRows`): each section's dock in one row and
  the same section's in the other are one panel, as long as the longer of the two where it stands (the
  start from the left, the middle centred, the end to the right), square where the rows meet and with no
  edge there (the shape run past the strip and cut there, `Scene.PastSeam`; a hard clip, a soft one let
  a line of wallpaper through). A separator splits the panel through both rows where both rows have one
  in that section; where only one row has one, or a section only one row holds, or a joined dock would
  run into another section's, each row's docks stand as they are, a quarter of the room between two docks
  off where one stands on another (`DockPanel.Parted`, `Scene.OffSeam`). The rows follow each other
  as a block is carried along one, out of it or into it, so the panel stays one. The window's region at
  rest is the joined docks.
- **Always two rows** (2026-10-12; *the person*: "the two row dock should always show up as two rows
  even if only one row is used, but should not show up if no widget is placed in the row"): a section
  only one row holds is two rows thick all the same — the other row has an empty half under or over
  each of its docks, joined, as long as it (`DockPanel.Empty`, `RowJoin.Join` with the row's band) —
  and a section neither row holds shows nothing. A row with nothing at all is the other's empty halves.
  In edit mode the empty half holds that section's empty room, fitted to it (`Scene.InHalves`): the
  place a widget is dropped into that row. On hover, a place's top row has its window whenever either
  row holds something there. The reserve stays the two rows whenever anything shows.
- **Settings**: the Type pictures have a fourth, **Dock, two rows** (`LayoutTypeArt`: three panels each
  two rows thick, as wide as the wider row). Words in the five languages
  (`settings.layouts.type.dockRows`, `settings.layouts.sizeRows.*`).

Tests: `DockRowsTests` (the type's slots, edges and sizes; each row's window its row; the row above and
below; switching to two rows and back moving nothing; the file round trip and an older build's
reading; the rows flush, the reserve, the grip, at the bottom and the top, 100 % and 150 %; the main
row's tooltip past the top row and the top row hiding past the main row; the joined panels and where
they do not join; each section held by neither, one or both rows; an empty row; the empty room in the
empty half), `NamedLayoutsTests` (the new type in the slot and switch theories),
`SceneTreeTests.EveryBarIsEditedWhereItStands` (two rows standing and on hover). Pictures:
`dock-rows-<bottom|top>-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-<150|100>.png`, `dock-rows-drag-dark-150.png`,
`dock-rows-groups-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png`, `dock-rows-hover-edit-dark-150.png`,
`dock-rows-<mixed|main-only>-<bottom|top>-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png`. By hand: switch a
Top and bottom layout to Dock, two rows and back (every widget where it was); open a folder of the main
row (it opens above the top row); drag a widget between the rows; drag the top row's inner edge; set
the dock to "When the pointer comes near" and bring it in.

## 131. The weather's lines are pressed by their parts (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "the weather widgets still are clickable the whole area, i want this changed, you should
be able to hover / click the individual days (even if they have the same search action associated),
same for the graph, you should be able to hover the individual hours. some parts you should also not
be able to click / hover, if the whole widget is clickable it generally is just weird".

No weather line lights or acts as a whole any more (`WeatherLineTile.LightsItsRows`, so
`FolderFlyout.LightsWhole` is false for `weatherNow`, `weatherHours` and `weatherDays` once set up; a line
not set up is still its whole "Set up in Settings"). Their targets, each with the subtle list-item
plate under the pointer, the pressed one while held (`RowPress`) and the focus ring with the keys on it:

- **The week** (`WeatherDaysTile`): each day's row (its box, half a gutter past its text either side, a
  pixel in at top and bottom). A click searches the weather on that day, "weather <place> <day>" by the
  region's full name for it (`SearchUrls.Weather`'s day, `Nls.DayName`, `DayRow.On`); today's is the
  plain search. Its tooltip names the day in full with its condition and chance of rain, which the row
  says only by a glyph. The air over and under the rows is nothing.
- **The hours** (`WeatherHoursTile`): the hour nearest the pointer across the graph (`DayGraph.PointAt`).
  Lit, its column (`DayGraph.ColumnOf`: an hour wide, never narrower than its glyph and a little air)
  wears the plate behind the graph and its point a ring on the line (`DayGraph.LitPoint`); its tooltip
  says its time, temperature, condition and chance of rain (`HourCell.Condition`). A click searches the
  weather — the graph is today's, and so is the plain search. The air over the graph is nothing.
- **The conditions** (`WeatherPartTile`): the conditions now (`NowTarget`: the glyph, the temperature
  with its arrow and the condition — `WeatherHeader.NowBox` on the whole header; the glyph to the
  condition on the compact line; the glyph to the temperature on one row) search the weather; the
  refresh button (`RefreshTarget`) fetches. The place, the age beside the button, what it feels like
  and the hours and days a tall line shows past the header are not pressed. (§370: the conditions are all
  the header draws, the place to what it feels like; the hours and days past it still are not.)

**The keys.** Arrows walk a line's targets — Up and Down the days, Left and Right the hours and the
conditions' two — and past either end are the folder's again, moving to the next line; Enter and Space
do what the target they are on does, and the first target's (the conditions, today, the first hour)
where they are on none.

Tests: `WeatherTargetsTests` (a target per day and per hour and none around them, the conditions and
the button against the place, the age and the feeling, the day's search, the keys),
`WeatherRowsTests.AClickSearchesTheWeatherAtItsPlace`, `LineHoverRuleTests`. Pictures:
`weather-hover-<dark|light>.png` (the pointer on the conditions, a day and an hour; the keys on the
button, a day and an hour; 225 % text). By hand: hover across the week and the graph in the weather
preset, click a day (the browser searches that day), Tab into the lines and walk them with the arrows.

## 132. A packaged app's jump list (2026-10-11)

The person: *"the whatsapp tasks dont show up correctly."* WhatsApp's open window was right — one
button, merged with its pin, its icon and title (the window, its WebView2 surface and its helper
windows were read live: the surface is a tool window in msedgewebview2.exe and is left out, as the
taskbar leaves it out). What was wrong was its jump list's Tasks: seven lines, each named
`5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop_cv1g1gvanyjgm!App`, each opening nothing.

A packaged app writes its list through Windows.UI.StartScreen.JumpList, and Windows keeps each line in
the app's CustomDestinations file as a link to a made-up path (the Desktop folder and the AUMID) whose
name is a BSTR, with the app's AUMID, the arguments it is activated with and its picture's address on
it (System.AppUserModel.ID, .ActivationContext, .DestListLogoUri). Read as an ordinary link, the line
was named after that path and pointed at it. Now (`JumpLists.Entry`) a line with an AUMID and an
activation context is the app's own: named by System.Title (BSTRs read too; an `ms-resource:` name
looked up in the app's package), drawn with its picture — `ms-appx:///…` resolved in the package
through its resources (WhatsApp ships only `NewChat.scale-200.png` for `NewChat.png`),
`ms-appdata:///local|roaming|temp/…` in the package's data — or with the app's icon where it has
none, and clicked, the app is activated with those arguments (IApplicationActivationManager, off the
dock's thread), as the taskbar does. A desktop app's link that only sets its AUMID so its window
groups (Chrome's) is still its command line. A desktop app's line that names its picture by address
(Windows Terminal's profiles) is drawn with it too.

The same lists were wrong for every app on the PC that writes one this way: Snipping Tool, Calculator,
Microsoft To Do, the new Outlook, the Microsoft Store, Codex and Spotify's "Recently Played".

Tests: `JumpListPackagedTests` (a CustomDestinations file written with the shell's own links and
WhatsApp's recorded properties: named and activated by the app; a desktop app's task with an AUMID
stays its command line; `ms-resource:` and `ms-appdata:` addresses). By hand: right-click WhatsApp —
New chat, New call and the recent chats with their pictures; click New chat; Snipping Tool's timers,
Calculator's modes, To Do's lists.

## 133. The faces on the taskbar are a section; a face is picked from a gallery (2026-10-11)

The person: *"adding a selecting a face needs improvement, there are just to many faces to just put
them into a dropdown list. fix this. also the already added faces should get an own section."*

- **A section of their own** (`FolderPage`): under the name, the heading **Faces on the taskbar**, as
  Windows heads a page's sections, over the faces the button wears, then "Add a face". Each face is an
  expander named after it, with its glyph (the folder's own icon for "Its icon") and the line saying
  what it shows; **Change** and, while there are several, Remove in its header; its rows in its body,
  as before. Dragged by the gripper or moved by Alt+Up and Alt+Down, as before. No dropdown anywhere.
- **The face gallery** (`Controls\FacePicker`, `Logic\FaceGallery`): "Add" and "Change" open a dialog,
  as Windows' own "Add a language" is a dialog with a search box over a long list. A search box, then
  the faces in their groups, each group's heading over its faces in two columns: **The folder** (what's
  inside, its icon), **Time & calendar**, **Connections** (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, hotspot, cast, nearby
  sharing, VPN), **Sound & media**, **System & performance** (the readings, battery, power), **Drives &
  devices**, **Info & messages** (weather, stock, news, mail, notifications, contacts), **Windows**
  (clipboard, desktops, keyboard layout, taskbar layout). "Other" holds a face nobody gave a group and
  shows only then; a test keeps it empty. A face is a tile: its glyph, its name and what it shows, a
  click, Enter or Space picking it and closing the dialog; Enter in the search box picks the one face
  found that can be. The search finds a face by every word typed in its name, what it shows, its group's
  name and the search words of the widget it shows ("ticker" the stock, "percentage" the battery), and
  in another language by its English words too (`CatalogueSearch.Matches`). A face the button may not
  wear (`FolderFaces.CanWear`) is greyed, the reason in place of what it shows: "Already on this
  button", or, adding to a button with the most faces, that it wears as many as it can. Changing, the
  face in that place has the check mark; picking it changes nothing. A face changed away from is
  remembered with its options while the page is open, as before (`FolderRows.FaceFor`).
- Words in the five languages (`settings.folder.faces.*`, `settings.folder.picker.*`,
  `settings.folder.faceGroup.*`); the dropdown's ("Face", "Face 1", …) went.

Tests: `FaceGalleryTests` (every face in a group once and in order, the search by name, blurb, group and
the widget's words, greyed with why, Enter's one face, the face a pick sets; the German groups and the
English search), `FolderFacesTests`. By hand: open a folder's page, "Add" a face (type "wifi", "ticker",
"Uhr" in German), "Change" one, and see a face already on the button greyed.

## 134. A separator has no page; its settings open the one "Separators" section (2026-10-11) — no bar separator since §511 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"the separators should not actually have an own configuration page, they should only have
a shared configuration page that applies theire style to all the separators."*

- **No page of its own** (`Logic\SeparatorPage`, `MainWindow.Open`): every way to a widget's page —
  edit mode, a widget's menu's Settings, a link, a test hook — goes through `MainWindow.Open`, which sends
  a separator, the taskbar's and a folder's alike (the file's `separator` and `divider`), to Appearance
  instead, its **Separators** section opened and brought into view with the accent around it for a
  moment, as "Find a setting" shows what it found (`ShowSeparators`, `Highlight(…, open: true)`). The
  widget page's card that only led there went (`IsSeparator`, `settings.widget.separator.look.*`).
- **One section, both kinds** (`AppearancePage`): "Separators" holds everything a separator's look is —
  on the taskbar the line, its width and colour and the space either side; in folders the gap between
  the cards a separator splits a list into, its last row, **Gap in folders**. "Separators in folders",
  a card of its own, went into it: the two are one thing called by one name (§120), so they are set in
  one place. The section's line says so: on the taskbar and in folders.
- **The file**: nothing changes. Separators carried no look of their own since §76 (an item's old
  `"separator"` options are dropped as the file is read, `SeparatorLineTests.AnItemsOwnLookIsDroppedFromTheFile`),
  and the two styles stay where they are, `"separators"` and `"dividers"`.

Tests: `SeparatorPageTests` (which widgets share the section; the routing, the widget page without a
separator card, the gap a row of "Separators"), `SettingsIndexTests`, `LineRowsTests`,
`SectionsStartCollapsedTests`. By hand: in edit mode open a separator's settings, on the bar and in a
folder: Appearance opens at "Separators", open; change the gap there and see a folder's cards move.

## 135. Combined groups (2026-10-11)

The person: "add some combined folder / widget groups / premade groups now. for example one that combine
the time and calendar stuff. you dont have to use every widget that there is it just needs to look good an
make sense. i think you can aim to make something like about 10 additional premade groups. they can also
have two or more columns as well."

- *What one is.* A preset with `Combined` set: two or three of the single groups' subjects side by side,
  a subject a list (`PresetItem.NewList`), so the folder is as tall as its tallest subject. A list is one
  card where its lines are one subject, its footer in it; a divider only where a list holds two. The
  button wears each subject's face side by side (`Preset.MoreFaces` after `Preset.Face`, each with the
  `PresetNeed` it needs: Quick settings' battery face only on a PC with a battery).
- *Where.* Last in `Presets.All`; the add list has each in its subject (§136; it headed them "Combined groups"
  after the others the day they came); "All ready-made folders" has them at the end of the end section, by library order.
- *The eleven.* Clock & calendar (§118, its clock lines now at their compact heights); Today (time over
  date + weather: the time header, the day's events ten rows and the calendar footer | the weather's
  three views); World clock (clock: this PC's time two rows, New York, London, Tokyo one row each,
  `PresetItem.Zone`/`Label`); Media center (now playing + speaker: now playing five rows, the apps |
  volume, output, mixer, sound footer); Quick settings (network, speaker, battery: the Wi-Fi and
  Bluetooth switches' lines first, as Windows' panel's first two tiles, the row of the other toggles
  — airplane mode, hotspot, energy saver, night light, do not disturb, VPN, `PresetItem.Toggles` —
  brightness, volume, and the battery under a divider on a PC with one; no power mode, 2026-10-11:
  "quick settings should not show power mode selector, they should show the wifi, bluetooth"); Network & internet (connection + VPN shield:
  Wi-Fi eight rows and footer | network activity, VPN connections and footer, the airplane, hotspot and
  nearby switches); Bluetooth & devices (rune + stick: Bluetooth eight rows and footer | wireless displays
  with Display as footer, removable devices); Inbox (envelope + bell: mail nine rows | notifications eight
  rows and footer); Notes & to-do (its icon: to-do ten rows | note ten rows; no clipboard history since 2026-10-12, "the
  notes and todo group should not show the clibboard history": that is a preset of its own); Markets (SPX
  ticker + headline: the Watchlist's four shares, wide | a feed twelve rows); Power & battery (charge +
  power glyph: battery, energy saver, power mode, footer | the power buttons, narrow).
- *Heights.* Every line that grows with what it holds (devices, apps, messages, networks) is held to a
  few rows, so each folder stands whole in the 70 % of a 1440p screen at 150 % with every such line at
  its most (`CombinedPresetTests`, which also pins each recipe and draws combined-<id>.png).

## 136. The add list is a tree of subjects (2026-10-11)

The person, on a proposal to arrange the add list as folders: *"you are 100% free to regroup
completely how it works. dont get influenced by how the groups are at the moment. do it so that it
makes the most sense to a new user."*; *"i dont think that ready made groups should really be a group
now anymore"*; Popular a *"fixed list"*; *"keep the quick settings folder"*; and of cast, projection
and nearby sharing, *"keep there, windows might not be a good group i dont know"*.

So the list asks the one question a new person has, what do I want to add, and answers it by
subject. `AddTree` (Karpo.Core\AddTree.cs) declares one tree for both pages as data: a folder
(`AddShelf`: an id for its words, `core.addTree.<id>.title`, and a glyph), a pick (`AddLeaf`: a widget
by its word, a premade widget or a preset by its id) or a line. `AddTree.On(page)` is a page's share:
the bar's page keeps its taskbar entries and the presets, a folder's its list widgets and the premade
widgets, and drops the rest; a folder left with one row is that row in its place, one left with none
is not there, a line stands only between two rows. A ready-made folder is a row as a widget is, in its
subject beside the widgets it is made of, with no "ready-made" of its own; a combined group (§135)
in the subject it is mostly about (Today in Time and calendar, Inbox in Notes and messages), its row
tagged "Group" at its end (since 2026-10-12, "the groups should be marked with a batch in the add widget
window": `FlyoutItem.Badge`, a pill of a control's fill and a card's hairline round secondary words, in
the tree and the search's results alike, the row's height unchanged; every ready-made folder's, a
combined group's and a folder of one subject's alike, since the person added "also the single topic
ones" the same day — a single widget and a subject's folder page wear none;
`AddListPresetsTests.EveryReadyMadeFoldersRowIsTaggedAGroup`, sheets add-badge-*.png). The families (§112) and the
library's groups (`WidgetCategory`, still the settings' order) no longer arrange the list.

| Column / folder | On the bar | In a folder |
|---|---|---|
| **Popular** (again from their homes) | Clock, Calendar, Weather, Sound, Wi-Fi, Battery, Media, Pin; a line; Folder, Separator | Clock, Calendar, Conditions, Volume, Battery, Now playing, Note, To-do, Pin; a line; Heading, Separator |
| Time and calendar | Clock, Clock & calendar, Today, World clock, Timer, Focus time, Stopwatch, Focus, Calendar | Clock, Time and date, Alarm, Timer, Focus time, Stopwatch, Clock actions, Calendar › (calendar, month, today's date, day's events, day, week and year views, calendar actions) |
| Weather and news | Weather, News, Stock, Stocks, Markets | Conditions, Next hours, Week's forecast, RSS feed, Stock |
| Music and sound | Media, Media center, Sound, Volume slider, Sound on/off, Microphone on/off, Spatial sound | Now playing, Media source, Volume, Output, Input, Mixer, the three switches, Sound actions |
| Connections | Network & internet, Wi-Fi › (folder, switch), Bluetooth › (Bluetooth, Bluetooth & devices, switch), VPN, Mobile hotspot, Airplane mode, Connectivity | Wi-Fi ›, Bluetooth ›, VPN ›, Mobile hotspot › (each its lines and its actions), Airplane mode |
| Quick settings | the Quick settings folder, a line, the ten toggles (again) | the row of toggles, a line, the ten toggles (again) |
| Battery and power | Power & battery, Battery, Energy saver, Power | Battery, Energy saver, Power mode, Power actions, Power buttons › |
| Screen and sharing | Brightness, Night light, Rotation lock, Live captions, Accessibility, Cast, Project, Nearby sharing | the same as lines, with the wireless displays, projection, nearby sharing's switch and details and their actions |
| System info | System, Processor, Graphics, Memory, Disk, Network activity, Security, Screen time | Processor ›, Graphics ›, Memory ›, Disk ›, Network activity › (graph, details), Task Manager actions, Security, Screen time › (screen time, screen time chart, app usage; since 2026-10-12, "screen time and app usage should go under one group") |
| Notes and messages | Notes & to-do, To-do, Notes, Inbox, Mail, Notifications, Do not disturb, Contacts | the same as lines, Notification actions |
| Files and tools | Pin, Drive, Network drive, Removable devices, Storage, Clipboard history, Snipping Tool, Settings | Pin, Drive, Network drive, Removable devices, Clipboard history and its actions, Snipping Tool, Settings, Actions |
| Start and taskbar | Start, Search, Task view, Widgets, Apps, Tray icons, Status icons, Show desktop, Virtual desktops, Taskbar layouts | Task view, Virtual desktops, Desktop actions, Taskbar layout |
| Keyboard and touch | Keyboard layout, Touch keyboard, Virtual touchpad, Pen menu | Keyboard layout, Keyboard actions |

Windows' shell is no group of its own any more: "Windows" named where the things come from, not what
they are for. Start's, the search's and the tray's are the taskbar's ("Start and taskbar"), what puts
the screen elsewhere or shares it is with the screen ("Screen and sharing": cast, projection, nearby
sharing, brightness), and typing and touch are theirs.

- **Exactly once.** Every widget, premade widget and preset has one home (`AddLeaf.Again` false);
  Popular and Quick settings show some again (`Again`), on purpose. `AddTreeTests` hold it for both
  pages, and that nothing is left over: a widget or a preset added to a registry and not to the tree
  fails them, and meanwhile stands in "More" at Browse's end (`AddTree.More`), never missing.
- **Easy to scan.** At most twelve rows in a column or a folder, never three folders deep, never a
  folder of one row (`AddTreeTests`). Names short enough for the column.
- **The rows** (`AddList.Rows`): every home has its command, a widget's its place in `Entries`, a
  preset's after the last; a row shown again has its home's, and no search words, so the search lists
  it once. A folder's row has a command past those, which picks nothing.
- **Search** as §7b: flat, with the path, in the tree's panel.

Tests: `AddTreeTests`, `QuickSettingsFolderTests`, `AddListTests`, `AddListSearchTests`,
`AddListPresetsTests`, `PremadeWidgetsTests`. Sheets: `add-list-<bar|list>[-1440p]-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`
(the tree), `add-list-submenu-dark-<100|150>.png` (Time and calendar open),
`add-search-<bar|list>-…-<empty|typed|row|greyed|none>.png` (the results). By hand: open the add list
on the bar and in a folder, walk a subject's submenu with the pointer and with the keys, search
"wi-fi" and see where each result is, type in an open submenu.

## 137. Every right click has something below its row; the row on top; Copy follows the pointer (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "most of the right click context menus of the taskbar widgets are empty, they should not
be, they should show options related to the widget face, if there are multiple faces it should show
all of them in order"; "the edit row should be on top of the context menu action"; "the pins should
get the top menu row as well"; "if you delete a widget via the context menu action there should be a
system confirmation dialog"; "edit taskbar and taskbar settings should go into the row menu as well.
(actually still configurable but as a default, then set mine to a default as well)"; "when copying a
widget it should go into edit mode, and then not just place it next but actually pin it to the mouse
until i left click somewhere i want it", "in edit mode the copy and paste context menu actions are
duplicated", "pasting should actually not be an option ... it should then be copied into the clipboard
too so that if he decides to paste it in another layout it would work still".

**A face's rows** (`Dock.FaceMenus.cs`). A folder on the bar offers, below its buttons, each face's
own rows (`ActsFor(FaceInfo)`), worked on the widget that face shows (`FolderIsland.WidgetOf`): a
timer's line, a drive line, the feed, what is playing, else the folder itself (`FolderIsland.Menu.cs`:
`RefreshFace`, `Radio`, `ToggleMute`, `Saver`, `PowerModes`). One face: its rows as they are. Several:
each face's under a heading with its name (a clock's label after it), in the faces' order, a rule
between two; the rows numbered one after another (`ActRows(first:)`), each remembering its widget
(`WidgetActRow.Works`) and a Refresh its face (`On`). It replaces the "first acting face" (§118):

| Face | Rows below the buttons |
|---|---|
| content, icon | Edit folder (edit mode on, the folder open in it) |
| clock | Adjust date and time · Open Clock |
| calendar | Open Calendar · Adjust date and time |
| dateTime | Adjust date and time · Notification settings (Windows' clock's two) |
| weather | Refresh · Change location (the folder's page) |
| wifi | Turn Wi-Fi off / on (greyed until known) · Diagnose network problems · Network and Internet settings |
| bluetooth | Turn Bluetooth off / on · Bluetooth settings in Windows |
| sound | Mute (ticked) · Open volume mixer · Sound settings · Troubleshoot sound problems |
| removable | each device: Open · Eject · Properties · then AutoPlay settings |
| timer, focus | Start/Pause · Stop · A minute longer · A minute shorter (the line's) · Open Clock |
| stopwatch | Start/Pause · Lap · Reset (the line's) · Open Clock |
| hotspot | Mobile hotspot settings |
| cast | Connect to a wireless display (Win+K's flyout) · its settings in Windows |
| nearbySharing | Nearby sharing settings in Windows |
| battery | Power mode (three rows, the one in force ticked) · Energy saver · Power & battery settings |
| power | Power & battery settings |
| mail | Refresh · Manage accounts |
| nowPlaying | Play/Pause · Previous track · Next track · Open player |
| cpu, gpu, memory, disk, networkActivity | Task Manager · Resource Monitor |
| stock | Refresh · Open in browser (its share's page) |
| news | Refresh · Open website |
| drive | Open · Eject · Properties (the line's drive) · Storage settings |
| networkDrive | Open · Disconnect · Properties · File Explorer |
| notifications | Clear all · Do not disturb · Notification settings |
| clipboard | Open clipboard history (Win+V) · Clipboard settings in Windows |
| contacts | Refresh · Manage accounts |
| desktops | New desktop · Rename this desktop · Delete this desktop · Task view |
| keyboard | Language and region settings in Windows |
| vpn | VPN settings in Windows |
| layout | each layout to choose (two or more) · Layout settings |

Every other entry (`ActsFor(BarKind)`): the Snipping Tool's snips and its page, Task view's New desktop
and its page, the volume slider's mixer, sound settings and troubleshooter, the Settings button's
Windows Update, and for every other one the page Windows keeps for it — its taskbar settings where it
keeps none (`PageOf(BarKind)`). The desktops face's special menu (`Topic.Desktops`) is gone into this.

**The row on top.** The buttons are always the menu's first line (`Flyout.WithPrimaryRow`); the "nearest
the pointer" rule of §129 is gone. A pin's jump list has the row too, above the list (`AppRows(buttons:)`):
Copy, Settings, and Remove, its unpinning — no "Unpin" row and no "Settings" row then. An open app that
is no pin keeps "Pin to taskbar".

**The bar's buttons in the row** (`BarMenuEntry.Row`, `BarMenus.CanBeInRow`, `Dock.BarButtons`). An action
(but the layouts) or a shortcut of the bar's menu can be a button of the row instead of a row of text;
"Edit taskbar" and "Taskbar settings" are, and since the menu is fixed (§27, 2026-10-12) only they. The bar's own menu draws them on top alone (at most
`MostInRow`, five); every widget's row has them after its own three, at the far end with a gap
(`FlyoutItem.PrimaryEnd`, at most `MostBarButtons`, two: five buttons is what a 256 DIP menu holds).
"Taskbar settings" as a button wears the palette, so the row never has two gears. The settings app's
Taskbar menu page had a toggle on each card for it, and a file whose menu was written down before the row
was set to the default once (`BarMenus.MigrateToRow`, `"menuButtonRow"`): both went with the page (§27);
the menu a file wrote down is not read any more at all.

**Remove asks.** Remove from any menu asks first in Windows' own task dialog (`FolderDeletes.ForMenu`,
`Dock.MenuDeleteQuestionFor`): "Remove “<widget>”?", "Its settings will be removed with it.", Remove /
Cancel (Cancel the default); several selected are counted; a folder with widgets asks §121's question.
Edit mode's Delete key asks only that one, as before.

**Copy** (was Duplicate; `Dock.EditCopy.cs`). One button; no Copy or Paste rows anywhere. It turns edit
mode on (for a folder's line, the folder arranged where it stands, `BeginEditFromFolderDrag`), makes the
copy as Duplicate did (`DuplicateIn`: options and new ids throughout, right after the original) and hands
it to the pointer: on the bar a block carried as one from the add list is (`Follow`), to every surface
of its display; in a folder a line carried among its lists with no button held (`FolderFlyout.Carry`,
`LandCarry`, `EndCarry`), never carried out of it. The hooks (`EditFollowHook`) hear the left press that
puts it down where the landing shows, and the right press or Escape that takes it out again — nothing
added. It also goes on edit mode's clipboard (`Clip`): Ctrl+V in edit mode, in this layout or another,
hands a copy of it to the pointer again — a bar's widget on the bar under the pointer, a folder's line in
the folder standing open arranged (`PasteLine`, `PasteLineIn`). Ctrl+C copies a lone line too.

Tests: `FaceMenuTests` (every face and every entry has rows; the multi-face order and headings; Windows'
sound and battery rows), `WidgetButtonsTests` (the row on top, the bar's buttons at its end, Copy's ids,
Ctrl+V of a line), `WidgetMenuTests.APinsMenuHasTheRowOnTopAboveItsJumpList`, `BarMenuRowTests` (an old
menu not read and the rest kept, the cap), `FolderDeleteTests.RemoveInAMenuAlwaysAsks`, `FolderCarryTests`
(carried with no button, put down, called off), `EditSelectTests.AWidgetsMenuHasOneCopyAndNoPaste`, and
the faces' presets' tests. Pictures: `menu-faces-*` (a clock, the weather and the sound in one folder),
`menu-pin-*`, `menu-bar-rest-*`, `menu-sound-*`, `menu-folder-cpu-*`. By hand: right-click a folder of
several faces; switch the Wi-Fi off and on from its face; Copy a bar widget and a folder's line, put each
down, then Copy and Escape, and Ctrl+V in another layout; Remove from a menu (the dialog), Delete in edit
mode (none for a plain widget).

## 138. The licence: Karpo Pro on the Microsoft Store (2026-10-11)

*"add a licence page to the application as well. like the themia-app repository does it ... we will
distribute the app via microsoft store so you should build the licencing around that. when there is
no licence the amount of widgets a user can place will be limited to lets say 20 and there should
only be the possiblity to create 2 layouts. other than that there should not be any other limits
enforced. now, the number of widgets should just be the ones that are actually shown in the
layouts, if there are hidden slots these wont count."*

Karpo is free on the Microsoft Store, and **Karpo Pro** is a durable add-on bought once. Ported from
Themia's licensing (`Themia.Core\Licensing\LicenseRules.cs`, `LicenseService.cs`, its License page).

**The free version** holds at most **20 widgets on a layout** and **2 layouts**. Every widget kind and
every setting is there; nothing else is limited. A limit only ever refuses to **add**: a copy over it
(Pro refunded, an import, a layout changed to a type that shows a row more) keeps everything it has,
and moving, changing and removing are never refused. Nothing is ever deleted because of a limit.

**What counts** (`LicenseCount`): per layout, every entry on its bars in a slot its type shows
(`TaskbarLayout.Shows`), once each.

- A **folder counts once**, whatever it holds. What a layout shows is the folder on its bar. The
  ready-made folders (the clock, Wi-Fi, sound, …) are made of many widgets inside and a new bar has
  nine of them; counting their insides would put a new install over the limit untouched. So adding
  to a folder is never refused.
- **Not widgets, never counted:** separators, pinned apps, and Windows' own taskbar buttons (Start,
  Search, Task view, the Widgets button, the open apps, the tray, the status icons, the pen menu, the
  touch keyboard, the virtual touchpad, Show desktop): free, as on Windows' taskbar
  (`LicenseCount.Free`). A new install's bar counts 9 of 20 (`LicensingTests.ANewBarLeavesRoom`).
- **Hidden slots don't count:** the top row of a Taskbar or a Dock. A layout can go over by changing
  to a Top + bottom; that is allowed (the person: the exploit is small, and
  not knowing why the limit was reached is worse).
- **Per layout**, not summed: a new layout starts as Windows' taskbar again, and two of them summed
  would already be most of one allowance.

**Where it is read.** Both processes ask the Store themselves (`Karpo.Dock\StoreLicense.cs`, compiled
into the settings app too), with the same pure rules (`LicenseRules.Decide`). The dock is the one that
refuses adds on the bar and runs without the settings app; the settings app sells Pro and makes
layouts. A state one wrote for the other to trust would be a file anybody could edit to unlock Pro,
and stale until its writer ran. Windows keeps the Store's licences per user and package, so the two
get the same answer, and each hears `StoreContext.OfflineLicensesChanged` when a purchase (here or in
the Store app) or a refund changes it; the dock also asks again whenever it opens the add list while
limited. Shared is only the offline grace's record, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\license.dat`: the Store's
last "owned", DPAPI-sealed for the Windows user, which carries Pro for **7 days** while the Store
can't be reached (`LicenseCache`, `LicenseRules.GraceUntil`; a damaged or future-dated record gives
nothing). Anything not clearly "owned" is the free version: an unknown state never unlocks Pro.

**Developer builds.** `StoreContext` needs package identity, which only the Store's MSIX has. A copy
without it — `dotnet run`, `artifacts\publish`, the tests — never asks the Store and is
**unrestricted**, "Developer build" on the License page (`PackageIdentity.IsPackaged`,
`GetCurrentPackageFullName`). `KARPO_LICENSE=free` makes such a copy act as the free version, to try
the limits by hand (the dock passes its environment to the settings app it starts). A packaged copy
ignores the variable.

**Where it is enforced.** Every add asks `LicenseGate` (Karpo.Core), the one place:

- **The bar's add list** (`Dock.License.cs`, `LicenseRows.Limited`): on a layout at its limit, "Get
  Karpo Pro" first under Popular with "20 of 20 widgets used" under it, every row that would count
  greyed with "Needs Karpo Pro" (a ready-made folder always counts), and what doesn't count as it was.
  A folder's add list is never limited.
- **Any add on the bar** — a pick, the edit bar's Folder, "Copy" (the copy that follows the pointer), Ctrl+V (all of it or none) — is
  held against the count before it is applied (`LicenseAllows`): refused, nothing changes and a small
  "Free version" flyout says "20 widgets per layout", "20 of 20 widgets used" and offers "Get Karpo
  Pro", which opens the settings on the License page (`--page license`).
- **New layouts** (Settings › Layouts): at 2, "Add layout" and every Duplicate are greyed and a bar
  over the cards says "Free version: 2 layouts. You have 2. Get Karpo Pro to make more." with a link
  to the License page (`SettingsModel.LayoutRefusal`).

**The License page** (Settings › License, in the side menu's foot above About): a card saying what
this copy is and why (Developer build, Free version, Checking, Karpo Pro, Pro while the Store can't
be reached until a date); where the limits apply, "What you use" — a card per layout with its widgets
"n of 20" over a bar (amber when full), the layouts "n of 2", and what counts as a widget; then
"Microsoft Store": Karpo Pro with its price as the Store gives it ("Get Karpo Pro · CHF 9.00"), the
Store's own purchase dialog owned by the settings window, and "Restore a purchase" › "Check again".
It follows the licence live. Words: `Logic\LicenseView.cs`.

**Store setup** (Partner Center, once): create the add-on — type **Durable**, lifetime **Forever**,
product id e.g. `karpo-pro`, its price — and paste its 12-character **Store ID** (`9XXXXXXXXXXX`) into
`StoreIds.ProAddOn` (`Karpo.Core\Licensing.cs`). Until then it is the placeholder
`PRO-ADDON-STORE-ID`: the button says "Karpo Pro isn't on sale yet" and no licence can match it. The
MSIX itself (manifest, identity, packaging) is not built yet; a sideloaded package has no Store
licence and is the free version, so the limits can be tried there; a real purchase only once the app
is published (hidden is enough) and installed from the Store.

Tests: `LicensingTests` (the tier, the grace, the Store ids, what counts, what is refused),
`LicenseRowsTests` (the add list and the refusal), `LicenseViewTests` (the page's words). Sheets:
`license-add-list-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`, `license-refusal-…`. By hand: with `KARPO_LICENSE=free`,
fill a layout to 20 and open the add list, Copy and Ctrl+V past it, add a third layout, and read
the License page; without it, nothing is limited.

## 139. No menu is its row alone: a line's own rows, the floor, and arranging's rows (2026-10-11)

*The person*: "the right click context actions when only shown as the row and nothing else to show it
just looks pretty bad in my opinion. make sure that there are also always items that are shown and not
just the row."

**A line's own rows** (`ActsFor(ListKind)`) take its face's where the kinds match (§137): the weather
lines Refresh · Change location; the stock line Refresh · Open in browser (its symbol's page); mail
Refresh · Manage accounts; contacts the person's rows, Refresh · Manage accounts; the clipboard line Clear
all (but the pinned) · Open clipboard history · Clipboard settings in Windows; a to-do line Clear completed
(greyed with nothing done); an alarm Open Clock; the apps playing Play/Pause · Previous · Next · Open
player; the layouts line Layout settings; a month Open Calendar · Adjust date and time; the Settings
button's line Windows Update; a separator's line, and a separator on the bar, Separator style (the shared
section, §134).

**The floor** (`Dock.MenuFloor.cs`, `Floored`). Where a widget's own rows at rest leave none that does
something now (`HasLiveRow`: no heading, rule, button or greyed row counts) — a heading, a note, a toggles
row, Sign out, a drive not plugged in, Security — the floor goes under them, after a rule: a folder's
line its folder's Edit folder (§141; it was Move up · Move down), an entry of the bar its page in Windows
(taskbar settings where it has none), a folder Edit folder.

**Arranged** (`EditMenuRows`). Edit mode's menu is the buttons, then Done editing; on one of several
selected, which Copy and Remove act on together, Select none over it (§141; the moves are gone).

Tests: `MenuFloorTests` (every list kind, every bar kind and every face has a live row at rest; every widget
arranged; the floor only under nothing live), `WidgetMenuTests` (the table), `MenuModePictures`
(`menu-folder-heading-*`, `menu-folder-weather-*`, `menu-folder-todo-*`, `menu-separator-*`, and every
widget's `-edit-` picture). By hand: right-click a heading, a note and a to-do line in a folder; right-click
a separator on the bar and in a folder; in edit mode right-click a widget (Done editing), and one of
several selected (Select none).

## 140. Fixed only where the content does not vary; every kind's rows have limits (2026-10-11)

The person: "widgets that cannot grow / shrink naturally (because they dont have a variable amount of
items in them) should not have an automatic height option, just the fixed one. also widgets where it
makes not sense to show the bigger / smaller than a certain value should have limits as well".

- **The model** (`Karpo.Core\ListWidgets.cs`): `ListWidget.Grows` (default true) says the line's
  content is a number of things that varies, so Automatic means something; false is Fixed only.
  `ListWidget.Heights` (default 1 to 32) is the fewest and the most rows a person may give the line,
  in either mode. `LineHeight.Limits(kind)` holds them to 1..32; `LineHeight.Within(kind)` holds a
  height to them and makes it fixed for a kind that does not grow. `LineHeight.For` and `Normalize`
  read every height through it, so a height a file holds outside the rules is set right **in place**
  on read (no shape bump, no reset): an automatic height of a fixed kind is fixed at the kind's
  `Rows`, or at its most where that was fewer; rows outside the limits are the nearest inside. A
  fixed kind starts `Exactly(Rows)`; `Rows` were chosen to be the tier the old automatic height drew
  at 100 % text (a graph's 87-DIP content is its compact tier, two rows; a clock's 78–96 its full
  tier, three). A kind whose limits leave one height and no mode has no height card (`HasHeight`).
- **The limits** come from each kind's forms (where `ListTiers` and its own drawing change, measured
  at 100 % text): the fewest is the height its drawing first holds, the most is where it draws
  nothing new, plus room for the largest text — a fixed line does not grow with the text, so a person
  reading at 225 % raises its rows, and the most holds the content there (`ListHeightOffscreenTests`).
- **The least column is withdrawn** (2026-10-13, §166): every kind may be one row; the fewest below
  is what its drawing first holds whole, and under it the drawing gives way as §166 says.

| Kind | Mode | Rows (start) | Least–most | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weatherNow | Fixed | 4 | 1–8 | one row, compact at 2, the panel header at 4; 8 holds it at 225 % text |
| stock | Fixed | 3 | 1–6 | one row, two text rows at 2, the third at 3; past that only a gap |
| cpu, gpu, memory, disk, network | Fixed | 2 | 1–12 | compact at 2, full at 3, the minute at 5; the graph grows after |
| media | Fixed | 2 | 1–6 | one row; art and controls at 2; timeline at 4 |
| drive, networkDrive | Fixed | 3 | 1–6 | one row, compact, header at 3, full at 4 |
| soundVolume | Fixed | 1 | 1–4 | the flyout's row; output over slider at 2; large level at 4 |
| brightness | Fixed | 1 | 1–4 | the volume's line (`SliderLine`), so its rows are the volume's: one row, two with the words over the slider, the level large taller |
| spatialSound and every switch | Fixed | 1 | 1–3 | one row, the note at 2, the full note at 3 |
| battery | Fixed | 2 | 1–6 | compact at 2, full at 3, every line at 4 |
| security | Fixed | 2 | 1–4 | compact at 2, protections at 3, full at 4 |

| stopwatch | Fixed | 1 | 1–8 | laps fill what it is given; nothing measures them |
| alarm | Fixed | 2 | 1–4 | compact at 2, full at 3 |

| month | Fixed | 8 | 8–10 | six weeks need 8; less cuts weeks off |
| timeHeader | Fixed | 3 | 3–5 | 92 DIP; less cuts the date |
| dateHeader | Fixed | 1 | 1–2 | a 48-DIP band |

| screenTime | Fixed | 4 | 1–6 | compact at 2, full at 3, the graph whole at 4 |
| powerMode | Fixed | 5 | 5–8 | the page's three modes; 8 holds it at 225 % text |
| projection | Fixed | 6 | 6–9 | the page's four modes; 9 holds it at 225 % text |

| rss, pin, calendar, the sound lists, notificationsList, mail, screenTimeApps, events, todo, note, wifi, bluetooth, hotspot, wirelessDisplays, clipboard, contacts, mediaSources, the details, desktops, keyboard, vpnConnections, layouts, removableDevices | Automatic or Fixed | as before | 1–32 | a number of things: messages, devices, events, facts (as many as the machine reads), a pin's folder contents |

  Not in the table: the list's own rows (one line), the divider, the actions line (§76, `FixedHeight`)

- **Settings** (`Controls\SizeCard.cs`, `Logic\HeightChoice.cs`): for a fixed kind the card has no

of "Faces on the taskbar", the gripper on a single face.

## 141. Screen time's ring, and screen time one folder of the add list (2026-10-12)

*The person*: "screen time and app usage should go under one group" and "add a screen time donut
chart as well, which shows the current day / selected day / hovered over day".

- **The add list** (§136): System info has a folder "Screen time" (`core.addTree.screenTime.title`)
  with the ready-made folder, the total, the ring and the apps. On the bar only the preset is left of
  it, so it is that row.
- **The ring** (`screenTimeChart`, ScreenTimeDonut.cs): one day's screen time as a donut, the day's
  five top apps clockwise from twelve o'clock, then "Other" — the smaller apps, an app under 2 % of the
  day (a sliver nobody could point at), and time counted for no app — in the bars' neutral grey
  (`ScreenTimeRing.Of`: the last piece ends at 360 exactly). The total and the day's name in the hole;
  where the hole is too small for them (three rows, the largest text) they head the legend instead.
  The legend, a row a piece with its time, stands beside the ring, or under it in a line too narrow.
- **Which day**: the day under the pointer in the folder, else the folder's day, else today
  (`ScreenTimeDonut.DayOf`). The total publishes the day of the bar (or the stretch of the area)
  under the pointer to a new channel, `Channels.DayHover` ("Follow the day pointed at", a switch of
  the ring's like every channel's), and withdraws it as the pointer leaves the bars, so the ring
  follows the pointer live from bar to bar and goes back to the day shown.
- **Colours**: the bars' (§69): an app among the fortnight's top apps wears the colour it wears in
  the bars; another of the day's top apps the next free one. High contrast: the text's colour, the
  gaps telling the pieces apart, the lit piece the highlight.
- **The pointer**: a piece or its legend row lights (the piece drawn 3 DIP out, the rest dimmed,
  the legend row a subtle fill) with a tooltip "Browser — 56 min (34%)"; its app is the folder's app
  pointed at (`AppHover`), so the apps' row and the bars light it, and a click picks it (`App`) as a
  row's does, a second lets it go. The app picked or pointed at elsewhere lights its piece here. The
  right click opens the app (`WidgetAct.OpenApp`).
- **Height**: Fixed (its pieces never vary), four rows new, three to six (`Heights`). Its `Range`
  starts at one row like every card's (ListBoundsTests); in a line taller than the largest ring the
  ring stands at the line's top, as every card's content does (ListScrollTests).
- **The ready-made folder**: the total four rows, the ring four, the apps six (eight before), so a
  new folder is two rows taller than before. A folder made before keeps its lines; add the ring from
  the add list.

Tests: `ScreenTimeDonutTests` (the pieces, the sliver, the angles, the day rule, the day pointed at
in a folder, the switch off, a piece's tip and pick, the bars' colours, every height in its line),
`ScreenTimeLinesTests.TheReadyMadeFolderFixesItsLines`, `ChannelsTests`, `AddTreeTests`. Sheets:
`screentime-ring-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (today, a piece pointed at, an app picked, a bar pointed
at, a day with nothing), `screentime-ring-heights-<dark|light>.png`, `screentime-ring-folder-*.png`.
By hand: open the Screen time folder, move the pointer along the bars and watch the ring follow and
come back; point at a piece and at a legend row; add the ring to an existing screen time folder.

## 142. Reordering a folder's lines moves as the bar's blocks do (2026-10-12)

The person: "the editing of the list views should be made as smooth as the taskbar, with that i mean
the reordering specifically". Before, a carried line stayed where it was and an accent bar marked
the seam it would go into; nothing else moved until it was let go, and then everything jumped.
Now it is the bar's drag (`Scene.Apply`, `Dock.EditCarry.cs`), in the folder's own window
(`FolderFlyout.Drag.cs`, the rules in `FolderDrag.cs`):

- **Lifted.** Past the drag threshold the line's card and content leave their list for a carrier
  over everything: a plate of the panel's base colour with its rim, under the bar's lifted shadow
  (12 DIP blur, 4 down). It follows the pointer by its offset alone, every move; nothing is drawn
  again. Carried off the folder it waits at the window's edge, faint.
- **The others give way.** The folder is planned again with the move made (`FolderDrag.Moved`,
  `Build`) and every other line glides to its place in that plan — in its own list and in another,
  across dividers and headings — in the bar's 167 ms with its decelerate easing, from the place it
  was last sent (the bar's `Slide`). The lists' clips, the cards (`FlyoutHost.SetPieces(glide)`) and
  each list's own buttons glide with them, lined up on the bar's side as the lists are
  (`FolderDrag.Down`); a ghost of the line's size, the accent's wash in an accent outline, stands in
  the gap (the bar's `ShowGhost`). Over a "+" for a new list the line's own list closes up behind
  it; that "+" itself stays put, being the place under the pointer.
- **Where it lands is read from the line** (`FolderDrag.Gap`). In its own list it passes a line once
  its leading edge is past that line's middle — its bottom going down, its top going up — so a tall
  line over the middle of a short one takes its place. Read from the pointer, as before, it had to
  be carried right past the short one, and let go over its middle it went back where it was (the
  person's "dropping onto the middle of a shorter line doesn't count as a move"). In another list,
  where nothing gave way yet, its middle against the lines' middles decides. Every line is read
  where it stands at rest, so the lines giving way never move the place under the pointer.
- **Auto-scroll.** Within half a line of a scrolling list's end the list scrolls itself, a step a
  frame (`DragScrollTimer`), up to 12 DIP, harder the deeper in (`FolderDrag.ScrollStep`).
- **Settle.** Let go, where every line shows is kept (`Snapshot`); the dock moves it and the folder,
  laid out again, glides every line from where it showed to its new place, the carried one on its
  plate, which sinks into the list (opacity to 0) as it lands (`Settle`). Any layout change of the
  arranged folder glides the same way: a line moved by **Ctrl+arrows** (new in the folder: a place up
  or down, or into the list beside at the same place, `FolderDrag.KeyPlace`), by its menu's moves,
  one added or removed. The keys stay on the line they moved.

Tests: `FolderDragTests` (the gap for lines of equal, taller and shorter heights, headings and
dividers, another list, the regression; the copy a move is planned on; Ctrl+arrows; the scroll
step; the bar-side alignment), `FolderDragMotionTests` (on a hidden desktop: the lifted line stands
where the pointer has it at every move, the heading gives way, let go it is a move and settles;
`folder-drag-motion-<dark|light>.png`, a drag frame by frame). By hand: drag a line down and up a list
with a heading and a divider in it, into the next list and back, onto the "+" between two lists, and
off the folder; hold one near the end of a list that scrolls; let go mid-glide; Ctrl+arrows on a
focused line in an arranged folder.

## 143. The processor's top processes (2026-10-12)

The person: "for the processor add top running processes by cpu as a widget as well".

- **The widget** (`cpuProcesses`, "Top processes", `ListKind.CpuProcesses`, `WidgetSource.Processes`,
  `Karpo.Dock\Performance\ProcessesLine.cs`): Task Manager's processes sorted by CPU, a line of a list
  only. A row per app, its processes together as Task Manager's Apps group them, by image name
  ("Google Chrome (23)", the shares summed): the app's icon and name (its file's description, through
  `ScreenTimeNames`), a thin accent bar of its share of the whole processor under the name, and the
