  share to a tenth of a percent in a column as wide as "100.0%", so nothing moves as figures change.
  As many rows as the line holds, a list row each (32/40/48 DIP by the item style, which it offers:
  size only); never stretched, never scrolled. Automatic or Fixed (`Grows`), five rows unmeasured, a
  new line automatic up to twelve.
- **The figures** (`Karpo.Dock\Performance\ProcessTop.cs`): `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation)`
  reads every process's kernel and user time with no handle, elevated and protected processes
  included, no WMI, AOT-safe (`DllImport` with blittable types). A share is the time used between two
  readings over the time that passed times the logical processors (`GetActiveProcessorCount`), Task
  Manager's CPU column. The System Idle Process (id 0) is never a row. A process the first reading did
  not have counts all its time; an id used again (another start time) is another process. The order is
  the share as shown (to 0.1 %), then the time used since start, then the name, so level apps stand
  still. An app's path is asked once, of the kernel by id (`SystemProcessIdInformation`), and turned
  into a drive letter or a share.
- **Read only while it shows**: every two seconds while the folder is open; half a second while its
  first figures wait. The last reading is kept, so a folder opened within a minute shows figures at once.
- **A click** opens Task Manager, as the graph's does (its last tab; Task Manager has no switch for
  the Processes tab). Up/Down walk the rows, Enter clicks. **A row's right click**: the app's name, "End
  task" — after Windows' own task dialog (Cancel the default), every process of the app still the one
  listed and not critical (`IsProcessCritical`); never Karpo or the kernel's; greyed where Karpo could
  open none to end (an elevated app while Karpo is not) — "Open file location", Resource Monitor.
- **Where**: the processor's preset (`Presets.CpuId`) is its graph, its details, the top processes
  (automatic up to `Presets.ProcessRows`, five) and the Task Manager footer; it stands whole in the
  70 % of a 1440p screen at 150 %. In the add list it is in System > Processor. A folder made from the
  preset before this has no such line (no migration): add it from the add list.

Tests: `ProcessTopTests` (the math, grouping, idle, order, paths, this PC read without a handle),
`ProcessesLineTests` (rows by height, reading while shown, click, menu; `processes-line-*.png`),
`PerformancePresetTests` (the preset fits), registries' tables. By hand: open the Processor folder —
rows fill within half a second, real icons and names, figures every two seconds; right-click a row
and End task an app of your own (Notepad), then try one run as administrator (greyed).

## 144. No moves in a menu; the selection rectangle begins on the bar and in a folder (2026-10-12)

*The person*: "move left move right should not be a context menu action." And: "the lasso select
should also work inside the taskbar, right now it only works if started outside."

**No moves** (`Dock.MenuFloor.cs`). No menu, at rest or arranged, has Move left · Move right or Move up
· Move down any more (§139 put them in edit mode's menu and under a line with nothing live); arranging
is dragging, and Ctrl+arrow from the keyboard. No menu is its row alone still (`MenuFloorTests`): a
folder's line with nothing live has its folder's **Edit folder** (`FolderKeyOf`: edit mode, the folder
open in it and picked, where the line is dragged); an entry its page in Windows; a folder Edit folder;
arranged, **Done editing**, with **Select none** over it on one of several selected. The four strings
are gone.

**The selection rectangle on the bar** (`EditClicks.OnPress`). A left press while arranged begins: on
the resize grip, a resize; on a widget, its carry, as before; anywhere else on a bar or a place — the
gaps between and round the widgets and the sections, the bar's background — the selection rectangle,
as on the dim: the bar holds the mouse, past the drag threshold `EditBand` is drawn and every widget of
the display it runs over is selected (`EditClicks.Overlaps`), with Ctrl or Shift what was selected
stays; a click there clears the selection, as before.

**In a folder.** There was none. A press on the room of a folder standing open arranged — between and
round its lines, the room over a shorter list, never a line or a "+" — begins the same rectangle
(`FolderFlyoutAction.BandPressed`, `BandMoved`, `BandReleased`, `BandLost`; the dock draws it), which
selects that folder's lines alone (`FolderFlyout.KeysIn`). Every selected line wears the accent's ring,
not only the one last clicked (`FolderFlyout.AlsoPicked`); Delete and Remove act on them all.

Tests: `MenuFloorTests` (no moves anywhere; the floor's Edit folder; arranging's rows),
`EditSelectTests` (the press: carry, rectangle or resize; what a rectangle overlaps),
`FolderEditClickTests.ADragOnTheEmptyRoomSelectsLines`, and `edit-select-inside-<look>-<scale>.png`
(`SceneTreeTests.EditSelectSheets`: a rectangle begun in the bottom bar's gap before Search, drawn into
Task view). By hand: in edit mode drag from a gap of the bar over two widgets; from the room over a
shorter list of an open folder over two lines; a press on a widget still carries it.

## 145. A click in edit mode only selects; Settings follows quietly; a properties panel (2026-10-12)

The person: "right now there is a problem that the application looses focus when the settings window
is opened automatically, so keyboard shortcuts dont work anymore then". Every click on a widget in
edit mode opened its page and brought the settings window to the front (2026-10-04), so Delete,
Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and the arrows went to Settings instead of the bar.

- **A click selects** (`EditClicks.OnBlock`): on the bar and on a folder's line alike; a folder still
  opens (or, standing open, closes). Space and Narrator's Invoke are the click. No click brings any
  window forward, so the bar keeps the keys.
- **An open Settings window follows, quietly** (`EditClicks.FollowArgs`, `SettingsApp.Follow`): the dock
  hands the page straight to the settings app's listening window (`karpo.settings.instance`) over its
  own WM_COPYDATA hand-off (`SettingsHandOff.InstanceMarker`), the arguments of the menu's "Settings"
  plus `--follow` — no process start, which is what brought the window forward, and no
  AllowSetForegroundWindow. The settings app reads it (`StartRequest.Show`): an open window navigates
  without `Activate`, restore or raise (`StartShow.Quietly`); a closed one opens nothing
  (`StartShow.Nothing`). Off the dock's thread; the `--clicked` stamp orders several.
- **Settings in front only when asked**: a double-click on a widget (the guard's second half,
  `EditClicks.OnDoubleClick`), Enter on the focused block (Enter or Space on a line in an arranged folder, whose keys carry no point), the
  Settings icon of the widget's menu, and the properties panel's "More settings".
- **The properties panel** — *gone since §147*: a folder line's height is set in a strip over or under
  the line, and the edit view offers a folder, a heading or a clock no options. As it was
  (`EditProperties.cs`, `PropertiesPanel.cs`, `Dock.EditProperties.cs`): with
  one widget selected in edit mode (not several, none, or a carry), a small Windows 11 flyout of the
  dock's own (296 DIP; the quick settings' controls) stands on the bar's inner side, beside what is
  open there — the selection's own flyout, the folder it is in — on the side with room, else at the
  selection. It holds the widget's kind as title; its name where it has one (a folder's name, a
  heading's text, a clock's or date's label); its height where it is a line of a folder with one
  (§140: "Fixed height" only where the content varies, rows stepped within the kind's limits,
  "Maximum rows" while automatic); and "More settings" in the footer band. Height changes apply at
  once; a name on Enter or when the keys leave the box (Escape puts it back); both saved as every dock
  change is (`Apply`), and the open settings window reloads them. It is a Tool host (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE):
  a click on its switch, steppers or link never takes the keys from the bar; its name box takes them
  for the typing and gives them back on Enter, Escape or F6. F6 on the bar in edit mode moves the
  keys into the panel.

Tests: `EditClickTests` (no click brings anything forward; double-click and Enter ask; the follow is
flagged and reads back as quiet / nothing), `SettingsFollowTests` (the follow handed to a listening
window flagged; it was `EditPropertiesTests`', which went with the panel). By hand: with Settings open,
click widgets in edit mode — Settings changes page behind, Delete/Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V/arrows still act on
the bar; double-click or Enter brings Settings forward.

## 146. Bars on the left and the right (2026-10-12)

The person: *"the taskbar at the moment i can only show at the top or bottom, but i want to be able
to show it on the left and right as well, same for dock and two row dock. implement that."*

The sides had gone from the model and the settings app on 2026-10-09 (§ on bars along the top:
"the sides go from the code"), when a side read as the bottom and edit mode made places down both
sides of a bottom bar. Layout, Scene, the appbar, the popups and the faces had kept everything a
bar down a side needs (`Layout.Vertical`, `Edge.Left`/`Right` switches throughout), so the sides
come back in the model and the settings app:

- **Any edge** (`Screen.Edge`): `Sections.Known(Edge)` keeps every edge this build knows and reads
  an unknown word as the bottom; `Config.Repair` writes only an unknown word back. A build from
  before reads `"left"`/`"right"` as the bottom (its own Known), so nothing breaks there.
- **`ScreenEdges`** has four edges again (`All`: bottom, top, left, right). A layout has bars on one
  edge, or on two opposite ones, never on two that meet, so no bar reaches across another's end.
- **Hover places down a side** (`HoverPlaces.For`, `RunOf`, `StripOf`, `Area`, `Touching`): a
  side's three places share its height as the top's share its width; the 1 px strip is the column
  along the side; a side another display touches is an inner edge (no place waits there at rest),
  as the top and the bottom are.
- **Top and bottom on a side is Left + right** (`TaskbarLayout.EdgeOf`): on a display whose edge is
  a side, its main row stands on that side and its top row on the other; on the top or the bottom
  it keeps the bottom and the top whatever the display's edge, as before (no layout of anybody's
  moves). Chosen over a fifth type: the person picks the side once, on the display, as for every
  other type, and switching a display between top/bottom and a side keeps the layout's widgets in
  their rows. The Layouts page still says "Top bar size" and "Bottom bar size" for its two bars;
  on a side they are the other side's and the display's side's.
- **Dock with two rows on a side**: two columns, the main one along the screen's edge and the other
  inward, each section's docks joined across them (`RowJoin`, which was edge-free already).
- **Keys**: on a bar down a side Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right carry the focused widget to the bar or
  column beside it (`TaskbarLayout.Step` orders a side's rows left to right; `Dock.StepRow`).
- **Popups** stop short of the other side's bar shown over the windows (`Dock.PopupRoom`), and in
  edit mode a side bar's popup, centred on its anchor, moves under the edit bar at the top of the
  display rather than over it (`FlyoutHost.ClearOf`).
- **The appbar** holds a strip on the left or the right (`ABE_LEFT`/`ABE_RIGHT`, as before), also on
  an inner edge between two displays, as Windows' own taskbar may; a bar outside Karpo's takeover
  keeps its own strip on its side (`DockWindow.EdgeArea`).
- **The clock face** down a vertical bar keeps two lines for a countdown the folder could run; with
  none running the time stands centred in them, not at their top (`ClockFaceDrawing.Paint`).
- **Settings**: the Displays page's Position is four pictures (`PictureChoice` of `EdgeArt`, which
  draws a bar down either side), no longer greyed for a Top and bottom; the map draws a band down a
  side (`DisplayMap`), the card says "Karpo on the left/right" (`DisplayCard.Doing`) and a widget's
  page "at the top of the left edge" and so on (`WidgetStand.Of`).

Tests: `SideBarPictures` (`side-<taskbar|dock|dock-rows|top-bottom>-<left|right>-<rest|edit|folder>-<dark|light>-150.png`;
the clock's folder opening away from its bar, inside the display, over no other bar),
`TopAndBottomOnASideIsLeftAndRight`, `EveryBarIsEditedWhereItStands` (each type on each side, 100
and 150 %), `HoverPlacesTests.ASidesPlacesRunDownIt` and `ADisplayBesideItMakesThatSideInner`,
`EdgeModesTests.OnlyAnEdgeWithABarIsAPlace`, `PopupRoomTests` (the sides), `NamedLayoutsTests`
(`"left"`/`"right"` read and written back). By hand: Displays page, Position Left and Right for a
Taskbar, a Dock, a Dock with two rows and a Top and bottom; maximized windows stop at a side bar;
hover a side bar in and out; open a folder, a menu, a tooltip and the window list from a side bar;
edit mode on a side (drag along the column, drop between the two columns, Ctrl+Left/Right); a side
bar on the edge between two displays.

## 147. A folder line's height in a strip at the line; no options in the edit view (2026-10-12)

The person, of §145's properties panel: "i dont really like where the edit box for the height is. also
it does not have to be winui3 styled, i would rather have it be part of the AOT as well. put it over or
under a widget in the list when i click the widget", and "the folder options should actually be
removed from the edit view".

- **The panel is gone** (`PropertiesPanel.cs`, `EditProperties.cs`, `Dock.EditProperties.cs`, F6, its
  strings): a widget on the bar, a folder, a heading or a clock has no options in edit mode; its
  settings are Settings' (the menu's Settings icon, a double-click, Enter), which still follows the
  selection quietly (§145). A folder's own buttons over its lists (+, width, remove) stay.
- **A height strip at the line** — *gone since §151: the height is set in the line's menu*. As it was
  (`LineHeightStrip.cs`, `FolderFlyout.Height.cs`): when one line of an
  open, arranged folder is selected — alone, nothing carried — and its kind has a height to set
  (`Folders.HasHeight`: not a heading, a divider, a list row or a kind of one fixed height), the folder
  draws a strip of its own in Direct2D, as wide as the line: "Height", Automatic | Fixed where the
  kind's content varies (§140), a "− N +" stepper within the kind's limits (the button at a limit
  off), and "More settings", which opens the line's page in front. A card of the flyout's colour and
  rim with a small shadow; the selected mode in the accent; Windows' compact (24 DIP) controls; 32 DIP
  tall at 100 %. Where the line is too narrow, "More settings" is a gear (its name a tooltip, as the
  stepper's buttons have), then "Height" goes, then the modes' words are cut.
- **An overlay, under or over**: it pushes nothing — the lines stand where they stand in edit mode and
  out of it (§142) — and stands 4 DIP under the line where its list has the room, else over it (a line
  at the folder's bottom edge); where neither (a list of one short line), on the side the window and
  the display have more room on, kept on screen. Never over the line itself; under the selected ring,
  which stays whole over its shadow.
- **It stays while the line is selected**, follows a scroll, and goes on a deselect, a second
  selection, a line lifted past the drag threshold, or a widget carried in.
- **Changes apply at once** (`FolderFlyoutAction.Height`, `Dock.SetLineHeight`): a step or a mode saved
  as every change of the dock's is; the folder is laid out for it and the strip moves with its line.
- **Keys**: + and − step the selected line's rows; Tab goes from the line into the strip (Tab and
  Shift+Tab walk its parts after the line), Left and Right along it, Up and Down step, Enter and Space
  press.

Tests: `LineHeightStripTests` (options per kind; presses and keys; the writes held to the kind; under,
over, the roomier side; one row inside narrow, medium and wide lines with the gear and label
fallbacks; on a folder: shown for the one line selected and not for a heading, two selected, a carry
or rest; its parts press and a step shows at once; the keys; pictures
`edit-height-<clock|calendar|battery|narrow>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`). By hand: in edit mode open a
folder, click a line — the strip under it (over the last line); step the rows, switch Automatic and
Fixed, watch the line change; Tab into it, + and −; More settings brings Settings forward; click a
heading — no strip; on the bar nothing stands beside a selected widget.

## 148. An arranged folder drawn out across the screen: guide lines and empty slots (2026-10-12)

The person: "when in edit mode and a folder is open, i want the design to look very different ...
there should be lines going from the top to the bottom of the screen which mark the left and right
edge of the folders. the folders that dont exists, i mean the ones on the left and right that you can
add, i dont want this add mechanic anymore. they should all also show up with those lines even if
they are empty. and they should also be a drop target, and they should also show the add button but
for the widgets, they should repeat all the way to the edges of the screen." Confirmed: an empty
slot is a medium column wide (360 DIP); a column that becomes empty is kept, so empty columns can be
left between others as spacers.

- **The window to the screen's edges.** Arranged, the folder's window reaches the work area's edges
  on every side but the bar's (`FlyoutHost.Spread`): from the top of the work area to the bar's inner
  edge on a bottom bar, from the bar's edge to the far side on a side bar. The panels stand where
  they stood. Only the folder's own things take the pointer — the lists and the 36 DIP round them as
  before, every "+", the height strip; the rest answers the hit test with `HTTRANSPARENT`
  (`FolderFlyout.PassesThrough`, `Dock.FolderPassesThrough`), so a press there reaches the dim, the
  bar or an edit bar under it exactly as without the folder (the dock's windows are one thread's).
- **Guide lines** (`FolderFlyout.Guides`): a hairline down the window at each list's left and right
  edge, just inside it as the rim is — over and under its panel, never across it — and at each
  slot's, the whole way down; in the scroll indicator's strong fill at 60 % (`GuideInk`), so it reads
  on the dim in both themes. A line stops short of a display's edit bar (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`).
- **Empty slots** (`FolderSlot`, `FolderFlyout.WithSlots`): a medium column's width, the lists' gap
  apart, repeated out to the edges on both sides — none on a side bar's side — the one the edge cuts
  there while its "+" fits. Each has a "+" (`FolderAddKind.Slot`), centred on what shows of it, level
  with an empty column's "+", which opens the add list; and the whole slot, half the gap either side,
  is a drop target for a carried line: its "+" lights and a ghost of the line stands in it on the
  bar's side. Adding or dropping makes a list where the slot stood: `FolderPlace.Slot(at, apart)` —
  a new list at 0 (left) or at the end (right), `apart` empty, medium lists between it and the others,
  for a slot further out (`Folders.InsertNew`). Old files are untouched: `Apart` is never stored.
- **The lists stay where they stand** (taken back 2026-10-12, §149: every layout is centred as a reopen is) while the folder is arranged (`FlyoutHost.HeldLeft`, a bar
  along the top or bottom): every layout keeps the panel's left edge rather than centring it on its
  button again, and a slot on the left that became a list moves it to where that slot stood, so the
  new list appears exactly in its slot and nothing else moves — the folder grows leftwards, as
  Windows' flyouts do from their anchor. The first column's remove does the same the other way. Out
  of edit mode (the folder closes with it) it is centred on its button again. A side bar's folder
  grows away from the bar anyway.
- **The side "+" is gone**, between the lists too (`FolderFlyoutAction.AddList`, `Dock.AddFolderList`
  removed): a column goes in by its slot. A line alone in its list dropped in the slot right next to
  it still changed nothing (`Folders.Move`, `FolderFlyout.Ghost`) — until §153, which made it a move;
  a slot further out moves it, its list kept empty.
- **Empty columns are kept anywhere** — between others, at either end. At rest one is its width of
  room and nothing drawn, as before (§ empty columns), so an outer one shifts the visible panels
  beside the button (taken back 2026-10-12, §158: an outer one takes no room at rest); arranged it is its "Add widgets here" panel with its buttons, unlike a slot.

Tests: `FolderSlotTests` (slots repeat to both edges at the medium width, their "+"; a side bar's on
one side; guide lines at every edge, not across a panel, cut by the edit bar; the model's slot places
and kept empty columns; the landing shown agrees with the move; on real windows: the window spans the
work area and lets its room through, a line dropped in a left slot and a widget added in one stand
where the slot stood with every other list unmoved), `FolderColumnsTests.TheSlotPlusAndTheEndPlusPick`,
`FolderDragEditTests`; pictures `folder-slots-<bottom|left>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png` (one list, two,
two with a line carried over the first right slot).

By hand: arrange a folder on a bottom bar — lines down the screen at both edges of every column and
slot, slots out to both screen edges with a "+" each; press a slot's "+" and add a widget: a column
there, nothing else moves; drag a line into the second slot out: a column there with an empty one
between; click the empty room, the bar and the edit bar while the folder is open — they behave as
without it; a side bar: slots on the far side only.

## 149. The folder edit view: no columns to delete, empty ones are slots, adding opens nothing (2026-10-12)

The person: "when adding a widget to a column the column does not immediately shift, you have to
reopen the layout"; "the overlay that shows the individual lines is infront of the configuration
window, it should just be on the same level as the other stuff"; "the notion of a column should kind
of be removed. for example an empty column should not display a drag widgets here text in edit mode.
it should keep its width though, so every column that you see on the screen, even if empty you should
be able to change its width"; "deleting a column should not even be possible anymore"; "when adding a
widget it should not open the settings automatically".

- **Laid out as a reopen lays it out.** The arranged folder's left edge was held through every layout
  (`FlyoutHost.HeldLeft`, §148), so a column added in a slot, or one made wider, grew the folder to one
  side while opening it again centred it on its button: the columns jumped only on the reopen. The hold
  is gone (`HeldLeft`, `FolderFlyout.HoldLeftFor` removed): every layout places the panel as a showing
  does, so what shows after a change is exactly what a reopen shows.
- **At the level of edit mode's windows.** The arranged folder's window spans the work area (§148) and
  is topmost; shown, laid out or activated it went over every topmost window, the settings app's too —
  which edit mode keeps on top — covering it, and its room let presses through only to Karpo's own
  windows. Now it stands on its display's dim and just under the lowest other app's window over it
  (`FlyoutHost.Floor`, `EditStack.UnderOthers`; the dock gives `ShadeOf`): placed so, and put back so
  after an activation (`FlyoutHost.Restand`, on showing and on `WM_ACTIVATE`). With no dim, and at rest,
  it is over everything as every popup.
- **An empty column is a slot of its width.** Arranged it draws no panel and no words (no `Runs`, no
  piece, `FolderPlan.Empty` only for a folder with no widget at rest); its guide lines run the whole way
  down as a slot's; it keeps `EmptyRows` of room on the bar's side, which its "+" and width button stand
  over — level with a slot's — and a carried line lands in. A folder whose lists are all empty draws no
  panel at all (`FlyoutHost.Pieces` empty: none).
- **Every column and every slot has the width button.** A slot's sits beside its "+" (the pair centred
  on what shows of the slot, `FolderFlyout.PairWidth`); its menu has medium ticked, and narrow or wide
  makes it an empty column of that width where it stood, the slots between it and the lists empty medium
  ones, as adding into it does (`Folders.SetSlotWidth`; `Pending.Column` carries the place).
- **No column delete**: the remove button, `FolderFlyoutAction.RemoveList`, `Dock.RemoveFolderList`,
  `Folders.RemoveList`, `FolderDeletes.ForColumn` and the strings `dock.delete.column*` are gone. A folder
  is still deleted as before.
- **Adding opens nothing.** A pick from the add list — the bar, a folder's "+", a slot's, the edit bar's
  add button — adds the widget and selects it; the settings app is not opened (`Dock.AddChosen`). A widget
  that needs setting up says so on its line or block ("Set up in Settings"), which opens its page.

Tests: `FolderSlotTests` (a drop and each kind of add, and a slot's width, laid out as the reopen shows
it; the arranged folder under the settings app on showing, layout and activation, over everything at
rest; slot pairs; `SetSlotWidth`), `FolderColumnsTests` (an empty column a slot arranged; every list's
pair, no remove; an empty list's and a slot's width ask), `FolderAddTests`; pictures
`folder-slots-<bottom|left>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png` (the fourth: a list between an empty narrow and
an empty wide column).

By hand: in edit mode open a folder and add a widget through a slot's "+" — it is a column at once,
the folder centred as when reopened, and Settings does not open; open Settings over the arranged
folder and click into the folder — Settings stays in front and clickable; an empty column shows only
its lines and its "+" and width buttons; make a slot wide — an empty wide column there; no column
has a delete button.

## 150. One edit mode: the bar's and an open folder's alike (2026-10-12)

"the editor for the folder view and the editor for the taskbar are different but still i want the
overall look and feel to be the same ... keyboard shortcuts, animations, context menus, dnd
behaviour". The bar and an open folder each arranged their own way from numbers typed in twice.
Now they read one keymap (`EditKeys`) and one look (`EditLook`); the bar is the reference except
where the folder's was the better one.

| | Bar before | Folder before | Both now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Escape | carried block back, then out | closed the folder mid-drag | carried thing back, then one level out |
| Home/End, Ctrl+A, Space, Enter, menu key, Shift+F10 | yes | partly | the same on both (`EditKeys`) |
| Ctrl/Shift-click, right-click | select | only plain click | select on both; a right press cancels a drag |
| Menu on the empty room | edit menu | none | edit menu (Select none, Done editing) |
| Lift | at the press, 0.9 opacity | after the threshold, opaque | at the press under the move cursor, 0.9; carried out of the folder 0.6 |
| Lifted shadow | 12 DIP blur, 4 down, 1.4x | the same, typed twice | `EditLook.LiftShadow*` |
| Move / settle | 167 ms decelerate; settled from the place it left | 167 ms; settled from where let go | 167 ms decelerate, settled from where it was let go |
| Drop ghost | jumped to the new gap | glided | glides in a move's time |
| Added item | faded in | popped in | fades in in a move's time |
| Hover wash | faded 83 ms | instant | fades 83 ms |
| Outline | hairline on the edge, brighter under the pointer | one hair in, 0.35 ink, never brighter | on the edge, 0.28/0.24, brighter (0.60/0.50) under the pointer or carried |
| Selected ring | 2 hairlines inside the edge | 2 hairlines outside | inside the edge |
| Focus rectangle | Windows' (2 px outer + 1 px inner, inside) | one outside ring | Windows' on a line; a "+" keeps the outside one, as the edit bar's buttons |
| Hairline | scale floored | scale rounded (2 px at 175 %) | floored, at least 1 px (`EditLook.Hair`) |
| Auto-scroll | — | ran from the press | only past the drag threshold |
| Drag threshold | `SM_CXDRAG` | `SM_CXDRAG` | unchanged (`EditClicks.PastThreshold`) |

Tests: `EditKeysTests`, `FolderEditClickTests`, `EditLookTests` (the hairline is the bar's at every
scale, a stroke stays inside its box, both surfaces glide on the one time); picture
`folder-edit-list-<dark|light>.png` (the first line hovered, its outline lit).

By hand: arrange the bar and open a folder side by side. Hover a block and a line — both fade in a
wash and brighten their outline. Press and hold one of each without moving — both lift at once and
go a little see-through; release — both settle where they were. Drag a line across its list — the
ghost glides along as the bar's does; let go half-way — it settles from there. Tab to a line — the
same two-tone focus rectangle as a block. Escape while carrying — it goes back, the folder stays open.

## 151. Several lines carried and copied together; the height in the menu; the copied look (2026-10-12)

The person: "dragging multiple widgets in folder edit mode should work." — "same for copy pasting,
copy pasting should also work into columns that are empty." — "the additional menu options that
appear when i click a widget in the folder should be moved to the context menu, the toggle switch and
the height settings. when you change the height it should also not close the context menu." — "the
item that is currently in the clipboard should get a look like an excel cell does when it is being
copied. same if you select multiples of course."

- **Several lines carried together** (`FolderFlyout.Group.cs`): a press on one of several selected
  lines of an arranged folder (a click, Ctrl/Shift+click, the lasso of §144) and a drag carry all of
  them: each lifted on its plate as one line is (§142), stacked one under the other in their order down
  the folder (list by list, each from the top), 2 DIP apart, the one taken hold of under the pointer,
  the stack kept inside the window. Where they would land is read in the folder with all of them closed
  up behind (`FolderDrag.ClosedGroup`): the stack's middle against the lines' middles in the list it is
  over or nearest, so none of the lines left has to give way first and nothing flickers; read back as
  the folder's own place (`FolderDrag.Unclosed`). The others give way for all of them at once, one ghost
  stands round the room they take; over an empty column they go to its top, over an empty slot they
  are a new list there. Let go, they land in their order (`Folders.MoveGroup`, `Dock.PlaceInFolderIn`:
  one `FolderFlyoutAction.Place` with every key). Selected widgets elsewhere stay where they are, and a
  group is never carried out onto the bar. A line selected alone is carried as before.
- **Lifted at the press, put back by Escape** — as one line is since §150: a press on one of several
  selected lines lifts them all at once under the move cursor, a little see-through over the lifted
  shadow (`EditLook`), and a click lets them settle back. Escape or a right press while they are held
  puts them all back where they were (`CancelMove`, `EditKeys.Escape`), nothing moved, and the release
  is no click; the folder stays open.
- **Copy and paste of several** (`Dock.EditCopy.cs`): "Copy" on one of several selected copies them
  all — the same folder's lines, or the same bar's widgets (`Dock.CopiedWith`) — and they follow the
  pointer together (a folder's carried as above, the bar's as pasted widgets are); Ctrl+C of several
  lines puts all of them on edit mode's clipboard (it held one line before and dropped the rest), and
  Ctrl+V hands copies of all of them to the pointer in the folder standing open arranged. A click puts
  them down wherever a carried line lands: between two lines, at a list's end, in an empty column, in
  an empty slot. Escape or a right click takes all of them out again.
- **The height in the line's menu** (`LineHeightRows.cs`): §147's strip is gone. A right click on a
  folder's line whose kind has a height (`Folders.HasHeight`), arranged or at rest, has under its other
  rows, ruled off, "Fixed height" with a Windows 11 toggle switch where the kind's content varies (§140)
  and "Height" with a "− N +" stepper of its rows within the kind's limits, a button greyed at a limit.
  Each change is saved at once and the line resizes behind the menu, which stays open and shows the
  height as it is now (`Flyout.Refresh`, in place, the lit row kept). "More settings" went with the
  strip: the menu's Settings button is the line's page.
- **Interactive rows in a menu** (`Flyout.Controls.cs`, `FlyoutItem.Control`): a toggle switch (40 × 20
  DIP, Windows 11's: ringed in the secondary text with its knob left when off, the accent with its knob
  right when on) or a stepper (two 24 DIP buttons of a control's fill and rim, the value between) at a
  row's end, where a shortcut would stand. A click on the toggle's row, Enter or Space flips it; a click
  on a stepper's button, Left/Right or −/+ on its row steps it. Either is `FlyoutEventKind.Adjust` and
  the menu stays open.
- **The copied look** (`MarchingAnts.cs`, `FolderFlyout.Ants.cs`, `EditView.Copied`): what is on edit
  mode's clipboard wears Excel's marching ants while edit mode is on — the accent's dashes, as thick as
  the selected ring (2 px at 100 %), 3 × the stroke long with gaps as long, on a band of the accent at
  30 %, moving one dash and gap along every 480 ms by the compositor alone (a looping key-framed
  `StrokeDashOffset`; standing still with Windows' animations off). On the bar round each block copied
  from, in its ring's place; in an arranged folder round each line, where its ring stands — on the
  edge, inside it, as §150 strokes every ring (`EditLook.Stroke`) — hidden while lines are lifted or
  glide. As in Excel they stay until Escape, the next copy, or the end of edit mode; a paste leaves
  them. Escape is §150's one keymap with a step between (`EditKeys.Escape`, `EditEscape.Uncopy`): on
  the bar what is carried goes back first, then the ants go, then edit mode ends. The clipboard itself
  stays.

Tests: `FolderGroupMoveTests` (moves of several within a list, across, into an empty column, to a
list's end, as a new list; nothing where nothing changes; the closed-up reading and its translation;
the stack; the dock's move; what a copy of one of several copies; the bar's copied parts),
`FolderGroupDragTests` (two selected lines lifted and stacked, aimed at and let go in the empty column
as one Place; Escape mid-drag; pasted lines put down in an empty column; the ants on copied lines,
marching, not while carried, back once settled; sheets `folder-group-<dark|light>.png`),
`LineHeightRowsTests` (rows per kind; flips and steps held to the limits; the menu shown again; on a
real menu a press on "+" and on the toggle's row adjust and the menu stays, Left/Right step, a Refresh
in place; `line-height-menu-<look>-<scale>[-fixed-7].png`), `SceneTreeTests.CopiedBlocksWearTheMarchingAnts`
(`edit-copied-<look>.png`).

By hand: in an arranged folder Ctrl+click two lines in different columns and drag one — both come,
stacked; drop them in an empty column and in an empty slot; Escape mid-drag. Select two lines, Ctrl+C,
then Ctrl+V and click an empty column. Right-click a calendar line: flip "Fixed height", press + and −
— the line resizes behind the menu, which stays open. Ctrl+C a widget on the bar and a line in a
folder: the marching ants; Escape once takes them off, again leaves edit mode.

## 152. A folder never scrolls: what does not fit is not shown, and arranged a warning says so (2026-10-12)

The person: "a folder should never show a scrollbar, it should hide the widgets that dont fit and show a
warning sign like the taskbar does it."

- **No folder scroll.** Each list of a folder was as tall as its widgets up to 70 % of the work area and
  scrolled past that on its own — the wheel over it (chained to from a line of items at its end, §109),
  Page Up and Down, a carried line held near its end, its own scroll indicator. All of it is gone
  (`FolderListPlan.MaxScroll`, `FolderPlan.PiecesAt`, `FolderFlyout.ScrollTo`/`ScrollOf`, the
  indicators, `DragScroll`, `FolderDrag.ScrollStep`, `Reveal`). A line of items still scrolls its own
  items (`ListScroll.cs`); at their end the wheel does nothing.
- **Whole lines from the end, list by list** (`FolderFlyout.Build`). A list shows the lines that fit under
  the most, top to bottom; the first that does not, and every line after it, is not shown — a short line
  after a tall one that did not fit too, so the order is never broken. A divider left last goes with
  them (it would part nothing from nothing) and is not counted. A first line taller than the most is
  given the most, and is all the list shows. A line not shown has no box — a card of no height at the
  foot of its list (`FolderPlan.Shows`/`Holds` false): it is drawn nowhere, found by no pointer or key,
  and a line carried under the last one shown lands before it (`FolderDrag.Gap`). Lines carried together
  (§151) the same: a line not shown is never one of them, and the group let go under the last line shown
  lands before the ones not shown, read against the folder as it shows now, not as it would with the
  group closed up (`FolderFlyout.AimGroup`). A height changed in the line's menu (§151) lays the folder
  out again, so lines come and go and the warning with them — against the work area the dock opened
  it in (`FlyoutHost.Work`, which leaves out the display's other bars), not the monitor's: laid out
  again against more room than it opened in, a grown line left nothing out.
  `FolderListPlan.Hidden` names the widgets not shown, in order; `FolderPlan.Hidden` all of them.
- **The warning, as the bar's** (`FolderAddKind.Hidden`). Arranged, a list that leaves widgets out has a
  third round button beside its "+" and its width, the three centred on the list: the edit bar's "not
  shown" button (`EditRail.Warning`) — Windows' warning orange #FC9A03, lighter under the
  pointer, darker pressed, the system highlight in high contrast — its glyph the hidden widget's own for
  one and the warning's for several (`FolderFlyout.HiddenGlyph`), its tooltip naming the one or counting
  them ("3 widgets aren't shown: this column has no room for them", `HiddenTitle`). Its press
  (`FolderFlyoutAction.NotShown`) is the edit bar's: one widget straight to its own menu, several listed
  by name ("This column has no room for these", `Dock.FolderNotShown`, `Topic.FolderHidden`), a row that
  widget's menu — the way to it, as the bar's list is the way to a widget with no block. The button stands
  pressed while its menu does. At rest nothing says so, as the bar says nothing of its own.
- New strings in every language: `dock.folder.notShownOne`, `dock.folder.notShownMany`,
  `dock.folder.noRoomList`.

Tests: `FolderHiddenTests` (which lines go for given work heights, list by list, whole lines from the
end; a tall line and the short one after it; a divider left last; a first line given the most; the
warning arranged only, centred with its pair; its words and glyph; a line carried under the last shown;
the open folder's warning press), `ListScrollTests.TheWheelScrollsALineToItsEndAndNoFurther` (the wheel
at a line's end moves nothing), `DividerStyleTests` (the cards end with the last line shown), and the
older plan tests turned from "scrolls" to "leaves out"; pictures `folder-hidden-<dark|light>-<rest|edit>.png`.

By hand: fill a folder column past the screen's height — no scrollbar, the last widgets not shown, the
column ends with a whole line; the wheel over it does nothing (over a line of items it scrolls the items,
and stops at their end); in edit mode the orange warning beside that column's "+" and width, its tooltip
saying how many, its click the widget's menu or a list of them; at rest no warning.

## 153. Every column of an arranged folder takes a line from another (2026-10-12)

The person: "not every column in the folder edit view is a drop target for the drag and drop" — "it was
an empty one, but only the empty one that is like one column away from the filled ones"; "i was dragging
a widget from another column".

- **The dead one** was the slot right next to the list the carried line was alone in, on either side:
  over it no ghost showed and letting go did nothing. `Folders.Move` (and `MoveGroup`, for lines that
  were their list on their own) read a new list beside the line's own list as its own place, and
  `FolderFlyout.Ghost` agreed — true while a list a line left closed up, false since it stays, an empty
  column (§148, §149): the line was asked to stand one column over.
- **Now a new list is always a move** (`Folders.Move`, `Folders.MoveGroup`, `FolderFlyout.Ghost`, which
  lost its count): the line stands in that slot, its old list staying behind empty, as for a slot
  further out. Only just above or below itself in its own list is still its own place; a group still
  moves nothing where every line would stand where it stands.

Tests: `FolderDropSweepTests` (in the open folder, a line pressed and carried over the middle of every
other column on the screen — list panels, empty lists, slots out to both edges, over the panel and high
above it — for lone lines, empty lists between and beside them and narrow and wide lists, at 100 and
150 %, bottom and top bars; whole lists carried together the same; the place heard, moved as the dock
moves it, puts the line in that very column), and `FolderSlotTests`, `FolderModelTests`,
`FolderGroupMoveTests` turned from "stays" to "moves". Picture `folder-drop-beside-own-<100|150>.png`:
the battery, alone in its list, carried into the slot beside it, its ghost there.

By hand: in edit mode drag a widget that is alone in its column into the empty slot right next to it —
it goes there, its old column left empty; the same from a column of several, and into every other column.

## 154. The accounts' colours on the lines (2026-10-12)

The person: *"in the account settings you should be able to set colors for different calendars, email
inboxes, or contact lists."* Each calendar, inbox and address book wears a colour, picked on the Accounts
page or worked out (the account's own, else Outlook's palette by place; `docs\accounts.md`, "Colours"),
and the lines draw it:

- **The calendar's lines and views** as before — an event in its calendar's colour — now the picked one,
  and a calendar without a colour of its own takes the palette's, never the accent.
- **The mail line** (§16, §95), taller than a row with more than one inbox shown: each message a bar of
  its inbox's colour on the gutter before its sender and subject, 3 px wide and as tall as its lines, as
  an event's (`EventsTile`), its words 11 px past the gutter. One inbox: no bar and no room kept. The
  one-row line shows the newest message as before.
- **The contacts line** (§102) with more than one book shown: each person's glyph in their book's colour;
  one book, and high contrast, the text's.

A colour picked is drawn at once and reads nothing (`AccountSet.Recoloured`). Pictures: `PartColourPictures`.

## 155. A peek leaves every bar in sight (2026-10-12)

The person: *"when hovering over a window it shows the preview of the window which is nice, but it also
hides the karpo taskbar which should not be."* Resting on a card of the window list peeks its window
(`LivePeek.Show`, DWM's ordinal #113): the window in front, everything else faded. The call's third
argument keeps one window, and Karpo passed the bar the card came from; but a bar is often several
windows — each place along an edge and each stacked row its own, and every other display's — and those
faded with the rest. The desktop peek from the Show desktop corner the same.

Now every bar window and the window list are marked `DWMWA_EXCLUDED_FROM_PEEK` as they are made
(`LivePeek.StaysThrough`, in the `DockWindow` and `Preview` constructors), the documented attribute
Explorer's own taskbars and thumbnail list carry: a peek, a card's window's or the desktop's, fades
everything but them. The third argument is still passed. Flyouts, menus and edit bars are not marked:
none is up while a peek shows.

Tests: `PeekExclusionTests` (on a hidden desktop: the list made is marked and DWM took it; what
`StaysThrough` says is DWM's answer). DWM does not read the attribute back, and no test peeks: a peek is
not one desktop's and would fade the person's own screen.

By hand: rest on a card of a window list — every bar on every display stays, the list too, the rest
fades; the same resting on Show desktop. With bars made of places or rows, each of them stays.

## 156. The lasso keeps to one kind; arranged, "Done editing" is the pencil's button (2026-10-12)

The person: *"when a folder is open the lasso select should always only select widgets from the folder,
everywhere actually."* — *"when the folder is closed the same should be true but for the taskbar
widgets"* — *"when already in edit mode there is the edit taskbar stylus still visible in the right click
context menu, it should not be, it should be replaced by a close/done edit mode button. the individual
"done editing" context menu entry should then be removed."*

**The selection is scoped** (`EditScope`, `EditSelection.cs`): it never holds a bar's widgets and a
folder's lines together.

- **The lasso.** While a folder stands open arranged, a drag begun anywhere — the folder's own empty
  room, a bar's or a place's room, any display's dim — selects that folder's lines alone
  (`Dock.BandPressed` routes every band to `ArrangedFolder()`); with none open, the bars' widgets alone,
  as before, never a line. With Ctrl or Shift held, what stays selected besides is of the same kind.
- **Clicks.** A Ctrl+click on one of the other kind (a bar's widget while lines are selected, a line of
  another folder) starts the selection over among its kind; a Shift+click already ran along one kind.
- **Opening and closing.** A folder opening keeps of the bar's selection only the folder itself — the
  one clicked, which wears its ring as before; closing drops its lines (every close comes through
  `Forget`).
- **Acting on it.** Delete and Ctrl+C in the open folder act on its lines alone, never a bar's widget
  selected meanwhile (`ActedOn(key, from)`). Carrying several together was one kind already (a bar's
  `GroupFor`, a folder's own `AlsoPicked`).

**"Done editing" where "Edit taskbar" stands.** Arranged, the pencil of the bar menu's row is "Done
editing" with Windows' Accept check mark (`DoneItem`, `CMD_DONE_EDITING`, `BarRows(…, editing)`), the
same place and size: in every widget's menu (the row's far end, `BarButtonsFor` reads `Arranging`), a
folder line's, the bar's room ("Add", "Done editing", the gear — the row as at rest) and an open folder's
room ("Add", "Done editing", as its lines' row ends). The row of text "Done editing" is gone
(`WidgetAct.DoneEditing` removed); "Select none" stays under the row on one of several selected and on a
room with anything selected. The words are the old `dock.menu.doneEditing`; no new string.

So a widget's menu while arranged, with one selected, is its row of buttons alone — the newer word
over 2026-10-11's "always items that are shown and not just the row", which is kept at rest.

Tests: `EditSelectTests` (`EditScope` — a line's folder from its key, an open folder's lines alone or the
bars' widgets alone, a Ctrl+click of the other kind starting over, opening and closing),
`FolderLineRemoveTests`, `BarMenuRowsTests.ArrangedTheEditButtonIsDoneEditing`, `BarMenuTests` (both
rooms), `MenuFloorTests`, `DockMenusLanguageTests`. Pictures (`MenuModePictures`):
`menu-<widget>-edit-*.png`, `menu-folder-cpu-edit-several-*.png`,
`menu-room-<bar|folder>-edit[-selected]-*.png`.

By hand: arrange the bar, open a folder, drag a rectangle from the bar's empty room, then from the dim
and on another display — only the folder's lines light up; close the folder and drag over the bar and
the folder's button — only bar widgets. Select two lines and Ctrl+click a bar widget — the lines let go.
Right-click a widget, the bar's room and the folder's room — a check mark where the pencil was, which
ends edit mode, and no "Done editing" row.

## 157. Reordering is a drag everywhere in Settings; the toggles stand in the middle (2026-10-12)

The person: *"in the toggle settings the order should be set by dragging and reordering, not by up and
down arrows. this is a general rule, i dont want reorder arrows, everywhere you can reorder something it
should be done with proper drag handles and then you can reorder by drag and drop."* And: *"the toggles
should be vertically centered."*

**One reorderable list** (`Controls\ReorderList.cs`). Every list in Settings that can be put in order is
a `ReorderList`: a `ListView` with reordering on and nothing of a list item's own look (no padding, no
hover or press fill, no selection), its rows the page's own template. Each row wears a `Gripper`, the six
dots Windows 11 draws as a drag handle, at its leading edge, its tooltip "Drag to move, or press Alt+Up
or Alt+Down" (`settings.common.reorder`, also each row's UI Automation help text). A row is dragged by
its gripper or anywhere on it; the rows under it open the gap where it will land, as Windows' own lists
do. Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused row one place, the keyboard staying on it, as in Language &
region's preferred languages. With fewer than two rows nothing drags and the grippers are drawn faded,
never hidden, so nothing moves sideways as a second row comes. The list moves the item in its source for
a drop and a key alike and then raises `Reordered` with the order it shows, each entry a row's place
before; `Logic\Reordering.cs` reads it (`OrderOf`, by the rows themselves; `Moved`; `Apply`) and a drop
where it was, or a drag let go outside, writes nothing. Inside a `SettingsExpander`'s body its rows'
cards take the expander's own row look (its `ItemContainerStyleSelector`, the right inset NestedRows
gives), so a reorderable group looks like any other; the list itself wears an empty style of its own,
as the expander gives every item without one its rows' card style.

Converted, which is every list in Settings with an order:

- **The toggles row's toggles** (`WidgetsPage.xaml`, `IslandOptions.ReorderToggles`): Move up and Move
  down are gone, and their words (`settings.widget.toggles.moveUp`, `moveDown`) with them. The rows are
  the expander's body, the gripper under the expander's icon, then each toggle's glyph and name, and its
  Remove.
- **A folder's faces** (`FolderPage`), dragged already: the same list now, the gripper the shared one
  (`settings.folder.faces.drag` became `settings.common.reorder`), and its Alt+Up / Alt+Down the list's.

Nothing else in Settings has an order to set; the dock's menus have no moves (§144), the desktops
line's desktops are dragged by their grippers (§116) and a folder's lines on the bar (§142).

**The toggles in the middle** (`TogglesTile.Fit`). A toggles line taller than its buttons — an
Automatic line rounded up to whole rows, a Fixed one of more rows — holds them in its middle, the air
shared above and below to a whole px, where §109 stood them at its top: a row of buttons is one control,
not a list read from the top. Rows that do not all fit are the whole ones that do, in the middle of
what they leave. Clicks and hover read the same plan. The switch lines (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the rest)
were centred already: the switch on the name at one row, on the name and the line under it taller.

`ReorderingTests` (first, last, the same place, out of range, rows told apart by identity),
`FolderFacesTests`, `FlyoutLinesTests.TheTogglesStandInTheMiddleOfATallLine`; `ListScrollTests` keeps
every other line at the top. Pictures by hand: `--test reorder <n> <up|down>` moves the shown page's
first reorderable list's row as the keys do (after `--test expand` for one in an expander), e.g.
`--island <folder>/<line> --owner layout:<id> --test expand --test reorder 0 down --shot toggles`. XAML's
renderer cannot picture a drag in flight: the gap opening under a dragged row is the ListView's own.

## 158. An outer empty column is no column at rest; "Add" in a folder's menu adds into the folder (2026-10-12)

The person: *"an empty column is sometimes not viewed as non existing column which leads to the folder
being shifted to the left without actually having widgets on the right side"* and *"when in non edit mode
and i click the add button on a folder widget it goes into edit mode and also opens the add dialog but
the folder closes and therefore i cannot place the widget anywhere"*.

- **At rest an outer empty column takes no room** (`FolderFlyout.Build`). An empty list kept its width at
  rest (§74, §148), so the box round the lists, which the host centres on the folder's button, ran past
  the panels that show: a trailing empty column pushed them left of the button, a leading one right —
  on every opening, every layout after a change and every reopening after edit mode. Now an empty list
  before the first list with widgets or after the last is of no width and no gap at rest, standing at
  the edge of the lists beside it (nothing is drawn or found there anyway): the box is the lists that
  show, centred on the button within the screen's edges as before. One between two lists with widgets
  keeps its width, a spacer. Arranged every column keeps its width, as §149 has it; arranging moves the
  lists with widgets as one by what an outer empty column adds, nothing else (taken back 2026-10-13,
  §164: arranged, an outer empty column hangs off the side of the lists with widgets, which stay where
  they stand at rest). A folder with no widget at all still shows its one empty panel.
- **"Add" in a line's menu over its folder, or a folder's on the bar** (`Dock.AddIntoFolder`). It turned
  edit mode on and opened the add list for the bar — after the widget with the focus — and the pick
  counted as handing the screen away (`PickHandsAway`), so the folder closed after it. Now "Add" stays in
  Karpo; the folder is held through edit mode's coming (`FolderFlyout.HoldOpen`), arranged where it
  stands (`FolderFlyout.Arrange`, as a drag into edit mode does) — opened arranged and picked, from a
  folder's menu, where it was not open, as "Edit folder" does — and its list's own "+" is pressed for
  the add list (`FolderFlyout.PressAdd`, then `AddInFolder`): the line's list (`Dock.ListOfLine`), the
  first for a folder's menu. What is picked lands there, as from that "+". The same while arranged.

Tests: `FolderColumnsTests.AtRestAnOuterEmptyColumnTakesNoRoom` (leading, trailing, several, narrow and
wide, a spacer kept, the same box as the folder without them), `.ArrangingMovesNothingButAnEmptyColumn`,
`.AtRestTheColumnsThatShowAreCentredOnTheButton` (real folders "a | ", " | a", "a |  | ", "a |  | b",
" | a b |  | " centred at rest, after being arranged, and laid out again when a column empties; picture
`folder-rest-centred.png`, a red line down from the button), `FolderMenuTests.AddInALinesMenuAtRestAddsIntoItsFolderLeftOpenAndArranged`.

By hand: a folder with a widget and an empty column right of it — at rest the widget's panel is centred
over the folder's button; the same with the empty column on the left. Right-click a line in an open
folder at rest and press "Add": edit mode comes, the folder stays open arranged, the add list stands by
that column's "+", and the widget picked lands in that column. Right-click a folder on the bar and press
"Add": the folder opens arranged with the add list for its first column.

## 159. A device line's devices can be hidden, in edit mode (2026-10-13)

The person: *"for input and output devices let me hide the ones i dont want, the hiding should work in
the edit mode, it should show all of the devices in edit mode actually and then i can hide them there
which greys them out in edit mode and hides them in normal mode."*

**Hidden is the line's** (`WidgetItem.HiddenDevices`, `hiddenDevices` in the file): the Windows endpoint
ids of the devices an output or a microphone line (`soundOutput`, `soundInput`) does not list. Only
those two lines keep it (`Normalize`, `WidgetItem.HidesDevices`); each id once, and nothing written
where nothing is hidden (`SetDeviceHidden`). It is the line's, not Windows': a hidden device may still
be the one in use, and the volume's line still names it as what it sets.

**At rest** a hidden device is not there: not a row, not in the line's height or its scrolling, not
in the one-row line (the first device not hidden, the one in use first), not in the widget's menu
(`SoundPartTile.Listed`). A line whose every device is hidden says it has none, as one on a PC without
any does.

**Arranged** the line lists every device, in the order it always does, and a hidden one stands greyed
where it would stand — the row's disabled ink, `TextDisabled` — so it can be found and shown again.
A click on a device, the one in use included, hides it or shows it again and is saved at once; the
folder stays open. It is the one click in an arranged folder that a widget keeps for itself (§145
otherwise: a click only selects): Ctrl and Shift still select more, a drag still moves the line, and
a click beside the rows — the heading, the microphones' mute, the air — selects the line as before.
Choosing a device is not edit mode's; nothing is set in Windows.

**A card's own edit click** (`CellIsland`): `Arranged`, which the folder tells every line as it opens,
is arranged and closes (`FolderFlyout.TellArranged`), before anything is measured; `CardEditTarget`,
what of the card's a click edits (0, the default, for nothing, and the click selects); and
`EditClick`, which writes the change into a copy of the widget's settings. The arranged folder asks
the card first (`FolderFlyout.Activate`, `FolderFlyoutAction.EditPart`), and the dock saves what it
wrote as every change of its own (`Dock.EditPart`, as `SetLineHeight`).

`SoundPartsTests`: `AHiddenDeviceIsNotListedAtRest`, `InEditModeEveryDeviceIsListedAndAClickHidesOrShowsIt`,
`HiddenDevicesAreTheDeviceLinesAlone`.

## 160. A widget's target reaches past what it draws (2026-10-13)

*"the widgets on the taskbar have a little padding to the taskbar, i want to keep that padding, but the
clickable area of the widget should actually go all the way out to the taskbar and also to the next
widget of course."*

Fitts, as Windows 11's taskbar has it. What is drawn does not change: the cards keep their inset off
the bar's edges and their gaps, and a hover still lights the drawn widget. Only where the pointer takes
a widget grows, in one place, `Layout.HitTest` (its `Reach`), so the hover, the click, the right-click
menu, the middle click, the wheel, the tooltip, a drag and edit mode's press and drag all follow it.

- **Across** a widget is its whole bar, from the screen's edge — the room a floating bar stands off it
  included — to the bar's inner side, but for the grip along that side, which drags the bar's height.
  On a dock of two rows each row takes its own band, the top row's starting where the main row's ends.
- **Along**, two neighbours share the gap between them at its middle; a separator at rest is no target,
  the room it stands in is shared out between the widgets either side of it. In edit mode a separator is
  a block, its grab zone first, and the gaps are still the widgets'.
- **At the ends** the first widget of the start reaches to the bar's start, the last of the end to its
  end, so a pointer thrown into the screen's corner lands on it.
- **Not** the room between two sections, what a spacer grows to: that stays the bar's, for its menu and
  edit mode's lasso. On a floating bar a dock's widgets reach to the dock's ends and no further; between
  two docks the press is the desktop's, as before.
- Inside a widget the outermost thing takes the room on its side: the first app button, the tray's
  chevron (or first icon), the last cell of a widget of several.

`WidgetReachTests` (islands and floating, four edges, 100 and 150 %, two rows, edit mode); its
`ReachPictures` paints each pixel by what it hits, the drawn blocks outlined
(`widget-reach-horizontal-*.png`, `widget-reach-vertical-*.png`).

## 161. Start, search, the app buttons and the folders down a side (2026-10-13)

*"make sure that all the widgets look good on the side as well. if possible dont try to flip text. go
ahead and check every taskbar widget"* — the bar's own buttons, the app buttons and the folders, checked
by picture on a bar on the left and on the right (`SideKindSheets`, `BusySideKindSheets`). Nothing
needed changing; what a side bar does with each, which the sheets now hold:

- **No text turns.** An app button never has its title across a side bar, whatever "Combine" says: it
  is its icon, as Windows' vertical taskbars were; its running mark and its progress stand on the
  screen's side of it, its badge on the icon's corner. A folder showing its name, the desktop switcher
  and the layout switcher wear their glyph alone in a square; search's box is its button.
- **Across**, every block is the bar's thickness and centred on it, at 28 to 96 DIPs, islands and
  floating. A separator is a line across the bar (on a dock, the gap between two docks); with no line
  it is a marker across the seam in edit mode.
- **Along**, a full bar folds its apps into "…" and gives up widgets as any bar does; past Windows' own
  buttons, which never give way, the tail falls off the end, which a thick bar on a short side meets
  sooner.
- Folders and flyouts from a side bar open beside it (`SideBarSheets`).

`side-kinds-<islands|floating>-<left|right>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`: six bars side by side, each at
rest and edited, the last at 48 DIPs with separators as a new config has them;
`side-kinds-busy-*-150.png`: 720 DIPs long with 30 apps open, at 28, 48 and 96 DIPs.

## 162. The faces of words down a side bar: rows, never turned (2026-10-13) — the date with its month and year, a reading on more rows, never cut, since §598 (2026-11-09)

*"the clock widget when on the side overflows, it should show minutes and hours on a different row.
also make sure that all the widgets look good on the side as well. if possible dont try to flip text."*

Down a bar on the left or the right a face is as wide as the bar is thick and grows along it, so its
text stacks onto rows, at the largest size every row fits the room a line has (`VerticalFit.Room`), one
size per kind of row, stepping down a ladder to 9 DIP (`VerticalFit.Ladder`). Measured on templates, as
everywhere (§12.2): nothing moves as the minutes, the prices or a timer go by.

- **Clock**: the time's parts one over another (`VerticalFit.Parts`): "22" over "58", then the seconds,
  then a 12-hour clock's AM/PM — at every thickness, never one turned line, which was the overflow. Under
  them, a little apart, the label in the quieter ink, in whole words on as many rows as it takes ("San" /
  "Francisco"), and what a timer in the folder has left, "04:59" on a row, its two figures over each other
  where five do not fit across. A label is stepped down, never shortened; only a word wider than the bar
  at 9 DIP is cut.
- **Time and date**: the clock's rows, then the date (the calendar face's stacked date, the day alone on
  a thin bar).
- **Timer, focus, stopwatch**: the glyph over the figures, a running one's "04" over "59"; at rest "25m"
  on a row. The figures were cut ("25…", "00:…") on a narrow bar: they were sized on the bar's width but
  drawn in a narrower room.
- **Stock**: the symbol over the price, each fitted across; the change under them in its colour where it
  fits at 11 DIP, else no change row. The chart behind is the bar's width (it stood a cell end to the
  left), and the price is centred on its real shape.
- **Weather**: the glyph over the temperature, fitted to the line's room (it was fitted to the bar's
  width). The detailed and forecast looks are the simple one down a side.
- **Input indicator**: "ENG" over "CH" sized on this PC's installed codes from the bar's code size down;
  it was sized on "WWW" and fell to 8 px on a thin side bar.
- **Calendar, mail**: as they were — the day's name over the date, the count on the envelope's corner.

`SideFacePictures` holds every face and format at 32 to 128 DIP, 100 and 150 %, on an islands bar and a
floating dock: inside its cell, as wide as the bar, centred across it, and each clock row measured to fit
at 100 and 150 % text; its sheets are `side-faces-<islands|floating>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.
`SideFaceBarSheets` draws them on whole side bars (`side-faces-bar-*.png`).

## 163. The system widgets down a side (2026-10-13)

*"also make sure that all the widgets look good on the side as well. if possible dont try to flip
text. go ahead and check every taskbar widget"*

Down a bar on the left or the right every system widget is as wide as the bar is thick, and its
content fits that width by standing in a column, never by turning: §12.4's third branch (text turned
bottom-to-top) is withdrawn for them.

- **Now playing** (the media preset's face) is the art alone, or the note where there is none, with
  the pause mark on it while the track is paused: one square cell (`MediaIsland.FaceLength`,
  `NowPlayingFaceDrawing.Measure` square down a side). Its title was turned bottom-to-top under the
  art; three or four letters fit across a side bar at any thickness, so the words are the tooltip's,
  the folder's and the flyout's there.
- **The performance readings** (CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network): the glyph over the figure, the glyph
  at the network's and the sound's size beside them (it was capped at 16 DIP and a speck on a wide
  bar), the figure stepped down until the widest the reading reads fits the room across
  (`VerticalFit`, `PerformanceIsland.FaceRoom`), not the bar's whole width.
- **The battery**: the figure under the glyph, stepped down the same way (`BatteryFaceDrawing.Room`).
- **The tray's chevron and the status icons' arrow** point the way their flyout opens, away from the
  bar: up from the bottom, down from the top, right from the left, left from the right
  (`SystemGlyph.Chevron`; a widget is told its bar's edge, `IslandStyle.Edge`, which changes no size).
- **Unchanged, and checked**: the volume and the brightness stand upright with their speaker and sun on
  top, louder and brighter upwards, a drag along the bar and the wheel as across one; the switches, the
  security shield, the status icons, the network, Bluetooth, sound, VPN, hotspot, cast, nearby
  sharing, project, removable devices, clipboard, notifications and mail faces are one square each, a
  count on the glyph's corner as across a bar; a drive is its picture over its letter over its
  capacity bar; several faces on one button stand one under the other.

`SideSystemTests` holds every system widget and preset at 28, 40, 48, 72 and 120 DIPs, 100 and
150 %, dark and light, islands and connected: each cell exactly the bar's width, its ink inside it and
centred across it (a badge measured on its glyph), with its sheets
(`side-system-<thickness>-<dpi>-<dark|light>-<islands|connected>.png`). `SideSystemBarSheets` draws
them in the real scene on a Taskbar and a Dock on the left and on the right
(`side-system-<taskbar|dock>-<left|right>-<36|64>-<dark|light>-150.png`); `TraySquareSheets` the tray
down the left. `MediaSizeTests.DownASideBarItIsTheArtAloneAndNoWords` holds the now-playing face.

## 164. Only the columns with widgets are centred, arranged too (2026-10-13)

The person: *"there is still the bug that even if a column is empty it is part of the container that
gets centered, this should not be . (only for columns that have a widget to their left and right)"*.

- **What is centred on the folder's button is its core** (`FolderPlan.Core`): the lists from the first
  with widgets to the last, an empty one between them included as the spacer it is; the whole box for
  a folder with no widget at all. At rest that was already the panel (§158). Arranged it was not: every
  column keeps its width there (§149), and the host centred the whole panel, so an outer empty column
  pulled the lists with widgets off the button, and entering edit mode moved them.
- **The host places the core** (`FlyoutHost.Core`): centred on the anchor, against an end, kept inside
  the work area, exactly as a panel of the core alone would be — which is where the folder stands at
  rest — and the panel round it wherever that puts it. So no list with widgets moves when edit mode
  begins (arranged in place or opened arranged) or ends; the outer empty columns hang off the sides of
  the core, the slots past them, and a layout after a change does the same (a column emptied, a widget
  put into an outer empty column). At a screen's edge that can be past the edge: an empty column's "+"
  and width button stand centred on what shows of it, as a slot's do, and are not there where too
  little of it shows (`WithSlots`), rather than piled at the edge.
- **A side bar**: the core is centred along the bar by its own height, so the empty columns' rows of
  room arranged no longer shift it. Across, the columns run away from the bar: an empty one on the far
  side hangs off, one on the bar's side has no room to hang into and pushes the core out.

Tests: `FolderColumnsTests.OnlyTheColumnsWithWidgetsAreCentredAndArrangingMovesNoneOfThem` (real
folders "a | (e)", "(e) | a", "(e) | a | (e) | (e)", "a | (e) | b", "(e) | a | (e) | b | (e)" on bottom
and top bars, at the screen's middle and at both ends, on left and right bars, narrow, medium and wide
empty columns: the core centred, each list with widgets the same box on the screen at rest, arranged in
place, opened arranged and at rest again; the outer ones and the slots outside it; pictures
`folder-core-<shape>-<edge>-<anchor>-<arranged|rest>.png`, a red line through the button),
`.ArrangedTheBlockFollowsTheColumnsThatHaveWidgets`, `.AtRestAnOuterEmptyColumnTakesNoRoom` (the core),
`FolderSlotTests.ALineDroppedInASlotIsLaidOutAsReopeningShowsIt`.

By hand: a folder with a widget and an empty column right of it, at rest and then in edit mode — the
widget's column stays over the button, the empty column and the slots beside it to the right; the same
with the empty column on the left, and with an empty column between two filled ones (that one is
centred with them). A folder near the screen's end: arranged, nothing with widgets moves.

## 165. The tray grows and shrinks with a dragged icon (2026-10-13)

*"the system tray widget should actually grow or shrink when i drag an icon from the more tray or vice
versa, right now the other tray icons just get pushed off the side."*

While a notification icon is dragged, the tray's block is as long as the icons it will have once it is
let go (`TrayDrags.MoreFor`, `Content.TrayMore`, `Layout.TrayMoreOf`):

- **In from the overflow**: over the tray, the block grows by one cell; the icons after the gap move on
  by a whole cell into it, and the bar makes room as it does for any widget whose size changes (the
  neighbours move, a full bar folds its app buttons into "…" first). The icons used to move half a cell
  either way inside a block that kept its length, so the first and the last went past its ends, under
  the chevron and the next widget.
- **Out behind the chevron**: over the chevron or the open overflow, a tray that shows the icon is a cell
  shorter and its other icons close up; the held icon follows the pointer over the chevron. *(§172: it
  follows the pointer anywhere, in a window of its own, and the tray keeps its place out of sight. At the
  bar's end the last icon's place at rest is past the bar there, and it wasn't drawn at all while the
  tray was shorter; it is now (`Layout.TrayIconRect`). The overflow, open for the whole drag, moves
  with the chevron as the tray grows and shrinks: `Flyout.Reanchor`.)*
- **Between the two** (the room between the bar and the overflow) the tray keeps what it last showed, so
  it doesn't grow and shrink back on the way (`TrayDragging.Aim`). Along the tray nothing changes size.
- **Let go**: the new length stays, the tray then having that many icons. **Called off** (Escape, a drop
  elsewhere, back into the overflow it came from): the tray is as it was, laid out again.
- The pointer is read against the tray as long as its icons, not with the cell the drag gave it, so the
  next widget's first cell is not taken for the tray's end (`TrayDrags.OnLayout`).
- **A tray of a set size** keeps it: the icons pushed past its room fade out while the gap stands, as
  the ones it has no room for go behind the chevron at rest (`Layout.TrayHolds`).
- Down a side bar the same, along its length.

`TrayDragRoomTests` holds the length in, out, after the drop and after a cancel, on the bottom and both
sides at 100 and 150 %, a set size, and the pointer read the same on a grown tray. `TrayGrowSheets`
draws it (`tray-grow-<rest|nogrow|in|dropped|out>-<bottom|side>-<100|150>.png`).

## 166. No widget has a least size of its own (2026-10-13)

*"remove the min size constraints on the widgets too."*

The person sets the size; nothing raises it. A size a person can set is a folder line's height
(§76; along the bar there is none, §12.6), and its rows are now **one to the kind's most** for every
kind: `ListWidget.Heights` (a least and a most) is `ListWidget.Tallest` (the most alone), and
`LineHeight.Limits` is `(1, Tallest)`. Settings' rows field (`SizeCard`, `HeightChoice.Limits`) and
the strip at the line (`LineHeightRows`) step from one. A new line still starts where its kind
starts (`Rows`, or Automatic up to its range), the measured height, so nobody who sets nothing sees a
change; a file's height is read as before, and one under an old least is now kept as it is (a month
of eight rows is eight, of one row one). No shape bump, nothing reset.

The kinds that had a least over one, and what each draws given less:

| Kind | Was | Given less |
|---|---|---|
| month | 8 | the whole weeks that fit, the picked day's week among them (else today's), then without the weekdays' row, at its shortest the title and arrows centred (`MonthTile.Placed`) |
| timeHeader | 3 | the air gives way to 4 DIP, then the date goes, then the time steps down to the row it has (`TimeHeaderTile.Lay`) |
| weatherHours | 4 | the conditions' glyphs go, then the day's line alone fills the line, no words (`DayGraph.Bare`) |
| weatherDays | 2 | the days whose rows fit whole; in one row today alone, its row the line's height |
| screenTimeChart | 3 | a smaller ring; too short for the least ring, no ring: the total and the day alone |
| powerMode, projection, nearbySharing | 5, 6, 8 | the page's title, and the controls that fit whole under it; a control cut by the line is neither drawn nor pressed (`QuickPageTile.Shown`) |
| dayView, weekView, yearView | 5 | the notes under the hours go before the hours shrink under 96 DIP; the week's headings only where they fit whole; the hours and the months still scroll in what is left (`CalendarLayout.Window`) |

Three mosts were raised, not lowered: a page cut at its most is now its whole rows and no more, and
measured at 225 % text the power mode needs 11 rows (it had 8), Win+P's modes 13 (9), nearby sharing
20 (11) — the table of §140 said they held it there, and they held half.

Kept, and why: the **most** of every kind (where it draws nothing more); the bar's own sizes, which
nobody sets (`WidgetSize.MinCells` is a kind's measurement on the bar, §12.6); the floor of one row,
so no line is zero or unclickable; a divider, a heading and a list row, which have no height to set;
the list widths (narrow, medium, wide), which are a folder's columns and not a widget's size.

Tests: `NoFewestTests` (every kind's limits start at one; each kind above, at every height under its
old least, is given exactly those rows and its own drawing, without the folder's clip, keeps its ink
inside them), `HeightLimitsTests` (a month of one row and of eight, nearby sharing of three, read in
place), `HeightLimitsPicturesTests` (`height-limits-<kind>.png` from one row, the weather's with a
forecast). By hand: set a month, a time header, the weather's hours and a power mode to one and two
rows in a folder; the field in Settings and the strip at the line go down to 1.

## 167. A first start gets Windows 11's taskbar, at the left (2026-10-13, 2026-10-14)

The person: "for the default layout when a user first starts karpo, show the date and time over each
other like windows does it and also group the notifications functionality with the bell there as
well. same with the other stuff ... so that it matches the windows 11 default behaviour / layout as
close as possible." Until now a new bar was the person's own "Default" of 2026-10-11 (Task view
beside Start, the search box between separators, Bluetooth, the sound, the battery, the clock, the
date and the bell each a button of their own). It is now Windows 11 24H2/25H2 out of the box,
`Sections.DefaultLayout`, button by button, with two changes the person asked for the next day:
"actually the start should be on the left together with the app pins and app widget as a default.
although this is not default windows behaviour. center should be empty by default", Search and Task
view kept between Start and the apps ("keep them there"), and "dont actually show the widgets
button":

| Section | Entry | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| start | Start, Search, Task view, the pins, the open apps | Windows' order, the search box (`ShowBox`) right after Start; no separators, so one run; at the left whatever Windows' own alignment (`TaskbarAl` is no longer read) |
| middle | nothing | the section is empty, not a spacer: a bar has none |
| end | the "^" and the tray, the pen menu and the touch keyboard (where the PC has them), the status icons | as before |
| end | the input indicator | the keyboard preset, kept though Windows shows its own only with two layouts (2026-10-10) |
| end | quick settings | the **quick settings preset** (`quickPanelGroup`): the network, the speaker and, on a PC with one, the battery on one button; Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the toggles, brightness, the volume and the battery inside |
| end | the clock button | the new **notification center preset** (`clockNotificationsGroup`): the time over the date (`dateTime`, the seconds as Windows' clock has them) with the bell and its count to their right; inside, one column of two cards, the notifications (Fill, §171: as tall as they are, up to what the calendar leaves under the folder's 70 %) over the calendar's header, month and focus session, no footers: what Windows' clock opens |
| end | show desktop | as before |

No Widgets button and no weather in its place (on 2026-10-13 the weather preset stood there, at
the far left, or before the tray where Windows' taskbar was left-aligned; with the buttons always at
the left there is one default, not two). No Bluetooth, sound, battery, clock, calendar or
notifications button of its own: Windows' taskbar has none; they are inside the two buttons.

What was added: the preset `clockNotificationsGroup` (combined, in the add list's Time after Clock &
calendar, its words in every language) and the weather face's fourth look `conditions`, Windows'
