Widgets button's (two lines at the largest of the text's sizes the card holds two of, as the
date-and-time face finds its own; the words' room the widest the language has for any weather, cut
at 140 DIP, so the face never moves; the simple look on a bar too thin for two lines and down a
side). Both stay in the add list; the weather preset itself keeps the simple look.

**Backward compatible.** Only a config without layouts is given it (`Config.FirstLayout`, which
`DefaultLayout`, `--renew-layout`, a new layout in Settings and the preset layout start from): a file
that has a bar reads and writes exactly as it did (`DefaultsTests.AnExistingBarIsLeftAsItIs`). No
shape bump, no migration. The presets are the person's still (`PersonsPresetsTests`), but a new bar
is no longer held to their "Default" (`ANewBarIsThePersonsDefault` went).

Windows' behaviours Karpo has a setting for were already Windows' defaults: the bar holds its space
(no auto-hide), buttons combined with labels hidden (`Combine`, read from Windows), the search box,
every open window on every bar an apps widget stands on (Windows' "all taskbars").

What can't match: the bar wears islands (2026-10-08, "bars are islands"), so Start, the search box,
the apps and the system corner stand on cards where Windows has one plain strip; the battery face
says its percentage, which Windows keeps for the tooltip; show desktop is a one-cell button, not
Windows' sliver; quick settings has no accessibility tile, gear or edit pencil.

Tests: `DefaultBarTests` (the sections button by button, without a battery, on a tablet, the same
left- or centre-aligned; the two buttons and their faces), `DefaultsTests` (a first start's
arrangement through `Config.Repair` and `AddDisplay`, and an existing bar untouched),
`CombinedPresetTests` (the recipe, and that it stands on a 1440p screen at 150 % with every line at
its most). Pictures: `WindowsDefaultSheets` (`windows-default-<look>-<scale>-<1920|2560>.png` and
`-corner-`, on a saved forecast, a battery at 76 %, seven notifications, three apps and four tray
icons) and `NotificationCenterPictures` (`windows-default-clock-flyout-<1080|1440>-<scale>.png`, §171). By hand: start
Karpo once with `KARPO_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at an empty folder and compare the bar with Windows' own;
click the clock and quick settings.

## 168. Fill: a folder line that takes the room its column has left (2026-10-14)

The person: "can you add a new size that you can give a widget which is grow / take up remaining
space which makes it grow to fill the full space", then "on the bar the widgets should not be able to
grow. only in the folder i meant". So a third height for a folder line, beside Automatic and Fixed
(§76); nothing on the bar changes.

**What it does** (`FolderFlyout.Build`). Every line is laid out as before, a Fill line at its
content's height held to one row and its kind's most (`LineHeight.Limits`); where a list is then past
the most a folder may be its Fill lines give way first, down to one row (§171), and the lines that
still do not fit are left out as before (§152). *Changed by §172:* a folder with a Fill line may be
all the room beside its bar (to the work area's far end less the gap and the margin), and that room
is what each list with Fill lines fills to — no longer the folder's tallest list. In such a list the
room left is shared among its Fill lines
equally, in px (whole px, the first a px more where it does not divide; `FillShares`), each up to its
kind's most (none for a kind without one of its own, §172); what one cannot take goes to the others,
what none can take stays empty at the list's end. The other lists keep their heights. An empty
column's slot arranged is never what is filled to,
so edit mode moves nothing (§149, §164). The plan is pure, so a widget added to or taken from any
list, a width or a height changed, re-flows the Fill lines as the folder lays itself out again. A
Fill line draws its kind at the height it is given, as a Fixed one does: a row-adaptive kind (the
agenda, notifications, a forecast's days) shows more, one that cannot use more stays top-aligned in
its card (the month's six weeks with room under them).

**In the file.** `"fill": true` on the line's `height`, written only where it is on: a file from
before reads as it did and writes back unchanged, and a build from before reads a Fill line as the
mode and rows it keeps under it. Going back to Automatic or Fixed finds those rows. No shape bump.

**Where it is set.** The line's right-click menu: its height rows are a radio trio, "Automatic
height" (only where the kind's content varies, §140), "Fixed height" and "Fill remaining space", each
picked without the menu closing (§151; `FlyoutControl.Radio`, Windows 11's radio button at the row's
end), then the "Height" stepper, greyed under Fill so the menu keeps its size. Settings' height card:
the dropdown has the same modes (Fixed and Fill where there is no Automatic); under Fill the rows
field is hidden and the header says "Fills the remaining space".

Tests: `FolderFillTests` (the share, a kind's most, the cap and the lines left out, several lists, the
tallest's Fill lines, a list changing beside one, rest and arranged alike, and the open folder
re-flowing), `LineHeightRowsTests`, `HeightChoiceTests` (the modes, the file, an old file). Pictures:
`folder-fill-<dark|light>-<100|150>-<rest|edit>.png`, `line-height-menu-<look>-<scale>-fill.png`. By
hand: give a month and an agenda Fill in a column beside a taller one, add and remove widgets in the
taller one, open edit mode, and pick the modes from the line's menu and from Settings.

## 169. The bell's count is never cut (2026-10-14)

The person: "for the notifications widget in the taskbar the number of notifications badge gets
clipped off". On the first start's clock button (§167) the bell stands last, and its count's pill
overhangs the bell's top-right corner by three fifths of its width. The button kept only its usual
end room (`max(Edge, 6 px)`) after the bell, and `GlyphBadge` held the pill inside a cell's square
about the bell's middle rather than inside the button's real cell, so the button's clip cut the
pill's right side: a sliver at "7", a third of "99+". The same held for the mail's count and stale
mark and the removable and hotspot counts wherever such a face stood before another face or at a
button's end, and for a lone square whose button is narrower than a cell.

Now, as on Windows 11, where the count is a small accent pill at the bell's top-right, whole inside
the button:

- A face measures a `Trail` (`FaceSize.Trail`): how far past its square its widest mark stands
  across a bar — the "99+" pill for the bell (only where it shows the count) and the mail (or its
  stale mark), the "9+" pill for the removable and hotspot faces; nothing down a side, where the
  pill stands across the bar's width. The folder's button keeps it after the face, before the next
  face, the name or its end (`FolderIsland.Parts`, `FaceBoxes`), so the button is one width
  whatever the count. A lone square with no name keeps its one cell and its glyph in the middle.
- The count is held a pixel inside the button's real cell (`FaceContext.Room`), not a guessed one:
  where the room is short (a lone bell at "99+", the clock button down a 48-DIP side) the pill moves
  onto the glyph rather than off the button.

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.TheBellsCountStaysWholeInsideItsButton` paints the default clock button, the
bell alone and the bell before the time and date with and without a count, at 1, 9, 10, 99 and
"99+", 100 to 175 %, 28 to 160 DIP, across and down a bar; the count's ink (the pixels that differ)
must be its whole pill, a pixel inside the cell, within the bell's room. `BellBadgeBarSheets` draws
a first start's bar at 9 and "99+", islands and connected, at the bottom and down the left, 28, 48
and 72 DIP, 100 and 150 %, light and with the hover on the button, and holds the button's block in
the bar's panel. Pictures: `bell-badge-cells.png`, `bell-badge-bar-*.png`.

## 170. Quick settings does what Windows' does: a line's ">" opens its page (2026-10-14)

The person: "can you functionality do the same stuff as you are able to do with the original win11
design? i dont think so. (switching wifi etc). fix that, you should also be able to do the same
functionality wise." Karpo had nearly every page Windows' quick settings has — the Wi-Fi networks
with connect, the key, "Connect automatically", hidden and enterprise networks, disconnect and
properties (§88); the Bluetooth devices with connect, disconnect, remove and their battery; the
sound's devices and mixer; the VPN's connections; nearby sharing; the hotspot — but each as a line of
a preset of its own. The first start's quick settings button (§167) held only the switches, and a
line in a folder had no way to open anything (§15), so Windows' ">" did not exist there.

**A line's page** (`Karpo.Core\FolderPages.cs`, `FolderIsland.Pages.cs`). Windows' tile switches
and its ">" swaps the panel for a page with a back arrow; Karpo's folder does the same, in place:
the line's column becomes the page — the other columns stay — and goes back on the page's back
arrow, on Escape, when the folder is arranged and when it closes. It is no popup, so §15 stands: the
folder is what it was, showing other lines for a while. The page's lines are made as it opens (keyed
`…/page/…`, their sources started as any line's) and dropped as it goes; nothing of a page is in the
config, a page's lines take no drag and have no menu, and the config changing under an open page
keeps it where its line still is. The table:

| Line | Its page |
|---|---|
| Wi-Fi (`wifiSwitch`) | the `wifi` line (networks, connect, key, hidden network, disconnect, properties, refresh) and the Wi-Fi actions |
| Bluetooth (`bluetoothSwitch`) | the `bluetooth` line (paired devices, connect/disconnect, remove, battery) and Bluetooth's actions, Add device among them |
| The volume (`soundVolume`) | "Sound output": the Output and Input dropdowns (§178), spatial sound, the volume mixer, the sound's actions |
| Accessibility | magnifier, color filters, narrator, mono audio, live captions, sticky keys, and its settings |
| VPN, nearby sharing, the mobile hotspot | their connections, their three modes, their network and devices, each with its footer |
| Cast, Project (`cast`, `project`, §179) | the wireless displays (fixed 8 rows) with Display and Add device; Win+P's four modes with Display |

A quick settings page has its own title row with the radio's switch, so its back arrow stands
before that title (`PageLayout.Back`, `QuickPageTile.Back`); a page of other lines starts with its
head, the arrow and the title on a quick settings title row's height (`PageHeadTile`). The arrow
pressed inside a page's own widget is done on the folder's next news, so no widget is disposed under
the press that let it go.

**The ">"**. A switch's line with a page, in an open folder and not on a page itself, ends in
Windows' chevron past a hairline, the glyph on the trailing gutter: the line switches, the chevron
opens the page, each lit by itself under the pointer as a split tile is (`SwitchIsland.PageTarget`). (Since §177 only the switch switches; the rest of the line, the chevron with it, is the page's.)
Accessibility switches nothing, so the whole of its line is the page. The volume's line has the
chevron at the slider's end (`SoundPartTile`), as 24H2's volume row has it. Brightness has none
(Windows' has none either). The toggles row stays icons only (§68, "no details/arrow").

**Three new switches** for the accessibility page, toggles on the bar and lines in a list, in the
add list in an Accessibility folder under Screen and sharing and among Quick settings' toggles
(`QuickSettings\Services\Assistive.cs`): the **magnifier** (on while its window stands; started by
Magnify.exe, stopped with Win+Esc), the **narrator** (on while Windows says a screen reader runs;
Win+Ctrl+Enter both ways) and **sticky keys** (SPI_GETSTICKYKEYS / SPI_SETSTICKYKEYS, told to every
window as Settings does). The narrator's and sticky keys' changes come as WM_SETTINGCHANGE, which the
dock now hands to the switches; the magnifier is read again a moment after a click. All three reach
Windows through `IAssistiveTools`, which the tests replace.

**The foot: Windows' pencil and gear**, a premade actions line `quickActions` (Edit, All settings):
Edit arranges the folder where it stands, its bar's edit mode on, as a line dragged at rest does
(`IslandView.Arrange`, `FolderFlyout.ArrangeAsked`) — Karpo's "add, remove, reorder tiles" — and All
settings opens Windows' Settings (`ms-settings:`), as Windows' gear does.

**A new quick settings** (`quickPanelGroup`, only a new folder or a first start; an existing config
is untouched): Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and accessibility, each with its ">"; airplane mode, energy saver and
night light; brightness and the volume with its ">"; under a divider the battery (where the PC has
one) and the foot. Windows' default tiles; the rest of its tiles (the hotspot, do not disturb, which
Windows keeps in the notification center, the VPN, cast, nearby sharing, project, rotation lock,
live captions) are added through Edit. The person's own quick settings folders keep what they hold
and get the chevrons on their Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, accessibility, VPN, nearby sharing, hotspot and
volume lines. §167's "quick settings has no accessibility tile, gear or edit pencil" no longer holds.

**What Windows does that this does not.** Cast's displays connect only in Windows' own Cast panel (no
public API for an unpackaged app, §114): the cast line opens it per display. Studio effects and
auto-brightness or HDR have no public switch. The media card over the panel while something plays: a
folder's line never takes no room, so it is the media center preset's, not the default's. The clock
button's calendar cannot be folded away, and the focus session's one-row line steps its minutes with
the wheel and its menu (its two-row line has the steppers).

Tests: `QuickPagesTests` (the page table; a page standing in its column and going back by the
arrow, Escape and the folder closing, the config unchanged; the chevrons' targets and what a click on
each does; the volume's; the foot's Edit and gear; the three switches on made-up tools, nothing
reaching this PC). Pictures: `quick-pages-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`, the default quick settings and
its Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound and accessibility pages. By hand: open quick settings on the bar, click
each ">" and back; connect to a secured network by typing its key; connect a paired headset; choose
another output; switch the magnifier, the narrator and sticky keys on and off; press Edit.

## 171. The notifications grow: Fill in the clock button, and a Fill line gives way (2026-10-14)

The person, after Fill (§168): "then you can actually make the notifications widget to grow." The
first start's clock button (§167) held its notifications to five rows, Automatic, so the whole would
stand on a 1080p screen at 150 %. Windows 11's notification center is as tall as its notifications,
up the screen, over a calendar that stays where it is.

**The preset.** `clockNotificationsGroup`'s notifications line is Fill (its five rows kept under it,
for going back to Automatic). It is the folder's one column, so it is the tallest, and §168 gives a
tallest list's Fill line nothing: it stands at its content, held to its kind's most — as many
notifications as there are, the empty state ("No new notifications") at its own height. Fill alone
could not keep the calendar on: a list past the 70 % left out its last lines, the focus session and
the month first.

**A Fill line gives way** (`FolderFlyout.Build`). Where a list is past the most a list may be (70 % of
the work area), its Fill lines give back what it is over, shared as the room is shared
(`FillShares`), each down to one row, before any line is left out; past that the lines that do not fit
are left out as before. So the notifications grow with their count up to what the calendar leaves
under the 70 %, and scroll under their count past it (`ListScroll.cs`); the calendar is never pushed
off. A list beside it, and a folder whose lists all fit, are as they were; the one change for a folder
of the person's is a Fill line in a list that was leaving lines out, which now shrinks to keep them
(it stood at its content before).

**Only a new one.** The preset is read where a folder is made (the add list, a first start's
`Config.FirstLayout`); a clock button already in a file keeps the height it has. No migration.

What it gave: at 1440p the notifications got up to 561 DIP at 100 % and 223 DIP at 150 %; at 1080p 309
DIP at 100 %, but at 150 % the calendar alone took 411 of the 470 DIP the 70 % left, so the
notifications were their count's line and a sliver, scrolling. *Superseded by §172:* a folder with a
Fill line is no longer held to the 70 %; the notifications reach the top of the work area as Windows'
do, and give way only past that.

Tests: `FolderFillTests` (a Fill line giving way first, two giving way equally, to one row and then
lines left out), `CombinedPresetTests.CombinedGroupPicturesAndFit` (every combined preset on the
1440p screen at 150 % with every growing line at its most: nothing left out), and
`SceneTreeTests.NotificationCenterPictures`: none, three and twelve notifications on 1080p and
1440p at 100 and 150 %, nothing left out, the notifications at their content or the folder at the
70 %, `windows-default-clock-flyout-<1080|1440>-<100|150>.png`. By hand: start Karpo on an empty
`KARPO_CONFIG_DIR`, open the clock with none, a few and many notifications, and scroll them.

## 172. A dragged tray icon opens the overflow and follows the pointer anywhere (2026-10-14)

*"when starting to drag a tray icon it should open the more tray icons area immediately, even if it is
empty, so that you are able to drop the tray icon in there. the tray icon you should be able to not
only move around in one axis but actually in both."*

As Windows 11's notification area does it:

- **The overflow opens as the drag starts** (`TrayDragOverflow`, `Dock.KeepOverflowOpen`): past the
  drag's threshold (a click opens nothing, `TrayClicks`), from the tray the icon was taken from, on
  its usual side. Where nothing is hidden the chevron comes with the drag a layout later (§30), and the
  overflow opens from it then. It used to open only for an icon rested on the chevron for Windows'
  hover time, and never with nothing behind it.
- **Empty, it is one empty cell** to let the icon go in; with icons, a cell more than they need, so the
  place after the last is inside the panel (`Flyout.SpareTiles`, only while a drag from the bar has it
  open). A drop anywhere in it hides the icon there (`TrayDrags.InOverflow`).
- **It stands open for the whole drag** and moves with the chevron as the tray grows and shrinks (§165,
  `Flyout.Reanchor`). When the drag ends (let go anywhere, or called off by Escape or a right press)
  it closes if the drag opened it; one open before the drag (the drag began in it) stays. A drop out
  of the overflow onto the bar still closes it, as choosing an icon in it does.
- **The icon follows the pointer in both directions**, held by its middle, across the bar and up into
  the overflow, drawn in a window of its own (`TrayCarry`, `TrayCarrying.Corner`), as a widget carried
  in edit mode is. It used to move only along the bar, inside its tray, and inside the overflow's
  panel. The bar keeps its place out of sight where the gap stands (`Scene.TrayDragIn`), so a drop
  there finds it in its new place and a cancel brings it home; the overflow keeps the place of one
  taken from it empty (`Flyout.DropGap`). The gap shows where it would land, on the bar and in the
  overflow, as before.

Tests: `TrayOverflowDragTests` (the overflow opened at once, empty or not, waiting for the chevron,
closed after unless it was open, not reopened once closed by something else; the carried icon's
corner in both axes), `TrayCarrySheets` (the bar, the overflow and the carried icon in one picture,
`tray-carry-<between|empty|into>-<bottom|side>-<look>-<100|150>.png`: the icon up off the bar beside an
empty overflow, over its one cell with the tray closed up, and over the spare cell of an overflow with
two icons; the overflow moved over the shorter tray's chevron; the last icon drawn in its closed-up
place at the bar's end). By hand: drag a tray icon with nothing hidden: the overflow opens at once,
empty; let it go there, then drag it back out onto the bar; press Escape and a right button mid-drag;
a click on an icon opens no overflow.

## 173. Fill fills all the room: up to the top of the screen (2026-10-14)

The person: "fill remaining space should actually fill all the remaining space, it does not, the
notifications should go up to the top of the screen in the default layout for example". Under §168 a
Fill line grew only to the folder's tallest other column, so in the clock button's one column
(§171) it gave nothing, and the 70 % (§152) left the notifications some 55 DIP at 1080p and 150 %.

**The rule** (`FolderFlyout.Build`). A folder with a Fill line may be all the room beside its bar:
from the anchor and its 12-DIP gap to the work area's far end less the placement's margin (8 DIP, 12
for a flyout at the bar's end, as the clock's is) — `FlyoutPlacement.Room`, what Windows'
notification center reaches up to; along a side bar the work area's height less a margin at each end.
Each list with Fill lines is that tall: its lines laid out first, then the room left shared among
its Fill lines as before (`FillShares`), each up to its kind's most; a kind with no most of its own
(`ListWidget.Tallest` left at the field's 32 rows: the notifications, an agenda, mail) has none as a
Fill line, so it reaches the top of a 4K screen too; room none can take stays empty at the list's
end. The other lists keep their heights, lined up on the bar's side as ever. The folder's most is
then that room for every list: lines that do not fit even there give way and are left out as in §171
and §152, and where lines are left out the Fill line takes back the sliver under the last one shown.
A folder without a Fill line keeps the 70 %. The live folder takes the room from its placement
(`FlyoutHost.Placement`), for showing, laying out again and dragging alike; a plan drawn without one
(a test, a picture) takes `FlyoutPlacement.Room(workHeight, scale)`, the clock's placement on a
bottom bar. A sheet (`ListFormPictures.Plan`), whose work area is taller than any screen so nothing
is left out, fills to a 1440p screen's room.

What it gives: the default clock flyout is 1008 DIP at 1080p and 100 %, 648 at 150 %, 1368 at 1440p
and 100 %; the notifications take everything over the date, the month and focus, whatever their
count — the empty state in a tall card, as Windows' "No new notifications" stands — and scroll under
their count past it. The calendar under them is whole every time.

Tests: `FolderFillTests` (the room, a kind with no most, the lists beside, a placement's room on each
bar, giving way under the room), `CombinedPresetTests.CombinedGroupPicturesAndFit` (a Fill preset up
to the room), `SceneTreeTests.NotificationCenterPictures` (none, three and twelve on 1080p and 1440p at
100 and 150 %: the folder the room, every other line as it would be unfilled). Pictures:
`windows-default-clock-flyout-<1080|1440>-<100|150>.png`, `folder-fill-<look>-<scale>-<rest|edit>.png`.
By hand: open the clock on a first-start config with none, a few and many notifications; give a line
Fill in a folder of two columns, on a bottom, a top and a side bar.

## 174. A new bar's separators and dividers are the person's (2026-10-16) — a new bar has no separator since §511 (2026-11-05)

The person: "ive added some dividers to the default layout and folders. i want you to apply them to
the default layout that spawns on a new installation." Their "Default" holds §167's bar with two
separators and one divider, and `Sections.DefaultLayout` and the presets it uses now have them where
they put them:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| the bar's end | a separator after the tray (before the pen menu and the touch keyboard where a PC has them, then the status icons), and one between quick settings and the clock button: three cards, the tray's icons, the keyboard with quick settings, the clock with show desktop |
| the clock button (`clockNotificationsGroup`) | the divider between the notifications and the calendar's header, as it was |
| the input indicator (`keyboardGroup`) | none, as it was |
| quick settings (`quickPanelGroup`) | none on a PC without a battery: the foot (Edit, All settings) right under the volume. The divider before the battery now needs a battery and goes with it; a laptop keeps it |

Only dividers and separators were taken over. What else their quick settings and clock button hold
differently was left as the presets make it: airplane mode, energy saver and night light three
switch lines (no labels) where the preset has the row of toggles; the notifications' Fill line fixed
at five rows where the preset's is automatic.

**Backward compatible.** Only a new bar (`Config.FirstLayout`) and a new quick settings folder are
made so; every existing layout and folder keeps what it has. The layout of every ready-made folder
(`PresetLayout`) still drops a new bar's separators before adding its own.

Tests: `DefaultBarTests` (the end section with both separators, `TheFoldersDividersAreThePersons`),
`DefaultsTests`, `InputButtonsTests`, `ResetTests`, `CombinedPresetTests`, `QuickPagesTests`.
Pictures: `windows-default-*.png`.

## 175. The add list opens where it has room (2026-10-16)

The person: "when the add button is all the way on the top of a screen the size of the flyout add
widgets is squished. then you cannot see anything except for the search box". A "+" of a bottom bar's
folder grown to the top of the display (§173) opened the add list upwards, away from the bar, into
the few pixels over it: the search field and one row. Nothing ever looked at the other side.

**The rule** (`FlyoutPlacement.Roomiest`, from `Flyout.Open` for the add list and every top-level
menu, never a submenu). It wants its whole height — its title, search field and tree, to the 70 %
every panel stops at — and needs its search field and eight rows (`Flyout.RoomiestRows`), all of it
where it is shorter. Away from the edge where that side has what it wants; else the other side, where
that has it; else the roomier side, where that has what it needs; else over the anchor
(`FlyoutPlacement.Over`), centred on it across the edge too (`OverStart`), with the work area's
whole height less a margin at each end. Off a side bar it is the width that has to fit, decided once
the columns are known. A flipped placement is the placement from then on: the host places, slides and
shadows it from its new edge, the search's relayouts keep it, and the rows' room is
`FlyoutPlacement.Room` of it (`Depth` across a side bar). One over the anchor is not pushed under
the edit bar (`ClearOf`), which would put it off the display.

Tests: `FlyoutRoomTests` (anchors at the top, bottom, either side and corners of a 1080p display at
100 % and a 1440p one beside it at 150 %: it stays with room, flips, takes the roomier side, stands
over the anchor inside the work area), `AddListRoomPictures` (the add list from a top "+" opening
upwards: it opens down, whole). Pictures: `add-list-top-<middle|corner>-dark-<150|100>.png`.
By hand: grow a bottom bar's folder to the top (a Fill line), arrange it and press its top "+"; the
same with a top bar's folder and its bottom "+".

## 176. Every tray icon slides on from where it is (2026-10-16)

The person: "not all of the tray icons get animated on their move, some just jump". A new scene slid
every icon that moved from where the last scene had it, but only an icon a drag had moved kept a glide
(`TrayGlide`) to go on from (`Scene.CarryTray`). The rest — the icons a tray grown or shrunk by a cell
for a drag moved (§172), the chevron coming with a drag, the icons an app's icon coming or going
moved — slid with nothing to say where they were: the drag's next move, which retargets each icon's
glide, started theirs from their new places, so they jumped there and slid back; and a scene laid out
again while they slid (icons change in bursts) started them from where they were going.

**The rule** (`TrayGlide.TakenUp`). Every icon a new scene moves along the bar is taken up where it
was, settling into its place as the scene slides it, whatever moved it; one that stays or changes line
is not. Moves within a drag go on from there (`GlideTray`), as do the scenes after. An icon pushed past
a tray of a set size fades as it slides behind the chevron, and back (`FadeTo`), where it vanished; the
one the pointer carries still goes at once.

Tests: `TrayDragsTests` (taken up along either axis, not when still or across, a gap opened from a
taken-up glide goes on from it), `SceneTreeTests.TrayIconsMovedByANewSceneGoOnFromWhereTheyAre` (a tray
at the bar's end grown for an icon from the overflow, then the gap after its first: the others stand
still, 100 % and 150 %; it failed before). Pictures: `tray-glide-frames-<100|150>.png`, nine frames 25 ms
apart. By hand: drag an icon out of the overflow onto the bar and along it quickly; drag one of a
tray's own behind the chevron; start and quit an app with a tray icon while others are shown.

## 177. Quick settings, looked at again: what the radios are on, fixed pages, the switch alone switches (2026-10-16)

The person, on their quick settings folder: "the wifi and bluetooth should show some information
about the device or network as well in the overview"; "the wifi and bluetooth flyouts that pop up
should have a fixed height, same for accessibility"; "night light was on but it was actually off on
the computer, it got disabled via schedule and then it didnt update"; "the toggle button should only
be clicked when you click it directly, everywhere else it opens the sub flyout"; "the brigtness and
volume icons should be aligned to be the same as the night light icon"; "the angle icons between the
toggles and the volume should also be the same size and aligned at the same position".

**What the radios are on** (`QuickSettings\Services\RadioLine.cs`). The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth switch
lines say, beside their names in the secondary ink, what Windows' tiles say on their
second line: the network Wi-Fi is connected to; the connected Bluetooth device, or the devices'
names and "N connected" where the names do not fit; "Not connected"; "Off". Read from the pages' own
sources (the networks and devices the pages list), started when the folder shows the line and
stopped when it closes, so nothing is followed while the folder is shut and a line never disagrees
with its page. Nothing is said until it is known: before the source's first read, during a first
scan that has listed nothing, for Bluetooth's "Not connected" until its watchers have had 400 ms, and
where Windows lists no networks to Karpo without location access.

**Beside the name, not under it** (2026-10-16, the person: "for the toggles, show the name of the
wifi or connected devices to the right of the title and not underneath"). The words stand on the
name's row, 8 DIP after the name's end, at the name's size in the secondary ink (`SwitchIsland.Beside`),
and the line is one row as every other switch's. The name is laid first and never gives way: the
words take what is left before the switch (the state, where a line shows words instead), the first
of their forms that fits whole (the devices' names, then "N connected"), else cut with an ellipsis
where four letters still show, else nothing. A taller line says them beside its name too, never as a
line under it. Only the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth lines have them.

**Fixed pages** (`FolderPages.PageRows`). The Wi-Fi networks and the Bluetooth devices are 8 rows,
fixed, so a page no longer grows and shrinks as networks come into range and devices connect: one
network or twelve, the page is 367 DIP. Past what it holds the page's rows scroll under its title
row, which stays (`QuickPageTile` is an `IListScroll`, ListScroll.cs), with the overlay scrollbar and
the wheel as any line's. The accessibility page's six switches are the same six always, so it was
already fixed (346 DIP); a row is 41 DIP, so the two are within a row of each other.

**Night light follows its schedule** (`NightLight.cs`). The state is the CloudStore value, which the
watch hears; the tile's handler, made once in the dock's process, kept answering "on" after the
schedule had turned night light off, and it was asked first. Now the value answers and the handler
only where the value does not read; a switch through the handler shows at once and the watch confirms
it. The watch is on the value's parent key and its subtree, so a key written again from scratch is
heard too. The other switches were checked for the same: energy saver follows
`GUID_ENERGY_SAVER_STATUS`, airplane mode the radio service's state, the radios their StateChanged,
game mode, color filters and mono audio their registry values, do not disturb its documented event,
the hotspot is read every paint — none of them asks a stale handler.

**The switch alone switches** (`SwitchIsland.ToggleTarget`). On a switch's line with a page (Wi-Fi,
Bluetooth, the VPN, nearby sharing, the hotspot) a click on the switch — its track and 4 DIP round it
— switches it, and a click anywhere else, the chevron, the name and the glyph with it, opens the page.
The hairline before the chevron is gone: it said the line was two halves split there. Under the
pointer the switch lights as WinUI's ToggleSwitch does (its track and knob) and the line does not;
anywhere else the whole line lights as the folder lights a line. A switch's line with no page
(airplane mode, energy saver, night light, …) stays one target that switches, as Windows' tile
without a ">" does: there is nothing else for a click there to do, and a dead line would be worse.
The keyboard's Enter on a line with a page switches it, as Space on Windows' tile does.

**One icon column, one chevron** (`SliderLine`, `SoundPartTile`). The brightness's and the volume's
buttons are centred on the list's icon column, where the switches' glyphs are, and their glyphs are
the list's glyph size (`Button.GlyphSize`, `ListForm.Glyph`) — they stood 10 DIP to the right. The
volume's ">" is the switches' chevron: 12 DIP, centred where theirs is.

**The switch on the right, the ">" just before it** (`SwitchIsland.SwitchColumn`, `ChevronGlyphBox`,
`WordsEnd`; the person: "the toggles should actually always align to the right. then the angled
buttons are directly do the left of them"). Every switch ends on the trailing gutter, 40 DIP wide, the
same x on every line, page or none, at every height (the whole widget's switch too, on the state's
row, no longer beside the state). A line with a page has its ">" 12 DIP before the switch's column —
also where that line draws no switch (accessibility, a switch whose state is not known yet, the
volume), so the chevrons are one column and the switches another. The line's words, the radio's
network or devices with them, end 14 DIP before the ">". Only the switch (and 4 DIP round it)
switches; the ">" and the rest open the page, as before. Tests: `QuickPagesTests.TheSwitchesAndTheChevronsStandInColumns`.

Tests: `QuickPagesTests` (only the switch switches and the rest opens the page, a line without a
page one target; the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth pages one height whatever they list, twelve networks
scrolling under the title; the sliders' glyphs in the icon column and the chevrons in one place at
1, 1.5 and 2x and both text sizes), `RadioLineTests` (what each radio's line says, and says nothing
it does not know), `NightLightTests.TheValueWinsOverAStaleHandler` (the regression). Pictures:
`quick-pages-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`, now with the folder as the person has it (airplane mode,
energy saver and night light as lines). By hand: open quick settings — Wi-Fi says the network,
Bluetooth the headset; switch Wi-Fi off and on from the switch only, and open its page from the name;
let night light's schedule turn it on or off with the folder open and closed; open the Wi-Fi page
where many networks are in range and scroll it.

## 178. The sound page's devices are dropdowns (2026-10-16)

The person: "the sound submenu of the quick settings should show the input and output device
selectable from a dropdown." The volume's page (§170) listed the output devices as rows and had no
input at all. Now it starts with two of WinUI's ComboBoxes, "Output" and "Input", over spatial sound,
the mixer and the foot, which stay as they were.

**A line on a page, not a new kind** (`SoundPartTile`). The page's `soundOutput` and `soundInput`
lines (keyed `…/page/…`) draw as a dropdown; the same kinds anywhere else are the lists they were, so
no config changes. The header in body text, 8 under it the field (32 DIP, taller with the text) from
gutter to gutter, with the device in use, its glyph and the down chevron (`ComboField`); it follows
Windows as the lists do, through the shared sound store. Where there is no microphone the Input field
says "No input devices" (no output: "No output device"), greyed, and opens nothing.

**The list is a menu** (`IslandView.Choices`, `FolderFlyoutAction.Choices`, `Dock.FolderChoices`). A
click on the field, or Enter or Space on its line, has the folder hand the dock the field's place on
the screen; the dock opens the devices as Karpo's menu over the folder, which stays open behind it as
for a line's menu: in Windows' order, the one in use ticked, as wide as the field
(`Flyout.ListWidth`), hung off the field's middle by half the field and 4 DIP (`Flyout.Show`'s gap),
so it clears the field downwards or, where there is no room below, upwards. A pick is the device
menu's `ChooseDevice`: Windows' default for every role through `ISoundSource`, the folder staying.

Pictured: `sound-choices-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (the field clicked in a real folder window, its
list open), and the page in `quick-pages-*.png`. By hand: open the sound page, pick another output
and another microphone from the dropdowns, and check Windows' sound settings follow; plug or unplug a
headset with the page open.

## 179. Quick settings: every tile Windows has, what is playing on top (2026-10-16)

The person: "add all of the windows default items in the quick settings, like hotspot, live captions,
project, display, nearby sharing etc." and "show now playing on top of the quick settings as well,
like windows does it, with a separator between".

**The tiles.** Windows keeps the tiles it pins by default in `HKCU\Control Panel\Quick Actions\Control
Center` (`UserLayoutPaginated`), in its order: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Airplane mode, Cellular, Studio
effects, Accessibility, VPN, Rotation lock, Energy saver (battery and AC-only), Live captions, Night
light, Mobile hotspot, Nearby sharing, Color profile, Cast, Project, LE audio, Audio sharing, Power
mode, Mobile devices; then the brightness and volume sliders. It shows each only where the PC has it,
and pages through them six at a time. Karpo's quick settings preset (`Presets.QuickPanelId`, a new
folder and a first start's) now has every one Karpo has a switch for:

| Windows' tile | In the preset |
|---|---|
| Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Accessibility | lines with their pages (§177) |
| Live captions | a line; its click starts them (Win+Ctrl+L) |
| Cast, Project | lines, new widgets `cast` and `project`: all of each is its page (`FolderPages`) — the wireless displays, Win+P's modes; on their own a click presses Win+K or Win+P |
| Airplane mode, VPN, Rotation lock, Energy saver, Night light, Mobile hotspot, Nearby sharing | the toggles row, in Windows' order; rotation lock only on a screen that turns (`PresetNeed.Rotation`, `WindowsTaskbar.ScreenRotates`, GetAutoRotationState), nearby sharing a toggle now (`Toggle.NearbyShare`) |
| Brightness, Volume | the sliders, the volume's ">" its page |
| Cellular, Studio effects, Color profile, LE audio, Audio sharing, Mobile devices | not in Karpo: no switch for them |
| Power mode | left out on purpose (2026-10-11): Power & battery's |

**Why a row and not lines for the plain tiles.** Every tile a line is some 750 DIP with the battery:
past the 70 % of a 1440p screen at 150 % (638 DIP), so the battery and the foot would be left out
(§171). Windows pages its grid; a list never scrolls, so the plain on/off tiles are the toggles row,
Windows' grid without its words, and the VPN, the hotspot and nearby sharing switch there — their
pages are a `vpn`, `mobileHotspot` or `nearbyShare` line away (Edit). The tiles that open something,
cast and project, and live captions, which Windows tells no app the state of, are lines. 621 DIP with
the battery, 7 DIP of the 1440p rule to spare; a turning screen's seventh toggle wraps to a second row.
On 1080p at 150 % (470 DIP) neither this nor what is playing over the old one fits: the foot is left out
there until the folder is arranged.

**What is playing.** The compact `media` line first, a divider under it, so it is a card of its own
over the tiles as Windows' media controls stand over its panel. Windows shows them only while
something plays; a line cannot hide, and coming and going would move every tile under the pointer, so
it stays and says "Nothing playing", its buttons quiet.

A folder already made keeps its lines: only a new folder and a first start get these.

Tests: `CombinedPresetTests` (the recipe on a laptop, a desktop and a tablet; it stands whole at 1440p
and 150 %), `QuickPagesTests` (the pages table with cast and project, the new folder, cast and project
all page), `DefaultBarTests.RotationLockOnlyWhereTheScreenTurns`, `TypedRegistryTests`. Pictured:
`quick-pages-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`, now with the Cast and Project pages, and
`combined-quickPanelGroup.png`. By hand: a first start's quick settings; play something and pause it;
open Cast and Project from their lines; switch the VPN, the hotspot and nearby sharing from the row.

## 180. Every menu is Explorer's: its row, its pictures, its shortcuts (2026-10-16)

*The person*: "in the whole karpo app context menus, use the icons that the file explorer uses. the
ones that have two colors. also make sure that the design of the right click looks exactly the same,
right now the top row does not match the design for example and the keyboard shortcuts are also not
shown in the context menus. you can also open my file explorer to copy the design if needed".

Explorer's menu was captured on the person's PC (Windows 11 26H2, dark, 150 %: a file's and the
folder background's) and every menu Karpo draws (`FlyoutLayout.List`: a widget's, the bar's, a
folder line's, a pin's jump list, edit mode's, submenus) is laid out to it (`Flyout.cs`):

- **Rows**: fills 28 DIP high and 32 apart (they were 32 and 36), 5 DIP in from the sides; 3 DIP
  above the first row and under the last; a rule 1 DIP with 4 DIP either side (it was 1 either
  side); the icon 16 DIP and the words 44 DIP in from the menu's edge, both in the middle of the fill.
  The rim of a dark menu is Explorer's #3B3B3B (`FlyoutHost.MenuRim`), not the flyouts' darker line.
  A submenu's chevron is Explorer's thin one (ChevronRight, 12 DIP) in the secondary colour, its
  middle 16 DIP in from the fill's end. At 150 % the capture and Karpo's picture of the same menu
  agree to a pixel or two in every place measured (`ExplorerMenuPictures`, the "file" menu).
- **The row of buttons** (`Flyout.Primary.cs`): each button its icon (16 DIP, 12 DIP under the rim)
  over its word (12 DIP text, 34 DIP under the rim), 58 DIP tall, at least 64 DIP wide, a hairline
  36 DIP tall between two, across the menu's whole width; the plate under the pointer 4 DIP in from
  the button's sides, 6 under the top and 5 over the rule; the rule under the row runs the menu's
  full width, hard under it. Explorer's five buttons are what make its menu as wide as it is: a
  widget's five (Copy, Settings, Remove, Add a widget, Edit taskbar) widen Karpo's past its 256 DIP
  the same way (`PrimarySpans`: one width each where the menu shares out so, otherwise each its
  least and an even share; a word longer than 96 DIP ends in an ellipsis, all of it in the tooltip).
  The bar's own buttons no longer stand apart behind a gap: Explorer's row has none. The row stays on
  top whichever way the menu opens (§129, the person's).
- **Explorer's pictures** (`Karpo.Core\ExplorerIcons.cs`): they are no font — Segoe Fluent Icons has
  no colour layers — but SVGs in Explorer's package under Windows
  (`SystemApps\MicrosoftWindows.Client.FileExp_cw5n1h2txyewy\FileExplorerExtensions\Assets\images\
  contrast-standard\theme-<dark|light>\*.svg`): a light glyph with a cyan part in the dark set, a dark
  one with a blue part in the light. Karpo reads them from there as a menu is drawn and draws them
  with Direct2D's SVG renderer (`Gfx.Svg`); none is copied into Karpo. A row still names its glyph,
  and the glyphs Explorer has a picture for draw as Explorer's: Copy, Cut, Paste, Delete/Remove,
  Rename, Share, Settings (Explorer's Options gear), Properties, Refresh, Undo, Redo, Add/New, Open in
  new window, the folders, Open with, Pin, Unpin, Select all/none, Close, Run as administrator,
  Personalize, Show, View, Sort, Print, Link, Install. The rest stay glyphs, as Explorer's own rows
  without a picture do; so does everything where Windows hasn't the files (Windows 10, an older 11),
  and in a high-contrast theme, whose rows turn colour under the pointer. A greyed row's picture is
  at 40 %. The settings app's "Remove" on an account (a WinUI MenuFlyout) has Explorer's Delete
  through an `SvgImageSource` of the same file (`MenuIcons`).
- **Shortcuts** (`MenuChord.cs`): shown as Explorer shows its own — 12 DIP, the secondary colour, in
  one column at the rows' right, each from the column's left, the widest ending 16 DIP in — and a
  button's in its tooltip, "Copy (Ctrl+C)". Only what Karpo does on those keys: Copy Ctrl+C and Remove
  Delete (edit mode's keys, `EditKeys`), Done editing Escape; a window's menu keeps its own (Alt+F4).
  While the menu stands open its shortcuts choose their rows (`Flyout.Press`): Delete on a widget's
  menu is its Remove, which asks as ever. The caps are in the menu's language (Strg and Entf in German,
  Suppr and Échap in French; `dock.keys.*`), not the keyboard's: Windows' key names follow the
  keyboard layout, and on the person's Swiss German keyboard an English menu would have said STRG.

Not changed: a list of an island's content (`FlyoutLayout.Panel`) and the add list keep their
measures; the add list is no context menu and keeps its glyphs.

Tests: `MenuLookTests` (the measures at 100, 125, 150 and 200 %: the row's buttons, plates, icon and
word; the rows' fills, icon, words; the shortcuts present where a row has one, in one column, the
widest 16 DIP in; Delete choosing Remove; Explorer's picture drawn where Windows has it; the spans;
the shortcuts' words in English, German and French; which rows have shortcuts; the pictures by
glyph), `MenuModePictures` (the tooltip "Copy (Ctrl+C)"). Pictures:
`explorer-menu-<file|sound|bar|arranged>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`. By hand: right-click a widget
and Explorer's empty background side by side, dark and light — the row, the pictures, the rule, the
rows' heights; hover a button for its tooltip; press Delete in a widget's menu.

## 181. A ">" with no switch after it stands on the gutter (2026-10-16)

The person: "the angled icons should not have a blank space on the right of them if they dont have a
toggle button to the right. it is alright if the layout is not consistend across all the different
toggles for this." §177's trailing columns put every line's ">" just before the switches' column,
so a line that draws no switch (Accessibility, Cast, Project, the volume, a switch whose state is not
known yet or that this PC hasn't got) kept an empty switch-wide gap after its ">".

Now a line's ">" stands just before its switch only where the line draws one
(`SwitchIsland.DrawsSwitch`: here, switchable, its state known); else it ends on the trailing gutter,
where a switch would end (`SwitchIsland.ChevronGlyphBox(box, style, switched)`). The words end before
the line's own ">" (`WordsEnd`), so a line without a switch gets the room back. The switches still
stand in one column; the ">"s now in two. The volume's ">" is a switchless line's, its button round
it kept inside the line. Clicks follow the drawing: the ">" is the page's part of the line wherever
it stands.

Tests: `QuickPagesTests.TheSwitchesAndTheChevronsStandInColumns` (each line's ">" before its switch or
on the gutter, its words before it), the volume's ">" in `QuickPagesTests` and `SoundChoicesTests`.
Pictures: `quick-pages-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`. By hand: open quick settings; Accessibility, Cast,
Project and the volume have their ">" against the right edge, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth before their switch.

## 182. A button of a menu's row says one word (2026-10-16)

The person: "shorten the item descriptors on the row depending on context, for example the ones that
are shown on the taskbar should only be: Add, Edit, Settings. without the taskbar everywhere ... if
possible generally it should only be one word". §180's row drew each button's whole name under its
icon: "Add a widget", "Edit taskbar", "Taskbar settings", "Done editing". The menu says what they act
on (a right click on the bar is the bar's menu), and Explorer's buttons are one word each.

A `FlyoutItem` has a `Word`, what its button says under its icon (`ButtonWord`: the word, else its
text); its text stays its tooltip (with its shortcut) and the name a screen reader says. Only the row
draws it; a row of text keeps its whole name.

| Button | Under its icon before | Now | Tooltip |
|---|---|---|---|
| bar: Add | Add a widget | Add | Add a widget |
| bar: Edit | Edit taskbar | Edit | Edit taskbar |
| bar: Done (arranged) | Done editing | Done | Done editing (Esc) |
| bar: Settings | Taskbar settings | Settings | Taskbar settings |
| widget: Copy, Settings, Remove | the same | the same | Copy (Ctrl+C), Settings, Remove (Del) |
| widget: the bar's at the end | Add a widget, Edit taskbar / Done editing | Add, Edit / Done | as the bar's |

The new words (`dock.menu.word.add`, `.edit`, `.done`; "Settings" is `dock.menu.settings`) are one
word in every language where its Windows has one (German "Hinzufügen", "Bearbeiten", "Fertig"; Hindi
and Marathi "संपादन", "पूर्ण"; Urdu "شامل", "ترمیم", "مکمل"); Bengali "যোগ", Vietnamese "Sửa". Telugu
and Tamil keep their single verb forms. Words this short leave each button at its least, 64 DIP, so
the bar's menu is as wide as its rows of text need, three buttons sharing it evenly.

Rows of text were left alone: "Pin to taskbar" and "Unpin from taskbar" name the taskbar they pin
to, as Windows' own do, and the settings app's menus have no row of buttons.

Tests: `MenuLookTests.TheRowsButtonsSayOneWord` (the bar's, the arranged bar's and a widget's words,
the tooltips whole, German). Pictures: `explorer-menu-<bar|sound|arranged>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.
By hand: right-click the bar: "Add", "Edit", "Settings" under the icons, the whole names on hover.

## 183. A switch on its way says so (2026-10-16)

The person: "during the enableling of a hotspot for example the toggle icon is still displayed dark,
but there should be a loading or enableling disabling state." A click asks Windows and Windows takes
its time — the hotspot's tethering manager seconds, a radio or a Settings handler a moment — and the
buttons kept the old state until the switch reported the new one (the hotspot's line even lost its
switch, as the tethering state reads "in transition" meanwhile).

**What Windows does.** Its quick-settings tile takes the new look at once on a click (the accent on,
or off), and the hotspot's tile says "Turning on…" while the hotspot starts; its Settings page shows
its switch where it was sent, greyed, until Windows has done it, and the switch takes no click
meanwhile. A failure puts the tile back where it was. (From Windows 11's own behaviour; not captured
on the person's PC for this change.)

**What Karpo does** (`QuickSettings\Services\SwitchPending.cs`). A click on a switch whose state is
known and whose click switches it begins a pending click: where it was sent and when. It ends when
the switch reads that state (confirmed), when the switch counts one more refusal
(`IQuickSwitch.Refusals`, counted where Windows says no: airplane mode, the hotspot, energy saver,
night light, rotation lock, spatial sound, the radios and the Settings-handler toggles — the real
state shows again at once, the tooltip's note saying why), or after 30 s, when the real state is
read again. One pending per switch (`Pendings.Of`), so a row's button and a line of the same switch
go busy together. Nothing shows for the first 200 ms: a switch that answers as it is asked (most do)
never flickers, and one confirmed within the click is never pending at all. A click while one is on
its way is ignored, the keyboard's Enter and Space with it.

While it shows:

- **The toggles row** (`TogglesTile`): the button takes the look of where it is going — the accent
  going on, the control fill going off — and a 12 DIP ring turns in its top right corner, 5 DIP in,
  clear of the glyph: in the ink on the accent on a button going on, in the accent on one going off,
  the quick settings' own ring (`Progress.Ring`, a whole turn in 1.5 s). The button does not light
  under the pointer. With Windows' animations off the ring stands still: the static sign of it.
- **A switch's line** (`SwitchIsland`): the switch where it is going, greyed as WinUI greys a
  disabled ToggleSwitch, and "Turning on…" or "Turning off…" beside the name in the secondary ink,
  where the radios say their network (§177), or as the state where the line shows its state in words.
  A line too narrow for them keeps its name, as ever.
- **On the bar**: the accent behind the glyph going on, at 60 %, the glyph at 60 %; the tooltip says
  "Mobile hotspot: turning on…".

The widgets wake themselves for it (`PendingClock`): when the busy look starts, at the timeout, and,
on a row in an open folder with animations on, every 33 ms while a ring turns — nothing else ticks.

band: padding 16,12,16,12 DIP with a 1 DIP rule over it on the overlay surface; a minus button
(Segoe Fluent E949, 12 DIP), the length in a room at least 73 DIP wide with 4 either side ("30"
semibold, " mins" in the secondary ink, the body's 14), a plus button (E710, 12); at the end a
standard (not accent) button at least 72 DIP wide, PlaySolid F5B0 at 12 DIP, 4, "Focus". Running,
the selector gives way to "Focusing" and the button to StopSolid EE95 "End session".

Before, a focus line one row tall was the timer's line (`CountdownLine`): its glyph, "Focus time",
the steppers round the length, an accent glyph button, a progress bar. Now a focus widget in a list
where nobody set its height is `FocusLine` (`CountdownTile.FocusInline`): 12 DIP, 32 DIP buttons,
12 DIP (56 DIP at the default text); the minus on the leading gutter, 4, the length's room (73 DIP
at the least, the widest reading at the most), 4, the plus; the start button on the trailing
gutter, at least 72 DIP, WinUI's 11 DIP padding, its glyph 12 DIP and 4 before its word (the
button's new `GlyphGap`). All standard buttons, as Windows'. A session named on its widget says the
name on its start button where it fits Windows' 126 DIP for that word, else "Focus".

Karpo says what Windows says in its taskbar's clock as well: while it runs, what is left, semibold,
on the leading gutter, then in the secondary ink "Focusing" (or the session's name), "Paused", or
"Focus time is over" (whole or not at all); at the end a glyph button that pauses (PauseSolid F8AE),
takes up again (F5B0) or starts again, 4, and End session, which clears it. No progress bar and no
glyph or name column: Windows has neither. The rule and the overlay surface are the folder's
divider's, not the line's. What gives way, narrowest last: a name too wide for the button becomes
"Focus", then the buttons lose their words, then the steppers go (the line's menu has Longer and

30 languages. Config untouched.

## 186. A press away from a menu over a folder closes the menu alone (2026-10-16)

The person: "when the right click context menu is open in a folder and i click away from the folder
it closes both, but it should only close the context menu first. on the next click the folder then."

**Why both closed.** The menu said where the press that closed it was (`FlyoutHost.DismissedAt`),
and the dock closed the folder under it too when that press was outside the folder (§15.3's old
rule, `FolderAfterMenu`). The press also went on to whatever it landed on: a click on another app
activated it, a click on the bar acted there, and a click on one of the folder's own widgets acted
on it once the menu had closed.

**What Windows does.** A menu over Start or a flyout uses up the press that closes it: the menu
closes, nothing under the pointer hears of the press, the flyout stays open with the focus, and the
next press closes it. Escape likewise closes the menu, and a second Escape the flyout.

**What Karpo does** (`PressHook.cs`, `FlyoutHost.UsesUpPresses`). A menu over a folder (a widget's
menu, a line's dropdown, an arranged folder's room menu) and a folder row's menu over a pin folder's
lists use up every press outside them and their submenus. The menu tells the mouse hook its windows
and its desktop as it shows, and again as a submenu opens. The hook, on its own thread, answers such
a press itself, and that button's release too, so the folder, a bar, another app and the desktop
never see it; it still tells the menu's thread, which closes the menu wherever the press was, the
bar included, and gives the focus back to the folder. The folder stays open (`FolderAfterMenu` no
longer reads the press) and closes for the next press as always. A click in the folder outside the
menu likewise only closes the menu, as in Windows: the widget under it does not act, and a right
click there takes a second one to open that widget's menu. The hook eats nothing while the menu's
window is hidden or its desktop is not the one with the input, so a test's hidden desktop never
takes the person's clicks. The folder still closes with the menu where the focus left for good
(Alt+Tab, the Windows key) or the pick opened another program. Menus on the bar still let the press
that closes them through (`LightDismiss.cs`: one right click goes from one widget's menu to the
next).

Tests: `FolderMenuTests.APressAwayClosesTheMenuOverAFolderAloneAndTheNextOneTheFolder` (real menu
over a real folder, the press handed over as the hook hands it), `PressHookTests` (what the hook
uses up, a release with its press), `LightDismissTests` (a used-up press closes the menu wherever it
was). By hand: open a folder, right-click a widget, click the desktop, the bar, another app and
another widget of the folder: each time only the menu closes and nothing else happens; the next
click closes the folder.

edge. Explorer doesn't do that: its buttons are 64 DIP each from the row's start, and where its menu
is wider than the row (a long row of text) the rest of the row stays empty. Now Karpo's are the

five buttons (Copy, Settings, Remove, Add, Edit) still fill theirs, as Explorer's five do. In Arabic,
Urdu and Persian the row starts at the right and the room is at the left (Mirror.cs).

screen reader is told all go by the buttons' rectangles, so they follow. Config untouched.

(the bar's three, English and Arabic, 100 and 150 %: the first at the start, a hairline apart, the

## 189. A folder's column reaches the top of the screen (2026-10-16)

The person: "the column still has a lot of space at the top but it already says that it does not have
any space left for some widgets." Their quick settings folder holds one column of twenty lines (a
three-row clock, memory, processor, network and media at two rows, two dividers, eleven switches and
sliders, the row of toggles, Edit / All settings), on a 1440p display at 150 % with a 48-DIP bar: 1392
DIP of work area. A folder without a Fill line stopped at 70 % of it (§152), 974 DIP, the share every
scrolling panel stops at; the column needs some 1030, so the volume and the foot were left out and its
warning said "this column has no room for them", with some 400 DIP of screen empty over it. Only a
folder with a Fill line went further (§173).

**The rule** (`FolderFlyout.Build`, `FolderFlyout.Reach`). Every folder's lists may reach the room beside
the bar (`FlyoutPlacement.Room`: from the anchor and its gap to the work area's far end less the
margin), less what an arranged list's buttons take past its far end, a "+" and its gap (30 DIP): a
list as tall as it may be still has its "+", its width and its warning on the screen, and since the
plan is the same at rest, nothing moves when edit mode begins. A Fill line fills to the same height,
30 DIP short of §173's. A line is left out only where it does not fit there; nothing scrolls. A plan
drawn without a placement takes the room of its work area as before, and never less than the 70 %, so
a sheet's work area taller than any screen still leaves nothing out.

What it gives: their column shows every line, some 1030 DIP of the 1342 it may reach, and a widget added
at its top that fits shows too.

Tests: `FolderColumnRoomTests` (their column on their screen; lines up to the reach show and the one
past it goes, at 100 and 150 %, with and without a placement's room; arranged, a full column's buttons
inside the room on a bottom and a top bar; a first line taller than the reach, a tiny work area, a
sheet; the open folder with a widget added), `FolderHiddenTests` and `FolderFillTests` (to the new
most). Pictures: `folder-column-room-<rest|added|edit>.png`. By hand: open quick settings on the 4K
display, see the volume and Edit / All settings; arrange it and add a widget with its "+".

## 190. The edit bar steps aside while a folder is open (2026-10-16)

The person: "the edit bar on top should actually not be shown when a folder is open. because people
could get confused that they want to place those widgets on the folder then."

In edit mode every display's edit bar ("Add a widget", "Folder", "Separator", settings, close) goes
out of sight as a folder opens and comes back as the last one closes, edit mode still on
(`EditDeckPlan.Shows`, `Dock.ShowDecks`). It goes and comes as it always does, with the popups' fade
(none with Windows' animations off). Every way a folder opens (`ShowFolder`, a drag in a folder at
rest turning edit mode on) and every way one closes (`Forget`) sets the edit bars again, and the
sections' edit bars with them; edit mode ending closes its folders once it is off, so no edit bar
flashes back on the way out. A folder's own "+" and its add list stay the way to add to the folder.

- **Nothing moves.** The edit bar keeps its place while it is aside (`EditDeck.Hide(aside: true)`,
  `EditDeck.Panel`): the popups of a top bar (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`) and the sections' edit bars keep
  clear of that room as before, so a folder placed again while it is open does not move up into it,
  and nothing jumps when the edit bar comes back. An arranged folder's guide lines no longer stop
  short of the edit bar: it is never in sight with them.
- **Escape.** With a folder open, Escape on the bar (or wherever edit mode's hook hears it) closes
  the folder first — the edit bar comes back — and the next Escape leaves edit mode
  (`EditEscape.CloseFolder`); a carried widget and the marching ants still go first. In the folder,
  Escape closes it as before.
- **Drags.** A press on the edit bar can't be under way as a folder opens; one under way in the
  folder or on the bar is not touched. A widget dragged out of a folder keeps the folder open, and so
  the edit bar aside, until it is let go.

Config untouched. Tests: `EditKeysTests.EscapeClosesAnOpenFolderBeforeItLeaves`,
`SceneTreeTests.EditBarShowsOnlyWithNoFolderOpen`, `FoldersOpeningAndClosingSetTheEditBars`,
`EditBarStandsAsideForAFolderSheets` (the real edit bar aside with its place kept, then back where it
stood). Pictures: `editbar-<top|bottom>-<edit|folder>-dark-150.png`. By hand: in edit mode open a
folder (the bar goes), press Escape (the folder closes, the bar fades back), Escape again (edit mode
ends); open a folder from a top bar and check it does not move when the bar comes back.

## 191. A stock line shows a currency pair (2026-10-16)

The person: "with the "stock" widget you should also be able to display currency exchange rates if
this is not already possible." It was possible, but only by knowing the trick: the price service the
stock widget already asks, Yahoo's chart endpoint, quotes a pair as a symbol of its own, `EURCHF=X`
(one euro in francs), with an intraday series, a previous close and every range a share has, so a
symbol box that was given `EURCHF=X`, or a search for "euro franc", already made a line that read
EUR/CHF. Nothing offered it, the yen was written to four decimals ("158.0040"), the face cut the
name to "EUR/CH", and the line under the name said "USD/JPY" a second time.

- **Source.** The same endpoint, no second service: it is free, needs no key, refreshes on the same
  online interval as the shares and is cached in `stocks.json` and marked stale the same way. The
  ECB's daily reference rates (frankfurter.app) were the alternative; they have no intraday series,
  so a 1-day graph would be a flat line, and a second service would be a second set of failures.
- **Choosing one.** The symbol box (`Controls\SymbolPicker.cs`, the stock line's card and the stock
  face's section alike) has a **Currency pair** button beside it. Its flyout has a From and a To list
  ("CHF – Swiss Franc", the names in the language Karpo speaks, read from the ICU Windows ships,
  `Logic\CurrencyNames.cs`), a swap button between them and **Show this rate**. It starts at the
  line's pair, or at the euro in the region's currency (the dollar in euros in the euro area;
  `CurrencyPairs.Start`). What the two make is looked up and kept exactly as a typed symbol is. The
  lists offer the 46 currencies the service quotes against one another (`CurrencyPairs.Codes`) and
  the region's own where it is not among them. The line under the box says "EUR/CHF · Euro → Swiss
  Franc" rather than the service's "EUR/CHF · CCY · CHF".
- **On the bar.** The pair is named "EUR/CHF", never cut (a pair's name is the one symbol allowed
  seven letters); its rate to four decimals, or to two where it is 50 or more — the yen, the forint,
  the rupee ("158.00 JPY"; `CurrencyPairs.Places`, the service says four for every pair); the line
  under the name says the rate in full, "1 USD = 158.00 JPY". The change, the graph, the colours, the
  ranges, the holding ("1,000 EUR") and the stale mark are a share's.
- **The file.** A pair is a symbol, `StockOptions.Symbol = "EURCHF=X"`: no new field, so every file
  reads and writes as before.

Tests: `CurrencyPairTests` (the symbol, the pair a picker starts at, the decimals, a real USD/JPY
answer read and written, the names from ICU, a file with a share and a pair written back unchanged),
`FolderRowsTests` (a pair's line under the box); pictures: `StockPresetTests.StockPairPictures`
(stock-pair-dark/light.png: a folder with a pair face, a share line and a pair line). By hand: on a
stock line's card, Currency pair → EUR to CHF → Show this rate; the line on the bar reads
EUR/CHF 0.9xxx CHF with a graph; swap and show again; set the face of a stock folder to USD/JPY.

## 193. The notifications are Windows 11's notification center (2026-10-16)

The person: "improve the layout of the notifications widget. it should follow the win11 style more
closely." The line (§100) drew rows: the bell and a count as its header, each notification a row on
the gutter, the switch at the end. Now it is laid out as Windows' own notification center
(`NotificationPartTile`), read from this PC rather than guessed: the XAML of Win+N is compiled into
`C:\Windows\SystemResources\Windows.UI.ShellCommon\Windows.UI.ShellCommon.pri` (26H2) —
`notificationcenterpage.xbf`, `notificationcenterview.xbf`, `grouptitleview.xbf`,
`notificationcontentview.xbf`, `toastcontentview.xbf` and their resource dictionaries — whose
string tables, property values and resource keys were read out of the XBF without touching the
desktop.

What Windows' XAML says, and what the line does with it:

- **The header** (`NotificationCenterTopBanner`: 48 DIP at the least, 16 DIP either side, columns
  `*`, Auto, Auto): "Notifications" (`NotificationsTextBlock`), then do not disturb's
  `ToggleButton` (`DoNotDisturbButtonStyle`, an AnimatedIcon bell, 4 DIP corners), then "Clear all"
  (`ClearAllButtonStyle` on `PlatedButtonStyle`: a standard button at least 24 DIP tall, padding
  8,0,8,2, 8 DIP from the bell). The line: "Notifications" semibold on the gutter, the bell 32 DIP
  square with its 16 DIP glyph, on the accent while on, and "Clear all" in the caption size in a
  standard button ending on the trailing gutter. No count, as Windows has none; one row keeps the
  bell, the count, the bell button and "Clear all". Where they do not fit (225 % text) the bell
  button gives way first, then "Clear all", as before. The header's divider brush is transparent in
  26H2's theme dictionary, so there is no rule under it.
- **An app's heading** (`GroupHeaderMinHeight` 32 DIP, `AppLogoIconSize` 16): its icon, 8 DIP, its
  name semibold in the caption size, over the cards' words; under the pointer a … (`AC_NotificationCenter_Group_Settings`,
  Segoe Fluent E712) and a × (E711) at the cards' inner edge. The … opens the line's own menu at the
  pointer (`IslandView.Menu`: Clear all, Do not disturb, Notification settings), the nearest thing
  Karpo has to Windows' group menu ("Turn off notifications", "Go to notification settings"); the ×
  clears the app. "See more (n)" and "See fewer" stay under a group of more than three.
- **A notification is a card** (`ItemOpaquePlating`): `NotificationCornerRadius` 4 DIP;
  `FlexibleItemViewBackgroundBrush`, which 26H2 aliases to `LayerOnAcrylicFillColorDefault` (#09FFFFFF
  dark, #40FFFFFF light; the card colour in high contrast); a 1 DIP rim of `CardStrokeColorDefault`
  (`NotificationItemPlatingBorderThickness` 1); 4 DIP between cards (`NotificationItemPlatingMargin`
  4,2,4,2), 12 DIP between groups. The cards stand between the list's gutters, their words 12 DIP
  in. Under the pointer the card lights with the subtle fill, pressed with the pressed one.
- **Inside a card**, as `toastcontentview`/`notificationcontentview` lay a toast out: its hero
  (placement hero) across the top, cut to 2:1 within the card's corners, at most 180 DIP; its own
  picture (appLogoOverride) 48 DIP (`StandardImageBorder`) with 12 DIP before the words; the title
  (`Title`, the body style, semibold) on two lines at the most, the body (`MessageText`, 14, the
  secondary ink `NotificationSecondaryTextBrush` = `TextFillColorSecondary`) on four — Microsoft's
  toast clamps, a toast's first text two lines and the other two four together
  (`NotificationPartTile.TitleLines`, `BodyLines`) — and its first inline picture (an image of no
  placement) under the words, at most 180 DIP tall. At the end of the title's first line, on a row
  as tall as a glyph button, when it came in the caption size and the secondary ink (`TimeStamp`); under
  the pointer the … and the × (`SettingsButton`, `DismissButton`, hidden at rest in Windows too) in its
  place; Windows' chevron after them where there is more. Where that row would leave the title less
  than three fifths of the words' room (a narrow line, a large text) the row holds the time and the
  buttons alone and the title starts under it, so a title is never cut to "…".
- **Expanded**, the whole title and body, then each input and the buttons across the card's width,
  side by side where each one's words fit its share, else one under another (32 DIP, 8 between).
- **Empty**: "No new notifications" (`NoNotificationsTextBlock`: the caption style, 18 DIP over and
  under) centred under the header; "Do not disturb is on" while it is; "Notifications can't be read"
  where they cannot.

Behaviour is as it was: grouping, folding, the chevron, activation, dismissal, typing and Clear all
(§19, §100); the item style (ItemStyles) still sets the items' sizes, room, pictures, previews and
times. The toast's hero and first inline image are now read with its logo (`ToastXml.Parse`,
`NotificationEntry.HeroPath`, `InlinePath`, local files only, as the logo). No new strings; nothing in
the config changed. A notification line's least height that lists them grew a little (its first
card's row is a glyph button tall), and an empty line is the header over the empty words rather than
the header alone.

Tests: `NotificationsPresetTests.EachNotificationIsACardOnTheGutters`,
`ATitleTakesTwoLinesAndABodyFourUntilExpanded`, `NothingOverlapsAtNarrowWidthsAndLargeText` (four
apps, a logo, a hero, an inline picture, an expanded card and a card under the pointer at 360, 280 and
220 DIP, 100 and 150 %, ordinary and 225 % text: nothing standing on anything, everything inside its
