## 194. No widget has a most height of its own (2026-10-16)

The person: "remove the max height for widgets. because then they cannot actually grow to the full
height of the page." Since §140 every kind whose content does not vary had its own most rows
(`ListWidget.Tallest`: a switch three, a clock six, the timer eight, a month ten), and every kind 32 at
the most; now that a column reaches the top of the screen (§189), those numbers were what stopped a
line, not the room.

- **The rule** (`LineHeight.Limits`, `LineHeight.Most`). Every card with a height is one row to
  `LineHeight.Most`, 200 rows, for every kind: past any screen (8K on its side at 100 % is 187 rows of
  41 DIP), so it only catches a typo. The real most is the room: the folder's menu steps a line's
  "Height" up to as many whole rows as its column's room holds on that screen and no further
  (`FolderFlyout.RoomRows`, `LineHeight.Room`, `LineHeightRows.For(item, room)`); a height above it,
  set elsewhere, steps down into it. Settings knows no screen the folder opens on, so its field takes
  1 to 200. The fewest is still one row (§166).
- **A line set past the room** (`FolderFlyout.Build`) is given what the lines over it leave of the
  room, down to one row, and the lines under it are left out as any line past the room is; first in
  its column it is the whole room. It used to leave itself out with every line under it.
- **Fill** (§168) has no kind's most to stop at: every Fill line, a switch's or a month's too, shares
  the room left; nothing stays empty at a list's end.
- **Kept fixed**, as before and for the same reasons, since they have no height to choose
  (`Folders.HasHeight`): a heading (a section heading's height), a divider (its hairline and air),
  the actions footer (`ListWidget.FixedHeight`), and the list's own rows (Task view, the Snipping
  Tool, Settings, the six power buttons). Every other card now has the height card and the menu's
  rows; none is left at one height by a most of its own.
- **Drawn at any height.** Every card was drawn at 40 rows, 150 %, dark (`tall-<kind>.png`). What
  fills does: the five graphs (the graph grows), the day and week views (the hours grow), the weather's
  conditions (its hours and week fill in under it), every list of items (more of them). What has no
  more to show stands at the line's top, as the person ruled for every widget on 2026-10-11 ("if the
  widgets cannot fill the space available to them they should be top aligned and not center their
  content somehow", `ListScrollTests.EveryLineStandsAtTheTopOfATallLine`): a switch, the clock, the
  timer's card (its ring grows with the width, not the height), the stopwatch, the alarm, the month.
  Centring them was tried and dropped for that rule. One drawing broke: a switch's ">" (a line with a
  page to open) stood in the middle of the line's height, alone half a screen under its name; it now
  stands beside the switch where one is drawn, else beside the words (`SwitchIsland.ChevronBand`).
- **The file.** Nothing is reset or rewritten: heights at or under the old mosts read as they were.
  A height over a kind's old most was held to it as it was read; it is now read as written (a clock
  of 99 rows is 99), and only past 200 is it held, to 200. A file from before the two modes with a
  most over 32 keeps it. The fewest is still held to one.

Tests: `HeightLimitsTests` (every kind 1 to the most, every card but the fixed ones has a height, a
file's height past an old most read as written), `NoFewestTests`, `ListBoundsTests`,
`WidgetBoundsTests`, `LineHeightRowsTests.TheStepperGoesUpToTheRoomAndNoFurther` (at 100 and 150 % and
on a tall screen: the step stops at the room's rows, the line there is given all of them),
`FolderFillTests` (a fixed kind fills, a tall screen, a line set past the room),
`HeightLimitsPicturesTests` (every fixed kind at 1 to 8, 12 and 20 rows; every card at 40 rows at
150 % in the dark theme, its ink inside its box), `RemovableHeightTests`, `HeightChoiceTests`.
Pictures: `height-limits-<kind>.png`, `tall-<kind>.png`. By hand: on a 1440p screen open a folder,
right-click a clock, press the Height "+" until it stops (at the top of the screen); set a switch with
a page (Bluetooth) tall and see its ">" beside its switch; set a switch to Fill in a column of its own.

## 195. The focus widget is Windows' Focus band at every height (2026-10-16)

The person: "did you properly updated the Focus time widget so that it looks like the one in win11
default?" Only partly. §193's band (`Clock\FocusLine.cs`, Windows 11's own `FocusSessionControl`) was
drawn only where the line was at least the band's 56 DIP tall *and* the old card's form was one row.
The person's focus line is one row set fixed in a folder: 40 DIP (60 px at 150 %), shorter than the
band, so it fell back to the timer's old one-liner (glyph, name, time, a play button); a line of two
rows or more was the old `CountdownCard` (compact line, whole widget). The band never reached their screen.

- **One row, any height.** `FocusLine.Arrange` takes the line's height and compacts the band into it
  (`FocusLine.Fit`): the 12 DIP of air over and under the buttons gives way first, down to 4 DIP, then
  the buttons, from 32 DIP down to 24, then the rest of the air. At 40 DIP (one row at the list's
  text) that is 4 DIP of air around 32 DIP buttons: Windows' band whole, only tighter. The minus, the
  length ("25 min", the number semibold, the unit secondary), the plus and the standard Focus button;
  running, what is left, the status, the toggle and End session, as in §193.
- **Taller.** The band at Windows' own size at the line's top, the rest left empty (2026-10-11: what
  cannot fill stands at the top). No other card: Windows' band has nothing more to show.
- **Nothing else draws the focus widget.** `CountdownTile.FocusInline` no longer asks the old card
  for its form, so the focus session never reaches `CountdownCard` or `CountdownLine`; those stay the
  timer's (its one-row line, and the fallback beside `TimerCard`, §182).
- **The face on the bar** is left as it was: the focus glyph and the length set ("25m") at rest, what
  is left ("22:47") running, quieter paused, the accent once over — the band's reading in a bar's room.
- **The file.** Nothing changes in it; the person's fixed one-row line keeps its height.

Tests: `FocusLineTests.AOneRowLineOfAnyHeightIsTheBand` (the regression: a line one row tall at
100/150/200 %, every text size, at and above the row's height, lays out the band's pieces alone,
inside the line), `FocusLineTests.ATallLineHasTheBandAtItsTop` (2, 4 and 8 rows),
`CountdownFormsTests.ItsLineSaysWhatItLaidOut` (steppers on one row too); `TheLineIsWorkedAtEveryHeight`

## 198. App badges follow their app at once (2026-10-16)

The person: "i feel like the whatsapp notifications counter does not really update correctly". §20's
badges were measured on this PC against the live store, read-only: a probe reading Windows'
`wpndatabase.db` every half second, a folder watch beside it, and the WhatsApp button's state as a
screen reader hears it from the running Karpo ("1 notification"), over twenty minutes of chatting.

**What WhatsApp does.** WhatsApp (5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop, 2.2639) sets its badge through
`BadgeUpdater` only (no overlay through the taskbar list). Its one `badge` row is replaced with a new
Id and arrival at every change and deleted outright (`Clear`) when the person opens the chat; the
count is mostly "1" (it counts chats, not messages, in its default setting), and while messages come
it writes every half second to second and a half ("1", "2", "1", "2", "1" in four seconds). It keeps
setting the badge with its window closed to the tray, so the pin shows it with no window open, as
Windows' taskbar does.

**What Karpo did.** It showed what the store held, up and down and cleared, with nothing lost: the
folder watch heard every write, and every row change reached the button. But each change came a
second or more late, because a read waited a second after the *last* write and every write pushed it
back: a burst of WhatsApp's writes held the badge where it was until WhatsApp stopped writing, and a
badge cleared as the chat opened stayed up a second over the open chat. And a read that failed on
the way (Windows holding the database) kept the last badge until the app happened to write again:
a clear lost that way stayed up indefinitely.

**Now** (`NotificationStore`): a write is read once Windows' burst of it has settled, 150 ms
(`SettleMs`), and never more than 400 ms after the first write not read yet (`MostWaitMs`,
`ReadDelay`), however long the app keeps writing; a read is a few milliseconds. A read that failed
on the way is tried again a second later, up to five times (`RetryAfter`); the next write starts
again. The notification list and the bell take the same reads, so they follow sooner too. Nothing is
WhatsApp's own: every packaged app's badge goes the same way.

Unchanged and checked: a badge is the app's newest row; 0, `none`, a missing row and anything Windows
would not show clear it; a count past 99 is "99+"; the glyphs are Windows' by name. After a restart of
Karpo or of the app, the button shows what the store holds then, never what Karpo showed last. The
look is §20's, Windows 11's: an accent pill on the icon's lower right with the figures or the glyph
(`app-signals-*.png` now holds 1, 9, 42, 99+ and the busy, alert and attention glyphs).

Tests: `NotificationStoreTests.ABadgeFollowsItsAppUpDownAndCleared` (a live store over a made-up
store with its own watch: 1, 2, 1, the row deleted, a glyph, 0), `ABurstOfBadgesShowsTheLastOneWithoutWaitingForTheBurstToEnd`
(the regression: a write every 100 ms for over a second is read on the way; it failed with the old
wait), `ABadgeIsWhatTheStoreHoldsAfterARestart`, `AReadWaitsForTheBurstToSettleButNotForever`,
`AReadThatFailedOnTheWayIsTriedAgainAFewTimes`; `SignalOffscreenTests` (`app-signals-*.png`). By
hand: with WhatsApp in the background, have a message sent to you: its pin shows the badge within
half a second; open the chat: it goes as fast.

## 201. Where a widget's words stand: start, middle or end (2026-10-17)

The person: "make it so that the widgets also get an alignment property, like center, left, right.
only for the ones where it makes sense, generally speaking some like weather, clock, air quality,
and others that you think make sense." A face on the bar keeps the room of the widest it can read
(§12.2: "12:59", "100%", "-88°"), and a heading, a date or a clock in a folder has the line's width;
what reads now is narrower. It now stands at the room's start, in its middle or at its end, as the
person picks (`Karpo.Core\Alignment.cs`).

- **Nothing moves until somebody picks.** Each kind's default is where it stood: the clock, the
  calendar, the weather, the timer, focus and stopwatch, the battery, the stock and the keyboard in
  the middle; the time and date and the five readings' figure at the end (Windows' clock is
  right-aligned; a reading's figure at the end of its room after its glyph); the news headline, the
  desktops' and the layouts' names and every aligned line at the start. A pick of the default is no
  pick (`Alignment.Choose`) and is not written, so a file says nothing until somebody chose otherwise.
- **The file.** A face's pick is its bag's `"align": "start" | "center" | "end"` (`FolderFace.Options`,
  `FaceOptionKind.Align`); a line's is the widget's own `"align"` (`WidgetItem.Align`), kept only on a
  line of an aligned kind. A word this build does not know reads as no pick (a face's is kept as it
  is, a line's dropped); no migration, and nothing else in a file changes.
- **Right to left.** Start and end are the reading direction's. A folder's line is drawn mirrored in
  Arabic, Urdu and Persian already (§36), so its start is the right with nothing more; the bar is not
  mirrored, so a face turns the pick itself (`Alignment.Fraction`). A kind's default stays where it is
  drawn in every language: Settings shows the time and date's right as "start" there.
- **Horizontal only.** Down a bar on its side a face stays in the middle of the bar's width, and what
  cannot fill a folder's line down it stays at the line's top. A face aligns within its own room: a
  folder of several faces keeps their run in the middle of the button.
- **What each does.** A face of one line of words (clock, calendar text, keyboard codes) moves that
  line; the time and date moves each of its two lines (on one line, the two as one run); a glyph with
  words (weather, battery, timer, focus, stopwatch, stock, news, desktops, layouts) moves the two as
  one run; a reading keeps its glyph at the start and moves its figure in the figure's room. A heading,
  the date header and the time header move each line between the gutters; the clock line moves its
  time, date and place in the words' room between its glyph's column and its dial, and its one-row
  form (a list row: glyph, date, time at the end) is not aligned.
- **Which kinds.** Faces: clock, calendar (text only), time and date, weather, battery, timer, focus,
  stopwatch, CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network activity, stock, news (with its headline), desktops,
  keyboard, layouts. Lines: heading, date header, time header, clock. **Not:** a glyph's square
  (content, icon, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, removable, hotspot, cast, nearby sharing, power, mail,
  notifications, clipboard, contacts, VPN), the drive faces (their capacity bar fills the room), what
  is playing (its words run to the art at the trailing end, the person's layout), the bar's own
  entries (each as wide as it is), and every line that fills: graphs, lists, sliders, switches, the
  toggles and actions rows, notifications, the calendars' month, day, week and year views, the
  weather's lines, media, the timer, stopwatch, focus and alarm cards. There is no air quality widget.
- **Settings.** A face's section and an aligned line's page have an "Alignment" card: Word's align
  left, centre and right as three buttons (`Controls\AlignChoice.cs`), the one in force pressed, each
  saying its word as its tooltip and to a screen reader; read from the right, the row starts at the
  right with align right. Its words are every face's same five (`core.align.*`, `FaceInfo.KeyOf`), in
  every language.
- **No menu row.** A widget's right-click menu is what Windows or the widget does there and then, or a
  page (§15, Dock.FaceMenus.cs); no row of it sets an option, so an "Align" submenu would be the only
  one, and is left out.

Tests: `AlignmentTests` (the faces and lines aligned and each default; nothing written for a file
without a pick, which reads and writes as before; a line's and a face's pick round-trip; an unknown
word and a line of another kind read as none; start and end from the right; the words in every
language), `AlignmentPictures.AFacesWordsStandWhereTheyAreAligned` (the ink of start, middle and end
further right each time, nobody's pick where the face stood, Arabic's start the end's ink, at 100 and
150 %), `AlignmentPictures.ALinesWordsStandWhereTheyAreAligned` (nobody's pick the start's, each piece
further right through the three, a centred time and date sharing a middle and an end). Pictures:
`align-faces-<100|150|ar>.png`, `align-lines-<dark|ar>-150.png`. By hand: pick each alignment for the
clock and the weather face in Settings and watch the bar; a heading in a folder; the same in Arabic.

## 202. A pin's menu at rest has no row on top (2026-10-17)

*The person*: "for pin widgets in not edit mode you should remove the top row in the context menu."

**At rest** a pin's right-click menu, on the bar or in a folder, is Windows' own taskbar menu for an
app: its jump list, the app's name, "Unpin from taskbar", and "End task" / "Close window(s)" at the
end nearest the bar; a pin in a folder has Windows' rows for its file (Run as administrator, Open file
location, Properties) under the app's name. No row of buttons, so no rule over the first row, and the
menu as wide as its rows. Copy, Settings, Remove, Add and Edit taskbar are gone from it: Windows' app
menu has none of them; "Remove" was the unpinning, which "Unpin from taskbar" is again; Settings and
Copy are a click on the pin and its menu in edit mode, Add and Edit the bar's own menu. "Ctrl+C" and
"Del" do nothing in it: a menu's shortcut is its rows' alone (`MenuChord`), and none of these rows has
one.

**While the bar is arranged** the pin's menu is as it was, every widget's arranged menu: the row on top
with Copy, Settings, Remove and the bar's Add and Done, arranging's rows under it. The other widgets'
menus, at rest and arranged, are unchanged (§137, §178).

`Dock.PinButtons(pin, arranged)` says which: a pin widget's `WidgetButtons` while arranged, none
otherwise, and none for an open app that is no pin; `AppMenuAt` asks it with `Arranging(window)`.

Tests: `WidgetMenuTests.APinsMenuHasTheRowOnTopOnlyWhileArranged` (at rest on the bar and in a folder:
no button, no shortcut, "Unpin from taskbar"; arranged the row and no "Unpin"),
`BarMenuTests.TheShellsRowsKeepTheirOrderAboveTheClosingRow`, `MenuModePictures.RestAndArrangedMenuSheets`
(the pin at rest has no buttons). Pictures: `ExplorerMenuPictures.PinMenuSheets`,
`pin-menu-<bar|folder>-<rest|arranged>-<dark|light>-150.png` (the first row not a button at rest, a
button arranged, no rule on top). By hand: right-click a pin on the bar and one in a folder, at rest
and in edit mode; Ctrl+C and Delete in the rest menu do nothing.

## 203. Explorer's volume icon in the tray's list (2026-10-17)

The person: "the sound tray icon is not shown in the config pane so there is no way for me to hide
it." The speaker on the bar's tray is Explorer's own volume icon, which Explorer adds to the
notification area like any app's, by GUID `{7820AE73-23E3-4229-82C1-E41CB67D5B9C}` ("Safely remove
hardware" is `{7820AE78-…}`); its tooltip is the device and its level ("Headphones (Bluetooth): 22%").
The dock did list it in tray-icons.json, and the tray page did show a row for it, but Windows keeps
no NotifyIconSettings record of it (its Settings counts it a system icon, not an app's), so nothing
said what it was: the row took explorer.exe's description and icon, "Windows Explorer" with a folder,
the device's name in small print under it. Nobody looking for a speaker finds that.

- **Its row is "Volume" with a speaker** (`TrayRows.VolumeIcon`, `IsVolume`): Windows' word for the
  icon (the "Volume" of Windows 10's system icons, `settings.tray.volume`, in all 30 languages as the
  sound volume widget's), its tooltip the line under it as for every row, and the Volume Mixer's
  speaker (SndVol.exe's icon, `TrayRows.PicturePath`) as its picture, read as an app's executable
  is. A second one of it (`#2`) is the same. Every other icon, Explorer's "Safely remove hardware"
  among them, is named and pictured as before.
- **Its choice is any icon's**: the three choices, written to `trayStates` by its GUID as before;
  "Hide completely" takes it off the bar and out of the hidden icon menu. The Sound widget and its
  page are not the tray's and stay as they are. Nothing in the file changes shape.

Tests: `TrayRowsTests.TheVolumeIconIsListedAsVolumeWithASpeaker` (the person's own two Explorer
icons as the dock wrote them: "Volume", the tooltip under it, SndVol.exe's picture),
`ExplorersOtherIconsAndAppsAreNamedAsBefore`, `HidingTheVolumeIconHidesItOnTheBarAndIsKeptInTheFile`
(the person's file with it dragged onto the taskbar; its row's "Hide completely" written, read back,
and the bar's split without it). Pictures: `SceneTreeTests.TraySoundSheets`,
`tray-sound-<shown|hidden>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`, the tray with the speaker first and the same
tray once hidden. By hand: open the tray page, find "Volume" with the speaker, pick "Hide
completely", and watch the speaker leave the bar.

## 204. Which windows get a button, as Explorer's taskbar decides (2026-10-17)

The person: "raycast is an app that is shown on the karpo app taskbar widget but is not shown on the
normal windows taskbar. why is that?" Raycast's launcher is a WPF window, unowned, visible and
uncloaked, with `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW | WS_EX_APPWINDOW | WS_EX_NOACTIVATE | WS_EX_LAYERED`. Karpo's rule
(the one Aero Dock's `running.rs` gave it, the same in `Apps.Probe`, `Desktops.Weigh` and
`DesktopPreviews.Listed`) let `WS_EX_APPWINDOW` win over everything, so it got a button. Explorer
gives it none.

The rule was measured rather than remembered: a throwaway harness made one top-level window per row
below, each with an AUMID of its own so each got a button of its own, shown without activation, and
read Explorer's real taskbar by UI Automation while Karpo hid it (the `Taskbar.TaskListButtonAutomationPeer`
buttons under the `DesktopWindowContentBridge` of Explorer's `Shell_TrayWnd`, whose automation ids are
`Appid: <AUMID>`). Windows 11, build 26300; twice, the same answers.

| Window | Explorer's button |
|---|---|
| plain (overlapped), popup without a caption | yes |
| `TOOLWINDOW` (with or without caption, minimised too) | no |
| `APPWINDOW` | yes |
| `TOOLWINDOW` + `APPWINDOW` (popup or captioned, owned or not) | **no** |
| `NOACTIVATE` (popup or captioned) | no |
| `NOACTIVATE` + `APPWINDOW` | yes |
| `NOACTIVATE` + `TOOLWINDOW` | no |
| Raycast's own styles, with and without `NOACTIVATE` | no |
| owned by a visible or a hidden window | no |
| owned + `APPWINDOW` | yes |
| `LAYERED`, `LAYERED` + `TRANSPARENT`, `TOPMOST`, `TOPMOST` + `APPWINDOW`, disabled | yes |
| zero size, far off the screen, minimised | yes |
| `PreventPinning` set | yes |
| without a title | yes |
| cloaked by its own app (`DWMWA_CLOAK`) | yes |
| `ITaskbarList::DeleteTab` after showing (plain or `APPWINDOW`) | no |
| `DeleteTab` then `AddTab` | yes |
| `AddTab` on a tool window or an owned one | no |
| shown plain, then made a tool window | no (taken off) |
| shown `APPWINDOW`, then `TOOLWINDOW` added | yes (kept) |

So a tool window never has a button, `WS_EX_APPWINDOW` or not; otherwise an app window always does;
otherwise a window has one when it is neither owned nor `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`; and `DeleteTab` takes it
away until `AddTab`. `AddTab` does not put a tool window or an owned one on the bar.

- **One rule, `Apps.Listed`**: a pure function of the extended style, the owner and the DeleteTab mark,
  and its `HWND` form, which reads them. The apps, the desktop switcher's apps and the desktop
  previews all ask it, where each had its own copy.
- **DeleteTab is seen**: Explorer marks a window `DeleteTab` names with the window property
  `ITaskList_Deleted` (1) and takes the property off on `AddTab`; it is the only trace the call leaves
  in the window, and `Listed` reads it with `GetPropW`.
- **Read once more after a window comes**: an app calls `DeleteTab`, or makes its window a tool
  window, just after showing it, and the shell hook says nothing of either. Half a second after the
  last `HSHELL_WINDOWCREATED` the windows are scanned again (`APPS_AGAIN`, a host timer, re-armed by
  each new window), and the bar is rebuilt only if the set changed.
- **Not Explorer's list as the authority**: it is readable while hidden, but it holds buttons, not
  windows (an AUMID and "N running windows"), it would cost a cross-process UI Automation walk of
  Explorer's XAML on every change, its shape is Explorer's to change between builds, and it
  is not there at all while Explorer restarts or under a shell replacement. The window facts above give
  the same answers for every case measured, locally and at once.
- **Left as they were**: Karpo still leaves out windows without a title and windows cloaked by their
  own app, both of which Explorer lists (an empty name on a button helps no one, and a store app's
  cloaked frame must stay off), and it judges a window by its styles now, not by the order they came
  in, so the last row of the table is the one case where Karpo and Explorer differ.

Raycast, and any launcher or overlay that makes its window a tool window, gets no button; every app window Explorer
lists still gets one. Tests: `TaskbarListedTests.AWindowGetsAButtonAsOnExplorersTaskbar` (the table,
one row per case), `DeleteTabsMarkTakesTheButtonAwayAndAddTabGivesItBack` (the property on a real
window). By hand: with Raycast running, no Raycast button on the bar; open its launcher, still none.

## 205. The next meeting on the bar (2026-10-17)

The person approved "Next meeting on the bar": the next calendar meeting with a countdown, and a
one-click Join for Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, Webex and the like. It is built on the calendars Karpo
already syncs (`CalendarStore`, the accounts' `AccountCalendars`), as a line and a face, and the meeting
preset that puts them together. No new service, and no new scope.

**What is read.** Graph's `calendarView` is asked for `isOnlineMeeting`, `onlineMeeting`,
`onlineMeetingUrl`, `responseStatus`, `showAs` and `bodyPreview` besides what it was asked for; all are
under `Calendars.Read`, which Karpo always asked for, so nobody signs in again. The link is found once,
as the event is read (`MeetingLinks.Find`): Teams' own join link first, then an add-in's
`onlineMeetingUrl`, then the place, then the first lines of the notes (`bodyPreview`, never the whole
body). A CalDAV event gives `CONFERENCE` (RFC 7986) or Google's `X-GOOGLE-CONFERENCE`, then `URL`, then
`LOCATION`, then `DESCRIPTION`. What is kept is the link alone (`Occurrence.Join`, `CalendarEvent.Join`)
and whether the event takes the person's time: `showAs: free`, `response: declined` and CalDAV's
`TRANSP:TRANSPARENT` make it `Free`. The offline cache keeps both, encrypted as the rest of it; a file
from before reads with no link and as taking time. CalDAV's `PARTSTAT=DECLINED` is not read: the parser
does not know which attendee is the person.

**Links** (`Karpo.Accounts\MeetingLinks.cs`). Known by host and path, never by a word near them:
Teams (`/l/meetup-join/`, `/meet/`, the launcher page round one, the government clouds, teams.live.com),
Zoom (zoom.us and every vanity host under it, ZoomGov, `/j/ /w/ /my/ /s/ /wc/`, `zoommtg:`), Google
Meet (its `abc-defg-hij` codes and `/lookup/`), Webex (`/meet/ /join/ j.php MTID=`), GoTo, Whereby,
Jitsi, Slack huddles, Amazon Chime and RingCentral. Outlook's Safe Links (`*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com`,
Teams' `atp-safelinks` page) and Google's `google.com/url?q=` are unwrapped, as often as they were
wrapped; a sentence's full stop, brackets, Outlook's `<…>` and an HTML body's `&amp;` are taken off.
A chat's or a channel's Teams link, a front page, a wiki page about a meeting are no meetings.

**Join** (`MeetingJoin`). A Teams link at teams.microsoft.com goes to `msteams:/l/meetup-join/…` and a
Zoom meeting by its number to `zoommtg://<host>/join?action=join&confno=…&pwd=…`, where this PC has a
handler for the scheme (its `URL Protocol` key, read, never written); everything else, and those where
the app is not installed, opens the link in the default browser, whose page offers the app. Off the
dock's thread, as every link Karpo opens.

**Which meeting** (`Meetings`). A meeting is timed (an all-day event is a day), not free nor declined,
and not over. The one on now comes first, the most recently started of two on at once; then the rest
by start. A meeting on for ten minutes gives way to one starting within five: that is where the
person is going. Every length is between instants — wall-clock times in the zone the calendar is shown
in, Windows' own, turned into UTC with RFC 5545's rule for the skipped and the repeated hour — so the
night the clocks change "in 40 min" is forty minutes.

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Meeting`, `MeetingFaceDrawing`). One row: the calendar's colour as a 3-DIP
mark, the title, " · " and how soon — "in 4 min", "in 1 h 5 min", "at 15:00" from three hours ahead,
"now" in its first minute, "started 3 min ago", "Tomorrow, 09:00" — and Join, the camera on a 24-DIP
pill as Windows 11's compact button. From the lead before its start until it ends a meeting is lit:
how soon in the accent and semibold, Join filled with the accent. The words fit their room by giving
up the title first (cut with "…" while two characters of it stand), then the title altogether
(`MeetingText.Fit`). Its options:

- **Show**: today's next meeting (the default; "No more meetings today" after the last), the next of
  the coming week ("No upcoming meetings"), or only shortly before one — then the folder takes no room
  on the bar until the lead before a meeting (`FolderIsland.Count`, as now playing's "hide while idle").
- **Highlight from**: 5, 10 (the default), 15 or 30 minutes before.
- **Width**: how soon only, a short title (the default), a long one. The face is measured from this
  alone (a template title and Windows' "in 2 h 55 min"), never from the meeting shown, so the bar does
  not move as meetings come and go.
- **Show the Join button** (on): its room is kept whether or not the meeting has a link; without one
  the words may use it.

Down a bar on its side the camera alone, in the accent while lit. A click on Join opens the meeting
(`IPointClickIsland`: the bar asks a widget whose cell has a button of its own before the widget's
click; only the meeting face answers); anywhere else the folder opens. The face is painted again on the
minute and as the calendars change; its tooltip is the title, its time and place, how soon and
"Join in Microsoft Teams". Its right click: the calendar app and the accounts.

**The line** (`ListKind.Meeting`, `MeetingTile`). One row: the next meeting on one line with Join.
From an event's 52-DIP row: today's meetings still to come, the one on now first, as the calendar
flyout lists events — the colour bar on the gutter, the title over how soon (only where that says more
than the time beside it), the time and the place, or the service where it has only a link; Join as
Windows' standard button with the camera and "Join", the accent's while lit, the camera alone on a
narrow line. With none left today it says so, and under it the next meeting of the week. Only Join
acts (`CellAct.Action`, `IslandView.App`): the meeting opens once the folder has gone. Automatic
height, two rows unmeasured, up to eight to start.

**The preset** (`Presets.MeetingId`, "Next meeting"): the meeting face over the meeting line and the
calendar's footer, in the add list's Time page beside the calendar's preset; the line is in the
calendar's family. Words in all 30 languages. Nothing in the file changes shape: a face and a line
kind more, which an older build reads as an unknown face (what is inside) and drops as an unknown line.

Tests: `MeetingLinksTests` (every service's shapes, what is no meeting, Safe Links and redirects, the
order of the fields, the apps' addresses and what Join opens), `MeetingTests` (the order, the filters,
two at once, the meeting about to start, the clocks going forward and back, a zone of its own, the
words, the fitting by width, the face's three settings, Graph's and CalDAV's fields, the cache, the
settings' round trip), `MeetingPictures` (meeting-faces-dark/light.png and meeting-lines(-light).png,
the click on Join on the face and on the line). By hand: with a Microsoft account that has a Teams
meeting today, add Next meeting from the add list's Time page; ten minutes before it Join turns to the
accent, and a click opens Teams.

## 206. A day view stays a day view (2026-10-17)

"If i place the day view it transitions into a week view on reload." The file was never wrong: it kept
`"dayView"` (the user's config.json holds two of them, with a week and a year view, as placed). The
reading was. A folder's widget knows its line (`CellItem.List`) only once it is stood in its folder's
view (`Folders.Project`), which is not in the file; `Load` and `BarItem.Clone` do it, `Config.Clone`
did not. Every edit the dock makes starts from `config.Clone()` and applies the copy, so after any edit
(a line made taller, a widget moved) every folder's widget had no line, and `CalendarViewTile` read "no
line" as its default, the week. A day or year view turned into a week view until Karpo was started again.

- **`Config.Clone` stands every folder's widgets in its view**, as `BarItem.Clone` does, so a copy reads
  as the file does.
- **`CalendarViewTile` takes its view from its word** (`ListWidgets.Find(Info.Id)`), as `SoundPartTile`
  and `QuickPageTile` already took theirs, so it no longer depends on the projection at all. No other tile
  read `CellItem.List` with a fallback.

Nothing to repair in anyone's file: the word was always written as placed. Tests:
`CalendarViewKindTests.AViewStaysItsViewThroughLoadsCopiesAndSaves` (day, week and year through load,
reload, the dock's copy and its save), `CalendarWeatherFolderTests.AViewIsItsWordsWithoutALine`. By hand:
put a day view in a folder, make it taller or move something on the bar, and it is still a day view.


## 207. A column's width of its own, and no limit but the screen (2026-10-17)

The person: "there should also be an option to set the columns width yourself and there should
basically be no limit on how wide."

- **Stored per list, in DIPs, additively**: `FolderOptions.CustomWidths` beside `Widths`, 0 for a
  list whose width is its preset's, null and not written until a list has one. A list given a width
  keeps the preset nearest it in `widths` too, which is what an older build reads. A width a preset is
  is stored as that preset (`Folders.SetWidthDip`), so a file of presets reads and writes exactly as
  before. A preset picked clears the list's own width, and the field goes once no list has one.
- **Limits**: the least is narrow's 280 DIPs (`FolderListWidths.LeastDip`), what the lines' designs
  need. The most kept is 16384 DIPs (`MostDip`), a sanity bound for hand-edited files that is wider
  than any display. The real most is the screen: `FolderFlyout.ListWidths` narrows a folder wider than
  its work area (less 12 DIPs a side) on that display only, the widest lists first down to a level the
  rest share (`Fit`), never under the least. The file keeps what was set, and the plan and the
  measuring of the lines ask the same function, so the two always agree.
- **On the bar, arranged**: each list has a width handle, a 4×32 DIP pill in the gap at its end, on
  its right, or on its left in Arabic, Urdu and Persian, where a column ends there. It takes the press
  across at least 10 DIPs, the pointer is the sizing arrow over it, and it lights under the pointer
  and in the accent while held. A drag lays the folder out live from a copy of its options, the file
  untouched, and the folder stays centred on its button. The handle is kept under the pointer by
  asking the plan where it would stand for each width (`Solve`), because adding the pointer's travel
  to the width would be halved by the centring. Widths are whole DIPs, the presets are soft detents
  (6 DIPs), and the most is what the display has room for beside the other lists. Letting go hands
  the dock the width (`FolderFlyoutAction.Resized`), which saves it. Losing the mouse puts the list
  back. The width menu beside the "+" ticks "Custom: N px" for a list with a width of its own, and a
  preset picked there replaces it.
- **In Settings**: the folder page has "Column widths", an expander with a row per list: Narrow,
  Medium, Wide or Custom, and the width in pixels beside them (a NumberBox, 280 and up).
- **Wide lines**: every kind was pictured 1200 DIPs wide at 150 % (`ColumnWidthPictures`). Each fills
  its width or stays at its start as its own rules say (graphs and sliders fill, rows and words keep
  to the start, the year view centres its months). Nothing needed changing.

Tests: `ColumnWidthTests`: the round trip, preset files unchanged, the limits, the width moving with
its list, widest-first fitting, a small display narrowing the folder but not the file, the menu, the
solver and detents, and the handle dragged live in English and in Arabic (UI). By hand: arrange a
folder, drag a column's handle well past wide, let go, and reopen the folder. On a smaller display
the same folder fits and the Settings row still says the width you set.

## 208. Join wherever a meeting is listed (2026-10-17)

The person: "also add the join button to meetings in the calendar or at other places where meetings
appear." Every list of events now gives a meeting the Join the next meetings' line has (§205), by one
rule and one drawing (`JoinButton.cs`): a timed event with a link Karpo knows (`MeetingLinks`) that has
not ended. An event over, one with no link, and an all-day event have none. Windows 11's standard
button with the camera and "Join", the camera alone where the word does not fit, filled with the accent
from ten minutes before the start until the end (`MeetingTile.Lead`).

**Where.**
- *The day's events* (`EventsTile`, the calendar preset's list, "Clock & calendar", "Today"): at the
  row's trailing gutter, up to 32 DIP tall in the middle of the row, "Join" with the camera where that
  leaves two thirds of the row, the words cut short of it.
- *The day and week views* (`CalendarViewTile`, laid out by `CalendarLayout.JoinIn`): on the block,
  against its right edge level with the first line, 24 DIP tall or the block's height, where the words
  keep 48 DIP beside it ("Join" with the camera where that holds, else the camera); in a narrow week
  column, the camera on a square at the block's foot under a line of words; failing that beside a little
  of the words; else none. Drawn over the hours, the now-line and the words, clipped to the hours' window.
- *The calendar's agenda* (`CalendarIsland`): in its whole form at the end of each meeting's row; its
  one-row and compact forms have no room for it.
- *The next meetings' line* (§205) as before, now with the keys, the menu and the tooltip below.
- *The year view* shows no events (dots under days), nor does the month (`MonthTile`): no Join. Nor the
  date-and-time face's default folder (the notification centre: notifications, the date, the month,
  focus), which lists no events; its "Clock & calendar" and "Today" folders list the day's events, and
  have it there.
- *The meeting face on the bar* has had its Join since §205; its right click now has "Join meeting" too.

**A click on Join is the Join's.** The line answers it with an app opening (`IslandView.App`); a line
that lists meetings (`IMeetingLine`) acts for that, though its kind's click acts on nothing
(`FolderFlyout.ActOf(cell, island)`), and the dock opens the meeting once the folder has gone
(`IMeetingLine.Open`, `MeetingJoin`: the app's own address where it is installed). In the day and week
views the Join is a target before the day under it (`CalendarViewTile.JoinTarget`), so it picks no day.

**The keys.** The lit Join is the line's default button, as an accent button is a dialog's: Enter or
Space on the line joins the meeting on now or about to start (in the views, the one on a day in view).
A line's buttons are not separate stops for Tab, which moves between lines.

**The menu.** A right click on a meeting with a Join — its row, or its block, with the button or too
small for it — has "Join meeting" first, then a rule, then the kind's own rows (`WidgetAct.JoinMeeting`;
the calendar kinds but the year's, and the meeting face). Over anything else the row is not there.

**Names.** Each Join's piece is called "Join" and the meeting's title ("Join Design review",
`JoinButton.Name`), the name a screen reader is to read once folders have a tree; its tooltip is the app
("Join in Microsoft Teams"), which the camera alone does not say. Two words more in all 30 languages
(`dock.meeting.joinMeeting`, `dock.meeting.joinNamed`). Nothing in the file changes.

Tests: `JoinEverywhereTests` — which events have a Join and when it is lit; the menus' rows; the day's
events, the day and week views and the agenda each with a Join exactly on the linked meetings not over,
a click on it joining and not the event's (no day picked), a click beside it not joining, Enter joining
the lit one, "Join meeting" over a meeting and not over a workshop; pictures join-events, join-dayView,
join-weekView, join-calendar (dark and light) and join-clockCalendar.png at 150 %. By hand: with a Teams
meeting today, open the calendar's folder: its row has Join, accent ten minutes before; in a week view a
one-hour meeting has the camera at its foot, a half-hour one none, and its right click has "Join meeting".

## 209. One widget, several styles (2026-10-17)

The person: "it should not be different widgets anymore, but one type of widget, calendar in this case,
with different styles, agenda, day view, week view, etc... change this for other widgets where it
applies too."

**The widgets and their styles** (`WidgetStyles`, Karpo.Core\WidgetStyles.cs). The file's word for the
widget is its "kind", the style its "style"; the first style is the word alone.

| Widget (`kind`) | Styles (`style`: the form it was, its old word) |
|---|---|
| Calendar (`calendar`) | Agenda (first: `calendar`), Day's events (`events`), Day (`dayView`), Week (`weekView`), Month (`month`), Year (`yearView`) |
| Weather (`weather`) | Now (first: `weatherNow`), Hourly (`weatherHours`), Daily (`weatherDays`) |
| Sound (`sound`) | Volume (first: `soundVolume`), Output device (`soundOutput`), Input device (`soundInput`), Volume mixer (`soundMixer`) |
| Performance graph (`performance`) | Processor (first: `cpu`), Graphics (`gpu`), Memory (`memory`), Disk (`disk`), Network (`network`) |
| Performance details (`performanceDetails`) | Processor (first: `cpuDetails`), Graphics, Memory, Disk, Network (`gpuDetails`, …) |
| Clock (`clock`) | Clock (first: `clock`), Date (`dateHeader`), Time and date (`timeHeader`) |

Kept apart, as planned: the timer, stopwatch, focus time, alarm and next meetings; the notifications
and do not disturb; the to-do list and the note; the switches (spatial sound among them: a toggle, not a
region of the sound panel); the drives; the processor's top processes. The readings' details are a
widget of their own beside the graph, the reading their style too: graph and details stand one over the
other in a reading's folder, and a style of "graph or details" crossed with the reading would have been
two choices for one.

**What a style is in code.** Each style was a widget and keeps its record in `ListWidgets` (its form):
its rows, its range, whether it grows, what draws it, what a click and a press do, the channels it
follows. A placed widget's `Kind` is its form's word in memory, so drawing, measuring, the menus' own
acts and the channels are unchanged, and nothing looks different. The file writes `CellItem.FileKind`
and `FileStyle`; they read back to the form (`WidgetStyles.FormWord`), whichever of the two a file
puts first. A style changed is a form changed: the folder remakes a line whose record changed, as it
did for any other change of kind.

**A style changed** (`WidgetStyles.Restyle`) keeps the line's id, its place, its height, its alignment
and every options record: `WidgetItem.Normalize` keeps a record another style of the widget reads
(`WidgetStyles.Keeps`) and makes only its own where there is none — a clock's zone and label kept
while it is the date, a graph's adapter and disk while it is the processor's, an output's hidden
devices while it is the mixer, an alignment while a style has none. The height is held to the new
style's rules as any height is (`LineHeight.Within`): an automatic height becomes fixed in a style
whose content does not vary (the month, a day view).

**Where it is chosen.**
- *The add list* (`Catalogue`, `AddTree`): one row per widget, its first style's, named, iconed and
  described as the widget, found by every style's name and words ("week" finds Calendar). The other
  styles are no rows. The readings' four folders under System are their presets now, the graph and the
  details one row each beside them.
- *Settings*: the widget's page starts with "Style", a dropdown of its styles (`IslandOptions.StyleIndex`);
  the page then shows the new style's cards. Its title is the widget and the style, "Calendar · Week"
  (`settings.widget.title.styled`), and the clock in its own style is "Clock".
- *The line's menu* (`StyleRows`, Karpo.Dock\StyleRows.cs), arranged and at rest: "Style" with a
  submenu of the styles, the one the line is in ticked at the row's end; a pick restyles it where it
  stands, saved at once, and the folder stays open (`Dock.PickHandsAway`).

**The file: a migration, no reset.** The shape stays 37 (a new shape would set every older file aside).
A line in a form's word from before styles reads as the widget in that style (forever: every old word is
still read) and is written back in today's words in place, by `LineMigrations.MergeStyles` from
`Config.Repair`: `CellItem.ReadInOldWords` says which lines the file wrote otherwise than they are
written now, and the file is saved once. Nothing else about a line changes: the same id, the same place
in the same list, the same height (fixed, automatic or fill), the same options. `Config.Migrated`
records `widgetStyles` the first time; it holds nothing back, since a file in today's words has nothing
for it. "calendar" and "clock" with no style were the agenda and the clock and are read so, unchanged. A
style this build does not know is the widget's first. "weather" and "sound" were taskbar words once
(shapes before 23 and 25, which are set aside whole), so no file reads them as anything else. An older
build reading a file written now drops the lines it no longer knows by their words.

**Presets** say the widget and its style (`PresetItem.Style`, `PresetItem.Form`): the calendar
preset's `{ Kind = "calendar", Style = "month" }`.

**Words**: each widget's name, line and search words (`core.styled.*`), each style's name
(`core.widgetStyle.<widget>.<style>`, reusing the forms' own translations where a style is called what
the form was), "Style" for the page and the menu and the page's title, in all 30 languages.

**Faces on the bar** (`FolderFaces`) are not merged here: the readings' five faces could be one face
with the reading as an option, but a face is chosen in a gallery of looks on the folder's page, with its
own options per reading (the adapter, the disk), and merging them is a change to that gallery and the
faces' file words of its own.

Tests: `WidgetStylesTests` — every old word written as its widget and style in place (id, place, height,
options), today's words needing nothing, the style read wherever it stands and an unknown one the first,
the person's folders (a day view 20 rows, notifications filling, the date, the month, focus, the volume)
the same lines after, a style changed keeping everything and changed back being what it was, an option
only one style reads kept, the add list offering each widget once, the menu's Style submenu, presets in
today's words. Pictures of the person's own folders before and after (`WidgetStylePictures`, dark,
150 %), pixel for pixel. By hand: open Settings on a calendar line, change its style to Week and back;
right-click a weather line in a folder, Style ▸ Daily; restart and check the folders look as before.

## 210. Five column widths, and no width of one's own (2026-10-18)

The person, on §207's handle: "there should not be a handle, it does not work nicely. actually lets
not let them decide the width, just add like 2 more widths as selection and that should actually
already be enough, it does not have to be custom."

**§207 is superseded**: the width handle in each list's end gap (`FolderFlyout.Resize.cs`, the
`Resized` action, `Grips`), "Custom: N px" in the width menu, the pixel box on the folder's Settings
page, `FolderOptions.CustomWidths`, `Folders.SetWidthDip` and their words in all 30 languages are gone.
What stays of it is the screen fitting.

- **Five presets** (`FolderListWidth`, `FolderListWidths.All`, narrow to widest): narrow 280, medium
  360, wide 480, and after them **extra wide 640** and **widest 800** DIPs — each a step wider than the
  one before (+80, +120, +160, +160). Written `"extraWide"` and `"widest"` in `widths`; the three there
  were read and write as they did, and an older build reads the new two as medium (`TolerantEnumConverter`).
  Named once (`FolderListWidths.Name`) for the dock's menu and Settings alike.
- **Where it is chosen**: the width menu beside a list's "+" while the folder is arranged (five rows,
  the list's own ticked), and on the folder's Settings page, "Column widths", a dropdown of the same five
  for each list. No handle, no pixels.
- **The screen is still the one most** (`FolderFlyout.ListWidths`, `Fit`): extra wide and widest beside
  another list can be more than a small display has; where the lists and their gaps are wider than the
  work area less 12 DIPs a side, the widest give way first to a level the rest share, none under narrow,
  on that display only — the file keeps the preset. Lines are measured at the width they are drawn at.
- **Migration, no reset**: a file a build of §207 wrote may have `customWidths`. It is read once
  (`FolderOptions.OldCustomWidths`, as `width` was before it): each list with a width of its own becomes
  the preset nearest it of the five (`FolderListWidths.Nearest`, medium where two are as near, else the
  narrower), a list without one keeps its preset, and the field leaves the file with the next save. An
  older file's folder-wide `width` now finds its nearest of the five too.

Tests: `ColumnWidthTests` — each of the five picked, written by name and read back with nothing to
repair; a file of the three old presets the same text after a round trip; `customWidths` 0/1200/300/600
becoming medium/widest/narrow/extra wide with the lines and name intact and the field gone; the widest
giving way first, and narrow + widest + medium at 150 % on a 1920 px display narrowing only the widest,
the file untouched. `FolderListWidthTests` pins the five, their DIPs, the nearest preset and the menu's
five rows. Pictures (`ColumnWidthPictures`, dark, 150 %): a list at each width, the width menu open, and
the fitted folder. By hand: arrange a folder, open a list's width menu and pick Extra wide and Widest;
open the folder's Settings page and check Column widths offers the five.

## 211. Air quality (2026-10-18)

The person: "add an air quality widget". It is a widget of its own, `airQuality`, beside the weather
and not a style of it: §209 merged widgets that are one subject in several looks, and the air is
another subject — another index, other readings, another service's answer — that only shares the
weather's place. It shares everything else a weather widget has: the place (`WeatherOptions`, this PC's
location for a new one, "Set up in Settings" where none), the online interval with the weather's
15-minute floor, the offline cache, the stale rule and its words, Refresh and "Change location" on its
menu, the Weather page of the add list.

**The source.** Open-Meteo's air-quality service (`air-quality-api.open-meteo.com`), the weather's own
provider: free, no key, CC BY 4.0. One request per place (`AirAnswers.Url`, two decimals of a degree)
asks for both indices, PM2.5, PM10, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide now,
the pollen of six plants now (Copernicus' European model: null outside Europe), and both indices hour
by hour for two days in the place's time. `AirQualityStore` keeps one fetch per place for every face and
line showing it, as `WeatherStore` does (keyed by `WeatherStore.KeyOf`, this PC's location resolved by
the same `WeatherStore.Where`), in `air.json` in the local folder. An answer with neither index is
none ("The air quality couldn't be read"); every other failure is said in the weather's words.

**The index.** Where nobody chose, the place picks: the European AQI (EEA) inside the European model's
area, 35-72° N and 25° W-45° E, the US AQI (EPA) everywhere else — what MSN Weather, Windows' own, shows
outside Europe. Chosen, it is the face's option (`AirQualityFace.Index`) or a line's
`WeatherOptions.AirIndex` ("european", "us"; never written for the region's, only on an air line, a word
from a newer build kept and read as the region's). Bands, rounded to a whole number first:

| | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| European | ≤20 Good `#50F0E6` | ≤40 Fair `#50CCAA` | ≤60 Moderate `#F0E641` | ≤80 Poor `#FF5050` | ≤100 Very poor `#960032` | Extremely poor `#7D2181` |
| US | ≤50 Good `#00E400` | ≤100 Moderate `#FFFF00` | ≤150 Unhealthy for sensitive groups `#FF7E00` | ≤200 Unhealthy `#FF0000` | ≤300 Very unhealthy `#8F3F97` | Hazardous `#7E0023` |

On the bar the US third level is "Sensitive groups".

**The face** (`FolderFaces.AirQuality`, `AirFaceDrawing`): a dot in the level's colour (a hairline of
the text's ink round it, so the pale cyan and the yellow read on a light bar) and the index, in three
widths — "32", "32 · Good" (the default) or "AQI 32 · Good". It is measured from "888" and the widest
level word of its index (both indices' where the place picks), never from the reading, and says the
fullest form that fits that room (`AirText.Fit`); where it stands is its alignment (§201, the middle by
default). Stale or left standing by a failure, the words are quiet and the dot faded; nothing yet, a grey
dot and a dash; no place, the pin and "Set location"; down a bar on its side, the dot over the index.
Its tooltip: the place, "European AQI: 32, Fair", the pollutants with their units, the pollen, the age.

**The line** (`ListKind.AirQuality`, `AirQualityTile`), each piece where it fits whole: one row, the dot,
the level and the index at the end; two rows, the index large with the level over the index's name;
from three, the place and the age over that, then the scale's bands with a mark where it stands, the
four main pollutants (µg/m³), the pollen (Europe; "No pollen in the air" out of season), and the next
24 hours as bars in their levels' colours, as tall as the line leaves them (28-64 DIP). Four rows
unmeasured, one to eight. Nothing on it is pressed.

**The preset** (`Presets.AirQualityId`, "Air quality"): the face over the line, beside the weather's
in the add list's Weather page; the first place chosen is given to the face and the line alike
(`WeatherPlaces.Spread`, which now gives a place to an air face as to a weather face, each piece keeping
its own index). Settings: the place as every weather widget's, and an Index card on the line's page; the
face's index and width among its options. Words in all 30 languages. Nothing in the file changes shape:
a face, a line kind and one optional word more, which an older build reads past.

Tests: `AirQualityTests` (the answer read, with and without pollen, and what is no answer; the request;
both indices' bands at their edges, colours and words; which index a place gets; the face's forms by
room; the reading, its hours from the place's present hour, staleness, failures and the tooltip; one
fetch per place, Refresh, a failure keeping the last answer; the line's and the face's index through
the file, a file from before unchanged, the preset and its place), `AirQualityPictures`
(air-faces-dark/light.png: every level of both indices at the three widths, the states, 150 %, on its
side, one width per setting; air-lines-europe/us(-light).png, air-lines-europe-100.png at one to eight
rows). By hand: add "Air quality" from the add list's Weather page; with location on it shows the
European index in Europe; set the face's index to US AQI and its width to "AQI 32 · Good".

## 212. The bar's strip after a dark screen (2026-10-19)

The person: "right now the karpo taskbar clipped in front of windows again. just now it resolved, but it
happens after a dark screen." Maximized windows ran under the bars on both 4K displays, then were fine
again minutes later.

**What appbar.log showed.** Three times since 18 October, the same shape. 10:42:52 today the second
display went away as the screens lit (a DisplayPort display sleeping is a display removed), its bar was
removed and made again 2 s later; the first display's bar was held at that moment. 0.5 s after, both
work areas were the whole screen (`work 0,0..3840,2160 reaches into Bottom strip 0,2092..3840,2160`),
and the guard did what it was built to: a position and a registration every half second for 15 s, then
1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 s. Every registration came back "ok", every position went out through Karpo's tray
in 0-1 ms with Explorer answering at once — and no work area moved. At 10:47:02, 4 min 10 s and 40
failed checks later, both displays were held again in the same millisecond, at no check of Karpo's: the
shell had worked the work areas out again on its own. 22:51-22:52 yesterday it took 33 s (ending on a
registration that took Explorer 257 ms, its busy moment); on the afternoon of 18 October it lasted
hours, a repair every 5 minutes. So Karpo noticed within half a second and asked again correctly every
time; asking the shell again could not help, because the shell, after the displays came back, took
appbar messages and recomputed nothing (why it stalls is Explorer's own; the record cannot say more).

**The fix.**
- **The work area set directly** (`AppbarHolder.SetWorkArea`, `IAppbarShell.SetWorkArea`): a check that
  still finds the strip missing after its repair sets the display's work area itself with
  `SPI_SETWORKAREA` (announced, as Explorer announces it): the work area as it is, less the bar's strip
  on its edge (`AppbarGuard.Carved`, only ever smaller) — what the shell would have set. A repair that
  takes sets nothing; a shell that later works it out agrees with it. With a wake at the screen's return
  the first look is half a second after it, so the strip is back within a second.
- **Never a loop** (`AppbarGuard.SetsWorkArea`): only for a bar the shell registered, three times in a
  row in the fast window, then once per backoff repair (1, 2, 4 ... 30 s, 5 min), counted afresh at a
  wake and at a held check. Never from a dock on a desktop of its own: an isolated config, the stage, or
  no Explorer taskbar on the desktop sets nothing, since the work area is the session's.
- **Looked at every 2 s** (`AppbarGuard.CalmCheckMs`, was once a minute): a strip lost without a word
  stood under the windows for up to a minute; one `GetMonitorInfo` per bar every two seconds.
- **A display lit again wakes the bars** (`Dock.Lit`, `GUID_SESSION_DISPLAY_STATUS` on, the notice
  screen time already asks for): a dark screen can end with no change of displays, resume or unlock.
- **The trace says why**: `woke: the displays changed / a display's scale changed / resumed / unlocked /
  a display lit again` (once per burst), `Explorer's taskbar was made again (TaskbarCreated)`, `work area
  ... still on the strip: set to ... directly -> ok (n in a row)`, and `held again after n failed checks,
  the work area set directly k times`.

Tests (`AppbarHolderTests`): after a dark screen the shell that drops every position has both work areas
set directly within a second and held at the next look; a repair that takes sets none; a shell that
puts the whole screen back is set three times in the fast window and then 1, 2, 4 s apart, afresh after
a wake; a refused bar sets none; the carved work area per edge, and one already clear left alone; the
rule's table; a display lit wakes, dimmed or dark does not. To watch: after the next dark screen,
`appbar.log` should show `woke: ...`, at most a line or two of `NOT held`, a `set to ... directly`, and
`held again` within a second; a run of `directly` lines that never ends in `held again` would mean
something puts the whole screen back each time.

**Superseded by §272** (2026-10-22): the look every two seconds, the half-second wake bursts and the
backoff are gone; the work area set directly is the second step of a repair, which comes on events and
one settle a second after, within a budget of four a minute.

## 213. A click in edit mode opens the widget's menu beside it; an open folder has edit mode to itself (2026-10-19)

The person: "left click in edit mode when i select a widget should not open or close a folder anymore
but it should bring up the current right click menu that is placed at one of four places around the
widget. this should be for folder and taskbar widgets. the folder can be opened with an additional item
in the edit box then. when the folder is opened the taskbar should not be able to be edited, the taskbar
should be darkened out too in the folder edit mode. in folder edit mode there should be a close icon at
the top right."

This supersedes what earlier sections said a click on a folder does in edit mode (`EditClicks.OnBlock`
opened or closed it; a double-click's folder stayed open behind the settings window).

**A click selects and opens the menu** (`EditClicks.OnBlock`: follow, then menu, for every kind). On a
bar's widget and on a line of a folder open arranged alike: the widget is selected (Ctrl and Shift as
before, Dock.EditSelect.cs), an open settings window follows quietly, and the menu its right click opens comes
up beside it — the same rows, a folder's with **"Open folder"** under its row of buttons (or "Close
folder" where it stands open; `Dock.EditMenuRows`, `WidgetAct.OpenFolder`/`CloseFolder`). A row, not a
sixth button: the row of buttons stays at Explorer's five at most (§188), and a row under it is what a
widget's menu at rest has too (Dock.MenuFloor.cs). Space, Narrator's Invoke and the menu key open the
menu the same way; Enter on a folder opens the folder, on any other widget its page in front, as before.
A Ctrl/Shift click that leaves the widget selected opens the menu for the selection (its Remove and
Copy act on them all); one that takes it out opens none.

- **Where the menu stands** (`MenuSides`): anchored on the widget's rectangle, never the pointer, 8 DIP
  off it, on the first side with the room for the whole menu. A bar's widget: away from the bar's edge
  (over a bottom bar's, under a top bar's, beside a side bar's), then along the bar, then towards the
  edge. A folder's line: after it, before it, under it, over it. After/before are mirrored in Arabic and
  Urdu. A side counts only where the widget's middle along it is inside the work area (a bar's strip is
  not), and with no side roomy enough the menu takes the roomiest of those, cut to it. `Flyout.BesideWidget`
  places it once it knows its size; `Roomiest` is skipped for it.
- **One click from widget to widget.** A press on another widget closes the menu and goes on to select
  that one and open its menu. On the bar the bar already handled its own presses (LightDismiss); over an
  arranged folder the menu no longer uses up the press (§186 holds at rest only: `UsesUpPresses` is off
  while the folder's bar is arranged). A click on the widget whose menu stands only closes it (the bar:
  `PressedOn` records `menuClosedBy`; a folder: the hook's dismissal of that line's menu), but the second
  half of a double-click there still opens its page in front. A drag is still a drag: a press past the
  threshold moves the widget and opens nothing. A click on empty room or the dim closes the menu and
  clears the selection, as before.
- **The selection's own flyout** (SelectedFlyout.cs) stays shut while the menu stands, and opens again after
  a pick from it; dismissed, it waits for the next selection.

**Folder edit mode.** A folder open arranged has edit mode to itself (`Dock.BarLocked`):

- **The bars are locked**: a press, a drag, a lasso from their empty room, a right click and the keys
  (but Escape, and Ctrl+V into the folder) do nothing on any bar or place of any display, nothing lights
  under the pointer, the sections' warning buttons go, and the folder stays. The dim still draws the
  folder's lasso (EditScope).
- **And dimmed** (`EditView.Locked`, `Scene.Scrim`): every bar and place under 40 % black, the dim's own
  (`EditShade.Alpha`), over their panels' shapes (a floating bar's rounded docks each), faded in and out
  over 167 ms (`EditLook.ScrimMs`) on the decelerate curve, at once with animations off; a bar rebuilt
  meanwhile is built dimmed. The edit bar on top stays aside, as since 2026-10-16.
- **Its ×** (`FolderFlyout.CloseBox`, `PaintClose`): Windows 11's close caption button on its own, 32 DIP
  square, 4 DIP corners, the 10 DIP ChromeClose glyph — at rest the flyout's solid surface and rim (it
  stands over the dim, where a caption button's clear rest would be lost), red `#C42B1C` under the pointer
  and `#C83C31` held, the × white; high contrast the highlight. It stands outside the lists, level with
  their "+" row, at the top right of the folder (top left in Arabic and Urdu) — under the bottom right on
  a top bar, the side away from the bar, where the window keeps room outside the panels. A click is
  `FolderFlyoutAction.CloseAsked`: the folder closes, the bars un-dim and are arranged again. Escape does
  the same, as it did.
- **Drags between a folder and a bar**: none moved anything before either (Partners: a line dragged out
  over a bar was refused and the folder said why; a bar's widget over a folder the same). Now no drag can
  start on a bar while a folder is open; a line carried out of the folder over a locked bar is still
  refused with the folder's sentence.
- **One folder**: only one folder is open at a time, in edit mode as out of it (`OneFolder`, since
  2026-10-09); with the bars locked another opens only once this one is closed.

Words: "Open folder" and "Close folder" (`dock.widgetMenu.openFolder`, `.closeFolder`) in all 30 languages.

Tests: `MenuSidesTests` (the order of sides for every edge and a line, mirrored; the first side with the
room, the roomiest without; a bottom bar's widget never slid sideways; the anchor and edge of each side;
"Open folder"/"Close folder" and "Select none" rows), `EditClickTests` (every kind follows then opens its
menu, a folder never toggles; a double-click opens the menu once and asks for the page once; Space and
Narrator), `FolderEditClickTests` (a line's click carries its card on the screen; the arranged folder's ×
at its top right, clear of the "+" buttons, closes it; none at rest). Pictures (`EditMenuBesidePictures`,
150 %, dark and light): `editmenu-<edge>` — the four sides on a bottom, top, left and right Taskbar;
`editmode-folder-<bottom|top>` — the folder open arranged over dimmed bars with its ×;
`editmode-folder-menu` — a line's menu beside it. By hand: in edit mode click a widget (menu beside it),
click another (one click), click the same (closes), double-click (settings); click a folder → "Open folder";
in the folder the bar is dark and ignores clicks; × and Escape bring it back.

## 214. No card behind the widgets unless one is chosen (2026-10-19)

The person: "remove the backgrounds of the widgets. it should be still configurable but as default it
should be transparent."

- **The automatic look draws no card**: on the islands look (a Taskbar layout) each widget used to sit on
  Windows' card — `CardBackgroundFillColorDefault` with a 1 px `CardStrokeColorDefault` (§23.6). Now
  `Scene.Automatic` leaves `CardFill` and `CardStroke` empty in the dark and the light look, so the widgets
  stand on the bar's own material, as a Dock's do. Nothing else of the islands look moves: the gaps, the
  grouping, the corners of the highlight under the pointer stay the card's.
- **Still a setting**: Appearance → Custom colors → "Widget cards" and "Card outline" (§60). A colour
  chosen there draws the card again, in that mode, as before; "Reset all" takes it away. Nothing new is
  written to the file: absent is the default, and the default is now no card, so every bar without a
  chosen card colour loses its cards at once (as the mail preview's default flip did).
- **High contrast keeps its cards**: Windows' window colour with its text colour round it, so each widget
  still has an edge where Windows asks for edges.
- **A card chosen or taken back is a build**: a change of colours alone is recoloured in place (§60), but
  there is no card brush to recolour where none was drawn, so a card colour going from automatic to chosen
  or back builds the bars again (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`, `CardsShown`); a chosen card in another colour
  is still recoloured in place.

Tests: `BarColorThemeTests` (`WithNothingChosenTheWidgetsWearNoCard` dark and light,
`HighContrastStillDrawsItsCards`, `ACardChosenOrTakenBackIsBuiltAgain` for the card and its outline).

## 215. The row of buttons is icons alone; a widget's settings and a folder's faces in its menu (2026-10-19)

The person: "the settings row should only have icons not descriptions of the icons. the settings for the
processor graph, inline them into the context menu, all of them. in edit mode for the taskbar, you should
inline the settings for the folder faces into the left click menu. later all of the settings should be
tried to be inlined there but for now just for all the folder faces. adding and removing and reordering a
folder face should all be possible."

**The row of buttons** (Flyout.Primary.cs) is icons alone, as Explorer's command bar was before its words
came and WinUI's CommandBarFlyout's compact buttons are: square 40 DIP buttons (`PrimaryButtonDip`), the
16 DIP icon in the middle, the plate 4 DIP in all round (`PrimaryPlateDip`), a 20 DIP hairline between two
and 1 DIP at the row's ends, packed from the row's start (§186); the row is 40 DIP tall, the rule under
it as before. The name and the shortcut are the tooltip ("Copy (Ctrl+C)") and the spoken name, as they
were. This supersedes §178's icon-over-word buttons; `FlyoutItem.Word` and its three words ("Add",
"Edit", "Done") went.

**One description of a setting, two places** (Karpo.Core\OptionRows.cs). A setting is an `OptionRow`
read from the thing it sets — a widget, a face of a folder — carrying the way to set it there (`Set`);
Settings' page and the menu write through the same calls, so a pick in the menu leaves the file exactly as
the page's control does. Its kinds, and what the menu makes of each (Karpo.Dock\OptionMenu.cs):

- **Toggle** — a row with Windows 11's toggle switch at its end; a click, Enter or Space flips it and the
  menu stays open, showing it as it is now (`Flyout.Refresh`).
- **Choice** — a row opening a submenu of the choices, the one in force ticked at the row's end; a pick
  sets it and the menu closes, as a pick in Windows' own submenus does. The value is not repeated beside
  the chevron: in a menu of one width it cut the setting's own name short.
- **Number** — a row with the "− N +" stepper (Flyout.Controls.cs); a step sets it, the menu stays.
- **Elsewhere** — what a menu has no control for: a line of text, a time zone among hundreds, a place to
  search for, a share, an icon from the gallery, an adapter or disk where they were not listed. However
  many, one row, **"More settings…"**, opening the widget's page in Settings.

A row's command is one of `OptionMenu.FirstId` (10000) on, and what it stood for is kept with the menu
(`OptionPick`), so a pick acts on the setting it named. A control may now stand in a submenu too: the
submenu tells the root (`WM_KARPO_FLYOUT_ADJUST`; the keys go through `ControlKey` down the open
submenus), and `Refresh` shows the open submenu again in place, its lit row kept.

**A performance graph's menu** (rest and edit mode, every style — processor, graphics, memory, disk,
network — and the details' forms): under its buttons and its act (Resource Monitor), ruled off, every card
its page has, in the page's order: **Style** (the widget's styles; this replaces §209's StyleRows, now one
choice of the general rows), **Graphics adapter** (graphics: the main card, then this PC's, then a named
one not attached now), **Disk** (disk: all disks, then this PC's), **Show a graph** (toggle) and **How
often it updates** (every second to ten), then the height's rows (§168). The adapters and disks are
listed by the samplers the page lists them with (`AttachedDevices`, shared with Settings), and only for a
graphics or disk graph. The keys are the page's own property names (`StyleIndex`, `PerformanceGraph`,
`PerformancePace`, `PerformanceAdapterIndex`, `PerformanceDiskIndex`), and a test reads the page's markup
so a card added there without a row here fails. The processor graph has no per-core/total, frequency,
temperature, scale, palette or alignment setting on its page; none was invented.

**A folder's faces** (the menu a click opens on an arranged bar, §213, and its right click there): under
its rows, ruled off, a heading **"Faces on the taskbar"**, then a row per face in the button's order, its
glyph and its name (a clock's label after it), opening a submenu of the face's settings — the rows its
section on the folder page has (`FaceRows.Rows`, each while its condition holds): switches, choices,
alignment, a reading's pace, adapter and disk, the weather's "Use my device's location", the stock's chart
range and years, the name beside a face alone on its button; its place, share, icon, label and zone
"More settings…" — then **Move earlier**, **Move later** and **Remove** *face*, greyed where they cannot
act (the first, the last, the only face). Last, **"Add a face"**: the face gallery's groups (FaceGallery,
now the core's) each a submenu of its faces, one the button cannot wear greyed (a face that does not
repeat and is worn; all of them once the button wears eight). Adding, removing and moving use the page's
own calls (`FaceRows.AddFace`, `RemoveFace`, `MoveFace` — a move is what the page's drag does,
`Reordering.Moved`) and close the menu: the button changes under it. A face's pick acts only while the face
in its place is still of the kind it was shown for. A folder has no "active face": its faces stand side by
side. Moving by a menu row is not an arrow: the page's list is still reordered by drag (2026-10-12).

Words: `dock.edit.moreSettings`, `.faceEarlier`, `.faceLater`, `.less`, `.greater` in all 30 languages;
the rows' titles and choices are Settings' own. `dock.edit.style` went with StyleRows.

Tests: `OptionMenuTests` (each kind's row; every face option and every graph setting set from the menu
leaves the same file as the page's control; faces added from the groups, greyed where they cannot be
worn, moved and removed as the page does, a stale pick ignored; the menu shown again in place; the graph's
rows against the page's markup, and every face's rows against its section; on a real menu a toggle in a
face's submenu acts from the keys and the submenu stays through a Refresh), `MenuLookTests` (the icon
row's measures at 100–200 %, its tooltips), `WidgetStylesTests` (the style choice). Pictures, 150 %, dark
and light: `option-menu-row` (the icon row), `option-menu-graph` (the processor graph, the pace's submenu
open), `option-menu-faces` (a folder's clock submenu), `option-menu-add` (Add a face › Time & calendar).
By hand: right-click a processor graph and flip "Show a graph" (the menu stays), pick a pace; in edit mode
click a folder, open a face, flip a switch, move it, add a face, remove one; hover the icon row for names.

## 216. Starting at sign-in sooner: a logon task beside the Run entry (2026-10-19)

"The taskbar has quite a while to start ... specifically when autostarting with Windows." Measured on the
person's PC from the event logs (Winlogon, Shell-Core's Run-key events 9705-9708) for the last eleven
sign-ins, and from appbar.log for the last one:

| | sign-in 2026-10-19 13:55:33.97 | the other ten |
|---|---|---|
| Explorer's shell ready (NotifyTrayStartIsReady) | +1.9 s | about +2 s |
| Explorer begins the Run entries (HKLM first) | +33.2 s | +25.6 to +35.0 s |
| Windows Security's tray icon, first in line, holds them | 19.1 s | 0.4 to 16.1 s |
| Karpo.exe started (HKCU Run) | +52.3 s | +26.1 to +50.3 s |
| Karpo's first log line, bars registered | +0.16 s, +0.21 s after its start | |
| Explorer's taskbar taken over, the strips held | +1.0 s, +1.2 s after its start | |

So of 53.5 s from sign-in to the bar, Windows waited 52.3 s before starting Karpo and Karpo took 1.2 s.
Explorer starts the Run entries late (its startup-app throttling) and one after another, each waited for.
Nothing in Karpo was going to win that back.

- **The logon task** (`Karpo.Core\StartupTask.cs`): while "Start with Windows" is on, the dock keeps a Task
  Scheduler task, `Karpo sign-in <SID>`, that starts it with `--startup --logon-task` when this person signs
  in: a logon trigger for their account alone, run as them with the least privileges (registered without
  elevation: tried from a medium-integrity shell with a throwaway task, then deleted), no delay, normal
  priority (Task Scheduler's default, 7, starts a program below normal with low I/O priority), no time limit
  (the default ends it after 72 hours), no battery conditions, IgnoreNew. Made through schtasks.exe off the
  dock's thread (50-150 ms), at every start and when the setting changes; remade when it starts another copy
  or was made by an older Karpo (its RegistrationInfo version, `1 <fingerprint of the path>`: schtasks hands
  the definition back in the console's code page, which loses letters such as "ë", so the path is compared
  by that ASCII stamp); removed when the setting goes off (by the dock, and by the settings app at once).
  Every Run-key person gets it on the dock's next start, quietly.
- **The Run entry stays**, and stays what decides: Task Manager's Startup apps, Settings > Apps > Startup and
  Karpo's card all show and switch it. A dock the task started goes on only while that entry would start
  Karpo (`TaskMayStart`: a Karpo.exe there, not switched off in Task Manager); otherwise it ends before it
  takes the mutex. When Explorer gets to the Run entry, its Karpo finds the task's running and ends on the
  instance mutex, as any second Karpo does. Refused by Task Scheduler (a locked-down PC), Karpo starts as
  before, from the Run entry.
- **The wait for Explorer's taskbar** (`Dock.Open`, `--startup`): now that Karpo may start before Explorer has
  made its taskbar, it waits for it only after the config, the window and the Direct2D device are made, and
  looks every 50 ms instead of 250, so the bars follow the taskbar at once.
- **Not done**: `Explorer\Serialize\StartupDelayInMSec = 0` would take the delay off every startup app,
  Windows-wide, and still leave them one after another behind Windows Security's icon; Karpo doesn't set it.

Expected: the bar about 1 s after Explorer's taskbar, some 3 to 5 s after sign-in, instead of 26 to 53 s.

Tests: `StartupRegistrationTests` — the task's definition (this person's logon, least privileges, priority 4,
no time limit, the arguments, an escaped path), reading it back, the stamp (ASCII, the path's spelling
aside), added once then left alone, remade for another copy, an older version or a broken definition,
removed when off, a refusal said; the task's copy follows the Run entry and Task Manager's switch, and only
the task's start is gated. By hand: after installing, start Karpo once (the task appears in Task Scheduler
as "Karpo sign-in S-1-5-…"), sign out and in; switch Karpo off in Task Manager's Startup apps and sign in
again (no Karpo); turn "Start with Windows" off in Karpo's settings (the task and the Run entry go).

## 217. One menu in edit mode; a folder's own edit bar (2026-10-19)

The person: "the separate right click menus in the edit mode should be removed. the folder should get
its own top edit bar with add widget add folder and close. the folder close button should be moved to
the top edit bar. the folder add buttons should be removed from the individual columns."
