This supersedes §213's folder × and what earlier sections said a right click does in edit mode, and the
columns' "+" (each list's end "+" since 2026-10-09, a slot's since 2026-10-12).

**One menu.** Edit mode has the one menu a click opens beside the widget (§213); a right click opens no
other (`EditClicks.OnRight`). On a bar's widget and on a folder's line alike it does what a click does:
selected, an open settings window following, the menu beside it — on one of several selected the menu
for them all, the selection kept, as Windows' lists keep it; on the widget whose menu its press closed
nothing more. On the room round the widgets, the bar's or a folder's, nothing: the room's own menu
(`EditRoomRows`, "Add", "Done editing", the settings' gear, "Select none") is gone with the right click
that opened it — the edit bars add, "Done" and Escape end edit mode, Ctrl+A and a click on the room
select and clear. The menu key and Shift+F10 open the same menu, as before. Out of edit mode every right
click is as it was.

**A folder's own edit bar** (Dock.EditDeck.cs, `EditDeck` with `folder: true`). While a folder is open
arranged the display's edit bar stands aside (§190) and the folder's stands in its place: the same
compact command bar, the same height, centred at the top of the display, over the dim and over the
folder's window (which passes the pointer through where it has nothing; its guide lines stop short of
the bar). Its buttons, by the display's bar's parts so the plan is the same (`EditDeckPlan.OnFolder`):

- **"Add a widget"** — the add list for the folder, hanging under the button. What is picked goes into
  the selected line's column — the one last clicked, else the first selected — else the column picked
  by a click on its room, else the first column that shows everything it has (the first of all where
  none does), at the list's end away from the bar, where its "+" stood (`FolderFlyout.AddPlace`,
  `AddPlaceIn`). The add flow is the one the "+" had (`AddInFolder`, `AddSpot` with the folder's id);
  a list too short for what it holds still says so with its warning. A line's menu "Add" goes into its
  own column the same way.
- **"Column"**, where the display's "Folder" stands. Folders do not nest (§9), so adding a folder in a
  folder means adding what a folder is made of: an empty column, medium wide, after the chosen column
  (else after the last; `Folders.AddList`), saved, and picked at once — the selection cleared — so "Add
  a widget" adds there next. New words: "Column" (`dock.edit.column`) in all 30 languages.
- **"Close folder"**, where "Close edit mode" stands, icon-only with its words as its tooltip (the
  menu's "Close folder"): the folder closes, the bars come back un-dimmed and the display's edit bar
  with them. Escape does the same, as before.

No "Separator" and no "Open settings" on it: a command bar's separator stands before "Close folder".

**No × on the folder.** The caption-style close button at the folder's corner (§213) is gone; nothing
stands there, and a press there is the room's (the selection rectangle).

**No "+" on the columns.** Each list keeps its round width button at its end away from the bar, centred
on it, and its warning beside it where it hides lines (`FolderAddKind.Width`, `Hidden`); each empty slot
keeps its width button alone. The "+" kinds (`End`, `Slot`) and `FolderFlyoutAction.Add` are gone, and
with them a slot's "+": a slot still becomes a column by a line dropped on it or a width picked for it,
and "Column" adds one beside the chosen column.

**Picking a column.** A click on a column's room — an empty one's "Add widgets here", or the room over a
shorter list — picks it as where "Add a widget" adds (`FolderFlyout.PickedColumn`), ringed in the
accent as a selected line is, while no line of the folder is selected; a line selected takes over (its
column), and a click on room that is no column's picks none. So every column, an empty one too, can be
added to.

Tests: `EditClickTests.ARightClickIsAClickAndTheRoomHasNoMenu`; `FolderEditClickTests`
(`ARightClickOnALineIsItsClick` — the same card as a click hands, at rest none;
`TheColumnsHaveNoPlusAndTheFolderNoCross`; a right click on the room opens nothing);
`EditDeckPlanTests.AFoldersEditBarAddsAColumnAndCloses`, `EditDeckClickTests.AFoldersEditBarStandsWhereTheDisplaysDoesAndAsks`;
`FolderAddTests` (no "+", `AddPlaceIn`: chosen, first with room, the end away from the bar);
`FolderColumnsTests.AClickOnAColumnsRoomPicksItForTheEditBar`; the columns' and slots' buttons in
`FolderColumnsTests`, `ListFolderTests`, `FolderSlotTests`, `FolderHiddenTests`. Pictures
(`EditMenuBesidePictures`, 150 %, dark and light): `editmode-folder-<bottom|top>` — the folder open
arranged over the dimmed bars, its edit bar at the top where the display's stood, no "+", no ×. By hand:
in edit mode right-click a widget (the same menu beside it, nothing at the pointer), the bar's room
(nothing); open a folder from its menu: its edit bar at the top; click a line, "Add a widget" (into its
column); click an empty column's room (ringed), "Add a widget" (into it); "Column" (a new empty column,
ringed); "Close folder" and Escape (the bars come back).

## 218. The widgets' cards are back by default (2026-10-19)

The person: *"revert the widget background change. as default the background of the widgets should be a
different color."* §214 is reverted: the automatic dark and light looks draw the widgets' cards again,
a colour from the bar's own as before §214, and a colour of one's own in Settings (Widget cards, Card
outline) still recolours them.

## 219. A menu stays open for a change; a submenu's row opens and shuts it (2026-10-19)

The person: *"in general, when i change a setting, choose something or do another action the submenu it
should not close the whole menu. because then if i want to change multiple things i always have to open
the stuff again. when a tree node is extended and i click it again it should close again. if i click
somewhere away from the node like it is already it should close the menu completely, as it is now."*

This supersedes §215's "a pick sets it and the menu closes" for a choice and "adding, removing and moving
close the menu" for the faces (Karpo.Dock\MenuKeeps.cs).

**A row that stays** (`FlyoutItem.Stays`). Picked by a click, Enter or Space, or a screen reader, it acts
and the whole menu stays, every submenu open, as a toggle's or a stepper's row already did: the menu says
`FlyoutEventKind.Adjust` (a submenu posts it to the root), and the dock acts and shows the rows as they
are now (`Flyout.Refresh`). Which rows stay, per kind:

| Row | Picked |
|---|---|
| A widget's setting: a toggle, a stepper's step, a choice in its submenu | stays; the switch, the value, the tick shown as they are now |
| A folder's face: "Move earlier", "Move later", "Remove …", a face from "Add a face" | stays; the faces shown again, a moved face's submenu open beside it where it went, a removed one's shut |
| "More settings…" (the widget's page in Settings) | closes |
| A line's height rows (radio buttons and stepper, §192) | stays, as before |
| A widget's own switch: Mute, Mute microphone, an app's mute, Shuffle, Energy saver, Do not disturb | stays; its tick flipped |
| A widget's own pick: an output or input device, the app a media line follows, a power mode | stays; the tick moved to it |
| A row whose words say its state: Play/Pause, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on/off, Repeat, a countdown's Start/Pause | closes: its words would be stale |
| A one-off command: Refresh, Clear all, Clear completed, Eject, Disconnect, Lap, Reset, a seek, Previous, Next, Longer, Shorter | closes |
| What takes the person elsewhere: a Settings page, an app, File Explorer, a file, a site, Join, Task view, End task (Windows' question) | closes |
| The row of buttons: "Copy" (the copy goes onto the pointer to be placed), "Settings", "Remove" (the widget is gone), "Edit taskbar" | closes |
| A taskbar layout picked in the bar's menu | closes: the bar is made again under it |
| A dropdown's choice, a list that is the whole menu: a column's width, a sound device's dropdown | closes, as a combo box does |

A widget's own switch or pick is shown ticked as the pick makes it (`MenuKeeps.Ticked`) rather than read
back, since Windows answers a mute or a device change a moment later; the next opening reads it.

**A row with a submenu** (`MenuKeeps.ParentClick`). A click on it opens its submenu where it is shut, and
shuts it, with every one under it, where it is open; the menu over it stays and the row stays lit.
Resting on a row a click shut does not open it again until the pointer has left the row. A submenu the
pointer resting opened (the system's menu delay) no more than 400 ms before the button went down, or
while it was down, is kept by that click, so the click that meant to open it does not shut it again; the
next click shuts it. The keys are as before: Right (Left in a mirrored menu) and Enter open a level, Left
and Escape shut one, Escape at the top closes the menu.

**A press outside** every level closes the whole menu, as before: FlyoutHost's light dismiss, a press in
a submenu's shadow margin, and over a folder the press used up for the menu alone (§185); edit mode's
pass-through is unchanged.

**Shown again in place.** `Flyout.Refresh` keeps the whole open path, not only the first submenu: level
by level, root first, the row a submenu hangs off is found again among the rows as they are now, by its
id and words, else by its words where they are one row's (a face moved, a row whose command shifted as
rows before it came or went; `MenuKeeps.Again`), and the submenu is shown beside it again without being
hidden first. Each level keeps its scroll and its lit row, and the keys stay where they were. A level
whose row is gone (a face removed, a setting a style change took away) shuts, with the levels under it.

Tests: `MenuKeepsTests` (the tables, `Ticked`, `ParentClick`, `Again`; on a real menu
`AChoicePickedKeepsEveryLevelOpenAndTheTickMoves`, `AParentsClickTogglesItsSubmenuWithoutFlicker`,
`TheKeysGoALevelAtATime`, `APressOutsideClosesEveryLevel`, `AMovedFacesSubmenuFollowsItAndARemovedOnesGoes`,
`ARefreshKeepsTheScroll`); `OptionMenuTests` (a pace picked from the keys stays);
`FolderMenuTests.ChoosingAnActThatStaysInKarpoLeavesTheFolderOpen` (Mute stays, ticked). By hand: a
graph's menu, "How often it updates", two paces in turn (the menu and the submenu stay, the tick moves);
click "How often it updates" again (its submenu shuts); in edit mode a folder's menu, a face, "Move later" twice (the
face's submenu follows it); a sound line's menu, Mute (ticked, the menu stays); a click away (all of it
closes).

## 220. Every setting of every widget is a row; the page reads and writes through them (2026-10-19)

The person: *"inline every setting of every bar widget (folder faces) and folder widget (lines) into its
edit menu; the Settings app keeps everything too; account management stays in Settings only — choosing
which calendar, To Do list or account a widget shows is a normal choice and must be inline."* This part
is the rows (Karpo.Core\OptionRows.Lines.cs): every card of the widget page (WidgetsPage.xaml), every row
of a face's section and every card of the folder page (FolderPage.cs) is an `OptionRow`, in the page's
order, shown where the page shows its card. How a menu draws them is §215's (OptionMenu.cs); the rows for
text, search, colour, icon, file and time fields are other parts' and come as kinds of their own.

**One write.** The page's controls read and write through the rows: `IslandOptions` asks `OptionRows.Of`
for the open widget with what the page has listed (`Sources`: the adapters, the disks, the drives, the To
Do lists, the notebook, the first day of the week) and sets a row with `SetRow`, then saves as before;
what only the page does around a write (a setup question answered, `PlaceChosen`, `DriveChosen`) runs
between the row and the save. The folder page's column widths go through `OptionRows.OfFolder`. The keys
are the page's property names (`DesktopsShowApps`, `AlarmOn`, …), a group's members its card's name and
the member's (`Toggle.Wifi`, `AlarmDay.1`, `Follow.day`, `StatusIcon.camera`, `ColumnWidth.0`).

**Lists** are choices of what was listed at menu-open (`OptionDevices`); where nothing was listed the row
is the page's. The drives: `DriveTargets.Attached`, the kinds the widget may show, then the drive it names
when that is not attached ("— not connected", which picks nothing): `OptionRows.DriveChoices`, the page's
list too. A to-do line's source: this PC, then each account's To Do lists as the dock last reported them,
never the network (Karpo.Accounts\TodoSources.cs, the page's list too); a list not named is its account's
default. The notebook's lists and notes: the notebook file the lines read. The dock lists them only for a
widget that offers them (`Dock.MenuSources`).

**A row a menu cannot set yet** says what it takes (`OptionRow.Field`): Text, Amount, Place, Zone,
Symbol, Search, Time, Icon. **A group** (`OptionRow.Group`) names the card several rows are one of — a
toggles row's toggles, an alarm's days, the status icons, the column widths — for a menu to put them in
one submenu. **A number's step** (`OptionRow.Step`): the volume's length steps four DIPs, as its slider;
a step past an end stops at it.

| Widget (options kind) | Rows: key — kind |
|---|---|
| any with styles | StyleIndex — choice |
| Virtual desktops | DesktopsShowApps — toggle |
| Weather, Air quality | WeatherUsesDevice — toggle; WeatherPlace — place; AirIndex (air quality) — choice |
| Stock | StockSymbol — symbol; StockLabel — text; StockRange — choice; StockYears (range in years) — number 1–50; StockHolding — amount |
| RSS | RssAddress — text |
| Processor, graphics, memory, disk, network | PerformanceAdapterIndex (graphics), PerformanceDiskIndex (disk) — choice of the PC's; PerformanceGraph — toggle; PerformancePace — choice |
| Clock, date | ClockSeconds (clock) — toggle; ClockZone — zone; ClockName (clock) — text |
| Drive, network drive | DriveIndex — choice of the drives attached |
| Timer, focus | CountdownMinutes — number 1–720; CountdownName — text; CountdownDoNotDisturb (focus) — toggle |
| Alarm | AlarmTime — time; AlarmOn — toggle; AlarmDay.0–6 — toggle each, group "Repeat"; AlarmName — text |
| Heading | HeadingText — text |
| Heading, dates, clock lines | AlignIndex — choice |
| Toggles row | Toggle.<toggle> — toggle each (on adds at the end, off takes out), group "Toggles"; the order is the page's drag |
| Actions line | ActionLeft, ActionRight — search |
| To-do line | TodoSourceIndex — choice of this PC and the accounts' To Do lists; NotebookIndex (on this PC) — choice of the notebook's lists |
| Note line | NotebookIndex — choice of the notebook's notes |
| Followers (calendars, screen time, …) | Follow.<channel> — toggle each |
| Windows search | WindowsSearchShowBox — toggle |
| Status icons | StatusIcon.<icon> — choice of three each, group "Status icons" |
| Volume | VolumeOrientationIndex — choice; VolumeLength — number 48–400, step 4; VolumeShowSpeaker — toggle |
| Screen time | ScreenTimeGraphIndex — choice |
| A line of items (mail, feeds, notifications, …) in a folder | ItemSizeIndex — choice; ItemsPreview, ItemsPictures, ItemsTime — toggle, each where offered |
| Brightness | BrightnessScreensIndex — choice |
| Pen menu, touchpad | InputButtonShowIndex — choice |
| One-button switches | SwitchShowLabel — toggle; SpatialFormatIndex (spatial sound), ColorFilterIndex (color filters) — choice |
| Folder | FolderName — text; ColumnWidth.<list> — choice each, group "Column widths" |
| Folder faces | §215: their options by kind (switch, choice, align, pace, adapter, disk — inline; text — text; zone — zone), the name beside a lone face — toggle, the weather's device — toggle, place — place, the stock's symbol — symbol, label — text, range — choice, years — number, the icon face's icon — icon |

Not rows, on purpose: the calendar's retired iCalendar address (copied or forgotten, its secret token
never shown), the empty toggles row's line, Windows' own pages opened from a card (location, the widget's
Windows settings), the notebook's New, Rename and Delete (they change the notebook, not the widget), and
the accounts themselves — signed in, reconnected and removed on the Accounts page. The pins' own page
(PinPage) is a pin's, no widget's, and not here. Nothing on the widget page chooses a calendar or a mail
account; none was invented.

Tests: `OptionRowsTests` — every card of WidgetsPage.xaml a row by its title or group (the two that are no
setting listed, each with why), every two-way control a row of its name, every FaceRowKind case and every
card of FolderPage a row, every Elsewhere row with its field; each row set through OptionRows leaves the
widget as the page's control did before it went through them, byte for byte; the lists offered (a drive
not connected, a To Do list by its account's default, the days from Monday); the volume's length stepped
by four and stopped at its end. `WidgetStylesTests`: a folder's rows are its own, no style. By hand: in
Settings, set a toggle, a choice and a number of a few widgets (a drive, a to-do line's source, an alarm's
days, a volume's length) and see them saved as before; on the bar, a to-do line's and a drive's menu offer
the lists.

## 221. Every column is there already; the folder's edit bar has no "Column" (2026-10-19)

The person: "in the edit folder view there is a column property at the top, remove that. in terms of
design there is no such thing as adding / removing a column. all the columns are already there
(conceptually), you can just change their width."

This supersedes §217's "Column" button and what it said a column is made by.

**No "Column".** The folder's edit bar (`EditDeck` with `folder: true`) is "Add a widget", the command
bar's separator and "Close folder" (`EditDeckPlan.OnFolder`: `AddPart`, `ClosePart`). `EditDeckAction.Column`,
the dock's `FolderDeckColumn` and `Folders.AddList` are gone, and the words "Column"
(`dock.edit.column`) with them in all 30 languages. Nothing anywhere adds or removes a column: the
room menu that could went with §217, the Settings page only sets the columns' widths.

**Every column is there.** Arranged, the folder shows its columns and, either side out to the screen's
edges, the empty slots (§148): each a column with nothing in it yet, a medium column's width, its guide
lines and its width button. There is no count to reach: the slots are as many as the screen holds. A
slot costs nothing until something is in it or its width is set — it is not in the file until then.
What makes one a column of the file is unchanged: a line dropped on it, a widget added into it, or a
width other than medium picked for it (`Folders.SetSlotWidth`), the slots between it and the columns
then empty medium columns; and an empty column stays in the file, a spacer at the width it was given.
The file reads and writes exactly as before.

**A slot is picked as a column is.** A click on a slot's room, level with the folder (the folder's
window takes that band now; above and below it the pointer still passes through, `PassesThrough`),
picks it (`FolderFlyout.PickedSlot`): ringed in the accent round the room an empty column would take
there (`FolderPlan.SlotRoom`), where "Add a widget" adds while no line is selected — a column of its own
there (`AddPlace` answers the slot's `FolderPlace.Slot`). A column's room clicked, or a line selected,
takes the pick over, and a click on room that is neither picks nothing, as before. When a widget is
added into the picked slot, or its width set, the column it became is picked
(`Folders.ListOfSlot`), so the next "Add a widget" goes there too; any other change to the columns
lets the slot's pick go, since the slots move with them.

Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests.AFoldersEditBarAddsAndCloses`,
`EditDeckClickTests.AFoldersEditBarStandsWhereTheDisplaysDoesAndAsks` (two buttons, no "Column");
`FolderColumnsTests.EverySlotHasItsWidthAndAClickOnItsRoomPicksIt`;
`FolderSlotTests.TheListASlotBecomesIsWhereItStood`; the empty columns' widths as before in
`FolderSlotTests.ASlotsWidthMakesItAnEmptyListThatWide` and `FolderListWidthTests`. Pictures:
`folder-slots-<bottom|left>-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`, its fifth folder a slot picked. By hand: in
edit mode open a folder: its edit bar has "Add a widget" and "Close folder" only; click the room of an
empty slot beside the folder (ringed), "Add a widget", pick one (a column there, still ringed); pick a
width for a slot (a column that wide, empty, kept after closing and opening the folder).

## 222. The menus' row: Cut, Copy, Remove at the end; faces on the first level; choices inline (2026-10-19)

The person: *"done editing and add a widget should be removed from the settings menu on the taskbar
widgets. reordering faces should be inlined on the first level and not on a sublevel, same for removing
a face. move earlier, move later and remove should be removed from the second configuration level. the
dropdowns on the second level e.g. the style or number format, alignment, etc, should all be inlined
into the second level and not be an additional level. remove the name of a folder as a configuration
option as it does not really show up anywhere anyways. the remove button on the taskbar widget settings
should be right aligned in the edit row. cut should be an additional option. settings should be removed
from the folder settings widget, as there wont be any additional things that you can configure in the
settings. in the row the order should be: cut, copy, space, then delete on the right side."*

**The row** (`Dock.WidgetButtons`, Flyout.Primary.cs). A widget's row of icon buttons, at rest and
arranged, on the bar and in a folder, a pin's while arranged: **Cut** (Ctrl+X), **Copy** (Ctrl+C), its
**Settings** — not a folder's: its faces are set in its menu, and its page has nothing more — then room,
and **Remove** (Del) alone against the row's far end, as Explorer's Delete stands apart; its far left in
a mirrored menu. `FlyoutItem.PrimaryEnd` now means that: `PrimarySpans` packs the far group against the
row's end (`endFrom`, `width`), no hairline over the room between, never over the first group where the
row has no room. The bar's own buttons ("Add a widget", "Edit taskbar" / "Done editing") are gone from
widgets' rows, with `BarButtons` and `MostBarButtons`: adding and leaving edit mode are the edit bar's
and Escape's, "Edit taskbar" the bar's own menu's. Tooltips "Cut (Ctrl+X)", "Copy (Ctrl+C)", "Remove
(Del)".

**Cut** (Dock.EditSelect.cs, Dock.EditCopy.cs). Ctrl+X in edit mode, on the bar and in a folder open
arranged (`EditKeyAct.Cut`, `FolderFlyoutAction.Cut`), and the row's Cut: what Ctrl+C would copy of what
it acts on (`Dock.Clipped`: the bar's widgets where there are any, else the lines) goes on edit mode's
clipboard as it is now and comes out of the file in one change, asking nothing — Ctrl+V puts it down
again, with new ids. No marching ants: what they would mark is gone. From a menu at rest it turns edit
mode on first, as Copy does, so the paste is a keystroke away. Karpo has no undo; the clipboard is the
way back. New words: "Cut" (`dock.menu.cut`) in all 30 languages.

**A folder's faces on the first level** (OptionMenu.cs, Flyout.Reorder.cs, Flyout.Controls.cs). Under
"Faces on the taskbar" each face is a row opening its settings, and at its end a grip (the settings
app's six dots) and a remove button (`FlyoutControl.Tools`, `FlyoutTool`): small icon buttons with a
plate under the pointer and a tooltip each, hit-tested apart from the row — a click elsewhere on the row,
the grip's included, opens its submenu. The face rows are one `FlyoutItem.Reorder` group: a row pressed
and moved past the drag distance follows the pointer up and down among them, the others sliding aside
as the overflow's icons do (`GapPlaces`), and let go it says `FlyoutEventKind.Reorder` with its new
place; Escape, a right press or the capture lost put it back. Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down on the lit row move
it a place; Delete on it is its remove button. The menu stays open through a move and a removal
(`OptionMenu.KeepsOpen`), shown again as the button is now, the moved face's row lit where it went
(`Flyout.Refresh(items, litId)`, `OptionMenu.FaceRowOf`); §219's "Move earlier" and "Move later" rows, whose face's
submenu followed it, are gone with the submenu's own rows — a drag closes the open submenu. No up and down arrows: dragging, as the standing
rule has every list that can be reordered, and the keys. One face: grip and remove greyed. The submenus
have no "Move earlier", "Move later" or "Remove" any more.

**No third level.** In a submenu — a face's settings — a choice (a style, a number format, an
alignment, a pace, an adapter …) is a group of its own (`OptionMenu.Rows(inline: true)`): its name as a
small heading, its choices as rows with the one in force ticked at the end, ruled off from the rows
round it; toggles and steppers as before, "More settings…" last. A pick sets it and the menu stays, the
tick moving (FlyoutItem.Stays, §219). A widget's own choices on its menu's first level (a line's style, a
graph's pace) stay submenus: they are the second level already.

**The folder's name.** The Name box is gone from the folder's page in Settings; the file keeps the name
as it is (a preset's title, else "Folder"). It is still what a screen reader calls the button, its
tooltip while empty, the title of the question before deleting it, the folder's page title in Settings,
and what the "Show name" row of a lone icon or contents face puts beside the button — that row stays,
reading the stored name.

Tests: `WidgetButtonsTests` (the row: Cut, Copy, Settings, Remove at the end, a folder's without
Settings, nothing of the bar's; Cut takes what Copy takes and Paste puts it back), `MenuLookTests`
(`TheFarEndsButtonsStandAgainstTheRowsEnd`, the shortcuts and tooltips, Ctrl+X), `RightToLeftPictures`
(Remove at the far left), `OptionMenuTests` (`InASubmenuAChoiceIsAGroupOfItsOwn`,
`EveryFacesSubmenuHasItsChoicesInline`, `AFaceIsMovedAndTakenOffAsThePagesListDoes`,
`ARowDraggedLandsWhereTheGapIs`; on a real menu `TheFacesAreMovedAndTakenOffOnTheMenusFirstLevel`: the
remove button by the mouse and its tooltip, the grip's click the row's, a drag by the mouse, Escape,
Ctrl+Up, Ctrl+Down and Delete, the lit row after a move, the row's ends LTR), `MenuKeepsTests` (a face's
choice picked inline, both levels staying; a face moved by Ctrl+Up, its submenu following it, and taken
off by Delete), and the menus' lists of buttons throughout. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `option-menu-row`, `option-menu-faces`,
`option-menu-cpu`, `option-menu-drag`, `option-menu-graph`, `menu-*`, `rtl-menu-ar`. By hand: right-click
a widget (Cut, Copy, Settings … Remove at the right; no Add, no Done); a folder's (no Settings); in edit
mode Ctrl+X a widget and Ctrl+V it back; open a folder's menu in edit mode, drag a face row up and down,
Ctrl+Up/Down and Delete on one, the trash button; open a clock face's settings (Clock and Alignment
inline, no third level).

## 223. Text and search fields in the menus (2026-10-19)

The person: *"inline every setting of every bar widget (folder faces) and folder widget (lines) into its
edit menu, so configuring happens in the menu; the Settings app keeps everything too."* §215 left what a
menu had no control for — a line of text, a place, a time zone, a share — to one "More settings…" row.
Those are fields in the menu now; only a stock's holding (an amount), an alarm's time and an icon (the
gallery's) are still the page's. Account management
(signing in, reconnecting, removing an account) stays in Settings alone.

**A text field** (`Karpo.Dock\MenuTextField.cs`, the row `FlyoutField`, `Flyout.Fields.cs`) is the
setting's name over Windows 11's text box, as WinUI's TextBox puts its header over it: the name where
the menu's words stand, the box from there to the row's end, 32 DIP with radius 4, a faint fill and a
thin outline whose bottom edge turns into 2 px of accent while it has the keys, the page's placeholder
greyed while it is empty, a clear button (✕) at its end while it has the keys and words, and a search's
magnifier after it. The row lights no plate under the pointer; its box lightens, the text cursor over
its words. What it holds and every edit is `TextEditing`'s, the model every Karpo field edits with:
caret and selection, the pointer (a click puts the caret, a drag selects, a double click the word),
arrows, Home and End (with Shift and Ctrl), Ctrl+A/C/X/V and Shift+Delete/Insert, Backspace and Delete
(with Ctrl a word), a surrogate pair in two messages as one character. An IME composes in its own window
put at the caret, and what it chooses arrives as characters, as in the notes. In Arabic and Urdu the
menu is mirrored and so is the box: its words at its right, its buttons at its left; words written right
to left are hit-tested and scrolled by DirectWrite.

**The keys are the field's.** A click in a field, or the arrows bringing the keys onto its row, put them
there (a search's words selected, so typing replaces them; a text field's caret at the end). While a
field has them every key is its own: the menu's arrows, its shortcuts (Delete for "Remove", Ctrl+C for
"Copy") and its accelerators hear none. Up and Down (Tab, Shift+Tab) go on to the rows round it. **Enter
keeps** what was typed; **Escape** first puts back what the setting says, then lets the keys go, and only
the third Escape closes the submenu or the menu. Words typed and left — the keys moved on, the menu
closed by a click away — are kept, as the page's box keeps them as it loses the focus. The keys are the
root menu's window's (a submenu takes no activation); the root hands them to the field that has them,
wherever the pointer roams.

**A search field** (`Karpo.Dock\MenuSearch.cs`) has its results as rows of the menu under it, each its
words and a quieter line — no icon and no tick, either of which would take a column of every row of the
menu as the results come and go and move its words or its shortcuts —; a greyed row says "Searching…", that nothing was found,
or that the service could not be asked, in the page's words. Typing asks a moment after the last key (the
page's 300 ms), at once where nothing is asked of a service; a newer search wins (an older answer is
dropped however late, and called off); a time-out nobody asked for is "could not ask", not a search left
searching. Down goes into the results; Enter or a click picks; typing or Backspace on one goes back to
the field, and so does Escape. A pick is proved before it is kept where the page proves it ("Looking up
AAPL…"), and refused in words where it is no good. Enter in the field keeps the first found for the
words typed, else the words where they are a thing of their own (a symbol written out — "F" is Ford —,
an address), else asks at once. Left
without a pick, the field says what the setting says again. The menu is shown again in place as the
rows come and go.

**What uses them** (`Karpo.Core\OptionFields.cs`: new `OptionRowKind.Text` and `.Search`). §220's rows
say which field each setting takes on its page (`OptionField`); every row of field `Text`, `Place`,
`Zone`, `Symbol` or `Search` is now a Text or a Search row where it stands among the widget's rows
(`OptionRows.Lines`), keeping its field, and `Amount`, `Time` and `Icon` stay "More settings…":

- Faces: the clock's **label** (text) and **time zone** (search); the weather's and the air quality's
  **place** (search, "Use my device's location" first, then Open-Meteo's places); the stock's **symbol**
  (search of the price service's listings, each looked up before it is kept), its **currency pair**
  (From and To, two choices) and its **name on the bar** (text).
- Widgets: a heading's **text**; a clock's **time zone** and **label**; a timer's
  and a focus session's **name**; an alarm's **name**; a weather's and an air quality line's **place**;
  a stock line's **symbol**, **pair** and **name on the bar**; an RSS line's **feed address** (read as a
  feed before it is kept); an actions line's **left** and **right** page (search of the actions by name
or section, as the page's picker finds them, "None" first); a pin's **name**. A folder has no name
(§222), in the menu or on the page.

**A time zone** is searched over Windows' zones as the page's box searches them (`TimeZoneSearch`: a
city, part of an id, "+9"): this PC's first, then the zones the person's other clocks show — their lines'
and their faces', most used first (`OptionFields.ZonesInUse`, read from the file as the menu opens) —,
and among what is typed the person's own first. **A currency pair** is two choices, the region's
currency and the world's most traded first (dollar, euro, yen, pound, franc, yuan, Canadian and
Australian dollar), then the rest by code; a pick makes the share's symbol the pair ("EURCHF=X") named as
the page names one ("Euro → Swiss Franc"), a currency the other already is swapping the two; nothing is
ticked while the symbol is a share.

**The same write as Settings.** What a field keeps is set through the very row the menu showed, on a
copy of the file, saved where it changed (`Dock.MenuFields.cs`, `FieldPicks.Keep`): a face's through
`FolderFace.Set` and `FolderRows`' writers, which are the core's now (`WeatherPlaces.Choose`,
`StockSymbols.Choose` and `.Label`); a widget's through `OptionTexts`, which the widget page's model
(`IslandOptions`) and the pin page call too. The searches the page's boxes make moved to the core with
them (`Places`, `PlaceQuery`, `Symbols`, `SymbolQuery`, `TimeZoneSearch`, `CurrencyNames`, `FeedCheck`),
so the menu and the page find, prove and say things alike. Nothing in the file changes shape.

New words: "Clear text" (`dock.edit.fieldClear`, the clear button's name) and "No time zone matches
“{text}”." (`dock.edit.zoneNotFound`) in all 30 languages; the rest are the page's own.

Tests: `MenuTextFieldTests` (the keys: editing, the clipboard, Enter, Escape twice, Up/Down/Tab, every
other key the field's, a surrogate pair, the box's length, the setting changing under typing, the clear
button); `MenuSearchTests` (the wait, a newer search winning, an answer after the field closed, nothing
found and no service, a time-out, a pick proved or refused, Enter, the zones at once);
`OptionFieldsTests` (each widget's fields; each face's and each widget's write the same as Settings', byte
for byte; the pair; the zones in use); `OptionMenuTests` (the kinds; a face's rows still its section's);
`MenuFieldTests` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1: a field keeps Delete, Home and Escape from the menu; Enter and Down
keep, the menu staying; words left as the menu closes; a zone's rows, Down into them, Enter picks; an
answer off the menu's thread). Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `menu-field-zone-<look>` (a clock face's
zone searched for "tok" in its submenu), `menu-field-place-<look>` (a weather face's place, "Use my
device's location" first), `menu-field-text-<look>` and `menu-field-text-rest-<look>` (a timer's name
typed and at rest), `menu-field-rtl` (Arabic, mirrored). By hand: open a clock's menu, click its label,
type, Enter (the clock shows it); its time zone, type "tok", Down, Enter; a weather face's place, "bern",
pick; a stock line's symbol, "apple", pick (looked up); Escape in a field (the setting back, then out);
type in another script with an IME (the composition at the caret).

## 224. Colours, icons, a pin's target and times in a widget's menu (2026-10-19) — a colour of one's own mixed in its picker, Windows' colour dialog and "Custom color…" gone, since §523 (2026-11-07)

The person: *"inline every setting of every bar widget and folder widget into its edit menu; the
Settings app keeps everything too."* §215 and §220 put the switches, choices and numbers in, and marked
the rest with the field they take; this puts in the settings that need a picker: a colour, an icon, what a pin opens, a time of day and a length. They are
rows of `OptionRows` like the rest (`Karpo.Core\OptionPickers.cs`; an alarm's time and a countdown's
length take the place of §220's rows of the same keys), read from the widget and set there
through the very write Settings' page uses, so a menu and the page leave the same file; the menu shows
them through `MenuPickers` and draws them in `Flyout.Pickers.cs`.

**What is inlined.**

| Setting | Where | Row kind | Settings' write it shares |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Widget cards, Card outline (the mode Windows is in) | every widget on a bar | Color | `ColorPalette.Write` (the Appearance page's `ColorRows.Write`) |
| Separators' colour | a separator, a folder's divider | Color | the same |
| A folder's icon | its icon face's submenu (was "More settings…") | Glyph | `FolderOptions.Glyph`, "" for the folder glyph |
| A pin's icon | a pin | Glyph | `PinOptions.Icon`, "" for the target's own |
| What a pin opens | a pin | Target | `PinOptions.Target` (the page's Browse…) |
| An alarm's time | an alarm (was §220's field row) | Time | `AlarmTimes.Picked` (the page's time picker) |
| A timer's or a focus session's length | a timer, a focus session (was a number) | Duration | §220's own row (`CountdownLength`), 1 to 720 |

There are no graph or face colours to inline: the bar's colours are Appearance's six slots, and a
widget's card and outline and the separators are the ones that belong to a widget. The bar, hover and
flyout colours stay Appearance's alone.

**A colour** is a row with a 16 DIP swatch of the colour in force where its icon stands (an empty
square for Automatic), opening a submenu: "Automatic" ticked as a menu ticks its choice; the recent
colours ("Recent colors", the ones mixed in a colour dialog, `BarColors.Recent`); the page's grid under
its heading — Windows' 48 accent colours, in Windows' order, for a line (the outline, a separator), and
the 24 backgrounds for the cards, as the page has offered since 2026-10-09 (accent colours behind text
are unreadable) — and "Custom color…". Swatches are 24 DIP, corners 4 DIP, a hairline round each, eight
to a line in a 30 DIP cell (Windows' grid); the one in force is ringed 2 DIP off it in the words'
colour, and the one lit, under the pointer or the keys', has a ring hard round it in the secondary
colour. A swatch picked sets it and the menu stays, as for every change (§219), the swatch now ringed;
the bars recolour in place (`Dock.Recolour`). The colours, the recent ones and the write moved from the settings app's
`ColorPresets` and `ColorRows` into `Karpo.Core\ColorPalette.cs`, which both now call.

**Custom color… is Windows' own colour dialog** (`ChooseColorW`, full open), owned by the bar, opened
on the colour in force with the recent colours as its custom colours: it has the hue and saturation
square, the lightness bar, the RGB fields, the keys and a screen reader as Windows' dialogs have, for a
few lines, where a picker of Karpo's own would have been a window, a hex field and keyboard handling
to write and keep. It has no alpha, so the colour keeps the alpha the slot's colour has, or its
presets' (cards 70 %, lines opaque), and it becomes the first recent colour, as the page's dialog does.

**An icon** is a row with the icon in force, opening a submenu: its default ("Default", the folder
glyph; a pin's "The target's own") ticked, then 48 glyphs of Settings' gallery in four groups of twelve
— Files, Places, Media, People and time (`Karpo.Core\MenuIcons.cs`), named by the gallery's own words —
six to a line, 20 px in a 32 DIP tile, the one in force on an accent-rimmed plate; then "More icons…",
the page with the whole gallery and its search. In a submenu already — a folder's icon face's settings — nothing opens a third
level (§222's rule for choices): the icon's name is a small heading and its default, its tiles and "More
icons…" stand under it, ruled off from the rows round it as a choice's group is, without the four
groups' headings (headings under a heading; twelve to a group, each keeps to two lines of its own). A
colour there would be the same: its heading, its swatches under their headings, "Custom color…". On a
menu's first level (a bar widget's card colours, a pin's icon) they stay a submenu.

**What a pin opens** is one row, "What it opens", its path under it in the quieter colour ("Nothing yet"
for none). A click opens Windows' open dialog (`TargetDialog`, a file or a folder, Settings' own), owned
by the bar, once the menu has gone; what it chose is set and saved, and the widget's menu comes back
where it stood (a bar's widget's; a folder's line's folder may have closed).

**A time of day and a length** are the setting's name as a heading and a row of steppers under it,
from the row's start: "− 7 + : − 30 + [AM]" — the hour and the minute, and an AM/PM button where the
clock Karpo shows is a 12-hour one (Localization's time pattern, else the region's: `OptionPickers.
TwentyFourHours`, which the alarm page's picker now asks too), the words for it the region's; "− 07 + :
− 30 +" on a 24-hour clock. The hour steps round the day (23:15 and an hour is 00:15), the minute round
its hour (07:59 and a minute is 07:00), as a time picker's columns turn; AM/PM crosses noon. A length is
"− 0 h + − 25 min +", stepping by the hour and the minute within a minute and twelve hours (an hour on
from 11 h 30 is 12 h), a button greyed at the end it steps towards. A press steps at once, and held
steps again after 400 ms and every 80 ms while the pointer stays on it (Windows' RepeatButton); the
menu stays open and shows it as it is now (FlyoutEventKind.Adjust, Refresh). From the keys: Left and
Right go from part to part, − and + (Page Down, Page Up) step it, Enter and Space press AM/PM; the part
with the keys is ringed while the row is lit.

**The tiles are rows.** A swatch or an icon is a FlyoutItem whose icon is a `FlyoutTile`: the menu lays
a run of them in lines across its width (`Flyout.TileSpots`, centred, each run starting on the same
columns) and otherwise treats each as a row — lit, pressed, chosen by a click, Enter or Space, its name
what a screen reader says. Left and Right walk a line, Up and Down go to the tile above or below, and
from a row over or under a run the keys land on its nearest line's first tile.

Hooks in the shared menu files are one or two lines each (marked "Flyout.Pickers.cs"): the row of
steppers' press and repeat timer, a tile's place and height, its drawing, its keys, and a row's `Lit`.

Strings (30 languages): Custom color…, More icons…, Default, the four groups, Hours, Minutes, AM or PM,
"{what}: decrease" and "{what}: increase" (the steppers' names for a screen reader).

Tests: `MenuPickersTests` — each colour, Automatic and a mixed colour leave the config as `ColorRows.
Write` and `ColorPresets.Remember` do; the cards' colours on a bar's widget, the separators' on a
separator, none on a folder's line; an alarm's time and a countdown's length as their page writes them,
round the clock and at a length's ends; a pin's target and icon and a folder's icon as their pages set
them; the steps' edges (`TimeSteps`); eight swatches and six icons to a line; the 48 icons are the
gallery's. On a real menu (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): the swatches walked by the keys and one hit by the
pointer, the steppers stepped by a press and the keys. Pictures (150 %, dark and light):
`menu-pickers-colors`, `menu-pickers-icons`, `menu-pickers-time`. By hand: right-click a widget in edit
mode, Widget cards ▸ a swatch (the cards recolour), Custom color… (Windows' dialog; the colour first in
Recent colors next time); a folder's icon face ▸ Icon ▸ an icon; a pin's "What it opens" (the dialog,
then the menu again); an alarm's time: hold "+" (it repeats), the keys; a timer's length at 12 h.

## 225. A widget's menu tidied: groups, a pin's own, room for its words, no rule on top (2026-10-19)

The menus §215–§224 filled had four rough edges.

**A group's rows stand together** (`OptionMenu.Rows`, `OptionRow.Group`). A toggles row's switches
("Wi-Fi", "Bluetooth"…) said which toggles the row shows, but in a list of the widget's own switches
they read as turning Wi-Fi on. Rows that share a group — the toggles shown, an alarm's seven days, the
status icons, a folder's column widths — are one row on a menu's first level, opening a submenu of them
under the group's name: "Toggles shown ▸", "Repeat on ▸" (`OptionRow.GroupTitle`, where the page's card
title, "Toggles", "Repeat", says too little away from its page), "Status icons ▸", "Column widths ▸".
In that submenu a choice is inline (a status icon's name as a heading, its three places under it): no
third level, as §220 has it. In a submenu already (a face's) the group is its heading and its rows,
ruled off as a choice's group is. A flip in the group's submenu keeps the menu and the submenu open
(§219).

**A pin's settings are all in its menu** (`OptionPickers.Into`, `OptionRows.OfPinFolder`), in its
page's order: what it opens, its name, its icon, and for a pin to a folder (`PinFolders.FolderOf`, the
disk's; `OptionPlace.Exists` in a test) how it shows, its titles where it shows the folder's contents,
and where a click on a folder goes — each written as `PinPage` writes it. `OptionRowsTests.
EveryCardOfThePinPageIsARow` reads the page's cards so the two cannot drift.

**A widget's menu is as wide as its longest row** (`Flyout.Grows`, `Flyout.Width.cs`): from 256 DIP
(`MenuWidthDip`) to 480 DIP (`MenuMostDip`), both with Windows' text size, and only past that is a
label cut ("Show the na…" was a face's "Show the name beside it" beside its switch). Its words are
measured whole beside what stands at the row's end, as the rows are laid out. A search's results and
what it says are not counted, so typing never moves the menu's sides; a run of tiles keeps the lines
it has in a menu of one width, centred. Every other menu — a jump list, the bar's — keeps its one width.

**A menu never begins with a rule** (`Flyout.WithoutLeadingRules`): a folder's faces, ruled off from
the rows over them, start with their heading where nothing stands over them.

Strings (30 languages): "Toggles shown", "Repeat on".

Tests: `OptionMenuTests.AGroupsRowsStandTogetherUnderItsName`, `OptionRowsTests.EveryCardOfThePinPageIsARow`
and `APinsRowsAreItsPagesAndWriteWhatItWrites`, `MenuCleanupTests` (no rule on top; on a real menu the
width grows to the longest row and stops at the most, a jump list and a menu of short rows keep 256
DIP, a toggle flipped in "Toggles shown" keeps its submenu open). Pictures (150 %, dark):
`menu-clean-toggles`, `menu-clean-alarm`, `menu-clean-pin`, `menu-clean-face`, `menu-clean-faces`. By
hand: a toggles row's menu in edit mode, Toggles shown ▸ a switch; an alarm's Repeat on ▸; a pin to a
folder: How to show, Show titles, Navigation; a folder's icon face ▸ "Show the name beside it" whole.

## 226. A setting changed in a folder's line shows at once (2026-10-19)

The person: "when changing the settings of a widget in the folder view it does not update the widget
shown". The change was saved, the menu stayed open and showed it, and the folder went on drawing the
line as it was until it was opened again.

**Why.** The dock's change reaches the folder as every change of the file does: `Apply` → `Arrange` →
`SyncIslands` → `FolderIsland.Configure`, which hands each line its new cell, keeps the widgets whose
record is the same (`CellIsland.Configure`) and makes again those whose record changed — a style is a
form (§209), so a graph restyled from the processor to the memory is a new widget under the same key.
The open folder (`FolderFlyout.FolderChanged`) took the folder's lines only when its layout's signature
changed (a widget come, gone or moved, a line another height). A setting changes none of that, so it
kept drawing the lines it held: the widget the folder had let go of, and every line's old cell, which
is what draws a list row's name (`IslandEdits.Header`).

**Now.** The open folder takes the folder's lines on every change: the same widgets with their new
cells, drawn again in place; another widget under a key (a style changed) laid out as any change of
widget is (`SameWidgets`). Every kind of row goes through this one path: toggles, choices, steppers,
text and search fields, a style. The bar was right already: its widgets are configured or made again
by `SyncIslands` and drawn by `Rebuild`, a folder's faces with its button.

Tests: `FolderMenuTests.ASettingChangedInALinesMenuShowsInTheOpenFolderAtOnce` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, at
rest and arranged: a graph restyled and a clock's label changed under an open folder, its cards where
they were; failed before). By hand: open a folder, right-click a graph line, change its style, its pace
and "Show graph"; a heading's text; a clock's label. Each shows at once, the menu still up.

## 227. Choices a level of their own again; grips first, Remove in the face's submenu; menus stand still (2026-10-19)

The person: *"the column width settings should be removed from the taskbar widget menu. the reorder
handles should be moved to the front of the items. the delete button should be moved to the submenu
again. the menus like style, or index, or location picker etc, should be shown as their own level again
as they were at the beginning. all the folder faces should get their own submenu even if they have no
configuration options. then just show the name and show that there are no configuration options."* And:
*"when the setting changed changes the contents of the previous menu it should not shift the submenu,
it should keep it open at the same location except for when it is closed. this is just to remove layout
shift during clicking through edit options."*

**No column widths in a widget's menu** (`OptionRows.Of`). A folder's "Column widths ▸" (§225) is gone
from its menu on the bar; the widths are set where the columns are, in the open folder's edit mode (the
column's width control), and on the folder's page in Settings (`OptionRows.OfFolder`, which the page
reads). `OptionRowsTests.EveryCardOfTheFolderPageIsARow` counts them as the folder's own rows, not the
menu's.

**Every choice is a level of its own, on every level** (`OptionMenu.Rows`, `MenuPickers.Rows`): §220's
inline choices (a heading and its choices in a face's submenu) are taken back. A choice — a style, an
index, a number format, an alignment, a pace, a status icon's place — is a row opening its choices, the
one in force ticked; a search (a place, a time zone, a share) a row opening its field and its results
under it; a colour its swatches, an icon its tiles under the gallery's headings. So a face's alignment
is a third level, a status icon's place under "Status icons ▸" a third, and nothing stops a fourth.
Toggles, steppers, a line of text, a target and a time's or a length's steppers stay rows; groups
("Toggles shown ▸", "Repeat on ▸", "Status icons ▸") stay submenus on every level. The `inline` mode of
both is gone.

**A face's row** (`OptionMenu.FaceSection`, Flyout.Controls.cs). Its grip stands at its start, in the
icons' column, the face's icon and name a column further in (`Flyout.Leads`; a `FlyoutTool.Grip` of a
row's tools is drawn there, every other tool at the end); its tooltip still says how to drag. The whole
row takes the drag and Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down still move the lit row. No button stands at its end any
more: "Remove" is its submenu's last row, ruled off, Delete its shortcut there, greyed for the last face;
picked, the face goes and the menu stays (its submenu shuts, its row being gone). Every face has its
submenu: one with nothing to set shows its name as a heading and "No settings for this face", greyed,
over "Remove".

**Menus stand still through a change** (`Flyout.Refresh`, `ReshowSubmenu`, `FlyoutHost.Held`). A
Refresh — a pick, a flip, a step, a face moved or removed, a search's results coming and going — shows
every level again with its panel's corner where it stood on the screen (`FlyoutHost.Spot.At`), not
placed again off its parent row's new place, and scrolled where it was; the root's corner stays too, so
a menu grows and shrinks downward and rightward (wider rows, `Flyout.Width`, included). A panel moves
only as far as it must to stay on the screen and, for the root, off its bar (`Held`); a level shuts only
where its row is gone or the person shuts it. A submenu keeps the side it took. A level that had to move
up to fit stays there when it shrinks again, rather than following each keystroke.

**A control at the row's end beside ticks** (`Flyout.ClearsCheckSlot`). In a menu whose rows keep the
check marks' slot, a toggle, a radio button or a stepper (a row with no tick and no submenu) stands at
the row's very end, as in every other menu, not a tick's room in.

Strings (30 languages): "No settings for this face".

Tests: `OptionMenuTests.AChoiceOpensALevelOfItsOwnOnEveryLevel`, `AGroupsRowsStandTogetherUnderItsName`,
`AFaceIsMovedAndTakenOffAsThePagesListDoes`, `EveryFacesSubmenuHasItsChoicesAsLevelsOfTheirOwn`,
`TheFacesAreMovedAndTakenOffOnTheMenusFirstLevel` (grip at the start and its tooltip, Remove from the
submenu and from Delete there); `MenuKeepsTests.AChoicePickedKeepsEveryLevelOpenAndTheTickMoves` (three
levels, none moved), `OpenLevelsStandStillThroughARefreshThatChangesTheirParent` (a row put over the
parent, the menu wider: corner and levels where they were; a level whose row went shuts),
`AHeldPanelMovesOnlyToStayOnTheScreen`; `MenuCheckTests.AControlStandsAtTheRowsEndBesideTicks`;
`OptionRowsTests.EveryCardOfTheFolderPageIsARow` (no column widths in the menu); `MenuFieldTests` and
`MenuPickersTests` (a search and an icon a level of their own). Pictures (150 %, dark and light):
`option-menu-cpu-choice`, `option-menu-empty`, `option-menu-drag`, `menu-field-zone`,
`menu-pickers-icons`. By hand: a folder in edit mode — a face ▸ Alignment ▸ pick: nothing moves; a clock
face ▸ Time zone ▸ type; a face with no settings; Remove from a face's submenu and with Delete.

## 228. A row says what it is set to; no cards' colours in a widget's menu; five results at most (2026-10-19)

The person: *"also show the set configuration value in the settings as well"*, *"widget cards and outline
should not be in the settings menu"* and *"when searching for a place for example, always show as if there
are 5 entries being displayed, you should be able to click expand if there are more items that are cutoff,
but show 5 at max as a default."*

**What a row is set to, at its end** (`FlyoutItem.Value`, `Flyout.Values.cs`, `OptionMenu.ValueOf`,
`OptionMenu.GroupValue`, `MenuPickers.Rows`). Every row that opens a level — a choice, a search, a colour,
an icon, a group — says what it is set to before its chevron, as Windows 11's settings rows do: "Style
Processor ›", "Time zone (UTC+09:00) Osaka, Sapporo, Tokyo ›", "Place Zürich ›"; a colour its swatch
("Automatic" in words where it follows Windows), an icon its glyph — both moved from the row's start to
its end. The words are the secondary colour, the value's right edge 8 DIP in from the chevron's box. The
row's name wins: the value has what the name leaves, cut with an ellipsis, and none at all under 40 DIP
(`Flyout.ValueRoom`); a swatch or a glyph is always shown. A menu that grows (`Flyout.Width`, §225) counts
the value whole, to `MenuMostDip`, so it is cut only where the menu can grow no wider. A choice with
nothing in force (a share's pair that is no pair) and an empty search say nothing. Groups: an alarm's
days as its line says them ("Weekdays", "Every day", "Mon, Wed"), "Never" for none; a toggles row's
toggles stand listed in the menu itself (an ordered list, below) and its heading says nothing; the status icons, each its own choice, say nothing — no one word sums them. §220 had dropped
the value when one menu width cut the setting's own name ("How oft…"); menus grow since §225, and the
name still wins. A screen reader hears the value as the row's status.

**No cards' colours in a widget's menu** (`OptionPickers.Into`). "Widget cards" and "Card outline" are the
whole bar's colours, not a widget's, and stand on Settings' Appearance page alone. A separator keeps its
line colour (and a folder's divider its own), the only colour rows a menu has.
`MenuPickersTests.TheColoursAreTheWidgetsOwn` holds that no widget of any kind has a card or outline row.

**Five results' room, five at most** (`MenuSearch.Few`, `Shown`, `Hidden`, `ShowAll`; `Flyout.Fields.cs`).
While a search's rows show, they stand in the room of five two-line results and a row for "Show more" —
a blank, disabled row (`Flyout.IsFieldSpacer`) makes up what they leave — so the menu keeps its height from none
found to two to twelve, "Searching…" and "nothing found" in the same room. Five show; where there are
more, "Show more (N)" under them (N the hidden ones) is reached by the arrows like a result, and Enter or
a click shows them all — the keys staying where it stood, on the first that was hidden, the menu as tall
as they need and scrolling past the screen. The next search (a key typed, Enter's search, the field
closed) shows five again. A search keeps up to `MenuSearch.Most` (40); the zones' finder finds up to 40,
the place finder asks Open-Meteo for 20 (`Places.SearchAsync(count)`; the page still asks for five). A
relayout while the keys are on a result keeps what was typed (`MenuTextField.Show(browsing)`) — before,
showing the menu again then put the setting's words back over the query.

Strings (30 languages): "Show more ({count})", "{count} shown", "Never".

Tests: `MenuValuesTests` (each kind's value, the groups' words, the name winning, on a real menu the value
between the name and the chevron, the five rows' room with none, two, twelve and nothing found, "Show
more" by the keys and a click, typing showing five again); `MenuSearchTests.FiveShowUntilShowMoreAndTypingShowsFiveAgain`;
`MenuPickersTests` (a separator's colour, its swatch and an icon's glyph at the row's end, no card
colours anywhere). Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `menu-values-rows`, `menu-values-face`,
`menu-values-weather`, `menu-values-place-2`, `menu-values-place-12`, `menu-values-place-more`. By hand: a
folder in edit mode — a weather face ▸ Place ▸ type "san": five and "Show more"; Down to it, Enter; type
again; a face's submenu with its values; a widget's menu without the card colours.

## 229. The performance widget: its reading and its style; paces from a second to a minute (2026-10-19)

The person: *"how often it updates should get better times, right now it is just seconds from 1 to
10"* and *"right now the styles are the different part of the system like the gpu or the cpu, but the
styles should really just be the different styles that the cpu widget can be displayed. fix that."*

§209 made the graphs one widget, "Performance graph", whose style was the reading (processor,
graphics, memory, disk, network), and the details another, "Performance details", the same way. What it
measures is no style. **Now there is one widget, "Performance", with two choices that do not touch each
other** (`WidgetStyles.Performance`):

- **Reading** — Processor, Graphics, Memory, Disk, Network: what it measures. The graphics' adapter and
  the disk's disk show under it as before.
- **Style** — how it shows it: **Graph** (the reading over its graph), **Numbers** (the figure alone)
  and **Details** (the facts behind the figure). These are all the forms the code draws. The line's
  heights (one row, compact, the whole widget, the tall "last minute") are a graph's height, not
  styles; a graph with its details under it is two lines, as the presets stand them.

A form is a reading in a style (`ListKind.Gpu` the graphics' graph, `ListKind.GpuDetails` their
details), so each `WidgetStyle` of the widget names its reading (`WidgetStyle.Reading`) and everything
that draws and measures a line asks the form as before. **Numbers is the graph's form drawing no
graph** (`PerformanceOptions.ShowGraph`): that was the "Show a graph" switch, which said the same thing
as the style and is gone from the menu and the page; the style choice is the switch now
(`WidgetStyles.LookNames`, `LookIndex`, `ChooseLook`). The reading choice keeps the style, Numbers
included, and the style choice keeps the reading (`ReadingNames`, `ReadingIndex`, `ChooseReading`);
both keep the id, the height, the alignment and every option, as a style changed always has.

**The file** writes both: `"kind": "performance", "reading": "gpu", "style": "details"` (`CellItem.FileReading`,
`WidgetStyles.FileReading`; a widget with readings says its style always). Every earlier shape reads
tolerantly and is written in today's words once, in place, by the styles' carrying over
(`LineMigrations.MergeStyles`), `Config.Migrated` getting `performanceReadings` (no reset, no shape
bump): `"performance"` alone (the processor's graph), `"performance"` with a reading as its style
(§209's), `"performanceDetails"` with or without one, and a reading's own word from before (`"cpu"`,
`"gpuDetails"`). A reading or a style this build does not know is the first. Presets say the widget,
its reading and its style (`PresetItem.Reading`).

**The pace** (`PerformanceChoices.Paces`): every second, 2, 5, 10 and 30 seconds, every minute — not
every second from one to ten. Not under a second: the dock reads each reading once a second for every
widget at once (`PerformanceData`, the one source per reading), so a faster widget would only draw that
second again. Not over a minute: a graph steps once a pace, so a five-minute one would sit still for
five minutes, and the source keeps the widest graph's steps at the slowest pace (`PerformanceData.Kept`,
513 × 60 samples, about 120 KB a source; some eight and a half hours at a minute a step). Any other
number reads as the nearest step, the faster of two as near (`PerformanceChoices.Nearest`): a line's
`seconds` in `WidgetItem.Normalize`, a face's `pace` where it is read (`FolderFace.Text`), so a file's 3
is 2 and its 7 is 5 without a migration. The tall line's caption says minutes past a minute's reach
("30 minutes", `PerformanceModel.SpanAt`). The pace is offered in every style: the details step at it too.

**The bar's faces** of the five readings keep a face each: a face is the figure alone, it has no style,
and one face with a reading choice would rename five faces people have placed for nothing. Their pace is
the same ladder.

Settings: a Reading card over the Style card, the pace a card of its own; the page's title "Graphics ·
Details". Strings (30 languages): the widget's name and line, Graph, Numbers, Details, the five readings
(renamed from the styles' keys), Reading, Every minute, "{minutes} minutes"; "Show a graph" and the
details widget's words gone.

The person's own folders (a processor's and a graphics' graph, two rows each, in §209's words) drawn
before and after from a copy of their file: the same pixels.

Tests: `PerformanceStylesTests` (every old shape in place with its id, height and options, today's words
needing nothing, the person's graphs, the two choices independent, the pace ladder and the nearest
step), `WidgetStylesTests` (the readings' forms in the file), `OptionMenuTests.AGraphsSettingFromTheMenuWritesWhatTheSettingsPageWrites`
and `AGraphsMenuHasEveryCardItsPageHas` (Reading, Style, adapter or disk, pace), `PerformanceCardTests`.
By hand: a performance line's menu — Reading ▸ Graphics keeps Details; Style ▸ Numbers drops the graph,
Graph brings it back; How often it updates ▸ Every minute, and the tall graph's caption says 60 minutes.

## 230. A face takes the least room that shows all it says (2026-10-19)

**Superseded by §244** (the same day): a face is now as wide as what it shows now, not the widest
its settings can read; its rooms below are its most.

The person: "some faces take up more space than they need, e.g. the air quality face. on the taskbar
the widgets should always take the least amount of space while still showing all the information they
have." A face is still measured from its settings and templates, never from what it reads (§12.2), so
the bar does not move as a value changes; but each template is now the widest its *current* settings
can really read, and nothing past the button's own ends (`WidgetShapes.Folder`: 2 × max(edge, 6 px)).

Every face of words was measured at 100 and 150 % against the widest it can read (`FaceWidthTests`,
face-widths-<100|150>.png/.txt). Most were already their template and no more: the clock (the
morning's and the evening's last second in its format), the calendar and the time and date (the widest
date of the year), the weather ("-88°" or "188°", the region's widest weekday, the language's widest
conditions up to 140 DIP), the timer and focus ("88:88", "720m"), the stopwatch, the battery and the
readings ("100%", "8.8M"), the keyboard (this PC's layouts). The meeting, the news headline, the drive,
the desktops' and the layouts' names and what is playing keep rooms of their own by design: their words
are anybody's and are cut, never measured.

- **Air quality.** Its room was "888" with the widest level word of both indices wherever the place
  picks: Zürich kept room for the US index's "888 · Sensitive groups". It is now each level of the
  indices its place can show, in the width option's fullest form, with as many figures as that level's
  band can have (`AirText.WidestAt`, `AirBands.Most`: "88 · Good" to "888 · Extremely poor"; the last
  band three figures). Where the place picks, its coordinates pick the index (`AirBands.ScalesAt`);
  both are kept only for this PC's location, which is not known until read, and within half a degree
  of the European area's edge, where the answer's grid point may land on the other side.
- **Stock.** The change's room was "-88.88%"; a rise is "+", which is wider, so a full price that rose
  was cut by the difference (4 DIP at 150 %). The room is "+88.88%" across the bar and down it.
- **Alignment.** One face of words somebody aligned (§201), in a button wider than the face — a cell's
  least — has the button's room inside its ends (`FolderIsland.FaceBoxes`): its start and end are the
  button's, no longer only the face's own, now tighter, room. Nobody's pick and the middle stand where
  they stood; several faces keep their run in the middle.

| Face (48 DIP bar, 150 %, English) | Before | After | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Air quality, standard, Zürich | 149.3 | 142 | its index's levels, figures by band |
| Air quality, wide, Zürich | 174 | 166.7 | the same, "AQI 888 · …" |
| Air quality, compact | 48.7 | 48.7 | "888" |
| Air quality, US / New York / this PC's location | 149.3 | 149.3 | "888 · Sensitive groups" is real there |
| Stock, change shown | 148 | 152 | "+88.88%", not cut |
| Every other face of words | — | unchanged | already its widest reading |

Widths are the button's, ends included, in DIP. Down a bar on its side nothing changed.

What this does not do: a face whose words differ a lot from one reading to the next — the air
quality's "32 · Fair" in the room of "888 · Extremely poor" — keeps the widest level's room. Sizing it
to the level it reads now would move the bar when the level changes (§12.2), and is the person's call.

Tests: `FaceWidthTests` — the air quality's widest level fills its face to its letters' side bearings,
every level at the top of its band fits in its fullest form, one width for all of them (Zürich, New
York, the US index chosen; three widths; 100 and 150 %; English and Arabic), Zürich's narrower than the
US index's; which indices a place keeps room for and each band's figures; a stock's widest rise inside
its room; the air quality still aligned (start, middle, end; in Arabic the start the right); an aligned
clock at its button's ends. By hand: an air-quality face in Europe set to a place (not this PC's
location) is a little narrower; align it to the start and the end; a stock face of a share that rose.

## 231. A widget added in a folder follows the pointer; Escape after a folder closes leaves edit mode (2026-10-19)

The person: "when in folder edit mode and i add a widget it should not immediately place the widget, it
should actually pin it to my mouse and let me place it the same way it would look when i drag and drop or
copy / cut a widget." And: "when i am in the folder edit mode and click esc i cannot click esc again to
get out of edit mode in taskbar edit mode."

**Added in a folder, carried.** A pick in the add list of a folder standing open arranged (its edit bar's
"Add a widget", or "Add" in a line's or the folder's menu) puts the line in where that bar adds
(`FolderFlyout.AddPlace`, §214) and hands it to the pointer at once, as Ctrl+V hands a pasted line
(`Dock.AddChosen` → `FollowInFolder`, `FolderFlyout.Carry`): drawn as it is, lifted, the landing
following the pointer between lines, into an empty column or a slot beside the lists — the carry a drag,
a copy and a paste already share. A left click puts it down where the landing shows; Escape or a right
click calls it off and it comes out again (`DropFollow`), nothing added. The bar's own "Add a widget"
(each display's edit bar) carried its widget on the pointer already (`AddSpot.Follows`); it is
unchanged, so the two are one gesture now.

**Escape, the second time.** Edit mode's keyboard hook lets Escape through where the window with the
keys closes on it itself (`Dock.EscapeIsTheirs`). That was any window of the dock's thread but a bar, a
frame or an edit bar. A folder opened from a menu's row ("Open folder", "Edit folder") took the
foreground from that menu, closing; Escape in the folder closed it and handed the keys back
(`FlyoutHost.Close`, restore) to the menu — closed and hidden by then, but the dock's own. So the next
Escape went to it, which heard nothing, and edit mode stayed. The folder itself, too, keeps the keys
through its fade. Now only a popup standing open takes Escape — one of the thread's open menu-mode hosts
(`FlyoutHost.OpenMenus`: a menu, the add list, an open folder) or a task dialog (`#32770`), visible and
no surface of edit mode (`Dock.EscapeTheirs`); anything else, the hook takes it: the folder closed, edit
mode ends.

Two more ways an Escape went for nothing there, closed too:

- The marching ants of lines copied in the folder (ants before edit mode, as Excel's) stayed on the
  clipboard's keys after the folder had closed, with no ants in sight; the next Escape took them off and
  seemed to do nothing. Escape takes the ants first only where they show — an arranged bar's widget, or
  a line of a folder standing open (`Dock.AntsInSight`).
- Windows takes a slow low-level hook away without a word, and opening or closing an arranged folder
  builds windows on the dock's thread. The keyboard hook goes in afresh when a folder opens or closes in
  edit mode (`EditFollowHook.Refresh`), not while an Escape it took is still to come up.

Tests: `FolderAddCarryTests` — a line added where the folder's edit bar adds is carried with no button
held, lands in the empty column where the pointer is, and called off lands nothing
(`folder-add-carry.png`, dark at 150 %: the new line over the empty column, the landing under it);
Escape is a popup's own only while it stands open (a closed menu, the folder after Escape — the
regression); the ants take an Escape only where they show.
By hand: in edit mode open a folder from its menu's "Open folder", Escape (the folder closes), Escape
again (edit mode ends). In the folder's edit bar "Add a widget" → a widget: it is on the pointer; a click
in the empty column puts it there; again, then Escape or a right click: nothing added.

## 232. A search's level opens whole, its field with the keys; a zone says its offset; a widget's menu one width (2026-10-19)

The person: *"the timezone selector (just generally these types of widgets i mean) should always show in
the same size, right now at first only the textbox shows and then when i search the items show, but the
items should show up even if i am not searching. additionally if someone opens the submenu it should
focus the textbox automatically as well"*, *"the timezone value should only show UTC + 1 or so, not the
complete text"* and *"these configuration menus should always have the same fixed width regardless of
contents."*

**A search's level opens whole** (`Flyout.Fields.cs`: `SearchLevel`, `FocusSearchLevel`; `MenuSearch.cs`).
Every widget's and face's search stands on a level of its own (§226) — a time zone, a place, a share, an
action's page —, and that level's search shows its rows always, from its first layout: what the finder
offers for nothing typed, five of them, "Show more (N)" and §228's five results' room. So the level
opens at the size it keeps while it is typed in, finds, finds nothing, asks the service or is put back
by Escape; a pick shows it again with what it offers for nothing typed. Before, its rows came only once
the field had the keys, and the level grew under the pointer. A text field elsewhere, and a feed's
address (which finds nothing as it is typed), are as they were.

**Nothing typed is never an empty list** (`OptionFinder.Suggested`, shown while too little is typed to
ask, after `Offered`):

- **A time zone**: this PC's, the zones the person's clocks show (most used first), then every other
  zone in Windows' order, by offset — five shown, "Show more (140)" the rest (`MenuSearch.Most` 200, so
  every zone fits). Each result says its places, its offset now under them ("Osaka, Sapporo, Tokyo /
  UTC+9"); this PC's its offset and its places.
- **A place**: "Use my device's location", its own place (ticked), then the places the person's other
  weather and air quality lines and faces show (`OptionFields.PlacesInUse`) — nothing asked of the
  service until two letters are typed, as before.
- **A share**: its own (ticked), then the shares the person's other stocks show
  (`OptionFields.SharesInUse`), named as the service named them when picked; each is looked up as it
  is picked, as any share is.
- **An action's page**: "None", then every page, as before.

The places and shares in use come with the zones (`OptionDevices.Places`, `.Shares`, from
`Dock.MenuSources`). There is no list of recent searches: what the person's widgets show already is
what they picked.

**Its field takes the keys as it opens** — by the pointer resting, a click or the keys alike
(`Flyout.OpenSubmenu` → `FocusSearchLevel`): its words selected and the caret at their end, so typing
replaces them; Down goes into the rows, Escape puts the words back and then lets the keys go, as §219's
fields do. Only the keys: the menu takes no activation it did not have (a submenu takes none at all).

**A zone says its offset** (`Karpo.Core\TimeZoneText.cs`, `OptionRow.Summary`, `OptionMenu.ValueOf`). At
a zone row's end only the offset in force today: "UTC+1", "UTC+5:30", "UTC−3" (a true minus sign),
"UTC" — Zürich "UTC+2" in summer and "UTC+1" in winter, not Windows' standard "(UTC+01:00)"; this PC's
zone its own offset. Its field and its results keep the whole name, so "Tokyo" is still found and read.
`TimeZoneText.Short(zone, now)` (and `Short(id, now)`, this PC's for no id, the id itself for one Windows
doesn't know) is the one helper for any other place a zone is said short (a date face's or line's
zone too).

**A widget's menu one width** (`Flyout.Configures`, `Flyout.SettingsWidthDip`, `Flyout.Width.cs`). §225 had
a widget's menu grow to its longest row, 256 to 480 DIP, so each level was a width of its own and a level
widened as a value changed. Now a widget's menu — its buttons, its settings, its faces — and every level
under it, a search's among them, are 320 DIP at 100 % text, growing with Windows' text size only: wide
enough for a setting's name and what it is set to side by side ("Clock    As the region writes it ›"). A
longer row is cut with an ellipsis, the name winning over the value (§228's `Flyout.ValueRoom`). Every
other menu keeps Windows' 256 DIP (a jump list, the bar's menu, a window's). `Flyout.Grows`, `MenuMostDip`
and `Flyout.Needed` are gone.

Tests: `TimeZoneTextTests` (offsets short; summer time, half and three-quarter hours, Newfoundland's
minus half hour, the UTC zone, this PC's, an unknown id), `MenuSearchTests` (nothing typed: every zone,
the person's first, by offset; a place's own and the others in use, nothing asked, a pick kept as it
was; a share's own and the others; every action), `MenuFieldTests.AZonesLevelOpensWholeWithItsFieldTakingTheKeys`
and `APlacesLevelOpensWholeAndKeepsItsSize` (opened by a click and by the keys: the field has the keys
at once, its words selected; the same size before typing, after, with nothing found and after the
service answers; the level the menu's width), `MenuCleanupTests` (a widget's menu and its levels 320 DIP
whatever they say, a jump list 256), `MenuValuesTests` (a zone's row says "UTC+9"), `MenuKeepsTests`.
Pictures (`MenuFieldTests.SearchLevelPictures`, 150 %, dark and light): menu-search-zone-open,
menu-search-place-open, menu-search-face-zone. By hand: a clock's menu ▸ Time zone — the list is there
before a key, the field has the caret; type "tok", then clear it: the level never changes size; the row
says "UTC+2" (summer) / "UTC+1" (after 25 October); a weather's Place — your place and your other
widgets' places before typing.

all the widget settings have been ported over correctly. if not port all of them over to the inline
mode."*

**The audit.** Every control of the settings app's widget pages, read card by card, against the rows of
the widget's menu (`OptionRows`, `OptionFields`, `OptionPickers`; the menu `OptionMenu`, `MenuPickers`):
