`OptionRowsTests.EveryOptionOfAWidgetIsARowOfItsMenu` holds it from now on, from the model's side: every
property the file keeps of every options record a taskbar entry or a folder's line may carry (read by
reflection) is a row of some widget's menu, or one of the few it names with why (a folder's faces and
lists, set where they are; what a symbol's or a feed's proving writes; retired fields kept so a file
round-trips) — and every row of every face, while it shows. It replaces the guards that read the
widget, folder and pin pages' markup.

**No "More settings…" any more** (`OptionMenu.Rows`). The row kind it stood for (`OptionRowKind.Elsewhere`,
`OptionPickKind.Elsewhere`, `OptionField.Amount/Time/Icon`) is gone: a list this PC or the accounts have
(the adapters, the disks, the drives, the To Do lists, the notebook) is no row where the caller listed
none, and the menu lists them as it opens. A new row kind, **Action** (`OptionRowKind.Action`), is a row
that does something once, asked first where it has a `DeleteQuestion` (the dock's `DeleteAsk`, Windows'
task dialog), and the menu closes; a new pick, **Move**, is an ordered list's row dragged into place
(`OptionMenu.Moved`; its rows are a `FlyoutItem.Reorder` group, `OptionMenu.ListGroup`, as a folder's
faces are, on the level they stand on).

**The menus' top row has no "Settings"** (`Dock.WidgetButtons`, `RestRows`, `WidgetRowsFor`): Cut, Copy,
Remove — but the tray's, whose icons are every tray's (`Dock.OpensSettings`), which opens the settings
app at General. A broken pin's flyout ends with "Locate…" ("Choose…") and "Remove this pin". A weather
line's "Change location" row went (its Location ▸ is the same menu's); a weather face's opens the
folder's menu in edit mode, where the face's place is.

**Edit mode** (`EditClicks`). A double-click on a widget, on the bar or in an open folder, opens its menu
again (`OnDoubleClick` = Menu; the first click's menu its second press closed), and Enter opens a folder or
any other widget's menu. No click has an open settings window follow the selection any more (`Follow`,
`FollowArgs`, `SettingsApp.Follow` and the `--follow` hand-off from the dock are gone).

**Set up** (`SetupFace`, `FolderFlyout`). A line or a card that needs a field of its own — a pin's
target, a share, a place, a feed, a drive — says "Set up" (or its gear) and its click opens its menu over
the folder, as a right click does; the mail, the calendar and the contacts still say "Set up in Settings"
and open the Accounts page. Nothing opens a widget's page any more (the dock's `OpenSetup`, `AddedArgs`).

**The settings app** keeps what is the app's: General (with the tray icons' block, `TrayIconRule` rows,
and its note before Karpo has run), Layouts, Displays, Appearance (the cards' colours and outline, the
separators), Localization, Accounts, License, About (now with the online widgets' data credits). Gone:
`WidgetPage`, `WidgetsPage`, `FolderPage`, `PinPage`, `TrayPage`, `IslandOptions*`, the size card, the
place, symbol, face, action and align pickers, the reorder list, the samplers and the target dialog it
compiled in, and their logic (`FolderRows`, `PerformanceCard`, `PinHeaderIcon`, `StatusIconChoices`,
`HeightChoice`, `WidgetStand`, `Reordering`, `AddedArrival`, `SetupFocus`). A link to a widget
(`--island`) shows General for a tray, Appearance's Separators for a separator, and the layouts for any
other; "Find a setting" reads the side menu's pages only (`SettingsIndex.Searched`).

No strings added; none removed (the widget pages' words stay in the 30 languages, unused, rather than
churn them).

`AnIconIsFoundInTheWholeGallery`, `AToggleRowsTogglesAreOrderedAddedAndTakenOut`,

## 234. "Hide it while nothing plays" hides it; a date in a zone of its own (2026-10-19)

The person: "hiding the now playing face while nothing is playing does not work, it always shows" and
"for the date the timezone is actually important too".

**Nothing plays.** The option (`NowPlayingFace.HideIdle`, the media preset's face) was read, and the
folder took no cell where its widget said it was idle (`FolderIsland.Count`), and a refresh after the
news laid the bar out again — but idle was `now is null`: no session at all. Windows keeps a paused
player's session for as long as the app runs (Spotify open, a browser tab that played once), and a
session with words is shown, so on a real PC the face was never idle and the folder never left. Now
nothing plays (`MediaIsland.Idle`, `MediaQuiet`) is no session, or the followed one paused, stopped or
closed — what the option says, "while nothing plays". A stop counts only after a grace of 5 s: a change
of track passes through "changing" and "paused", and a pause and play a moment later should not take the
folder off and put it back. What has not played since the face was made is nothing at once (Karpo
started with Spotify paused: no folder). When the grace starts the widget wakes its folder once it is
over, so the bar is laid out again then without waiting for other news; a track starting lays it out at
once. Off (the default), nothing changes: the face stays and says "Nothing playing" or shows the paused
track.

**A date in a zone.** The calendar face and the time-and-date face have a zone option as the clock face
has (`FaceOptionKind.Zone`, key `zone`, searched for in the menu with the clock's finder); the clock
widget's date and time styles (`DateHeader`, `TimeHeader`) carry the clock's options
(`WidgetOptionsKind.Clock`), so they have its zone row — not its seconds nor its label — and a clock
switched to its date style keeps its zone. Unset is this PC's, as before; nothing is written for it.
Set, the date is the zone's today (`Clock.NowIn`), which around midnight is another day; the
time-and-date face shows the zone's time with it — a time here over a date there would be neither — and
its hover says the zone's name under the long date, as the clock face's does. The faces are measured
over a year as before, so a zone moves nothing. The zones they are set to are among the zones in use a
zone's search offers first (`OptionFields.ZonesInUse`).

A zone's row says what it is set to short (`TimeZoneText.Short`, `OptionMenu.ValueOf`): "UTC+9",
"UTC+5:30", "UTC−3", its offset now with summer time counted; this PC's in words.

Strings (30 languages): the two faces' "Time zone", the clock face's own words.

Tests: `MediaReadsTests.NothingPlaysIsNoSessionOrAPauseOutlastingItsGrace`,
`MediaPresetTests.HidingWhileNothingPlaysIsTheFacesOption` (paused hides) and
`TheBarIsLaidOutAgainAsATrackStopsAndStarts` (a refresh reports the change both ways; within the grace
nothing; a short grace runs out by itself), `DateZoneTests` (the options and rows, nothing written
unset, 23:30 here is tomorrow in a zone ahead on every date display, the short offsets),
`TypedRegistryTests` (the clock's family). Pictures: `SceneTreeTests.NowPlayingAndDateZoneSheets`,
now-playing-date-<playing|idle>.png — the bar at 150 % with the media folder playing and gone while
paused, the clock button and a calendar face in Tokyo's tomorrow at 23:30 here.
By hand: with "Hide it while nothing plays" on, pause the player — the folder leaves the bar about five
seconds later and comes back as soon as it plays; set a calendar face's zone to one across midnight.

## 235. A face's submenu under its name; a line carried off its column takes no room (2026-10-19)

**Every face's submenu starts with its name** (the person: *"always show the name of the face in the
folder settings on the second level"*). §227 headed only an empty face's submenu with its name, over
"No settings for this face"; a face with settings started straight with its rows, so a submenu of
"Show seconds", "Clock", "Time zone" did not say whose they were. Now every face's second level is the
face's name as a heading (the heading row the empty face had), then its rows — or "No settings for
this face" —, then the rule and Remove (`OptionMenu.FaceSection`). The heading is the face's title as
its first-level row says it (`Dock.TitleOf`).

**A line carried off its column leaves it flush on the bar's side** (the person: *"when i drag a
folder widget away from a column into another column the widgets move to the top although they should
stay at the bottom ... the container so to speak does not change the size properly"*). While a line is
carried over no place of the folder — an empty slot beside the lists, where it would become a list of
its own, or off the lists — the lines stood by a plan of the folder with the line put at its own
list's end (`FolderDrag.Closed`, `ClosedGroup`). That end is away from a top bar, so there it looked
nearly right; but the line still took its room. On a bottom or side bar a list's end is its bottom:
the carried line's room sat at the bar's side and the lines over it rose to the top of the column. On
every bar the column kept its height, its panel as tall as before around a gap.

Root cause: the carried line still counted in its old column. Fix: `FolderFlyout.Build` takes the
lines carried off (`away`): they are in no list's flow — no height, no gap, a box of nothing at the
list's far end —, so the lines left close up on the bar's side and the list, its panel and the
folder's box are as tall as what is left (`ShowArranged` for one line or several over no place;
`Planned`, by which lines carried together are aimed, the same). Over a place the plan is the move
itself, as before, and the drop is laid out as before. Nothing in the config changes.

Tests: `FolderColumnFlushTests` (bottom, top, left and right bars at 150 %: carried from the taller
list over a slot, the two lines left stand where they stood — up where the carried one stood on a top
bar —, and the list is as tall as they are; let go, it is a list of its own and every list stands on
the bar's side of a panel as tall as the tallest; `folder-column-flush-<edge>.png`). Without the fix
the heading stood at the column's top (0 for 181 px) on a bottom bar. `OptionMenuTests`
(`EveryFacesSubmenuHasItsChoicesAsLevelsOfTheirOwn`, `AChoiceOpensALevelOfItsOwnOnEveryLevel`) check
the name heading first. By hand: on a bottom bar, carry the top line of a tall column toward an empty
slot — the lines under it stay put and the column shrinks from the top; a face's row in an arranged
folder's menu opens under the face's name.

## 236. Tides (2026-10-19)

The person: *"add a tides widget"* — tide times for people at the coast. A widget of its own,
`tides`, beside the weather and the air quality, for the same reason the air is one (§211): another
subject that only shares the weather's place. It shares everything else a weather widget has: the place
(`WeatherOptions`, this PC's location for a new one, the place picker of the menu and the page), the
offline cache, the stale words, Refresh and "Change location" on its menu, the Weather page of the add
list. Its one setting is the place; heights are in feet where temperatures are in Fahrenheit
(Localization's scale, else the region's), as the weather's wind is in miles.

**The source.** Open-Meteo's marine service (`marine-api.open-meteo.com`), the weather's own provider:
free, no key, CC BY 4.0, worldwide. `sea_level_height_msl` every quarter of an hour (`minutely_15`) and
every hour, yesterday to the day after tomorrow, asked in Unix seconds (`timeformat=unixtime`; checked
live 2026-10-19: with local times the service writes one offset for the whole answer, so on the day the
clocks change every time after the change would be an hour off). The quarters are read, the hours where
the quarters have no value. A place inland or out of the model's reach answers with every value null:
"No tide data here, pick a coastal place". It is a model, with the surge in it, less exact near coasts
and **not for navigation** (Open-Meteo's own words); heights are over mean sea level, not a chart's
datum, so a low is often below zero and the figures are not a harbour's tide table's. The larger lines
say so in a quiet line over the curve ("Modelled by Open-Meteo, not for navigation").

**Highs and lows** are worked out, not given (`TideTurns.Find`): hysteresis on the samples — the top
so far is a high once the sea has fallen back from it by 15 % of the series' range (3 cm at least), the
bottom a low once it has risen as far — so the model's ripples and an estuary's small second low (Hoek
van Holland's 7 cm bump, seen live) are no turns. A flat top is its middle; a single sample's top is
placed between its neighbours by a parabola (to the minute, not the quarter hour). A null or a gap ends
a run, and neither a run's first sample nor its last top is a turn: the sea may have come from further
or go on past it. The next turn is the first after now; the sea rises where it is a high (else as the
series moves); the height now is straight between the two quarters around now.

**Times** are the place's clock: this PC's zone where the place kept this PC's offset when the answer
was made (so a turn after the clocks change is right), else the answer's own offset (`TideClock`).

**Fetching** (`TideStore`, `tides.json`): one fetch per place for every face and line, keyed as the
weather's (`WeatherStore.KeyOf`), every six hours — the answer is a three days' forecast — and on
Refresh; between fetches the next turn, how soon and the height now are worked out of the series every
minute. A failure keeps the last answer with its age, quiet; stale too after three intervals missed.

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Tides`, `TidesFaceDrawing`): the arrow of the way the sea goes and, by its
Show option, "High 14:32" (default), "High 14:32 · 2.1 m", "High in 3 h 10 min" or the height now,
"1.2 m". Measured from templates (the widest time of the region's format, "High" and "Low", "-88.8 m",
18 h 58 min), never the reading; aligned (§201, the middle). No place: the pin and "Set location";
nothing yet or off the sea: the drop and a dash (its tooltip says why); down a bar on its side the arrow
over the time or the height. Tooltip: the place, the height now and the way, the next four turns with
their heights, the age. A click opens the folder, as every face's: the line is what it opens to.

**The line** (`ListKind.Tides`, `TidesTile`), one row to six, four unmeasured, each piece where it fits
whole: one row, the arrow, "High 14:32 · 2.1 m" and the height now at the end; two rows, the height now
large beside the next turn over how soon; from three, the place and the age over that; then the curve
from three hours ago to 21 hours on, **edge to edge and down to the line's bottom edge** under the rim
(`UnderRim`), as the stock's day and every graph of a list (§192), its area filled with the accent's
fading fill and no plate (§9, "One gutter"), a hairline from the band's top to the foot and a mark at
now, each high's time over it and each low's under it — the band ends a low's time and 4 DIP short of
the foot, so the lowest time stays inside the line and clear of the folder's rounded corner; a time is
left out, dot and all, where it would cross the gutter or another. Where the line is taller the rows
come in **under the head, over the curve**, each only where the curve keeps its least under it: the
next four turns across ("High" over "17:32 2.4 m"), then the model's line; the curve takes the rest,
with no pad at its foot (2026-10-19: *"the tide graph should go all the way to the bottom of the
widget"*; until then the turns and the model's line stood under the curve and its fill stopped short).
Nothing on it is pressed (Refresh and the place are on its menu): there is nothing to act on.

**The preset** (`Presets.TidesId`, "Tides"): the face over the line, after the air quality in the add
list's Weather page; the first place chosen is given to the face and the line (`WeatherPlaces.Spread`).
The file gains a line kind and a face with one option; nothing changes shape, nothing is migrated.
Words in all 30 languages.

Tests: `TidesTests` (the answer in instants, quarters before hours, no series is no answer, nulls are no
tide; the request; turns to the minute and the centimetre, ripples and a second low, a flat top, a
parabola's lean, series' ends and gaps, the day the clocks change; the next turn and the way; heights in
metres and feet, the separator, no "-0.0"; the reading, inland, waiting, failed and stale; one fetch per
place, a failure keeping the answer, a tides.json that cannot be read; the face's option, a tides line
through the file, a newer word, a file from before, the preset and its place, the add list),
`TidesPictures` (tides-faces-dark/light.png: the four forms at 100 and 150 %, no place, waiting, inland,
stale, on its side; one width per setting whatever it reads; tides-lines(-light|-inland|-100|-100-light).png
at one to six rows; the curve's foot is the line's bottom at four to six rows, the turns and the model's
line over it), and the registries (`TypedRegistryTests`, `ListGutterTests`: the curve reaches both edges).
By hand: add "Tides" from the add list's Weather page; pick a coastal place (Brest, Boston) and an inland
one (Zürich); the next turn, its countdown and the mark move with the minute; the face's Show choices.

## 237. Public holidays in the calendar, from Nager.Date (2026-10-19)

The person: *"not a widget but add possibility to add public holidays to the calendar from the
nager.date api"*.

**One more calendar, not a widget's option.** No calendar widget picks its calendars: the month, the
agenda, the day and week views, the bar's calendar and the next meeting show every calendar the store
has (CalendarStore, docs\accounts.md "What is synced": "No widget picks one calendar"). So the holidays
are a calendar beside the accounts', the person's for every widget: a source of the store
(`HolidayCalendar : ICalendarSource`, Karpo.Dock\Calendar\HolidayCalendar.cs), all-day events in its
colour, and every view draws them as it draws any calendar's — the month's day gets its dot, the day's
list and the agenda name it with "All day", the week's all-day row a block. Nothing in the views knows
holidays. They are not in accounts.json: they have no account and no secret, and an older Karpo that
met a kind of account it does not know would set the whole file aside. They are the config's
(`Config.Holidays`, `HolidayOptions`: on, country, region, the other days, colour), left out of the
file until somebody turns them on, read tolerantly (`HolidayOptionsConverter`: a hand edit costs the
holidays, never the config), roaming with the rest of the person's settings.

**Where they are set.** The Accounts page, a section "Public holidays" between the accounts and "Add an
account": its switch and its colour's swatch in the header, as an account's calendar has them (the same
`PartColorButton`; Automatic is the holidays' red, Outlook's `#D13438`, the palette's first, as printed
calendars mark holidays), and under it Country (Windows' region's first, "As in Windows (Switzerland)",
then every country by Windows' own name for it in Karpo's language, ICU's `uloc_getDisplayCountry`),
Region (shown for a country that has regions: "Whole country", then its cantons, states, provinces by
their own names) and "Also show other days". And a calendar's menu (§220–228): a calendar line and a
folder wearing the calendar face (the bar's calendar) have the rows **Public holidays** (a toggle),
then while on **Country** (a search, five at first, Windows' region's first), **Region** (a choice) and
**Also show other days** (a toggle) — `OptionHolidays`, written into the config the menu was read from
(`OptionPlace.Config`, also for a search's pick, `FieldPicks.Keep`). The colour stays the page's, as an
account calendar's colour is. Settings' widget page leaves them to the Accounts page.

**Which days** (`PublicHolidays.Shown`): type Public only unless "Also show other days" (bank, school,
authorities', optional holidays and observances). With a region, the whole country's and that region's.
**Without one, the whole country's alone** — the cleaner of the two: Switzerland lists some thirty
holidays, most of them a few cantons', and every one marked "regional" in a day's list would be noise
and wrong for most who read it; the Region row's description says so. One exception, the service's own
way of writing a national day: a holiday listed for every region the country has, two at the least
(the United Kingdom's New Year's Day: England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, `global: false`), is
the whole country's. A day the service lists twice (Epiphany: Public in Ticino, an observance in Uri and
Schwyz) is shown once. Picking a region while the country follows Windows makes the country that one,
so a move of Windows' region never leaves a region of another country. **The name**: the English name
where Karpo speaks English, else the country's (`localName`), which a person living there knows it by;
the other one, where it differs, is the event's second line ("All day · Weihnachten"). The date face's
tooltip says today's holiday under the long date.

**The service**: `https://date.nager.at/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country}`, keyless. Its countries
(AvailableCountries) and every region its answers for 2026 and 2027 name are listed in the core
(Karpo.Core\HolidayPlaces.cs), so neither the page nor a menu asks it anything; a region it names later
still shows, by its code.

**When it asks.** Never while off: the calendar is no source then and reads no file. On, a year is one
request: this year and the next as soon as somebody looks (the store's Open; a look while off is
remembered, so turning them on fetches at once), and a year a view reaches (stepped back to last year,
or forward), never more than five either side of this one. A year's answer is asked again when it is a
week old (`HolidayCalendar.Fresh`), after a failure not before half an hour (`Retry`); a timer looks at
most every six hours and at the new year. Kept in `holidays.json` in the local folder (the islands'
files, as the weather's forecast; public days need no DPAPI): read once on the pool before the first
request, written after every answer, the person's country's years only. Offline the kept years stay,
however old; only a country of which nothing was ever had shows "Couldn't get the public holidays". An
isolated run (tests, `--smoke`) has no holiday calendar in its store at all.

Strings (30 languages): the calendar's name, its problem, the page's description and keywords, Country
(its description, "As in Windows ({country})", search, not found, pick), Region (its description, Whole
country), "Also show other days" and its description.

Tests: `HolidaysTests` (the saved answers of Switzerland 2026 and 2027, the United Kingdom and the
United States read; an answer that is no list; the whole country, a region, the other days and a day
once; a national day written per region; the names; every region the answers name listed; a file of
before reads and writes no holidays, a hand edit costs nothing else; the menu's rows, a country taking
its region, a region pinning its country), `HolidayCalendarTests` (off asks nothing and is no calendar;
on, this year and the next, red, all day; another region or colour asks nothing; the turn of the year,
last year when a view reaches it, not a far one; kept on disk and asked again a week on, offline shown
from the file; nothing kept and offline is the problem, retried after half an hour; a day's names).
Pictures: `HolidayPictures` (`holidays-preset-<dark|light>.png`: Zürich's holidays beside a family
calendar before Christmas, Christmas picked, 225 % text; `holidays-lines-<dark|light>.png`: the agenda
and the week view). By hand: Settings ▸ Accounts ▸ Public holidays on: the bar's calendar shows
Switzerland's four national days at once (with a Swiss Windows region), Region ▸ Zürich adds Good
Friday and St. Stephen's Day; the swatch recolours them; the bar's calendar's menu has the same rows;
holidays.json appears in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo; off, it no longer grows.

## 238. A now-playing face beside other faces hides by itself (2026-10-19)

The person: "on my bar the now playing still does not hide when paused when set as folder face. (there
are multiple folder faces)". Their quick settings button wears Wi-Fi, sound and now playing, the last
set to "Hide it while nothing plays", with a now-playing line inside.

**Why it stayed.** §234 fixed what "nothing plays" means, but the hiding was the folder's alone:
`FolderIsland.Count` took the folder off the bar only where every face was a now-playing face set so.
Beside other faces the face kept its room by design (the §234 note said so), and the button's length was
measured over all its faces whatever played, so on a button of several faces nothing ever went.

**Now.** Which faces are on the bar is a live question, as how many cells a widget has is
(`FolderIsland.FacesOnBar`): every face but a now-playing face set to hide while nothing plays, while
nothing does (`MediaIsland.Idle`, its grace as §234). The button is measured over those
(`ShapeContext.Faces`, given by `CellIsland.Shaped`, read by `WidgetShapes.Folder` → `Parts`), painted
over those (`FaceSizes`, `FaceBoxes` take the list), and the meeting face's Join and the tooltip's lines
follow them too. So the face goes with its room and the room between it and its neighbour; the others
keep their order and length, and the button is as long as a button of just them. How long each face is
stays its settings'. The re-layout is the one §234 has: the line's news, or the grace running out,
wakes the folder, its refresh finds its cell another length (`CellIsland.Moved`) and the bar is laid
out again; a track starting puts the face back. Where the now-playing face is all it wears, nothing is
left (`FacesOnBar` empty) and the folder leaves the bar as before.

Tests: `MediaPresetTests.BesideOtherFacesOnlyTheNowPlayingFaceGoesWhileNothingPlays` (Wi-Fi, sound and
now playing: playing three faces; paused, Wi-Fi and sound, the cell and the face boxes those of a button
of just the two; playing, back), the single-face tests of §234 unchanged; `NowPlayingBesidePictures`
(now-playing-beside-playing/idle.png, 150 % dark). By hand: pause the player and wait 5 s — only the
track and its art leave the button; play — they are back.

## 239. Sports scores (2026-10-19)

The person: "implement: sports scores" — a favourite team's live score or next match, as Google's
sports card shows it. A widget of its own, `sports`: a line of a list, and on the bar the sports preset,
a folder wearing the score as its face.

**The service.** ESPN's public site API, no account and no key (`site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports`):
a team's schedule (`/{sport}/{league}/teams/{id}/schedule`; for football, the soccer kind, `soccer/all/…`
— every competition the team plays in, its results and, with `?fixture=true`, its fixtures), a league's
scoreboard for a day (`/scoreboard?dates=yyyyMMdd`, the day as ESPN files it, in New York: the live
clock and the league's other matches), and ESPN's own team search (`site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/search`).
Nothing personal is in a request: the team's id, the league's slug, a day, what was typed. Nothing is
asked before a team is set. Read in Karpo.Core\Sports.cs (`SportsAnswers`), tested on ESPN's own
answers saved on 2026-10-19 (Karpo.Tests\Sports\Saved): a schedule writes a score `{ "displayValue": "2" }`,
a scoreboard `"2"`; a kick-off `timeValid: false` is "TBD", its day alone.

**The leagues** are one table (`SportsLeagues.All`): football's big five, the Eredivisie, Portugal,
Scotland, Belgium, Switzerland, Austria, Turkey, the Championship, MLS, Liga MX, Brazil, Argentina,
the Champions, Europa and Conference Leagues, the Nations League, the EURO, the World Cup and the
Libertadores; the NFL and college football; the NBA, the WNBA and college basketball; MLB; the NHL. A
search finds a team only in a league of the table (its own league, else its home league): "chiefs" is
Kansas City, not a rugby side. Each league says how it tells a game's time (`SportsClock`).

**The setting** is the team (`SportsOptions`: sport, league, ESPN's id, its name and abbreviation as
found; written `"sports"` on the line, and only there). One row, `SportsTeam`, a search (§223): in the
line's menu its field, five teams and "Show more" (§228), each with its league and abbreviation — the
menu alone, as every widget's setting is since §233. A file's team that is no team of the table, or an
id ESPN could not have given, is no team; the line asks for one ("Set up", `SetupField.Team`, whose click
opens its menu at the field). A file from before has none: no shape change, no migration.

**What it shows** (`SportsPick`): a match on now; else one ended within six hours of its kick-off, until
the next is within an hour; else the next — one put off or called off says so in its place until its
day is gone, one past its kick-off and not begun stays the next for three hours; else the last played;
else "No matches coming up". In words (`SportsText`, `SportsReading`): "MON 2–0 CAG 53'" (the home side
first in football, the visitors first in America's sports, "CAG 0–2 MON"), "vs RMA Sat 20:00" at home
and "@ PSG Tomorrow 21:00" away, "BAR 5–2 BET Final", "vs RMA Postponed". The clock is the league's in
signs every language reads: "67'", "45'+2'", "HT" (translated); "Q3 5:32", "OT", "2OT"; "H2 5:32";
"P2 12:04"; "▲5" and "▼9" for the inning's halves. A kick-off is this PC's zone in Karpo's time format
(`Nls.Time`): "Today 20:00", "Tomorrow 20:00", the weekday within the week, the date past it.

**How often** (`SportsPace`) — the one exception to Karpo's one online interval (`OnlineUpdates`), because
a live score fifteen minutes old is a wrong score: every 30 seconds while a match is on, every minute
from a quarter of an hour before a kick-off, else the online interval but never past that quarter of an
hour before the next kick-off. While a match is on only its league's scoreboard is read, the schedule
again every half hour; Refresh reads it whole. A failure waits the pace, then twice that each time it
repeats, never more than half an hour, and leaves the last answer standing: stale (failed, or older
than twice its pace and a minute) the scoreboard's head says its age in the alarm ink, the face's words
are quiet. Never a made-up score. One fetch per team for every face and line (`SportsStore`, keyed
`sport/league/id`), kept in `sports.json` in the local folder for a restart. The islands tick every
half minute and only ask the store whether a fetch is due, so the dock's timer is armed once, not as a
match begins and ends.

**The logos** come from ESPN's picture server alone (`a.espncdn.com`), at 64 px through its resizer
(`/combiner/i?img=…&w=64&h=64`), the dark ground's drawing (`/500-dark/`) on a dark list, kept in memory
(64 at most). Until one comes, a quiet circle with the side's first letter.

**The line** (`ListKind.Sports`, `SportsTile`, one to six rows, three unmeasured, fixed): one row, a red
dot while it is on (else the team's logo), the score or "vs Real Madrid", and the clock (red), "Final"
or the day at the end; from two rows the scoreboard — the competition (or the age) and the clock or the
day over the two sides, each with its logo and its name either side of the score, the loser's name
quiet after a final; under it, a row each, while it is on the league's other matches of the day, then
the matches to come ("vs Real Madrid · LALIGA … Sun 21:00"), else the results before, each list under
a small heading; at the foot where it stands, "1st in Spanish LALIGA · 9-0-0". **A click opens the match
on ESPN** in the browser (the team's page where there is no match), once the folder has gone, as a
headline's story opens (§98): not a folder of its own — ESPN's match page is the detail the line has no
room for, and a line opens no popup (§15). Its menu: Refresh and Open website, then the team's field.

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Sports`, `SportsFaceDrawing`): the folder's first sports line's match, as a
drive face shows its drive line's — one team, set in one place; the folder registers that team with the
store as a user of its own, so the face is fresh with the folder shut. "MON 2–0 CAG 53'" after a red dot
while it is on, "vs PSG Tomorrow 21:00", "BAR 5–2 BET Final". Its width is its team's league's widest
template — a score with the league's widest clock, a kick-off on the widest day, "Postponed" — never the
reading (§12.2); its one option is where its words stand (§201, the middle). Down a bar on its side, the
dot over the score or the time. Without a team, its glyph and "No team yet". Its menu is the line's.

**The preset** (`Presets.SportsId`, "Sports scores"): the face over the line at three rows, in the add
list beside the news and the markets; the line alone on a folder's page.

Words in all 30 languages (`core.widget.sports.*`, `core.preset.sportsGroup.*`, `core.face.sports.*`,
`settings.widget.sports.team.*`, `dock.sports.*`); "vs" and "@" are sport's own signs, not words.

Tests: `SportsAnswersTests` (results, fixtures, both halves live, America's schedules and scoreboards,
every status a state, what is no answer, a search kept to the table, the requests, the hosts opened and
asked, a scoreboard merged), `SportsRulesTests` (live first, a final's six hours, put off and late, the
last played, the saved answers, the paces, the back-off, scoreboard only, every league's clock, home or
visitors first, what the face says, stale), `SportsStoreTests` (one fetch per team, half a minute then
the scoreboard, a failure kept and backed off, the last user gone, the failures' words),
`SportsConfigTests` (a new line asks, the team through the file, a hand-edited team dropped, older and
newer files, every registry, the search row), `SportsPictures` (sports-lines-<live|next|final|stale|unset|waiting>.png
at one to six rows, dark, light, 100 %; sports-faces-<dark|light>.png in every state, one width a team).
By hand: add "Sports scores" from the add list, search "barcelona" in its line's menu and pick Barcelona;
the face shows its next match; during a match the clock moves every half minute; click the line to
open ESPN.

## 240. Earthquakes (2026-10-19)

The person: *"add earthquake alert widget"* — the USGS's feed, free. A widget of its own, `quakes`, on
the Weather page of the add list beside the air quality, as a preset (`Presets.QuakesId`, "Earthquakes":
the face over the line) and as a line.

**The source.** The USGS's GeoJSON summary feed of the past week's earthquakes of 2.5 and up
(`earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/2.5_week.geojson`): public domain, no key, renewed
every minute behind a CDN, some 30 KB compressed. One feed for every widget, not the FDSN query service
with a latitude, longitude and radius: each widget's radius and magnitude are worked out on the PC from
the one answer (`QuakeFilter`), so the place it is for never leaves the machine, one fetch serves every
widget whatever it is set to, and the USGS asks polling clients to use the summary feeds. Only events
of type "earthquake" are kept (the feeds carry quarry blasts and explosions too). `QuakeStore` fetches
it every five minutes while any earthquake widget stands somewhere — not every online widget's
interval: an alert an hour late is none — and at once on Refresh; a failure waits 5, 10, 20 … minutes
to an hour, and the last answer keeps showing with its age (stale after three missed fetches, as the
weather's rule). `quakes.json` in the local folder keeps the last answer, this PC's last position and
every event id seen.

**The settings.** The place is the weather's (`WeatherOptions`: this PC's location for a new one, the
place picker, "Set up in Settings"; none needed for the whole world). Beside it, on a line
`WeatherOptions.Quakes` (`QuakeOptions`: `radius` km, `magnitude`, `alerts`), each written only where it
is not its default, on a face its options (`QuakesFace`: `radius` "km100" … "world", `magnitude` "m25" …
"m7", `alerts`, `width`, the alignment): **Distance** 100, 250, 500, 1,000, 2,000 km or worldwide;
**Minimum magnitude** 2.5+, 3+, 4+, 4.5+, 5+, 6+, 7+; **Alert me to new earthquakes**, on. The defaults
are quiet: 1,000 km, 4 and up. A hand-edited number reads as the nearest choice (750 km is 1,000), a
word from a newer build as the default. They are rows of the face's and the line's menus (§219–233),
where a widget's settings are. Nothing in the file changes shape: a face, a line kind
and one optional record more, which an older build reads past.

**Distances** are the haversine's on a sphere of 6,371 km, the bearing the initial great-circle one, said
as the nearest of the compass's eight points in the language's letters ("1368 km E", "NO" in German),
always in km, as the USGS writes them. The magnitude is "M4.8" in the language's decimal sign; its dot
is the class's colour, Windows 11's signal colours: under 4 green `#6CCB5F`, 4 yellow `#FCE100`, 5
orange `#F7630C`, 6 red `#E81123`, 7 `#C30052`, 8 and up `#881798`, with a hairline round it so the
yellow reads on a light bar.

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Quakes`, `QuakeFaceDrawing`): the past day's latest earthquake in its radius
over its magnitude, its dot and "M4.8", "M4.8 · 120 km" (the default) or "M4.8 · 120 km NE · 2 h ago";
a quiet day a grey dot and "No earthquakes in 24 h" ("–" compact). Measured from templates — "M8.8", as
many figures as the radius has, the widest point and age, the quiet words — never from the reading;
aligned (§201, the middle). No place: the pin and "Set location"; waiting: a dash; stale: faded. Its
tooltip: the place and how far it looks, the earthquake, where in the USGS's words, how deep, the age.

**The line** (`ListKind.Quakes`, `QuakesLine`): one row, the newest's dot, magnitude and distance, its
age at the end; two rows, the earthquakes alone, two lines each (the magnitude and where, then how far
and when), as many as fit; from three the head over them — the place, "Within 1,000 km", the feed's
age — then the week's, newest first. A quiet week says so. A row lights under the pointer and its click
opens the earthquake's page on the USGS's site once the folder has gone (`CellAct.Action`); its menu
refreshes it and opens its page.

**Alerts.** Karpo has no packaged identity and cannot raise a toast (as the timer and the alarm cannot,
§106), so a new earthquake is said as theirs are: Windows' notification sound once, and the accent's
dot on the button of the folder that holds the widget or wears its face, until it is opened
(`FolderIsland.Due`); the face shows it at once. The dock watches the store from its start
(`Dock.Quakes.cs`), so a folder shut all day still hears of one. New is: none of the event's ids (the
feed's `ids`, every network's) seen before, or seen under the widget's minimum and revised over it
(`QuakeNews`); never on the first answer ever, never for an event older than three hours (a PC woken
from a day's sleep rings for none of yesterday's), never twice — the seen ids outlive a restart and are
kept eight days, past the feed's week. A widget says one only with its alert on and the earthquake in
its radius over its magnitude (`QuakeNews.Says`). Several in one answer ring once.

Strings in all 30 languages (km and the compass's points neutral in `UntranslatedTests`; the "M" of a
magnitude is its symbol, written in code).

Tests: `QuakeTests` (a real answer of 2026-10-19 read, the quarry blast left out, what is no feed;
distances, bearings, points and their words; the classes; which a widget shows, the reading's week and
day, staleness and failures; news once and only while fresh, by alias, a magnitude revised up, seen ids
forgotten past the week; the store's news across two restarts, its wait after failures, polling held to
the interval; the choices' nearest steps and words; a line's settings through the file, a hand-edited
radius, the face's options, a file from before unchanged, the preset and its place; which folder says
it), `QuakePictures` (quake-faces-dark/light.png: every class at the three widths, quiet, no place,
waiting, stale, worldwide, 150 %, on its side, one width per setting; quake-lines(-quiet)(-light).png and
quake-lines-100.png at one to eight rows; a row's click opens its page). By hand: add "Earthquakes" from
the add list's Weather page; with location on it lists the week's near you; set Distance to Worldwide
and Minimum magnitude to 6+ to see some at once; turn the alert off and on in the face's menu.


## 241. The calendar always follows the folder's day; public holidays in every style, in a submenu of their own (2026-10-19)

The person: "always follow the folders day", "public holidays should get their own submenu", "public
holidays you should also be able to set on other styles of the calendar not just the agenda view", "also
show other days should be removed as it is not clear what is meant".

**Following is not a choice.** A follower had a switch per channel it follows (§9: "Follow the folder's
day", "Follow the day pointed at", "Follow the folder's app", "Light the app pointed at"), stored as the
ids switched off (`WidgetItem.Unfollowed`). Off, a line kept a day (or an app) of its own beside a month
that had picked another — a folder whose lines disagree, which only looked broken. So the switches went,
every one of them, not the day's alone: a channel a kind follows (`ListWidget.Follows`) is followed,
always (`Channels.Follows` is the record's word), and the mechanism has no opt-out left to special-case.
Every calendar style follows the day — agenda, day's events, day, week, month, year — and each that
publishes it still does. A file's `"unfollowed"` is read past (an unknown key) and not written again;
nothing else of the line changes, and no config is reset. Gone with it: `Channel.Follow`/`FollowNote`,
`Channels.SetFollows`/`Normalized`, the menu's `Follow.` rows and the `core.channel.*.follow*` words.

**Public holidays in every style.** The holidays were already one more calendar of the store (§237), so
every style drew them — listed by the agenda and the day's events, an all-day chip in the day and the
week, a dot in their red under the day in the month and the year — but their rows were offered by the
agenda's menu alone (`OptionHolidays.Shows` asked for the agenda's options kind). Now any line of the
calendar widget (`WidgetStyles.Calendar`) and the folder wearing the calendar face offer them. The month's
day, the year's and the week's heading of a holiday now say which one it is as their tooltip
(`CalendarLines.HolidayTip`, from the one holiday calendar's `NamesOn`, as the calendar face's tooltip).

**Their own submenu.** The rows are one group (`OptionRow.Group` = "Public holidays"): "Show public
holidays", and while on the country and its region. The group's row says what they are set to at its end
— "Off", or the country ("Switzerland") — through `OptionRow.GroupSummary`, which the menu shows in place
of the group's own reading where a row gives one.

**"Also show other days" went.** It was the holidays' `Observances`: bank, school and optional holidays
and observances beside the public ones — a name nobody could read for what it did. The holidays are the
public ones, always (`PublicHolidays.Shown` takes no switch). A file's `"observances"` is read past and
not written again; the Accounts page's card went with it.

Words in all 30 languages: `core.holidays.show`, `core.holidays.off`; the channels' switches and
`settings.holidays.observances.*` removed.

Tests: `ChannelsTests` (every calendar style follows; an old opt-out read past and not written),
`CalendarWeatherFolderTests.TheViewsFollowAndPublishTheDay` (a step of the day view moves every view, the
month and the events), `WidgetStylesTests` (an old line's opt-out through the style migration),
`HolidaysTests` (public days alone, an old "observances" read past, the rows on every style, one group
saying "Off" or the country, the menu's submenu), `HolidayPictures.HolidaysInEveryStyle`
(holidays-styles-dark.png at 150 %: agenda, month with its events, day, week and year; the month's and
the week's Christmas say "Christmas Day"). The opt-out tests of the screen-time lines and the agenda went.
By hand: in a calendar folder, pick a day in the month — every other calendar line shows it; open a
week line's menu — "Public holidays ▸ Off"; turn them on, pick a country; hover a holiday's day in the
month.

## 242. The currency converter (2026-10-19)

The person: "implement: … currency converter", from the pitch "1 EUR = 0.94 CHF on the bar, click to
convert any amount". It is a widget of its own, `currency`, a line of a list (`ListKind.Currency`,
`CurrencyTile`), and on the bar the currency preset (`Presets.CurrencyId`, "Currency converter"): a
folder wearing the currency face over the converter at four rows, beside the stock's in the add list's
page of the weather and the news (`AddTree`). Its icon is Windows' calculator.

**The source is the stock widget's.** §191 already reads a pair from Yahoo's chart endpoint as a symbol
of its own, "EURCHF=X", so the converter asks the stock store for the pair over a day and nothing else:
no second service, the same online interval with the stocks' five-minute floor, the same `stocks.json`,
the same refusal to go round a gate, and a converter and a stock line of one pair are one fetch. The ECB's
daily rates (frankfurter.app) were not needed. A pair of one currency asks nothing; its rate is 1. The
folder follows its face's pair as a second user of the store beside the stock face's share
(`StockStore.Use` with the widget to wake).

**What it converts** (`CurrencyOptions`, the line's own): From and To, ISO codes, and the amount, 1 where
nobody set it. A currency nobody chose is not written and is read as the region's pair — the euro in the
region's currency, the dollar in euros in the euro area (`CurrencyPairs.Start`) — from Windows' region
(`LOCALE_SINTLSYMBOL`), not .NET's, which the dock's invariant globalization makes nobody's. A code that is
none, an amount that is none or negative, reads as the pair's and as 1; nothing else in the file changes,
and a file from before has no record. **The face reads the line**: its folder's first converter
(`Currencies.LineOf`), so the bar and the converter it opens are one pair and one amount, set in one
place; the face's own options are only how much it says and where. A currency face in a folder without
a converter converts a new one's.

**Written and read in the person's marks** (`NumberMarks.Region`, `LOCALE_SDECIMAL`/`STHOUSAND`):
"1’234.50" in Switzerland, "1.234,50" in Germany, "1 234,50" in France. A converted amount has its
currency's ISO minor unit (the yen none, the dinar three) and four places under one ("0.0057 EUR"); a rate
has a pair's four or two (`CurrencyPairs.Places`) and four significant figures under a hundredth. An
amount typed is read in the region's marks where it could be either — "1,500" is fifteen hundred in the
US and one and a half in Germany — and a mark followed by anything but groups of three is the decimal
point everywhere ("1.5" is one and a half in Germany too); spaces and apostrophes group; Arabic-Indic
figures are figures; nothing negative, nothing past a trillion (`Currencies.Parse`).

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Currency`, `CurrencyFaceDrawing`): "100 EUR = 94.12 CHF", the amount and its
currency quiet, the worth in the text's ink; set to "The result", "94.12 CHF". Its room is the settings':
the worth keeps the room of its pair's amounts ten times over, from a table of each currency's usual
rate to the dollar (`Currencies.WorthTemplate`), never the rate read, so the bar does not move with the
market. No rate yet, a dash; past due or left standing by a failure, the worth quiet. Down a bar on its
side the currency over the worth. Its tooltip: the sentence, the rate with its age, and why a newer one
is not there. Right click: Refresh.

**The line**, at every height, each piece where it fits whole: one row, the two fields with their
currencies and the swap (⇄) between them — the converter itself, at every height; two rows, the rate
under them, "1 EUR = 0.9412 CHF", its age at the end, in the alarm's ink once past due; three, the two
currencies' names over the fields ("Euro → Swiss Franc", ICU's names); four and more, the pair's day at
the foot between the gutters, drawn as a stock line draws its day, in the colour of its move. The fields are WinUI's text box
(`InlineEditor` while typed in): type in either and the other is worked out as you type; Tab goes to the
other, Enter keeps, Escape takes back, a figure typed on the line starts the field the amount was given
in. The swap turns the pair round and leaves the amount given where it is, in the currency now there; the
day is turned over with it. What is typed and swapped is the line's while the dock runs and is never
written — the bar's pair and amount are the settings'; a change to them starts the converter from them.
Typing that is no amount leaves the other field empty, never a made-up number. With no rate the worth is
a dash and the rate's row says why, or "Getting the rate…". Right click: Refresh.

**Every setting is a row** (§220): From and To, choices of the pair picker's currencies with the region's
and the common ones first (picking the other side's swaps the two), and the amount, a text field in the
region's marks. The face's menu has its converter's three rows before its own (`OptionRows.OfFace`). They
are its settings' only home, as every widget's are now (§233). There are no grid cards any more (§16 went
with the grid, 2026-10-09), so the converter is a line and a face, as every widget is.

Words: the widget, its preset, its face and its two widths, "Getting the rate…", "Amount", in all
30 languages.

Tests: `CurrencyConverterTests` (the region's pair, decimals, the marks written and read both ways and
what is no amount, the face's room, a rate coming, standing past due and never made up, the swap, the
rows and the face's, the file read tolerantly and a folder of a converter loaded with the rest intact,
every registry), `CurrencyPictures` (currency-faces-dark/light.png: two widths, three pairs, waiting, past
due, one currency, 150 %, on its side, one width per setting whatever the rate; currency-lines(-light,
-100, -waiting).png at one to six rows; currency-typing.png; typing both ways, Escape, Enter, the swap, a
settings change). By hand: add "Currency converter" from the add list; it shows the euro in your region's
currency; click it, type in the second field, swap; right-click the bar while arranging and set From,
To and the amount; check the numbers use your region's separators.

## 243. Every settings row one row; height, a time and a place's device switch a level of their own; the face's bin back on its row (2026-10-19)

The person: "select none should not be a menu action", "use my devices location should be a submenu
entry in the place selector, also toggleable", "height should get its own submenu, when having automatic
height the height property that can still be set should be called max height", "for the face settings
move the delete button into the root view again. on the right side before the angled arrow", and "right
now some of the configuration items have a different size than the other ones, all of them should not
be bigger than a single entry, if needed split a configuration up into multiple entries".

**No "Select none".** Edit mode's menu on one of several selected widgets had it under the buttons
(Dock.MenuFloor.cs); Escape and a click on empty room already clear the selection, so it is gone, with
its act (`WidgetAct.SelectNone`) and its words in every language. `EditMenuRows` is a folder's "Open
folder" / "Close folder" alone now.

**The device's location is the place's switch** (`OptionRow.Within`, OptionMenu.cs). A place's search
(the weather's, the air quality's, the tides', a line's and a face's) opens its level with "Use my
device's location" at its top, a toggle switch at the row's end; on, the field below it greyed (no keys,
nothing asked) and its five results' room kept, so the level is the same size on and off; off, the place
it had in the field and the search as before. The row the level opens from says "Device location" at
its end while it is on (`OptionRow.Summary`, new words `dock.edit.deviceLocation`). It was a toggle of
the widget's own over the place row *and* the search's first result (`OptionFields.Device`, the finder's
`Offered`) — two controls for one setting; both are gone. The write is the same: the switch sets
`UseDeviceLocation` as before (`FaceRows.UseDevice` for a face), a place picked turns it off
(`OptionTexts.SetPlace`). The core keeps the switch a row of its own in the list (keys `WeatherUsesDevice`
and a face's `device` unchanged), marked as heading the place's level, so every pick still finds its row
by its key.

**Height is a level** (LineHeightRows.cs). A folder line's menu has one "Height" row, ruled off, saying
what it is at its end — "Automatic, up to 6 rows", "Fixed, 3 rows", "Fill" (the settings app's words,
`settings.widget.size.*`) — opening the radio trio and the rows' stepper. The stepper is named for what
its rows are: under Automatic they cap the height (`LineHeight`: automatic is the content's height "up to
N rows"), so it is "Max height" (new words `dock.edit.height.max`); under Fixed they are the height,
"Height"; under Fill, greyed, it is named for the mode Fill keeps under it. A step or a mode keeps the
level open, shown again in place (`LineHeightRows.Updated` replaces the one row).

**A face's bin on its row.** A folder's face row on an arranged bar's menu is its grip at the start and
a bin at its end before the chevron (`FlyoutControl.Tools`, as an ordered list's rows have; one helper,
`OptionMenu.Handles`, for both), its tooltip "Remove (Del)"; Delete on the lit row takes the face off; on
the last face it is greyed. Its submenu has no "Remove" and no rule any more (§226 and §230 had moved it
there).

**One row each.** Every row of a settings menu is a menu row's height, 32 DIP:

- *A text field* (Flyout.Fields.cs) is its name at the row's start and Windows' text box at its end, the
  row's fill high and 55 % of its width (`FieldShare`), the name cut before it; on a search's own level
  the box fills the row, its placeholder saying what to type (an icon search's too). §219 to §239 had the
  name over a 32 DIP box: two rows.
- *A search's results* are one row each, the quieter words (a country, a zone's offset, a section) at the
  row's end as a value, not a second line; a greyed row says its first sentence. Five results' room is
  six rows ("Show more" the sixth).
- *A time of day and a length* (MenuPickers.cs) are one row saying it ("7:30 AM", "1 h 25 min") opening a
  level of a row per part, its name at the start and a stepper at the end: "Hours", "Minutes" and, on a
  12-hour clock, "AM or PM" with a button of its value. §224 had the name as a heading over a row of
  steppers side by side. That row was a control of its own (`FlyoutSpin`, `SpinPart`, its own drawing,
  keys and hit boxes); it is gone: every stepper of every menu is `FlyoutControl.Stepper`, which now
  steps as its button goes down and again while it is held (Windows' RepeatButton, 400 ms then 80 ms;
  `StepperPress`), with a `Switch` form for AM/PM — the height's and a number's steppers repeat too.
- *A pin's target* says what it opens at its end (the file's or the folder's name), no path line under it.
- *Tiles* (a colour's swatches, an icon's glyphs) stand in cells a menu row square (`TileCellDip`), so a
  line of them is one row; at most eight swatches and six icons to a line (`FlyoutTile.Across`), centred,
  in the settings menus' full width (§230's 320 DIP; they had kept the lines of Windows' 256 DIP menu).
- Headings stay as they are (a level's name, a group's), and an icon's level does not give its search the
  keys as it opens: its tiles are what it offers, its default lit (§230's focus is a search level's alone).

A value on a row with no chevron (a result, a target) stands at the row's very end, its words a gap
before it (`FarSlot`); it had stood a chevron's room in and could run into the words.

Words: `dock.edit.height.max`, `dock.edit.deviceLocation` in all 30 languages; `dock.widgetMenu.selectNone`
gone. No config change.

Tests: `MenuFloorTests.ArrangedNoMenuHasSelectNone`, `MenuSidesTests` (a folder's rows), `LineHeightRowsTests`
(one row opening its level, "Max height" and "Height", the value, Updated; on a real menu, the pictures
line-height-menu-<look>-<scale>-<auto|fixed>.png with the level open), `OptionMenuTests` (the bin on a
face's row, Delete, greyed on the last; no Remove in the submenu; no heading among a face's rows),
`MenuKeepsTests` (a face taken off by Delete on its row), `MenuFieldTests` (the place's level: the switch,
the field greyed and the same size on and off, menu-field-place-device-<look>.png and
menu-field-place-<look>.png), `OptionFieldsTests` (the switch sets a face as the page did), `MenuSearchTests`
(no device row among a place's suggestions), `MenuPickersTests` (a time's and a length's levels, the AM/PM
switch, every row one height, a press steps at once; tiles a row square, eight and six; the target's
name; menu-pickers-time-<look>.png), `MenuValuesTests` (six rows of room).
By hand: arrange the bar, open a folder's menu: the bin on each face's row before the chevron; a weather
face's Place: the switch on top, the field greyed while on; a folder line's Height: one row and its level;
an alarm's Time: a level of Hours, Minutes, AM or PM; hold a stepper's "+": it repeats.

## 244. One model of a folder's geometry; a widget added no longer shifts the columns (2026-10-19)

The person: "when adding a widget in the folder edit mode somehow the alignment goes back to as if
there are hidden columns there. i want you to tackle this problem from the ground up. in general i dont
want you to just plaster over the code again and again. i want you to audit and try to remove code where
you have similar behaviour to, make the application more simple."

**The bug.** "Add a widget" in an arranged folder (§231) put the new line into the file where the
folder's edit bar adds (`AddPlace`: the picked column, else the first column showing everything it has)
and *then* handed it to the pointer. The commit laid the folder out with the line standing there. In the
person's folders that first column is an empty spacer outside the column of widgets (three empty columns,
the widgets, two empty), so the spacer became a column with widgets; the columns with widgets are what is
centred on the button (`FolderPlan.Core`, §158), and every column slid over by one and a half columns —
exactly as if the spacers were hidden columns of widgets. A paste (Ctrl+V put the copies at the end of the
first column) did the same. Root cause: the layout counted a line that had no place yet.

**The model.** A folder's geometry is one function of two things:

- *the folder* (`FolderOptions`): its columns left to right — every list, empty ones kept as spacers
  (§148) — each its width (`FolderListWidths`, narrowed to the display by `ListWidths`/`Fit`) and its
  lines top to bottom; arranged, the slots beside them out to the screen's edges (`WithSlots`), each a
  column with nothing in it yet, a medium column's width, the lists' gap apart (§221);
- *what is pending* (`FolderPending`): the lines carried — by their index — whether they are new (added,
  pasted, copied: no place in the folder yet), and where they would land (`To`: a gap of a list, a slot,
  or null over no place).

`FolderFlyout.Build(…, pending)` is that function: where `To` is set the folder is laid out with the move
made (`FolderDrag.Moved`, a copy, `Folders.MoveGroup`); where it is null the carried lines are in no list
— no height, no gap, their box their own size past their list's far end, outside its panel, so drawn
nowhere and found nowhere — and their columns close up on the bar's side (§230). The columns stand flush
with the bar's side (bottom, side bars: bottoms level; top bar: tops level); at rest an empty column
outside the ones with widgets has no width, between them it keeps its width; arranged every column keeps
its width, the outer ones hanging off what is centred. Height: each list as tall as its lines up to the
room (`Reach`, `ListMost`, `RoomRows`), Fill lines sharing what is left, the lines past it hidden whole
from the list's end with the warning (§185, §192). The open folder calls it through one door,
`FolderFlyout.Layout(island, pending, natural)`, for:

- **rest** — `pending.AtRest`: new lines in no list (so the commit that puts them in, to be drawn, moves
  nothing), lifted lines at their places;
- **the lines giving way** while a carry aims (`ShowArranged`: `Pending(aimed)`);
- **reading a landing** among the lines left (`Between`: the folder with the carried ones in no list).

**One hit test.** `FolderFlyout.Aim(point)` is where carried lines would land, for every carry: a slot
the pointer is over (half the gap either side its too, `FolderPlan.SlotAt(x, slack)`) is a list of its
own there; over the columns — their panels, the gaps, the room over and under them — a gap of the list
nearest (`Between`, `FolderDrag.Gap`: one line lifted from its place reads its own list by its leading
edge; new lines, or several, read the stack's middle against the lines' middles in the folder without
them); anywhere else nowhere. A landing shows where letting go moves something (`Lands`, which asks
`FolderDrag.Moves`, which is the move itself on a copy). A press-drag's moves, a carry with no button
(`Carry`, `LandCarry`), a drag handed over from rest (`HandOver`) and a layout under a carry
(`FolderChanged`) all aim there; before, the last three each had their own reading and two of them read a
slot as a gap of the nearest column.

**One commit.** Every landing is `Folders.MoveGroup` (the dock's `PlaceInFolder`): a drop, a click
putting a carry down, Ctrl+arrow; one line is a group of one (`Folders.Move` is `MoveGroup`). Lines that
come in are put in where they make no column (a widget added: the end of the last list; a paste: the end
of the first; a copy: beside its original) and carried at once (`Dock.CarryInto`: `FolderFlyout.Expect`
before the commit, so its layout leaves them out, then `Carry`); let go over no place they land at their
home — where the edit bar adds, for an add or a paste (a picked slot: a column there, made only then) —
through the same move. Escape or a right click takes them out again (`DropFollow`), and a cancelled add
into a picked slot leaves no empty columns behind any more. A cut line comes back by a paste.

Two more places counted what is not laid out. An outer empty column's width button is centred on what
shows of it (`WithSlots`), and "empty" was read from which lines it holds (`CardList`): a line come in
made its column not empty and its button jumped. It reads the layout now (no card in the column). And
while lines gave way, every column's button took its place across from the plan they give way to,
which is not slotted, so an outer column's button jumped off what shows of it; it keeps its place
across and goes up or down with its column's end (`AddAt`).

**Deleted as duplicates.** `FolderFlyout.Ghost` (both), `GhostFor`, `AimGroup`, `Planned`,
`CarriedSpan`, `InList`; `FolderDrag.Closed`, `ClosedGroup`, `Unclosed`, `GroupGhost`, `MovedGroup`
(one `Moved` for one line or several); the body of `Folders.Move`; the three 13-argument `Build` calls
(now `Layout`); the slot loop of `FolderFlyout.SlotAt` (now `FolderPlan.SlotAt` with its slack); the
dock's `FollowInFolder` and the three ways add, paste and copy committed and carried (now `CarryInto`).
`FolderFlyout.Group.cs` is `FolderFlyout.Pending.cs`. Not merged, on purpose: the band click picking a
column or a slot (`ListAt`, `SlotAt` without slack: a click picks room, it lands nothing),
`PassesThrough`, the slots' and guide lines' pass on top of the plan (`WithSlots`, `Guides`: they need
the screen the folder stands on), and the drag's motion (`Raise`, `Settle`, `Glide`). Nothing in the
config changes.

Tests: `FolderPendingTests` — `AWidgetAddedAndCarriedLeavesEveryColumnWhereItStands` (the person's two
folders, bottom, top, left and right bars at 150 %: every line where it stood through the commit, the
carry and the aim; let go away, it lands at home as a `Place`; failed before with the column of widgets
644 px off on a bottom bar), `ADropAPasteAndAnAddToOnePlaceAreLaidOutAlike` (a drop, an add and a paste to
a gap and to a slot are laid out as the folder after the move, at rest and arranged, every bar),
`LinesComeInAreLaidOutNowhere`, `EmptyColumnsAreSpacersAndSlotsCarryThemOn`, and the pictures
`folder-model-<rest|add|drag|drop>.png` (bottom bar, dark, 150 %). Tests of the removed duplicates now
test the one rule (`FolderModelTests.ALineMovesExceptJustAboveOrBelowItself`,
`FolderGroupMoveTests.AGroupDragReadsItsPlaceAmongTheLinesLeft`, `FolderDragTests`, `FolderSlotTests`).
By hand: open the folder with empty columns either side in edit mode, "Add a widget", pick one: nothing
moves; the widget is on the pointer; a click in a column puts it there; Escape: nothing added, nothing
moved.

## 245. A face is as wide as what it shows now (2026-10-19)

The person: *"yes, size all faces to their current content"*. Every face on the bar takes the width
what it shows **now** needs, and the button's ends (`WidgetShapes.Folder`: 2 × max(edge, 6 px)) — no
longer the room of the widest it could ever read. The bar may move when a value changes; that is
accepted. **This supersedes, for a folder's faces, §12.2's "a widget's size follows its settings,
never its state" and §230's "measured from its settings and templates, never from what it reads"**
(and the stable rooms §96, §97, §98, §99, §116, §127, §205 and §210 kept). Kinds that are not faces
keep §12.2.

**How.** The bar measures a folder with the folder itself (`ShapeContext.Island`, set by
`CellIsland.Content`), and each face's `Measure` reads what its `Paint` draws from the same place
(`FaceContext.Folder`): one answer for the cell and the drawing. `FolderIsland.Parts`, `FaceSizes` and
`FaceBoxes` take the folder; without one (Settings' picture) a face measures what it paints with
none. Figures are tabular (`TextLine` sets DirectWrite's `tnum` on every line, and measures through
`TextLine.Template`, which reads every digit as an eight): a reading of the same shape is one width,
so a clock's seconds, a running timer and a price moving through the day never move the bar — only a
figure more or fewer, AM to PM, a sign, a new day or another word does.

**Re-layout.** Nothing new: `CellIsland.Redraw` already compares what each cell wants with what the
bar was told (`Moved`) and asks for a rebuild instead of painting in place where it differs. The
dock's tick (`Dock.FaceTicks`, `MinuteChanged`, the islands' `Tick` and `Refresh`) gathers every
island's answer and builds the bar once for all of them (`RequestRebuild` on the `REBUILD` timer, or
one `Rebuild` after the loop). The scene glides every block that moved or changed size from where it
was (`Scene`: `Offset` and `Size` key frames over `MoveMs`) where animations are on, and snaps where
they are off.

| Face | Across a bar it is as wide as | Its most, cut past it |
|---|---|---|
| Clock | the line it reads: the time, then "· label" and a running countdown's figures | — |
| Calendar (text) | today's date as it reads | — |
| Time and date | the wider of the time and the date read now (two lines), or both on one | — |
| Weather | the pieces as they read: glyph, temperature, today's high and low, the days, the words | each piece's widest box (`WeatherRow`) |
| Air quality | the fullest form of its level that fits | the widest level's room (`AirFaceDrawing.Room`) |
| Timer, focus, stopwatch | what it says: "5m" at rest, "04:59" running, a name before it | — |
| Battery | the charge it shows ("7%", "100%"); the bolt's square before a reading | — |
| Processor, GPU, memory, disk | the figure, never under two figures ("88%") once known; the dash its own width | — |
| Network activity | the rate, never under "8.8M" once known (a rate crosses units every second) | — |
| Stock | the symbol, the price and the change as they read ("+" is wider than "-") | — |
| News | the headline, or why there is none | the headline's room (`HeadlineTemplate`) |
| Now playing | the title and artist (one line, or the wider of two) or "Nothing playing", and the art | the entry's three cells of words (`MediaIsland.Column`) |
| Drive | the icon, its name as it reads in the most room, and the capacity bar's least | two cells; "Set up" keeps the two |
| Desktops, layouts | the glyph and the name | the room of "Desktop 88" (`Switchers.NameRoom`) |
| Keyboard | the codes in use ("ENG" over "CH"), never under a square | — |
| Meeting | its words fitted into its width's room, and Join where the meeting has a link | the width option's room |
| Removable, hotspot, mail, bell | the glyph's square and the count it shows now on its corner | — |
| Tides (§236) | the arrow and what it says ("High 14:32", the height, how soon) | its Show option's widest |
| Sports (§239) | the score, the kick-off or "Final", and the red dot while it is on | the league's widest (`Room`) |
| Earthquakes (§240) | the dot and the fullest form that fits, a quiet day's words, or the dash | the widest reading's room |
| Currency (§242) | "100 EUR =" and the worth as it reads ("94.12 CHF"), or the worth alone | the pair's widest worth (`Currencies.WorthTemplate`) |

Down a bar on its side a face is rows over each other and its length is its rows; those keep their
settings' room as before. The performance faces' floor is a decision against thrash: a processor's
load read every second crosses 9 % often, and a one-figure reading would move the bar each time.

**Alignment** (§201) acts only where there is room to act in: one face of words in a folder somebody
set wider than it reads (a chosen width), or in a cell's least. There its words stand at the
button's start, middle or end as before (`FolderIsland.FaceBoxes`); nobody's pick is the middle.

Tests: `FaceWidthTests` — every face's button is its faces measured with the folder and its two ends,
its ink filling the face (`EveryFaceIsWhatItShowsAndTheButtonsEnds`); a short and a long reading
differ by their words (`AShortReadingAndALongOneDifferByTheirWords`: a 12-hour clock, a share, the air,
a desktop's name, a title); a 12-hour clock going from 9:59 to 10:00 asks for the bar again, the new
layout's clock is wider and the folder after it moved by as much, and 10:01 asks for nothing
(`AFaceThatReadsWiderLaysTheBarOutAgain`); a clock with seconds ticks two minutes, and its narrowest
and widest figures, in one width, never asking for the bar (`AClockWithSecondsTicksInOneWidth`); the
air quality as wide as its level; alignment in a folder set wider. The "one width whatever it reads"
tests of the battery, timer, stock, news, now playing, performance, drive, desktops, layouts,
keyboard and weather faces now hold "as wide as what it shows, up to its most" and "one width while
it reads the same shape". `face-content-150.png` draws the bar with every face at a short and a long
reading. By hand: watch a clock with seconds (no wobble), start a timer in a clock's folder (the bar
makes room), switch between a short and a long desktop name, and play a track with a short title.

## 246. Submenus open on a click only; a line of text is a level of its own (2026-10-19)

The person: *"the sub menus should [not] open on hover, only when i click them deliberatly. the text
box inputs / configuration items should have an additional level and should show the text box entry
on that additional level. it should autofocus when opened. amount you own should also get an
additional level"*.

**A submenu opens by a click or the keys, never by the pointer resting.** Karpo's menus are all
`Flyout`s, so this is one change there. The pointer over a row only lights it; a click, or Right or
Enter on the keys, opens its submenu; the open one stays open wherever the pointer goes after; a
second click on its row shuts it, the menu over it staying (§219); another parent's click opens its
own in place; a press outside every level closes the menu (`LightDismiss`). Gone with it: the
submenu timer and Windows' menu delay (`SPI_GETMENUSHOWDELAY`), the pending row, and §219's "a
submenu the pointer opened within 400 ms of the press is kept by it" (`MenuKeeps.ParentClick`,
`HoverGraceMs`) with the "held shut" row resting could not reopen: there is nothing to reconcile a
click with any more (`Flyout.ParentClicked` opens or shuts).

**A line of text** — a clock's label, a timer's, an alarm's and a focus session's name, a heading's
words, a pin's name and path, a share's name on the bar, a list's name, the currency amount and a
stock's **amount you own** — is a row "Name  value ›", the words it holds at its end, cut short as
every row's value is (`OptionMenu.ValueOf`), nothing where it holds none. It opens a level of its
field alone: Windows 11's text box across the row, its placeholder saying what to type (§240 to
§245 had the box on 55 % of the row beside the name; that variant, `FieldShare`, is gone: every
field fills its row). The level, opened by a click or the keys, gives its field the keys at once,
its words selected and the caret at their end (`FocusFieldLevel`, §230's for searches, now every
field's). **Enter** keeps what was typed and shuts the level, the keys back on its row, and the menu
is shown again with the row saying what is kept; **Escape** puts the setting's words back and shuts
it, keeping nothing; the next Escape is the menu's. A feed's address (a search that only proves what
is entered) shuts once its feed is proved. Searches that find as they are typed in (a zone, a place,
a share) keep their level open for their results, as before. A stock's amount still keeps only a
number (§228): "ten" changes nothing.

Tests: `MenuKeepsTests.ASubmenuOpensOnlyByAClick` (the pointer resting on a parent past any delay,
its timers handed to it, opens nothing; a click opens, the pointer over another parent and a plain
row leaves it open, a second click shuts it, another parent's click switches) and
`TheKeysGoALevelAtATime` as before. `MenuFieldTests.ATextLevelOpensWithItsFieldTakingTheKeys`
(focused and selected on a click and on Right; Delete and Home are the field's; Escape reverts and
shuts), `EnterKeepsWhatWasTypedAndShutsTheLevel`, `TheAmountYouOwnIsALevelOfItsOwn` ("ten" keeps
nothing, "2,5" keeps 2.5 and the row says "2.5"); `OptionMenuTests` and `OptionFieldsTests` hold the
rows' shape. Pictures: `menu-field-text-rest-*`, `menu-field-text-open-*` and `menu-field-text-*` (a
timer's name's row, its level just opened, typed in). By hand: rest on the rows of a widget's menu
(nothing opens), click through two levels and move the pointer about (they stay), rename a timer by
its level with Enter and with Escape.

## 247. Guide lines through the bars; no column picked; a "+" on every column again (2026-10-19)

The person: *"the folder columns lines end at the taskbars at the moment but i want them to continue
all the way through. a column should not be selectable in general. add back the add button per
column"*. This supersedes §217's "Picking a column" and its removal of the columns' "+", and §221's
"A slot is picked as a column is"; it builds on §244's one model (`FolderPending`, `Aim`,
`Folders.MoveGroup`, `Dock.CarryInto`) and adds no path of its own.

**Through the bars.** Arranged, the folder's window reaches the edges of its display, its bars too
(`FlyoutHost.Spread` is the display's rectangle now, not a flag; the dock hands `Monitor.Bounds` to
`FolderFlyout.Show`, `display:`), and the guide lines run down the whole window (`Guides` over
`FolderFlyout.Window`), so every line goes from the top of the screen to its bottom, over a bottom or
top bar and through it; they still stop short of the folder's own edit bar. What can be taken hold of
stays off the bars: `Visible` — what the buttons are kept in, the slots reach and a carry aims in — is
the window cut to the work area and to the bar's inner side (the anchor's). Over the bar the window
lets the pointer through (`PassesThrough`: the room round the lists counts only inside `Visible`), so
the bar under it keeps its press, and stays locked as before (§212). The bars are lifted to the top at
every build; the dock puts them back just under the folder each time (`ShowFolderDeck`,
`EditStack.KeepUnder`), so the lines stay in sight over the dimmed bars.

**No column is picked.** A click on a column's room, an empty one's or a slot's, picks nothing: it is
the room's press and release (the selection rectangle, a click clearing the selection as elsewhere).
Gone: `FolderFlyout.PickedColumn`, `PickedSlot`, `PickedColumnShown`, the picked column's ring
(`columnVisual`, `columnRing`), `FolderPlan.SlotRoom`, `InSlotRoom` (a slot's room level with the folder
took the pointer only to be picked; it goes through to the dim again), the band release's picking, and
the dock's re-picking after a slot's width or an add into a slot (`FolderWidthChosen`, `AddChosen`).
`ChosenColumn` is the selected line's column alone.

**A "+" per column.** Every list and every slot has its "+" again (`FolderAddKind.Add`), the round
accent button the width button is, Segoe Fluent Icons' Add on it, first in the column's row: "+", width,
then the warning where the list hides lines, the group centred on the column — over it on a bottom or
side bar, under it on a top bar; a slot's and an empty column's pair level with each other
(`WithSlots`). A click is `FolderFlyoutAction.Add` with its place — a list's end away from the bar as
the edit bar's add reads it (`AddPlace(list)`, `AddPlaceIn`), a slot's own `FolderPlace.Slot` — and the
dock opens the add list there, away from the bar (`AddInFolder` with the bar's edge), the button held
pressed until the list goes (`sizing`, `MenuClosed` from `EndAdding`, or at once where no list opened).
What is picked comes in carried exactly as from the edit bar (`AddChosen` → `CarryInto`): in where it
makes no column, laid out nowhere, the landing following the pointer, a click putting it down where it
shows; over no place it lands at its home, which is now that column's place — a slot's a column there,
made only then. The folder's edit bar's "Add a widget" is unchanged: the selected line's column, else
the first with room. No new words: the "+" has no tooltip, as the width button has none.

Tests: `FolderSlotTests.TheGuideLinesRunThroughTheBars` (bottom, top, left, right: the window is the
display's, every line reaches its top and bottom, through a bottom or top bar, every button in the work
area, a press on the bar goes through); `FolderColumnsTests.AClickOnAColumnsRoomPicksNothing`,
`EveryColumnsPlusOpensTheAddListAndWhatIsPickedLandsThere` (a list with widgets, an empty one, a slot
on either side: the add list asked for away from the bar at the "+", the carried pick let go over no
place lands in that column), `EveryColumnAndSlotHasItsPlusAndItsWidthAndNoRemove`;
`FolderEditClickTests.TheColumnsHaveTheirPlusAndTheFolderNoCross`; the buttons' order and centring in
`FolderAddTests`, `ListFolderTests`, `FolderHiddenTests`, `FolderSlotTests`. Pictures:
`editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<dark|light>-150.png` now show the folder's window laid over the dimmed
bars (`WindowShots.SaveTogether(over:)`), the lines through the taskbar and each column's "+" and width;
`folder-slots-*` lose their picked slot. By hand: in edit mode open a folder: the guide lines run
