through the taskbar; click a column's empty room (nothing is ringed); click a column's "+" (the add
list above it), pick a widget (on the pointer), click away from the folder (it lands in that column);
a slot's "+" the same (a column there); the edit bar's "Add a widget" still lands in the first column
with room.

## 248. The power mode at every height, down to one row (2026-10-19)

The person: *"power mode does not currently adapt nicely to small sizes, it should work all the way
down to one cell height."* The line (`PowerModePage` in a `QuickPageTile`) was one drawing — the
heading, what it is about and the three modes as 40-DIP rows — and a line shorter than that showed
the rows that fit: at one row its heading and nothing to click; at two and three, the heading and the
caption. Now the page fits itself to the height it is given (`QuickPage.Fits`, `PageLayout.Room`), the
fullest of four forms that fits, every mode a click away in each, nothing scrolling:

| Form | What it shows | Where (100 % text, medium list) |
|---|---|---|
| Whole | the heading, what it is about, the modes as rows, a refusal under them — as before | its own height, five rows and up |
| Listed | the modes as rows of 32 to 40 DIP (at large text never under a line of its words and 8 DIP, `RowLeast`), under the heading where it fits; a refusal, then what it is about, where they fit too | three and four rows |
| Strip | the mode's gauge in the list's icon column, "Power mode" and the mode in force at the row's end; under them the three modes as a segmented control from gutter to gutter, worded where all three words fit | two rows |
| One | the gauge and the mode in force (`ListTiers.Row`: the control wins, the name takes what is left), the segmented control of the three gauges at the row's end, in the row's middle band | one row |

A refusal takes the mode's place on the short forms, in the critical colour; a plan with no modes is
the heading over why where both fit, else the gauge and why on one row. Where "Power mode" has no room
on the strip's row (225 % text), the mode stands after the gauge rather than at the end of an empty
row. At 225 % text one and two rows are one height, so both are the one-row form; the strip comes at
three rows and the rows at five.

**The segmented control** (`QuickSettings\Controls\Segmented.cs`) is the Windows Community Toolkit's
Segmented, as Windows' own apps use it for a choice of a few: a track (`ControlAltFill` inside the
control stroke), the chosen segment raised on it (the control fill and stroke) with the toolkit's
16 × 3 DIP accent pill under its content, the others subtle and lit under the pointer. A segment is
its glyph, its word beside it where every segment's fits; a segment of its glyph alone names itself
in the tooltip (`QuickPageTile.CardTip`). Each is a control of the page: a click, or Up and Down to
ring one and Enter, sets its mode as a row does.

**Measuring without moving the keys.** A page that fits itself is measured whole in a layout of its
own (`QuickPageTile.Whole`): the folder measures its lines whenever it likes, and building the whole
page into the line's own layout would take the keyboard off a segment the person had rung. The line's
`ScrollHeight` is the height it was given, so it never scrolls. Every other quick page is unchanged:
its room is ignored and it lays out and scrolls as before.

The bar: the power mode is a line of a list and nothing else (`QuickPageTile.PaintCell` refuses a bar),
so there is no bar face to fit; the battery face's menu keeps its power mode submenu.

Tests: `PowerModeFormsTests` — at one row to eight and its own height, at 100, 150 and 200 %, 100,
150 and 225 % text, every list width, a mode in force, a refused one and a plan with none: everything
it places between the gutters and inside the line, nothing on anything else (the segments on their
track), one-line words never cut through, all three modes a control, one row the one-row form, a taller
line never a smaller form, nothing scrolling, and on the usual width one row says the mode whole
(`TheLineIsWorkedAtEveryHeight`); at one row a click on a segment asks for its mode, marked and said at
once, the one in force asks nothing, a segment names itself, and Up and Enter set one
(`OneRowSetsTheMode`). Sheets: `power-mode-line-150-dark.png`, `-light.png` and `-text225.png`, its
own height and one to six rows, in each state and on a narrow list. By hand: set a power mode line to
one row and to two, and pick each mode by a click and by the keys.

## 249. An icon on every settings row and every choice; the icon picker, Windows' own (2026-10-19)

The person: *"add icons to all of the submenus / subitems, like the different styles or so"* and
*"improve the icon picker"*.

**Every row, every choice.** A widget's and a face's settings rows each carry their icon with them:
`OptionRow.Glyph`, a choice's `OptionRow.ChoiceGlyphs` (a choice past them has the row's), a group's
row `GroupGlyph` on its first row. They are set where the row is made (`OptionRows`, `OptionFields`,
`OptionPickers`, `OptionHolidays`), a face's option with the option (`FaceOption.Glyph`,
`ChoiceGlyphs`), a widget's style with the style (`WidgetStyle.Glyph`, `ReadingGlyph`), and the glyphs
themselves are named by what they stand for in one place (`Karpo.Core\OptionGlyphs.cs`), so one thing
has one icon in every menu. `OptionMenu` and `MenuPickers` only hand them on (`OptionMenu.IconOf`): a
toggle, a stepper, a line of text's row and a search's (each opening its field's level, §246), a
group's row, a picker's row and every choice in a submenu, a time's and a length's parts, "Add a
face"'s groups and faces, a line's height and its modes. The only rows without one are headings,
greyed rows that only say something, and a field filling its own level (the row it opens from has
the icon).

They are Segoe Fluent Icons glyphs, picked off a sheet of every glyph the font has on Windows 11, and
Windows 11 Settings' own where it has the same row. Where a glyph is one of Explorer's commands it
draws as Explorer draws it (§178, `ExplorerIcons`: Rename, New, Delete, Refresh, Personalize); none is
used whose Explorer picture means something else (View's is a grid, Properties' a wrench).

**The icon picker** (`MenuPickers`, `Flyout.Pickers.cs`, `Flyout.Fields.cs`), as Windows' emoji and
icon pickers are. §224 to §245 had 48 icons a row tall in four groups and the rest of the gallery
only as search results under them.

- **The whole gallery**, each glyph once (`MenuIcons`: Settings' `IconSearch` gallery under six
  headings — Files, Places, Media, People and time, Devices, Tools and symbols; the last two are new
  words in every language), "Default" the first tile before them (the folder's glyph, or for a pin the
  app's own icon's, ECAA). Each tile is a 40 DIP cell with a 20 DIP glyph, seven to a line in a
  settings menu, lit under the pointer, the one in force ringed in the accent, its name in a tooltip
  as the pointer or the keys rest on it (`Flyout.Tips`, any level now).
- **The search field at the top** (`FlyoutField.Filters`), which has the keys as the picker opens and
  stays there while the tiles scroll under it (the level's pinned row: its visuals in a container over
  the clipped rows, its fill moved with the scroll so the pointer and the caret find it). Typing
  leaves the tiles whose words hold it (`IconSearch.Matches`: every gallery id of the glyph, in
  Karpo's language and English) in place of the grid, without headings, "No icon of that name." where
  none do. It keeps nothing: Enter or Down go on to the first tile, Enter picks it; typing or
  Backspace on a tile go on in the field; a tile's Escape shuts the picker.
- **One height** (`Flyout.PickerHeightDip`, 400 DIP), whatever a search leaves, and it opens on the
  icon in force, scrolled into the middle (`ChosenTileInView`).
- Fixed in passing: the gallery had a pie chart the font hasn't (E9D4, now EB05), "health" drawn as an
  empty circle (EA3A, now E95E), "leaf" the bank's glyph (now E8BE) and "construction" Manage's (now
  E822).

Tests: `MenuIconsTests` — every row of every widget's and face's settings, every choice and every
group's row has a glyph, with every list listed, holidays on in a country with regions, a notebook
to write in and a pin to a folder (`EveryRowAndChoiceHasAnIcon`); a widget's styles and readings
each their own (`EachStyleHasAnIconOfItsOwn`); every row of the menus made of them, however deep, has
its icon (`EveryRowOfAMenuHasItsIcon`); every glyph is in SegoeIcons.ttf with an outline, read off its
cmap and loca (`EveryGlyphIsInTheFont`); the picker is its field, "Default" and the whole gallery
under its six headings (`ThePickerIsTheWholeGalleryUnderItsHeadings`); and on a real menu the field
has the keys as the picker opens, the icon in force is ringed and in view, a search leaves its
matches at one height, Down, Enter and Backspace go between the field and the tiles, a pick sets it
and keeps nothing as words (`ThePickerAndTheMenusOnARealMenu`). `MenuPickersTests` and
`OptionRowsTests` follow the new picker. Pictures: `menu-icons-<calendar|performance|performance-style|clock|weather|volume|faces>-<look>.png`,
`menu-icons-picker[-search]-<look>.png`, `menu-pickers-*-<look>.png`, at 150 %. By hand: open a
folder's icon, type, arrow into the tiles and hover one for its name; check a right-to-left language's
alignment icons.

## 250. No card behind the widgets by default; a separator is a thin line, its style one to choose (2026-10-19) — no bar separator since §511 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"the taskbar widgets background should be transparent as a default. the divider on the
taskbar should be a thin line and not just a space as a default. style should be configurable"*.

**Cards** (§214 again, which §218 had reverted):

- **The automatic look draws no card**: `Scene.Automatic` leaves `CardFill` and `CardStroke` empty in the
  dark and the light look, so the widgets stand on the bar's own material. The islands look's gaps,
  groups and highlight corners stay as they were.
- **Still a setting**: Appearance → Custom colors → "Widget cards" and "Card outline". A colour chosen
  there draws the card in that mode; "Reset all" takes it away. Nothing is written or migrated: a file
  with a card colour keeps its cards (the person's own has a dark-mode card, `#B3000000`, so its dark bar
  keeps them until Widget cards is set back to Automatic); a file with none is transparent at once.
- **High contrast keeps its cards**: Windows' window colour with its text colour round it.
- **A card chosen or taken back is a build** (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`, `CardsShown`): with no card drawn
  there is no brush to recolour; a chosen card in another colour is still recoloured in place.
- **Edit mode**: a part whose card has no fill counts as uncarded, so it gets the edit block's wash
  instead of standing there with nothing behind it.

**Separators**:

- **Shape** (`LineStyle.Shape`, `SeparatorShape`): `line` (the default), `dot`, `space` (nothing drawn,
  only the room and the split into two groups, which was the default until now). One style for every
  separator, as before (§54, "a shared configuration page").
- **Line**: Automatic's hairline (one device pixel, two at 200 %), half the highlight's height, centred,
  in the strong separator colour (`SeparatorInk`). That colour stays the strong one rather than Windows'
  quiet divider stroke: at one pixel the quiet one was barely there (`SeparatorInk`'s note).
- **Dot**: `SeparatorInk.DotDip` (4 DIPs) round, whole pixels (4 / 6 / 8 px at 100 / 150 / 200 %), as long
  along the bar as across, in the middle of the gap, in the same colour; the line width does not apply.
- **Where it is set**: Appearance → Separators → "Style" (a box: Line, Dot, Space only; it replaces the
  Line switch; "Line width" is enabled for a line, "Line color" for a line or a dot), and the separator's
  own menu, "Style" with the same three choices before its colour (`OptionPickers.Shape`, written as
  Appearance writes it). A folder's divider is no line and has no Style.
- **The file**: `"separators": { "shape": "line" | "dot" | "space", "width", "space" }`, still left out
  while it is the default. A file from before the shapes said `"line": true | false`; true reads as a
  line, false as space (somebody chose that), and a file with neither, the common case (the person's
  included), gets the new default line. `"line"` is read and never written again. An unknown shape from
  a newer build reads as the old `line` value, else a line. No reset.
- **A dock** still draws no separator (§81): the shape is space there whatever Appearance says.

Strings: `settings.appearance.separatorStyle.dot` and `.space` in all 30 languages; the box reuses
"Style" (`settings.widget.style.header`) and "Line" (`settings.appearance.line.header`).

Tests: `BarColorThemeTests` (`WithNothingChosenTheWidgetsWearNoCard` dark and light,
`HighContrastStillDrawsItsCards`, `ACardColourInTheFileIsKept`, `ACardChosenOrTakenBackIsBuiltAgain`);
`SeparatorLineTests` (`ByDefaultASeparatorIsAThinLine`, `ADotIsItsSideAlongTheBarAndSpaceIsNothing`,
`AFileFromBeforeTheShapesReadsAsItSaid`); `MenuPickersTests.ASeparatorsStyleIsWrittenAsTheAppearancePageWritesIt`;
`LineRowsTests` and `SettingsIndexTests` (Style in place of Line). `AnAppGroupWearsOneCardAndLightsEachButtonOnIt`
and `RecolouringShowsWhatABuildInTheColorsShows` now choose their cards. Pictures:
`cards-divider-<before|after>-<dark|light>-150.png` (the bar of the config at `KARPO_BAR_CONFIG`, else a
new bar with two separators) and `separator-style-<line|dot|none|spaced|thick>-…`. By hand: Settings →
Appearance → Separators → Style; a separator's menu in edit mode → Style; Custom colors → Widget cards
to bring cards back (and back to Automatic to clear the dark card on the person's bar).

## 251. What this PC hasn't got is shown greyed, never a message or a gap (2026-10-19)

The person: *"if there is no brightness to set it should still show the slider just greyed out.
this should generally be the case for configuration options that are not available, you should
still show its contents just greyed out. do the same for the battery widget as well, show contents
as if there is a battery available but just show them greyed out."*

**One way, every widget.** A widget whose thing this PC hasn't got answers
`CellIsland.UnavailableOn(screen)` with why (null where it has it); a folder's face answers
`IFaceDrawing.Unavailable`. The widget then draws its own layout with a stand-in reading, and the
bar and the folder do the rest: the drawing is greyed (`Unavailable.Paint`, from `PaintBar`,
`PaintOn` and the folder's faces), nothing takes a press, a drag, the wheel or a click (`PressOn`,
`WheelOn`, `TargetOn`, `HoverOn`, the bar's `IslandClick`, the folder's click; a line does not
light as a whole), and the why is the tooltip over all of it, on the bar too where the entry shows
none otherwise ("Brightness isn't available on this PC" and the reason under it,
`CellIsland.NotOnThisPc`; §367: in a folder only, the bar shows none — a screen reader still hears it). Greying is one colour matrix over the recorded drawing: of each pixel
only how far it stands out from the backdrop is kept, in Windows' disabled ink
(`IslandInk.Disabled`), so the text comes out exactly as disabled text, a track quieter, the accent a
grey between, nothing with a hue. No widget recolours itself for it.

**What each shows.**

| Widget | Where it hasn't got it | Shown greyed | Replaced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brightness, bar and line | no display it sets has a brightness (or, set to its own screen, that one) | the slider at 50, the level "50" | the sun alone with no track; "No brightness to set" |
| Battery line | no battery, or a charge Windows can't read | "100%", fully charged, plugged in, the full bar | the bolt and "No battery" / "This PC runs on power from the wall." |
| Battery face | the same | the charging glyph and "100%", as wide as a full one | the bolt alone in a square |
| One-button switches (airplane mode, night light, energy saver, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound and microphone, spatial sound, rotation lock, …), bar and line | `IQuickSwitch.Available` false | off: the glyph, the name, the line's switch off | glyph and words in the disabled ink, "Not available" for the switch; rotation lock where the screen does not turn took itself off the bar (`IQuickSwitch.Offered`, gone) |
| Volume, bar | no output device | the slider at 50 | the muted speaker and an empty track |
| Volume line (sound) | no output device | its row: the speaker, the slider at 50, "50" | "No output device" |
| Bluetooth face | no radio | the rune | the rune dimmed |
| Mobile hotspot face | no adapter that can host one | the antenna | the antenna dimmed |

**Menus keep what doesn't apply, greyed.** The battery face's power modes stay under their heading
where the plan offers none, every one greyed and none ticked; an output or input line's menu keeps
its heading over a greyed "No output device". Rows that were already greyed rather than left out
stay so (energy saver without one, the radios without an adapter, mute without a microphone).

**Left as they are.** What a new layout or a preset holds on this PC (`PresetMachine`: no battery
preset or battery line on a desktop, no rotation lock where the screen does not turn) — that is what
a new install contains, not something placed. The device lists (outputs, microphones) still say
there is none: a device made up to list is one somebody could look for. Windows' own buttons that
Windows hides without a pen or a touchscreen, the quick-settings pages' notices (Wi-Fi with no
adapter, Bluetooth with no radio, the hotspot's reasons, the power mode page with no modes), a sleep
or hibernate button Windows' power menu does not offer (already greyed, its click nothing, its
tooltip why), and the performance figures that could not be read ("–") are unchanged.

Tests: `UnavailableWidgetTests` (the text's ink goes to the disabled ink exactly and the accent to a
grey; the brightness, the battery line and a switch on the bar and as lines draw the same ink box as
the thing at the stand-in reading, every pixel grey and no stronger than the disabled ink; nothing
takes a press, the wheel or a target; the tooltip is why), `SoundPartsTests.AVolumeRowWithNoOutputIsGreyed`
(and the output's menu's greyed row), `BatteryPowerPresetTests.TheFacesMenuGreysThePowerModesWhereThereAreNone`
and `TheBatteryFaceIsAsWideAsTheChargeItShows` (no battery: as wide as 100 %, its tooltip why),
`BrightnessWidgetTests` and `HotspotPresetTests` as changed. Pictures:
`unavailable-{brightness,battery,switch}-150-{dark,light}.png` (available left, not right),
`battery-face-*` and `battery-preset-*` ("On the wall"). By hand, on the desktop: the brightness and
battery widgets placed on a bar and in a folder, hovered (the tooltip), clicked and wheeled (nothing).

## 252. No edit bar for an open folder; its face on the bar closes it, in the accent (2026-10-19)

The person: *"in the folder edit mode the top edit bar should be removed, the whole folder face should
become the close button and should have the primary color."* This supersedes §217's "A folder's own
edit bar" (its "Add a widget" and "Close folder") and §247's "The folder's edit bar's 'Add a widget'
is unchanged".

**No edit bar at the top.** While a folder is open arranged nothing stands at the top of the display:
the display's edit bar still stands aside, its place kept (§190, `EditDeckPlan.Shows`), and the
folder's own is gone — `EditDeck`'s `folder:` mode, `Folder`, `FolderButtons`, `EditDeckPlan.OnFolder`,
`ActionAt`'s `folder:`, the dock's `folderDeck`, `ShowFolderDeck` and its message routing. The guide
lines run to the top of the screen again: `FolderFlyout.Guides` has no rooms to stop short of any more
(`avoid` gone). What `ShowFolderDeck` also did — keep the display's bars just under the folder's
window, so its lines run through them (§247) — is `KeepBarsUnderFolder`.

**Adding.** A column's "+" adds into that column (§247), Ctrl+V pastes. "Add" in a line's
menu, or in the folder's own menu, opens the same add list where that column's "+" opens it, away
from the bar (`Dock.FolderAdd`, `FolderFlyout.PlusOnScreen`): the line's column, or for the folder's
menu the selected line's, else the first with room (`AddPlace`). No key opened the folder's edit
bar's add, so none needed routing.

**The face is the close button.** The folder's button on the bar — the widget that opened it — stands
over the bar's dim (`Scene.CloseFace`, over `scrim`), so it alone is not dimmed, filled as an accent
button over its whole edit block (`GrabRect`, the edit radius): AccentFillColorDefault (`FlyoutTheme.Accent`,
AccentLight2 on dark, AccentDark1 on light, Highlight in high contrast), and under the pointer and
pressed its secondary and tertiary fills (90 % and 80 %) laid over the bar's ground as one opaque
colour (`Scene.Over`), so the dimmed face under it never shows through. Cards or none, it is the
same: it is drawn over the card, not into it. The face is drawn again on the fill in the ink that
reads there (`Scene.OnAccent`): TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary is the other mode's text — black on
dark's light accent, white on light's dark one — so its cells are the island's own in the other
mode's look (high contrast: the highlight's text on the highlight), live as the face is (a second
style the island keeps and redraws, `CellIsland.kept`). Its badge reads the same way, inverted.

A press on the face presses it (`DockWindow.LockedPressed`, `EditClicks.OnLocked`), holding the
mouse; its release on it closes the folder by Escape's path (`EscapeTo(EditEscape.CloseFolder)`): the
bars come back un-dimmed, the display's edit bar with them, edit mode on. Released off it, or the
mouse lost, nothing. Every other press, drag, lasso and right click on the locked bars still does
nothing (§213), and of the keys only Escape (the folder closes) and Ctrl+V. Its tooltip "Close
folder" (the menu's words, `dock.widgetMenu.closeFolder`, no new ones) is the folder's own tip
(`FolderFlyout.FaceTip`), off the face's side away from the bar, over the folder after the usual
moment: the bar's tooltip stands in the bar's window, which the arranged folder's window covers.

Tests: `EditClickTests.ALockedBarTakesOnlyAPressOnTheFoldersFace` (only the face's part presses,
Escape still closes the folder, the press and release wired, no `folder: true` deck);
`EditedDisplay` with a folder (`editmode-folder-*`, `editbar-*-folder`): the face's part is the
close button, its fill the accent, a pixel of the face's room the accent undimmed in the picture,
hover and pressed three different opaque fills, the folder closed takes it and the dim away, the tip
says "Close folder" clear of the face; `FolderMenuTests` (the add list from a line's menu hangs from
its column's "+"). Gone: `EditDeckPlanTests.AFoldersEditBarAddsAndCloses`,
`EditDeckClickTests.AFoldersEditBarStandsWhereTheDisplaysDoesAndAsks`, the edit bar cut of
`TheGuideLinesMarkEveryEdge`. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `editmode-folder-<bottom|top>` — the
clock's face in the accent over the dimmed taskbar, its tip over the folder, nothing at the top. By
hand: in edit mode open a folder from its menu: nothing at the top, the folder's face on the bar in
the accent, readable in light and dark; hover it (lighter in light, darker in dark, "Close folder"),
press and drag off (nothing), click it (the folder closes, the bars and the edit bar come back);
click any other widget of the bar (nothing); Escape (closes it too); a line's menu "Add" (the add
list from that column's "+").

## 253. One markets widget: shares, currencies and coins (2026-10-19)

The person: *"the currency exchange is just merged into the stock widget but with no system. some
entries are for currency conversion while other are for the stock. rewrite this completely"*, then
*"i want to merge them so that there is only one stock and currency widget. crypto should be able to be
shown as well."* The stock widget and the currency converter (§242) are one widget, **Markets**
(`markets`, `ListKind.Markets`, `FolderFaces.MarketsId`), a line of a list and a folder's face. Its
**first setting is its type** — Stock, Currency or Crypto — and every other row belongs to that type
alone (`MarketRows.Of`). **This supersedes §242 and the stock's own widget**; their sections stay as
history.

**The record** (`MarketOptions`, `Karpo.Core\Markets.cs`; `"market"` in the file): `type`, then what
each type keeps — a share's `symbol`, `label` and `detail`; a rate's `from`, `to` and `amount`; a
coin's `coin` and `to`; and shared by all, `range`, `rangeYears`, `holding` and `style`. A record keeps
what another type set, so switching the type and back loses nothing, but no row of one type ever shows
on another (`MarketRowsTests.NoRowOfOneTypeShowsForAnother`).

| Type | Rows, in order |
|---|---|
| Stock | Type · Symbol (Yahoo search; a currency or coin listing refused, pointing to its type) · Label · Range (+ years) · Amount you own · Style |
| Currency | Type · From · To · Swap · Amount ("100 JPY = 0.59 CHF"; empty is 1) · Range (+ years) · Style |
| Crypto | Type · Coin (22 common coins first, then Yahoo's crypto search) · In (its currency, the dollar unless chosen) · Range (+ years) · Amount you own · Style |

A face's rows are the same but the holding (a face never says it), then where it stands. Every row
and every choice has its icon (§249; `MarketRows.KindGlyph`, `StyleGlyph`). **Style**:
*Price, change and chart* / *Price only* for a share and a coin; for a rate the same two and
*Converter* — the two fields with the swap between them (`MarketConverter`, the old tile, now a part of
the markets line) on a line, "100 EUR = 92.69 CHF" on a face. A share or a coin never reads the
converter style (`MarketOptions.StyleOf`).

**One data layer** (`Karpo.Dock\Markets`). One question, `MarketAsk(Kind, Name, To, Range, Years)`, keyed
`"stock:MSFT 5y"`, `"currency:EURCHF 1mo"`, `"crypto:BTC-USD 1d"`; one store (`MarketStore`: who
uses what, the refresh by range, stale after three refreshes past due, the busy back-off, one cache
file `markets.json`); one reading (`MarketReading.Of`) and one drawing for every type
(`MarketIsland` for the line, `MarketFaceDrawing` for the face). The sources, by type
(`MarketSources`): a share is Yahoo's chart endpoint by its symbol; a rate is Yahoo's pair, its
inverse, or through the dollar (two legs met point by point), then the ECB's reference rates
(`api.frankfurter.dev`, no key, 30 currencies, a working day a point); a coin is Yahoo's `XXX-YYY`,
or `XXX-USD` times the dollar in its currency (Yahoo has no ETH-CHF), then CoinGecko's keyless API
(price and up to a year of history; past a year the price alone). Each route that answered with a
chart is remembered. The first answer with a chart wins (`FirstCharted`); one without is the answer only
where none has a chart. Every request is a plain GET with Karpo's own agent and no cookies; a 401 or 403
stops the asking (`MarketGateException`), a 429 backs off (`MarketBusyException`).

**Numbers.** Shown in invariant figures ("81,917.38"); a typed amount reads with the region's marks.
A rate's decimals follow its size (`Currencies.RatePlaces`), a share's Yahoo's hint, a coin's the hint
from one up and below one at least as many as its first figures need (SHIB). Faces size to what they
show (§245): across a bar the words as they read now; down a bar on its side one size for every
ordinary price ("888.88"), a longer one (a coin's thousands) the size it fits at, never cut.

**Migration** (`LineMigrations.CarryMarkets`, recorded once as `markets` in `Config.Migrated`; no
reset). The old `stock` and `currency` lines and faces are read forever (`CellItem.OldStock`,
`OldCurrency`, `FolderFace.OldStock`) and carried in place — same id, same place, same height: a stock
of a share is a share; `XXXYYY=X` and `XXX=X` (the dollar in XXX) are a rate, the holding its amount; a
converter is a rate in the converter style; `BTC-USD` and the like are a coin. Presets: one *Markets*
folder (`stockGroup`, now titled Markets) and *Markets and news*; the separate currency preset and add
entry are gone. The person's file (a copy, read only) carries its one line `CHFUSD=X`, five years,
three rows high, to a rate CHF/USD as it stood (`MarketMigrationTests.ThePersonsFileIsCarriedOver`,
with `KARPO_PERSON_CONFIG`).

**Gone.** `CurrencyPairs`, `StockSymbols`, `StockOptions`/`StockRanges`/`StockHoldings`,
`CurrencyFaceDrawing`, `StockFaceDrawing`, `StockHeader`, `CurrencyReading`, the `currency` widget,
its face and preset, and their strings (renamed to `core.market.*`, `settings.widget.market.*`,
`dock.markets.*`, `widget.markets.*` in all 30 files). The old stock and currency code was about 4,400
lines (12 files and the stock types in `Config.cs` and `FaceDrawings.cs`); the markets code is about
4,850 (14 files) with the coins, CoinGecko, the ECB and the type rows added.

Tests: `MarketSourceTests` (each type's routes from canned answers: direct, inverse, cross, ECB,
CoinGecko, a coin found by its ticker, an answer without a chart giving way, the failure that says most), `MarketLiveTests` (only with `KARPO_LIVE_TESTS=1`: 44
pairs over a day and five years, 12 coins in USD, EUR, CHF, JPY and GBP over a day, a month and five
years, 7 shares and index/future/foreign listings, the ECB and CoinGecko on their own — all answered on
2026-10-19; KWD/ISK over a day was the only answer without a chart), `MarketRowsTests` (each type's
rows and nothing of another's), `MarketMigrationTests` (every old shape), `MarketReadingTests`,
`MarketRangeTests`, `MarketHoldingTests`, `MarketOffscreenTests`, `MarketPresetTests`, and
`MarketPictures` (`markets-lines-*.png`, `markets-faces-*.png`: a share, a rate, a rate alone, the
converter and two coins at every height and across and down a bar).

## 254. A face with nothing to set has no submenu and no chevron (2026-10-20)

The person: "if a face has no settings dont show the submenu. also dont draw the angled arrow then".
§227 gave every face of a folder's menu a submenu, one with no settings saying "No settings for this
face" under its name; that row and its words (`dock.edit.faceNoSettings`, every language) are gone.
A face with no settings (`OptionRows.OfFace` empty) is now its row alone (`OptionMenu.FaceSection`):
the grip at its start, its icon and title, its bin, no `Children`, so no chevron. A click on the row
or Enter on it does nothing and the menu stays (a row of tools without a submenu,
`Flyout.Controls.cs`); its grip drags it among the faces and its bin and Delete take it off as
before. A face with settings is unchanged: its submenu under its name, its bin before the chevron.

The bins stand in one column: a row dragged into order among rows with a submenu (one
`FlyoutItem.Reorder` group with a chevron in it), without one itself, keeps the chevron's slot empty
(`SlotBeside` in `Flyout.Open`, measured and drawn), so the bin of a face without settings is in line
with the others', not one slot further out.

Tests: `OptionMenuTests.EveryFacesSubmenuHasItsChoicesAsLevelsOfTheirOwn` (every face with no options:
no children, no far slot, grip and bin, the bin takes it off; the rest as before);
`TheFacesAreMovedAndTakenOffOnTheMenusFirstLevel` (on a real menu, the clock and "What's inside": the
bins' middles at one x, a click and Enter on the content face's row nothing, one panel, the menu
open). Picture: `option-menu-empty-<dark|light>`. By hand: arrange the bar, open the menu of a folder
wearing a face with no settings (What's inside, for one) and one with settings: no chevron on the
first, its bin in line with the other's, a click on it opens nothing; its bin takes it off.

## 255. A widget for the device's location says where the device is (2026-10-20)

The person: "if the widgets use the current location they should not just show current location on
the widget but the actual location that was picked". A weather, air-quality, tides or earthquake
widget — a line or a face — with "Use my device's location" on said "Current location"; and where a
place had been picked before the switch went on, it said that place's name over the device's data.

**One rule, for all of them** (`Karpo.Core\PlaceNames.cs`). `PlaceNames.Of(options)` is what every
place-based widget calls its place: the place picked, as picked ("Zürich, Zurich, Switzerland"); with
the device's location on, what the device's position is called (`PlaceNames.Device`); "Current
location" only until that is known, or where no name was found. `PlaceNames.Known` is the same
without the placeholder, for a face's tooltip, the web search of a weather line and the edit list's
detail. `PlaceNames.Forms` is the full name and its short form before the first comma ("Zürich"),
which the lines pick between by the room they have, as they did. While Windows gives no position the
place kept beside the switch is what is fetched (`WeatherStore.Where`), so then that place is what is
said. No widget writes "Current location" or splits a name itself any more
(`DevicePlaceTests.NoWidgetNamesItsPlaceItself` holds it).

**Written as a picked place is.** The name, then its region and its country where they say something
the name does not (`PlaceNames.Label`, `Detail`), the rule the place search's results now share
(`Places.SearchAsync`): "Zürich, Kanton Zürich, Schweiz" in German, "Atlantic Ocean" out at sea.

**Looked up once per position** (`Karpo.Dock\Islands\DeviceNames.cs`). Every place-based store asks
where the device is through `WeatherStore.Where`; when Windows answers, the name of that position is
looked up there, before the forecast, the air or the tides are fetched, so the answer comes with its
name. The source is BigDataCloud's free client-side reverse geocoding
(`api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client`): no account, no key, and made for exactly this —
an app on the device asking about the position the device just gave (its terms rule out a server
asking for others). Open-Meteo, which the place search uses, finds places by name only; Windows'
`MapLocationFinder` wants a Bing Maps key from a desktop app, and Bing Maps is retired; Nominatim
asks apps to keep to one request a second across all their users. The position is sent to two
decimals (about a kilometre, what the forecast sends already), in Karpo's language ("de", "pt",
"zh"; English for the test language), and asked once per such square and language however many
widgets ask at once. The newest eight names are kept in weather.json with the forecasts (`names`,
newest first; a file from before has none), and the newest is what the device is called from the
dock's start (`WeatherStore.Restore`), offline too. A position with no name is kept, empty, so it is
not asked again; a failed look-up is not kept and not tried again for a quarter of an hour, and
meanwhile the widgets say "Current location" — not the name of where the device was before. A
language changed since: the name in another language until the next fetch asks in the new one.

**The menu's place row** says where the device is, short: "Zürich (this device)"
(`dock.edit.deviceLocationAt`, in every language); "Device location" until that is known, and while
Windows gives no position.

Settings, a process of its own, still titles such a widget "Current location": it does not read the
dock's weather.json.

Tests: `DevicePlaceTests` — the service's answer read (Zürich in German, the open sea, no city, a region
named as its city, nothing named, not JSON), the request's two decimals and language, a position named
once for three widgets at once and kept newest first and only eight, a failure leaving "Current
location" and not asked again at once, a nameless position kept empty, the names through weather.json
(and a file from before, and one with nulls), the one rule for a picked place, the device's name, the
place kept while Windows gives none, `WeatherReading`, the menu row and the edit list's header, and no widget naming its place
itself. Pictures (UI tests, dark, 150 %): `device-place-<weather|air|tides|quakes>.png`, the four lines
for the device's location saying "Zürich, Zurich, Switzerland" (or "Zürich" where the age takes the
room); the air, tides and earthquake faces' tooltips start with it. By hand: with Windows' location on
for desktop apps, a weather line, an air line and an air face for the device's location: the line says
the town the PC is in, the face's tooltip too, the menu's place row "<town> (this device)"; restart
offline: the same name at once; Windows' location off with a place kept: that place's name.

## 256. "What's inside" is no face any more; "Its icon" is "Icon" (2026-10-20)

The person: *"whats inside should not be a folder face option anymore. its icon face should be renamed
to just icon."* This supersedes §67's **What's inside** (the default face) and everything since that
offered it.

**Gone.** The face that showed a folder's first four widgets' icons in a 2×2 (`content`) is offered
nowhere: not in the gallery, not in the bar's "Add a face" (`FaceGallery`'s Folder group is the icon
alone), not in `FolderFaces.All`. Its descriptor (`FolderFaces.Content`, `ContentId`), its drawing
(`ContentFace`, `FolderIsland.PaintPreview`, `PreviewCells`), the widgets' pictures made for it
(`IPreviewIcon`, the pin's and the drive's `PaintPreviewIcon`), its right click (`ActsFor`), its strings
(`core.face.content.*` in all 30 files), Settings' `FolderButtonArt` (the old folder page's "Button on
the taskbar" pictures, left only in the controls gallery) and their tests are gone.

**A new folder wears its icon** (`FolderFace.Kind`'s default, and so `FolderOptions.Faces`'), the one
somebody chose or the folder glyph, and a face this build does not know reads as the icon
(`FolderFaces.Of`), the old word `content` among them, wherever it is met: a pasted folder, a file the
carrying over has not reached.

**Carried over in place, never reset** (`LineMigrations.CarryContentFaces`): a folder's face of what is
inside is its icon where it stood among its faces, the name beside it as it was set (both take one), its
icon as chosen; one after it, or every one where the folder wears its icon already, goes, since the icon
is the folder's one of a kind (`Repeats` false). The icon stays, so a folder never wears none. The file
is written back once and `migrated` says `contentFace`. No preset and not the default bar wore it: every
preset's folder wears its icon or a face of its own, which is unchanged.

**"Its icon" is "Icon"**, its id `icon` as it was: Symbol, Icône, Icono, Icona, Ícone, Pictogram,
Pictogramă, Ikona, Ikon, Simge, Значок, Εικονίδιο, أيقونة, نماد, آئیکن, आइकन, आयकॉन, আইকন, ஐகான்,
చిహ్నం, ไอคอน, Biểu tượng, アイコン, 아이콘, 图标, 圖示.

The person's file (a copy, read only) wore no face of what is inside: its five folders wear the battery
and power; the removable devices, a drive, the air and the icon; the tides; the Wi-Fi, the sound and what
is playing; and the time and date with the notifications. It reads unchanged and is not marked
(`FolderFaceMigrationTests.ThePersonsFileKeepsItsFaces`, with `KARPO_PERSON_CONFIG`).

Tests: `FolderFaceMigrationTests` (a new folder's icon; the old word and unknown ones read as the icon;
the carrying over alone and among other faces, with the icon worn already, and twice; a file in today's
words left alone), `FaceGalleryTests` (the Folder group is the icon alone, `content` offered nowhere),
`FolderFaceTests.TheIconFaceIsCalledIcon`.

## 257. Editing a widget is edit mode's alone; the folder's close button is the accent and a × (2026-10-20)

The person: *"the right click context menu actions that are copy, remove, duplicate etc whatever, or
change the appearance of a widget should only appear in edit mode. they should be removed from all
other places"*, and *"when the widget in the folder edit mode is the close button it should just be
all blue and not show the widgets content actually, additionally there should be a close icon there
as well"*. This supersedes the rest half of §202's and §220's row ("at rest or arranged"), §228's
settings rows at rest, and §252's face drawn again on the accent.

**One place decides.** `Dock.WidgetMenu` asks one question: is the bar arranged? Arranged, the menu
is edit mode's — the row (`WidgetButtons`: Cut, Copy, Remove; the tray's Settings), the widget's
settings (`OptionRowsFor`, a folder's faces
on the bar, the colours) and a folder line's height (`LineHeightRows`). At rest it is
`Dock.RestMenuRows`: the widget's own acts and nothing else — a line's (`ActsFor(ListKind)`), an
entry's (`ActsFor(BarKind)`), a folder's face by face (`FaceRows`), the floor's row where none is live
(Dock.MenuFloor.cs: its page in Windows, else its folder's "Edit folder"). The status icons' own
rows (`IWidgetMenu`) at rest, on the bar and behind their arrow, are theirs alone too. Gone:
`RestRows` (the row put on top of every menu at rest), the settings and the height added to every
menu after the split, and the two acts that were settings by another name: `WidgetAct.WeatherLocation`
("Change location" on the weather, air, tides and quakes faces — the place is the face's setting, in
edit mode's menu) and `WidgetAct.SeparatorStyle` ("Separator style" on a separator and a divider — its
style is edit mode's menu's row), with their words in every language.

| | At rest | In edit mode |
|---|---|---|
| A widget on the bar | its acts (the clock's date and time, a status icon's page, the Snipping Tool's snips…), else its page in Windows | Cut, Copy, Remove; its settings |
| A folder on the bar | each face's acts under its name (Refresh, mute, the radios, the power modes, the desktops, the layouts…), else "Edit folder" | Cut, Copy, Remove; its settings; its faces (a click opens it, §253) |
| A line in a folder | its kind's acts (play, mute, devices, End task, Join meeting, Clear all…), else "Edit folder" | Cut, Copy, Remove; its settings; its height |
| A pin | Windows' own app menu: jump list, the app, Unpin from taskbar, close windows, End task; in a folder its file's rows | Cut, Copy, Remove above the jump list |
| The tray | its icons' apps' menus; its own place: its page | Cut, Copy, Settings, Remove |
| The bar's room | Add, Edit taskbar, Taskbar settings; the layouts; Task Manager | none (§214) |

**What stays at rest, and why.** "Edit folder" (the floor, and a folder's content face) and the bar's
"Edit taskbar" are ways into edit mode, not edits. The bar's own menu is unchanged: its "Add" turns
edit mode on and opens the add list, "Taskbar settings" opens the app, as Windows' taskbar's own
right click offers its Taskbar settings. A pin's "Unpin from taskbar" is Windows' own row of an app's
menu (§202), as "Pin to taskbar" is for an open app that is no pin. "Manage accounts" and "Layout
settings" open pages of the app that are no widget's appearance. A widget whose own rows are none
still has a menu, the floor's (2026-10-11: no menu that is nothing); only one the file has lost has
none.

**The close button.** The face of the folder open arranged (§252) is a plain accent button over its
edit block — the same fill, hover and pressed — with nothing of the face on it: Windows' ChromeClose
(E8BB, `Dock.GlyphCloseFolder`, the caption button's ×) centred, 16 DIPs (never more than half the
block), in TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary (`FlyoutTheme.TextOnAccent`; high contrast: the highlight's
text). Its tooltip is "Close folder", as before. Gone: drawing the face's cells again in the other
mode's look (`Scene.OnAccent`, the scene's `islands`).

Tests: `RestMenusTests` (every ListKind line, every bar entry, a folder wearing each face and one of
several: no button, no submenu, every row one of its acts, none of the row's
words; edit mode's row unchanged for all, the tray's with Settings) — generic, so a kind added later is
held to it; `WidgetMenuTests`, `FolderMenuRowsTests`, `BarMenuTests`, `MenuFloorTests`,
`FaceMenuTests`, `WidgetMenuTitleTests`, `ShortcutWidgetTests` read the rest menu from `RestMenuRows`;
`EditedDisplay` with a folder: the close button draws the × alone (`Scene.CloseShown.Draws`), a pixel a
quarter in from its side is the accent, its middle the ×'s ink. Pictures: `menu-<widget>-<rest|edit>-*`
(MenuModePictures: the rest menus without the row, the edit menus with the row and the settings),
`editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<dark|light>-150`. By hand: right-click a widget, a folder and a line at
rest (its acts only, no Cut/Copy/Remove, no Style, Place or height); the same in edit mode (the row
and its settings); open a folder in edit mode: its face on the bar is the accent with a ×, light and
dark, hover and press it.

## 258. One search for what a markets widget tracks; the chart as an area, a line or candles (2026-10-20)

The person, about the markets widget (§253): *"remove the from and to in the stock widget and just let me
search for currency pairs as it is already possible"* and *"add different chart styles to the stock widget,
optionally a candle chart"*. **This supersedes §253's type and its From, To, Swap, Coin and In rows.**

**One symbol.** What a markets widget tracks is one symbol as Yahoo writes it, and what it is follows from
the symbol alone (`MarketSymbols`, `Karpo.Core\Markets.cs`): `EURCHF=X` a rate (and `CHF=X` the dollar in
francs, kept as `USDCHF=X`), `BTC-EUR` a coin in a currency (a ticker, a dash and an offered currency;
`BRK-B` and `EUR-CHF` are no coin), anything else a share, a fund, an index or a commodity. There is no type
setting: `MarketOptions.KindOf` reads the symbol, and the data layer (`MarketAsk.Of`, `MarketSources`) still
routes each kind its own way — a share Yahoo's chart; a rate Yahoo direct, inverse, through the dollar, then
the ECB; a coin Yahoo, through the dollar, then CoinGecko. A pair is stored as `EURCHF=X` rather than
`EURCHF`, so no six-letter word is ever taken for a pair by guessing. A widget nobody set has no symbol and
asks for one ("Set up"); the region's default pair is gone with the type.

**The search** (`MarketSearch`, `MarketFinder`, `Karpo.Core\MarketSearch.cs`) is the Symbol row: a search
field on a level of its own, autofocused, five results and "Show more", what it tracks at the row's end
("AAPL", "EUR/CHF", "BTC/EUR") and its type's glyph on the row. It finds:

| Typed | Found first, without asking anybody |
|---|---|
| `EURCHF`, `EUR CHF`, `EUR/CHF`, `eur-chf`, `EUR to CHF`, `EURCHF=X` | EUR/CHF |
| `euro franc`, `Euro Swiss Franc`, `swiss franc us dollar`, `CHF USD` | EUR/CHF, CHF/USD (names in Karpo's language or English, ICU's) |
| `BGN USD` | BGN/USD: any two ISO 4217 codes Windows names, quoted or not — the rate's routes find one |
| `BTC EUR`, `BTC-EUR`, `BTCEUR`, `bitcoin euro`, `EUR BTC`, `eth in chf` | the coin in that currency |
| `eur`, `yen` | the currency against the region's, the dollar and the euro, each way |
| `bitcoin`, `ETH` | the coin in the dollar, the region's currency and the euro |
| `apple`, `^GSPC`, `gold` | nothing of its own: Yahoo's listings |

Words that name a pair or a coin whole ask nothing more; otherwise Yahoo's search follows, its shares,
indices, futures, pairs and coins after what the words named, each once (a listed pair or coin becomes one).
Offline, what the words named stands. Each row says what it is: a pair "EUR/CHF" with *Currency pair · Euro →
Swiss Franc* at its end, a coin "BTC/EUR" with *Crypto · Bitcoin* (the type first, as a row's value is cut
from its end), a share its name with its symbol and exchange ("Euronet Worldwide, Inc." · *EEFT · NASDAQ*).
Before anything is typed: what it tracks, ticked, then what the person's other markets widgets track — pairs
and coins too now (`OptionFields.SharesInUse`). Enter on words alone keeps the pair or coin they name, else a
symbol written out ("F" is Ford), looked up. A share is looked up before it is kept (its name, exchange and
currency its Detail); a pair or a coin needs no proving. A pick of another kind clears the amount owned.

**Rows** (`MarketRows.Of`): Symbol · Name on the bar (every kind now) · Chart range (+ Years) · Amount you
own (a share or a coin, on a line) · Style · Chart (wherever a chart is drawn: the full style, and the
converter on a line) · Amount (a pair in the converter style: what its first field starts at). The amount is
the converter's alone: a rate in another style is said for one (`MarketOptions.AmountOrOne`). The converter
is a style offered for a pair only, as before.

**Charts** (`MarketChartStyle`, `"chart"` in the file; `MarketChart`, `MarketCandles`):

| Chart | Drawn |
|---|---|
| Area (default, what §253 drew) | the line, its area under it fading to the foot, in the colour of the move |
| Line | the line alone |
| Candles | a candle a stretch: wick high to low, body open to close, Windows' finance green where it closed up, red where down; whole pixels |

A candle is a quarter of an hour over a day, an hour over five days, a day over a month, and over a longer
range each of Yahoo's points (a day, a week or a month, `MarketAsk.Interval`). Yahoo's chart answers each
point's open, high and low (`MarketPoint`, read beside the close, kept in `markets.json` as `bars`; an older
cache reads as closes); the inverse turns them over (the high the low's), a cross through the dollar divides
them by the other leg's price at that moment. **Without them** — the ECB's daily rates, CoinGecko's prices,
an older cache — candles are made of the closes: each opens at the close before it and reaches as high and as
low as the closes in it go. They are candles still, never a line in their place: a day of the ECB is a
candle per day, close to close. Where the chart is narrow, neighbours are joined from the newest
(`MarketCandles.Fit`) until each has at least `MarketChart.Pitch` px (5, or a twelfth of the chart's
height), so a face on a one-row bar draws a dozen readable candles rather than a smear; candles are drawn on
the line, the converter's chart and the face alike. Stale or in high contrast they are the quiet ink, those
that closed up hollow. Bars (OHLC ticks) were left out: at a bar's height they read as a smear of hairlines.

**Migration** (`LineMigrations.FoldMarketSymbols`, recorded once as `marketSymbols` in `Config.Migrated`; no
reset). A §253 record's `type`, `from`, `to` and `coin` are read (`MarketOptions.OldType` …) and folded into
its symbol where it stands, line or face: Currency CHF→USD is `CHFUSD=X`, Crypto BTC in EUR `BTC-EUR`, a
rate nobody set the region's pair it showed, a coin nobody set `BTC-USD`; its amount, holding, label, range,
style, height and place kept; the old words never written again (`MarketMigrationTests.ATypeAndItsCurrenciesAreItsSymbol`).
`MarketOptions.Normalize` folds too, so a record from anywhere reads. The §246 carry-over of `stock` and
`currency` lines writes symbols directly.

**Gone.** The Type, From, To, Swap, Coin and In rows, `MarketRows.Kinds`, `KindName`, `KindGlyph`, `Pick`,
`Side`, `CurrencyFinder`, `CoinFinder`, `SymbolFinder`; `MarketOptions.Kind`, `From`, `To`, `Coin`, `Pair`,
`CoinPair`, `Of`, `DefaultCoin`, `CoinCurrency`; the region's default pair and every `region` parameter it
needed (`MarketAsk.Of`, `MarketReading.Of`, `MarketWords`, `MarketConverter.Configure`, `MarketIsland.Region`);
`CurrencyNames.Entry`, `Currencies.Ordered`'s extras; and 15 strings in all 30 files (`type.*`, `from`, `to`,
`currency.*`, `swaps`, `coin.*`, `in`, `symbol.isCurrency`, `symbol.isCrypto`). New: `chart.header`, `.area`,
`.line`, `.candles`, `found.pair`, `found.crypto`; the symbol's placeholder now "Apple, EUR/CHF, gold, BTC…".

Tests: `MarketRowsTests` (what a symbol is; pairs in every spelling, coins, a currency or a coin alone,
shares left to the service; the search's rows mixed with a canned Yahoo answer, offline, Enter, proving;
each kind's rows on a line and a face; picks; the chart and the converter's amount), `MarketChartTests`
(open, high and low read, cached, inverted and crossed; a day's quarter-hour candles from a fixture; candles
of closes alone; joining from the newest; the reading's chart and candles, swapped), `MarketMigrationTests`
(§253's shapes), `MarketSearchPictures` (`markets-search-open-*.png`, `markets-search-eur-*.png`) and
`MarketPictures.TheChartStyles` (`markets-charts-lines-*.png`, `markets-charts-faces-*.png`: a share over a
month, a pair over a day and a coin over six months in each chart, and candles of closes alone, on a line one
to three rows high and on the face across and down a bar, dark and light at 150 %).

## 259. Faces without a most; several icons, each its own; the button grows to show them all (2026-10-20)

The person: *"you should therefore also be able to add multiple faces with a different icon"* and *"there
should not be a limit to the number of faces you can add to a folder, at some point the widget did not
scale / grow properly anymore which should be fixed. the folder face should always grow to show its
contents without clipping the faces."*

**Why the button stopped growing.** A folder's entry on the bar (`BarEntries`, `FolderList`) had the
default size, `WidgetSize.Automatic`, whose most is `WidgetItem.MaxWidth`: **eight cells**. Its shape
(`WidgetShapes.Folder`, from `FolderIsland.Parts`) measured every face, but the layout held that length in
the entry's range (`PartSpec.For` → `WidgetBounds.For` → `Layout.AllotCells`'s `room.Clamp(natural)`), so
past eight cells (some 350 DIP on a 48-DIP bar) the button stayed eight cells and its cell clipped the
faces after them (`FolderIsland.PaintCell`'s clip). The tests never saw it: they sized the island with a
style's default room, which is any width, never the room the bar gives a folder.

**The fix, a rule and not a case.** A most of the most there is (`WidgetItem.MostCells`) now holds nothing
back (`WidgetBounds.Open`: `Clamp` and `Allows` leave the content its length, however long; the fewest
still holds, a fixed width is still that width). The folder's entry starts its most there, as the open
apps' and the status icons' already did, for the same reason: its content is its measure. The open apps'
own case in `Layout.ButtonRoom` is gone, the rule covers it; the pin's stays. The only limit left is the
bar's own room: a bar too short for its widgets still makes its app buttons narrower and folds them into
"…" first, then drops widgets from the end of the run, the last placed first (`Layout.NotShown`), and
edit mode's rail says how many are not shown. A folder is never squeezed or cut.

**No most of faces.** `FolderFaces.Most` (8) is gone, and with it the greyed "Add a face" of a full button,
the gallery's "The button wears as many faces as it can" (`settings.folder.faces.full`, out of all 30
files) and the hand-written file's faces past eight being dropped on reading (`FolderOptions.Normalize`).

**The icon is the face's.** Each icon face has its own icon (`FolderFace.Glyph`, written as `"glyph"` on
the face where somebody chose one; null, and not written, for the folder glyph; `GlyphOrDefault`), set by
its own picker in its submenu (`OptionPickers.Folder(face)`), drawn by `IconFace` and shown on its row of
the folder's menu. So the icon repeats (`FaceInfo.Repeats`), and "Add a face" offers it whatever the button
wears. The name beside the button (`ShowName`) stays the folder's: it is the folder's name, beside a face
alone on its button.

**Carried over, never reset.** The folder's one icon of before (`"glyph"` on the folder) is read
(`FolderOptions.OldGlyph`) and given to each of its icon faces that has none of its own, in
`FolderOptions.Normalize`, which runs after the face of what is inside became the icon (§256), so that one
gets it too; it is not written again. A folder whose faces are no icon loses it: nothing showed it. A
preset's glyph is its icon face's (`Presets.Folder`).

**Which faces repeat.** Those whose settings make two different: the icon (its icon), the clock, the
calendar and the time and date (their zones), the five readings (their adapter, disk and pace). The rest
stay once, and why: the Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the sound, removable devices, the hotspot, cast, nearby sharing,
the battery, power, the mail, the bell, the clipboard, contacts, VPN, desktops, the keyboard and layouts
show the one thing the PC has; the timer, the focus session, the stopwatch, news, the drives and sports
read the folder's first such line; now playing the one player. The weather, the air, the tides, the quakes
and markets keep a place or a market of their own on the face, but the folder follows one of each
(`FolderIsland`'s one weather place, `SampleAir`, `SampleTides`, `SampleQuakes`, `SampleMarket`), so a second
would show the first's: they stay once until the folder follows each face's own. The meeting face's
options choose among one calendar's meetings: a second would say the same meeting again.

Tests: `FolderFacesTests.AButtonOfManyFacesIsAsLongAsAllOfThem` (twelve faces of mixed kinds, three icons,
at 100 and 150 % across a bar and down one, in the folder's own room: as long as its faces, past eight
cells, its last face inside it, the bar laying it out that long; it fails with the old most),
`EachIconFaceHasItsOwnIcon`, `TheFacesAreReadWhateverTheFileHolds` (nine faces read as nine),
`TheFacesAreAddedRemovedAndReordered`, `AFaceOfTheFoldersOneOfAKindIsWornOnce`,
`FolderFaceMigrationTests.TheFoldersIconIsCarriedOntoItsIconFaces` and `WhatIsInsideIsItsIcon`,
`FaceGalleryTests.WhatCannotBeWornIsGreyedWithWhy`, `OptionMenuTests` (a button of twelve still offers the
icon), `WidgetBoundsTests.ARangeAndAFixedSizeAreTheSameSetting`, `NeverCombineTests.WhatHoldsAppButtons`.
The sheet `folder-many-faces.png` (`FolderFacesTests.ManyFacesSheet`): the twelve, dark at 150 % on bars of
48 and 32 DIP, and at 100 % dark and light.

## 260. Alignment in its row; one widget removed without a question; a folder opens on a click (2026-10-20)

The person: *"alignment left center right should not have a submenu, it should just show three buttons
on the same level"*, *"if i just remove one widget there should not be a confirmation dialog, only when
there are multiple ones"* and *"in taskbar edit mode the left click currently opens the settings for
the folder, this should be mapped to the right click now and the left click should open the folder."*
This supersedes §227's "choices a level of their own" for an alignment, the menu's always-asking
"Remove" (2026-10-11), and §212/§213's folder click and "Open folder".

**Alignment in its row.** Every alignment — a heading's, a date's, a clock line's, and every face's
that has one (§201) — is one row: its icon and "Alignment", and at its end three icon buttons, start,
middle and end (`OptionGlyphs.Aligns`, mirrored in Arabic, Urdu and Persian), Windows 11's segmented
control as the Community Toolkit's Segmented draws it and quick settings' power mode has it (§248):
one track of ControlAltFillColorSecondary in the control stroke (`FlyoutTheme.ControlAltFill`, new),
the one in force raised on it in a control's fill and stroke with the accent's 12 by 2 DIP pill under
its icon, the others lit under the pointer, 32 by 24 DIP each (`FlyoutControl.Segments`,
Flyout.Controls.cs). A click on one sets it and the menu stays, the row shown again with it raised; a
click on the one in force or elsewhere on the row does nothing. With the row lit, Left and Right go
along the buttons as they stand (mirrored in a mirrored menu, stopping at either end), lighting the one
they are on, and Enter or Space picks it; in a face's submenu Left no longer closes the submenu while
the row is lit (Escape does). A root menu's tooltip names each. The row says nothing at its end any
more: the raised button is what it is set to. The rows are marked `OptionRow.Segmented`; only the
alignments are — the other choices of three with icons (a clock's hours, the volume's orientation…)
have longer words and stay a level of their own, which §227 asked for.

**One widget removed asks nothing.** The menu's "Remove" and the Delete key ask one question now
(`FolderDeletes.ForRemoving`): one widget — on the bar or a folder's line — and an empty folder go at
once; several selected ask "Remove N widgets?" in Windows' task dialog; a folder with widgets in it
still asks how many go with it, alone or among others (the 2026-10-11 rule, kept: a folder of widgets
is several). Gone: `FolderDeletes.ForMenu`, `Dock.MenuDeleteQuestionFor`, `RemoveSelected`'s
`fromMenu`, and the words "Remove “{name}”?" and "Its settings will be removed with it."
(`dock.delete.widgetTitle`, `dock.delete.widgetContent`) in all 30 languages. A face's bin in a
folder's menu never asked, and still doesn't.

**A folder opens on a click.** While the bar is arranged a click on a folder selects it and opens it,
arranged in place (`EditClicks.OnBlock` → `EditClickAct.Open`, the dock's `OpenArranged`); its face is
then its close button (§252). Space and Enter on it, and Narrator's Invoke, do the same. Its menu is the
right click's: a right click on any widget of the bar — a folder's too — opens its one menu beside it
(`EditClicks.OnRight`, now whether the menu opens; `EditRightPress` gone), selecting it alone where it
was not selected and keeping several where it is one of them. Every other widget's click still selects
it and opens its menu (§212: the person asked for that of widgets, and only remapped the folder). A
click on a folder whose menu its press closed opens it all the same. The second click of a
double-click lands on the face, the close button by then, and does not close the folder again
(`CloseReleased` asks the double-click guard, `ClickActs`). The menu's "Open folder" and "Close folder"
rows are gone (`EditMenuRows`, `WidgetAct.OpenFolder`, `WidgetAct.CloseFolder`, the dock's
`ToggleFolder`, `dock.widgetMenu.openFolder` in all 30 languages; "Close folder" stays the face's
tooltip). A folder's lines in a folder open arranged are as they were.

Tests: `AlignSegmentsTests` (every alignment segmented and nothing else; the row's three buttons and
their picks; Left and Right along them, mirrored; on a real menu a click and the keys pick, in a face's
submenu too, the submenu kept), `FolderDeleteTests.OneWidgetGoesWithoutAQuestionSeveralAreCounted`,
`EditClickTests` (a folder's click opens it, a right click opens the menu, a double-click leaves the
folder open, Space and Enter), `MenuSidesTests.AFoldersMenuNoLongerOpensTheFolder`. Pictures (150 %,
dark and light): `menu-align-line-*`, `menu-align-line-keys-*` (the keys on the middle button),
`menu-align-face-*` (a clock face's submenu). By hand: a heading's and a clock face's alignment — click
each button, the text moves at once, the menu stays; arrows and Enter on the row; in Arabic the start
button stands on the right. Remove one widget from its menu and with Delete (no question), two selected
(asks), a folder with widgets (asks). In edit mode click a folder on the bar (it opens; its face closes
it), double-click one (it stays open), right-click it (its menu, no "Open folder"), right-click and
click a clock (its menu either way).

## 261. The tray's icons are its menu's; none on General (2026-10-20)

The person: *"tray icon configuration should go into the tray icon menu and not be shown in general
settings"*. This supersedes §228's "Tray · where each icon shows — kept, moved to **General**", and the
tray's "Settings" in edit mode's row (§228; §257's table, "Cut, Copy, Settings, Remove").

**Edit mode's menu, as every setting.** Where an icon shows is how the tray looks, so by §257's one rule
its rows are edit mode's menu's and not the menu at rest: a click or a right click on the tray while the
bar is arranged gives Cut, Copy, Remove, then "Tray icons ›". At rest the tray's menu is as it was (the
floor: its page in Windows), and an icon is still dragged onto the chevron or back onto the bar there. An
icon hidden completely shows nowhere to be dragged: these rows are the way back for it now
(`TrayLayout`'s header says so).

**The rows** (`OptionTray`, Karpo.Core\OptionTray.cs, called from `OptionRows.Of` beside
`OptionHolidays.Into`). One group, "Tray icons" (`settings.tray.icons.header`, the tray's glyph), as the
status icons are one; in it a row per icon the tray holds now (`Dock.TrayMenuIcons`, from `TrayHeld`, so
Windows' update icon is the status icons' where a bar shows them), in the bar's order
(`TrayLayout.InOrder`), each identity once:

| Part | What |
|---|---|
| Icon | the icon's live picture as the bar draws it (`OptionRow.Picture`, its identity; `Dock.TrayPicture`, handed to `OptionMenu.Section` / `Rows` as `pictures`); the tray's glyph where it has none |
| Name | as Windows' "Other system tray icons" names it (`OptionTray.NameOf`): its executable's description, else its product name (`FileVersionInfo`, read once per executable, `Dock.TrayIconName`), else its tooltip's first line, else its file's name, else "Tray icon"; Explorer's speaker "Volume" (`OptionTray.VolumeIcon`). Two of one name (Explorer's "Safely remove hardware" and "Meet Now") are called by their tooltips: a menu row is one line (§243), and has no line under its name as General's card had |
| At its end | where it shows (§228) |
| Its level | Show on taskbar, Show in hidden icon menu, Hide completely, each with its icon (`OptionGlyphs.Taskbar`, `More`, `Hide`, the status icons' own), the one in force ticked: its state, or Windows' choice where nobody chose (`TrayLayout.State`) |

A pick writes `Config.TrayStates` as a drag does, its place in the order kept (`TrayLayout.Set`), into
the config the menu was read from (`OptionPlace.Config`, as the holidays' rows), which
`Dock.OptionPicked` saves (`Apply`, which tells Windows' own records, `PromoteChoices`); the menu stays,
the tick where it went (`MenuKeeps`), and the bar splits its icons again behind it. The choice is the
person's, not the tray's: every tray's menu has the same rows, and a change in one is in all. The icons
are listed for a tray alone (`OptionDevices.TrayIcons`, `Dock.MenuSources`); without them or a config to
write to there are none. The status icons' copy of the three states gave way to `OptionTray.States` and
`IndexOf`.

**Gone.** The tray's "Settings" button, which opened General at its icons (`WidgetButtons`' `settings`,
`WidgetSettingsItem`, `OpensSettings`, `CMD_MORE_SETTINGS`, `OpenWidgetSettings`,
`EditClicks.SettingsArgs`): the tray's row is every widget's, Cut, Copy, Remove. In the settings app:
General's "Tray icons" block and its note before Karpo has run, `SettingsModel.Tray.cs` (`TrayIconRule`,
`FillTrayIcons`, its watch on tray-icons.json), `Logic\TrayRows.cs`, `Logic\TrayPng.cs` (Windows'
IconSnapshot read from its PNG), `Shell.Generic`; a link naming the tray (`--island`, an older
`--page tray`) shows the Layouts, as one naming any other widget does. Three strings in all 30 files:
`settings.tray.intro`, `settings.tray.empty`, `settings.tray.icons.description`. Kept: tray-icons.json
(`TrayCatalogue`), which the dock reads its icons' order back from at its next start and an old file's
words are read with (`ConfigWords.TrayStates`); its `Record` is still written, though nothing reads it now.

Tests: `TrayMenuRowsTests` (a row per icon in the bar's order, each once, its three choices and their
icons, the one in force; none without icons or a config, none on another widget; the names, Explorer's
speaker, two of one name; a pick written as a drag writes it and read back, the order kept, one hidden
completely still listed and brought back, Windows told; the menu's group with each icon's picture and
value, the menu kept open; shown again after a pick; General and the strings gone),
`MenuIconsTests.EveryRowAndChoiceHasAnIcon` (the tray's rows among every row), `WidgetButtonsTests`,
`RestMenusTests.EditModesMenuKeepsTheRow`, `BarMenuTests.TheBarsSettingsRowIsNotNamedLikeAWidgetsOwn` (no
widget's row says "Settings", the tray's included), `TrayStatesTests` (the list's folder, from the gone
`TrayPictureTests`); gone with what they held: `TrayRowsTests`, `TrayPictureTests`,
`EditClickTests.TheTraysSettingsNameItsWidget`. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `menu-tray-icons-*`
(the group open), `menu-tray-icons-choices-*` (an icon hidden completely, its choices open). By hand: in
edit mode click the tray: Cut, Copy, Remove, "Tray icons ›", each icon with its own picture and where it
shows; set one to Hide completely (gone from the bar and the overflow, still listed), then back to Show on
taskbar; right-click the tray at rest (no such rows); Settings ▸ General (no tray icons).

## 262. The price is never cut; the change whole or not at all (2026-10-20)

The person: *"in the stock widget when it only shows one row high it cuts off the price and price change in
percent but there would still be space to display it. try to never cut off the price. same happens with
price change in other sizes, mitigate that as well."* This supersedes the ticker line's one-row order
(`MarketIsland`, 2026-10-11: "the name next … the change where the row still has the room for it"), the
line's change room of "-88.88%" and §162's "the change … where it fits at 11 DIP" down a side bar.

**Why it was cut.** A line measured the change's room on "-88.88%" (`MarketIsland.Ticker`), but a rise
starts with "+", which Segoe UI draws wider than the hyphen: every rise with two figures before the point —
"+12.34%" — was drawn in a room too narrow for it and cut to "+12.3…", and a coin's "+112.34%" to
"+112.3…", at every height (the second row's change too). On one row the change also gave way wherever the
name did not stand whole beside both figures, so a wide line said its price alone with room to spare. Down
a bar on its side the price was fitted to the bar down to 9 DIP and drawn cut where even that was too wide
("734,5…", "1,234.…" on 32 DIP), and the change's row was sized on "+88.88%" alone and dropped wherever the
price stood under 11 DIP.

**What it does now — the price first, the change second, the name and the chart after them:**

- **Rooms on shapes, the sign a plus.** The change's room is the wider of "+88.88%" and its own shape, every
  figure an eight and its sign a plus (`MarketText.ChangeShape`: "+112.34%" is "+888.88%"), so it changes
  only with a figure more, never as the change ticks or turns (§12.2), and the change always fits it.
- **The price never cut, on a line.** At the list's figure (20 DIP) where its shape fits the line's room
  after the glyph's column; else a DIP smaller at a time, down to the list's text; else, at that, the first
  of its shorter forms whose shape fits (`MarketIsland.PriceFit`, `MarketText.PriceForms`, below).
- **One row: the change before the name whole.** The change stands beside the price wherever the row holds
  both beside the least the name still reads as (its first four letters and "…", as `ListTiers.Name` cuts
  it), or where the name has no room even beside the price alone and the two figures fit the row; the name
  takes what is left. The compact line's one-row branch follows the same rule; the currency and the range
  still need the name whole.
- **Down a bar on its side.** The price as it reads where its shape fits the bar at the smallest size, else
  the first shorter form that does (`MarketFaceDrawing.PriceForm`), then sized as before — one size for every
  ordinary price. The change at 11 DIP at the least — as small as an ordinary price where that is under it —
  in the first of its forms that fits ("+12.34%", "+12.3%", "+12%", `MarketText.ChangeForms`; a change that
  rounds to nothing has no shorter form), each sized on its own shape and the ordinary day's of as many
  decimals, so every face of a bar has its change row or none, at one size (§245); no row where no form fits.
  The change is never cut short: dropped whole as the last resort.
- **Shorter forms of a price**, each the whole of what it says as far as it goes: "734,567.89", "734,568"
  (no decimals, from three figures before them), "734568" (no thousands' marks, from a thousand), "734.6K"
  (thousands, millions or billions to a tenth, from ten thousand). Across a bar the face is as long as what
  it says (§245) and shows the price as it reads; the tooltip always says it whole. Only a bar too thin for
  every form (a coin of small units, "0.000123", on a 32-DIP side bar at 100 %) still cuts its shortest.

Tests: `MarketFitTests.TheLinesAtEveryHeightAndWidth` (a six-figure share, a share in francs with a holding,
a coin in the thousands, a coin of small units up 112.34 %, an index, a price-only share, an ordinary share
and a rate, one row to four at the narrow and the medium list, at 100 and 150 % and at 100 % with Windows'
text at 150 %, dark and light: every figure drawn — `MarketIsland.Figured` — measures within its room, and at
the app's text every full line shows its change at every height),
`TheFacesOnEveryBar` (across 32 and 48 DIP, down 32, 48 and 64: across the price and the change as they read;
down the price whole in the bar's room, a shorter form only where its own does not fit, the change whole
where it has a row, "734.6K" on 32 DIP) and `APriceAndAChangeHaveShorterFormsNeverCutOnes`; `MarketPresetTests`
(one size down a bar whatever the face reads) holds. Pictures: `markets-fit-lines-<dark|light>-<100|150|100-text150>.png`,
`markets-fit-faces-<dark|light>-<100|150|100-text150>.png`.

## 263. A markets widget's click searches it in the browser (2026-10-20)

The person: *"when i left click on the stock widget it should open the stock in the default search in the
browser"*. This supersedes, for a markets widget, §260's (and every earlier) "a folder opens on a click" at
rest and the markets line's click that did nothing (`ListWidgets`: `CellAct.Nothing`, `MarketIsland.Click`:
"A click does nothing but a converter's swap"). Edit mode's clicks are unchanged: they never reach a
widget's click (§260).

**What is searched.** The app's one engine (`Config.SearchEngine`, `SearchUrls.Search(Config, …)`, as the
weather's click), for what the widget tracks, by what its symbol is (`SearchUrls.MarketQuery`,
`SearchUrls.Market`): a pair its two codes, `EUR CHF` (`EURCHF=X`; `CHF=X` is `USD CHF`); a coin its ticker
and currency, `BTC EUR`; a share, a fund or an index its symbol and the word for a share,
`MSFT stock` — `widget.markets.search`, "{symbol} stock", in all 30 languages ("{symbol} Aktie",
"action {symbol}", "{symbol} 株価"…). The engines answer the first two with their converter or the coin's
price in any language; the share's word is what makes a symbol a quote. Nothing where there is no symbol
yet. The menu's "Open in browser" (Yahoo's quote page) stays the menu's.

**The line.** A ticker's click (the full and the compact style, at every height) chooses the search and asks
the folder to go (`IslandView.App`; the line's act is now `CellAct.Action`), and the dock opens it once the
folder has gone (`Dock.FolderForward` → `MarketIsland.Open`), as a headline's story opens; so a ticker's line
now lights as a whole under the pointer (`FolderFlyout.LightsWhole`). A converter's click is its swap and
its fields', as it was, and its parts still light themselves. A line with no symbol is its "Set up", as before.

**The face.** A button that wears the markets face alone is the widget on the bar: a click anywhere on it —
and Narrator's Invoke, which is its click — searches what the face tracks there and then
(`FolderIsland.Click` → `SearchMarket`; `FolderIsland.MarketOpening` stands in for the browser in tests),
instead of opening the folder. Beside other faces only a click in the markets face's own room (its box
along the bar, the bar's whole thickness across; `FolderIsland.ClickAt` → `MarketAt`, beside the meeting
face's Join) searches; the rest of the button, and its click without a point, open the folder as before.
A face with no symbol yet opens the folder. Across a bar and down one alike. The folder of a markets face
alone is still opened by pointing where Settings' hover flyouts are on, and in edit mode.

Tests: `MarketClickTests.EachKindIsSearchedForAsItsQuote` (the queries and addresses with Google, DuckDuckGo,
Bing and a custom engine), `ATickersLineSearchesItOnceTheFolderHasGone` (a share, a pair and a coin: the click
forwards, `Open` searches once; a converter's and an unset line's click open nothing; the ticker lights
whole, the converter not), `AMarketsFaceAloneSearchesItOnItsClick` (anywhere, across and down a bar; an unset
face opens the folder), `AMarketsFaceAmongOthersSearchesOnlyInItsOwnRoom` (a clock and a pair: the clock's
room and the pointless click open the folder, the pair's room searches); `TypedRegistryTests` (markets acts),
`LineHoverRuleTests` (a ticker lights whole).

## 264. The search engine dropdown wears each engine's logo (2026-10-20)

The person: *"search engine configuration should show the search engine logo too."* The General
page's "Search engine" card (§28, `SettingsModel.Search.cs`) listed the engines by name
only. Each entry of its dropdown is now the engine's logo, 16 DIP square, then its name, 12 DIP
apart, in the list and on the closed box beside the chosen name; the person's own address (Custom)
has no logo and wears the card's globe glyph (Segoe Fluent Icons E774) in the text's colour. The
engine is chosen nowhere else: the bar only searches with it (the weather's click,
`SearchUrls.Weather`), and the file's import summary names it in words (`TransferSummary`).

**The entries.** `EngineLogos.Items` (new, the settings app) makes one `ComboBoxItem` per engine in
`SearchUrls.All`' order, its content a row of the picture and a `TextBlock` that ends in an ellipsis,
its automation name the engine's name (the picture is `AccessibilityView.Raw`, so Narrator reads the
name once). An item that is its own container keeps its content, so the shared dropdown template
(`ChoiceItemTemplate`, a name alone) is not touched and every other dropdown keeps it
(`SettingsChoiceTests` unchanged); WinUI moves the chosen entry's content into the closed box, which
is how the logo shows there. An entry stands in one dropdown only, so the page makes two lists,
`GeneralPage.SearchEngines` for the plain card and `SearchEnginesCustom` for the card that opens on
the address, both bound `SelectedIndex` to `SearchEngineIndex` as before. The names still come from
`SettingsModel.SearchEngineChoices`, Custom in the language shown; the pages are built again when the
language changes, and the entries with them.

**The logos.** `assets\search-engines` holds each engine's favicon as its own site serves it,
downloaded 2026-10-20 into an empty scratch folder and checked (PNG or ICO, 16 to 256 pixels,
a few kilobytes) before being copied in: `google`, `bing`, `duckduckgo`, `ecosia`, `startpage` and
`brave`, each `-16.png` and `-32.png`. Google, DuckDuckGo and Ecosia: their `favicon.ico`'s own 16 and
32 frames; Startpage: its `favicon-16x16-gradient.png` and `favicon-32x32-gradient.png`; Bing: its
`favicon.ico`'s one 32 frame, the 16 scaled down from it; Brave: search.brave.com's `favicon.ico`'s
16 frame and its `favicon-96x96.png` scaled down to 32 (high-quality bicubic); the folder's
`README.md` names every address. They are the owners' trademarks, shown only to say which engine a
search goes to. `Karpo.Settings.csproj` copies them next to the exe (`Assets\SearchEngines`), so the
published `settings\` folder carries them and they show offline. Which size is read is
`EngineLogo.SizeFor` (new, `Logic\EngineLogo.cs`): the 16 at 100 %, the 32 above it, decoded at the
size it stands in the screen's pixels (`DecodePixelType.Logical`), asked again each time the entry is
