shown, so a window moved to a screen of another scale reads the size that fits there. A file name is
the enum's name in lower case (`EngineLogo.File`); none for Custom.

**Dark, light and high contrast.** Every logo is drawn on a shape of its own — Google's G on its
white disc, DuckDuckGo's orange disc, Ecosia's green tree, Brave's orange shield, Startpage's white
tile, Bing's blue-and-teal b — so each stands on the dark card as on the light one; pictured both
ways. In high contrast the logos stay in colour, as Windows' Settings keeps an app's own icon in
colour there and unlike the side menu's decorative pictures (§31, `MainWindow.Icons.cs`):
a logo names the engine, and its own backing keeps it apart from a black or white page; the names and
the globe take the contrast theme's text colour, the entries' own. A contrast theme is not pictured:
turning one on is Windows' own setting, and `KARPO_SETTINGS_CONTRAST` only changes the side menu.

Tests: `EngineLogoTests` — every engine of the enum is in `SearchUrls.All` and every one but Custom
has its 16 and its 32 in `assets\search-engines`, each a PNG of that size by its header and a few
kilobytes; Custom wears the glyph; every file there is an engine's and the README names it; the
project copies them to `Assets\SearchEngines` and `EngineLogos` reads them from there, and a build of
the settings app made since the project named them has every one beside its exe; both dropdowns list
the made entries, a list each, in the shared style; `SizeFor` at 100, 125, 150, 200 and 300 % and for a
scale that is none. Pictures (on a hidden desktop, an isolated config, `--page general --test size
1100 900 --test go "search engine"`, with `--test open-choice "Search engine" 1200` for the list):
dark with Google and the list open, light with DuckDuckGo, light with Startpage's list open, dark with
Brave Search, dark with Custom (the globe on the box, the address under it). By hand: open Settings,
General, Search engine — each entry its logo, the chosen one's on the closed box; pick Custom and back;
switch Windows to light, dark and a contrast theme; on a 150 % screen the logos are sharp.

## 265. Several holiday calendars, and no word of where they come from (2026-10-20)

The person: *"you should be able to add multiple holiday calendars, dont tell from where the data comes
from"*. **This supersedes §237's one country with its switch** (the Public holidays toggle, the Country
search and the one Region choice), and every place §237 named the service to the person.

**A list.** `HolidayOptions.Calendars` is a list of `HolidayCountry` (a country, ISO 3166-1, empty for
Windows' region's; a region of it, ISO 3166-2, empty for the whole country), in the order they were added,
each once; the colour stays one for them all. **None listed is off** — there is no switch any more
(`HolidayOptions.On` is `Calendars.Count > 0`), and none listed asks the service nothing, as off did. A
country may stand twice with different regions (Zürich and Ticino), never the same calendar twice; the
whole country beside one of its regions is allowed (the region's days are a few more). One following
Windows' region and the same country chosen are one (`PublicHolidays.Calendars`).

**The calendar shows the union** (`HolidayCalendar.Gather`): every calendar's holidays, a year of a country
one request whatever regions of it are listed, a holiday two calendars have on the same day under the same
name once. With one calendar nothing changes. With several, each holiday says whose it is
(`HolidayShown.Label`): the country's name, or the region's where two of one country are listed ("Zürich,
Ticino", not "Switzerland" twice). It is said after the other name on the event's second line in a day's
events ("All day · Weihnachten · Switzerland, United Kingdom"), in the month's tooltip ("Christmas Day ·
Switzerland, United Kingdom"), and in the agenda after when it is ("Saturday, 26 December · All day ·
Switzerland"), so the two St. Stephen's Days, Zürich's on the 26th and the United Kingdom's on the 28th,
read apart (`CalendarEvent.Whose`, null for every other event and for one calendar alone); in a medium
agenda the line is cut with an ellipsis where it is longer than the row ("· All day · Swit…"), as any
event's is. A
country whose request fails is the calendar's problem while nothing of it is kept, the others shown all the
same; `holidays.json` keeps each listed country's years.

**In a calendar's menu** (`OptionHolidays.Rows`): the one submenu "Public holidays ▸", saying at its end
"Off" or the countries ("Switzerland, United Kingdom", each once). In it a row for each calendar — named for
its country, its region on a second line under the name, opening its Region choice where the country has
regions (none, no submenu and no chevron, §254), a bin at its end taking it out, Delete while the row is
lit, the menu staying, shown again without it — then **Add a country**, a search (Windows' region's first,
the countries listed ticked, found by name or code), each pick one more calendar. This is the faces' idiom
(§259: each its row with a bin, "Add" after them), as a new row kind: `OptionRowKind.Item` with
`OptionRow.Rows` (its own rows) and `OptionRow.Remove`, picked as `OptionPickKind.Remove`
(`OptionMenu.ItemGroup` keeps every bin in one column); `OptionRows.Find` and `Flat` reach an item's own
rows, so a region picked a level down is set through its calendar's row (`OptionMenu.Row`,
`FieldPicks.Keep`). Keys: `HolidaysCalendar<n>`, `HolidaysRegion<n>`, `HolidaysAdd`.

**On the Accounts page** (`AccountsPage.ShowHolidays`, `SettingsModel.Holidays.cs`): the section's header
keeps the colour's swatch, its switch gone; under it a card for each calendar (the country's name, its
region's box where it has regions, a Remove button), then "Add a country" (a box of every country, Windows'
region's first; a pick adds it and the box empties). Both go through `OptionHolidays.AddCountry`, `Remove`
and `SetRegion`, so the page and the menu leave the file alike.

**Where they come from is said nowhere.** Gone: "from Nager.Date" at the end of the Accounts page's
description and "Nager.Date" in its search keywords, in all 30 languages (the only two strings that named
it; no menu, tooltip or problem did). The service is the code's business alone (its comments, the request).

**Migration** (no reset; `HolidayOptionsConverter` and `LineMigrations.CarryHolidayCalendars`, recorded
once as `holidayCalendars` in `Config.Migrated`). A file of before has `"on"`, `"country"` and `"region"`;
read, it is carried over in place: on, its country with its region is the list's one calendar (an empty
country still Windows' region's); off, the list is empty, as nothing was shown; the colour kept, §240's
`"observances"` read past. The file is written back once with `"calendars": [{ "country", "region" }]`
alone; the old words are never written again. A hand edit costs one calendar at most: an entry that is no
object, has no country or one that is no code is passed by, a region of another country is none.

**Strings** (30 languages): new `core.holidays.add` ("Add a country") and `settings.holidays.remove`
("Remove {country}"); gone `core.holidays.show` and `settings.holidays.country.header`; the description and
keywords without the service.

Tests: `HolidaysTests` (several calendars round-trip, each once, a region of another country none; none
listed is off, the colour kept; §237's one country carried over on, on with Windows' region, and off, the
file written back once with the list alone; hand edits of the list; the labels, two of one country told
apart by their regions, Windows' region's one with its country; the rows: added, a region given, a country's
whole calendar once, the same region never twice, taken out one by one to Off; "Add a country"'s finder; the
real submenu's items, bin, Delete, kept open, a region picked a level down; **no string of any language, nor
any menu row, names the service or its host**), `HolidayCalendarTests` (two countries one calendar, each
year asked once, Christmas once saying both, St. Stephen's Day each's own; two regions of one country one
request, told apart by region; a country that fails is the problem, the other shown, nothing of it kept),
`MenuIconsTests` (an item's own rows have icons), `MenuKeepsTests` (Remove keeps the menu open),
`OptionMenuTests.TheHolidaysCountriesAreListedAndTakenOutOnARealMenu`. Pictures (150 %, dark and light):
`holidays-several-*` (Zürich's and the United Kingdom's holidays in the agenda and a month with Christmas
picked and its events), `option-menu-holidays-*` (three countries, Zürich under Switzerland) and
`option-menu-holidays-removed-*` (the first taken out with Delete). The summary at the submenu's end is cut
with an ellipsis where the countries are more than it has room for ("Switzerl…"), as any long value is. By hand: Settings ▸ Accounts ▸ Public
holidays: add Switzerland and the United Kingdom, Region ▸ Zürich on the first card; the bar's calendar
shows both, Christmas once, its day's list saying "Switzerland, United Kingdom"; Remove the United Kingdom;
the bar's calendar's menu ▸ Public holidays lists the same, its bin and Delete take one out; an old
config.json with `"on": true, "country": "CH", "region": "CH-ZH"` opens as one calendar, Zürich.

## 266. Reset: the layouts, or every setting, as a new install has them (2026-10-20)

The person: *"reset settings file should also be possible."* — asked with their own layout made what a
fresh install of Karpo makes. Until now only one layout could be made new, from the command line
(`Karpo.exe --renew-layout <id>`, `LayoutRenewal`, its pins kept); nothing reset the file.

**Two resets, at the foot of About.** The settings app's About page has a closed expander **Reset**
under "Settings file", where Windows' own app pages put theirs, with two rows: **Reset layouts**
("Bars, folders and widgets as on a new install") and **Reset all settings** ("Every setting as on a
new install"), each with a "Reset…" button (`AboutPage.OnResetLayouts`, `OnResetAll`). Each asks first
in a dialog whose safe answer, Cancel, is the default: what goes, what stays, and where the file there
was is kept — "Your accounts and their sign-ins stay. The settings you have now are kept next to
config.json as config.json.before-reset-<date>." Reset all adds that "Start with Windows" stays as it
is on this PC (the import's own line, `settings.about.import.startupStays`). Done, the window's
message bar says "Layouts reset" or "Settings reset" and names the kept file
(`SettingsModel.Reset`, beside the import in SettingsModel.Transfer.cs); the pages refill from the new
file, and after a reset of everything the window speaks Windows' language again. The expander's
keywords (reset, restore defaults, factory reset, start over, new install…) find it from the search.
20 new keys `settings.about.reset.*` in all 30 languages.

**What a new install has** is what Load makes of no file at all (`Config.Defaults`, now internal):
the layout of Windows 11's own taskbar with the apps pinned to it now (`Config.FirstLayout`, §13 and
the 2026-10-13/14/16 choices), and every other setting at its default. Nothing older is read for it:
not a `config.shape<N>.json` a start kept aside, not `config.json.bak`, nothing of PierNet's or
pier's (those imports went with shape 17, 2026-09-25; README said otherwise and no longer does). A
`config.json` in an older shape is kept aside by the load before the reset, as at any start.

**What each keeps** (`ConfigReset`, Karpo.Core\ConfigReset.cs, with `ResetScope`):

- `ResetScope.Layouts`: `Layouts`, `DefaultLayoutId` and `Screens` become a new install's — so every
  display shows the new layout, at the bottom, as a display Karpo never saw. Everything else in the
  file stays as it was: the appearance, the language, the formats, the tray icons' places, the online
  interval, "Start with Windows".
- `ResetScope.All`: the whole file a new install's, but `StartWithWindows`, this PC's own choice as an
  import keeps it (`SettingsModel.Import`). `Language` goes back to none, Windows' own.
- Neither touches anything outside config.json: the accounts and their sign-ins
  (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\accounts.json`, its secrets DPAPI blobs — docs\accounts.md; config.json holds
  none of them), the licence (`license.dat`), the caches, screen time's history, and the tray icons the
  dock has seen (`tray-icons.json`). A calendar or mail widget that goes with its layout is only a
  widget: the account it showed stays signed in, for whatever shows it next.

**The file.** `ConfigReset.ResetFile` loads config.json as both apps do, makes the new install's
config in the language it will speak (the one chosen for the layouts, Windows' for everything — the
folders' names are written in it — then S speaks what it spoke before), and writes it in whole
through `Config.Replace`, as an import does: under the config lock, the file there was copied to
**`config.json.before-reset-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>`** beside it first (and kept as config.json.bak too, as
any save keeps one). `Replace` takes the name's middle now (`"before-import"`, `"before-reset"`) and
never writes over a copy kept before: a second one in the same second is `…-2` — an import's too. A
reset is a file replaced whole (`Config.ReplacedAt`) and no edit of Karpo's own
(`Config.KarposOwnEdit`), so the running dock takes it on its next reload as it takes an import, and
the pins the reset took off are no unpin: they stay on Windows' taskbar (WindowsPins.cs). The layouts
alone of a file a newer Karpo wrote are not reset (an `IOException`, as a save refuses it); all of it
may be. The same from a script: `Karpo.exe --reset-settings layouts|all` (the bar's exe, no window,
no mutex, as `--renew-layout`), which prints where the old file is kept.

Public API, for a script or another app: `ConfigReset.FirstInstall()` (a new install's config on this
PC), `ConfigReset.Reset(Config current, ResetScope scope, Config? fresh = null)` (in memory, the given
config left as it is), `ConfigReset.ResetFile(ResetScope scope, out string? backup)` and
`ConfigReset.ResetFile(Config current, ResetScope scope, out string? backup)` (written; the backup's
path, null when there was no file).

Tests: `ConfigResetTests` — a reset of everything equals what Load makes of no file in the same
folder, ids aside, "Start with Windows" kept, and loads back the same; a reset of the layouts makes
layouts and displays a new install's and leaves every other part of the JSON as it was; the in-memory
reset leaves its config alone; the old file kept beside config.json byte for byte, a second reset
kept under another name; no file, nothing kept; an older `config.shape16.json`, an older `.bak` and a
`PierNet\config.json` beside it neither come back nor are touched; an older config.json is kept aside
and the reset is a new install's; the reset file loads with no recovery and writes nothing back, and
its next save merges; `accounts.json` and `license.dat` byte for byte as they were, and no account in
config.json; the replace mark moves and the reload is no Karpo edit; the language followed and S's
own left as it was; a newer Karpo's layouts refused and its file untouched. All in the test run's
folder (`KARPO_CONFIG_DIR`), never %APPDATA%. By hand: About → Reset → Reset layouts on a config with
two layouts and a display at the top (one bar, at the bottom, the rest as it was; the kept file in
%APPDATA%\Karpo); Reset all settings with a language chosen and "Start with Windows" off (Windows'
language, the switch still off); Cancel changes nothing.

## 267. The bars undimmed under an open folder; its face is itself again; a red close button at its top (2026-10-20)

The person: *"right now when a folder is open it hides the taskbar is in the background, this should
be reverted again. the folder widget that is open should also not be the close button anymore, at
least not visually. there should be a red close button at the top"*. This supersedes §213's "And
dimmed", §252's "The face is the close button" and §257's "The close button" as they drew it, and
§217's "No × on the folder".

**The bars are not dimmed.** What hid the taskbar was the bars' own dim under a folder open arranged
(§213, 2bc04c46): every bar's and place's panels under 40 % black (`Scene.BuildScrim`, `scrim`, faded
over `EditLook.ScrimMs`), on top of edit mode's dim of the display the bars are lifted over. Gone,
with `EditView.Locked` and `Scene.Dimmed`: the bars and places look as they do in edit mode with no
folder open. They are still locked (§213) — a press, a drag, a lasso, a right click and the keys but
Escape and Ctrl+V do nothing on them, and nothing lights under the pointer but the folder's face —
and they still stand just under the folder's window (`KeepBarsUnderFolder`, §247), which is clear
over them but for the guide lines the person asked to run through them; that is unchanged.

**The face is itself.** The folder's face on the bar is drawn as it is — its cells, its card where it
has one — in edit mode's selected ring, since the click that opened it selected it (§260), and with
edit mode's hover under the pointer: the one block of a locked bar that lights. Gone: the accent over
its edit block, its hover and pressed fills, the × on it (`Scene.CloseFace`, `BuildCloseFace`,
`closeFaces`, `CloseShown`, `Scene.Over`, `EditView.Closes`, `CloseHot`, `ClosePressed`) and its
tooltip (`Dock.FaceTip`, `FolderFlyout.FaceTip`). A click on it still closes the folder by Escape's
path (`DockWindow.LockedPressed`, `CloseReleased`, `EditClicks.OnLocked`, §260's double-click guard
kept): the button closes what it opened, as a second click on a folder at rest does.

**A red close button at the top.** Arranged, the folder has Windows 11's close caption button on its
own again, as §213 had it, but red at rest (`FolderFlyout.CloseBox`, `PaintClose`, `DrawClose`,
`CloseColours`): a 32 DIP square, 4 DIP corners, ChromeClose (E8BB, `Dock.GlyphCloseFolder`) at 10
DIPs in white on `#C42B1C`, the caption button's red (`CloseRed`); under the pointer the red at 90 %
and pressed at 80 %, as an accent button's secondary and tertiary fills are. High contrast has no
red: at rest the button face (the window colour) with its rim and the text's ×, under the pointer and
pressed the highlight and its text. It stands outside the lists at their top right, flush with the
lists' box, centred on the "+" row's line (18 DIPs off the panel) and clear of every column's
buttons — top left in Arabic and Urdu; on a top bar under the lists' bottom right, the side away from
the bar where the "+" row is (the folder's top there is against the bar, with no room) — kept on the
screen and off the bars as the columns' buttons are (`KeepIn`, `Visible`). It takes the pointer where
the window otherwise lets it through (`TargetAt`, `PassesThrough`). Under the pointer it says "Close
folder" (`dock.widgetMenu.closeFolder`, no new words) after the usual moment, off its side away from
the bar, or its other side where the work area has no room there (`CloseTip`). A click is
`FolderFlyoutAction.CloseAsked`, which the dock takes Escape's path for (`EscapeTo(EditEscape.CloseFolder)`):
the folder closes, the display's edit bar comes back, edit mode stays on. Pressed and let go off it,
nothing. At rest a folder has no close button, as before: it is a flyout, closed by a click elsewhere,
Escape or its button, as Windows' flyouts are.

Tests: `FolderEditClickTests.TheArrangedFolderHasARedCloseButtonAtItsTop` (a bottom and a top bar:
its size, its side away from the bar on the "+" row's line, flush right, clear of the columns'
buttons; rest, hover and pressed; "Close folder" clear of it; let go off it nothing, a click
`CloseAsked`; at rest none), `TheCloseButtonIsRedAndHighContrastsSystemColours`,
`TheColumnsHaveTheirPlus` (was `TheColumnsHaveTheirPlusAndTheFolderNoCross`);
`EditClickTests.ALockedBarTakesOnlyAPressOnTheFoldersFace` (`CloseAsked` goes Escape's way; the scene
has no dim and no close face); `EditedDisplay` with a folder (`editmode-folder-*`, `editbar-*-folder`):
the face selected and drawn as itself — under a quarter of its pixels the accent — the red button on
the screen and off every bar, red a quarter in and white at its middle in the picture, its tip, its
press and its click. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<dark|light>-150`
— the taskbar undimmed, the clock's face as itself in its ring, the red × at the folder's top right
(bottom right on a top bar) under the pointer, "Close folder" by it. By hand: in edit mode click a
folder (the taskbar stays bright, its face shows the clock, a red × at the folder's top right); hover
it ("Close folder"), press and drag off (nothing), click it (the folder closes, the edit bar comes
back); open it again and click its face (it closes too), and Escape; a top bar (the × under the
folder); high contrast (the button face, the highlight under the pointer).

## 268. Settings levels in place of the menu's rows, for the markets widget: an experiment (2026-10-20)

The person: *"i want to try to swap the settings in place so that for the settings it does not open a
new submenu for each level. i mean the "inline" settings. but do this independent of the other changes
as i just want to be able to try it out, also just implement this for the stock widget for now."*

**An experiment, on its own branch.** This lives on `experiment/inline-settings`, cut from master at
§260 and kept apart from the work after it, to be tried by hand; it is not merged unless the person asks.
It is switched on for one menu alone: a markets widget's (§253, §258), on the bar or as a folder's line
(`Dock.InlineMenu`, `Pending.Inline`, `Flyout.Inline`). Every other menu — every other widget's, a
folder's faces, the bar's, a jump list — cascades exactly as §246 has it.

**A level in place** (`Flyout.Inline.cs`). In an inline menu a row with a submenu — clicked, Right or
Enter on it, Narrator's Invoke — opens no window beside the menu: the menu's one window shows the level
instead, as Windows 11's quick settings open a page ("< Sound output") and a phone's settings a screen.
Its first row is its head, the back arrow (Segoe Fluent's Back, E72B, `PageHeadTile.BackGlyph`, the one
the folder's pages start with; Forward, E72A, in a mirrored menu) and the level's name in the semibold, a
rule under it; under that the very rows the submenu would have had, as deep as they go — a level opened
from a level opens in place again. Nothing of the machinery is markets': the root menu keeps the open path
(`levels`, each the row it opened from and the scroll under it) and shows the deepest level's rows as its
own, so its keys, its fields, its controls, its ticks and what it tells the dock are a submenu's as they
were.

**Back.** A click on the head, **Escape**, **Backspace**, **Left** (Right in a mirrored menu) or the
mouse's back button shows the level under it again, the row it opened from lit and scrolled where it was.
Escape goes back rather than closing, as it shuts a cascading submenu before the menu (§246); on the
menu's own rows it closes the menu. Whatever has the keys hears them first: a field its Backspace and its
arrows, a stepper and the segments (§260) their Left. A line of text's level (the amount owned, the name
on the bar) still shuts by Enter, keeping what was typed, or by Escape, giving it back (`CloseLevel` goes
back); a search's level (the symbol, §258) opens whole, its field with the keys, its rows before anything
is typed and the service's answer once it is in, and Escape there gives the words back, then lets the keys
go, then goes back. Words typed and left in a field are kept as the level is left, as they are when a
submenu shuts.

**Where it stands.** The window stays. Its width is the widget menu's one width (§230); its height the
level's, kept from the edge of the panel nearer the work area's: the foot of a menu over a bar at the
bottom, so a taller level grows up from the bar and never over it, the top of one under a bar at the top;
inside the work area as a Refresh keeps a menu (`FlyoutHost.Held`, §226). A level is never placed afresh
(`MenuSides`, `Roomiest`): every level keeps the placement the menu's first showing took, so it never moves
to the widget's other side, and a long level scrolls in the room that side has.

**The slide.** The level's rows come in 16 DIP from the way they go — in from the end, back from the
start — over 167 ms, decelerating (`Flyout.SlideIn`), where Windows' animations are on. Only their offset
moves, never their opacity: `FlyoutHost.Open` animates no opening because DWM can stop every app's
animations, which left popups unseen; stopped here, the rows are where they belong or 16 DIP off it.

**A Refresh** (whoever showed the menu showing it again after a pick, `Flyout.Refresh`) finds the open
levels again in the tree as it is now by their rows (`MenuKeeps.Again`) and shows the deepest in place,
its lit row and scroll kept; a level whose row is gone falls back to the deepest found.

Rough: the head is a row (it is lit under the pointer and the keys stop on it) rather than a page's title
with a button; Narrator reads it by the level's name alone, not as "Back"; an icon picker's level (§249),
whose field stands pinned over its tiles, would put the head under that field's clip — no markets row has
one, so it is untried.

Tests: `InlineMenuTests` — `OnlyAMarketsWidgetsMenuOpensInPlace`; `AClickSwapsTheRowsInPlaceAndTheHeadGoesBack`
(the chart range's level in the one window, its head and its choices, its left, right and foot where the
menu's were; a pick keeps the level and a Refresh moves the tick; the head goes back, the range lit, the
menu as it was), `TheKeysGoInAndBack` (Right, Enter and Space in, onto the first row; Left, Backspace and
Escape back; Enter on the head; Escape then closes), `LevelsGoAsDeepAsTheyGoAndARefreshKeepsThem` (three
deep and back a level at a time; a Refresh keeps the deepest and its lit row; one without the level's row
falls back), `TheSymbolsSearchGetsItsAnswerInPlace` (the keys at once, its own rows, "eur"'s seven, the
panel's size kept; three Escapes back), `EnterKeepsTheAmountAndGoesBack` ("2,5" kept as 2.5),
`AnotherMenuStillCascades`. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `inline-markets-top-*`, `inline-markets-range-*`
(the range's level, a choice under the pointer), `inline-markets-search-*` ("eur" typed). By hand: in edit
mode right-click a markets widget, click Chart range, Style and Symbol (the menu stays where it is; its rows
slide in), go back by the arrow, Escape, Backspace and Left; search "eur" and pick a pair; type an amount
owned and press Enter; right-click a clock and see its submenus still open beside the menu.

## 269. Keep awake (2026-10-20) — its screen always kept on, no "Keep the screen on", since §586 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the setting to keep awake the computer should also be added as widget to karpo"*. A
switch in the spirit of PowerToys Awake: while it is on, Windows' idle timer does not put the PC to
sleep, and, where asked, does not turn the screen off either.

**The widget.** `WidgetInfos.KeepAwake` (`keepAwake`, `QuickSwitch.KeepAwake`, a toggle: `Flips`,
"Keep awake on/off" in the add list), System, Segoe Fluent Icons' coffee cup (EC32), as PowerToys
Awake's tray icon is a cup; its page is Windows' Power & battery (`ms-settings:powersleep`, the
battery's own link), where the timeouts themselves are. It is every form a one-button switch has, drawn
by `SwitchIsland` as the others: a button on the bar (`BarKind.KeepAwake`, `Toggle`), the accent
behind the cup while it is on, its name beside it with "Show its name"; a folder's line
(`ListKind.KeepAwake`, `Switch`), its switch at the end; a toggle of a toggles row (`Toggle.KeepAwake`,
the last of `Toggles.All`, not in a new row's defaults: it is no tile of Windows' quick settings). The
add list has it in Quick settings beside energy saver (Again) and at home in Battery and power after
the power mode (`AddTree`). Its tooltip says "Keep awake: on", or a timed one's time left ("Keep awake:
40 min left"), over what a click does ("Keeps this PC from going to sleep by itself", "…, and its
screen on"); a line one row tall says the time left beside its name, as Wi-Fi's network is said
(`SwitchIsland.LineOf`), and a line three rows tall says it large where the state is.

**How it keeps the PC awake** (`Karpo.Dock\QuickSettings\Services\KeepAwake.cs`). A power request
of Karpo's own: `PowerCreateRequest` with a simple reason string, "Keep awake is on in Karpo" in
Karpo's language, then `PowerSetRequest(PowerRequestSystemRequired)`, and
`PowerRequestDisplayRequired` while the screen is kept on (`PowerRequest`, TerraFX's bindings, as the
dock's other calls). Not `SetThreadExecutionState`, which PowerToys Awake uses: a request says who and
why in `powercfg /requests` (Karpo.exe under SYSTEM, and DISPLAY, with its reason), where an execution
state is a bare process; it belongs to a handle, not to a thread, so the dock's thread, a menu's pick
and the pool's timer that ends a timed one can each set or clear it, where `ES_CONTINUOUS` holds only
while the thread that set it lives and would want a thread kept for it; and it ends with its handle —
cleared and closed when it is turned off, when its time is up and when the last widget for it goes
(`KeepAwake.Leave`), and closed by Windows with the process, so a Karpo that exits or crashes keeps
nothing awake. Nothing of Windows' power plan or settings is changed, and the lid, the power button
and Start's Sleep still put the PC to sleep.

**One service.** `KeepAwake` (one per thread, as do not disturb's: the dock's one thread has the one
every widget, toggle and menu shares) holds whether it is on, for how long (`Minutes`, `Left`) and the
screen; `KeepAwakeSwitch` is the widget's `IQuickSwitch` over it (`QuickSwitches.Windows`), keeping
nothing of its own. A timed one's time is a `TimeProvider` timer on the pool, set for the next whole
minute of what it has left (said in minutes rounded up, BatteryText's words: "1 h 20 min", "1 min"),
which tells the widgets each minute and lets go at the end. Where Windows refuses, it stays off,
counts a refusal (the click's wait ends, §182) and the tooltip says "Windows didn't let Karpo keep this
PC awake." until the next. A run that may not reach the person's world (every test, the smoke) is
given `NoRequest`, and `QuickSwitches.For` stands the real switch down there as for every switch.

**Not kept.** Whether it is on is written nowhere: a Karpo started again starts with it off, as
PowerToys Awake starts passive, so no file left behind keeps a PC awake that nobody remembers asking.
What a click turns on is the widget's (`SwitchOptions.AwakeMinutes`, `AwakeScreen`; neither written at
its default, a length it does not offer read as until turned off, another switch's dropped:
`WidgetItem.Normalize`): edit mode's menu has "How long" (Until turned off, the default; For 30
minutes; For 1 hour; For 2 hours; For 4 hours — `KeepAwakeLengths`) and "Keep the screen on" (off),
each with its icon (§249: the cup, the stopwatch E916, clocks E823, E917 and the history clock E81C;
the monitor E7F4).

**Its menu at rest** (§257: its acts, nothing of edit mode's), on the bar and as a line alike
(`Dock.AwakeActs`, `WidgetAct.AwakeFor`, `WidgetAct.AwakeScreen`): the five lengths (no heading: a
widget's menu opens on an act), the one running ticked, each turning it on from now for that long (the screen as it is kept now, or
from off as the widget says); a rule; "Keep the screen on", ticked while it is, greyed while keep awake
is off; "Power and battery settings in Windows". The lengths and the screen keep the menu open, the
tick moving (`MenuKeeps`), and none closes a folder (`HandsAway`). Its on and off are the click's,
as for every switch. A bar entry's rows are now worked on the entry's own island (`BarMenuRows`'
`widget`), which is how a length picked from off reads the widget's screen. 15 new keys
(`core.widget.keepAwake.*`, `dock.quick.keepAwake.*`, `settings.widget.awakeLength.header`) in all 30
languages.

Tests: `KeepAwakeTests` — in the catalogue on both pages, in Quick settings after energy saver and in
Battery and power, a toggle, the cup, Windows' own switch a `KeepAwakeSwitch`; a click holds the
request, the next lets it go; the widget's screen held, its menu taking it off while it runs and
nothing while off; a timed one says 30, 29 … 1 min left, told each minute, and lets go at its end,
four hours "4 h", another length from now, until turned off never ending; a refusal leaves it off and
says so; the last widget gone turns it off, one never started counts for nothing; only the widget's
options in the file, and turning it on writes nothing; the rest menu's rows (the same on the bar and in a folder), icons, ticks, greying, a
length and the screen picked, its page; edit mode's two rows and what they write; Windows' own
`PowerRequest` held, the screen added and taken off, and let go — its handle closed and no longer a
request Windows knows (`TheRealRequestIsLetGo`, the one test that holds a real request, for a few
milliseconds); the line and the tooltip say the time left. All the others run on a request and a clock
of the test's own. The registry tables follow (`SectionsTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`,
`ListGutterTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`, `SwitchWidgetTests`), and so do `WidgetMenuTests` (a row for
each length, its acts staying in Karpo), `MenuKeepsTests` and `OptionRowsTests` (the two options' rows). Pictures:
`keep-awake-bar-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (off, on, with its name, at a 40 and a 48 DIP bar),
`keep-awake-lines-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (off, on, timed with 40 min left, three rows tall with
the screen kept on, at 100 % and 225 % text), `keep-awake-menu-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.
By hand: add Keep awake to the bar, click it and run `powercfg /requests` in an elevated prompt
(Karpo.exe under SYSTEM with its reason; under DISPLAY too with the screen kept on); pick "For 30
minutes" from its menu and watch the tooltip count down; turn it off, and `powercfg /requests` lists
nothing of Karpo's; quit Karpo while it is on, and nothing is left.

## 270. A style shows the same thing; the output and input devices are widgets of their own again (2026-10-20)

The person: *"fix style configuration, a style should not be input or output device, these dont show the
same type of data, a style should be a weather widget that shows the weather in different styles like a
grid, row, or list, or just for todays weather. fix this everywhere, only same data shown (or similar
data, sometimes more verbose or less verbose) should be combined in the style property."*

**The rule.** A style only switches between drawings of one subject: the same data, or the same data
drawn more or less fully. What a widget is *of* — which device, which part of the PC — is never a style:
it is a widget of its own, or a choice of its own beside the style, as the performance widget's reading
has been since §229. **This supersedes §209's Sound row** (Volume, Output device, Input device, Volume
mixer as one widget's styles) and its add list of one sound row.

**The audit** — every choice called Style, or drawn with the Style brush (§249), on a line, a face, a
menu or a Settings page:

| Where | Widget or thing | Its styles | Kept or split | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line | Calendar (`calendar`) | Agenda, Day's events, Day, Week, Month, Year | kept | One calendar, its days and their events: listed (the agenda, a day's), laid on hours (a day, a week), a month's grid, a year's (its days alone, the least of it). Every one follows the folder's day (§241). |
| Line | Weather (`weather`) | **Today** (was "Now"), Hourly, Daily | kept, one renamed | One place's weather, one `weather` record: today's — the conditions now with the day's high and low —, the next hours in a row over their curve, the days ahead in a list, a row a day. "Now" said less than the line shows; it is the person's "just for todays weather". There is no grid, and none was made up. |
| Line | Sound (`sound`), now **Volume** | Volume, Volume mixer | kept; **split by §317** | How loud it plays: one level, the output's, or app by app, each with its level and mute — the same quantity and the same acts (drag, wheel, mute), the mixer the more verbose. Windows' own volume mixer is the system's level over the apps'. §317: the person sees two widgets (the system's level, each app's), so `soundVolume` and `soundMixer` are widgets of their own and `sound` is gone. |
| Line | Sound | Output device, Input device | **split** | Which device plays and which one listens: lists of devices to pick, no level, and the microphones not even the same direction. Widgets of their own again, `soundOutput` and `soundInput`, as before §209. |
| Line | Performance (`performance`) | Graph, Numbers, Details | kept; **Details split by §317** | How one reading is shown (§229); what it measures is its Reading, no style. §317: the details are other facts, not the load drawn another way: **Performance details** (`performanceDetails`), a widget of its own with the Reading choice. |
| Line | Clock (`clock`) | Clock, Date, Time and date | kept; **Date split by §317** | Now, in the line's zone (one `clock` record, §230): the time, the date, or the time with its seconds over the date. §317: the date's click sets the folder's day: **Today's date** (`dateHeader`), a widget of its own. |
| Line, face | Markets · Style | Price, change and chart; Price only (Rate… for a pair); Converter | kept | One symbol's price: with its change and chart, alone, or — a pair's only — the rate worked out for an amount. |
| Line, face | Markets · Chart | Area, Line, Candles | kept | One price history drawn three ways; the candles add each stretch's open, high and low. |
| Line of items | Items (`ItemStyles`) | size, parts | kept | How the same items are drawn. |
| Separator | Style | Line, Dot, Space only | kept | No data: how the split is drawn (§250). |
| Face | Calendar · Look | The date as text, a calendar page | kept | Today's date. |
| Face | Weather · Look | Simple, Detailed, 3-day forecast, As Windows | kept | One place's weather, less or more of it. |
| Face | Tides · Show | The next tide, with its height, how soon, the sea now | kept | One place's tides. |

Not styles, and left as they are: the meeting face's Show (which meeting — today's next, the next any
day, only shortly before: a filter, not a drawing, and not called a style), the faces' widths, and the
performance faces, one per reading as §229 kept them.

**What the sound widget became.** One widget called **Volume** (`WidgetStyles.Sound`; its file word stays
`sound`, so every volume and mixer line reads and writes as it did), its styles Volume (first) and Volume
mixer. Its add list row is "Volume", found by its own words and its styles' ("mixer", "volume mixer",
and "sound", its name until now); its menu and its page offer Style ▸ Volume, Volume mixer, and the
page's title is "Volume · Volume mixer". **Output device** (`soundOutput`) and **Input device**
(`soundInput`) are widgets of one style each, rows of their own beside it in Add ▸ Music and sound
(`AddTree`), with the names, icons, lines and search words they had before §209
(`core.widget.soundOutput.*`, `core.widget.soundInput.*`, which stayed): "microphone" finds the input
device and no longer the volume. Their menus and pages have no Style row. Their hidden devices are
theirs alone (`WidgetItem.HidesDevices`): a volume line no longer keeps a list of hidden devices it could
only use as another widget. The volume slider on the bar (`volume`, "Volume slider") is unchanged.

**In code.** `StyledWidget.SplitOff` holds the words of styles a widget had that are widgets of their own
now — the sound widget's `output` (`ListKind.SoundOutput`) and `input` (`ListKind.SoundInput`) — read by
`WidgetStyles.SplitOffOf(kind, style)` and `WidgetStyles.FormWord`, so a style word no longer offered
reads as what it showed and never falls to the widget's first style. `WidgetStyles.Of(ListKind.SoundOutput)`
is null, so the file's word is the form's own (`CellItem.FileKind`, no `FileStyle`), and every place that
asks — the add list (`Catalogue`), the Style row (`OptionRows`), the page's title (`IslandTitles`),
`Restyle` — treats it as any widget of one style. Nothing draws, measures or acts differently: the forms
and their records are §209's.

**The file: a migration, no reset, no shape change.** A line written `"kind": "sound", "style": "output"`
(or `"input"`, either key first) reads as the output devices (the microphones) and is written back once
as `"kind": "soundOutput"` (`"soundInput"`) with no style, in place: its id, its place in its list, its
height (fixed or automatic, its rows) and its hidden devices as they were. It is §209's
carrying over (`LineMigrations.MergeStyles`, `CellItem.ReadInOldWords`), which notes a line read as a
split-off style (`CellItem.ReadAsSplitOff`) and records `soundDevices` (`LineMigrations.StylesSplit`) in
`Config.Migrated` once, beside `widgetStyles`. The forms' own words from before §209 (`soundOutput`,
`soundInput`) are today's words again and need nothing; `"sound"` alone and with `"mixer"` are as they
were. A build from before this one reads `soundOutput` and `soundInput` as its sound widget's output and
input styles (form words §209 reads forever), so a file written now loses nothing going back.

**Presets** say the devices by their own words: the sound folder (`soundGroup`), the media center, and
quick settings' sound page (`FolderPages`).

**Words**, in all 30 languages: `core.styled.sound.title` is each language's "Volume" (the volume line's
own, `core.widget.soundVolume.title`); its line ("The volume, or each app's volume") and search words
(audio, speakers, and "sound", its name before) are new; `core.widgetStyle.weather.now` is "Today" (each
language's `widget.weather.today`), and the weather's line says the shapes ("Today's weather, the next
hours in a row, or the days ahead in a list"); `core.widgetStyle.sound.output` and `.input` are gone.
`UntranslatedTests.Same`: "Volume" is French, Italian, Dutch, Indonesian and Brazilian Portuguese
Windows' own word; German's widget is no longer "Sound".

Tests: `StylesSameDataTests` — every style of every widget listed with what it shows and a widget's
styles one subject, none a device picker (a new style must be listed first); the styles and titles the
audit leaves; `"sound"` with `"output"` and `"input"` written as their own widgets in place (id, place,
height, hidden devices; marked once; nothing more on a second read), the style before the kind, the
devices' own words and the volume's and mixer's needing nothing, §209's sound folder the same lines;
the add list's Output device and Input device rows (name, icon, line, words, in the tree) and the Volume
row found by "mixer" and not by "microphone"; a volume line's Style submenu Volume and Volume mixer, the
devices' menus without one; the presets and the sound page in the devices' words. `WidgetStylesTests`
(the sound's options, the widgets' titles), `WidgetItemTests` (the file in today's words: the
microphones as `soundInput`), `SoundPartsTests.HiddenDevicesAreTheDeviceLinesAlone` (the mixer keeps
none now), `AddListSearchTests.AResultSaysWhereItIs` ("volume mixer" finds Volume),
`UntranslatedTests`. By hand: Add ▸ Music and sound has Volume, Output device and Input device; a
volume line's menu ▸ Style lists Volume and Volume mixer only; a file with `"sound"`, `"style": "input"`
opens as the microphones, where it stood, and is saved as `soundInput`.

## 271. Every widget's menu opens its levels in place; a search lists all it finds (2026-10-22)

The person: *"on a new branch online i tested the inlined menu style. i want you to port all the widgets
to the inline menu style now. the lists with the x entries shown should not be limited anymore, they
should show all the items with the fixed height so that the list is just scrollable in the end."*

**One rule, every settings menu.** This supersedes §268's "for the markets widget alone": every menu that
Configures (`Dock.ShowFlyout`: a widget's menu, `Topic.LayoutEditor`) opens a row's submenu in place of
its rows (`Flyout.Inline.cs`), as §268 has it — edit mode's menu of every bar widget and every pin, of a
folder's line, and of a folder with its faces, where a face's row opens its face's settings in place under
its name. Their menus at rest are of the same topic and take the same rule; none of their rows has a
submenu. `Dock.InlineMenu`, `Pending.Inline` and `Flyout.Inline` are gone: the rule is `Configures`, the
flag that already gave these menus their one width (§230). The face's own heading on its level (§230:
"always show the name of the face … on the second level") went with it: the level's head names it.

**What still cascades.** A menu of commands whose submenus Windows itself opens beside it: the add list's
subjects (Windows' "New ›", §7b) and Start's quick links' "Shut down or sign out ›" (Win+X's). A jump
list, the bar's own menu, a tray icon's and the rest have no submenus. So the cascade stays, but only
what those menus use of it: a submenu's rows are commands, never a field, a control or a row that stays.
What served a settings submenu alone is gone — a control's Adjust posted up to the root (`Adjusted`), the
field's keys handed down the open submenus (`FieldHolder`, `KeysOwner`, `FieldStateOf`), a field's level
shown again beside its row (`ReshowSubmenu`), `CloseLevel`'s submenu, `ControlKey`'s hand-off, a Refresh
that kept every level of submenu open (`keepSubmenu` and its path), `StaysOn` walking the submenus, and
the tests' `HotIdDeepest`, `DeepestLevel` and `FieldShowingIn`. A Refresh is one now: the open levels
found again in the tree, shown where the menu stands, from the edge nearer the work area's (§268).

**The head.** Its tooltip and what Narrator calls it is "Back" (`dock.page.back`, a folder page's back
button's word: no new string), a button; the menu is named for the level.

**What stands still.** A level's head and its rule stand at its top while its rows scroll under them,
and on a search's level its field and what stands over it (a place's device switch), on an icon
picker's its field (`Flyout.pinned`, §249's one pinned field made a band): the pointer over the band
finds only its rows, the keys scroll a row out from under it, and the scroll indicator runs beside the
rows under it. An icon picker's head no longer falls under its field's clip (§268's rough edge).

**Every result, one room.** §228's five results and "Show more (N)" are gone (`MenuSearch.Few`, `Shown`,
`Hidden`, `Expanded`, `ShowAll`; the menu's `fieldMores`, `fieldSpacers`, `IsFieldSpacer`,
`FieldSpacerHeight`; `dock.edit.showMore` in all 30 languages). A search's level is one height: its head,
its field and six rows' room (`Flyout.SearchRows`, §228's five and its "Show more" row), every result a
row and the rest a scroll away; it keeps that height with nothing typed, while typing, with nothing found
and greyed (the device's location on), so the menu never changes size as the person types, and a key
typed scrolls it back to its top. An icon picker's level is its head, its field and `PickerTilesDip`
(360 DIP, nine lines of tiles; §249's 400 DIP held the field and the tiles). The finders' own caps that
served "Show more" went too: a zone's search lists every zone that matches (40 before), the holiday
countries every country (40 before). `MenuSearch.Most` (200) stays, above every zone Windows has; what a
service is asked for (places, ESPN's 20 teams, Yahoo's 8 symbols) and the few pairs and coins a markets
search makes of the words alone are the search's, not a list cut short. A widget's own menu at rest lists
its sound devices and apps (12) and its drives (8) as Windows' own menus do; no setting is cut.

Tests: `InlineMenuTests` — `EveryWidgetsMenuOpensItsLevelsInPlace` (every bar and list widget's edit
menu, a folder's with three faces: every row with a submenu, and every such row on its level, opens in
place in the one window under its head, and the head goes back, the row lit), `AMenuThatIsNoWidgetsStillCascades`,
`AClickSwapsTheRowsInPlaceAndTheHeadGoesBack`, `TheKeysAndTheBackButtonGoInAndBack` (Right, Enter, Space
in; Left, Backspace, Escape and XBUTTON1 back), `LevelsGoAsDeepAsTheyGoAndARefreshKeepsThem`,
`AFolderFaceOpensItsSettingsInPlace`, `TheSymbolsSearchGetsItsAnswerInPlace` (seven found, seven rows),
`EnterKeepsTheAmountAndGoesBack`, `AZonesLevelShowsEveryZoneInTheRoomItKeeps` (every zone a row, the
level's height the head, the field and six rows; the wheel scrolls the zones under the head and the
field, which stay put and alone take the pointer; typing keeps the panel), `AnIconPickersHeadAndFieldStandOverItsTiles`;
`MenuValuesTests.ASearchsLevelKeepsOneHeightAndShowsEveryResult` (twelve found, the keys down to the last
scroll the level, the field where it stood), `MenuSearchTests.EveryRowFoundIsShown`; the menus' tests on
levels in place (`MenuKeepsTests`, `MenuFieldTests`, `MenuPickersTests`, `MenuIconsTests`,
`OptionMenuTests`, `AlignSegmentsTests`, `TrayMenuRowsTests`, `MenuCleanupTests`). Pictures (150 %, dark
and light): `inline-markets-top-*`, `inline-markets-range-*`, `inline-markets-search-*`,
`inline-zones-scrolled-*`, `inline-folder-top-*`, `inline-folder-clock-*`, `inline-folder-picker-*`,
`menu-values-place-scrolled-*`. By hand: in edit mode right-click a clock, a weather widget, a folder and a
folder's line; open a level, a level of it, and go back by the arrow, Escape, Backspace, Left and the
mouse's back button; type in a time zone's search and see the menu keep its size, every zone a scroll
away under the field; open a folder's icon face's icon picker and scroll its tiles under its head and
field; open a subject of the add list and the power row of Start's right-click menu and see them still
open beside.

## 272. One reconcile for the bars, their strips, full screen apps and Explorer's taskbar (2026-10-22)

The person: *"an application like anno 1800 does not properly work with karpo, when it want to go into
fullscreen mode it does not work"* and *"the karpo taskbar locking needs to be bullet proof in every
scenario ... there should be zero bugs for the hiding / showing of the karpo bar, also the windows
taskbar ... in the end i want it working everywhere but with the most simplest solution. in general if
you need timers anywhere try to solve it differently. if you do need them then let me know."*

**Why Anno 1800 could not go full screen.** appbar.log, 2026-10-21 12:23:23 and 13:08:30: `woke: the
displays changed`, then `[DISPLAY1] setpos Bottom 0,439..640,480`, and a second later the display back at
3840x2160 (`setpos Bottom 0,2098..3840,2160`), twice in a row at 12:23. Anno's exclusive full screen
switches the display to a mode of its own (640x480 while it starts, then its resolution). Three things
then worked against it:
- *The full screen check measured the wrong display.* The bar made way only on the shell's
  ABN_FULLSCREENAPP, and only where the window in front covered the display *as the last arrange had
  listed it*: the 640x480 game against 3840x2160 never covered it, so the bar never made way.
- *The change of mode was taken for a change of displays.* The arrange laid the bar out on the game's
  mode — `SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST)`, in front of the game —, asked for its strip there (the setpos
  above), and the wake that came with it looked at the work area every half second, ready to set it with
  SPI_SETWORKAREA.
- *Nothing looked again.* ABN_FULLSCREENAPP comes once; after the arrange nothing asked whether the
  game was still in front.

A window in front of an exclusive full screen game, or a work area moved under it, makes it give the
display up; the mode went back, the game with it.

**The model.** Per display: whether it has a full screen app (its *front window* — the last app
window that came to the front on it — shown, not minimized or cloaked, an app's in an app's band, and
covering the display as it is now; or, while Windows says a Direct3D app runs full screen
(`SHQueryUserNotificationState`, QUNS_RUNNING_D3D_FULL_SCREEN), the foreground window's display whatever
its rectangle says on the way into its mode; never a maximized window with a caption); each bar shown or
out of the way; the strip each bar holds and whether the work area leaves it out. Globally: whether
Explorer's taskbar is hidden and auto-hidden, and whether edit mode is on (it shows every bar). What
should be comes from the settings, the displays and the full screen apps; what is, from the work areas
(`GetMonitorInfo`), Explorer (`ABM_GETSTATE`, its windows) and the bars' windows.

**The one reconcile** (`BarKeeper.Reconcile`), on events only:

| From | Event | Stir |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | WM_DISPLAYCHANGE, WM_DPICHANGED | Displays, Scale — the full screen look runs at once, before the arrange lays anything out |
| Windows | resume (PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC), unlock (WTS_SESSION_UNLOCK), a display lit (GUID_SESSION_DISPLAY_STATUS on) | Resumed, Unlocked, DisplayLit |
| Windows | TaskbarCreated | ExplorerBack: every bar registered again |
| Windows | WM_SETTINGCHANGE(SPI_SETWORKAREA), ABN_POSCHANGED, ABN_STATECHANGE | WorkArea, Neighbours |
| Windows | EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND; the watched windows' DESTROY, SHOW, HIDE, LOCATIONCHANGE; ABN_FULLSCREENAPP (a hint, never the truth) | Front, Moved |
| Karpo | start, an arrange, a setting changed, edit mode on or off | Start, Build, Settings |

A *disturbance* (start, displays, scale, resume, unlock, a display lit, Explorer back, settings) is what
can change a work area without a word to the bars: it makes every repair budget whole and asks for one
settle. The rest are consequences of a change, often Karpo's own, and never refill a budget — so a shell
that puts the whole screen back at every repair is never fought for ever. A reconcile, in order:
1. **Full screen** (`BarKeeper.Look`): each display's front window against the display as it is now; a
   display that turned full screen has its bars hidden at once — not only put behind, so a game gets
   independent flip — with what they had open closed (flyouts, folders, the window list, tooltips); one
   that stopped being full screen has them laid out on the display as it is then (`Remeasure`), shown
   without the activation, and looked after as after a disturbance.
2. **Strips:** each bar not on a full screen display pushes what it should hold (`Reserve`: only a
   change is sent), then looks at its work area (`AppbarHolder.Verify`, asking the shell nothing). A
   strip missing, left short (moved out towards the edge and the move dropped), or a registration
   refused, is repaired by a ladder — the position again; after that registered again, the position,
   and the work area set directly (SPI_SETWORKAREA, the work area less the strip, never larger than the
   shell's) — within a budget: at most 4 repairs a bar a minute, and none within a second of the last
   thing sent for it (the settle shows whether that took), so the several notices one change brings
   never spend the budget in a moment.
3. **Explorer's taskbar** (`IExplorerTaskbar`): hidden while "Hide the Windows taskbar" is on and the
   session is not ending, put back as the person had it otherwise (`Taskbar.TakeOver`, `PutBack`, the
   record and StuckRects3 as §23.2 has them); after an Explorer restart its new taskbar is auto-hidden
   again (`Taskbar.Rehide` — a new Explorer comes up with the person's own state) and hidden; after the
   takeover every strip is asked for again, on the edge. The strips come first, so at the takeover each
   bar holds its strip beside the taskbar before the taskbar lets go of its own: no display is ever
   without one.

A display with a full screen app is never touched: no build (`DockWindow.Build` marks it stale), no
topmost, no `Peek`, no strip, no registration (an Explorer restart meanwhile registers it once the app is
gone, `AppbarHolder.Lost`), no work area, and nothing anywhere activates a window. A change of display
mode never rebuilds what the game's display shows.

**Timers.** One is left: `RECONCILE`, one-shot, 1 s (`BarKeeper.SettleMs`), armed by a reconcile that
sent something or followed a disturbance, and again only where its own look sent something. It is needed
because Explorer can take an ABM_SETPOS and not act on it, and a display can come back with its work area
whole, without a word (§212's dark screens): no event says so. While all is well nothing runs at all —
no look every two seconds any more. Gone: the per-bar check (every 0.5 s for 15 s after a wake, every
2 s after that, for ever, with a 1–30 s and 5 min backoff), the 50 ms poll for 5 s at the takeover, the
wake bursts, `AwaitTakeOver`/`TakeOver`/`Waiting`, `FullscreenChanged`, `MakesWayForFullscreen` and
`fullscreenLater`. Left as they were, outside the reconcile: the sign-in wait for Explorer's tray (once,
before the bars, so Karpo's tray window never stands in Explorer's place as it starts), the show desktop
corner's 600 ms of keeping the bars over the desktop (now never over a full screen app), and the guard's
waits.

**Explorer restarting.** The end of the Explorer whose taskbar is hidden is waited for on the thread
pool (`RegisterWaitForSingleObject`, no polling); from then until its next taskbar is covered, one
WinEvent hook for every window shown anywhere hides that taskbar the moment it shows
(`Taskbar.ExplorerGone`), and TaskbarCreated's reconcile auto-hides and covers it again. Quitting, a
crash and a kill put the taskbar back as before (`Dispose`, the guard, the record); a kill of Karpo's
whole group in Task Manager also ends the guard, and the next start puts it back.

**The watch** (`FrontWatch`): EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND for every app, and for the threads of the
foreground window and each full screen display's front only, DESTROY/SHOW/HIDE and LOCATIONCHANGE —
never the focus and selection events an app's thread raises at every key; one message waiting at a
time. So a video full screen on one display keeps its bars away while the person works on the other,
and they come back the moment it leaves full screen, ends, or a window there comes to the front. The
desktop (Win+D) brings them back; Task view and Start over a game change nothing.

**The trace** (appbar.log), one line per change and per thing done, none while nothing changes:
`woke: …`, `[DISPLAYn] full screen app in front: <program> (<class>) at … on …[, Direct3D full screen];
its bars make way and are left alone`, `… full screen app gone: its bars come back`, `register`, `setpos`,
`NOT held: … (repair n) -> Position|Direct`, `work area … set to … directly`, `held again after n
repairs`, `… left as the shell has it until something changes`, `took over from Explorer's taskbar …`,
`Explorer's taskbar was not auto-hidden (a new Explorer) …`, `Explorer ended: …`.

Tests: `BarKeeperTests` on a made-up desktop (`BarWorld`: displays, an Explorer with an appbar list that
can stall, apply late, drop, refuse, reset the work area with or without a word, fight a work area set
directly, count its taskbar after it let go, restart; windows in front; the dock's message order and its
one timer) — start with Explorer ready, not there yet, auto-hidden by a killed Karpo, stalled, refusing;
the second display's takeover quirk; Explorer restarting; the setting off and on; the person's own
auto-hide; quit; crash; a dark screen; a display unplugged and back; resolution and scale; lock, resume,
a display lit; Explorer misbehaving every way; the bar to the top, hiding; a borderless game; Anno's
exclusive mode switch, with and without Direct3D's word; a video on the other display; minimized,
closed; the desktop and Task view; a maximized window; popups closing; edit mode; Karpo's own window in
front; the trace; an idle dock doing nothing for an hour. `BarKeeperPropertyTests`: 1000 random runs of
60 events each break no rule on the way (nothing sent for a full screen display, no bar over a full
screen app, no message loop, no settle that never stops) and end as they should, then stay quiet.
`AppbarHolderTests` (the ladder, the budget, the strip moved out, the shapes), `FullscreenTests`
(`Fills`, `Fronts`), `TaskbarStateTests` (`Rehide`), `NoActivationTests` (no activation in the
reconcile's code, MakeWay's show without it), `FrontWatchTests` (what is read off real windows on a
hidden desktop). A Direct3D swap chain in exclusive full screen can't be had in a test: it takes the
output of a display the person sees.

By hand: Anno 1800 in Fullscreen and in Windowed fullscreen — it goes and stays full screen, the bar gone
from its display and back after; Alt+Tab out and in; a video full screen on one display while working on
the other; restart Explorer (Task Manager ▸ Windows Explorer ▸ Restart) — its taskbar never shows, the
bars keep their strips; sleep and wake, a monitor switched off and on, unplugged and back; lock and
unlock; "Hide the Windows taskbar" off and on; quit Karpo, and end its process in Task Manager's Details
— the taskbar comes back as it was. appbar.log should show one line per change and nothing while idle.

## 273. Steam's tray icon came and went every three seconds: Karpo kept asking every app for its icons (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the steam icon is appearing and disappearing again. why is that? is that a steam issue? is
there a way to fix that?"*

**What was seen**, live, with nothing of Karpo's or Steam's touched: the dock's `tray-icons.json` had
Steam's icon (`steam.exe|1`) in it for 1.6 s and out of it for 1.4 s, every 3.0 s, for as long as it was
watched. A plain window listening for TaskbarCreated heard three to six of them at the start of every
one of those cycles, and the first `Shell_TrayWnd` in z-order switched from Karpo's tray window to
Explorer's hidden taskbar and back with each: Explorer's taskbar stepped in front a few ms after Steam's
icon came in, Karpo's window was put first again 30 to 60 ms later with a TaskbarCreated, Explorer's
stepped in front again, and so on until the burst ran out. appbar.log said Karpo's tray had passed
489 462 messages on to Explorer in seven hours.

**What Steam does**: on every TaskbarCreated it takes its icon away at once (NIM_DELETE) and adds it
again about 2.8 s after the last one it heard (uID 1, no GUID, its window the same throughout). On
Windows' own taskbar that is a blink after an Explorer restart, the only time Explorer says
TaskbarCreated, and never seen otherwise. Steam's way of answering, but not Steam's fault.

**What Karpo did**: apps find the tray by the first `Shell_TrayWnd` in z-order, and Explorer's hidden
taskbar puts itself in front of Karpo's tray window whenever it lays itself out again — an icon its
tray takes in or lets go (every call is passed on to it), its taskbar shown. `Tray.EnsureFirst` (§34; after
every arrange, every window coming to the front, a bar shown) put Karpo's window first again *and asked
every app for its icons* (TaskbarCreated) each time. Steam's answer was a delete and, 2.8 s later, an
add, which Explorer's tray took in, so its taskbar stepped in front, the next look asked again, and
Steam deleted its icon again: a loop, every three seconds, for ever. Karpo kept a deleted icon for the
grace (`TrayPictures.GraceMs`, 1.5 s, made for WhatsApp's in §51), shorter than Steam's 2.8 s: on, then off. Every
other app answered each burst too (WhatsApp's delete and add, everyone's adds), which is where the
messages went.

**Now**: the place is taken back without a word (`Tray.Raise`). The apps are asked once more only by the
first look after they were asked — at Karpo's start, after Explorer's taskbar was made again, for a new
icon size —, since answers to that asking may have reached Explorer alone while its taskbar stood in
front (the takeover hides it just after the start's asking). Never twice for one asking, so the asking
can't feed itself (`TrayFirst`, Karpo.Core: `Asked`, `Look` → nothing, raise, or ask again). No timer.

What is left: on those three askings Steam's icon still goes for about three seconds, as it does on
Windows' taskbar after an Explorer restart; at Karpo's start it simply comes three seconds after the
others. An icon an app adds in the moment Explorer's taskbar stands in front (tens of ms) reaches
Explorer alone, as before; a change to an icon Karpo doesn't know is refused, so most apps add it again.

Tests: `TrayFirstTests` (a first tray does nothing; one put behind is raised and nobody asked; only the
first look after an asking asks again, once; a look that finds the tray first ends it), `TraySteamTests`
(Steam's answer played through `Tray.Apply` on the tests' clock, Explorer's taskbar stepping in front
for every icon it takes in or lets go and the dock looking after each: the icon there for good from
Karpo's start, two askings in a minute; the rule before kept it coming and going, with more than ten).

By hand: watch Steam's icon on the bar for a minute — it stays. `tray-icons.json` (next to config.json)
is rewritten only when an icon comes or goes, not every 1.5 s. Restart Explorer: every icon comes back,
Steam's about three seconds after the rest.

## 274. A settings menu is one height on every level (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the height of the inline menu that changes should be constant for all of them, so that
navigating does not change its place or height"*. Since §268 each level shown in place was its own
height, kept from the foot over a bottom bar: going into a level or back moved the menu's top edge.

**One height for the tree.** As a menu that Configures opens, `Flyout.TallestLevel` measures every level
of its tree — its own rows (and its title), every row's level in place, as deep as they go, a search's at
its field and six rows' room, an icon picker's at its field and `PickerTilesDip` — as `Open` lays them
(`LevelHeight`: the rows' fill from their words' line height, a rule, a heading, the row of buttons, a
line of tiles, a row with its reason under it), and the menu is the tallest of them on every level, to the
most the room on its side of the screen holds (the placement it took: `MenuSides` and `Roomiest` are
given the tree's height, so the menu opens on a side with room for all of it). A shorter level's rows
stand at its top under its head, the rest of the menu empty; a level taller than the room scrolls in it.
Going in, going back, a field's results coming and going: the rect never changes.

**A Refresh** measures the tree again only where it is another (`measuredTree`; a search's answer shows
the same tree again) and the menu grows where the tree grew, its foot over the bar kept (§268), and never
shrinks while it is open; the next showing measures afresh.

**Gone:** the per-level sizing in `Open` — a search's and a picker's level's own height (`band` plus
`ListRoom`) over the rows' —; `ListRoom` now only says what such a level wants in the tree.
`PinnedThrough` and `ListRoom` tell a level by its head (`IsLevel`) rather than by the menu's state, so a
level not shown can be measured; `LevelRows` makes a level's rows for both.

Tests: `InlineMenuTests` — `EveryWidgetsMenuOpensItsLevelsInPlace` now holds every widget's menu (every bar
and list widget, a folder with three faces) to one rect on its own rows, on every level and deeper level,
and back, no level that lists no search scrolling, and some level filling the height (neither short nor
over); `AClickSwapsTheRowsInPlaceAndTheHeadGoesBack` (the range's level the menu's rect, and so after a
pick's Refresh), `TheMenuIsOneHeightOnEveryLevelAndARefreshOnlyGrowsIt` (three levels deep and back, one
rect; a Refresh with a taller level grows it once from its foot, one without it keeps it),
`ATreeTallerThanTheScreenIsCappedAndItsLongLevelScrolls` (80 rows a level: the menu the room's height on
every level, the long one scrolling), `AZonesLevelShowsEveryZoneInTheRoomItKeeps` (six rows' room at least,
in the menu's rect). Pictures (150 %, dark): `inline-height-top-dark`, `inline-height-clock-dark`,
`inline-height-hours-dark` — a folder's menu with its faces, its clock face's level and the clock's
format under it, one frame. By hand: in edit mode right-click a clock, a weather widget and a folder with
faces on a bottom bar and on a top bar; go into levels and back by the arrow, Escape and Backspace, and
see the menu's edges stay; type in a time zone's search; pick a choice and see nothing move.

## 275. Every face on the bar is what it shows and the padding, nothing more (2026-10-22)

The person, 2026-10-22: "some of the faces in the taskbar have space around them although they dont
need it. make it so that every face on the taskbar only takes as much space as it needs plus the current
padding as well of course."

**The rule.** A folder's button along the bar is its faces side by side (§244, each what it shows now),
each face's count past it while it shows one (`FaceSize.Trail`, §169), `FolderIsland.Between` between
them, its name where it shows one, and its two ends (`FolderIsland.Ends`: `Fit.Edge`, never under 8 DIP since §506,
6 before, across a bar and down one alike) — in whole px, and nothing more (`FolderIsland.Length`,
`WidgetShapes.Folder`). The shape says so (`WidgetShape.Exact`, `WidgetShape.Hug`): the layout takes the
length as it is (`IslandCells.Exact`, `Layout.WholeSpan`) instead of holding it to one grid cell at the
least (`Layout.AllotCells`/`ExactSpan`, which every other widget still goes through).

**Where the room came from**, measured on the person's bar (41 DIP) and on every face alone and between
two others at 48 DIP, 100 and 150 %, across and down:

- A lone glyph's button held to one cell: `GlyphAndText.Square` and `ExactSpan`'s one-cell floor made the
  icon, power, Wi-Fi, sound, Bluetooth, bell, mail, removable, hotspot, cast, clipboard, contacts, VPN
  faces (and a quake or keyboard face shorter than a cell) a 38 px square for 30 px of glyph and ends at
  100 %, 58 for 44 at 150 %. Windows 11 sizes its tray and quick settings buttons to their icons and
  padding, not to the bar's thickness, so no minimum is kept: a lone glyph's button is its glyph and its
  ends, narrower than the bar is thick.
- The drive face before a drive is chosen kept the entry's two cells and drew its glyph in the middle of
  them (the person's "Test" folder: 82 px for a 24 px glyph at 150 %). It is now the glyph and its words
  ("Not set"), as the other faces before their place is set say "Set location"; the glyph alone down a
  side. A drive set: the icon, the name, the bar's least, its own Side round them now drawn inside the
  face's box so the button keeps the standard ends (it kept Side, 4 px, before); down a side, the icon
  over its capacity bar (two cells before), the name the tooltip's, as a side bar's other faces' words are.
- Down a side bar: the timer and focus faces kept two rows of figures at rest, when they say one ("25m");
  the air quality, tides, quakes and sports faces before their place or team is set kept a reading's
  rows for the pin alone. Each is what it shows now.
- A lone square's count stood in the cell's slack; with no slack it keeps its room past the glyph as a
  face among others always did, so a count coming or going lays the bar out again (mail, bell, removable,
  hotspot), as a clock does at ten o'clock (§244).

**Deleted**: the one-cell floor for folders; the lone-square special case in `Parts` (its count's trail
dropped, its `Square`); the aligned face's "button's room inside its ends" branch in `FaceBoxes` (§201
moved a face's words only inside a button set wider than it, which no bar does now; a face's own room
still aligns, the two lines of the time and date); `WidgetShape.Row`, `FirstTakesTheRest` and
`CellIsland.Fill`, which nothing used since the now-playing widget became a face.

**Kept**: the performance faces' floor of two figures ("88%", a rate's "8.8M"): a reading taken every
second crossing 9 % would lay the bar out every second, so a one-figure reading keeps one figure's room.
A glyph's box is the icon font's em, which the glyph's own design does not fill (Bluetooth's rune); the
now-playing art's square holds its note while there is no art; a line's leading down a side bar.

Tests: `FaceSlackTests.EveryFaceIsItsContentAndThePaddingAndNothingMore` (every face, alone and between
two others, across and down, 100 and 150 %: the button is its faces and ends, a glyph's never a cell, the
ink at the ends); `SceneTreeTests.ThePersonsBarIsItsFacesAndTheirPadding` (the person's folders on their
41 DIP bar, face-slack-bar-dark-150.png and its table); the face presets' size tests now hold the glyph
and its ends, and the count's room only while it shows.

By hand: the bar's lone glyph buttons (a power or bell folder alone) narrower than the bar is thick;
the "Test" folder's drive face says "Not set" right after its glyph; a count arriving on a lone bell or
mail face widens it by the count and back.

## 276. Every widget's menu one height; the Height row at its foot; a count's room kept (2026-10-22)

The person: *"keep the room for the count"*; *"the menu does not have the same height everywhere, i also
want it to have the same height between widgets. i believe at the momement it has the height of its
largest child, but it does not have to be that, it can also just scroll the contents which is fine as
well"*; *"height should always be aligned at the bottom and should also not scroll"*.

**A count's room, kept.** §275 had a lone glyph face with a count (the bell, the mail, the removable
devices, the hotspot) take the count's room only while it showed one, so the button widened as a count
came and narrowed as it went, and the bar was laid out again. Each of those faces now keeps the room its
widest count stands past the glyph — "99+" for the bell and the mail (the mail's stale mark inside it),
"9+" for the removable devices and the hotspot — whatever it shows, alone or among other faces
(`FaceSize.Trail` from `GlyphBadge.Trail` and `RemovableFaceDrawing.CountTrail`, no longer read off the
folder's state). The bell keeps none where it is set not to count. A count coming or going paints the face
again in place and never lays the bar out. The rest of §275 stands: the button is its faces, their room and
its ends, never a cell; the glyph keeps its place at the face's start, the count's room after it.

**One height for every menu.** §274 made a menu one height on its levels, its own tree's tallest, so a
clock's menu and a folder's were different heights. Every menu that Configures, every widget's and on
every level, is now `Flyout.SettingsHeightDip`, 440 DIP — a row of buttons, a rule and twelve rows, about
Windows 11's quick settings — times the scale and Windows' text size (`SettingsHeight`, as the width's
§230), to the most the room on its side of the screen holds (the placement it took; `MenuSides` and
`Roomiest` are given that height). A shorter level's rows stand at its top, the rest empty; a longer one
scrolls, its head and a field pinned at its top as before. The rect never changes while it is open,
whatever a level or a Refresh brings.

**The Height row at the foot.** "Height should always be aligned at the bottom" is read as the folder
line's "Height ›" row (`LineHeightRows`): it was the root's last row, scrolling away with the rest in a
long menu. A row may now say it stands at the menu's foot (`FlyoutItem.Foot`, only the Height row does):
it and the rule over it are laid at the bottom of the rows' room, among the rows that stand still
(`pinned`, as a level's head is at its top), the window's clip leaving their band (`footH`) to them, the
rows scrolling over it; the pointer finds only them there, the keys scroll a row down to just over them,
and the scroll bar runs between the top band and the foot. It is in the same place in every line's menu,
short or long. Its own level (three modes and the stepper) fits the height without scrolling. The menu's
own bottom edge already stays where it stood over a bottom bar (§268), so nothing else was needed for the
other reading.

**Gone:** §274's measuring of the tree — `TallestLevel`, `LevelHeight`, `LevelsHeight`, `levelsHeight`,
`measuredTree`, the Refresh's grow-only rule — and what only it used: `ListRoom`, `SearchRows`,
`PickerTilesDip`, `LevelRows`.

Tests: `InlineMenuTests.EveryWidgetsMenuOpensItsLevelsInPlace` (every bar and list widget's menu, and a
folder with faces: one rect on every level, and every widget's as tall as the others'),
`EveryMenuIsOneHeightAndALongLevelScrollsInIt` (a two-row menu and a three-level one the same height; a
Refresh to nine rows fits, to eighty scrolls, the rect never changing), `TheRoomOverTheBarCapsTheHeight`,
`TheHeightRowStandsStillAtTheMenusFoot` (a calendar line's menu with and without sixteen rows more: the
Height row last, in one place in both, still where it was scrolled to the end with the last row over it,
the keys reaching it, its level not scrolling); `MenuValuesTests.ASearchsLevelKeepsOneHeightAndShowsEveryResult`
(the menu's one height); the mail, bell, removable and hotspot presets' size tests and
`StateSizingTests.TheBellKeepsItsBadgesRoomWhateverIsWaiting` (one size whatever the count, the widest
count's room); `FaceSlackTests` counts a kept count's room as the face's. Pictures (150 %, dark):
`inline-height-widgets-dark` (a folder's, a clock's and a markets line's menus side by side, one height),
`inline-height-foot-dark` (a line's menu short, long, and long scrolled to its end, the Height row at the
foot of each), `inline-height-level-dark` (the Height level).

By hand: in edit mode right-click a clock, a markets line and a folder with faces, and see the menus one
height; in an open folder right-click a line with many settings, scroll, and see "Height" stay at the
bottom; let mail or a notification arrive on a lone mail or bell face and see the bar not move.

## 277. Faces have no alignment; a folder's lines keep theirs (2026-10-22)

The person, 2026-10-22: "i believe alignment actually does not do anything anymore for the folder face
widgets. remove it from all of them as configuration option".

**Why it was dead.** §201 gave twenty-two faces an "Alignment" (start, middle, end) for their words in a
room wider than they read. §244 made a face what it reads now and §275 made the button exactly its faces
and their padding, so a face of one line has no slack to stand in: every pick drew the words in one
place (`AlignmentPictures.AFaceOfOneLineHasNoRoomToAlignIn` held exactly that). Only a face of two lines
had room — the narrower line of the time and date, of the keyboard's language over its region, of the
converter's code over its worth — and there the face's own place is the right one.

**Gone, from every face**: the option (`Alignment.Option` in each `FaceInfo`), its kind
(`FaceOptionKind.Align`) and the shared `core.align.*` keys for faces (`FaceInfo.KeyOf`), the face menu's
segmented row (`OptionRows.OfFace`'s Align case), `FaceContext.Align`/`Across` and the aligned paths of the
face drawings (the time and date's, the performance figure's, the news headline's, the glyph-and-name's,
`GlyphAndText.Row`'s and `FaceDrawings.Line`/`Put`'s `along`, the keyboard's), and the face half of
`Alignment` (`Key`, `Words`, `Word`, `Parse`, `Flip`, `Picked`, `FractionOf`, `Standing`, the face
`Shown`/`Choose`; `Fraction` lost its right-to-left turn, which only faces used). The string
`core.align.description`, read only by the face option's row, is gone from all 30 languages. Faces left with
