no option at all (timer, focus, stopwatch, battery, markets, sports, desktops, keyboard, layouts) have no
submenu, as the icon faces.

**Fixed places.** Each face draws where its default stood: the words in the middle of their room, the
performance figure at its end after the glyph, the news headline and the desktop's and layout's name after
their glyph. The time and date's two lines stand at their end, right-aligned as Windows' clock has them,
in every language (it was the face's default, `End`, and is now its only place); its one-line form is the
time at the start and the date at the end, as before.

**The file.** A face's `"align"` from before is read as nothing and dropped from the face's bag where the
file is read (`FolderFace.Normalize`), so it is not written again; nothing else of the file changes and no
shape is bumped.

**Kept: a folder's lines.** A heading, the date header, the time header and the clock line are as wide
as the folder and read narrower, so their alignment acts (`align-lines-dark-150.png`: start, middle and
end each in its place). Their row (`OptionRows.Align`, segmented, `core.align.title/start/center/end`),
`WidgetItem.Align` and the line half of `Alignment` stay.

Tests: `AlignmentTests.NoFaceHasAnAlignment` (no face in `FolderFaces.All` has an "align" option; the
option kind is gone), `AFacesAlignmentFromBeforeIsReadAsNoneAndNotWrittenAgain` (a clock face with
`"align": "end"` and seconds reads with seconds and no align, is written without it, the heading's own
alignment kept), the lines' tests as before; `AlignmentPictures.TheTimeAndDateStandAtTheirEnd` (the time
and the date end at one right edge, the narrower starting further in, at 100 and 150 %, in English and
Arabic; `align-datetime.png`); `AlignSegmentsTests` holds only the line's row; the face presets, the market
migrations and the option rows no longer list "align".

By hand: right-click a clock, a battery or a markets face in edit mode and see no Alignment row (and no
submenu on a battery or timer face); a heading in an open folder still offers Left, Center and Right.

## 278. A price whole where it fits; the keyboard face among others (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the price of a stock is cutoff even though there would be space to show it"*; *"keyboard
layout face does not show anything"*.

**The price.** Reproduced with the person's own line (Apple over five years, named "Apple", four rows in
the "Test" folder) at 150 %: "262.…" with room to spare, at every height and list width. A line keeps its
price the room of its widest shape, every figure an eight (§262), but measured and drew it in Segoe UI
Variable's own figures, which are proportional: at a list's figure size (30 px at 150 %) a "2" is wider
than an "8", so "262.24" was 92 px in the 91 px "888.88" kept, and DirectWrite trimmed it. Any price heavy
in twos could be cut; "412.34" and "81,912.34" happened to fit, which is why §262's pictures never showed
it. The face on the bar was right all along: it measures and draws its figures in tabular figures
(`TextLine.Template`/`Lay`, §245), where every figure is an eight's width. The line now does the same:
`MarketIsland.FigureWidth` (the tabular template) is the price's and the change's room and what `PriceFit`
steps sizes and forms on, and `Figure` draws them as tabular `TextLine`s against their end. A shape's room
holds every price of that shape, and a ticking price no longer shifts its figures.

What gives way where a row truly is short is §262's, now held for prices of wide figures: the range, then
the currency, then the change, then the name down to the least it reads as ("BRK…"); only then the price a
size smaller, a DIP at a time to the list's text, and last a shorter form of it ("734,568", "734.6K"). The
price is never cut with an ellipsis.

**The keyboard face.** The person's "Tides" folder wears the tides, calendar, keyboard, desktops and
clipboard faces. The keyboard face reads the layout in use from the folder's own indicator
(`FolderIsland.Keyboard`), and the folder made one only where the keyboard was its *first* face
(`options.Face.Info == FolderFaces.Keyboard`), a check from before a folder wore several (§244). Second, it
had no indicator: it kept its room and drew nothing, and the dock never told it a layout changed. It asks
`options.Wears(FolderFaces.Keyboard)` now, as every other face that keeps a reading in the folder does. The
VPN face's switch had the same first-face-only check (`FolderFaces.SwitchOf(options.Face.Info)`): beside
other faces it stayed dimmed with no tooltip whatever the connection. The folder now follows the first
switch face it wears (`WornSwitch`).

Tests: `MarketPriceRoomTests.ThePriceIsWholeWhereverItFits` (the person's Apple line and lines of 222.22,
81,912.34, 158.00 JPY and 1.2105, one row to four high at the narrow and the medium list, 100 and 150 %:

on a 41 DIP bar never trimmed; markets-price-room-dark-100/150.png), `ATabularPriceIsAsWideAsItsShape`;
`MarketFitTests` holds its figures to their tabular width;
`FaceSlackTests.EveryFaceDrawsAmongOthersWhatItDrawsAlone` (every face between an icon and the power glyph

`SceneTreeTests.ThePersonsBarIsItsFacesAndTheirPadding` has the "Tides" folder's five faces now and holds

## 279. A long list is searched; the holidays in the calendar face; no face headings at rest; a double-click is two clicks; the edit menu says what the widget is (2026-10-22)

The person: *"long select lists that have more than 10 items or so should be searcheable"*; *"public holidays
setting should be in the calendar widget/face itself, not on the root configuration"*; *"if you cant rename
a desktop it should also not show up as context menu action"*; *"when i right click a folder it shows its
context menu options, it should not show a title for each face"*; *"double clicking a widget should not
open its context menu, it should just behave like two normal clicks behind each other"*; *"show the widget
type in the edit context menu somewhere"*.

**A long list is searched.** One rule in the menu, not per row (`Flyout.Searchable`, `Flyout.Inline.cs`): a
level opened in place with more than ten rows to pick (`ListFilterFrom`; `Listed`: no heading, rule, tile,
field or head) and no field of its own has a search field under its head — the icon picker's filter
(§249, `FlyoutField.Filters`), placeholder "Search" (`dock.menu.search`). It has the keys as the level
opens, stands still under the head as the rows scroll, and leaves the rows whose words hold every word
typed, without headings and rules; none says "No matches" (`dock.menu.noMatch`), greyed. A row's words
(`FilterWords`) are its own where it has them (an icon's, a widget's, a face's), else its words, their
English where they are a text of Karpo's (`Strings.EnglishOf`, a reverse look-up of the language's table),
its second line and its value. Enter and Down go on to the first row; typing on a row goes back into the
field; Escape gives every row back. A pick keeps the level, its field and what is typed. Ten or fewer
rows stay a plain list; a search's level (a zone, a place, a country) and an icon picker keep their own
field. Its id is `InlineFilterId` less the depth, so a level's words are never another's.

**The holidays in the calendar face.** A folder wearing the calendar face had "Public holidays ›" among
the folder's own rows (`OptionHolidays.Shows` took the folder); they are now the calendar face's rows, on
the face's own level (`OptionRows.OfFace` takes the `OptionPlace`, `OptionHolidays.Into(FolderFace, …)`),
and `FaceSection`, `OptionMenu.Row` and `FieldPicks.Keep` pass the config through so a pick there writes.
A calendar line keeps them among its own rows, where they were. Still the person's, one list for every
calendar (§265).

**Rename a desktop, only where it can be.** `Dock.DesktopRows` leaves "Rename this desktop" out where
`CanRename` is false — no shell call on this build (`DesktopControl.Available`), or no desktop Windows has
told of (`Switchers.ActionsFor` now also wants the index among the desktops). A greyed row offered
nothing: there is no other way to name a desktop. A delete Windows refuses stays greyed with its reason;
the switcher line's pencil stays, greyed with its tooltip.

**No face headings at rest.** A folder's right click at rest (`Dock.FaceRows`) is its faces' rows in their
order, a rule between two faces' and no heading (§257's face names gone). Without the names, a row that
reads as one above it is the same command and stands once (the clock's and the calendar's "Adjust date
and time"). Headings inside a face's own rows (the sound's devices, "Power mode") stay; edit mode's menu
keeps its face rows.

**A double-click is two clicks.** Edit mode told a double-click's second half apart (`EditClickGuard`,
`EditClicks.OnDoubleClick`, `Dock.ClickActs`, `MenuClosedClick`, §213/§260) and opened the menu again
with it, and the second click on an opened folder's face did not close it. All gone: a click whose press
closed the widget's own menu does only that (`EditClicks.Acts`), however soon after the last. So on a
widget the first click opens its menu and the second closes it; on a folder the first opens it and the
second, on its face (`CloseReleased`), closes it; in an open folder a line's menu likewise. Rows of
Windows' own that read a double-click (a tray icon's, handed to its app; text fields' word selection) keep
it. Enter still opens a folder or the menu.

**The edit menu says what the widget is.** Under the row of buttons, over the settings, a heading in a
menu heading's small grey semibold (`OptionMenu.Section`'s `title`): the widget's kind and what tells it
from others of its kind — `IslandEdits.Header`, the name Narrator already gave the menu ("Clock · Osaka,
Sapporo, Tokyo", "Folder · Work", "Weather · Bern"). It stands on every edit menu, on the bar and in a
folder, settings or not, and a Refresh says it again (`OptionMenu.Updated` takes the heading over the rows
with them, so a label typed shows). A face's level already names the face in its head. At rest the menus
stay title-less (the 2026-10-10 rule).

Tests: `LongListSearchTests` — `ALevelOfMoreThanTenRowsIsSearched` (ten no, eleven yes, a field or tiles
no, toggles yes), `ARowIsFoundByItsEnglishToo` (German "Entfernen" found by "remo"),
`ALongChoiceIsSearchedInPlace` (26 cantons: the field under the head with the keys, "gall" leaves St.
Gallen, nothing found says so, Escape gives all back, Enter onto the first and Enter picks it with the
level staying, typing on a row goes back to the field; ten cantons: no field); `HolidaysTests.ACalendarsMenuHasTheRows`
(the folder's own rows have none, its calendar face's have them, another face's not);
`SwitcherTests.TheFacesMenuIsTheSwitchersOwn`, `BarMenuTests.RenamingAndDeletingSayWhatWindowsWillDo`;
`FaceMenuTests.SeveralFacesRowsFollowInTheirOrderUnderNoHeading` (no heading, a rule between, the same
command once); `EditClickTests.ADoubleClickIsTwoClicks` (menu open, shut, open; folder open, shut; no guard
left in the dock); `WidgetMenuTitleTests.AnEditMenuSaysWhatTheWidgetIs`. Pictures (150 %, dark):
`menus6-list-search-dark` (the cantons whole and searched for "bas"), `menus6-folder-rest-dark` (a clock,
calendar and sound folder at rest), `menus6-edit-type-dark` (a clock's and a folder's edit menus).

By hand: in edit mode open a choice with many entries (a drive's, a holiday region's) and type; open a
calendar folder's menu, go into its Calendar face and find "Public holidays"; right-click a desktops face
where renaming is not possible; right-click a folder with several faces at rest; double-click a widget in
edit mode (its menu opens and shuts) and a folder (it opens and shuts); see the grey line under the edit
menu's buttons.

## 280. The folder's close button at its top centre, not red; an empty folder opens only arranged; the bars in front of the folder (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the folder close button should be center top. there should not be a red close folder
button. when a folder is empty it shows empty areas where "add widgets here text appears", it should
actually not be openable when it is empty in viewing mode, only in edit mode. the taskbar still is
behind the folder edit view. this should not be."* This supersedes §267's "A red close button at the
top" (its place and its red) and §247's and §267's bars "kept just under the folder's window".

**At the top centre.** The arranged folder's close button (`FolderFlyout.CloseBox`) is centred on the
lists with widgets (`FolderPlan.Core`, what stands centred on the folder's face), on a row of its own
past the columns' "+" row on the side away from the bar — over the lists on a bottom or side bar, under
them on a top bar — its far edge `CloseReachDip` (68 DIPs: a "+" and its room, the button and its room)
off the lists. On the "+" row's own line it would stand on the "+" of a folder of one column, or of the
middle one of three, so it has a row of its own. Every list keeps that row on the screen: `Reach` takes
`CloseReachDip` off the room, where it took the "+" row alone — the same at rest, so nothing moves as
edit mode comes (§185), and a folder as tall as it may be is 38 DIPs shorter than before. It is kept on
the screen as the columns' buttons are (`KeepIn`). Its tip, "Close folder", stands beside it on its row,
after it in the reading direction (`CloseTip`: `Edge.Left`, `Edge.Right` in Arabic and Urdu), where it
covers neither the "+" row nor the lists; the room-above-or-under choice (`CloseTipRoomDip`) is gone.
Same size, glyph, target and action (`CloseAsked`, Escape's path).

**Not red.** A Windows 11 standard button (`PaintClose`, `CloseColours`): the flyout's material (its
`Base`, opaque) under ControlFillColorDefault, Secondary under the pointer and Tertiary pressed, a
ControlStrokeColorDefault rim, ChromeClose in the primary text, the secondary pressed. High contrast as
before: the button face with the window text's rim and ×, the highlight and its text, no rim, when lit.
Gone: `CloseRed`, `White`.

**An empty folder opens only arranged.** `OneFolder.Opens(empty, arranging)`: at rest a folder with no
widget in it (`FolderIsland.Empty`) does not open — a click, Enter, Space and UI Automation's invoke all
come to `Dock.ShowFolder`, which asks before anything opens or closes for it; arranged it opens as
before, its empty columns what is added into. Its tooltip still says it is empty
(`widget.folder.empty`).

**The bars in front of the folder.** The folder's window still spans its display (`FlyoutHost.Spread`),
on its dim, but stands under the bars as under the settings app: the dock's folder stands under every
window over the dim that is another app's or one of its bars (`FlyoutHost.StandsUnder`, was `Others`;
`EditStack.UnderOthers`), each time it is placed or activated. The bars, lifted to the top at every
build, stay in front of it with nothing putting them back: gone are `Dock.KeepBarsUnderFolder` and
`EditStack.KeepUnder`. They are still locked, not dimmed (§267), and the folder's face still closes it.
The guide lines still run through the bars (§246): each bar draws what runs through it itself, over its
panels and under its widgets — the bar in front, the lines on it (`Scene.Guides.cs`: `BuildGuides`, one
piece per panel clipped to it with its corners, just under `zones`; `EditView.Guides`, the bar's px;
`Scene.GuidesOn`, the folder's screen lines cut to the bar). The folder tells the dock when its lines
move on the screen (`FolderFlyout.GuidesMoved`, from `PlaceGuides`; `GuidesOnScreen` is no longer for
tests alone), and the dock shows every arranged bar's edit view again (`ShowEdits`, also what
`DecksFollowFolders` ends with), each asking `GuidesOver` for its lines. Where a floating bar has no
panel the folder's own lines show through it.

Tests: `FolderEditClickTests.TheArrangedFolderHasItsCloseButtonAtItsTopCentre` (was
`TheArrangedFolderHasARedCloseButtonAtItsTop`; bottom and top bar: centred on the core, 68 DIPs off,
every "+" between it and the lists, its tip beside it over no "+", hover, press, click `CloseAsked`),
`TheCloseButtonIsAStandardButtonAndHighContrastsSystemColours` (was `TheCloseButtonIsRed…`: the control
fills, neutral, no red; high contrast's system colours); `OneFolderTests.AnEmptyFolderOpensOnlyArranged`;
`FolderSlotTests.TheArrangedFolderStandsUnderTheBarsAndTheSettingsApp` (was `…UnderTheSettingsApp`: a

folder's window laid under the bars, each bar drawing its lines (`Scene.GuidesShown`), the close button
centred and neutral in the picture with its × apart from it, and down some line through a bar most of
the bar's panel shows the line. Pictures (150 %, dark and light): `editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<dark|light>-150`.
By hand: in edit mode open a folder: the taskbar in front, the guide lines on it, behind its widgets;
the × at the folder's top centre (bottom centre on a top bar), grey, over the "+" row, "Close folder"
beside it; click it (the folder closes); a folder with nothing in it: a click at rest does nothing, in

## 281. "Add a face" at the foot of a folder's menu (2026-10-22)

The person: *"add a face should also be bottom aligned and never scroll"*.

**At the foot.** A folder's edit menu on the bar ends with its faces, then "Add a face ›"
(`OptionMenu.FaceSection`). That row is now a foot row (`FlyoutItem.Foot`), as a folder line's "Height ›"
is since §276: a rule over it, the two standing still at the foot of the menu's one height. Under two faces
it stands at the bottom with the room empty over it; under fourteen the faces scroll behind it. The
pointer, the keys and the scroll bar take it where it stands (`footH`); its level opens in place and Back
finds it where it was.

between two foot rows is now the foot's too, so foot rows stack, each under its rule. No menu has both
today (a folder's faces are on the bar, a line's height in a folder); one that did would have "Add a face"
over "Height", as Dock.WidgetMenu adds the height after the settings. A rule at the end with no foot row
after it is no foot.

## 282. Refresh is a small button on the line, never a menu's row (2026-10-22)

The person: "refresh should not be a context menu action for any of the widgets"; "the capability to
refresh should be a small refresh button in the widget somewhere". Several lines and faces had a
"Refresh" row in their right click (weather, air, tides, earthquakes, markets, news, sports, mail,
contacts, the calendar's lines and views); the weather's conditions and the news line had a 32-DIP
button of their own, each laid out its own way (the news' with `RefreshRing`).

**No menu reads anything again.** `WidgetAct.Refresh` is gone with its label, glyph, its `RunAct` case
and what only it served: the faces' `RefreshFace` and the folder's `RefreshAir`, `RefreshTides`,
`RefreshSports`, `RefreshQuakes`, `RefreshMail` and `RefreshMarket`, and the face rows' "whose Refresh"
mark. A face whose only row was Refresh (weather, air, tides, earthquakes) now offers none of its own;
the folder's floor rows stand as for any face with nothing.

**One button, every refreshing line's** (`RefreshButton.cs`). A widget that reads what it shows again is
an `IRefreshable` — whether there is anything to read (`CanRefresh`), whether a read is on its way
(`Refreshing`), when what it shows was read (`UpdatedUtc`), and `RefreshNow` — and says which row the
button stands on (`CellIsland.RefreshRow`: its head's, or its one row; `RefreshEnd` where the row's end is
its own, a view's arrows). `CellIsland` does the rest for all of them:

- *Where:* the row's middle, the glyph's edge on the trailing gutter; the line keeps `RefreshRoom` clear
  at that row's end (the button and 4 DIP), the rest of the line laid out as before. A line too narrow
  to keep 120 DIP of its own beside it has none. On a scrolled line it stands in the head, which stays.
- *How:* Segoe's Refresh (E72C), 12 DIP in a 20-DIP square, in the secondary ink on nothing; under the
  pointer the subtle fill and the text's ink, pressed the pressed fill — a Windows 11 subtle button.
  Where a line says when it was read ("Updated 15 minutes ago": the weather, the air, the tides, the
  earthquakes), that stands just before it; a stale mark (docs\accounts.md, "Offline") stands before it too.
- *Says:* "Refresh", and under it when what the line shows was read (`WeatherAge.Updated`).
- *Does:* its click is asked before the widget's own (`FolderFlyout.Activate` → `RefreshClick`): the
  store reads again now, however fresh; while that read is on its way the glyph is in the tertiary ink,
  takes no click and turns a whole turn in 1.5 s on a timer of the button's own, armed only while the
  folder shows the line, the button is drawn and Windows' animations are on (off, it stands still).
  The PIM stores say when a read runs (`MailStore`, `ContactStore`, `TaskStore`, `AccountCalendars`,
  `CalendarStore.Reading`).

The weather's conditions and the news line lost their own buttons for it (the news' `RefreshTarget`,
the weather's `RefreshTarget`, its key stop and `RefreshRing`); the two strings only they used
(`dock.weather.refresh`, `dock.rss.refresh`) left all 31 tables. No new strings.

**Which lines have it:** the weather's conditions, air quality, tides, earthquakes (on its head or its one
row), sports (the scoreboard's head), markets (a ticker's name row), news, mail, contacts (beside the
search box), the calendar's agenda, the day's events, the day/week/year views (before the arrows), and a
Microsoft To Do list (its name's row). **Read on their own clock only:** the weather's next hours and
week (they stand under the conditions' line, which has it), the next meetings (each row's end is its
Join), a currency converter, and every face on the bar — a face is too small, and its click opens the
folder whose line has the button.

Tests: `RefreshButtonTests` — `NoMenuOffersRefresh` (every list kind, face and bar entry),
`EveryDataLineShowsTheButtonClearOfItsContent` (twelve kinds at one and four rows, 100 and 150 %: the
button inside its line, its target the button's, no piece of the line under it; none at 150 DIP),
`TheClickAsksTheStoreAndTheGlyphTurnsWhileItReads` (one ask, turning, a second click asks nothing,
still with animations off, at rest once the read lands), `ThePointerOnTheButtonLightsItAlone`;
`NewsPresetTests.TheRefreshButtonReadsTheFeedAndTurnsItsGlyph`, `WeatherTargetsTests`, and the menus'
tables updated. Pictures (150 %): `refresh-buttons-dark`, `refresh-buttons-light`.

By hand: open the weather, markets, news, mail and calendar presets; hover and click the ⟳ at a line's
top right (or its one row's end), watch it turn while it reads, and see "Updated …" in its tooltip;
right-click any widget or face and see no Refresh.

## 283. A bar's close never quits Karpo; Alt+F4 on a bar is Windows' Shut Down dialog; the log says why the dock quit (2026-10-22)

On 2026-10-22 the installed dock quit cleanly at 14:34:39 (the guard: "exit code 0: it quit; ... so it
stays down"), six seconds before the PC went to sleep, and stayed down after the wake. No crash, and
karpo.log said nothing about why. Every window of the dock's class took WM_CLOSE for quit: the settings
app's Quit Karpo and `Karpo.exe --quit` found "the dock" with FindWindow by class (and title), which was
the primary display's bar as often as the host, so the bars had to quit on a close too. That made Alt+F4
on a bar that had the keys (Win+T, edit mode, the focus handed back by a closing folder) — DefWindowProc
turns it into SC_CLOSE, then WM_CLOSE — and any program that closes the windows it finds a quit of all
of Karpo. Windows' own taskbar answers Alt+F4 with the Shut Down Windows dialog, as the desktop does.

One model now (`Karpo.Dock\Closing.cs`), answered once in `Dock.DispatchNow` for every window of the dock:

| Close | What happens |
|---|---|
| WM_CLOSE to the host, wParam `DockHost.QuitBy.Settings` / `.Command` | the dock quits, and karpo.log says who asked |
| WM_CLOSE to the host without that mark (another program; SC_CLOSE through DefWindowProc) | ignored, and a line says so |
| Alt+F4 / SC_CLOSE on a bar | Windows' Shut Down Windows dialog: SC_CLOSE posted to Explorer's own `Shell_TrayWnd` (hidden or not, never Karpo's tray spy), the very message Alt+F4 on Explorer's taskbar gives it; Explorer is let to the front first |
| WM_CLOSE to a bar | ignored, and a line says so |
| a menu, folder, quick settings, preview, edit bar | its own handler: a menu or a folder closes as Escape closes it |

and no close goes on to DefWindowProc, whose answer is DestroyWindow (`Closing.Default`, the last word
of `Dock.WndProc` and of the submenu, folder level, tray spy, taskbar list and peek strip procedures):
a menu used to be destroyed behind its owner by Alt+F4 and made again on its next showing.

- **The host has a class of its own**, `karpo.host` (`Karpo.Core\DockHost.cs`); the bars keep
  `karpo.dock`. The settings app (`KarpoProcess.Window`: Quit Karpo, Identify, Edit on the taskbar,
  whether edit mode is on, a start handed over) and `--quit` find the host by it, never a bar; the dock
  answers all of those before it looks at which window heard them, so nothing else changed for them.
- **One way out:** `Dock.Quit`, reached only through `Closing.Answer` for the host's marked close. The
  dock has no quit row of its own (the settings app's About page has Quit Karpo). The session's end
  (WM_ENDSESSION) puts the taskbar back as before and writes its own line.
- **karpo.log** gets one line per way out: "dock: quitting: the settings app's Quit Karpo asked",
  "dock: quitting: Karpo.exe --quit asked", "dock: Windows is signing out or shutting down: ...". With the
  guard's own line after it, "why is Karpo not running" is answered in the file.
- **The guard** (asked: should it start again a dock that quit cleanly, but not by a way of Karpo's?): no
  change. A clean exit now comes only from the host's marked close (logged), the session's end (the guard
  already stays down while Windows shuts down) or a WM_QUIT another program posts to the dock's thread
  (no such program is known). Should the last ever show — a guard line "exit code 0: it quit" with no
  "dock: quitting" line before it — a WM_QUIT the dock did not ask for can return an exit code of its own
  for the guard to restart on.

No new strings, no timers, no config change. Tests: `ClosingTests` (real windows answered as the dock
answers them, the dialog the test's own counter) — `AltF4OnABarAsksForTheShutDownDialogAndQuitsNothing`,
`ACloseSentToABarIsIgnored`, `AnyOtherWindowIsNeverDestroyedByAClose`,
`TheHostQuitsOnlyForKarposOwnCloseAndSaysWhoAsked` (the line in karpo.log), `EachWayOutHasALineOfItsOwn`.

By hand: Win+T to give a bar the keys, then Alt+F4: Windows' Shut Down Windows dialog, Karpo stays; open
a folder or a menu and press Alt+F4: it closes, Karpo stays; Settings, About, Quit Karpo: the dock quits,
and karpo.log ends with "dock: quitting: the settings app's Quit Karpo asked" and the guard's line.

## 284. A place is shown by its town alone (2026-10-22)

The person: "the location name that is shown should generally just be the name of the city or village,
in my case Gais for example, not Gais, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Schweiz."

**One rule, in `PlaceNames`.** `PlaceNames.Known`/`Of` — what every place-based widget says (the
weather's lines and faces, air quality, tides, earthquakes, their faces' tooltips, the edit list's
header, the bar menu's place row at rest and its device summary) — now give the town alone:
`PlaceNames.Short` is a place's words up to the first comma, trimmed ("Gais, Appenzell Ausserrhoden,
Schweiz" → "Gais", "New York, NY, United States" → "New York"); a place that is itself a region or a
country is that ("Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Schweiz" → "Appenzell Ausserrhoden"); a name with nothing
before its first comma takes the first thing it has; empty stays empty. The device's reverse-geocoded
name is written the same way (city, else locality, else the region — §253), so it shortens by the same
rule, and with no locality it falls back to what the service did name.

**Nothing in the config changes.** A place is still kept whole as it was picked (`WeatherOptions.Place`),
and shortened only when shown. The whole words are still used where they tell places apart:
`PlaceNames.Whole` for a web search of a line's weather, and the search's results with region and
country as their detail. The places offered before anything is typed (§230) are now listed the same way
— the town as the title, where it is as the detail (`PlaceNames.Parts`) — and picking one keeps its
whole words as before. The Settings app's weather title reads `PlaceNames.Short` instead of its own
split.

**Deleted:** `PlaceNames.Forms` (the long-then-short pair the lines fitted): with one short name there is
nothing to fall back to, so the weather, air, tides and earthquake lines fit `[place]` alone.

Tests: `DevicePlaceTests.APlaceIsShownByItsTown` (the helper's cases), `APlacePickedIsKeptWholeAndShownShort`
(the weather reading and the menu's row say "Gais", the search's words whole),
`EveryWidgetCallsItsPlaceByTheOneRule` and the faces' tooltips updated; `MenuSearchTests` (the places in
use, town over detail). Pictures: `device-place-*.png` say "Zürich".

By hand: a weather, air quality, tides and earthquakes line set to a place picked with region and country
(and to the device's location): each says the town alone; its menu's place row says the town; its
search lists region and country beside each result.

## 285. A row a reading for the performance widget in the add list (2026-10-22)

The person: *"performance should be split into multiple entries in the add widgets menu, it should still
be one widget but with different configurations depending on what i add. (e.g. ram, gpu, cpu, etc...)"*.

**One notion, the styles' own.** A widget with styles was one row of a folder's add list, its first style
(§209). A widget with readings (§228) is now a row a reading, each that reading's first style
(`StyledWidget.Offered`): what a widget measures is what it is *of*, never a style (§270), so the person
says which when adding it. Today that is the performance widget alone: System info lists **Processor,
Graphics, Memory, Disk, Network activity** one after another, each the reading's name and icon as the
widget's own Reading choice has them (`TitleOf`, `GlyphOf`; its line the reading's graph's, `BlurbOf`). A
pick adds the one performance widget measuring that reading, in its graph ("kind": "performance",
"reading": "gpu", "style": "graph"); its menu and its page still change the reading and the style. Every
other widget with styles is still one row.

**Found by its own words.** A reading's row is found by the widget's words and its name, and by its own
reading's styles' names and words alone (`KeywordsOf`): "ram" finds Memory, "gpu" Graphics, "cpu"
Processor, and none of them another reading; "performance" finds all five.

**"Network activity".** The Network reading's name is "Network activity" now, in all 30 tables (each the
words the face and the ready-made folder already had, `core.face.networkActivity.title`), in the Reading
choice too: the Wi-Fi widget is "Network", and two rows of one name in one list are a choice nobody can make.

**Unchanged:** the bar's list has each reading's ready-made folder (the Group badge), and a folder's
"Add a face" each reading's face, as before.

**Icons back.** §228 had lost the calendar widget's and the performance widget's icons from the source
(their code points dropped), so Popular's Calendar stood bare; they are `WidgetInfos.Calendar.Glyph` and
`OptionGlyphs.Reading` again.

Tests: `AddListTests.EachReadingIsARowAddingThePerformanceWidgetMeasuringIt`, `EveryRowHasItsIcon`,
`NoTwoWidgetsOfAPageShareAName`; `AddListSearchTests.EachReadingIsFoundByItsOwnWords`;
`WidgetStylesTests.TheAddListOffersEachWidgetOnceAReading`. Pictures (150 %, dark):
`add-perf-readings-submenu` (System info open), `add-perf-readings-search` ("ram").

By hand: in a folder press "+", open System info and add Memory: a memory graph; its menu's Reading
still switches it. Type "gpu" in the list's search: Graphics.

## 286. A widget's menu as tall as its rows; the edit menu's heading once (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the right click context menus on the folders should not have a fixed height, these should
change with their contents."*; *"in my test just now the title of the folder was repeated many times in
the face edit context menu."* This replaces §276's one height (and §274's tree's tallest before it).

**As tall as its rows.** Every widget's menu — a folder's at rest and arranged, a line's, every other
widget's — and every level it opens in place is as tall as its rows, to the most the room on its side of
the screen holds, and scrolls past that, as Windows' own menus and quick settings' pages are. A folder of
one face has a short menu, one of fourteen a long one. One rule for every menu, not the folder's alone:
§276's fixed 440 DIP left a two-row menu mostly empty on every widget. The foot rows (§276, §281: "Height
›", "Add a face ›") are at the bottom of the rows' room as before, which is now the end of the rows; past
the room they still stand still under the rows that scroll.

**Levels.** A level opened in place is its own rows' height; the window keeps its sides and the edge at
what it opened from — the foot over a bottom bar, so it grows and shrinks upwards from the bar, the top
under a top bar (`KeepPlace` now asks the placement's edge; it took the edge nearer the screen's, which,
for a menu filling the room, could be its top and moved the foot off the bar). Back, the menu is as it
opened; a Refresh that brings more rows or fewer (a face added or taken off, a toggle showing more) makes
it taller or shorter the same way. *Why not the tallest level of the tree*, which would keep a level from
changing the height (§274): every folder's tree has "Add a face" and its groups (the Info group ten faces),
a clock face a zone search listing every zone, an icon face the whole icon gallery — the tallest is the
room's height or near it on nearly every folder, which is the fixed height again; and measuring the tree
took a second layout of every level (§274's `LevelHeight`, deleted in §276). So each level is its own,
the bar side standing still, as Windows 11's quick settings pages do.

**A field's level, one room.** A level a field searches or filters — a zone's, a place's, a symbol's
search, an icon picker, a long list (§279) — is what stands over its rows (its head, a switch, the field)
and room for `ListFilterFrom` rows under them — ten, as many as a list shows before it is searched, so a
searched list is never shorter than an unsearched one —, whatever it lists, the rest a scroll away:
§271's *"show all the items with the fixed height so that the list is just scrollable in the end"* (its
six rows, §228's five and "Show more", gone with §276). Typing, answers coming, nothing found: nothing
moves, and every such level is one height.

**The heading once.** §279's heading ("Folder · Work") had id 0, outside `OptionMenu.Holds`. `Updated`
found the section by its first held row and walked back over headings to take the heading in; a folder
has no settings of its own, so its section's first held row was the faces' heading, a rule under the
title in between, and every Refresh put another title over the faces. `Section` now gives the heading an
id among the picks (an `OptionPickKind.None`, as the faces' heading has), so it is the section's first row
and is replaced with it; the walk back is deleted.

**Gone:** `Flyout.SettingsHeightDip` and `SettingsHeight`, `levelsTall`, and `Updated`'s walk back over
headings.

Tests: `WidgetMenuTitleTests.AFoldersEditMenuSaysWhatItIsOnceThroughEveryRefresh` (a folder of three faces
shown again four times after a face is moved: one heading, the same count of rows); `InlineMenuTests` —
`EveryWidgetsMenuOpensItsLevelsInPlace` (every widget's menu and every level and deeper level its rows'
height, a field's level its field's room, its sides and foot kept, back the menu as it opened),
`EveryLevelIsAsTallAsItsRows` (three levels deep and back; a two-row menu shorter; a Refresh to nine rows
grows it, to one shrinks it, to eighty is searched, its field's room, scrolling), `TheRoomOverTheBarCapsTheHeight` (a
long menu the room's height, scrolling; a short level its rows', its foot on the bar),
`AFoldersMenuIsAsTallAsItsRowsAtRestAndArranged` (one face and three, at rest and arranged, and the clock
face's level), `AddAFaceStandsStillAtTheMenusFoot` and `TheHeightRowStandsStillAtTheMenusFoot` (the foot
row at the same screen pixels under two faces or no extra rows and under forty, scrolled too),
`TheSymbolsSearchGetsItsAnswerInPlace`, `AZonesLevelShowsEveryZoneInTheRoomItKeeps` (the field's room, one
rect as it is typed in); `MenuValuesTests.ASearchsLevelKeepsOneHeightAndShowsEveryResult` (ten rows' room,
one height with none, two, twelve and nothing found). Pictures (150 %, dark): `menu-height-folders-rest-dark`
(a folder of one face and of three at rest), `menu-height-folders-edit-dark` (arranged, and the clock
face's level), `inline-height-widgets-dark`, `inline-height-foot-dark`, `inline-add-face-foot-dark` (two
faces; forty at their top and their end), `inline-folder-picker-*`.

By hand: right-click a folder of one face and one of several, at rest and in edit mode: each menu ends
under its last row, standing on the bar; go into a face and back (the bar side stays, the top follows the
rows); type in a zone's or a place's search and an icon picker's filter (nothing moves); move a face,
toggle a face's setting and add a face several times in one menu: "Folder · …" stays one line.

## 287. No close button on the arranged folder; its lines end at the bars; a right click on a locked bar closes the folder into a menu; no press on what does nothing (2026-10-22)

The person: *"the column lines in edit mode still go over the taskbar, this should not be. remove the
close button in folder edit mode. in edit mode when i have the folder open and i right click on the
folder or any other folder it should close the folder and open the context menu of the folder. if a
folder does not have any contents to be viewed / opened it should not have an animation when i click
it"*. This takes back §280's close button and its bar-drawn guide lines; the bars stay in front of the
folder's window (§280's `FlyoutHost.StandsUnder`).

**The lines end at the bars.** The folder's guide lines are laid out in the room its buttons and slots
already keep to (`FolderFlyout.Visible`, `Guides(shown, Visible())`, was the whole window), and that
room is the work area the dock hands the folder: `DockWindow.FolderWork`, the display's work area less
every other bar of it (`WorkArea`, as before) and now less its own bar's strip too (`Takes`: its panels,
the room between a floating bar's docks and the room off the screen's edge). A line ends at the bar's
edge; nothing of it is under a bar's material or shows between its panels. The panel is placed as
before: its room is measured from the anchor, which stands off the strip already. Gone: the bars'
drawing of the lines (`Scene.Guides.cs`, `EditView.Guides`, `Scene.GuidesOn`, `GuidesShown`), the dock's
`GuidesOver` and `ShowEdits` (its loop back in `DecksFollowFolders`), `FolderFlyout.GuidesMoved`.

**No close button.** `FolderFlyout.CloseBox`, its visual, `DrawClose`, `PaintClose`, `CloseColours`,
`CloseDip`, `CloseTarget`, `CloseReachDip`, `CloseOnScreen`, `CloseDrawn`, its tip (`CloseTip`,
`TipPanelOnScreen`; the folder's tips stand over their part alone now, so the tip's side went too),
`FolderFlyoutAction.CloseAsked` and the dock's case for it, `Dock.GlyphCloseFolder`, and the string
`dock.widgetMenu.closeFolder` in all the tables. `Reach` takes the "+" row alone again, 30 DIPs: a folder
as tall as it may be is as tall as before §280. It closes by its face on the bar, by Escape, and by a
right click on a widget of a bar.

**A right click on a locked bar.** `Dock.EditRightClick` no longer returns for `BarLocked`: on a widget —
the open folder's face, another folder, any widget — the folder closes first by Escape's step
(`EscapeTo(EditEscape.CloseFolder)`) and the widget's menu opens beside it at once (`ClickMenu`), the one
path a right click takes on a bar that is not locked. On the room round the widgets nothing, and the
folder stays. A left press on a locked bar is as before: on the folder's face it closes it, anywhere
else nothing.

**No press on what does nothing.** One rule for a widget's click at rest and for its press:
`CellIsland.ClickDoes(screen)` — false where this PC hasn't got the widget's thing (§247), for an empty
folder (`FolderIsland`, by `OneFolder.Opens(Empty, arranging: false)`) and for brightness's sun (the widget
is its slider; a click off it did nothing already). `Dock.ClickDoes` asks it (Windows' buttons, the apps
and the tray always act); `IslandClick` asks it before the widget's click, where the greyed widgets'
check stood, and `DockWindow.PressShown` asks it for the press: no give (`Scene.Press`) and no pressed fill
(`Highlight`) on such a face, its hover as before. Arranged, an empty folder opens as before, and its
press is edit mode's own.

Tests: `FolderEditClickTests.TheArrangedFolderHasNoCloseButton` (was `…HasItsCloseButtonAtItsTopCentre`
and `TheCloseButtonIsAStandardButton…`); `EditClickTests.ARightClickOnALockedBarClosesTheFolderAndOpensTheMenu`,
`ALockedBarTakesOnlyAPressOnTheFoldersFace` (no `CloseAsked`); `FolderSlotTests.TheGuideLinesEndAtTheBars`
(was `…RunThroughTheBars`: every line from the work area's far edge to the bar's, none on its strip, on
all four edges) and the dock's wiring (`FolderWork`, no `GuidesMoved`, no `Scene.Guides.cs`);
`OneFolderTests.APressShowsOnlyWhereTheClickDoesSomething`; `FolderFillTests` and `FolderHiddenTests` read 30 again;
`EditedDisplay`'s folder pictures: no guide line overlaps any bar's strip, and some ends at the folder's
own bar's edge. Pictures (150 %): `editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<dark|light>-150`.

By hand: in edit mode open a folder on a bottom taskbar and on a floating dock: the lines stop at the
bar's top edge, none over the bar or between its docks; no × anywhere; right-click the open folder's
face, another folder and a widget: the folder closes and that menu opens at once; at rest click an empty
folder (nothing gives) and one with widgets (it gives and opens).

## 288. A configuration menu one height; the folder's one heading (2026-10-22)

The person: *"now all of the context menus have a different size but the ones that are opened by left
click and show the widget configuration or show the folder configuration or the taskbar widget
configuration should have a fixed height. basically only the context menus in view mode should have a
variable / automatic height."*; *"right click folder widget configuration should only show one header, it
should not show the header for the faces"*. §286 made every widget's menu as tall as its rows, edit mode's
too; this splits it by what the menu is.

**Two kinds of menu, one rule each.** A *configuration menu* — edit mode's menu of a widget on the bar,
a folder, a folder's line, however it is opened (a left click, a right click, the rail's list of widgets
not shown): `Dock.WidgetMenu` while the bar is arranged — is `Flyout.SettingsHeightDip` (440 DIP, §276's,
back) tall on every level, a field's level (a zone's, a place's search, an icon picker, a long list) too,
and every widget's the same, to the most the room on its side of the screen holds. Its rows stand at its
top, the foot rows (§276, §280: "Height ›", "Add a face ›") at its foot, a longer level scrolls between.
Going in and back, a Refresh, typing: nothing moves. Every other menu — a widget's at rest, the folder's
right click at rest, a dropdown over a folder — keeps §286: as tall as its rows. One property says which:
`Flyout.Configuration`, set from `Pending.Configuration`, which `WidgetMenu` sets to `Arranging(window)`;
nothing per widget. (The bar's own edit menu is not a widget's; it can opt in the same way.)

**The folder's one heading.** Edit mode's folder menu said "Folder · Work" (§279, `OptionMenu.Section`)
and under it, ruled off, "Faces on the taskbar" (§226). `FaceSection` has no heading or rule of its own
now: the faces follow the folder's heading directly, "Add a face" ruled off at the foot. A face's level
has only what every level has, its head (the back arrow and the face's name). The string
`settings.folder.faces.header` is gone from every language.

**Back:** `Flyout.SettingsHeightDip` and `SettingsHeight` (deleted in §286), as the configuration menu's
height alone. **Gone:** the faces' heading and the rule over it.

Tests: `InlineMenuTests` — `EveryWidgetsMenuOpensItsLevelsInPlace` (every widget's configuration menu
and every level and deeper level of it the one height, sides and foot kept),
`TheRoomOverTheBarCapsTheHeight` (capped by the room, its short level the same),
`AddAFaceStandsStillAtTheMenusFoot` and `TheHeightRowStandsStillAtTheMenusFoot` (the foot at the same
pixels under two rows and forty, a short menu's room under its rows), `AZonesLevelShowsEveryZoneInTheRoomItKeeps`
(the zones' level the one height), `AFoldersMenuIsAsTallAsItsRowsAtRestAndOneHeightArranged` (at rest its
rows', arranged one height with one face or three, a face's level and a clock line's too),
`EveryLevelIsAsTallAsItsRows` (a menu at rest, unchanged);
`WidgetMenuTitleTests.AFoldersEditMenuSaysWhatItIsOnceThroughEveryRefresh` (the folder's heading the
menu's only one, the first face right under it, through four Refreshes), `AFacesLevelHasNoHeadingOfItsOwn`
(every face). Pictures (150 %, dark): `menu-height-folders-edit-dark`, `menu-height-folders-rest-dark`,
`inline-height-widgets-dark`, `inline-add-face-foot-dark`.

By hand: in edit mode click a folder of one face, one of many, a clock and a weather widget: every menu
the same height, "Add a face" at its foot; go into a face, a zone's search and back: the menu stays put.
The folder's menu says "Folder · …" once, its faces right under it. At rest right-click the same
widgets: each menu ends under its last row.

## 289. A click on another widget while a folder is open arranged closes it and clicks there (2026-10-22)

The person: *"its not possible to click another folder while one folder is open in edit mode"*. A
folder open arranged locks the bars under it (§212), and `DockWindow.EditPressed` returned for the lock
before it read what was pressed: `LockedPressed` took the open folder's own face and nothing else, so a
left press on another folder was swallowed there. The folder's window was not in the way (the bars stand
in front of it, §280) and `PressedOn` leaves it open (`StaysOpen`); the press reached the bar and stopped.

**One rule for both buttons.** A left press on a locked bar now keeps §287's right-click rule
(`EditClicks.OnLocked(part, closing, press)`, `LockedPress`), `press` what it would begin on a bar not
locked (`EditClicks.OnPress`):

- on the open folder's face (`Closes`): pressed, and its release on it closes the folder, as before (§251);
- on any other widget (`Unlocks`: `EditPress.Own`), another folder's, any widget's, a widget of another
  bar while the folder is this one's: the folder closes by Escape's step (`EscapeTo(EditEscape.CloseFolder)`)
  and the press goes on as on a bar not locked. It picks the block up; its release is the click
  (`EditActivate`), so another folder opens in the one click and any other widget's menu opens, as its
  right click's does. A drag from there moves the widget, as unlocked;
- on the room round the widgets and the resize grip (`Stays`): nothing, and the folder stays.

`LockedPressed` lost its own check. A widget lights under the pointer on a locked bar as on any bar
(`EditView` no longer lights the open face alone), since its click reaches it now.

Tests: `EditClickTests.ALeftClickOnALockedBarClosesTheFolderAndClicksAsUnlocked` (the rule, three clicks
done the dock's way: another folder opens in one click, its face closes it, a widget's menu opens; the
dock's one switch on the lock, the folder closed before the bar's own press; no lock in `EditView`'s
light); `APressOnTheOpenFoldersFaceClosesIt` (was `ALockedBarTakesOnlyAPressOnTheFoldersFace`); the
right-click test is unchanged.

By hand: in edit mode open a folder, then click another folder on the bar (it opens, the first gone, one
click), click the open folder's face (it closes), click a widget (the folder closes, its menu opens),
press another widget and drag it (it moves), click the bar's empty room (the folder stays).

## 290. A bar's looks in its edit menu; a separator's and a divider's whole (2026-10-22)

The person: *"when i right click in edit mode onto the taskbar all the appearance settings should appear
in the context menu. the same should be for the divider context menu."*

**The bar's menu.** On an arranged bar a right click on the room round the widgets (the panel, the grip
band) opened nothing since §214. It now opens the bar's looks at the pointer (`Dock.LooksMenu`;
`EditClicks.OnRight` now says which menu: `EditRight.None`, `Widget` or `Bar`), a menu of the widgets'
topic (it Configures: its levels open in place, §271; a pick sets without closing it, §219), headed with
the bar's type and layout ("Taskbar · Default"). Its rows are every look the settings app has for that
bar, wherever the app keeps it: **Position** (the display's edge, the Displays page's), **Type**, **Size**
and **Show** (the layout's, the Layouts page's — Size and Show this bar's own, a Top and bottom's top bar
its `TopSize` and `TopShow`; `TaskbarLayout.SetShowOf` new beside `SetSizeOf`), **Material**, **Opacity**
(only while the material has one, as Appearance greys it; a stepper of 5 %) and **Custom colors ›** (the
taskbar background, the cards, their outline, the highlight and the flyouts, each Appearance's swatch
row in the mode Windows is in, as every colour row of a menu is since §224). Not in it: which layout a
display shows (the bar's own menu at rest lists the layouts; switching in edit mode would change what is
being arranged), the layout new displays get, a layout's name and icon (what it is, not how it looks),
and "Reset all" (an action, not a look: each colour's Automatic tile does it). A change is saved and
shown at once (`LooksPicked`, from `OptionPicked`); one that takes the bar's window away — another edge,
another type, a bar that only comes in on hover — closes the menu with the window (`Forget`). A locked
bar's folder closes first, as for a widget's menu (§287).

**One description, both places.** `Karpo.Core\BarLooks.cs` says once what a bar is offered — the edges,
the types, the sizes (`SizesWith`: a dragged size offered in its place), the ways of showing, the
materials and their names — and writes each (`WriteEdge`, `WriteSize`, `WriteShow`, `WriteMaterial`,
`WriteOpacity`, and the separators' `WriteLines` and `WriteGap`, which were the settings app's
`Logic\LineRows.cs`, deleted). The settings app's pages take their lists, names and writes from it
(`SettingsModel.TypeName`, `ShowName`, `Sizes`, `DisplayEdges` and `LayoutsPage.Shows` gone); the menu's
rows are `BarLooks.Rows`, acted through `OptionMenu.ApplyRow`, the one way a pick acts on a row, a
widget's (`OptionMenu.Apply`) and a bar's alike.

**The separator's and the divider's menus** had the style and the colour, the divider's the colour. A
separator's menu now has Appearance's "Separators" whole and in its order: Style, **Line width** (a
stepper, 0 says "Automatic"; only while it is a line), **Line color** (named as Appearance names it, no
longer "Separators"; only while something is drawn) and **Space on each side** (steps of 4 px). A
divider's menu has **Gap in folders** (steps of 2 px) over its colour. A number row may say words in
place of its figure (`OptionRow.Said`: "Automatic", "70%", "8 px"), and a stepper's words wider than its
least room keep 6 DIP either side (`Flyout.StepGapDip`), so "Automatic" no longer touches the +.

Tests: `BarLooksTests` — `EveryLookTheSettingsAppHasIsARowOfAMenu` (every two-way binding of a look on
Appearance and the Displays page and every `SetLayout…` of the Layouts page is a row of the bar's, the
separator's or the divider's menu, or listed with why not, so a card added to a page fails it; the
materials in the page's order), `EachLookOfTheBarsMenuSetsWhatItSays` (edge, type, the top bar's own size
and show, a dragged size offered, opacity only with a material that has one, stepped, a colour of the
dark mode alone), `TheSeparatorsAndTheDividersMenusSetTheirLooks`; `LineRowsTests` and `MenuPickersTests`
write through `BarLooks`; `EditClickTests.ARightClickOpensTheMenuAndTheRoomItsLooks` and
`ARightClickOnALockedBarClosesTheFolderAndOpensTheMenu` (the looks' menu after the folder closes).
Pictures (150 %, dark): `bar-looks-dark` (the menu, its colours' level, its sizes' level),
`separator-looks-dark` (a separator's and a divider's menus).

By hand: in edit mode right-click the bar between widgets: the looks menu at the pointer; change the size,
the material, the opacity and a colour and see the bar follow with the menu open; move it to the top
(the menu closes with the bar's window, the bar stands at the top); on a Top and bottom right-click each
bar and set its size apart; right-click a separator and step its width and its space, and a folder's
divider its gap.

## 291. Tray icons a face's width apart; a removable face with nothing plugged in only while arranged (2026-10-22)

The person: "make the tray icons a little closer together, they dont have to have the 1by1 ratio
anymore" and "if there is no removable device it should not show up as a face in view mode, only in edit
mode".

**The tray's cells.** A notification icon's cell was the bar's square (`TrayCell` both ways, 2026-10-05's
"they should have it", the 1x1): as long along the bar as the bar is thick, for a 16-DIP icon. It is now the icon
and the room between two faces side by side (`FolderIsland.Between`, half either side), the face rule of
§275 rather than a tray constant: `Layout.TrayStep` = `TrayIconPx` + `Between`, never longer than the
bar's thickness, 24 DIP on the 48-DIP bar (36 px at 150 %), Windows 11's own tray slot — 21 DIP since §506 made
`Between` 5 DIP. Across the bar the
cell keeps the bar's usable thickness (`TrayCell`), so the hover, the press and the hit are as tall as
before. Everything that counted cells along the bar counts `TrayStep`: the block (`trayCells × TrayStep`),
the chevron's cell, a tray of a set size (`TraySpills`, `TrayHolds`), `Locate`; the hit test, the drag
(`TrayDrags`, `Scene.TrayDragIn`) and the screen reader's bounds already did. The hidden icon menu keeps
its square grid (`TrayOverflowCell` = `TrayCell`), as Windows' has; the icons in it are the same size.

**A face with nothing to show.** One rule for every face, where now playing had its own:
`IFaceDrawing.NothingToShow(face, folder)` (false by default) says a face has nothing to show now — the
removable face with nothing plugged in (always), now playing set to "Hide it while nothing plays" while
nothing does (§234). `FolderIsland.FacesOnBar` leaves such a face out at rest, with its room and the room
beside it; a folder with no face left takes no cell (`Count`), as §238 had it for now playing. While the
bar is arranged every face is on it (`CellIsland.Arranged`, which a folder's lines already had; the dock
sets it on every island at each rebuild, which edit mode's start and end are), so the face can be found,
moved and set — now playing too, "Nothing playing" where it used to leave a placeholder block.
A device plugged in or out (WM_DEVICECHANGE → `RefreshIslands`, or the face's minute tick) changes the
face's cell, `CellIsland.Moved` reports it and the bar is laid out again, as a track starting does.

Not changed, same in kind: the meeting face set to show a meeting only shortly before it
(`FolderIsland.MeetingIdle`, §205) also leaves the bar with nothing to show, but by the folder's own
count; arranged it would show an empty face, so it stays as it is (a placeholder block in edit mode).

Tests: `TrayCellsTests` (`EveryTrayCellIsTheIconAndItsPadding`, `OnTheTaskbarsBarACellIsWindowsSlot`,
`EveryTrayCellIsNarrowerThanItIsThick`, the picture centred, the cells touching, the drop cells, every
point of the block a hit, a set size holding whole cells); `TwiceOverTests.EachTrayHasItsOwnChevron`,
`TrayOverflowDragTests`, `TrayDragRoomTests`, `NarratorTests` count `TrayStep`;
`RemovablePresetTests.WithNothingPluggedInTheFaceIsOnTheBarOnlyWhileArranged` (no cell at rest, the
face arranged, a device plugged in and taken out lays the bar out again both ways). Pictures:
`SceneTreeTests.TrayCellSheets` (was `TraySquareSheets`): tray-cells-<look>-<32|48|64>-<bottom|left>-
<dark|light>-<100|150>.png; tray-bar-*.png; removable-face-*.png (the first face arranged).

By hand: the tray icons stand about as close as Windows 11's, the hover a tall narrow plate; drag one
along the tray and into the hidden icon menu and back. With no USB stick in, a removable folder is gone
from the bar and back in edit mode; plug one in at rest and it appears, take it out and it goes.

## 292. One order, one depth and one kind of row for every widget's settings; what a pin opens is one row (2026-10-22)

The person: *"for all the widgets, go ahead and make sure that the configuration is implemented as
similarly as possible, same order, same depth, same types of menus."*; *"path and what it opens should be
combined, can also be combined in a submenu. improve the folder link/show contents widget configuration in
general, it should be as easy as possible to configure everything"*.

**The audit** (every widget kind's and every face's rows, dumped from `OptionRows.Of`/`OfFace`): the types
were already one per kind of value — every on/off a toggle, every named choice a level of its choices,
every free text a field's level, every find-by-typing a search's level, numbers a stepper in the row,
times and lengths a level of steppers, alignment alone its icons in the row (§253; §226 took back
in-row choices for the rest). What differed: **the order** — what a widget shows (the place, the zone,
the reading's adapter, the public holidays) stood first on some and after the style, the seconds or the
label on others, and a behaviour (an alert, a highlight) before the look on some faces; **the words** — a
style was "Style" on the lines, "Look" on the calendar and weather faces, "Show" on the tides, air and
quakes faces, "Width" on the meeting face, "Graph" on screen time; and **one value in two rows** — a
pin's target was a row opening Windows' dialog and a "Path" row of its own.

**The convention.** Every row says which part of the menu it belongs to (`OptionRow.Slot`, `OptionSlot`),
and `OptionRows.Of` and `OfFace` lay the rows out by it (`Laid`, stable within a part), whatever order a
widget's code adds them in:

1. **Subject — what it is of**: the place (its device switch heading its level), the time zone, the
   symbol, the feed, the team, the drive, the reading, what a pin opens, the list, an alarm's time and
   days, a timer's length, the toggles and the status icons it shows, an icon face's icon.
2. **Scope — what of it it shows**: the reading's adapter or disk, the amount owned, the chart's range,
   the distance and the magnitude, the air index, the public holidays, which meeting, how a pin shows a
   folder.
3. **Style**: one row, "Style", the Style icon (§270: drawings of the same data).
4. **Look — the rest of how it is drawn**: the chart, the item size, the parts it shows (seconds, 12 or
   24 hours, preview, pictures, time, its name beside it, the art, the count, Join), a colour.
5. **Words**: a name, a label, a heading's text, a pin's icon.
6. **Placement**: alignment, which way a slider runs, how long it is.
7. **Behaviour — what it does**: what a click does or turns on, alerts, do not disturb, when it shows,
   which screens, the highlight, hiding while idle, how often it updates.

and then, as before, the foot rows ("Add a face ›", "Height ›", §276, §281). The kind of a row follows its
value, and with it its depth: on/off a toggle (in the row); named choices a level of them, ticked, the
choice at the row's end, searched past ten (§279), alignment's self-explaining icons alone in the row;
a whole number a stepper (in the row); a time or a length, free text, what is found by typing, a colour, an
icon a level of their own; on/offs or choices of one subject a group's level. A face's option says its
part (`FaceOption.Slot`; by its kind where it says none: a zone the subject, an adapter or a disk the
scope, a text the words, a pace the behaviour, a switch the look), and a style option is called "Style"
(`FaceInfo.TitleOf`) with the Style icon: the calendar's and weather's "Look", the tides' "Show", the
meeting's "Width" and the air's and quakes' "Show" are each "Style" now; screen time's "Graph" too. The
six titles and `settings.widget.screenTime.graph.header` left all 30 tables.

What moved (before → after): the weather lines Style, Place → Place, Style; a clock line Style, seconds,
Time zone, Label, Alignment → Time zone, Style, seconds, Label, Alignment; the time and date lines Style,
Time zone → Time zone, Style; a graphics or disk graph Reading, Style, adapter → Reading, adapter, Style;
the calendar lines' Public holidays from last to after what they are of (before Style); a markets widget
Symbol, Name on the bar, Chart range, Amount you own, Style, Chart → Symbol, Amount you own, Chart range,
Style, Chart, [Amount], Name on the bar; the volume slider's speaker before its direction and length; the
alarm Time, Alarm on, Repeat on, Name → Time, Repeat on, Name, Alarm on; virtual desktops' item size first
as on every line of items; the clock face's zone first and its label last; the calendar face's zone and
holidays first; the meeting face Show, Highlight, Width, Join → Show, Style, Join, Highlight from; the
quakes face's Style before its alert. Nothing of the file changes: every row reads and writes the keys
and values it did.

**What a pin opens, one row.** "What it opens ›" says the name of what it opens at its end ("Work",
"example.com", "Nothing yet"); its level (`OptionFields.OfPinTarget`, a search) is **Browse…** — Windows'
open dialog, a file or a folder (`OptionPickers.Browse`, a head over the field as a place's device switch
is, `OptionMenu.Rows`) — over a field holding the whole path, with the keys as it opens. Under the field,
before anything is typed, the folders the person's other pins open (`OptionFields.PinsInUse`) and
Windows' own (Home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Videos, wherever the person moved them,
by File Explorer's names: `Dock.PinFolderRows`); typed, what is typed where it reads as a target of its
own (a path, an address; `TargetFinder.OwnTarget`) first, then the folders under a path as far as it is
typed ("C:\Us" → "C:\Users", 50 at most, none hidden, none on a network or a share: `TargetFinder.Under`,
off the menu's thread), then the folders above by their names ("docu" → Documents); the one it opens
ticked. Enter keeps the first found, else the words typed as the settings app's Path box took them
(`PinTargets.Normalize`; "%USERPROFILE%\Music" now as written). Then, for a folder: How to show, Show
titles (showing its contents), the pin's Name — its field says the folder's own name while empty
(`PinTargets.NameOf`, which `MenuPickers.TargetName` was) —, its Icon, and Navigation, what a click on a
folder does, last. The "Path" row (`OptionPickers.PinTargetPath`, `settings.pin.target.path`) is gone; the
pin's keys and values in the file are as they were.

Tests: `MenuConventionTests` over every taskbar entry, every folder line, a pin to a folder, a markets
widget of each type and style, and every face — `EveryRowSaysItsPartAndTheyStandInTheOneOrder` (no row
without a part, the parts in order), `ARowsTypeFollowsItsValue` (in-row choices only alignment's icons, a
search only what it is of or what of it, a Browse… only over its search, an icon on every row, one style
called Style with its icon, a place "Place", a zone "Time zone", a pace "How often it updates"),
`EveryStyleIsInTheStylesPart`, `ARowsDepthFollowsItsType` (a toggle, a number, alignment and an action in the
row; every other kind one level, nothing deeper but a group's); `PinTargetMenuTests` —
`WhatItOpensIsOneRowWithBrowseOverItsField`, `NothingTypedOffersTheFoldersAndAPickKeepsOne`,
`TypingFindsAFolderOrKeepsThePathTyped` (on a folder of the test's own); `OptionRowsTests`,
`OptionFieldsTests`, `MenuPickersTests`, `MarketRowsTests`, `WeatherFaceTests` in the new order and words.
Pictures (150 %, dark): `config-widgets-dark` (the weather, a clock, a markets line, a graphics graph, a
calendar), `config-faces-dark` (the weather, earthquakes and meeting faces' levels), `config-pin-dark` (a
pin to Documents, its "What it opens" level, "C:\" typed, a pin to a web address).

By hand: in edit mode right-click a weather line, a clock and a markets line and see what each shows first,
its Style next; open a clock face's and a meeting face's settings in a folder's menu; right-click a pin,
open "What it opens", pick Documents, then type "C:\Us" and pick Users; press "Browse…"; type
"example.com" and press Enter; see the folder's rows appear and go.

## 293. The guard keeps Karpo down only when Karpo asked it to quit; a dock ended from outside with exit code 0 starts again (2026-10-23)

Twice (2026-10-22 14:34:39 and 2026-10-23 05:00:14) karpo.log had only the guard's line, "dock 6684 ended
at 05:00:14.178 after 5 h 19 min, exit code 0: it quit; putting the Windows taskbar back; it quit, so it
stays down", and no "dock: quitting: …" before it. The dock had been started from a shell inside the
Claude app, which ended every process it had started as it updated itself, with exit code 0. The guard
(it had broken away from that job and lived on) read 0 as a quit, and Karpo stayed down for hours.

**The signal is the exit code of the one way out, and nothing else gives it.** `Closing.Answer`, for the
host's marked close only, sets `Closing.Asked` to who asked (`DockHost.QuitBy`) just before `Dock.Quit`;
`Program.Main` returns `Closing.ExitCode(…)`: that value (`0x4B510001` the settings app's Quit Karpo,
`0x4B510002` `Karpo.exe --quit`) when it is set, else 0 (the loop ended by a WM_QUIT Karpo did not post,
which the dock writes a line for) or `DockExit.Fatal` on an error (an error on the way out of an asked
quit is still that quit). The exit code is part of the process object the guard already holds open, so
there is nothing to race and nothing left behind (a named event, a file); a process ended from outside is
left with the code its ender passes — 0, 1, -1, DBG_TERMINATE_PROCESS — never Karpo's own.

| Exit code | The guard's line | Then |
|---|---|---|
| `0x4B510001` / `0x4B510002` | it quit (asked by the settings app's Quit Karpo / Karpo.exe --quit) | stays down |
| 0 | ended without quitting (another program ended it with 0, as a job or a process tree ended whole may, or a WM_QUIT Karpo did not post) | started again |
| 1, -1, `0x40010004`, `0xC000013A`, crashes, 2, any other | as before | started again |
| any, while Windows signs out or shuts down (SM_SHUTTINGDOWN) | as before | stays down |

Restarts keep `GuardPolicy`'s limits (2 s, 20 s, 120 s; never a fourth within 10 minutes). The restarted
dock is started outside every job the guard is in (`DockLauncher`: breaking away, else Explorer's own
ShellExecute), so whatever ended the old one cannot end it.

**The guard and jobs:** the dock starts its guard with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` (`Dock.StartGuard`),
and in the incidents it lived on. Inside a job nested in one that refuses breaking away it can still sit
in the outer one (`DockLauncher`'s note, measured 2026-09-27); starting it through Explorer instead would
lose the environment (`KARPO_CONFIG_DIR`: a test dock's guard would restart a dock on the person's own
config) and the app package's view of `%APPDATA%`, so that is left as it is. A dock the logon task or
Explorer starts is in no such job.

**Quitting for an install swap:** `Karpo.exe --quit` (any build since §283) posts the marked close to the
running host; the dock writes "dock: quitting: Karpo.exe --quit asked", ends with `0x4B510002`, and its
guard leaves it down. A dock from before this change ends with 0 there, which its own (older) guard also
takes for a quit. Stop-Process or a kill restarts it.

No new strings, no timers, no config change. Tests: `GuardPolicyTests` (`A_dock_Karpo_asked_to_quit_stays_down`,
`A_dock_ended_with_0_without_quitting_is_started_again`, `While_Windows_signs_out_or_shuts_down_no_end_is_restarted`,
the crash table and the cap), `DockExitTests` (`Only_Karpo_s_own_quit_is_a_quit_and_0_is_an_end_from_outside`),
`ClosingTests` (`TheExitCodeIsWhoAskedAndOnlyTheHostsMarkedCloseSetsIt`: the codes, and in the source only
`Closing.Answer` sets `Asked` and `Program.Main` returns it; the host's marked closes set it, nothing else does).

By hand: Settings, About, Quit Karpo: karpo.log ends with "dock: quitting: …" and the guard's "exit code
0x4B510001: it quit (asked by the settings app's Quit Karpo); …; Karpo asked it to quit, so it stays down".
End the dock in Task Manager: the guard's line says "ended from outside" and the bar comes back 2 s later.

## 294. A click on a notification reaches its app again; what an activation could not do is said in karpo.log (2026-10-23)

The person: "when clicking on a notification nothing happens. should something happen?" It should: a click on a
notification brings its app forward with the toast's own launch arguments, a button activates with its own
arguments and what was typed and chosen, Windows' Dismiss clears it (§185, `ToastActivation.cs`).

**Why nothing happened.** A click that brings an app forward is an app opening for the folder (`CellAct.Action`,
`IslandView.App`): the line keeps the activation, the folder hides, and the dock hands it on once the folder has
gone (`Dock.FolderForward` → `NotificationPartTile.ActivatePending`). But `FolderFlyout` hides *before* it
forwards, and hiding tells every widget it is no longer shown (`FolderIsland.Closed` → `Visible(false)`), where
the notification line dropped its pending activation with the rest of the showing's state. So the dock always
found nothing to hand on, and nothing was written anywhere: karpo.log had no line because no activation was ever
attempted. It was so from the line's first day (5ca91853); the tests called `ActivatePending` with the folder
still open. A background button (a "Like", a reply sent with Enter) was handed on at once and worked.

**The fix.** The pending activation is a hand-off, not part of the showing: `Visible(false)` leaves it, and
`ActivatePending` takes it, as every other line's chosen thing (a message, a headline, a clip) already outlived
its folder's closing.

**Saying what failed.** Every road of `ToastActivator.Run` now reports an HRESULT (`IActivationPlatform`: the COM
activator's `CoCreateInstance` or `Activate`, `ActivateApplication`, `ShellExecuteEx` with its last error), and
`Run` returns the road that reached the app with every road that failed on the way (`ActivationOutcome`). Where
anything failed, one line goes to karpo.log (`ToastActivator.Line`), e.g.
`Notifications: activating <AUMID> (Foreground): Activator {clsid} 0x80040154; reached by Package` — the app,
how it was asked, each failed road and why, and what came of it ("nothing reached" where all failed). Never the
arguments or the inputs: they are the person's.

**Fallback.** As before, each road gives way to the next: activator, packaged activation, the shortcut's
program with the arguments, then the app opened by `shell:AppsFolder\<AUMID>`. New: a protocol activation whose
URI Karpo refuses (no scheme, `file:`) or Windows cannot launch (no handler) opens the app instead, as Windows
does when a toast's own activation cannot be made, and the line says why.

| Toast's app | Road taken |
|---|---|
| protocol (`activationType="protocol"`) | the URI; refused or failing → the app opened |
| a COM activator (shortcut's `ToastActivatorCLSID`, `AppUserModelId\<AUMID>\CustomActivator`, a package manifest's `ToastNotificationActivation`: Teams, new Outlook, Chrome) | `INotificationActivationCallback::Activate`, with `CoAllowSetForegroundWindow` for a foreground one |
| packaged, no activator (WhatsApp) | `IApplicationActivationManager::ActivateApplication` with the arguments |
| desktop, no activator | its Start menu shortcut's program with the arguments |
| none of those, or all failed | the app opened |

The right to the foreground: `AllowSetForegroundWindow(ASFW_ANY)` on the dock's thread as the activation is
handed on, while Karpo still has it from the click (unchanged).

No new strings, no timers, no config change. Tests: `NotificationsPresetTests.AClickOnACardInTheOpenFolderStillReachesItsAppOnceTheFolderHasGone`
(a click made with window messages on a real folder: the folder goes, and the activation still reaches the
made-up activator; failed before the fix), `NotificationCentreTests` (`AnActivatorThatDoesNotAnswerFallsThroughAndIsLogged`,
`WhereEveryRoadFailsTheLineSaysSo`, `AProtocolActivationLaunchesOnlyAUriElseOpensTheApp`, and the roads for each
kind of app as before).

By hand: open the notifications folder and click a notification of Teams, the new Outlook, a browser and an app
of words alone: each comes forward (a chat or mail opened at the message where the app supports it) and the
notification goes. Then look at karpo.log: no "Notifications: activating" line where it went the first way; where
a line is there, it names the road that failed and the HRESULT.

## 295. A reading's face in its graph (2026-10-23)

The person: *"the taskbar cpu gpu ram etc widgets should get a graph style as well"*.

**One Style row, the line's two words.** The Processor, Graphics, Memory, Disk and Network activity faces
have a Style row (§292: its part the styles, after the adapter or disk, before the pace): **Numbers**, the
face as it always was and still is where nobody chose (a file without the key reads so), and **Graph**.
The words are the performance widget's own (`core.widgetStyle.performance.figure`, `.graph`): a face's
choice may take its words from a widget's (`FaceOption.Words`), so no string was added. The file keeps
`"style": "graph"` in the face's bag. The face's style is what its line's is
(`PerformanceFace.Options(face).ShowGraph`, §229: Numbers is the graph's form drawing none), so the face, its
menu and the line say one thing.

**What it draws.** The glyph and the figure where they stood, and between them a room for the graph
(`PerformanceIsland.GraphRoom`: about a square of the bar's thickness, 32 DIP at the least). The reading's
recent history is the face's ground, as a reading's line has it behind its words (§24) and the markets face
behind its ticker (§246): across the bar edge to edge, along it to half the room between two faces (so two
graph faces side by side never overlap), on the card's corners, faded under the glyph and the figure and
full in the room between them, the newest step at the end. Down a bar on its side, the glyph over the room
over the figure. The value is always shown, over the graph's end, as on the line.

**One painter, one history.** The line's graph and the face's are one drawing (`PerformanceIsland.Graphed`
over `Sparkline.Paint` and `GraphBackdrop`): a share against the whole, a rate against the busiest step kept
(`Sparkline.Ceiling`, never under 64 KB/s), the accent's line over its gradient (the highlight in high
contrast), 2 DIP a step. The face draws the source it already held (`FolderIsland.PerformanceOf`, the
history every reading keeps from the dock's start), a step every pace it is set to (`PerformanceData.Paced`),
painted again in place on the folder's tick at that pace: no timer, no new store. Its reading for the clock's
tick is the figure and the steps drawn, so a step paints it again and only a figure more or fewer lays the bar
out (§244). The line's scratch for its points is one array a thread now, the face's too.

**Its length** (§275): the figure face's and the graph's room, nothing more; the room is fixed for the bar,
so the history scrolling never moves it.

Tests: `PerformancePresetTests.EachReadingsFaceIsItsNumbersOrItsGraph` (the Style row, its words, Numbers
chosen, Graph kept), `TheGraphFaceIsItsFigureAndARoomWhereItsHistoryIsDrawn` (each reading at 28, 48 and 72
DIP, across and down, 100 and 150 %: the figure face's length and the room, one thickness; ink in the room
with a history and none before one; a step repaints in place), the faces' options in
`EachReadingIsItsGraphAndItsDetailsOverTaskManager` and `OptionMenuTests.AFacesOptionsAreRowsByTheirKinds`.
Pictures: `performance-graph-face-<dark|light|contrast>.png` (the five faces in Numbers and in Graph, and
three graphs in one button, on a 48 DIP bar at 100 and 150 %; the graphs down a bar on its side).

By hand: in a folder's menu open a Processor face's settings, Style ▸ Graph: the button grows by about its thickness and
the last minute or less scrolls behind the figure; a network face's graph rescales to its busiest moment; set
the pace to 5 seconds and the graph steps every five; put a memory graph face beside it in one button.

## 296. Edit mode stays on through a change of the bar's position, type or way of showing; the edit bar stands across from the bars (2026-10-23)

The person: *"when changing position of the taskbar it ends the edit mode"* and *"when the taskbar is shown on
the top the edit bar should be shown on the bottom"*.

**Why edit mode ended.** Edit mode was held by a window: `Dock.editor`, the bar it was begun on (null: off).
Another edge, another type or another way of showing — from the bar's looks menu in edit mode (§290) or the
settings app, both `Apply` → `Arrange` — gives the display a new window (the arrange keeps a bar only on the
same standing edge and row), and `Forget`, for the old window, ended edit mode "with its bar's display". So
the bars came back at rest.

**Edit mode is the dock's.** Every display is in edit mode at once (2026-10-07); which bar holds it is only
where the keys fall back to. The arrange now hands it on before it forgets the windows that went
(`Dock.EditHolder`): the bar that held it while it is still a bar; else its display's bar now, the one made
again; else another display's; and it ends only with no bar left (`Forget`, as before, for that last case).
The new windows come in edit-dressed (the arrange's Show step, `BeginEditing`, as a place made in edit mode
always did); the dims, the edit bars and the sections' edit bars follow the arrange as at every build, and
they are kept by display, not by window. A change of displays or of scale (WM_DISPLAYCHANGE, WM_DPICHANGED)
and the session locking still end it.

The looks menu goes with the window it was opened on, as §290 has it: reopened on the new bar it would stand
at a pointer no longer by that bar and at its first level, so it closes; edit mode stays, the bar is arranged
where it now stands, and a right click on it opens the menu again.

**Where the edit bar stands** (`EditDeckRoom.Side`, `EditDeckPlan.Place`): centred, on the side across from
the display's bars. Something along the top (a Taskbar's or a Dock's bar, shown all the time or its places
brought in) and nothing along the bottom: at the bottom, 8 DIPs over the display's bottom. Otherwise at the
