top, as before — over a bar at the bottom; beside bars at the sides, which leave the top free (it stays where
it always was rather than moving to a side); and on a Top and bottom under the top bar (or the deepest top
place), 8 DIPs below it, since between two bars no side is across from both. `Dock.DeckRoom` measures both
edges now (`EditDeckRoom.BottomDepth`). What the edit bar opens hangs from its side (`EditDeckSpot.Edge`,
`EditDeck.ListEdge`, which replaces the constant `EditDeckPlan.ListEdge`): the add list opens up from "Add a
widget"'s top on an edit bar at the bottom and down from its bottom on one at the top (`AddAnchor`), the
tooltips likewise; the popups and the sections' edit bars keep clear of wherever it stands
(`FlyoutHost.Avoided`, `DeckPanels`), as before.

No config change, no new strings, no timers.

Tests: `EditHolderTests` (`EditModePassesToTheBarMadeAgain`: kept, its display's new bar, another display's,
none; `TheArrangeHandsEditModeOnBeforeTheOldBarGoes`: the hand-over before `Forget`, the looks' change through
`Apply`); `EditDeckPlanTests` (`TheEditBarStandsAcrossFromTheBars` for a Taskbar and a Dock along each edge, on
hover or not, and a Top and bottom; `TheEditBarIsCentredOverNothing`, now on the sides too;
`TheMarginScalesWithTheDisplay`; `ItsListsOpenAwayFromItsSide`, was `ItsListsDropDownFromTheTop`);
`SceneTreeTests.EveryBarIsEditedWhereItStands` (the real window across from the bars) and
`TheEditBarsAddListOpensAwayFromIt` (was `…OpensUnderIt`: from an edit bar at the bottom it opens upwards,
clear of a bar at the top). Pictures (150 %, dark): `editbar-top-edit-dark-150.png` (a Taskbar at the top, the
edit bar at the bottom), `editbar-bottom-edit-dark-150.png` (for comparison),
`top-<taskbar|dock|top-bottom>-edit-dark-150.png`.

By hand: in edit mode right-click the bar, Position › Top: the bar stands at the top, still arranged, the dim
up, the edit bar now at the bottom; "Add a widget" opens upwards. Type › Dock, then Show › On hover: still in
edit mode. The same from the settings app's Layouts and Displays pages while in edit mode. A Top and bottom:
the edit bar under the top bar.

## 297. A folder fills to the same far edge off a top bar as off a bottom one, arranged too (2026-10-23)

The person: *"when the taskbar is shown on the top the fill space does not properly extend all the way
to the bottom (the space is too big)"*.

**What was wrong.** At rest a folder was already the mirror of a bottom bar's: the room it is laid out
against (`FlyoutPlacement.Room`, less the "+" row, `FolderFlyout.Reach`) runs from the anchor and its gap
to the work area's far end less the margin, on every edge. Arranged it was not. In edit mode every popup
of a bar not along the bottom keeps clear of the display's edit bar (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`,
`FlyoutHost.ClearOf`), which stands under a top bar, and keeps clear of its room while it stands aside
for an open folder (§190). The folder was laid out against the room from its bar, then pushed down
under the edit bar's room. On a 1040 DIP display at 100 % that put it 48 px lower and 10 px past the
screen's foot, so its "+" row had no room left and its Fill line was too tall for the room it stood in.
A side bar's folder, which reaches up to the work area's top, was pushed down the same way. A bottom
bar's folder skipped the rule, so it alone came out right.

**The rule now.** The edit bars are never in sight while a folder is open (`EditDeckPlan.Shows`, §190),
so a folder keeps clear of none of them (`FlyoutHost.HidesEditBars`, set by `FolderFlyout`'s host).
Arranged, it stands exactly where it stands at rest, off every edge: its far end is as far from a top
bar's screen edge as from a bottom bar's, a left bar's folder stands where a right bar's does, and
nothing moves when edit mode begins. Every other popup of a top or side bar still keeps clear of the
edit bar and of its room while it is aside.

No config change, no new strings. Tests: `FolderFillTests.AFolderFillsAsFarOffEveryBar`. It takes a
folder with a Fill line off a bar on each edge, at rest and arranged, at 100 and 150 %, with the edit
bar placed as the dock places it, and checks that the Fill list is the reach and the panel stays inside
the work area. It also checks that the top bar's far gap and height match the bottom bar's within 1 px,
that the left bar's folder mirrors the right bar's, and that the arranged folder stands where it does at
rest. It fails on the old placement ("Top arranged at 100 %: 108..1050 outside 48..1040"). Pictures:
folder-edgefill-<edge>-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png. `EditedDisplay`'s folder pictures no longer require the
folder to keep off the edit bar's rectangle.

By hand: a Taskbar along the top, edit mode, open the clock's folder (a Fill line in it). Its far end
and its "+" row should stand as far from the screen's foot as they stand from the screen's top with the
bar along the bottom, and as far as they stand at rest.

## 298. An add that knows its place puts the widget there; only one that doesn't sticks it to the pointer (2026-10-23)

The person: "when i click the add on a specific column or specific slot then it should immediately place it
there and not stick to my mouse. only when the slot is not clear from the context it should stick it to my
mouse". Since §230 every pick in a folder's add list was carried on the pointer, the column's "+" (§246)
included, whose place was only where the line landed when let go over no place.

**One optional place per add.** Every way into the add list hands it a place or none, and that alone says
what a pick does (`AddSpot.Follows`, true where no place is known; `AddSpot.InFolder` for a folder's, from
a `FolderPlace?`; `Dock.BeginAdd` for the bar's, from a `BarSlot?`):

| Where the add was pressed | Place | A pick |
|---|---|---|
| A folder column's "+" | that column's end away from the bar (`FolderFlyout.AddPlace(list)`) | goes in there at once, picked (ringed), the list closing |
| A folder slot's "+" | a column of its own at that slot (`FolderPlace.Slot`) | goes in there at once, the slots between becoming empty columns as a drop makes them |
| "Add" of the bar's own menu (a right click on the bar's room) | where the menu was opened (`DockWindow.ListSlot`) | goes in there at once with edit mode's focus, as before |
| A "+" at a bar group's end | the index it stands at, through `BeginAdd`'s slot | goes in there at once |
| A display's "Add a widget" (its edit bar), its "Folder" and "Separator" | none | follows the pointer, a click puts it down (§7b), as before |
| A folder's add with no column (`Dock.FolderAdd` with no list: a folder's own "Add a widget") | none | carried in the folder as since §230; let go over no place, it lands where the folder adds (the selected line's column, else the first with room) |

"Add a face" (§281) adds a face to the folder's button from its menu; it never went through the add list
and is unchanged. Ctrl+V still carries what was copied: a paste has no place either.

**What went.** `AddChosen` carried every pick into a folder standing open, whatever opened the list, and
kept the "+"'s place only as the carry's home; now a carry is only `Follows`', its home the folder's own
add place, and a known place is `AddList.Add`'s straight away (`Folders.AddNew` at the cell, as before
§230). `BeginAdd`'s guess for a list opened with no place — after the block with the focus, else the bar's
end (`FocusedIndex`) — is gone: no place means the pick follows, and the display's add button opens its
list through `BeginAdd` too, so the bar has one way in.

No new strings, no timers, no config change. Tests: `AddListTests.APlaceKnownTakesThePickAtOnceAndNoPlaceFollows`
(a column's place, a slot's, and none, which follows and goes in where it makes no column),
`FolderColumnsTests.EveryColumnsPlusOpensTheAddListAndWhatIsPickedGoesInThereAtOnce` (every column's and
slot's "+" on a real arranged folder: the place it asks for is the spot's, which follows nothing, and the
widget stands in that column), `FolderAddCarryTests` (no place: carried, as before).

By hand: open a folder arranged, press a column's "+" and pick a widget: it stands at that column's end,
ringed, nothing on the pointer; the same from an empty slot's "+" makes a column there. The display's "Add a
widget" still hands its pick to the pointer.

## 299. An empty column's buttons at its end; edit mode's dim half black (2026-10-23)

The person: *"when a column is empty the add and width button should be all the way on the bottom or
top of the column, right now there is some spacing between them although there is no widget. the
background should be even a little darker / lighter when in edit mode."* This takes back the
`EmptyRows` of room an arranged empty column kept on the bar's side (§74, §149).

**An empty column has no height, arranged or not.** Arranged, an empty list was `FolderFlyout.EmptyRows`
(3) rows tall with nothing drawn in it; its "+" and width button stood past that room, and every slot's
level with them (`FolderPlan.EmptyRoom`): about 120 DIPs off the lists' side by the bar, over nothing.
Now `Flow` gives an empty list no height arranged as at rest, so its buttons stand at its end by the one
rule every list's do: `AddApartDip` (6 DIPs) off it, where its first line would stand, as far as a
filled list's are off its last line. A slot's stand at the same height (`WithSlots`: the lists' side by
the bar, `apart` off it). Gone: `FolderPlan.EmptyRoom`. `EmptyRows` is left for what it still is, the
panel of a folder with no widget at all at rest. Arranging now moves nothing, an empty column's height
included (§74's exception gone). A drop still lands in an empty column or a slot anywhere down its guide
lines (`OverColumns`, `SlotAt`: the window's room, not the list's box). An arranged folder whose
lists are all empty is a panel of no height; the host's rim geometry is never sized below nothing
(`FlyoutHost`: it threw, and what stands outside the panel, its buttons, was left unplaced). A widget
carried from the bar is offered to the folder over its panel as before, so over an all-empty arranged
folder there is none to say why it won't take it.

**The dim half black.** Edit mode's dim over every display (`EditShade`) is 50 % black (`Alpha` 0x80,
was 0x66, 40 %): one value in every theme, as before. Its colour is in one place (`EditShade.Ink`),
which the pictures' dim takes too. The desktop still shows through.

Tests: `FolderColumnsTests.AnEmptyColumnIsRoomAtRestAndASlotArranged` (no height arranged; on a bottom
and a top bar the empty column's "+" as far off its end as the filled ones' are off their last lines,
`AddApartDip`, and every slot's "+" level with it), `.ArrangingMovesNothingButAnEmptyColumn` (an empty
column 0 tall both ways), `FolderSlotTests.TheSlotsRepeatToBothEdges` (the slots' buttons `apart` off
the lists' side by the bar), `ListFolderTests.ArrangingAFolderMovesNothing` (a folder with no widget
arranged: no height), `FolderColumnsTests.AClickOnAColumnsRoomPicksNothing` (the empty column's room
beside the other's lines), `FolderOfferTests` (a folder of one line: its panel takes the offer),
`MultiListPictures.EmptyListSheets` (the all-empty folder arranged shows its buttons; it came back
blank), `EditStaysOnTests.TheDimIsHalfBlack`. Pictures (150 %, dark and light):
`folder-slots-bottom-150-<look>`, `folder-empty-lists-<edge>-<look>-<scale>`,
`editmode-folder-<bottom|top>-<look>-150`.

By hand: in edit mode open a folder with an empty column on a bottom and on a top bar: its "+" and width
button just off the lists' edge by the bar, level with the slots' and with a one-line column's; drag a
widget into the empty column and into a slot from high on the screen (it lands); the desktop under edit
mode a little darker.

## 300. A "+" at every section's inner ends on the bar in edit mode (2026-10-23)

The person: *"there should be add buttons for widgets in the taskbar edit mode as well, they should be left
and right in the center bar. (if no widget is there only show one add button) and they should be on the
right of the left group and on the left of the right group. then they should also be added for every other
group in the same fashion as i described."* The bar has had no "+" of its own since §7b moved the adds to
the edit bar (2026-10-07) and the sections' edit bars lost theirs; a folder's columns have theirs again
since §247. This gives the bar the same button.

**One rule, over a section's place** (`Layout.AddEnds`): a section's "+" stand at its inner ends, the ones
facing the bar's middle — the start's after its last widget, the end's before its first, the middle's
before its first and after its last — and a section with nothing in it has one, alone, in the middle of
its empty room (§7b's three cells, where a dragged block is still dropped). Along the bar, so down a bar
on a side the start is the top and the end the bottom. It is the same rule on every bar of every layout:
a Taskbar, both bars of a Top + bottom, each row of a Dock with two rows, a dock's sections (outside the
dock's panel, a dock's gap from it), a place along an edge (its one section's). The bar is not mirrored
right to left (§36), so neither are its "+".

**The look**: the round accent button of a folder's columns, drawn by the same hand
(`FolderFlyout.PaintAdd`): `FolderFlyout.AddDip` (24 DIP) across and never more than a cell, centred
across the bar, Segoe Fluent Icons' Add in the text on the accent; lighter under the pointer, darker
held down and while its add list is open. No tooltip, as the folder's "+" has none.

**Room of their own, in edit mode only** (`Layout.addRoom`, in `SectionLengths` and `Positions`): a "+"
and the widgets' gap (a dock's: the room between two docks) are part of its section's length, beside the
widgets, so it covers none and no widget reaches over it; at rest they are nothing. Overlaying the room
between the sections was the other way: it moves nothing, but that room is not there on a full bar, and
a "+" laid over a widget there could not be told from it. With room of their own nothing moves either: the
start runs from the bar's start and its "+" after it, the end to the bar's end and its "+" before it, and
the middle grows by the same room either side, so it stays exactly centred (whole pixels both sides). A
full bar makes the room as it makes any (§7b): placeholders, then the app buttons fold into "…". A
dock's panel ends at its widgets' room (`SectionPanels`, the docks), the "+" outside it.

**A click** (`HitKind.Add`, `Hit.Add`, `Layout.AddAt`; ahead of every widget's reach in `HitTest`, in edit
mode only) acts on its release on it, as a button does (`DockWindow.AddReleased`, the press held while it
is down, let go where the mouse is lost): the add list opens hanging from the "+" away from the bar
(`DockWindow.AnchorAt`, the pointer's anchor's rule), for that end of that section (`Dock.AddAtPlus` →
`BeginAdd` with the "+"'s `BarAdd.Slot`: `StartSlot` before the section's first entry, `EndSlot` after its
last); the line where the pick will land stands beside it meanwhile, and the pick goes in there, selected
(`AddChosen`, the place given, not following the pointer). On a bar locked under a folder open arranged
the folder closes first, as a press on a widget does (§289).

**Carrying**: the "+" are no place to drop on. While a block is carried along the bar, onto it from
another surface, or several together, they are out of sight (`Scene.ShowAdds`) — the sections stand
otherwise meanwhile — and their room stays, so the widgets do not move as they go and come back; a drop
reads the section and the gap as before (`DropSlot`, `SectionAt`: the room of a "+" is its section's).

**Narrator**: each "+" is a button of the bar's tree in edit mode (`BarUia.Entries`, `Add<n>`), named for
its section as the sections' edit bars named theirs ("Add a widget to the left", "… to the middle", "… to
the right"; the top and the bottom down a side, `AddList.HereIn`), and Invoke opens its add list. The
keys' walk along the bar (`EditStops`) is the blocks' still: Tab does not stop on a "+".

Tests: `BarAddTests` — the rule (`ASectionsPlusStandsAtItsInnerEndsAndAloneWhereItIsEmpty`), every
section's "+" beside its widgets on every edge and as a dock, on none of them, outside the docks, hit as
`Hit.Add` (`EverySectionHasItsPlusBesideItsWidgets`), an empty section's one in its room on the centre
(`AnEmptySectionHasOnePlusInItsRoom`), a place's one (`APlaceHasItsOwnSectionsPlusAlone`), none at rest
and nothing moved by their room (`ThePlusTakesRoomInEditModeAloneAndMovesNoWidget`), each adding at its end
of its section through `IslandEdits.ToList` and `AddList.Add` (`EachPlusAddsAtItsEndOfItsSection`);
`SceneTreeTests.EveryPlusIsDrawnWhereTheLayoutSaysAndNoneAtRest`,
`APlusLightsPressesAndStepsAsideForACarriedBlock`. Pictures: `bar-add-{taskbar,empty-middle,dock,left,busy}-<look>-<scale>.png`
(`BarAddSheets`).

By hand: Edit taskbar; a "+" after the left's widgets, either side of the middle's and before the right's;
nothing moved as edit mode came. Click the middle's left "+", pick a widget: it is the middle's first; the
right's "+": the right's first. Empty the middle: one "+" in its room, on the centre. Drag a widget along
the bar: the "+" go while it is carried, nothing jumps, it lands where the ghost showed. The same on a bar
down a side, on a dock (beside each dock), and with a folder open arranged (its first click closes it).

## 301. The folder's buttons on the edit bar while a folder is open arranged (2026-10-23)

The person: *"there should also be a top edit bar for the folder in the same style as the taskbar edit
mode has it."* The folder had had a bar of its own once (§214, §220: "Add a widget" and "Close folder",
a second `EditDeck` made with `folder: true`), which §251 took away with the close button on the face;
§287 took the folder's last close button away. This brings the bar back, and as one bar, not a second.

**One bar changing its buttons.** The edit bar of the display the folder is open arranged on stays where
it stands, in the same window, and shows the folder's buttons instead of the bar's
(`EditDeckPlan.Content`: `Bar` with no folder open, `Folder` on the folder's display, `None` — out of
sight, its place kept as since §190 — on the other displays). `EditDeck.Show(…, folder: true)` re-lays
the same host in place (a Tool host's reopening is not animated), so it reads as the bar changing its
content; the same painter, metrics, glyphs, accent, separator, hover and pressed fills and tooltips. It
stands in front of the folder's window, which spans the display (`EditStack.KeepOver` at every build,
and the folder's `StandsUnder` counts the edit bars as it counts the bars). It stands where the bar's
buttons stand (§296: at the top, or at the bottom under bars along the top alone), and what it opens
hangs away from that side (`EditDeck.ListEdge`), as for the bar's.

**The buttons, mapped from the bar's** (`EditDeckPlan.OnFolder`, `ActionAt(part, folder)`):

| The bar's | The folder's |
|---|---|
| "Add a widget" | "Add a widget" (`AddToFolder`): the same add list a column's "+" opens, for where the folder adds (`FolderFlyout.AddPlace`: the selected line's column, else the first with room), hanging from the button as the bar's does (`FolderAdd(…, from:)`, `EditDeck.ListEdge`) |
| "Folder" | none: folders do not nest |
| "Separator" | none: a separator is the bar's (`AddList.AddQuick` refuses a folder) |
| "Open settings" (the gear) | "Folder settings" (`FolderSettings`): the folder's own menu, the one a click on its face opens on a bar not locked (`WidgetMenu` on its key, its faces too), from the gear (`MenuBeside`, the sides of a widget of a bar along the edit bar's side); the folder stays open behind it |
| "Close edit mode" (the cross) | "Close folder" (`CloseFolder`): the folder closes by Escape's step, and the bar's buttons come back |

There is no heading: the bar's has none. Escape, a click on the folder's face and a click on another
widget still close the folder (§251, §287, §289).

**Nothing moves.** With fewer buttons the panel is narrower, centred where the bar's stood; `EditDeck.Panel`
stays the bar's place (`barPlace`), so the folder, the popups and the sections' edit bars keep clear of
the same room whichever buttons show, and nothing moves as they change and change back.

Strings: `dock.edit.closeFolder` ("Close folder", the 30 translations §287 removed, back under a key of the
edit bar's) and `dock.edit.folderSettings` ("Folder settings"), in all 30 languages. No config change, no
timers.

Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests.TheFoldersButtonsAskTheSameForTheFolder` (the mapping and the plan without
"Folder" and "Separator"); `EditDeckClickTests.TheFoldersButtonsClickAsksForTheFolders` (a real edit bar
changes its buttons in the same window and place, each click asks for the folder's, and back);
`SceneTreeTests.EditBarShowsTheFoldersButtonsWhereItIsOpen`, `FoldersOpeningAndClosingSetTheEditBars`,
`TheFoldersButtonsDoTheirThingForTheFolder` (the dock's wiring); `EditBarShowsTheFoldersButtonsSheets`
(editbar-<top|bottom>-<edit|folder>-<dark|light>-150.png: the folder's buttons as tall and centred where
the bar's stood, the bar's place kept, every button back once it closes).

By hand: in edit mode click a folder on the bar: the edit bar changes to "Add a widget", the
gear and the cross. "Add a widget" opens the add list beside it and the widget lands in the folder; the
gear opens the folder's menu beside it, the folder still open; the cross closes the folder and the bar's
buttons come back where they stood. With two displays the other display's edit bar is out of sight
meanwhile.

## 302. Show desktop without its icon; every number in its unit; the pickers at the rows' inset; a separator's room a pixel a step (2026-10-23)

The person: *"show desktop widget should get another style as well where no icon is shown. in edit mode
it should still show an icon but also in the greyed out color"*, *"the icons and color selectors have
additional padding on the left and right which i dont want. just the normal padding that all the other
selectors have."*, *"the width of the spacer has no unit. make sure that all properties that have a unit
also have it in the ui."* and *"make the steps of the spacing property in the spacer smaller. 1px"*.

**Show desktop's style.** Its menu has one row more, **Style**: **Icon** (as it always was) or **No icon**,
Windows 11's far corner of the taskbar, which shows the desktop with nothing drawn on it
(`ShowDesktopOptions`, `ShowDesktopStyle.Corner`, `Karpo.Core\ShowDesktop.cs`; `WidgetOptionsKind.ShowDesktop`;
`OptionRows.ShowDesktopStyle`). The file says `"showDesktop": {"style": "corner"}` for a corner and nothing
for the icon, so every file reads as it did and the default is unchanged; a word this build does not know
is the icon. The bar's part says it (`PartSpec.Bare`): at rest the scene draws no glyph and no card for it
(`Scene`, the card loop and the Show desktop button), the room, the hit, the tooltip and the click as
before, and the pointer lights its plate as a button's; it stands in no group, so no group's card runs
over an empty corner (`Layout.Groupable`). While the bar is arranged it draws its icon in the disabled ink
(`IslandInk.Disabled`, exactly what §247's greying gives a glyph in the words' colour), so it can be found,
moved and set.

**Every number in its unit.** A number row says what it is counted in, one way for all
(`OptionRow.Unit`, `OptionUnit` Pixels or Percent, `OptionUnits.Say`, and `OptionRow.Shown`, what the
stepper says: its `Said` words, "Automatic", else its value in its unit); `OptionMenu` shows `Shown`. The
audit of every number of every widget's, face's and bar's menu: the bar's opacity ("70%", as before), a
separator's line width ("2 px", "Automatic" at 0; a hairline is a pixel at 100 %, as Appearance's
"In pixels" says), its space on each side and a divider's gap ("6 px", as before), the volume slider's
length (a bare figure until now, "120 px"). A chart's years is a count its title names ("Years"), no unit.
A time and a length are no number but a level of their parts, each saying "h" or "min" (§240); every other
value with a unit — a pace, a distance, a keep-awake length, a bar's size — is a choice whose words say it.
A folder line's height is counted in rows, which its row says ("Fixed, 3 rows").

**A separator's room a pixel a step.** "Space on each side" steps by 1 px (was 4), and so does a folder's
"Gap in folders" (was 2): the person's "spacer" is the separator, and the divider is the separator in a
folder (its menu is headed "Separator"), so both rooms step alike. `BarLooks.SpaceStep` and `GapStep` gone;
the opacity keeps its 5 %, the slider's length its 4 px.

**The pickers at the rows' inset.** A colour's swatches and an icon's tiles stood in a block centred in the
menu, eight 32-DIP cells (seven 40-DIP ones) in a menu 310 DIP wide inside, so 27 DIP (15) more than a row's
inset either side. A line of tiles now spans the rows' own width (`Flyout.TileFill`): its first fill where a
row's starts, its last where a row's ends, the rest evenly between, each cell still square. The columns are
counted as before (as many as the room holds, at most the run's `Across`: eight colours, Windows' grid), so
at 100 % and 150 % alike; the icon picker's field and heads stood at the inset already.

Tests: `MenuConventionTests.EveryNumberSaysItsUnit` (every number row of every menu and the bar's has a unit
but the years, and its stepper says it); `BarLooksTests.TheSeparatorsAndTheDividersMenusSetTheirLooks` (a
step is a pixel, said in pixels); `MenuPickersTests.TheTilesStandInLinesAcrossTheMenu` and
`ThePickersActOnARealMenuAndThePicturesAreDrawn` (a line's first tile starts where Automatic's row starts,
its eighth ends where it ends); `OptionRowsTests` (the style row writes the option); `TypedRegistryTests`;
`SceneTreeTests.TheCornerIsKeptInTheFileAndTheIconIsNothing`, `TheBareCornerDrawsNoIconAtRestAndItsIconArranged`
(no glyph, no card, the icon's room at rest; the glyph arranged) and `ShowDesktopSheets` (nothing stands
out of the corner at rest; arranged its icon fainter than the icon style's). Pictures: show-desktop-<icon|
corner>-<rest|hover|edit>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png; menu-pickers-colors/icons-<look>.png;
separator-looks-dark.png (a separator's menu as it starts and with a width and a room chosen, a divider's,
Show desktop's).

By hand: in edit mode right-click Show desktop, Style, No icon: the corner is empty at rest, lit under the
pointer, and a click still shows the desktop; arranged, its icon is grey. Right-click a separator and step
its width and its space (each a pixel, in px). Open a colour's and an icon's level: the tiles reach from the
rows' left edge to their right.

## 303. A side bar's folder: every column centred on its face; the first column next to the bar on either side (2026-10-23)

The person: *"when shown on the left or right the columns from the middle folders should all be centered,
right now the largest column give the alignment"*, and *"when shown on the left or right it does not
properly align the columns in edit mode. the first column then should start on the left respectively on
the right side."*

**What was wrong.** `FolderFlyout.Build` knew two bars: a top bar, whose columns hang from it, and "any
other", whose columns stand on it, bottoms level. A side bar fell into "any other": its columns' bottoms
were level and the tallest gave the line, so a short column stood below the face, not beside it. Across,
the columns always ran left to right: on a left bar from the bar, on a right bar towards it, so there the
first column was the farthest. And arranged, an empty column outside the ones with widgets on the bar's
side "had no room to hang into and pushed the core out" (§158's side-bar rule, `FlyoutHost`): edit mode
moved the columns with widgets away from the bar by the empty columns' widths — on a left bar for empty
first columns, on a right bar for empty last ones (the person's own folders have both).

**The bottom bar's rules, turned by edge.** Two answers of the edge, used wherever the folder lines its
columns up, and the core's placement across the bar:

- `FolderFlyout.Over(edge)`: how much of the room a shorter column leaves stands over it — 0 on a top bar,
  1 on a bottom bar, ½ on a side bar. Each column's top is `Round((height − its height) × Over)`: a side
  bar's columns all have their middle on one line, the folder's middle, which the host centres on the face
  (`FolderPlan.Core`, its top found the same way). At a screen's end the block is kept on the screen as one
  (`FlyoutPlacement.Along`), as a bottom bar's is across, so every column still shares one middle. The same
  share lines up what an arranged folder draws besides: an empty column, of no height since §299, at the
  folder's middle, and the slots' buttons level with its own (`WithSlots`), a carried line's ghost in a slot (`SlotGhost`), and how far a layout with lines giving
  way stands from the one at rest (`FolderDrag.Down`/`At`, now taking the edge: half the difference on a
  side bar).
- `FolderFlyout.FirstOnRight(edge)`: on a right bar the first column is on the right, next to the bar, and
  the others leftward — the columns' lefts mirrored in `Build`, so every box made from them (lines, cards,
  buttons, core) follows. On every other bar the first is on the left: where a bottom or top bar starts,
  and next to a left bar. The slots before the first column stand on its side and those after the last on
  the other (`WithSlots`); a side bar's room ends at the bar, so only its far side has slots. Ctrl+Left and
  Ctrl+Right move a line into the column on that side as it stands (`KeyMove` turns the key on a right bar).
- **Across a side bar the core stands where it would alone** (`FlyoutHost`, `Core`), as it does along a
  bottom bar: the first column with widgets the flyout's gap from the bar, arranged as at rest, and what
  hangs off the core's bar side hangs under the bar, as an empty column past a screen's edge does along a
  bottom bar — drawing nothing, its buttons not there where too little of it shows (`WithSlots`), nor its
  guide lines then (`Guides`, on a bottom bar's screen edge too), and no place for a carried line where
  the room ends (`OverColumns` keeps to `Visible`, as a slot already did): a line let go over the bar
  lands where the edit bar adds, not in the column under it. The "never nearer the bar" clause is gone;
  an empty column on the far side hangs off there.

So a side bar's folder reads from the bar outwards on both sides, at rest and arranged alike, and
arranging moves no column with widgets on any bar. Bottom and top bars are unchanged.

No config change, no new strings. Tests: `FolderSideColumnsTests` (the plan on left and right bars at rest
and arranged — every column's middle the folder's, the first column at the bar, the others the lists' gap
apart away from it, each column's buttons over its own top — and on bottom and top bars as before; a side
bar's slots beyond the last column, their buttons and an empty column's on one row over its end at the middle; an empty column under the bar not there, no buttons and no guide lines;
real folders of columns of three, one and two lines on left and right bars with the face at the top end,
the middle and the bottom end: centred on the face in the middle, one middle for all at the ends, on the
screen, the first column the flyout's gap from the bar, arranging moving none;
`.ArrangedTheColumnsWithWidgetsStayNextToTheBar`, the regression: "(e) | a b c | d | (e)" arranged on
both, the columns with widgets where they stood at rest, the empty first one under the bar with no buttons,
the empty last one beyond; pictures `side-<edge>-<along>-<rest|arranged>.png`,
`side-<edge>-empties-<rest|arranged>.png`), `FolderColumnsTests.OnlyTheColumnsWithWidgetsAreCentredAndArrangingMovesNoneOfThem`
(now with "(e) | (e) | a b | (e)" on left and right bars; a right bar's empty columns after the ones with
widgets hang off to the left), `FolderTitleTests`, `FolderFillTests` and `FolderColumnFlushTests` (a side
bar's columns on their middle; a line carried out closes its column up to the middle),
`FolderDragTests.TheLinesGivingWayStandAsTheListsLineUpOnTheBarsSide` (half the difference on a side bar).

By hand: a left and a right bar, a folder in the middle group with columns of different heights: every
column's middle level with the folder's face. Arrange it: nothing moves, empty columns on the bar's side or
not; on the right bar the first column is the one next to the bar. Near either end of the bar the columns still share one middle and stay on the
screen; there a tall column's "+" comes in over its top edge, as it did before.

## 304. Every field typed in offers what it can: the other widgets' values, well-known feeds (2026-10-23)

The person: *"for everywhere where you can enter text freely there should be some suggestions on the input
(e.g. the feed, there should be some feeds already to preselect)"* and *"suggestions for text fields like
rss feed should also be other rss feeds contents."* §292's pin target (TargetFinder: the folders other pins
open and Windows' own before anything is typed, matches as it is typed) is the model, now one finder for
every free field: `SuggestFinder` (Karpo.Core\OptionSuggestions.cs).

**One finder.** Nothing typed: what the person's other widgets hold in a field of the same kind
(`WordsInUse.Of(config)`, by the row's key, their lines' and their faces', each once, in the order first
met; `OptionDevices.Words`, from `Dock.MenuSources`), then what the field knows of its own; the value it
holds ticked. Typed: the words themselves first where they are a value of their own, then what holds them
in its name, its quieter line or its value, those starting with them first. Enter keeps the first found,
so the words typed stay usable ("Ho" is kept as "Ho", not "Home"); Enter on an empty field keeps it
empty (nothing typed asks nothing: `LeastLetters` 1, the suggestions as `Suggested`). A field with
nothing to offer but what it holds already gets no finder and stays a plain line of text
(`SuggestFinder.Of` returns null). A line of text keeps a pick's value or the words
(`FieldPicks.Keep`). The pin's `TargetFinder` and the feed's `FeedFinder` are `SuggestFinder`s now: the
filtering, the ticking and the "each once" are the one finder's; the pin's keeps its disk listing
(`More`), its typed target (`Own`, `Typed`) and its paths compared without their last "\" (`Same`).

**The tick.** A search's results said which one the setting holds (`OptionFound.Chosen`) but the menu
never drew it. Every result row is checkable now (`Flyout.WithFields`: `Checked: found.Chosen`): the one
held ticked at the row's far end, in the slot every result keeps for it, so nothing moves as the ticked
one comes and goes.

**The fields** (every field of the configuration menus):

| Field | Offered |
|---|---|
| RSS feed's address | the person's other feeds (as each named itself, under its site), then 25 well-known feeds (`KnownFeeds.All`: BBC News, The Guardian, The New York Times, NPR, Al Jazeera; The Verge, Ars Technica, Hacker News, WIRED, TechCrunch; Nature, NASA, ScienceDaily; CNBC, BBC Sport; tagesschau, heise online, DER SPIEGEL; SRF News, NZZ, RTS Info; Le Monde, EL PAÍS, ANSA, NHK), each read as a feed on 2026-10-23, the person's language's of their region first (Karpo's language, Windows' region: `PublicHolidays.Home`), then their language's, their region's, English, the rest. Typed: an address (words with a dot, a colon or a slash) a row of its own first; words find a feed by name, site or address. A pick is read and proved a feed before it is kept, as before. |
| What a pin opens | as §292 (the pins' folders, Windows' own, a path's folders), through the one finder |
| Clock label, a clock face's label | the other clocks' labels, then the places of its zone ("Osaka", "Sapporo", "Tokyo"; this PC's for none) |
| Heading's words | the other headings' words |
| Timer's, focus session's name | the other timers' and focus sessions' names |
| Alarm's name | the other alarms' names |
| Markets label | the name the service gave what it tracks ("Microsoft Corporation") |
| Time zone, place, share, team, Windows Settings page, holidays' country, icon | searches already, unchanged |
| Pin's name | none: free; its field already says the name Windows gives what it opens, which empty keeps |
| A list's or a note's name (new, rename) | none: free names |
| Holding, converter's amount | none: numbers |

No new words (the feeds' names are names, `// not-ui`), no config change, no timers.

Tests: `FieldSuggestionsTests` (a feed's field: the other feeds then the well-known, its own ticked, each
once, typing filters, an address its own row, words no address refused; the well-known feeds by language
and region; a clock's label: the others' labels then its zone's places, typed words first, a pick or the
words kept, a clock face's alike; the names; Enter keeps the words typed and an empty field empty),
`OptionMenuTests.EveryFacesSubmenuHasItsChoicesAsLevelsOfTheirOwn` (a line of text's field may have its
suggestions), `FieldSuggestionsPictures` (config-suggest-dark.png: a feed's level with nothing, "heise"
and "example.com/f" typed, a clock's label's level).

By hand: an RSS line's menu, Feed address: the other feeds and the well-known ones under the field, its
own ticked; type "heise" and pick it (it is read first); type an address and Enter. A clock's Label: the
other clocks' labels and its zone's cities; type a word that one of them starts with and Enter: the word
typed is kept.

## 305. A press on the refresh button is its own; a read it asked for shows how it landed (2026-10-23)

The person: "clicking reload sometimes closes the folder, this should never be", and "when clicking reload
there should be a successfull animation that the user can see that it was successfull".

**Why it closed.** The button's press stayed the folder's (§282): the folder took the click at the release,
and asked the line what was under the *release* (`FolderFlyout.Activate` → `PartOf`). A press on the button
let go a pixel off it — the hand moving as it clicks — was the line's own click there: on a line of one row
of earthquakes, of a market, the click that opens the page and closes the folder. A press dragged off it
began carrying the line out of the folder. Reproduced on a real folder with real messages (the test below
fails so on §282's code: "let go a pixel off it: the folder said Forward").

**The press is the button's.** A press on it takes the pointer (`CellIsland.PressOn` true), as a slider's
does: the moves are its (`DragOn` lights it pressed while they are on it, as a Windows button), the release
is its (`ReleaseOn(up: true)`, the folder's button-up), and it reads again only where it is let go on it.
Nothing it does ever reaches the line's click or the folder's drag, in any state: turning, twice quickly,
the capture lost (no click). A press beside it let go on it is a click of neither (`Activate` returns for
`RefreshButton.Target`). Its **reach** is the room the line keeps clear for it (`RefreshButton.Reach`): the
4 DIP before it, its row's whole height, and on to the line's edge where it stands on the trailing gutter
(not over a view's arrows) — so a press a pixel beside the glyph is the button's, which lights as the
pointer comes into it, and its tooltip stands there too.

**How it landed.** A read a click asked for (`RefreshButton.Asked`) is watched until the line says none is on
its way (`Take`, at each wake and paint), then shows its mark: the accent's check (Segoe CheckMark, as the
clipboard's "Copied") where nothing went wrong, standing 1 s; the caution warning (Segoe Warning,
SystemFillColorCaution #FCE100 / #9D5D00, the text's colour in high contrast) where the line says why it did
not (`IRefreshable.Problem`: the store's problem, or the stale mark's "Last updated 14:05 — couldn't
refresh"), standing 3 s with the tooltip "Refresh" over that reason. The mark pops in over 250 ms (from 0.4
of its size to a little past it and back, ease-out-back, fading in) and gives way to the glyph over 200 ms.
With Windows' animations off it stands still for its time and goes at once. Timed by the clock, so a mark
whose moment passed while the folder was closed is not shown later.

**One timer, as before.** The button's own (§282) carries it: a frame (33 ms) while the glyph turns or the
mark pops in or fades; one tick at the end of the stand otherwise (the whole mark is one tick with animations
off); stopped while the folder does not show the line.

Every refreshing line says its `Problem`: weather, air, tides, earthquakes and sports their store's, markets
and news their feed's, mail, calendars and To Do their accounts' (or their freshness tip), contacts theirs.
No new strings, no config change.

Tests: `RefreshButtonTests.APressOnTheButtonNeverReachesTheLine` (a real folder of an earthquakes line of one
row and six, driven by messages: the middle, the reach's four corners, let go a pixel off and far off, off
and back, pressed beside and let go on it, twice quickly, while reading, the capture lost — the folder stays
open and reads again exactly when let go on the button; a click on the line still opens its earthquake);
`TheReadItAskedForShowsHowItLanded` (check and warning, their tooltips, stands, fades and ticks, animations on
and off); `TheMarksArePictured` (refresh-marks-<dark|light>.png).

By hand: open a folder with a market or earthquakes line, press its refresh button and slide off it before
letting go: the folder stays, nothing opens. A read that lands shows the check for a second; offline, the
warning for three, with the reason in its tooltip.

## 306. A feed wears its site's icon, or one chosen; every icon picker one grid after a cross (2026-10-23)

The person: *"for the rss show the favicon of the website from which the news come from. alternatively
you should also be able to select an icon to override the selection. whenever you can select an icon to
override there should be the cross icon to select as well to clear the selection. icons should not be
grouped into sections / groups anymore."*

**The icon picker** (`OptionPickers.Icons`, `MenuIcons`, `MenuPickers`), the same for every icon chosen in
place of a default — a folder's icon face (§259), a pin's icon, and now a feed's:

- **One grid.** The gallery (§249) is one run of tiles with no headings: files, places, media, people
  and time, devices, tools and symbols still follow one another, alike ones together, but nothing stands
  between them (`MenuIcons.Ids`; `MenuIconGroup` and `MenuIcons.Title` are gone). The search field over
  it filters as before.
- **The cross first.** Its first tile is Cancel's cross (E711, `OptionGlyphs.Clear`), named "Default" in
  its tooltip and to Narrator: it takes the icon chosen away and leaves the default — the folder glyph,
  the pin's target's own icon, the feed's site's icon. It is ringed while nothing is chosen and walked by
  the keys as any tile (Down from the field onto it, Right along its line). It replaces "Default" (the
  folder glyph's tile) and "The target's own" (the app icon's tile), so an icon is cleared one way
  everywhere. The row's end shows what is drawn — the icon chosen, else the default
  (`OptionRow.Fallback`), never the cross.
- Settings' own picker (a layout's icon) was one grid already and chooses no override; it is unchanged.

**A feed's mark** (`RssIsland.Mark`): on its line and on the news face alike, the icon chosen in its menu,
else its site's own icon at the glyph's size, else the news glyph — as it was before the icon has come,
and where the site has none. A site's icon is drawn as it is, square, where the glyph stood; nothing
moves when it comes.

- **Where it comes from.** The web pins' favicon store (`FaviconStore`): the site's page for its
  `<link rel="icon">`, then `/favicon.ico`, fetched once a month and kept in `favicons.json` beside the
  other caches, with Karpo's own agent and no cookies, never through a third-party service. The site is
  the one the feed names (`Feed.Site`), else the host it is read from (`RssStore.SiteOf`). After every
  address of the site's own, the icon the feed names for itself (`Feed.Icon`, `FaviconStore.Picture`'s
  `declared`): Atom's `<icon>` (square by RFC 4287), or an RSS `<image>` that says it is square (its
  width its height; one of no size is 88 by 31 by the spec, a banner); Atom's `<logo>` never. It is kept
  with the feed in `rss.json` (`RssSaved.Icon`), held to http and https as every link of a feed.
- **When.** Asked as the feed is drawn once it has been read (`RssStore.Icon`); its coming wakes the
  feed's widgets through the feed's own signal, as a read does, and the face's reading changes with it.
  No timer, no request before a feed is set; the dock keeps the feeds' sites in memory beside the pins'
  (`Dock.KeepFavicons`).
- **Choosing one.** The feed's menu has **Icon** among its words, after the feed (§292: `OptionSlot.Words`),
  the picker above. `RssOptions.Glyph`, `"glyph"` in the file, left out while none is chosen; a value
  that is not one glyph of the icon font reads as none (`WidgetItem.Normalize`). No reset, nothing
  migrated.

Strings: `dock.edit.iconsFiles`, `iconsPlaces`, `iconsMedia`, `iconsPeople`, `iconsDevices`,
`iconsSymbols` and `settings.pin.icon.own` left all 30 tables; the cross says `dock.edit.defaultIcon`.

Tests: `OptionRowsTests.EveryIconPickerClearsByItsCross` (a folder's, a pin's and a feed's: the cross
first and ticked, no groups, the gallery in order, a pick and the cross taking it away, the feed's row
among its words); `MenuIconsTests.ThePickerIsTheWholeGalleryInOneGridAfterTheCross`; `MenuPickersTests`
(a pin's and a folder's cleared by the cross, the keys along the one grid); `RssIconTests` —
`AFeedNamesItsSquareIconAndNoBanner` (Atom's icon, a square RSS image, relative ones, no size, a banner,
a logo, a script link; kept in rss.json), `TheSitesOwnFaviconIsAskedFirst`,
`WithoutTheSitesOwnTheFeedsIconIsWorn`, `TheIconIsKeptAndASiteWithNoneHasNone` (favicons.json read
again with no request; a site with none draws nothing),
`TheChosenIconWinsOverTheSitesWhichWinsOverTheNewsGlyph`, `TheFeedsIconIsTheOnePicker`. Pictures
(150 %): `rss-icons-<dark|light>.png` (the face and lines of one, three and six rows with no site icon,
its site's and one chosen), `rss-icons-picker-<look>.png`, `menu-icons-picker-<look>.png`,
`menu-pickers-icons-<look>.png`.

By hand: put a news feed in a folder (a site with a favicon, a newspaper's): its line and the news face
wear the site's icon once read; in edit mode right-click the line, Icon, pick a star, then the cross; a
folder's icon face and a pin's icon open the same picker, the cross first.

## 307. Taskbar separators and folder separators, each its own look; a separator splits only its own row of a dock (2026-10-23) — a separator is empty space, with no look, since §505 (2026-11-05); no bar separator since §511 (2026-11-05) — moving stripes since §524 (2026-11-07)

The person: *"separators should basically be split into folder and taskbar separators. they should have
all configuration properties independent form each other. the folder separator for now always was just
a space, it should be able to be a dot or line now as well."* And: *"dock two rows, the spacers should
only be on their column / row and not stretch over."*

**One look, twice.** A separator's look is `LineStyle` — its **Style** (a line, a dot or space alone),
its **Line width** (hairlines, 0 Automatic), the room on each side (**Space on each side**, a pixel a
step) — and its **Line color** is a colour of one's own. There are two kinds of separators
(`SeparatorKind`: `Taskbar`, the bar's separator; `Folder`, a folder list's divider), each with every one
of those of its own: `Config.Separators` and `Config.FolderSeparators` (the file's "separators" and
"folderSeparators", each left out while it is its default), and the colours `ColorSlot.Separator` and
the new `ColorSlot.FolderSeparator` ("folderSeparator" in each mode's colours). `SeparatorStyles` reads,
writes and names the colour of either by its kind; `BarLooks.WriteLines(config, kind, change)` is the one
write, and changes the other kind not at all. `DividerStyle` (a gap and nothing else) is gone.

Defaults: the taskbar's a thin line with no room, as since §246; the folders' space alone, 3 px either
side — the list split into two cards 6 px apart, exactly as a divider split it (§78).

**No config reset.** A file's "dividers" (`{ "gap": N }`) is read, never written
(`Config.DividersInFile`, `DividersBefore`): the folder separators become space alone, half the gap either
side, rounded up (`LineStyle.FromGap`), so a folder splits as it did; an old divider line's look (§78) or
null is the default. A "folderSeparators" the file has wins over its "dividers", in either order. The
next save writes "folderSeparators" (where it is not the default) and drops "dividers". The taskbar's
separators, the layouts and the colours are not touched.

**One painter.** `SeparatorInk.Ink(block, shape, upright, thickness, length, dot)` says what a separator
draws in its room and where: a line upright (a bar along the bottom or top) or lying (down a side bar,
and across a folder's list), a dot round, each in the middle on whole px; nothing for space alone. The
bar's separators (`Scene`) and the folder's (`FolderFlyout.Build` → `FolderPlan.Inks`, drawn by the
folder's separator visuals, `dividerMarks`) both ask it. A folder's line is its panel's hairlines
(`SeparatorInk.InFolder`: Automatic one, never the bar's doubled two, since a list's rows have padding of
their own), as long as a row's text runs (inset by `RowInset` at each end, as a menu's separator); its
dot the bar's dot. Its colour is the folder separators' own, else the strong colour of a line that must
be seen, as the bar's (`SeparatorInk.ColorOf`).

**A folder separator's room** (`FolderFlyout.SeparatorRoom`, was `DividerGap`): space alone is both
sides together, at least 2 px (`LeastGapDip`), and **splits the list into two cards** as before; a line
or a dot is its ink and its space either side, and **keeps the list one card**, drawn across it. Why not
a line in the gap between two cards: the gap shows the desktop, and a line there stands on nothing, the
reason a floating dock's separators draw none (§81). Two lists stand a separator's room apart (the person,
2026-10-10; `FolderPlan.ListGap`). Arranged, space alone still wears its rule across the gap; a line or a
dot is shown as it is at rest. The open folder plans again when the look changes (its signature has the
style, width and space).

**Menus and the settings app.** A separator's menu and a divider's menu have the same rows, built once
from the kind (`BarLooks.Separator(place, kind)`: Style, Line width while a line, Line color while
anything is drawn, Space on each side) — the divider's "Gap in folders" is gone. Appearance has two
sections in place of "Separators": **Taskbar separators** and **Folder separators**, each the same four
cards bound to its own `LineChoices` (one class, made for each kind) and its own colour pair; a
separator's settings open its kind's section (`SeparatorPage.KindOf`, `ShowSeparators(kind)`). The
Folder separators' Style card says what its style does to the list.

Strings, in all 30 languages: `settings.appearance.taskbarSeparators.header`/`.description`,
`settings.appearance.folderSeparators.header`/`.description`, `settings.appearance.line.folderDescription`;
`settings.appearance.separatorSpace.description` no longer says "on the taskbar"; gone:
`settings.appearance.separators.header`/`.description`, `settings.appearance.dividerGap.*` and
`settings.appearance.custom.separator.header` (the taskbar separators' colour is named by its section).

**A separator splits only its own row of a two-row dock** (`RowJoin.Join`). A section's docks are one
panel of both rows. Before, only where both rows held a section in as many docks did they join, pairwise;
where one row alone held it, the other row's empty half was cut under each of its docks, so a separator
in one row cut through both; and where separators split the rows unalike, the section fell apart into
separate docks. Now: pairwise where both rows have as many docks that stay apart (a separator in both
rows at one place, which the person asked to go through both, 2026-10-11); otherwise the section is one
span from its first dock's start to its last's end — each row's first dock reaches back to it, its last
on to it, the gaps between a row's docks its own, the other row's dock running on past them; a row
holding nothing there has one empty half under all of them. Along y alike, for the columns of a dock
down a side. A joined section still keeps clear of every other section's, else stands as it is
(`Parted`).

Tests: `LineRowsTests` (each kind writes its own; `OneKindsChangeLeavesTheOthersAlone`: style, width,
room, colour and a menu's row of one kind leave the other's as they were; ranges); `FolderSeparatorTests`
(the default splits 6 px apart; the space reaches the plan; `ALineOrADotKeepsTheListOneCard`, its ink
where the painter puts it; `TheOldGapIsTheFolderSeparatorsSpace`: the old "dividers" gap read into the
folder separators, odd gaps, old line looks, "folderSeparators" winning either way, the rest of the file
intact; `TheOpenFolderDrawsItsSeparators`, the real folder's visuals read back off the compositor);
`SeparatorInkTests.ThePainterDrawsEachShapeEitherWay`, `AFoldersLineIsItsPanelsHairlines`;
`DockRowsTests` (one row's separator, separators unalike in both rows, an empty row's one half, and
columns); `BarLooksTests` (the divider's menu has the folder separators' rows, every page binding of
both sections a row of a menu); `SeparatorPageTests`, `SettingsIndexTests` (the two sections and their
cards). Pictures: `folder-separators-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (space, line, dot, a thick line),
`folder-separators-window-<line|dot|space>-dark-150.png` (the real folder),
`dock-rows-split-<bottom|left>-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png` and `dock-rows-groups-*` (two-row docks with
separators), `separator-style-*` (the taskbar's).

By hand: Appearance shows "Taskbar separators" and "Folder separators"; make the folders' a line and a
dot and see a folder's list stay one card with the line or dot across it, the taskbar's separators as
they were; set each kind's colour apart. Right-click a divider in edit mode: Style, Line width, Line
color and Space on each side, the folders' own. In a Dock with two rows put a separator in one row's
middle only: its gap stands in that row, the other row's dock (or its empty half) runs on under it.

## 308. One wording for every menu; what can't apply is left out; web widgets open where they read from (2026-10-23)

The person, from the review of every context menu (artifacts\menus-sheet, sheets 1–5): one wording
rule everywhere; hide what can't apply instead of greying; no "Edit folder" as filler; headings that
name what they are; one order for the desktops' rows. Approved item by item (1, 2, 3, 6, 9; 10, the
separators' menus, is another rework's, and nothing here words a separator's rows).

**One name per Windows page** (`WindowsPages`, Karpo.Core\Widgets.cs). Every page of Windows' Settings
Karpo offers is one `WindowsLink` there, under Windows 11's name for it and "settings" — "Sound
settings", "Power & battery settings", "Network & internet settings", "Date & time settings" — never
"in Windows". A widget's page (`WidgetInfo.Settings`), a menu row's (`Dock.PageOf(WidgetAct)`: the
date and time, notifications, sound, network, power, hotspot, AutoPlay, storage, Windows Update) and a
status icon's (`Indicators.Page`) take the same entry, so the review's "Power and battery settings in
Windows" beside "Power & battery settings", "Sound settings in Windows" beside "Sound settings" and
"Notification settings" twice are one each. The Wi-Fi switch's page is the network's
(`ms-settings:network`), and the Snipping Tool's print screen key is Accessibility's Keyboard page,
named once ("Keyboard accessibility settings"): same page, same name. The clock's "Adjust date and time"
is the date and time's page, "Date & time settings"; the Settings button's "Windows Update" is "Windows
Update settings"; the metered icon's "Data usage" is "Data usage settings". An entry with no page of its
own still has Windows' "Taskbar settings"; it is another command than the bar menu's gear, which opens
Karpo's settings (`BarMenuTests.NoWidgetsMenuAtRestHasTheBarsRows` now looks at commands).

**Actions start with a verb.** An app opened says "Open" and its name, through `dock.widgetMenu.openApp`
("Open Task Manager", "Open Resource Monitor", "Open File Explorer"); the volume mixer is one act,
"Open volume mixer" (`WidgetAct.VolumeMixer` is gone); a site is "Open website" everywhere (the markets'
"Open in browser" and `WidgetAct.OpenMarketSite` are gone into `OpenWebsite`, which finds a share's page
too). The bar's own menu and the Start button's keep Windows' own words ("Task Manager"), as Windows'
taskbar and Win+X menu have them.

**A switch says what a pick does**: "Turn X on" / "Turn X off" (`Dock.TurnText`), the Wi-Fi's and the
Bluetooth's radios, energy saver on the battery and do not disturb on the notifications as the status
icons do ("Turn energy saver off", "Turn do not disturb off", "Turn airplane mode off", "Turn mobile
hotspot off"). Energy saver and do not disturb were ticked rows that kept the menu open; worded as the
radios are, they close it as the radios do (`MenuKeeps.Switches`).

**What can't apply is left out** (`ActRows`). A row the widget's own control would do nothing with now
is not made: nothing playing (play, previous, next, the steps, the player), a timer not running (Stop),
the steppers while it runs, a stopwatch's lap and reset, nothing to clear, no do not disturb or energy
saver on this PC, a radio Windows has not said of yet, a site the feed has not named, the Snipping
Tool's recorder on one too old, keep awake's screen while it is off, an app's "End task" where none of
its processes would end. Only a choice this PC has nothing for — the power modes, the output devices —
stays greyed under its heading, saying so, as before; and a delete Windows refuses, which says why. A
heading left over nothing goes, and a rule at an end. Where nothing is left the floor stands as before
(Dock.MenuFloor.cs): an entry's page, else "Edit folder" — so a menu is never empty.

**Web widgets open where they read from, and refresh** (`ForecastActs`, `MapActs`, `WebsiteActs`). The
weather's lines and face and the air quality's: "Open forecast" — weather.com at the place
(`weather/today/l/<lat>,<lon>`, the air quality's `forecast/air-quality/l/…`); the tides': "Open on map",
OpenStreetMap marked at the place; the earthquakes': "Open on map", USGS's map of the quakes the feed
lists; markets, news and sports: "Open website". Then "Refresh": the line's refresh button's click
(`IRefreshable.RefreshNow`), the folder's line that reads the same for a face (`FolderIsland.RefreshLineOf`;
the row works that line, `WidgetActRow.Works`), only where there is anything to read. This brings back a
menu row §282 took away, at the person's word in this review ("Refresh (the line's refresh)"); the
button stays, and every other line (mail, contacts, the calendars, To Do) keeps the button alone. A
place followed from the device is where a forecast last found it (`WeatherStore.DeviceAt`); with no
place known there is no row. Two faces whose rows read alike show the first one's, once, as any
repeated row.

**"Edit folder" only where nothing else is.** The icon face and a face with no rows of its own add none;
the floor's "Edit folder" stands only in a menu with nothing else, and last. The review's weather,
air, tides, quakes, markets, news and sports menus that were "Edit folder" alone have their own rows.

**Headings** (`IslandEdits.Header`). A folder's edit heading is its name, else the first face it wears,
else "Folder" — not "Folder · Folder" or "Folder · Clock". A pin's names its file without the extension
("Pin · notepad", as "Pin · budget"); a web pin's address stays as it is. The bar's menu has a "Layouts"
heading over the layouts (`BarMenus.Lines`), so the ticked one reads as the layout shown.

**One order for the desktops**: New desktop, Task view, Rename, Delete — the desktops face's
(`DesktopRows`), the desktops line's and Task view's line (`TaskViewActs`), and Task view's entry (New
desktop, then its page).

Strings: `core.link.*` are "X settings" in all 30 languages (English, and each translation's "in Windows"
taken off; German, French, Spanish and Simplified Chinese written again); `core.link.dateTime`,
`core.link.dataUsage`, `dock.quick.indicator.energySaverTurnOn`, `dock.quick.indicator.dndTurnOn`,
`dock.widgetMenu.openForecast`, `dock.widgetMenu.openMap` added in all 30; `core.link.notifications`,
`core.link.storage`, `core.link.autoPlay`, `core.link.windowsUpdate` and `core.link.keyboard` moved from
their old keys with their translations; gone: `dock.widgetMenu.soundSettings`, `networkSettings`,
`powerSettings`, `volumeMixer`, `openInBrowser`, `windowsUpdate`, `dock.quick.networkSettings`,
`dock.quick.indicator.networkSettings`, `airplaneSettings`, `hotspotSettings`, `energySaverSettings`,
`notificationSettings`, `dataUsage`, `dock.menu.adjustDateTime`, `core.link.printScreen`. No config
change.

Tests: `MenuWordingTests` — `EveryWindowsPageIsItsNameAndSettings` (each page once, "… settings", every
widget's page one of them; no translation says "Windows" where English does not),
`NoRowSaysInWindowsAndEveryPageRowSaysSettings` (every menu at rest and every status icon),
`ThePagesThatWereTwoAreOne`, `EverySwitchSaysTurnOnOrOff`,
`AMenuAtRestShowsOnlyWhatWorksAndEditFolderOnlyAlone` (no greyed row, never empty, "Edit folder" alone
and last), `AWebFaceOpensWhereItReadsFrom`, `AHeadingNamesWhatItIs`, `TheBarsLayoutsStandUnderTheirHeading`,
`TheDesktopsRowsAreInOneOrder`; `RefreshButtonTests.OnlyWhatReadsFromTheWebOffersRefresh` (was
`NoMenuOffersRefresh`) and `AWebLinesMenuOpensItsSourceAndRefreshesIt`; the menus' tables and words
updated across the menu, folder and preset tests. `EveryMenuSheet` re-rendered.

By hand: right-click a weather, markets or news folder and its line: "Open forecast"/"Open website" and
"Refresh"; a timer or the media folder with nothing running: only what works (Open Clock, or Edit
folder alone); the battery and notifications faces: "Turn … on/off"; a status icon: "Turn … off" and
"… settings"; any entry: no "in Windows"; the taskbar's own menu with two layouts: "Layouts" over them;
the desktops folder: New desktop, Task view, Rename, Delete; edit mode on a folder: its name as the
heading.

## 309. The layouts in the bar's edit menu: on par with the settings app (2026-10-23)

The person: *"in the taskbar context menu there should also be the option to select the taskbar shown and
add / remove additional taskbars. it should basically be on par with the configuration from the
configuration app."*

§290 left out of the bar's looks menu (a right click on an arranged bar's room) which layout a display
shows, the layout new displays get, a layout's name and icon, and Reset all. They are in it now.

**Layouts ›**, the menu's first row, names the layout shown and wears its icon. Its level (`BarLooks.Layouts`):

- every layout as a row of its own, with its icon, the one this display shows ticked, and **None** after
  them where Karpo may be hidden on this display (another display attached shows it) — the Displays page's
  dropdown (`DisplayLayoutChoice`, moved to Karpo.Core), as the bar's menu at rest lists the layouts. A choice
  shows that layout here and the menu stays, read again: its heading, Type, Size, Show are now that layout's.
  These rows stand in the level itself, not a level further down (`OptionRow.Inline`, the second exception
  to "a choice is a level" after the alignment's segments), ruled off from the rows after them;
- **Add layout ›** and **Duplicate ›**, each a level with a name field (the name it gets if nothing is typed
  as its placeholder: "New layout", "Default copy"): Enter makes it — Windows 11's taskbar as a new install's,
  or a copy of the one shown with new widget ids — and shows it on this display at once, so it is the one
  being arranged. The settings app makes one and opens its card with the name focused; here making and naming
  are one step. Past the free version's layouts both are greyed with the licence's sentence under them
  (`OptionRow.Enabled`, `Why`);
- **Name ›** and **Icon ›** of the one shown (the gallery a folder's and a pin's icon come from; Default is
  the layouts' own glyph), **Delete**, asked first in Windows' dialog ("Delete “Default”?", the Layouts page's
  sentence), greyed with "There is always one layout" on the last one; a deleted layout's displays show the
  layout new displays get;
- **New displays show ›**, the Displays page's last card.

Under **Custom colors ›** Appearance's **Reset all**, greyed while every colour is Automatic.

What the menu acts on is the layout the bar shows: another one's name or icon is set by showing it first.
Edit mode stays through a switch (§296): the same type and edge keep the bar's window, which is rebuilt with
the other layout's widgets, arranged; another type makes the bar again and `EditHolder` hands edit mode to it.

**One model.** Karpo.Core's `BarLooks` makes, copies, names, draws and deletes layouts and says which a display
shows and new displays get (`Add`, `Duplicate`, `NewName`, `CopyName`, `WriteName`, `WriteIcon`,
`WriteShown`, `WriteNewDisplays`, `GlyphOf`, `NameLongest`) and resets the colours (`AnyColor`,
`ResetColors`, which were the settings app's `ColorRows.Any` and `Reset`). The settings app's model writes
through them (`SettingsModel.AddLayout`, `DuplicateLayout`, `RenameLayout`, `SetLayoutIcon`,
`ChooseDisplayLayout`, `NewDisplayLayoutIndex`, `ResetColors`); its own copies are gone. The dock keeps a
typed name through `LooksKept` (`FieldKept` for a looks menu) and asks before a delete in `LooksPicked`.

Left out, each no setting of a bar: a card being open, a display's Identify (the menu stands on that bar),
Refresh (the dock follows Windows' display changes itself) and Appearance's link to Windows' own colours.

No config change. No new strings: the rows are the settings pages' words (and the folder's "Delete “{name}”?").

Tests: `BarLooksTests.EveryLookTheSettingsAppHasIsARowOfAMenu` now reads every two-way binding, swatch and
button handler of Appearance and Displays and every write of a layout's card, and holds each to a row, the
four above the only ones left out; `TheLayoutsLevelChoosesMakesNamesAndDeletesAsTheSettingsAppDoes`;
`TheMenuShowsTheLayoutsAndGreysWhatCannotBeDone` (inline and ticked, ruled off; greyed under the free licence;
Reset all); `AnotherLayoutShownInEditModeIsTheOneArranged`. Picture (150 %, dark): `bar-layouts-dark.png`,
the menu and its Layouts level; `bar-looks-dark.png` with Reset all.

By hand: in edit mode right-click the bar's room, Layouts ›: pick another layout (the bar shows it, still
arranged, the menu's heading follows); Add layout ›, type a name, Enter (a Windows 11 taskbar under that name,
shown and arranged); Duplicate ›, Enter; Name ›, Icon ›; Delete (asked, then the default layout shows); with
two displays pick None on one (its bar goes, edit mode stays on the other); New displays show ›.

## 310. The edit bar stands out and comes in; no "Folder" or "Separator" on it; a folder's room stops short of it (2026-10-23)

The person: *"the edit bar on the top should be more visible, users might not see it. maybe also with an
entry animation so it is more visible to the eye. folder and separator should go away from the edit
bar."* And since §301 the edit bar is in sight while a folder is open, so an open folder growing to the
far edge could run under it.

**Its buttons.** "Add a widget", a command bar's separator, "Open settings" and "Close edit mode"
(`EditDeckPlan.Parts` = 3: `AddPart`, `SettingsPart`, `ClosePart`). "Folder" and "Separator" are gone:
the bar's add list offers both as picks of their own, in Popular (`AddTree.Popular`: `folderList`,
`separator`), found by the search as any widget; picked from "Add a widget" they follow the pointer as
any pick does. `EditDeckAction.Place`, `EditDeckEvent.Kind`, `Dock.DeckPlace`, `EditDeckPlan.FollowSpot`,
`OnFolder`, `AddList.Quick` and `AddList.AddQuick` went with them. The folder's buttons are now the
bar's three, asking for the folder's (`ActionAt(part, folder)`), so the bar stands the same with either
and §301's `barPlace` is gone: `EditDeck.Panel` is where it stands.

**Its look** (`EditDeck`): as tall as a bar, 48 DIPs (`ButtonDip` 32 → 36, `PadDip` 4 → 6); "Add a
widget" an accent button, the primary command (`EditDeckPlan.IsAccent`: the accent fill, its hover and
pressed shades, glyph and words in `TextOnAccent`); the panel in an accent rim, whole px
(`FlyoutHost.AccentRim`; high contrast keeps the system's). The rest as before: the flyouts' surface,
its shadow, the icon-only gear and cross with their tooltips.

**Its entry** (`FlyoutHost.Enter`): as it comes into sight — edit mode starting, back from standing
aside for a folder on another display — it slides in from its side by the room its window keeps there
(its margin: from the screen's edge, or from the bar's inner side, so nothing of it is cut) and fades
in, 250 ms (`FlyoutHost.Rise`) on Windows' decelerate curve (`EditLook.Decelerate`): composition
animations on the panel's root, no timer. Nothing with animations off (`Look.Animations`). Not when it
is drawn again where it stands (a change of scale, the folder's buttons and back): those buttons are the
same three, so nothing visible changes and nothing animates. Every other popup still opens unanimated.

**A folder's room** (`DockWindow.FolderWork`): the work area less the other bars, its own bar's strip
and, in edit mode, the edit bar's band of that display (`Dock.DeckBand`, `EditDeck.Band`,
`EditDeckSpot.Band`), taken as a bar along the edit bar's side takes its strip: from that edge to the
panel's inner side (`Dock.PopupRoom`). One rule for every edge: off a bottom bar the folder reaches up
to the edit bar's margin at the top, off a top bar down to its margin at the bottom — the mirror, the
same gap —; off a side bar it stays under it; under a Top + bottom's top bar it starts under it. The
band holds while the edit bar stands aside too (it comes back as the folder opens there), and is none at
rest. Its guide lines and empty slots keep inside the same room. §297's `FlyoutHost.HidesEditBars` is
gone: a folder goes through the popups' one rule (`ClearOf` over `Avoided`), which never moves it now,
its room already clear of the edit bar.

No config change, no new strings, no timers.

Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests.TheButtonsStandInOneRowWithTheSeparatorBeforeSettings`,
`TheSettingsAndCloseButtonsAreSquareWhateverTheirWords`, `EachButtonAsksForItsOwnAndTheFoldersForTheFolder`,
`AFoldersRoomStopsShortOfTheEditBarsBandMirrored`; `EditDeckClickTests.EachButtonsClickAsksForItsOwn`,
`ItComesInAnimatedOnlyWithAnimationsOn` (one entrance as it comes and as it comes back, none for the
folder's buttons and back, none with animations off, at the top and at the bottom);
`EditRailTests.TheAddListOffersTheFolderAndTheSeparator`; `FolderFillTests.AFolderFillsAsFarOffEveryBar`
(arranged: the room less the band, never under the edit bar, top mirroring bottom, as near its bar as at
rest); `EditedDisplay`'s folder pictures (the folder and its guide lines clear of the edit bar).

By hand: start edit mode: the edit bar slides in from the top (from the bottom under a top bar) and
fades in; "Add a widget" is accent-filled, the bar has an accent rim. With animations off in Windows it
is just there. Folder and Separator are in "Add a widget" › Popular. Open a folder with a Fill line in
edit mode off a bottom bar and off a top bar: it stops short of the edit bar, the same gap either way.

## 311. A widget's own look: its card, outline and highlight over the bar's, under Height (2026-10-23)

The person: *"you should be able to override the style on a per widget basis. the settings for this should
go under the height settings."*

**One model.** The bar dresses every widget alike in Appearance's custom colours (`BarColors`, §57) over
Windows' own. A widget may now wear its own of the three that are a widget's (`WidgetLooks.Slots`): its
card, the card's outline and the highlight under the pointer, each for the light mode and the dark mode
apart, in the very record the bar's are (`WidgetItem.Colors`, a `BarColors`, written `"colors"` on the
widget: `{"dark": {"card": "#FF1E3A5F"}}`). Automatic is nothing in the file and follows the bar. One
resolver: `Palette.Over` — the widget's own over the bar's, colour by colour (`WidgetLooks.Over`, `Own`).
What existed per widget before was only a separator's and a divider's colour, which is every separator's
(Appearance's "Separators", §290); a separator and a divider have no look of their own, wearing no card
(`WidgetLooks.Has`). `Normalize` keeps only the three, as the file wrote them (a word that does not read is
kept and read as Automatic, as the bar's); the bar's own background, separators, flyouts and the recent
colours are never a widget's. No reset, no shape change: a file without it is as it was.

**Drawn wherever a card's colours are resolved.** On the bar every part carries its widget's own colours
(`PartSpec.Colors`, from `PartSpec.For`, the one place an island becomes a part); the scene's one theme
(`Scene.Theme`) is resolved per part where a widget has its own (`Scene.TokensOf`: the bar's look with
`own.Over(look.Colors)`), and every brush that draws a card, its outline, its edit wash and the highlight
(`ShadeOf`) reads its part's tokens. A colour picked recolours in place as before (`Swatch` keeps whose
tokens a brush reads, `Recolour` reads them again). A widget with a card or an outline of its own wears it
on a dock too, which wears no cards else, its corners its highlight's (`OwnCard`); in a group it is its
piece of the group's card (§245). A folder's button is a bar entry, so its faces wear the button's. A
folder's line stands on the folder's surface and wears nothing of the bar's: its own card fills it at rest,
its outline rings it, its highlight lights it, pressed at two thirds (`FolderFlyout.InkOf(…, own)`,
`OwnOf`, `RimOf`); every line now wears a fill and an outline brush of its own, set in place
(`washes`, `rims`; the three shared brushes `lineHover`, `linePressed`, `lineRest` are gone). High
contrast ignores a widget's colours as it does the bar's.

**In the menu, under Height.** "Appearance ›" (the Palette icon) is the last row of a widget's menu on an
arranged bar, ruled off and standing still at the foot (`FlyoutItem.Foot`, §276, §281): under "Height ›" on
a folder's line, under "Add a face ›" on a folder, alone at the foot elsewhere. Its level
(`WidgetLooks.Rows`, `OptionMenu.LookSection`): **Card**, **Card outline** and **Highlight**, each the
Appearance swatch row of the mode Windows is in (`OptionPickers.Swatches`, which the bar's colours'
`Colors` now is too: Automatic, the recent colours, the grid, "Custom color…"), the card and the outline
offering **None** after Automatic (`ColorPalette.Clear`, transparent: no card where the bar has one); and
**Reset all**, both modes back to the bar's, greyed while there is nothing of its own. A colour row says
"None" at its end for none. An action that asks nothing is done where the menu stands, which stays
(`OptionMenu.Rows`: `Stays` when there is no `Ask`; greyed with no `Set`); the one other action, a
notebook's delete, asks and closes as before. A pick is found through `OptionMenu.Row` (the widget's rows,
then its look's), so a swatch, the colour dialog (`MenuBrowse`) and Reset act as every row does.
`OptionMenu.Settings` is now the one assembly of a widget's settings in its menu — the section, the faces
and "Add a face", the height, the look — which `Dock.OptionRowsFor` and the menu shown again after a pick
both use (the height moved in from `WidgetMenu`, so a refresh keeps the foot rows in order).

Strings: `dock.edit.look.card` ("Card") and `dock.edit.look.none` ("None"), in all 30 languages; the row
is Settings' "Appearance", the outline and highlight Appearance's own names, "Reset all" Appearance's.

Tests: `WidgetLookTests` — `AWidgetsOwnColoursStandOverTheBarsInTheirModeAlone` (the resolver: own over
the bar's, a mode's alone, only the three, a separator none), `TheFileKeepsAWidgetsThreeColoursAsItWroteThem`,
`AppearanceStandsAtTheMenusFootUnderHeight` (a line: Height then Appearance, the foot's run; a folder: Add a
face then Appearance; at rest and on a separator none; the level's rows, Reset greyed),
`EachColourIsTheWidgetsOwnAndAutomaticFollowsTheBarAgain` (a swatch per row, None, a custom colour's alpha,
Automatic, Reset all in both modes), `AFoldersLineWearsItsOwnCardAndHighlight`;
`SceneTreeTests.TheBarDrawsAWidgetsOwnCardOutlineAndHighlight` (a real scene: each card's own colour, the
bar's beside it, the own outline, the own highlight and the bar's on another). Pictures (150 %, dark and
light): `widget-look-bar-<look>` (a widget alone in its own card, lit in its own highlight; one in its own
card and outline in a group with one following the bar), `widget-look-folder-<look>` (a line in its own
card and outline), `widget-look-menu-<look>` (a line's menu with Height and Appearance at the foot, the
Appearance level, the card's colours).

By hand: in edit mode right-click a widget on the bar, open "Appearance" at the foot and pick a card, an
outline and a highlight: the widget follows with the menu open, the others keep the bar's; pick "None"
for the card on a bar with cards; "Reset all"; switch Windows to light mode and see the widget follow the
bar there until set for light too. In an open folder do the same on a line, under its Height.

## 312. A click on any line is asked of its own card: one target unless the line says where its buttons are (2026-10-23)

Found while fixing the refresh button (§305): a click on a sports line did nothing. The person's log had it
for the air quality's: *"dock, caught and carried on: NotSupportedException: airQuality has no length along a
bar: it is a component, sized by the room its folder gives it."*, thrown at `CellIsland.Length` ←
`TilePaint.CellAt` ← `CellIsland.TargetOn` ← `FolderFlyout.PartOf` ← `Activate`.

**Why a line's click measured the bar's cells.** What a click on a card hits (`CardTarget`) and what the card
draws (`PaintCard`) are two virtuals, and each defaulted to the bar's cells: the cell under the point
(`TilePaint.CellAt`), the cells in a row. A kind that drew its own card and said nothing of its targets kept
the first default for a drawing it no longer had. Where a line's drawing has no shape in `WidgetShapes`, its
cells' lengths come from `Length`, which a component (`CardOnly`, a list's line) refuses: it has no cells
along a bar. So the folder threw on every press on the sports line, the air quality's, the tides' and a
network drive's; the dock caught it, and the click did nothing. Elsewhere it answered a cell nobody drew, and
held only because those kinds have one cell, so the answer was 0. Eleven kinds — the battery, the clock, a
