divider, a heading, the graphs, the quick-settings pages, Security, a shell, the time header, a note and a
to-do list — had each written `CardTarget => 0` by hand to get away from it; the four that had not were the
ones that broke.

**One default.** `CardTarget` is 0, the widget's own click, unless the kind says where its card has buttons of
its own (a meeting's Join, a month's arrows, a mixer's mute). The bar's cells are asked only where the bar's
drawing is what is on the screen (`TargetOn`, a card with no room for a card drawing). The eleven hand-written
zeros are gone. No line kind needs an override to not throw, and none changes what it does: a line that drew
its cells answered 0 already, having one.

What each click does is unchanged: the sports line hands the dock its match's page (or the team's) on ESPN and
the folder goes (`SportsTile.Click`, §239); the air quality's and the tides' lines do nothing but their refresh
button, and the folder stays open; a network drive's opens the drive.

Tests: `LineClickTests.EveryLineAnswersAClickFromItsOwnCard` — every kind a list holds, set up on the gutter
sheets' stand-ins (`ListGutterTests.StoodIn`), in a real folder of its own on a hidden desktop: a press at
points all over the line asked of the folder (`PartAt`), none throwing; the sports, air quality and tides
lines clicked with real messages (the sports line forwards an app opening and the folder goes; the other two
say nothing and the folder stays). On the old code it fails for exactly the four: sports, air quality, tides
and a network drive.

By hand: open a folder with a sports line and click it: the match opens in the browser. Click an air quality
or a tides line: nothing happens, and nothing is written to karpo.log.

## 313. Icon buttons name themselves when lit; pins get Windows' rows; do not disturb for a time; no "Group" tag (2026-10-23)

From the menus sheet (artifacts\menus-sheet, tiles 1, 6–10, 43, 48, 137, 138), four approved items.

**Icon buttons say their name when lit, and only then.** The rows of icon buttons — the bar's own
menu's Add, Edit taskbar and Taskbar settings (tile 1), an arranged widget's Cut, Copy and Remove — had
this since §214: no words on the button, a tooltip with its name and shortcut ("Copy (Ctrl+C)") after
the pointer or the keys rest on it, at once from one button to the next, and Narrator calls each a
button by its name. It was the root menu's alone: a submenu's tools (a segmented row's buttons) said
nothing. Now every icon-only control of every menu level tips the same way (`Flyout.Tips`,
`ToolTipFor`; a submenu's tooltip is made as its root's, `tipDock`/`tipClass`). No look changed.

**Pins: Windows' rows for what they open, one rule on the bar and in a folder** (`Dock.PinRows`, under
the app's own row in `AppRows`). A file or a folder this PC has: "Run as administrator" where it means
something (a program, as before), "Open file location" (Explorer with it selected), "Copy as
path" (in quotes, as Explorer's) and "Properties" (Windows' own dialog, ShellExecute "properties"). A
link: "Copy link". None for an app by its id, a shell place, a pin whose target is gone. A pin in a
folder had the first three through its kind's acts (`ActsFor(ListKind.Pin)`, now empty); the bar's
had none. The copies go to the clipboard through the menus' one seam (`MenuVerbs.Copy`,
`OpenFromMenu`), stay in Karpo (an open folder stays). Because the rule is the target's, an app pinned
by its .exe gets them too, on the bar as it already did in a folder.

**A pin's way off says where it goes** (`UnpinItem`): "Unpin from taskbar" on the bar, "Remove from
folder" in a folder (tile 10 said "Unpin from taskbar" and took it out of the folder). A missing pin
(tile 9) says the same, not "Remove this pin", and its menu is one for the bar and a folder
(`BrokenMenu`, `BrokenRows`): its first row the pin's name, greyed with a warning glyph, and why it
can't open and its target under it as the row's detail — no drawn title any more, as no widget menu
has one. A row's detail now wraps instead of ending in "…" (`Gfx.Wrapped`, for every `FlyoutItem.Detail`:
the add list's reasons too), so the explanation is read whole.

**Do not disturb for a time** (tiles 43, 48; `DoNotDisturbRows`). The notification list's and the
bell's menus had one switch ("Turn do not disturb on/off" since §308). Now, by Windows' state: off — "Turn do not disturb on",
"Turn on for 1 hour", "Turn on until tomorrow"; on — "Turn do not disturb off", with "Until 14:30"
under it while on for a time; none where Windows won't let Karpo switch it ("Notification settings"
is the way then). The on and off rows are §308's words for the switch (`TurnText`), the same the
status icon's menu says. One-off commands: a pick closes the menu. They work the widget's own service
(`INotificationActs.Dnd`, the one the header and the bell show); a menu at rest, with no widget
to ask, has none, as §308 leaves out every control there.
Windows' own schedule can't do a one-off: it is a daily range, the person's, and changing it for an
hour would change their setting. So the end is Karpo's own timer (`DoNotDisturb.TurnOnUntil`, a
`TimeProvider` timer that looks at least once a minute, so a PC that slept through the end turns it
off within a minute of waking). At the end it turns off only the person's own on; a rule of Windows'
holding it on stands. Any other say ends the time: a switch in Karpo, or turning it off in Windows'
notification center. "Until tomorrow" ends at the next local midnight (`DoNotDisturb.Tomorrow`, a
clock change's night too). The end is not written anywhere: a Karpo that exits before it leaves do
not disturb on, as Windows' own toggle would.

**"Notification settings" with the bell's rows** (tile 48). A folder's faces' menu shows a command
several faces offer once (§257); it kept the first, so the time-and-date face's "Notification settings"
took it from the bell's group after it. It keeps the last now (`FaceRows`): the bell's group is whole,
the date and time's is "Date & time settings". A clock and a calendar read "Open Clock" — "Open
Calendar", "Date & time settings".

**No "Group" tag in the add list** (tiles 137, 138; the person: "remove the group indicator from the add
widget menu"). The pill a ready-made folder's row wore since 2026-10-12 is gone, and with it
`FlyoutItem.Badge`, its drawing and its string (`dock.add.groupBadge`, 30 languages).

Strings: `dock.menu.removeFromFolder`, `dock.widgetMenu.copyAsPath`, `dock.widgetMenu.copyLink`,
`dock.dnd.forAnHour`, `.untilTomorrow`, `.until` in all 30 languages (on and off are §308's
`dock.quick.indicator.dndTurnOn`, `.dndOff`); `dock.pin.remove` and `dock.add.groupBadge` removed. No config change.

Tests: `MenuModePictures.EveryIconButtonSaysItsNameWhenLitAndToNarrator`; `FolderMenuRowsTests.
APinsTargetHasWindowsOwnRows`, `TheNotificationListsMenuSwitchesDoNotDisturb`; `BarMenuTests.
ABrokenPinsFlyoutIsWhatMendsIt`; `WidgetMenuTests.APinsMenuHasTheRowOnTopOnlyWhileArranged` ("Remove
from folder"); `DoNotDisturbTests.OnForATimeTurnsItselfOffAtItsEnd`, `ATimeEndsWithAnyOtherSay`,
`TomorrowStartsAtMidnightHere`, `DoNotDisturbRowsFollowItsState`; `FaceMenuTests.
TheBellsRowsKeepNotificationSettings`; the menus sheet (`EveryMenuSheet`) re-rendered.

By hand: hover the bar menu's three icons and an edit menu's Cut/Copy/Remove: a tooltip after a
moment, none before; Home/arrows show them too. Right-click a pinned file, folder and web link: the new
rows; "Copy as path" pastes a quoted path, "Properties" opens Windows' dialog. A pin in a folder says
"Remove from folder". In a notification menu turn do not disturb on for an hour: the bell shows it,
the menu says "Turn do not disturb off" with the end time, and it goes off by itself.

## 314. The edit menu's caption: the widget's type, over the menu; Add a face under the faces; one rule over the foot (2026-10-23)

The person: *"height and appearance should not have a divider between them in the menus"*; *"add a face should
not be bottom aligned anymore but right under the faces list."*; *"the widget titles in the edit menus should just
be the widget type, not anything else like place or so."*; *"the type of the widget should be shown over the edit
menu, right now it is shown inside the edit menu, it should be shown over it and centered on the edit menu"*.

**One rule over the foot** (`OptionMenu.Foot`). The rows that stand still at a configuration menu's foot — a folder
line's "Height ›" (`LineHeightRows.Row`) and a widget's "Appearance ›" (`OptionMenu.LookRow`, §311) — are put
there together under one rule, none between them. Each built its own rule before (`LineHeightRows.Rows`,
`LookSection`), and `Flyout.FootFrom` took a rule between foot rows into the foot (§281's stacking); both gone:
`FootFrom` is the run of foot rows at the end and the one rule over it. `OptionMenu.Settings` is still the one
assembly; `LineHeightRows.Updated` replaces the height's row alone.

**Add a face under the faces.** "Add a face ›" is no foot row any more: it is the folder's faces' last row, with
no rule between, as "Add a toggle" is a toggles list's, and scrolls with them. Only Height and Appearance stand
still at the foot (§280's foot for it is gone).

**The caption** (`Flyout.Caption.cs`). A configuration menu (§288) names what it is of by its type alone —
`IslandEdits.Kind`: the widget's kind's name ("Clock", "Conditions", "Pin"), "Folder" for every folder;
`BarLooks.Kind`: "Taskbar" — never a place, zone, label, folder name, pin target or layout name
(`IslandEdits.Header` stays the name of a menu at rest; `BarLooks.Title` is gone). It is no row of the menu
any more (§279's heading in `OptionMenu.Section`, its `title`, gone): it stands over the menu's panel, centred on
its width, 6 DIP off its top, on every level the menu opens in place. A plate of the menu's own material, rim and
corners, 28 DIP tall, its words in a flyout title's 14 DIP semibold and 12 DIP either side, never wider than the
menu — legible over any desktop, as the menu is.

It is part of the menu's window, in the room over the panel (`FlyoutHost.Caption`, drawn in `Outside`): it comes,
stays through a Refresh and goes with the menu. The host places the caption and its gap as the panel's top, so
the panel keeps its one height (§288) and its place from the widget: over a bottom bar the panel's foot is where it
was and the caption over it; under a top bar the caption stands the gap off the widget and the panel under it;
beside a widget the two are centred on it together. `MenuSides` and `Roomiest` choose a side with room for both,
and the room that caps a configuration menu's height is less the caption's band. A press on the caption is the
menu's: it closes nothing and does nothing (`FlyoutHost.OnPanel`, `Flyout` on `WM_LBUTTONDOWN`). Narrator names the
menu by it (`UiaName`). Set by the dock as `Pending.Caption` → `Flyout.Caption`: `Dock.WidgetMenu` while arranged,
`Dock.LooksMenu`; no other menu has one.

No config change. No new strings.

Tests: `WidgetMenuTitleTests` — `AnEditMenuIsNamedByTheWidgetsTypeAlone` (every bar and list kind, a clock with
zone and label, a weather line with a place, a file pin, a named folder: its kind alone, no heading of it in its
menu), `AFoldersEditMenuHasNoHeadingThroughEveryRefresh` (Add a face right under the faces through four
Refreshes), `TheCaptionStandsOverTheMenuCentred` (bottom and top bar: the panel as tall as without, centred
under the caption a gap below it; over a bottom bar the panel where it stood, under a top bar the caption where
the panel's top stood; kept through a Refresh; a press on it closes nothing; Narrator's name);
`InlineMenuTests.AddAFaceStandsRightUnderTheFaces` (two faces and forty: a row's pitch under the last face, no
foot; keys and its level), `TheFootIsItsRowsUnderOneRule`; `WidgetLookTests.AppearanceStandsAtTheMenusFootUnderHeight`;
`OptionMenuTests.AFaceIsAddedFromTheGallerysGroups`. `EveryMenuSheet` draws the caption with each configuration
menu.

By hand: in edit mode click a clock line in a folder: "Clock" over the menu, centred; Height and Appearance at the
foot with no rule between; a folder: "Folder" over it, "Add a face" right under the faces; the bar's room
right-clicked: "Taskbar". On a top bar the caption stands between the bar and the menu. Click the caption: the
menu stays.

## 315. A row's name and its value share it; no "Refresh" in any menu (2026-10-23)

**Name and value share the row** (the person: "when selecting a timezone value the value display (UTC+X)
sometimes is not shown when the title is too wide. this is also for other locations as well, this should
not be, the width should be shared by title and value"). §228 had the name win: the value had what the
words left and none under 40 DIP, so a long name — a longer language's, a face's place — lost its value.
One rule now for every row with a value at its end, a submenu's, a search's result, a place's
(`Flyout.Share`, Flyout.Values.cs): both whole where they fit; else the one within its share — the value
two fifths of the row (`ValueShare`), the name three — whole, the other the rest; else each its share,
both cut with an ellipsis. A value is never left out. `ValueRoom` and `ValueLeastDip` are gone. Steppers,
toggles and swatch/glyph values are unchanged (their width is kept whole, as before).

**No "Refresh" in a menu** (the person: "refresh should be remove from the context menu action in web
widgets"; earlier: "refresh should not be a context menu action"). §308 had put the line's Refresh back
in the menus of weather, air quality, tides, earthquakes, markets, news and sports, lines and faces. They
offer only where they read from now — Open forecast, Open on map, Open website; the refresh button on
the line is the one way to read again (§280). `WidgetAct.Refresh` is gone with its row, label, glyph,
`RunAct` and `HandsAway` cases, and `FolderIsland.RefreshLineOf`; `dock.widgetMenu.refresh` stays, the
button's tooltip. No config change.

Tests: `MenuValuesTests.TheNameAndTheValueShareTheRow` (was `TheNameWins`),
`ALongNameAndItsValueShareTheRow` (wide name and value both shown and cut, short ones whole, Arabic too;
menu-values-shared-<en|ar>.png); `RefreshButtonTests.NoMenuOffersRefresh` (back, was
`OnlyWhatReadsFromTheWebOffersRefresh`), `AWebLinesMenuOpensItsSource`; the web widgets' expected rows
in `MarketPresetTests`, `NewsPresetTests`, `FaceMenuTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`.

By hand: a clock face's Time zone and a weather face's Place in a long language (German, Tamil): the
value shows, cut if need be. Right-click a weather, markets, news or sports line or face: no Refresh;
the line's button still refreshes.

## 316. A card outline all the way round; faint column lines; a folder's lines ringed only when selected (2026-10-23)

The person: *"card outline just changes color of top and bottom line and not all the way around"*, *"make the
column lines more faint"*, *"in folder edit mode dont show the lines around a widget, only when selected. (keep
the outline of the taskbar widgets the same though, just change them for the folder)"*.

**A widget's own outline runs all the way round its piece.** In a group a widget is its piece of the group's
one card (§245): the card is drawn past the piece's seams and clipped back, so a piece has no edge at a seam.
A widget's own outline (§311) took the same road and coloured only the top and the bottom of its piece (and
the rounded end of a group's first or last). Now a piece with an outline of its own also draws its square
sides, a band the outline's width just inside each seam, between its top and bottom
(`Rounded.Sides`, from `Scene.PlaceCard` where `OwnOutline`): the piece is outlined round, nothing moves,
and a neighbour's edge is not drawn twice (each piece draws only inside itself). The sides are in the
outline's own brush, so a colour picked recolours them in place, and the trailing one rides on a glide
(`GrowFrom`). The bar's card outline (Appearance's "Card outline") is the group's: it runs round the group
as one card, its ends and its long sides, and no line at a seam inside it, as before. A card alone was
always outlined round. High contrast ignores a widget's colours, as before.

**Fainter guide lines.** An arranged folder's guide lines down the screen are the scroll indicator's ink at
0.3 of it (`FolderFlyout.GuideStrength`; it was 0.6): about 0x2A white on the dark look, 0x22 black on the
light. High contrast draws them in the system's colour whole, a hairline.

**An arranged folder's lines wear no outline.** The hairline every line wore while the folder was arranged,
brighter under the pointer and carried (`PaintEditDress`, `LightDress`), is gone: a line shows only what it
is, its wash under the pointer as before, and the selected line (and every other selected one) the accent's
ring (§246). A line's own card outline (§311) still rings it. The bar's blocks keep their edit outline
unchanged (EditLook's ink). `FolderPlan.EditHair`, the dress's width, went with it.

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.ACardOutlineRunsAllTheWayRound` (a real bar at 150 %, dark and light: a widget's own
outline on all four sides of a card alone, a group's first piece and a piece in its middle; the bar's outline
on all four sides of a card alone and on a group's end and long sides, none at its seam;
`widget-look-outlines-<look>.png`), `FolderSlotTests.TheGuideLinesAreFaint`, `FolderEditClickTests.
AnArrangedFoldersLinesWearNoOutlineButTheSelectedRing` (a real arranged folder: nothing on an unselected
line's edge, the accent's ring on the selected; `folder-edit-unselected-<look>.png`).

By hand: give a widget in the middle of a group its own card outline (Appearance › Card outline): it is
outlined on all four sides, its neighbours keep theirs. Arrange a folder: the column lines are faint, no line
has an outline until it is clicked, and the bar's blocks look as before.

## 317. A note's toolbar in its title's row; a line's note picked, made, renamed and deleted in one level (2026-10-23)

The person: *"for the notes move the edit bar to the topbar area next to the title"*; *"the note selection /
creating / removing needs to be way better in the edit menu. it is to complicated."*

**The toolbar in the title's row** (`NoteTile.Tools`). Since §87 the note's toolbar (heading, bold, italic,
struck, code, link, the three lists, quote) was a row of its own under the title, 34 DIP of every note line.
It stands in the title's row now, at its end, its last button on the gutter, the title's words before it
and cut short where they meet it, as a Windows command bar stands beside a page's title. The title keeps the
room for its words up to 96 DIP (`MinTitle`, with the text size); where the rest has no room for all ten
buttons, those that fit stand there and "More" (…) at the row's end, which opens the rest in rows under the
title as before. At the narrowest at large text the row is the title and "More" alone. The note's words
start right under the title's row: every note line shows 34 DIP more of its words. Everything else is as it
was: the tooltips with their keys, pressed where the caret's words are what a button makes, a press keeping
the caret and the keys, the toolbar faint at rest and a press there starting the typing, a press on the
title's words (not on a button) still the line's to carry. In Arabic and Urdu the line is mirrored as every
line is (`Mirror`), so the buttons stand at the row's left and the title at its right.

**One row for the line's note** (`OptionRows.NotebookRows`, `OptionRow.Owned`, `OptionOwned`). The menu had
"Note ›", then "New note ›" (a field; nothing was made unless a name was typed), "Rename note ›" and "Delete
this note?" as rows of their own, the last two only for the note shown, so another note was renamed or
deleted by showing it first. Now "Note ›" is the one row, saying the note shown at its end; its level:

- **New note** at the top: a click makes a note and shows it on the line at once, the menu staying, the new
  one ticked. It is called "Note", or "Note 2" and on where that is taken (`Notebook.NewNoteName`, as a new
  layout is named; a to-do list "Tasks", "Tasks 2": `NewListName`; a line's first typing into no note too);
- a rule, then **every note**, the one the line shows ticked: a click on its row (off its buttons), Enter or
  Space shows it, the menu staying (a long list is searched past ten, as every level);
- at each row's end two icon buttons with their names and keys as tooltips (§313): **Rename** (F2) opens the
  note's name in a field in place (`FlyoutTool.Level`: a tool that opens a level as a row's submenu does; a
  Refresh keeps it open, going back lights the note's row), Enter keeps it, Escape goes back; **Delete**
  (the Delete key) asks Windows' question first ("Delete this note?", "“Ideas” is deleted, from every line that
  shows it."; `OptionMenu.AskOf`), then deletes it from every line, which then shows the notebook's first.

The buttons stand on every row rather than appearing under the pointer: the faces' and the holidays' bins do
the same (§240, §265), and a touch or keyboard person sees them too. A to-do line on this PC's notebook has
the same level for its lists ("List ›", "New list"). Without the notebook to write in (none read) the level
is the choice alone. A choice's row with tools is picked by a click off them, Enter or Space
(`Flyout.ControlClicked`, `ControlKey`).

Strings: `widget.note.newNoteNumbered`, `widget.todo.newListNumbered` in all 30 languages;
`settings.widget.notebook.renameNote`, `.renameList` and the long unused `.new` and `.create` removed. No config
change: the line's note and list keys are as they were.

Tests: `NotebookLinesTests.TheToolbarStandsInTheTitlesRowAndKeepsTheRestUnderMore` (every width and text
size: the buttons in the title's row, inside the gutter, the last at the row's end, the title's room, "More"
exactly where not all ten fit, the words under the row; More's rows at the narrowest),
`TheToolbarFormatsWhereTheCaretIs` (in the title's row); `OptionRowsTests.ALinesNoteIsPickedMadeRenamedAndDeletedInItsLevel`
(made and shown in one step, "Note 2", the level's rows, ticked, picked, renamed, asked and deleted, lists
alike, no other row of it); `NoteMenuTests.TheNotesLevelPicksRenamesAndDeletesInPlace` (on a real menu: the
level in place, a click picks, the pencil and F2 open the name's field in place through a Refresh, Enter keeps
and goes back onto the row, Delete is the bin's, New note shown again ticked); `MenuIconsTests` over the new
rows. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `notes-toolbar-dark-150.png` (typing at three widths, More open on the
narrowest), `notes-toolbar-dark/light.png`, `note-menu-top-dark.png`, `note-menu-level-dark.png` (150 %).

By hand: open a folder with a note line; the toolbar stands beside the title; narrow the list (or set a large
text size) and see "…" take the rest; type and use the buttons. In edit mode open the note line's menu,
Note ›: New note (a "Note 2" shown at once), click another note, the pencil (type a name, Enter), F2 on a row,
the bin (asked, then gone from every line showing it).

## 318. Different data, different widgets: Volume mixer, Today's date and Performance details split off (2026-10-23)

The person: *"right now a lot of the widgets are grouped with style, e.g. the volume slider and volume
mixer are (to the user at least) the same widget just with different styles. they show something
different / have different behaviour. widgets like these should therefore not be grouped together as
different styles. fix this for all widgets. give me a list of them so i can decide which ones to
ungroup."* The list (`artifacts/style-groups.md`) tested every style: the same data and behaviour drawn
differently stays a style; different data or a different click is a widget of its own. The person's
pick: *"split 1, 2, 4"*. This supersedes §270's rows for Volume, Clock and Performance (its table says
so); the calendar, the weather, the markets, the faces' looks and the rest stay as §270 left them.

**1. Volume and Volume mixer.** The sound widget (`sound`) is gone. **Volume** (`soundVolume`, the
system's level and its mute) and **Volume mixer** (`soundMixer`, each app's level and mute) are widgets
of one style each, as the output devices and the microphones have been since §270. Add ▸ Music and
sound lists Volume, Volume mixer, Output device and Input device, each with its own name, icon, line and
words (the forms' `core.widget.soundVolume.*` and `core.widget.soundMixer.*`). Neither menu has a Style
row. The bar's volume slider (`volume`) is untouched: nothing moves between the bar and a folder
(Partners), so there is no bar or face equivalent to change.

**2. Today's date.** The clock's Date style was the one style a click acts on (it sets the folder's day,
`Channels.Day`). It is **Today's date** (`dateHeader`), a widget of its own on the Calendar shelf (Add ▸
Time and calendar ▸ Calendar), its zone still its row (it keeps the `clock` record). The Clock keeps
Clock and Time and date, the same subject drawn more or less fully.

**3. Performance details.** The details are other facts (speed, processes, handles, memory committed and
cached, read and write rates, the adapter), not the load drawn another way. **Performance details**
(`performanceDetails`, `WidgetStyles.PerformanceDetails`) is a widget of readings like Performance: its
Reading row changes what it measures and keeps it details. It has one style, so no Style row and no
`"style"` in the file. Performance keeps Graph and Numbers (the graph's form drawing none) and its Reading.
*The add list:* its model (§285) is a row per reading, what it measures said when it is added, so the
details are a row per reading too. Five more rows would make System info fifteen, past the tree's twelve
(`AddTreeTests`), so they stand in a folder of their own after the readings: System info ▸ **Performance
details** ▸ Processor details, Graphics details, Memory details, Disk details, Network details. Each row
is named and iconed as its form ("Processor" twice in one list would be no choice) and found by its
form's words ("threads", "ram", "details"). Its page in Settings is called by the form's name ("Graphics details").

**One model, no special cases.** A split-off style and a gone widget are one table
(`WidgetStyles.SplitOffOf`): `("sound", "output" | "input" | "mixer")`, `("clock", "date")` and
`("performance", "details")` name the widget of its own they are now, and `"sound"` alone (or in a style
it never had) is `soundVolume`. `FormWord` reads that word with the line's reading, so `"performance",
"details", "gpu"` is the performance details measuring the graphics. `StyledWidget.SplitOff` (one
widget's table) went into it. A widget whose line has nothing to choose but its reading
(`WidgetStyles.Chooses`: one look) is its form to the person: no Style row (`OptionRows`), no `"style"`
in the file (`FileStyle`), its add list rows its forms' names and icons (`TitleOf`, `GlyphOf`), its page
its form's title (`IslandTitles`). `StyledWidget.ReadingWords` lets the details speak the performance
widget's reading names (`core.widgetReading.performance.*`). `WidgetStyles.OldDetailsWord` is gone: the
2026-10-17 `"performanceDetails"` with the reading for its style is the new widget's word, read as before.

**The file: a migration, no reset, no shape change.** Every old form is carried once, in place, by
§209's carrying over (`LineMigrations.MergeStyles`): its id, place, height and options kept.

| The file said | It is now |
|---|---|
| `"kind": "sound"` (or with `"style": "volume"`) | `"kind": "soundVolume"` |
| `"kind": "sound", "style": "mixer"` | `"kind": "soundMixer"` |
| `"kind": "clock", "style": "date"` (its `clock` record, the zone, kept) | `"kind": "dateHeader"` |
| `"kind": "performance", "reading": R, "style": "details"` (its `performance` record kept) | `"kind": "performanceDetails", "reading": R` |
| `"kind": "performanceDetails", "style": R` (2026-10-17), `"cpuDetails"` … (before §228) | `"kind": "performanceDetails", "reading": R` |

`Config.Migrated` records `widgetStyles` and `soundDevices` (§270's name, now for every split-off style)
once. A build from before this one reads `soundVolume`, `soundMixer` and `dateHeader` as its styled
widgets' forms (form words are read forever) and `performanceDetails` with a reading as that reading's
details, so a file written now loses nothing going back.

**Presets** say each widget by its word: the sound folder and the media center `soundMixer` and
`soundVolume`, quick settings' sound page `soundMixer` (`FolderPages`), the quick panel `soundVolume`, the
calendar and the notification center `dateHeader`, each reading's folder `performanceDetails` with its
reading.

**Words**, in all 30 languages: `core.styled.performanceDetails.title`, `.blurb`, `.keywords` and
`core.addTree.performanceDetails.title` new; `core.widgetStyle.performance.details` is
`core.widgetStyle.performanceDetails.details`; the clock's and the performance widget's lines no longer
name the date and the details; `core.styled.sound.*`, `core.widgetStyle.sound.*` and
`core.widgetStyle.clock.date` gone.

Tests: `StylesSameDataTests` — the styles as kept (`performance: graph`, `performanceDetails: details`,
`clock: clock time`), every style one subject (the details "facts", no longer "usage");
`ASplitStyleIsItsOwnWidgetInPlace` (each old form above in a file between two other lines: the form,
id, height, zone or performance options, the file's kind, reading and no style, marked, nothing more on
a second read); `TheSplitWidgetsOwnWordsNeedNothing`; the §209 sound folder in today's words;
`TheAddListHasEachSplitWidgetAsARowOfItsOwn`; `NoSplitWidgetHasAStyleRow` (the details' Reading keeps
them details; the clock's Style is Clock and Time and date); `PresetsSayTheSplitWidgetsByTheirOwnWords`.
`PerformanceStylesTests` (old shapes, the details' reading choice), `WidgetStylesTests`,
`OptionMenuTests.AGraphsMenuHasEveryCardItsPageHas` (the details without Style),
`AddListTests.EachReadingIsARowAddingThePerformanceWidgetMeasuringIt` (and the details' folder),
`AddListSearchTests.AResultSaysWhereItIs`, `UntranslatedTests`.

By hand: Add ▸ Music and sound has Volume and Volume mixer; a mixer line's menu has no Style row. Add ▸
Time and calendar ▸ Calendar has Today's date; a clock line's Style lists Clock and Time and date. Add ▸
System info ▸ Performance details ▸ Memory details adds a memory details line whose Reading switches it
to another reading's details. A config with `"kind": "sound", "style": "mixer"` and `"kind": "clock",
"style": "date"` opens with the same lines where they were, saved as `soundMixer` and `dateHeader`.

## 319. A place opens on the map chosen; now playing hides while nothing plays, greyed when arranged; a folder pin's contents wear its icon (2026-10-23)

The person: *"for opening a place on a map you should be able to set the default map provider in which it
will get opened. provide a few to select from."*, *"now playing widget should have the setting to be hidden
if nothing is playing. this should be on by default. in edit mode it should appear regardless of the setting
of course, just also in the muted style"* and *"for the pin widget when showing a folder and its contents the
icon is not respected, the one from the folder is always shown."*

**The map.** One setting for the whole app, on the General page under the search engine: **Map**, a combo of
OpenStreetMap, Google Maps, Bing Maps, Apple Maps and HERE WeGo (`Config.MapProvider`, `"mapProvider"` in the
file, left out until chosen; null is OpenStreetMap, what "Open on map" always opened; a name this build does
not know reads as none, `Config.Repair`). Every "Open on map" builds its address in one place,
`MapLinks.For(latitude, longitude, zoom, label)` (Karpo.Core\MapLinks.cs), on the map the dock took from the
config as it applied it (`MapLinks.Use`, beside the online interval). Each address shows the place marked,
checked against the provider's own documentation: OpenStreetMap `?mlat=&mlon=#map=z/lat/lon`; Google's
documented Maps URLs `maps/search/?api=1&query=lat,lon` (a pin; that form takes no zoom); Bing
`maps?cp=lat~lon&lvl=z&sp=point.lat_lon_title`; Apple's unified URLs `maps.apple.com/place?coordinate=&name=`
(a pin and a place card, in any browser); HERE `share.here.com/l/lat,lon,title?z=`. A title's own marks never
part the address (Bing's `_` and `~`, HERE's comma). Windows' Maps app (`bingmaps:`) is not offered: Microsoft
took it off the Store and made it stop working in July 2025.
What opens on a map: the tides' "Open on map", line and face, the place under its name at a town's zoom (a
place followed from the device unnamed); the earthquakes' over a quake, that quake under its place in USGS's
words (`QuakesLine.MenuQuake`, zoom 7) — over the head, and on the face, USGS's map of them all, the feed's
own site, as before. The menus' rows are made when they open, so a change applies to the next one.

**Now playing while nothing plays.** "Hide it while nothing plays" is on by default (`NowPlayingFace.HideIdle`'s
default "true"): a face whose file says nothing hides, a file that says false keeps it — nothing is written or
migrated. While the bar is arranged the face is on the bar whatever it says (§291), and where it would be gone
at rest it is drawn greyed — one rule for every face there only because the bar is arranged
(`IFaceDrawing.NothingToShow` while `Arranged`, painted through `Unavailable.Paint`, the look §247 gives what
is not on this PC and §302 Show desktop's bare corner): now playing with nothing playing, the removable face
with nothing plugged in. Set off, the idle face stays at rest and arranged in its own ink, "Nothing playing".

**A folder pin's contents wear the pin's icon.** A pin to a folder showing its contents heads its line with the
folder's name and icon; the name was the pin's (its own, else the folder's) but the icon was always the
folder's own, read from the shell beside the listing. Now the head follows the one precedence every drawing
of a pin has (`Item.Icon`, which `PinContents` asks with the folder source): the glyph chosen, drawn in the
line's ink; a file chosen, its icon; else the folder's own. A change of icon reads the line again. The bar's
row of buttons has no head (the pin's own button, while there is nothing to list, was the pin's already), and
the list a click opens from the bar has no title row.

Strings: `settings.map.provider.header`, `.description`, `.keywords` in all 30 languages (the maps' names are
their own, in no language).

Tests: `MapLinksTests` (every map's address, titles that cannot break it, the names, the file keeping the
choice and reading none and an unknown one as OpenStreetMap, the tides' row following the choice; run alone,
the map being the process's); `QuakePictures.TheLineListsWhatItsHeightHolds` (over a quake its spot, over the
head USGS's map); `MediaPresetTests.HidingWhileNothingPlaysIsOnUnlessAFileSaysOff`,
`HidingWhileNothingPlaysIsTheFacesOption`, `ArrangedTheFaceIsThereGreyedWhileNothingPlays` (no cell at rest,
greyed arranged, fainter than one set to stay, playing alike); `FolderPinContentsTests.ThePinsOwnIconHeadsItsContents`
(the glyph drawn with no folder yellow, a file's icon, the folder's with none, chosen later). The tests that
draw or measure the face idle or paused (`MediaPresetTests`' drawing tests, `MediaSizeTests`, `MediaRowTests`,
`FaceWidthTests`) set it to stay, as they draw what it looks like at rest. Pictures:
now-playing-idle-<dark|light>.png, folder-pin-icon-<dark|light>.png.

By hand: Settings, General, Map: Google Maps; right-click a tides line, Open on map: Google Maps at the place.
Pause the player: the media folder leaves the bar about five seconds later; edit mode: it is there, grey. A
folder pin showing its contents: right-click in edit mode, Icon, a star: the line's head is the star.

## 320. A column is never narrowed to fit: what doesn't fit runs off the screen and the folder says so; Fill lines reach the margin (2026-10-23)

The person: *"in one of my folders i cannot make the columns any wider because i believe i triggered
an edge case with moving a widget all the way to a side so that the columns cannot grow anymore
without pushing it over the edge. ... rather than limit the user in what he can do layout wise i think
we should rather allow a widget / widgets to clip over the edge and then just warn the user about
that."* And: *"the widgets that are set to grow dont grow all the way to the screen edges - padding of
course. they have way to much space."* This takes back §207's and §210's "a folder wider than its
display narrowed there, widest first" and the "+" row §185 and §287 kept at rest.

**Why a column could not be widened.** `FolderFlyout.ListWidths` narrowed a folder wider than its work
area (`Fit`) and counted every list, the empty ones too. A widget moved to a far slot leaves the slots
between as empty medium columns (`Folders.InsertNew`). The person's News folder had six of them
before a widest clock and a wide feed: 5220 px of lists on a 3840 px display at 150 %. `Fit` cut every
list to one level, 474 px, so the clock and the feed were 474 px whatever width was picked. At rest those
empty columns have no width at all (§158), so the folder was narrowed for columns it did not draw.

**No narrowing.** Each list is its preset on every display (`ListWidths(options, scale)`). Gone:
`Fit`, `FitMarginDip`, and the work width `Build` and `Natural` took for it. The folder is placed as
before: the lists with widgets centred on the face and kept inside the work area while they fit
(`FlyoutPlacement.Along`); longer than the work area, they start the flyouts' margin in and their far
end runs past the screen's edge. Across a side bar the same rule: a folder wider than the room beside
the bar keeps its near side the gap off the bar and runs past the far edge (`FlyoutHost.Arrange`, Left
and Right). It used to be moved back in over the bar. Nothing refused a move or an add for width; that
stays so.

**Every list's buttons where they show** (`WithSlots`). One rule for a list with widgets and an empty
one: the group ("+", width, warning) is centred on what shows of the list inside the room, and there
is none where too little shows. The buttons of a column wholly off the screen were kept on it one by one
(`KeepIn`) and piled up at the edge over its neighbour's. A list as tall as the room has no room past
its far end for them, so they stand just inside it, `AddApartDip` in, over its first line (§303's side
bars had this already).

**Off screen, said.** Arranged, `FolderPlan.OffScreen` lists the lists with widgets that run past the
room (`Visible`), nearest first; empty ones never count. A chip says *"Part of this folder is off
screen"* (`dock.folder.offScreen`, in all 30 languages) on the first of them, at its middle, against the
edge it runs past, `WarningMarginDip` (12) in (`WarningBox`). It is drawn in Karpo's warning orange with
its stroke and ink (`EditRail.Warning`, as a column's warning button), 4 DIP corners, the warning glyph,
at least 32 DIPs tall, and its words cut with an ellipsis where the screen is narrower
(`FolderFlyout.OffScreen.cs`: `PlaceWarning`, `WarningSize`, `PaintWarning`). It takes no press and goes
once everything fits. Nothing is said at rest.

**Fill lines reach the margin.** `Reach` kept a row for an arranged list's buttons (a "+" and its gap,
30 DIPs) at rest too, so nothing would move as edit mode came. So every folder, and every Fill line,
ended 30 DIPs more than the flyouts' margin short of the work area's far end: 57 px from the top of the
person's display instead of 12. `Reach` is the room now (`FlyoutPlacement.Room`: the anchor and its gap
to the far end less the margin), on every edge, at rest and arranged. The buttons of a list that tall
stand inside it (above). Arranged, the room still stops short of the edit bar's band, which is in sight
while a folder is open (§310). The folder then ends the margin short of the edit bar and no further. No
margin is taken twice: `DockWindow.FolderWork` takes the band to the edit bar panel's inner side, and
`Room` the one margin off that. There is no band at rest.

No config change.

Tests: `FolderClipTests` (pure: lists past the room `OffScreen` nearest first, never an empty one, each
list's buttons on what shows of it, none for one wholly past it; a tall list's buttons inside its far
end on a bottom and a top bar; the chip against the edge on the cut list. Open folder: the person's
News folder on 3840 px at 150 %, every column its preset at rest and arranged, nothing said; widened to
widest beside widest on 1920 px, the far column past the edge, `OffScreen` and the chip on it arranged,
its buttons on the screen; a side bar's wide folder off its far edge, never over the bar),
`ColumnWidthTests.NoDisplayNarrowsAColumn` (replaces `TheWidestGiveWayFirst` and
`ASmallDisplayNarrowsTheWidestNotTheFile`: the regression, 474 px before), and
`FolderFillTests.AFolderFillsAsFarOffEveryBar` (now also the far end exactly the margin from the work
area's, on all four edges, at rest and arranged, every button on the screen; `Room` less 24, not 54).
Pictures (150 %): `folderclip-news-<3840|1920>-…-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-150`,
`folderclip-side-<left|right>-edit-dark-150`, `folder-edgefill-<edge>-<rest|edit>-dark-150`.

By hand: in edit mode open a folder and pick Widest for two of its columns on a 1080p display. They
widen, the far one runs off the screen, and the orange "Part of this folder is off screen" stands on it
at the edge. Narrow one and the chip goes. At rest nothing is said. Open the notifications folder (a Fill
line): its top 8 DIPs under the screen's top at rest, and 8 DIPs under the edit bar in edit mode, the
"+" and width buttons just inside its top.

## 321. A note shows its marks on every line, at rest and typing (2026-10-23)

The person: *"the notes widget should always show the markup elements too, not only when i am on the
line. (e.g. the #, **, -, [], etc)"*. Since §87 the note line was a live preview: marks hidden, shown
only on the line or run the caret was at, so a line changed its look (and its width) as the caret went
by. Now there is one rule for every line, caret or not:

- **Every character shows.** `Markdown.Show(note, line)` no longer takes the selection; a shown line is
  its text (`MdShown.Text`), and `ToShown`/`ToSource` are an offset, so caret, selection and hit-testing
  map one for one. The per-character map (`From`), `LeadShown`, `MdLine.LeadByCaret` and
  `NoteEdits.Stepped` (the arrows stepping over a hidden lead) are gone.
- **Styled as before, marks faint.** A heading is big and semibold, its `#`s too, in the tertiary ink;
  `**bold**` bold between faint `**`; italic, struck, code (`` ` `` faint, the words on their plate) and
  links (words underlined in the link colour, `[` and `](address)` faint and no link) alike. A list's
  `-`, `*`, `1.` and a quote's `>` faint; a quote's words in the secondary ink. Fences and rules show as
  their faint text (no hidden fence rows, no drawn divider). A task's `[ ]`/`[x]` is `MdStyle.Box`, in
  the link colour as something to click, and a ticked task's words are struck (now a run's style, not a
  layout flag).
- **No drawn stand-ins.** The bullets, numbers, check boxes and quote bars `NoteLayout` drew beside the
  words, and the indent and marker column they needed, are gone: a row's text starts at the note's edge
  (code 8 DIP in on its plate), and nesting is the item's own spaces.
- **A click on a task's `[ ]`** (with a third of its width either side) ticks it, at rest or typing,
  and the pointer there is the arrow; anywhere else the click puts the caret at the character under it.
  Home and End are the wrapped line's ends (the "smart Home" past the marker went with the hidden
  marker). Backspace at an item's words still takes its marker away, as a word processor's list does.
- The layout no longer depends on the caret, so moving it lays nothing out again (`NoteTile.Body`'s key
  is the text, width and size).

No config or note format change. Tests: `MarkdownTests` (every line kind's text and runs with its marks,
the box and a ticked task's strike, marks on a line other than the first, every place one for one over a
set of broken notes), `NoteEditorTests.ArrowsGoThroughTheMarksACharacterAtATime`,
`NotebookLinesTests.TheNoteIsEditedAsItIsShown` (marks at rest and typing, a click lands on the
character under it, rows unmoved by the caret, Home), `ALinkOpensAndATasksBoxTicksTheNote` (the `[ ]`
ticks at rest and clears while typing, the words place the caret, the box is not the text cursor).
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `notes-marks-<dark|light>-150.png` (at rest, typing in the bold, a selection
over two tasks), and `notes-note-*`, `notes-toolbar-*` as before.

By hand: open a note line; every `#`, `**`, `-`, `[ ]` shows faint at rest; click into it and nothing
shifts; click a task's `[ ]` to tick it; arrow through a list's marker.

## 322. Links: the map, the weather site and the finance site a widget opens on, one row each (2026-10-23)

The person, approving item 15 of the review: "Open forecast" (weather, air quality) and the markets' "Open
website" configurable like the map (§319). One model for all of it: `LinkProviders` (Karpo.Core\LinkProviders.cs,
was MapLinks.cs) builds every address Karpo opens a place, a forecast or a share on, with one choice per kind in
the file — `"mapProvider"` as §319 wrote it, `"weatherProvider"`, `"marketsProvider"` — each left out until
chosen, none being what Karpo always opened (OpenStreetMap, weather.com, Yahoo Finance), and one this build does
not know read as none (`Config.Repair` through `LinkProviders.Known`). The dock takes all three as it applies the
config (`LinkProviders.Use(config)`); the menus' rows are made when they open, so a change applies to the next one.
`Dock.MapPage`, `Dock.ForecastPage` and the markets' `MarketPage` are the only callers; `Dock.MarketSite` and the
weather.com strings in the dock are gone.

**Weather** (`LinkProviders.Forecast(lat, lon, air)`), each opened for Zürich, Sydney and New York on
2026-10-23 and showing that place, not where the request came from: weather.com `weather/today/l/lat,lon` (air:
`forecast/air-quality/l/…`); MSN Weather, Windows' own, `msn.com/en-us/weather/forecast?lat=&lon=` (only the
en-us market keeps the place; the others redirect by the visitor's address and drop it); Yr
`yr.no/en/forecast/daily-table/lat,lon`; meteoblue `meteoblue.com/en/weather/week/<lat>N<lon>E`, south and west
as negative numbers (air: `weather/outdoorsports/airquality/…`). A site with no air quality page of its own —
MSN's canonical page for it is the forecast, Yr has none outside Norway — opens its forecast. Not offered:
AccuWeather (an address needs its own location key), MeteoSwiss (postcodes only), Weather Underground (no
coordinates: 404).

**Markets** (`LinkProviders.Quote(symbol)`), a symbol as the price service writes it: Yahoo Finance
`quote/<symbol>`; Google Finance `finance?q=<symbol>` for a US share (it finds the exchange; "BRK-B" too),
`finance/quote/<symbol>:<exchange>` for another exchange's ("NESN.SW" `NESN:SWX`, "0700.HK" `0700:HKG`),
`quote/EUR-CHF`, `quote/BTC-EUR`; TradingView `symbols/<symbol>/` for a US share (a class `BRK.B`),
`symbols/<exchange>-<symbol>/` for another's (Hong Kong without its leading zeros, a Nordic class `VOLV_B`),
`symbols/EURCHF/`, `symbols/BTCEUR/`. Nineteen exchanges by their Yahoo suffix, each code opened with a share of
it on both sites (Oslo has no page on Google Finance). What a site cannot name — an index ("^GSPC": Google finds
some and not others, TradingView names them its own way), a future ("GC=F"), an exchange not in the table —
opens on Yahoo Finance, where the widget reads it, never on a page that is not it. A share line's click is
unchanged: it searches with the search engine chosen (§263), already a choice of its own.

**Sports: ESPN only, no row.** A match's and a team's page are ESPN's own ids, which no other site takes, and
no other site has a documented address by a team's name across the sports ESPN covers; a choice of one is no
choice.

**Settings.** The General page's Map card is now the **Links** section, after Online's search engine: its
heading, then a card each — Map, Weather, Markets — each Windows' combo of that kind's sites under their own
names (`SettingsModel.Links.cs`, one pair of helpers for the three rows). The import summary names
`weatherProvider` and `marketsProvider` by their cards.

Strings: `settings.links.section`, `settings.links.weather.header`, `.description`, `.keywords`,
`settings.links.markets.header`, `.description`, `.keywords` in all 30 languages (the section is "Weblinks" in
German and "Koppelingen" in Dutch, where "Links" is "left"; the sites' names are their own, in no language).

Tests: `LinkProvidersTests` (was `MapLinksTests`): every map's address and its titles; every weather site's at a
place north-east and south-west, with and without air; every finance site's for a US share, a class, other
exchanges, a rate, a coin, and Yahoo where it cannot name one; no symbol, an unknown site; the names and
defaults; the file keeping each choice under its key and reading an unknown one as none with the rest intact;
the dock's map and forecast rows following the choice, and a share line's "Open website" (UI); the General
page's Links heading and its three cards bound to their rows. `QuakePictures` uses `LinkProviders.Place`.

By hand: Settings, General, Links: Weather meteoblue; right-click a weather line, Open forecast: meteoblue at the
place; an air quality line: meteoblue's air quality. Markets Google Finance; right-click a NESN.SW line, Open
website: Nestlé on Google Finance; a ^GSPC line: Yahoo Finance.

## 323. The edit menu's type in its top row; a line named by the widget it is; the tray's places said short (2026-10-23)

The person: *"actually move the title into the toprow inside the menu again, leave the add a widget as it
is"*; *"some type names read oddly: 'Conditions' for weather, 'Processor graph'"*; *"the Tray icons level
cuts its values off"* ("Show on task…", "Show in hidden i…").

**The type in the top row** (`Flyout.Primary.cs`). §314's caption on a plate over the menu is gone —
`Flyout.Caption.cs`, `FlyoutHost.Caption` with the window's room for it and its placing, `OnCaption`,
`Pending.Caption` —, and the menu stands where and as tall as it did before §314. A configuration menu's type
(`Flyout.TypeTitle`, set from `Pending.TypeTitle`: `IslandEdits.Kind` in `Dock.WidgetMenu` while arranged,
`BarLooks.Kind` in `Dock.LooksMenu`) is the start of its top row, the row of its buttons: in a flyout
title's 14 DIP semibold, 16 DIP in, upright in the row's middle, cut with an ellipsis 12 DIP short of the
buttons. The buttons stand at the row's far end then (`PrimarySpans`' `apart`): Cut and Copy, 12 DIP, Remove
— as §220 had Remove apart from them. The bar's looks menu, which has no buttons, has the row for its type
alone, "Taskbar", ruled off the same. `WithPrimaryRow` puts it in as the row's first item
(`TypeTitleId`, greyed, so nothing lights, presses, walks to or reads it as a row); `IsButton` tells the
buttons from it. On the menu's own rows only: a level shown in place has its head ("← Height"), and the type
is back on the way out; through a Refresh it stays. Narrator names the menu by it. Mirrored in Arabic,
Urdu and Persian: the type at the right, the buttons at the left. The add list is as it was.

**A line is named by the widget it is** (`IslandEdits.Kind`). A line of a widget of styles or readings
(`WidgetStyles`) is that widget, as the add list offers it and its Style and Reading rows change it: every
weather line "Weather" (never "Conditions", "Next hours", "Week's forecast"), every performance line
"Performance" whatever it reads (never "Processor graph"), the details "Performance details", the calendar's
styles "Calendar", the clock's "Clock" — their `core.styled.*.title`, in every language already. A widget of
one style keeps its own name ("Today's date", "Volume mixer", "Pin"); a folder is "Folder". The catalogue's
names (`WidgetInfo.Title`), the add list and Settings' pages are unchanged. The rest of the kinds read
plainly as they are; no string changes.

**The tray's places said short** (`OptionTray.Said`, `OptionRow.ChoicesSaid`, `SaidOf`). §315 shares a row
between its name and its value: an app's name and "Show in hidden icon menu" never both fit 320 DIP, so the
value had its two fifths and was cut. A choice row may say each choice short at its end: the tray's icons
and the status icons say "On taskbar", "Behind arrow", "Hidden" (`settings.tray.said.*`, all 30 languages;
German "Taskleiste", "Hinter Pfeil", "Ausgeblendet"), whole beside a long name; their levels still offer the
choices in full ("Show on taskbar", "Show in hidden icon menu", "Hide completely").

No config change. New strings: `settings.tray.said.taskbar`, `.arrow`, `.hidden`.

Tests: `WidgetMenuTitleTests.TheTypeStandsAtTheStartOfTheTopRow` (bottom and top bar: the panel where and as
tall as without a type; the type 16 DIP in inside the panel, upright in the buttons' row; Remove at the far
end, Cut and Copy before it apart, all after the type; kept through a Refresh; none on a level, back on the
way out; Narrator's name; the looks' row alone over its rows; Arabic turned), `AnEditMenuIsNamedByTheWidgetsTypeAlone`
(the dock sets `TypeTitle`; the caption's code gone), `ALinesTypeIsTheWidgetItIsAStyleOf` (English and
German); `TrayMenuRowsTests.TheIconsLevelSaysEachPlaceWhole` (every value whole, English and German, 100 and
150 %; menu-tray-said-<en|de>-<100|150>.png), `TheIconsAreOneRowOpeningEachWithItsPicture`,
`AfterAPickTheMenuShowsItWhereItWent`. `EveryMenuSheet` draws the type in each configuration menu's row.

By hand: in edit mode click a clock line: "Clock" at the start of the row of Cut, Copy and Remove, inside the
menu; a weather line says "Weather", a processor graph "Performance"; open Height and come back. Right-click

## 324. One way to manage the person's own things: a to-do line's lists of every source, the holiday calendars, the accounts (2026-10-23)

The person: *"To-do sources take two rows, and Microsoft To Do lists can't be created or renamed from the
menu."*; *"Holiday calendars delete without asking, and adding is a separate search row."*; *"Accounts can
only be managed in the Settings app."* And the standing rule: one pattern for managing items everywhere,
duplicates deleted.

**One pattern** (`OptionRow.Owned`, `OptionOwned`, `OptionThing`; `OptionMenu.OwnedLevel`). §317's level of a
line's notes is now the shape of every list of the person's own things: one row, saying what it holds at its
end; its level the way to add one at the top — an action ("New note", "New list"), a search opening in place
("Add a country"), a choice of kinds ("Add an account") —, a rule, then each thing a row: under a heading for
where it comes from where they come from several, what tells it apart on a second line under its name (a
calendar's region, an account's kind), its own rows its submenu (the bins stay in one column all the same),
and at its end the buttons it allows: rename (F2, its name's field in place, `FlyoutTool.Level`), sign in
again, delete (the Delete key; asked first in Windows' dialog, `OptionMenu.AskOf`, the dock's `DeleteAsk`).
The menu stays and is shown again as it is now. A choice's things (a line's note, its list) are ticked where
in force and picked by a click on their row; a `OptionRowKind.Things` row's (the holidays, the accounts) are
only managed. Gone as duplicates: §265's `OptionRowKind.Item`, `OptionRow.Rows` and `.Remove`,
`OptionPickKind.Remove` and the holidays' group of rows; §317's parallel `Names` and `Deletes` lists.

**A to-do line's list** (`OptionRows.TodoListRow`, key `TodoListIndex`). It was "Tasks from ›" (this PC, or
"{list} ({address})" for each To Do list) and, for this PC's notebook only, "List ›" beside it. Now it is one
"List ›", saying the list shown; its level:

- **New list** at the top: one made on this PC ("Tasks", "Tasks 2"…, §317) and shown at once. A To Do list
  is not made from the menu: Graph gives a new list's id only once it answers, and the line would have
  nothing to show until then; a list made on this PC is shown in the same step;
- **On this PC**, a heading, and the notebook's lists; then **each account's address**, a heading, and its
  To Do lists as the dock last read them, its default first (an account not read yet: its "Tasks"). The
  headings stand only where there are accounts' lists. The list shown is ticked;
- a pick of this PC's list clears the account and names the list (`TodoOptions.List`); of an account's names
  the account and its list (`Account`, `TaskList`), as "Tasks from" did; a list gone is its account's
  default, else its first, as before;
- **rename and delete** where it is kept allows them: this PC's in the notebook (§317); an account's in
  Microsoft To Do (`Tasks.ReadWrite` has been asked for since 2026-10-16): `PATCH` and `DELETE
  /me/todo/lists/{id}` (`ITaskReader.RenameListAsync`, `DeleteListAsync`; `TaskStore.RenameList`,
  `DeleteList`, through the dock's `ITodoLists`), shown at once — the lines, the menu, the Accounts page's
  report — and sent there and then, the account read again after, whether To Do took it or not (docs\
  accounts.md, "To Do"). Never the default "Tasks", which To Do keeps, nor a list not read yet; where To Do
  is not written (no store), an account's lists have no buttons. Delete asks "Delete this list?" and
  "“Groceries” and all its tasks are deleted from Microsoft To Do on all your devices.".

`TodoSource` is an account's list alone now (`Account`, `List`, `Name`, `Default`); this PC's are the
notebook's (`Karpo.Accounts\TodoSources.cs`).

**The holiday calendars** (`OptionHolidays.Rows`). One row, "Public holidays ›", saying "Off" or the
countries; its level "Add a country" at the top, its search a level of its own opening in place (Windows'
region's first), a rule, then each calendar, its region under its name and its region's choice its submenu;
its bin asks first: "Remove Switzerland?", "Its public holidays no longer show on your calendars.". The
Accounts page in Settings is as it was.

**The accounts** (`OptionAccountRows`; the dock's `Dock.MenuAccounts.cs`; `Karpo.Accounts\AccountSignIn.cs`).
Every widget that shows what the accounts hold — a mail line, a calendar of every style and the meetings,
the contacts, a to-do line — and the calendar, meeting, mail and contacts faces have "Accounts ›", saying
the addresses of those that give what it shows, or "No account yet". Its level: "Add an account" (the kinds
that give what it shows — "Microsoft account", "Mail server (IMAP)", "CalDAV and CardDAV" — a choice; a
to-do line's one kind an action), a rule, then each such account, its kind under its address, "Sign in
again" on a Microsoft account's, and Remove, asked first with the Accounts page's own question ("Remove
me@outlook.com?", "Karpo stops showing what this account holds…"); removed, it is gone from Karpo for every
widget, as the page removes it. What adds, signs in again and removes is the Accounts page's own, moved
into `AccountSignIn` (`AddMicrosoftAsync`, `SignInAgainAsync`, `Remove`, `Keep`) and used by both: a
Microsoft account signs in in the browser there and then, one sign-in at a time, what goes wrong logged.
A mail server and a CalDAV server ask for a password, which a menu's field would show in clear: their "Add"
opens the Accounts page, as a Microsoft account's does where this Karpo has no app registration; they have
no "Sign in again" (they are added again there with their password, as before). Core does not know
Karpo.Accounts: the dock lists the accounts and does what is asked (`OptionDevices.Accounts`,
`OptionAccounts`), so a test gives its own.

Strings: `core.holidays.removeTitle`, `core.holidays.removeBody`, `dock.menu.accounts.signInAgain` and
`widget.todo.deleteRemoteListBody` in all 30 languages; `settings.widget.todo.source.header`,
`.description` and `.list` removed. No config change: a line's `TodoOptions` and `NoteOptions` are as they
were, and the holidays' calendars too.

Tests: `OwnedLevelsTests.AToDoLinesListsAreEveryListOfEverySourceInOneLevel` (one row; New list, the
headings, every list, the tick, the buttons where allowed and none on a default or unread list or where To
Do is not written; an account's list picked, renamed and deleted asked first through the seam; this PC's
picked again; New list made and shown; no headings without accounts),
`AWidgetsAccountsAreAddedSignedInToAgainAndRemovedInItsLevel` (which widgets and faces; the accounts that
give what it shows; Add's kinds, a to-do line's one an action; Sign in again on a Microsoft account's alone,
not asked; Remove asked with the page's question; all through the seam, nothing of the widget changed);
`HolidaysTests.CountriesAreAddedGivenTheirRegionsAndTakenOut` and `TheMenuListsTheCalendarsInALevelOfTheirOwn`
(the one row, Add at the top, its search's level, the rule, the calendars, the bins in one column, asked
first, a country added from the field); `OptionMenuTests.TheHolidaysCountriesAreListedAndTakenOutOnARealMenu`
(on a real menu: Add first, Delete asks and takes it out, the level stays); `TaskStoreTests.AListIsRenamedAndDeletedAtOnceAndInToDoButNeverTheDefault`;
`ToDoTests.AListIsRenamedAndDeletedThere` (Graph's calls); `OptionRowsTests`, `MenuConventionTests`,
`MenuIconsTests`, `MenuKeepsTests` over the new rows. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`, dark, 150 %):
`items-todo-lists-dark.png`, `items-holidays-dark.png`, `items-accounts-dark.png`.

By hand: a to-do line's menu has one "List ›": pick a To Do list, rename it (F2) and see it renamed in To Do;
"New list" makes "Tasks 2" on this PC. A calendar's "Public holidays ›": "Add a country" first; the bin asks.
A mail line's "Accounts ›": "Add an account › Microsoft account" opens the browser; "Sign in again"; Remove
