## 325. A card's outline over its highlight; the search box in the card's colours (2026-10-23)

The person: *"A widget's highlight covers its outline, muddying the colour."* and *"The search box ignores
card and outline colours."*

**Fill, highlight, outline.** A card was one shape, its fill and its outline together, under the bar's
one highlight (and the ghost and flash that fade it), so a lit or pressed widget's outline was washed by
the highlight: a blue outline under an orange highlight came out green. Now every card is drawn as two
shapes of the same geometry (`Scene.Card`): its fill in the part's back layer as before, and its outline
in a new per-part layer, the rims (`Layer.Rim`, `Scene.rims`), over the highlight and over what stands on
the card. The scene's layers are now zones, cards' fills, highlight, contents, outlines, the keyboard's
focus rectangle (its own layer over the outlines it goes round; it was in the highlight's), edit mode's
marks, and a carried block. Both shapes glide, are carried and lifted with their part (`LayersOf`), and a
group's piece and its sides (§316) are the outline's shape. In edit mode a block's wash under the pointer
and its hairline moved from the marks' layer into the rims, under the card's outline and over what stands
on the block as before: a chosen outline keeps its colour lit or not; the hairline still shows where a
card has no outline and at a group's seams (stronger under the pointer there); it fades in with edit mode
as the wash does. The selected ring, the clipboard's ants and the focus rectangle stay over everything:
they mark the block, so the accent's ring goes round over a chosen outline. A card outline is only drawn
where somebody chose one (§246), so bars in Windows' colours look as before.

**The search box is its part's card.** Windows' search box (Layout.SearchBoxed) wore only Windows' text
box's colours. It now goes through the one resolver every card does: `Scene.ChosenOf(part)` is the
colours somebody chose that a part is drawn in, its widget's own over the bar's (`Palette.Over`, §311),
and `TokensOf` resolves a part's tokens from it. Where the part wears a card (`Scene.Carded`: a bar of
cards, or a card or outline of its own; the card loop uses it too), its plate takes the chosen card and
card outline (`Scene.PlateInks`; the outline replaces the edge's elevation gradient, solid). Its fill
changes with the pointer as Windows' does only while neither its card nor its highlight is chosen
(`LightsAsWindows`); else the plate stays at rest and the highlight lights it as any card, in the chosen
or the automatic highlight, pressed at two thirds (`ShadeOf`). Each colour left Automatic is Windows'
own, so a bar in Windows' colours shows Windows' box unchanged. Bar colours picked in Settings recolour
the plate in place (`Recolour` → `DressPlate`). High contrast keeps Windows' colours. The plate's edge is
a rim like any card's, over the highlight.

No config change. Tests: `SceneTreeTests.ALitWidgetKeepsItsOutline` (a real bar at 150 %, dark and
light: a widget's own outline under a strong own highlight and the bar's outline on a group, at rest,
under the pointer and pressed, and arranged at rest and hovered; along each side the outline is as much
of its pixel, weighed against the card as it is lit, as at rest; drawn under the highlight it was a tenth
of it), `TheSearchBoxWearsTheCardsColours` (the bar's card, outline and highlight; the box's own over
them; all Automatic keeping Windows' look and its own lighting; at rest, hovered and pressed; the plate's
fill, its four edges and the highlight's shade). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `widget-look-lit-[edit-]
<rest|hover-own|hover-bar|pressed-own|pressed-bar|selected>-<look>.png`,
`search-box-colors-<bar|own|automatic>-<rest|hover|pressed>-<look>.png`.

By hand: give a widget a card outline and a strong highlight of its own (Appearance at the foot of its
menu): hover and press it, the outline keeps its colour. Arrange the bar, hover and select it. Pick a card,
a card outline and a highlight in Settings › Appearance: the search box takes them; give the search box
its own in its menu; set them back to Automatic and it is Windows' box again.

## 326. The edit bar shows the layout, on every display, one width, and slides in (2026-10-23)

The person: *"if none layout is selected for a screen, in edit mode it should still show the edit bar
ontop, additionally add the layout that is shown to the top edit bar. also make the top edit bar have a
fixed with in folder and taskbar edit mode that is the same width. also add a slide in animation from
the top or bottom for the edit bar."* And, approved: *"In edit mode a Fill folder is shorter by the edit
bar's height, so its top jumps when edit mode starts."*

- **Every display is in edit mode**, one that shows None too: its dim and its edit bar
  (`Dock.EditedDisplays`, the displays attached, rather than the bars' windows). There "Add a widget"
  stands greyed (AccentFillColorDisabled; no bar to add to) and asks for nothing (`EditDeck.Adds`).
- **The layout's button**, first on the edit bar (`EditDeckPlan.LayoutPart`): a drop-down button — the
  layout's icon and name, or "None" with the hidden eye, and a chevron the way its list opens (down at
  the top, up at the bottom). It opens what the bar menu's Layouts level chooses from
  (`BarLooks.Shown`, §309, now one method both use): every layout and None where Karpo may be hidden
  there, the one shown ticked (`Dock.LayoutChoice`, `LayoutChoiceItems`). A pick closes it, as a
  drop-down's does, and is written as the menu's (`LooksPicked`): edit mode stays (§296). On a display
  showing None the bar holding edit mode owns the menu, which stands on that display, in its work area
  at its scale (`Pending.Work`, `Pending.Scale`).
- **One width.** The layout's button is `LayoutDip` (200 DIP) wide whatever it says, a long name ending
  in an ellipsis; with the folder's buttons the folder's name (and the open-folder glyph) stands in its
  place as a label, no chevron, no button. The edit bar is the same width in either mode and on a None
  display, each button where it stood as a folder opens or closes.
- **Slides in.** `FlyoutHost.Enter` starts the panel wholly past its window's edge on its side — the
  room there and its own depth (`FlyoutHost.EnterFrom`) — so it slides in from over the screen's edge
  (from under a bar where it stands under one) while it fades in, 300 ms on the decelerate curve
  (`Rise`, 250 before); as edit mode starts and as it comes back from standing aside; never with
  animations off.
- **No jump.** A folder's room stops short of the edit bar's band at rest as in edit mode
  (`EditDeckPlan.Band`, from the display's room alone, `Dock.DeckBand`; `DeckRoom` reads every bar by
  what it takes, `DockWindow.Takes`, at rest too). Chosen over letting the edit bar stand over the
  folder's far end: that would cover the folder's top or its column buttons (§310 took that away), and
  the band is no more than the margin, the bar and the margin. A Fill folder now stands the same as edit
  mode starts and ends, off every edge, top mirroring bottom.
- **Fixed with it** (a bug of §309): "Add layout ›" and "Duplicate ›" with nothing typed and Enter made
  nothing; a field that makes something (`OptionRow.Makes`, `FlyoutField.Makes`) keeps an empty Enter,
  and the layout is made under the placeholder ("New layout", "Home copy").

No config change. Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests` (four parts, `TheLayoutsButtonIsOneWidthWhateverItSays`,
`TheBandIsTheEditBarsWhateverItsWidth`, `ItSlidesInFromPastItsEdge`, the layout button's action, none
on the folder's name), `EditDeckClickTests` (`ItIsOneWidthWithTheBarsButtonsAndTheFolders`,
`OnADisplayShowingNoneItOffersTheLayoutsAndAddsNothing`, the layout click and its anchor),
`FolderFillTests.AFolderFillsAsFarOffEveryBar` (at rest and arranged the same, every edge),
`BarLooksTests.TheEditBarsLayoutButtonChoosesTheLayoutOrNone`,
`MenuFieldTests.EnterInAFieldThatMakesSomethingMakesItWithNothingTyped`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`editbar-<top|bottom>-<edit|folder>-<dark|light>-150.png`, `editbar-none-<dark|light>-150.png`,
`editbar-layouts-<dark|light>-150.png` (the list open), `editbar-widths-<dark|light>-150.png` (a long
layout name over the folder's buttons).

By hand: set a second display to None and start edit mode — its edit bar says None, "Add a widget" is
grey, pick a layout from it and the bar comes there, edit mode on. Watch the edit bar slide in from the
top (bottom with a top bar). Open a folder while arranging: the bar keeps its width, the folder's name in
the layout's place. A Fill folder: open it at rest, then in edit mode — it stands the same.

## 327. The meeting face hides by the faces' one rule; a folder's line hides at rest too: now playing while nothing plays (2026-10-23)

The person, approving the review's two items: *"The meeting widget uses its own hiding method; it should
move onto the shared one."* and *"The Now Playing line inside a folder can't hide yet, because folder lines
have no way to hide."*

**The meeting face.** Set to show a meeting only shortly before it (`MeetingFace.Soon`, §205), with none
that close, the face has nothing to show, and says so by the one rule every face has (§291):
`MeetingFaceDrawing.NothingToShow` is `MeetingFaceState.Hidden`. Gone: `FolderIsland.MeetingIdle`, its own
count beside `FacesOnBar` (`Count` is `FacesOnBar.Count == 0 ? 0 : 1` alone). So, as now playing and the
removable devices: at rest it is off the bar, and beside another face only it goes (§237; before, a meeting
face beside a clock stayed and said "No more meetings today"); arranged it is there greyed (§319's
`Unavailable.Paint`), saying there is none, where it used to leave a placeholder block.

**A line with nothing to show.** One mechanism for a folder's lines, the line's `NothingToShow`:
`CellIsland.NothingToShow` (false by default) says the line has nothing to show now; a kind that can say so
has a `ListWidget.IdleKey`, the strings key of its menu's switch, and its line keeps that switch in
`CellItem.HideIdle` (`"hideIdle"`, written only as `false`: absent is on, as the face's §319 default, so a
file from before hides such a line and nothing is migrated; `CellItem.Normalize` drops it on a kind that
never hides). `CellIsland.HiddenAtRest` is the two together. The now-playing line opts in
(`MediaIsland.NothingToShow`: not the apps playing, and `Idle`, the face's own quiet with its grace), its
switch in the face's words, "Hide it while nothing plays", among its Behaviour rows (`OptionRows.HideIdle`).
Another line opts in by an `IdleKey` and an override, nothing else.

- **At rest it takes no room.** `FolderIsland.Resting` lists the lines hidden now; `FolderFlyout.Build`'s
  `resting` leaves them out of every list's flow (no room, no gap, a box of no size: drawn nowhere and
  found nowhere), so the lines under one close up and a column it was all of is an empty outer column,
  which at rest is no column (§149): the others stand as they would without it. The layout's signature
  has each line's `HiddenAtRest`, so a track stopping or starting lays the open folder out again.
- **Arranged it stands where it stands**, greyed (`CellIsland.PaintOn`, the look of a widget not on this
  PC, §247): `Build` ignores `resting` while editing, so nothing moves as edit mode comes or goes.
- **A folder with nothing left is an empty folder** (§280): `FolderIsland.Empty` is every line hidden at
  rest (none at all included). A click at rest opens nothing and does not press, its tooltip says it is
  empty, arranged it opens; one open at rest when its last line goes closes, as a light dismiss
  (`FolderFlyout.FolderChanged`). Its face is the face's business: the media preset's hides by its own
  switch, one set to stay is on the bar.

The two switches are each their own (the face's and the line's), both on by default.

Tests: `MeetingPictures.TheSoonFaceWithNoneCloseIsGoneAtRestAndGreyedArranged` (no cell at rest, greyed
arranged as wide as today's "none left", beside a clock only it goes and comes back);
`MediaPresetTests.TheLineHidesWhileNothingPlaysUnlessAFileSaysOff` (read, written, dropped on a clock, the
menu's switch), `TheLineIsGoneAtRestWhileNothingPlaysAndGreyedArranged` (at rest the line under it at the
list's top, its own column gone, the folder as wide as the rest, one set to stay there; arranged all where
they stand; a track starting brings it back; greyed fainter than one set to stay, playing alike),
`AFolderWithEveryLineGoneIsEmptyAtRest`. `StandsOut` is one helper for a face's and a line's ink. Pictures:
meeting-soon-<dark|light>.png, now-playing-line-rest.png, now-playing-line-arranged.png,
now-playing-line-greyed.png.

By hand: a meeting folder set to "Shortly before": gone at rest with nothing close, grey in edit mode. A
folder with a now-playing line and others: pause the player, about five seconds later the line is gone
from the open folder and the rest closes up; edit mode: it is there, grey. Right-click the line: "Hide it
while nothing plays", off: it stays.

## 328. Empty columns outside a folder's widgets go; the width menu says which widths run off the screen (2026-10-23)

The person, on §320's audit: *"Empty columns pile up and can't be removed"* and *"the width choice
gives no hint that a width will run off screen; only the chip warns afterwards."* Their file had News
with seven empty columns before its one of widgets, Quick settings five, Test five, Notifications four:
each widget moved to a far slot left the slots between as empty columns (`Folders.InsertNew`), and
moved back, the column it left stayed too (§221: "deleting a column should not even be possible").
At rest they have no width (§158); arranged they hang off the folder's side, often past the screen,
with no buttons, and nothing can take them away.

**A move or a removal drops the empty columns it leaves outside** (`Folders.Trim`). After a line or
several are let go (`Folders.Move`, `MoveGroup`) and after a line is taken out (`Folders.Take`, and
through it `Folders.Remove`: a delete, a cut, a carry onto the bar or into another folder, Settings'
remove), the empty lists before the first list with widgets and after the last go, each with its
width. An empty list between two with widgets stays, a spacer the person may have set, at its width.
A folder with no widget left keeps its first list. No column is ever deleted by hand; there is still
no "remove column". A far slot is no empty column: a widget moved or added there still makes a list
there and the lists between it and the others (`FolderPlace.Slot`), and a slot's width still makes an
empty column of that width (`Folders.SetSlotWidth`), kept until a move or a removal in that folder.

`Take` says where the line stood so Settings' undo puts it back: its place where its list stays, a new
list at the start or the end where its list went (`FolderPlace.NewList`). While lines are carried, the
folder is shown as the move would leave it with every list where it stands
(`Folders.MoveKeepingLists`, `FolderDrag.Moved` and `Moves`): the drag's landing is read against the
plan as shown, and a list dropped there would move every line a column over in the panel. Letting go
trims; the lists with widgets stay where they stood (they are what is centred on the button, §158), and
the empty one that hung off their side is a slot again.

**A file that piled them up is trimmed once where it is read** (`LineMigrations`, `Config.Repair`),
never reset: every folder's outer empty columns go, the inner ones and every kept column's width as
they were, every widget where it was. `Config.Migrated` says `outerColumns` once it dropped any, and the
dock says so too as a slot's width makes an empty column outside (`LineMigrations.KeepOuterColumns`),
so that column is the person's and no read of the file drops it again. A file in today's words is left
alone and not marked.

**The width menu marks a width that runs the folder off the screen** (`Dock.FolderWidthRows`). Before
the menu opens, the open folder works out, for each of the five widths, whether the lists with widgets
would then run past the screen's edge (`FolderFlyout.RunsOffAt`, `RunsOff`): their box
(`FolderPlan.Core`) as much longer or shorter as the column gets, against the most it may be where it
is placed (`FlyoutPlacement.CoreRoom`: along a top or bottom bar the work area's width less the margin
it starts in by; beside a side bar from the bar and its gap to the work area's far side). That is
exactly what `FolderPlan.OffScreen` and the chip (§320) say once it is picked. A marked row wears the
warning glyph and, under its name, *"Runs off the screen"* (`dock.folder.width.offScreen`, 30
languages), ticked or not, and still picks: nothing is refused for not fitting. A column outside the
lists with widgets, and a slot, never run the folder off (an empty column past the edge is never said
to be either).

Tests: `FolderTrimTests` (the person's folders read once: outer empty columns gone, inner ones and
widths kept, a slot's width after it kept on the next read, a file with none not marked; a move out of
the outermost list, to a far slot and back, several together, a move that changes nothing, the drag's
copy keeping every list; a removal from the first, the last and a middle list put back where it was,
the last widget leaving one list), `FolderClipTests.AWidthThatRunsOffIsKnownBeforeItIsPicked` (pure:
which widths of which list run off, none outside or for a slot; the rows marked and enabled) and
`TheWidthMenusMarksAreWhatPickingSays` (every width of both columns of a widest clock and a list beside
it on a 1920 px display at 150 %, bottom, left and right bars: marked exactly where, picked, the folder
says it is off screen). `FolderPendingTests` and `FolderDropSweepTests` read a drop against the lists
as shown (`MoveKeepingLists`); the person's spacers there are marked kept. Picture:
`folder-column-menu-offscreen.png` (wide ticked, extra wide and widest marked).

By hand: in edit mode open News: no empty columns hang off its side. Move a widget to the third slot
out and back: the columns it made go with it. Open a column's width menu on a 1080p display beside a
widest column: the wider widths say "Runs off the screen"; pick one, and the folder's orange chip
appears as the menu said.

## 329. A folder takes the full height; in edit mode the edit bar stands over it (2026-10-23)

The person, on §326's no-jump rule (a folder's room short of the edit bar's band, at rest too): *"show
full heihgt, in edit mode just display the edit bar over the folder"*.

- **One room, at rest and arranged.** `DockWindow.FolderWork` is the work area less the bars alone
  (its own strip too, §287): a Fill folder reaches the far edge less the flyouts' 8 DIP margin (§320),
  off every edge, top mirroring bottom, left mirroring right, and stands exactly where it stood at rest
  as edit mode starts or ends. Gone: `EditDeckPlan.Band`, `EditDeckPlan.Tall`, `EditDeckSpot.Band`,
  `Dock.DeckBand` — the band rule of §310 and §326.
- **The edit bar over it.** The edit bar of the folder's display stands in front of the folder's window
  as before (`EditStack.KeepOver`, §301; the folder's `StandsUnder` the edit bar's windows), so a click
  on it is its own and one anywhere else the folder's (its window lets the room round its things
  through). The folder is never moved off it: the popups keep clear of the edit bar
  (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`), a folder's host not (`FlyoutHost.UnderEditBar`). What of the folder is under
  it, its guide lines and the top (or the foot) of a Fill list, is covered.
- **Its buttons stay reachable.** A column's "+" and width buttons the edit bar would cover — a list as
  tall as the room keeps them just inside its far end (§320) — stand just past it instead, the
  buttons' gap off it: under an edit bar at the top, over one at the bottom; ones beside it stay where
  they are (`FolderFlyout.WithSlots`' `covered`, a slot's too). The dock hands the edit bar's place
  over as the folder opens and again as the edit bar shows (`FolderFlyout.Covered`, which lays the open
  folder out again on a change).

Other popups and the sections' edit bars keep clear of the edit bar as before. No config change.

Tests: `FolderFillTests.AFolderFillsAsFarOffEveryBar` (every edge at 100 and 150 %: the far edge less
the margin, at rest and arranged the same, the edit bar over a top or bottom bar's folder, no button
under it), `ButtonsTheEditBarWouldCoverStandPastIt` (top and bottom edit bar, the rest untouched);
`SideBarPictures`/`EditPlacePictures` (a folder arranged: over no bar, the edit bar over it, no button
under it). `TheBandIsTheEditBarsWhateverItsWidth` and `AFoldersRoomStopsShortOfTheEditBarsBandMirrored`
went with the band. Pictures: `folder-edgefill-<bottom|top|left|right>-<rest|edit>-dark-150.png`, the
edit bar over the folder in edit mode.

By hand: a Fill folder off a bottom bar, open at rest, then start edit mode: nothing moves, the edit
bar slides in over the folder's top, the folder's buttons under it. The same off a top bar, the edit bar
at the bottom. Click the edit bar's buttons over the folder: they work; click the folder beside it: the
folder's.

## 330. The edit bar opens the display's settings and the taskbar's (2026-10-23)

The person: *"the taskbar and screen settings menu add them to the top edit bar."*

The bar's looks menu (§290, §309: the right click on an arranged bar's room) has two kinds of settings:
the display's — which layout it shows or None, where its bar stands, what new displays show, the
Displays page's — and the taskbar's — its layouts made, copied, named and deleted, its type, size, way of
showing, material, opacity and colours, the Layouts and Appearance pages'. The edit bar now opens each.

- **One list, cut three ways** (`BarLooks.Rows(…, LooksScope)`, `LooksScope.All | Display | Taskbar`):
  `All` is the right click's menu as it was; `Display` is `Shown` (every layout and None as rows of
  their own, the one shown ticked), `Position` and `NewDisplays`, ungrouped; `Taskbar` is the rest, its
  Layouts level without the display's two rows. `Position` and `NewDisplays` are row makers of their own
  now, shared by `All` and `Display`. Nothing twice, nothing lost: the two halves are the whole. A pick
  is found and written in the whole (`Dock.LooksRow`), so every write is the one it was.
- **The layout's button is the display's** (`EditDeckAction.Display`): it keeps showing the layout (or
  None) as §326 asked, and now opens the display's half, a configuration menu named "Display"
  (`BarLooks.Kind(…, scope)`, `dock.edit.display`), under it. Decided against a separate "Screen"
  button: the layout shown is the display's setting, so a second button would be a second way to the
  same choice. Identify is left out: in edit mode each display has its own edit bar already.
- **"Taskbar"** after it (`EditDeckPlan.TaskbarPart`, `EditDeckAction.Taskbar`, `dock.edit.taskbar`, the
  taskbar glyph and a chevron): a drop-down button whose words are the same whatever the bar's type, so
  its width never changes; its menu is named by the bar's type as the right click's is. Greyed
  (TextDisabled, no hover, no click: `EditDeck.Pressable`) on a display that shows None (no bar to set;
  `EditDeck.HasBar`, was `Adds`) and with the folder's buttons (the bar is locked under the folder,
  §212), where it stands all the same.
- **Where they open** (`Dock.DeckLooks`): under their buttons, away from the edit bar's side
  (`EditDeck.AnchorOf`, `ListEdge`), configuration menus (one height, §288) that stay open as a row is
  set, as the right click's does (§326's layout list closed on a pick; now it is a menu with more than
  the choice). On a None display the bar holding edit mode owns the display's menu, on that display in
  its work area at its scale (`Pending.Work`, `Scale`). A colour chosen in Windows' dialog brings the
  same half back from its button (`Pending.LooksScope`, `MenuBrowse`). `LayoutChoice` and
  `LayoutChoiceItems` are gone.
- **One width.** Five parts now (layout, Taskbar, Add, Settings, Close); `EditDeckPlan.IsDropDown` gives a
  drop-down its chevron's room after its words. The bar is the same width with the bar's buttons, the
  folder's and on a None display, each button where it stood.
- The right click on the bar's room still opens the whole menu.

No config change. Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheEditBarsTwoMenusAreTheBarsMenuCutInTwo` (the halves, their
order, groups, titles, the display's rows in the menu, a pick written; replaces
`TheEditBarsLayoutButtonChoosesTheLayoutOrNone`), `TheEditBarsButtonsOpenTheirHalvesTheDocksWay`;
`EditDeckPlanTests` (five parts, Taskbar's width with its chevron, `IsDropDown`, its action and none on
the folder's buttons), `EditDeckClickTests` (the Taskbar click and its anchor, greyed with the folder's
buttons and on a None display, the buttons where they stood). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`editbar-display-<dark|light>-150.png`, `editbar-taskbar-<dark|light>-150.png` (each menu open under its
button; replace `editbar-layouts-*`), `editbar-widths-*`, `editbar-none-*`, `editbar-<top|bottom>-*`.

By hand: start edit mode; click the layout's button: "Display" menu with the layouts, Position and New
displays show; pick another layout, the menu stays and the button says the new name. Click "Taskbar":
the bar's type, size, material, colours; change the size. On a display set to None, "Taskbar" is grey and
the layout's button still works. Open a folder while arranging: "Taskbar" grey, nothing moves.

## 331. A live camera: a webcam's or IP camera's picture in a folder, by MJPEG, snapshots, HLS, DASH and video (2026-10-23)

The person: *"add live webcam stream widget again. it should support the most common protocols."* No
earlier camera widget was in this repository's history, so it is built new: **Live camera** (`camera`,
`ListKind.Camera`, `WidgetInfos.Camera`, `CameraOptions`, `CameraLine`), a line of a list on the
"Weather and news" shelf after the earthquakes. **No face on the bar**: a moving picture at a face's 24 px
is no picture, and decoding a stream for as long as a bar shows would cost the battery all day; the line
is read only while its folder shows it.

**The ways a camera is read** (`CameraProtocol`, Karpo.Core\Cameras.cs; the dock's Karpo.Dock\Cameras):

| Protocol | What reads it | Here |
|---|---|---|
| MJPEG over HTTP(S) (`multipart/x-mixed-replace`) | Karpo's own reader (`MjpegReader`): parts by their Content-Length or to the next boundary, the boundary found however a camera names it, JPEGs by their markers where none is named; WIC decodes the newest, at most one a 33 ms, older ones dropped | works (Axis, Foscam, mjpg-streamer, Panasonic paths; ffmpeg's `mpjpeg`) |
| A snapshot (JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, WebP) | one GET a pace (5 s to 10 min, a minute new), asked with the last ETag and Last-Modified so an unchanged picture is a 304 | works |
| HLS (`.m3u8`), MPEG-DASH (`.mpd`) | Windows.Media.Playback's `MediaPlayer` through `AdaptiveMediaSource`, its frame server drawing each picture into a D3D11 texture of the line's own, read back at most one a 33 ms | works (live and on demand); a manifest Windows' adaptive reader turns down (DASH-IF's `dash-if-simple` profile) is tried with Media Foundation's own reader, and said where that fails |
| A video over HTTP (MP4, MPEG-TS, MKV, WebM, …) | the same player, looping a file | works for what Windows decodes (H.264; HEVC with its extension) |
| RTSP (`rtsp://`, `rtspt://`, `rtspu://`) | Media Foundation's RTSP source, through the same player | **not for an H.264 IP camera**: Windows' RTSP source carries ASF and MP3 alone; against an H.264 stream it opens and fails to decode (0xC00D003A). The line says so — "Windows can't play this RTSP stream: try the camera's MJPEG or snapshot address" — which nearly every such camera also serves |
| A web page (YouTube, a site's camera page) | read once for a stream it names itself: its `og:video`, else an `.m3u8` address written in it (JSON escapes undone) | a page that names none — a YouTube video's — says "A web page, not a stream: use the stream's own address" |

The protocol is **automatic**: guessed from the address (its scheme, its file's ending, the paths cameras
serve at: `mjpg/video.cgi`, `videostream.cgi`, `nphMotionJpeg`, `?action=stream`, `snapshot.cgi`,
`jpg/image.cgi` …), else from the camera's answer (`Cameras.FromAnswer`: its content type, else its first
bytes — a boundary, a JPEG's or PNG's start, `#EXTM3U`, `<MPD`, an MP4's `ftyp`). The Protocol row
overrides it. A user name and a password in the address are the camera's: sent to it alone (Basic or
Digest, as it asks; RTSP's own), never in the page a click opens.

**The line** (`CameraLine`, five rows unmeasured — about 16:9 at the list's width — one to twelve):

- *One row*: the newest picture small in the icon column (the camera glyph before one), the camera's name,
  and at the end how it is — "Connecting…", why not, a snapshot's time, or a red dot while it moves — the
  refresh button after it.
- *From two rows*: the picture over the line between the list's gutters, its corners a control's,
  filling it (cut at its edges) or **whole** inside it on a quiet fill, as **Fit** says. Its name on a
  plate of the list's own ground at its foot, a red dot before it while it moves, how it is after it; the
  refresh button on such a plate in its top corner. Before a picture: the glyph, the name and how it is in
  the middle, a long reason on up to three lines.
- What goes wrong is said over the last picture, which stays; the stream tries again after 5, 10, 30 and
  then every 60 s, a picture resetting that. The refresh button (§280, §305) connects again from the start;
  its check or "!" says how that went.
- A click, or Open website in its menu, opens the camera's page in the browser: a known camera's own page,
  else its address (without a password); an RTSP camera has none.

**Battery and work.** Nothing is asked, held open or decoded while the line does not show: `Visible`
starts the stream as the folder opens and stops it as it closes (the request let go, the player
disposed), the last picture kept to show at once next time. Pictures are decoded no larger than the line
draws them, into three arrays taken in turn (`PixelRing`), never one a frame. A moving picture is drawn on
the open folder's quick tick (`FolderFlyout.ArmQuick`, 33 ms) and only where a newer picture came
(`CameraLine.Streaming`, `Fresh`); a snapshot and every change of state wake the dock as any line's news
does. **Timers**: the stream's own retry and snapshot waits (`Task.Delay`, only while shown), and the quick
tick while a picture moves — no other.

**Settings** (§292): Camera (its address: a search over the person's other cameras, then public ones,
its own ticked; an address typed kept as typed), Protocol (Automatic, MJPEG, Snapshot, HLS, MPEG-DASH,
Video file, RTSP) — the subject; Fit — the look; Name (empty: a known camera's name, else its host) — the
words; How often it updates (a snapshot's, where it is or nobody knows yet) and Mute (a stream Windows
plays, where it is or nobody knows yet; muted unless turned off) — the behaviour. "Set up" asks for the
camera (`SetupField.Stream`). The file: `"camera": {"url": …}` and only what differs from its defaults
(`protocol`, `seconds`, `fit`, `mute`, `name`); a newer build's protocol reads as automatic; no reset, no
migration.

**The public cameras offered** (`KnownCameras`, each read through the line's own stream on 2026-10-23,
`CameraLiveTests` with `KARPO_CAMERA_LIVE=1`; the person's country first): foto-webcam.eu's snapshots
of Pizol, Wildhaus and Hoher Kasten (Switzerland), the Zugspitze and München (Germany), Wien and Innsbruck
(Austria), Malcesine and Meran (Italy); Pula's forum live (Croatia, HLS, WhatsUpCams); DASH-IF's live test
picture (MPEG-DASH). No public MJPEG camera whose owner publishes it as such answered (the classic test
streams are gone; the many open ones on the net are people's cameras left unsecured, and are not offered).
NASA's and Akamai's live HLS test channels answer with playlists whose streams are gone, and are not
offered.

**One drawing for a picture.** `PopupPaint.Covered` draws a picture over a box filling it or whole inside
it with rounded corners, the right way round in a mirrored line; now playing's art (MediaIsland, MediaLine)
draws through it too, and MediaIsland's own copy is gone.

Strings (30 languages): `core.widget.camera.*`, `core.camera.*` (the rows and the protocols' names),
`dock.camera.*` (states and reasons). Tests: `CameraRulesTests` (the protocol from the address and from the
answer, the boundary, addresses and the page a click opens, a page's own stream, the file, setup, the rows
by protocol and what they set, the field's suggestions, Switzerland first), `MjpegReaderTests` (five
cameras' ways of writing parts, whole, a byte at a time and in odd pieces; no boundary; noise held to a
picture's room), `CameraStreamTests` (on a camera of the test's own on the loopback, `FakeCamera`: an MJPEG
stream's pictures move and are said once; a snapshot asked again at its pace and not sent again unchanged;
a 404, a page and nobody there said and tried again; a line reads only while it shows),
`CameraLinePictures` (camera-lines-dark/light.png, 150 %: moving, a snapshot, whole, connecting, failed with
and without a picture, RTSP, not set up, at one, two, five and eight rows), `CameraLiveTests` (off unless
asked), and the registries' (`TypedRegistryTests`, `ListGutterTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `OptionRowsTests`,
`SetupLinkTests`, `UntranslatedTests`).

By hand: Add ▸ Weather and news ▸ Live camera into a folder; Camera ▸ Pizol: its picture and "17:04" on
the plate; type a camera of your own (`http://user:password@192.168.1.20/axis-cgi/mjpg/video.cgi` or the
like): it moves, the red dot on; close the folder and see in Task Manager that Karpo's network goes quiet;
set Fit to Show it whole; press refresh; type a YouTube address: it says it is a page.

## 332. A line of text is cleared however it is left; numbers typed are offered amounts (2026-10-23)

The person: *"clearing a label in the clock widget does not work, it just keeps its old value. this should
be fixed for similar input fields as well."* and *"add input recommendatations for number fields as well.
(e.g. how many stocks you own)"*

**Why a cleared label came back.** Enter on an emptied label did keep it empty (the setters take "" as
the default, `OptionTexts`, `FaceRow.Set`). But §304 gave every line of text that has anything to offer a
finder (`SuggestFinder`), and a field with a finder was a *search* to the menu (`Flyout.Fields.cs`): a
search's words only find, so when it is left without a pick — the menu closed by a click away, its level
shut by the back row, the keys on another row — they go back to what the setting says (`CloseSearches`,
`BlurField`, `EndFields`), where a plain line keeps them, as the page's box keeps its words as it loses
the focus. A label, a heading, a timer's, focus session's or alarm's name, a share's name on the bar:
cleared (✕ or select all and Delete) and left, they came back. And Enter kept their level open, as a
search's does, where a plain line's shuts.

**One rule: a line's words are its value** (`Flyout.Line`). A field is a line of text where it has no
finder or its finder only suggests (`OptionFinder.Suggests`: `SuggestFinder` yes; a feed's and a pin's
target's, which are proved or picked, and every other search, no). A line:

- Enter keeps the words, empty too, and shuts the level (`TextLevel` is a line's level now);
- leaving it any other way keeps them too (`LetGo`): the keys on another row, its level shut by the back
  row or from its suggestions, the menu closed;
- a suggestion picked is kept and shuts the level as Enter does;
- only Escape puts the setting back, keeping nothing.

A search's words still go back when it is left (`LetGo` reverts). What a field kept is what it holds until
the menu is shown again with the setting (`MenuTextField.Kept`), so it is kept once. The clear button (✕,
WinUI's, inside the box while it has the keys and words) was there already; it empties the field, which
the rule above then keeps.

Cleared, each line falls back to its default: a clock's label to its zone's first city (this PC's: none), a
clock face's likewise, a heading to nothing, a timer's, focus session's or alarm's name to its kind's
title, a pin's name to the name Windows gives what it opens, a share's name on the bar to its symbol, the
amount owned to none, a converter's amount to 1. A layout's name and a list's or a note's name refuse
empty as before: a thing keeps a name (`BarLooks.WriteName`, `Notebook.Rename`).

**Numbers typed are offered amounts** (`AmountFinder`, Karpo.Core\OptionSuggestions.cs), the one
suggestion mechanism (§304's `SuggestFinder`):

| Field | Offered |
|---|---|
| Amount you own (a share, a coin) | what the person owns of the same thing first, then of the rest (`WordsInUse`: each once, the thing beside it, "12.5 · AAPL"), then 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 — a coin 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10 |
| A converter's amount (a line's, a face's) | the other converters' amounts, then 1, 10, 100, 1000 |

The one held is ticked. Typed, the number is a row of its own first, written as the field writes one; then
the amounts that start with the figures ("2": 2, 25); words that are no number have no row, and Enter keeps
them for the row's write to refuse, as before. Amounts are written for a field in the person's own decimal
sign (`Currencies.Typed(value, marks)`, `NumberMarks.Region`) so they read back as themselves: "0,125" in
Germany, where "0.125" — what the field showed until now — read back as 125.

**The other numbers are not typed** and have no suggestions: steppers (a bar's opacity, a separator's width
and room, a chart's years, a slider's length) and a timer's or focus session's length (hours and minutes
steppers, §228) are set by steps.

**Audit, every field of the configuration menus:**

| Field | Kind | Suggestions | Cleared |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clock label, clock face label | line | others' labels, the zone's places | zone's first city |
| Heading's words | line | others' headings | nothing |
| Timer's, focus session's name; alarm's name | line | others' names | kind's title |
| Share's name on the bar | line | the listing's name | the symbol |
| Pin's name | line | none | Windows' name |
| Amount you own, converter's amount | line (number) | amounts, §329 | none; 1 |
| A layout's name, add, duplicate; a list's or a note's name | line | none | refused / made under its placeholder (§326) |
| Time zone, place, team, Windows Settings page, holidays' country, symbol, feed address, what a pin opens, icon filter | search / filter | as before | left: back |

No new words, no config change.

Tests: `FieldSuggestionsTests.EveryLineOfTextIsEmptiedByNothingKept` (each line's write emptied, back to its
default; a line's finder suggests, a search's does not), `AnAmountsFieldOffersTheAmountsOwnedThenRoundOnes`,
`AnAmountIsWrittenToReadBackAsItself`; `MenuFieldTests.ALineWithSuggestionsKeepsItsWordsHoweverItIsLeft`
(regression: a clock's label emptied and Enter, emptied and the menu closed, emptied with ✕ and the back row,
each kept empty; Escape keeps nothing; a suggestion picked is kept and shuts the level; a zone's words left
go back). Picture: `config-suggest-amount-dark.png` (an amount owned, with "2" typed, a converter's amount).

By hand: a clock line's Label: select all, Delete, click outside the menu: the label is gone (the clock says
its zone's city). Again with ✕ and the back arrow; and with words typed and Escape: unchanged. A share's
Amount you own: the other holdings and round amounts; pick 10. A converter's Amount: 1, 10, 100, 1000.

## 333. The bar's size a number; the Layouts level lists the layouts as a folder's faces are (2026-10-23)

The person: *"taskbar size should be a number input and not a select input"* and *"improve the design
of the layout settings on the taskbar context menu. they should be in behaviour be similar to the faces
one."* §309's Size was a choice of six (32 to 80, and a dragged size beside them); its Layouts level was
the layouts as rows to pick, then Add layout ›, Duplicate ›, Name ›, Icon › and Delete — the last four
only ever for the layout shown.

**Size is a stepper in pixels** (`BarLooks.Rows`, `OptionRowKind.Number`, `OptionUnit.Pixels`, "48 px"),
over all a bar may be (`Config.MinHeight` 28 to `MaxHeight` 160, what the layout code clamps to), a step
of four (`BarLooks.SizeStep`: every old size a step from 28), each button greyed at its end. Each bar's
own: a Top and bottom's top bar has its own row on its own menu. A size dragged on the bar's edge says
itself and steps from there; whatever is set is held to the range (`WriteSize`).

**A size is typed too**, as §332 types an amount: the stepper's row has a chevron after the stepper, and
a click on the row off its buttons, Enter or Space opens its level (Left and Right still step): a number
field (`OptionRow.SetText` on a `Number` row: `OptionMenu` gives it a level of its `FlyoutField`, as a
line of text has), its finder an `AmountFinder` (one mechanism with the amounts'). Nothing typed it
offers the person's other bars' sizes — every layout's, a Top and bottom's two, each with its layout's
name — then the usual ones, `BarLooks.Sizes` (32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80; still the settings app's box's),
each once, the bar's own ticked (`BarLooks.SizesOffered`). Typed, the number is a row of its own first,
then the sizes starting with its figures. Kept as §332 keeps a line (Enter, leaving, a pick):
`BarLooks.WriteTyped` reads it in the region's marks, rounds it and holds it to 28–160; emptied, the
default 48; words that are no number change nothing. The dock keeps it as it keeps a layout's name
(`Dock.LooksKept`, a pick's value or the words).

**The Layouts level is the person's own things'** (§324: `OptionOwned`, `OptionMenu.OwnedLevel`), listed
as a folder's faces are (§226, §240, §314). The row "Layouts" names the one shown (or None, its icon
the hidden eye); it is the display's choice (`BarLooks.Shown`'s, key `BarLayout`, so the edit bar's
layout button, §326, §330, picks through it too: one choice, two menus). It stands in the whole menu
(the right click) and in the edit bar's Taskbar half (§330, `LooksScope.Taskbar`). Its level:

- **Each layout a row**, in `Config.Layouts`' order, its icon and name, the one shown ticked. A click
  on it shows it on this display, the level staying; its chevron (or Right) opens its own level in
  place, under its name (`Flyout.Splits`: a choice's row with tools and a submenu; Enter and Space pick
  it). At its start a grip: dragged, or Ctrl+Up/Down, it moves among the layouts, and the order is the
  file's (`OptionThing.Move`, `OptionPick.Moves`, `OptionMenu.Moved`, `BarLooks.MoveLayout`) — what
  every display shows and new displays get are by id and stay. At its end a bin (Delete), asked first
  in Windows' dialog, greyed on the last layout with *"There is always one layout"* in its tip.
- **A layout's own level**: Name ›, Icon › and Duplicate, each of that layout, shown or not
  (`BarLooks.KeyOf(row, layout)`). Duplicate makes "Home copy" at the end in one click and shows it here.
- **"Add layout"** right under the list, as "Add a face" is: Windows 11's taskbar as "New layout"
  ("New layout 2"…) in one click, shown here. Things put in order have their Add under them; others
  (notes, accounts, calendars) keep it at the level's top (`OptionOwned.Ordered`). Add and Duplicate
  are greyed past the free version's layouts, saying why.
- **Under a rule** (`OptionOwned.After`), in the whole menu only: None, ticked while Karpo is hidden
  here, offered only while another display shows Karpo; and New displays show ›. In the Taskbar half
  they are not there: the Display half (the layout's button) has them once — which layout this display
  shows, None among its rows, Position, New displays show (`BarLooks.Layouts(…, display: false)`).

The ticked layout rows keep the tick's slot whether ticked or not, so every bin stands in one column.
`OptionRow.Makes`, `FlyoutField.Makes` and §326's Enter-with-nothing-typed for Add and Duplicate are
gone with their fields.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheLayoutsLevelManagesEachLayoutAsAFoldersFacesAre` (pick, None and the last
display without it, a layout not shown named, drawn and copied, Add twice, drags kept in the file's order
with the shown and the new displays' layout kept, delete asked and the last greyed),
`TheMenuShowsTheLayoutsAsAFoldersFacesAndGreysWhatCannotBeDone` (the level's rows in order, grips and
bins, Add under the list and greyed past the licence, a single layout's grip and bin greyed),
`ALayoutsRowIsPickedAndItsChevronOpensItsLevel` (a real menu: row click picks, chevron opens, Enter and
Right, the bin), `EachLookOfTheBarsMenuSetsWhatItSays` (the stepper's range, unit, step, the top bar's
own, typed values held, buttons greyed at an end), `ASizeTypedIsOfferedTheOtherBarsSizesThenTheUsualOnes`
(what is offered and ticked, typed rows, rounding, the range, empty, no number; the menu's field level),
`TheEditBarsTwoMenusAreTheBarsMenuCutInTwo` (the halves share the shown layout's choice alone; None and
new displays' in the Display half and the whole), `MenuFieldTests.ABarsSizeIsSteppedAndTyped` (a real
menu: the row's click and Enter open the level, typed and kept, Right steps). Pictures: `bar-looks-dark.png`
(the menu, its colours, its size's level), `bar-layouts-dark.png` (the menu, the Layouts level, Work's level).

By hand: in edit mode right-click the bar: Size steps by four in px; click the row off its buttons, type
150 and Enter: the bar is 150 px; the list offers your other layouts' sizes. Open Layouts: drag a layout by its
grip; click one to show it; its chevron opens Name, Icon, Duplicate; rename a layout that is not shown;
"Add layout" makes one at once; the last layout's bin is greyed. The edit bar's Taskbar › Layouts has
no None and no New displays show; the layout's button has them.

## 334. The taskbar and the folders each have their own look; folders open on hover (2026-10-23)

The person: give folders their own look settings, separate from the taskbar's (the settings proposal,
P1, decisions Q2 A, Q3 A and Q7: *"folders behave like the other widgets: open on hover (same rule as
the taskbar's flyouts on hover) and corner radius etc. implemented now"*).

- **One type, used twice.** `SurfaceLook` (Karpo.Core\SurfaceLook.cs): a material, its opacity, colours
  for the light and the dark mode (`BarColors`), its separators' style (`LineStyle`, §307) and whether
  what stands on it opens on hover. `Config.Taskbar` ("taskbar") and `Config.Folders` ("folders"),
  `Config.LookOf(Surface)`. `Surface { Taskbar, Folders }` replaces `SeparatorKind`; `SeparatorStyles.Of`
  reads a surface's separators (its default where the file has none). The recent colours are the
  config's own (`Config.RecentColors`, "recentColors"), every surface's and mode's.
- **The colours.** `ColorSlot` is a surface's: `Background` (the bar, or a folder's panel), `Card`,
  `CardOutline`, `Hover`, `Separator`, and the taskbar's alone `Menus` (every menu and widget flyout,
  Q3 A). Gone: the shared `Flyout` and `FolderSeparator` slots, `Config.Material/Opacity/Colors/
  Separators/FolderSeparators/HoverFlyouts`, `BarLooks.Colors` (now `SurfaceLooks.Slots(surface)`).
- **One resolver.** A widget's own (§311) over its surface's over Windows': a widget on a bar over the
  taskbar's (`Scene.Theme`, as before), a line of a folder over the folders' (`FolderFlyout.OwnOf`: its
  card, outline and highlight; never the taskbar's). The folder's panel is `FlyoutTheme.Folder`: the
  folders' material over a taskbar flyout's surface — Follow Windows is that surface itself (acrylic
  with transparency effects, solid without), Acrylic the blur under the tint at the folders' opacity,
  Translucent the tint alone over the desktop (`FlyoutTheme.SeeThrough`), Clear the rim alone, Opaque
  the solid body; a chosen background is the tint at its own alpha, as the bar's is; the folders'
  highlight lights what lights in the panel. No shadow under a see-through panel. Menus and widget
  flyouts keep the taskbar's "menus" colour. High contrast ignores all of it. The dock's `Look` carries
  the folders' `SurfaceTone` beside the taskbar's material, opacity and colours; an open folder takes a
  new look where it stands (`FolderFlyout.Relook`, `FlyoutHost.Restyle`); a change of the folders'
  colours builds (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer` recolours the taskbar's alone).
- **No change on screen (Q2 A), no reset.** A file of before is read once (`SurfaceLooks.Carry`, in
  `Config.Repair`): the taskbar takes the material, the opacity, the bar's, cards', outline's, highlight's
  and separators' colours, the flyouts' colour as its menus', the separators and "hoverFlyouts"; the
  folders take Follow Windows, the flyouts' colour as their panel's, no card, outline or highlight (a
  folder's lines wore none), the folder separators' colour and style (or the older "dividers" gap). The
  old keys are never written; `Config.Migrated` says "lookSplit" once; a block the file already has wins
  over them. `Material` reads tolerantly now: a word of a newer build is Follow Windows.
- **The menus.** One builder, `BarLooks.Appearance(config, surface, dark)`: Material, Opacity (only
  with Acrylic or Translucent), Custom colors › (the surface's slots, Reset all), its separators › (the
  separator's rows, §307), and Open … (On click / On hover). The bar's menu in edit mode (§290) has the
  taskbar's under its layout rows; a right click on an arranged folder's own room, on no line, opens the
  folders' (`FolderFlyoutAction.Looks`, `Dock.FolderLooksMenu`, `LooksScope.Folders` beside §330's halves, titled "Folders"), over the folder,
  which shows each change as it is made. The edit bar's Folders ▾ (P2) is to use the same builder.
- **Folders open on hover (Q7).** `SurfaceLook.OpenOnHover` of the folders: a rest on a folder that has
  something to show opens it, by the taskbar flyouts' rules (`WidgetHover`, now with `Opens`/`On`: each
  surface its own switch), and leaving it closes it again; a click still opens and closes it. The
  taskbar's switch is the old "Open widget flyouts". A corner radius has no setting on the taskbar, so
  the folders get none either.
- The settings app (going away) binds its Appearance page to the taskbar's look, the folder separators'
  colour to the folders'; nothing new there.

Strings: `dock.folders.background` ("Folder background"), `dock.folders.openOnHover` ("Open folders"),
30 languages.

Tests: `SurfaceLookTests` (a file of before carried once, each surface as it drew, the folder's panel
and menus the same records as before, a new block winning, carried once only, a new file untouched; a
widget's own over its surface's alone; the folders' materials; each surface's menu writing its own;
folders opening on hover by their own switch; the folders' colours built, the taskbar's recoloured),
`SceneTreeTests.TheTaskbarAndTheFoldersEachWearTheirOwnLook` (the real bar in the taskbar's card whatever
the folders', the real folder in the folders' panel, cards, outlines and highlight, read off the
compositor and the capture, and following its own surface's change alone). The tests of the separator
and colour pages, the separators' menus and the file read the surfaces now. Pictures:
`surface-look-bar[-other-folders]-<dark|light>-150.png`, `surface-look-folder[-changed]-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: with your config, nothing looks different after the update. In edit mode, open a folder and
right-click its empty room: "Folders" — set a card colour and Opaque: the folder's lines and panel
change, the bar does not; right-click the bar's room: the taskbar's Custom colors are as they were.
Set "Open folders: On hover" there, leave edit mode, rest on a folder: it opens; move away: it closes.

## 335. The edit bar's "Folders" and ⚙ Settings menus; the folder's name opens its menu (2026-10-23) — the menus a settings panel since §520 (2026-11-06)

The settings-in-the-dock plan's P2 (the person, 2026-10-23, approving it: Q1 A, "the folder's name on the
edit bar opens that folder's menu; the gear always means Settings"). The edit bar reads
`[Layout ▾] [Taskbar ▾] [Folders ▾] [+ Add a widget] | [⚙] [×]`, one width in every mode.

- **Six parts** (`EditDeckPlan`: `LayoutPart` 0, `TaskbarPart` 1, `FoldersPart` 2, `AddPart` 3,
  `SettingsPart` 4, `ClosePart` 5). "Folders" is a drop-down as "Taskbar" is (its words and a chevron,
  `IsDropDown`); the gear stays square and icon-only, a drop-down with no chevron as Windows' "More" is.
  The words are the same with the bar's buttons, the folder's and on a None display, so the bar is one
  width and every button stands where it stood (`EditDeckPlan.For`, the layout's 200 DIP).
- **Folders ▾** (`EditDeckAction.Folders`, `dock.edit.folders`): the folders' look and behaviour, §334's
  one builder (`BarLooks.Appearance(config, Surface.Folders, dark)`: material, opacity, colours,
  separators, open on hover), the very menu a right click on an arranged folder's room opens
  (`LooksScope.Folders`), opened from under the button the way the display's and the taskbar's are
  (`Dock.DeckLooks`, `EditDeckPlan.PartOf(scope)`). A colour picked in Windows' dialog brings it back
  under "Folders" (from a folder's room: over the folder). Enabled in every mode, a None display too
  (owned by the bar holding edit mode). A row added to that builder is on the edit bar with nothing else.
- **⚙ Settings ▾** (`EditDeckAction.Settings`, `dock.edit.settings`): Karpo as a whole, `KarpoMenu.Bands`
  in `Karpo.Core\KarpoMenu.cs`, one builder per section, each in its own file (`KarpoMenu.<Section>.cs`,
  every one `(Config, KarpoServices) → IReadOnlyList<OptionRow>`), in four bands ruled off from each
  other: Start with Windows, Language, Formats, Online · Accounts, Public holidays · Karpo Pro, Back up
  and reset, About Karpo · Quit Karpo. A section with no rows is not in the menu, nor a band with none:
  nothing stands empty or greyed for what is not there yet. Now:
  - **Online ›**: the map, the weather site and the finance site (§322, `LinkProviders`), each a choice of
    its sites by name, written to `mapProvider`, `weatherProvider`, `marketsProvider` as the General
    page's Links cards write them.
  - **Accounts ›**: §324's level (`OptionAccountRows.Row`) unfiltered: every kind to add, every account.
  - **Public holidays ›**: §324's level (`OptionHolidays.Rows`), the one every calendar widget has.
  - **Quit Karpo**: asked first (the About page's words), then the dock posts its host's marked close,
    `DockHost.QuitBy.Menu` (0x4B510003): `Closing.Answer` quits as for the settings app's and `--quit`,
    karpo.log says "the edit bar's Quit Karpo asked", the guard leaves it down (`DockExit`).
  - Start with Windows, Language, Formats, Karpo Pro, Back up and reset, About Karpo: no rows yet.
  What a section needs that Core has not (the accounts, the way out) comes in `KarpoServices`.
- **The folder's buttons** (Q1 A): the folder's name in the layout's place is a drop-down now
  (`EditDeckAction.FolderMenu`): it opens that folder's own menu (`Dock.OpenFolderMenu`, was
  `FolderSettings` from the gear). The gear means ⚙ Settings in every mode; "Taskbar" stays greyed
  (§330), "Folders" stays enabled. `dock.edit.folderSettings` is gone.
- **The settings app is no longer opened from the edit bar** (`dock.edit.openSettings` is gone); the
  other ways to it are the plan's P6.
- **⚙ in the dock** (`Karpo.Dock\Dock.SettingsMenu.cs`): `ShowSettingsMenu(display)` opens it under the
  gear (owned by the bar holding edit mode on a None display, as the display's menu is); a pick
  (`SettingsPicked`), a field (`SettingsKept`, through `FieldPicks.KeepRow`, shared with the widgets'
  menus now) and a colour dialog (`MenuBrowse`) find their row again in `KarpoMenu.Rows` read from a
  copy of the config, so a row a later phase adds to a section works with nothing to wire.
  `Pending.SettingsMenu` names the menu.

Seams for the later phases: P3 fills `KarpoMenu.Startup`, `.Language`, `.Formats` and adds the
interval and search engine to `.Online`; P4 extends `.Accounts` (each account's parts, the IMAP and
CalDAV forms) and `.Holidays` (colour); P5 fills `.Pro`, `.Backup`, `.About`. The folders' settings
(corner radius and the like) go into `BarLooks.Appearance` for `Surface.Folders` (§334).

New strings `dock.edit.folders`, `dock.edit.settings` in every language (Windows' own words, as the
folders' category and the bar menu's "Settings" have them); `dock.edit.openSettings`,
`dock.edit.folderSettings` removed. No config change.

Tests: `KarpoMenuTests` (the bands and the sections left out, Online's sites written, every account, the
holidays' level, Quit asked then the way out, Folders ▾ the folders' look and its button, ⚙'s items ruled
off by band, the dock's wiring and the host's quit for `QuitBy.Menu`); `EditDeckPlanTests`
(six parts, Folders' width with its chevron, the gear square, each button's action in both modes and what
opens under its button), `EditDeckClickTests` (Folders and the gear under their buttons, the folder's
name opening its menu, the None display's Folders and gear); `ClosingTests`, `GuardPolicyTests`
(0x4B510003 stays down). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `editbar-folders-`, `editbar-folders-separators-`,
`editbar-settings-`, `editbar-settings-online-`, `editbar-settings-accounts-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: start edit mode: Layout, Taskbar, Folders, Add a widget, the gear, the cross. Folders: the
folders' material, colours, separators and "Open folders"; open a folder and change its background. The gear: Online, Accounts, Public
holidays, Quit Karpo; pick another map and open a place on the map. Open a folder while arranging: the
folder's name has a chevron and opens its menu, the gear still opens Settings, nothing moves. Quit Karpo
asks, then the dock quits and the Windows taskbar comes back.

## 336. A layout's row opens its own level, as a face's does (2026-10-23)

The person, on §333's Layouts level: *"click should open its settings like faces"*. §333 made each
layout's row a split button (a click or Enter showed it on this display, its chevron or Right opened its
level); one row with two behaviours, and the one people reach for first switched the bar under them.

**One behaviour, a face's.** A layout's row opens its own level in place, under its name, by a click
anywhere off its grip and bin, Enter or Right, as a folder face's row does, whether it is shown or not.
It switches nothing. The Layouts row is no choice any more: a `Things` row (`BarLooks.LayoutsRow`,
"Layouts"), saying the layout shown (or None) at its end, its level `OptionOwned` as before. The layout
shown is still ticked (`OptionThing.Ticked`, a tick on a thing that is no choice: `OptionMenu.OwnedLevel`
sets `Checked` from it), the tick's slot kept on every row so ticks and bins each stand in one column.
Grip, bin, Add layout, None and New displays show are as §333 left them.

**Which layout this display shows** is the Display half's choice (`BarLooks.Shown`, `ShownRow`: the edit
bar's layout button, §330), and only that menu has it as a choice. In the whole menu (the right click),
which has no Display half beside it, a layout's level has **"Show on this display"** first
(`BarLooks.HereRow`, keyed by the layout; `settings.layouts.showHere`, new in every language), which
sets the display's choice and is greyed on the layout already shown. The edit bar's Taskbar half leaves
it out, as it leaves out None and New displays show: the layout button beside it picks. Add layout and
Duplicate still show what they make here at once.

Gone with the split button: `Flyout.Splits`, `Flyout.OnChevron`, the row's `Chevron` area and the
test-only `Flyout.ChevronMiddle`; a row of tools with a submenu is again simply a submenu's row
(`Flyout.ControlKey`'s Enter and Space only pick a choice's row with tools that has no submenu, §317).
No config change.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheLayoutsLevelManagesEachLayoutAsAFoldersFacesAre` (the row a `Things` row, the
tick following "Show on this display", greyed on the shown one, none ticked under None),
`TheEditBarsTwoMenusAreTheBarsMenuCutInTwo` (the shown layout the Display half's choice alone; the
Taskbar half's rows pick nothing, ticked, no "Show on this display"), `TheMenuShowsTheLayoutsAsAFoldersFacesAndGreysWhatCannotBeDone`
(rows no longer stay-picks; the level's four rows), `ALayoutsRowOpensItsLevelAsAFacesRowDoes` (a real menu:
a click, Enter and Right open the level, the shown one's too; "Show on this display" is the pick; the
bin), `AnotherLayoutShownInEditModeIsTheOneArranged`. Picture: `bar-layouts-dark.png` (the menu, the
Layouts level, Work's level and the shown one's, its "Show on this display" greyed).

By hand: in edit mode right-click the bar, open Layouts, click a layout that is not shown: its level
opens (Show on this display, Name, Icon, Duplicate) and the bar stays as it is; "Show on this display"
switches it. The edit bar's Taskbar › Layouts: a click opens the layout's level, no "Show on this
display"; the layout button switches.

## 337. ⚙ Settings: Start with Windows, Language, Formats and Online; the taskbar's behaviour (2026-10-23)

The settings-in-the-dock plan's P3 (G1 to G8, R1 to R9; Q4 A: *"combine/previews/flyouts on hover under
Taskbar ▾"*). The settings app's General and Localization pages are now all on the edit bar, each row
reading and writing the very key the page does, through logic both share in Core.

- **Start with Windows** (`KarpoMenu.Startup`): the ⚙ menu's first row, a toggle on `startWithWindows`,
  on while the setting is and Task Manager hasn't turned the entry off. Read and turned as the General
  page's card is, by `StartupSwitch` (Core, moved out of `SettingsModel.Startup`): off removes the Run
  entry at once, on again after Task Manager clears its "disabled" without changing the setting; the dock
  writes the entry as it applies the setting (`Dock.SyncStartup`, as before). What holds against it is
  its second line — "Turned off in Task Manager's Startup apps", "Karpo sets this up the next time it
  starts", "… again …" — and nothing where it is plainly on or off (a toggle's `OptionRow.Why` is drawn
  now, `OptionMenu`). Windows' side comes in `KarpoServices.Startup` (the real keys,
  `StartupSwitch.Windows`), so tests turn it through a seam of their own.
- **Language ›** (`KarpoMenu.Language`): "Windows default (Deutsch)", then every language in its own
  words (`Languages.ChoiceNames`, moved out of `SettingsModel.Language`; Windows' preferred languages in
  `KarpoServices.Windows`), more than ten, so the level is searched (§279). A pick writes `language`; the
  dock speaks it at once (`Dock.Apply`: `Languages.Apply`, the bars built again), which closes the menu
  made in the old words, and ⚙ opens again under the gear in the new ones (`SettingsPicked`).
- **Formats ›** (`KarpoMenu.Formats`, a level): every setting of the Localization page but the language —

## 338. ⚙ Settings › Accounts: each account's parts and colours, the mail and CalDAV servers' forms with a masked password; the holidays' colour (2026-10-23)

The settings-in-the-dock plan's P4 (Q6 A: "a masked password field in the dock's menu"). The Accounts
page's rest, in every Accounts level alike — ⚙ Settings' (every account, §335) and each widget's (those
that give what it shows, §324) —, the same rows (`OptionAccountRows`):

- **Add an account ›** is a level of the kinds that give what is shown, each its line under it as the
  page's cards said it: *Microsoft account* (signed in to in the browser, greyed with why where this
  Karpo has no app registration), *Mail server (IMAP) ›* and *CalDAV and CardDAV ›*, each its form. One
  kind alone (a to-do line's Microsoft) is the action itself. Nothing opens the settings app any more:
  `Dock.AddAccount`'s `OpenSettings(AccountsArgs)` is gone.
- **The form** (`Karpo.Core\AccountForm.cs`): Email address, Password (masked), Set the server myself,
  and while set: Server, Port (IMAP's; empty for its security's usual 993 or 143, which its placeholder
  says), Security (IMAP's; SSL/TLS or STARTTLS), User name; a rule; Test connection; Add. A draft, not the
  config: each field keeps its words on the form (`AccountForms`, the dock's one, kept while menus come
  and go), and a row's setter changes nothing of the config, so nothing is saved. Test and Add stand
  greyed with what is missing under them in the page's words ("Type the email address and its password.",
  a port from 1 to 65535); a try greys every field, the one tried saying what it does ("Looking for
  anna@example.com's mail server…"), and how it went stands under it once back — "Connected to
  imap.example.com.", the server's own refusal, "anna@example.com was added (imap.example.com)." —, the
  menu staying open. An edit takes the last outcome away. Add empties the form and wipes the password;
  the menu closing does too (a form being tried is emptied once it is back).
- **Trying** is the page's code, moved to `AccountSignIn.MailAsync`/`DavAsync` (Karpo.Accounts) and used by
  the page too: discovery and a sign-in, the account kept with its password as every account's secret is
  (`AccountBook`, DPAPI). The dock runs it on a thread of its own with the sign-in's patience
  (`MenuAccountTry`), and the answer comes back through the dock's dispatcher queue, where the menu
  standing open is shown again (`MenuAccountsChanged`). A server set by hand with its security or port is
  taken at its word: tried first, before autoconfig, SRV and the usual names (`MailDiscovery.FindAsync`);
  the page, which sets neither, still tries what was typed last.
- **The masked field** (`OptionRow.Masked` → `FlyoutField.Masked` → `MenuTextField.Masked`): it draws a
  bullet (●, Windows' PasswordBox's) for each letter and measures the bullets, so the caret and a click
  stand where they show; copy and cut do nothing (paste does); a double click selects all of it, not a
  word; the IME is off while it has the keys (its composition window would show the words); a screen
  reader finds an edit named for its row with UI Automation's IsPassword, and nothing in the menu's tree
  holds its words (a field exposes no value). Its row has no text of its own: it says ●●●●●●●● at its end
  while the form holds a password, whatever its length. What it holds is wiped as its level goes and as
  the menu closes, once what it kept is the menu's; the form holds the password as characters it clears.
  .NET's strings cannot be wiped: the typed words pass through one on their way to the form and to
  `AccountBook`, as they did on the page.
- **An account's submenu** is what is synced of it, as the page's card was (`AccountSyncRows.Menu`, moved
  with `AccountRows` to Karpo.Accounts): a heading per kind, a switch per calendar, address book, inbox
  and To Do list with its count under its name, under a heading why it did not sync (or that it has not
  where it lists nothing) with Windows' warning glyph, "Reconnect to sync tasks" where To Do was never
  allowed, then under a rule "Colors ›": each part that wears one, under its kind, Automatic or one of
  Outlook's twelve (`PartColours`, the palette moved to Core) or one's own in Windows' dialog. A switch
  writes `AccountBook.SetSynced`, a colour `AccountBook.SetColour` ("#RRGGBB", none for Automatic): the
  page's writes, which the dock hears. A colour row says the swatch of what the part wears, picked or not.
- **⚙ Settings › Public holidays ›** has their colour under the calendars, ruled off (`KarpoMenu.HolidayColour`):
  Automatic (the holidays' red) or the same palette, written to `holidays.colour` as the page wrote it.

Kinds new to the menus' rows, for any section: `OptionRowKind.Level` (a row opening a level of its own
rows, `OptionRow.Level`; `OptionRows.Flat` finds them) and `OptionRowKind.Heading` (a heading; without a
title, a rule); `OptionRow.Detail`, a second line under a switch's or an action's name. A widget's switch
pick now lists its sources too, and its colour dialog finds its row with them, so an account's part works
from a widget's menu as from ⚙.

New strings `dock.accounts.port`, `.portBad`, `.security`, `.test`, `.connected` in every language
("Port" is Windows' own word in cs, de, fr, id, ms, pl and ro). No config change.

Tests: `AccountFormTests` (what a form needs, the rows writing the form and never the config, Test and Add
through the caller with their busy and outcome lines, the menu closing empties the forms, an account's
switches and colours going to the caller as the page wrote them, the password's field on a real menu:
bullets, IsPassword, nowhere in the tree, Enter keeping it), `MenuTextFieldTests` (bullets, no copy or
cut, wiped), `KarpoMenuTests` (every kind in Add an account, the holidays' colour), `OwnedLevelsTests` (a
widget's Add an account opens the mail server's form), `AccountSyncRowsTests` (an account as a menu lists
it), `DiscoveryTests` (a server set with its security tried first). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`settings-accounts-`, `settings-account-`, `settings-imap-password-`, `settings-imap-form-`,
`settings-imap-refused-dark-150.png`.

By hand: ⚙ › Accounts › an account: turn a calendar off and on (the bar drops and shows it), pick a
colour, Reconnect. Add an account › Mail server: type an address and an app password, Test connection,
then Add; the account appears in the list and on a mail line. Narrator on the password's field says
"password". The same from a mail line's Accounts › Add an account. Public holidays › Color.
