## 340. Every way to the settings opens the edit bar's menus; nothing starts the settings app (2026-10-23)

The settings-in-the-dock plan's P6 (X5, X6, X8, X9; Q5 A: drop Identify). Everything the settings app
held is on the edit bar since §334–§339, so every way that started it now opens edit mode with the
edit bar's menu that holds what it asked for, under its button, at its level (`Karpo.Dock\
Dock.EditEntries.cs`, one table, `EditEntries.Landing`):

| Way in | Lands on |
|---|---|
| A bar's own menu's "Taskbar settings" (at rest or arranged), a pin's | Taskbar ▾ on that bar's display |
| The Layouts face's "Layout settings" | Taskbar ▾ › Layouts |
| A face's "Manage accounts" (mail, contacts, meeting) | ⚙ › Accounts |
| "Get Karpo Pro" in the add list and in a refusal | ⚙ › Karpo Pro, on that display |
| A second start of Karpo.exe (the Start menu, Explorer, a pin) | ⚙ on the main display |

- **How it opens.** `OpenEditMenu`: edit mode on the bar of that display (or the main display's, or the
  one holding edit mode where it shows None), the display's edit bar's Taskbar ▾ (`DeckLooks`) or ⚙
  (`ShowSettingsMenu`) under its button, then the landing's level opened in place (`OpenShownLevel`,
  the menu's first-level row by its key, as a click opens it; §339's "back on Back up and reset" uses it
  too). From a menu's row it runs once that menu has gone (`OpenEditMenuLater`, `Later`).
- **A second start.** Karpo.exe finds the dock running (its mutex), finds the host, gives it its right
  to come to the front and posts it `DockHost.SettingsMessage` ("karpo.settings"), then ends
  (`SecondStart.Ask`, Program.cs). Not for an automatic start — Windows' Run entry (`--startup`), the
  logon task (`--logon-task`), the guard's restart (`--restarts`) — nor on a config of its own
  (`SecondStart.Asks`). The host keeps it through a menu's modal loop (`Deferrable`).
- **A widget waiting to be set up** (a card or a line in a folder, §228): its "Set up" opens the
  widget's own configuration menu over the folder (`FolderFlyoutAction.Setup` → `WidgetMenu(…,
  configure: true)`: its settings alone, a configuration menu, at rest too — at rest a widget's menu is
  otherwise its acts alone, §253, which had left a field's "Set up" with nothing to set). One that needs
  an account (mail, contacts, a to-do list) opens at its Accounts level (`SetupLink.ToAccounts`,
  `OptionAccountRows.Accounts`). `SetupLink.Args` is gone.
- **Gone from the dock:** the `SettingsApp` class (finding settings\Karpo.exe, `KARPO_SETTINGS`,
  launching and raising it, `WM_KARPO_SETTINGS_MISSING` and its "Settings app not found" flyout with
  "Open config file", the hand-off `WM_COPYDATA` and `WM_KARPO_SETTINGS_HANDED`), `OpenSettings`,
  `OpenDisplaySettings`, `Dock.EditSettings.cs` (the "karpo.editing" handshake that kept the app on top
  in edit mode), "karpo.edit" (the app's "Edit on the taskbar"), "karpo.identify" with `BarFor`,
  `DockWindow.Identify` and `Scene.Identify` (Q5 A: the Display ▾ menu names the display),
  `EditClicks.LayoutsArgs`, `LicenseRows.PageArgs`, `Dock.FaceMenus.AccountsArgs`, the dead
  `Islands.SettingsItem` and the add list's settings arguments that `Follow` never got.
  `SettingsHandOff` moved into the settings app's own code until P7 deletes it.

No config change, no new strings (the "settings missing" and Identify strings go in P7 with the
others nothing uses).

Tests: `EditEntriesTests` — `NothingStartsTheSettingsApp` (no line of Karpo.Dock, Core or Accounts, but
comments, names the launcher, the hand-off, the folder's variable, a deep link, the handshake or
Identify's message), `EachWayInLandsOnItsMenu`, `EachLevelIsARowOfItsMenuThatOpens` (the dock's own ⚙
and Taskbar ▾ items: the first row picked by the landing's key is on the first level and has a level),
`TheDockGoesEachWay`, `ASecondStartAsksWhereAPersonStartedIt`; `SetupLinkTests.AnAccountLinkOpensTheWidgetsAccountsLevel`.
`IdentifyTests` and `SettingsLaunchTests` are gone with what they held. `NativeBoundaryTests` names why
§338's and §339's new thread starts (the licence's continuations, the account try's task and its post)
let nothing out; it failed on master since §338.

By hand: right-click the taskbar › Taskbar settings: edit mode, Taskbar ▾ open under its button. Add a
widget past the free limit › Get Karpo Pro: ⚙ › Karpo Pro. A mail face's Manage accounts: ⚙ › Accounts.
With Karpo running, start Karpo.exe again (Start menu or Explorer): edit mode on the main display, ⚙ open,
in front. Sign in with Karpo starting at logon: no ⚙ pops up. In a folder, click a mail line with no
account: its menu opens over the folder on Accounts.

## 341. The settings app is gone (2026-10-23)

The settings-in-the-dock plan's P7. Since §340 nothing started it, so the WinUI 3 settings app goes, and
Karpo is one native executable. The references to "the settings app" in the §s before this one stay as
history; where a setting lives now is the edit bar (§335–§339).

- **Deleted:** `Karpo.Settings\` (92 files, about 13,900 lines: the window, its pages, controls and
  `Logic\`) and its entry in `Karpo.slnx`; `assets\settings-icons\` (its side menu's icons) and
  `assets\branding\lometics.svg` (About's mark is `lometics-128.png`, inside the dock, §339).
- **Publishing** (`scripts\publish.ps1`): the bar alone, native AOT; no `settings\` folder, no Windows
  App SDK runtime beside it, nothing to stage for a second process. An install swap replaces the whole
  folder, so an installed copy's `settings\` goes with the update.
- **Its words:** every `settings.*` key nothing of Karpo's reads any more — the pages' intros,
  descriptions, keywords, the side menu, the search, the window's chrome, Identify, the "settings app
  not found" flyout — 356 keys, in all 30 languages (10,680 lines). The rest stay: the edit bar's rows
  read them (most of ⚙'s and the looks' words are the pages' own). The icons' names stay too, read by
  the icon's id (`IconSearch.Key`).
- **Left in the dock:** the `KarpoRepo` build-path metadata in Karpo.exe (only the settings app's search
  used it) is gone; `DockHost.QuitBy.Settings` stays, an exit code the guard knows.
- **Tests.** The test project no longer compiles the app's `Logic\`; the tests of what went with it are
  gone (24 files: navigation, chrome, search and its index, start and hand-off, the display map and
  cards, colour pages, side menu icons, the settings source reader, the XAML ratchet of
  `HardCodedEnglishTests`, `SearchWordsTests`, …). The tests of logic that lives in Core moved from
  `Karpo.Tests\Settings` to `Karpo.Tests\Core` (`CountdownLength`, `DisplayLayoutChoice`, `FaceGallery`,
  `FormatsSummary`, `HeightLimits`, `IconSearch`, `OnlineUpdateRow`, `PlaceQuery`, `SymbolQuery`,
  `TimeZoneSearch`, `TimeZoneText`, `CalendarCards`, `ShortDescriptions`, `LineRows`, `EngineLogo` — this
  one now checks the logos the dock carries in its exe). The repository's source is read through
  `RepoSource` (Karpo.Tests), not through the app's folder.
  - `ConfigCoverageTests` replaces `BarLooksTests.EveryLookTheSettingsAppHasIsARowOfAMenu`, which read the
    app's XAML: every row of ⚙ Settings, the bar's whole menu, Folders ▾, a separator's and a divider's
    menu is acted on a copy of a config every way it can be (each choice, a step either way, flipped,
    done, words typed), and every settable property of `Config` — and of `taskbar`, `folders`, `formats`
    and `holidays` one level down — is written by one, or named with why none does (`version`,
    `migrated`, the tray's order and states, the recent colours, §334's keys only read). A property added
    to `Config` fails it until a row writes it.
  - `SettingsWordsUsedTests`: every `settings.*` key left is read by the dock, Core or the accounts.
  - `EditEntriesTests.TheSettingsAppIsGone`: no project, no slnx entry, no tests' copy, no publish step.

By hand: publish and start Karpo.exe: one file, no `settings` folder. Upgrading an installed copy
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Karpo`): the folder is replaced whole, so its old `settings\` goes; a Start menu
shortcut that pointed at `settings\Karpo.exe` points at nothing — it should point at `Karpo.exe`, whose
second start opens ⚙ (§340).

## 342. The edit bar stays over the arranged folder, whatever moves the folder's window (2026-10-24)

The person: "the top edit bar sometimes clips behind the folder column lines." In edit mode with a
folder open, the folder's window, which spans the display for its guide lines (§246), sometimes stood
over the edit bar with the folder's buttons (§297, §329) and over the bars (§279).

- **Why.** The folder's level — over its dim, under the lowest of the bars, the edit bars and other
  apps' windows over it (`EditStack.UnderOthers`) — was put back *after* each move that raised it:
  `FlyoutHost.Restand` on showing and on `WM_ACTIVATE`. Activation brings a window to the top of every
  topmost window, and a menu closing hands the focus back to the folder (`FlyoutHost.Close`'s restore,
  `SetForegroundWindow`) inside the dock's own handling of a message: the dock is busy then, its
  window procedure turns the folder's `WM_ACTIVATE` away, and nothing put it back. Any other raise (no
  activation at all) was never put back either.
- **One rule, as the move is asked for.** The folder's `WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING` sets where it goes in
  the z-order (`FlyoutHost.Stand`, `FolderFlyout.Stand`): its level, whatever asked — its placing, a
  click, the focus handed back, Windows picking it next, anything raising it. The dock's window
  procedure hands it over before the busy check (`Dock.FolderStands`), as it does energy saver's and
  UI Automation's messages, so it holds in a menu's loop too. Nothing is put back after a move, so the
  folder never stands over the edit bar even for a frame. `Restand` is gone, and so is `ShowDecks`'
  lift of the edit bar over the folder (`EditStack.KeepOver(deck, folder)`): the folder never goes
  over a visible edit bar, and one shown again comes up on top as every popup does.
- **Shown without activating.** A `SetWindowPos` that activates the window puts it at the top
  whatever its `WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING` says (seen on the hidden desktop: the hidden folder shown and
  activated in one call landed over everything). So an arranged folder is shown with `SWP_NOACTIVATE`
  and activated by `Open`'s `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus` right after, which `Stand` holds; it is
  the active window for the keys as before. Every other popup is shown as before.
- **Tests.** `FolderSlotTests.TheEditBarStaysOverTheArrangedFolder`: a real dim, edit bar with the

## 344. The edit bar without its accent ring; new displays may show None; "Add a widget" leaves the folder open (2026-10-25) — new displays always show the default layout, no None, since §636 (2026-11-09)

The person:

- *"dont show the blue selection around the top edit bar."*
- *"new displays should also be able to show none."*
- *"add a widget should not close the folder"*

What changed:

- **No accent ring.** §310 drew the edit bar's rim in the accent (`FlyoutHost.AccentRim`) so it stood out
  over the dim; it read as a selection. Gone: the edit bar wears a flyout's own rim, the surface's
  neutral stroke, as every other popup of Karpo's does (high contrast the system's, as before), and
  `AccentRim` with it. What still draws the eye is the slide-in (§310) and the accent "Add" buttons.
- **New displays show › None.** After the layouts the row offers None with the hide glyph
  (`BarLooks.NewDisplays`, `WriteNewDisplays(config, null)`), stored as `Config.NewDisplaysHidden`
  (`"newDisplaysHidden"`, a bool beside `defaultLayoutId`; unset in older files, read as false: a new
  display shows the layout, as before; nothing migrated). `DefaultLayoutId` stays as it is — the layout
  such a display shows once Karpo is turned on there, and what a display without an entry shows —, and
  picking a layout again clears None. Applied where a display first seen gets its entry
  (`Config.NewScreen`, through `AddDisplay` in `Dock.Arrange`): Karpo off there (`Screen.Enabled` false),
  so it gets no bar and Windows' taskbar stays (`Taskbar.SetDisabledDisplays`, as for None picked by
  hand). Never the only display shown: with no display showing Karpo yet the new one does, and
  `Arrange`'s fallback to the primary still holds. A reset of the layouts resets it too (`ConfigReset`);
  the transfer summary names it as it names `defaultLayoutId` ("New displays show").
- **"Add a widget" leaves the folder open.** §343 closed an open folder first; now the button only opens
  the bar's add list from itself (`DeckAdd`, `AddSpot.Follows`), the folder standing open arranged behind
  it as it does through every menu (`OneFolder`, `FlyoutHost.StaysOpen`). The pick goes onto the bar at
  the place nearest the pointer and is carried there (`AddChosen`, `Follow`, §298); a click puts it down
  where the ghost shows. That click is the follow hook's and is kept from what is under the pointer
  (`FollowGesture`), so the bar locked under the folder (§212) never hears a press that would close the
  folder. Carried over the open folder, the folder says it takes nothing from the bar, as for a dragged
  block; let go there, the widget stays on the bar where it went in. "Add to folder" is unchanged.

No config reset: one new optional key. Strings: none new (`settings.displays.none` reused).

## 345. Each layout its own taskbar look and behaviour; Hide the Windows taskbar is a general setting (2026-10-25)

The person:

- *"hiding windows taskbar should be a general setting, not a layout one"*
- *"the taskbar settings as far as i know are not local to the taskbar but are global, this should not be,
  the style and stuff like that should be fully configurable independently on the layout, they should be
  scoped to the layout."*

**One model.** Everything Taskbar ▾ sets is the shown layout's now. `TaskbarLayout` gained `Look`
(a `SurfaceLook`: material, opacity, light and dark colours with the menus' among them, separators, flyouts on
hover; the file's `"look"`), `Combine` and `Previews`. `Config.Taskbar`, `Config.Combine` and `Config.Previews`
are gone; the file's top-level `"taskbar"`, `"combine"` and `"previews"` are read once and never written
(`TaskbarBefore`, `CombineBefore`, `PreviewsBefore`). One resolver, `Config.LookOf(surface, layout)`: the
taskbar's is `layout.Look`; the folders' stays `Config.Folders` for every layout. Scoping the folders too
would change that resolver alone (and give `TaskbarLayout` a folders' look).

**Migration, no visual change** (`SurfaceLooks.Spread`, `migrated: "layoutLooks"`): every layout gets a copy
of the file's one taskbar look (or what `Carry` made of a pre-§334 file's top-level keys), its combine and its
previews. A layout whose own `"look"` the file has keeps it. Done once; a second load changes nothing, and old
keys an older build writes again are read past. No reset, no shape bump.

**New layouts and copies.** Add layout starts from the default look (Follow Windows, Windows' combine,
previews on); Duplicate copies its source's look (deep: `SurfaceLook.Copy`), combine and previews
(`TaskbarLayout.CopyAs`). Reset layouts (⚙ › Back up and reset) now resets their looks with them, being the
layouts'; the folders' look and every other setting stay.

**Rendering.** `ScreenEdges`' `EdgeBar.Of` names the layout a bar is of; `Config.WithEdge` carries it into the
bar's config copy (`Config.Bar`, `BarLayout`: the default layout in a config made in code). `Layout` reads its
separators from it, `AppButtons.Lay` its combine. The dock's `look` is Windows' look and the folders' tone
only; `Look.Wearing(SurfaceLook)` dresses it in a layout's (material settled, opacity, colours; none in high
contrast), and `Dock.LookOf(layout)` / `LookOn(display)` / `DockWindow.Look` are what a bar is built and
recoloured in and **what every popup opened from it wears**: the widget and tray menus, quick settings,
window previews, the folder and its menus, pin folders, the edit rail, and the edit bar over a display its
layout's. So Q3's "menus follow the taskbar's look" is now "the look of the bar they open from". Per-widget
colours (§311) still lay over the layout's. Window previews and flyouts on hover are each bar's layout's
(`ShownLayout.Previews`, `WidgetHover.Opens/On(config, layout, …)`). `Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer` compares every
layout's colours; `Recolour` builds again where a bar's look changed by more than its colours (a see-through
background settles its material otherwise).

**Menus.** Taskbar ▾ (and the bar's whole menu) builds `BarLooks.Appearance(config, layout, surface, dark)`
and `Behaviour(config, layout, surface)` for the display's layout; Behavior is Combine, Window previews and
flyouts on hover. A separator's rows write its own bar's layout's look (`OptionPlace.Layout`, the dock's
`PickerPlace(of, key)` from the widget's owner). `SeparatorStyles.Of/Set`, `ColorPalette.Write`,
`OptionPickers.Shape` and `BarLooks.WriteLines` take the `SurfaceLook` itself.

**Hide the Windows taskbar** is ⚙ Settings' second row, after Start with Windows (`KarpoMenu.HideTaskbarRow`,
`KarpoMenu.Startup.cs`): a toggle writing the one global `"hideTaskbar"`, as before.

No string added or removed.

Tests: `LayoutLookTests` (each layout gets the old look once, a copy each, second load no change; a layout's
own wins; old keys read past once given; a pre-§334 file gives every layout its bar; Duplicate copies, Add
starts default; the Taskbar menu of display 2 writes layout 2 alone; a separator's rows write its layout's;
a bar laid out wears its own layout's; the menus colour follows the bar's layout, none in high contrast; no
popup in the dock's bare look; another layout's colours recolour in place), `SceneTreeTests.EachLayoutsBarWearsItsOwnLook`
(two layouts' bars, cards, background and separators read off the pixels), `KarpoMenuGeneralTests` (hide row in
⚙, writes `hideTaskbar`; behaviour writes `layouts.0.combine`, `.previews`, `.look.openOnHover`),
`ConfigCoverageTests` (a layout's `look.*`, `combine`, `previews` each written by a row; the old top-level keys
named), and the existing look, separator, reset, transfer and migration tests moved onto the layout.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `layout-look-<home|work>-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: two displays showing two layouts. Taskbar ▾ on one: change Material, a colour, Menus, Separators,
Combine — only that display's bar changes; right-click a widget on each bar: each menu in its own bar's menus
colour. Duplicate a styled layout: the copy looks the same; Add layout: Windows' look. ⚙: Hide the Windows
taskbar under Start with Windows; Taskbar ▾ › Behavior no longer has it.

## 346. Each layout its own folders' look (2026-10-25)

The person, of the folders' look §345 left global: *"scope this to layout too"*.

**One model.** `TaskbarLayout` gained `Folders` (a `SurfaceLook`: the panel's material, opacity and colours,
the lines' cards, outlines and highlight, the folder separators' look and colour, and whether a folder opens
on hover; the file's `"folders"`, beside `"look"`). `Config.Folders` is gone; the resolver,
`Config.LookOf(surface, layout)`, returns `layout.Folders` for the folders as it returns `layout.Look` for the
taskbar. The file's top-level `"folders"` is read once and never written (`Config.FoldersBefore`).

**Migration, no visual change** (`SurfaceLooks.SpreadFolders`, `migrated: "layoutFolders"`): every layout gets
a copy of the file's one folders' look (or what `Carry` made of a pre-§334 file's top-level keys, now handed
on by `ref` as the taskbar's is). A layout whose own `"folders"` the file has keeps it. Done once; the old key
an older build writes again is read past. No reset, no shape bump. One-time: the legacy cleanup deletes it
with §345's.

**New layouts and copies.** Add layout starts from the default folders' look; Duplicate copies its
source's (`TaskbarLayout.CopyAs`, deep). Reset layouts resets the folders' looks with the layouts, being
theirs; every other setting stays.

**Rendering.** `Look.Wearing(taskbar, folders)` dresses Windows' look in both of a layout's looks (the
folders' tone: material as chosen, settled where the panel is made, `FlyoutTheme.Folder`; opacity; colours,
none in high contrast); `Look.Wearing(config, layout)` is the one call `Dock.LookOf(layout)` makes, so
`DockWindow.Look` — what a folder opened from a bar is shown and relooked in — carries that bar's layout's
folders. `ReadLook` no longer reads the config at all. A folder's separators come from its owner's layout
(`FolderIsland`: `config.LayoutOf(owner)`), its opening on hover from its bar's (`WidgetHover.Opens/On(config,
layout, …)`). A change to a layout's folders' look builds again, as the folders' colours always did
(`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`).

**Menus.** Folders ▾ (edit bar) and an arranged folder's room menu build `BarLooks.Appearance` for the
display's shown layout (`LooksScope.Folders`, `ActiveLayout(bar.Display)`), so they write that layout's folders
alone. A divider's rows write its folder's bar's layout's (`OptionPlace.Layout` from the widget's owner, as a
separator's do).

No string added or removed. `TransferSummary.Title("folders")` is left for the legacy cleanup, as
`"taskbar"` was.

Tests: `LayoutFoldersTests` (every layout gets the one folders' look once, a copy each, second load no
change; a layout's own wins; the old key read past once given; Duplicate copies, Add starts default; Folders
▾ on display 2 writes layout 2's folders alone and not its taskbar look; a divider's rows write its layout's;
open on hover per layout; two layouts' folders dressed apart, none in high contrast),
`SceneTreeTests.EachLayoutsFolderWearsItsOwnLook` (two layouts' real folders: panel, cards, the captured plate,
the separator's shape and colour), `ConfigCoverageTests` (each property of a layout's `folders.*` written by a
row; the old top-level `"folders"` named), the reset tests (the folders' look resets with the layouts), and
the existing look, separator and migration tests moved onto the layout. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`layout-folders-<home|work>-dark-150.png`.

By hand: two displays showing two layouts. Folders ▾ on one: change Material, Background, Separators,
Open on hover — only the folders on that display's bar change; open a folder on each bar: each in its own
layout's panel and separators. Duplicate a layout: its folders look the same; Add layout: Windows' look.

## 347. Each tray widget its own icon states and order (2026-10-25)

The person, about which icons sit on the bar and which behind the "^": *"actually scope them not to the
layout but scope these settings to the widget even."*

**One model.** A tray's icons are its own options: `BarItem.TrayIcons` (`TrayIconOptions`, the file's
`"trayIcons": { "states": {...}, "order": [...] }` on the tray's entry; `WidgetOptionsKind.Tray`), absent while
it says nothing. `Config.TrayStates` and `Config.TrayOrder` are gone; `TrayLayout` (`InOrder`, `State`,
`Choice`, `Split`, `Off`, `Set`, `Apply`) takes a tray's `TrayIconOptions`. Two trays — on two layouts, or two
on one bar — show the same live icons each its own way. An icon a tray names nothing for still goes where
Windows' own choice says (IsPromoted), per tray, as before.

**Every reader reads its tray's own.** The dock keeps one split per placed tray, by its key
(`Dock.traySplits`, `TraySplit.Of(options, icons)`, built in `ReadTray`); `Content.Trays` hands each tray part
its icons and its chevron (`BarTray`, `Content.TrayOf`/`TrayOverflowOf`), the layout measures each by its key
(`Measures.Trays`, carried with the part through `Carry`/`With`/`Without`), and the scene draws and repaints
each its own (`Scene.SetTray(gfx, key => …)`). A click, a press, a hover, a tooltip, the app's popup rects
(`PublishTrayRects`), the keys (`KeyStops.Of`) and Narrator (`BarUia.Entries`, `Describe`) read the icon of
the tray the hit is in (`Dock.TrayIconAt`); the overflow a chevron opens holds that tray's spilled and hidden
icons (`TrayOverflowOf(window, chevron)`). `KeyStops.Of` and `BarUia.Entries` lost their tray count: each tray
part's own is the layout's.

**A drag stays in its tray.** `TrayDragging.Tray` is the key of the tray it was taken from — off its bar, or
out of the overflow its chevron opened —, and only that tray, its chevron and that overflow are drops
(`TrayTargetAt`: `TrayDrags.OnLayout` on that part; `OnTrays`, which read whichever tray was under the
pointer, is gone). Only that tray grows, shrinks, opens a gap and stands its chevron for the drag. The drop
writes that tray's options in the copy saved (`TrayLayout.Apply(home.TrayIcons ??= new(), …)`).

**The Tray icons level** of a tray's menu (§261, §323) lists its own places and writes its own
(`OptionTray.Rows(tray, icons)`: `Set` into `tray.TrayIcons`); it needs no config any more, only the live
icons. Picking in one tray's menu leaves every other tray as it was.

**Windows' one choice per icon.** A choice made in a tray is told Windows as before, but worked out before the
save (`Apply` → `TrayChoices` → `TrayLayout.NewChoices(before, after, appHidden)`, per tray by its layout and
id): every other tray that had chosen nothing for that icon gets the place it shows it in now written down as
its own, so Windows' new word does not move it. Karpo's own write read back is no word from the person
(`WindowsChoices.Told`): one tray's choice is not followed by every tray. A switch in Windows' Settings is the
person's word on the icon, and every tray follows it (`TrayLayout.FollowWindows(config, …)`), one that hides
the icon completely excepted.

**One-time conversion** (`TrayLayout.Spread`, `migrated: "trayWidgets"`; the legacy cleanup may delete it): the
file's top-level `"trayStates"` and `"trayOrder"` (`Config.TrayStatesBefore`, `TrayOrderBefore`, read and never
written) are copied into every tray widget of every layout that has none of its own, a copy each, once. A
file of the oldest words (`trayVisibility`, the modes) still reads through `ConfigWords.TrayStates` into those
keys first. `TrayLayout.Repair` renames each tray's identities as before.

No string added or removed.

Tests: `TrayLayoutTests` (two trays split the same icons each its way; a drop writes its own tray alone;
Windows' switch followed by every tray; a choice in one tray pins the other where it showed it; the states of
before given every tray once, a copy each, a tray's own kept, never again, not written back),
`TrayMenuRowsTests` (a pick writes the tray whose menu it is), `TwiceOverTests` (two trays of their own states
lay out, stop the keys and show to Narrator apart; a drop reads only its own tray),
`SceneTreeTests.TwoTraysDrawTheirOwnIcons` (pictures `twice-own-<look>-<scale>.png`),
`TrayArrivalsTests.KarposOwnWordReadBackIsNoChange`, `ConfigCoverageTests.TheTraysStatesAreWrittenByItsRows`
(the old top-level keys named as read once), `OptionRowsTests` (`TrayIconOptions.States` a row, `.Order` a
drag's), `TypedRegistryTests` (`WidgetOptionsKind.Tray`), and the tray, persistence, reset and merge tests
moved onto the tray widget.

By hand: two layouts on two displays, each with a tray. Drag an icon behind the "^" on one: the other bar keeps
it where it was; open the "^" on each: each lists its own. Edit mode, right-click one tray › Tray icons, Hide
completely an icon: the other tray still shows it. Two trays on one bar: each drags, overflows and lists its
own. Switch an icon in Windows' Settings › Other system tray icons: both trays follow.

The person:

- *"for the top edit bar split it into three groups for the general settings, the taskbar settings and the
  folder settings"*

  configuration again."*

The edit bar reads, one width always:

`[⚙] [🖥 Display ▾]  │  [Layouts ▾] [Taskbar ▾] [+ Add a widget]  │  [Folders ▾] [📁 Folder name ▾] [+ Add to folder]  │  [×]`

- **Nine parts, three groups and the cross** (`EditDeckPlan`: `SettingsPart` 0, `DisplayPart` 1 ·
  `LayoutsPart` 2, `TaskbarPart` 3, `AddPart` 4 · `FoldersPart` 5, `FolderPart` 6, `AddToFolderPart` 7 ·
  `ClosePart` 8; `GroupOf` 0–3), a command bar's separator between two groups as before (three now). The gear
  stays icon-only (its words its tooltip, a drop-down with no chevron as Windows' "More"), so the bar grows by
  Display ▾ and one separator alone: about 1,190 DIP in English. The folder's two show only while a folder
  is open, their room kept; toggling, the red cross and the z-order are §343's.
- **Never wider than the display's room.** At about 1,190 DIP it would run into a dock's two rows along a
  side of a 1280 DIP display, or past a display in a long language. `EditDeckPlan.Widest(room, scale)` is
  what `Place` leaves it between the sides (8 DIP margins, or a side bar and the window's room, §343), and
  `For(scale, widths, widest)` takes the excess off Layouts ▾ and the folder's name alike, down to
  `NameLeastDip` (120 DIP), their names ending in an ellipsis. The display's room alone decides it, so the
  bar is still one width with a folder open or none and whatever the names say.
- **Display ▾** (`EditDeckAction.Display`, `LooksScope.Display`, `BarLooks.DisplayRows`, named "Display",
  `dock.edit.display` back in 30 languages with §343's words): this display's own, as the Displays page had
  them — Position ›; under a rule and the heading "Layout on this display" the layouts and None (where Karpo
  may be hidden here, `DisplayLayoutChoice`) as the menu's own rows, the one shown ticked, a click showing it
  here (`Shown` inline); under a rule New displays show ›. Usable on a display that shows None: that is where
  a layout is picked for it.
- **One place each, nothing twice.** Layouts ▾ (`LooksScope.Layouts`) manages the layouts alone: each layout
  a row with its grip, its bin and its own level (Show on this display, Name, Icon, Duplicate), Add layout.
  Its tick on the shown layout, its None and its New displays show are gone (`OptionOwned.After` empty,
  `BarLooks.NoneRow` removed): they are Display ▾'s. "Show on this display" stays in a layout's level, a
  shortcut to the same choice, greyed on the one shown. Taskbar ▾ (`LooksScope.Taskbar`) is the shown
  layout's taskbar without Position: Type, Size, Show, Material, Opacity, Custom colors, Taskbar separators,
  Behavior. The right click on the bar (`LooksScope.All`) is the three in the edit bar's order: Position,
  Layout on this display › (a choice of its own level there, not inline), New displays show, Layouts ›, then
  the taskbar's. The Layouts row no longer says the shown layout (its own glyph, no value): Layout on this
  display › says it.
- **The cross leaves an open folder open, at rest** (`LeaveEdit(keepFolder: true)`, `EndEdit(…, keepFolder)`,
  `OneFolder.Rests`): edit mode ends as before, and the folder arranged on the bar is not closed but
  `FolderFlyout.Rest()` — `Arrange()` undone where it stands: a line being carried put back, nothing selected
  or on the clipboard, no guide lines or "+" buttons, its window the panel's again (no longer spread over the
  display, so topmost over the bars as any popup), the keys to it, and a press elsewhere or another window
  closing it as at rest. An empty folder closes, as it never opens at rest. Escape is unchanged (it closes the
  folder first, then edit mode), and so is every other end of edit mode (the session locking, displays
  changing, the bar's menu's Done…): they close it.

No config change. Strings: `dock.edit.display` added in 30 languages.

Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests` (nine parts in four groups, three separators, Display a drop-down, each button's
action, which show; `OnANarrowDisplayTheNamesGiveWay`), `SceneTreeTests.EveryBarIsEditedWhereItStands` (a
dock's two rows and a Top and bottom along a side of a 1280 DIP display: the wider bar clear of them), `EditDeckClickTests` (Display asks for its own; usable on a None display),
`BarLooksTests.TheEditBarsDisplayLayoutsAndTaskbarMenusAreTheBarsMenuCutInThree` (the three are the whole in
order, none shared; Display ▾'s rows, its inline layouts and None ticked and picked; Layouts ▾ with no tick and
nothing after; Taskbar ▾ without Position; the whole menu's Layout on this display a choice),
`TheLayoutsLevelManagesEachLayoutAsAFoldersFacesAre`, `NewDisplaysShowOffersNone`,
`TheEditBarsButtonsOpenTheirMenusTheDocksWay`; `OneFolderTests.AFolderKeptAsEditModeEndsRestsWhereItStands`
(a real folder arranged then rested: open, not arranged, no "+", its window no longer the display's, the
panel where it stood, closed by a press elsewhere; the dock's wiring); `SceneTreeTests.TheFoldersButtonsDoTheirThingForTheFolder`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `editbar-display-`, `editbar-layouts-`, `editbar-taskbar-`,
`editbar-widths-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: start edit mode: ⚙, Display | Layouts, Taskbar, Add a widget | Folders, an empty room | red cross.
Display: Position, the layouts with this display's ticked and None, New displays show; pick another layout
there: the bar changes. Layouts: the layouts without ticks, Add layout, nothing under. Taskbar: Type first,
no Position. Open a folder while arranging, click the red cross: edit mode ends, the folder stays open at
rest (no "+" buttons), a click elsewhere closes it. Again with Escape: the folder closes first.

## 349. No migration or legacy code: the file has one shape, today's (2026-10-25)

The person: *"remove all the migration code / legacy code from the codebase. this application is published
newly"*.

There is one shape of config.json, today's. The file is read as it is; a word this build does not know reads
as its default, as before (`Config.Repair`, the tolerant converters); nothing of an earlier build is read,
carried over or written down. Gone:

- **The one-time changes and their marks.** `LineMigrations` (the power commands' one line, the readings'
  details, the drive's contents, the styles' words, the performance readings, the split-off styles, the
  markets, the faces of what is inside, the markets' one symbol, the holiday calendars, the outer empty
  columns, `KeepOuterColumns`) and `Config.Migrated`, the file's "migrated" list, which is no longer read or
  written. A file's empty columns outside its widgets are now read as they are, as every other; only a move
  or a removal drops one (§328).
- **The words of earlier builds read as today's** (`ConfigWords`, deleted whole): the date entry, Phone Link,
  "Folder contents" and "folderClick", spacers as sections, the tray's modes and "trayVisibility", the online
  widgets' own intervals, the desktop switcher, cast and nearby sharing, the flyout entries (keyboard, VPN,
  project, layouts) and the web search widget. Such a word is now a kind this build does not know, dropped
  where the file is read, as any.
- **The keys read once and never written**: the top-level look of before §334 (`material`, `opacity`,
  `colors`, `separators`, `folderSeparators`, `dividers`, `hoverFlyouts`) and its carrying over
  (`SurfaceLooks.Carry`, `LookBefore`, `ColorsBefore`, `ModeColorsBefore`, `DividersBefore`,
  `LineStyle.FromGap`); the one `taskbar`, `combine`, `previews` and `folders` of before §345/§346
  (`SurfaceLooks.Spread`, `SpreadFolders`, `TaskbarLayout.LookRead`/`FoldersRead`: a layout's `Look` and
  `Folders` are plain properties again); the one `trayStates`/`trayOrder` of before §347
  (`TrayLayout.Spread`); a separator's `line`; a line's `atLeast`/`atMost` (`LineHeight.Read`); a folder's
  `width`, `customWidths` and `glyph` (`FolderListWidths.Nearest`); a face's `align` and a stock face's
  `stock`; a line's `stock` and `currency`; a market's `type`, `from`, `to` and `coin` (`MarketOptions.Fold`);
  a drive's `contents`; the holidays' one `on`/`country`/`region` (`HolidayOptions.Carried`); a weather face
  without a place taking its folder's (`WeatherPlaces.Adopt`).
- **The old words of the widgets with styles**: a reading as the performance widget's style (2026-10-17's
  "performance", "gpu"), and a style that is a widget of its own now ("sound" with "output", "input" or
  "mixer", "sound" alone, "clock" with "date", "performance" with "details"; `WidgetStyles.SplitOffOf`,
  `CellItem.ReadInOldWords`, `Reworded`). The presets that still said a reading as a style say it as its
  reading now ("performance", "reading": "network", "style": "graph").
- **The reset of an older shape** (`IsOlder`, `StartOver`, `KeepOlder`, `OlderPath`, `ShapeOf`, the
  config.shape<N>.json files, `ConfigTransfer.OlderRefused` and its three strings in 30 languages). A file
  that says an earlier version, or none, is the person's settings all the same: read as it is and written
  back with this build's. What stays: a file from a newer Karpo is still read and never written
  (`FromNewerKarpo`), and a file that does not read is still kept aside as config.json.broken-<time> with the
  last good version put back — recovery from damage, not an upgrade.
- **Moving the local state of the "pier" folder** (`Config.MoveLocalState`, `OldLocalFolder`) and **putting
  back the taskbar alignment an earlier build set** (`Karpo.Dock\TaskbarAlignment.cs`,
  `WindowsTaskbar.KeptAlignmentPath`, `Kept`, `ParseKept`).
- `TransferSummary.Title`'s names of the dead top-level keys, and an import's check for a plain config.json
  now asks for one of today's keys (`version`, `layouts`, `screens`).

Kept on purpose: the calendar's retired `feedUrl`, `showNextEvent` and `refreshMinutes` and a clock's `view`,
which are still written with their records and are in the person's own file (dropping them would change it);
the tolerant readers that hold a hand edit or a newer build's word to a default; `TrayLayout.Repair`'s
renaming of a packaged app's identity, which an app's update needs, not an older file. The local caches and
data files (weather.json, screentime*.json, the market cache) keep their own readers.

The person's config.json, already converted by the build before this, reads and writes the same under both
builds: loaded and written out by each, the two texts differ by its "migrated" list alone, and neither load
writes the file back.

No config change beyond "migrated" no longer being written. Strings: `core.config.startedAgain`,
`core.config.olderRefused` and `core.config.olderNotKept` gone in 30 languages.

Tests: the migration tests went (`LineMigrationsTests`, `MarketMigrationTests`, `FolderFaceMigrationTests`,
`FlyoutFoldersTests`, `DesktopSwitcherMigrationTests`, and the old-shape parts of `ResetTests`,
`SurfaceLookTests`, `LayoutLookTests`, `LayoutFoldersTests`, `TrayLayoutTests`, `TrayStatesTests` — now
`TrayCatalogueTests` —, `StylesSameDataTests`, `WidgetStylesTests`, `PerformanceStylesTests`,
`OnlineUpdateConfigTests`, `HolidaysTests`, `SearchUrlTests`, `FolderListWidthTests`, `ColumnWidthTests`,
`FolderSeparatorTests`, `WeatherPlacesTests`, `CastNearbyPresetTests`, `PhoneLinkRemovedTests`,
`FolderContentsRemovedTests`, `BarMenuModelTests`, `BarMenuRowTests`, `AlignmentTests`, `LoadSaveTests`,
`ConfigResetTests`, `SectionFilesTests`, `TransferTests`), and `ConfigCoverageTests`'/`OptionRowsTests`' lists
lost their read-once names. New or rewritten for today's shape: `ResetTests.AnEarlierVersionIsReadAsItIsAndNeverReset`,
`LayoutLookTests.EachLayoutReadsItsOwnLook`, `LayoutFoldersTests.EachLayoutReadsItsOwnFolders`,
`FolderTrimTests.AFilesEmptyColumnsAreReadAsTheyAre`, `WidgetItemTests.TheFileReadsAndWritesBackByteForByte`,
`PerformanceStylesTests.TheWordsReadAsTheWidgetWithItsReadingAndStyle`, `ListBoundsTests.AFilesHeightIsReadAsItSays`,
`SeparatorLineTests.TheShapeReadsAsTheFileSaysIt`; the fixtures `PersonsLayouts.json` and `WidgetItemTests`'
file are in today's words (converted once by the build before this).

By hand: nothing changes on screen. Start Karpo on your config.json: the bars, folders, looks and trays as
they were; the file loses its "migrated" list at the next save.

## 350. Every menu's icon buttons together at the top row's end (2026-10-25)

The person: *"the top edit row in the context menu should show all of the icons right aligned. now some of
the icons are shown in the middle somewhere."*

Why they were in the middle: the row had two layouts for its buttons in `Flyout.PrimarySpans`. A button
marked `FlyoutItem.PrimaryEnd` (a widget's Remove, §220) stood against the row's far end while the others
were packed from the start; after a type at the row's start (§323) all were moved to the end but Cut and
Copy kept `PrimaryApartDip` (12 DIP) before Remove. In a configuration menu that left Cut and Copy in the
middle of the row, Remove alone at the end; the bar's menu (Add, Edit, Settings), with no type, had its
buttons at the row's start.

Now one routine places them in every menu: `PrimarySpans(least, edge, rule, width)` packs the buttons
together against the row's far end, `PrimaryEdgeDip` in, with a hairline between each two. Any spare room
is left empty at the row's start, where a type stands when there is one (cut with an ellipsis as before).
A mirrored menu turns the row as it turns everything (Mirror.cs), so the buttons stand at its far left.
A row narrower than its buttons still starts them at the row's start, as before. This applies to the bar's
menu, every widget's and folder line's edit menu, and Explorer's file menu in the pictures. The bar's looks
have no buttons, and a level shown in place has its head instead of the row.

Remove is no longer set apart. It stays last, as Explorer's Delete is, with the same hairline before it as
between the others; the hairline and the Delete glyph mark it, and Remove still asks before taking several
widgets (§253). `FlyoutItem.PrimaryEnd` and `Flyout.PrimaryApartDip` are gone; `WithPrimaryRow` keeps the
buttons in the order they are given.

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `MenuLookTests.TheRowsButtonsStandTogetherAtItsEnd` (pure: flush to the end, gaps alike, one alone,
whole pixels, a row too narrow), `AMenuHasExplorersMeasures` and `AFewButtonsKeepTheirWidthsAtTheRowsEnd`
(the bar's menu, en/ar at 100/150 %: the last flush to the end, the room at the start),
`WidgetMenuTitleTests.TheTypeStandsAtTheStartOfTheTopRow` (type at the start, buttons flush to the end with
gaps alike, in Arabic at the far left), `OptionMenuTests`' folder menu and `RightToLeftPictures.MenuSheets`
(gaps alike). `EveryMenuSheet` now checks every menu it draws: the last icon button the edge and plate in
from the panel's right, the gaps alike.

By hand: right-click the bar (Add, Edit, Settings at the row's right), and a widget and a folder line in
edit mode (the type at the left; Cut, Copy, Remove together at the right).

## 351. Every setting at one level; a link where a lower level needs it (2026-10-25)

The person: *"some settings appear multiple times like account, then i can also change account settings in a
widget for example. i would rather not have that. i think in that case it would be better to link into the
account settings instead of duplicating them, just so that it is easier for the person to understand what
level of settings the person is editing."*

Every setting is at one level — a widget's, a folder's, a layout's (Layouts ▾, Taskbar ▾, Folders ▾), a
display's (Display ▾) or Karpo's as a whole (⚙ Settings) — and that level's menu alone sets it. Where a
lower level's menu needs what a higher one owns, it has a **link row** (`OptionRowKind.Link`, its target an
`OptionLink`; Karpo.Core\OptionLinks.cs): named for what it leads to, its owner's icon, the arrow out (Segoe
Fluent Icons' OpenInNewWindow, `OptionMenu.GlyphLink`) where a value stands, no chevron. Picked, the menu
closes and the owner's menu opens at its level by the edit bar's ways in (`EditEntries.Of`, `Landing`,
`OpenEditMenu`: edit mode first where the bar was at rest, the menu under its button, its level open in
place). A screen reader hears what it opens as the row's help (`FlyoutItem.Opens`, UIA HelpText): "Opens
Accounts in Settings" (string `dock.menu.linkOpens`, in every language).

The audit (each duplicated setting, where it is owned, where else it was):

| Setting | Owned by | Was also in | Now there |
|---|---|---|---|
| The accounts: add (Microsoft, IMAP and CalDAV forms), remove, sign in again, each part's sync and colour | ⚙ › Accounts | every widget showing what they hold (mail, contacts, to-do line, meeting, calendar in every style) and the calendar, meeting, mail and contacts faces (§324, §338) | "Manage accounts ↗" → ⚙ › Accounts |
| The public holidays' calendars and regions | ⚙ › Public holidays (`holidays`) | every calendar line and the calendar face (§237–§324) | "Public holidays ↗" → ⚙ › Public holidays |
| The taskbar separators' look (style, width, colour, room) | Taskbar ▾ › Taskbar separators (`layouts.look.separators`) | every separator's menu (§290, §307) | "Taskbar separators ↗" → Taskbar ▾ › Taskbar separators |
| The folder separators' look | Folders ▾ › Folder separators (`layouts.folders.separators`) | every divider's menu | "Folder separators ↗" → Folders ▾ › Folder separators |
| Which layout a display shows | Display ▾ (`screens`) | Layouts ▾ › a layout › "Show on this display" (§336) | "Show on this display ↗" → Display ▾ |

A separator has no look of its own (Config: one style per kind since 2026-10-09), so its menu has no override
to keep: the link alone, beside Cut, Copy and Remove. Kept where they were, each at one level already: ⚙'s
Online (the sites, the search engine), Formats, Language and Hide the Windows taskbar (no widget sets them);
the display's Position; a layout's taskbar look and behaviour, and its folders' (their open-on-hover is the
folders' own, not the taskbar's flyouts'); a widget's own colours (Appearance ›, §311 — the widget's
override of the layout's, written into the widget); each tray's icon states (§347); which list a to-do or
note line shows, and the lists and notes themselves (the person's content, managed nowhere else). The bar's
right click in edit mode keeps the display's, the layouts' and the taskbar's rows in one menu: the three
menus' rows, an entry to those levels, not a level of its own.

Simplified with it: `OptionDevices.Accounts`, the dock's `ShowsAccounts` and the accounts listed for every
widget menu are gone; `OptionAccountRows.Row` lists every account and every kind (the per-widget filter, the
one-kind "Add an account" and `OptionAccount.Gives` went with it); a widget that needs an account to show
anything ("Set up") opens ⚙ › Accounts, not its own menu. `EditEntry` has Holidays, TaskbarSeparators,
FolderSeparators and Display; `EditMenu` Display and Folders; `EditEntries.ScopeOf` the looks each menu shows.

No config change. Tests: `ConfigCoverageTests.NoSettingIsSetAtTwoLevels` acts every row of every level — ⚙,
Display ▾, Layouts ▾/Taskbar ▾/Folders ▾, every widget and every face — in every way and fails where a setting
of the file (each property of a layout and its looks, of a nested object), or the accounts, is written from
two levels, or where a widget's rows write anything but the widget; what a layout's Add, Duplicate and
Delete do to the displays is declared there as a consequence. `LinkRowsTests` (which menus link where; a link
row as the menu shows it and as the dock goes; pictures `links-mail-dark.png`, `links-calendar-dark.png`,
`links-separator-dark.png`, `links-divider-dark.png`, dark, 150 %), `EditEntriesTests.EachLinkLandsWhereItsSettingIs`;
the holidays', accounts' and separators' tests now act on ⚙'s and the looks' rows.

By hand: in edit mode, a mail line's menu ends its rows with "Manage accounts ↗"; pick it — the menu closes,
⚙ opens with Accounts open. A calendar's "Public holidays ↗" opens ⚙ › Public holidays; a separator's
"Taskbar separators ↗" opens Taskbar ▾ with the separators' level open; a divider's in an open folder Folders ▾.
At rest, a mail widget waiting for an account: its "Set up" opens edit mode and ⚙ › Accounts. Narrator on a
link reads its name, then "Opens … in …".

## 352. The edit bar as a breadcrumb: Display › Layout › Folder › Widget, one Add, Undo and Redo, Done (2026-10-25) — a panel since §520 (2026-11-06)

The person, on the edit bar redrawn as a breadcrumb read in one order (where → add → undo → global → finish):
*"sounds good try that. add the widgets settings from the bar too, labels on hover sound good too"*.

`[🖥 Display 1 ▾] › [▦ Work ▾] › [📁 News ▾] › [🕑 Clock ▾]      [+ Add a widget] │ [↶] [↷] │ [⚙] [Done]`

- **The crumbs** (`EditDeckPlan` parts 0–3, `IsCrumb`; `EditDeckState`, `Dock.DeckState`), each a drop-down
  toggled as §343's, a › between two (`EditDeckPlan.Trail`), a crumb that does not apply not there and no gap
  for it:
  - **Display ▾** — the display by Windows' name for it, or "Display 1" (`MonitorInfo.Name`): §348's menu,
    unchanged (`LooksScope.Display`).
  - **Layout ▾** — the layout shown, by its icon and name; none on a display that shows None. Its menu
    (`LooksScope.Layout`, `BarLooks.LayoutRows`, named "Layout") is the layout's whole in sections under their
    headings: **Taskbar** (Type, Size, Show, Material, Opacity, Custom colors ›, Taskbar separators ›),
    **Folders** (the layout's folders' Material, Opacity, Custom colors ›, Folder separators ›, Open folders),
    **Behavior** (combine, previews, flyouts on hover, rows of the menu's own, no longer a group ›), then
    ruled off **Manage layouts ›** (the Layouts level of §333, its row now titled so). The folders' rows are
    keyed `Folders:` + their key (`BarLooks.FoldersKey`, `FolderRow`) so a pick never finds the taskbar's row
    of the same look above them. It took the place of §343's Layouts ▾, Taskbar ▾ and Folders ▾, deleted
    (`LooksScope.Layouts`/`Taskbar` gone; the right click on an arranged folder's room keeps
    `LooksScope.Folders`; `BarLooks.Appearance` is `Looks` + `Behaviour`). The right click on the bar's room
    stays the union: Display ▾'s rows (its layout a choice of its own level) then Layout ▾'s.
  - **Folder ▾** — while a folder is open arranged on the display: the folder's own menu (§335).
  - **Widget ▾** — while one widget alone is selected (`Dock.SelectedAlone`): with no folder open a widget of
    the display's bars (a folder clicked too), with one open a line of it (`EditScope`), named by its kind with
    its icon (`IslandEdits.Kind`): the configuration menu a click on it opens, from under the crumb
    (`WidgetCrumbMenu`, `CrumbMenu`; a line's over the folder, which holds itself open for it). Several
    selected: no crumb — their shared Cut, Copy and Remove are the right click's. The selection changing
    sets the edit bars again (`ShowSelection` → `ShowDecks`).
- **One width, calmly.** The trail has the room of all four crumbs at their widest (`CrumbMostDip`
  140/160/160/140 DIP, a longer name ending in an ellipsis), "Add a widget" the end of its own room
  (`AddMostDip` 200), so everything after the trail — Add's end, Undo, Redo, the gear, Done — stands where it
  stands whatever is shown: a folder opening or a widget being selected moves nothing under the pointer but
  the trail growing into its empty room. A bar that grew and shrank would move its centre, and with it every
  button, as the selection changes under the pointer, and the window would have to be resized frame by frame
  (no timers); this is about as wide as §348's bar (some 1,140 DIP in English). On a narrow display the four
  crumbs give way alike down to `CrumbLeastDip` (96), as §348's names did.
- **One "Add a widget"** (a standard button, filled and rimmed): with a folder open arranged on its display
  "Add to News" (`dock.add.to`), into the folder, its pick carried (§298, `FolderAdd`); otherwise the bar's add
  list, its pick carried (`DeckAdd`). Greyed on a display showing None (`EditDeckState.CanAdd`). "Add to
  folder" is gone.
- **Undo and Redo** (`EditHistory<Config>`, `Karpo.Dock\EditHistory.cs`): every change made in edit mode is
  committed through `Dock.Apply`, which records the config as it was before (`history.Record(config)`, while
  edit mode is on, saved, changed, and not an undo's own) — a widget moved, added, cut, pasted, removed, a
  setting of any menu, a layout made, shown, renamed, deleted; a bar's height dragged, which a drag writes in
  place, records its old height (`KeepHeight`). Undo gives the step before, Redo the one undone, applied
  through `Apply` again (`StepTo`) as `Config.Restored(earlier)` — the earlier settings saved as the file the
  current config knows would be saved, so `Config.Save`'s merge never keeps the later change as someone
  else's. At most 50 steps; a new change drops the redo; one history an edit mode (cleared as it begins and
  ends), and someone else's change to the file (`ConfigChanged`) clears it. Edit mode and a folder open stay;
  the selection keeps what is still there. Nothing while a widget follows the pointer. The buttons are
  icon-only, their words and keys their tooltip ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)", `MenuChord.Undo`/`Redo`), greyed with
  nothing to step. **Ctrl+Z** undoes, **Ctrl+Y** and
  **Ctrl+Shift+Z** redo (`EditKeys`, held down they step on): on the bar, a locked one too, and in an arranged
  folder (`FolderFlyoutAction.Undo/Redo`), and wherever the keys are through edit mode's keyboard hook
  (`FollowGesture.Key`, `FollowInput.Undo/Redo`) — unless one of the dock's menus is open, which has them.
- **⚙** unchanged. **Done**, the accent button (Windows' accent, its text on the accent: white in light
  mode, dark on dark mode's light accent, as Windows draws them), ends edit mode as the red cross did: a
  folder open stays open, at rest (§348). The red cross, `EditDeck.CloseRed`/`Red`/`OnRed`, are gone.
- **Labels on hover**: a crumb shows its kind under it — "Display", "Layout", "Folder", "Widget"
  (`EditDeck.TipOf`) — in the edit bar's tooltip, which Undo, Redo and the gear keep for their words; it stays
  through a redraw in place under the pointer.
- **Ways in** (`EditEntries`): "Taskbar settings" opens Layout ▾ (its Taskbar section first); the Layouts
  face's "Layout settings" Layout ▾ › Manage layouts; the rest unchanged. §351's links land in the crumbs'
  menus: a separator's "Taskbar separators ↗" Layout ▾ with its Taskbar section's separators' level open, a
  divider's "Folder separators ↗" Layout ▾ with its Folders section's (keyed `Folders:` + the style's key), a
  layout's "Show on this display ↗" (in Manage layouts) Display ▾; "Manage accounts ↗" and "Public holidays ↗"
  ⚙ as before. `EditMenu` is `Display`, `Layout`, `Settings` (`EditEntries.ScopeOf`); `ConfigCoverageTests`'
  levels read Layout ▾ as the layout's and Display ▾ as the display's.

No config change. Strings: `dock.edit.layout`, `dock.edit.undo`, `dock.edit.redo`, `dock.edit.done`,
`dock.edit.manageLayouts` added; `dock.edit.close`, `dock.edit.addToFolder`, `dock.edit.taskbar`,
`dock.edit.folders` gone, in 30 languages.

Tests: `EditDeckPlanTests` (the order, the trail, no gap for a crumb not there, one width whatever is shown,
the crumbs giving way, each part's action, which show per state, the words and labels), `EditDeckClickTests`
(each click; `TheCrumbsFollowWhatIsEdited` — no folder, a widget, a folder, both, a None display, Undo/Redo
greyed; `ItsLabelsShowOnHover`; `DoneIsDrawnInTheAccent`), `EditHistoryTests` (stepping, redo dropped, the
last 50, a move, an add, a remove, a setting, a layout added and deleted undone and redone through the file,
the one choke point, the keys and the hook), `BarLooksTests.TheEditBarsDisplayAndLayoutMenusAreTheBarsMenuCutInTwo`,
`TheEditBarsCrumbsOpenTheirMenusTheDocksWay`, `KarpoMenuGeneralTests.TheTaskbarsBehaviourIsAGroupOfItsMenu`,
`EditEntriesTests`, `SceneTreeTests.TheCrumbsAndButtonsDoTheirThing`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`editbar-states-`, `editbar-label-`, `editbar-display-`, `editbar-layout-`, `editbar-layout-manage-`,
`edit-deck-done-<dark|light|contrast>`.

By hand: start edit mode: "Display 1 ▾ › Default ▾", Add a widget, ↶ ↷ greyed, ⚙, Done. Hover each crumb: its
kind under it. Click a widget: its crumb comes, its menu from it is the click's. Open a folder: its crumb, "Add
to <name>" adds into it; nothing right of the trail moved. Move a widget, change the material, add a layout:
Ctrl+Z undoes each, Ctrl+Y redoes; Done keeps the folder open. Layout ▾: Taskbar, Folders, Behavior, Manage
layouts at the bottom.

## 353. Every button of a line is "Clear all"'s size (2026-10-25)

The person, of a notifications line and a focus line side by side: *"there are multiple buttons in this
image, the ones on the bottom + - and clear and the notification button and focus time button. i would
like all of them to have the size of the clear button. in general."*

**The standard.** The notifications' "Clear all" (Windows' PlatedButtonStyle, §185) is the one button of
every folder line and every face's card: 24 DIP tall, or the small text's line and 3 DIP over and under
it where that is taller (a large text size); 8 DIP of padding either side of its words; corners 4; the
small text, 12; a glyph the small text's size, 4 DIP from its word; 8 DIP between two buttons. A glyph
alone is a square of that height. A toggle is the same button, the accent's while on; a stepper is two
glyph buttons with the value between; a subtle button (the transport, a row's pin) has no plate until the
pointer comes but is the same size; a hyperlink button ("Turn on", "Open news.example.com") likewise.

**One model, one painter.** `LineButton` (Karpo.Dock\Islands\LineButton.cs) holds the sizes for a scale
and text size (`LineButton.Of`), measures a button (`Width`, `At`, `Square`) and paints it through the
quick settings' own WinUI button (`Controls.Button`, given the sizes: `TextSize`, `Padding`, `GlyphSize`,
`GlyphGap`, `PictureSize`), so hot, pressed, disabled, the focus rectangle and high contrast are one
drawing everywhere. `LineSketch.Button` draws one and writes it down as pieces ("<name> plate", saying
its style, and "<name>"). A line that places the quick settings' controls itself (the sound line) dresses
them (`LineButton.Dress`).

**Hit areas.** A button under WinUI's 32 DIP keeps a hit area of 32 round it (`LineButton.Hit`), grown
evenly, so two glyph buttons 8 apart meet and do not overlap; held inside the line where the line is
shorter. Where the buttons stand 2 DIP apart (a card's … × chevron), or the target box is also the hover
plate (the calendar views' arrows), the hit area is the button.

**Every in-line button, before → after** (at 100 %, text 100 %; "std" = 24 tall, 8 padding, 12 text and glyph):

| Line | Button | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notifications | Clear all | 24 tall, 8 padding, 12 text | std (the standard itself) |
| | Do not disturb | 32 square, 16 bell, subtle off / accent on | 24 square, std, WinUI ToggleButton: standard off, accent on |
| | a card's or a heading's …, ×, chevron | text line + 6 (≈26) | 24 square, subtle |
| | See more / See fewer | 24, subtle | std, subtle |
| | an expanded card's buttons | 32 (WinUI field), 14 text, 11 padding | std; the card's text boxes and selections keep 32 |
| Focus band | −, + and the pause toggle | 32 square, 12 glyph | 24 square |
| | Focus / End session | 32 tall, ≥ 72 wide, 11 padding, 14 text | std, as wide as glyph and word; the band 56 → 48 |
| Timer, one row | −, +, stop, start | 32 square, 16 glyph | 24 square, 12 glyph; the line 50 → 48 (12 over and under, as the focus band) |
| Timer, compact / whole | −, +, clear, start | 22–32 (a 0.7–1 scale), 32 of text with its word | std; the scale gone; clear a square in the minus's place (it spanned both) |
| Timer, Clock app card | play / reset circles | 32 (squeezed to 24), 12 apart | 24 circles, 8 apart |
| | − / + icon buttons | 32, 16 glyph | std, subtle |
| Stopwatch, one row | lap, reset, start | 32 square, lap–reset 4 apart | 24 square, 8 apart |
| Stopwatch, Clock app card | start, lap, reset circles | 32, 12 apart | 24, 8 apart |
| Alarm | Snooze, Dismiss | 32 of text, 11 padding, 14 text | std (glyph alone 24 square); its switch unchanged |
| Now playing | previous, play, next | 32 (one row, compact), 40 (whole), touching, glyph 50–62 % | 24 square, subtle, 8 apart, 12 glyph |
| | shuffle, repeat | 40, the accent glyph while on | 24 toggles, the accent's fill while on |
| Volume mixer | an app's mute (its icon) | 32, 20 picture | 24, 20 picture |
| | the microphones' mute, the page's ">" | 36 | 24 (the ">" keeps the switches' chevron size) |
| Meetings, events, agenda | Join | 32 (row − 4 or − 8), 14 text | std |
| Day and week views | Join in a block | 24 of text | std (shrunk to the block where it must be) |
| Day and week views | ‹ › | 32 square, not text-scaled, 4 apart, 4 into the gutter | 24 square, 8 apart, on the gutter |
| Month | ‹ › | 32 of text, 4 apart, the secondary ink | 24 square, 8 apart, subtle |
| Screen time | ‹ › | text line + 8 (≈27), 2 apart | 24 square, 8 apart |
| Clipboard | Clear all | text line + 8 (≈27), 14 text, subtle | std, subtle |
| | Turn on | ≈27, 14 text, accent words | std hyperlink button |
| | pin, delete | text line + 6, 2 apart, 14 glyph | 24 square, 8 apart; "Copied" the same size, 12 text |
| Contacts | Email, Call, Copy | text line + 6, 2 apart, 14 glyph | 24 square, 8 apart, subtle (quieter where its row is not lit) |
| To Do | a task's trash | 28 of text | 24 square |
| Desktops | rename, delete | 28 of text, 2 apart | 24 square, 8 apart |
| Removable devices | Eject | 32 of text, ≥ 64 of text wide, 14 text | std |
| Markets converter | swap | 32 of text, 16 glyph | 24 square, standard |
| Actions footer | its two buttons | 28 of text, 11 padding, 16 glyph, 14 text | std, subtle (`ActionsTile.ButtonHeight`, `Between`, `WordsIn`, `GlyphSize` gone) |
| News | Open site | 32 of text, hyperlink, never lit | std hyperlink button, lit under the pointer |
| Any widget not set up | Set up | 32 of text, accent, 14 text | std, accent |

**Left as they are**, not buttons of this family: the quick settings tiles (TogglesTile), switches and
sliders, a slider line's icon-column button (the volume's mute, the brightness's sun: the line's leading
glyph), a page's back arrow in its head (the page's header, as the quick settings' own), the refresh glyph
in a line's corner (RefreshButton: a 20 DIP subtle glyph with a reach of its own over the row, already the
standard's 12 DIP glyph), the note's toolbar (a toolbar), the date header's and screen time's "today"
(the heading's own words), text boxes, selections and dropdowns, and the quick settings pages and the
flyouts' own buttons.

Deleted with it: `FocusLine`'s ButtonDip, LeastButtonDip, GlyphDip, SideDip, StartDip; `CountdownLine`'s
ButtonDip; `CountdownCard`'s LeastControl, ControlScale, Controls, LeastWidth and its scale search;
`StopwatchCard`'s ButtonDip and GapDip; `TimerCard`'s IconDip, IconGapDip, ButtonsGapDip, ButtonLeastDip;
`ClockAppPaint.RoundDip`, `GlyphDip`, `SubtleGlyphDip` and its subtle look; `MediaIsland.ButtonDip`,
`WholeButtonDip` and its glyph painter; `JoinButton.Context`; the news line's own site control; four
copies of a transform helper (`Shifted`).

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `LineButtonTests` — `TheStandardIsClearAllsButton` (the sizes at 100–200 % and 100–225 % text),
`ItsHitAreaIsWinUIsAndNeighboursDoNotOverlap`, `EveryLinesButtonsAreTheStandardSize` (the focus band, the
timer's and the stopwatch's rows, the month's arrows), `ClockButtonsPictures`
(buttons-clock-<dark|light>-150.png); `NotificationsPresetTests.TheHeadersSwitchIsDoNotDisturb` (the bell
and "Clear all" one size, the bell standard off and accent on); the focus band's, the countdown line's,
the timer card's and the actions line's tests on the new sizes.

By hand: open the notification center (the bell and "Clear all" one size, "Focus", − and + the same
height), the clock beside the calendar (the timer's, the stopwatch's and the month's buttons), now
playing, the volume mixer, a meeting's Join.

## 354. Windows shown after their content: one frame per message, fenced on the commit (2026-10-25)

The person, 2026-10-25: "there are always flickers, e.g. the add buttons flicker, and other stuff flickers as
well. this should not be. make sure to fix this everywhere." Phase 0 of the flicker design (rules R1-R3; the
later phases are fixed geometry, retained views, menu sessions): the fence and the harness.

**What was wrong.** A window's content (composition) reaches DWM when the dock's thread commits, after the
handler returns; `SetWindowPos`, `ShowWindow` and `DestroyWindow` reach it at once. So a window shown in the
handler that drew it came up a frame before its content (a blank first frame: every menu, folder, edit bar,
tip, new bar), and one destroyed in the handler that made its replacement left a frame with neither (a folder
switched for another, a bar replaced by an arrange). The dims went before the bars came out of edit mode's
dress, and a block dropped was drawn nowhere until the bar drew it.

**The fence** (`Present\WindowTable.cs`, `Present\Surfaces.cs`). Every message the dock handles is a frame:
`Dock.WndProc` (and `Signaled`, `Drain`, the first `Arrange`) open one round `Dispatch`
(`Surfaces.Begin(compositor)`; frames nest). What a frame asks of a window — `Show`, `Hide`, `Raise`,
`Level` (an arranged folder's own level, `FlyoutHost.Stand`), `Destroy`, `Focus` — is written in a table as
the state it wants, not done. As the outermost frame ends with anything asked, the compositor is asked for a
commit (`Compositor.RequestCommitAsync`); when it answers (on the dock's queue), the plan is applied:
- the stack in one batch (`BeginDeferWindowPos` … `EndDeferWindowPos`): the raised windows top first, each
  under the one before (the last asked on top, as one raise after another left it), the shown ones where
  they stand; the arranged folder after it, as its `WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING` places it;
- the hides (and what each asked to do once out of sight: a popup's tree let go of, the carry window's
  pictures); the destroys, each window hidden, its content closed, then destroyed — a popup that fades as it
  closes not before its fade is over (`FlyoutHost.Dispose`: a folder's close fade runs out);
- the focus (`SetForegroundWindow`, `SetFocus`) of what was shown for the keys (a menu, a folder);
- what waited for the screen (`Surfaces.AfterPresent`): the snip and the shortcut a folder's line starts,
  after every folder is gone (two `DwmFlush` calls, once, where the handlers flushed themselves).

The latest state wins: a window shown and hidden again before its fence lands is never shown. Each change
carries its frame, and a fence applies its frame's and the earlier ones', never a later frame's. Moves and
sizes (`Surfaces.Place`, `Move`) are done at once — a window that moves while it shows is rule R2's, the
next phase. The frame's questions answer as the frame will leave things: `Surfaces.Visible`, and
`EditStack.Above`/`UnderOthers` (`Surfaces.Above`/`Over`), so the dim's lift and the edit bars' `KeepOver`
see the dim shown and raised in the same frame. The plan runs as the dock's handlers do (busy, `Dock.Presenting`).
A modal loop inside a handler (a file dialog, the colour dialog, a task dialog) sends what the frame asked
first (`Surfaces.Present`). Should a commit never answer, the plan goes after 250 ms (`Surfaces.FenceMs`);
`Dock.Dispose` applies whatever is left (`Surfaces.Flush`). Outside a frame (a test driving a popup itself)
a change is done at once, as before. Native AOT: the smoke pass shows a window in a frame and checks it is
hidden until its commit and shown by it ("fence: RequestCommitAsync, landed by its commit in 16 ms");
`Compositor.GetCommitBatch` is the fallback, unused.

Every show, hide and destroy goes through it: `FlyoutHost` (menus, submenus, folders, the edit bar, the
sections' edit bars, tips, the calendar and every other popup), `DockWindow` (`Show`, `Lay`'s raise, `Reveal`,
`KeepAboveDesktop`, `MakeWay`, `Dispose` — the scene with the window), `EditShade`, `EditCarry`, the selection
rectangle, the tray's carry, the window list (`Preview`). `Arrange` destroys the bars it no longer needs only
once their replacements show, in the same plan. `EndEdit` is one update: the arrange that drops the places'
windows, in its own frame, so the dims and the edit bars go in the same plan as the bars come out of their
dress (it was a rebuild, then the arrange's own a moment later).

**The harness** (`Karpo.Tests\Present`). `FrameFilm` films a transition as the screen shows it: Karpo's
windows captured as DWM holds them (`PrintWindow`, `PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT`), laid in their z-order over a
backdrop nothing draws, before, then f0 — after the transition, before anything is pumped, what DWM shows
between the handler and its commit — a frame every few ms while the queue is pumped, and the end; a strip
and its numbers to `KARPO_PNG_DIR` (`film-<name>.png`, `.txt`). Tier 1: f0 is the before or the end, every
frame once everything landed the end. Tier 2: what is in sight before and after is in sight in every frame.
Tier 4 (`RawWindowCallsTests`): no raw `SetWindowPos`, `ShowWindow`, `DestroyWindow` or `DeferWindowPos`
in Karpo.Dock outside `Surfaces`, but for the listed files and counts — other apps' windows, Explorer's
taskbar, LivePeek's strip, the task dialog, windows that never show — held both ways, so the list shrinks.
Each film runs twice, as Karpo did before (`Surfaces.Unfenced`), where it must see the flicker, and fenced:

| Film | f0 before the fence (old) | fenced |
|---|---|---|
| menu first show | the window up, 18 % of the area empty (black) | f0 = before; drawn at its first frame |
| folder first show | 23 % empty | f0 = before |
| edit bar first show | 62 % empty | f0 = before |
| folder switch | old one gone, new one empty: neither | one of the two in sight in every frame; animated, the old one fades out over the new one |
| a block dropped | carry gone, the bar not drawn yet: nowhere | in the carry window until the bar draws it |
| edit mode on / off | the dim up empty / gone while the bar still edit-dressed | f0 = before; then the end in one plan |
| a bar replaced | the old one gone, the new one empty | the old one until the new one shows |

What it does not fix yet (the later phases): between the commit and the fence (one frame on hardware, some
30 ms here on a software device) the windows already in sight show their new content while the window
operations wait — a bar re-dressed a frame before its dim comes or goes; a window that moves or resizes
while it shows (a menu refreshed to another height, a folder spread for edit mode) is still a frame out
(R2); the "+" buttons and fades restarted by rebuilds (R1). The z-order is still asked as it was, one raise
after another, now applied as one; the design's full stratum plan (`ZPlan`) comes with the edit chrome model.

No config change, no strings. Tests: `WindowTableTests` (the rules with a fake window system),
`FlickerFilmTests` (each film, the fence landing by its commit, the stack in one batch),
`RawWindowCallsTests`. By hand: open folders back to back (no empty frame between); change the bar's edge in
edit mode (no gap); leave edit mode with a folder open (the dim goes as the bars come to rest); drop a widget
(it never vanishes); a snip from a folder's clock (no folder in it).

## 355. A popup's window stands still: placement in composition, the chrome kept (2026-10-25)

Phase 1 of the flicker design (rule R2, and R1 for the popups' chrome), after §354's fence. The person,
2026-10-25: "there are always flickers ... make sure to fix this everywhere."

**What was wrong.** A popup that changed size or place while it showed moved its window at once and its
content at the commit: a menu shown again for a pick with another number of rows, a level opened in place,
a folder spread for edit mode or back to rest, the edit bar at another scale — each a frame of the new window
round the old content (the old rows at the top of a taller window, a folder drawn at its window's corner).
No order of the two can fix that: content first shows the new rows in the old window, window first the old
rows in the new one. And every showing made the chrome again — a new host backdrop, shadow and rim per
`FlyoutHost.Open`, per refresh, per keystroke — and a new backdrop shows nothing until DWM has sampled it:
the edit bar, the rails and the tips on acrylic flashed see-through.

**The spike first** (`Present\FixedFrameTests`), as the design asked:
- a window's region takes the pointer inside it and lets it through outside, over what the window draws
  there too (clicks, hover and drags go by the same hit test) — and DWM shows nothing of the window outside
  it either. So the region cannot be the panel alone, as the design had it: it would cut the shadow off. It
  is where the window stood: the panel and its shadow's room, which took the pointer before as well;
- the full screen tests: Windows takes a window covering a whole display for a full screen app (edit mode's
  dim already turned do not disturb on, `DoNotDisturb.Dimmed`); a hidden desktop cannot show Windows' own
  judgement (`SHQueryUserNotificationState` answers busy there whatever is shown, nothing activates), so the
  frame is kept a px short of the display, which no "covers the display" test passes; Karpo's own
  (`FullscreenApps.Fills`, `Fronts`) never counts its own windows;
- UI Automation reads a fragment root's bounds where it gives them, its window's only where it gives none:
  a menu's and a panel's root now give the panel (`Uia`, `Flyout.BuildUia`, `PanelAccess`).

**The frame** (`FlyoutHost`). A popup's window spans its display less a px on its right and its bottom
(`FlyoutHost.FrameOn`) — one frame for every popup, rest or arranged: an arranged folder reaches under the
bars (§246), a side bar's folder hangs past its inner side (§303), so the work area would not hold them. The
window is placed once, out of sight (`Surfaces.Place`, counted by `FramesPlaced`), again only for a showing
on another display. Where the popup stands is a box in it — what the window was — moved and sized in
composition, clipped as the window clipped it, so nothing slides in from further than before (`Enter`,
§326) and no shadow runs further. The panel, `Content`, `Outside`, `PanelOnScreen`, `ToPanel`, `Contains`
are where they were; `Panel` is in the window's px as before, `Origin` the frame's corner.

**The region** (`Surfaces.Region`, `WindowTable.Region`). The box is the window's region. In sight and in
a frame it grows at once to hold the old box and the new — room added, nothing shown that was not — and
shrinks to the new once the frame's commit has landed, with the rest of the plan; out of sight, or outside a
frame, at once. The latest asked wins, a later frame's waits for its own fence, the same asked again asks
nothing (`WindowTableTests`).

**The chrome, kept** (`FlyoutHost.Chrome`, `Wear`, `PanelChrome`). One tree per window, made with it:
stage, box, root (what fades and slides), under (each panel's shadow and plate), body (the content, clipped
to the one panel's shape), over (the rims), outside. A showing empties the content and dresses the panels
in place — colours, shadow, rim, corners at the scale — and makes a material only where its kind changes
(the backdrop under a tint, a tint alone, the solid base) or a shadow comes or goes. The one panel of a
popup and a folder's pieces are the same `PanelChrome`, placed by one `PlacePanels`; `Restyle` (§334) dresses
in place where it made every piece again. A showing that ends lets its content go once the window is out
of sight; the chrome stays for the next.

So a menu refreshed to another height, a level opened in place, a folder arranged or rested, the edit bar,
the rails and the tips changing size or place: composition only, whole in one commit; and none of them makes
a backdrop again. The films (`FixedFrameFilmTests`, tier 1 animations off, tier 2 the panel's lasting part in
sight in every frame, tier 3 no material and no window placed), f0 — what DWM shows between the handler and
its commit — against the before and the end:

| Film | before §355 | now |
|---|---|---|
| menu shown again taller | 15.2 % off the before, 7.6 % off the end | the before |
| menu shown again shorter | 10.2 % off the before (the old rows cut by the new window) | the before |
| a level opened in place | 15.9 % / 14.3 % | the before |
| folder spread for edit mode | 18.1 % / 19.0 % (drawn at the window's corner) | the before |
| folder back to rest | 10.1 % / 9.1 % (blinked out) | the before |
| edit bar at another scale | 5.9 % / 17.1 % | the before |

The harness: a capture gives what a window leaves clear as black, and a window spanning its display is clear
nearly all over, so `FrameFilm` lays black as nothing over the windows under it, cut to the window's region
(DWM's cut); `WindowShots.Save` takes the region where it is given no part. That is also what the screen
shows of a window up before its content — nothing, a frame late, not a black frame — so §354's first-show
films are filmed fenced alone. The source rule (`RawWindowCallsTests`) counts `SetWindowRgn` too, and holds
who moves or sizes a window (`Surfaces.Place`, `Move`) to a list: a popup's frame, edit mode's dim, the carry
windows under the pointer, and what later phases take — a bar's window, the window list.

Left for later phases: the rows, folder lines and "+" are still made again per showing (R1, phases 2 and 3:
the lit row's fade, the "+" snap); bars still move their windows (phase 4); a popup shown again on another
display while it stands is the one move in sight. No config change, no strings. By hand: pick in a menu whose
height changes (no jump), open a level of ⚙ and go back; toggle edit mode with a folder open and leave it
with the folder kept (no blink, no jump); on Glass or Acrylic open and close a folder in edit mode and hover
the edit bar's buttons (no see-through flash); a full screen video on one display, a menu opened on the other
(notifications still come, do not disturb stays as it was); Narrator on a menu (its outline on the menu, not
the screen).

## 356. A menu's rows kept; a menu is a session by what it is (2026-10-25)

Phase 2 of the flicker design (rule R1 for menus, and its UI session store), after §354's fence and §355's
still windows. The person, 2026-10-25: "when i open / close a folder or some other transition happens i want
that the menus that can be preserved in state should be preserved ... there are always flickers"; and on the
design's open question, "yes go ahead, reopen where i left it".

**What was wrong.** Every showing of a menu made all of it again. A pick in a configuration menu (a toggle, a
choice, a stepper's held tick every 80 ms), a level opened or gone back from, a field's search answering, the add
list's search keystroke: `Flyout.Open` threw away every row and made each one new — its text surfaces drawn
again, its sprites, its lit plate made at nothing with the 83 ms fade, then lit — so the row under the pointer
blinked at every pick, an open submenu shut, and a 12-row configuration menu made 14 elements, some 180
composition objects and 14 text surfaces per Refresh. And a menu was the bar window's it opened from, not a
menu by what it is: a bar made again under it (another edge, type or way of showing, from Taskbar ▾ or ⚙)
closed it; another language closed ⚙ and opened it again at its top; a Browse dialog, a backup or an import
closed the menu and opened it fresh, its level, scroll and focus gone.

**Kept rows** (`Flyout.Retained.cs`). Each thing a menu shows — a row, a rule, a heading, its title, the add
