list's field — is an element kept by a key: the level it is of (its holders' ids), its kind, its id and which of
that id it is. Each has a signature: the row as it draws (`Drawable`: what it holds below — a submenu's rows, a
tool's level, a search's finder — left out), the menu's measures (`MenuSig`: width, scale, theme, columns, text
room…) and where in the row it stands. A showing again reconciles: the same is kept, its container moved to where
the row stands now (its boxes with it, `Row.Shift`); changed is drawn again, alone, and its lit plate goes over
to the new one as it is (`Plate`), lit or not; gone is let go of in the same commit (`Sweep`), but for the rows
of the levels under the one standing, which wait out of sight, unlit, and show again as they were when it is
gone back from. Text and glyph
surfaces are drawn once for what they say and shared (`Drawn`, counted by the elements that show them). What
stands round the rows — the clip, what stands still over and under them, the scroll indicator, the plates'
brushes — is the showing's frame, made once (`Frame`). The host keeps its content through a showing again
(`FlyoutHost.Show(keep:)`): nothing emptied, the window not shown, raised or focused again. The lit row, the
tool under the pointer and its tooltip, and an open submenu (a menu that cascades) stay with their row by its key
through a Refresh (`LitAgain`, `SubmenuAgain`); `Show` (another menu in the same window) starts unlit. A row whose
parts a drag moved off their places (a tray gap, a reorder) is drawn again. Everything goes to the host as the
menu closes (`ReleaseKept`), which lets it go once the window is out of sight.

Measured (`RetainedMenuTests`; a configuration menu of twelve switch rows): a first showing makes 14 elements,
196 objects and 14 surfaces, which is what every Refresh made before; now a Refresh with the same rows makes 0, 0
and 0, and a pick that flips two switches 2, 24 and 0. The lit row filmed with animations on, in high contrast so
its plate is the highlight's own colour: before, frames between the before and the end as the plate faded in
again; now every frame is the before or the end.

**Sessions** (`MenuSessions.cs`, `Dock.MenuSessions.cs`, `Flyout.Memory.cs`). An open menu is a session of a menu
by what it is, its `MenuKey`: the edit bar's ⚙ by its display, a bar's looks (or the half of them a button of the
edit bar has) by its bar and scope, a widget's configuration by its key and whether it stands over a folder.
- Its rows read again from the config as it is now, `Pending.Again`, one per kind (⚙'s bands, the looks, a
  widget's settings); `MenuAgain` shows them where the menu stands, after every change of the config wherever it
  came from (`Apply`: a pick, the file changed, an import) — a menu that shows the same makes nothing. The three
  pick handlers' own refresh blocks are that one call now.
- **A bar made again under it** (`Arrange`) hands it on to the window its display stands on now
  (`MenuSessions.Successor`, `Dock.HandOn`; `Pending.Owner` changes): it stays open, in place, its rows read
  again once the build is done. A menu over a folder, and one that is no configuration menu (a jump list, the
  overflow), still closes with its window.
- **Another language** keeps a configuration menu open: its rows read again in the new words, its levels found by
  their rows' ids where their words no longer match (`MenuKeeps.Again(byId:)`), its type renamed. Any other open
  flyout was made in the old words and closes, as before.
- **Where it was left** (the person's decision): an edit-mode configuration menu that closes — a click elsewhere, a
  pick that closes, Escape, a Browse dialog, a backup, an import or a reset, another menu in its place — is kept
  where it stood by its key (`MenuMemory`: its level path by id and words and each level's scroll, the scroll, the
  lit row, words typed in a field and not kept yet with its caret, the field with the keys, the add list's search;
  never a password's), and opens there again for the rest of the edit session (`OpenWhereLeft`, `Flyout.Recall`).
  Edit mode's start and end forget them all. A menu at rest opens at its top, as Windows' do; an edit bar's entry
  (a link row, "Taskbar settings", a second start, §340) opens where it lands. So Browse a colour and cancel, and the
  menu is as it was; Back up and reset brings ⚙ back on its level however deep it was.

The edit bar's Display ▾, Layout ▾ and ⚙ are such menus: kept rows, handed on, reworded and remembered alike.

Tests: `RetainedMenuTests` (tier 3: a Refresh with the same rows makes nothing, a pick draws its rows alone and
its plate stays lit, a stepper's step its row alone, rows that only moved are moved, an open submenu stays where
it stands, a level in and back makes no material, places no window and makes no row of the menu's own again; tier 1
with animations on: the picked row
stays lit in every frame; tier 4: a menu hands its host nothing per showing), `MenuSessionTests` (the rule: kept in
edit mode only, by key, forgotten as the session ends, an entry lands; the successor; a row again by its id; a
menu shown again opens on its level, scrolled, the keys where they were; words typed and left are back; another
language keeps the level; a rebuild keeps the menu open and in place, nothing made, nothing moved in any frame).
No config change, no strings.

For phase 3: folders keep making their lines and "+" again (`RemakeVisuals`); the tooltip of a menu's buttons and
tools is still a host shown afresh per tip (`Flyout.Primary.cs`, phase 5's retained tips); the rows of quick
settings, the calendar and the pin folder's levels are still made per showing. By hand: pick again and again in a
configuration menu (the lit row steady); hold a stepper (the row steady); switch the language in ⚙ (it stays on
its level); change the bar's edge or type from Layout ▾ (the menu stays open); Browse a colour and cancel (the
menu as it was); open a level of a widget's menu, click away, open the widget's menu again (on that level), and
leave edit mode and open it again (at its top).

## 357. A folder's lines kept, and the folder with them; where it was left (2026-10-26)

Phase 3 of the flicker design (rule R1 for folders, and its session store for them), after §354's fence,
§355's still windows and §356's kept menus. The person, 2026-10-25: "when i open / close a folder or some
other transition happens i want that the menus that can be preserved in state should be preserved ... there
are always flickers, e.g. the add buttons flicker"; on the open question, "yes go ahead, reopen where i left it".

**What was wrong.** A folder's layout whose shape changed — a line added, removed or moved to another list, a
list more, edit mode's "+" coming, a list's warning beside them, a slot more — threw away every visual of the
folder and made each again (`RemakeVisuals`): every line's card and surface, every "+", the guide lines; and
every layout drew every "+" again ("every button drawn afresh"). The "+" were known by their place among the
buttons, so a warning come beside an earlier list moved the pressed look, the keys' ring and the open width menu
onto another button. A look changed made it all again too (`Relook`). And a folder was a new window each time it
opened, let go of as it closed: a switch to another folder made a window and drew it in the switch, and switched
back, everything was made again — the day picked, the month stepped to, a notification expanded, how far a line
was scrolled, all gone.

**Kept elements** (`FolderFlyout.Retained.cs`). Each thing a folder shows is an element kept by a key: a line by
its widget's key (its card with its fill and outline, its content, a separator's mark), a list's view by its
place, a card's clip by its list, its place and whether it is the one under the rim, a column's button by what
it is (`AddKeyOf`: a list's "+", width or warning by its list, a slot's by its side and how far out). Every
layout reconciles (`Reconcile`): what is kept is moved to the view it stands in now, what is new is made, what
is gone is let go of. A button is drawn again only where its look, its glyph or its size changed, the empty
lists' words only where they or the folder's size changed. What stands round them — the guide lines, the ghost,
the landing, the rings and the marching ants, the focus rectangle, the off-screen chip, the lifted lines'
plates — is the folder's for its window's life (`Frame`), coloured in place where the look changes (`Dress`; the
ants and plates, made in a look and at a scale, are made again). The button the keys are on and the one whose
menu is open are followed by key through a layout, so a warning coming moves them along, never onto another. A
settle's buttons glide from where each showed, by key, with one come or gone among them too. Nothing of it is
the host's showing's: the folder hands its host nothing per showing and empties nothing (tier 4), only as it
goes for good (`ReleaseKept`).

**A folder kept** (`Dock.Folders.cs`). The dock keeps one folder's view a key (`folderViews`; the eight opened
last, closed ones dropped past that and for folders no bar shows any more): closed, its window is hidden with
everything it drew; opened again or switched back to, it shows what it has, drawn again where it stands — no
window made in a switch, whose first frame a loaded machine could show late (the switch film flaked so at 185 ms
under the full suite). A closed folder's window still hears its closing fade's end.

**Where it was left** (`FolderMemory.cs`). As a folder closes it reads where it stands (`FolderIsland.Remember`):
each line's scroll and its own view of what it shows (`CellIsland.ViewMemory`: the month and the week stepped to
and the day view's scroll, `MonthTile`, `CalendarViewTile`; the notification groups opened, the notifications
expanded and their choices, `NotificationPartTile`), what the widgets agreed on (the day picked,
`ChannelValues.Snapshot`), the line whose page stood open, the line with the keys. A folder opened in edit mode
opens where it was left in that edit session (`FolderMemories`, the person's rule for menus, §356); edit mode's
start and end forget them. At rest a folder opens at its start, as Windows' flyouts do and as it always has.

**A folder and its menu through an arrange.** An arrange that makes a folder's bar again (another edge, type or
way of showing) used to leave the folder on the window gone and close any menu over it. Now the folder is handed
on to the window its display shows it on (`FoldersFollow`), shown there where its face stands, as it was (its
memory, at rest too) — nothing of it made again; a configuration menu over it is handed on with it (`HandOn`
covers menus over folders) and stands beside its line where that is now (`Flyout.Follow`); where no window shows
the folder any more it closes, its menu with it. A folder that closes takes the menu over it with it, kept where
it stood (§356) for the edit session.

Measured (`RetainedFolderTests`): a layout with nothing changed, arranged or at rest, makes no element, no object
and no surface and draws no button; 26 lines come into a list past its room make 26 lines and the one warning,
every line there was and the next list's buttons the very ones they were; arranging makes the buttons alone
(`FolderRepaintTests`); a folder switched back to makes nothing, and the switch has one of the two in sight in
every frame (tier 1 and 2, animations off and on; `FlickerFilmTests` films the dock's switch with kept views);
opened where it was left it is on its day, stepped and scrolled as it was, opened afresh at its start; a menu
beside a line follows it, on its level, nothing made.

For phase 4: the bars still build their scenes per rebuild (`Scene.Build`); a folder's tooltips are a host shown
afresh per tip (`FolderFlyout.Tips.cs`, phase 5's retained tips); edit mode's buttons are let go of at rest and made
again as it begins. No config change, no strings. By hand: add a widget into a folder and toggle a list's hidden
warning (the "+" steady); switch folders in edit mode and back (scroll, month and day kept); leave edit mode and
open the folder again (at its start); change the bar's edge from Layout ▾ with a folder open (it follows the
bar, as it was).

## 358. A bar's tree kept, and its window standing still (2026-10-26)

Phase 4 of the flicker design (rule R1 for the bars, rule R2 for their windows), after §354's fence, §355's
still popups, §356's kept menus and §357's kept folders. The person, 2026-10-25: "there are always flickers,
e.g. the add buttons flicker, and other stuff flickers as well. this should not be. make sure to fix this
everywhere. i dont just want a fix i want a solution as a whole".

**What was wrong.** Every rebuild — a setting changed, a widget added or moved, a tray icon come, edit mode
on or off, the height dragged — made every bar's whole tree again (`Scene.Build`): every card, button, icon,
label, indicator, tray cell, separator and edit mark new, matched to the last tree's by string keys to glide
(`latest`, `movables`, `Comparable`). So the highlight under the pointer faded in again and the tooltip with
it at every rebuild; edit mode's "+" were no movables at all and snapped to their new places while the blocks
beside them glided, and faded in over 170 ms as edit mode began; a block's edit marks faded in again where
it had been made anew; a slide out of hiding was cut off by a rebuild (`Present(shown, false)`). And a bar's
window was moved and sized to its bar at every layout, at once, its content a commit later: another height,
the edit mode's dress, a place's stretch shared out again showed the old bar in the new window for a frame.

**Kept elements** (`Scene.Retained.cs`). A bar's scene is made once, with its window, and laid out again by
`Scene.Update(layout, content, look, …)` at every rebuild. Each thing it shows is an element kept by a key —
a part's card and rim by the part, an island's cell by its widget and index, an app's button, plate, label,
badge and indicator by its part and its app, a tray icon by its tray and its icon, a separator by its key,
the "+" by its section and its end, a block's edit dress by its part, the panel by its kind — with a signature
of what it is drawn from (`Sig`: a glyph and its size and ink, a surface it shows, whether a card is filled).
An update keeps what draws the same, places it where it stands now — gliding there from where it stood, where
the bar is laid out as before (`Glided`; a card by the part of it that shows, `GlideCard`) — makes again only
what draws otherwise, and lets go of what is gone in the same commit (`Sweep`). Each element owns what is made
for it (`Element.Bag`), closed when it goes. A part's containers are kept by its key too (`partViews`), with
edit mode's wash and hairline in layers of their own under what the part shows (`Layer.Under`, `RimUnder`).
The icons a pin is drawn with are asked for at every update, so they are not swept while they show; a tray
icon's new picture is painted into its own surface in place. A key two parts share is told apart by its
occurrence.

What is the window's is made once and only coloured again (`Dye`): its layers, the highlight, the ghost and
the launch flash, the keyboard's ring, the tooltip, the indicators' and plates' brushes, the host backdrop
brush (a field now, where it was a table of every target's: `Scene.Forget` is gone). So:
- **the highlight and the tooltip stay** through a rebuild: an update finds their item again by what it is
  (`Relight`, `Retip`) and moves them with it, never fading them in again;
- **the "+" are kept and glide with the blocks** (a layer of their own over the zones, `adds`), and come at
  once as edit mode begins — the marks fade in, the "+" stand; their three looks drawn once for a size and an
  accent, worn by every "+";
- **a colour chosen is set in place**: every brush in a colour somebody may choose is a swatch of its part's
  tokens (§311) — the bar's look's (§345) or its widget's own — read again at every update; a card coming or
  going is the only change of colour that makes anything;
- **a slide goes on**: an update leaves the bar shown or hidden as it is, sliding or not (`presented`); it is
  put at once only where it is shown or hidden otherwise, or stands elsewhere in its window;
- a press, the keyboard's ring and a carried block's lift stay with their element; a block dropped glides
  into its slot from where the carry window held it.

Measured (`RetainedBarTests`): laid out again with nothing changed — a new layout and new content of the same,
as the dock does —, a bar and a dock, at rest and arranged, animations on and off: nothing made, nothing drawn,
nothing more held (`Scene.Churn`). A separator added before the apps, arranged: its line and its dress made,
nothing else; every other card, button, tray icon and "+" the very element it was, the "+" and the buttons
after it gliding from where they stood by what the layout moved them. A widget's card colour and the bar's
changed: nothing made, the swatches the new colours.

**The window stands still** (`Layout.FrameFor`, `DockWindow.Frame`, rule R2). A bar's window is its edge's
strip at the most thickness the edge can take — a bar at `Config.MaxHeight` (two rows until §438) and a floating bar's room off
the edge, with the tooltips' room on its inner side, as the height drag's window was —; a place's along
its whole edge. It is placed again only when its display or its edge's room changes (`Surfaces.Place`, once);
the bar is laid out in it, the scene at `Shift` from its corner. So another height, a height dragged, another
type of bar on the same edge (a bar a dock), a place's stretch shared out again is the
scene laid out again in a window that does not move, whole in one commit. Everything a bar does is in the
layout's px: the pointer is taken from the window's as it comes (`FromClient`, `Dock.WindowMessage`), points on
the screen through the layout's corner (`Local`, `OnScreen`), and `WindowRect` and the bar's UI Automation
bounds are the layout's own (the edit bar keeps clear of it, Narrator outlines it). The region is through
Surfaces now, as a popup's (`Surfaces.Region` takes rectangles: a bar's panel or docks and its grip): grown at
once, shrunk once the frame's commit has landed; `SetWindowRgn` is gone from Dock.cs (the raw-calls rule: 3
calls left there, the host window's). Another edge or another way of showing is another window, made, laid out,
shown, and the old one let go of in the same plan (§354); Arrange keeps every window whose edge and row stay.

Films (`RetainedBarTests`, tier 1 animations off: every frame the before or the end; tier 2: one of the bars in
sight in every frame):

| Film | before §358 | now |
|---|---|---|
| another height | the window sized at once, the old bar in it for a frame | the before, then the end |
| a bar a dock | the window sized at once | the before, then the end |
| another edge | (unfenced) a frame with neither | one of the two in every frame |
| a rebuild under the pointer, animations on | highlight and tooltip faded in again | every frame the before, no fade begun (`FadesIn`) |
| edit mode on, animations on | the "+" faded in over 170 ms | each "+" absent or whole in every frame |

What is left (phase 5 and after): the islands still forget their surfaces at every rebuild and paint them again
into the same ones (`IIsland.Forget`, CellIsland's `previous`/`Reuse`), which costs a redraw but never shows;
every `Lay` still raises its bar (`Surfaces.Raise`), the z-order plan's (`ZPlan`) to replace; the edit chrome
(the dims, the edit bars, the rails) is still shown and placed by hand. No config change, no strings. By hand:
add or remove widgets in edit mode (the "+" glide with the blocks, none faded in); hover a widget while a setting
changes (the highlight and tooltip stay); change the bar's height in settings and drag it (no jump); switch the
bar to a dock and back from Layout ▾ (no jump); an auto-hidden bar coming in while a setting changes (it goes on
sliding in); the tray's icons and the clock as they change.

## 359. Edit mode's chrome as one model, and the z-order a plan (2026-10-26)

Phase 5, the last, of the flicker design (rules R1 and R3 for edit mode's own windows, its §5.1 `ZPlan`), after
§354's fence, §355's still popups, §356's kept menus, §357's kept folders and §358's kept bars. The person,
2026-10-25: "there are always flickers ... make sure to fix this everywhere. i dont just want a fix i want a
solution as a whole".

**What was wrong.** Edit mode's chrome was shown piece by piece from wherever something changed: every build
of a bar showed the sections' edit bars again — twice where one stepped aside for another, two places in one
build —, the edit bars again, reopened for a px of room worked out from bars half built, the dims from the
arrange and again after it. Where each stood was asked by hand: the dim raised as it came, the bars lifted over
it (`ShowShades`), each edit bar and rail lifted back over the dim (`EditStack.KeepOver`), an arranged folder
putting itself under the lowest of a list of windows (`EditStack.UnderOthers`, `Floor`, `StandsUnder`), every
`Lay` raising its bar (`Surfaces.Raise`). And §354's limit: between the commit and the fence the windows in
sight show their new content while the window operations wait — so the bar wore its edit dress a frame before
its dim came, the edit bar's folder crumb came a frame before the folder. Measured (film
`chrome-edit-on-fence-alone`): the frame between the commit and the fence 84 % off the end, the bar dressed on
an undimmed desktop. And the bar's tooltip, since §358 drawn in a window whose region is the bar's panel, was
cut off whole: a region is all DWM shows of a window (§355's spike), and the tooltip stands beside the bar.

**Clear windows** (`WindowTable`, `Surfaces.Enlist(…, clear: true)`). A window whose content is clear while it
is out of sight — the dim, the edit bars, the rails, every popup's host (menus, folders, the calendar …), the
tooltips, the carry, the selection rectangle, the tray's carry — comes into sight as its frame ends, before the
commit: nothing of it shows until the commit brings its content, which lands with every other window's in that
one commit. It goes out of sight by its content going clear in the frame's commit (the dim's opacity, a host's
root, `FlyoutHost.HideNow`), the window hidden at the fence after it, where nothing of it shows any more. So the
window operations only ever add room where nothing shows, and what the screen shows changes in one commit: the
dim and the bars' edit dress, the edit bar's folder crumb and the folder, a dropped block leaving the carry and
landing on its bar. A showing asks nothing where the window is already in sight with nothing pending, a hide
nothing where it is out of sight: a model reconciled again asks the fence nothing.

**The z-order a plan** (`Present\ZPlan.cs`). Every window of Karpo's has a stratum, bottom first: the dims, an
arranged folder, the bars, the edit bars, popups (a folder at rest, the calendar, quick settings, a pinned
folder's list, the window list), menus (and submenus), tooltips, what is carried. In a stratum a rank (a place
with only its edge's band under its display's places that hold something), then the latest shown or brought to
the front (`Surfaces.Front`) on top. As a frame ends the plan of the windows in sight is worked out and applied
as one `DeferWindowPos` batch, each window just under the one before it, the first over every topmost window:
a window sinking to a lower stratum goes there then, with the clear windows coming; one rising (a folder back at
rest, over the bars again) keeps its place until its content is there and rises at the fence — never an
arranged folder's spread content over the bars, nor a rest folder under them, for a frame. The plan goes only
where it changed, or where the dock asks for it again (`Surfaces.Restack`: a bar out of hiding, the desktop
shown — over another app's always-on-top window come up since). `EditStack` is gone, and with it every hand
raise: `Lay`'s, `Reveal`'s, the dim's lift loop, `KeepOver`, `Level`. An arranged folder's
`WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING` (§342: activated by a click, given the focus back by a menu) puts it just under the
window the plan has over it (`Surfaces.PlannedAfter`), for any window under the bars — a stratum rule now, not
a list of windows it stands under.

**One model a display** (`EditChrome.cs`). The dock works out what edit mode shows of each display
(`Dock.ChromeModels`): dimmed; its edit bar, saying what the display stands as, or aside for a folder open on
another display; each section's edit bar where it stands, clear of the others, of the bars and of the edit bars
— their panels worked out before anything is shown (`EditRail.PanelFor`, `EditDeck.PanelFor`, both
`FlyoutPlacement.PanelAt`, the host's own placing), so each rail is shown once, where it stands —; none while a
folder is arranged; the selection rectangle on the display a drag over its dim is on (it was the dock's one
window). Each display's chrome is reconciled to it (`EditChrome.Update`) as the frame that changed anything of
it ends (`Surfaces.Begin(…, ending: PresentChrome)`: the dock's frames reconcile once, at their end, from what
the frame left), and at once where what follows needs it (edit mode begun or ended, an arrange done). What is
the same moves nothing; a build's `ShowRails`, `ShowShades`, `ShowDecks`, `DecksFollowFolders`'s re-show and
`openingFolder` are one stir (`StirChrome`). Edit mode begun or ended, a folder opened or closed in edit mode, a
display come or gone: one model, its windows and its content in one commit.

**Tooltips kept** (`TipView.cs`, `BarTip.cs`). The edit bar's, the rails', a menu's icon buttons' and tools', a
folder's line's parts' and its note were a host shown afresh per tip; each is one `TipView` its owner keeps, in
the tooltips' stratum, taking no pointer: moved to the next button it is its panel moved in composition, its
words a surface drawn once per what they say. A bar's tooltip is drawn by its scene into a window of its own
(`BarTip`), as large as the bar's window and placed with it, in the tooltips' stratum, shown as the tooltip comes
(`Scene.TipShown`): the bar's region cuts nothing of it any more (film `bar-tip-cut`: nothing of the tooltip on
the screen; `bar-tip-show`: whole).

**Widgets drawn only as they change** (`IIsland.Rebuilding`, `Rebuilt`). Every rebuild — an app opened, a tray
icon come, a widget's size changed — made every widget forget what it drew and paint every cell again. Now a
widget keeps its surfaces by style through a rebuild; the styles a rebuild asked nothing of are set aside, and
closed as the next one ends; a cell given another length gets a surface of its size. What draws it again is
what changes it: its settings or the config's besides its layouts (`Config.Said`, `SharedSaid`, in the dock's
`SyncIslands`), edit mode on or off (`CellIsland.Arranged`), another look (another style).

**Raw window calls only in Surfaces** (`RawWindowCallsTests`): the few left outside the plan — another app's
window restored or minimized, Explorer's taskbar hidden and shown, Windows' task dialog and the tray's window for
the apps topmost, message windows and the host let go of, the peek's strip under the window it outlines — are
named calls of Surfaces' too (`OtherApp`, `Topmost`, `Gone`, `Beneath`, `Away`); the allow-list is Surfaces alone.

Films (`EditChromeFilmTests`, `TipFilmTests`, `RetainedBarTests`; tier 1 with animations off, now for every frame,
the frames between the commit and the fence too, held open 120 ms as a loaded machine may take them —
`Surfaces.FenceHoldMs`, tests only — and the dim in a colour a capture can tell from nothing, which gives
what is translucent flattened on black):

| Film | before §359 | now |
|---|---|---|
| edit mode on | a frame of the bar dressed, no dim (84 % off the end) | every frame the before or the end |
| edit mode off | (the dim's hide at the fence, content at the commit) | every frame the before or the end |
| edit mode on and off, a folder kept open | the folder's spread over the bars possible for a frame | every frame the before or the end; the folder under the bars, over its dim |
| a folder opened and closed in edit mode | the crumb a frame before the folder | every frame the before or the end |
| a tooltip shown, moved, hidden | a host made per tip | every frame the before or the end; moved: no showing made, words drawn once |
| a bar's tooltip | cut off by the bar's region | whole, in every frame the before or the end |

Tests besides: `TheFenceAloneShowedTheBarDressedBeforeItsDim` (the dim's window shown at the fence, as
before: looked at between the commit and its fence, the bar dressed with no dim), `ZPlanTests` (every stratum rule, the rank, the latest, what a window goes under),
`WindowTableTests` (the plan in one batch, a clear window early, a sinking one early and a rising one late, the
plan only where it changed or asked again, the frame's ending), `IslandChurnTests` (a rebuild that changed
nothing draws nothing), `ThePlanGoesInOneBatchByStrata`, `EditModesWindowsStandByTheirStrata`,
`TheArrangedFolderStandsUnderTheBars`, `TheEditBarStaysOverTheArrangedFolder` on the plan.

The rewrite is done: no window of Karpo's is shown, hidden, raised or destroyed but through the plan, a frame's
windows and content land together, and every surface — bars, popups, menus, folders, the edit chrome, tooltips —
is kept and updated in place. Left, and small: the edit bar draws its buttons afresh when what it says changes (a
crumb, Undo greyed) — one commit, its chrome and material kept, but not element by element; the carry and the
selection rectangle move their windows with the pointer at once (what they show the same); quick settings', the
calendar's and a pinned folder's rows are still made per showing (§356). No config change, no strings. By hand:
enter and leave edit mode on two displays, with a folder open and without (no frame of the dim without the edit
dress or the other way round; the edit bar and rails come in once, no z-order flash); open and close a folder in
edit mode and switch folders (the crumb with the folder); click an arranged folder and close a menu over it (the
edit bar and the bars stay over it); hover a bar's buttons (the tooltip whole, beside the bar) and the edit bar's
(the tip moving from one to the next); open apps with a busy bar (the widgets not redrawn).

## 360. Input reaches the bars: a tooltip's window takes no press (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26, right after installing §356–§359: "karpo does not work anymore. i cannot open or drag
anything around." The build before them (§355 and the full screen fix) worked.

**What was wrong.** §359 drew a bar's tooltip in a window of its own (`BarTip`), as large as the bar's window
(the edge's strip at its most thickness, §358), standing over it in the tooltips' stratum, and counted on
`WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` to let the pointer through. That style lets nothing through a window that is not layered:
Windows' hit test, and `WindowFromPoint` with it, found the tooltip's window over the whole bar. A tooltip is up
whenever the pointer rests on anything of a bar, so the moment the pointer came to a button its tooltip's window
came over the whole bar and took every press; the bar heard the pointer leave, took the tooltip away, the window
went at the fence, the bar heard the pointer again and showed the tooltip again. No press reached a bar for as
long as the pointer was on it. Every test passed: none asked Windows what is under a point.

**The fix** (`BarTip.At`, `Scene.TipPlaced`). The tooltip's window takes the pointer only where it shows
something, as a popup's does (§355): its region is the tooltip and as far as its shadow reaches, and never the
bar's panel — the shadow falling on the panel is cut there. The scene says where the tooltip stands as it comes,
moves (another button, or the button moved by an update or the bar's corner, §358) and goes; the region grows at
once and shrinks once the frame's content is on the screen (`Surfaces.Region`), so it holds the tooltip in every
frame, and the window still comes and goes with the tooltip in one commit (§359). `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` is gone
from it: it promised what it did not do. The pointer on the tooltip itself is the tooltip's, as on Windows' own.
(§359's `Scene.TipShown` is `TipPlaced` now.) And a bar let go of closes its scene before the tooltip window's
content, which holds a part of the scene: the other way round, the scene's tooltip was closed under it and the
quit logged an `ObjectDisposedException` from `Scene.HideTip` (karpo.log, 2026-10-26 08:52).

**Tests** (`InputReachesTheBarsTests`). `InputReachesTheBars`: the real dock — `Karpo.exe --stage` on a desktop
of its own (no mutex, no appbar, no taskbar, a config of its own; `KARPO_INPUT_CONFIG` names a config to copy in,
else a first start's; `KARPO_INPUT_EXE` a published Karpo.exe to run instead of this build), at 150 % on a display left of the main one as the person's second display stands — and a
thread on that desktop asking `WindowFromPoint` over every entry along the bar (stage-map.json) and over a grid of
the display: at rest; the pointer moving over six buttons in turn (posted moves, every 15 ms for 0.6 s each),
their tooltips coming and going; a folder opened by a click and closed by another; the bar's menu opened by a
right click and closed by Escape; edit mode on (a second start's ⚙) and off (Escape). Over every entry, its bar's
window; away from what is open, never a window of Karpo's; a tooltip's window up never meeting a bar's region; no
bar disabled, and at rest no window of the dock's holding the mouse (`GetGUIThreadInfo`).
Before the fix, on the person's own config: 80 points over the bar answered "Karpo tooltip" while the pointer was
on a button. `ATooltipsWindowTakesNoPointer`: one bar in the test's process with its `BarTip`, the tooltip up over
three buttons in turn and gone — every point of the panel the bar's, the tooltip's window under no point away
from the tooltip. Films unchanged (`bar-tip-show`, `-move`, `-hide`: the tooltip whole, every frame the before or
the end).

No config change, no strings. By hand: rest the pointer on a bar's buttons and click (the app or folder opens, the
tooltip shows beside the bar), drag a pinned app and a widget in edit mode, on both displays.
## 361. Layouts managed in Display ▾; every window kept where the plan stands it (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26: *"managing layouts should happen in the screen settings not all the way on the bottom of
the layout settings."* And, on the build before §359: *"in edit mode the folder is darker as well after some
interactions. (it clips behind)"* — an arranged folder gone under the edit-mode dim.

**Display ▾ manages the layouts.** Which layout a display shows and the layouts themselves are one list, in the
menu where that choice is made (`BarLooks.DisplayRows`; `BarLooks.Layouts` with `OptionRow.Inline`, its level's
rows the menu's own — `OptionMenu`'s inline `Things`, as §343 had it):

`Position ›` │ **Layouts**: `⠿ Default ✓ 🗑 ›`, `⠿ Work 🗑 ›`, … `+ Add layout` │ `None`, `New displays show ›`

Each layout a row as a face is (§333, §336): its grip, its bin, the one this display shows ticked, a click, Enter or
Right opening its own level — **Show on this display** (an action again, §336's, greyed on the one shown; §351's
link to Display ▾ is gone, the two being one menu), Name, Icon, Duplicate. Add layout right under them, made and
shown here in one click. Under a rule None (where Karpo may be hidden here, ticked while it is; `BarLooks.NoneRow`,
a choice of one standing in the menu) and New displays show. `BarLooks.Shown`, `ShownRow`, `ShownHeading` and
`ManageHeading` are gone: no row of its own says which layout shows; the ticks and None do. **Layout ▾** is the shown
layout's own alone — Taskbar, Folders, Behavior (`LayoutRows`; its `license` went to the display's). The right
click on the bar keeps the union: Position, Layouts › (saying the one shown, its level the same list), then Layout
▾'s. Ways in: the Layouts face's "Layout settings" opens Display ▾ (`EditEntries`), its layouts on its first level;
`EditEntry.Display` and `OptionLink.Display` are gone. Levels (`ConfigCoverageTests.NoSettingIsSetAtTwoLevels`):
the layouts made, copied, put in order, deleted, named and drawn, which one a display shows and what new displays
show are the display's; a layout's type, size, look and behaviour the layout's — nothing written from two, and the
consequences list is gone (a layout made or deleted moving the displays is the display menu's own doing now).
Strings: `dock.edit.manageLayouts` and `settings.displays.layout.header` gone from the 30 languages; the heading is
`core.barMenu.layouts` ("Layouts").

**The folder under the dim.** On today's dock it does not happen: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests` drives the real dock
(`Karpo.exe --stage` on a hidden desktop, two folders of reading lines) through edit mode on; a folder opened; a
click on a line, between two lines and beside the folder; a line's menu by a right click and Escape; Display ▾,
Layout ▾, Folder ▾ and ⚙ each opened and closed by its button (⚙ by Escape); the other folder opened from the bar;
a line dragged; a material and then the type (a Dock) picked in Layout ▾ by its keys, the menu over the folder;
the file changed from outside (the size); Escape — and after each holds the plan the dock last applied (each
window's stratum: dims under the arranged folder under the bars under the edit bars) and Windows' own z-order of
the dock's windows (`GetWindow`) to it, window for window. To read them a stage run writes the plan as it applies
it (`stage-z.json`, `Stage.Planned`) and what edit mode shows besides the bars — the edit bars' buttons, the
arranged folder's panel and lines (`stage-edit.json`, `Dock.MapEditForStage`, as each frame ends).

It found one window out of its place: a pick in Layout ▾ shows the menu again and gives it the focus, after the
plan's stack, and the focus raised the menu over the edit bar's tooltip — Windows' order no longer the plan's,
and the plan, unchanged, never applied again. §342's guard kept only windows under the bars (an arranged folder)
from Windows' moves. Now **every window of the plan** is (`Surfaces.Keep`, from the dock's window procedure before
anything else, and the submenus'): a move in the z-order Windows is about to make outside the plan's own stack — an
activation, the focus given, anything raising or lowering it — goes just under the window the plan has over it
instead. `FlyoutHost.Stand`, `FolderFlyout.Stand` and `Dock.FolderStands` are gone into it.

No config change. Tests: `BarLooksTests` (the Layouts level ticked with None and New displays show after it;
Display ▾'s rows and picks; Layout ▾ without layouts; a real menu's row opening its level from Display ▾, Show on
this display an action that stays, None a pick), `EditEntriesTests` (Layout settings lands on Display ▾ with its
layouts), `LinkRowsTests` (the looks link nowhere), `ConfigCoverageTests`, `ArrangedFolderStandsTests`,
`FolderSlotTests.TheEditBarStaysOverTheArrangedFolder` (on `Surfaces.Keep`). Pictures: `editbar-display-`,
`editbar-display-layout-` (Work's level opened in Display ▾), `editbar-layout-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: edit mode, Display ▾: Position, then Layouts with the shown one ticked, grips and bins, Add layout, None,
New displays show; click Work: its level, Show on this display switches the bar and the tick moves. Layout ▾: Taskbar,

## 362. App buttons as Windows 11's: the list on a click, dialogs, minimizing, attention, every desktop (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26, on the research report comparing Karpo's app buttons with Windows 11's taskbar
(artifacts\taskbar-behaviour-diff.md): "implement all the points from 1 to 12, 12 i want this option but it
should be configurable." Each point, and what Karpo does now:

1. **A click on a button of several windows shows their list.** `AppClicks.Decide(…, list: true)` answers
   `ShowList` for a plain click on two or more windows; nothing is brought forward. The list is *held*
   (`Dock.HoldPreview`, Dock.AppList.cs): no hover wait, grace or pointer watch closes it; a second click on
   the button does, as does a press anywhere else (`PressHook.Also`, the menus' hook), Esc (a hot key taken
   only while it is held: the bar never has the keys from a click), a card chosen, or another window brought
   forward (Alt+Tab). A list the pointer put up and then clicked becomes held. Ctrl+click (`AppAsk.Cycle`)
   walks the windows as before, and so does every click where Windows' own `LastActiveClick` is 1
   (`AppClicks.Lists`, read with each click). Where no button can show a list — a pin in a folder, which
   closes; Win+N — the walk stays the rule.
2. **Dialogs.** The window in front is walked up its owners to the first with a button
   (`WindowOwners.ButtonOf`, in `Dock.Front`): with Save As or Find in front the app's button shows active and
   a click minimizes the app with its dialog. Bringing a window forward activates its last active popup
   where that is another window, shown and enabled (`WindowOwners.ActivationTarget`, in `Apps.Activate`): a
   modal dialog over a disabled owner gets the keys.
3. **The list's order** is the order the windows were first seen (`Dock.Listed`, `InOpenOrder` over
   `Apps.All`), so cards stand still; the button keeps its windows by recency for its clicks.
4. **One minimize** (`Apps.Minimize`): never a window without WS_MINIMIZEBOX (`WindowMenus.Minimizes`), and
   asked of the app as its own button does (WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_MINIMIZE); the click, Win+N, a window menu's
   Minimize and "Minimize all windows" all go through it.
5. **Never waiting on another app.** Other apps' windows are restored, minimized and maximized by
   `ShowWindowAsync` (`Surfaces.RestoreOther`, `MinimizeOther`, `MaximizeOther`, new named calls beside
   `OtherApp`, which stays for Explorer's taskbar). Where `SetForegroundWindow` is refused, the key tapped to
   get the last input is no longer Alt — which put the window in front into its menu bar's keyboard mode —
   but the unassigned 0xE8, marked as Karpo's (`TaskbarKeys.MaskKey`, `Ours`).
6. **Cards.** A card's click is a button of one window's rule: the window in front minimizes, another comes
   forward (a tab's card never minimizes: its tab need not be the one shown). Windows 7–11 behave so; no
   Microsoft page says it, it is long-known behaviour. A card's right click is its window's own menu
   (`Preview.RightClicked`, `Dock.CardMenu`), as Shift+right click on its button.
7. **Win+T.** The keys on a button with windows show its list, held (`Dock.KeysList`); the arrow away from the
   bar goes into the cards, the arrows along it walk them, the one towards it comes back (`Dock.ListStep`);
   Enter is a card's click, Delete closes its window, the menu key opens its window's menu, Esc puts the list
   away first and leaves the bar the second time.
8. **Files dragged** onto a button of several windows open their list after Windows' hover time; the list is
   a drop target that takes nothing (`DropTarget.Create(…, refuses: true)`), and resting on a card for the
   hover time brings its window forward and puts the list away, so the files can be dropped into it.
9. **Attention.** Measured on a desktop of its own (a throwaway shell window, `SetShellWindow`): each beat of
   a flashing is a shell message, HSHELL_FLASH (0x8006) lit and HSHELL_REDRAW (6) dark, at the caret's blink
   time; a count ends lit; FLASHW_STOP is a redraw and nothing after; a title change is a redraw too. So a
   redraw that changed nothing of the window marks a possible stop, which holds once no flash came for
   1.2 s (`AttentionFlash.Stopped`, `Apps.SettleAttention`). The button blinks Windows' foreground flash
   count (SPI_GETFOREGROUNDFLASHCOUNT) at the caret's blink time, then stays lit until the window is
   activated or its flashing stops; it bounces once, as the attention begins; Windows' "Show flashing on
   taskbar apps" off (TaskbarFlashing = 0) shows none. A timer wakes only for the next blink or a settle
   (`AttentionFlash.NextMs`), never for a button lit for good. Not told apart: a stop right after a title
   change sends nothing, and the button stays lit until the window is activated.
10. **Apps run as administrator.** Windows (UIPI) drops every message Karpo posts to them, without a word,
    and UI Automation is held to the same rule unless a program is signed uiAccess, which Karpo is not.
    Explorer's taskbar reaches them as the shell; Karpo cannot. What it does (`Apps.Above` reads the
    integrity): minimize, maximize and restore without asking (ShowWindowAsync); close through user32's
    `EndTask(hwnd, FALSE, FALSE)` — Windows asks the window (WM_CLOSE) itself, nothing is ended — off the
    dock's thread; where Windows refuses that too, the button says so for five seconds ("… runs as
    administrator, so Karpo can't close it. Close it from its own window."). Not verified against a real
    elevated window: the tests cannot elevate.
11. **Smaller pieces.** Alt+Shift+arrow on a pinned button moves its pin a place along the bar
    (`Dock.MoveButton`, edit mode's `StepIsland`), the keys going with it; an open app nothing pins keeps its
    place. Win+Alt+Enter on a button opens the taskbar's settings (edit mode, Layout ▾'s Taskbar section).
    ITaskbarList::ActivateTab / SetActiveAlt (the band's WM_USER+50, lParam the window) mark that window
    active — a tab's mark goes to its window — until another app's window is activated
    (`AppSignals.ActiveTab`, `ActiveAltEnds`).
12. **Every desktop's windows, a layout's choice.** Layout ▾ › Behavior › "Show windows from": This desktop
    (the default, as before) or All desktops — Windows' "On the taskbar, show all the open windows", in
    words a menu row holds whole (`TaskbarLayout.AllDesktops`, the file's "allDesktops", left out while
    off; copied with the layout). While any layout has it, `Apps` lists the shell-cloaked windows of other
    desktops too (`Win.Elsewhere`), and each bar takes those its own layout shows; a click on one switches to
    its desktop first (`Dock.Bring`, `Desktops.Activate`). `OpenApp`'s dead `anyDesktop` is gone: the window
    says where it is.

Strings: "Show windows from", "This desktop", "All desktops" and the administrator tip, in every language.
Tests: `AppClicksTests` (the list, Ctrl, LastActiveClick), `AppButtonRulesTests` (owners, the popup, the
minimize rule — real windows with and without a minimize button —, the list's order, the blinking and the
settle, the arrows in a list, the active mark), `PreviewCardTests` (a card's right click, the card a drag
rests on), `KarpoMenuGeneralTests` and `LayoutLookTests` (the row, the file, the copy). By hand: click a
button of several windows (the list stays as the pointer leaves; a click elsewhere, Esc or the button again
closes it); Ctrl+click; Save As in front (the button active, a click minimizes the app); a card of the window
in front (minimizes); right-click a card; Win+T and the arrows; drag a file onto a button of several windows
and rest on a card; a flashing app (blinks, then lit; stopped by the app, it clears); an admin terminal's
minimize and Close window; Alt+Shift+arrow on a pin; "All desktops" on, a window on another desktop clicked.

## 363. The rewrite's leftovers: the edit bars' buttons kept, what goes with the pointer moved in the commit, a pinned folder's lists kept (2026-10-26) — the taskbar's part superseded by §492 (2026-11-03)

The person, 2026-10-26: "fix the remaining leftovers too" — what §359 left of the flicker design, each read on
master first.

**The edit bar redrew every button** (§359: "draws its buttons afresh when what it says changes"). It did:
`EditDeck.Open` emptied its host's content and made every shape, glyph and words again for any change — a
crumb's words, Undo greyed, a crumb come — and a section's edit bar (`EditRail`) did the same each time it moved
with its section. One commit and the chrome kept (§355), so nothing blinked on a solid look, but every surface
was new, a press was dropped, and nothing of it was retained. Now both keep their buttons (`KeptButtons.cs`, the
menus' and folders' rule R1 at the size of a command bar): each button, › between two crumbs, separator and the
rail's focus ring is an element kept by a key with what it is drawn from (words, glyph, ink, fill, rim, size,
scale; never where it stands). Shown again while it stands, the host keeps its content (`FlyoutHost.Show(keep:)`,
§356) and the elements are reconciled: the same moved, the changed made again alone, the gone let go of, in one
commit; the button under the pointer keeps its lit fill (the very brush) and its tooltip. Out of sight — the edit
bar aside for a folder on another display, a rail with nothing to say — they stay, and come back as they were.
The rail's "not shown" glyph swaps a brush kept per glyph (it made a brush per message). Measured
(`KeptEditBarTests`): Undo coming makes 1 element, a crumb renamed 1, a folder crumb coming 3 (it, its › and
"Add to"), aside and back 1 ("Add a widget" back), a rail moved or saying something else 0; a crumb renamed,
filmed, every frame the before or the end.

**The carry and the selection rectangle moved their windows at once** (§359: "move their windows with the
pointer at once"). They did, and the tray's carry too: `Surfaces.Place`/`Move` at every pointer move, while what
they belong to — the bar's ghost where the block would land, the selection's marks, the tray's gap — reached the
screen with the commit: the window a frame ahead of its content and of the rest (rule R2 and R3 broken). Filmed
as the dock's handler runs a move (the carry moved and its bar changed in one frame), f0 was neither the before
nor the end: the carry 2.9 % off the before and 20.0 % off the end, the rectangle pulled back up and left 37.9 % /
20.1 %, the tray's icon 5.8 % / 20.0 %. Now the three are one window kind (`PointerWindow.cs`), as a popup's is
(§355): it stands still over every display — the box round them all, a px in from each of its outer sides, so no
display is wholly covered (the full screen rule, §355) and nothing it shows is cut where one display ends —,
placed once and again only when the displays change; what it shows is placed in it in composition and its region
is where it shows (`Surfaces.Region`: grown at once to hold the old place and the new, shrunk to the new once the
frame's commit has landed), all DWM shows of it. A move is now in the same commit as everything else the frame
changed. `EditCarry`, `EditBand` and `TrayCarry` keep only what they draw; their three copies of the window's
making are gone, and `Surfaces.Move` with them (the raw-calls rule: the movers' list is `PointerWindow.cs` once
where it was `Dock.EditCarry.cs` twice, `Dock.EditSelect.cs` and `TrayCarry.cs`; Surfaces' own calls 14).

**Quick settings, the calendar and a pinned folder's lists** (§356, §359: "rows still made per showing"):
- The calendar has been a folder preset since §80 (2026-10-10): its lines are a folder's, kept with it since
  §357, where it was left in an edit session. Nothing left to do.
- Quick settings' pages have been lines of folders since §88 (2026-10-10, `QuickPageTile`): kept with their folder
  (§357). A page is made as its folder opens and stopped as it closes — its sources listen to the system only
  while it shows, which is what they are for, not a rebuild. The one quick-settings popup left is the rename
  desktop dialog (`QuickFlyout`): it now keeps its panel — its layers and the surfaces of what stays — through
  its showings (`QuickPanel.Rest`), another scale or look a panel of its own. Each showing is a dialog for a
  desktop, its name selected, as Windows' own; nothing of one showing is shown in the next.
- **A pinned folder's lists** (`PinFolderFlyout`) made a panel per showing and dropped their rows: opened again,
  a list showed "Reading…" in a short panel until the read came back, then grew to its rows (filmed with a read
  taking 150 ms, as a folder on a disk does: two frames 10.5 % off the before and 69.8 % off the end). Now a list
  keeps its panel and its rows, by their items' names, while it shows the same folder, and the flyout keeps what
  each folder was last read to hold (`ReadsKept`, 16): a list opened again shows its rows at once, the very rows,
  and the read it asks for draws only the rows that changed (`QuickPanel.Set(repaint: false)`; a row's own look
  compared, `Widget.Invalidate`); the listing, which comes before its icons, keeps the icons it has meanwhile.
  These are popups at rest, which open at their top with nothing lit (the person's rule, §356); edit mode's
  configuration menus reopen where they were left (§356) and folders likewise (§357), as before.

`FlickerFilmTests.ThePlanGoesInOneBatchByStrata` failed once more in the full suite and again in a loop with the
suite's start running beside it: never the plan, always "not settled" — its fence had not landed when the film's
harness stopped waiting, 2 s after asking, the test's thread starved by every core rendering in software for the
tests starting with it (the test took 14 s). The fence lands within a frame or its 250 ms limit; the harness now
waits on the thing itself up to the suite's ceiling (`FrameFilm.Settle`, `Patience.Ceiling`), as every other wait
of the tests does, and says how the fences went where it gives up. No race in the plan was found.

No new timer (the test's slow read is a `Task.Delay` of the test's own). Deleted: `Surfaces.Move`; the edit bar's
and the rail's own `Sprite`/`Shape` and their per-showing `host.Keep`; the three pointer windows' own window and
target; `QuickPanel.Detach` (now `Rest` between showings and `Release` for good).

No config change, no strings. Tests: `KeptEditBarTests`, `PointerWindowTests` (the frame over the displays; the
carry, the rectangle and the tray's carry filmed with their bar, every frame the before or the end, the window
placed once; and the way it was — a window moved at once — seen as a frame of neither),
`PinFolderFlyoutTests.AListOpenedAgainShowsItsRowsAtOnce`,
`QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests.TheRenameDialogKeepsItsPanelThroughItsShowings`, `RawWindowCallsTests`. Each film fails
on the code before this section. By hand: in edit mode, hover Done and undo a change (Done stays lit, Undo greys
alone); open a folder (its crumb comes, nothing else moves or flashes); drag a widget slowly along a bar and
across to a bar on the other display (the block and the blue landing together, never the block ahead; whole

No config change. Strings: `dock.edit.ofLayout`, `dock.edit.thisDisplay`, `settings.layouts.size.top`, `.size.bottom`,

## 365. What is set in a level leaves the person on its level (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26: *"when entering a new name for the layout and clicking enter i am not brought back to the
previous level but i am brought back to the root level of the configuration. this should not be. fix this
generally if this occurs in other places too. also fix this for other field types as well."*

**What was wrong.** A configuration menu shown again after a change (`Dock.MenuAgain` → `Flyout.Refresh`, after
every change of the config wherever it came from) finds its open levels again by the rows they opened from
(`MenuKeeps.Again`): the row of the same id and words, else the one row of the same words. Only another language
(§356) also looked for the row of the same id. But a row's words may be what was just set in its own level: Display
▾ › Work › Name, "Office", Enter — the Name level shut (one back, §246), the field's commit came after it, the
config changed, Work's row now said "Office", no row said "Work", and every level was let go of: the menu's own
rows. Not the field: any change made under a row whose words it changes. The real dock did it (on the code before
this section `ALayoutNamedOnTheRealDockIsBackOnItsLevel` fails: "Enter left the layout's level"), and so did every
kind of field under such a row: a line of text by Enter, by its level's head or by Up, a number typed or stepped, a
switch, a segment, an action that stays, a choice, a colour, an icon, a time, a search's pick, a thing named in its
own level; a thing renamed by its pencil kept its level but lost its lit row, the keys nowhere
(`EveryKindOfFieldLeavesThePersonOnItsLevel`, every case wrong before). In Karpo's menus such rows are a layout's
(Display ▾ and the bar's right click: its Name), a clock face's (Folder ▾ and a folder's menus: its label, which its
row says, `Dock.TitleOf`) and a thing renamed by its pencil (a line's notes and lists).

**One rule** (`MenuKeeps.Again`): the row of the same id and words; else the one row of the same words (a row
moved, its command moved as rows before it came or went); else the one row of the same id — its words changed under
it: renamed, another language. A row's command is numbered before the rows of its level (`OptionMenu`: "the row
first"), so nothing done in a level moves the row it opened from. It finds the levels of a Refresh and of a menu
opened where it was left (§356) — one walk for both now, `Flyout.LevelsAgain`, each by `Flyout.HolderIn` (a row, or
a tool whose level it was: a note's rename, §317) — and the lit row after them. So a field whose editing is a level
of its own (a line of text, a number typed, a rename) goes back one by Enter or its head, as §246 has it; anything
else stays where it is (§219: a choice's level for the next pick). A level whose row is gone, or opens nothing any
more, still falls back to the deepest found. No timer.

Deleted: `Again`'s `byId`, `Refresh`'s and `MenuAgain`'s, the flyout's `againById` and the dock's `reword` (another
language is the rule's third case); `ToolHolderIn` and `Recall`'s own walk of the levels (`LevelsAgain`);
`LooksKept`'s own copy of what a kept field sets (`FieldPicks.KeepRow`, which keeps a number typed as it keeps a
line of text, whichever menu it is of).

No config change, no strings. Tests: `LevelAfterCommitTests` (the layout named in Display ▾ on its real rows, back on
its level under its new name, Name lit; the same on the real dock, `Karpo.exe --stage` on a desktop of its own; every
kind of field committed two levels deep under rows renamed by every change), `MenuKeepsTests`, `MenuSessionTests`
(another language and a renamed row keep the level; a row gone does not). By hand: edit mode, Display ▾, a layout,
Name, type, Enter (back on the layout's level, under its new name, Name lit); its Icon, pick one (the picker stays);
a folder with a clock face: Folder ▾, the face, Label, type, Enter (back on the face's level, the face renamed); a
to-do line's lists, the pencil, Enter (the list's row lit, renamed); switch the language in ⚙ (it stays on its level).

## 367. No tooltip over a widget or a folder on the bar (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26: *"remove the tooltips when hovering over a folder face or widget face"*.

**What goes.** The pointer resting on a widget or a folder on the bar shows no tooltip, at rest and in edit mode
(edit mode showed none already): not a face's words, not a folder's name over them (§123), not the title of the
widget's kind, not why a widget is greyed (§247), not the age of mail that could not be refreshed (the stale mark's
words over the envelope, §95, docsccounts.md). That was every widget kind with `BarEntry.Tooltip` true — the
switches, Security, the status icons — and the folders, named by the one exception, `NamesFor`. What a face says is on
the face; a click opens the rest.

**What stays.** The tooltips Windows' taskbar has: an app's button (its window's title, else its name; none for a pin
this PC can't open, nor for a pin to a folder), Start, search, task view, show desktop, Windows' other buttons (the
widgets board, the Snipping Tool, Settings, the pen menu, the touch keyboard, the virtual touchpad; none for a Snipping
Tool not installed), and a tray icon's, the app's own. The edit bar's and the rails' buttons, and the parts inside an
open folder (`FolderFlyout.Tips.cs`, the stale mark on a line, a greyed line's why), keep theirs. A screen reader hears
what it heard (`Dock.DescribeCell`, from each widget's `Tooltip`), and now also why a widget this PC hasn't got is
greyed (`CellIsland.UnavailableOn`), which only the bar's tooltip used to say — the brightness and battery among them.

**One rule** (`BarTooltips.For`, which `Dock.TooltipFor` asks): an app's button, Windows' parts, a tray icon; nothing
else. `IslandTooltips` is `BarTooltips` now (`Karpo.Dock\BarTooltips.cs`), as no island is in it.

Deleted: the bar's island case in `Dock.TooltipFor`, and the hover's check for a widget whose flyout a rest opened
(it shows none anyway); `BarEntry.Tooltip` and its 35 answers, `IslandTooltips.ShowsFor` and `NamesFor`;
`FolderIsland.BarTip` and `FolderIsland.StaleTip` (the mail face's words already carry the age for a screen reader);
`FolderBarTipTests`, `IslandTooltipsTests`' table of kinds, and the presets' asserts on them. `CellIsland.StaleTip`
stays: a line's stale mark says it. The room the window keeps for a tooltip stays six lines (`Layout.TooltipLines`): a
tray icon's tip, the app's own, may run as long. The smoke run's tooltips were on Start, app buttons and the tray
already.

No config change, no strings. Tests: `BarTooltipsTests` (no tooltip over a widget's or a folder's cell, nor anybody
asked; an app's button, the tray, Start, search, task view, show desktop and Windows' buttons keep theirs),
`TooltipRoomTests`, the preset tests. By hand: rest the pointer on a widget, a folder, the clock, the mail and a greyed
brightness slider (no tooltip); on an app's button, Start, a tray icon (theirs, as before); open a folder and rest on a
line's part (its tooltip, as before); Narrator on a widget (it reads as before).

## 368. Sunrise and sunset (2026-10-26)

The person: *"add a sunset and sunrise widget. similar as the one in themia"*. Themia's Sun (the person's other
app: `Themia.Widget.Sun`, its root SPEC's Sun and moon sections [S-160]..[S-169], [S-1490]..[S-1492], [S-170],
[S-3100]..[S-3107], [S-6045], [S-6046], [S-649]) brought over the Karpo way: a widget of three styles, a face and a
preset, the weather's place, nothing fetched.

**The astronomy** (`Karpo.Dock\Weather\Sun.cs`), ported from Themia's `SolarPosition`, `SkyPath`,
`SunPathGeometry` and `SunDayBar` with their shape kept: the day is the *solar* day at the place's longitude
(Themia's [S-06], so Sydney's morning is not handed yesterday's times), an absent event is a polar day or night and
never a made-up time, the next event is the earliest still ahead of the solar days before, of and after now
([S-07]), civil twilight is the centre 6° under the horizon, noon carries the sun's height, the daylight its change
since yesterday, and nothing reads the clock. **What differs:** Themia's sunrise equation reads the declination and
the equation of time once, at transit — up to a minute and a half off in the middle latitudes and minutes near the
polar circles, measured against NOAA's formulas. Here they are NOAA's (Meeus's low-precision series, nutation and
obliquity in), read again at each event's own instant until it settles: within seconds of the US Naval
Observatory's tables. The sun's place now (`SolarPosition.Now`) is its declination and hour angle from the same
series, where Themia went through the subsolar point. Times are instants, written in this PC's zone on the
region's clock (`Nls.Time`, the person's format), as Themia writes them: without a zone database the place's own
clock is not known.

**The widget** (`WidgetStyles.Sun`, "sun"): Themia's styles ([S-6045]) are its styles, each a form of its own as
the weather's and the calendar's are (§209): **Arc** (`sunArc`, the first, so "sun" alone is the arc), **Day bar**
(`sunDayBar`) and **Times** (`sunTimes`), drawn by one line (`SunTile`). The arc is the sun's real path, altitude
against how far it is through its passage, flat in winter and tall in summer, between 13 % and 87 % across, its
axis the highest the sun gets at the place all year; what the sun has travelled today in the accent with the
graphs' fading fill under it, the rest in the quiet ink, the night under the horizon dashed and squeezed into a
sixth of the room, the horizon a divider from gutter to gutter, the sun's dot dimmed while it is down. The day
bar is the local day midnight to midnight (always the clock's 24 hours since §657), its daylight in the accent's lighter
step between the sunrise and sunset ticks, the dot at now ringed in the ground; it keeps its least and no share of
the line ([S-6046]). The place's name stands quiet in the picture's top corner where it is tall enough.

**The ladder** ([S-170], [S-1492], [S-3102]; `SunTile.Plan`), one row to eight, four unmeasured: one row is the
next event's glyph (Segoe Fluent Icons' sun on the horizon, U+ED39 rising, U+ED3A setting), "Sunset in 1 h 39 min"
or "Sunset" where that does not fit, the picture small beside its time — **the picture is never dropped**, it keeps
its room and the words give up theirs. From two rows the picture over the strip: the sunrise, the daylight and the
sunset, each centred under what it names (the curve's ends, the bar's ticks), each time's glyph where a side column
(26 %) holds it, how soon under the next one where no row says it, the daylight only where it stands clear of the
times ([S-649]). Then the rows, as many as fit while the arc keeps 45 % of the line: sunrise, sunset, daylight
(its change, "+2 min 14 s", "−58 s", "Same as yesterday"), solar noon (the sun's height), civil dawn, dusk; one row
is the next event alone. The next event's row says how soon and is the one emphasised, and shows the next one's
time (tomorrow's sunrise once today's has passed). Inside the polar circles the daylight leads, saying "Polar day"
or "Polar night", the dashes of the sunrise and sunset last. The times style is the rows alone from 4 DIP under the
line's top, the place's name over them where all six stand. **Events** (`WeatherOptions.SunEvents`, Themia's
Events switch): the arc's and the bar's rows, on unless set off, written only off, kept through a change of style
and on no other kind's record; the times style offers none.

**The face** (`FolderFaces.Sun`, `SunFaceDrawing`): the glyph and "18:32" (default), "Sunset 18:32" or "Sunset in
3 h 10 min" (`SunFace.Show`); the sun or the moon and "Polar day"/"Polar night" inside the circles; measured from
templates (the region's widest time, both words, eighteen hours fifty-eight, the polar words) and as wide as what it
says (§244); no place, the pin and "Set location"; this PC's position not known yet, the pin and a dash; down a bar
on its side the glyph over the time. **The preset** (`Presets.SunId`, "Sunrise and sunset"): the face over the arc,
after the earthquakes in the add list's Weather page; the first place chosen is given to both (`WeatherPlaces.Spread`).

**The place** is the weather's (`WeatherOptions`, its device switch and search rows, `PlaceNames`): no second
location system. A face of a place is now one question, `FolderFaces.HasPlace` (the weather, air, tides, quakes
and sun faces), which `FolderFace.Of`, `FaceRows` and `Spread` ask instead of four lists. **Coordinates typed** into
any place search are the place (`PlaceQuery.Coordinates`: "47.37, 8.54", "47.37 8.54", "-33.87; 151.21", a degree
sign after either), asked of nobody; a latitude outside −90..90 or a longitude outside −180..180 finds nothing and
says so ("Latitude runs from −90 to 90, longitude from −180 to 180"); a place so kept has no words and is called by
its coordinates (`PlaceNames.Of`, "Current location" before). This PC's location (`SunPlaces`): the position the
weather last had from Windows (`WeatherStore.DeviceAt`), else asked once through `WeatherStore.Where` (which names
it, §253) and not again for a quarter of an hour where Windows gave none; the lines and folders waiting are woken
when it comes (`StoreSignal`); while nothing is known the line says "Finding this device's location…", and where
Windows gives none and no place is kept beside the switch, its "Set up" at the place.

**No timer.** Nothing is fetched and nothing ticks for the sun: the line redraws on the dock's minute
(`MinuteChanged`), the face is read on the dock's clock tick as every face's (its `Reading` changes with the
countdown's minute or the event passing), and this PC's position wakes them once when it comes.

The file gains three line words in one widget ("kind": "sun", "style": "dayBar"/"times"), a face with one option,
and `sunEvents` where it is off; nothing changes shape, nothing is migrated. Words in all 30 languages. The stage's
catalogue (`scripts\stage\catalog.json`) has a sun line under the weather's days, Zürich, three rows.

Tests: `SunTests` (sunrise, sunset, civil dawn and dusk and noon within a minute of the Naval Observatory's tables
for Zürich at midsummer and on the day its clocks go forward, New York on America's, Quito at the equinox,
Reykjavik at midwinter, Cape Town in January, any moment of a solar day the same day; Sydney's next sunrise on the
day its clocks change; the next event always ahead; Tromsø's polar day and night, its winter twilight, the poles;
the change and the words; the arc's ends and noon; the day bar on a 23-hour day; coordinates typed, refused off the
Earth, kept and named; the Events switch and the styles; the face's option, sun lines and the switch written and
read back, a newer word, another kind writing no switch; the preset and its place; the add list), `SunPictures`
(sun-faces-dark/light.png: the three forms at 100 and 150 %, sunrise next, polar day and night, no place, this PC
not found, on its side, each inside its cell; sun-arc/dayBar/times(-light|-100).png, sun-arc-no-events.png,
sun-arc-polar-day.png, sun-dayBar-polar-night.png at one to eight rows; the ladder: one row, the picture's least and
its 45 %, rows by height inside the line, none with Events off). By hand: add "Sunrise and sunset" from the add
list's Weather page; with this PC's location on, the face and the line find it; pick a place, and type "69.65,
18.96" (Tromsø) into the search; switch the three styles and Events in edit mode; watch the dot and the countdown
move with the minute and the face turn from sunset to sunrise as the sun sets; the catalogue picture
(`Stage.cs catalog`) still fits its column.

## 369. Sports: follow a league, browse its teams, logos everywhere, the table (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26: *"improve the sports score widget. think about how you would like to use it as customer.
from a UX UI perspective (maybe be able to follow turnaments, browse teams, add logos for teams in the search etc.
you have creative freedom on this)"*.

**The friction, used as a fan would** (§239's widget, drawn and tried on ESPN's answers of 2026-10-26):
- Only a team could be followed. A World Cup, the Champions League or "the Bundesliga today" could not, though
  that is how half of football is watched.
- The search was the only way in: typed words, ESPN's answer, no pictures. Nobody remembers that the club is
  "1. FC Union Berlin"; a fan thinks "the Bundesliga" and looks for the badge.
- No table anywhere: "1st in Spanish LALIGA · 9-0-0" in small type was all of it.
- The face showed the folder's first sports line only: a second team followed in the same folder never reached the bar,
  even while it played.
- A click on the line opened the shown match whatever was clicked: the rows of the coming matches and results opened
  the wrong page.
- A logo not come yet was a grey disc with a letter, every side alike; the logos were fetched again after every
  restart (memory only).

**What changed.**
- *A league or a tournament may be followed* (`SportsOptions` with no `team`, `IsTeam` false, key `sport/league`).
  The line shows the league's round: a head with the league's name and the round's first day ("Today", "Tomorrow",
  "Fri, 30/10"), a dot and red while a game is on; a row per game — the home side's logo, "Bayern 2–1 Dortmund" (the
  abbreviations where the names don't fit), and the clock, "Final" or the kick-off ("Sat 15:30" where it is not the
  head's day); then the table from the top. One row: the shown game, "Elversberg – Mainz Fri 20:30", with the league's
  logo, the dot while one is on. Which game is shown is §239's rule (`SportsPick.Of` with no team): one on now, a
  result for six hours, the next. The round is the days from the shown game's (`SportsPick.Day`): three for football
  of either kind, whose rounds are a weekend (`SportsLeagues.RoundDays`), one for the leagues that play daily.
  Tall enough (eight rows of room under the head), the table keeps three rows and the round four at the least.
- *The table* (`SportsAnswer.Table`, `SportsGroup`, `SportsPlace`): ESPN's standings, read from its older path
  (`apis/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/standings`; the site path answers with a link alone). Football by its rank with
  its points; the others by their seed with their record, the place their row's (ESPN gives two the 8th seed). A
  cup's groups ("Group A") and the conferences each a table, named where there are several. A league shows its first
  group from the top; a followed team its group around it (seven rows at the most, its results under them), its row
  strong, under two coming matches at the most — where a table shows, the "1st in …" line goes.
- *Browse in the menu's search* (`OptionFields.FollowFinder`): the field is "Team or league". With nothing typed, every
  league of the table, each with its logo and its sport ("Football", "Ice hockey"), the one followed ticked; a pick
  follows the league. Typed, the leagues it names (`SportsSearch.Leagues`: their name, ESPN's longer name — "German
  Bundesliga", "World Cup" — or slug, case and accents ignored; the name beginning with it first, then holding it as a
  word), then every team of the first (ESPN's `/{sport}/{league}/teams`, by name), then what ESPN's search finds, each
  once: "bundesliga" is the Bundesliga, the Austrian Bundesliga and the Bundesliga's eighteen clubs.
- *Logos in the search's rows*: `OptionFound.Picture`, drawn where the row's icon stands once it has come
  (`Flyout.Pictures`, which the dock points at the sports logos); the glyph until then, the menu shown again as each
  comes, as a search's answer is. Asked for the menu's ground (the dark drawing on a dark menu).
- *Logos kept on disk* (`SportsLogos`, shared by the lines, the face's folder and the menus): ESPN's picture server
  alone, 64 px through its resizer, in memory (256) and as the file ESPN gave in `sports-logos\` in the local folder,
  named by a hash; fetched again after a month, the old one kept while offline; one that could not be had left alone
  five minutes. Every league of the table has its logo (`SportsLeague.Logo`, as each league's scoreboard gave it).
- *A monogram until a logo comes*: the side's first letters, white on a disc of a deep colour of its own (one of
  twelve, by its id), so two sides never look alike while the pictures come (`SportsText.Monogram`, `Tint`).
- *The face shows the most pressing of its folder's sports lines* (`FolderIsland.SportsAll`, `SportsPick.Lead`): a game
  on now, then a result just in, then the soonest next game, then the last played; the first line among equals. The
  folder reads each through a user of its own with the store (`SportsStore.Use(user, team, wakes: folder)`), so each is
  still one fetch for the face and its line. Its width is the widest of what its lines can say; a league's game reads
  "ELV – M05 Fri 20:30".
- *A click opens what is under it* (`SportsTile.CardTarget`, rows lit under the pointer as a quake's are): a game or a
  match row its match on ESPN, the scoreboard or the one row the shown match, a table's row the team's page. Open
  website opens the shown match, else the team's page or the league's (`SportsTile.PageOf`).
- The line is one to twelve rows (was six): a round and its table want the room.

**How often.** As §239: the store's pace is the shown match's (half a minute while one is on, a minute as one begins,
else the online interval, never past a kick-off). A league fetch is its scoreboard of the day ESPN shows; where that
holds nothing still to play, the next round's days from its calendar (`SportsAnswers.NextDay`, only where ESPN lists
the days *with* games: baseball's calendar lists the days without), at most three asks; and its table. While a game
is on only the scoreboard is read, the table again every half hour. A team's full fetch reads its league's table too;
a table that cannot be had keeps the last. ESPN takes one day a request (a range answers 400). The lines still tick
every half minute and only ask whether a fetch is due: one timer for the bar, no new one.

**The config.** `sports` on a line: `{ "sport", "league", "team", "name", "abbreviation" }` as before. A league
followed is `team: ""`, `name` the league's, no abbreviation. A team's entry is unchanged: nothing to convert.

Words in all 30 languages: `core.sports.soccer|football|basketball|baseball|hockey`, `dock.sports.table`; changed
`settings.widget.sports.team.header|placeholder|notFound`, `dock.sports.noTeamText`, `core.widget.sports.blurb`, the
keywords (league, table, standings, tournament, world cup, champions league). "Today", "Tomorrow" and "Yesterday" are
the calendar's.

Tests: `SportsLeagueTests` (a league's teams, the tables of football, the NBA's conferences and the World Cup's groups,
the calendar's next day, the requests, a league found by its words, a league through the file and through the search
row, the search's leagues then teams then ESPN's each once and failing in part, a round's days, the face's lead, the
table around a team, a league's words, the monograms, the pages), `SportsLogosTests` (once and kept, on disk across a
restart and again after a month, the dark drawing's fallback, the failure left alone, everyone told, the file's name),
`SportsStoreTests` (a face's users and a league's fetch), `SportsPictures` (sports-lines-<table|league|league-nba|league-live|badges|table-badges>
at one to twelve rows, the faces with a league's), `SportsMenuPictures` (sports-menu(-coming)-<dark|light>.png), on
ESPN's answers saved on 2026-10-26 (Saved\league-*.json, standings-*.json).

By hand: in a sports line's menu open "Team or league": every league with its logo; pick the Bundesliga — the line

The person, 2026-10-26: *"i also believe that the click area on the weather widget is way off. its only like half of

**Where it was.** The person's weather widget is a line in a folder (the conditions now, `WeatherPartTile`, four rows

150 % on a 4K display's size, `WindowFromPoint` over every pixel of every entry at rest and with each folder open and
closed again: the bar's window everywhere, and a press across each folder opened it. In the dock's own process every
pixel each part draws asked of `Layout.HitTest` (`BarHitsWhereItDrawsTests`, below): Windows' buttons, the app buttons,
the tray, Show desktop, every widget kind the bar draws and a folder wearing every face, alone and four at once, on every
edge, 32 DIP at 100 % and 150 %, 48 DIP and a dock at 150 %, and after widgets came and went and the height changed mid-glide:
every drawn pixel is its own part's. The one exception is by design: the grip band along the inner edge (`Layout.GripRect`,
