room left (2026-10-04) — so on a thin bar or a dock the edge of a badge, a side bar's glyph or a dock's focused button
under it starts a height drag. Left as it is; a decision for the person.

`InputReachesTheBarsTests` asks every third pixel of each entry, not its middle. `WeatherTargetsTests`: every point of the
header is the conditions but the button's reach; the air under it on a tall line nothing; one row all of it.

## 371. Sports: Automatic height (2026-10-26)

The person, 2026-10-26: *"auto height should also be possible with the sports widget"*.

**Where it was.** The sports line was Fixed only (`ListWidget.Grows` false, §138): a team with nothing under its
scoreboard still took its three rows, a league's round and table the twelve it was set to, with empty room under the
last row, and the ready-made folder's line was `Exactly(3)`.

**What changed.** The sports line has Automatic (`Grows` true), so its menu's height level offers it as every
measured line's does, and a new line starts automatic up to twelve rows (`LineHeight.StartFor`), the ready-made
folder's too (its explicit three rows gone). `SportsTile` is an `IListContent`: its height is what its plan draws at
the most its line may be — the person's rows, a Fill line's past any screen (`LineHeight.Most`) — never the room it
was last given (`SportsPlan.Height`, the foot of its last row and the pad under it):
- *Nothing to show* — no team or league yet, nothing come yet, ESPN unreachable before any answer: the one row.
- *A team*: the scoreboard, then while it is on the league's other matches, the matches to come, the table around
  it, the results, each a row under its heading, and where no table is, the standing at the foot; as many as fit
  in its most and no more. A team with nothing but its match is the scoreboard alone, under two rows.
- *A league*: its head and the round's games, then the table's heading and rows.

So the line ends under its last row at every most, and drawn at that height draws the same as at its most: nothing
lost, nothing cut, no room no row could take. A taller most never makes it shorter. When the answer comes or a
match goes on, the folder measures the line again with its news and lays it out once, as the weather's and the
markets' lines do.

**A league's share said in px.** The table kept its three rows from "eight rows of room" and the round had "the room
less four": a line as tall as what that drew had a row less of room, and so a game fewer. Now the round has what is
left over the table's gap, heading and three rows, four games at the least; shorter, the round first and the table
what is left. The same games and table rows as before at the heights the pictures show.

**The config.** Nothing converted: a line the person set fixed stays fixed; its menu switches it (Automatic at the
same rows).

Tests: `SportsHeightTests` — Automatic offered where a new line starts, the ready-made folder's line, the menu's
switch; on ESPN's saved answers (a team on now, next, final, with its table; a league's round and table, the NBA's,
one with a game on) at one to twelve rows, at 100 % and 150 % and 225 % text: drawn at its height the same as at
its most, nothing past its foot, under a px of air under its last row, never shorter for a taller most; Fill its
whole content; nothing to show one row; in a folder the line given what it measures
(sports-auto-<live|next|final|table|league|league-nba|league-live|unset|waiting>-<dark|light>.png: Automatic up to
2, 4, 6, 9 and 12 beside Fixed 12).

By hand: in a sports line's menu, Height: Automatic. A team: the line ends under its last result or the standing; a
league: under the table. Set it up to 4 rows and to 12: shorter and taller, no empty room. While a match goes on, the
line grows by the league's other matches and settles once.

## 372. WhatsApp's count measured again, and a count in a folder (2026-10-26)

The person: *"the unread message count of whatsapp just does not update in karpo. fix this completely. not just a
quick fix."* §198 measured WhatsApp 2.2639; this PC now runs 2.2640.100.0, WhatsApp's new build (`WhatsApp.Root.exe`, a
WinUI 3 shell around WhatsApp Web in WebView2). Measured read-only again, as §198 did: a probe reading Windows'
`wpndatabase.db` every half second (every `badge` row and every row of WhatsApp's handler), a folder watch beside it,
WhatsApp's windows and the running Karpo's WhatsApp button as a screen reader hears it, for 40 minutes; and the
package itself, its manifest and its IL (a throwaway reader of the assembly's metadata, nothing run).

**What WhatsApp 2.2640 does.** Exactly what 2.2639 did, through the same door: its count goes through
`BadgeUpdateManager.CreateBadgeUpdaterForApplication()` and nothing else (`TaskbarManager.UpdateAppBadge`: `Clear()` at
0, else `<badge value="n"/>` from Windows' own `BadgeNumber` template). The updater is the process's own, so the row is
the package's AUMID, `5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop_cv1g1gvanyjgm!App`, which is also its process's and the person's pin's
(its window carries none of its own). No overlay through the taskbar list (no `ITaskbarList3` anywhere in it), no
count in its tray icon (`H.NotifyIcon`, `logo.ico`, a fixed tooltip), no count in a title. Two things of WhatsApp's
own decide whether the row moves at all:

- Its setting "Show taskbar badge" (`WindowsTaskbarNotificationSetting`): Always, Never, or *only while the app is
  open*, which clears the badge whenever the window is closed to the tray (`SystemIntegrationsManager.UpdateTaskbarBadge`).
- The count is the web page's: only WhatsApp Web calls `updateTaskbarBadge`. This build *suspends* that page while
  the window is closed to the tray (`WebLifecycleController.DoUpdateWebState`: minimised to the tray, suspending
  allowed → `TrySuspend`, WebView2's `TrySuspendAsync` and a low memory target); messages still arrive as toasts
  through its WNS push channel, but nothing counts them until the page runs again.

Either way Windows' own taskbar shows exactly what the store holds, and so does Karpo: the store is the one source.

**What the store held.** No WhatsApp row of any kind (no badge, no toast) the whole time: WhatsApp sat closed to the
tray with nothing unread, and no WhatsApp message came during the probe; the rows of To Do (a count of 2, rewritten
twice) and the Phone Link's 11 were read on every write, the folder watch heard every write, and the button
said "WhatsApp" throughout. A long-lived connection writing a WAL database that no longer grows (as Windows' service
does) was checked apart: the watch hears every write, 2,006 events for 2,000 writes across checkpoints. Not measured
this time: WhatsApp's own rows moving, which needs a message to the person; §198's twenty minutes of them still stand
(the same door, the same row, replaced at every change and deleted when read).

**What Karpo got wrong, and now does not.** Nothing on the bar's own pin: the badge follows the store up, down and
cleared, with no window and after either restart (§198, its tests unchanged and green). But a pin *in a folder* never
showed a count at all: the dock gave a folder's pins their running indicator alone (`Dock.MarkFor` built a `Mark`
without its `TileSignal`), and neither a pin's line nor a folder's button drew one. WhatsApp pinned in a folder had no
count to update. And the badges were not even read when a folder held the only pins on the bars (`SyncBadges` looked
at the bars' own entries alone). Now:

- A pin in a folder carries what its app says on its button, as the bar's own pins do (`Dock.MarkFor` →
  `SignalFor`): its badge, or its window's overlay, on its icon's corner, at the bar's place and size
  (`SignalPaint.Corner`, the scene's `SignalShape.Corner`), in the popup's accent with the text on it
  (`SignalPaint.BadgeInk`), on its list line (`FolderFlyout.PaintListLine`), its own line (`PinTile.PaintLine`) and a
  cell (`PinTile.PaintCell`). With no window open too.
- The folder's button shows its pins' badges together, so the count is seen with the folder shut: the counts added up
  ("99+" past 99), or a glyph where nothing counts (`Badge.Together`, `FolderIsland.PinBadge`), on the corner where a
  rung timer's dot stands, lower right as on an icon. It goes when they go.
- The badges are read while any bar shows app buttons or pins in a folder (`SyncBadges`).

Not done: a folder does not show its pins' progress, and a folder in a folder does not add its pins to the outer one.

Tests: `PinOffscreenTests.APinInAFolderShowsItsAppsBadgeAndTheFolderButtonAllOfThem` (the regression: a pin's mark
carries its badge with no window, the folder's button draws 3 + 2 = 5 and nothing once they are read;
`pins-folder-badge.png`, `pins-list-badges.png`), `AppSignalsTests.AFoldersBadgeIsItsAppsBadgesTogether`; the store's
own (`NotificationStoreTests`) and the bar's (`SignalOffscreenTests`, `SignalSceneTests`) unchanged and green.

By hand: have a WhatsApp message sent to you with WhatsApp's window open in the background: the pin shows the count
within half a second, and it goes as the chat is opened. Then close WhatsApp to the tray and have another one sent:
if the count does not move, look at WhatsApp's own taskbar-badge setting among its notification settings ("Always" keeps it
from the tray, as far as WhatsApp still counts there) — Windows' own taskbar would not move either. Put WhatsApp in a
folder: its line shows the count, and the folder's button too.

## 373. Start opens on the clicked button's display (2026-10-28)

The person: *"sometimes when clicking the start button the start just appears no the wrong screen."* Windows' Start
opens on the display its launcher, Explorer's `IImmersiveLauncher`, is connected to. Windows connects it to the display
of the taskbar clicked, and otherwise keeps it with the foreground window: read on 26300 (read-only, `GetMonitor`
against `IImmersiveMonitorService.GetFromHandle` for each display), it named the foreground window's display. Karpo's
bars never take the foreground and Explorer's taskbars are hidden, so the Start button's `SC_TASKLIST` (§26) opened
Start wherever the app in use was: on the right display only while that app stood on the button's.

Now the button's click connects the launcher to its bar's display (`ConnectToMonitor`, the bar's `MonitorFromWindow`)
and opens Start there (`ShowStartView`), as that display's own taskbar button does (`StartLauncher`,
`Desktops.OpenStart`). Where the launcher can't be had, won't connect or won't show, the taskbar is asked as before,
and where there is none the Windows key is pressed; no key is pressed otherwise (§26, Raycast). The interfaces are
undocumented: their slots are ExplorerPatcher's, checked on 26300 against the registered proxy's own table
(`PCShellCommonProxyStub.dll`: 14 methods; `IsVisible` at 7 and `GetMonitor` at 11 answering), and they are called only
where the shell hands out exactly these IIDs. Where on the display Start stands is still Windows' own; the Windows key
alone is Windows' own too, and opens Start where Windows connected it last — after a click on a Karpo Start button,
that button's display.

Tests: `TaskbarKeysTests.StartOpensOnTheDisplayOfTheButtonClicked` (the regression: the launcher was never connected
to the button's display — red with "Expected: [2827] Actual: []"), `StartIsAskedOfTheTaskbarNotPressed` (the launcher
refusing to connect or to show), `WithoutADisplayTheLauncherIsLeftAlone`, `StartIsTheWindowsKeyWithoutATaskbarToAsk`.

**Karpo vanishing while desktops switch** (the person, same day: *"when switching desktops karpo vanishes for a brief
amount of time. is this the normal behaviour?"*). Looked at read-only, without switching the person's desktops: the
bars are tool windows with no view of the virtual desktop manager's, exactly as Explorer's taskbars are (both band 1,
never cloaked, `GetWindowDesktopId` "not found", `IsWindowOnCurrentVirtualDesktop` true): on every desktop, nothing to
pin. Karpo does nothing to its windows on a switch (`DesktopsChanged` reads the desktops and rebuilds in place; the full
screen look leaves shell views alone). Not changed: the switch itself was not seen. What was seen meanwhile is
Explorer's secondary taskbar showing itself over the bar for 15–200 ms every minute or two, idle, until Karpo hides it
again (§272's `Taskbar.Keep`).

By hand: with Karpo's Start buttons on two displays, click into an app on display A, then click the Start button on
display B: Start opens on B, every time; and the Windows key afterwards opens it on B too.

## 374. A settings menu opens at its top (2026-10-28)

The person: *"the settings menus dont always open at the root level although they should"*.

**What was wrong.** §356 kept where each edit-mode configuration menu was left (`MenuMemories`, by a `MenuKey`)
and opened it there again for the rest of the edit session; a menu at rest opened at its top. So the same menu
opened at its top or on a level depending on whether edit mode was on and on how it had closed: a pick that
closed it or another menu taking its place kept the level; a press elsewhere (a click away, a press on its own
edit-bar button) did not even keep that — the flyout's host had closed already as the flyout took its
`LastLeft`, so the menu kept whatever an earlier menu of the shared flyout had been left at, under its own key.
Seen on the real dock: Display ▾ gone into a layout's level, ⚙ opened in its place by a second start and closed,
Display ▾ again — on the layout's level.

**The rule now.** Every opening by the person — a right click on the bar, a widget's or a folder's menu, a
folder line's, the edit bar's Display ▾, Layout ▾, ⚙ and crumbs, an entry's landing — is at the menu's top.
Only the same menu standing open keeps its level: a Refresh after a pick, a field kept, another language, a bar
made again under it (§356, §365, unchanged). And a menu the dock itself closed for a dialog of Windows' and shows
again — a colour mixed in Windows' colour dialog, a pin's target browsed (`MenuBrowse`) — comes back where it
stood (`Pending.Stood`, taken as the pick closes it, or as the dialog comes over it; `Dock.Resume` hands it to
the one showing). Back up and reset's acts still bring ⚙ back on their level (§339: `OpenShownLevel`, as before).

Gone: `MenuMemories`, `MenuKey`, `Dock.Left`, `OpenWhereLeft`, `entryLanding`, `Flyout.LastLeft`. Kept:
`Flyout.Remembered` and `Recall` (Flyout.Memory.cs) for the resume. No config change, no strings.

Tests: `MenuOpensAtTopTests.DisplayMenuOpenedAgainStandsAtItsTop` (the real dock, Karpo.exe --stage on a desktop
of its own: Display ▾ into a layout's level, then ⚙ in its place by a second start, ⚙ by its button, and a press
on its own button; each time Display ▾ opened again is at its top — Home, Down, Right, End, Enter duplicate the
layout). Red before the fix: "Display ▾ after a second start's ⚙ took its place did not open at its top: the
layouts are Default". `MenuSessionTests.AMenuShownAgainWhereItStoodIsOnItsLevel` (a menu shown again is at its
top; recalled, on its level, scrolled, the keys where they were). The real dock's harness of
`LevelAfterCommitTests` is shared (`OnTheDock.Run`, `EnterEditMode`).

By hand: in edit mode open a widget's menu, go into a level, click away, open it again: at its top. The same with
Display ▾, Layout ▾ and ⚙ (closed by their own button, by Escape, by another menu in between). Pick "Custom
color…" in a widget's Appearance › Card and cancel the dialog: the menu is back on Card's level.

## 375. A folder's look for the widgets inside it (2026-10-28)

The person: *"for a folder i should also be able to set the appearance of the widgets inside the folder"*.

**One chain, one step longer.** A line of a folder wore its widget's own colours (§311) over the folders' look of
its layout (§334, §346) over Windows'. A folder now has a look for its widgets between the two: the same three
colours a widget's own look has (`WidgetLooks.Slots`: card, card outline, highlight), for the light and the dark mode
apart, in the same record (`BarColors`), kept on the folder (`FolderOptions.LineColors`, the file's `"lineColors"`
on the folder; nothing while it follows the folders'). The resolver is the one there was, `Palette.Over` all the
way: `WidgetLooks.InFolder` — a line's own over its folder's (`WidgetLooks.Inside`) over the folders' — which
`FolderFlyout.OwnOf` now asks, so the card, its outline and the highlight of every line follow it; a divider wears
none, high contrast none. The rule: what a widget sets for itself wins, colour by colour; what it leaves Automatic
is its folder's, and what the folder leaves Automatic the folders' look of the layout. The folder's own colours
(`WidgetItem.Colors`) stay its button's on the bar, never its widgets'. `Normalize` keeps only the three
(`WidgetLooks.Kept`, a widget's own look's rule).

**In the folder's menu.** Its "Appearance ›" (at the foot, §311) has its button's three colours, a rule, then
**Widgets inside ›** (the Tiles icon): the same three swatch rows, written on the folder for its widgets, and its
own **Reset all**, greyed while it gives them nothing. Appearance's Reset all takes back both, the button's and the
widgets'. Picks go through `OptionMenu.Row` as every row of the look does, so a swatch, None, "Custom color…" (the
colour dialog) and Reset act as anywhere; the open folder takes it at once (a folder's change builds, §334).

Strings: `dock.edit.look.inside` ("Widgets inside"), 30 languages.

Tests: `WidgetLookTests.AFoldersWidgetsWearItsLookUnderTheirOwn` (the chain: the folders' alone, the folder's over
them, a mode's alone, a line's own winning colour by colour, a divider none, the folder's own colours never its
widgets'), `TheFoldersAppearanceSetsTheLookOfItsWidgets` (the level's rows, none on a line or a bar widget, a card
picked inside written on the folder and not on its button, the file keeping the three, each Reset all);
`OptionRowsTests.EveryOptionOfAWidgetIsARowOfItsMenu` (`FolderOptions.LineColors` is Widgets inside's rows). Red first:
the build, `'WidgetLooks' does not contain a definition for 'InFolder'`, `'FolderOptions' does not contain a
definition for 'LineColors'`, `'S' does not contain a definition for 'DockEditLookInside'`. Pictures (150 %, dark
and light): `folder-look-inside-<look>.png` (a folder of five lines in its look for its widgets, one in its own
card, a divider wearing none; the folder's Appearance and its Widgets inside level beside it).

By hand: in edit mode click a folder on the bar, Appearance › Widgets inside › Card: every line of the folder takes
the card, its button on the bar does not; give one line a card of its own: it keeps it. Reset all in Widgets inside:
the lines follow the folders' look again. Switch Windows to light mode: the folder's widgets follow the folders'
there until set for light too.

## 376. A folder's face: lit while it is open, one corner everywhere; a line's outline all the way round (2026-10-28)

The person: *"the folder that is open in karpo should be highlighted in some way (maybe different background or
so)"*, *"if a folder face is on the edge of a section its corners are rounded. this should not be, or at least they
should have the same roundness of corners everywhere"* and *"the card outline property in the folder is not
displayed properly. the outline only shows on certain borders"*.

**The open folder's face is lit** (`Scene.Open`, `Dock.FacesShowOpen`). In Windows' language for a button whose
flyout is open — the clock while its calendar stands, the focused app's button: that button's plate,
SubtleFillColorSecondary with its elevation border (`Tokens.ActiveBack`, `ActiveStroke`, `ActiveLine`), over the
face's whole card in the corners its highlight has, under the highlight and under the face. In the part's own
colours (§311): a highlight of its own is its plate, as the focused app's is the bar's. The pointer over it lights it
by the step the focused app's button lights by (`HoverOnActive`), a press takes that step back, so hover and press
still read over it. The dock says which folder is open as one opens, closes (every way: `Forget`) and is handed on
to another bar by an arrange; the scene keeps it through every update and recolour. None while the bar is arranged,
where edit mode's own marks say what is selected. High contrast: the ring in the highlight's colour.

**One corner for a face everywhere** (`Layout.Joined(part, alone)`, `Scene.ComposeCards`). A widget in a card or an
outline of its own (§311) was drawn as its group's piece: square on a side it met a neighbour on, rounded on the
group's end — so a folder at the end of its section was round on one side and square on the other, and its
highlight, round at all four corners, did not fit it. Such a card is its own now: it runs on into no neighbour and no
neighbour into it, rounded at all four corners wherever it stands in its group, as its highlight is. It stands where
it stood; the group's other pieces meet it with their own ends. A group with no colours of its own is one card as
before.

**A line's outline all the way round** (`FolderFlyout.LineInsets`). A line's card is in its card's view, clipped
inside the panel's rim (`CardClip`, `FlyoutHost.RimInset`); its outline was a hairline on its box's edge, so every
side that lay on the card's edge — both sides of every line, the top of the first, the bottom of the last — was cut
off, and only the seams between two lines showed it. The line's shape stands in by the rim on those sides now, its
corners with it: its fill shows as it did, to the clip, and its outline is inside it on all four, at every scale.

Tests: `FolderOutlineTests.ALinesOutlineRunsAllTheWayRound` (every side of every line of a folder in the folders'
outline, dark and light at 100, 125, 150, 200 %; red before: *"line 0 (energySaver)'s left side is #FF513D24, not
its outline #FFFF8C00"*, every outer side), `SceneTreeTests.AFaceOfItsOwnHasTheSameCornersWhereverItStands` (the four
corners of a folder face in its own card at its group's start, middle and end), `SceneTreeTests.TheOpenFolderFaceIsLit`
(open differs from at rest, its edge from a face merely hovered, hover and press over it from it; closed again it is
as at rest; in the bar's colours and its own). Pictures: `folder-outline-<look>-<scale>.png`,
`folder-face-own<place>-<look>.png`, `folder-face-open-<state>-<which>-<look>.png`.

By hand: open a folder from the bar and move into it — its face stays lit until it closes, by a click, Escape or
another folder; hover and press it while open. Give a folder at a section's end a card colour of its own: all four
corners round. Set a card outline for the folders (or one widget in a folder): every line outlined on all four sides.

## 377. A clock's click searches the time where it stands (2026-10-28)

The person: *"the time widget you should be able to click as well, it should then google the current time for the
timezone/place in the prefered search engine"*.

**What a click does.** The clock's line (`ClockTile`, in a list or a grid folder, the world clock's lines among them)
and the clock flyout's header (`TimeHeaderTile`) act now (`CellAct.Action`): a click searches the time with the app's
one engine (⚙ › Online › Search engine, `Config.SearchEngine`, §337) once the folder has gone, as a ticker's search
does (§263). The query is `SearchUrls.Time`: a clock of another zone *"time in <its city>"* — the zone's first city,
the one its line names (`Clock.City`: "(UTC+09:00) Osaka, Sapporo, Tokyo" → Osaka) — and this PC's own clock *"time"*
alone, which every engine answers with the time where the PC is. A label is the person's own word ("Home", "Mum") and
no place an engine knows, so it is never the query. Each language words the query (`widget.clock.search`,
`widget.clock.searchHere`). The line lights as a whole now, being one thing to press (`LineHoverRuleTests`).

**The bar's clock is unchanged.** The bar has no clock of its own: it is a folder wearing the clock face (the clock
preset), and its click opens that folder — the notifications, the month, the clock — as Windows' own clock opens its
calendar and notification center. Searching there would take away the one way to the calendar; the search is the
lines' inside it.

**One door for "open once the folder has gone".** The markets' ticker and both clocks are `IOpensOnceGone` (the
address the click chose, opened once by the dock in `FolderForward`); the markets' own branch there went into it.

Tests: `ClockSearchTests` — the address for a place, for this PC's time, encoded ("São Paulo", "Eastern Time (US &
Canada)"), with each engine and a broken custom one; a zone's city; the clock's line and the header for Tokyo and for
this PC's time, labelled or not: the click forwards, lights as a whole and opens the search once.

By hand: open the clock's folder (or the world clock's) and click a clock: the browser searches the time there, with
the engine chosen in ⚙ › Online. The bar's clock still opens its folder.

## 378. The agenda in one column, the date on top and a heading per day (2026-10-28)

The person: *"the agenda should not have the date on the side, it should have it on top. (only one column)"*.

**Where it was.** The calendar's agenda line (`CalendarIsland`) stood today's page — the weekday over the large
number and the month — in a column at the leading edge, and the events in a second column beside it, as far as the
page took no more than two fifths of the line; every event of a later day said its day again ("Tomorrow · 09:30–09:45",
"Thursday, 24 September · 08:00–…").

**Now, one column at every height.**
- *One row*: unchanged — the next thing coming and when.
- *The compact line* (two rows at the default text): the day's date on one line, the weekday in the accent and the
  date after it ("Tuesday 22 September"), the next event under it on one line (when, then what) under its day's
  heading where it has one, and "N other events" where there is a row for it: this form does not scroll.
- *The whole agenda*, from where its first event fits under the page (three rows and a bit at the default text; it
  was four and a half when it waited for two events, with a compact line of two and empty room under them before
  that): the page on top, the events under it with the line's whole width, each its title over when it is. Every day
  after the page's is a heading of its own — "Tomorrow", then the long date ("Thursday, 24 September"), small and
  semibold in the secondary ink — over its events, as Outlook's agenda and Windows' calendar list them, so an event
  says only its time. Taller than its content the line scrolls (ListScroll), as before.
- A picked day (a month beside it, §9 "Channels") is its own page with every event of it, so no heading.
- With nothing to list, the date over why, under it.

The refresh button and the stale mark stay at the end of the date's row; a meeting's Join at the row's end
(§206). The page is no longer a shared drawing (`Page`, `PageWidth` went: nothing else drew it).

Tests: `AgendaColumnTests` — on the busy week at every height from one row to the most and half-way between, at 100
and 150 % and at 100 and 225 % text: every event, colour, time and heading stands under the date and begins where it
begins (red before: "colour 0 … beside the date, whose foot is at 54", 490 such); the whole agenda has a heading for
each later day over its first event, none for today, and each event says only its span (red before: "Tomorrow ·
09:30–09:45"). `ListLinesTests`, `LineHeightPicturesTests`, `ListFormTests`, `JoinEverywhereTests` green
(line-height-agenda-*.png, list-calendar*.png, list-form-calendar.png, join-calendar*.png).

By hand: a calendar line in a folder, Automatic and Fixed at 1 to 8 rows: the date on top, the events under it in one
column, "Tomorrow" and the later days as headings; at two rows the date's one line over the next event.

## 379. Every pixel is somebody's: a menu row is its slot, a tooltip takes no press, one thing to do is the whole line (2026-10-28)

The person, 2026-10-28: *"for the weather widget the button is still not the whole widget, there are some spaces that
when hovering over dont get highlighted. this should not be. it should highlight the whole area for all the widgets"*,
*"the size menu item is not clickable in the whole area as the other ones are"*, *"sometimes also just areas of the
settings menu header you cant click to go back. fix all of those click box issues. sometimes you need to click twice
until your input it taken etc. fix this as a whole"*.

**Found by sweeping, not by reading.** Three sweeps ask every third pixel what it is, the way input asks it:
`MenuHitSweepTests` moves and presses the pointer over a real menu on a desktop of its own (edit mode's menus of a
weather line, a calendar, a pin, a markets line, the volume and a folder: their own rows, scrolled, and every level one
deep); `AMenusTooltipTakesNoPress` asks Windows (`WindowFromPoint`, from the menu's own thread as its input is) what is
under each pixel of a tooltip standing over the menu; `LineHitSweepTests` draws every kind a list holds as the open
folder draws it, asks it as the folder asks (`CellIsland.TargetOn`), then lights each part under the pointer and
compares the drawing. What they found, red before the fix:

- **Menus: a row was its plate.** Every row of every menu took the pointer only on its plate, 5 DIP in from the sides
  and 2 DIP short of the rows over and under it — a dead frame round each row (244 to 404 points a row). "Height" and
  "Appearance" at the foot the same.
- **A level's head was its plate too:** the padding over it, its sides and its rule under it went nowhere (870 points of
  the band); a click at the head's corners did not go back.
- **A tooltip took the press under it** — why a click sometimes had to be made twice. A menu's tooltips (an icon
  button's name, a level head's "Back") stand over the menu where there is no room outside it — on a bottom bar's menu
  the buttons' tooltips stand over "Height" and "Appearance" under them, which is why it was the size row that would
  not click — and a folder's (a toggle's name over the row above it) over the folder's lines. `TipView` counted on
  `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`, which lets nothing through a window that is not layered (§360): 276 to 4400 points of each
  tooltip were the tooltip's. The first click went to it, the pointer leaving the menu put it away, the second landed.
- **Folders: one thing to do was not the whole line.** The weather's conditions (`WeatherPartTile`, §370) took and lit
  the header inset 4 by 2 DIP, and on a tall line nothing past the header: 561 of 6000 points of the line did nothing at
  its own height, 7401 of 12840 at eight rows. Today's date (`DateHeaderTile`) the same: a box round the date, the rest
  of its band dead (1300 of 1920 points).
- **The week's columns** picked their day under the pointer and lit only the day's heading (`CalendarViewTile`).

**The fix, one rule each, not a case each.**

- **A menu row takes its whole slot** (`Flyout.Row.Reach`, `Row.Takes`): a row of a list out to the menu's sides and
  halfway to the rows over and under it, so the slots meet; an icon button its whole span; the panel's padding over the
  first row (where no title or field stands) and under the last is theirs (`RowAt`). `RowAt` is the one question the lit
  row, the pressed one and the one a release picks are asked by, so what lights is what a click picks, everywhere. A
  rule and a heading between rows keep their band. The plates are drawn as they were.
- **A level's head takes its band**: the padding over it, edge to edge, and its rule.
- **A tooltip takes no pointer**: its window answers every hit test with `HTTRANSPARENT` (`TipView.PassThrough`), so
  the press goes to the menu, the folder or the bar under it, all on the dock's thread as `HTTRANSPARENT` needs. Every
  tooltip is a `TipView`: a menu's, a folder's, the edit bars' and the rail's.
- **A line that is one thing to press is the whole line, lit by the folder** (`FolderFlyout.LightsWhole`, in the
  widget's own highlight colour, §311): the weather's conditions and today's date light no parts of their own
  (`LightsItsRows` false; the date's line `CellAct.Action`); a click anywhere on them is the line's (`Click(0)`: the
  weather searched, today the folder's day), Enter too; the refresh button is still its own, carved out of the line.
  The weather's hours and days and every line of several parts keep their parts (§131).
- **The week's and the day's columns light with their day**: everything a day's press acts on lights — its heading and
  its whole column (`CalendarViewTile.PaintCard`).

**What the folder sweep holds** for every kind: a line the folder lights whole is left to the folder; otherwise every
part a press acts on lights under the pointer, a press acts nowhere farther than 6 DIP past what lights (a button's air,
as Windows' have; a slider pressed along its track lights its thumb; a timer's number, turned by the wheel, lights
nothing), nothing lit is dead to a press, and a line of clicks alone, the same pieces whatever happens, whose one part is
a quarter of it or more, is that part over the whole line. Pictures: `line-hit-<kind>-<height>.png` in KARPO_PNG_DIR,
each kind's largest part lit.

**Not changed.** The bar was swept by §370 (`BarHitsWhereItDrawsTests`); its grip band stays the bar's by design. A
press outside an open menu closes it and is not passed on, as Windows' own menus do.

By hand: open a widget's menu over a bottom bar, rest on the Copy button until its tooltip shows, then click "Height"
right under the tooltip: its level opens at the first click. Click between two rows and at a row's very ends: the row
lights and acts. Open a level and click its head's corners and its rule: it goes back. In the News folder the weather
line lights whole under the pointer, past "Feels like" and the hours under it, and a click anywhere but the refresh
button searches the weather. In a folder with the week view, hover a day's column: the column lights with its heading.

## 380. A pin and a folder's contents, two widgets again; what a pin opens by its name and its picture, and the apps (2026-10-28) — the taskbar's part superseded by §492 (2026-11-03)

The person: "lets split folder and pin again. so: a pin always only shows the link to a webpage, application,
folder, etc. and opens the location on click. a folder always shows the contents of the folder and inherits the
navigation properties etc. from the pin widget." §32 had made them one widget, a pin to a folder set to show its
contents; they are two again (`Karpo.Core\PinFolders.cs`).

- **A pin** (`pin`) is its target's icon and name, and a click opens the target, on the taskbar and in a list: an
  app, a file, a web address, a folder in File Explorer. It has no way to show and no navigation any more; a pin
  never carries them (`WidgetItem.Normalize` clears them). Its menu: What it opens, its name, its icon.
- **Folder contents** (`folderContents`, `WidgetInfos.FolderContents`, glyph Folder open) show what one folder on
  this PC holds: on the taskbar a button an item (`BarKind.FolderContents`, `Dock.FolderRows.cs`; the folder's own
  button until there is something to list), in a list a line of its items (`ListKind.FolderContents`,
  `FolderContentsLine` drawing through `FolderContentsView`, which was `PinContents`). They keep what the pin had for
  a folder: Navigation (File Explorer, one level, all levels deep) for a subfolder, and Show titles on the taskbar.
  They point at their folder with the pin's record (`PinOptions`: the folder, a name, an icon), so the head of the
  line is the pin's head as before. Their menu: Folder, its name, its icon, Show titles (taskbar), Navigation.
  Files ▸ in the add list has both, side by side; the drive presets' contents line is one (`Presets`, `folderContents`).
- The app buttons' layout counts a folder's contents' buttons as it counts a pin's (`BarKind.IsButtons`,
  `IsPinned`, `Layout`); they claim no app's windows.

**What it opens, by its name and its picture** (the person: "what it opens, for the pins should show the pin icons
and the proper names, not the weird ass names"). The row said the target's last part: "File Explorer.lnk",
"SpotifyAB.SpotifyMusic_zpdnekdrzrea0!Spotify". It says the name Windows gives it now, as the pin on the bar does
(`TargetChoices.NameOf`, the dock's `TargetLooks.Name` → `PinItems.NameOf`): a shortcut without ".lnk", an app as
Start names it, a known folder as File Explorer does ("This PC", "Downloads"), a site by its host; the name's field
hints the same. Before Windows has said, a person's name still (`PinTargets.NameOf`: ".lnk" dropped, an app by its
package's name, never its ID). Every row the picker offers wears its target's own picture, read off the menu's
thread one after another and kept (`TargetPictures`, through `Flyout.Pictures` as a team's logo is, §369), its glyph
until it has come.

**The apps** (the person: "what it opens should also show a list of apps if possible"). Under the folders, under a
heading each ("Folders", "Apps"; `OptionFound.Group`), the apps of Start's All apps: the shell's Apps folder,
packaged apps and the Start menu's shortcuts alike, each by its name and opened through the Apps folder
(`shell:AppsFolder\<ID>`, as a pin dragged from Start is; `InstalledApps`, read once a minute at most). Typing finds
an app by its name, never by its ID. A folder's contents are offered folders alone. The folders the person's other
widgets show come first (`OptionFields.PinsInUse`: folders only now, by their names).

**Reading… for ten seconds** (the person: "when showing folder contents the reading text is there for around 10
seconds or so. just too long"). Measured on the person's Downloads (21 items): the listing 8–23 ms, the folder's
picture 60 ms, the icons 30–120 ms — the read itself never took long. Two things held the names back: a line read its
folder only at its next sample — a tick, or another widget's news in the folder, which in an open folder can be many
seconds away — after it was made or given another folder (set up in its menu, or made while its folder stood open);
and every read (the line and the lists) waited on the shell for the folder's picture before it said a single name,
which a slow icon handler holds for as long as it likes. Now a line reads its folder the moment it is given one
(`FolderContentsView.Configure`; a share still only while shown), and the names are said the moment they are listed,
the folder's picture and then the icons after them (`FolderReader.Pictured`, for `FolderContentsView` and
`PinFolderFlyout` alike). With a shell 30 s slow to draw, the names were held 30 s before and show at once now.

**File Explorer behind the folder** (the person: "when i click to open a system folder in file explorer the file
explorer opens behind the karpo folder and the karpo folder does not close"). A click on the line opened what it
pointed at there and then and told the folder nothing, so the folder stayed open and in front. It is an app opening
now, as every other line's click is (`IslandView.App`, `FolderFlyout.Forwards`): the folder goes first, and only then
is it opened (`FolderContentsLine.Open`, from `Dock.FolderForward`), once. And File Explorer may take the foreground:
its window is the running Explorer's, which the new explorer.exe hands it to, so the right to come forward is passed
to any process before it is asked (`FolderReader.OpenWithShell`, `AllowSetForegroundWindow(ASFW_ANY)`), while Karpo
still has it from the click.

What a file holds: `{"kind": "folderContents", "pin": {"target": …, "name": …, "icon": …, "navigation": …,
"showTitles": …}}`; a pin's `"show"` is a word no build reads. No migration (the person's own file is converted
once).

Tests: `PinFolderSettingsTests` (`APinNeverListsWhatAFolderHolds`, `AFolderListsWhatItHoldsAndNavigates`,
`TheFileWritesOnlyWhatWasChosen`), `OptionRowsTests.APinsRowsAreItsPagesAndWriteWhatItWrites`, `PinTargetMenuTests`
(`WhatItOpensSaysTheNameWindowsGivesIt`, `NothingTypedOffersTheFoldersThenTheApps`, `ThePinnedFoldersAreOfferedFirst`,
`TypingFindsAFolderOrAnAppOrKeepsThePathTyped`), `TargetLooksTests` on this PC's shell (a shortcut of the test's own,
This PC and Downloads, the apps with File Explorer among them, a picture coming), `FolderContentsLineTests`
(`TheNamesShowBeforeTheIcons` with a shell held 30 s, `ALineReadsItsFolderAsSoonAsItHasOne`,
`WhatAClickOpensClosesTheFolderFirst`, and the line's own before). `FolderContentsRemovedTests` went.

By hand: in a list folder add Files ▸ Folder contents and pick Downloads in its menu: the names show at once. Click a
subfolder (navigation File Explorer): the folder closes and File Explorer comes up in front. Right-click a pin ▸
What it opens: "File Explorer", "Spotify" and the like with their icons, the folders, then the apps; type "spot".

## 381. A device connecting stays in the Bluetooth list (2026-10-29)

The person: "when connecting a device it shorty disappears from the bluetooth device list."

**Why.** The paired devices are two watchers, one for the connected ones and one for the rest (§10: the query says
what a property list cannot, `WindowsBluetooth.Searches`). A device connecting leaves the one and joins the other, and
each tells it on its own pool thread, in either order. A watcher's Removed took the device out of the list, so: left
first, the device was gone until the other's Added put it back — the blip, with its row rebuilt, its open card closed
and "Connecting…" given up as arrived; joined first, the late Removed took it out *for good*, until the panel was opened
again. A headset switched off did the same the other way.

**Now** the list is its own plain model (`BluetoothList`, no WinRT in it, so the tests feed it what a connection
reports): a device is listed while any watcher has it and connected while the connected ones' has it, so the order
the two speak in no longer matters and a late word from the watcher it left cannot disconnect it. One that no watcher
has is kept as it was, in its place, for `MovingMs` (2 s; the move takes a few ms), then leaves; the panel is told to
look again then. A device removed here leaves at once (`Forget`): it was unpaired, there is nothing to wait for. Its
kind, level and audio survive the move as they survived any other update.

Tests: `BluetoothTests.ADeviceMovingBetweenWatchersNeverLeavesTheList` (connecting and disconnecting, either watcher
first; red before: the device missing between the two, or gone for good), `ALateWordFromTheWatcherLeftDoesNotDisconnect`,
`ADeviceNobodyTakesBackIsGoneAfterAWhile`, `WhatWasReadSurvivesTheMove`.

By hand: open the Bluetooth list, open a paired headset and Connect: its row stays where it is with "Connecting…",
then reads Connected. Switch the headset off: it stays and reads Paired. Remove a device: it goes at once.

## 382. The status icons' tooltips are back (2026-10-29)

The person confirmed: the status icons get their tooltips back — the network, the sound, the battery, Bluetooth and
the bell — in Windows 11's words. §367 stays for everything else: no tooltip over a widget's face, a folder's face or
a folder's button.

**Which.** A face is a status icon when it is the Wi-Fi, sound, Bluetooth, battery or notifications face
(`BarTooltips.IsStatusIcon`). Over one of those on the bar, at rest, the tooltip is its own words, the same the face
already gave a screen reader: the network's name and "Internet access" / "No internet access" (and "Connected to VPN:
…"), or "Not connected"; "Speakers: 45%" or "Speakers: Muted" with the output's own name; "Battery status: 87%
remaining", "… available (plugged in)", "Fully charged (100%)"; "Bluetooth on" / "off"; the bell's "Notifications" or
how many are new. A greyed one says why (no battery, no radio), as before §367. Every string is the one Karpo already
had; no new strings.

**Each over its own icon**, as on Windows' taskbar: a folder's button wearing the network, the sound and the battery
side by side has three tooltips, not one. `FolderIsland.StatusTipAt` finds the face under the pointer (`FaceAt`, the
face's room along the bar and the bar's whole thickness; the markets face's click asks the same now, which was its
own copy of it) and answers its words and its room; the scene puts the tooltip over that room (`Scene.Tooltip`'s
`part`, kept through a re-layout like the item it is in). Moving from one icon to the next is the same hit, so the
pointer's move asks again (`Dock.ShowTooltip`) when the icon under it changes. Over the clock beside them, the
folder's name or the button's ends: none. The tooltip is the bar's own, so it takes no press, as every bar tooltip.

Tests: `BarTooltipsTests.OnlyTheStatusIconsAreStatusIcons`, `AStatusIconSaysWhatWindowsSays`,
`EachStatusIconHasItsOwnTooltipAndTheClockNone` (across and down a bar; red before: nothing over any of them),
`NoWidgetOrFolderHasATooltipWhatIsNotAWidgetKeepsIts`; the markets face's `MarketClickTests` on the shared `FaceAt`.

By hand: rest on the network icon (its name, "Internet access"), slide to the speaker (the tooltip moves over it
and says the output and its level), to the battery and the bell; rest on the clock or a weather face: no tooltip.

## 383. Another height, while the bar glides: one height for the panel, the strip and the window (2026-10-29)

The person: "right now when resizing the taskbar the layout gets completely messed up"; asked how: "both [dragging
the edge and the height setting] ... some elements changed its size but the bar did not really grow on the bottom
... right now i cannot reproduce."

**Not reproduced.** What was looked at: the drag (`BeginResize`, `ResizeMoved`, the 33 ms `ResizeTick` laying the bar
out through `LiveHeight`, `EndResize` keeping or putting back) and the menu's height (`Apply`), both a `Rebuild` that
lays every bar out again; the window, which by §358 stands still at its edge's most thickness (`Layout.FrameFor`) and
so never has to grow; the strip held, sent once at the drag's end (`Reserve` waits while `Resizing`) and at every
other build; the region, which grows at once and shrinks once the content has landed (`WindowTable.Region`). The
likeliest cause on paper — a glide (167 ms) still running when the next height lays the bar out without one, and
Composition finishing the old animation over the new size — does not happen: filmed on a hidden desktop, the bar
ends exactly as a bar laid out at that height from the start.

Kept as tests, since they pin what the person saw break: `BarResizeTests.EveryHeightIsOneHeightForThePanelTheStripAndTheWindow`
(heights up and down, quick, bottom and top, 100 % and 150 %, a bar and a dock: the panel is the thickness, the strip
held reaches from the edge to the panel's inner side, a bar's flush with the edge, the layout inside its window) and
`AHeightLaidOutMidGlideEndsAtThatHeight` (an app opening, then heights at a drag's pace mid-glide; the screen once
landed against a bar laid at the last height; films `film-bar-resize-*.png`). No code changed.

By hand, if it comes back: note the bar's style (islands or dock), whether something changed just before (an app
opening, edit mode), and whether it was a top or bottom bar; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\appbar.log` around that time.

## 384. A desktop chosen in the list switches without the slide that hid the bars (2026-10-29)

The person: *"when switching desktops karpo vanishes for a brief amount of time. is this the normal behaviour?"* and
*"when switching desktop whole karpo disappears"*. A read-only logger (8 ms, every switch of a run) saw the bars
shown and never cloaked throughout. What covered them was Explorer's `VirtualDesktopHotkeySwitcher`, a window per
display, the whole display, for 0.4–0.7 s, in band 2 (`ZBID_UIACCESS`), above band 1, where every app's window is,
always-on-top or not, Karpo's bars too. It is the slide of a switch by the keys (`twinui.pcshell.dll`,
`virtualdesktopswitchanimator.cpp`): what shows through it is what it draws, the windows of the two desktops and
Explorer's own taskbars, not Karpo's bars, tool windows with no view of the virtual desktop manager's (§373).

Every switch of that run came from the Virtual desktops folder's list: the list took the foreground, a row was
chosen, and in the same 8 ms the foreground went to the desktop being left and the slide began, `Desktops.Go`'s keys.
On the person's build, 26300, `DesktopControl` was not used (only 24H2 and 25H2 builds were known), so a row pressed
Ctrl+Win+arrow and Explorer slid over the bars. 26300 is a known build now: checked read-only, `QueryService` hands
out 53F5CA0B, its registered proxy (`ActXPrxy.dll`) has the table's 25 methods, and `GetCount`, `GetCurrentDesktop`
and `FindDesktop` answer at their slots with the registry's desktops. A row switches straight (`SwitchDesktop`, which
does not slide; `SwitchDesktopWithAnimation` is the one that does), and the bars stay.

Not changed, because it can't be from band 1: Ctrl+Win+arrow typed is Explorer's slide, over the bars as over any
app's window. Above it a window needs band 2 itself (UIAccess: a signed build installed under Program Files, raised
again over each slide as it starts); drawn in it, a view of the virtual desktop manager's pinned to every desktop,
which puts the bars in Alt+Tab and Task View. Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visual effects ▸ Animation effects off is
the person's own choice to try.

Tests: `PeekAndPagingTests.TheShellsDesktopInterfaceIsUsedOnlyOnCheckedBuilds(26300)` (red: "Expected: True Actual:
False").

By hand, on 26300 with two desktops: choose the other desktop in the Virtual desktops folder: no slide, the bars stay
in sight, the desktop arrived at has its last window in front. Ctrl+Win+arrow typed still slides, the bars out of sight
until it ends.

## 385. A folder's alignment: Automatic, Left, Center, Right (2026-10-29)

The person: *"you should be able to set the alignment of a folder. e.g. left right center and auto, in auto it
means that the folder alignes to the face that opens the folder"*.

**Where each stands.** A folder hangs off its face — the middle of the face's inner side (`DockWindow.WidgetAnchor`),
the gap every popup keeps off the bar (12 DIP) — in its display's work area less its bars (`FolderWork`), as before.
Along the bar its alignment (`FolderOptions.Align`, `FolderAlign`) decides, through the one placement every popup has
(`FlyoutPlacement.Along`; `FolderFlyout.PlacementOf` turns the one into the other):

- **Automatic** — centred on the face that opened it, kept inside the screen: a face near an end pushes it in to the
  8 DIP margin there. Centred rather than edge-aligned because that is what reads as *hung from the button* on a
  Windows 11 bar — its jump lists and, with a centred taskbar, Start stand centred on their button — and because it
  is where every folder stood until now (`Dock.PopupAlign`, `FlyoutAlign.Center`), so **Automatic is the default**:
  a new folder, and a folder in a file without the key, opens where it always did. Nothing moves.
- **Left** — against the work area's left, 8 DIP in (`FlyoutAlign.Start`, the popups' start margin).
- **Center** — in the middle of the work area, wherever its face is (`FlyoutAlign.Middle`, new).
- **Right** — against the work area's right, 12 DIP in (`FlyoutAlign.End`, the end margin Windows' calendar keeps).

Left and Right are the screen's, in every language; down a side bar they are its top and its bottom. A display
beside another has its own: the work area is the display's. A folder wider than its display starts at its start
whatever its alignment, the far end giving (§320). What is placed is the folder's core, the lists with widgets
(`FolderPlan.Core`, §158), an arranged folder's empty lists hanging off it as before — so a Left folder's empty first
column hangs past the screen's edge in edit mode, as an Automatic one's did at the screen's end.

**Placed again.** A folder that grows or shrinks while open is placed again by the same rule (`FlyoutHost.Resize`):
a Right folder grows leftward, a Center one both ways. The alignment is in what decides its layout
(`FolderFlyout.Signature`), so one changed in its menu while it stands open moves it there at once
(`FlyoutHost.Resize` takes the new `FlyoutAlign`). The dock hands a folder no placement any more; `Show`'s `align`
is a picture's or a test's placement of its own.

**In its menu.** The folder's own rows (§364): its name, "Show the name beside it", then **Alignment** — four buttons
in the row as a line's alignment's three are (§253): Automatic (the Automatic icon), Left, Center, Right (Word's
three, never mirrored: they are the screen's sides), Automatic in force until somebody picks.

The file: `"align": "left" | "center" | "right"` in the folder's options (`"folder": {…}`), not written while it is
Automatic; a word this build does not know reads as Automatic (`TolerantEnumConverter`, `Normalize`). Nothing to
convert: a file without the key opens every folder where it opened.

Strings: `dock.folder.align.auto` ("Automatic"), 30 languages; Left, Center and Right are `core.edge.left`,
`core.align.center` and `core.edge.right`, the title `core.align.title`.

Tests: `FolderAlignTests` — the rule, pure (`ANewFolderAndAFileWithoutOneAreAutomaticWhichIsWhereAFolderAlwaysStood`,
`EachAlignmentStandsWhereItSaysAlongATopOrBottomBar`, `AutomaticNextToTheScreensEdgeIsKeptOnTheScreen`,
`OnADisplayBesideAnotherTheAlignmentIsThatDisplays`, `AFolderWiderThanTheScreenStartsAtItsStartWhateverItsAlignment`,
`DownASideBarLeftIsItsTopAndRightItsBottom`), the file (`TheFileKeepsAnAlignmentOnlyWhereItIsNotAutomatic`), the menu
(`TheFoldersMenuSetsItsAlignment`), and on a real folder (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1)
`TheOpenFolderStandsWhereItsAlignmentSays` (bottom and top bar, at rest and arranged) and
`ChangedOrGrownWhileOpenTheFolderIsPlacedAgainByItsAlignment`; `OptionRowsTests` (`FolderOptions.Align` is the
row), `AlignSegmentsTests` (the folder's row segmented too, four), `FolderFacesTests` (the folder's own rows). Red
first: the build, `The type or namespace name 'FolderAlign' could not be found`. Pictures: `folder-align-bottom.png`,
`folder-align-top.png` (Automatic, Left / Center, Right, two by two; the face red on a grey bar).

By hand: right-click a folder on the bar (or click it in edit mode) › Alignment › Left: open it, it stands at the
screen's left; Center: the middle; Right: the right; Automatic: over its face again. With it open in edit mode,
pick another: it moves at once. Add a column to a Right folder: it grows leftward, its right edge still.

## 386. A click in edit mode opens the settings on the edit bar, a folder's with the folder (2026-10-29) — a click selects, the settings panel follows, since §520 (2026-11-06)

The person: *"right now when i left click a widget the configuration opens besides it, i want the configuration to
open on the topbar where the breadcrumbs are (where you can already configure the widgets as well.) same for when i
left click a folder, then the folder settings should open too. (the folder should also still open.)"*

- **A widget** (on a bar, or a line of the folder open arranged): a click selects it, its crumb comes on the edit bar
  (Widget ▾, §352) and its settings hang from that crumb — the very menu a click on Widget ▾ opens, by the one path
  (`Dock.CrumbSettings` → `OpenCrumb`, which Widget ▾ and Folder ▾ call too; `WidgetCrumbMenu`, `CrumbMenu`).
  Nothing opens beside the widget any more. The edit bar follows the selection as the frame ends (§359); a click
  brings the crumb at once (`PresentChrome`), so the menu and its crumb come in one frame. A second click on the
  widget closes them, and a click on the crumb does too (§343, `DeckOpened`).
- **A folder's face**: the folder opens arranged as before (§253) and its own menu hangs from Folder ▾
  (`EditClicks.OnBlock`: `Open`, then `Settings`; `EditClicks.Crumb` names the crumb: Folder ▾ for a folder, Widget ▾
  for anything else).
- **Space, Enter and Narrator's Invoke** are the click, the same (`EditKeyAct.Click`/`Open` both
  `Dock.EditActivate`). Enter opened the widget's menu beside it before.
- **Ctrl+click and Shift+click** change the selection; the settings open where that leaves one widget selected,
  none where it leaves several (no Widget ▾ then; their shared Cut, Copy, Remove are the right click's).
- **Kept as they were**: a right click on a widget, a folder or a line, and the menu key and Shift+F10, open the
  menu beside it (`Dock.BesideMenu`, was `ClickMenu`; `LineMenu`) — a context menu where it was asked for, as
  Windows has it; and the right click on the bar's or the folder's room, the looks. These were not the edit bar's
  path twice: the same menu (`WidgetMenu`), placed by the widget rather than by its crumb.
- Gone: the click's own menu beside the widget (`ClickMenu` from a click, `LineMenu` from a line's click, Space or
  Enter), `EditClickAct.Menu` (`Settings` now), the Enter case that opened the menu.

No config change, no strings. A stage run's `stage-edit.json` says the menu open, whose it is and where it stands
(`"Menu"`), for a test.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.ALeftClickOpensTheSettingsFromTheEditBar` (the real dock: a click on Task view,
a second closing it, a folder's face — the folder open and its menu from Folder ▾ —, a line from Widget ▾, a right
click on a line beside it), `EditClickTests` (`AClickSelectsOpensTheSettingsAndBringsNothingForward`,
`AClickOnAFolderOpensTheFolderAndItsSettings`, `EnterOpensTheMenu`, the double-click and the keys),
`EditBarFolderPictures.TheCrumbsAndButtonsDoTheirThing`, `KarpoMenuTests.TheEditBarsMenusAreTheDocksWay`.

By hand: edit mode, click a widget on the bar: its settings drop from "Widget ▾" at the top, nothing beside it;
click it again: they close. Click a folder: it opens and its settings drop from "Folder ▾". Click a line in it: its
settings from "Widget ▾", the folder staying. Right-click a widget: its menu beside it, as before. Space or Enter on a
widget with the keys: as a click.

## 387. A press is no carry until it moves: the bar's "+" stay through a click (2026-10-29)

The person: *"when i open a folder in edit mode the blue plus buttons flicker"*.

A press on a block of an arranged bar took it up at once (`DockWindow.EditPressed` set the dragged key, and
`EditView` said `Dragging` from then on): the block was lifted into the carry window, its blue ghost shown in its
gap, its selection ring and focus gone and **every "+" of the bar hidden** (`Scene.ShowAdds`: none while anything is
carried) — until the release, which, a click, put all of it back. So every click on a block blinked the bar's "+"
off for as long as the button was held, and a click on a folder's face, which opens the folder, most visibly.
Measured on a stage dock (the folder's own "+" and the bar's traced per frame, the folder's never moved): the bar's 4
"+" went to 0 at the press and came back at the release.

The rule every other drag of Karpo's keeps (`EditClicks.PastThreshold`, the system's drag threshold) now holds for the bar's
blocks too: a press is a carry only once the pointer has left the drag threshold (`EditView` says `Dragging` only
`dragMoved`). Until then nothing is lifted, no ghost, no gap, no "+" hidden, and the carry window is not shown
(`MoveCarry` finds nothing lifted). Past it, the carry is as it was. Nothing else of the press changed: it still takes
the capture, the focus and the hold that makes a folder.

A folder's own lines are lifted at their press still (`FolderFlyout`); that hides none of its "+".

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AFolderOpenTakesItsBarsPlusesAsideWithoutABlink` (was
`APressOnAFoldersFaceLeavesTheBarsPlusesStanding`; the real dock: a press held on a folder's face, the bar's "+" from
`stage-edit.json`'s `"BarAdd"` the same before and held, and in every filmed frame of the press; before: "held down
on the folder's face, the bar shows 0 of its 4 "+""). Since §397 the folder, once open, takes them aside.

By hand: edit mode, press and hold on a folder on the bar: the "+" stay; let go: the folder opens and they go (§397).
Press a widget and drag it: the "+" go once it moves, as before.

## 388. One style for every widget: the line kit (2026-10-29)

The person, 2026-10-28: *"the widget to widget style has quite a lot of variance to it. this makes the layouts feel
bloated or not coherent with each other. find out a system of how we could reduce this and make the widgets more
similar in style and appearance to each other."* The proposal (a survey of what every one of the 107 list kinds
drew: 21 text sizes, 13 glyph sizes, 10 corners, 5 header styles, 9 empty-state looks) was read, and the answer
was *build it*, with six answers (2026-10-29):

1. **The big number is fixed.** Hero is always 28; a taller line shows more items, not bigger type, timers and
   stopwatches too. Display 40 only for a time that is the widget.
2. **No 11 for dense calendars.** Everything is at least 12; the year view shows fewer months across and the week's
   hour labels go to 12 too.
3. **Page rows move onto the list's columns** (text at 44), the quick-settings flyout with them: one design.
4. **A single reading has no place header**: its subject is its row's name.
5. **The accent** is only for something on or selected, a widget's one main action, and a chart or a meter. Not
   for words (a calendar's weekday, rain percentages), not for "Set up" buttons and not for links.
6. **An empty face on the bar** is its glyph and "–", never words like "No calendar".

**The kit** (`Karpo.Dock\Islands\LineKit.cs`), in DIP at 100 %, times the scale, text times the text scale:

| | |
|---|---|
| Type (`LineType`) | Caption 12 · Body 14 · Body strong 14 semibold · Value 20 · Hero 28 · Display 40 |
| Glyphs (`LineGlyph`) | Inline 12 (in a caption, a button) · Row 16 (the leading column) · Feature 24 (beside a Hero) |
| Space (`LineSpace`) | 2 · 4 · 8 · 12 (the gutter, `ListForm.Gutter`) · 16 |
| Corners (`LineCorner`) | 4 (controls, plates, a chosen row) · 8 (cards, panels) · the pill |

**The ratchet** (`LineStyleTests.EveryLineDrawsOnTheKit`). `PaintWatch.Styled` is told every line of text, glyph
and fill a painting draws, with its size, weight, family, ink and corner (`PopupPaint.Fill`/`Stroke` report theirs).
The test draws every list kind on the gutter tests' stand-ins at its own height and at one, two and four rows, and
holds what it drew: text sizes in the ramp, glyphs in 12/16/24, corners 0/4/8 or a pill, the words that lead a row
on the gutter or the text edge (a grid's labels stand in its columns: the month, day, week and year views, the
weather's hours, the screen-time ring's legend), no words in the accent, at most one accent-filled control. Each
offence is `"<kind>: <rule> <value>"`; the allowlist holds what a kind is still let off, and the test fails on a new
offence and on an allowed one no longer committed, so the list only shrinks. It started at 112.

**Phase 1: the type and glyph ramp.** The big number is fixed (answer 1): `ListTiers.FullValuePx` (26 growing to 36
with the height, and any size between when squeezed) is gone; `ListTiers.HeroPx` is the kit's Hero, 28, at every
height, the Value 20 where a line has not the room, never a size between. A time that is the widget is the Display,
40, a step down where it has not the room (`ListTiers.DisplayPx`, `LineType.Largest`): a timer's and an alarm's whole
widget, the stopwatch's Clock-app page (its hundredths the ramp's step under it, `LineType.Under`; it was up to 100
DIP, 69 drawn, so a taller stopwatch now shows more laps), the clock's header (34 in a 44 row before, now 40 in its
line). An alarm's compact time is the Hero (26 before). A countdown's unit is the Caption beside a Value, the Body
beside a Hero (11 to 14 before). Glyphs: the leading column's glyph is the Row 16 on one row and in the compact line
(the compact line's 20 went), the Feature 24 beside a Hero; the weather's condition glyph 24 (34), its trend arrow
16, its hours' glyphs 16; a drive's and a pin's whole-widget picture the Feature in the leading column, their words on
the text edge (a drive's 36 at the gutter with its name at 56, a pin's 36 with its name at 56); the drive header's
picture column the list's own; the media's note 24 on a plate with the 4 corner (half the art, up to 59, with a corner
of 8 % of it); a countdown's glyph alone on the kit's sizes. No 11 anywhere (answer 2): the day, week and year views'
labels, hours and small months' days are the Caption, 12 (`CalendarLayout.SmallPx`; `TinyPx` went), the year view's
day cells 22 by 20 DIP (20 by 18), so it shows fewer months across where the width is short; the weather hours'
rain chance 12. A note's code is the Caption (13), its toolbar's heading mark the Body (15). The ratchet went from 112
to 44.

**Documented exceptions** (left in the allowlist on purpose): a badge on a glyph's corner (a secured network's
lock, a missing command's warning, a muted app) is part of its glyph, 8 to 9; the note toolbar's numbered-list
pictogram draws its figures inside a glyph's square (6.7).

**Automatic height for the earthquakes, the stopwatch, the toggles and the week's weather** (the person,
2026-10-29: *"auto height for them too"*, after the sports line's, §371). The four are `Grows` now, so their menus
offer Automatic and a new line starts automatic up to its kind's most; each is an `IListContent` whose height is
what it draws at the most its line may be (`LineRows.Most`, the person's rows or a Fill line's past any screen,
which the sports line now asks too):
- *Earthquakes*: the head and every earthquake's row that fits, and its air; one row with nothing to list (nothing
  come, a quiet week, out of reach, not set up); its whole most where its rows stand alone on two rows.
- *Stopwatch*: one row while it has no laps; else the Clock app's page with as many laps as its most holds, or the
  page's small window (the time over the buttons) where its most holds none (`StopwatchClockCard.Height`).
- *Toggles*: the rows of buttons that fit its most (one row of the list at the least); one row with none chosen.
- *The week*: a row a day of those that fit and the air under them; one row without a forecast, or where not even a
  day fits.
Drawn at that height each draws the same as at its most and ends under its last item; a taller most never makes it
shorter. The person's own lines keep their fixed heights (the ready-made clock's stopwatch at one row, the
stopwatch's at five, the weather's week at seven, the quick settings' toggles at two, as their file has them); a line's menu switches it.

Tests: `AutomaticHeightTests` — offered where a new line starts; each kind automatic up to one to its most rows at
100 %, 150 % and 225 % text, drawn the same as at its most, under a px of air under its last item, never shorter;
nothing to list one row. Red first: the quakes line was no `IListContent`; the stopwatch's three laps drew one row at
every most; the toggles left up to 42 px under their last row; the week ran its last day 8 px past its line.

**Phase 2: one Status, one meta, fewer headers.** Every empty, error, loading and set-up state is the kit's one
Status (`LineStatus`, `LineKit.cs`): one row at the line's top — the kind's glyph in the leading column in the
tertiary ink, one sentence at the text edge in the secondary ink, at most one action, a standard `LineButton`
against the trailing gutter (or the refresh button's room). Never centred, never large, never the accent's.
- *Not set up* (`SetupFace`, every kind that needs a field or an account: a feed, a stock, a place, a drive, a
  pin, a team, a camera, the mail, the contacts): that row with "Set up" (the gear alone where short). It was
  centred in the box with an accent "Set up in Settings" (2026-10-10's "center center"), and from four rows a
  large glyph over the words over the button. A line not set up measures one row, so an automatic one is a row
  (`FolderFlyout`'s measure).
- *The earthquakes, the air quality, the tides* with nothing come or out of reach: the Status with their glyph and
  the refresh button (a grey dot and the sentence before, and the air's under a place header); a quiet week too.
- *The clipboard* with nothing copied: "Nothing copied yet" and a standard "Turn on" where Windows' history is off
  (a 20 semibold headline, a paragraph and an accent link before). *The mail* with nothing to list or still reading:
  the Status (a 20 semibold headline). Both are one row when automatic.
- *The taskbar layouts* with only one: the Status (a 12 sentence at its own inset).
The clipboard's and the mail's header is the kit's Header: the Row glyph and the Body strong title on the list's
row (it was the Value 20 with a 20 glyph).

**Answer 4: no place header over one reading.** The air quality's and the tides' head is their subject ("Air
quality", "Tides") in the Body strong, with the place and the reading's age as the meta at its end ("Zürich ·
1 h ago"), the age alone where both do not fit.

**One meta wording.** A line's "how fresh" reads "Now", "15 min ago", "2 h ago" everywhere (`WeatherAge.Ago`, the
existing strings `widget.rss.age.now`, `dock.clock.minutes`, the feeds' ages and `dock.quakes.ago`; no new
strings): the weather, the stocks, the earthquakes, sports, the air and the tides (it was "Updated 15 minutes
ago" and "Updated at 13:20"). The refresh button's tooltip keeps the long form.

Tests: `SetupLinkTests.ThePromptIsOneStatusRowAtTheTopOfItsLine` (red first: every kind's prompt was centred, its
words at 107 px, its button off the trailing gutter); `MailPresetTests`, `ClipboardPresetTests`, the readings'
`Updated` in `SportsRulesTests`, `AirQualityTests`, `TidesTests`, `SportsPictures`, `WeatherRowsTests` (the age now
gives way beside a long place). The ratchet: 38.

**Phase 3: rows and buttons on the list's columns.** Answer 3: the quick settings' rows (`Controls.ListRow`) are on
the list's own columns, in a folder's lines and in the quick-settings flyout alike (one design). A row has an 8 DIP
pad, the list's glyph column (20, at the text's size) and the list's gap (12) before its words (`ListRow.PadDip`,
`ListRow.TextLeft`); it was 12, 20 and 14. A page laid out as a line places its rows their pad outside the gutter
(`PageLayout.ListRowLeft`), so the glyph stands on the gutter, the name at 44 where every name begins (58 before:
Wi-Fi's networks, Bluetooth's devices, the hotspot's, Cast, Win+P, nearby sharing, the power mode, the keyboard
layouts, the sound lists' devices), and a chosen row's plate and pill 4 DIP from the line's edges, as Windows marks
one. The opened Wi-Fi and Bluetooth cards line up with the rows. In the flyout the rows stand 8 DIP in, so their
glyph is at 16 and their words at 48 (20 and 54 before).
- *Meters from the text edge*: a drive's and a network drive's bar, its figures and its words under the name, in
  the compact line (the drive header) and the whole widget; they ran from the gutter.
- *One arrow convention*: ‹ › move through time in every view; the month's and the year's ˄ ˅ went.
- *The stopwatch's controls are the lines' `LineButton`*: the start the accent's, lap and reset standard, at the
  lines' one size (the Clock app's round buttons went); its time and buttons from the text edge (centred before).

`ListGutterTests` lets a chosen row's plate and pill stand a row's pad outside the gutter for the kinds that list
these rows (`RowPlates`), and their titles lead with their first letter's own air. `PowerModeFormsTests` lets a row
stand its pad outside the gutter. The ratchet: 27.

**Phase 4: one meter, the accent's three uses.** A meter is the kit's one, 4 DIP and a pill, at every height
(`ListTiers.MeterPx`): the battery's, a drive's, the drive header's (6 on a compact line growing to 12 with the
height before). Answer 5, the accent only for something on or selected, a widget's one main action, and a chart or
a meter:
- the calendar's weekday over its date, the year view's month that holds today: the secondary ink and the text's
  (today's circle still says which day);
- the week's and the hours' chance of rain: the secondary ink;
- the feed's "Open news.example.com" is a standard button (an accent link before), its plate on the gutter;
- the to-do list's "+ Add a task" and the desktops' "+ New desktop": the secondary ink (accent links before);
- the clipboard's "Turn on" a standard button (phase 2).
A slider line's button is square (36 by 40 before), so its words begin at the text edge (46 before). The ratchet: 17.

**Phase 5: an empty face on the bar** (answer 6). A face with nothing to show is its glyph and a dash in the
secondary ink (`FaceDrawings.Empty`, `FaceDrawings.Dash`; the glyph alone down a bar on its side), as wide as the
two (`FaceDrawings.EmptyWidth`). It was a sentence or a word: "Set up" (a stock with no symbol, every face not set
up, `SetupFace.OnBar`), "Not set" / "No drive chosen" (a drive, a share), "No team yet" (sports), "No feed" or why
the feed failed (news), "No calendar" (the meeting). The faces that already said nothing with a dash (the weather,
the earthquakes, the air, the tides, the sun) are unchanged; the earthquakes' "Quiet day" is a reading and stays.

Tests: `EmptyFaceTests.AnEmptyFaceIsItsGlyphAndADash` — the stock, a drive, a share, sports, the news and the meeting
with nothing to show, at 100 % and 150 % and on its side, say nothing but the dash (red first: "Set up", "Not set",
"No team yet", "No feed", "No calendar"); `MeetingTests.WithNoCalendarTheFaceIsADash`; the faces' widths and slack
(`FaceSlackTests`) on the new width.

**Where it stands.** The ratchet's allowlist went from 112 to 17. What is left, each on purpose or for later:
- *Documented exceptions*: a badge on a glyph's corner is part of its glyph (`Hibernate: glyph 8`, `SoundMixer:
  glyph 9`, `Wifi: glyph 9`); the note toolbar's numbered-list pictogram (`Note: text 6.7`).
- *Not done yet* (words that lead a row off the gutter and the text edge): the timer's and the focus's compact
  steppers (`Timer`, `Focus`), the alarm's and Security's whole widget (`Alarm`, `Security`), the agenda's and the
  meeting's colour-barred items (`Calendar`, `Meeting`), the notifications' cards (`NotificationsList`), the feed's
  thumbnail rows (`Rss`), the footer's buttons (`Actions`), the sun's arc and day bar labels (`SunArc`,
  `SunDayBar`), the tides' turns (`Tides`), the weather's header from four rows (`WeatherNow`). Each is a layout of
  its own to move onto the blocks (the proposal's "What each kind becomes"); the allowlist names them.

By hand: open a folder of each kind. Every not-set-up widget is one row with "Set up" at its end; the quick
settings' Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Cast, power mode and keyboard rows begin their names where every other line does, in a
folder and in the quick-settings flyout; a tall weather, battery, CPU or timer line keeps its big number at 28 (40 for
a time) and shows more, not larger; the calendar's weekday and the rain chances are grey; the year view shows two
months across; a stock, sports or news face with nothing set is its glyph and "–".

## 389. Every account's items synced, widget or not (2026-10-29)

The person: *"all the items from the accounts should always be synced even if someone does not have the contacts
widget placed as example."*

**Before.** The calendars, the mail and To Do's tasks were synced from the dock's start for every account
(`Pim\PimSync.cs`, §77), but the contacts were read only when a folder with the contacts line opened (§11's old
rule): no line placed, no read, and the Accounts page said "Read when the contacts list first opens". The contacts
were one read of every account together, so one account failing dropped its people until the next good read. Beside
`PimSync`, the config kept two data sources that did the same again for the widgets it named — `CalendarData` (opened
the calendar store) and `MailData` (a second, counted `MailStore.Keep`) — adding nothing.

**Now.** `PimSync` is the one owner: at the dock's start it keeps all four stores reading for as long as it runs —
calendars, mail, tasks and **contacts** — for every account that gives them, whatever the config holds. `ContactStore`
is built as the mail's is: one sync per account (`ContactStore.Sync`, its books from its last good read), read side by
side at the online interval, a minute after its own failure (the others go on), at once when the accounts change (a
book turned off or on, an account added), re-armed when the interval changes, its timer stopped with no account that
gives contacts. An account removed is not asked again and its people leave the list. An account that fails keeps the
people it gave last; one that never answered is the line's problem, as before. The contacts are still kept in memory
only (no file). The line reads the store's memory: a folder opened over an on-time sync reads nothing; its Refresh asks
every account again now.

**What went.** `CalendarData` and `MailData` (`Sources\StoreData.cs`) and their keys in `SourceKinds` — the accounts'
widgets have no data source; `MailStore.Unkeep` and the keep counts of the mail and the tasks (a flag now: the dock
keeps them, or a watcher does); the contacts' read-on-open freshness (`readAt`); the string
`settings.accounts.sync.contactsLater` — the contacts heading says "Not synced yet" like the others until the first
read lands.

Tests (red before, green now): `PimSyncTests.AnAccountIsSyncedFromTheStartWithNoWidgetAtAll` (no widget: the contacts
read once, the people there, the timer armed; before: 0 reads),
`PimSyncTests.WithNoAccountTheStoresRestAndAnAccountAddedIsReadAtOnce`, `PimSyncTests.AnAccountRemovedStopsAndIsDroppedFromTheCache`
(its people gone, not asked again, the timer stopped with the last),
`ContactsPresetTests.ALinePlacedAfterTheSyncShowsItsPeopleWithNoReadOfItsOwn` (the line placed after the sync: its five
people, still one read), `StoreTests.AnAccountThatFailsKeepsItsPeopleWhileTheOthersAreRead`,
`OnlineUpdatesTests.TheContactsAreReadAgainAtTheIntervalAndFollowAChangeAtOnce`,
`OnlineUpdatesTests.AContactsFailureRestsItsMinuteWhateverTheInterval`; `DataSourcesTests` (no source for the
accounts' widgets).

By hand: with a contacts account and no contacts line anywhere, start Karpo and open the Accounts page: the contacts
heading says when they were synced and how many each book holds. Then add the contacts preset and open it: the people
are there at once. Remove the account: its people leave the line.

## 390. Every screen's edit bar stays while a folder is open on one (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the top edit bar on other screens gets hidden as soon as i open a folder."*

It was the rule, not a slip: §190 took every display's edit bar out of sight while a folder was open (so no one
took it for the folder's), §301 brought the folder's display's back with the folder's buttons, and the others stayed
aside (`EditDeckPlan.Content`'s `None`, the model's edit bar with no state, `EditChrome.Update`'s
`Deck.Hide(aside: true)`). On two screens that read as the edit bar vanishing from the screen the person was not
looking at.

- **Every display's edit bar stands** through a folder opening, standing open and closing on another display: in sight,
  over its dim and its bars (its stratum, §359), saying what its display stands as (`DeckState`); the folder's crumb
  and "Add to <name>" on the folder's display alone. `EditDeckContent`, `EditDeckPlan.Content` and the model's "no
  state" are gone: the edit bar of a display shows the folder where the folder is arranged on it
