  (`ChromeModels`), and is shown in every model (`EditDeckModel.State` is never null).
- **What it does there** is what it does with the folder open on its own display: "Add a widget" opens that display's
  add list, its pick carried onto its bar, the folder staying open (§344, the follow hook's click put down past the
  locked bar); its crumbs, Undo, Redo, ⚙ and Done as ever.
- **Two screens on a stage.** `Karpo.exe --stage x,y,w,h[,dpi][;x,y,w,h[,dpi]…]` is a made-up display per rectangle
  (`Stage.Displays`, the first the primary; `stage`, `stage-2` …), so a test drives the real dock on the person's two
  screens.

`EditDeck.Hide(aside:)`, its kept `aside` place and `Aside` were then used only by tests; gone with §402. No config
change, no strings.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AFolderOpenLeavesTheOtherScreensEditBar` (the real dock on two 2560 × 1440 screens at
150 %: edit mode; a folder opened on the first — each screen's edit bar shows "Add" and "Done", the window under its "Done"
its own edit bar, the folder's crumb on the first alone —, its settings closed, the folder closed, one opened on the
second, "Add" on the first opening its add list with the folder staying; before: "a folder opened on the first screen: screen
1's edit bar shows 0 parts, no "Add" or "Done""), `StageTests.ADisplayARectangle`,
`EditBarFolderPictures.FoldersOpeningAndClosingSetTheEditBars`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `film-two-screens.png`
(both screens' tops, before and with the folder open on the first).

By hand, on two screens: edit mode; open a folder on one: the other's edit bar stays where it stood; close it, open one
on the other screen: the same the other way round. With a folder open on one screen, "Add a widget" on the other: the
add list opens there, the folder stays; pick a widget and put it down on that screen's bar.

## 391. One margin at the screen's ends: an Automatic folder pushed to the right stands where a Right one does (2026-10-29)

The person: *"an automatic aligned folder all the way on the right side and a right aligned folder are not at the
same position seen from the right side."*

**What was wrong.** A popup kept two margins from the work area's ends along its bar (`FlyoutPlacement.MarginDip`):
12 DIP for a panel placed at the end (`FlyoutAlign.End`, Right), 8 DIP for every other (§385) — and a centred panel
pushed against an end (Automatic's face near the screen's right) kept the 8. So the two sat 4 DIP apart (6 px at
150 %), and down a side bar the same at its bottom.

**The rule now.** One margin, `EdgeMarginDip`, 12 DIP: at either end and wherever a panel is pushed against one.
Windows 11's own: Start (left-aligned), quick settings, the calendar and the notifications stand 12 DIP in from the
screen's sides, as they stand 12 off the taskbar (the gap, `GapDip`, unchanged). The second constant is gone
(`EndMarginDip`, `SideMarginDip`). So a folder at Automatic pushed against an end is exactly where that end's alignment
puts it, Left at the start and Right at the end. Every flyout keeps the same 12: a centred flyout near an end (a
widget's, Automatic folders) moves 4 DIP in, and the far end across the bar (how tall a flyout may grow, `Room`) keeps
12 instead of 8, as the layouts drawn without a placement already assumed (`FlyoutPlacement.Room(height, scale)`). A
widget's edit-mode menu beside it keeps its own 8 (`MenuSides.MarginDip`, a menu's, with its 8 DIP gap).

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `FolderAlignTests.PushedAgainstAnEndAutomaticStandsWhereThatEndsAlignmentPutsIt` (bottom, top, left and right
bars: Automatic at the far end == Right, at the start == Left). Red first, the far end only: "Expected: Tuple (1362,
90, 1902, 490) Actual: Tuple (1368, 90, 1908, 490)". `SpacingHomesTests.AFlyoutsMarginFromTheWorkAreaIsDecidedInOnePlace`
(every `FlyoutAlign` 12), and the pins of 8 moved to 12: `FlyoutFitTests`, `FlyoutRoomTests`, `FolderFillTests`,
`FolderClipTests`, `QuickFlyoutOffscreenTests`, the rest of `FolderAlignTests`.

By hand: a folder at Automatic, its face the last thing on the bar's right: open it; set it to Right and open it
again: its right edge does not move. The same with the face the first thing on the left and Left.

## 392. A choice of one goes back once it is made (2026-10-29)

The person: *"when i select someting in a single select menu, like a country i should be brought back after
selecting and not just stay in the same menu."*

**What was wrong.** §219 kept every level open after a pick, for the next change: right for switches and steppers,
where one change is seldom the last, but on a level of one choice (a country, a language, a unit, a zone, a search
engine, a colour) the pick is the whole errand, and the person had to go back by hand to see it said on its row.

**The rule now.** The row a level opens from says whether its level is one choice (`FlyoutItem.PickOne`), where the
rows are made, once for every menu: a choice's (`OptionRowKind.Choice` as a level; the person's own things of a
choice too, `OptionOwned`), a search's (a zone, a place, a share, a team, what a pin opens), a colour's and an icon's
(`MenuPickers`). A choice picked on such a level — by the pointer, the keys, a screen reader, a tile, a long list
searched first (§279), a search's result — still says Adjust and the menu still stays (§219); the menu's own
showing for it (`Flyout.Refresh`, the dock's `MenuAgain`) then goes back to the level under it, as Back does: the
rows slide back, the row it opened from lit, saying the new value at its end. Not before: until the dock has set it,
that row would still say the old one. The menu's own showings for its fields' rows and beside its widget
(`Flyout.Reshow`, `RelayoutFields`, `Follow`) never go back. A group of switches, a level of rows (a server's form),
the person's things of no choice (holiday calendars, layouts), a time's parts, a height's level (modes and a
stepper), a line of text (which Enter already shut, §332) and a number typed stay as before. "Custom color…" still
closes the menu for Windows' dialog and brings it back on the colour's level (§374). No per-menu case: the one rule
in the menu (`Flyout.Picked`, `PickedOne`), the one flag where rows are made.

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `OneChoiceTests` — `TheLevelsOfOneChoiceSaySo` (which kinds are one choice), and on a real menu
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `APickInAOneChoiceLevelGoesBackShowingIt` (by the pointer and by the keys),
`ALongListSearchedThenPickedGoesBack` ("gall", Enter, Enter: St. Gallen said on its row), `AGroupOfSwitchesStaysOnItsLevel`;
`MenuFieldTests.AZonePickedGoesBackToTheClocksRowsSayingIt` (a search's result). Red first: "Expected: Tuple (0, 10000)
Actual: Tuple (1, 10004)" (still on the cantons' level), the long list's and the zone's the same. Changed to the new
rule: `MenuKeepsTests.AChoicePickedKeepsTheMenuOpenAndTheTickMoves`, `InlineMenuTests.AClickSwapsTheRowsInPlaceAndTheHeadGoesBack`,
`MenuPickersTests.ThePickersActOnARealMenuAndThePicturesAreDrawn` (a swatch), `LevelAfterCommitTests` (choice, colour,
icon and a search's pick back on "Inner"); `OpenLevelsStandStillThroughARefreshThatChangesTheirParent` (a level not
marked one choice stays) unchanged.

By hand: edit mode, any choice in a widget's menu, or ⚙ › Language: pick one: back on the menu, the row saying it.
A clock's Time zone: type "+9", pick Tokyo: back, the row saying it. A long list (a holiday region): type, Enter,
Enter: back. A group of switches (the status icons): flip one: the level stays.

## 393. A stage holds nothing of the person's dock: a quit is a quit, and the next start is the dock (2026-10-29)

Seen by the coordinator: the installed dock quit by `Karpo.exe --quit`; its guard wrote "it quit (asked by
Karpo.exe --quit); a newer dock has taken over, and the taskbar is left to it", though no other dock ran, so
Windows' taskbar was not put back either; the logon task's `Karpo.exe --startup --logon-task` 6 s later ended at
once without a line in karpo.log; started again 30 s later, it came up.

**Why.** The guard knows a newer dock by the instance mutex (`Local\karpo.dock`): held, a dock runs. The `--quit`
process never touches it. But a stage dock (`Karpo.exe --stage`, a recording's or a real-dock test's —
`LevelAfterCommitTests`, `MenuOpensAtTopTests`, `ArrangedFolderStandsTests`, `InputReachesTheBarsTests`, run by
the agents that day) created it too, only not minding that it was held: Stage.cs said "no mutex", Program.Main took
one all the same. So while a stage ran, the mutex outlived the person's dock: its guard took the stage for a newer
dock and left the taskbar to it, and the logon task's start found the mutex held and ended as an automatic second
start does, asking nothing and saying nothing. Once the stage had ended, a start worked.

**Now.** The instance is `DockInstance`'s: `Take(stage, …)` — a dock's own where nobody holds it, its handle held
for as long as it runs, another dock's where one does, and nothing at all for a stage —, and `Held()`, the guard's
`NewerDock`. Only the person's dock holds it, so a quit while a stage runs puts the taskbar back and stays down, and
the next start is the dock. An automatic start that does find a dock running, and a logon task's start while the
Run entry would not start Karpo, now say so in karpo.log ("start: … a dock runs already, so this one ends").

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `DockInstanceTests` (names of their own, never the dock's): `AStageRunningAsTheDockQuitsIsNoNewerDock` (a dock,
a stage beside it, the dock gone: the guard's decision is StayDown and the next start's instance is its own; red:
"Expected: StayDown Actual: LeaveToNewer"), `AStageStartedFirstLeavesTheDockItsInstance` (red: held after a stage
alone), `TheFirstDockHoldsItAndASecondStartFindsItHeld`.

By hand: with a stage recording running (scripts\stage), quit Karpo by `Karpo.exe --quit`: Windows' taskbar comes
back, and karpo.log says "Karpo asked it to quit, so it stays down"; start Karpo again at once: it comes up.

## 394. The errors Karpo knows of, on the edit bar, each opening what it is of (2026-10-29)

The person: *"show the errors that happen in the main edit topbar and make them clickable so that they can be shown."*

**One list** (`Faults`, `Karpo.Dock\Faults.cs`): each source keeps its failure where it happens and says what is wrong
of it now, all at once (`Faults.Set` by `FaultKind`); what it no longer says is gone — an error that resolves itself
disappears —, what it says again keeps when it began. Newest first; the same message of the same thing once (an
account's calendars and mail failing for one reason are one row). Its sources (`Dock.Faults.cs`, `FaultSources`):

- **Widgets**: every widget of the bars and of their folders (`FolderIsland.Widgets`) that reads what it shows from
  somewhere, has something to read and whose last read failed — `IRefreshable { CanRefresh, Problem }`, the one
  interface the refresh button's "!" and the stale mark already read (§280, §305). Named and drawn as its crumb is
  (`Dock.SubjectOf`: its kind, its icon). Read again as a widget has news (`IslandReady`), after the islands are
  synced (`SyncIslands`) and as edit mode begins.
- **Accounts**: what the account layer last said (`SyncReport`, which ⚙ › Accounts shows): each part whose last sync
  failed ("Couldn't sync: …"), To Do waiting for consent; by the account's address. `SyncReport.Put` now raises
  `SyncReport.Told`, which the dock hears on its thread (`DispatcherQueue`) and reads the report again; and as edit
  mode begins.
- **Settings** (config.json): the file that does not read (`ConfigReload.Broken`), cleared as it reads again; one
  that could not be saved (`SaveConfig`), cleared by the next save; what reading it at the start had to do
  (`Config.Recovery`), cleared by the next save. All three went only to a console a windowed Karpo does not have.

Not taken: karpo.log's lines (`Troubles.Note`/`Report`) — English, for whoever reads the log, of faults Karpo carries
on from with nothing to click; a service's failure that matters to the person shows through the widget it feeds.

**On the edit bar** (`EditDeckPlan.ErrorsPart`, `EditDeckState.Errors`): an indicator before "Add" — Windows 11's
InfoBar error mark (StatusCircleOuter in the critical colour, `IslandInk.Critical`, its ✕ in the inverse text; high
contrast: the text colour) and the count ("99+" past 99) —, only while there are errors, in a room the plan keeps
for it with errors or none (`EditDeck.MostCount`), so nothing moves as errors come and go: without them it is the
trail's room going on. Its label on hover "3 errors" (`dock.edit.errors`). A click lists them under it
(`EditDeckAction.Errors`, `Dock.ShowFaults`, `Topic.Faults`, a menu toggled by its button as the crumbs' are, §343),
titled with the count: each row its icon, what failed, why under it, since when at its end (`FaultSince`: the time
today, the day before). A row picked (`FaultChosen`, `OpenFault`):

- a widget of a bar: selected, its settings from Widget ▾ as a click on it opens them (§386, `EditActivate`) — a
  folder's face its folder opened, its settings from Folder ▾ —, a folder open closing first;
- a line of a folder: its folder opened arranged, the line selected, its settings from Widget ▾ (`LineSettings`);
- an account: ⚙ › Accounts (`EditEntry.ManageAccounts`), where it signs in again;
- the settings: ⚙.

Strings: `dock.edit.errors` (one/other), `dock.fault.broken`, `dock.fault.notSaved`, in 30 languages. No config change.
A stage run's `stage-edit.json` lists the errors (`"Fault"`, by what each is of) and every edit bar button.

Tests: `FaultsTests` (a fault there until its source says it no more, since when kept; each source its own; newest
first, one row a reason; a widget's fault its failed read; an account's what its last sync said),
`EditDeckMoveTests.TheGripLeadsAndTheErrorsStandBeforeAdd`, `EditDeckDragTests.ItsErrorsShowWithTheirCountAndAskForTheirList`
(one width with errors or none, the count, the list from under it, "3 errors"),
`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AWidgetsErrorIsOnTheEditBarAndItsRowOpensIt` (the real dock: an RSS line whose feed nobody
answers; its error on the edit bar, the list under the indicator, its row picked opens the folder and the line's
settings from Widget ▾). `EditDeckPlanTests` follow the two new parts. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`editbar-errors-<dark|light|contrast>-150.png`, `editbar-errors-label-*`, `film-editbar-errors.png`.

By hand: edit mode with a widget that cannot read (a feed at a wrong address, the network off): the red mark and its
count before "Add"; click it: the list; pick the row: the widget's settings from Widget ▾ (its folder opened). Fix it
(Refresh once the network is back): the mark goes. With no errors nothing is there and nothing else moved.

## 395. The edit bar moves by its grip, and stays where it was left in the edit session (2026-10-29) — no grip, nothing moves it, since §630 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the top edit bar should be movable, just by draggin it. (it should get a drag handle.)"*

- **The grip** (`EditDeckPlan.GripPart`, `GripDip` 20): at the edit bar's start, before the gear, a reorderable row's
  six dots (`PopupPaint.Gripper`, now the one drawing `DesktopsLine` uses too) in the secondary text; no button, its
  label on hover "Drag to move" (`dock.edit.move`). A click on it does nothing.
- **Dragged** (`EditDeck.Drag`): a press on the grip takes the pointer (the move cursor); each move puts the panel
  where the press had it moved by the pointer's delta, inside the display's work area (`EditDeckPlan.Within`) — the
  window stands still over the display and the panel moves in it (§355, `FlyoutHost.Reanchor`), so it follows
  smoothly. Let go, it says where it was left (`EditDeckAction.Moved`); the dock keeps it for the edit session
  (`Dock.DeckLeft`, §402) and the
  chrome follows: the sections' edit bars keep clear of it, popups of a bar along the top avoid it, a folder's
  covered buttons stand past it, its menus hang from its crumbs where they stand now.
- **Where it stands** (`EditDeckRoom.Moved`, `Work`; `EditDeckPlan.Place`): where it was left, pushed back inside
  the work area where it reaches past it (a longer language); what it opens hangs down from it in the work area's
  upper half and up from it in its lower half (its chevrons with them). At its own spot again (§296) where the place
  kept is off the work area now — the bars grown over it.
- **Kept per display, for the edit session** (§402; it was kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\edit-bar.txt` across edit
  modes and starts until then): moving the edit bar is no edit of the person's settings (no Undo step, no menu row),
  so not config.json, and no config change.

Tests: `EditDeckMoveTests.ADraggedEditBarStandsWhereItWasLeft` (there; menus by the half; pushed inside; its own spot
when off), `ADragStaysInsideTheWorkArea`, `EditDeckDragTests.DraggingItsGripMovesItByThePointersDelta` (by the delta,
the crumbs' anchors with it, clamped, the place said on release, shown again there; a click moves nothing),
`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.TheEditBarMovesByItsGripAndStaysWhereItWasLeft` (the real dock: dragged by 300, 250;
Display ▾ hangs from the moved crumb; a folder opened and closed: still there; Escape and edit mode again: at its own
spot, §402). Pictures:
`film-editbar-moved.png`, `editbar-errors-label-*` (the grip's label).

By hand: edit mode, drag the dots at the edit bar's left: it follows the pointer and stops at the screen's edges and
the taskbar; open Display ▾ and Layout ▾: they hang from it; drag it to the lower half: they open upward. Open and
close a folder: it stays where you left it. Done, edit mode again: it is back at its own spot (§402).

## 396. Theming: nine colour roles, one chain, themes; a folder's face, panel and widgets; a colour picked shows at once (2026-10-29)

The person: *"i believe that flyout background does not properly update"*; *"the theming with the colors and material
theme currently is a little bit all over the place, it grew over time. i want you to properly audit all the surfaces
that you can customize and where there is an inheritance structure … it should bascially be able to range from very
simple (i just select a general theme like terminator or matrix etc.) to very specific where you can set the border
color of the individual widget. but still it should be very undestandable and simple to the user to configure."*;
*"color automatic should be renamed to inherited because that is what it is"*; *"folder appearance should have two
rows, one for the widgets inside and one for the folder face"*; *"in an easy way you should also be able to set the
folder outline and folder background color"*.

**What it was.** Each layout had two palettes side by side, the taskbar's (§334: background, card, outline, highlight,
separator, menus) and the folders' (background, card, outline, highlight, separator), with no link between them: an
orange card for the layout reached no folder line, "Flyout background" coloured menus and widget flyouts but not the
folders, a folder's background was a second background, the dividers' colour a second separator colour. Nothing
coloured a flyout's rim, one folder's panel, the text or the accent, so a green-on-black look could not be had. A
colour row said "Automatic" whether it followed Windows or the level above, never what it came to.

**Nine roles** (`ColorRole`, `ColorRoles`), each one thing wherever it is set: **Taskbar background** (the bar), **Flyout
background** (every panel: menus, widget flyouts, quick settings, folders), **Widget cards** (on the bar and as a
folder's lines), **Card outline**, **Flyout outline** (every panel's rim), **Separators** (the bar's and the folders'
dividers), **Highlight** (under the pointer, the open app's button, the open folder's face, a lit line or menu row),
**Text color** (Karpo's text and glyphs; the quieter ones are it, fainter by Windows' own steps) and **Accent color**
(on and chosen; every shade of Windows' accent while Inherited). Material and opacity stay how the bar and the folders
are made (`layouts[].look`, `layouts[].folders`).

**One chain** (`Palette.Over` all the way): Windows' own → the layout's **theme** (`Themes`) → the layout's own colours
(`LayoutLook.Colors`) → for the roles a folder or a widget may have, the folder's and the widget's own. A bar widget:
its own card, outline, highlight over the layout's. A folder's face: the folder's own three over the layout's. A
folder's panel: the folder's own flyout background and outline over the layout's (`WidgetLooks.OfPanel`,
`FolderFlyout.Worn`). A folder's line: its own over the folder's look for its widgets (§375) over the layout's. Menus,
flyouts, the text, the accent and the separators: the layout's. High contrast over all of it, Windows' system colours.
Each level's **Inherited** is the level above's; colours stay a mode's (light, dark), and a theme with a mode of its own
draws in it (`LayoutLook.DarkIn`), its colours of one's own that mode's.

**Themes** (the simple end): **Follow Windows** (nothing set; the default, what Karpo always looked like), **Graphite**
(always dark, solid, Windows' accent), **Paper** (always light, warm white, grey outlines, ink-blue accent),
**Phosphor** (a green terminal on black), **Infrared** (a red display on near-black), **Deep sea** (navy, pale text,
cyan). Picking one takes the layout's own colours back in both modes, so what is picked is what shows; a folder's and
a widget's own stay (`BarLooks.WriteTheme`).

**At each level, one row pattern** (`OptionPickers.Swatches`): a colour row says at its end what it is set to, and while
Inherited says **Inherited** with a swatch of what it inherits (`OptionRow.Inherited`: the levels above, else about what
Windows draws, `ColorPalette.Windows`); its level Inherited first, ticked and with that swatch, None for a card or an
outline, the recent colours, the grid, "Custom color…". The text gets the other mode's neutrals before Windows' colours.

- **Layout ▾** opens on **Appearance**: **Theme** (the six) and **Colors ›** (the nine roles, Reset all), then the
  Taskbar's type, size, showing, material, opacity and separators, the Folders' material, opacity, separators and
  Open folders, and Behavior. The separators' "Line color" and the folders' own colours are gone into the roles.
- **A folder's Appearance ›**: **Folder background**, **Folder outline**, then **Folder face ›** (card, card outline,
  highlight, Reset all) and **Widgets inside ›** (the same, §375), then Reset all.
- **A widget's Appearance ›**: card, card outline, highlight, Reset all.

**A colour picked shows at once.** Two faults kept a picked flyout background from showing: the open menu was shown
again after a pick in the look it was opened in (`Flyout.Refresh` kept it; now `Dock.MenuAgain` hands it the window's
look as it is, `Refresh(…, look:)`), and the cheap path for a change of colours alone (`OnlyColorsDiffer` →
`Recolour`, bars only) returned before the open folder and menu were dressed again. Both that path and a change of
Windows' look now end in `Dock.Relooked`: every popup standing open dressed again in its window's look. A theme, a
text or an accent change is a build (the widgets draw those themselves: `Look.Ink`, the accent's shades,
`IslandStyle` keeps them), which re-dresses the open folders and the menu as before.

**The file** (no reading of the old words; the person's own file is converted once):

```
layouts[].look.theme                               new: "graphite" | "paper" | "phosphor" | "infrared" | "deepSea"; not written for Follow Windows
layouts[].look.colors.{light,dark}.background      → .taskbar
layouts[].look.colors.{light,dark}.hover           → .highlight
layouts[].look.colors.{light,dark}.menus           → .flyout
layouts[].look.colors.{light,dark}.flyoutOutline, .text, .accent   new
layouts[].folders.colors                           gone: .background → each folder's colors.{mode}.flyout;
                                                   .card/.cardOutline/.hover → each folder's lineColors; .separator → look.colors
islands[…].colors.{mode}.hover, folder.lineColors.{mode}.hover      → .highlight
a folder's colors.{mode}.flyout, .flyoutOutline    new: its panel's
```

Strings: `settings.appearance.custom.inherited` ("Inherited"), `…custom.flyoutOutline.header`, `…custom.separator.header`,
`…custom.text.header`, `…custom.accent.header`, `settings.appearance.theme.header` and the five themes' names,
`dock.edit.look.face`, `dock.edit.look.outline`; 30 languages. Account and calendar colours keep "Automatic" (it is the
account's own colour, nothing inherited).

Tests: `FlyoutBackgroundTests.AnOpenMenuShownAgainWearsTheFlyoutBackgroundAsItIsNow` (red first: *"shown again after the
pick: the panel is #FF1E3A5F, not the rose picked"*) and `EveryPathOfAChangeDressesTheOpenPopupsAgainInTheWindowsLook`
(red first: `Relooked();` not on the colour-only path); `SceneTreeTests.EveryRoleReachesItsSurfacesLive` (each role
changed while a folder and a menu stand open: the bar's tokens, the folder's panel, rim, lines and highlight, the menu's
panel, rim, highlight and text, the widgets' ink, the separators); `ThemeChainTests` (the chain level by level, the
themes and their mode, a theme picked takes the layout's own back, Layout ▾'s Appearance, each level's rows saying
what they inherit, the file); `WidgetLookTests.TheFoldersAppearanceHasItsPanelItsFaceAndItsWidgets`; `BarColorsTests`
(every role under its name). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `theme-<theme>-<look>.png` (each theme on a bar with an open
folder and its menu), `theme-own-<look>.png` (a folder's and a widget's own colours), `theme-roles-*.png`.

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Theme › Phosphor: the bar, every folder and every menu go green on black at once; Colors ›
says Inherited with Phosphor's green beside each; set Flyout background with a menu open: the menu and an open folder
change at once. A folder's Appearance: Folder background and Folder outline colour only that folder's panel; Folder
face › its button on the bar; Widgets inside › its lines. Follow Windows again: Karpo as before.

## 397. A folder open takes its bar's "+" aside (2026-10-29)

The person: *"dont show the add buttons on the taskbar anymore if a folder is open."*

In edit mode, while a folder stands open arranged, its columns' "+" are where to add; the bar's own "+" beside them
were a second set of the same blue buttons, for another place, under the folder's. Now the bar the folder is open on
shows none of its "+" (`EditView.FolderOpen`, `Dock.FolderOpenOn`; `Scene.ShowAdds` hides them as it does while a
block is carried — the room they take stays, so nothing moves). The folder closed, by its face, Escape, a click on
the bar or another folder's face, they are back.

- **In the same frame**: the bar's edit view is shown again where the folder opens and closes
  (`DecksFollowFolders` → `ShowEdit`), in the handler that shows or hides the folder; a folder switched for another
  closes and opens in one handler, so the "+" never come back between the two. No fade: they go and come as they do
  for a carry.
- **No blink on the press** (§387): the press on the face hides nothing; the release opens the folder and the "+"
  go once.
- **Only the folder's own bar**: a folder is a place of its own display — its dim, its edit bar (§297) —, and
  another display's bar is not the one it opens from; its "+" add to that bar, as before. (Every bar stays locked
  under the folder, §212: a press there closes the folder and goes on, the "+" too.)
- **A press where a "+" stood aside** is a press on the bar's room (`EditPressed`): the folder closes (§366), no add
  list opens. Narrator still names the bar's "+" and Invoke still adds at them (`Dock.Uia`).

No config change, no strings. A stage run's `stage-edit.json` lists the folder's own "+" (`"FolderAdd"`), and the
bar's (`"BarAdd"`) now in screen px.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AFolderOpenTakesItsBarsPlusesAsideWithoutABlink` (the real dock: a press held on a
folder's face, let go, the face clicked again, a click where a "+" stood; filmed over the bar, each "+" goes once and
comes once — before: "with the folder open on it, the bar shows 4 of its 4 "+""; with §387 undone the film says
"held down, the "+" 0 goes"; without the press rule, "a click where a "+" stood aside opened a menu"),
`SceneTreeTests.APlusLightsPressesAndStepsAsideForACarriedBlock` (`FolderOpen`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`film-pluses-open.png`, `film-pluses-close.png`.

By hand: edit mode, click a folder on the bar: it opens and the bar's "+" go, the folder's own stay; click the
folder's face again, or Escape: it closes and they are back, no blink either way. Switch straight from one folder to
another: the bar's "+" stay away. With two displays: the other display's bar keeps its "+".

## 398. A folder's contents go into a subfolder in place, with a way back (2026-10-29) — the taskbar's part superseded by §492 (2026-11-03)

The person: *"the folder widget should also change the contents inline on navigation and not actually open the
submenus on the left or the right."* A subfolder clicked in a folder's contents (§380) opened a list beside it, as a
submenu stands: out of an open folder beside the line (`PinFolderBeside`, the cascade of lists side by side), and from
the taskbar a list whose own subfolders opened lists beside it in turn. Now a subfolder's items take the place of its
parent's, in the same line or the same list, as a settings menu's level opens in place of its rows (§268, §374).

- **The line** (`FolderContentsLine`, `FolderContentsView`). A click on a subfolder's row (navigation "Show its
  contents") shows that subfolder's items in the line, the folder staying open and nothing opening. Its head is the
  way back: Windows' back arrow on a subtle button in the picture's column ("Back" its tooltip, the forward arrow where
  mirrored), the subfolder's name where the folder's was, its count after it; the rest of the head opens the folder
  shown in File Explorer, as it did the folder's own. A subfolder's row has a chevron at its end where it goes in, as a
  menu's row with a level; the dates stand before it. Back shows the parent as it was left — its rows at once, never
  "Reading…" first. The folder shown is the one read and followed, and an Automatic line is as tall as what it shows,
  growing and shrinking as it goes in and back. A file still opens with its program, the folder closing first (§380).
- **The keys**, with the line's focus: Up and Down walk its rows (past either end the folder's), the row in the keys'
  ring; Enter on a subfolder goes in, the keys on its first row, and on a file is the folder's click, which opens the
  file the keys are on; Backspace and Left (Right where mirrored) go back, the keys on the subfolder left. The pointer
  moving takes the ring away. A folder of Karpo's tells Narrator nothing of its lines yet, so the line's rows have no
  names of their own there.
- **On the taskbar** a subfolder's button of a folder's contents still opens that subfolder's list from the bar (a
  bar has no room to go in in place), and in the list its subfolders go in in place, in its one window: a head that
  stands while the rows scroll, the back arrow ("Back" to Narrator, a button) and the subfolder's name (the list's
  name to Narrator). Back — the arrow, Escape, Backspace, Left, the mouse's back button — shows the parent as it was
  left, scrolled where it was, the keys back on the subfolder left where they brought it back; Escape on the list's
  own folder closes it. Enter on a subfolder goes in, the keys on its first row. The list stays where it opened, its
  foot over the bar, its height its rows'. Every row keeps the chevron's room where a subfolder has one, so the dates
  line up. Opened again it starts on its own folder; a line keeps where it was gone into (a folder opens where it was
  left, §357) until it is given another folder.
- **One walk** (`Drives\FolderTrail.cs`): the folders gone into from the root, and what each level was left showing
  and how far scrolled; the line and the list walk it alike.
- **Two navigations.** "Show its contents" (one level: a subfolder's subfolders in File Explorer) and "…, all levels
  deep" (the cascade) are one now: once a subfolder opens where its parent was, depth costs nothing. The navigation
  is File Explorer or "Show its contents" (`PinFolderNavigation.Explorer`, `Contents`); the string
  `core.pinFolder.click.cascade` went from every language. The file's `"navigation": "cascade"` is a word no build
  reads (File Explorer); the person's own file has `"contents"` only, so nothing to convert.

**Gone:** `PinFolderBeside` and the cascade of `PinFolderFlyout` (`FolderCascade`, a window per level, its own window
class and procedure, the rows held lit, `ShowBeside`), the folder's `FolderFlyoutAction.Beside`, `OpensBeside`,
`AlsoInside`, `Hold`/`HeldLine`/`HeldPart`, `RowOnScreen`, and the line's `BesideFolder`, `Hold` and `RowBox`; the
dock's routing of a cascade out of a folder. `FlyoutHost.ShowBeside`/`BesideX` stay: the menus' submenus use them.

Tests: `FolderContentsLineTests` — `ASubfolderOpensInPlaceOfTheItems` (red first: the click was an app opening of the
subfolder, `App` for `None`; now the line shows Karpo's items, its head the back arrow with "Back", chevrons on the
subfolders, Back at once), `TheNavigationAppliesToTheFolderClicked`, `ALinesHeightFollowsTheFolderShown`,
`TheKeysWalkInAndBack`, `GoingInAndBackIsPictured` (folder-nav-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png);
`PinFolderFlyoutTests` — `AFolderLinesSubfolderOpensInTheLineNotBesideIt` (red first: the open folder answered
`Beside`, the dock's cue for a list beside the line; now `None`, the folder open, the Automatic line laid out as tall as
the subfolder's five items and back), `ASubfolderGoesInInPlaceAndAFileOpens`, `BackShowsTheParentAsItWasLeft`
(scroll, keys, Narrator), `AListOpenedAgainShowsItsRowsAtOnce`, `EachLevelIsPictured`
(pin-folder-contents-…png, pin-folder-inside-…png); `PinFolderSettingsTests.TheNavigationsAreTwo`,
`TheTrailGoesInAndBackAsItWasLeft`. The cascade's tests went with it.

By hand: a list folder with Files ▸ Folder contents on Downloads, navigation "Show its contents", height Automatic:
click a subfolder — its items in the line, the folder stays; the back arrow; the line's height follows. With the keys:
Tab to the line, Down, Enter, Backspace. On the taskbar a folder's contents with titles: click a subfolder's button,
go two folders in, scroll, Back — where it was. Right-click a folder's row in the list: Open in File Explorer.

## 399. A To Do list Microsoft refuses fails alone; every account's parts stay in its settings (2026-10-29)

The person: *"there is one error, invalid request. the settings for the account (which calendars / contact lists to
show etc.) should still be available although there might not be any widget that uses it yet."*

**What the error was.** The edit bar's one error (§394) was the Microsoft account's **Tasks** part: "Couldn't sync:
…: Microsoft answered 400: Invalid request" — Graph's bare `{"error":{"code":"invalidRequest","message":"Invalid
request"}}`. Calendars, contacts and mail synced. Not new with §389: the tasks have synced from the start since §87's
To Do; §394 only made the failure visible. Graph answers that 400 to a filtered read of some To Do lists (Flagged
email's; themia met the same on the lists' `tasks/delta`, and their plain `tasks?$top=100` read is answered), and
`TaskStore` read every list in one try: one list refused failed the account's whole To Do — no list listed, so ⚙ ›
Accounts › the account had no list to turn off, no to-do line could show any, and the error stayed.

**The fix, at both ends:**

- `MicrosoftTodo.TasksAsync`: a list whose filtered read (`$filter=status ne/eq 'completed'`) is answered 400 is
  read plain — `…/tasks?$top=100`, every page — and split here as the filters would have: the open tasks (at most
  2000), the newest completed (200). A plain read refused too stays the error it is.
- `TaskStore`: a list To Do refuses (a 4xx for its tasks; never the sign-in, the network or a 5xx, which still fail
  the account) fails alone: the other lists are read, every list is listed, the refused one keeps what it had and
  says why — on its row in ⚙ › Accounts › the account, in place of its count (`SyncItem.Problem`, a new optional
  field of sync-report.json), on a to-do line showing it (`TaskListState.Failed`, or its tasks with the stale mark),
  and as its own row of the edit bar's errors (`FaultSources.Accounts`, keyed by the list): *Microsoft To Do won't
  give the tasks of “Flagged email” (Microsoft answered 400: Invalid request). Turn this list off if you don't need
  it.* (`dock.accounts.taskListRefused`). Its switch is right under it; turned off, it is asked no more and the error
  goes. A refused list waits the online interval, not the minute a failure waits: asking again sooner hears the
  same. Where To Do refuses the lists themselves, the account's Tasks say so (`dock.accounts.taskListsRefused`).

**The account's settings without a widget.** ⚙ › Accounts › an account lists every calendar, address book, inbox and
To Do list with its switch whatever is placed: PimSync syncs every part of every account from the dock's start
(§389), and the menu reads what it synced (`SyncReport`, `AccountSyncRows.Menu`). What hid the To Do lists was the
read above. The switches are one setting in one place — an account's `off` in accounts.json (`AccountBook.SetSynced`);
since §351 no widget has a copy of it, a widget that shows what the accounts hold links here ("Manage accounts").
An error's row still opens ⚙ › Accounts, where the account's submenu is one click on.

Strings: `dock.accounts.taskListRefused`, `dock.accounts.taskListsRefused`, in 30 languages. No config change;
sync-report.json gains an optional `problem` on an item, written by the dock itself.

Tests: `ToDoTests.AListGraphWillNotFilterIsReadPlainAndSplitHere`, `AListRefusedReadPlainTooStaysRefused`;
`TaskStoreTests.AListToDoRefusesFailsAloneAndCanBeTurnedOff` (the others read, every list listed with its switch,
the refused row's words and its error row, off: not asked and no error);
`PimSyncTests.WithNoWidgetTheAccountListsEveryPartWithItsSwitch`.

By hand: edit mode — the "invalid request" error is gone, or (if Microsoft refuses a list's plain read too) is a row
naming the list. ⚙ › Accounts › the Microsoft account: under Tasks every To Do list with its count and switch.

## 400. The Layout menu: the layout's bars, then Appearance, Folders and Behavior (2026-10-29)

The person: *"improve the "layout" menu. right now you have to scroll on the first level and it is not that well
structured."*

**What was wrong.** Layout ▾ (§352, §396) had everything of the layout on its first level, in four sections under
their headings: Appearance (Theme, Colors ›), Taskbar (Type, Size, Show, Material, Opacity, Taskbar separators ›),
Folders (Material, Opacity, Folder separators ›, Open folders), Behavior (Combine, Window previews, Show windows from,
Open widget flyouts) — 1021 px of rows in the 653 px a configuration menu has (§288) at 2560×1440 150 %: half of it a
scroll away, two "Material" rows on one level.

**Now** (`BarLooks.LayoutRows`), as Windows' Settings puts a page's rows behind a few:

`Type › · Size − 48 px + · Show › │ Appearance › · Folders › · Behavior ›`

- The layout's bars first: Type, Size, Show (a Top and bottom's two bars each, named, §364). No headings — the menu's
  name says whose they are ("Layout · Work").
- Ruled off, its pages, each a level of its own (`OptionRowKind.Level`; keys `BarLooks.AppearancePage`,
  `FoldersPage`, `BehaviourPage`, the keys the headings had):
  - **Appearance** — Theme, Colors › (the nine roles and Reset all, `BarLooks.ColorRows`, §396), then how the taskbar
    is made: Material, Opacity (where the material has one), Taskbar separators › (`BarLooks.Looks`).
  - **Folders** — Material, Opacity, Folder separators ›, Open folders: the very rows of the folder room's right
    click (`BarLooks.Appearance(…, Surface.Folders)`), keyed apart by `FoldersKey` as before.
  - **Behavior** — Combine, Window previews, Show windows from, Open widget flyouts (`BarLooks.Behaviour`, whose rows
    no longer carry a group of their own).
- The right click on the bar (`LooksScope.All`) has the same under "Layout" (`dock.edit.layout`), after "This display"
  — the edit bar's two crumbs' cut.
- Every setting once, row keys unchanged. Gone: the headings `AppearanceHeading`, `FoldersHeading`,
  `BehaviourHeading`. The layouts themselves stay in Display ▾ (§361). No config change, no new strings.

**A level deep opens with the levels over it.** A separator's "Taskbar separators ↗" and a divider's "Folder
separators ↗" (§351) land on Layout ▾ › Appearance › Taskbar separators and Layout ▾ › Folders › Folder separators:
`Flyout.OpenLevel` opens a row's level wherever it stands, the levels above it first (`PathTo`), Back going up one at a
time. `EditEntries.Landing` keeps its keys.

Tests: `LayoutMenuTests` — `TheLayoutMenuIsItsBarsThenItsPages` (the first level, a Top and bottom's, the right
click's), `EachPageHoldsWhatItSays` (Appearance starts with Theme, Colors), `TheLayoutMenusFirstLevelNeedsNoScroll`
(under its crumb at 2560×1440 150 % and 100 %, 1920×1080 125 %, Taskbar and Top and bottom, and the right click's:
red before, "2560×1440 at 150 %, Taskbar, Layout: 1021 px of rows in 653"), `ALevelDeepInTheMenuOpensWithItsLevelsAbove`
(red before: depth 0). `BarLooksTests`, `ThemeChainTests`, `KarpoMenuGeneralTests`, `KarpoMenuTests`,
`EditEntriesTests`, `ArrangedFolderStandsTests` (the keys walked) and `EveryMenuSheet` read the pages. Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `editbar-layout-`, `editbar-layout-topbottom-`, `editbar-layout-appearance|folders|behaviour-<dark|light>-150.png`,
`bar-looks-dark.png`, `theme-*.png` (the Appearance page and its Colors).

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾: six rows, nothing to scroll; each page opens and goes back. A separator's "Taskbar
separators ↗" opens Layout ▾ on Appearance › Taskbar separators; Back twice is the menu's top. Right click on the bar:
This display, then Layout, the same six.

## 401. One style for every widget, the structure: every line built from the kit's blocks (2026-10-29)

The person, after §388 landed: *"the style is basically the same as before. the screenshots / mockups you showed me at
the beginning i believe had bigger changes in them."* They were right: §388 put in the kit's tokens (sizes, weights,
the accent's rules, the one Status) but each kind still laid itself out by hand. The mockups (the proposal's
`time-`, `places-`, `states-` and `system-before-after.png`) show the structure: every line a stack of the same
blocks, every name at the text edge, every reading on the trailing gutter, one row height, no blank areas.

**The blocks** (`Karpo.Dock\Islands\LineKit.cs`, drawn on a `LineSketch`, so one pass lays out, draws and writes down
where each piece stood; hit targets come from the boxes they return):
- `LineRow` — the *Row*: the glyph (16) in the list's leading column on the gutter, the name (Body) at the text edge,
  a caption (Caption, secondary) under it, the reading (`RowReading.Value` 20 semibold, `Body`, or `Meta` 12
  secondary) and the controls (`RowControl`: a `LineButton` of the three kinds, or room the line draws in itself — a
  switch, the art) against the trailing gutter. 40 DIP, 52 with a caption; its pieces stand on its middle; the reading
  wins, the name and caption are cut. A strong name makes it the *Header*; a `Marker` (an event's colour) or the
  reading on the name's line makes it one of the *Items*. `LineRow.Join` joins a caption's parts with " · ".
- `LineHero` — the *Hero*: the Feature glyph (24), the value in the Hero 28 (Display 40 for a time) at the text edge,
  a status in the Body's secondary ink beside it on its baseline, caption lines under it; on the gutter without a glyph
  for a time that heads its line (the clock).
- `LineMeter` — the meter, 4 DIP, a pill, from the text edge to the trailing gutter.
- `LineStatus` (§388) — the Status, unchanged.
The refresh button is the kit's subtle icon button: the Row glyph, 16, on a 24 DIP plate (12 on 20 before).

**Each kind on them** (the proposal's "What each kind becomes"):
- *Timer, focus, stopwatch*: one Row at every height — glyph, name, the time in the Value ("5 min", the unit no longer
  a caption), subtle − + (the stopwatch's lap and reset), the accent start on the trailing gutter; running, a meter
  under the words; the stopwatch's laps 32 DIP rows under it. No stepper row, no "▶ Focus" row. The timer keeps its
  − + (the mockup's has none; it had them before). `FocusLine`, `TimerCard`, `StopwatchClockCard`, `ClockAppPaint`
  and the countdown card's layouts went.
- *Alarm*: a Row with its caption ("Off · Weekdays", "Rings in 21 h · Weekdays", "Ringing"), the time in the Value,
  the switch on the gutter; Snooze and Dismiss in its place while it rings. 52 DIP, automatic. Off, its time is grey.
- *Clock*: the time in the Display on the gutter over the date (secondary), the analog face kept at the trailing
  side (the proposal: the mockup only left it out), sized to the two; about two rows, automatic.
- *Agenda*: a Header (the calendar's glyph, "Wednesday 23 September" strong, the refresh) over its events as Items —
  the calendar's colour in the leading column, the title at the text edge, when under it with a later day said first
  ("Tomorrow · 08:00–09:00", as the approved mockup has it, in place of §378's heading per day). Taller than its
  events it scrolls them under the header. *A meeting* is the same item with Join at its end.
- *Now playing*: a Row — the title over the artist at the text edge, previous/play/next subtle, a 40 DIP cover on the
  trailing gutter; taller, the timeline and the app's row. 52 DIP, automatic.
- *A drive, a network drive*: a Row with its caption ("Local disk · 512 of 931 GB used"), "419 GB free" at its end,
  the meter under it from the text edge; 64 DIP, automatic. `DriveHeader` went. *A removable device*: a Row with its
  caption and a standard "Eject"; nothing plugged in, the Status.
- *The weather*: a Header (the place's pin, the place strong, "15 min ago", the refresh) over a Hero (the condition's
  Feature glyph, the temperature, the condition beside it, "Feels like · High · Low" under it); taller, the hours,
  then the days as rows. Automatic at header and hero (107 DIP; four rows, 159, before). The trend arrow went.
  `WeatherHeader` went.
- *Air quality*: a Row ("Air quality", "Fair · 23"); taller, its gauge, pollutants, pollen and hours. *Tides*: a Row
  with its caption ("Rising · High 17:32 · 2.4 m", "0.1 m") over the curve edge to edge; the place-and-age header and
  the turn columns went (the age is in the refresh's tooltip). *The sun*: the kit's rows, times in the Body, notes as
  captions. *Earthquakes*: a Header ("Earthquakes", "Zürich · Within 2,000 km", the refresh) over Items, or over one
  Status row with nothing to list (two rows automatic then, as the mockup draws it). All automatic.
- *The battery*: a Row with its caption ("On battery · About 3 h 17 min remaining", "76%") and the meter; taller, energy
  saver and the power mode as captions. *Security*: a Row with its caption (where it stands over who is in charge, the
  shield in the accent while protected, no accent plate); taller, a Row per protection. Both automatic.
- *Mail, a feed*: a Header (glyph, name strong, "3 unread", the refresh) over Items at the text edge, 52 DIP, the age on
  the name's line, unread strong. *A graph line* of two rows: the Row over its graph as a band, edge to edge, no longer
  behind the words ("Peak" went from the row). *Notifications*: the app's picture in the leading column.
- *Nothing to show is one row*: a camera with no picture, one taskbar layout, no VPN connection — the Status, and an
  automatic line of it one row (the camera starts automatic and grows to its picture when one comes).

**The ratchet** (`LineStyleTests`) holds the blocks' anatomy too: a row's glyph in the leading column (a Feature glyph
up to the text edge), and whatever ends a row in its trailing half — a reading, a button's plate, a switch, an icon
button — on the trailing gutter. The readings' details and a footer count as grids, a clock face's hands and ticks are
no row's end. The allowlist went from 41 (§388's 17 and what the anatomy found) to 16, every one documented: a badge
on a glyph's corner (`Hibernate`, `SoundMixer`, `Wifi`), the note's toolbar (`Note`), a chart's labels at the points
they name (the sun's arc and day bar, the tides' turns), Bluetooth's level text in its fixed slot, the volume's level
before its ">".

**Heights.** A line whose blocks are not whole rows starts Automatic, as tall as its blocks: the battery, Security, the
clock, the alarm, now playing, the drives, the weather, the air, the tides, the sun's times, the camera. A person's own
fixed heights are kept. The person's file holds the clock lines at fixed 3 rows (drawn fine, the face larger) and the
drive lines at fixed 3 (about 54 DIP of air under the meter); the test fixture `PersonsLayouts.json` has them
automatic. The weather preset's conditions are fixed at 4 rows (the header, the hero and today's row).

Tests: `TimeAnatomyTests`, `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests`, `PlacesAnatomyTests`, `StatusRowTests` (red first: the timer
48 px and not 40, the focus's glyph and name off their columns, the alarm 76 px; the agenda's glyph at 340 not 24, the
media title at 12, a drive 118 px not 64, the eject without a plate; the weather 148 px, air, tides and sun with no
automatic height; the camera given 200 px for one row, the layouts 48, VPN 52); `AutomaticHeightTests`,
`AgendaColumnTests.ALaterDayIsSaidInItsEventsCaption`, `MailCardTests`, `NewsPresetTests`, `RemovableHeightTests`,
`LineStyleTests`. `StyleScenesPictures` draws the four mockup scenes as Karpo draws them, dark and light, at 150 %.

By hand: a folder of each scene. The timers, the stopwatch and the alarm one row each, start on the right; the clock's
time large on the gutter beside its face; the agenda a header over its events; the drives a row and a meter; the
weather a header over the temperature; an empty or unreachable widget one row. Whether the agenda's day in each
event's caption reads as well as the day headings did; whether mail's and the feed's items at the text edge (44)
