## 402. The edit bar starts every edit mode at its own spot; no edit bar stands aside (2026-10-29) — always at its own spot since §630 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the edit bar should go back to the original position after a reentering of the edit mode."*

- **Where it was dragged lasts the edit session** (§395): through menus, a folder opening and closing, a widget
  selected, Undo; edit mode left — Done, Escape, anything (`EndEdit`) — and begun again (`BeginEdit`), each display's
  edit bar stands at its own spot (§296) again. The places are the dock's `deckMoves` (display id → `EditDeckAt`),
  forgotten as edit mode begins and ends, as where its folders were left is (`folderMemories`, §357).
- **Nothing written.** `EditDeckPlaces` and its `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\edit-bar.txt` are gone; Karpo no longer reads
  or writes the file (a leftover one is ignored). No config change, no strings.
- **No edit bar stands aside** (§390's leftovers): `EditDeck.Hide(aside:)`, its kept `aside` place, `Aside` and the
  `aside` fallback of `Panel` are gone — since §390 every display's edit bar stands while a folder is open, so only
  tests used them. `Panel` is where it stands while open, null otherwise; `Hide()` is edit mode ending. Comments that
  spoke of edit bars standing aside for a folder say what is true now.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.TheEditBarMovesByItsGripAndStaysWhereItWasLeft` (the real dock: dragged by 300, 250;
Display ▾ hangs from the moved crumb; a folder opened and closed: still moved; Escape and edit mode again: Display ▾
where it stood before the drag, no edit-bar.txt; before: "edit mode again: Display ▾ at -1690,271..-1536,325", the
moved place, not -1990,21). Adapted for the aside going: `KeptEditBarTests.TheEditBarDrawsOnlyWhatChanged` (the folder
closing: its crumb goes, nothing made), `EditDeckPlanTests.ItComesInAnimatedOnlyWithAnimationsOn` (it comes in again
as edit mode starts again), `FolderSlotTests` (the edit bar's step aside and back dropped),
`EditBarFolderPictures.FoldersOpeningAndClosingSetTheEditBars` (its check for `Deck.Hide(aside: true)` dropped).

By hand: edit mode, drag the edit bar by its dots somewhere else; open and close a folder, open Display ▾: it stays
where you left it. Done (or Escape), edit mode again: it is back at its own spot, on every display.

## 403. Dark mode, a toggle of Windows' own mode, on the bar, in a folder and in a toggles row (2026-10-29)

The person: *"create a dark / light mode toggle widget and add the toggle also to the toggles widget. (if not already
done so). it should toggle the windows style."* Nothing of the kind existed: Karpo read Windows' mode for its own look
(`Dock.ReadLook`, `SystemUsesLightTheme`) and nothing wrote it; no widget, no toggle.

**The widget** (`WidgetInfos.DarkMode`, `darkMode`, `QuickSwitch.DarkMode`): a one-button switch like night light —
the bar's button (`BarKind.DarkMode`, the name beside it as an option), a folder's line of one row with its switch
(`ListKind.DarkMode`) and a toggle of a toggles row (`Toggle.DarkMode`), one switch behind the three
(`SwitchData.KeyOf`), offered where the person picks the row's toggles (`Toggles.All`), not on a new row. Windows 11
has no quick settings tile for it, so it is named as Settings says it, "Dark mode" ("Dark mode on/off" in the add
list), with the sun half dark (E793) that Windows' own apps switch their theme with; its page is Personalization's
Colors (`WindowsPages.Colors`, "Colors settings"). In the add list's Quick settings after night light, and at home
in the screen's folder after it. Six keys in all 30 languages.

**What it reads, writes and follows** (`QuickSettings\Services\DarkMode.cs`): HKCU
`Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize`, `AppsUseLightTheme` and `SystemUsesLightTheme`
(0 dark, absent light, as Windows reads them).
- *On while the apps are dark.* The two differ only in Settings' "Custom"; then the apps are most of the screen and
  what "dark mode" means to most people, while Karpo's bars (following Windows) wear Windows' own mode.
- *A click sets both*, dark (0/0) or light (1/1), as Settings' Dark and Light do — from "Custom" it is off, and a click
  makes everything dark — and then tells every window, `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` with "ImmersiveColorSet" (on the pool,
  `SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG`), so Explorer, the apps and Karpo change at once. A refused write tells nobody and says so.
  Before the mode has been read, a click opens its page.
- *Followed through the dock's own notice*: the `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` the dock reads its look again on
  (`Dock.SettingChanged`) is handed to the widgets' data too, and the switch reads the values again, on the pool. No
  registry watch of its own.
- Karpo's theming (§396) is untouched: with "Follow Windows" the bars follow the switch as they follow Settings; a
  theme that forces its mode keeps it, and the switch still says Windows'.

Tests: `DarkModeTests` — the catalogue, the bar, the line, the toggles row and the add list (red first: none existed);
a value's meaning; on is the apps' mode, unknown until read; a click writes both and then broadcasts once, from
"Custom" to dark and back to light; a refusal broadcasts nothing and counts; before the read a click opens Colors; a
`WM_SETTINGCHANGE` reads it again, a power broadcast does not. A store and a broadcast of the test's: nothing reads or
changes this PC's mode. Registry tables in `TypedRegistryTests`, `SectionsTests`, `ListGutterTests`,
`WidgetMenuTests`, `VolumeAndSwitchTests`. Pictured as `dark-mode-bar-<dark|light>.png` (the button off, on, and with
its name) and `dark-mode-lines-<dark|light>.png` (its line off and on, and a toggles row holding it on, at 100 and
225 % text).

By hand: add Dark mode to the bar and a toggles row; click it: Explorer, Settings, the apps and Karpo's bars go dark
together, the button and the toggle lit; click again: all light. Switch the mode in Windows' Settings: the button
follows. With Settings on "Custom" (Windows dark, apps light) the toggle is off; a click makes both dark.
## 404. The sun's times a widget each; Add where there is none; the daylight left, in words (2026-10-29)

The person, 2026-10-29: *"the daylight, sunset, solar noon, sunrise, etc. metrics should actually be individual
widgets — if no vpn connection is setup there should be the add button — if there is only one layout there should also
be the add button, the text when there is only one layout should be shorter, just the first sentence or so. —
earthquakes should show if there are none. — daylight should not show the - before the remaining time but should say
1h 23min left."*

**The sun's times are widgets** (`WidgetInfos.Sunrise` … `Dusk`, `ListKind.Sunrise` … `Dusk`, words `sunrise`, `sunset`,
`daylight`, `solarNoon`, `dawn`, `dusk`). Each is one Row of the kit (§401) drawn by `SunTile` (`SunTile.Time`): its glyph
in the leading column, its name at the text edge, its note as a caption, its time in the Body on the trailing gutter;
Automatic where it starts (one to two rows), 52 DIP with a note and 40 without, its note left out on a fixed row of 40.
Its place is a weather widget's, as the sun's is. What each says:
- *Sunrise, sunset*: the next one, whichever day it falls on, and how soon ("07:01", "in 15 h 22 min");
  `SolarPosition.NextEvent(…, only)`, `SunDay.NextSunrise`/`NextSunset`. Inside the polar circles a dash and which it is.
- *Daylight*: today's length; while the sun is up how much is left ("1 h 39 min left", `SunText.Left`), else the change
  since yesterday in words ("3 min 10 s shorter than yesterday", `SunText.Change`), a polar day or night where neither.
  Why the change after sunset and not "Sun set 17:18" or tomorrow's length: the sunset is the sunset's own widget, and
  the change is what the row said before — only its bare "−3 min 10 s" read as time left. No sun value starts with a
  sign now; the noon's "−3°" (the sun under the horizon at a polar noon) is an angle and stays.
- *Solar noon*: its time and the sun's height then. *Dawn, dusk*: civil twilight's times, no note.
The sun widget is its picture alone: two styles, the arc and the day bar, over the strip of sunrise, daylight and
sunset; the times style, the rows under the picture and their switch (`WeatherOptions.SunEvents`, "Show the times")
went. The ready-made folder (`sunGroup`) is the face over the arc and the times the times style started with: sunrise,
sunset, daylight, solar noon. The add list's Weather page has a folder "Sunrise and sunset": the ready-made folder, the
sun, the six times.

**One reckoning per place.** Every line and face of one place reads one `SunDay` a minute (`SunDays.Of`, keyed by place
and zone, forgotten as the minute turns): the six times and the arc of a folder work the sun out once, not seven times.

**The file.** `"kind": "sun", "style": "times"` and `"weather": { "sunEvents": false }` are no longer written or read
(the style's word reads as the arc, the switch is dropped). The person's own file holds no sun line; nothing to convert.

**Add where there is none.** *The VPN* with no connection: its Status ("No VPN connections set up") has a standard "Add"
against the trailing gutter, which opens Windows' VPN page (`ms-settings:network-vpn`, `VpnChoices.AddLink`; Settings has
no address for its add dialog) as the folder goes (`SwitchChoice.Add`, `PageLayout.Alone(row, action)`). *The layouts*
with one: "The only taskbar layout" (its first sentence; "more are made in Karpo's settings" went) and "Add", which
once the folder has gone makes a layout and shows it on this display as Display ▾'s "Add layout" does — one path,
`BarLooks.AddShown`, refused past what the license holds (`LayoutsLine.TakeAdd`, `Dock.AddLayout`).

**Earthquakes with none** were already said by §401: the header ("Earthquakes", "Zürich · Within 1,000 km") over the
Status "No earthquakes in the past 7 days" (the line's window; the face's is 24 hours), the Status alone on one row.
Pinned now (`PlacesAnatomyTests.TheEarthquakesSayWhenThereAreNone`, green when written).

Tests: `SunTests` (`EachTimeIsAWidgetOfItsOwn`, `TheDaylightSaysHowMuchIsLeftAndNeverABareMinus`, the change in words,
`TheSunWidgetIsItsPictureInTwoStyles`, the preset, the add list), `PlacesAnatomyTests.EachSunTimeIsOneRow`,
`TheSunsTimesOfOnePlaceShareOneDay`, `VpnPresetTests.WithNoConnectionTheStatusOffersToAddOne`,
`LayoutsPresetTests.OneLayoutSaysSoAndOffersToAddOne`, `TheLinesAddIsTheDisplayMenusAddLayout`. Red first: no such
widgets; the daylight's note "−3 min 10 s"; "+2 min 14 s"; a new `SunDay` per line; no button on either Status; the long
layouts sentence. Pictures: `sun-times-<dark|light>-<afternoon|evening>.png`, `vpn-preset-*`, `layouts-preset-*`,
`quakes-none-*`.

By hand: the sun folder from the add list — the arc over four times; the daylight's note in the afternoon and after
sunset; the VPN folder with no connection, "Add" opening Windows' VPN page; the layouts folder with one layout, "Add"
making and showing "New layout".

## 405. One look, simple: a theme, three colours, an opacity and a separator style per surface, outlines (2026-10-29) — a separator is empty space, with no look, since §505 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"the styles are still way to complicated. i think there are actually too many customization options. i want
to make it more simple."* §396's nine roles, two materials, separator widths and rooms, per-mode colours and a folder's
face/panel/widgets-inside split are gone. What is left:

**The theme is the main control** (`Appearance.Theme`): Follow Windows (default), Graphite, Paper, Phosphor, Infrared,
Deep sea. A theme is a mode (null: Windows'), three colours and whether it outlines (`ThemeLook`, `Themes`).

**Three colours** (`Tone`: Background, Accent, Text; `Tones`, the file's `ChosenTones`), each Inherited until set, stored
once, opaque, for both modes. Everything else is derived by fixed rules (`ToneRules.Derive`), so it always matches:

| Derived | Rule (dark mode / light mode) | Without a pick |
|---|---|---|
| Taskbar | the background, adapted for the mode (`Adapt`) | Windows' |
| Flyouts, folder panels | background lifted 5 % towards the text / 50 % towards white; at 90 % / 85 % over the blur | Windows' |
| Cards | lifted 9 % towards the text / 70 % towards white, at 70 % | none (Windows draws none) |
| Text | the text (else Windows') made light / dark enough for 4.5:1 on the bar, the panels and the cards (`Readable`) | Windows' while neither background nor text is picked |
| Separators, highlight | the text at 54 % / 45 % (ControlStrongFill's steps); at 10 % / 7 % | Windows' while neither is picked |
| Accent | the accent made 3:1 on the bar and the panels | Windows' |
| Card / flyout outline | Outlines on: the text at 32 % / 45 % (dark), 32 % / 40 % (light) | none |

`Adapt`: a dark mode's background shines at most 0.06 (relative luminance), a light mode's at least 0.55, hue and
saturation kept; one of the other mode's (brighter than mid grey in the dark, darker in the light) has its HSL lightness
mirrored first. Every preset of the mode's grid is in its band and so stays as picked: a navy bar picked in the dark is a
pale blue of the same hue in the light, a bright red bar a dark red in the dark. The quieter texts are the text, fainter
by Windows' steps, as since §396.

**One chain** (`Tones.Over`): Windows → theme → Customize (`Appearance.Colors`) → a folder's own → a widget's own. The dock
derives every surface from the tones in force there (`Look.Dressed`, `Look.In`): a bar from Karpo's; a folder's button,
panel and lines from the folder's over Karpo's (`FolderFlyout.Worn`, `LineLook`); a widget on the bar from its own
(`Scene.LookOf(part)`, which its widget draws its text and accent in too); a line from its own over its folder's.

**Opacity, one per surface** (`SurfaceStyle.Opacity`, a 0–100 % stepper; Material is gone), mapped by `SurfaceStyle.Made`:
100 % solid; 1–99 % the blur under the colour at that opacity (acrylic, as Windows' own); 0 % no plate at all. Without
Windows' transparency effects anything between is solid, as Windows draws its own surfaces then (unblurred see-through
text over a wallpaper reads badly, and the person turned the blur off in Windows); high contrast is solid. Defaults: the
bar 70 (what Follow Windows always drew), a folder 90 (Windows' taskbar flyouts').

**Separators, one choice per surface** (`SeparatorStyle`: Line, Space, None; `SeparatorStyles.Of`): the room is the style
system's — a bar's line none either side, its Space 8 DIPs, a folder's 3 either way —, the line Automatic's hairlines.
The dot, the width and the room numbers are gone; no number had to stay.

**Outlines, one switch**: the cards and the flyouts outlined or not; a theme says it, Customize may say otherwise (written
only where it differs from the theme's).

**One appearance for all of Karpo** (`Config.Appearance`, the file's top-level `"appearance"`), not per layout: the menus
read and write the one whatever layout they are on. A layout keeps only its behaviour (`SurfaceLook.OpenOnHover`).

**Menus.** Layout ▾ › Appearance ›: Theme, Customize › (Background, Accent color, Text color, Reset all), Taskbar opacity,
Folder opacity, Taskbar separators, Folder separators, Outlines (`BarLooks.AppearanceRows`). Its Folders page is gone: Open
folders went into Behavior beside Open widget flyouts. The folder room's right click: Folder opacity, Folder separators,
Open folders. A folder's and a widget's Appearance ›, the same rows: Background, Accent color, Text color — Inherited with
the inherited colour's swatch, as drawn in the mode —, Outlines (Inherited (On/Off), On, Off), Reset all
(`WidgetLooks.Rows`). A separator's and a divider's links land on their row in Appearance.

**Live.** Every surface re-derives from the tones on every change: the cheap path (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`, now
Customize's colours and the recent colours) recolours where the windows' looks differ by their colours alone (`Recolours`,
the `Tones` set aside), and `Relooked` dresses the open folder and menu again, as §396's fix did; a text, an accent, a
theme, or a background or outlines made or taken back (cards made or gone) is a build.

**The file** (no reading of the old shape; the coordinator converts the person's own once):

```
appearance.theme                       ← layouts[default].look.theme (omitted for windows)
appearance.colors.background|accent|text|outlines  ← look.colors.{dark|light}.taskbar|accent|text; outlines where cardOutline/flyoutOutline
appearance.taskbar.opacity|separators  ← look.material/opacity (opaque 100, clear 0, else opacity); look.separators (line/dot line, space>0 space, space 0 none)
appearance.folders.opacity|separators  ← folders.material/opacity (auto 90); folders.separators
layouts[].look, layouts[].folders      → { openOnHover } only
islands[..].colors                     → { background (card; a folder's flyout), accent, text, outlines (cardOutline) }
islands[..].folder.lineColors          → gone
```

Strings: `settings.appearance.customize.header`, `…custom.background.header`, `…taskbarOpacity.header`,
`…folderOpacity.header`, `…outlines.header|on|off|inherited`, `…separatorStyle.none`; `settings.appearance.material.followWindows`
→ `settings.appearance.theme.windows`; the materials', nine roles', dot, width, room and face/inside words deleted; 30 languages.

Tests: `ToneRulesTests` (each rule; every theme and 2000 seeded random picks read at 4.5:1 / 3:1; the adaptation),
`ThemeChainTests` (the chain level by level, the themes, a theme taking Customize back, the same rows at every level, the
file), `AppearanceTests` (the opacity mapping, the separator styles, the file, Layout ▾ › Appearance's seven rows, the folder
room's three, hover), `BarColorThemeTests`, `LineRowsTests`, `WidgetLookTests`; live:
`SceneTreeTests.EveryColourPickedReachesItsSurfacesLive` (Customize's background, accent, text and outlines set while a folder
and a menu stand open: the bar, the folder's panel, lines and rim, the menu's panel, text and rim, the widgets' ink and
accent, the dividers). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `theme-<theme>-<look>.png`, `theme-custom-<look>.png`,
`theme-own-<look>.png`, `theme-opacity-<100|70|30>-dark.png`, `theme-outlines-<on|off>.png`,
`theme-live-<folder|menu>-<look>-150.png`, `widget-look-folder-<look>.png`.

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Appearance: seven rows. Theme › Phosphor: everything green on black; Customize says
Inherited with Phosphor's colours. Customize › Background a navy: the bar, the menus and the folders navy at once; switch
Windows to light: a pale blue of the same hue, dark text. Taskbar opacity 30: the blur shows through; 100 solid; 0 no bar.
A folder's Appearance › Background: its button, its panel and its lines; a widget's Text: that widget's words.

## 406. No alignment for widgets; the item size only where it changes the drawing (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the item size for a lot of widgets gets ignored. remove it from the widgets if it does not make a
difference anyways."* and *"the alignment settings for the widgets (e.g. the clock) should be removed."*

**The alignment went** (§201's lines, §253's segmented row on them). A heading, the date, the time and date and the
clock lined their words up at the start, the middle or the end of the line; since §401 every line stands on the kit's
anatomy (the name at the text edge, the reading on the trailing gutter), so their words stand at the text edge, always.
Gone: `Karpo.Core\Alignment.cs` (`WidgetAlign`, `Alignment`), `WidgetItem.Align` (the widget's `"align"` in the file),
the menu's Alignment row on those lines (`OptionRows.Align`), `OptionGlyphs.Aligns`, `CellIsland.LineAlong` and the four
painters' offsets (`HeadingTile`, `DateHeaderTile`, `TimeHeaderTile`, `ClockTile`), the words `core.align.start` and
`core.align.end` in every language. Faces had none since §277. **A folder's alignment stays** (§385, `"align"` inside
`"folder"`): the one segmented row left, with `core.align.title` and `core.align.center`.

**The item size, kind by kind.** Each kind that offered it drawn at Compact, Standard and Large with things to show:
- *Changes the drawing, kept*: the mail, a feed, the notifications, the clipboard, the contacts (their text 13/14/16,
  the room between items, the pictures), a day's events (rows 40/52/64), the to-dos, screen time's apps, the desktops and
  the top processes (rows 32/40/48 and their text).
- *Drew nothing different, gone*: the **agenda** (its events are the kit's rows, §401; only `ItemForm.Time` was read)
  — it keeps its Time switch, its size is no longer offered (`ItemOffer.Sized`); the **removable devices** — Large drew
  as Standard and Compact only dropped the caption the kit's row has, so they offer no item style at all. The layouts'
  rows read a size no layouts line could have; that went too.

The file: a widget's `"align"` and the removable devices' `"items"` are no longer read or written, nor the agenda's
`"items": { "size" }` (its `"time"` stays). No migration (§349): the person's own file was converted once.

Tests: `OptionRowsTests.NoWidgetHasAnAlignment` (red first: `AlignIndex` on the heading, dates and clock),
`ListScrollTests.AnItemSizeIsOfferedOnlyWhereItChangesTheDrawing` (every kind whose menu has Item size drawn with things
to show at the three sizes, each different; red first: "RemovableDevices: Large draws as Standard", "Calendar: Compact
draws as Standard", "Calendar: Large draws as Standard"), `ItemStylesTests` (the agenda's size dropped, the removable
devices without items), `AlignmentTests` (no line or face has one; a file's `"align"` on a line read as nothing; only
the folder's words left), `AlignSegmentsTests` (the folder's row the one segmented; `menu-align-folder-<look>.png`),
`AlignmentPictures.TheTimeAndDateStandAtTheirEnd` (the face, unchanged).

By hand: right-click a heading, a clock, the date in edit mode: no Alignment row; a folder's own menu still has its
four. An agenda's menu: Time, no Item size; a removable devices line: neither.

## 407. A click in edit mode opens a widget's settings beside it again (2026-10-29) — a click selects, the settings panel follows, since §520 (2026-11-06)

The person: *"the settings for the individual widget should show up besides the widget again and not at the top when i
click / select a widget"*. This takes back the widget half of §386. The folder half stays.

- **A widget on a bar** (`Dock.EditActivate`): a click selects it and opens its menu beside its block. The menu is
  `Dock.BesideMenu`, the same one a right click, the menu key and Shift+F10 open: away from the bar's edge where there is
  room, else along the bar (`MenuSides`). Space, Enter and Narrator's Invoke are the click. Ctrl+click and Shift+click open
  the menu where the widget ends up selected, the menu of all the widgets selected, the same as a right click on one of
  them (§214). A second click closes the menu (`EditClicks.Acts`).
- **A line of the folder open arranged** (`Dock.LineMenu`, which now takes how the line gets selected): a click, Space,
  Enter, a right click and the menu key all go through this one method. It selects the line, then opens its menu beside
  the line's card (after it, else before it, else under or over it). The folder stays open. `LineSettings` is gone.
- **A folder's face**: unchanged from §386. A click opens the folder arranged and its own menu hangs from Folder ▾
  (`EditClickAct.Settings`, `Dock.CrumbSettings`). Next to its face, that menu would stand over the folder that just
  opened. The person spoke only of widgets, and a folder's settings are the folder's, not a widget's.
- **Widget ▾ and Folder ▾** on the edit bar still open the same menus there (`OpenCrumb`, §352), for the widget selected
  alone and the folder open.
- **An error's row** (§394, `Dock.ShowWidget`) does what a click on the widget does: a bar's widget is selected with its
  settings beside it; a folder's line opens its folder arranged, gets selected and has its settings beside its card
  (`FolderFlyout.LineRect`). A folder's face still opens the folder and its settings from Folder ▾.
- **§387 kept**: a press does not pick a widget up until the pointer moves. A click lifts nothing and hides no "+".
- `EditClicks`: `OnBlock` returns `Menu` for a widget and `Open`, `Settings` for a folder. `Act(kind, menu, open, settings)`
  runs them in that order. `EditClicks.Crumb` is gone: only a folder's click opens a crumb now, and that crumb is always
  Folder ▾.

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.ALeftClickOpensAWidgetsSettingsBesideIt` (was `ALeftClickOpensTheSettingsFromTheEditBar`;
on the real dock: a click on Task view opens its menu beside the block and from no crumb, and a second click closes it; a
click on a folder's face opens the folder with its menu from Folder ▾; a click on a line opens its menu beside the line;
Widget ▾ opens the line's menu from the crumb; a right click on another line opens that line's menu beside it). The run
before the fix failed with "a click on Task view: the menu stands at -1752,87..-1272,747, not beside the widget at
-2143,1375..-2085,1433", hanging from Widget ▾. `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AWidgetsErrorIsOnTheEditBarAndItsRowOpensIt`
(picking the row puts the line's menu beside the line; the run before the fix failed with "the menu stands at
-1518,87..-1038,747, not beside the widget at -1572,1297..-1032,1357"). `EditClickTests` (`OnBlock`, `Act`'s order and
the dock's one path for each surface).

By hand: in edit mode, click a widget on the bar. Its settings open beside it, not at the top. Click it again: they close.
Click a folder: it opens, with its settings under "Folder ▾". Click a line in it: its settings open beside the line.
Click "Widget ▾": the same settings open from the top. Press Space or Enter on a focused widget: it acts like a click.
Pick a widget's error from the edit bar's error list: its settings open beside it.

## 408. The feed's pictures on the left, its name opens the site; the agenda's times always on the left; no tides disclaimer (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the rss widget should show the images of the articles on the left side where the others show the icons."*
*"for the rss the open xyz button should not be on the bottom but should be when i click on the title of the feed."*
*"the items in the agenda view when the time is not shown are way to spaced out. it should not be possible to not show
the time in the agenda view."* *"in the agenda view show the time on the left for starting and endtime. (over and under
the blue bar if possible)"* *"remove disclaimer, modelled by open meteo not for navigation."*

**A feed's headlines** (`RssIsland`). Each headline's picture (the feed's `media:thumbnail`, enclosure or image, fetched
and cropped square by `RssStore.Picture` as before) stands in the list's leading column, the kit's Feature size (24 DIP)
grown into the room before the text edge as a Hero's glyph is (`ListTiers.GlyphBox`), its corners a control's (4), on
the headline's middle; while it comes, where the feed gives none and where the item style hides pictures, the feed's mark
(its icon chosen, its favicon, the news glyph) stands there instead. A new headline's dot sits on the picture's top
corner, ringed in the list's ground. The words keep the text edge (44) and now run to the trailing gutter: the picture at
the line's end (2026-10-11) went, and the leading column is no longer empty.

**The feed's name opens its site.** The footer went: no "Open news.example.com" button, no foot band that stayed while
the headlines scrolled (`ScrollFoot`), a line as tall as its header and its headlines. The header (the feed's mark and
name, up to the stale mark and the refresh button) is the site's target (`SiteTarget`), lit and pressed as a headline
is, its tooltip "Open news.example.com"; a click opens the site in the browser as a headline's story opens. What the
footer said beside the button — why the newest read failed — is the kit's stale mark (`StaleMark`) on the header's row,
as the mail's and the agenda's: "Last updated 14:05 — couldn't refresh" and the reason in its tooltip.

**The agenda's times** (`CalendarIsland`, the agenda style). Its item style offers nothing any more (`ItemStyles.Offer`: §406 took its size,
this its Time); an agenda line's `"items"` (`"time": false` among them) is dropped.
Every event's row (52 DIP, the kit's item with its caption's line kept, `RowSpec.CaptionLine`) reads left to right: the
start time (Body) on the gutter on the title's line over the end time (Caption, secondary) on the caption's line; the
calendar's colour bar from the one's top to the other's foot, a gap past the times' column; the title a gap past the bar,
and under it the day where it is not the header's ("Tomorrow", "Thursday, 24 September") and whose holiday it is. An
all-day event, and a day in the middle of a longer one, says "All day" (Caption, secondary) on the title's line and has
no end; an event without a length has its start alone. The times' column is as wide as the region's widest time of day
(or "All day"), so no event's times move another's title; the titles of every event stand at one edge. The day's span
left the caption ("Tomorrow · 08:00–09:00" became "Tomorrow" with 08:00 over 09:00).

**The tides' disclaimer went**: "Modelled by Open-Meteo, not for navigation" (`dock.tides.model`, every language) is no
longer drawn over the curve; the curve starts right under the row at every height (`TidePlan` lost its `Model`).

Tests (red first): `NewsPresetTests.TheWholeLineIsThePanel` (a "site" piece found; the pictures at the line's end),
`.TheFeedsNameOpensItsSite` (a 58 px foot band), `.AFailedReadMarksTheHeader` (no stale mark);
`ItemStylesTests.EveryLineOfItemsOffersWhatItsItemsHave` (the agenda offered Time); `AgendaColumnTests.
EveryEventSaysItsStartOverItsEndOnTheLeft` (no start or end on any event), `.ALaterDayIsSaidInItsEventsCaption` (the
span in the caption); `TidesPictures.TheLineDrawsWhatItsHeightHolds` (the curve at 111 px, not 78, under the model's
line); `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests` (no start times on the gutter). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `news-preset-*.png`,
`rss-list-news-*.png`, `agenda-times-<dark|light>.png`, `tides-lines*.png`.

By hand: a news folder: each headline's picture on the left, the favicon where an article has none; hover the feed's
name: it lights, its tooltip says the site; click: the site opens. An agenda: every event's start over its end beside
its colour bar, "All day" for a holiday; no Time row in its menu.

## 409. Back from a page or a level, what is lit is where the pointer is; Quit Karpo at ⚙'s foot; New displays show first (2026-10-29)

The person: *"when clicking into a widget like the wifi one, when returning it is highlighted until i hover over it
again, this should not be"*, *"quit karpo should be all the way on the bottom and sticky"*, *"new displays show setting
should be on the top"*.

**The highlight left behind (the root cause).** A widget that lights its own parts (the Wi-Fi line's switch and its
">" part, §170) is told where the pointer is on it (`CellIsland.HoverOn`) and keeps that until told it has gone. The
open folder kept the widget it told by its *index* (`FolderFlyout.hovering`); a click on the ">" put the page's lines
in the column (`FolderIsland.OpenPageOf`), so that index named a line of the page, and the Wi-Fi line, out of the
lines, never heard the pointer leave. Back, it came back with its ">" part still lit, until the pointer went over it
again. The folder's own lit line already followed the pointer through a new layout (§357's `hot`); the widget's parts
did not.

**One rule, both places: back by the pointer, what is lit is what the pointer is on now; back by the keys, the row it
was opened from.**

- **A folder.** It keeps the widget it told by what it is, not where it stood: the one it leaves hears the pointer has
  gone wherever it is now, in the lines or out of them (`FolderFlyout.Gone`). Every layout (`LayOut`) asks the line and
  the part under the pointer again, where the pointer last moved to on the screen as the panel stands now
  (`PointerOnPanel`, rather than `GetCursorPos`), and tells the widget — not while a line is carried or a slider held.
  The pointer gone from the folder: nothing lit. Back from a page by the keys (Escape), the keys are on the line the
  page was of (`pageOf`), its focus ring showing, as Windows' own quick settings give them back.
- **A menu's levels** (§268, §392). The menu knows what drove it last — the keys (and a screen reader) or the pointer —
  and where the pointer last was over it (`Flyout.Driven`). Back from a level by its head, the mouse's back button or
  a choice of one clicked (§392's going back), the row under the pointer is lit, or none (`RowUnderPointer`); by
  Escape, Backspace, Left, Enter on the head or a choice picked by the keys, the row the level opened from, as before.

**Quit Karpo stands still at ⚙'s foot.** ⚙ Settings' last band, Quit Karpo, is its foot (`FlyoutItem.Foot`, §276):
under its rule at the bottom of the menu, the other rows scrolling over it, always in view (`Dock.SettingsItems`). No
new mechanism: §276's foot, which "Height ›" and "Appearance" stand in.

**New displays show first.** It is the display's rows' first (`BarLooks.DisplayRows`): Display ▾'s top row, ruled off
from Position; the right click's first under "This display". It is no row of the Layouts level any more (its
`OptionOwned.After` gone; the holiday calendars' colour keeps that).

No config change, no strings.

Tests (red first): `QuickPagesTests.BackFromAPageLightsWhereThePointerIsAndTheKeysStayOnTheLine` ("back from its
page, the Wi-Fi line is lit with the pointer elsewhere"; the keys' half "Expected (2, True) Actual (1, True)"),
`OneChoiceTests.BackByThePointerLightsWhatThePointerIsOn` ("Expected: Not 10000, Actual: 10000": the region's row lit
with the pointer where the canton was), `KarpoMenuTests.TheSettingsMenuIsTheSectionsRuledOffByBand` (the foot: "Expected
12 Actual 14") and `QuitKarpoStandsStillAtTheFoot` (Quit moved as the rows scrolled), `BarLooksTests` and
`LayoutMenuTests` (New displays show first; "Actual [BarPosition, Layouts, LayoutAdd]"); on the real dock
`LevelAfterCommitTests` and `MenuOpensAtTopTests` walk one row more to the layout. Changed to the rule:
`InlineMenuTests` (the head clicked, a pick, the back button: what is under the pointer; Add a face's and Height's back by
Escape), `MenuKeepsTests.AChoicePickedKeepsTheMenuOpenAndTheTickMoves`, `OneChoiceTests.APickInAOneChoiceLevelGoesBackShowingIt`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `editbar-settings-foot-top-dark-150.png`, `editbar-settings-foot-scrolled-dark-150.png`,
`editbar-display-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: the quick settings folder, click Wi-Fi's ">", move the pointer to another line, click the back arrow: the Wi-Fi
line is not lit; the line under the pointer is. Again, but move the pointer out of the folder and press Escape: nothing
lit. Tab to Wi-Fi, open its page, Escape: the focus ring on Wi-Fi. A widget's menu, a choice level (a country): click a
country: back, the row under the pointer lit, not the country's row unless the pointer is on it; the same by Enter: the
country's row lit. ⚙ on a short screen: Quit Karpo at the bottom under a rule, the rows scrolling over it. Display ▾:
New displays show first.

## 410. A folder's lines edge to edge: square, one card a section, only the sections round (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the widgets themselves in the folder have a gap between them, this should not be, there should bascially
be no folder background visible at all. the widgets themselves should also not have rounded corners, only the folder
sections should have them . (as they already do)"*.

**No room between two lines** (`FolderFlyout.Build`'s `Flow`). The 2 DIPs every line kept from the next are gone: a
section — a column, or the part of one a separator of Space only splits off (`FolderListPlan.Runs`) — is tiled by its
lines, the first at its top, each the next's edge, the last at its foot. Each line's edges are on whole px, so two that
meet never share a pixel and leave the panel to show through it. The landing bar of a carried line stands on the seam
itself (`MarkFor`), where it stood in the middle of the gap.

**A line is square** (`FolderFlyout.LineShape`; the line's shape a `CompositionRectangleGeometry`, which has no corners
to round). Its card, its highlight under the pointer and pressed are the whole of its box; the section's clip, as
rounded as ever (`CardClip`, the panel's `Radius` less its rim), rounds the top line's top corners and the last line's
bottom ones. Its shape stands past its box on every side, so its visual's edge — the box — cuts its fill exactly where the
next one's begins, without the soft edge a shape has. §376's inset of a line's outline by the rim is gone with its
rounded corners (`LineInsets`).

**Outlines** (Outlines on, §405): the section is outlined by its own rim, round its rounded corners; between two lines a
single hairline, the seam over a line drawn once, by the line under it, inside its top. No line draws one beside a
separator's line, which parts the two alone.

**Separators.** They stand only where somebody put one (a folder's divider), never between every two lines, so none of
the three brings the gap back. **Space only**, the folders' default, splits a column into two sections, its room bare
between them: the sections with rounded corners the person meant. **Line** keeps one section and draws its hairline
across it; its room now wears the folder's card (`OwnOf`; the divider stands on the section, `FolderPlan.CardRun`, in its
clip), so no panel shows there either. **None** is as §405 left it.

**Unchanged**: the edit-mode ring round a selected line and the keyboard's focus ring, the ghost of a carried line and the
lifted line's plate keep the panel's radius — marks over a line, inside it, as the bar's are, and so inside a section's
rounded corner too —; the "+" and width buttons outside the panels; drops and the slots beside the lists.

Tests: `FolderFlushTests.ALinesSectionIsTiledByItsLinesAndOnlyTheSectionIsRound` (two columns, each split by a separator,
at 100, 125, 150 and 200 %, Space only and Line, at rest and arranged: every section tiled by its lines — and Line's
separators — with no gap, a line's shape a rectangle past its box, outlined only on the seam over it; red before:
*"100 % Space: line 0 and line 1 stand 2 px apart, not edge to edge"*), `FolderSeparatorTests.ALineKeepsTheListOneCard`
(a Line's separator on its section: `CardRun` `[0, 0, 0]`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`, 150 %):
`folder-flush-<graphite|paper|deepsea>-<space|line>-150.png`, each at rest, a line hovered, and arranged with the top
line selected and the battery hovered.

By hand: Theme Graphite, open a folder: the widgets of a section one plate, no darker lines between them, square; only the
section's outer corners round. Hover a switch: the highlight square, to the section's edge. Theme Paper (outlines): one
hairline between two lines, the section's rim round it. Folder separators › Line: one section through the separator,
its hairline alone. Edit mode: the selection ring round the top line inside the section's rounded corners.

## 411. One set of rules for every menu: the ratchet, Find and Type fields, Height in the menu, one home for each setting (2026-10-29)

The person approved the menu audit (artifacts\menu-rules-proposal.md: 247 settings menus, 15 rules) on 2026-10-29: "go
with all your recommendations except for the point 5. the search fields should always already show stuff even if
nothing is inputted". So every recommendation holds — inline buttons only for a place or a direction, Height in the
menu itself, "Add a …" always right under its list, an account's form fields on the form, noun titles, the bar's right
click is Layout ▾ and "Display ↗", a page's row says nothing, "Add a face" uses the catalogue and its search — and a
search field always lists something before anything is typed.

**The rules** (Karpo.Tests\Menus\MenuRulesTests.cs holds each over every settings menu MenuCorpus builds: each widget
kind's, each face's, each premade folder's, Display ▾, Layout ▾, both right clicks, ⚙, the add lists):

| # | Rule | How it is read off a menu's rows |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | No setting more than one level below the first; its choice or field one more. A form counts as one. | no row on a fourth level |
| R2 | The first level never scrolls. | its rows fit a configuration menu's height |
| R3 | One control per kind: a switch for on/off; a choice a level that goes back; icon buttons in the row only for a place or a direction of four or fewer; a stepper with its unit; no radio buttons; no choice of two with "Off". | no Radio, Segments only for Alignment/Position/Direction, no two-choice level with Off |
| R4 | Every setting says its value at its row's end; an empty line of text says what applies, greyed; a row opening a page says nothing. | value on a setting's row, none on a page's |
| R5 | A pick goes back; Add goes back to its list, the new row lit. | PickOne on every choice's and Add's level |
| R6 | Find: empty, "Search …", a magnifier, something listed before anything is typed, the setting's own ticked first. Type: its words, no magnifier, Enter keeps them. | FlyoutField.Finds and its finder's rows for nothing typed |
| R7 | One word per concept (the glossary below); titles are nouns. | the glossary's banned words; no "How/What/Which…", "it", "you" in a level's title |
| R8 | Sentence case, "and" not "&", "Add a …". | |
| R10 | No headings in a settings menu: a rule, or a page of its own. | no Header row |
| R11 | "Reset all" the one name of a reset, last on its level. | |
| R12 | The switch that turns it on first; nothing destructive mid-level; Quit last. | |
| R13 | No icon twice on a level: a choice's options wear icons only where each has its own. | the person's own things and pictures aside |
| R14 | A value at most about 20 characters (24 in the test); a title never cut. | |
| R15 | Every setting has one home; anywhere else links to it with ↗. | the bar's right click is Layout ▾'s rows and "Display ↗" |

What breaks a rule and is still to be mended is MenuRulesAllowed.cs's Allowed, one line each; a line that is kept now
fails too, so it only shrinks (184 lines when it was written, then 92, 74, 60 and 0 as the phases landed). What a rule
leaves alone on purpose is its Exceptions, each with why: Windows' own Settings pages by their own names ("Bluetooth &
devices"), the layouts' and the tray icons' own icons.

**The glossary** (R7): one word for each concept, in every language the word's one string:

| Concept | The word | Not |
|---|---|---|
| what a widget, a folder, a layout or an alarm is called | Name | Label, Name on the bar, Text, Title |
| whether its name stands beside it | Show name | Show its name, Show the name beside it |
| how often it reads again | Update interval | How often it updates, Update online widgets |
| everything back as it was | Reset all | Follow Windows for everything, Reset colors |
| which way a slider runs | Direction | Which way the slider runs |
| what a pin opens | Target | What it opens |
| how long it keeps the PC awake | Duration | How long |
| where a widget is | Place | Location |
| which screens a brightness slider dims | Screens | Screens it dims |
| spatial sound's | Format | When on |
| how much of a share is owned | Amount owned | Amount you own |
| a way to add | Add a … | Add layout and show it here, Add an account › (a level of kinds) |
| what a face takes from its folder's line (§477) | Inherited | From the folder, Automatic, Linked, Default |
| which of a line's views it shows (§484: the sports line's) | View | Page, Tab, Shows, Show as |
| whether anything of Karpo's moves (§489) | Animations | Motion, Transitions, Folder animation |
| how fast it moves (§489) | Animation speed | Animation duration, Motion speed |
| how many days an agenda lists, today the first (§496) | Days ahead | Show events for, Horizon, Look ahead |

**The search field** (Flyout.Fields.cs, MenuSearch.cs; FlyoutField.Finds). Two kinds, told apart by what the field keeps:

- *Find* — a search over many things (a zone, a place, a share, a team, a country, what a pin opens, an action) or a
  filter (an icon picker's, Add a face's): it opens **empty**, its placeholder "Search <things>", a magnifier at its end,
  and lists before anything is typed — the setting's own ticked at the top (MenuSearch.Chosen), then what the person's
  other widgets use, then the whole list or the best suggestions: every zone, every country, a share's well-known ones
  (MarketFinder.Popular), a place's great cities (OptionFields.PopularCities), every league. Typing filters it. It opens
  empty rather than with its value in it because a value in the box would be the first search — the list filtered down
  to that one thing, or the person deleting it before they could see anything — while empty, the list is whole and the
  value is still there, ticked, first; and every Find field does the same.
- *Type* — a line of text (a name, a label, an amount): it opens with its words, no magnifier, what it suggests under it,
  and Enter keeps the words.

**Height** (LineHeightRows.cs): a folder line's foot is "Height ›" — Automatic, Fixed, Fill, a pick going back — and
"Rows − 6 rows +" (Max rows under Automatic), in the menu itself; the level of radio buttons is gone.

**Values** (OptionMenu.ValueOf, FlyoutValue.Implied): an empty line says what applies, greyed (a folder's "Folder", a
label's "None"); a search with nothing "None"; a row opening a page (Appearance, Formats, Accounts, Public holidays,
Karpo Pro) nothing. A choice whose words show an example after a colon says its name alone (OptionRow.SaidOf).

**What changed, menu by menu**: Display ▾ — Position its four icons in its row, the layouts under a rule and no heading,
"Add a layout", "Duplicate". Layout ▾ › Appearance — the colours on it (Customize gone, one level closer), each row its
own icon, "Reset all" last. Behavior — Window previews a switch, "Combine buttons". The bar's right click in edit mode —
Layout ▾'s rows and "Display ↗". ⚙ — Formats says nothing at its end, "Reset all" last under a rule; Accounts lists the
accounts, then "Add a Microsoft account", "Add a mail account ›" and "Add a CalDAV account ›", each form's fields on the
form (two levels from ⚙, four before); Public holidays: the calendars, then "Add a country"; a country's row opens its
regions themselves; Online's "Update interval". Widgets and folders — the glossary's words, Alarm on first, the volume's
Direction its icons in its row, "Add a face" a Find field over every face (groups ruled off) going back to the faces
with the new one lit, "Add a toggle" going back too, a to-do line's lists ruled off by source and named under each.

## 412. The agenda batched by day: a heading per day, no day in an event's caption (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the agenda view should show the date batched and not for each entry"*.

**Where it was.** Since §401 every event of a later day said its day in its caption ("Tomorrow", "Thursday, 24
September"), so a day of four meetings said "Tomorrow" four times; §408 had already moved the times to the left, which
left the day alone in the caption.

**Now** (`CalendarIsland`, the agenda's items). The events are batched by day: every day after the header's is a
heading of its own over its events — the kit's row (`LineRow`, 40 DIP), its name in the Body strong in the secondary ink
on the gutter where the times begin, set a gap lower than the row's middle so it stands with its own events and not
half-way between them and the day before's; "Tomorrow", then the long date (`CalendarText.DayName`), as Outlook's agenda.
An event's caption keeps only what is left: whose holiday it is (§265); the 52 DIP item, its start over its end at the
colour bar (§408), is unchanged. The line's height counts the headings (`ListHeight`: the header, 52 DIP an event, 40 a
heading), so an automatic agenda holds every day and the scrolling one scrolls them all.

**Today has no heading: the header is it.** The header already names the day ("Tuesday 22 September", a picked day's
"Tomorrow 23 September"); a "Today" heading right under it would say the day twice and cost a row. So today's events
stand straight under the header, the first heading is the next day that has events, and a picked day (§9 "Channels"),
all of whose events are its own, has none.

**An event longer than a day** stands under every day of it the agenda lists (it stood once, under the day it started,
or under today going on): on its first day its start alone, on a day in the middle of it "All day", on its last its end
alone at the bar's foot (it said yesterday's start over today's end); an all-day one of several days "All day" under
each. Within a day what fills it comes first, then by start (`Agenda` now gives each event with its day; `TimesOn` a
start or an end may be absent).

Tests (red first): `AgendaColumnTests.EveryLaterDayIsAHeadingOverItsEvents` (was `ALaterDayIsSaidInItsEventsCaption`;
red: "headings [], not one for each of 09/24/2026, 09/26/2026") — on the sample week (today, Thursday, Saturday) and the
busy one at 100 and 150 % and 100 and 225 % text, drawn as tall as the line says: one heading per later day in order, on
the gutter, each event under its own day's heading or today's under the date, its caption only whose; `.ALongerEventStandsUnderEveryDayItSpans`
(red: the conference once with "09:00" over "17:00" two days later); `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests` (the height counts a
heading's 40 DIP; a heading on the gutter is no event's start). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `agenda-days-<week|busy>-<dark|light>.png`,
`agenda-times-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder, Automatic and fixed: today's events under the date, "Tomorrow" and the later days as
small grey headings over their events, no day under any title; a multi-day event under each of its days.

## 413. The agenda's events one line each: the title and whose after it, the times in the Caption (2026-10-29)

The person: *"the entries contents should be shown in one line."*

**Where it was.** Since §408 every event was the kit's item of 52 DIP with its caption's line kept (`RowSpec.CaptionLine`):
its start (Body) on the title's line over its end (Caption) on the caption's, and under the title, for a public holiday
of several calendars, whose it is (§265). Most events have no caption, so the second line was the end time alone and the
rows stood loose.

**Now** (`CalendarIsland`, the agenda's items; `LineKit`). Every event is one row of 40 DIP, as the header and a day's
heading (`RowHeight`, one height for the three), with one line of content: the title at the titles' edge and after it on
the same line, in the secondary ink, whose holiday it is ("Autumn equinox · Switzerland, United Kingdom"), cut with an
ellipsis at the trailing gutter, the title first. The kit's row has it as `RowSpec.CaptionBeside` (the caption after the
name with " · ", in the name's size so the two share a baseline; the row stays 40 DIP); `CaptionLine` went, the agenda its
only user. Where the agenda shows a location is unchanged: it never did.

**The times stay start over end** (§408, the person: "over and under the blue bar if possible"), both now in the Caption
(12): the start in the text's ink at the bar's top, the end in the secondary at its foot, the bar the two lines and a hair
tall (34 DIP) on the row's middle, so neighbouring events' bars keep a gap. A time alone — "All day", a start with no
end — stands on the title's line; an end alone at the bar's foot (§412). Two Caption lines read well in 40 DIP at 100,
150 and 225 % text (the pictures), so the alternative, "09:00–10:00" on one line, was not taken: it would widen the times'
column by about half and take the room from the titles. The column is as wide as the widest time in the Caption (or "All
day"), narrower than before.

**Height.** An automatic agenda is the header and 40 DIP an event and a heading (`ListHeight`); an event that was 52 is 40.

Tests (red first): `AgendaColumnTests.EveryEventIsOneRowOfOneLine` (red: "the line 432 px, not the header, 6 events and 2
headings of 40 px each"; "when 0 "Switzerland, United Kingdom" not after event 0 "Autumn equinox" on its line") — a
holiday of two countries today and a long-titled one on Thursday, at 100 and 150 % and 100 and 225 % text: every piece of
an event inside its 40 DIP row, the title on the row's middle, whose after it on its line inside the gutter;
`.EveryLaterDayIsAHeadingOverItsEvents` (the caption on the title's line, not under it); `.EveryEventSaysItsStartOverItsEndOnTheLeft`
(unchanged rules, still green: start over end at the bar's ends); `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests` (red: "its height at
224, not 200", "2 of 4 times on the gutter in the Caption", "two titles 92 px apart, not a 40 DIP row"). Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `agenda-days-<week|busy>-<dark|light>.png`, `agenda-one-line-<dark|light>.png`, `agenda-times-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder: each event one line beside its two small times, a holiday of several countries saying
whose after its name; the line shorter than before for the same events.

## 414. The agenda's times on the right, on the title's line (2026-10-29)

The person: *"start stop should be shown on the right side and not on the left. also in one row / line"*.

**Where it was.** Since §408 every event's start stood over its end on the left, in a column on the gutter, the
calendar's colour bar between them and the title (§413 kept the two times stacked in the Caption, the bar 34 DIP).

**Now** (`CalendarIsland`, the agenda's items). Every event is the kit's item (§401) as a meeting's row is
(`MeetingTile`): its calendar's colour bar in the leading column (`RowSpec.Marker`), the title at the text edge and whose
holiday it is after it (§413), and when it is the row's reading against the trailing gutter, on the title's line, one
line, the kit's Meta (Caption 12, secondary): `CalendarText.Span` — "09:00–10:00" (en dash, the region's time of day),
an event with no length its start, "All day" for an all-day event and a day in the middle of a longer one; a longer
event's first day "From 09:00" and its last "Until 17:00" (the words the calendar's flyout already says,
`dock.calendar.from`/`until`, every language). A meeting's Join stands after it, the time a gap before the button. The
reading wins: the title and whose are cut with an ellipsis before the time is. Where that would leave the title not even
"m…" (225 % text in a 100 % folder with a meeting's Join) the Join is the camera alone, and if still too narrow the time
is its start alone ("16:00"). The row is 40 DIP as before; the day headings stay on the gutter.

**Gone**: the times' column (`TimesWidth`), `TimesOn` (start/end apart; `CalendarText.Span` says it whole) and the bar
drawn by the agenda itself; `FillsDay` is `Span`'s "All day".

Tests (red first): `AgendaColumnTests.EveryEventSaysWhenOnItsTitlesLineOnTheRight` (was `EveryEventSaysItsStartOverItsEndOnTheLeft`;
red: "start 1 "14:00" 12,83..39,99: a time left of the titles", "colour 0 56,43..59,77 not in the leading column, 12..44",
"event 0 "Autumn equinox" says no time on the right, not "All day""; then, at 225 % text, "event 3 "Quarterly planning…" has
no title shown", which the camera-alone Join and the start-alone time answer) — on the sample week with a long-titled
meeting with a Join and a three-day conference, at 100 and 150 % and 100 and 225 % text: no time left of the titles,
the bar in the leading column, every title at the text edge, the time the span, one line on the title's line, a gap past
the title and its caption, ending on the trailing gutter or a gap before the Join; `.ALongerEventStandsUnderEveryDayItSpans`
(red: no "time 0", it said "16:00" at the bar's foot; now "Until 16:00", "From 09:00", "All day"…);
`.EveryEventIsOneRowOfOneLine` (the time on the title's line too); `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests` (red: "words of 12 px at
12..40, left of the titles at the text edge 44", "0 times on the trailing gutter for 0 titles at the text edge", "a colour
bar at 56..59, not in the leading column"). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `agenda-times-<dark|light>.png`,
`agenda-days-<week|busy>-<dark|light>.png`, `agenda-one-line-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder: each event's colour bar, its title, and at the row's right end "09:00–10:00" small and
grey; a meeting's time just before its Join; a long title cut with "…" and its time whole.

## 415. The account forms say what a field needs again; Theme its own icon (2026-10-29)

Two things §411 left behind, the person's approval of the coordinator's recommendations (2026-10-29).

**A form's field says what it needs** (OptionAccountRows.FormRows, OptionMenu, Flyout.cs). §411 put an account
form's fields on the form, each one's name its box's placeholder, and with that the words that told a field apart
went: "Gmail and iCloud need an app password" was nowhere. They are back, as Windows' TextBox says its Description:
on a quieter line under the box (the row's `Detail`), in the secondary text, in line with the box's words, the box
still one row tall and its name still its placeholder (R4, R10: no heading, no row of its own). The mail form's
password "Gmail and iCloud need an app password", its server "Found from the address when empty", the user name
"If it isn't the email address"; the CalDAV form's address "The address the server knows you by", its password "An
app password where the server offers them", its server "A host or the server's full address". The mail address says
nothing (its old placeholder, "you@example.com", is gone from every language: the box says "Email address"), nor
the port (its placeholder the usual port). Every word was in all 30 languages already.

Tests: `AccountFormTests.AFormsFieldsSayWhatTheyNeedUnderThem` (each field's Detail, and on the menu the password's
item carrying it with its name the placeholder; red before: *"Expected [null, "Gmail and iCloud need an app
password", …] Actual [null, null, null, null, null]"*). Picture: `settings-imap-form-dark-150.png`.

**Theme its own icon** (OptionGlyphs.Theme). §411 gave Layout ▾ › Appearance › Theme U+E793, the glyph the Dark mode
toggle wears (§403), so a theme read as Windows' dark mode switch. It wears U+EF1F now, two colours swapped: a whole
set of colours at once, apart from the Dark mode toggle's and from its level's own colours — Background's palette,
Accent color's brush, Text color's letter (R13). The Dark mode toggle keeps U+E793.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheThemesIconIsNotDarkModes` (Theme's glyph is not `WidgetInfos.DarkMode`'s and no other row of
Appearance wears it, light and dark; red before: *"Assert.NotEqual() Failure: Strings are equal"*); MenuRulesTests'
R13 caught the brush, Accent color's, on the way. Picture: `menurules-layout-appearance.png`.

## 416. A folder's None separator: no gap, one section (2026-10-29) — a separator is empty space, with no look, since §505 (2026-11-05)

The person approved (2026-10-29): a folder separator whose style is None still kept the lines either side 2 DIPs apart
(`LeastGapDip`, space alone's least) and split its column into two sections, the panel showing between them. None is
now not there to see: no line, no gap, one section.

**No room, no split** (`FolderFlyout.SeparatorRoom`, `Splits`). A separator's room is its line and its space either side
(Line), its space both sides together (Space only, at least `LeastGapDip`), or none (None). Only one that `Splits` — space
alone with room — ends a section (§410's `Runs`); Line's and None's stand on the section (`FolderPlan.CardRun`), so the
lines either side of None's meet edge to edge, tiled as §410 tiles a section, the seam between them outlined once where
outlines are on. A list of nothing but separators is one card, the whole of it, whatever they look like.

**Two columns stay apart** (`FolderFlyout.ListGap`): a separator's room, never less than `LeastGapDip`, so under None
each column is still a panel of its own.

**Still there.** The separator stays in the folder (switch the style back to Line or Space only and it shows again) and
in the plan, on the seam, no room tall: at rest nothing of it shows. Arranged it wears space alone's rule — two
hairlines — across the seam and its grab, `DividerDip` tall, centred on it, so a click there selects it and opens its
settings (beside its grab: `LineRect` and a click's `Field` are where a line is taken hold of, `FolderPlan.Grab`), a
drag carries it, a lasso takes it (`KeysIn`, by its grab). Nothing moves between rest and arranged.

Tests: `FolderSeparatorTests.ANoneSeparatorLeavesOneSectionWithNoGap` (100, 125, 150 and 200 %, at rest and arranged:
no gap, the separator no room on the seam, one section, `CardRun` `[0, 0, 0]`, one piece; arranged its rule across the
seam and its grab round it; red before: *"Expected: 0 Actual: 2"* at 100 %), `TheSpaceReachesThePlan` (None's gap 0,
was `LeastGapDip`), `UnderNoneTwoColumnsStayTheLeastGapApart`, `ACardAGroupAndNoEmptyCard` (a lone separator one card
under every style), `FolderFlushTests.ALinesSectionIsTiledByItsLinesAndOnlyTheSectionIsRound` now over None too (red
before: *"Expected: 1 Actual: 2"* sections a column), `DividerEditLookTests.ArrangedANoneSeparatorIsARuleAcrossTheSeam`
(the real folder: at rest no rule; arranged the rule across the seam, a click on the seam the separator's settings,
selected its ring). Pictures: `folder-flush-<graphite|paper|deepsea>-none-150.png`,
`divider-edit-none-dark-150-<rest|arranged|selected>.png`, `folder-separators-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.

By hand: Layout ▾ › Appearance › Folder separators › None: a folder's lines either side of a separator one plate, no
gap, no line. Edit mode: a thin rule across the seam where the separator is; click it: selected, its settings open.
Line or Space only again: the separator back as it was.

## 417. A line lit under the pointer in edit mode without a flash (2026-10-29)

The person: *"when hovering over a widget in the edit mode it flickers quickly before the hover background is shown"*.

**Where.** Filmed (`FrameFilm`, animations on), the pointer onto a widget and off it: a block of the bar arranged and at
rest, and a line of a folder arranged and at rest, in Windows' look and in Graphite. Only the folder's line, arranged, in a
theme with cards blinked: half way through its fade it stood far lighter than at rest and than lit (Graphite: red 40 at
rest, 57 lit, 80 half way), then settled. The bar's blocks are lit by a plate whose opacity fades over a colour that stays
(`Scene.Apply`, `Scene.Highlight`), which cannot overshoot; at rest a folder's line takes its colour at once.

**Why.** An arranged line's fill is one brush whose colour fades to each new one (`FolderFlyout.Retained.cs`, `washFade`),
and the compositor interpolates a colour straight, its alpha and its colour each on their own. The hovered line wore its
highlight *in place of* its card (`FolderFlyout.InkOf`): Graphite's card is the panel lifted at 70 %, its highlight the
text at 10 % — half way, a half-clear light grey, brighter than either end. Leaving the line did the same backwards.

**Now.** `InkOf` lays the highlight (and the pressed shade) *over* the line's card, as the bar lays its highlight over a
widget's card: the brush goes from the card to the card lifted, its alpha and colour barely moving, so every step of the
fade is on the way between the two. A line without a card (Windows' look) rests at the highlight's own colour with no
alpha, so only the alpha fades. A lit line in Windows' look is as before; in a theme with cards a touch lighter than before
(the highlight over the card, not over the panel), as a widget on the bar is lit.

Tests (red first): `HoverFilmTests.ALinesWashFadesOnTheWayBetweenItsColours` (every theme, dark and light, rest, lit and
pressed each to each: the straight interpolation over the panel never past either end; red: "Graphite dark, None to
LineHover at 50 %: 80 in channel 0, the ends 40 and 57"), `.ALineOfAFolderLightsOneWay` (the real folder's window, a
switch's line hovered and left by `WM_MOUSEMOVE`, arranged and at rest, Windows and Graphite, filmed: every frame on the
way, `FrameFilm.Film.OffTheWay`; red: "hover-line-graphite-edit-in: f2 at 91 ms is off the way: 118.3 from the before, 69.2
from the end, the whole way 49.0"), `.ABlockOfTheBarLightsOneWay` (a bar's block as `EditHoverChanged` and `HoverChanged`
tell the scene; green before and after). Strips (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `film-hover-<bar|line>-<windows|graphite>-<edit|rest>-<in|out>.png`.

## 418. The agenda a little denser: the kit's compact row, 32 DIP an event and a day (2026-10-30)

The person: *"make the agenda view a little more dense"*.

**Where it was.** Since §413 every event was one line in the kit's row of 40 DIP, as the header and each day's heading
(§412): one line of 14 px words in 40 left about 10 DIP of air over and under every title, and a heading cost a whole row.

**Now** (`LineKit`, `CalendarIsland`). The kit has one more token, the **compact row** (`LineRow.CompactDip` = 32,
`LineRow.Compact(style)`, times the scale and the text size): a dense list's row of one line. Not less: 32 is a
button's reach (`LineButton.ReachDip`), what a pointer hits comfortably, and it holds the Body's line with the kit's
tight air over and under it at every text size. In the agenda:
- **an event** is a compact row (40 → 32): its colour bar, its title, whose, its time and a meeting's Join (24 DIP,
  4 over and under it) as §414 had them. The colour bar stays the title's line tall, so it follows the row with the text.
- **a day's heading** is a compact row (40 → 32), its name a gap (8 DIP) lower than the row's middle: about 17 DIP
  between the day before's last title and the heading's name, 9 between the name and its first event's title, so a day
  reads as a group.
- **the header** is unchanged, the kit's row of 40.
- **an event's row is the pointer's from its top to its foot**: a click anywhere on it is the event's (its menu's "Join
  meeting", as before), and now its Join lands across the row's whole height too, its button grown to a button's reach
  sideways (`LineButton.Hit`) — before, only the 24 DIP button itself (at 225 % text a 42 px button in a 72 px row).

**Height.** An automatic agenda is the header's 40 and 32 an event and a heading (`ListHeight`): a fifth less for the
same events. Two folder rows (77 DIP) now hold the header and the first event, not the one-row form. A fixed height shows
more events; where the line ends its last row is cut and scrolls in (ListScroll.cs), as before, but now mid-row, since
32 is not a folder row's step.

**Others that could take the token later** (not changed now): the to-do list's own Compact item size (`TodoTile`, a
literal 32), the stopwatch's laps (`StopwatchCard.LapDip`, a literal 32), and mail's and the feed's items if they ever
become one line (52 with a caption now).

Tests (red first): `AgendaColumnTests.EveryEventIsOneRowOfOneLine` (red: the line's height and every event's row 40, not
the header's 40 and 32 each; now also every heading's name inside its own compact row); `.EveryLaterDayIsAHeadingOverItsEvents`
(more air over a heading than under it; green before and after); `.AnEventsWholeRowIsItsHitArea` (new; red: "a press at
321,166 in the row 165..197 misses join 3", at every scale and text size); `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests` (red: "its height
at 200, not 168", "two titles 80 px apart, not a 32 DIP row"); `LineStyleTests.TheKitsRowsAreThreeHeights` (new: 40, 52
and the compact 32, never under a button's reach, a Body line and its air inside it, at 100/150 % and 100/225 % text).
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `agenda-days-<week|busy>-<dark|light>.png`, `agenda-days-<week|busy>-text-225.png` (new),
`agenda-times-<dark|light>.png`, `agenda-one-line-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder, Automatic and fixed: the events closer together, each still one line with its time on the
right; "Tomorrow" close over its events with more room above it; a Join pressed at the very top or foot of its row joins.

## 419. Today a day like the others in the agenda; its header the calendar's name (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the agenda view should show todays date just normally and not this special as it does now"*.

**Where it was.** Since §378 the agenda's header was the day's date ("Tuesday 22 September", strong, with the calendar's
glyph and the refresh), and since §412 it stood for today's heading: today's events under it, every later day a small
grey heading of its own. Today alone was said big and strong, in other words than the other days.

**Now** (`CalendarIsland`). Every day, today too, is a heading over its events, the same compact row (§418), the same
words (`CalendarText.DayName`: "Today", "Tomorrow", then the long date), the same ink and air. A picked day (§9
"Channels") is its own heading under the header as well ("Thursday, 24 September"), and a picked day with nothing on it
says which day it is: its heading over "No events on this day".

**The header stays, as the kit's plain Header** (§401): the calendar's glyph, its name ("Calendar", the widget's title)
in the Body strong, the stale mark and the refresh button at its end — what mail's, the feed's and the earthquakes'
headers are. It is kept, not dropped, because it is where the refresh and the stale mark (§408) live on every widget that
reads an account or a feed, the row the events scroll under (ListScroll.cs), and what names the line in a folder of many;
putting the refresh on the first day's heading would have made it move with the days and stand apart from the others.
`DateOf` went: the header names no day.

**Height.** An automatic agenda is the header's 40 and 32 an event and a heading (`ListHeight`), today's heading now
counted; a picked empty day the header, its heading and the message's row. The line is one row (`OneRowOnly`, the next
thing coming) below the header, a heading and an event (104 DIP): a header over "Today" alone would show nothing coming,
so a line of two folder rows (77 DIP) is now the one-row form, not the header and a cut-off first event.

## 420. A folder's contents back on its own folder once its folder closed (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the folder widget should not keep its state after the widgets folder opened or closed again. it should
show the root path again after this."* A Folder contents line gone into a subfolder (§398) stayed there: its Karpo folder
is kept closed with all it drew (§357), the line with it, and a line kept where it was gone into until given another
folder. Opened again, the folder showed the subfolder.

**Now.** As its folder closes — any way: a click away, Escape, its face, another folder, edit mode beginning or ending —
the line is told it is out of sight (`FolderIsland.Closed`) and goes home (`FolderContentsView.Home`,
`FolderTrail.Home`): its own folder, its items as they were left shown at once (never "Reading…"), read again and
followed as the folder next opens; its keys' ring and lit row gone. Opened again it shows its own folder, its scroll at
the top as every line's is at rest. Going in and back within one opening is as before. It is the rule the month and the
day already kept (`MonthTile.Visible`): what was stepped to is this look's.

**§357 is unchanged.** What it keeps it keeps for the subfolder too (`ViewMemory`/`RecallView`: the trail as it stood
and the items shown, `FolderTrail.Copy`/`Take`): a folder handed on to another window by an arrange while open shows
the line where it was gone into, and in edit mode a folder reopened in the same edit session is where it was left, as
its other lines are. At rest a folder opens at its start, now this line too. A line's own folder changed meanwhile
starts on that one.

**The bar's list** (a subfolder's button of a folder's contents on the taskbar) already started on its own folder each
time it opened (`PinFolderFlyout.Show`, `trail.Start`); unchanged.

Tests: `PinFolderFlyoutTests.AFolderLineShowsItsOwnFolderAgainOnceItsFolderClosed` (the real folder window: into Karpo,
closed, its own folder at once and as tall as before when opened again; handed on while open, still in Karpo; red
first: "Expected C:\Users\Ann\Projects, Actual C:\Users\Ann\Projects\Karpo" once the folder had closed),
`PinFolderSettingsTests.TheTrailGoesInAndBackAsItWasLeft` (`Home`, `Copy`, `Take`). No config change, no strings.

By hand: a folder with Files ▸ Folder contents, navigation "Show its contents": go two folders in, click away; open the
folder again — its own folder, at the top. Same with Escape and with another folder's face.

## 421. A page's whole head is its way back; a folder's contents open nothing but an item (2026-10-30)

The person: *"for the wifi submenu or bluetooth submenu or also the folder view there is the back button, but the back
button is only on the topleft, i want the whole header area to be the back button."* And: *"the folder opens in file
explorer when i click somewhere inside of it. this should not be."*

**One head, everywhere** (`QuickSettings\Controls\BackHead.cs`). Four heads had a way back, each its own: a subtle
36 DIP button before a quick settings page's title (`PageLayout.Title`, `QuickPageTile`), the same button drawn by hand
on a page's own head (`PageHeadTile`, the sound and accessibility pages), a hand-lit square on a folder's contents line
gone into a subfolder (`FolderContentsView`, §398) and a button on a folder's list from the taskbar (`PinFolderFlyout`).
All four are now one widget, the whole head row:
- **the target is the row**, edge to edge and top to foot; what the head carries of its own stands over it and keeps
  its own press, as a Windows settings card's switch does over the card: the Wi-Fi page's switch and refresh, Bluetooth's
  and the mobile hotspot's switch. No other head has any (Cast, Project, VPN, nearby sharing, the sound and accessibility
  pages' own heads, a folder's subfolder).
- **under the pointer the row lights in one plate**, its host's rows' plate across the head (a quick settings page's on
  the list's row columns, `ListRowLeft`; a folder's contents line 4 DIP in, as its items; the taskbar's list 4 DIP in),
  pressed darker; on the switch, the switch lights alone. Windows' back arrow at its start (forward where mirrored),
  "Back" its tooltip over the arrow; the title is its host's words over the plate.
- **Narrator** hears where it goes: "Back, Wi-Fi", "Back, docs" (`BackHead.Said`, `PanelAccess.Describe`).
- The keys are as before: Escape, Backspace, Left; Enter or Space with the keys on a page's head.

`PageHeadTile.BackGlyph` and the three copies of the forward glyph went to `BackHead.Glyph`/`ForwardGlyph` (the menus'
level heads, §268, use them too). No config change, no new strings.

**A folder's contents open nothing but an item** (`FolderContentsLine.Click`). §380 and §398 had a click on the line's
head, beside its rows or under them — and Enter with no row the keys are on — open the folder shown in File Explorer.
None does now: a file's row opens the file, a subfolder's goes in or opens in File Explorer as the navigation says
(§380, §398), a subfolder's head goes back, and anything else does nothing. That was the one way the line opened File
Explorer by itself (the taskbar's buttons of a folder's contents and the list's rows are items; the taskbar's stand-in
button while nothing is read is the pin's, outside a folder). File Explorer is the right click's: the line's menu at
rest has **Open in File Explorer** (`WidgetAct.OpenInExplorer`), on the folder shown — a subfolder gone into, that
one — opened as the list's folder rows open it (`FolderSource.Open`, File Explorer whatever else has taken folders),
the folder closing. No button for it in the head: the person asked the taskbar's list for none ("dont show open in
file explorer"), and the right click is where the list has it too.

## 422. The app playing on the now-playing line's left (2026-10-30)

The person: *"now playing widget should show the app that is playing on the left side."*

**Where it was.** Since §401 the line's leading column stood empty — "the art is the line's picture" — and where the
track plays (`NowPlayingSource`: the session's app's icon, or the favicon of a known site a browser plays it on) was a
badge, 14 to 24 DIP, in the cover's corner, and only on a cover of 40 DIP or more: never on one row, never without art.

**Now** (`MediaLine.cs`, `MediaIsland.Where`). Where it plays stands in the list's leading column, where every other
line stands its glyph (§401): the icon at the kit's Row glyph size (16 DIP by the text scale), centred in the column on
the first row's middle — one row, the row with its caption and the whole widget alike (`MediaLine.App`, the row's glyph
column from `LineRow`). Where no icon was found (an app the shell has none for, a site's favicon still on its way) and
while nothing plays, the note stands there, quiet while nothing plays. Under the pointer the icon names where it plays,
which the icon alone does not say: "Spotify", "youtube.com · Brave" (`CardTip`, the folder's tooltip, §359). The badge
went (`MediaIsland.Badge`): the leading column says it now, bigger and at every height.

**The cover stays on the right.** It is the track's picture, the icon the app's: two different things, and the person
asked for the art on the right (2026-10-11). Without art the cover's slot keeps its plate with the note, so nothing
moves as the art comes and goes; with no icon found either, the note then stands at both ends, which is rare.

**The bar's face is unchanged.** Its words start on the face's leading end and the art ends it (§96, 2026-10-11), its
length is the words' and the art's (`FaceLength`); an icon before the words would take a cell's worth from a title on a
28 DIP bar and add a third picture to one row. Not done; a face option could add it if wanted.

**Also** (seen in the pictures): one row with the room for "Hey · Pixies" drew "Hey · Pixi…" — the artist's box was the
two measured less the title, each rounded up, a pixel short of the artist alone. It reaches the room's end now.

## 424. The month scrolls smoothly, as Windows' calendar flyout does (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the month calendar should scroll smoothly."*

**Where it was.** The wheel and ‹ › stepped the month at once, a whole month a notch (§388, §401). In a folder the
step did not even draw the line again: only the next thing that drew it (a hover, a minute) showed the new month.

**What Windows does** (checked in WinUI's source, the CalendarView behind the taskbar's flyout): the month view is a
ScrollViewer over the weeks with a snap point on each month's first week (`CalendarPanel`'s snap point filter,
`GetIsFirstItemInScope`), so a scroll ends with a month aligned — its first week at the top, the six weeks a month
shows at rest. The heading is the month with the greater share of its own days in view, a tie the earlier's
(`CalendarViewGeneratorHost.UpdateScope`); the other months' days are dimmed. Karpo matches it: **it snaps**.

**Now** (`Calendar\MonthScroll.cs`, pure; `MonthTile`; `Islands\LineStrip.cs`):
- **A wheel's notch and ‹ ›** glide to the month after or before the one the weeks are going to, aligned, in 250 ms on
  Windows' decelerate curve (the bar's moves' `EditLook.Decelerate`); a second notch before the first has landed goes on
