  from where that one was going. Up is the month before, as before.
- **A touchpad** (a wheel delta that is not whole notches) moves the weeks by what it says, three lines of text a notch's
  worth as a list's items move (`ListScrolled.Notch`); 120 ms after its last move — a precision touchpad's own inertia is
  a run of small moves, so after the fling — they glide to the **nearest** month's alignment (the snap point Windows'
  manipulation ends on), which may be the month before the one heading them.
- **The heading follows** the month most in view as the weeks pass; that month's days in full ink, the others' quieter,
  as at rest. (Windows lifts the dimming while a finger drives the scroll; Karpo keeps it, following the heading, so
  nothing changes ink at the start and the end of every scroll.)
- **A day picked** in another month (a dimmed day clicked, the keys, Page Up/Down, Home) glides there too.
- **On the compositor.** In a folder the weeks are a strip of their own (`IStripLine`, `FolderFlyout.PlaceStrip`): 30
  weeks drawn into a surface once, under a window clipped over the line, its sprite bound by an expression to the
  month's property set ("top" − "y"); a glide is a key-frame animation of "y" the compositor runs, a touchpad's move
  sets it. The UI thread draws the line again only when the heading turns, the strip no longer holds the weeks on their
  way, the pointer lights a day, or a day is picked — never a frame of the scroll. The folder's quick tick asks the month
  (`Slid`) while it moves and settles a touchpad. Hit tests, tooltips and pieces read where the weeks stand at that
  moment, by the same curve; a day's target is its DayNumber, so a press and its release either side of a glide are one
  day. Anywhere nothing hosts the strip (a picture) the line draws the weeks where they stand.
- **A line too short for six weeks** (§166) shows the picked day's weeks of the heading's month, which turns half-way, so
  there the month steps at once as before; a touchpad's deltas add up to notches.
- Unchanged: today's ring, the day picked, the dots, the year view. Animations off: every move lands at once.

Tests (red first): `MonthScrollTests` (11: aligned positions, the heading rule, a notch's eased glide on time and never
back, notches adding up, a pan and its settle on the nearest month, a pan taking over a glide, a month glided to or
jumped, the ease, the calendar's ends; red: all eleven on a stub); `MonthScrollFilmTests` (films over the weeks, a
folder of one month, animations on: a wheel notch, a touchpad's small moves, the › arrow clicked — every film through
places between, never back, landing aligned, the heading the next month; red before: "before vs end 0.0 %", the wheel
and the arrow did not even redraw the line, end shift 0 not 160). Day clicks in tests are `MonthTile.Target(day)`.
`FrameFilm.Shoot` takes a `pumped` hook, the dock's timers a test's window does not get. Strips (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`film-month-<wheel|touchpad|arrow>.png` and `month-<wheel|touchpad|arrow>-line.png` (the whole line before and after).

By hand: the calendar folder — a wheel notch down glides to the next month (no jump, the heading turning half-way);
spin several notches fast; a touchpad's two-finger scroll moves the weeks with the fingers and settles on a month when
let go; ‹ › glide; click a dimmed day of the next month; Page Down; a month at 225 % text (short) still steps.

## 425. A pin's Target: a choice of kind first — App, Folder, File, Website, Settings page — each its own level (2026-10-30)

The person: *"for the pin widget it should be more clear to add an app, folder, website, etc. right now the user does
not see that he can add a website for example. put them under separate menus, its okey if it is more than two levels
deep in the end."* Target's level was one Find field over folders and apps (§292, §380): a website or a Settings page
could only be typed into it, and nothing said so.

**Now** (`OptionFields.OfPinTarget`, `OptionRowKind.Level`): Target says what the pin opens at its end — its name as
Windows gives it and, before it, its picture (`OptionRow.ValuePicture`; a value's words with a picture before them,
`Flyout.cs`) —, and opens the kinds, each a level of its own, the kind in force ticked and saying the target
(`OptionRow.Ticked`, `PinTargets.KindOf`, `PinKind`), the others saying nothing:

| Kind | Its level |
|---|---|
| App | a Find field, "Search apps", over Start's All apps with their icons (`NamedFinder`: by name only, words typed are never a target) |
| Folder | "Browse…" (Windows' folder dialog, `TargetBrowse.Folder`), then a Find field over This PC and the Recycle Bin (`TargetChoices.Places`), the folders the person's pins show and Windows' own; a path typed lists the folders under it (`TargetFinder`, §292) |
| File | "Browse…" (files alone, `TargetBrowse.File`), then a Find field over the files used lately — Windows' Recent folder, local files still there, newest first, 20 at most (`RecentFiles`); where Windows keeps none, the newest files on the Desktop and in Documents —; a path typed is kept |
| Website | a Type field, "https://…", opening with the address in force; an address typed is offered as its host with its site's picture (`SiteFinder`, `PinTargets.Site`: http or https, a host with a dot, localhost or an IP; a bare domain https's), words that are none say "That isn't a web address"; the sites the person's pins open offered under it (`OptionFields.SitesInUse`); Enter keeps it |
| Settings page | a Find field, "Search Settings pages", over the pages of Windows' Settings the actions line knows (`SettingsActions.Pages`, `PageFinder`), each with its glyph and its section; a pin to one is named by it (`PinTargets.NameOf`) |

A link of no such kind (mailto:, a game's) ticks none; its name still stands on Target. A pick goes back to the kinds
(each kind's row is one choice, §392), its row ticked and saying the target. A folder's contents keep their one level,
"Browse…" over a field of folders (`OptionFields.OfFolderTarget`).

**A website's picture** is the site's own, fetched (`Favicons`), so it may come after the row first asked for it:
`TargetPictures` no longer keeps "none" for a site, and asks again when a site's picture arrives (`Again`, from the
dock's `FaviconArrived`), the row waiting told then.

**A search whose words are its value** (a website, a camera's address, §331): Enter or leaving the field kept nothing,
since a line's commit carries no pick and the row kept only picks. `FieldPicks.KeepRow` now keeps what the finder makes
of the words (`OptionFinder.Typed`) where nothing was picked.

**Adding a pin.** Nothing opens on its own when a widget is added (the person, 2026-10-12: "when adding a widget it
should not open the settings automatically"). But a widget that still needs its one thing has its settings open where
that is set (`WidgetSetup.RowOf`, `Dock.WidgetMenu` → `OpenShownLevel`): a new pin's first click in edit mode, or its
"Set up", lands on Target's kinds, Back to the rest; the same for every widget that needs a field (a stock's symbol, a
feed's address, …). The row each field is was a test's table; it is Core's now (`SetupLinkTests` reads it).

**The menu rules** (§411). Rows stand three levels deep (the pin's menu › Target › a kind's field), so R1 holds. R4 —
a setting's row says its value — would ask a "None" of the four kinds not in force: those are documented exceptions
(`MenuRulesTests.Exceptions`, "R4 Target › App" and the rest); the allowlist stays empty.
`MenuConventionTests.ARowsDepthFollowsItsType` knows a choice of kinds as it knows a group.

Strings, in every language: `settings.pin.kind.*`, `settings.pin.app.placeholder`, `settings.pin.file.placeholder`,
`settings.pin.website.placeholder`, `settings.pin.website.invalid`, `settings.pin.settings.placeholder`; gone:
`settings.pin.target.placeholder`, `.folders`, `.apps`. No config change.

Tests (red first: "Expected [Target, Name, Icon], Actual [Folder, Name, Icon]" — the old single level — and a site's
picture never told): `PinTargetMenuTests` (`TheTargetLevelOffersEachKindItsOwnLevel`, `EachKindOffersItsOwn`,
`AWebsiteTypedAndEnteredBecomesTheTarget`, `ATargetIsOfOneKind`, `TargetSaysTheNameWindowsGivesIt`,
`PickingAnAppOrAFolderSetsIt`, `ThePinnedFoldersAndSitesAreOfferedFirst`, `TypingFindsAFolderOrKeepsThePathTyped`,
`WhatAPinNeedsIsTarget`; on a real menu `APickGoesBackToTheKindsSayingIt`: Spotify picked, then example.com entered, each
back on the kinds, ticked and said), `TargetLooksTests.ASitesPictureThatComesLaterIsShown`, and the pin's rows in
`OptionRowsTests`, `OptionFieldsTests`, `MenuPickersTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `pinpick-target-dark.png`,
`pinpick-kinds-dark.png`, `pinpick-website-dark.png`; `config-pin-dark.png` on the Folder kind.

By hand: edit mode, add a Pin: its first click opens on Target's kinds. Website, type "github.com", Enter: back on the
kinds, Website ticked; the pin shows GitHub's icon once fetched. Folder › Browse… is Windows' folder dialog; File ›
Browse… shows files alone. Settings page, type "display".

## 426. A separator that grows: Style Grow takes the free room (2026-10-30)

*Withdrawn by §435: the person meant a folder's divider, not the bar's separator. Nothing below is in the bar any more.*

The person: *"spacers should also have a style grow, in which case they grow and take up the available space."*

**What it is.** A separator on a bar has a **Style** of its own now (its menu, over the "Taskbar separators ↗" link):
**Inherited (Line)** — the layout's look by name, Line, Space only or None, as every separator has had since §405 — or
**Grow**. The link stays at the menu's foot under its rule (§423's R16); a row of a widget's own that stands at the foot
now goes under the foot's one rule with the others, first (`OptionMenu.Settings`), wherever it was added. A growing separator is room alone, no line, as long as the free room of its section: the widgets after it go
to the section's far end. The file: `"separator": { "style": "grow" }` on the separator's entry (`BarItem.Separator`,
`SeparatorOptions`, `SpacerStyle`); absent is the layout's look, as before, and nothing else is ever written.

**The rule** (`Layout.Growth`, run wherever the bar is laid out, so at rest and for every arrangement edit mode tries):

1. The sections' rule holds (§13): **the middle stays centred.** A growing separator in the start grows up to the
   middle, a gap off it; one in the end grows from the middle, a gap off it. The middle stands where it stands without them.
2. **One in the middle** grows the middle evenly both ways, so it stays centred, as far as the nearer of the start and the
   end lets it (a gap off); then the start's and the end's take what is left on their sides. A middle that was already
   pushed off centre (§13's step 2) has no room to grow evenly, and its spacers stay at nothing.
3. **With nothing in the middle** the room between the start and the end is shared by the start's and the end's together.
4. **Several in one section share its room evenly**, in whole pixels, the odd ones to the first.
5. **A full bar gives them nothing**, never less: the room is what is left once everything fits (the widgets give way
   as before, never to a spacer), and a spacer of no room stands exactly as one with no line at rest did.
6. **Live**: it is the bar's layout, so it follows every change — a tray icon coming, a button's label, an app opening.

**At rest** its room is the bar's, as the room between two sections always was: a press there is the bar's (its menu, the
lasso), and the widgets either side reach only to its edge. **On a dock** (Floating) it parts its section into two docks,
its room the desktop's between them, half of the docks' gap either side. **Down a side** the same, top to bottom.

**Arranged** it shows its whole room: a separator's edit line at either end and a hairline between them, a measure of its
room (`Scene.ComposeGrowth`), and that room is its grab zone, lit under the pointer and ringed when selected; it is dragged
like any other. Its own room before it grows is edit mode's marker (two hairlines), so on a full bar it is still something
to take hold of. Edit mode's empty rooms are sections like any other: with nothing in the middle, arranging the bar shows
the middle's empty room at the centre, and a start's growing spacer grows up to it rather than to the end — the widgets
after it move in by that much while the bar is arranged.

**A folder's face** is one widget to it, whatever faces it wears. **A folder's divider** has no Grow: a list's room is
already the lines' to take, by a line set to Fill (§168), which is the same wish down a column; a divider is a hairline with
no height of its own, so Grow there would be a second Fill that shows nothing.

Tests (red first): `SpacerGrowTests` — `OneGrowingSpacerTakesTheFreeRoom` (bottom, left, right; red: "Expected 1877,
Actual 49"), `TwoGrowingSpacersShareIt`, `AFullBarGivesItNothing` (red: 1 px, not 0), `TheMiddleStaysCentred` (red: 941, not
1839), `AMiddleSpacerGrowsTheMiddleEvenly`, `AStartsAndAnEndsShareTheRoomWithNoMiddle`, `ItGivesWayAsTheTrayGrows`,
`AtRestItsRoomIsTheBars`, `ArrangedItIsItsWholeRoom`, `ADragInAfterItIsMadeRoomFor`, `InADockItPartsTheDockAndGrowsBetween`,
`TheFileSaysGrowAndNothingElse`, `TheDocksPartsCarryIt`; `SpacerStyleRowTests` (red: no Style row); `OptionRowsTests`
(`SeparatorOptions.Style`), `TypedRegistryTests` (the separator's options kind), `MenuRulesTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`spacer-grow-<sections|two|dock>-<bottom|left>-<rest|edit>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (`SceneTreeTests.SpacerGrowSheets`).

By hand: a separator's menu › Style › Grow: the widgets after it go to the section's end, the middle stays put; two
share; arrange the bar and drag the spacer and a widget past it; a tray icon coming and going: the spacer shrinks and
grows, the tray stays at the end.

## 427. A folder has no name; the edit bar's crumbs say "Folder" and "Widget" (2026-10-30) — a panel since §520 (2026-11-06)

The person: *"the folder name should basically be removed as it is not needed anywhere"* and *"in the edit topbar where
the folder name is shown it should show just 'Current Folder' or something like that. same for the widget then.
'Current widget' but not a specific name"*.

**Where it was.** A folder had a `name` ("Folder" until a preset or the Name row set one) and a `showName` switch (§364):
the name beside its icon face on the bar, its crumb on the edit bar (§326, §343), its menu's spoken heading, "Add to
<name>" over the add list, "Delete “<name>”?", and what Narrator read of its button. The widget crumb said the widget's
kind ("Clock", §352).

**Now.**
- **No name.** `FolderOptions.Name`, `ShowName`, `NameShown`, `FaceInfo.Named`, the Name and "Show name" rows
  (`OptionRows.FolderName`/`FolderShowName`, `OptionFields.OfFolderName`, `OptionTexts.SetFolderName`), the name's
  measuring and painting beside the button (`FolderIsland.Parts` is `Along`, the faces alone) and the string
  `core.folder.defaultName` are gone. A folder's own rows are its alignment (§385) alone, its faces after them. A preset
  names no folder (its title stays the add list's). The file writes neither key; one that has them reads as before
  without them (no migration: the person's file is converted once, `convert-foldername.py`).
- **Where the name stood**, the word "Folder" (`core.widget.folderList.title`, the kind's own) or the icon:
  the button on the bar is its faces only; the add list's heading **"Add to folder"** (`dock.add.toFolder`, every
  language) or "Add to taskbar"; a folder's menu heading and Narrator's name for the menu "Folder" (`IslandEdits.Header`:
  a folder is its kind, as `Kind` always said); Narrator on its button what its faces say, else **"Folder, 3 widgets"**
  (`FolderIsland.Tooltip`); the delete question **"Delete 1 folder?"**, counted as several are; the error list names a
  widget by its kind already (§394), a folder "Folder".
- **The crumbs** (`EditDeck.Buttons`): the folder's says **Folder ▾** by the open folder's icon, the widget's **Widget ▾**
  by the widget's kind's icon — never which. "Folder"/"Widget" rather than "Current folder"/"Current widget": the crumbs
  are a breadcrumb read left to right (Display › Layout › Folder › Widget), so "current" is what each already means, and
  the short words match §423's "Display" and "Layout"; a crumb at its most (§352) never ellipsizes them. Unlike those two,
  whose names are their labels on hover (§423), these two's labels are their words again ("Folder", "Widget"): a folder
  has no name, and the user asked for no specific name for the widget. Their menus are the widget's configuration menu as
  before, which draws no title (§323).

The §411 glossary's "Name" is a widget's, a layout's and an alarm's; a folder has none.

Tests (red first): `FolderFacesTests.AFolderHasNoName` (red: "Expected null, Actual System.String Name"; its rows
`[FolderAlign]` alone, no Name or Show name in its menu); `FolderButtonTests.NoNameStandsBesideTheButton` (red: a file
saying `"showName": true` drew a 72 px button, the icon's square 30); `FolderModelTests.AFoldersNameIsNotKept` (red: the
name written back) and `.AFolderIsWrittenAsItsLists` (`["face", "lists"]`); `ConfigCoverageTests` (a folder's own rows
write `align` alone); `AddListTests.TheHeadingSaysWhereItGoes` (red: "Add to Glance"); `EditDeckPlanTests.ItsWordsSayWhereAndWhat`
(red: the crumbs said "News" and "Tokyo", now "Folder" and "Widget"). Preset tests tell a folder's preset by its faces
(`PresetsTests.MadeBy`), the person's by their file's old names (`PersonsPresetsTests.PresetOf`).
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `editbar-states-<dark|light>-150.png`, `editbar-<top|bottom>-folder-<dark|light>-150.png`,
`folder-button-<icon|clock>-<dark|light>.png`, `menu-align-folder-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: edit mode, open a folder: the crumb reads "Folder ▾"; select a line or a widget: "Widget ▾" by its icon; a folder's
menu has Alignment and its faces, no Name; "Add" in a folder says "Add to folder".

## 428. A list's items lit edge to edge, each touching the next (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the items when hovering over them in a widget like the rss or folder widget should go from edge to edge
and also touch each other. (the hover effect at least.) do this for items in other widgets as well."* Approved: the
lists inside widgets (headlines, a folder's contents, mail, notifications, the clipboard, contacts, the agenda and the
day's events, to-dos, markets, sports, screen time's apps, desktops, processes, removable drives, media sources, alarms,
layouts) and the quick settings pages' (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound's devices, Cast, VPN, keyboard layouts, power mode). Not
the toggles, the month's days, action buttons, a timer's controls.

**Where it was.** Every list lit its own plate: in from the line's edges by 4 to 6 DIP (mail's and the feed's
`MailIsland.Around`, the drive flyout's `Plate`s of a folder's contents, processes, screen time, media sources, the
desktops' and layouts' `PlateOf`, Sports', To Do's), 1 to 4 DIP short of the next item, rounded — with a band of the
line between two items that lit nothing, and in mail, the feed, the clipboard and contacts took no press either. A
quick settings row (`ListRow`) stood 4 DIP in from a line's edges with 2 DIP of nobody's room between it and the next.

**Now: one item, the kit's** (`LineItem` in `LineKit.cs`). An item's **band** is what lights under the pointer, pressed
while a press is down on it, and what takes the press: the line's whole width, edge to edge, from where the room over
it is halved with the item over it to where the room under it is halved with the one under it (`Band`, `Around`). The
items of a list touch: moving down a list lights one after the other, no gap, no overlap. Square (`Light`): the line's
own clip rounds what reaches a corner — a folder's section since §410. What an item shows stands where it stood; only
what lights grew. The chosen one of a list (the layout in use, the desktop shown, the output, the connected network's
opened card) is the same band in the selected fill (`Chosen`), a step quieter under the pointer so it shows it is lit
(before, the hover and the selected fill were the same colour and the chosen row did not light), its accent pill 4 DIP
in (`Pill`). A control on an item — a Join, an Eject, a pin, the clipboard's delete, the microphones' mute — keeps its
own hit and light over the band. The keys' focus ring stays where it was, in from the edges, so the clip leaves it whole.

- **The kit's lines** (drawn on a `LineSketch`): the feed's headlines and its name (the header is the site's item,
  edge to edge to the first headline), mail's messages, the clipboard's items, contacts' people and an open person's
  details (an open person a square block in the control fill, no longer a rounded card), notifications (the card
  stays; its band reaches over the room round it to the next card, a heading between two apps parting them), the
  one-row forms of mail and the feed (the newest is the line's one item, all of it).
- **Rows already the line's width** now light all of it (the plate fields went: `BoardRow.Plate`, `ProcessesLine.Row.Plate`,
  `SourceRow.Plate`, `DeviceRow.Plate`, `AppRow.Plate`): a folder's contents and its subfolder's head (`BackHead` lit
  square across a line), processes, removable drives, media sources, screen time's apps, desktops and "New desktop",
  layouts, Sports' matches and scoreboard, To Do's tasks, "Completed" and "Add a task".
- **The quick settings pages** (`ListRow`, `PageLayout.Row`): a list's row is placed across the page's whole width with
  its glyph's column at `ListLead` (the gutter on a line, 16 DIP in a flyout) and the room between it and the row before
  it — where nothing but room stands between — halved between the two (`Over`, `Under`); an opened network's or
  device's card is an item as its row is (`PageLayout.Card`). `ListRowLeft`/`ListRowRight` and `ListRow.TextLeft` went
  for `ListLead`, `ListTextLeft`, `ListTextRight`. Sound's devices (`SoundPartTile.LayDevices`) the same, the mute over
  the microphone in use with its words kept short of it (`ListRow.Keep`). A page's head in a folder's column lights
  across it as a line's head does.
- **The agenda and the day's events**: an event with nothing to do (no meeting) is not an item and lights nothing — a
  light that does nothing would break §379; a meeting's row is its Join's, all of it, edge to edge, lit whole with its
  button (it took a press only across the button's reach since §418).
- **Markets and alarms** are a line each, not a list: a market's line is lit whole by the folder, edge to edge since
  §410; an alarm's only press is its switch. The sound mixer's apps are controls (a mute, a slider), no item: unchanged.
- To Do and a quick settings page take their presses themselves (`CardPress`); each now also answers a hit test with
  what is there (`CardTarget`), so a sweep — and the folder's `PartAt` — sees their rows.

Tests: `ItemHoverSweepTests.EveryListsItemsLightEdgeToEdgeAndTouch` (new): every kind above with items to show, drawn as
the open folder draws it and asked as it asks (`CellIsland.TargetOn`), every pixel down the line's leading edge and a
grid over each item: each takes the pointer at both edges and lights exactly its band (its middle row from edge to
edge, its leading half as tall as what takes it), every pixel of it its own or a control's on it, and it meets the next
unless something drawn (a heading) stands between them. Red first for all 24 kinds (57 failures): *"Rss: 0 items take
the pointer at the line's leading edge, not 4"*, *"FolderContents: item 1000 takes 0-540 × 60-114 and lights 6-534 ×
63-111"*, the same for mail, notifications, the clipboard, contacts, the agenda, events, To Do, Sports, screen time,
desktops, processes, removable drives, media sources, layouts and every quick settings page and sound list. Pictures
(`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `item-hover-<dark|light>.png`, every kind on a folder's section with its second item lit.
`LineHitSweepTests`' `Drawn` and `Apart` are shared with it. `MediaPresetTests` asks a row's band, not its plate.

By hand: Theme Graphite, open the News folder and move the pointer down the headlines: each lights from the section's
left edge to its right, the next lighting where the last ends, no dark line between. The same in a folder's contents,
mail, the clipboard, contacts, processes, the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth lines (a network opened onto its key: its card edge to
edge), the sound devices. In the agenda, a meeting's row lights whole and joins wherever it is clicked; an event that is
no meeting lights nothing. The layout in use is a shade quieter under the pointer.
## 429. Styles: ours and the person's, each with a light and a dark set, applied to a widget or a folder (2026-10-30)

The person: *"right now the appearance is given by individual properties / styles. i want to change this. there should be
a global list of styles that come from us (the user can add his own as well though), and you can basically just apply
them to widgets. you are not able to control each individual property for every widget. this should make the styling
more simple for the users."*; *"per style there should be appearance settings for dark and light mode, so that a switch
can also work seamlessly."*

**A style** (`Styles`, `ItemStyle`, `Styled`) is a name and, for each mode, what §405 lets a level say: Background, Accent,
Text (a colour or Inherited) and Outlines (On, Off, Inherited). The set of the mode drawn is in force (`Styled.In`), so a
switch of Windows' mode or of the Dark mode toggle (§403) swaps every styled widget at once. The Dark set is the Light
one's until it is set apart ("Same in dark mode" off; `ItemStyle.Dark` null while on): then the light colours are drawn
in the dark too, adapted as §405 adapts a colour stored once (`ToneRules.Adapt`, `Readable`), so somebody who sets one
mode has a sensible other. Set apart, the Dark set starts as a copy of the Light one.

**Ours** (`Styles.BuiltIn`), read-only, named in every language, hand-picked so the text reads 4.5:1 and the accent 3:1
as picked in both modes (`StyleTests.OursReadAsPickedInBothModesAndEveryTheme`):

| Style | Light (background / accent / text, outlines) | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| Default | everything Inherited (no style) | the same |
| Subtle | text #5C5C5C, outlines off | text #B4B4B4, outlines off |
| Accent | background = the accent in force (adapted: a pale tint) | the same (a deep tint) |
| Outlined | outlines on | outlines on |
| Contrast | #FFFFFF / – / #000000, outlines on | #000000 / – / #FFFFFF, outlines on |
| Blue | #B4D4F7 / #0F5FB0 / #0A3566 | #0B2540 / #5AAEF0 / #D2E7FC |
| Green | #B0E0BC / #0E7A3E / #0A4422 | #0A2A18 / #45C97C / #CDF0D8 |
| Orange | #F9CFA8 / #B54A00 / #632900 | #33190A / #FF9A4D / #FFE0C7 |
| Red | #F6BDBD / #C42B1C / #731010 | #380F0F / #FF7A70 / #FFD6D3 |
| Purple | #D8C6F2 / #7440C2 / #3F1D73 | #23163A / #B994FF / #E9DDFF |

A light-mode card is the background lifted 70 % towards white at 70 % (§405's rule), so the light colour styles are pale
tints whose text carries the hue; the dark ones deep tints.

**Applying.** A widget's and a folder's Appearance (at the menu's foot, §311) is one choice (`WidgetLooks.Row`): Default,
ours, the person's, each with a swatch of its look in the mode drawn (`Styles.Swatch`: its card, its rim where it
outlines, a line of its text), the one worn ticked and said at the row's end, a pick going back; "Styles ↗" under them. A
link is a way out, no row to pick, so it does not count towards a long list's search field (§279, `Flyout.Searchable`):
ten styles and the link are no search, nor Appearance's ten rows and its link.
§405's Background, Accent, Text, Outlines and Reset all rows of an item's own are gone. The row keeps the word
"Appearance": a widget's "Style" is already its form's (a calendar's Agenda, Week), §411 R7. The chain is §405's: Windows
→ theme → Customize → a folder's style → a line's style; a widget on the bar its style over Karpo's; a folder's style is
its button's, its panel's and its lines' unless a line wears its own (`FolderFlyout.Worn`, `LineLook`, `Look.In(Styled)`,
`PartSpec.Style`, `Scene.OwnTones`). A separator and a divider wear none.

**Styles ↗** (Layout ▾ › Appearance, after Outlines; and every Appearance choice) opens the styles' own menu under Layout
▾'s crumb (`LooksScope.Styles`, `BarLooks.StyleRows`, `EditMenu.Styles`): ours, each with its swatch and a copy button
at its row's end; ruled off, the person's, each with a copy and a bin, opening its level — Name, Light background, Light
accent, Light text, Light outlines, a rule, "Same in dark mode" and, while it is off, Dark background, accent, text and
outlines (each row Customize's picker in that mode, saying what it inherits there); "Add a style" under the list (R9), the menu's foot under its rule (§423, R16). A
style's level is the menu's second, so its colours' choices are its third (R1); its own menu rather than a page under
Appearance, which would put them on a fourth. A copy of ours is the person's ("Blue copy"); a style deleted is asked
first ("Widgets and folders with this style go back to Default."), and everything that wore it wears Default
(`Styles.Delete`). The global Theme, Background, Accent, Text, opacities, separators and Outlines are §405's and say what
Default and Inherited are.

**The file** (no reading of the old shape; the coordinator converts the person's own once with
`karpo-coord\convert-styles.py`):

```
islands[..].colors {background, accent, text, outlines}  → gone
islands[..].appearance: "<style id>"                      new: ours ("blue") or the person's; left out for Default
appearance.styles: [{ id, name, light: {background?, accent?, text?, outlines?}, dark?: {…} }]
                                                          new; "dark" left out while it is the light one's ("Same in dark
                                                          mode"), {} where it is set apart and inherits all
```

An id no style has reads as Default and is kept. (`islands[].style` is a widget's form already, hence "appearance".)

Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.*` (the list's name, the ten styles', Add a style, New style, the copy's name, the
delete question, the eight mode rows, Same in dark mode); 30 languages. `OptionGlyphs.Styles` (MapLayers).

Tests: `StyleTests` (Default and an unknown id inherit; ours named, both modes, read-only; ours readable as picked and in
every theme; the Dark set the Light one's until set apart; a line's style over its folder's over Karpo's; added, named,
copied, deleted with what wore it back to Default; the file), `WidgetLookTests` (the foot's one choice with swatches and
Styles ↗, no colour rows of an item's own; a pick worn and kept; each swatch its style in the mode drawn; live:
`AStyledLineTakesItsOtherSetWhenTheModeFlips` — red with the mode's set ignored: *"dark: the styled line is not its dark
set's #B31C3B2D"*), `ThemeChainTests` (the chain with styles, a style's rows say what they inherit in their mode, a pick
stored in its mode), `MenuRulesTests` (the Styles menu, a style of the person's set apart, all rules, the allowance empty),
`LinkRowsTests`, `EditEntriesTests` (Styles ↗ lands on the styles), `ConfigCoverageTests` (appearance.styles written by
the Styles menu). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `styles-<windows|graphite|paper>-<look>.png` (every style on bar widgets and
folder lines), `styles-choice-<look>.png`, `styles-menu-<look>.png`, `styles-live-<look>.png`, `widget-look-folder-<look>.png`.

By hand: edit mode, a widget's Appearance › Blue: a blue card; switch Windows to light: a pale blue card with dark blue
text, at once. Layout ▾ › Appearance › Styles ↗: the styles menu under Layout; Add a style, set its Light background,
turn "Same in dark mode" off and set a Dark one; switch modes: the widgets wearing it change. Delete it: they go back
to Default.

## 430. One click on what opened a menu closes it, for every menu (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the add button to add a widget, when the menu is already open and i click again it reopens it and
flickers. it should just close it / toggle. this should be for all the menus. make sure this is the case"*.

**What was wrong.** Each surface knew in its own way what had opened the popup a press closed: a bar by the
popup's `Pending.Hit` (set by hand by each opener), the edit bar by a table of its own (`EditDeckMenus`, §343), a
folder's face by its own `dismissed` record. The add list a bar's blue "+" opens (§387) set no `Hit`: a click on the
"+" while its list stood closed it, and the release opened it again — the close-and-reopen flicker. An arranged
folder's own "+" (§397) was the same: the popups' hook closes the list before the press reaches the folder's window,
which then opened it again.

**One rule now** (`Openers`, `PopupOpener`, LightDismiss.cs; `Pending.Opener`): every popup remembers what opened
it — the window, the thing in it (a bar's hit, an edit bar's button, a folder's line by its widget's key or its "+"),
and the button. The dock follows the click being handled from its press to its release (`Dock.Pressing`, called
where a press lands: `PressedOn` for the bars, `DeckPressed` for the edit bars, `FolderMessage` for a folder's
window; `Released` once the release is handled): what opens meanwhile is stamped with what the press went down on
(`ShowFlyout`), and the openers of the popups its press closed are noted — closed by the bar or the edit bar itself,
or by the popups' hook before the press got there (`FlyoutHost.Heard`: the hook's press at this point, the popups
dismissed since). A popup whose opener is one the press just closed does not open (`Openers.Reopens`): one click on
an opener closes what it opened, whoever closed it and whoever opens what. `EditDeckMenus` is gone; `DeckOpened` now
only says that a menu hangs from an edit bar button that did not open it (a face's click, a pick, a second start).

- **Another opener** while a popup stands: the press closes it and its click opens its own, in the one click; the
  popup window is never empty between (a menu takes the new content in place).
- **The other button on the same thing**: a right click on what opened a flyout closes the flyout and opens its menu,
  as before (`LightDismiss.Consumes`).
- **Right click, decided:** a right click on what a right click opened a menu from closes the menu and opens nothing,
  as the Windows 11 taskbar does with a jump list (`LightDismiss.Consumes` for a menu, now by its opener); a right click anywhere else closes
  it and opens that thing's menu at once.
- **Keys:** a menu or flyout takes the keys as it opens, so no opener has them while it stands: Escape closes it.
  The edit bar's buttons take no focus.
- **Tests' presses** (`PressHook.StagedBit`): a stage test posts the hook's press to the dock's sink itself (a stage's
  desktop never has the input); only a stage run (`Stage.On`) takes it.

The openers, each opened, clicked again, and from one to another (`MenuToggleTests`, the real dock on a stage, every
press first through the hook as the mouse sends it): at rest a folder's face (each of the bar's), the bar's right
click, a face's right click, Start's right click (quick links), a folder's face to the other's, a folder open to its
face's right-click menu, one right-click menu to another; in edit mode Add, Display ▾, Layout ▾, ⚙, Folder ▾, Widget ▾,
the errors' indicator, each to the next, the bar's blue "+" (red before: closed and opened again), a folder's face (the
folder and Folder ▾), Add into the folder, the folder's own "+" (red before), a line's settings beside it (§407), one
line's to another's, a widget of the bar's settings beside it. Not on a stage, unchanged and by the same rule: the
tray's chevron, "…" of the app buttons, the window list (a stage has no tray icons nor windows); Start's left click is
Windows' own Start.

No config change. Tests: `OpenersTests` (the rule), `MenuToggleTests.EveryOpenerOnTheBarTogglesItsPopup`,
`.EveryOpenerInEditModeTogglesItsMenu` (each film's moments open or closed, never open again once closed; a switch
never a moment with neither), `EditBarFolderPictures.TheToggleIsTheDocksOwnPress`. Strips (`KARPO_TOGGLE_DIR`, else
`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `film-toggle-<opener>.png`.

By hand: in edit mode click a bar's blue "+", then the same "+": the list closes, no flash; the edit bar's Add twice;
open a folder, a column's "+" twice; a line's settings, the line again; right click a widget twice.

## 431. Today always first in the agenda, over "No events" when nothing is on it (2026-10-30)

The person: *"in the agenda today should also appear if no event is there and then it should just say no event"*.

**Where it was.** Since §419 today is a heading like any other day's, but only a day with events had one: with nothing
on today the agenda began at "Tomorrow" (or a later day), so it never said that today is free; with nothing in the whole
week the header stood over "No events coming up". A picked day with nothing on it (§419) already had its heading, over
"No events on this day".

**Now** (`CalendarIsland`). The agenda's first day — today, or the day picked in a month beside it — always has its
heading. With nothing on it, under its heading one compact row (§418) says **"No events"** (`dock.calendar.noEvents`,
in every language already): the kit's Status row (`LineStatus`, §401), the Body at the text edge where the titles begin,
in the secondary ink. It is no item: not lit, nothing a press lands on, no menu. Then the later days follow as before.
With nothing in the whole week the agenda is the header, "Today" and "No events", and says nothing further: the empty
day says it, and a line that shows a week of nothing needs no second sentence. A picked empty day is the same code and
now says "No events" too (`NoEvents`, `FirstEmpty`); its heading names the day, so "on this day" said it twice. The
one-row form is unchanged: the next event, or the day and "No events coming up" / "No events on this day" where there is
no heading to name it. While the calendars are read or could not be, the header stands over that (`Message`), no heading.

**Height.** An automatic agenda counts the empty day: the header's 40, and 32 for its heading, its "No events" and every
event and later heading (`ListHeight`). The least that is not one row (header, heading, one compact row, 104 DIP) holds
the header, "Today" and "No events".

Tests (red first): `AgendaColumnTests.AnEmptyTodayIsItsHeadingOverNoEvents` (new; red: "the line 168 px, not the header's
40, today's heading and its row and 2 events and 2 headings of 32 px each", "says [head Calendar, day 2026-09-24 Thursday,
24 September, …], not [head Calendar, day 2026-09-22 Today, status No events, day 2026-09-24 …]") — the sample week without
today's events and an empty week, at 100/150 % and 100/225 % text: the order top to bottom, "No events" at the text edge on
its row's middle, tomorrow's heading two compact rows under today's, a press on it no event's; `AgendaMediaDriveAnatomyTests`
(the stand-ins' Wednesday has nothing: red "its height at 168, not 232"; now one Body row in the headings' ink at the text
edge between today's heading and the next, no colour bar on it); `FlyoutLinesTests.TheAgendaFollowsTheDayTheMonthPicks` (a
picked empty day's heading over "No events"). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `agenda-empty-today-<dark|light>.png`,
`agenda-nothing-<dark|light>.png`, `list-form-month-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder on a day with nothing in the calendar: "Calendar", then "Today" over a grey "No events",
then "Tomorrow" or the next day with its events; pick an empty day in a month beside it: its heading over "No events".

## 432. One height, or a few sizes: a widget that shows one form has no Height; every size whole rows (2026-10-30)

The person: *"a lot of widgets just have one height like the now playing widget or also the alarm one. (or maybe just
a second height where they actually fix their contents properly). for these widgets i would not like the user to be
able to change their height manually. it should basically just be a fixed height."* And: *"try to design on the cell
height as well, so that it is possible to actually make designs where the widgets combined give the same folder
height."* The height survey (every kind at 1 to 16 rows) sorted the kinds; the rule they approved:

- **A, one form**: no Height at all, no Fill; the line is its form.
- **B, a few forms**: a **Size** in the Height's place — Compact, Medium where the kind has a distinct middle form,
  Full — never a count of rows.
- **C, content that grows**: the Height as it was (Automatic, Fixed, Fill and the rows); a chart that stretches stops
  where its information is whole.

**The kinds** (`ListWidget.Forms`, `Starts`, `MostRows`; `LineSize.cs`). Rows at 100 % and the list's text:

| Class | Kind | Sizes (rows) | Starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Timer, Focus time, Date header, Dawn, Dusk | 1 | — |
| A | Toggles | 2 (a row of buttons more per row of toggles) | — |
| A | Weather hours | 4 | — |
| A | Win+P (Projection) | 6 | — |
| A | Nearby sharing | 9 | — |
| B | Now playing | Compact 1 · Medium 2 (the row with its caption) · Full 3 (the timeline and the app) | Medium |
| B | Battery | Compact 1 · Medium 2 (the meter) · Full 3 (energy saver, the power mode) | Medium |
| B | Security | Compact 1 · Medium 2 (who is in charge) · Full 4 (a row per protection) | Medium |
| B | Time header | Compact 1 · Medium 2 (the time in the Hero, the date kept) · Full 3 | Full |
| B | Volume, Brightness | Compact 1 · Medium 2 (name over slider) · Full 4 (the level large) | Compact |
| B | Alarm, Sunrise, Sunset, Daylight, Solar noon | Compact 1 · Full 2 (the caption, the note) | Full |
| B | Drive, Network drive | Compact 1 · Full 2 (the caption, the meter under) | Full |
| B | Clock | Compact 1 · Full 3 (the face as large as the rows) | Full |
| B | the 25 switches | Compact 1 · Full: the name over what a click does, 2 (3 where it wraps at 100 %) | Compact |
| B | Pin | Compact 1 · Full 2 (the name large over what it opens) | Compact |
| B | CPU, GPU, Memory, Disk, Network details | Compact 1 (the first fact) · Full: every fact (2–5) | Full |
| B | Power mode | Compact 1 (the segmented modes) · Full 5 (the page) | Full |
| B | Markets | Compact 1 (the ticker) · Full 3 (the words over the chart) | Full |
| B | Sun day bar | Compact 1 (the next event) · Full 3 (the place, the bar, the times) | Full |
| B | Screen time chart | Compact 1 (the total) · Full 4 (the ring and its whole legend) | Full |
| C, capped | CPU, GPU, Memory, Disk, Network graphs 5 · Screen time 4 · Tides 3 · Sun arc 3 | Max rows | as before |
| C | every list, Weather now, Weather days, Air quality (six tiers), Month (a week more a row), Camera … | Height | as before |

Dawn and dusk have no note, so they are one row and nothing else. Air quality keeps its Height: its six tiers each
add something; the month too: a taller month shows more weeks.

**Whole rows, always** (`FolderFlyout.Build`'s `Tall`, `LineSizes.RowsFor`). A sized line is what it measures of its
form (`IListContent.ListHeight`, which reads the line's size), rounded up to the fewest whole rows of the folder's
cells at every scale and text size — a form of 52 DIP is two rows, 77 — and draws its form at their top: the open
folder keeps what it measured (`CellIsland.FormMeasured`), and the line is drawn and hit in that band alone
(`CellIsland.Scrolled`), the rest of its last row air, never its form a tier taller. A form that spreads over its line
(the clock's face, the slider's large level, the screen time ring, the toggles' buttons, which stay in the middle)
measures its whole rows (`LineRows.Whole`). Every kind measures now: the switches, the pin, the volume and the
brightness, the sun's day bar and the screen time ring measured nothing before and fell to constants. The switch and
the pin draw their size's tier whatever the height (`CellIsland.SizedTier`).

**Lines stacked add up row for row, not across lines.** Lines stand flush, without the gap a row has inside a line, so
two lists of the same rows line for line (2, 2, 1, 3, 2 beside 1, 2, 2, 2, 3) are the same height, but a line of four
rows (159) is not two of two (154), and one row is 40 where n rows are 41n − 5. Making any combination add up would be
one row pitch for every line (41n, or 40n): every line of every folder a few pixels taller — the person's call.

**The menu** (`LineHeightRows`). A kind of one form has no Height row and no Size row. A kind of a few has "Size" at
the menu's foot where Height stands — a choice saying its size and opening its sizes, each with its own glyph (smaller,
size, larger), a pick going back — and nothing to step. A chart that stretches steps to its most and fills no further
(`LineHeight.MostAt`): its rows counted at the list's text, and as many more as a larger text makes its words, since
the rows do not grow with the text (the graphs' 5 are 12 at 225 %); a height a file holds past it is kept. Four keys in
all 30 languages (`dock.edit.size.*`).

**The file.** A line of a few forms keeps `"size": "compact" | "medium" | "full"` and no `"height"`; one of one form
keeps neither; the rest as before. No migration: the person's file is converted once (`convert-heights.py`: Automatic
→ where the kind starts, the form its Automatic drew; Fixed n → the fullest size whose rows fit in n, the form it drew;
a capped chart held to its most). Presets give sizes (`PresetItem.Size`): the media center's and the stocks' lines
Full, the world clock's cities Compact; the processor's preset lists four top processes, not five, so it still stands in 70 % of a 1440p screen at 150 % now its
details are whole rows.

**What else changed** (the survey's surprises): the pin re-centred from three rows — its compact and whole forms
stand at the line's top (`LineRows.Top`), and the whole form says what it opens before "Open", which the running
indicator says anyway; the date header was a 48 DIP band, a row and a bit, and is the list's row; Win+P's and nearby
sharing's pages are cut no more (their whole page, whole rows); the markets' chart and the day bar's bar leave no
empty band above them (a sized line is no taller than its whole rows). To-do's "Add a task" stays at the line's foot:
the person asked for it there (2026-10-11), so it is theirs to change.

Tests (red first): `SizedLinesTests.EverySizeIsWholeRowsAndItsFormIsWhatItDraws` (every sized kind in every size at
100 and 150 % and 100 and 225 % text: measured, the fewest whole rows, Compact one row, the rows declared at 100 %,
its first ink in its first row, never past what it measured, no band of air; red: "Media Compact … Compact is 77 px,
not one row", "Pin Compact … measures nothing", the switches, volume, brightness, day bar and ring "measures
nothing"), `.ALargerSizeIsMore` (red: "Media: Medium measures 52, not more than Compact's 52"),
`.ListsOfTheSameRowsAreTheSameHeight`, `LineSizeTests` (the classes, the file's size and no height, a size unknown
read as the start, the caps, presets), `LineHeightRowsTests.ASizedLineHasASizeAndNoHeight`,
`.AChartThatStretchesStepsToItsMostRows`, `ListScrollTests.APinsFormStandsAtTheTopOfATallBox` (red: "Full in 3 rows:
icon at 67, name at 49, past the first row (60)") and `.EveryLineStandsAtTheTopOfATallLine` with the sized kinds and a
pin with a target. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `sized-<compact|medium|full>.png`, `sized-sizes-<group>.png` (each
kind's sizes side by side), `sized-stacks-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: a folder with now playing, a battery, a switch and a clock; right-click each in edit mode: "Size" with its
sizes, no Height; pick one, the line changes at once and the menu goes back. A timer or a toggles row: neither. Two
lists of the same rows line for line end level. The pin with a target in Full: the name large, what it opens under it,
at the top.

## 433. A row's words end short of the control over its band, wherever it stands (2026-10-30)

`ListLinesControlsTests.NothingALineLaysOutOverlaps` failed for the microphones' line two rows tall and more: *"its
Microphone Array (Realtek(R) Audio) and its Mute microphone overlap"*. Nothing was drawn under the mute: the test held
a `ListRow` to its bounds, and since §428 a row's bounds are its band, the line's whole width, which the mute stands
over by design. The name was cut short of it (`ListRow.Keep`, a width the line worked out from the button's size and
the gutters). Now:

- **A row knows the control over it** (`ListRow.Control`, for `Keep`): its words end a button's gap
  (`LineButton.GapDip`) short of the control's left edge, wherever the control stands, so a moved or resized mute
  can't leave the name under it.
- **A row says where it showed what it shows** (`ListRow.Shown`: its glyph and its words, as last drawn), and the test
  holds a sound line's rows to that rather than to their bands.

The kit's rows (`LineRow`: removable drives' Eject, a meeting's Join) take their controls' room from their reading
already (`RowSpec.Controls`), media sources keep their check's room, and the mixer's apps draw no name: unchanged.

Tests (`ListLinesControlsTests`): `ALongNameIsCutShortOfItsRowsControls` (new): an output and a microphone named at
length, every height and size, the words where they are drawn (`PaintWatch.Said`) clear of the mute; red with the room
not kept (*"... runs under its Mute microphone (324..348)"*). `ARowsLongNameIsCutShortOfEverythingAtItsEnd` (new): a
`ListRow` with a long name and second line ending in its menu's "...", a chevron, a battery and its level, a control,
and all of them: its words clear of each. `NothingALineLaysOutOverlaps` green.

## 434. Every event lights and opens in a calendar; a meeting's Join a button on its row (2026-10-30)

The person: *"an event should light up anyways and open a calendar."* §428 had left an event with no meeting unlit (a
light that does nothing breaks §379) and made a meeting's whole row its Join.

**Now every event is an item** — the agenda's (`CalendarIsland`, its one-row form's next event too), the day's events'
(`EventsTile`) and the next meetings' (`MeetingTile`): its row lights edge to edge under the pointer (`LineItem`, §428),
pressed while pressed, and a click on it opens the event in a calendar once the folder has gone, as every other line's
opening does (`IslandView.App`, §380; `EventChoice`, the dock's `IMeetingLine.Open`). Where it opens (`EventLinks.Target`),
the first there is:

1. **its own page** on its account's site: a Microsoft event's in Outlook on the web (Graph's `webLink`, now asked for
   with calendarView's fields, kept on the occurrence as `Occurrence.Link` → `CalendarEvent.Link` and in
   calendar-cache.json; https only, `MailLinks.Web`);
2. **its calendar's web calendar on the day it is listed under** (`ICalendarSource.Web`, `CalendarLinks.Day`): Outlook on
   the web's day view (`outlook.live.com/calendar/0/view/day/Y/M/D` for a personal address — outlook.\*, hotmail.\*,
   live.\*, msn.com —, `outlook.office.com/calendar/view/day/Y/M/D` for any other), Google Calendar's for a Google CalDAV
   account (`calendar.google.com/calendar/u/<address>/r/day/Y/M/D`), iCloud's calendar for an iCloud one (it takes no
   day). Google's own event links need an id CalDAV does not give, so a Google event opens on its day;
3. **the person's web calendar on that day** — the first of their calendars that has one (`CalendarStore.Web`): a public
   holiday, an event of a CalDAV server Karpo knows no site of;
4. **the calendar app Windows has** (`CalendarApp.Link`, "Open Calendar"'s: `outlookcal:`, then `ms-calendar:`), at
   today: neither link takes a day it is documented to open at, and on Windows 11 with the new Outlook `outlookcal:` is
   often a key with no app under it, which `CalendarApp.Find` already passes by. The new Outlook's `ms-outlook:` is not
   tried: nothing documents a calendar or a day for it;
5. **nothing**: the row is no item and lights nothing (§379 holds).

**A meeting's Join is a button on its row, not the row.** The row opens the meeting as every event's opens (its notes,
who comes, where — what a person looks for before joining, and what the Join cannot show); the Join, Windows' standard
button at the row's end, joins: across the row's height and a button's reach (`LineButton.Hit`, kept in its row, §418),
its own target past every row's (`JoinButton.Target`, which the day and week views' `JoinTarget` now is too). This is
§428's own rule for a control on an item (an Eject, a pin, a delete): the item lights under it too, the button lights
itself. A whole-row Join would have made a meeting the one event whose row cannot open it. Enter still joins the lit
meeting; the right click's "Join meeting" is unchanged.

**One seam each.** The calendar app a test stands in is `CalendarApp.Stand` (was `ActionsTile.CalendarLink`); Windows'
answer is kept five seconds (a line lays out on every move of the pointer). What opens is `MeetingJoin.Launch`, a
meeting's and an event's, with the one test seam `MeetingJoin.Opening`. The day and week views are a grid of blocks, a
press on one picking its day (§379): unchanged.

Tests (red first): `EventOpenTests.AnAccountsWebCalendarIsItsSitesDayView` (red: null for every account),
`.AnEventOpensItsPageElseItsCalendarsDayElseThePersonsElseTheApp` (red: null),
`.AnAccountsEventKeepsItsPageAndItsCalendarItsDay` (a Microsoft account's event through the store; red: no day view),
`.EveryEventRowOpensItsEventOnceTheFolderHasGone` (the agenda, the day's events and the next meetings: a click on each
row an app opening, nothing opened until the folder has gone, then its page, its calendar's day or the person's day; a
Join its meeting; red: *"the agenda's "Customer workshop" opened nothing"*, *"the agenda's "Design review" opened
msteams:/l/meetup-join/…, not https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?itemid=AAMkReview…"*, *"the meetings' "1:1 with Anna"
opened nothing"*), `MicrosoftReaderTests.AnEventOpensAtItsWebLink` (red: null), `ItemHoverSweepTests.EveryListsItemsLightEdgeToEdgeAndTouch`
(events no longer exempt: the agenda and the day's events with a holiday, plain events and meetings, and the next
meetings; red: *"Calendar: 2 items take the pointer at the line's leading edge, not 5"*, *"Events: 2 … not 5"*,
*"Meeting: 0 … not 3"*); `AgendaColumnTests.AnEventsWholeRowIsItsHitArea`, `JoinEverywhereTests.TheDaysEventsJoinTheirMeetings`
and `MeetingPictures.TheFaceAndTheLineAreDrawnAndJoin` now take the Join as its own target and the rest of the row as the
event's. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `event-click-<dark|light>.png` (the agenda at rest, a plain event, a holiday, a
meeting's row and its Join under the pointer), `item-hover-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: an agenda in a folder: move the pointer down it: every event lights edge to edge, a holiday and a plain event
too. Click a Microsoft event: the folder closes, Outlook on the web opens on it; a holiday: your calendar on the web on
that day. Hover a meeting's Join: the row lit, the button lit over it; click it: the meeting joins; click its title: the
meeting opens in Outlook on the web.

## 435. A folder's divider that grows; the bar's separator does not (2026-10-30)

The person: *"spacers should also have a style grow, in which case they grow and take up the available space"*, then,
on seeing §426: *"oh no the spacer should only be available in the folder. the taskbar should not get a spacer that can
grow"*.

**Withdrawn from the bar.** §426 is gone whole: a bar's separator has no Style row (its menu is the "Taskbar separators ↗"
link again), no `"separator"` options on its entry, no growth in the bar's layout (`Layout.Growth`, `PartSpec.Grow`) and
no edit-mode measure (`Scene.ComposeGrowth`). Kept from it: a widget's own row that stands at the menu's foot goes under the
foot's one rule with the others (`OptionMenu.Settings`), which the divider's link now uses.

**A divider's Style** (its menu, over the "Folder separators ↗" link): **Inherited (Space only)** — the folders' look by
name, Line, Space only or None (§405, §416) — or **Grow**. The file: `"divider": { "style": "grow" }` on the divider's
line (`CellItem.Divider`, `DividerOptions`, `DividerStyle`); absent is the folders' look, and nothing else is ever written.

**The rule** (`FolderFlyout.Build`, at rest and arranged alike):

1. A growing divider is **Space only's gap made bigger**, whatever the folders' look (`GrowStyle`): it always parts its
   column into two sections, each rounded (§410), and draws nothing at rest. Room inside one section would read as an
   empty widget; two sections read as "the lines after it go to the foot".
2. ~~It takes the room its column has **free beside the folder's tallest column**: its column then is as tall as the
   tallest, its last line at the foot (on a bottom bar its top level with the others').~~ *Corrected by §482:* it takes
   **all the room the folder has**, the room a Fill line fills to (§173): its column reaches the top on a bottom bar,
   the bottom on a top bar, the far end beside a side bar, whether or not another column is taller.
3. **Several in a column share that room evenly**, in whole px, the odd px to the first (`FillShares`).
4. **With Fill lines** (§168) in its column, Fill lines and growing dividers are alike: they share the room Fill fills to
   (all the room the folder has, §173) evenly. Neither outranks the other: whoever put both asked for both; one taking
   only what the other leaves would leave one of them nothing, since a Fill line takes all of it. A Fill line of a chart
   that stretches stops at its most (§432, `FillMost`); its share past that goes on to the others, evenly — so a growing
   divider beside a capped chart takes what the chart leaves, and the column still reaches the room (`FillShares`). A
   divider has no most.
5. ~~**No free room, no growth**: the tallest column's, and an only column's, stay Space only's gap. A folder sizes to its
   content (Automatic), so a growing divider never makes a column taller — it uses room that another column (or a Fill
   line's column) makes. With every column Automatic and none with Fill, a divider in the tallest column grows nothing.~~
   *Corrected by §482:* a growing divider makes its column as tall as a Fill line makes its own, the tallest and an only
   column's too; the other columns keep their heights.
6. Lines left out under the most (§152) are left out first; a divider grows only in what the column shows.

**Arranged** nothing moves; its rule lies across the middle of its room, as Space only's does across its gap, and its
whole room is its grab: lit selected round the whole of it, a click there its settings, a drag carries it.

Tests (red first): `FolderDividerGrowTests` — `OneGrowingDividerTakesTheColumnsFreeRoom` (red: "Expected 400, Actual
86"), `TwoShareIt` (red: 132, not 400), `AFillLineAndAGrowingDividerShareTheRoomEvenly` (red: grew 0, not 729),
`ACappedFillChartLeavesTheRestToTheGrowingDivider` (red, the cap dropped: the chart 503, not its 5 rows, 200),
`NoFreeRoomGivesItNothing`, `AnInheritedDividerDoesNotGrow`, `ItPartsTheColumnIntoTwoSections` (red: 1 section under
Line and None; the grab not the room), `TheFileSaysGrowAndNothingElse`; `DividerStyleRowTests` (the row, its write, over
the link; the bar's separator has none); `OptionRowsTests` (`DividerOptions.Style`), `TypedRegistryTests` (the divider's
options kind), `MenuPickersTests`, `MenuRulesTests`. `SpacerGrowTests`, `SpacerStyleRowTests` and the `spacer-grow-*`
pictures went with §426. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `folder-divider-grow-<graphite|paper>-<rest|selected|hover>-150.png`
and a row of the three, `folder-divider-grow-<graphite|paper>-150.png`.

By hand: a folder with two columns, the shorter one's separator › Style › Grow: its lines after it go to the column's
foot, ~~the column as tall as the other; add lines to the other column and the gap grows~~ (§482: the column all the
folder's room); arrange: the whole gap selects it.
A bar separator's menu: no Style.
## 436. A list's items from the line's edges, each as tall as the others (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the items should also go all the way to the top or bottom edge if applicable. right now for some of the
widgets there is a small strip on the top that is not selected that i dont want to happen."* and right after: *"the last
item should not be stretched unenccecarily though. it should still have the same size as the other items"*.

**Where it was.** Since §428 the items of a list touch, but a list kept its own air at the line's edges: 4 DIP over the
first desktop, layout and keyboard layout (`DesktopsLine.Pad`, `LayoutsLine.Pad`, the keyboard page's first `Gap(4)`),
lit by nothing — the strip on the top — and under the last item the list's foot: 4 to 10 DIP under the clipboard's,
contacts', notifications', the day's events', To Do's "Add a task", the desktops', layouts', sound devices' and every
quick settings page's last row (`ListForm.Pad`, `PageLayout.Finish`'s 8 DIP, `SoundPartTile`'s 8 DIP).

**Now** (`LineItem`, the rule in its summary): a list keeps no air over its first item where nothing stands over it, nor
under its last at the height the line asks for. The room is not given to the first or the last band — that would stretch
them — it goes: the rows move up to the line's top, and the line asks for that much less. Every band keeps the height
every other has: the first and the last as much room on their open side as on the other, half the room between two
items (`LineItem.Foot`). A line set taller than its items leaves the room under the last unlit; no band grows into it.

- **Desktops, layouts**: their rows from the line's top, the line as tall as its rows (the `Pad`s went).
- **The quick settings pages on a line** (`PageLayout.Edges`, once for every page): a first row with nothing over it but
  room — no title, or the way back (§428's `BackHead`, an item itself) — starts at the body's top, the room over it cut
  to the half of the room under it, everything under it moving up as much; a last row with nothing under it ends the
  body, half the room the page left under it its band's, as `Row` halves the room between two. A title that is only words, a heading, a notice or a button under the rows keep
  their air. The flyout is as it was.
- **Sound's devices** (`SoundPartTile.Tail`): half the 2 DIP between two rows past the last; without a heading the
  first's band from the line's top. The mixer's apps are controls: unchanged.
- **The clipboard, contacts** (`LineItem.Foot` of their `Above`), **notifications** (half the room between two cards
  under the last card; under "See more" the list's pad), **the day's events** (none under an event, 8 DIP under words),
  **To Do** ("Add a task" the line's foot, its band the line's edge, kept on the foot of a taller line).
- A heading or a header that is only words stays unlit; the item under it reaches up to its row (unchanged).

Tests: `ItemHoverSweepTests.EveryListsItemsLightEdgeToEdgeAndTouch` sweeps every kind (and a subfolder gone into, its
head the way back) twice: at the height it asks for and 70 DIP taller. New: no strip over the first item with nothing
drawn in it; at the height asked for, no strip shorter than an item under the last with nothing drawn in it; in either,
the last item no taller than the tallest of the others (alone, no taller in the taller line). Red first, 37 failures:
*"Desktops: a strip of 6 px over its first item, nothing drawn in it, nobody's"*, the same for layouts and the keyboard
layouts; *"Keyboard: a strip of 15 px under its last item"*, the same under the clipboard, contacts, notifications,
events, To Do, desktops, layouts and every quick settings page and sound list. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`item-edges-<dark|light>.png`, the feed, a folder's contents and a subfolder, mail, notifications, the clipboard,
desktops, layouts, Wi-Fi and keyboard layouts with their first and their last item lit, as tall as asked for and taller.

By hand: Theme Graphite, a folder with the desktops, the layouts or the keyboard layouts: point at the first row — lit
from the section's top edge; at the last — lit to its bottom edge, as tall as the others. Set a line taller: the room
under the last stays unlit. The clipboard's, Wi-Fi's and the sound devices' last rows reach the section's foot.

## 437. Notifications on the kit: a Header, a heading per app, each notification an item edge to edge (2026-10-30)

The person: *"notifications dont look good yet. they should be redesigned with the edge to edge style as well. they
should fit in with the other widgets in terms of style."*

**Where it was.** The last list still drawing Windows' cards (§185): every notification a rounded card on the gutters
(4 DIP corners, the layer fill and its stroke), 4 DIP between two, its words 12 DIP inside it, a title on two lines over
a body on four, a 48 DIP picture beside them and a hero across the card's top. §428 only gave each card a band reaching
over the room round it; the cards stayed. The header was "Notifications" on the gutter with no glyph; an app's heading
the Caption; "See more" a button at a row's end; nothing new a line of words centred under the header, three rows tall.

**Now: the kit's list, as mail's and the feed's** (`NotificationPartTile`: `Lay`, `Grouped`, `ItemOf`, `Item`):
- **The Header** (`LineRow`): the bell in the leading column in the accent, "Notifications" strong at the text edge, how
  many as its meta ("7"), do not disturb's toggle and "Clear all" against the trailing gutter. Where they do not fit the
  count gives way first, then the toggle (it is on the line's menu), then "Clear all" (the menu's, each app's ×).
- **An app's heading**, as the agenda's day (§412, §418): a compact row (32 DIP), the app's icon in the leading column,
  its name strong in the secondary ink at the text edge, a gap lower than the row's middle so it stands with its own;
  under the pointer the × that clears the app's notifications. No item: it lights nothing.
- **A notification is the kit's item** (§428): no card, no rounded plate — its band of the line, edge to edge, from its
  heading or the notification over it to the one under it, touching; lit while the pointer is on it, its controls
  included, as a WinUI list item is; a click opens its app with the toast's own arguments, as before. Its title strong on
  one line at the text edge, when it came on that line against the trailing gutter (the Caption, secondary), its body in
  the Caption's secondary ink on two lines under it, cut with an ellipsis: mail's sender, age and subject. A toast's own
  picture (appLogoOverride) stands in the leading column at the Feature size, as a headline's (§408). Under the pointer,
  in the time's place, the chevron (where there is more to it) and the ×, each a subtle button with its own target over
  the band, inside it; the title's room ends short of them at rest too, so nothing moves as the pointer comes. Where that
  leaves the title less than half the line (a narrow line, a large text) they stand on a row over it.
- **Its buttons**, Windows' own, the line's standard buttons (`LineButton`) under its words from the text edge, side by
  side, the next row where one does not fit: folded all but a box's (Send); expanded every one, under its boxes and
  selections (WinUI's shapes, unchanged) and its pictures.
- **"See more (2)" / "See fewer"**: an item of a compact row, edge to edge, the chevron in the leading column.
- **Nothing new**: the kit's Status (§388), one row — the bell, "No new notifications" (do not disturb's words while it
  is on, why where they cannot be read) — do not disturb's toggle at its end. The line asks for one row.
- **From the line's edges** (§436): the last band ends on the line's foot at the height it asks for (the header and the
  blocks, no pad); a taller line leaves the room under it unlit. No hairlines between items: mail and the feed have none.

**The same height for the same content.** A notification's band is its air (8 DIP at the item style's size, over and
under), its title's line, its body's lines and its row of buttons with a gap over it, no more: two whose bodies take one
line are the same height; one whose body takes two is one Caption line taller, never more (the body is cut to two); one
with buttons a row of buttons and a gap taller. Reserving two body lines for every notification would leave a strip of
air under a short one that reads as a gap; mail's rows are equal because its subject is always one line.

**Kept**: grouping by app and its order, the newest three and See more / See fewer, the × per notification and per app,
Clear all, do not disturb's toggle, the line's menu (right click), a click opening the app (and clearing it), buttons and
boxes activating with their arguments and values, Enter in a box, the chevron expanding all of it, scrolling under the
header, the one-row form, the item style's size, preview, pictures and time, the bell face. **Changed**: the … on a
notification and on an app's heading went (it opened the line's menu, which a right click opens); the title one line
and the body two until expanded (were two and four); a toast's buttons show folded (they showed only expanded); its
hero and inline picture show only expanded (the chevron offered where it has one); the chevron shows under the pointer
only; an app's icon shows whatever the item style's pictures (the heading's glyph, not a toast's picture).

Tests (red first): `ItemHoverSweepTests.EveryListsItemsLightEdgeToEdgeAndTouch` — its notifications two apps, chat's
three (a body of one line, one cut to two, one with buttons) over mail's one (`Sampled`), and a new rule for every kind:
nothing rounded taller than a row drawn across the line (*"NotificationsList: 8 rounded cards drawn across the line,
e.g. 18-522 × 100-200"*); `LineStyleTests.EveryLineDrawsOnTheKit` — a new rule, no words on a rounded fill across the
line taller than a row (*"NotificationsList: words on a card"*); `NotificationsPresetTests.TheLineIsTheKitsHeaderOverItsItems`
(no card; the bell and an app's icon in the leading column, "Notifications" and the words at the text edge, the bands
edge to edge and touching, the × on the trailing gutter inside its band; red: card pieces found),
`.ANotificationIsAsTallAsWhatItShows` (red: 127 px, not 85), `.NothingNewIsTheKitsStatus` (red: 130 px, not one row's
60). To the new anatomy: `ATitleTakesOneLineAndABodyTwoUntilExpanded`, `TheChevronExpandsANotification`,
`NothingOverlapsAtNarrowWidthsAndLargeText` (inside its band, not its card), `ListLinesTests.TheNotificationLineIsItsOwnListAtEveryHeight`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `notifications-beside-<dark|light>.png` (new: mail, the feed, the notifications at rest, one
lit, its × lit), `notifications-preset-*.png`, `item-hover-*.png`, `item-edges-*.png`.

By hand: open the notifications: a header as mail's, each app's heading with its icon, each notification lighting from
the section's left edge to its right, the next lighting where it ends; point at one: the chevron and × where its time
was; × clears it, a click opens the app; a chat toast's Like under its words; nothing new: one row.

## 438. The dock with two rows goes (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the dock with two rows style should be removed."*

The fourth layout type of §130 is gone, whole: `LayoutType.DockRows` (`"dockRows"`), its Type choice and its words
(`settings.layouts.type.dockRows`, every language), `LayoutTypes.Stacks`, `TaskbarLayout.RowsAt`, `EdgeBar.Rows`, the
window a row (`DockWindow.StackIndex`, `IsStacked`), the rows' joined panels (`RowJoin`, `Scene.JoinRows`,
`DockPanel.Joined`/`Parted`/`Empty`, `Scene.InHalves`, the strip's hard clip the joins needed), and a row's place among
its edge's (`Layout.Stacking`: the room a row on another kept in what the main row reserved, its tooltips, popups and
edit bars past it, the shared height drag). The Type choice offers **Taskbar, Dock, Top and bottom**. Each edge has one
bar again, so a window is its edge's or its place's, and `Layout.FrameFor` is the edge's strip at one bar's most
thickness rather than two. Top and bottom keeps both rows (`BarRow.Main`, `BarRow.Top`) and Ctrl+Up/Down between its
bars (`TaskbarLayout.Step`).

No config changes: the person's file has Taskbar layouts only. A file that still says `"dockRows"` reads as a value
outside the enum (`TolerantEnumConverter`), which `Config.Repair` makes a **Taskbar**; every widget keeps its row and
section, the top row's unseen until the layout is a Top and bottom.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheTypeChoiceOffersTaskbarDockAndTopAndBottomOnly` (red first: the choices were Taskbar, Dock,
"Dock, two rows", Top and bottom). `DockRowsTests` and the `dock-rows-*` picture sheets went with the type; the
theories that listed it (`NamedLayoutsTests`, `EdgeModesTests`, `LicensingTests`, `EditPlacePictures`,
`SideBarPictures`) list the three.

## 439. Changed elsewhere: the brightness follows the keyboard's keys; the hotspot, the magnifier and the battery line's power mode too (2026-10-30)

The person (2026-10-20): *"when i change the brightness on my keyboard it does not change it on the widget. fix that.
also fix that for other widgets if there is a similar bug for them"*. The fix was made then on a branch that never
reached this version (built on the code of 2026-10-20); this restores it on today's code. Nothing a later section
decided is touched: the brightness is still one slider with no flyout (§35, §103), greyed where it sets nothing (§247),
quiet on the bar (§367).

**Why it stood still.** `Brightness` read every display when it was made, after each write of its own and on
`WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` (`DisplaysChangedIfMade`); nothing else asked it to read again (its `Refresh` had no caller but the
tests). The keyboard's brightness keys, Windows' quick settings and Settings slider, adaptive brightness and the power
plan dimming all move a laptop's own screen without Karpo, and the widget kept the level it last read.

**The built-in screen.** Windows sends the power setting `GUID_VIDEO_CURRENT_MONITOR_BRIGHTNESS` — the level the panel
shows now, a DWORD 0–100 — to a window registered for it, as `WM_POWERBROADCAST` / `PBT_POWERSETTINGCHANGE`, on every
change and once at registration. Seen on the person's laptop on 2026-10-20 with a probe's window (the level moved by
`WmiSetBrightness`, Settings' slider's road, and by the power plan's own brightness, and put back exactly): it came every
time within 20 ms with the new level. `GUID_DEVICE_POWER_POLICY_VIDEO_BRIGHTNESS`, the plan's level, which dimming and
adaptive brightness leave alone, is not the one followed.

- The dock's host registers for it at the start beside energy saver (`Brightness.Follow`, through `EnergySaver.Register`,
  now shared), undone with the dock.
- `WndProc` hands the notice to `Brightness.HeardIfMade` whatever the dock is doing (in a menu's loop too), which makes
  nothing where no widget made the service. `Brightness.Read(POWERBROADCAST_SETTING*)` reads the level; `PanelSaid(level)`:
  where every built-in screen is at that level already and none is being written, it is our own write coming back and
  nothing is read; else the worker reads the built-in screens again (`Step(…, panelsOnly)`: WMI, a few ms, never a
  monitor's DDC/CI; every display on a PC where none was found built in) and raises `Changed` only where a level moved.
- The host's own `WM_POWERBROADCAST` case keeps this notice from the islands (`Dock.BrightnessOnly`): the battery and
  energy saver read again on any power setting and have nothing new to read for a brightness key.
- No timer, no WMI event sink.

**An external monitor.** DDC/CI has no event: a monitor's own buttons tell nobody, and polling would wake an idle bar.
The widget reads every display again where somebody is about to look: as it comes into view (`BrightnessIsland.Visible`:
its bar shown, its folder opened) and as the pointer comes onto it — the bar's cell (`CellIsland.PointerCame`, called from
the bar's `HoverChanged` for the widget under the pointer; nothing for any other kind) or a line (`CardHover`, coming onto
it, not moving over it). `Brightness.Look` does it at most every `LookEveryMs` (3 s), timed from the service being made,
which read them all (`Brightness.StandClock` for the tests).

**A drag is the pointer's.** A level read during a drag must not move the thumb under the pointer: the bar's slider draws
the level the drag last asked (`dragged`, `BarLevel`) while it holds the thumb and the displays' once it lets go
(`Release` asks for a paint); the line's slider kept its own already (`Slider.Dragging`).

**The others the audit of 2026-10-20 found not following**, checked again on today's code (all three as they were then):

- **The mobile hotspot.** Its switch heard `NetworkStatusChanged` alone, which a hotspot switched in Windows' own panel
  does not always raise. Now it also hears the hotspot's adapter and address coming and going (`InterfaceWatch`:
  `NotifyIpInterfaceChange`, `NotifyUnicastIpAddressChange`, as the wired line follows its cable), finds the manager again
  on the pool, one look for a burst, and once more `HotspotSwitch.AgainMs` (1.5 s) after the last (`HotspotSwitch.Heard`;
  it is handed what it finds, what it follows and a clock). New since then and the same: the hotspot face's and page's
  source (`WindowsHotspot`, the mobile hotspot preset of §93) heard `NetworkStatusChanged` alone too, and the face waited for its
  30 s look; it now follows the same news the same way (`HotspotSwitch.Follow`, `WindowsHotspot.Heard`, one read for a
  burst in `Poll`).
- **The magnifier**, started or stopped by Win+Plus or Win+Esc, said nothing. The dock's shell hook sees its `MagUIClass`
  window come and go (`WindowsAssistive.IsMagnifier`, seen with a probe on 2026-10-20: `HSHELL_WINDOWCREATED`, then
  `HSHELL_WINDOWDESTROYED`, the class readable at both), handed to the islands as `AssistiveSwitch.WM_KARPO_MAGNIFIER`
  (`WM_APP + 0x2E`, never posted), and the switch reads it `MagnifierAgainMs` (300 ms) later.
- **The battery line's "Power mode"** (its tallest form): its source was made but never started, so a mode changed in
  Settings › Power & battery showed at the line's next minute. The source is started as the line first draws it
  (`BatteryIsland.Times`), and its news draws the line.

Everything else the audit listed (the volume and mutes, the sound devices, the radios, airplane mode, night light, energy
saver, the toggles, rotation lock, the VPN, nearby sharing, the battery, the power mode line, the keyboard layout, do not
disturb, now playing, the narrator, sticky keys, spatial sound) follows Windows' own news, as it did.

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `BrightnessTests` — `TheBuiltInScreenMovedElsewhereIsReadAgainWhenWindowsSaysSo` (the panel read again on the
notice, a monitor not), `OurOwnWriteComingBackReadsNothing` (and the same level heard while a write is on its way read
all the same; another setting's notice not brightness's), `TheNotificationIsReadForItsLevel` (clamped, too short, another
setting, none; `BrightnessOnly`), `WithNoScreenFoundBuiltInTheNewsReadsEveryDisplay`,
`ALookReadsEveryDisplayAtMostEveryFewSeconds`. `BrightnessWidgetTests` (`KARPO_UI_TESTS`) — `ALevelChangedElsewhereIsDrawn`
(the bar's thumb where the keys left it, found by its ink; the bar and a line asking to be drawn; the line's slider at the
