new level), `AChangeDuringADragDoesNotMoveTheThumb` (bar and line), `AMonitorsButtonsAreReadAsTheWidgetComesIntoViewOrUnderThePointer`.
`ChangedElsewhereTests` — `TheHotspotFollowsTheNetworksNews`, `TheHotspotsFaceFollowsTheNetworksNews` (new: a read for a
burst, once more after it, let go with it), `TheMagnifierIsReadAgainWhenItsWindowComesOrGoes`,
`OnlyTheMagnifiersWindowIsTheMagnifiers`, `ABatteryLineFollowsThePowerModeMovedElsewhere` (followed from its first paint,
not its measure: today's `ListHeight` asks the source nothing). Pictures: `brightness-followed-<before|after>.png`.

By hand, on the laptop: a brightness widget on the bar; press the keyboard's brightness keys — the thumb follows each
press; the same from Windows' quick settings slider and Settings › Display; hold the bar's thumb and press a key — it
stays under the pointer and shows the key's level on letting go; a monitor over DDC/CI moved with its own buttons, then
the pointer onto the widget — it follows. Switch the mobile hotspot in Windows' quick settings — the hotspot switch and
the hotspot face follow within a second or two. Win+Plus, then Win+Esc — the magnifier switch follows. Change the power
mode in Settings › Power & battery with a tall battery line open — its "Power mode" follows.


## 440. Quick settings starts at Wi-Fi while nothing plays: a divider the hidden line leaves at an end goes with it (2026-10-30)

The person (2026-10-20, on quick settings with what is playing over it): the now-playing line should be gone while
nothing plays. §319 and §327 decided that since, and better: "Hide it while nothing plays", on by default for every
now-playing line and face, no migration. They are kept as they are. One piece of the fix made then on a branch that
never reached this version is not in them, and is restored here.

**What was left.** Quick settings is what is playing, a divider, then Wi-Fi and the rest (`Presets.QuickPanelId`).
At rest with nothing playing the line leaves the list's flow (§327, `FolderFlyout.Build`'s `resting`), but the divider
under it stayed, alone at the list's top: no card split (a divider first parts nothing, `FolderListPlan.Runs`), its
room bare over Wi-Fi — 9 px at 150 % (`ADividerTheHiddenLineLeavesAtAnEndGoesWithIt` before the fix: the divider at
0..9, Wi-Fi from 9).

**Now** (`FolderFlyout.GoneAtRest`). The lines gone at rest take along each divider that, with them gone, would stand
first or last in its list or right after another divider — only one beside a line gone, so a divider the person put
at an end of a list stays where they put it, and one between two lines that stay stays. Those dividers have no box at
rest, as the lines (§327). Arranged nothing moves: every line and divider stands where it stands, greyed or not, as
before. Quick settings at rest with nothing playing starts at Wi-Fi, flush with the folder's top, as Windows' own panel
does with nothing playing; a track starting brings the line and its divider back.

No config change, no strings.

Tests: `MediaPresetTests.ADividerTheHiddenLineLeavesAtAnEndGoesWithIt` (new; red before: Wi-Fi's top 9 px under the
list's) — the quick settings preset at 150 % at rest with the line hidden: the line and the divider of no size, Wi-Fi at
the list's top and its first card's; arranged both stand; the rule alone: a divider left first, last or after another
goes, one the person put at an end beside no line gone stays, nothing gone takes nothing.

By hand: open quick settings with nothing playing: its first line is Wi-Fi at the folder's top, no gap over it; play
something: what is playing comes back over it with its divider; edit mode: both stand, the line greyed.

## 441. Styles all the way: every look setting a style's; Karpo wears one, a folder or a widget another (2026-10-30)

The person: *"ok the thing with the styles is not how i imagined it. right now there are still a lot of settings that can
be edited individually from the styles, e.g. the taskbar opacity, folder opacity etc. this should all be put into the
styles. then you should be able to give the whole application a style, and then override on a deeper level if you want
to. (e.g. for a specific folder or widget i can give it another style.) the opacity, the colors, the primary color, the
accent colors, the outline settings, etc. should all go into the style. the style itself can be rather complex or have
many settings but in the end i just want to apply the styles and not actual individual settings to widgets."*

**Replaces** §405's Theme, Customize (Background, Accent color, Text color, Reset all), Taskbar opacity, Folder opacity,
Taskbar separators, Folder separators and Outlines as settings of their own (Layout ▾ › Appearance's rows, the folder
room's right click's), §396's and §405's themes as a concept of their own (`Theme`, `Themes`, `ThemeLook`: gone), and
§429's "Default/Karpo's look" as something else than a style. §405's derivation (`ToneRules`), §429's styles, their
Light and Dark sets and "Same in dark mode", and §435's divider Style (Inherited/Grow, layout, not look) stay.

**A style holds every look setting** (`ItemStyle`, `Styled`), each Inherited until it says it:

| Setting | Kept | Karpo | A folder | A widget (bar or line) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode: Follow Windows (Inherited), Light, Dark | once | yes | yes | yes |
| Background, Accent, Text | per mode | yes | yes (button, panel, lines) | yes |
| Outlines (On, Off) | per mode | yes | yes | yes |
| Taskbar opacity (0–100 %) | per mode | yes | — | — |
| Folder opacity (0–100 %) | per mode | yes | yes (its panel) | — |
| Taskbar separators (Line, Space only, None) | once | yes | — | — |
| Folder separators (Line, Space only, None) | once | yes | yes (its dividers) | — |

What a level cannot use is left aside there (`Styled.At`, `StyleLevel`): a widget wearing Graphite is dark and graphite
but the bar keeps Karpo's opacity. The separators are once for both modes, not per mode: they make room, and a mode switch
only recolours, never moves anything (a deviation from per-mode everything, for that reason).

**One list, one concept** (`Styles.BuiltIn`, read-only, a copy the person's to change): **Follow Windows** (nothing set:
Windows' own look, what Karpo wears by default); the five themes, which set everything — **Graphite** (dark, #161616, no
outlines), **Paper** (light, warm white, ink-blue accent, outlines), **Phosphor**, **Infrared**, **Deep sea** (dark, their
§396 colours, outlines) — each with 70 % / 90 % and Line / Space only, as they drew; then §429's colour styles, which set
colours (and Subtle/Contrast/Outlined the outlines) and leave mode, opacities and separators Inherited — **Subtle**,
**Accent**, **Outlined**, **Contrast**, **Blue**, **Green**, **Orange**, **Red**, **Purple**.

**One chain**, setting by setting, in the mode drawn at each level (`Look.Wearing`, `Look.In(Styled)`, `Styled.On`):
Windows → the style Karpo wears (`Appearance.Style`) → a folder's → a widget's (a line over its folder's, a bar widget over
Karpo's). A level's mode is its style's, else the level above's (Windows' at the top). A widget or folder drawn in another
mode than what it stands on, where neither it nor what it stands in has a background, brings Windows' own background of
its mode, so its text never stands on the other mode's bar (a dark Graphite widget on a light bar is a dark card).
`Look.Dressed` makes the bar and the folders from the opacities too (`SurfaceStyle.Made`); a folder's dividers are its
style's (`Styles.SeparatorsOf`, `SeparatorStyles.Of(config, surface, folder)`).

**Menus.**
- **Layout ▾ › Appearance** is one choice, the style Karpo wears (`WidgetLooks.KarpoRow`): ours, Follow Windows first and
  ticked by default, then the person's, each with its swatch; "Styles ↗" under them. No other look row anywhere.
- **A folder's and a widget's Appearance** (`WidgetLooks.Row`, unchanged in form): Default (what it stands in), ours but
  Follow Windows (worn by a widget it would be Default again), the person's; "Styles ↗".
- **The folder room's right click**: Open folders, and its foot, Layout ↗.
- **A separator's and a divider's menu** link to "Styles ↗" (`OptionLink.Styles`; `OptionLink.TaskbarSeparators` and
  `FolderSeparators` are gone): their look is a style's.
- **Styles ↗** (`BarLooks.StyleRows`): "Built-in styles ›" (ours, a level of their own: fifteen are too many for a first
  level, R2), ruled off the person's, "Add a style" the foot. A style of the person's (`BarLooks.StyleLevelRows`): Name;
  ruled off Mode, Taskbar separators, Folder separators; ruled off Light background, accent, text, outlines, taskbar
  opacity, folder opacity; ruled off Same in dark mode and, set apart, the Dark six. Each Inherited until set and saying
  what it inherits — Karpo's style, or Windows' where the style is the one Karpo wears; an opacity a choice of Inherited,
  100 % to 0 % by tens (a value of another step from the file among them). Its level is the menu's second, every choice
  the third (R1); MenuRulesTests' allowance stays empty.

**Live.** Every surface is dressed again from the config on every change, as since §396 (`Dock.Relooked`); the cheap path
(`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer`) is now another colour of the person's style Karpo wears that no widget or folder wears too.

**The file** (no reading of the old shape; the coordinator converts the person's own once with
`karpo-coord\convert-styles2.py`):

```
appearance.theme, .colors, .taskbar, .folders      → gone
appearance.style                                   new: Karpo's style's id; left out for Follow Windows ("windows")
appearance.styles[].mode                           new: "light" | "dark"; left out for Inherited
appearance.styles[].taskbarSeparators, .folderSeparators   new: "line" | "space" | "none"; left out for Inherited
appearance.styles[].light|dark.taskbarOpacity, .folderOpacity   new: 0–100; left out for Inherited
islands[..].appearance                             unchanged: ours ("graphite", "blue") or the person's id
```

Converted: nothing customised → Karpo wears the theme's built-in; anything customised → "My style", a copy of the theme with
those values, worn by Karpo. The person's own styles keep their settings, every new one Inherited.

Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.mode|light|dark|builtIn`, `…lightTaskbarOpacity|lightFolderOpacity|darkTaskbarOpacity|
darkFolderOpacity` new; `settings.appearance.theme.header`, `…taskbarOpacity.header`, `…folderOpacity.header` deleted; the
themes' names are ours'; 30 languages.

Tests (red first, with the old code): `StyleChainTests.AStyleHoldsEveryLookSetting` (red: *"Expected True, Actual False"*
— the mode not taken from a style), `TheThemesAreOursAmongTheStyles` (red: ours were the nine colour styles),
`LayoutsAppearanceIsTheStyleKarpoWears` (red: *"Expected Choice, Actual Level"*), `EverySettingInheritsKarposThenItsFoldersThenItsOwn`
(red: opacities *"(0.4, 0.6)"* expected, *"(0.7, 0.9)"*), `AnotherModeBringsItsOwnBackground` (red), `AWidgetWearsAStyleAndNothingElse`
(red: Follow Windows' place); with the feature `AStylesLevelHoldsEverySetting`. Rewritten: `ThemeChainTests`, `AppearanceTests`,
`StyleTests`, `LineRowsTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `BarLooksTests`, `MenuPickersTests` (the colour picker on a style's
rows); live: `SceneTreeTests.EveryColourPickedReachesItsSurfacesLive` (Karpo's style's colours set, then Deep sea picked,
with a folder and a menu open). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `style-karpo-<windows|graphite|paper|phosphor>-<look>.png`
(the bar, an open folder and Layout ▾ › Appearance), `style-override-<look>.png` (Karpo in a style of the person's, a folder
in Blue, a line of it in Orange, a bar widget in Graphite), `style-editor-<look>.png`, `style-opacity-<100|70|30>-dark.png`.

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Appearance › Phosphor: everything green on black, at once. Styles ↗ › Add a style, set its
Light background and Folder opacity 100 %, pick it in Layout ▾ › Appearance. A folder's Appearance › Blue: its button, panel
and lines blue, the bar as it was; a widget in it › Graphite: a dark card in a light Windows. A separator's menu: "Styles ↗".

## 442. A finer grid: every line whole cells of half a row, n cells n times one; each form designed to fill its cells (2026-10-30)

The person, of two columns of sized lines (§432's `sized-stacks-dark.png`, "Ten rows beside ten rows"): *"on this
image there are a lot of spaces in between the individual widgets. i want them to be smaller / more densly together.
why is that here that it looks so airy in between?"* The why: every size was rounded up to whole rows of 41n − 5 DIP,
its content at the top — now playing's row with its caption, 52 DIP, stood in 77, the battery's 64 in 77 — so the air
gathered under each line. Their answer: *"yes make the grid finer but also optimize the layouts of the widgets so that
they then fill up the remaining space properly. so a combination of 1 and 3 actually."* And from before: *"design on
the cell height as well, so that it is possible to actually make designs where the widgets combined give the same
folder height."*

**The cell** (`FolderOptions.CellDip`, `FolderFlyout.CellPx`, `LineRows.Cell`): 20 DIP, half the list's row, times
the scale and the text scale, on a whole px (20, 25, 30, 35, 40 … px; 45 at 225 % text). Every line of a folder is a
whole number of cells and **n cells are n times one, exactly**: no gap between cells or lines, so a line of four rows
is two lines of two, and any two columns whose lines add up to the same cells end level, whatever the lines are. A row
is two cells (40 DIP), the fewest a line takes (`LineHeight.Fewest`). The cell grows with the text as the words do, so
"6 rows" is six rows of the list at every text size (a chart's most is the same count at every text, `LineHeight.MostOf`;
§432's text-scaled `MostAt` is gone).

- A sized line (§432) is the fewest whole cells its form measures (`LineHeight.CellsFor`); its form stands in **their
  middle** (`CellIsland.Scrolled`), the less than a cell left over shared over and under it as padding.
- An Automatic line is its content rounded **up** to whole cells (`LineHeight.Given(content, cell)`), at most its cells;
  a Fixed line its cells; a Fill line takes the room its list has left as before.
- **The file keeps cells**: `"height": { "fixed": true, "cells": 13 }` — no `"rows"` (no migration: the person's file
  is converted once, `convert-grid.py`, each `"rows": n` to `"cells": 2n`; n rows were 41n − 5 DIP, 2n cells 40n). The
  menu's stepper steps a cell and says rows, halves and all: "6 rows", "6½ rows" (`LineHeightRows.Count`; the key
  `dock.edit.height.rowsAndAHalf` in all 30 languages, each language's plural with "½" after the count).

**The kit on the cells** (`LineKit.cs`): a row two cells (40); a row with its caption **three** (60, not 52), the name
and the caption one block on its middle; a row with its caption **and a meter** three as well — the meter in the block
under the caption (`RowSpec.Under`, `LineMeter.Room`/`Under`), not a band under the row. The compact 32 of a dense list
stays an inner pitch; the line it is in is rounded up to cells. A list of caption rows (removable drives, quakes) is
then 60 an item, three cells.

**Each form on its cells** (at 100 %; rows ×2 in the registry, `ListWidget.Cells`, `LineForm.Cells`, `MostCells`, all
in cells):

| Kind | Compact | Medium | Full | How it fills them |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Now playing | 2 | 3 | 6 | Medium the kit's caption row; Full that row with the timeline under the artist in its block, the times in the middle of the next cell, the app's row (2) |
| Battery | 2 | 3 | 5 | the caption row with the meter in its block; Full the saver and power mode lines in the middle of a row under it |
| Security | 2 | 3 | 7 | the caption row; Full and a row per protection (3 + 2 + 2) |
| Drive, network drive | 2 | — | 3 | the caption row with the meter in its block (was 64 in 77) |
| Volume, brightness | 2 | 4 | 7 | Medium the flyout's 36-DIP button row over its slider, in the middle; Full the large level, the air spread over, between and under — none under the slider, whose box keeps its own |
| Clock | 2 | — | 5 | the face as tall as the cells; the time and the date in the middle of its height |
| Time header | 2 | 4 | 5 | the time and the date in the whole cells that hold them with 6 (Medium) or 8 DIP of air, the rest shared over and under (Full 100, was 102 in 118) |
| Alarm, the sun's times | 2 | — | 3 | the caption row |
| Switches | 2 | — | 3, or 4 where what a click does wraps | the name over its description |
| Pin | 2 | — | 4 | the large name over what it opens, in the middle |
| Timer, focus, date header, dawn, dusk | 2 | | | the row |
| Toggles | 3 | | | the buttons in the middle |
| Weather hours, Win+P, nearby sharing, power mode, markets, day bar, ring, details | | | 7, 12, 18, 10, 6, 6, 8, as their facts | their page or chart in the middle of the cells |

The two picture sheets add up: now playing, the battery, a timer, a clock and an alarm (3 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 3) beside a
pin, Security's row, the volume, a drive and the time (2 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 5), 16 cells each; and now playing whole, a
battery's row, Security whole and a timer (6 + 2 + 7 + 2) beside a clock, the volume large, an alarm and a pin
(5 + 7 + 3 + 2), 17 each — both level at 100, 125 and 150 %. (At 225 % text a form may say less to fit its width — now
playing keeps play alone — and two columns need not add up then.)

Tests (red first): `FolderGridTests.ColumnsOfTheSameCellsEndLevel` (fixed lines 8 | 4 + 4 | 2 + 6 | 3 + 3 + 2 at 100,
125, 150, 200 % and 100, 125, 225 % text; red with rows: *"100 %, 100 % text: columns of the same cells are 323, 318,
318, 313 px"*), `.NCellsAreNTimesACell`; `SizedLinesTests.EverySizeIsWholeCellsAndItsFormFillsThem` (every sized kind,
every size, 100 and 150 %, 100 and 225 % text: whole cells, its declared cells, inside its line, and no more air under
its form than over it, give or take 4 DIP; red: *"Media Medium … 18 px of air under its form, 12 over it"*, Security
Medium, Battery Medium *"24 px … 13 over it"*, the volume's Full *"14 px … 7 over it"*, the switches, the drives, the
sun's times …; the clock was not red by ink, its face filling its rows, but its words stood at the top of it and now
stand in its middle), `.ListsOfTheSameCellsEndLevel` (both sheets), `LineHeightRowsTests.TheStepperSaysRowsAndHalves`,
`LineSizeTests.AFormIsTheFewestWholeCellsThatHoldIt`, `ListBoundsTests.TheRule` (in cells), the file's `"cells"` read
and written (`ListBoundsTests`, `HeightLimitsTests`, `RemovableHeightTests`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`sized-stacks-<dark|light>.png`, `sized-mixed-<dark|light>.png`, `sized-sizes-<group>.png`, `sized-<size>.png`.

By hand: a folder of now playing, the battery, a timer and a clock beside Notes, Security, the volume, a drive and the
time header: the two columns end level, each line's words in the middle of its band, no band of air under any. A
line's Height stepper: "Rows − 6½ rows +", a click a half row. A list of mail or devices: as dense as before, at most
a few px more at its foot.

## 443. The clock's looks: Time only, Stacked, Analog; the volume's ">" on the speaker's row (2026-10-30)

The person: *"the speakers widget layout seems off"* and *"the clock should also have the mode where it just shows the
time without the date. add some more clock styles as well. (digital, two numbers etc...)"*

**The volume's line** (`SliderLine.Lay`, the brightness's too). In a folder the ">" to the outputs' page was placed
by the volume itself, centred on the whole line: in Medium it stood alone at the trailing edge between the speaker's
row and the slider's, and the slider ran from under the speaker's button to short of the ">". Now `SliderLine` places
the ">" (`Boxes.Page`) as the last control of the speaker's row, its middle level with the speaker's, and the row's level
and the output's name end before it; a slider with a row of its own (Medium, Full) runs from where the words begin to the
trailing gutter, its thumb at either end touching them. Compact is the flyout's row — speaker, slider, level, ">";
Medium the speaker, the output and the level with the ">" over the slider; Full the speaker and the output with the ">",
the level large, the slider. `Lay` takes the line's width and whether it has a page instead of the gutters.

**The clock's looks** (`ClockStyles`, `ClockTile`). The clock's Style row (§411's glossary: a widget's form is its
Style) was the clock and the time and date. The clock's form now comes in looks, entries of the same choice, as a
reading's figure is its graph's form drawing no graph (`WidgetStyles.LooksOf`'s `Look`, now with `Is` and `Make` for
any such entry): *Analog and digital* (the clock as it was, first), *Time only*, *Stacked*, *Analog*, then *Time and
date* (the other form, unchanged). Each its own icon: a clock in a frame, a figure, lines over each other, the face,
the date and time. A pick keeps the line, its id, size and options, and goes back (R5). "Show seconds", the zone and
the label apply to every look; the time is Windows' own format, so 12 or 24 hours as the region says.

| Look | Compact (one row, 2 cells) | Full (the fewest whole cells, §442) |
|---|---|---|
| Analog and digital | glyph, the date or the place, the time in the Value | the time as the Display over the date and the place, a face beside them (5 cells, 6 with a place) |
| Time only | glyph, the time in the Value where names begin, the place quiet at the trailing gutter; no date | the time as the Display, the place under it; no date (4 cells, 5 with a place) |
| Stacked | glyph, the date or the place, the hours over the minutes in the Body strong, a 12-hour mark before them | the hours over the minutes as the Display, the seconds and the mark small beside them, the date and the place beside the pair (5 cells) |
| Analog | glyph, the date or the place, a face as tall as the row (the quarters' ticks alone) | the date and the place, the face beside them as tall as the line (as the clock as it was: 5 cells, 6 with a place) |

New clocks start as the clock as it was. Stacked splits the time Windows wrote by its runs of figures
(`ClockTile.Split`: "2:20 PM" is 2, 20 and "PM"; "午後 2:20" is 2, 20 and "午後"). Four strings in all 30 languages
(`core.clockStyle.*`).

**The file.** The clock's options say the look: `"clock": { "style": "timeOnly" }` (`timeOnly`, `stacked`, `analog`);
the clock as it was says nothing, so the person's five clocks (Full, no style) need no conversion and read as they
were. A word not known is the clock as it was (`ClockStyles.Known`, in `Normalize`).

Tests (red first): `VolumeLineTests.TheChevronIsOnTheSpeakersRowAndTheSliderUnderTheWords` (every size, 100 and 150 %,
100 and 225 % text; red: *"Medium at 100 %, 100 % text: the ">" stands at 38, the speaker's row at 18"*, *"the track
starts at 22, not where the words do (44)"*, *"the ">" stands between the rows"*), `ClockStylesTests` (the Style row's
looks and icons, a pick, the file's `"style"` and an unknown word; red: *"Actual: ["Clock", "Time and date"]"*),
`ClockStyleLinesTests.EachLooksPartsAreInsideItsLineAndItShowsWhatItIs` (red: *"TimeOnly Compact … a date, which it
does not show"*), `.EachLookFillsItsCells`, `.StackedSplitsTheTime`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`clock-styles-<dark|light|225>.png`, `slider-sizes-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png`, `slider-sizes-225.png`.

By hand: a folder with the volume in Medium: the ">" at the end of the speaker's row, the slider under the words. A
clock's right click in edit mode: Style, five looks each with its icon; Time only shows no date at either size.

## 444. A style's outline all the way round its widget, among widgets with none (2026-10-31)

The person: *"if a style that is applied to a widget has outlines, the outlines should be applied to all the widget
borders, right now it does only show for some of the borders."*

The why: §410 draws a section's outline as the section's own rim, round its rounded corners, and between two lines a
single hairline, the seam drawn by the lower line inside its top; every other side of a line's shape stands past its
box, cut off. That holds where every line is outlined as the folder is. A line wearing a style with outlines (§441) in
a folder without them — or outlined in another colour — showed only the seam over it, if a line stood there; its sides,
its foot and its section's ends were the section's rim in the folder's colour or nothing.

**The rule** (`FolderFlyout.LineShape`, `LineDrawn`, `SectionRim`). A line's outline is **its own** where it differs from
the folder's card outline (the one every line wearing no style has; clear for none):
- **The seams**: over it, drawn by itself inside its top wherever a line stands right over it (as §410); under it, by
  itself inside its foot too where the line under it is not outlined alike. Lines outlined alike: one hairline. Lines
  outlined differently: each its own edge, side by side. A line with none under an outlined one: the outlined one's.
- **An outline of its own** runs round all four sides inside its box: the ring (`Line.Ring`, a rounded rectangle over
  its fill in the same brush), its sides inside the section's clip next to the panel's rim, at its section's top or foot
  round the section's rounded corners (the clip's radius less half a hairline, concentric with it), elsewhere its ends
  past the box — there the seams are the line's rectangle's, square. Beside a separator's line (Line) it draws its edge
  inside its band too, so its outline is whole; a line outlined as the folder is still leaves that side to the separator.
- **Outlined as the folder is**: as §410 — the section's rim round the section, single hairlines between lines.

Under the pointer and pressed the ring stays over the highlight (§325), in its line's visual, so it goes with a line
carried or lifted. **The bar** was already right (§376: a widget in an outline of its own is a card of its own, rounded
at all four corners, ringed by `Rounded.Sides`); held now with a style's outline.

Tests: `FolderOutlineTests.AnOutlineOfItsOwnRunsRoundItsLineAmongPlainOnes` (a style with a magenta text and outlines on
a switch between two plain ones, the battery at its section's top, a switch at its section's foot, the memory alone in
a section; dark and light, 100, 125, 150, 200 %, at rest, the first hovered, and in a folder outlined as Karpo outlines
it: every side and every rounded corner in the outline's own colour; red before: *"folder-outline-own-dark-150-rest:
line 1 (airplaneMode)'s bottom is #FF242424, 0.00 of its outline #FF643564"*, its left and right only the panel's grey
rim, *"0.19 of its outline"*, the same for every own line's outer sides and corners), `FolderFlushTests` (every line of
every section, its rectangle and ring: none outlined; outlined as the section, a single hairline and no ring; its own
among plain ones and among lines outlined otherwise), `SceneTreeTests.AStylesOutlineRunsRoundItsWidgetAmongPlainOnes`
(the bar, green from the start). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `folder-outline-own-<look>-<scale>-<rest|hover|outlined>.png`,
`widget-look-own-outline-<rest|hover>-<look>.png`.

By hand: a folder with no outlines; a widget in it › Appearance › a style with Outlines on: its line outlined on all four
sides, round the section's corners where it stands at its top or foot. Theme Paper (outlines) with one line wearing a
style of another colour: that line ringed in its colour, the seams beside it two hairlines, the rest single.

## 445. A to-do line's lists under their account's name, said once (2026-10-31)

The person: *"the task lists should be grouped under the account name and not the email that is shown for every list
again and again. same for other account widgets if applicable."*

**Where it was.** A to-do line's List level (§324, §411) ruled the lists off by where they come from and said the
place on a second line under every list: "On this PC" under each of this PC's, the account's address under each of
its To Do lists — an account of nine lists said its address nine times, and named the account by its address.

**Now** (`OptionMenu.OwnedLevel`). Where the person's own things in a level come from more than one place, each place
is a heading over its run, its name said once: "On this PC", then each account by its name; no list says where it is
kept. "New list", which makes one on this PC, stands right under them (R9) under a rule, so it is not read as the last
account's. From one place alone — this PC's lists without an account, or one account's lists and none on this PC —
there is no heading at all: the level's title says what they are, and a heading over everything would say nothing.
So with a single account the heading stands only where this PC has lists too, to tell the two apart.

**An account's name** (`AccountNames.Of`, Karpo.Accounts): the name the account gave (a Microsoft account's display
name, a DAV server's), else its address; and where two accounts would read the same — the person's own Microsoft
account and their work's, both "Ann Smith" — each its address, which tells them apart. The same name everywhere:
⚙ › Accounts lists an account by it, its address under it (one by its address has its kind under it, as before), and
a to-do line's lists stand under it (`TodoSource.AccountName`, from `TodoSources.Of`). The remove question and an
error still say the address: there it is what is meant.

**The other account widgets.** None lists things per account: the mail, the calendars, the agenda and the contacts
show what every account holds as one, and which inboxes, calendars and address books an account syncs is ⚙ ›
Accounts › the account's (§351, §399), already one submenu per account, under headings by kind. Nothing else said
the address again and again; the contacts' header naming the one address book's account ("312 contacts in …") says
it once and keeps the address.

**The menu rules** (§411). R10 — no headings in a settings menu — keeps one exception, read off the rows: a heading
straight over a ticked row of a level of the person's own things, the place a choice's things come from. The menu
corpus's to-do line now has its lists as the dock lists them (renamed and deleted in place: `MenuCorpus.NoLists`),
this PC's and an account's, so R10 and R13 walk the headings; R13 treats a choice's things in such a level as the
person's own, buttons or none. The allowance stays empty.

No config change, no new strings.

Tests (red first): `OwnedLevelsTests.AToDoLinesListsAreEveryListOfEverySourceInOneLevel` — two accounts × two lists
and this PC's: three headings ("On this PC", "Ann Smith", "Contoso"), no list with a second line, the rule over "New
list", the two "Tasks" each its own account's; from one place no heading (red: *"Expected ["On this PC", "Home", "Ann
Smith", …] Actual ["Home", "", "Tasks", "Groceries", "", …]"*); `.AnAccountIsListedByItsNameItsAddressUnderIt` (red:
*"("me@outlook.com", "Microsoft account")"*); `AccountNamesTests` — `AnAccountIsShownByItsNameElseItsAddress`,
`TwoAccountsOfOneNameAreShownByTheirAddresses`, `AnAccountsToDoListsCarryItsName` (red: the addresses, the sources'
names null); `MenuRulesTests.EveryMenuKeepsTheRules` (red with the corpus's lists before the rule's exception: *"R10
List › On this PC — a heading"*, *"R10 List › Ada Lovelace — a heading"*). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`items-todo-lists-dark.png`, `items-accounts-dark.png`.

By hand: a to-do line's right click in edit mode › List: "On this PC" over this PC's lists and the Microsoft account's
name over its To Do lists, no address under any list, "New list" under a rule. ⚙ › Accounts: the Microsoft account by
its name, the address under it.

## 446. A folder slides in from its bar and goes back the same way; Folder animation in Behavior (2026-10-31) — superseded by §489 (2026-11-02)

The person: *"add animations (optional that also can be configured) for when opening / closing folders."*

**Where it was.** A folder came up at once (§355: "Opening is not animated", as every popup of Karpo's) and went
with the 83 ms fade every popup closes in.

**Now** (`FolderMotion.cs`, `FlyoutHost.Move`). A folder comes in as Windows 11's taskbar flyouts do and goes back
the same way, all on the compositor: one value per showing, the panel's opacity and its offset from its bar, run
on Windows' curves; nothing drawn per frame, nothing laid out again, the window standing still (§355).

| Folder animation | Comes in | Goes |
|---|---|---|
| Slide (the default) | 200 ms, decelerate (0, 0, 0, 1), 32 DIP out from its bar's side, fading in | 120 ms, accelerate (0.7, 0, 1, 0.5), back toward its bar, fading out |
| Fade | 167 ms, decelerate, where it stands | 83 ms, accelerate |
| Off | at once | at once |

- **Its bar's side**: down from a top bar, up from a bottom bar, out from a side bar. The box (§355) is clipped at
  the bar's inner side, so it comes out from under the bar, as Windows' flyouts do. Arranged it fades where it
  stands: its guide lines and slots reach the display's edges, which a slide would show moving.
- **Windows' Animation effects off**: Off, whatever is chosen (`Look.Animations`).
- **Another folder opened while one is open** (a click on the next face, or hovering across the faces): the new one
  is there at once and the old one goes under it, as it closes. Never a frame of neither and never two moving
  across each other.
- **A close as it comes in**, or an opening as it goes: it turns back from where it is (`MotionClock`, the eased
  progress read at the moment), in the share of the time that is left of the way. No jump to the whole folder,
  and no start from nothing.
- **Input at once**: the panel takes presses, hover and the keys where it ends from the first frame (the window's
  region and its hit tests are where it stands). Menus over it, edit mode and the open face (§376) do as before.
- **Never left invisible**: §355 kept popups from animating in because DWM can stop every app's animations at once.
  The opening's timer puts the panel where it ends (`FlyoutHost.Arrived`, 250 ms after its time) whether or not DWM
  ran it, as the close's timer always hid the window. A folder shown again while open (an arrange handing it on,
  §357) stands where it stands. Other popups keep their 83 ms fade out and still come up at once.

**The setting** (`BarLooks.Behaviour`, `FolderAnimationRow`). Layout ▾ › Behavior, last, under "Open folders":
"Folder animation", Slide, Fade, Off, a pick going back (§411 R3, R5). It is the layout's, as Open folders is. In the
file it is the layout's `"folderAnimation"`: `"slide"`, `"fade"`, `"off"`. Left out it means Slide, so no config needs
converting. A word this build does not know reads as Slide (`Config.Repair`). Four strings in every language
(`settings.general.folderAnimation.*`).

## 447. The day's events look as the agenda's: one row, drawn by one class (2026-10-31)

The person: *"for the days style, events should look similar as in agenda view."* The calendar's styles are Agenda,
Day's events, Day, Week, Month, Year (§209). The day's events (`events`, `EventsTile`) were the flyout's list (§80):
52 DIP a row, the time and the place under the title, its own colour bar and Join, its own size and parts to choose
(`ItemForm`) — the agenda's rows (§413, §414, §418) drawn a second way. That is the style meant: the one whose events
are a list like the agenda's and looked otherwise. The Day (`dayView`) is the day on hours, an event a block as tall
as it lasts beside the others at its time, the week's grid with one column; its blocks are left as they are (the
marker, the title, the time under it, the Join), as a time grid draws them: listed, the Day would be the day's events
twice.

**One class.** `AgendaEvents` (Calendar\AgendaEvents.cs) draws a day's heading, a status row ("No events") and an
event's row, and keeps what the pointer and the keys do with them — the lit row, the press, the click that opens the
event or joins the meeting, Enter, the menu's "Join meeting", a Join's tooltip (§434). The agenda (`CalendarIsland`)
and the day's events are both made of it; what each had of its own is gone (the day's events' `Lay`, `EventRow`,
`RowKind`, its painting and its hit-testing; the agenda's row helpers).

**The day's events now:** the day's name ("Today", "Tomorrow", the date) strong in a 40-DIP row with the refresh at its
end, as before; under it every event of the day as the agenda's row: one compact row (32 DIP), its calendar's colour
in the leading column, its title at the text edge and whose holiday it is after it, when it is ("All day",
"14:00–15:00", its start where the title would have no room) against the trailing gutter in the Caption's secondary
ink, a meeting's Join at its end; lit edge to edge under the pointer, opening the event in a calendar. "No events",
"Loading…", no calendar and what went wrong are the kit's Status rows, compact too. The line is its name's row and a
compact row for each; held shorter, its events scroll under the name, as before.

**Config:** the day's events offer no item style any more, as the agenda (`ItemStyles.Offer`: no parts, not sized):
a line's `"items"` (a size, `"preview"`, `"time"`) is dropped when the file is read and written again. No migration.

Tests (red first): `DayEventsRowsTests.TheDaysEventsAreTheAgendasRows` — today's events in both lines at 100 and 150 %,
100 and 225 % text: every piece of an event (its colour, title, whose, time, Join) where the agenda's same event has
it in its row and saying the same, a compact row each, the line its name's row and the rows (red, 90 in all: *"the
day's events 300 px tall, not its heading's 40 and 5 rows of 32"*, *""Focus time" has no time in the day's events, the
agenda's time 1 "14:00–15:00""*, *"… has no colour …"*); `ItemStylesTests.EveryLineOfItemsOffersWhatItsItemsHave` (the
day's events offer what the agenda does). `EventOpenTests`, `JoinEverywhereTests.TheDaysEventsJoinTheirMeetings` and
`CalendarWeatherFolderTests` read the rows as the line lays them out (`EventsTile.Rows`, its pieces);
`ItemHoverSweepTests` holds them lit edge to edge. Picture (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `day-events-<dark|light>.png`, the
agenda, the day's events and the day side by side, the meeting under the pointer.

By hand: a calendar line in Day's events: each event one row as in the agenda, the time on the right, a meeting's Join
at its end; hover: the row lights edge to edge; click: the event opens. The Day: unchanged.

## 448. config.json is never lost to a save that failed, a file held at the start, or a newer Karpo (2026-10-31)

The person: *"i dont want people complaining ... that a settings file get overwritten"*. config.json's write
itself was sound (a temporary file through to the disk, File.Replace with config.json.bak, the lock, the three-way
merge, the recoveries); what was around it was not:

- **A save that failed was gone.** The dock's three saves (`Apply`, `KeepHeight`, `SaveConfig`) wrote the failure to
  a console a windowed Karpo does not have, or raised an error only edit mode shows. The bars showed the change; after
  a restart it was gone. Now every save of the dock's goes through one way (`Dock.KeepConfig`, `ConfigSaves`): a
  change the file does not take is remembered, tried again on a timer (`CONFIG_SAVE`: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s … a minute), after
  the file changed and was read again, and as Karpo ends — quit, and the session ending (`WM_QUERYENDSESSION`, then
  `Shutdown`). It is an error of the settings' on the edit bar at once (§394); once it has failed three times in a row
  the bar's own menu leads with "Settings not saved", why under it, and a click tries again — outside edit mode.
- **A file from a newer Karpo** is never written: not by a save of this build's (as before), and now not through a
  merge either — a newer Karpo's write met by this build's save refused it (`NewerConfigException`) instead of being
  merged through this build's model, which dropped what it doesn't know. Said at once, plainly (`dock.fault.newer`),
  and not tried again until the file changes.
- **A file held as Karpo started** (a backup tool, a scanner) left the defaults standing until the file next
  changed, and the first save merged the defaults into the person's file (the display they stood on took the
  default layout). The defaults now stand in as `Config.Unread`: never saved (`Config.Save` refuses), read again on
  a timer (`CONFIG_READ`: half a second, doubling to eight) until the file reads, and then replaced by the file as it
  is, nothing of the defaults' on top. A reload that met the file held (`ConfigReload.Busy`) is read again the same way.
- **The lock** another process held past a save's patience (5 s) let the save go ahead without it, where that
  process's save under way could come down on top. Now a save or an import refuses (the dock tries again), a load or
  a reload reads and writes nothing back. A lock that cannot be opened at all (an elevated Karpo's) is as before.
- **A folder's lines** (`lists`, a list of lists) merged as the saver's whole: a line Karpo.exe --add-preset-layout
  or a hand edit put into a folder while the dock edited the same folder was lost. They merge as one folder now
  (`ConfigMerge.MergeLists`): each list by the islands its lines hold, a line moved between lists where the side that
  moved it put it, the lists told apart by their place. A folder's faces, which have no id, merge by their kind.
- **A load writes the file back only for ids it made up** (`Config.MadeUpIds`), which another process would make up
  differently. Not for anything else Repair does — what it drops (a widget of a kind this build doesn't know), clamps
  or fills in, every process does alike as it reads. The next save writes it.
- **The shape follows the model** (`ConfigSchemaTests`, `ConfigWords.txt`): every property, enum word, folder line's
  kind and face kind the file may hold is listed under the shape it belongs to, and one added without raising
  `Config.Shape` fails the test. So a newer build's file says a newer shape whenever it holds something an older build
  doesn't know, and the older build leaves it alone instead of saving it without that. Keeping what a build doesn't
  know in the model (`[JsonExtensionData]`, which does work under AOT) was tried and set aside: a key this build has no
  property for is also how a key Karpo retired reads, and those are meant to leave the file.

Strings: `dock.fault.newer`, `dock.notSaved.title`, in 30 languages. No config change.

Tests: `ConfigSavesTests` (a change made while the file is held lands once it is free, with no other edit; tried
again less often, told after three; a newer file told at once and never written; a file held at start read again
until it reads, its defaults never written; every save of the dock's through ConfigSaves), `RecoveryTests
.AFileLockedAtStartIsNeverWrittenOverAndIsReadOnceItIsFree`, `LockTests`, `NewerFileTests`, `ConfigMergeTests`
(a folder's lines in the current shape, faces by kind, a line the CLI added surviving the dock's edit of the folder),
`ConfigSchemaTests`.

## 449. A meter keeps a button's gap from every control (2026-10-31)

The person: *"for example in the focus time when the timer is running the progress bar and the pause button touch.
this should not be. fix this for similar widgets where this happens as well."* A running timer's meter was drawn a
tight step over its row's foot from the text edge to the trailing gutter, under the buttons standing on the row's
middle: at 100 % its top at 32 DIP, the pause button's plate ending at 32.

**The rule.** No meter, progress bar, timeline or slider (as far as its thumb goes) comes nearer a control — a line
button, plated or subtle, a switch, the refresh button — than a button's gap (`LineButton.GapDip`, 8 DIP), across or
down, nor into where a press on the control lands (`LineButton.Hit`).

**In the kit** (`LineMeter`): `LineMeter.Box` places a meter from the text edge to the trailing gutter, or the gap short
of the first of its row's controls it would otherwise come nearer than the gap. Every meter on a row goes through it:
`Under` (the battery's and a drive's, in the room under the caption), `Foot` (the timer's and focus's while they run:
now under the words, ending under the time), and now playing's timeline (whose own "short of the transport" went).
The sound rows (`SoundRows.Line`, `MixIn`) start their slider a button's gap after the speaker's and each app's
button (4 and 6 DIP before).

Tests (`ListLinesControlsTests`): `NoMeterComesWithinAGapOfAControl` (new): every kind a list holds, each sized kind
in each size and every other at its own height and at 1, 2, 4 and 6 rows, at 100 and 150 % and 100 and 225 % text,
with the timers, focus and the stopwatch running and a track playing with its timeline; the meters and controls as
drawn (`PaintWatch.Spaced`, told by `TilePaint.Bar`, the slider, the button, the switch and the refresh button). Red
first: *"Focus Full 40 px tall at 100 %, 100 % text: its meter (44, 32)..(348, 36) 0 px from a control
(292, 8)..(316, 32), not 8"*, the timer the same, the volume's and the brightness's one row (*"4 px from a control"*),
the mixer at 225 % text (*"6 px"*). `MetersKeepTheirGapPicture`: `spacing-meters-dark.png`.

By hand: a focus session running: the bar under "Focus time" and the time, ending where the time ends, clear of the
stop and pause buttons. The volume on one row: a little more room between the speaker and the slider.

## 451. Refresh in the right click: no refresh button on any line (2026-10-31)

The person: *"the refresh buttons should be removed and they should go into the right click context menu."* This
undoes §280 and §315 (the small ⟳ at a line's trailing gutter, a menu never saying "Refresh") and §305's press rules
for it. Every line that reads what it shows from somewhere it can read again (`IRefreshable`: the weather's lines, air
quality, tides, earthquakes, sports, markets, news, mail, contacts, the agenda, the day's events, the calendar's
views, a to-do list from To Do, a camera) now:

- **draws no control for it.** `RefreshButton` is gone and with it every line's room for it (`RefreshRow`,
  `RefreshEnd`, `RefreshRoom`, `RefreshBox`, its target, its press, its tooltip, its turning glyph and its ✓/!).
  Headers reflow: the title, the reading or the meta runs to the trailing gutter, and where a read failed the stale
  mark (StaleMark.cs) takes the trailing slot — it is what says why and since when (its tooltip). The weather's age
  ("15 min ago") stays at its header's end, now on the gutter, where the place still reads whole beside it. No line's
  height changes; a camera's plate on the picture's corner is gone.
- **ends its menu at rest with "Refresh"** (`WidgetAct.Refresh`, the existing "Refresh" string in every language):
  the refresh glyph, and under it when it last read ("Updated 15 minutes ago", `WeatherAge.Updated`, the button's
  tooltip's words) where the line knows. Last, after the line's own rows ("Open forecast", "Open website", "Manage
  accounts", the person or the meeting under the pointer), as Explorer's Refresh follows its view rows. Added for every
  line in one place (`FolderMenuRows`), so no kind's table lists it. Like every act (§308) it is left out, not greyed,
  while a read is on its way and where there is nothing to read (no place, no feed, no account). The pick reads it
  again at once, however fresh, and the folder stays open (`HandsAway` false). Edit mode's menu has no acts, so none
  there; a face's menu on the bar has none either (a face is its folder's).
- **Keys:** no key ever refreshed a line, so none does now.

`CellIsland.ReleaseOn` lost its `up` (only the button's press told a release from a lost capture), and the folder no
longer special-cases the button's target.

Tests (red first): `RefreshMenuTests.NoLineDrawsARefreshControl` — every refreshing line, one row and four, 100 and
150 %: no refresh glyph drawn (PaintWatch), no tooltip saying "Refresh", no press anywhere reading again (red, every

*"Weather: a press on it read it again 1 time(s)"*); `EveryRefreshingLinesMenuEndsWithRefresh` — the glyph, the age
under it, the pick asks the weather's and the market's stores, none while a read is on its way (red: *"Weather: its

has no Refresh"*). Changed with it: `PlacesAnatomyTests` (the tides' height on the gutter), `WeatherRowsTests` (the age

`refresh-headers-<dark|light>.png`, every refreshing line on one row and four;
`refresh-menu-<weather|news|mail|calendar>-<look>-150.png`.

By hand: open a weather, news or mail line: no ⟳ in its header, the title or reading running to the edge; right-click
