## 455. Show from: a widget picks the calendars, address books and mail folders it shows (2026-10-31)

The person: *"for the widgets like the contacts widget for example i should be able to select on a widget level which
data / accounts / email folders to show. do this for the similar widgets as well."*

**Where it was.** Every calendar line, the meetings, the mail and the contacts showed what every account holds as one
(§445); ⚙ › Accounts › an account turns a part off for every widget at once (§351, §399). Karpo read each account's inbox
and no other mail folder.

**Now** (`Karpo.Core\WidgetSources.cs`). ⚙ › Accounts stays the one home of what is synced and its colour. On top, a
widget's own menu has **Show from ›** (first among what it shows, over "Accounts ↗"): a level of switches, one per part
it may show — under each account's name where more than one place gives them (§445's rule: from one place, no heading) —
staying on the level as a switch does; at its row's end "All" (the mail's "All inboxes"), the one part's name, or "3 of
6". The last switch on stays on: a widget shows from something.

| Widget | Show from |
|---|---|
| Calendar in every style (agenda, day's events, day, week, month, year), the meetings | each account's calendars, and each country of the public holidays (under "Public holidays") |
| Contacts | each account's address books |
| Mail | each account's inbox (on unless switched off), then its other folders (off unless switched on), a folder in a folder named after its parent ("Inbox / Projects") |
| To-do line | none: it shows one list, picked in its List level (§445) |

**A to-do line keeps one list.** Its list is where a new task goes and what a rename and a delete act on; a line of
several lists would need a list picked for every add, and §445's List level already is its "Show from", grouped by
account. Nothing else shows an account's parts. The faces (the calendar's date, the mail's envelope and badge, the
meeting's, the contacts') show every part, as before.

**What is listed** (`Karpo.Accounts\SourceParts.cs`): every account's calendars, books or mail folders as the dock last
synced them (sync-report.json, as a to-do line's lists, §399) — never the network; a part turned off in ⚙ › Accounts is
not offered. The public holidays' countries from the config (`WidgetSources.HolidayParts`).

**The stores filter; nothing is read twice.** A widget's picks are a `SourceFilter`. The calendar store's `EventsIn` (and
`Meetings.Ahead`, `CalendarLines.EventsIn`) take it before the same event of two calendars is made one, so a calendar not
shown hides none of another's (an account calendar by `ICalendarSource.Part`, the holidays by country). `ContactStore.View`
and `MailStore.View` keep each widget's list (and unread count) until the store changes, made from the same last read,
coloured by part where more than one account's or book's is shown.

**The mail folders are synced only while a widget shows them** (superseded by §639: a folder is turned on in ⚙ › Accounts). `IAccountReader.InboxAsync` became `MailAsync(folders,
count)`: one read per account lists every folder and reads the inbox and the folders asked for — the union of every mail
line's picks in the config (`WidgetSources.Folders`), which the dock tells the store whenever the config is applied
(`MailStore.Want`; a folder newly picked is read at once). What it costs, per account and interval:

- IMAP: the same one connection; one LIST more, and per folder shown a STATUS, an EXAMINE and a FETCH of its newest 30.
- Microsoft Graph: `mailFolders` (100 a page) and the `childFolders` of each folder that has some (to 4 deep, 500 folders
  at most), and per folder shown one request for its newest 30; its counts come with the list.

A folder that will not open fails alone and keeps what it gave (accounts.md, "Parts that fail alone"). The counts stay
right: the mail face's badge and a line that picked nothing count the inboxes alone, as before; a line that picked
folders counts the unread of what it shows. The cache keeps a shown folder's newest 30 beside its inbox's
(`MailCacheAccount.Folders`), so a folder-limited line works offline; the report lists the folders (`SyncPart.Folders`),
which ⚙ › Accounts does not show (the inbox's switch is the account's mail).

**Config.** A widget's `sources`: the parts it picked, each its account's address and its part's key —
`"ann@example.com|calendar:<id>"`, `"ann@example.com|contacts:<id>"`, `"ann@example.com|mail"` (the inbox),
`"ann@example.com|mail:<folder id>"`, `"holidays|CH"` (a country, or a region: `"holidays|CH-ZH"`). By address because
signing in again keeps it where the account's id would not, and the config roams to PCs whose ids differ. Absent — every
widget nobody set — is every calendar and book and every inbox; nothing is written while the switches are the defaults.
Kept only on the widgets above (`WidgetItem.Normalize`). Nothing to convert: the key is new.

**The menu rules** (§411): R10's exception reads "a heading straight over a ticked row of a level of own things, or over
a switch of a group of switches" — the place they come from; R4 reads such a group as one setting. The allowance stays
empty.

Strings: `dock.menu.showFrom.title`, `.all`, `.inboxes`, `.some`, in every language.

Tests (red first): `WidgetSourcesTests.AContactsLineLimitedToOneBookShowsOnlyThatBooksPeople` (red: *"Expected ["Bob
Work"] Actual ["Ada Home", "Bob Work"]"*), `.AMailLineLimitedToAFolderShowsThatFoldersMessages` (an account with two
folders; red: *"Expected ["In the archive"] Actual ["In the inbox"]"*), `.ACalendarLimitedToOneCalendarShowsOnlyItsEvents`
(the agenda and the next meetings; red: *"Expected ["Standup"] Actual ["Dentist", "Standup"]"*),
`.AFolderIsReadOnlyWhileAWidgetShowsItAndListedForTheMenu`, `.ShowFromListsTheSyncedPartsUnderEachAccountsNameEachASwitch`,
`.AMailLinesFoldersAreOffUntilPickedAndOneAccountHasNoHeading`, `.OnlyTheAccountsWidgetsHaveShowFromAndTheFileKeepsWhatWasPicked`;
`SyncChoiceTests.AMicrosoftAccountListsItsFoldersAndReadsOnlyThoseAsked`; `MenuRulesTests.EveryMenuKeepsTheRules` (the
corpus now lists parts; red: *"R10 Show from › Ada Lovelace — a heading"*, *"R4 Show from — a page saying "All""*);
`ShowFromPictures.ShowFromIsALevelOfSwitchesThatStaysOnItsLevel` (a switch flipped: on its level, lit where it was;
`showfrom-<contacts|mail|calendar>-dark.png`, and the widget's level `showfrom-<…>-row-dark.png`).

By hand: edit mode, a mail line's menu › Show from: each account's inbox on, its folders off; turn Archive on — the line
shows the archive's newest beside the inbox's a moment later, its count the two's unread; the mail face's badge stays the
inboxes'. A calendar line › Show from › Birthdays off: its events leave that line and no other.

## 456. A stepper's buttons stand still as it steps (2026-10-31)

The person: *"when changing row height the minus button always shifts with every half step. this should be fixed."*
A line's "Rows − 6 rows +" steps in cells of half a row since §442, and its value's slot between the buttons was as
wide as the words it said now (`Flyout.ControlWidth`, its draw in `Flyout.Controls.cs`): "6½ rows" is wider than "6 rows",
the "+" stands at the row's end, so the "−" moved left and back every half step. Every stepper did it — a number's
("8 px" to "12 px"), a length's hours, the height's — wherever its words changed width; the half rows made it every step.

**The fix, one rule for every stepper.** A stepper says its range (`FlyoutControl.Stepper.Range`): every text its value
may say, built by `Stepper.Over` from every whole number of its least to its most, and on to its value where that stands
past them (a kind's default past its most, Tides'). Its slot is as wide as the widest of them and its value
(`Flyout.StepValueWidth`, each text measured once a size), in the menu's row widths and its drawing alike, so neither
button moves over its whole range. Every stepper gives one: a number row's in its unit (`OptionMenu`, "28 px" … "160 px"),
the height's rows ("1 row" … as many as the folder's room holds, `LineHeightRows.Rows`), a time's hours and minutes, a length's
(`MenuPickers`), and AM/PM's switch both words. Every number, not a step apart: a bar's size typed off its steps steps
from there, and a menu's figures need not all be one width (they are not drawn tabular). The menu itself was one width already (a list menu's
width is its own, not its rows'); the tests hold that too.

Tests: `StepperSlotTests` (new): `TheHeightsMinusStaysPutEveryHalfStep` (on a real menu at 100 % and 150 %, "6 rows" to
"6½ rows", "7 rows", "1 row", "10 rows" and back: the "−" and "+" where they were, the panel the same; red first: at
"6½ rows" the "−" stood further left), `EveryStepperKnowsItsRange` (every stepper of the menu corpus and a 12-hour time's:
its range holds its value and more), `EverySteppersMinusStaysPutOverItsRange` (each of them on a real menu at each value
of its range, up to 60 spread over it: its "−" — AM/PM's button — and its "+" still, the panel the same).

## 457. The contacts wear their pictures (2026-10-31)

The person: *"the contacts widget should also display the peoples profile picture if applicable."* A row of the
contacts line (§102) led with the contact's glyph, whoever it was.

**Now** a person with a picture wears it in the leading column: a circle (`PopupPaint.Covered` with half its side as
the corner, the one picture drawing the notifications and the feed use) at the kit's Feature size (24 DIP) times the
item style's picture size, standing where the feed's pictures stand (`ListTiers.GlyphBox`) — never so large that it
leaves less than the kit's gap (8 DIP) before the name, so Large items' pictures do not touch it — on the name and
the line under it (on the name alone in an open row, or with Preview off). Somebody without one, or whose picture has
not come yet, wears the glyph as before (in their book's colour with more than one book). The item style offers
**Pictures** for the contacts now, on unless turned off (`ItemStyles.Offer`, as the clipboard's): off, everyone wears
the glyph. A file that never set it shows them; no config change.

**Where they come from** (`docs\accounts.md`, "Contacts' pictures"). A Microsoft account: the contact's
`/me/contacts/{id}/photo/$value`, under the Contacts.Read Karpo always asked for — no new permission. A contact says
nothing of whether it has one, so its `changeKey` (now read with it) is its picture's version and a 404 is "none".
CardDAV: the card's PHOTO — 4.0's data: URI, 3.0's and 2.1's base64 (folded over lines), or an address, fetched
signed in on the account's own server and as nobody anywhere else; the book's read keeps only a hash of it
(`Person.Photo`), and the card is read again when that changes (`DavReader.PhotoAsync`). IMAP gives none.

**Kept** (`Karpo.Dock\Pim\ContactPhotos.cs`). After each read the store hands everyone over and the pictures are made
ready on the pool, in the order the line lists the people: those in memory stay, those on disk are taken in, the rest
are fetched four at a time, each drawn as it comes. A picture is decoded and cut down to 64 px at most (a row's at
Large and 200 %) and kept as `contact-photos\<key>.bin` in the local folder, encrypted for this Windows user as the PIM
caches are (`PimCache.Protect`); the key is a hash of the person's id and their picture's version, so a new picture is
a new file and nothing of the person is in a name. An empty file is "they have none", so nobody is asked twice for one
version. An account that fails a picture (offline, signed out) is asked no more in that pass and nothing of it is
kept; the next read asks again. Once every account has been read, the file of anybody no longer listed is deleted; a
start where an account cannot be read keeps its people's. The line reads memory alone: drawing never waits on a disk
or a network. An isolated run and the tests keep the pictures in memory only.

Tests: `Pim\ContactPhotosTests` (the key; fetched once, kept encrypted and taken from the disk at the next run; "none"
kept; a new version fetched again and the old file gone; a failing account keeping nothing and asked again; pruning
only once every account was read; a file that is no picture); `Accounts\DavTests` (PHOTO as a data: URI, folded
base64, 2.1's BASE64, an address, none, not base64; the read keeping a hash; the card read again, the password only
on its own server, a card gone); `Accounts\MicrosoftReaderTests` (the changeKey, the photo's $value, 404 as none, a
refusal); `ContactsPresetTests.ARowWearsThePersonsPictureElseTheGlyph` (the circle at the Feature size before the
name, on the name and its detail, the glyph for the others, the gap at Large, Pictures off); `ItemStylesTests`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `contacts-photos-dark.png`, `contacts-photos-light.png`.

By hand: with an account whose contacts have pictures, open the contacts folder: the pictures fill in a moment after
the people; Edit → the line → Pictures off shows the glyphs again.

## 458. Fly in: a folder's widgets fly out of its face, its outline drawn round them last; the choice played as it is lit (2026-10-31) — superseded by §489 (2026-11-02)

The person: *"show a preview of the folder animation when selecting it. add a folder animation where the individual
widgets themselves fly in from the location of where the folder was opened from. then at the end the outline of the folder
should also be animated in, but with a reveal."*

**Fly in** (`FolderFlight.cs`, the plan, pure; `FlyoutHost.Fly`, the clock; `FolderFlyout.Flight.cs`, the lines). A fourth
Folder animation, between Fade and Off, its picture the tiles; every choice now wears its own (R13: up from the bar, a fade,
the tiles, none). In the file `"folderAnimation": "flyIn"`: a word an older Karpo does not know, so the file's shape is 39
(§448's `Config.Shape`, `ConfigWords.txt`); nothing to convert.

| Part | Comes in | Goes (the same run back, 2.5 times as fast) |
|---|---|---|
| The panel's material, its shadow | 100 ms, straight, from the start | last |
| Each line (its card, content, a separator's mark) | from the face's middle (the middle of the folder button's inner side) to its place, 240 ms on Windows' decelerate curve, growing from 60 %, faded in over its first 40 %; the nearest the face first, each 25 ms after the one before (all of them within 150 ms, so a full folder is no slower) | back to the face, the farthest first |
| The outline (each section's rim) | drawn on round the section (its rim's trim, 0 to 1), 200 ms, decelerate, once the last line has landed | first |

Three lines: 490 ms in, 196 ms out. All of it on the compositor: one value, the flight's `Progress`, run straight from 0
(shut) to 1 (open) by a key frame animation; the material, the outline and each line read where they stand from it by
expressions — the same sums as the plan's (`FolderFlight.Expression`: the curve is 3x^⅔ − 2x, which is (0, 0, 0, 1)
exactly), so what the tests hold is what runs. Nothing drawn per frame, nothing laid out again, the window still (§355).

- **Seen where the folder stands**: the lists' and the sections' clips are lifted while any line is on its way (scaled a
  thousand times about their middles), so a line crossing another section shows, and put back as the last lands. The box
  of §355 still clips at the bar's inner side: the lines come out of the bar at the face. A folder set Left, Right or
  Center far along the bar from its face has them come in over its room's edge nearest the face.
- **Reversal, switching, edit mode, Windows' animations off, input**: as §446. A close as it comes in turns the one
  clock back from where it is (`MotionClock`); an opening again in the middle of a close the same. Another folder opened
  while one is open is there at once. Arranged (edit mode) a fade where it stands — and a folder at rest arranged in place
  (`FolderFlyout.Arrange`) lands at once and goes by a fade. Windows' Animation effects off: at once. The plan is where the
  lines end from the first frame, so presses, hover and the keys find them there.
- **Never left invisible**: the opening's timer (`FlyoutHost.Arrived`, 250 ms after its time) puts the clock at its end,
  lets the material and the outline go whole and tells the folder (`Landed`), which lets each line go of the clock and puts
  it where it stands — whether or not DWM ran any of it. A folder shown again lets go of a flight first.
- `PlaceLines` sets a line's place only where it changed, so a widget's news in the first half second leaves a line on its
  way alone.

**The preview** (`FolderPreview.cs`, when, pure; `Dock.FolderPreview.cs`, which folder; `Flyout.Lit`). In Layout ▾ ›
Behavior › Folder animation (and the bar's right click, the same rows), the choice under the pointer or the keys, lit
150 ms, plays once on a folder of the bar the menu is of: the folder nearest the pointer that has something to show and
is not open, its own kept view (§357), shown from its face at rest as a look (`FlyoutHost.Previewing`: no focus taken —
the menu keeps the keys —, no press closing it, the menu over it by its stratum). It comes in by the choice, stands 700 ms,
and goes by it. Another choice lit ends it at once and plays that one; a pick plays at once; the menu gone, or a folder
opened for real, ends it at once. Run across the choices, only the one rested on plays. Why a real folder of the bar, not a
picture: it is the animation itself, where it will be seen, with what the folder shows; and a folder not open has nothing
of edit mode, the selection or the open face's look to disturb — it is not one of the open folders. No folder on the bar
(or each open): nothing plays.

Tests (red first): `FolderFlightTests` (the style, its times for a folder's lines, each line from the face, the nearest
first, the stagger shrinking for a full folder, the outline only once the last has landed, the close run back with the
outline first; red: *"Expected [2, 1, 5, 0], Actual []"*), `FolderPreviewTests` (lit a moment plays and goes, another
ends it at once, a pick at once, the menu gone ends it; red: *"Expected Open FlyIn 700, Actual Nothing"*),
`FolderMotionFilmTests.AFolderFliesInLineByLineAndItsOutlineComesLast` (filmed six times slower: the lines' top only
rises, from under where it ends, the outline under a fifth drawn while a line is on its way and in part on a frame after,
the end exactly the folder shown still, nothing bound once landed; the close: the outline gone before the lines leave; red
with the lines left unbound: *"the lines first showed at 527, near where the top one stands (527), not near the face
(720)"*), `.AFlyInCutShortLeavesNothingBehind` (red: *"the lines were never bound to the flight"*),
`.APreviewTakesNoFocusAndGoesAtOnceOrByItsStyle`, `KarpoMenuGeneralTests.TheTaskbarsBehaviourIsAGroupOfItsMenu` (four
choices, four pictures, `"flyIn"`). Strips (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `film-folder-fly-<open|close>.png`. One string in every
language (`settings.general.folderAnimation.flyIn`).

By hand: Layout ▾ › Behavior › Folder animation: rest on Fly in — the folder nearest the pointer comes up out of its face
line by line, its outline drawn round it last, stands, and goes back; arrow down to Off — the one playing goes at once and
Off plays (there, then gone). Pick Fly in, then open a folder from a bottom bar: the widgets fly up out of the button, the
outline drawn on last; close it as it comes in: it turns back. Theme with outlines (Paper): the rim drawn on. Edit mode:
a folder still fades. Animation effects off: at once, the preview too.

## 459. Styles by part: a text style and five parts' colours; ours four and Follow Windows, overridden not renamed (2026-10-31) — its Folder buttons merged into the Taskbar widgets by §499 (2026-11-04) — no styles since §507 (2026-11-05): each layout's look its own values, a widget's its own — a colour's opacity the slider of its picker, no stepper, since §523 (2026-11-07)

**Replaces §441** (and with it §429's model): a style's Mode, its three colours and Outlines per level, its opacities and
separators, the chain Windows → Karpo's style → a folder's → a widget's, "Same in dark mode" with §405's adapting of a
colour for the other mode, and the fifteen built-ins (the §396 themes and §429's colour styles) are gone.

The person: *"an opacity selector … integrated into the color selector and … an option to have None"*; *"the styles have
settings for all the individual parts like the taskbar widgets, the folder widgets, the folder panel and the taskbar
itself … add all of those style settings into one style under correct headers"*; *"you should be able to change the
default styles but it should be on an override basis … the name should not be editable"*; *"the styles that we have should
as a default never have outlines"*; *"when i select multiple i should be able to set the appearance of all of them
together"*; *"the styles are not reachable via root menu … remove display settings link from display settings … improve
the editor … there should also not be a big differentiation between our styles and custom user styles"*; dark mode *"a
different set of colors though, not directly integrated"*; separators back in Layout; *"the button should be separately
configurable from the panel"*; *"just add four individual styles that are high quality. in a style you should also be able
to set the text style as well"*.

**A style** (`Styles`, `Styled`, `ItemStyle`) is a name, a **text style** (`TextStyle`: Font — Segoe UI Variable, Segoe UI,
Bahnschrift, Sitka, Georgia, Cascadia Mono (Consolas where it is not installed) — and Weight — Light, Regular, Semibold) and
the colours of five **parts** (`StylePart`, `PartPaints`):

| Part | Colours | What it dresses |
|---|---|---|
| Taskbar | Background, Outline | the bar; its opacity is the background's alpha (100 % solid, 1–99 % the blur under it, None no plate) |
| Taskbar widgets | Background, Outline, Text, Accent | every widget's card on the bar |
| Folder buttons | Background, Outline, Text, Accent | a folder's face on the bar (the tray's, the clock's, the quick settings' too: they are folders) |
| Folder panel | Background, Outline | an open folder's panel — and every menu and flyout, which are panels too |
| Widgets in folders | Background, Outline, Text, Accent | a folder's lines; the menus' text is theirs |

Each colour (`Paint`) is Windows' own (nothing set), a colour with its opacity, or **None** (not there: no plate, no line);
None is offered for a background and an outline only. The panel has a Background of its own because a clear bar (None)
leaves nothing to derive a panel from, and a panel's opacity was a setting the person had (§441's Folder opacity). Every
other colour is derived from a part's own (`ToneRules.Dress`): its text made 4.5:1 and its accent 3:1 on what it stands on
(its card where that is solid, else the card and its ground), the highlight and a separator's line its text at Windows'
own steps (`HighlightOf`, `SeparatorOf`); a surface is drawn in the mode its background reads in (dark below mid grey),
else Windows'. **Different colours in dark mode** is a second set of every part's colours, drawn while Windows is dark;
without it the one set is drawn in both modes, unadapted. The weight is the base the kit's ramp (§388) stands on: Regular
400/600 as always, Light 300/500, Semibold 600/700. The font is the one Karpo wears, everywhere — the bar, the widgets,
the folders, the menus (`Gfx.Typeface`, set by `Dock.Apply`) — laid out on Segoe UI Variable's line height and baseline
whatever its own, so nothing is cut at 225 % text and no row changes height; the measuring caches are keyed by it
(`TextLine.Template`, `CountdownCard.Baseline`). A widget wearing another style takes its colours, not its font: one font
keeps every row and card on the kit's one ramp.

**No inheritance between styles.** Karpo wears one (`appearance.style`; Follow Windows by default). A widget, a folder's
button and a folder's panel each may wear another whole style and use its part: a widget its Taskbar widgets, a folder's
button its Folder buttons (`WidgetItem.StyleId`), a folder's panel its Folder panel and, for its lines that wear none, its
Widgets in folders (`WidgetItem.PanelStyleId`); a line its own style's Widgets in folders on its panel. Default is Karpo's
(a line's: its panel's). In the Dock: `Look.Wearing` (Karpo's), `Look.Part` (a bar part), `Look.Panel` (a folder,
`FolderFlyout.Worn`), `Look.Line`; `Look.Dressing` says the four parts a look is dressed in, `Palette.TaskbarOutline` the
bar's outline (`Tokens.Border`), `Palette.PanelText` the menus' text (`FlyoutTheme`).

**Ours** (`Styles.BuiltIn`): **Follow Windows** (everything Windows' own) and four designed ones, each a light and a dark
palette, no outlines, every text ≥ 4.5:1 and accent ≥ 3:1 as designed (`StyleTests.OursReadAsDesignedInBothModes`):

| Style | Font | Light: bar / cards / text / accent | Dark: bar / cards / text / accent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Graphite — calm neutral | Segoe UI Variable | #EBECEE 88 % / white 72 % / #1D2024 / #3456C8 | #1B1C1F 88 % / #2A2C30 80 % / #ECEDEF / #8FA6FF |
| Paper — warm paper | Sitka | #F1EBDF 92 % / #FBF7EF 90 % / #3A3027 / #A84B24 | #25201B 92 % / #332C25 90 % / #F0E6D5 / #E89B6C |
| Harbor — deep navy and teal | Bahnschrift | #D8E3EE 90 % / #EEF4F9 85 % / #0E2A44 / #06708A | #0B192A 90 % / #142A42 85 % / #DDEBF7 / #4CC8DF |
| Bloom — plum and raspberry | Segoe UI Variable Semibold | #FFE4D6 92 % / #FFF4EC 90 % / #4A1530 / #C4285A; buttons #F7CFDE | #1E0F24 92 % / #33183D 88 % / #FBE7F0 / #FF5C93; buttons #5C1E47 |

Each has its panel a step off its bar (Graphite #F6F7F8 / #232428, Paper #F6F1E7 / #2A241F, Harbor #E6EEF5 / #0F2236, Bloom
#FFEDE4 / #26132D, 92–96 %) and its lines' cards on it. Every setting of ours is **"Default (…)"** until the person
overrides it: the override is an entry of theirs under our id saying only what is overridden (no name); Default again or
**Reset all** takes it out. Ours are never renamed nor deleted, and are **duplicated** into the person's (every setting
written out: nothing inherited). The person's own are the same but that their Default is Windows' own, and they are named
and deleted.

**Menus.**
- **Layout ▾**: Type, Size, Show; ruled off, **Taskbar separators** and **Folder separators** (Line, Space only, None —
  Karpo's, every layout alike, `appearance.taskbarSeparators|folderSeparators`); ruled off at its foot **Styles ↗** and
  Behavior. A separator's and a divider's menu link to Layout ↗.
- **Display ▾**'s foot is **Styles ↗** (Windows' display settings gone).
- **Styles** (`LooksScope.Styles`, under Layout ▾'s crumb): **Karpo's style** (a choice of every style, each with its
  swatch); ruled off, every style alike, ours and the person's, each with its swatch, the one Karpo wears ticked, a click
  opening its editor, the person's with a bin (asked first; what wore it wears Default); **Add a style** its foot.
- **A style's editor** (`LooksScope.Style`, a menu of its own named for the style — so a colour's picker is its third
  level, §411 R1, and its first never scrolls, R2): Name (the person's only), Font, Weight; ruled off, Taskbar ›,
  Taskbar widgets ›, Folder buttons ›, Folder panel ›, Widgets in folders › — each its colours, and, under a rule, its
  "Dark …" colours where the style has them —; ruled off **Different colours in dark mode**; its foot **Duplicate** (the
  copy's editor opens) and **Reset all** (last, R11). The bin is the list's, not the editor's (R12: a delete last, and Reset
  all last). Identical for every style.
- **The colour picker** (`OptionPickers.Paints`): Default with its swatch, None (a background, an outline), the recent
  colours, the grid, Custom color…, and **Opacity − n % +** stepped by ten; a colour picked keeps the opacity in force.
- **A widget's Appearance** (its foot, `WidgetLooks.Row`): Default ("Default (Paper)") and every style, each with the
  swatch of the part it would draw; a folder has **Button appearance** and **Panel appearance**. With several widgets
  selected the pick is every one's (`OptionPlace.Together`, `Dock.PickerPlace`) and the row says the style they share,
  else **Mixed**.

**Live.** A style's colours are now a build (`Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer` is the recent colours alone): they make cards, a
plate's text, each part's own look; every open folder and menu is dressed again as before (§396).

**The file** (no reading of the old shape; the coordinator converts the person's own once with
`karpo-coord\convert-styles3.py`):

```
appearance.style                         unchanged (an id; "windows" left out)
appearance.taskbarSeparators, .folderSeparators   new: "line" | "space" | "none", the default left out
appearance.styles[]                      { id, name?, font?, weight?, darkColours?, light?: { taskbar?, widgets?, folderButtons?,
                                           folderPanel?, folderWidgets? }, dark?: {…} }; a part { background?, outline?, text?,
                                           accent? }, each "#RRGGBB", "#AARRGGBB" or "none"; an entry under one of ours' ids
                                           its overrides; mode, outlines, the opacities, separators: gone
islands[..].appearance                   unchanged key (a widget's, a folder's button's style); "style" is a widget's form
islands[..].panelAppearance              new: a folder's panel's style
```

Converted: "outlined" and every built-in that is gone → Follow Windows / Default; a style of the person's → its
background, text and accent on its widget parts (Taskbar widgets, Folder buttons, Widgets in folders), outlines on → those
parts' outline, a dark set apart → `darkColours`; Karpo's style's separators → Layout ▾'s.

Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.karpo|font|weight|weightLight|weightRegular|weightSemibold|darkColours|widgets|
folderButtons|folderPanel|folderWidgets|outline|darkOutline|harbor|bloom|buttonLook|panelLook|mixed|opacity|defaultOf` new;
§441's and §429's style, mode, outline and opacity strings and the three themes gone, deleted; 30 languages.

Tests (the model replaced wholesale: the new model's tests were red by not building against §441's API; behaviour red
against it where they read the old menus): `StyleTests` (ours Follow Windows and four, named; no outlines; read as designed
in both modes; a style's parts, text and dark set and the file; ours overridden, reset, never renamed; a copy inherits
nothing; each wears its part, button apart from panel, a line its panel's; a deleted style worn by nothing; a row's Default),
`StyleMenuTests` (Layout ▾ and Display ▾ end in Styles; Styles is Karpo's style and every style; one editor for all; a
folder's two Appearances; several selected wear one style, "Mixed"), `MenuPickersTests.NoneAndTheOpacityAreTheColoursOwn`,
`LineRowsTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `LinkRowsTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (every style's editor in the corpus, the allowance
empty), `AppearanceTests`, `BarColorThemeTests`; live: `SceneTreeTests.EveryColourPickedReachesItsSurfacesLive` (each part
set with a folder and a menu open, then Harbor picked). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `style-<windows|graphite|paper|harbor|
bloom>-<look>.png` (the bar, a widget in another style, a folder open with a line lit, Styles' choice open, in the style's
font: read back), `style-panel-outline-<look>.png`, `style-editor-<look>.png` (a part's colours, the picker with None and the
opacity), `style-text-225.png` (Sitka at 225 % text; `AFontAt225PercentText` holds every font's line Segoe UI Variable's).

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Styles ↗ › Karpo's style › Harbor: the bar navy, its text Bahnschrift, the folders and menus
navy, at once; switch Windows to light: the light set. Styles › Paper: its editor; Folder panel › Outline › a colour: only the
panels outlined; Reset all: back. Select three widgets, Appearance › Bloom: all three; one other: "Mixed".

## 460. A kind's most is one number: the tides start at 3½ rows, not 7 (2026-10-31)

Found fixing the steppers (§456): a new tides line's menu said "7 rows" with its "+" greyed, and one "−" dropped it to
"3½ rows". The tides are a chart that stretches (§432): past seven cells — the row with its caption and the curve at its
least — the curve is only drawn taller, so its menu stops there (`ListWidget.MostCells`, `LineHeight.MostOf`). But a
kind's most was two numbers. The menu's stepper held a line to `MostOf`; everything else — where a new line starts, a file
read, a step's height (`LineHeight.Limits`, `Within(kind)`) — held it to `LineHeight.Most`, past any screen, the same for
every kind. And a new line of a kind that grows starts Automatic up to its range's most (`ListWidget.Range`), which for the
tides §432 left at six rows when it capped them at three (§440 doubled both: 14 cells, a most of 7). Nothing held the two
together, so the start was past the most, and the menu said a height its stepper could not reach. The sun's arc was the
same: it started "8 rows" with a most of 3.

**The fix, one most for the kind.** `LineHeight.Limits(kind)` is `Fewest` to `MostOf(kind)`: `Most` for every kind but a
chart that stretches, which stops where its information is whole. Every height of a kind goes through it — where a new
line starts, a file read (`WidgetItem.Normalize`), the menu's step and mode — so nothing past the most is drawn or said
anywhere; the menu's choice is the room on its screen held to those limits (`LineHeightRows.For`, its own `MostOf` gone).
§432's "a height a file holds past it is kept" went with this: it was for a most that changed with the text size, and
since §442 a chart's most is the same count at every text. The ranges say it too: each capped chart's range ends at its
most — the tides 1 to 3½ rows, the sun's arc 1 to 3, the five graphs 1 to 5, screen time 1 to 4 (the graphs and screen
time are fixed, so their start was right; their ranges only said more than they could be). A new tides line starts
Automatic up to 3½ rows: the row and its caption with the curve at its least, its content's own height; one row where it
has nothing to show.

No migration: a file's tides line of 14 cells reads as 7, Automatic as it was — the content's height, which is what it
drew anyway (the person's own file has one).

Tests: `HeightLimitsTests.EveryKindsDefaultLiesWithinItsLeastAndMost` (new: every card's unmeasured cells, its range, where
it starts and a new line of it lie in its limits, and a kind that grows starts Automatic up to its range's most, unheld;
red first: "Tides: its range's most is 14 cells, outside 2 to 7", "Tides: starts automatic up to 7, not automatic up to
its range's most, 14", the same for the sun's arc at 16 of 6, and the graphs' and screen time's ranges of 12),
`.EveryPresetsHeightIsAllowed` (each preset's line inside its kind's limits), `.EveryKindStartsInsideItsLimits` and
`NoFewestTests.EveryKindMayBeOneRow` (the limits a row to `MostOf`), `TidesTests.TheWidgetIsInTheWeatherPageAfterTheAirQuality`
(the range 2 to 7, a new line Automatic up to 7); `HeightLimitsPicturesTests` draws a capped chart up to its most, once.

By hand: edit mode, add the tides to a folder, right-click it: "3½ rows", "+" greyed, "−" steps to "3 rows".

## 461. No line says "more": it lists everything and scrolls (2026-10-31)

The person: "when a folder has more items to show it should actually not say that but just scroll." §109 made every list
line scroll instead of saying "N more" (ListScroll.cs), but two lines still said it, and the arithmetic behind it was
still there.

**What still said it, and what each does now.**

- **The notifications** (`NotificationPartTile`): a group of more than three showed its newest three and "See more (2)",
  which opened it whole, and "See fewer" folded it again (Windows' own notification center does this). Now a group lists
  every one of its notifications, newest first, under its heading; held shorter than them the line scrolls under its
  header as it already did. The fold row, its target (`Spot.Fold`), the groups the showing opened
  (`NotificationView.Open`, also what §357 kept), the never-used `collapsed` layout and the two strings went.
- **A folder's contents** (`FolderContentsLine` over `FolderContentsView`, the folder widget and a drive's contents): it
  listed at most 100 items and said "30 more items" in its last slot, and it did not scroll at all: past its most it
  summarised. Now it is a scrolling line (`IListScroll`): every item a row, as tall as all of them, and held shorter its
  items scroll under the folder's own row, which stays (its picture, name and count, or the way back in a subfolder). The
  keys walk every row and bring the one they come to into sight (`ScrollReveal`). A folder's list from the taskbar
  (`PinFolderFlyout`) said the same "N more items" under its rows; it already scrolled, so the label went.

**A bound on work, not a "more".** A list now asks for everything a read walks (`FolderReader.MostListed`, 4096, which
was already where the reader stopped walking): past it the items are only counted, for the head's "N items", and never
said. Laid out whole, a folder of thousands would measure every name on every hover, so the line lays out only the rows
it draws (`CellIsland.Hidden`) or the one under the pointer, and measures the date column once a read. The taskbar's row
of a folder's buttons keeps its own 100 (`FolderRows.MostButtons`), as before: a bar face, which folds behind "…".

**What went with it.** `WidgetFill` kept a last slot for a summary row ("12 other apps") and said it (`Says`); nothing
asked for a summary any more but the folder's contents, so the summary went: `WidgetFill` is how many whole items fit,
and nothing more. `LineRows.Items` (unused), `DriveListing.MoreLine` and `MostEntries`, and the words of every summary
no line said any more — `dock.notifications.seeMore`/`seeFewer`, `dock.drives.more`, and the unused count pairs the
summaries were written in (`widget.todo.otherTasks`/`tasks`, `dock.mail.otherMessages`/`messages`,
`dock.clipboard.otherCount`, `widget.calendar.otherEvents`/`events`, `widget.removable.otherDevices`/`devices`,
`widget.screenTime.otherApps`/`apps`, `widget.sound.otherDevices`/`devices`/`otherApps`/`apps`,
`widget.rss.otherHeadlines`/`headlines`) — from all thirty languages.

**Left as they are.** Not a list that can scroll, so not this: a week or day view's all-day row past three lanes, two
lanes and "+N" a day (`CalendarLayout`); the month's days, at most three dots each; a desktop's row in the desktops line,
four app icons and "+N" (`SwitchRow.Plus`); the now-playing line's list of apps, which leaves out silently what does not
fit. On the bar, not in a folder: the app buttons' "…", the tray's overflow, the bell's "99+". The settings import's
summary, "and 2 more", is a message, not a line.

Tests: `NotificationsPresetTests.ALongGroupListsEveryNotificationAndTheLineScrolls` (red first: five titles of seven, the
"See more (2)" row), `FolderContentsLineTests.AFolderOfMoreThanFitsScrollsToItsLastItem` (130 items held to five rows:
all listed, scrolls under the head, the last drawn and pressed at the foot, nothing drawn says "N more"; red first: 100
listed), `FolderReadingTests.AListIsListedWholeAndFewerAreCounted`, `WidgetFillTests` (whole items, no slot kept);
`FolderWidgetHoverTests`' line is now as tall as its items, so the overlay scrollbar does not show beside its rows.

By hand: a folder widget on a folder of a few hundred files, held to a few rows: the wheel scrolls to the last; the
notifications with four from one app: all four, no "See more".

## 462. Patterns: a part's background patterned, one sheet a group (2026-10-31) — the Folder buttons' pattern the Taskbar widgets' since §499 (2026-11-04) — a pattern is a value of a look since §507 (2026-11-05) — its choices a grid of tiles since §634 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"you should be able to set a background pattern for the folder widgets and for the taskbar. make up some
default patterns. the pattern is part of the styles settings and should be continuous between widgets inside the same
group but not between groups of widgets."*

**A part's Pattern** (`Pattern`, `PartPaints.Pattern`, Karpo.Core\Patterns.cs) is a style's setting like its colours, in
each of its modes: **Taskbar** (the bar), **Taskbar widgets** and **Folder buttons** (the cards on the bar) and **Widgets in
folders** (a folder's lines); not the **Folder panel**, which every menu is too and a folder's lines cover
(`StyleParts.HasPattern`). The bar's own pattern shows where its cards don't — between the groups, and through a card as far
as the card lets it, a floating dock's panel all of it —, so a patterned bar of cards needs its cards patterned: the person's
"continuous between widgets inside the same group" is the cards'. A folder's button stands in the bar's groups with the
widgets, so it has the setting too; one wearing another pattern than its widgets is dressed apart, a card of its own, as one
in other colours always was (§311, `Look.Part`).

**Ours**: None (the default), and eight, each a tile that repeats without a seam, laid out per pixel at the display's scale
(DIPs below; a line half a px wide each side at 100 %, 0.45 DIP at more, every feature drawn round by its distance, the grid's
lines whole pixels — a px at 100 and 150 %, two at 225 %):

| Pattern | What it is | Its period | Its ink |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dots | round dots, every other row half a period along | 8 | 16 % |
| Grid | hairlines across and down | 12 | 8 % |
| Lines | rising lines at 45° | 7 | 10 % |
| Crosshatch | both diagonals | 9 | 8 % |
| Waves | gentle waves, 1.75 DIP high | 28 × 9 | 11 % |
| Checks | 4-DIP squares | 8 | 4.5 % |
| Contours | a topographic map's lines over a land of six waves | 120 | 12 % |
| Grain | a paper's grain, a px each (two at 200 % and over) | 64 px | 8 % |

**Its ink** is the part's text colour as the style says it (Windows' own text where it says none; the bar's the cards'
text where that shows on the bar, else Windows'), at the pattern's strength (`Patterns.Strength`), never over
`ToneRules.PatternMost` (16 %), a light ink at 70 % of it (`PatternOnDark`: light lines on a dark card stand out more) —
so it is drawn in every style's own colours, light and dark. **Readable over it** (`ToneRules.Dress`): a text and an accent
are made readable (4.5:1, 3:1) on every surface they stand on with the patterns on it too — the card's, and the bar's under
a card that lets it through —, and where no colour reads as well on a pattern as on the same surface bare (a mid-tone card)
the pattern gives way, half as strong at a time, else none: a pattern never takes a text under what it reads at bare. Ours
read at 4.5:1 over every pattern at its full strength. High contrast draws none.

**One sheet a group** (Karpo.Dock\PatternLayer.cs). Each group is one sheet of its pattern, laid from the group's own corner,
and each card of it shows the piece of that sheet it stands on — a window onto it, not a pattern of its own:
- **On the bar**, a group is a run of widgets sharing one card (§54, `Layout.Joined`): the sheet starts at its first card's
  corner (`Layout.GroupStart`); a separator, a spacer, a search box (a field, its own card, drawn without a pattern) or a
  card of its own (§311) ends it, and the next group starts its own.
- **In a folder**, a group is a section (§410): a column, or the part of one a separator of Space only splits off
  (`FolderListPlan.Runs`); a separator of Line or None stands on its section and wears its piece too
  (`FolderFlyout.OwnOf`). Two columns side by side are two sheets; one split, two.
- **The bar's own** is one sheet across the bar, a floating bar's docks windows onto the one strip (`PatternLayer.Also`).

Drawn as a layer of its own over the card's fill (`Rounded.Pattern` on the bar, clipped to the card's rounded piece; a line's
card's child in a folder, its section's clip rounding it), under what stands on it: a sprite with a surface drawn once with
Direct2D — the tile as a bitmap brush that wraps, its origin where the card stands on its sheet, a tile's pixel on a pixel —
and drawn again only where its pattern, its ink, its size, its scale or its place on the sheet changed: at a build, never
per frame. A hover, a press, a glide, edit mode's carry, a folder's slide and §458's flight move or light the card with its
layer; the bar's highlight lights over it, a folder's line's lit wash (§417: one brush, its card and its highlight) under it.
A pattern picked is a build like any style's setting (§459): live, on every bar, open folder and menu.

**Menus**: a part's level in a style's editor ends each mode's colours with **Pattern ›** (**Dark pattern ›** in a style with
different colours in dark mode): Default with what it is ("Default (None)"), None and every pattern, each with its swatch — the
part in the style's colours wearing it (the bar itself for the Taskbar; a card on the style's bar, a line on its panel),
smaller and stronger than on a card (`SwatchPatternScale` 0.6, `SwatchPatternBoost` 2.5) so a corner of it shows, no line of
text across it (`Styles.PatternSwatch`) —; a pick goes back (R5). Ours' patterns are overridden per setting like their
colours, Default again or Reset all taking the override out; a copy writes its patterns out. Ours wear None: each is designed
whole and calm, and a pattern is the person's to add.

**The file** (shape 41, `ConfigWords.txt` written again): a part of a style's set may say `"pattern"`: `"dots"`, `"grid"`,
`"lines"`, `"crosshatch"`, `"waves"`, `"checks"`, `"contours"`, `"grain"`, or `"none"` (None over a pattern of ours, or a dark
set's over its light one's); left out, Default. A word this build does not know, and a pattern on the Folder panel, read as
Default (`ItemStyle.Normalize`).

```
appearance.styles[].light|dark.taskbar|widgets|folderButtons|folderWidgets.pattern   new: the pattern's word
```

Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.pattern|darkPattern|patternDots|patternGrid|patternLines|patternCrosshatch|
patternWaves|patternChecks|patternContours|patternGrain` new; None is the separators' `settings.appearance.separatorStyle.none`;
30 languages.

Tests: `PatternTests` (every pattern tiles seamlessly at 100 to 300 %: the sheet a period on is the sheet, a tile's opposite
edges meeting as its neighbouring pixels do; each draws something and leaves room; the grid's lines whole pixels; the ink
capped, a light one fainter; ours read 4.5:1 over every pattern whole; colours at random never less readable over a pattern
than bare — red before the pattern gave way: *"round 74: text 4.35:1 over its pattern"*; the setting per mode, Default,
"none", the file's word read back, a copy, Reset all, the panel none, an unknown word Default; a look wears its patterns),
`StyleMenuTests.APartsPatternIsAChoiceOfSwatches`, `AnEditorIsTheSameForEveryStyle` (a part's level one row longer, the
panel's not), `MenuRulesTests` (every style's editor, the allowance empty), `ConfigSchemaTests`; live:
`SceneTreeTests.AGroupOnTheBarIsOneSheetAndTheNextItsOwn` (two widgets one sheet from the first's corner, the one past a
separator its own, the bar's from its corner) and `ASectionOfAFolderIsOneSheet` (three sections, three sheets, every line's
from its section's corner, at 100, 150 and 225 %). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `pattern-<name>-<light|dark>-<100|150>.png`
(a copy of Graphite with the pattern on its bar's cards and its folders' lines, a folder of two columns, the first split, a
line lit, the editor's Pattern open), `pattern-<name>-taskbar-<light|dark>-150.png` (on the bar alone),
`style-<id>-contours-<light|dark>.png` (each of ours).

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Styles ↗ › Graphite › Widgets in folders › Pattern › Contours: every open folder's lines
contoured at once, the lines of a section running on into each other, the next section's own; Taskbar widgets › Pattern ›
Dots: the bar's groups dotted, each from its own corner, the clock apart (its Folder buttons have none; give them Dots too and
it joins its group again); Taskbar › Pattern › Grid: the bar between the groups. Switch Windows to dark: the light ink.
Default again: gone. A display at 150 % and one at 100 %: as crisp on both.


## 463. Fill fills: a camera's picture over its whole line, its outline over it (2026-10-31)

The person: *"the video camera when set to fill does not fill the whole widget although i want it to."*

**The why.** §331 drew a camera's picture in one room for both Fits: the line between the list's gutters with 4 DIP of
air over and under it, its corners a control's (`CameraLine.PictureBox`). Fill covered that room, not the line: a frame of
the gutter's width down each side and a strip over and under it showed the line's ground. The automatic height was that
room's too (the picture's shape at the width between the gutters, plus the air). Nothing else drew a band: the cover
arithmetic (`PopupPaint.Covered`) was right, and there was no header row, stale mark or plate in the way.

**The rule** (`CameraLine.Room`, `Fills`):
- **Fill** (the default): the picture over the whole line, edge to edge — cut at its edges, centred, its shape kept, square;
  only the folder's clip rounds it, where its section's corners are. An automatic line is the picture's own shape at the
  line's whole width. A picture is decoded as large as it is drawn covering the line (its longer side then, at most three
  times the line's), no longer at the line's longer side, which blurred a tall picture in a wide line.
- **Show it whole**: as before — whole inside the room between the gutters, on its quiet fill, letterboxed.
- The name's plate stands on the gutter either way (`PictureBox`), as before.
- **Lit.** A filling picture covers the folder's fill under its line, so it wears that fill over itself: under the pointer
  and pressed (RowPress, the whole line one target, let go by the click, the pointer leaving or the folder closing), the
  kit's subtle fill (`LineItem.Light`) laid over the picture, as the folder lights the line.
- **Its outline over it.** A line's outline — the seam over it and under it, and the ring of an outline of its own (§410,
  §444) — was a stroke of the line's card, under its content: a picture to its edges covered it, as a graph running under
  the rim already did. It is now a visual of its own (`Line.Edge`, its stroke `Seam` and the `Ring`) inside the line's
  content visual, over what the line draws, so it goes with it carried, lifted and flown in; the card keeps the fill alone.
  A strip (§424) sits under it. Every line's outline is where it was; only where content reached the edge does it now show.

Checked for the same fault and not affected: now playing's art (MediaLine, MediaIsland), a feed's pictures (RssIsland), a
contact's photo (ContactsLine) and a notification's logo draw through `PopupPaint.Covered` into a box of their own size —
an icon, a thumbnail — and have no Fill; no other line has a fit.

No config change.

Tests (red first): `CameraFillTests.FillCoversTheWholeLineAndWholeIsLetterboxed` — a checkered picture, wide, tall and
4:3, in lines of two, five and eight rows and automatic, three widths, 100 and 150 %, drawn over a key colour in its
section's rounded clip: Fill leaves no pixel of the key inside the corners, the checks square at the covering scale with
a corner at the line's middle both ways; Whole at the fitting scale with bars; lit under the pointer and pressed (red:
*"100 %, 640×360 in 540×80 (2 rows), Fill: 4752 px of the line are not picture, the first at (8, 1)"*, *"400×300 in
270×80 (2 rows), Fill: a check is 12.0 px across, not 13.5 (covering at 0.675)"*).
`FolderOutlineTests.AnOutlineRunsOverAPictureThatFillsItsLine` — the real folder, a camera of one colour between two
switches and alone in a section, its outline its own and the folder's, dark and light, 100 and 150 %: the picture to the
line's edges, the outline over it on every side (red: *"folder-outline-camera-dark-100-own: line 1 (camera)'s bottom is
#FF308050, 0.00 of its outline"*, every side, and the seam over it in an outlined folder). `LineHoverRuleTests` reads a
line's fill from its card's first shape. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `camera-fill-<100|150>.png`,
`folder-outline-camera-<look>-<scale>-<own|outlined>.png`, `camera-lines-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: a camera in a folder, Fit Fill: its picture to the line's edges, rounded where the section is; hover and press
it: it lights; Fit Show it whole: letterboxed between the gutters; Appearance › a style with Outlines on it: ringed over
the picture.

## 464. Each layout wears a style; nothing worn through a folder; no surface over another (2026-10-31) — a folder's face wears its Face style's Taskbar widgets since §499 (2026-11-04) — no style is worn since §507 (2026-11-05): the layout's look, a widget's own values over it

The person: *"the appearance settings are not correct yet. first of all no inheritance anymore. i should be able to set the
folder flyout style (it would just take the outlines color or no outline as style) and the folder face style, which shows
in the taskbar. the widgets in the folder should only inherit their style from the layouts style, everything should as a
default inherit its style from the layout style and not the folder settings or similar."*; then *"yeah lets make it per
layout. folder flyout should not have a background color because it is never visible. generally speaking: i also dont want
that items stack their background, with that i mean that if a folder face is transparent for example it should not show the
background of the taskbar but it should show the desktop directly. same for the widgets in the folder. with that i want to
make it easier to tune the look and feel without it being dependent on stacked surfaces."*

**Replaces** §459's *"Karpo wears one (`appearance.style`)"*, its chain *"a line that wears none wears its panel's style"*,
§459's Folder panel background and §441's folder opacity.

**What each wears** (`Worn`, Karpo.Core\WidgetLooks.cs; `Styles.WornId|Worn(appearance, layout)`):

| What | Wears | Default |
|---|---|---|
| a layout's bars | its style (`TaskbarLayout.Style`, the file's `layouts[].style`) | Follow Windows |
| a widget on the bar, a line in a folder | its own style's part (Taskbar widgets / Widgets in folders), `appearance` | its layout's |
| a folder's face | its **Face style**'s Folder buttons (`appearance`) | its layout's |
| a folder's open flyout | its **Flyout style**'s Folder panel **outline** alone, or **No outline** (`panelAppearance`, `"none"`) | its layout's |
| menus, flyouts | the layout's Widgets in folders' background, text, accent; its Folder panel's outline | — |

Nothing a folder wears reaches its lines; nothing is worn through anything. The style definitions (`appearance.styles[]`,
ours with the person's overrides) stay Karpo's, every layout alike. **The font** is one for all of Karpo: the style the
default layout wears (`Gfx.Typeface` measures every row and caches by it; a font a layout would need a Gfx a bar).

**The Folder panel is an outline** (`StyleParts.TonesOf`): its background is gone from the editor, the file's is not read.
A folder draws no panel (`FlyoutTheme.Folder` is `Bare`: its rim alone, no plate, no shadow). **Menus and widget flyouts**
take the Widgets in folders' background — their rows are lines too — **laid over Windows' own flyout**, never in its place
(`FlyoutTheme.Chosen`, `ToneRules.Over`): None and 0 % are Windows' flyout itself, a see-through colour no more see-through
than it, so a menu reads over any desktop, its text made 4.5:1 on what that comes to.

**No surface over another.** Every surface is drawn straight over the desktop:

- A card (a widget's, a folder's face) with a background of its own is its own surface: its colour on the blur of the desktop
  where it is see-through (the window's host backdrop in its shape, `Scene.Rounded.Frost`), on nothing at 0 % or None, solid
  at 100 % — and, without Windows' transparency effects, solid, as the bar is (`SurfaceStyle.Made`, `Scene.Theme`).
- The bar's blur, colour and pattern are drawn only where no card stands: cut out under every card
  (`Scene.DressCards`, Karpo.Dock\Native\CutPath.cs — a Direct2D geometry, the strip less each card's rounded shape, handed to
  a CompositionPath by a hand-made IGeometrySource2DInterop), a floating dock's panels too. A clear face shows the desktop.
- A card of Windows' own background is no card: the widget stands on the bar, as Windows' own buttons do (Follow Windows
  is as it was).
- In an open folder nothing is under the lines: each line's background is its own over the desktop (`FolderFlyout.LineFill`):
  its colour on the blur where it is see-through, Windows' taskbar flyout's surface for Windows' own; the gaps between
  sections show the desktop. A line's background is a sprite on whole px over its blur, a px over the line above, so two
  lines meet with no seam of what is under them.
- Text is made readable on a card over the desktop (Windows' own surface of Windows' mode in its place), not over the bar
  (`ToneRules.Dress`); the bar's pattern is under a card only where it has no background of its own.
- Hit-testing is unchanged: the bar's window and a folder's pieces take clicks where they did.

**Blur, and its limit.** The blur is DWM's host backdrop, one brush per window, drawn in each see-through card's and line's
shape under its colour; with transparency effects off there is none and see-through colours are drawn solid. Pictures taken
with PrintWindow cannot show it (nor any alpha): a see-through card shows over black there. The edit mode's lifted line and
a floating dock's shadow are still drawn under what they carry.

**Ours** keep their look: each card's and line's colour is what §459's card over its bar (line over its panel) came to
(Graphite light cards #FAFAFB at 96 %, lines #FDFDFE at 99 %, …; `Styles.BuiltIn`).

**Menus.** Layout ▾: **Style** (`BarLooks.LayoutStyleRow`), every style with its swatch, ruled with the separators; the
right click on the bar has it too. Styles ↗ is every style, the layout's ticked (Karpo's style's choice gone). A widget's
**Appearance**: **Layout's style** ("Layout's style (Paper)", ticked while it wears none) and every style. A folder's **Face
style** and **Flyout style** (the layout's, **No outline**, every style by its outline's swatch). No "Default", "Inherited" or
"Panel" in them.

**The file** (shape 42; the person's converted once by `karpo-coord\convert-styles4.py`, no reading of the old):

```
layouts[].style                    new: the style the layout wears; "windows" / none left out
appearance.style                   gone (moved to every layout's style)
appearance.styles[].*.folderPanel  { outline?, … }: background gone (not read)
islands[..].appearance             a widget's, a line's, a folder's face's own style
islands[..].panelAppearance        a folder's Flyout style; "none" for No outline
```

Converted: `appearance.style` to every layout's `style`; a folder panel background dropped — of the person's own styles
folded into their Widgets in folders (taken where the lines have none, laid under a see-through one); a see-through widget's
or face's background of the person's laid over their bar's; the rest kept.

## 465. Windows' taskbar never shows while Karpo runs, and always shows when it does not (2026-11-01) — at the bottom while hidden since §591 (2026-11-09), left there once shown since §600 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"hiding / showing the windows taskbar does not work / does not change anything. stuff like this should also
not happen. find out why and fix wholistically."*; then *"when karpo is running the windows taskbar should never show. also
not configurable or similar. when karpo is not running, if possible, the windows taskbar should show. (even if karpo
crashes the windows taskbar should either appear or karpo should start again, whatever is the best / most resilient
strategy.)"*

**Why the toggle did nothing.** Putting the taskbar back set *the person's own* state again: a record file
(`taskbar-state`), else Windows' own (StuckRects3), else ABM_GETSTATE. Explorer saves its live state into StuckRects3
(byte 8 was `0x03`, auto-hide, on the user's PC, and still was minutes after the taskbar was shown again: it saves later,
at its end or a sign-out), so an auto-hide of Karpo's once saved there read as the person's, and every put-back since 2026-10-31 said *"put back: auto-hide on, as before Karpo"* (appbar.log): the taskbar
came back auto-hidden, off the screen, and turning the setting off changed nothing to see. The 2026-10-16 fix (StuckRects3
over ABM_GETSTATE) rested on Explorer *never* saving Karpo's auto-hide there.

**Replaces** §345's *Hide the Windows taskbar* row (`hideTaskbar`, `KarpoMenu.HideTaskbarRow`), the record file and every
"as the person had it" (`Taskbar.Own`, `ITaskbarRecord`, `AutoHideIn`), and the taskbars hidden only on the displays Karpo
is off on (`Taskbar.SetDisabledDisplays`): Windows' taskbar is hidden on every display while Karpo runs.

**Now** (Karpo.Dock\Taskbar.cs): nothing is kept. Hidden is auto-hide on and its windows hidden (`TakeOver`, `Cover`);
shown is auto-hide off and every display's taskbar window shown (`PutBack`), whoever shows it and however Karpo ended.
Hidden whenever the dock runs (`Dock.HidesTaskbar`: not on a made-up display, not while the session ends — so the next
sign-in starts with a taskbar, should Karpo not start). A new Explorer, or the person's own switch in Windows' settings, is
auto-hidden again at the next reconcile (`Rehide`). A file that still says `hideTaskbar` is read, the word dropped
(`TransferSummary` names it as the file writes it); `taskbar-state` is a retired file (`RetiredFiles.Local`).

**However Karpo ends** the taskbar shows, or Karpo comes back:

| How it ends | What shows the taskbar | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Quit, sign-out, shutdown | the dock (`Dispose`, `SessionEnding`) | stays shown |
| An exception nothing caught | the dock's last handler (`Program`), then the guard | the guard starts Karpo again |
| A crash, a kill, End task, a hang ended | the guard (`DockGuard.Run`: `Taskbar.Restore` at once) | Karpo started again 2 s, 20 s, 120 s later; never a fourth time in 10 minutes |
| The guard ended from outside | — | the dock starts another at once (`Dock.Guard.cs`: its end waited for on the pool, `WM_KARPO_GUARD_GONE`), four guards per dock at most |
| Dock and guard ended together | nothing can | the taskbar stays hidden until Karpo starts again (at sign-in where it starts with Windows) |

Tests: `TaskbarStateTests` (hidden is auto-hide on, shown is off whatever it was before Karpo; a second put-back changes
nothing; a lost auto-hide hidden again), `BarKeeperTests.AnAutoHideKeptFromAnEarlierKarpoIsNeverPutBack`,
`ACrashIsShownByTheGuard`, `TheSessionEndingShowsTheTaskbarAndACancelHidesItAgain`, `BarWorld` (Explorer keeps every
ABM_SETSTATE, as on the user's PC; Explorer's taskbar shown and not auto-hidden whenever Karpo does not hide it). Live
(`Karpo.Resilience`, docs/resilience.md): every rule now says Explorer's taskbar is never shown while Karpo runs;
`guard-killed` (a new guard within 5 s) and `dock-killed` (the taskbar shown, not auto-hidden, within 2 s; Karpo back with
its bars, its guard and the taskbar hidden within 40 s).

By hand: ⚙ Settings has no *Hide the Windows taskbar*. Quit Karpo: Windows' taskbar there, not auto-hidden, windows
maximized above it. End Karpo.exe in Task Manager (the dock, not the group): the taskbar shows, and a few seconds later Karpo
is back and it is gone.

## 466. Windows' menus: a taskbar button each, grouped, and one thing open at a time (2026-11-01)

The person: *"add widgets that open the windows native menus like the notifications or the quick settings. they should be
grouped together."*; the list they validated, *"Yes, core set"*; then *"also in general if possible i want only always one
thing open at a time, so if i open a windows menu with a shortcut it should close the karpo folder or when i open a karpo
folder it should close the windows menu / flyout."*

**Eight taskbar entries** (`BarKind`, `BarClick.Panel`, drawn as the widgets board was: one glyph in a button's well,
`BarEntries.IsWindowsMenu`; *§474:* the notifications, quick settings and the widgets board wear Windows' own faces now),
each opening Windows' own popup, never one of Karpo's (`WindowsButtons.Target`):

| Entry | Opens | How |
|---|---|---|
| `quickLink` | the quick link menu, Start's right click | Win+X |
| `windowsNotifications` | the notifications and calendar | Win+N |
| `windowsQuickSettings` | quick settings | Win+A |
| `windowsSound` | quick settings' sound output page | Win+Ctrl+V (`ShellTarget.Held`) |
| `windowsNetworks` | quick settings' Wi-Fi page | `ms-availablenetworks:` (no shortcut opens it) |
| `windowsCast` | cast, the wireless displays | Win+K |
| `windowsClipboard` | clipboard history | Win+V |
| `emojiPanel` | the emoji panel | Win+. (VK_OEM_PERIOD) |

The shortcut is what a person presses, so it opens what they would. The bar never takes the focus, so what clipboard
history pastes and the emoji panel types goes to the app the person was in. Taskbar-only: a line in a folder can open no
popup (§15). Licence-free, as Windows' own buttons are (`LicenseCount.Free`). The quick link menu goes beside Start, the rest
at the bar's end. Titles that would clash with Karpo's own widgets say *panel*: Cast panel, Clipboard panel, Emoji panel.

**Grouped.** The add list's *Start and taskbar* folder opens with a *Windows menus* folder (`AddTree`, `windowsMenus`):
Start, Search, Task view, Widgets and the eight, twelve, the most a folder holds. It is a folder in a folder because
Browse is twelve subjects already. The catalogue has the same twelve as its own group, *Windows menus*
(`WidgetCategory.WindowsMenus`), after Taskbar. Config shape 43: the eight words are new to the file.

**One thing open at a time.**

- *A Windows menu opening closes Karpo's flyout:* as it already did. A flyout closes when another window takes the focus
  (`FlyoutHost`, `WM_ACTIVATE`), and as the Windows key goes down.
- *A Karpo flyout opening closes Windows' menu* (`WindowsPanels.CloseFor`, run by `FlyoutHost.Opening`): Search and Start as
  before, and now three more panels (`WindowsPanel`). Each holds the foreground for as long as it is open, so each is read
  from the foreground window alone, by its process and its class (seen on 26300):

  | Panel | Window |
  |---|---|
  | `Notifications` | a `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow` of ShellExperienceHost.exe |
  | `QuickSettings` (and its sound, cast and Wi-Fi pages) | the `ControlCenterWindow` of ShellHost.exe |
  | `ExplorerMenu` (the quick link menu, Explorer's other menus) | a `Xaml_WindowedPopupClass` of explorer.exe |

  Each is closed by Escape, sent only while it is the foreground window.
- *A second click closes:* the buttons of those three toggle as Start's does (`SearchToggle`, one per panel, and
  `PanelWatch` noting when each went). A press that already sent the menu away leaves it closed. Quick settings' four
  buttons are one panel: the button that opened it closes it, and another goes to its own page over it
  (`WindowsPanels.ForPage`).

**Not yet:** clipboard history and the emoji panel never take the foreground (their host is TextInputHost.exe), so a Karpo
flyout does not close them yet, and a second click on their button is Windows' own shortcut again.

Tests: `WindowsSearchTests` (which window is which panel, which button opens which, the page rule, a flyout closing each
panel, a press that closed quick settings), `WindowsButtonsTests`, the registries' lists, `AddTreeTests` and
`CataloguePagesTests`.

By hand: add the eight from *Start and taskbar › Windows menus*. Each click opens its popup, and with the focus in Notepad,
Clipboard panel and Emoji panel put what is picked there. With quick settings open, its button closes it and the Sound
button goes to the sound page. With the notifications open, open a Karpo folder: the notifications close. With a folder
open, press Win+A: the folder closes.

## 467. The styles are ⚙'s: one Styles row, every style its editor; nothing links to them (2026-11-01) — gone with the styles, §507 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"you should be able to edit and create and copy styles as before. right now the list of styles is just a fixed
list."*; then *"styles have multiple links to them, but the styles should just be one entry on the top settings level (global
settings blue cog) and it should show the list of styles and it does not have to adhere to the two levels rule."*

**Why it was a fixed list.** §464 made Styles ↗ (a menu of its own under Layout ▾'s crumb) a list of every style with the
layout's ticked, so it read as a choice; each row was a link to its editor, but a style of the person's carries its bin at
its row's end, and a click off a row's tools only ever picked a choice (`Flyout.ControlClicked`, §317): the person's own
styles did nothing when clicked, and the editor, Add and Duplicate were behind a link from three other menus.

**One home.** ⚙'s second band is **Styles ›**, **Accounts ›**, **Public holidays ›** (`KarpoMenu.Styles`,
`BarLooks.StylesLevel`). Styles is every style — Follow Windows, Graphite, Paper, Harbor, Bloom, the person's — each with
its swatch and its own level, its editor (`BarLooks.EditorRows`, §459's: the person's Name, Font, Weight, the five parts each
opening its colours and patterns, Different colors in dark mode, Duplicate and Reset all at its foot); the person's with a
bin, asked first; ruled off, **Add a style** right under them (R9, §452). None is ticked: which is worn is said where it is
worn. Ours are changed by overriding and put back by Reset all, never renamed nor deleted.

**Made, opened.** Add a style, or Duplicate in an editor, makes the style and its editor opens in place: from Styles a level
in, from an editor in place of it, Back going to Styles (`Dock.ShowMadeStyle`: `Styles.Made` the style the pick made,
`OptionMenu.ThingRowOf` its row, `Flyout.ShowLevel` its level from wherever the menu stands — the levels it is not under
give way, those over it open; `Flyout.OpenLevel` is it from the menu's own rows).

**Live.** Every pick in an editor is a pick of ⚙: set, saved and shown at once (`Dock.SettingsPicked`, `Apply`): every
layout, widget, folder face and flyout wearing the style draws it, ⚙ shown again where it stands. Deleted, a layout that wore
it Follows Windows and a widget, a face or a flyout wears its layout's; no id of it is left in the file (`Styles.Delete`).

**No links** (§485: one is back under each choice of a style, to ⚙ › Styles). Gone: Layout ▾'s and Display ▾'s **Styles ↗**, the bar's right click's (Layout ▾'s rows), a widget's
Appearance's and a folder's Face style's and Flyout style's under their choices (`OptionRow.ChoiceLink` gone), and with
them `OptionLink.Styles|Style`, `LooksScope.Styles|Style`, `EditEntry.Styles`, `EditMenu.Styles`, `BarSpot.Style`.
Picking stays where a style is worn: Layout ▾ › **Style** (the layout's), a widget's **Appearance**, a folder's **Face
style** and **Flyout style**, each listing every style with its swatch, so none needs a way out (R15: a style is the
person's thing, made in ⚙; which one a layout or a widget wears is that layout's or widget's own setting, set there alone).
Display ▾'s foot is **Add a layout** (R16), Layout ▾'s **Behavior**.

**Deeper than three levels.** ⚙ › Styles › a style › a part › a colour › its picker is five deep. The menu rules make one
exception of it (`MenuRulesTests.DeepAllowed`, `GoesDeep`): R1 alone, under ⚙ › Styles alone, walked to its end for every
other rule (R2 to R16 hold in it). Nothing else may go deeper.

**One row more.** ⚙'s first level is thirteen rows and three rules, 411 DIP: a configuration menu is 464 DIP now
(`Flyout.SettingsHeightDip`, 440 till now: a row of buttons, a rule and thirteen rows), so it still never scrolls (R2). Every
configuration menu is that height. ⚙ holds every style's editor, about 1600 commands a style: `OptionMenu.Most` is a million
(2000 till now).

Strings: none new, none gone (Styles is `settings.appearance.styles.header`).

Tests: `StyleMenuTests.SettingsHoldsTheOneWayToTheStyles` (one Styles row on ⚙'s first level; no row named Styles nor
anything opening them in any other menu of the corpus; Layout ▾'s and Display ▾'s feet), `EveryStyleInTheListOpensItsEditor`,
`AddAndDuplicateOpenTheNewStylesEditor` (on the desktop), `OursAreResetTheirsAreDeleted`, `AnEditorIsTheSameForEveryStyle`,

`MenuRulesTests.OnlySettingsStylesMayGoDeeperThanThreeLevels`, `EveryMenuKeepsTheRules` (⚙'s editors now in its corpus);

<light|dark>.png`.
