## 468. A folder's contents are their own folder's height at every level (2026-11-01) — the taskbar's part superseded by §492 (2026-11-03)

The person: *"a folder when having auto mode or max height or similar should always be the height of the root level. it
should not change its height dependent on level / contents except for the root level of course."* The folder (widget) is
a folder's contents (§380) whose navigation shows a subfolder's items in place (§398) — the person's own is Automatic up
to 24 cells, "Show its contents". Going in, an Automatic line was as tall as the subfolder shown (§398: "growing and
shrinking as it goes in and back"), so the open Karpo folder around it grew and shrank with every level; the list a
folder's contents' button opens from the taskbar did the same ("its height its rows'").

**The deeper levels.** A subfolder gone into, as deep as the folders go — by a click on its row, Enter, or a folder
handed on while open (§357) — and back by the head, Backspace, Left, Escape or the mouse's back button: in the line of a
folder (`FolderContentsLine`, `FolderContentsView`) and in the taskbar's list (`PinFolderFlyout`). Both walk one trail
(`Drives\FolderTrail.cs`).

**The root cause.** Each sized itself by what the level shown holds: the line's `ListHeight` (what the open folder lays
an Automatic or Fill line out at, `IListContent`) counted the shown folder's items, and the list's `Build` made its
panel as tall as the shown folder's rows and the subfolder's head.

**One rule, in the trail.** `FolderTrail.Sizing`: a level is sized by the root's items as the root was left; the root by
what it shows. Both ask it and measure the answer their own way:

- **The line.** `ListHeight` is the root's head and rows (`FolderContentsView.ListHeight`, `Tall`) whatever level
  shows; what it lays out and scrolls is the shown folder's (`ContentHeight`, the line's `ScrollHeight`). So the folder
  sizes it as the root at every level: a subfolder of fewer items stands under the head with room left under them (its
  rows sharing it up to a list row each, as any line set taller than its rows does), one of more scrolls them under the
  head (ListScroll.cs), the keys bringing the row they come to into sight. Going in starts at the top; back out, the
  folder is as far scrolled as it was left (`FolderContentsLine.Into`/`Back`, the trail keeping the scroll).
- **The list.** At a level under its folder the body is kept (`PanelContent.Kept`) at the root's body less the head:
  the whole list as tall as on its folder, the head over the rows, fewer leaving room, more scrolling. Never less than
  one row under the head (a folder of a single subfolder is shorter than a head and a row; going into it grows the list
  that once). One body measure (`BodyHeight`, `MessageHeight`) for the level shown and for the root.
- **Width** did not jump and does not: the line is its column's width, the list `WidthDip`.

**The root changing.** Only the folder shown is followed (its watcher), so what changes in the root while a subfolder
shows changes nothing then; back on the root it shows what it was left showing at once, is read again, and the line or
the list takes the root's new height there.

**A race found on the way.** The list kept one read come back, taken by whichever post came first: back out and
straight into another subfolder, the root's re-read's post took the subfolder's read and dropped it, and the list said
"Reading…" until it closed. The read is now kept with the read it belongs to (`arrived` and its generation), taken only
by that read's post, and an earlier read never overwrites a later one.

**Not changed.** A Fixed line is its height, as it was. A quick settings line's page (§170) is not a level of this: the
folder's column becomes the page, whose heights are their own at the person's asking (§177: the Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and
Cast pages fixed; §200: the sound page growing with its mixer), and a folder's list never scrolls as a whole (§152) — a
page held to its folder's height would leave lines out. A menu's levels are a menu's. The folder animations (§446, §458)
play as the folder opens and closes; a level changes nothing of the panel's size now, so they are as they were.

Tests: `PinFolderFlyoutTests.EveryLevelOfAFolderLineIsItsOwnFoldersHeight` (red first: the line 220 px in Karpo for its
own 400; now an Automatic line of ten in an open folder, gone into five and into thirty: the line and the panel as tall
and as wide as with the ten, the five not scrolled, the thirty scrolled to the last by the keys, back out unscrolled),
`EveryLevelOfTheListIsItsOwnFoldersHeight` (red first: 232 px for 368; then the race above: the thirty stayed
"Reading…"), `AFolderLinesSubfolderOpensInTheLineNotBesideIt` (as tall in Karpo as on Projects);
`FolderContentsLineTests.ALinesHeightIsItsOwnFoldersAtEveryLevel` (was `ALinesHeightFollowsTheFolderShown`: the ten's
height in the five and in an empty folder, what it scrolls the shown folder's, the root grown while Karpo shows sizing it
once back); `PinFolderSettingsTests.EveryLevelIsSizedByTheRoot`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`folder-nav-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (every step the root's height, Receipts 2026's thirty scrolled to the last),
`pin-folder-inside-…png`, `pin-folder-level-<fewer|more>-dark-100.png`.

By hand: a list folder with Files ▸ Folder contents, Automatic, "Show its contents": click a subfolder of few items and
one of many — the folder keeps its size, the many scroll; the wheel and the keys in it; Back. From the taskbar, a folder's
contents' subfolder button: the list the same. Add a file to the root while in a subfolder, then Back.

## 469. Unfold and Ripple: a folder's columns open out from its face one after another; its sections come in as a ripple (2026-11-01) — superseded by §489 (2026-11-02)

The person: *"add some more folder animations. you can also work with the groups in the folder or the columns to make
animations that target those things. make two more high quality animations"*

**Two more Folder animations**, after Fly in, before Off (Layout ▾ › Behavior › Folder animation; the bar's right click the
same): **Unfold**, its picture a page opening out, and **Ripple**, groups in a frame (R13: six choices, six pictures). In the
file `"folderAnimation": "unfold"` / `"ripple"`: words an older Karpo does not know, so the file's shape is 43
(`Config.Shape`, `ConfigWords.txt`); nothing to convert. Two strings in every language
(`settings.general.folderAnimation.unfold|ripple`).

Both are §458's machinery: the panel stands still, one value runs (the flight's `Progress`, straight, 0 shut to 1 open, a key
frame animation), and every part reads where it stands from it by an expression of the same sums as the plan
(`FolderStaging.cs`, pure; `FolderFlight.Expression`): Windows' decelerate curve (0, 0, 0, 1) exactly, 3x^⅔ − 2x. The close is
the opening run back, 2.5 times as fast (the last in is the first out; a decelerate run back is an accelerate); a close as it
comes in turns back from where it is (`MotionClock`).

| | Unfold (the columns) | Ripple (the sections) |
|---|---|---|
| What moves | each section's clip, grown from nothing out of its side nearest the face; its lines gliding 24 DIP along with it and fading in over the first 30 % of its way; its outline uncovered with it (an inset clip on its rim) | each section's views grown from 92 % about its middle (their clip with them); its lines rising 10 DIP from the bar's side, fading in over 40 %; its outline grown with it and faded in over 35 % |
| Which way | the column over the face (the face's middle inside its width) up out of its bar (down from a top bar); a column beside it from its side nearest the face, outward; from a side bar every column outward | each about its own middle |
| Order | the columns by how far they stand across from the face — as far, at once (a face between two: both) — 60 ms apart (150 ms at most between the first and the last); in a column its sections nearest the face first, 25 ms apart (50 at most) | a wave out from the face: each section starts as far into 150 ms (55 ms a section where there are few) as it is from the face, between the nearest (at once) and the farthest; its lines nearest the face first, 20 ms apart (60 at most) |
| Each | 260 ms | 300 ms the section, 240 ms a line |
| Three columns, five sections (face under the middle) | in 345 ms, out 138 ms (set at the bar's start: 380 / 152) | in 450 ms, out 180 ms |

- **The timing is the folder's**: how many columns and sections it shows, and where its face is. The host asks the folder once
  the panel is placed (`FlyoutHost.Timing`, before the clock starts): `FolderFlyout.Staging` lists the sections in the
  host's panels' order (`FolderPlan.Pieces`) and the lines shown, and `FolderMotion.Timed` sets the whole. Fly in now goes the
  same way (its plan as a staging: `FolderFlight.Staging`), so one binding serves all three (`FolderFlyout.BindFlight`;
  `FlyoutHost.BindRims` for the outlines: Fly in's drawn on, Unfold's uncovered, Ripple's grown).
- **A divider of space** between two sections goes with the nearer of them.
- **Only what keeps the blur right moves** (§464: every line its own surface over the host backdrop). The first idea for
  Unfold was the columns turned about their near edge in perspective, a folding screen; rejected: a backdrop brush samples
  the desktop in the screen's space and is not drawn through a 3D projection, and pictures cannot show it (PrintWindow, §464),
  so it could not be checked. Offsets, uniform scales, clips and opacity keep each line's blur where the line is. A clip
  scaled along one axis squeezes a section's rounded corners on its way (the leading edge's radius shrinks with it), never at
  the end.
- **Nothing outside**: Unfold's lines glide inside their section's clip, which grows from the section's own edge, so no line
  shows past its section or over the one below; Ripple stays inside its sections (92 % to whole).
- **The end is exact**: as the opening's timer runs out (`FlyoutHost.Arrived`) every line is let go of and put where it
  stands, every section's clip and views at their size (`Land`), every outline whole, unclipped, seen (`Unfly`).
- **As every style**: Windows' animation effects off, at once; another folder opened while one is open, there at once;
  arranged (edit mode), a fade where it stands; input finds every line where it ends from the first frame; the preview plays
  them as they are lit (§458).

Tests: `FolderStagingTests` (both are styles whose parts move; Unfold's column over the face first from the bar, those beside
from their side, sections 25 ms apart, lines with their section 24 DIP back, 345 ms; from the bar's start, a left, a right and
a top bar, six columns no slower, one section; Ripple's wave by distance, lines 20 ms apart rising from the bar's side, 450 ms;
every part one way and exactly in place at the end; the close the last in first out, 40 % of the time; a plan over another
time), `FolderFlightTests.FlyInIsAStyleOfItsOwn` (`Timed`, the six choices), `FolderPreviewTests.EveryChoicePlays`,
`KarpoMenuGeneralTests.TheTaskbarsBehaviourIsAGroupOfItsMenu` (six choices, six pictures, `"unfold"`, `"ripple"`),
`ConfigSchemaTests`; live `FolderMotionFilmTests.TheStagedSumsRunOnTheCompositor` (every sum started on what it moves,
with every number it reads; red: *"An invalid subchannel was specified in the expression"* — an expression's names are the
same in either case, and a size's `F` stood in for the clock `f`, so every sum of a part that grows threw where the folder
swallows it: the size is `G`), `.AStagedFolderLandsWholeAndOneCutShortLeavesNothingBehind` (each lands exactly as the folder
shown still, nothing bound; cut short and opened again by Slide, the same); films
`FolderMotionFilmTests.AFolderUnfoldsColumnByColumnOutFromItsFace` and
`.AFolderRipplesInSectionBySectionOutFromItsFace` (eight times slower: a frame with the first part in well ahead of the
later ones on the way in and on the way out, nothing outside the folder, the end exactly the folder shown still, nothing
bound once landed, nothing in sight once closed), `.TheStagedAnimationsFromEveryEdge` (strips: bottom, left and right bars,
light and dark). Strips (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `film-folder-<unfold|ripple>-<open|close>.png`,
`film-folder-<style>-<edge>-<light|dark>-<open|close>.png`.

By hand: Layout ▾ › Behavior › Folder animation: rest on Unfold — the folder nearest the pointer opens column by column out
from its button, the outlines unfolding with their columns; rest on Ripple — its sections come in as a ripple from the
button, the lines settling in each. Open a folder of three columns from a bottom bar, a top bar and a side bar; close one as
it comes in (it turns back). A see-through Widgets in folders background (Graphite's): the blur under each line stays with it
as it moves. Edit mode: a fade. Animation effects off: at once.

## 470. One keyboard: every entry on the bar and every target of a folder's lines is a stop (2026-11-01)

*The person*: "keyboard navigation should be implemented for all the widgets and generally for the whole application."

Until now the keys reached the bar's app buttons (Win+T) and its tray (Win+B), a folder's lines as wholes, the menus and
the quick panels. Nothing reached a widget on the bar, and inside a folder the keys stopped at the line: a line's own
buttons, items, steppers and transport buttons had no key unless that line had written a walk of its own, and 21 of
them had, each with its own index and its own ring. The audit is `%TEMP%\karpo-coord\keyboard\keyboard-audit.md` at
the time; what it found and decided is here.

**The model, one for everything** (Windows' own):

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Win+T, Win+B | the keys onto the bar's app buttons, onto its tray, as before; no other global key is taken |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | the next, the one before, group, round: a region of the bar, a folder's line, a menu's or panel's row |
| arrows | the nearest stop that way; a line that walks its own interior (a calendar, the to-do list, a page of controls, a text field) takes them first and lets go at its edges |
| Home, End | the first, the last stop of the region or the line; again, the folder's first, last line |
| Page Up, Page Down | a window's worth further in a line that scrolls; a slider ten steps; a calendar a month (its own) |
| Enter, Space | what a click on the stop does |
| Menu key, Shift+F10 | what a right click on it opens |
| Escape | one level back: a field lets go, a page goes back, a folder or menu closes and the keys go back to what opened it; on the bar, back to the window that had them |
| F2, Delete | rename, remove, where the line has them (to-do, desktops; edit mode's Delete with its undo) |
| Ctrl+arrows (edit mode) | move the widget, as before |

The ring is the one the bar and the folder already drew — the focus ink's band and the window's hairline inside it
(`EditLook.Ring`) — shown only while the keys are in use.

**The bar** (`KeyStops`, `Dock.Keys.cs`). Its stops are the entries a screen reader lists (`BarUia.Entries`), in three
regions: the app buttons and "…", the tray's icons and chevron, and everything else along the bar — Start, search, task
view, Windows' buttons, every widget's cells, the clock, show desktop. Tab and Shift+Tab go round the regions in the order
they start along the bar; the arrows walk the region round; Enter is the click (`Dock.Click`) and the menu key the right
click (`Dock.Context`) on any stop. A widget whose click opens its folder opens it with the keys in it on its first stop
(`FolderFlyout.TakeKeys`); Escape closes it and the keys are on the widget again (the bar keeps them through Karpo's own
windows). UI Automation's SetFocus puts the keys on any entry.

**A folder** (`FolderFlyout.Keys.cs`). A line's stops are its hit targets (`LineFocus`): every target its click reaches,
found where its own hit test answers over the whole of its laid-out content — a scrolled line's items out of sight
included — or, where a line lays its targets out as one list (`ILineTargets`: the news, mail, the agenda, the events,
the notifications), read from that list in one layout. What the pointer reaches, the keys reach; nothing to declare or
keep in step. The arrows walk a line's stops by where they stand (`FocusNav.Toward`) and cross to the line beside at its
edge, onto its stop nearest that way; Tab goes line to line. A stop out of sight is scrolled into it
(`ListScrolled.Revealing`). Enter and Space are `Activate` with the stop's target, which is `Click(target)` — the very
call a click there makes; the menu key opens the line's menu at the stop, and a line whose menu is about one of its items
reads the stop the keys are on (`CellIsland.KeyedPart`; the processes). A slider's stop steps (`CellIsland.CardStep`):
Left and Right one, Page Up and Down ten, Home and End to its ends (the brightness line). A line's stops are kept until
the folder changes or closes, so a key held asks the line once.

**Lines that walk themselves** say so (`CellIsland.WalksItsOwnKeys`) and keep their keys: the month and the day, week and
year views, the weather's hours and days, the to-do list and a note, the contacts, the clipboard, the desktops, a page of
quick settings, a folder's contents, the market converter. Those with targets of their own say which their keys are on
(`OwnKeyedTarget`: the quick pages, the weather's, the to-do list, the desktops, the clipboard), so the sweep holds them to every target too. Four lines whose walks were the kit's done again lost
them: the toggles, the actions, the layouts and the processes (their `keyed`, their `CardKey` and their own rings went;
`LineButton.Paint`'s `focused` with them).

**One engine** (`FocusNav`): `Step` (round or held), `Toward` (the nearest that way: straight ahead first, nothing off
to the side where two overlap across the way, the one nearer the middle on a tie), `ReadingOrder`. The bar's
`KeyStops.Move` went into it.

**Not done** (the sweep's allowlist, `KeyboardSweepAllowed.cs`): the month's and the calendar views' arrow buttons (their
keys are Page Up and Down, no stop) and an unlit Join in the day and week views; the clipboard's Clear, Turn on and a
row's Pin and Delete. Also: the sound lines' sliders are no targets (a press, not a click) and so no stops yet; edit
mode's resize by Shift+arrows (folder heights were being changed beside this); a folder has no UI Automation tree yet
(`FlyoutUia` is the menus'), so Narrator follows the bar and the menus but not a folder's stops.

Tests: `KeyboardSweepTests.EveryTargetOfEveryLineIsReachedByTheKeys` (every list kind in the real folder at 100 and
150 %: every target a click reaches is a stop or its own keys reach it, every stop reached by the arrows, the keys come in
on the first with the ring, the ring's middle is a click on the stop the keys are on, Escape closes; its allowlist only
shrinks — 21 kinds when written, 5 now), `ASliderStepsByTheKeys`; `FocusNavTests`; `TaskbarKeysTests`
(`EverythingElseAlongTheBarIsARegionAndTabGoesRoundThem`, `EveryKindOnTheBarIsAStop`). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`keys-bar-…`, `keys-folder-…`, `keys-flyout-…` (the weather's), `keys-menu-…`, each `<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`.

By hand (Karpo the taskbar): Win+T, Tab to the widgets, an arrow to the clock, Enter: its folder opens with the ring on its
first stop; the arrows through a line's buttons and items, Enter on one; Escape: the ring on the clock again. A long news
line: Down past what shows scrolls it. The brightness line: Right and Left step it.

## 471. One keyboard, finished: one ring, the calendars' arrows and Joins, the clipboard, the sound sliders, sizing by the keys, and Narrator in a folder (2026-11-01)

*The person*, on §470's open ends: "sounds good. go ahead" — to one ring, the calendars' arrows as stops, edit
mode's Shift+arrows, the sound sliders, and Tab staying line to line.

**One ring.** A line that walks its own keys (§470) drew its own ring round the hour, the day, the row its keys were
on, and the folder drew its ring round the whole line as well: two rings. Now one shows at a time. Such a line says
whether it rings what its keys are on (`CellIsland.RingsOwnKeys`: the weather's hours and days, the month, the to-do
list, the contacts, the desktops, a page of quick settings, a folder's contents), and while it does the folder draws
none (`FolderFlyout.FocusRing`); while it rings nothing (no hour chosen yet, a task being typed, a note, the day and
week views, which fill the day picked and ring nothing) the folder's ring is the one. The keys gone to another line
or to a stop beside its own, the line is told (`CellIsland.OwnKeys(false)`) and puts its ring out; come onto it, a
line with something to ring rings it at once (the month its day picked).

**A line's own keys beside stops of the folder's.** A line that walks its own keys was one stop, so what stood beside
its own walk had no key: the month's and the calendar views' arrows, a Join that was not lit. Where such a line lays
its targets out as one list (`ILineTargets`), it now says which of them its own keys reach (`CellIsland.OwnKeysReach`:
the days); the others are stops of their own, and its own are one stop more — target 0, where they stand together
(`LineFocus.Parts`). The folder's arrows walk between them as between any stops; on its own stop the line's keys come
first, and only there (`FolderFlyout.OwnKeyed`); what they move (the hours scrolled, a day picked) moves the stops
beside them, which are found again (`OwnKeysMoved`).

- **The month** (`MonthTile`): its arrows are stops; Enter on one steps the month (Page Up and Down still do, from
  the days). Up and Down stay in the month shown and let go at its first and last week — Up onto the arrows, Down to
  the line below; Left and Right go on into the months either side, as before. Its targets are one list now
  (`LineTargets`, its hit test too; `DayAt` went).
- **The day and week views** (`CalendarViewTile`): their arrows and every Join seen are stops (an unlit Join too);
  Enter on a Join joins that meeting. Their days stay their own keys' (Left and Right a day, Up and Down the hours,
  letting go at their ends; Enter on them joins the lit meeting, as before). Their hit test, their tooltips and their
  stops are one list (`LineTargets`; `JoinAt` and `At` went).
- **The year view** walks no keys of its own any more: its arrows moved the day a month at a time, so its days had no
  key. Its arrows and every day are the folder's stops, walked where they stand; Enter on a day picks it; Page Up and
  Down still turn the year and Home goes to today (its `CardKey`, which lets the arrows go).
- **The clipboard** (`ClipboardLine`) walks no keys of its own: "Clear all", "Turn on", every row and its pin and
  delete are the folder's stops (its targets one list, `LineTargets`), the ring the folder's. The row the keys are on,
  or whose button they are on, is lit with its buttons showing (`CellIsland.LightsKeyedPart`, drawn again as the keys
  move), so the ring never goes round a button that is not drawn. Enter on a row still pastes once let go (its
  `CardKeyUp`); on a button it is that button's click, in place. Its own walk, its `keyed` and its own ring went.
- **The markets converter** walks no keys of its own: its two fields and its swap are stops; Enter on a field types
  in it, Escape and Enter end that, and Tab keeps what is typed and goes on to the next line, as every line's field
  lets it go (it went from field to field, which left the folder's ring on the other).
- **The contacts** say where their keys are (`OwnKeyedTarget`), as the sweep wants of every line that walks itself.

**Tab stays line to line** in a folder, the arrows within a line and across to the next at its edge, as §470 has it;
Shift+Tab the line before, round. A line's own field takes Tab only to let it go.

**The sound sliders are stops.** The volume line's slider and every app's in the mixer are targets of the line's hit
test now, as the brightness line's slider is — a press on one is still the drag it was (`CardPress`); only the keys
see it as a stop — so the folder's arrows walk onto them, and there the keys step them (`SoundPartTile.CardStep`):
Left and Right a level, Page Up and Down ten, Home and End to its ends, Up and Down walking on. The step is the panel
slider's own (`Slider.Step`; its keys and its wheel step by the same `StepTo`), so a slider steps alike on the sound
page and in a folder. The quick settings' sound page stepped its sliders by the keys already. The tests run on a
made-up machine (`SoundParts.Made`), never this PC's volume.

**Edit mode sizes by the keys** (`EditResize`, `EditKeys`: Shift+arrows, `EditKeyAct.Resize`). With a widget chosen
by the keys, Shift+Down makes a folder's line a cell taller and Shift+Up a cell shorter: its menu's rows stepper ("+",
"−"; `LineHeightRows.Act`) in either mode, held to its kind's fewest and most (`LineHeight.Limits`) and to the room the
folder has on its screen (`RoomCells`), nothing under Fill. A sized line (§432) goes to the next size its kind offers,
or the one before, as its "Size" row does. Shift+Right and Shift+Left make a bar's widget wider and narrower where a
face of it has a width choice (Compact, Standard, Wide: the meeting's, the air's, the quakes'), through that row of
its menu. Nothing else has a size to step: a bar's widget has no height, a folder's line no width (its list has one).
What changes is written as the menu's change is (`Dock.ChangeWidget`, which the menu's height and size share now), so
it is one step of the undo, and a screen reader is told the new size as the menu says it ("4 rows", "Full", "Wide").
Ctrl+arrows still move the widget, Ctrl first where both are held.

| Key | Does (added to §470's) |
|---|---|
| Shift+arrows (edit mode) | size the widget the keys chose, as its menu does: a line a cell, a bar's widget a width |

**Narrator in a folder** (`FolderFlyout.Uia.cs`). A folder had no tree, so a screen reader heard its window and
nothing in it. Now it is a pane of its lines in the order the keys walk them; a line with stops is a group of buttons,
each named by its tooltip where it has one (an arrow, a pin), else by what the line says inside it (`ILinePieces`),
else by its widget; a line the keys stop at whole is one button. The stop the keys are on is the focused element and
UI Automation is told as they move (`Uia.FocusMoved`), so Narrator follows a folder's keys as it follows the bar's and
a menu's. Pressed by a screen reader a stop is Enter on it, posted as the keys' own press; focused, the keys go there.

**The sweep sees every line with something in it.** Its folders (`LineClickTests.Folder`) give the lines that read a
store as they are made one of made-up items — an inbox, a few people, a clipboard whose history Windows keeps off so
Karpo keeps its own (three texts, one pinned: Clear all, Turn on, every row's Pin and Delete), a day of meetings with
their Joins for the calendar, the events, the meeting and the day and week views, a week of earthquakes, a fortnight
of screen time, and the markets line as a converter at a saved rate — and the calendar app is stood in
(`CalendarApp.Stand`), so an event opens somewhere on any PC. What it found: the screen time's total line missed a
piece of a bar too thin for the scan, and the ring round the screen time's ring stood over another piece. Both lines
lay their targets out as one list now (`ILineTargets`): the total's steps, the day's name, every top app's piece down
to the gap under it and the day's column (its stop the part above its pieces); the ring's pieces at their legend rows,
or on the piece itself where the legend has none. A line that walks its own keys is walked from its own stop each way
(Down, Right, Up, Left, the folder opened afresh for each), and at every press one ring shows, its own or the folder's.

**The allowlist is empty** (`KeyboardSweepAllowed.cs`): every target of every kind is reached by the keys.

Tests: `KeyboardSweepTests.EveryTargetOfEveryLineIsReachedByTheKeys` (now with the one-ring check),
`OneRingShowsAtATime`, `NarratorFollowsTheFolderKeys`; `ClipboardPresetTests.TheKeysChooseARowWhenLetGoAndPressItsButtons`;
`SoundSliderKeysTests.TheSoundSlidersStepByTheKeys`; `EditResizeTests` (the keymap; a line's height a cell as its
stepper; the limits and Fill; a fixed kind stays fixed; a sized line's sizes; no width for a line; a bar widget's
widths; what is said; `ShiftDownInTheArrangedFolderMakesTheLineACellTaller` through the folder's keys), `EditKeysTests`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `keys-flyout-…` (one ring now), `keys-own-ring-…`, `keys-month-arrow-…`, `keys-join-…`,
`keys-clipboard-pin-…` (`KeyRingPictures`), `keys-sound-slider-dark-100.png`, `edit-resize-keys-before.png` and
`-after.png`.

## 472. Layout presets: "Add a layout" offers Windows, Karpo, Focus, Planner and Monitor; Windows' opens Windows' own (2026-11-01)

The person: *"for karpo when creating a new layout at the moment we only have one default one that we create. i want you
to make some more presets that can be selected on creation. one should be one that mimics windows as close as possible,
with the same widgets and also the windows native menus behind them, and then there should also be the one that we
currently have and maybe a few others that are high quality layouts that can be selected. those just give the initial
state and nothing more."*

**The menu.** Display ▾'s foot, **Add a layout**, opens a level of the layout presets (`BarLooks.Layouts`, a choice row
with `OptionRow.Adds`: none ticked, nothing said at its end): each its name, its icon and, under it, what it is for
(`OptionRow.ChoiceDetails`, the choice's `FlyoutItem.Detail`). A pick makes the layout, shows it on this display and goes
back to the list, the new layout's row lit (R5; `Dock.LooksPicked` → `MenuAgain(litThing)`, `OptionMenu.ThingRowOf`).
Past what the licence holds the row is greyed, saying why (a choice row now greys as an action did). The layouts line's
"Add" in a folder, which offers no presets, makes Karpo's as "New layout", as before (§485: it opens this level now).

**A preset is only where a layout starts** (`Karpo.Core\LayoutPresets.cs`): a record — its name and line
(`core.layoutPreset.<id>.title|blurb`), icon, type, sizes, the style it wears, and what stands where, the ready-made
folders made as the add list makes them (`Presets.Folder`) — and one act, `LayoutPresets.Make`. The layout made is
ordinary: named after the preset ("Windows", "Windows 2" where taken; `BarLooks.PresetName`, `settings.layouts.numbered`),
wearing its icon; nothing in the file names the preset, nothing links back. What this PC has (`LayoutMachine`: Windows'
taskbar pins, pen and touch, the battery) decides what Windows would show.

| Preset | Type, style | On the bar | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Windows** | Taskbar 48, Follow Windows | *§485: no Widgets button at the start (the person: "no").* Middle: Start, the search box, Task view, the pins, the open apps. End: the "^" and its icons, pen and touch where Windows shows them, the status icons, quick settings' button (the network, the sound, the battery), the clock (the time over the date beside the bell), show desktop. The three are Windows' own widgets, no folder of Karpo's (§474). No separators, no input indicator (Windows shows it only with two layouts). | Windows 11 as it comes, its menus Windows' own |
| **Karpo** | Taskbar 48, Follow Windows | Exactly a new layout's until now (`Sections.DefaultLayout`): Windows' buttons at the left, the tray, the status icons, the keyboard, quick settings and the clock (Karpo's folders) at the right. | Today's default |
| **Focus** | Dock, Graphite | Start dock: a focus session (its minutes on its face). Middle: Start, the pins, the open apps. End: the tray, quick settings, the clock and calendar. | Nothing but what is in use; calm |
| **Planner** | Taskbar 48, Paper | Start: Start, search, the pins, the apps. Middle: the next meeting, the inbox (the mail beside the notifications), the to-do list beside a note, a focus session. End: the tray, the status icons, quick settings, Today (the time over the date and the weather: the day's events and the forecast), show desktop. | The day at a glance; the mail says "No mail account · Set up" and the calendar "no calendar to show" with none |
| **Monitor** | Top + bottom, top bar 32, Harbor | Top: the desktops at the left; the processor, graphics, memory, disk and network, each its figure, at the right. Bottom: Start, search, Task view, the pins, the apps; the clipboard, the tray, the status icons, quick settings, the clock, show desktop. | How the PC is doing, always in sight |

**A new config's first layout stays Karpo's** (`Config.FirstLayout` is `LayoutPresets.Make(Karpo)` under the default's
id and name): the person chose it (2026-10-14) and nothing here asks to change it.

~~**A folder may open Windows' own**~~ *Removed by §474* (the person, 2026-11-02: "it should not be implemented in the
folder"): §472 gave a folder an option, `FolderOptions.Opens` (the file's `"opens"`), by which its face opened the menu of
Windows' its first face stood for — the network's quick settings, the clock's notifications, the weather's Widgets board —
and the Windows preset's three folders were set to it. There is no such option now: a folder of Karpo's opens itself, and
Windows' menus are Windows' own widgets, which wear Windows' faces (§474).

**What the Windows preset opens:** Start, Search and Task view are Windows' own buttons (§26, §28); quick settings'
button and the clock are Windows' own widgets (§474), opening quick settings and the notifications (§485: no Widgets
button); show desktop does what Windows' sliver does. Two stay Karpo's, honestly: **the
"^" overflow** — Explorer's own overflow lives in its taskbar, which is hidden while Karpo runs (§465), and nothing opens it
without it; Karpo's tray is the one the icons talk to (§34) — and **the input indicator**, left off: Windows' input
switcher has no call to open it without switching the layout (Win+Space switches), and Windows shows the indicator only
with two keyboard layouts.

**The second click** (an open question here until §473): a second click on the clock closes the notifications, as §466's
button does — see §473, §474.

**The file** (shape 44, `ConfigWords.txt` written again): `islands[..].folder.opens`. §473 changed its words (shape 45);
§474 took it out of the file (shape 46).

Strings, 30 languages: `core.layoutPreset.{windows,karpo,focus,planner,monitor}.{title,blurb}`, `settings.layouts.numbered`
(`core.folder.opens.{title,folder,windows}` went with the option, §474).

Tests: `LayoutPresetsTests` — `EachIsAValidLayout` (repair changes nothing, the file reads back as written, every kind
known, every folder's lines a folder holds at heights their kinds allow, ids unique, the battery only with one; a
laptop and a desktop), `EachHasItsNameItsLineAndAnIconOfItsOwn`, `APickAddsOneLayoutOfThePresetAndNothingLinksBack`
(one layout, its type, sizes, style, icon, widgets, shown; the other layout untouched; no key about a preset; "Windows
2"), `PastTheLicenceAddIsGreyedAndMakesNothing`, `KarposIsTodaysDefaultAndANewConfigsFirst`,
`WindowsIsWindows11sTaskbar`, `WindowsOpensWindowsOwnSurfaces` (§474: Windows' own widgets, their shortcuts never
pressed), `AddALayoutListsThePresetsAndGoesBackToTheNewRowLit` (KARPO_UI_TESTS);
`BarLooksTests`, `LayoutsPresetTests` (Add a choice of presets), `ConfigSchemaTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`, `SceneTreeTests.LayoutPresetSheets`):
`layout-preset-<id>-<light|dark>.png` at 150 %, each preset's bars over a wallpaper and, but for Windows', its clock's
folder open (the Planner's inbox), the time, weather, battery and notifications stand-ins; `layout-presets-add-dark-150.png`,
the Add level. The Monitor's reading faces say "–" there: a folder's face reads its line's source, which no picture feeds.

## 473. One way to open Windows' menus: a folder's face that opens one is §466's button for it (2026-11-01)

*Corrected by §474:* the person rejected the folder option this section kept (2026-11-02: "it should not be implemented in
the folder, these widgets should be their own widgets"). `FolderOptions.Opens`, `FolderOpens`, `FolderOpenings`, the
folder's **Opens** row and the folder-face path into §466's buttons (`FolderOptions.OpensWindows`, the folder arm of
`Dock.WindowsButtonAt`, `Dock.FolderClicked`, `FolderIsland.ClickDoes`' exception) are gone; the Windows preset's three
are Windows' own widgets wearing Windows' faces. What stays of this section is what it did for §466's buttons: the one
toggle (`WindowsMenus`), the second click that closes, the keyboard-opened panel on its one button's page, and the Widgets
board as a panel. Below, read "a folder's face that opens Windows' own" as "Windows' own widget" (§474).

Two pieces of work had landed side by side: §466's buttons for Windows' menus, which open each by its shortcut, close it on a
second click and give way to Karpo's flyouts (one thing open at a time), and §472's folder option `Opens`, which sent its
own shortcuts from a table of its own (Win+A, Win+N, Win+W) and none of the rest — so the Windows preset's clock sent Win+N
again on a second click, and a Karpo flyout did not close the Widgets board it opened. The person's rule is one mechanism,
no duplicates. §472 wanted *"the same widgets and also the windows native menus behind them"*: the same widgets are the
folders (the clock shows the time, the network button its icons), which §466's glyph buttons are not, so the option stays
and the folder face **becomes the button**.

**One table.** `FolderOpenings.WindowsOf(face)` names §466's entry a face stands for — the network, the sound, the battery
and Bluetooth `windowsQuickSettings`; the time, the date, the calendar and the bell `windowsNotifications`; the weather
`widgetsBoard` — and `FolderOptions.OpensWindows()` is that entry where the folder is set to open Windows' own (null
otherwise, and for a face that stands for nothing of Windows'). From there everything is §466's: what is pressed is
`WindowsButtons.Target(kind)`, which panel answers and how it closes is `WindowsPanels.PanelOf(kind)`, and the toggle is
`WindowsMenus`. The dock reads the button a hit is in one place (`Dock.WindowsButtonAt`: one of Windows' buttons, or a
folder's face at rest that opens Windows' own), for the press and for the click; `Dock.FolderClicked` hands such a face to
`OpenWindowsButton`, the very path of the bar's buttons. Hover still never opens Windows' own; arranged, the folder opens
to be arranged. An empty folder that opens Windows' own still shows its press (`FolderIsland.ClickDoes`).

**Deleted:** `WindowsButtons.Target(FolderOpens)`, `QuickSettingsKey`, `NotificationCenterKey` (§472's second table of
shortcuts); the press in `Dock.FolderClicked` that sent them without the toggle; `FolderOpens.QuickSettings`,
`NotificationCenter`, `WidgetsBoard` (a second list of Windows' surfaces) and their three strings in 30 languages
(`core.folder.opens.{quickSettings,notificationCenter,widgetsBoard}`); `FolderOpenings.Said`. The dock's own
`menuToggles`, `menuOpenedBy` and `ToggledMenu` moved into `WindowsMenus` (`WindowsPanels.cs`), which a test drives with a
stand-in for the panels.

**The second click** (§472's open question): it closes. The clock is `windowsNotifications`' button, so its press reads
the notifications as Start's button reads Start (`SearchToggle`, `PanelWatch`): open at the press and still open, the click
closes them by Escape and Win+N is not sent again; sent away by the press itself, the click does nothing, so nothing
reopens. The same for the network's quick settings and the weather's Widgets board. A face and the bar's button for the
same menu are one toggle (quick settings opened by the network face closes on the Quick settings button; the Sound button
goes to its page over it, `WindowsPanels.ForPage`). One fix on the way: a panel Karpo did not open (its shortcut pressed on
the keyboard) is now on its one button's page where it has one button (`WindowsMenus.OneButton`: all but quick settings),
so a press that sent it away is no longer followed by its shortcut, which reopened it; quick settings opened from the
keyboard still lets the Sound button go to its page.

**The Widgets board joins §466's panels** (`WindowsPanel.WidgetsBoard`): WidgetBoard.exe's `WindowsDashboard` window
(MicrosoftWindows.Client.WebExperience; seen on 26300 with the board closed: hidden, `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW | WS_EX_TOPMOST`, no
`WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`, so it may take the foreground). It is read from the foreground window by process and class as the
others are, closed by Escape, and a Karpo flyout closes it. The board was not opened to check this: where it does not take
the foreground it reads as closed, and its button and the weather face send Win+W as before, which Windows toggles itself.
The `widgetsBoard` button on the bar toggles the same way now.

**The file** (shape 45, `ConfigWords.txt` written again): `islands[..].folder.opens` is `"windows"`; `"folder"`, the
default, is not written; the three shape-44 words leave the file (a word this build does not know reads as the folder).
The person's config never held `"opens"`.

**The menu:** a folder's **Opens** offers "This folder" and "Windows' own", the latter with its button's name under it
("Quick settings", "Notifications", "Widgets"; `FolderOpenings.Detail`).

Tests: `LayoutPresetsTests` — `EveryFaceForAWindowsMenuIsThatMenusButton` (exactly Windows' taskbar's nine faces, each a

## 474. Windows' own widgets wear Windows' faces; a folder of Karpo's opens itself (2026-11-02)

The person, on §472/§473's folder option: *"it should not be implemented in the folder, these widgets should be their own
widgets and the face and the contents (obviously) cannot be edited. only if they use ours, but ours is just a folder face
with widgets as presets inside."* So there are two kinds of thing, never one folder with a switch:

- **Windows' own**: a taskbar entry of its own (§466) that looks like Windows' button and opens Windows' menu. Its face is
  Windows' and fixed, and there is nothing inside it: nothing to set, no contents.
- **Karpo's own**: a folder — a face with widgets inside, the ready-made ones presets (Presets.cs) — every bit editable.

**Removed** (§472's option and §473's path into it): `FolderOptions.Opens` and `OpensWindows()`, `FolderOpens`,
`FolderOpenings`, the folder's **Opens** row (`OptionRows.FolderOpensRow`) and its strings in 30 languages
(`core.folder.opens.{title,folder,windows}`), the folder arm of `Dock.WindowsButtonAt`, `Dock.FolderClicked` (a folder's
click is `ShowFolder` again), `FolderIsland.ClickDoes`' exception and the hover check on `OpensWindows`. The file's
`"opens"` and `"windows"` are gone: shape 46, `ConfigWords.txt` written again. No migration: the person's config never held
`"opens"` (read, 2026-11-02), and an older file's is not kept (a property this build does not know).

**Three of §466's entries wear Windows' faces** (`Karpo.Core\WindowsFaces.cs`), one entry per menu — the glyph-only
variants are gone, since Windows' taskbar has none of them: its Widgets button is the weather, quick settings' button its
three icons, its clock the time and the bell.

| Entry | Face (fixed, `WindowsFaces.Of`) | Opens (§466) | Wheel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widgetsBoard` | the weather: its glyph, the temperature over the conditions (`WeatherFace.Conditions`), where this PC is | the Widgets board, Win+W | — |
| `windowsQuickSettings` | the network (Wi-Fi's bars, Ethernet), the volume, and the battery (its charge, charging) on a PC with one | quick settings, Win+A | the volume, as Windows' |
| `windowsNotifications` | the time over the date in Windows' own formats, the bell beside it (its count, do not disturb's "zZ") | the notifications and calendar, Win+N | — |

Their faces are Karpo's own (`FolderFaces`), drawn by the code that draws a folder's (`FaceDrawings`, `FolderIsland`) from
the same readings — `SystemStatus` for the network and the volume, the battery probe, the weather store, the notification
store and do not disturb, the clock — so nothing is drawn twice. In the registry: `BarEntry.Drawing` is
`WidgetSource.WindowsFaces` (`BarEntries.WindowsFace`), the shape a folder's button's (`WidgetShapes`: exactly its faces),
the island a `FolderIsland` whose faces are fixed (`FolderIsland.FacesOf`) and which is no folder (`FolderIsland.IsFolder`,
false): it holds nothing, its `Click` asks for nothing of Karpo's, it always does something (`ClickDoes`), and
`ShowFolder` never opens one, arranged or not. `BarEntries.IsWindowsButton` (the scene's glyph buttons) leaves the three
out; `BarEntries.IsWindowsOwn` is every entry whose click opens Windows' own, faces included (`WindowsButtons.Target`).

**Behaviour, §466's unchanged.** The dock reads Windows' button a hit is in one place (`Dock.WindowsButtonOf`: a glyph
button's, or a widget wearing Windows' face; a folder of Karpo's never), for the press (`WindowsMenus.Pressed`) and the
click (`Dock.Click` → `OpenWindowsButton`): one at a time, a second click closes by Escape, a press that sent the menu away
leaves it closed, a Karpo flyout closes it. Hover never opens one (`OpenHoverFlyout` asks the same first; `OpensOnHover`
only for a real folder). In edit mode each is arranged as any entry (a click selects it and opens its menu); on the
keyboard each is a stop, Enter its click (§470); a screen reader hears Windows' button's name, then what its faces say
("Quick settings", "Wi-Fi, Home, Internet access", …; `FolderIsland.Tooltip`), the status icons' tooltips over each face
as on Windows' (`StatusTipAt`).

**Lit while open**, as Windows lights its own button: the hook that notes when a panel goes now also follows which is in
front (`PanelWatch.Front`, `WindowsPanels.FrontChanged`), and the dock lights that menu's button on the bar of the display
the menu is on (`Dock.FacesShowOpen`, the open folder's plate, §376) — the button that opened it, else the one wearing
Windows' face for it, else its first (`WindowsMenus.Lit`). The glyph buttons light too (the Sound button over quick
settings it opened). A Karpo folder open and a Windows menu in front are never both: one thing open at a time. The Widgets
board lights only where it takes the foreground (§473: not checked by opening it).

**Their menus.** At rest: their faces' rows, Windows' own icons' (the network's troubleshooter and page, the volume's mixer
and settings, the battery's power mode, the clock's date and time, the bell's), worked on the widget (`Dock.BarMenuRows`);
the weather's has none without a forecast, and then the entry's page, Windows' taskbar settings. A row several faces offer
stands once, and now its act too (`FaceRows` drops the act of a row it leaves out). In edit mode: what any entry has —
cut, copy, remove, its place —; no face, no option, no contents (the item has no folder's options).

**The Windows preset** (`LayoutPresets.Windows`): quick settings' button and the clock at the right are two of these
entries (§485: the Widgets button at the left went); no folder of Karpo's stands for a Windows menu, and the other presets (Karpo, Focus,
Planner, Monitor) keep Karpo's folders.

**The add list**: the three stay in §466's *Windows menus* group (Start and taskbar › Windows menus; the catalogue's
group), as they were; their rows show their glyph and words as every row does, and their faces on the bar.

Tests: `LayoutPresetsTests` — `WindowsIsWindows11sTaskbar` (no folder in it), `WindowsOpensWindowsOwnSurfaces` (the three
are Windows' own, their targets and panels; no other preset has one), `WindowsOwnWidgetsWearWindowsFaces` (the faces,

`AClickOnWindowsFaceIsWindowsButtonAndOnAFolderNever`, `ItsMenuIsItsFacesRowsAndNothingToEdit`,
`EachDrawsWindowsFacesFromTheReadings` (stand-ins: the faces' readings, its name, no folder; KARPO_UI_TESTS);
`WindowsSearchTests` — `AWindowsFacesSecondClickClosesTheMenuItOpened` (the clock, quick settings' button, the Widgets

`windows-widgets-corner-*.png`, `windows-widgets-lit-<dark|light>-150.png` (quick settings' button lit).

By hand: in the Windows layout, the clock shows the time over the date and the bell; click it: the notifications open and

The person: *"the camera widget should not show the lighter background behind the fit all image, it should show

as a player's bars) under the picture's room, so the bars beside or over and under the picture were lighter than the
