## 476. The bar's cut let go of without a crash (2026-11-02)

Karpo ended twice with an access violation in dcomp.dll (+0x40182, a read of 0x30; 2026-11-01 12:06 after 15 h,
11-02 10:33 after 11 h; the guard started it again). The dump: *OptionPicked > Apply > Arrange > Rebuild > DockWindow.Lay >
Scene.Update > DressCards > Cut > CompositionPathGeometry.Path*. §464's cut (the bar's background less its cards) set its
geometry's Path to null whenever a bar went from cards to none — a setting picked in a menu rebuilding the bars without a
card — and **a CompositionPathGeometry whose Path is set to null after it had one crashes the process** (every time: a
loop setting a path, then null, died on the first null).

Now the Path is never set to null (Scene.Cut): with no card the geometry keeps its last path, unused, and no clip holds
it (`cutting`); the bar is drawn whole. Test: `SceneTreeTests.ABarThatLosesItsCardsIsDrawnWholeAndLives` (an Islands bar
of see-through cards made Floating and back three times through Scene.Update; red first: the test host died in set_Path).
*(Since §512 a floating bar wears its cards too: the test takes them away by the look, the widgets' background unset,
and back.)*

## 477. A face's source: Inherited from its folder's line, or its own (2026-11-02)

The person: *"for the news face i should be able to set the source, as default it should be set to inherited which means
it takes the source from the first folder widget, but you should also be able to configure it yourself without any folder
widget present. same goes for similar widgets that inherit positions or data from the folder widgets."*

**Which faces** (`FaceSources.LineOf`, read off the registry `FolderFaces.All`; `TheFacesThatReadALineEachHaveASource`
holds the list to it):

| Face | What it takes | From which line |
|---|---|---|
| News | the feed (`RssOptions`) | the folder's first feed line (`FolderIsland.Feed`) |
| Drive | the drive (`DriveTargetOptions`) | the folder's first drive line (`FolderIsland.DriveLineOf`) |
| Network drive | the share | the folder's first network drive line |
| Sports | the team or league (`SportsOptions`) | the folder's sports lines, all of them (§369, `FolderIsland.SportsAll`) |

The faces with a place or a market — the weather, the air quality, the tides, the earthquakes, the sun and markets — keep
their own since §80, §210, §236, §240, §368 and §246, never a line's, so they already work with no line and have nothing to
inherit. Left out on purpose: the timer, focus and stopwatch faces read the running countdown of their folder's line (its
state, started and paused on the line); a source of their own would be a timer of their own, not a source. Now playing reads
Windows' one session (a widget of its own already where the folder has no player line); the mail, the meeting and the bell
read the accounts and Windows, never a line.

**One mechanism** (`Karpo.Core\FaceSources.cs`). A face that takes a line's source is **Inherited** unless set: it shows its
line's, exactly as before. Or it has one of its own, kept on the face in the very record the line keeps it in — the face's
`"rss"`, `"drive"` or `"sports"`, as a feed, a drive or a sports line writes it — and then it shows that with no such line in
the folder at all; a line that comes later does not change it. `FaceSources.Line(folder, face)` is what it shows: its own
(`Own`: a line of the face's kind holding the face's record, id `face-<kind>`), else the folder's first line of the kind
(`Inherited`). The dock reads an own source through that line, made, attached, refreshed and let go as a line of the folder
is (`FolderIsland.Configure`'s `Placed`, keyed `<folder>/face-news`; not among the folder's lines): `Feed` and
`DriveLineOf` are its island, so the face's drawing, its tooltip, its tick and its menu (Refresh, the site) are the line's
as before. Sports needs no island: `SportsAll` is the face's own team where it has one, which the store follows as it
follows the lines'.

**The row** (`FaceRowKind.Source`, `FaceSources.Row`, key `source`): the line's own picker, no second one — the feed line's
address search (`OptionFields.OfFeed`, which `OfRssAddress` now calls), the drive line's choice of drives
(`OptionRows.DriveRow`, taking the record and where to keep it), the sports line's team search (`OfSportsTeam`) — writing the
face's record, with **Inherited** its first choice (`Inheriting`): a choice's first, ticked while in force; a search's first
row whatever is typed (`InheritingFinder`, nothing to prove), ticked while in force, and the row says it greyed at its end.
It says what it takes: "Inherited (BBC News)", "Inherited (Local Disk (C:))", "Inherited (Barcelona)"; "Inherited" where
the folder holds no such line (`core.face.source.inherited`, `core.face.source.inheritedFrom`, 30 languages; the glossary's
word, §411 R7). Picking Inherited drops the face's own record. The row is the face's first (its subject, §292), among the
face's own settings — the folder's bar configuration menu's face rows; a drive face's lists the drives attached (the dock
lists them for a folder wearing one, `Dock.MenuSources`), and Inherited and its own drive alone where they are not listed.

**The file** (shape 47, `ConfigWords.txt` written again): a face's `rss`, `drive`, `sports`, each the line's record. Absent
is Inherited, and nothing is written for it; a record on a face that takes no such source, or one that is no source (an
address that is none, a team no league of the table has), is read as Inherited and leaves the file. No migration: every face
of a file from before is Inherited, which is what it showed. The person's config: one news face (folder `f4a438be`) whose
folder holds no feed line, so it showed its glyph and a dash; it stays Inherited until a feed is picked for it. No drive,
network drive or sports face.

Tests: `FaceSourceTests` — `TheFacesThatReadALineEachHaveASource`, `ANewsFaceInheritsItsFoldersFirstFeed`,
`ANewsFacesOwnFeedNeedsNoLineAndInheritedFollowsTheLineAgain`, `ADriveFacesSourceIsTheDriveLinesChoiceWithInheritedFirst`,
`ASportsFaceFollowsItsOwnTeamOrItsLines`, `AnOwnSourceIsWrittenAsTheLineKeepsItAndInheritedIsNothing`; `FaceSourceBarTests`
— a news face's own feed read and drawn with no line (RssSamples' store) and following the line again once Inherited, a
drive face's own drive's line, a sports face's own team shown from a stand-in answer. Nothing is fetched.

## 478. A style's separators: the bar's in its Taskbar, a folder's dividers in its Widgets in folders (2026-11-02) — a separator is empty space, with no look, since §505 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"taskbar and folder separator configuration should go into the style as well and also respected as such."*

**Replaces** §459's *"separators back in Layout"* — Layout ▾'s **Taskbar separators** and **Folder separators**, Karpo's,
every layout alike (`appearance.taskbarSeparators|folderSeparators`) — and with them what §464 left Karpo-wide of a look.

**In a style.** What a separator draws — **Line**, **Space only** or **None** (§405: the room each keeps the style system's,
the line's width Automatic; its colour the part's text at Windows' step, `ToneRules.SeparatorOf`, as before: a separator has
no colour of its own to set) — is now a setting of every style, one for each kind, held by the part it stands among:

| Setting | Part | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Taskbar separators** — every separator on the bar | Taskbar (the bar it stands on) | Line (§246) |
| **Folder separators** — every divider in a folder's lists | Widgets in folders (a divider is a line of the list, §307) | Space only (§78) |

Each is the same in both modes (a shape, not a colour), so it is said once per style, not once per mode
(`ItemStyle.TaskbarSeparators|FolderSeparators`, `Styled.TaskbarSeparators|FolderSeparators`, `Styled.SeparatorsOf(surface)`;
`StyleParts.SeparatorsOf(part)` which part holds which). Ours — Follow Windows, Graphite, Paper, Harbor, Bloom — draw what Karpo
always drew, a line on the bar and room in a folder: none of them clearly wants otherwise (their looks are colour and type),
and a change of default here would change every person's bar. A style of the person's is the same while it says nothing.
Like every style setting: ours overridden in the person's entry under our id, **Default (Line)** again or **Reset all** taking
the override out (`Styles.WriteSeparators`, `SeparatorsOverrideOf`, `DefaultSeparatorsOf`, `ResetAll`); a **Duplicate** says
what it draws; a word this build does not know is the Default.

**Respected as such** — the drawing rule (§464: each layout wears a style, no inheritance, nothing worn through a folder):

- A **bar** draws the Taskbar separators of the style its **layout** wears (`Layout`: `SeparatorStyles.Of(appearance,
  config.BarLayout, Taskbar)`). Two layouts in two styles draw two looks; a floating dock still draws no line (its separators
  split it, as before).
- A **folder's dividers** draw the Folder separators of the style its **layout** wears (`FolderIsland.Configure`:
  `config.LayoutOf(owner)`), every folder of a layout alike, a folder in a folder too. Not the folder's **Face style** (its
  button's) nor its **Flyout style** (its outline alone, §464), and no line's own style: a divider wears no style (it has no
  Appearance, `WidgetLooks.Has`), and the dividers are the folder's lists themselves, which §464 dresses in the layout's
  style. A divider's own **Style** says what it inherits from there: "Inherited (Line)" on a layout in a style whose Folder
  separators are a line (`OptionPickers.DividerStyleRow`, the menu's layout); Grow stays its own (§435).

**Menus.** ⚙ › Styles › a style › **Taskbar** ends, ruled off from its colours (and its dark colours), in **Taskbar
separators**; › **Widgets in folders** in **Folder separators** (`BarLooks.PartRows`, `SeparatorsRow`, key
`StyleSeparators.<part>:<id>`): Default with what it is ("Default (Space only)"), Line, Space only, None, what is in force
said at the row's end; its choices are the level under it, within §467's exemption (⚙ › Styles › a style › a part › its
choices, as a colour's picker). The other three parts hold no separators. **Layout ▾** is Type, Size, Show; ruled off, its
**Style**; ruled off, Behavior — the two rows gone (R15: every setting one home; §467: the style's settings are in its editor
alone, which nothing links to). A separator's and a divider's menu keep their way to **Layout ▾** (Layout ↗, R16's foot):
it lands where their layout's Style is picked, which is what draws them.

**The file** (shape raised to 48 on `land-all`, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no migration code):

```
appearance.taskbarSeparators, .folderSeparators   gone (not read)
appearance.styles[].taskbarSeparators             new: "line" | "space" | "none", Default left out
appearance.styles[].folderSeparators              new: likewise
```

**Converted once** by `karpo-coord\convert-separators.py in.json out.json [shape]`: each of the two old keys that says other
than Karpo's default goes to the entry of every style a layout wears (`layouts[].style`; Follow Windows, itself one of ours,
where a layout names none or one that is not there) — an override under our id for ours, the setting itself on a style of
the person's, a style that already says its own keeping it —, so every bar and folder looks as before; the keys leave
`appearance` (an empty one leaves the file); `version` to the shape. The person's config (a copy, shape 45): neither key set
(every bar a line, every folder room alone, both layouts — Default and Hello — Follow Windows), so nothing moves; the file is
unchanged but its version, and reads with no repair.

Strings: none new, none gone (the rows keep `settings.appearance.taskbarSeparators.header` and
`settings.appearance.folderSeparators.header`, now in a style's editor).

Tests: `StyleSeparatorsTests` (ours and a style of the person's draw a line on the bar and room in a folder; overridden one by
one, Default again, Reset all, a copy, the file and an unknown word; `EachLayoutDrawsTheSeparatorsOfTheStyleItWears` — Work
in Paper with Space only and a line, Home in Harbor, each layout's bar laid out with its own, the old Karpo-wide keys read as
nothing); `StyleMenuTests.APartHoldsItsSeparators` (the two rows last in their parts, ruled off, none in the others, picked,
Default, Reset all, reached in ⚙ › Styles, neither in Layout ▾ nor the right click), `AnEditorIsTheSameForEveryStyle`,
`APartsPatternIsAChoiceOfSwatches`; `StyleTests.ARowsDefaultIsTheStylesOwn`; `DividerStyleRowTests.ItInheritsItsLayoutsStyle`;
`LineRowsTests` (each kind's row apart, in a style); `AppearanceTests`, `BarLooksTests`, `LayoutMenuTests` (Layout ▾ without
the two rows), `ConfigSchemaTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (the allowance empty). Live (`KARPO_UI_TESTS=1`):
`SceneTreeTests.EachLayoutsBarDrawsItsStylesSeparators` and `FolderSeparatorTests.EachLayoutsFoldersDrawItsStylesDividers`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `style-separators-<work|home>-<dark|light>.png` (Work in Paper: room alone; Home in Harbor: lines),
`style-separators-folders-<dark|light>.png` (one folder on each: a line, room alone, each in its layout's style),
`menurules-style-taskbar.png`, `menurules-style-taskbar-separators.png`, `menurules-style-folder-separators.png`.

By hand: ⚙ › Styles › Paper › Taskbar › Taskbar separators › Space only: every bar of a layout wearing Paper draws room
between its groups, a layout in another style its lines still. Widgets in folders › Folder separators › Line: every folder on
those bars draws a line across its lists; its Flyout style changed: the dividers stay. Reset all: back. Layout ▾: no
separators.

## 479. Sports read whole: every state, every column, every group and round, in views of their own (2026-11-02)

The person: *"make sure the sports scores widget shows all the data fully and understandable. for example for the fifa
world cup or for the uefa games or for the super league or for other games. make sure that the data is easy to
understand and properly displayed. that if there are more settings / views or not all of the data is showable on one
screen that you can configure this as well. only if needed of course."*

**The audit** (`%TEMP%\karpo-coord\sports\sports-audit.md` at the time), on ESPN's real answers saved on 2026-11-02 for
the World Cup (its knockout months, a group day, the final, its twelve groups), the Champions League (the round of
16's two legs, its final, the matchday now, the 36 of its league phase), the Premier League, the Swiss Super League,
Sporting CP's schedule and the NHL's and NBA's tables (Karpo.Tests\Sports\Saved, cut to the fields read):
- *Who went through was not said.* "Germany 1–1 Paraguay Final" after a shoot-out; "Sporting 5–0 Bodo/Glimt Final" with
  no aggregate, no extra time, no leg; the round ("Round of 32", "Group F") nowhere.
- *Cut off with no way to see it.* The line never scrolled (§461): the round, the coming matches (two over a table), a
  team's table (seven rows), a league's table (what fitted), and every group but the first (the World Cup's B to L)
  could not be reached. No tooltip anywhere, so a name cut or swapped for its abbreviation could not be read whole.
- *A table of one figure.* Rank, team and points; the NHL's figure ESPN's "12-2-2, 26 PTS" as written; no played, goal
  difference, wins, draws, losses or games behind, no zones.
- *Dates without years.* The Swiss Super League's round of September 2025 read "28 Sept", as if this season's.
- *The Swiss Super League is not on ESPN this season.* Its scoreboard, standings and team schedules stop in September
  2025 (ESPN's core API has no 2026 season); every other league of the table is current. No other free, keyless source
  covers it in full (TheSportsDB's free key gives one next match and five table rows; SofaScore refuses). Left as an open
  question for the person; the line says what it has honestly (below).
- The score on the scoreboard was 24 DIP, off the kit's ramp; it is the Hero's 28.

**What a match says now** (`SportsText`, `SportsMatch`, `SportsSide`):
- *How it ended*: "Final", "AET" after extra time (`STATUS_FINAL_AET`), "Pens" after a shoot-out
  (`dock.sports.afterExtraTime`, `dock.sports.pens`), on the face, the one row, a result's row and the scoreboard; a
  shoot-out on now is "Pens" in its clock's place.
- *Its detail*, a caption under it (`SportsText.Detail`): its round where no heading says it ("Round of 16"), its leg
  ("1st leg", "2nd leg"), a shoot-out's outcome — "Paraguay win 4–3 on penalties", the winner's goals first; "Penalties
  3–2" while it is on — and a tie's — "Sporting advance 5–3 on aggregate" once decided, "Aggregate 3–3" while it is on —
  joined by dots. Read from ESPN's `shootoutScore`, the tie's `series` (`aggregateScore`, the winner of a completed one),
  a schedule's score (`aggregateScore`) and `advance`, `leg`, and the round from a scoreboard's note after the
  competition's name ("FIFA World Cup, Round of 32") or a schedule's stage that is not the season's own name.
- *Names* the fullest that fit (`ListTiers.Name`): "Paris Saint-Germain 1–1 Arsenal", "PSG 1–1 Arsenal", "PSG 1–1 ARS".
- *An old date* says its year ("28.09.2025", a day's heading "Sun, 28.09.2025"), so a season over never reads as this one.
- *A team's result in a cup* says its competition with its round ("Taça de Portugal · Semifinals · 1st leg"), and a
  result after extra time "AET" under it; the scoreboard of a last match played after extra time too.

**Views, only where there is more than one thing to show** (`SportsPage`, `SportsReading.Pages`): Matches always;
Table where ESPN keeps one; Knockout for a cup whose knockout has begun (the World Cup, the EURO, the Champions, Europa
and Conference Leagues, the Nations League, the Libertadores). The view is chosen in the line's settings' View (§484; it
was first a segmented control at the line's head, gone since), kept in its options (§483); one its competition does not
offer now shows Matches. No other setting was added: what is followed (a team or a league) was there, a second line
follows a second, and every match and result is listed, so no range is needed.

**Laid out once, whole, and scrolled** (`SportsTile.Layout`, `SportsLayout`, `SportsRow`; `IListScroll`): from two rows
the line lays out its view whole — the same at every height — and the shared ListScroll scrolls all of it; under two rows, or with nothing to show, the one row. Automatic (§371) is as tall as that content up to the
person's most. The pointer, the keys, the tooltips and the drawing read the one layout (the targets kept from the last
painting went, and with them `SportsPlan`). Rows are the kit's: a match 40 DIP, 60 with its caption; a table's place
the compact 32; a heading a caption with a gap over it.
- *Matches*, a team: the scoreboard (the competition and how it stands over the two sides about the score, its detail
  under the score; the side that lost or went out quiet), then while it is on the league's other matches, then every
  match to come and every result, each under its heading; "1st in …" at the foot where there is no table. A league:
  its round's days, each under its day's heading — with the round where the day's games share one ("Sat, 20.06. · Round
  of 32"), else on each game ("Group F") —, a game a row; "No matches coming up" under a round that is the last there is.
- *Table*: every group, its name over its columns' letters, a place a row: its zone's colour (ESPN's `note`: the
  Champions League's places, the play-offs, relegation) at the leading edge, the place, the logo, the fullest name that
  fits and the figures. Football P, GD, Pts, and W, D, L where the name keeps 120 DIP beside them; ice hockey the same
  without draws; America's W, L, GB; at the narrowest list and the largest text, the points alone (`SportsColumns`). A
  followed team's row strong, brought into sight when the table is shown.
- *Knockout*: every round in order under its name, its matches as a league's, each with its day and time to come.
- *Tooltips* (`SportsTips`, `SportsTile.CardTip`): a match — both sides' full names about the score, the competition and
  the round, how it ended or its clock or the word for one put off with its day and time in this PC's zone, its detail;
  a place — its rank and full name, its zone, every figure by its name ("Played 9 · Won 8 …"); a group's heading — what
  its letters stand for. The one row's tooltip is the reading's (§239).

**The knockout's data** (`SportsAnswers.Stages`, `KnockoutStages`, `KnockoutMonths`, `MonthUrl`, `SportsStore.Knockout`):
a cup's scoreboard lists its stages with their days ("Group", "Round of 32" … "Final"); the stages after its last group
or league phase are its knockout. ESPN refuses a range of days but answers a month whole (`?dates=202607`), so the
knockout is read a month at a time, from its first stage to its last's beginning or five weeks ahead, whichever is
sooner — nothing while the knockout is further off (the Champions League now). A month over and read before is kept in
the answer (`SportsAnswer.Knockout`, `KnockoutMonths`, in sports.json) and not asked again; a month that cannot be had
keeps what the last answer held of it. The World Cup now is two asks once, then none.

**The Swiss Super League** with ESPN's data as it is: a league whose last round is past says "No matches coming up" under
it, its date with its year; no table view where ESPN keeps none. A source of its own is the person's choice.

**The face** (`SportsFaceDrawing`): "ESP 1–0 ARG AET", "PAR 1–1 GER Pens", the year on an old date; its templates hold
those, so its width is still its widest reading's (§12.2). Its tooltip adds the detail ("Paraguay win 4–3 on
penalties"). What it reads is `SportsReading.From` on the folder's held answers, the one function a face's own source can
call.

Words in all 30 languages: `dock.sports.afterExtraTime`, `pens`, `penalties`, `wonOnPenalties`, `aggregate`,
`advanceOnAggregate`, `firstLeg`, `secondLeg`, `matches`, `knockout`, `column.played|won|drawn|lost|difference|points|behind`
and each one's `…Name`.

Tests: `SportsCompetitionTests` (a shoot-out's winner and score, live and decided; extra time and a plain final; the
World Cup's 32 knockout matches and six rounds; two legs, their aggregates and who advances, from a scoreboard and from a
schedule; a table's every column and zone, hockey's and basketball's; the stages, the knockout months, a month read once
and kept through a failure; each competition's views; an old date's year; a match's tooltip),
`SportsCompetitionPictures` (`EveryRowSaysItselfWholeAndTheColumnsFit`: every case and view at every list width, at 100 %
and 150 % and 225 % text — each lays out whole and scrolls, every match's and place's tooltip names it
whole, every name keeps room beside its columns; `EveryCompetitionInEveryView`:
sports-<worldcup-final|worldcup-shootouts|worldcup-groups|ucl-matchday|ucl-second-legs|premier-league|super-league|sporting|nba>-<matches|table|knockout>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png
at one, four and eight rows and whole), `SportsPictures` (the layout's rows, a game's click, the table shown, a place's
click), `SportsHeightTests` (the same layout at every height, scrolled where taller, whole cells), on
ESPN's answers saved on 2026-11-02 (Saved\wc-*.json, ucl-*.json, standings-*.json, eng-day, sui-now, sporting-2025).

By hand: follow the FIFA World Cup: Matches shows the final with "AET"; Knockout lists the round of 32 to the final,
"Paraguay win 4–3 on penalties" under Germany–Paraguay; Table shows all twelve groups. Follow the Champions League: the
matchday's games and the league phase's 36 with their zones. Follow Sporting: its results with "2nd leg · Sporting
advance 5–3 on aggregate". Hover a name cut short: its tooltip says it whole. Pick Table in the line's View (§484).

## 480. A folder shown again at once after its animation stands whole (2026-11-02)

The person: *"sometimes when i open a folder it does not open properly and might have a transparent background or is stuck
on a part of the animation."* A folder that went by its animation (Fly in, Unfold, Ripple: landed, or cut short) and was
shown again without one — a switch to another folder skips the animation — showed only its outlines, its background clear
(Fly in, 40 % of the folder off), or its sections a strip short (Unfold, Ripple, 10–12 %). Its lines stood where the close
had taken them, at the face: `Land` stops the parts' expressions (a stopped part keeps where the clock had it) and put the
lines back by the folder's plan alone, and `Closed` had dropped the plan as the close began.

Now every part bound to the clock keeps where it stood at rest as it was bound (`FolderFlyout.rests`), and `Land` puts it
back there, open or not; then where this showing has it. Tests: `FolderMotionFilmTests.AFolderShownAtOnceAfterItsAnimationStandsWhole`
(Fly in landed and cut short, Unfold landed, Ripple cut short, each then shown at once against the folder shown still; red
first, 40.37 %, 10.68 %, 11.58 %), and `TheStagedAnimationsFromEveryEdge` passes again (it failed every run: its still
picture was this folder).

## 481. A folder is edited like every other widget: its face's menu on a click, its panel's once it opens; the top row says its buttons' names (2026-11-02) — a click on its face selects it and opens it, no "Open", no double-click, since §527 (2026-11-07)

The person: *"when in edit mode and i left click a folder it currently opens it and shows the edit menu on the top, i want
to change this. it should not open the folder, it should open the configuration menu like it does for the other taskbar
widgets and then it should show only the faces and face appearance settings ... and an additional open button ... then
when i open the folder it should show the folder options with the menu on top like it does already. in general this
change is to make the editing more similar for all the widgets. additionally there should be the option to show the name
of the actions in the toprow, but this is a general change for the whole application. (default should be it shows
them)"*.

**A click on a folder's face** in edit mode is a click on any widget (`EditClicks.OnClick`, which replaces `OnBlock`,
`Acts` and `Act`): the folder is selected and its menu opens beside it (`Dock.BesideMenu`, §407), the same path as its
right click, Space, Enter, the menu key, Narrator's Invoke and Widget ▾; with Ctrl or Shift the selection grows and the
menu is for them all (§459, "Mixed" where they differ). §253 to §473 a click opened the folder and hung its whole menu from
Folder ▾ (§386).

**Two menus, one rule.** A folder's settings are split by what they draw (`Karpo.Core\Folders.cs`: `FolderSide`,
`FolderSides`): what is drawn on the bar — its faces (`FolderOptions.Faces`, each face's own rows) and the style its face
wears (`StyleId`, the `look` row) — is its **face's**; everything else — its own rows (`OptionRows.Of` for a folder: where
it stands as it opens) and its flyout's outline (`PanelStyleId`, the `flyoutLook` row) —
changes only the folder opened, and is its **panel's**. `OptionMenu.Settings` takes the side in place of its `faces`
switch; for any other widget the side changes nothing (one menu).

| The face's menu (a click, its right click, Widget ▾) | The panel's menu (Folder ▾, the folder open) |
|---|---|
| top row: Folder · **Open**, Cut, Copy, Remove | top row: Folder · Cut, Copy, Remove |
| each face, a grip, its own rows, a bin | Alignment (its four buttons) |
| Add a face | |
| foot: Face style | foot: Flyout style |

Every setting has one home (R15): `FolderMenuSidesTests.EveryFolderSettingHasOneHome` builds both menus of every
ready-made folder and of a folder wearing each face and holds that no setting is in both and that between them they are
all of the folder's. The corpus (`MenuCorpus`) has each ready-made folder's panel menu too ("folder … (opened)"), so the
menu rules hold over it (R2, R16: its Flyout style is its foot).

**Open** (`CMD_OPEN_FOLDER`, the words of a widget's "Open", Segoe's FolderOpen) is the first of the face's top-row
buttons, as Explorer's menus have Open first. Picked, the menu goes and then (`Later`) `Dock.OpenFolderEditing` selects
the folder, opens it arranged (`OpenArranged`) and opens its panel's menu from Folder ▾ (`CrumbSettings`, §386) — as a
click did until now. Its face closes it again (§252), any other click on the bar too (§366).

**The keys and a double-click.** Enter and Space on a folder are its click: the face's menu, "Open" a key away (Up onto
the top row, §214). A **double-click** on a folder's face opens it, as File Explorer opens a folder: its first click opens
the face's menu, its second opens the folder when it comes within Windows' double-click time of the click that opened
the menu (`Dock.ClickedAgain`). Its press closes that menu, which uses the press and its release up (`Dock.PressedOn`,
`LightDismiss.Consumes`): the folder opens from there, on the second press as Windows' own double-click is, once the
press is done with (`Later`); where the menu did not stand yet, from the release (`EditClicks.OnClick`). On every other widget a double-click
stays two clicks (§276: the menu opens and closes). The probes of the real dock open folders by double-clicks
(`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.DoubleClick`, `MenuToggleTests.DoubleClick`).

**Names in the top row.** Karpo's `topRowNames` (`Config.TopRowNames`, on; a file without it shows them; shape 49,
`ConfigWords.txt` written again) is set by **⚙ › Styles › Show names in the top row** (§485: ⚙ › General's now), a switch under a rule at the
Styles level's foot (`KarpoMenu.TopRowNames`): how Karpo looks as a whole, and ⚙'s first level holds no more rows
without scrolling (R2: twelve rows and three rules are 411 DIP of its 390). The dock hands it to every menu it shows
(`Flyout.ButtonNames`, set in `ShowFlyout` and again in `MenuAgain`). On, each button of a menu's top row says its name
under its icon, as WinUI's AppBarButton says its Label: the row 56 DIP tall (`PrimaryNamedDip`, 40 without), the 16 DIP
icon and the name in a caption's 12 DIP under it 4 DIP apart, the two in the button's middle; every button of the row
one width (`Flyout.NamedWidth`): the widest name and 10 DIP either side, never under the 40 DIP square, never so wide the
row's type ("Folder", "Clock") loses its own words' room (to two fifths of the menu) — a name longer than that is cut
with an ellipsis (German's "Ausschneiden" in a folder's row of four). The tooltip stays, with the shortcut. Off, the row
is icons alone as §214 had it. A row of a type alone (⚙, Layout ▾) stays 40 DIP. The menus keep their one height
(§288): with names the first level has 16 DIP less room, which R2 now counts per menu (`MenuRulesTests.RoomDip`: a menu
with buttons less the named row); no menu of the corpus scrolls.

Its words in 30 languages (`settings.appearance.topRowNames`); the buttons' names are Cut, Copy, Remove and Open's own.
`TransferSummary` names the key on an import.

Tests: `EditClickTests` (every kind's click is its menu; a double-click's second opens a folder alone; the dock's paths),
`FolderMenuSidesTests` (each menu's rows; one home; one menu for every other widget), `MenuSidesTests`,
`StyleMenuTests`, `TopRowNamesTests` (on unless off, written and read back; its one switch in ⚙ › Styles; `NamedWidth`;
the row drawn with and without names in English, German and Arabic at 100 to 150 %), `MenuRulesTests` (R2 per menu, the
panel menus in the corpus), `ConfigSchemaTests`.

## 482. A folder's growing divider grows its column to all the folder's room (2026-11-02)

The person: *"the spacer grow does also not work properly. it only grows to the highest widget in the folder and not all
the way to the top or bottom."*

**Where it was.** §435 gave a growing divider only the room its column had free beside the folder's tallest column
(rule 2), and none at all where there was none (rule 5: an only column, the tallest one). So a divider set to Grow in a
folder of one column did nothing, and in a shorter column stopped level with the tallest, never at the top of the screen.

**The root cause.** `FolderFlyout.Build` grew lists twice: those with a Fill line to the folder's room (`fillTo`, §173),
then those with a growing divider to a second measure, the tallest list's content (`tallestList`). The second path and
its measure were the rule the person rejected.

**Now** (`Build`, one loop): a list that has a line that takes room (`Takes`: a Fill line or a growing divider) grows to
the room a Fill line fills to: all the room the folder has (`Reach`: from the bar to the work area's far end less the
margin, or the room a placement gives), under the most. `tallestList` and its loop are gone.

1. **Its own column reaches the room**: on a bottom bar to the top, on a top bar to the bottom, beside a side bar to the
   room's far end, the lines after the divider at the column's foot. The folder then stands as tall as with a Fill line.
2. **The other columns keep their heights**, lined up on the bar's side as every shorter column is (§303, `Over`):
   bottoms on a bottom bar, tops on a top bar, middles beside a side bar. A column grows only for a line of its own;
   a folder with a growing divider in one column does not stretch the others.
3. **Several share, Fill lines alike** (§435 rules 3 and 4, unchanged but against the whole room): growing dividers and
   Fill lines in one column share the room evenly in whole px (`FillShares`), a capped chart's leftover going on.
4. Lines left out under the most (§152) are left out first, as before: a column already at the most has nothing to give.
5. Arranged nothing moves (§435): the room is the work area's, the same at rest and in edit mode; only the size changed.

**Checked beside it.** §468: the folder contents line keeps its root's height; a growing divider's column is a column of
the open folder, not a level, and changes nothing there. §469's Unfold, Ripple and Fly in play from the plan's columns
and sections, so a full-height column unfolds and ripples as a Fill line's always has. Every bar edge and DPI: the room
is `Reach` at the panel's scale, as Fill's (tests at 100 % and 150 %, every edge with a placement's room).

Tests (red first): `FolderDividerGrowTests` — `OneGrowingDividerTakesTheFolderRoom` (was
`OneGrowingDividerTakesTheColumnsFreeRoom`; red: 400 for 1016 at 100 %, 600 for 1004 at 150 %), `ItGrowsWithNoTallerColumn`
(was `NoFreeRoomGivesItNothing`; red: 86 for 1016, 129 for 1004), `TwoShareIt` (red: 400 for 1016),
`OnEveryBarItReachesTheRoomGiven` (bottom, top, left, right; red: 120 for 700); the Fill, capped chart, Inherited,
sections and file tests unchanged and green; `FolderFillTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`, `FolderDividerGrowPictures`):
`folder-divider-grow-<bottom|top>-<one|two|one-fill|two-fill>-150.png` and a row of the four,
`folder-divider-grow-<bottom|top>-150.png`.

By hand: a folder of one column, its divider › Style › Grow: the lines after it at the top of the screen's room on a
bottom bar (at its foot on a top bar); add a second, taller column: the growing column still reaches the room, the other
stands on the bar at its own height.

## 483. A sports line's view is kept; its rounds are said in Karpo's words (2026-11-02)

The person's answers to §479's questions (2026-11-02): no paid or keyed source for the Swiss Super League (ESPN alone,
nothing to do); *the chosen view is remembered*, per line, across restarts; *round names are translated* where Karpo
knows them.

**The view kept** (`SportsOptions.View`, the line's `sports.view`: `"matches"`, `"table"`, `"knockout"`; shape 50,
`ConfigWords.txt` written again). Matches, which a file that names none is, is not written. It is picked in the line's
settings' View (§484; first a segment's click at the line's head, written through an edit target's path, both gone),
saved as every setting is. The line reads it as it is made and whenever its options come again (`Configure`). A view the
competition does not offer now (a knockout kept for a league, a table ESPN has dropped) shows Matches, and the file is
left as it is until another view is picked. A word a newer build may write reads as Matches (`TolerantEnumConverter`).

**Rounds in Karpo's words** (`SportsRounds.Name`): one function, read by a knockout's round headings, a league's day
heading, a table's group headings, a match's caption (`SportsText.Detail`), its tooltip (`SportsTips.Match`) and the
face's tooltip (`SportsReading.Tooltip`). ESPN's name is matched lower case, its dashes and slashes spaces ("3rd-Place
Match", "Semi-finals", "Rd of 16", "Promotion/Relegation Playoffs"); the group's letter and a round's number are carried
into the words. Mapped, every name in the answers saved on 2026-11-02 and the stages ESPN's competitions are listed
with: Final; Semifinals; Quarterfinals; Round of 16; Round of 32; Round of *n*; the third-place match; Group *X*; the
group stage ("Group", "Group Stage"); the league phase; the knockout play-offs ("Knockout Round Playoffs"); the play-off
round; Playoffs; the preliminary round; Qualifying *n*th round; the *n*th round ("Second Round", "2nd Round", "Round 2");
Matchday *n*; the championship and relegation rounds; the relegation play-off; the regular season, postseason and
preseason; 1st and 2nd leg (`dock.sports.firstLeg`, `secondLeg`). A name Karpo does not know is shown as ESPN sent it
("Second Phase", "1950 Group Stage", a conference's name). Team and competition names are names, never translated.
English keeps ESPN's American words in sentence case ("League phase", "Third-place match").

Words in all 30 languages: `dock.sports.round.final|semifinals|quarterfinals|of16|of32|of|thirdPlace|group|groupStage|
leaguePhase|knockoutPlayoffs|playoffRound|playoffs|preliminary|qualifying|numbered|matchday|championship|relegation|
relegationPlayoff|regularSeason|postseason|preseason` (23; `{group}`, `{teams:int}`, `{number:int}` where the language
puts them — "F조", "64강", "第5節", "13. Spieltag"). Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Turkish and Indonesian write the Final
as English does (`UntranslatedTests.Same`).

Tests: `SportsRoundsTests` (each known name in English and German, unknown names passed through, letters and numbers
placed by Korean, Japanese and Turkish, every round, group and stage of the saved answers Karpo's own, the caption and
the tooltip in German), `SportsConfigTests.TheChosenViewIsWrittenOnlyWhereItIsNotMatchesAndReadBackAsWritten`,
`SportsCompetitionPictures.TheChosenViewIsKeptInTheLinesOptions` (read as made and as its View writes it, Matches shown
for a kept Knockout the Premier League has none of, its options untouched),
`SportsRoundsPictures` (sports-rounds-<worldcup-shootouts-knockout|worldcup-groups-matches|worldcup-groups-table>-<en|de>.png).

By hand: follow the World Cup, pick Knockout in its View, restart Karpo: Knockout is still shown. Switch Karpo to German: "Sechzehntelfinale",
"Gruppe F" under a group's game, "Gruppe A" over the table.

## 484. A sports line's view is a setting, not a selector at its top (2026-11-02)

The person (2026-11-02): *"the different sports views should be configurable in the settings but not actually shown at
the top as selector."*

**Gone from the line**: the segmented control at its head (§479) — its row (`SportsRowKind.Segments`), its targets
(`SportsTile.SegmentTarget`) and stops for the keys, its tooltips, its drawing (`PaintSegments`, the views' words and
glyphs), the head that stayed while the rest scrolled (`SportsLayout.Head`, the line's `ScrollHead`), and the test's
`SegmentsWidth`. With it went what only it needed: QuickSettings' `SegmentedItem` drawn at its bounds (its `Local`
painting; power mode's segments paint as before, and `Widget.AtBounds` stays for the line buttons and the back head),
and §483's write of a click (`IslandView.Kept`, its `FolderFlyoutAction.EditPart` branch, `SportsTile.EditClick`). The
list starts at the line's top again, and every height follows from that (automatic heights are the content's, §371);
a league's first day heading names the league in every view, the line's first words now that nothing stands over them.

**The setting** (`OptionRows.SportsView`, `OptionRows.SportsViewRow`): "View" in the line's settings, after "Team or
league" (`OptionSlot.Scope`, Explorer's View glyph), a choice opening its level that goes back on a pick (R3, R5):
Matches, Table, Knockout, each its own glyph (a calendar's days, a table, a branching; R13; `OptionGlyphs.SportsViews`),
the one kept ticked, written into `sports.view` as before (no shape change). All three are always offered — the
simplest, and a table or a knockout ESPN has not begun yet is shown once it has. A view kept that the competition does
not offer now shows Matches, the file left as it is (§483), and the row says so at its end: "Knockout (not yet)"
(`settings.widget.sports.view.notYet`). What is offered now is the answer the store holds for the line's team or league
(`SportsStore.ViewsOf`, read as the line reads it; `OptionDevices.SportsViews`, filled by `Dock.MenuSources`); with
nothing held the row says the view's name alone. Only a line has it: the sports face is one row.

"View" joins the glossary (R7): which of a line's views it shows, not Page, Tab, Shows or Show as
(`MenuRulesTests.Glossary`).

Words in all 30 languages: `settings.widget.sports.view.header` and `settings.widget.sports.view.notYet` (`{view}`); the
views' names are §479's `dock.sports.matches|table|knockout`.

Tests: `SportsViewRowTests` (the row, its three views and their glyphs, after the team; a pick written and the same one
nothing; "(not yet)" only for a view not offered, the file kept; none on the face),
`SportsCompetitionPictures.TheLineDrawsNoSelectorAndTheKeysReachEveryRow` (every view of the World Cup from the line's
top, nothing staying while it scrolls, the keys' stops the rows that open something and nothing else, no view named at
the head), `TheChosenViewIsKeptInTheLinesOptions` (what the row writes comes back to the line; the Premier League's kept
Knockout says "(not yet)"), `SportsPictures` (a league's list from its top, its first heading naming it; the table by
its View), `SportsMenuPictures.TheViewRowAndItsLevel` (sports-view-<row|level>-<dark|light>.png), `OptionRowsTests`
(`SportsOptions.View` is the View row's).

the table, the line staying where it was. Follow the Premier League with Knockout kept: Matches shown, View says
"Knockout (not yet)".

## 485. ⚙ › General; Windows' battery follows Windows; Windows' own found by what they show; the Windows layout without the Widgets button; the layouts line's Add is the presets; Styles ↗ wherever a style is picked (2026-11-02) — Styles ↗ gone with the styles, §507 (2026-11-05)

The person's answers to §472, §474 and §481's open questions, and one more: *"wherever i can select the styles there
should also be a link to the styles configuration."* Kept as they are (the person: no change): German's cut names in the
top row (§481), the folder panel menu's Cut, Copy and Remove (§481), the separators' menus' "Layout ↗" foot (§478).

**⚙ › General** (§481's switch: *"no, put it somewhere else, this is more of a karpo preset"*). "Show names in the top
row" is how Karpo looks as an app, not a style's, so it left ⚙ › Styles' foot. ⚙ had no level for Karpo's own ways, and
its first level holds no row more without scrolling (R2: eleven rows and three rules are 379 DIP of its 390). So ⚙'s first
row, "Start with Windows" (§337), became **General ›** (`KarpoMenu.General`, `settings.general.header` in 30 languages,
the gear's icon): a page of **Start with Windows** (its Why under it, as before) and **Show names in the top row**. The
first level is as many rows as before; nothing scrolls. Same key (`topRowNames`), no shape change. ⚙ › Styles is the
styles alone again (`KarpoMenu.Styles`). The menu rules read ⚙'s sections as pages (R4): a page of two switches says
nothing at its end, as Formats and Online do; it is no group of switches of one kind ("3 shown").

**Windows' own battery follows Windows** (§474's quick settings button). Windows 11's Settings › System › Power & battery
› "Battery percentage" is `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced`, DWORD
`IsBatteryPercentageEnabled` (1 on; missing or 0 off, as Windows ships it): read with the clock's seconds
(`WindowsTaskbar.BatteryPercent`), never written. The dock follows both as it followed the seconds alone: read once, again
on `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`, and the bars built again where either changed (`WindowsTaskbarFollowed`, which `WindowsClock` and
`WindowsBatteryPercent` read). Quick settings' button's battery is then the glyph alone (`FolderFace.NoPercent`, set by
`WindowsFaces.Of(kind, battery, percent)`, kept in no file), narrower, its tooltip still saying the charge. Karpo's own
battery face, in a folder, says the percentage always, as it did.

**Found by what they show** (the add list's search, §7): the clock (`windowsNotifications`) by clock, time, date and
notifications (calendar it had); the Widgets button by weather, forecast and widgets; quick settings' button by wifi,
network, volume, sound and battery — each language's own words in its `core.widget.*.keywords` (30 languages), the English
ones besides, as every row is found.

**The Windows layout without the Widgets button** (§472, §474: *"no"*). `LayoutPresets.Windows` has nothing at the
start: Start, search, Task view, the pins and the apps in the middle; the tray, pen and touch, the status icons, quick
settings' button, the clock and show desktop at the end. Windows' own are quick settings' button and the clock. The
Widgets button stays in the add list (Start and taskbar › Windows menus). §472's table: the Windows row's "Start:
Windows' Widgets button, the weather" is gone.

**The layouts line's Add is the presets** (§472's open question). With one layout, the line's Status's "Add" (§404) no
longer makes Karpo's as "New layout": once the folder has gone it opens Display ▾ at **Add a layout**
(`EditEntry.AddLayout`, landing `BarLooks.AddRow`), the presets' one picker, as "Layout settings" opens Display ▾. A pick
there makes the preset under its name and shows it, its row lit (§472). `Dock.AddLayout` and `AddShown`'s preset-less path
are gone; `BarLooks.AddShown` takes the preset.

**Styles ↗ wherever a style is picked.** §467 took every link to the styles away; now each place a style is picked ends,

## 486. Sports: every match says whether it is on now, played or to come (2026-11-02)

The person (2026-11-02): *"it should also show which events are actually active right now and which ones are from the
past."*

**On now** (`MatchState.Live`): a red dot before its clock, both strong in the live red (Windows' critical ink, the
camera's moving dot's, §463), its names strong; the score the scoreboard's Hero as before. A league's Matches lists its
games on now first, under **"Live now"** (`dock.sports.liveNow`) with a red dot before it and the round where they share
one, whatever their day; the day headings after hold the rest. A knockout's round with a game on keeps its dot at its
end. A followed team's scoreboard says **"Live · 67'"** (`dock.sports.live`, `SportsTile.Status`) after its dot. Stale,
the reds go quiet as before (§239).

**Played** (`MatchState.Final`): how it ended — "Final", "AET", "Pens" — and, where no day's heading says its day (a
knockout's round, a team's results, the scoreboard of the last played), its day too: "AET · 1 Jul", "Final · 17 Mar"
(`SportsText.Row` with no day; the "AET" that stood under a team's result moved there). The losing side quiet, the winner
and the score as the text is (`SportsText.Lost`: ESPN's winner of the match, a shoot-out's too, else the higher score; a
draw has none; `SportsTile.Result` draws the three parts the fitting form is made of, `SportsTile.Parts`). Where the whole
would leave the names no room for even their abbreviations (225 % text, the narrowest list) a row says its shortest: a
result its day, a kick-off its time today or its weekday (`SportsText.Short`); the tooltip says the rest.

**To come**: its kick-off in this PC's zone and the region's format, "20:45" under its day's heading, "Today 20:45",
"Tomorrow 23:00", "Sun 03:00", "19 Jul 21:00" under none — as before.

**Headings in tones** (`SportsTone`, `SportsRow.Tone`): over what is done quiet (the text's secondary ink) — a day gone
by, a round played whole, "Results" —; over what is on or to come strong (the text's own ink) — today and the days
after, the rounds still to play, "Coming up", "Also playing" —; "Live now" in the live red. A league's first heading still
names it first (§484), now as the heading's quiet lead (`SportsRow.Lead`; `Words` is the whole, its tooltip).

**A knockout shown brings its round now into sight** (`SportsTile.ScrollReveal`, `Current`): the round a game of is on,
else the first with a game to come, from its heading down as far as the line holds — so the World Cup's quarterfinals
are what is seen, not the round of 32's sixteen results; a knockout played whole stays at its top.

**In words** (tooltips; `SportsTips.Match`, `SportsReading.Tooltip`, so the face's too): "Live, 67 minutes played",
"Live, half-time", "Live, Q3 5:32" (`SportsText.LiveSaid`); "Finished today", "yesterday", "3 days ago", past a month
"Finished", then "AET" where it was and its day and time (`SportsText.Finished`); "Starts today at 20:45", "tomorrow at",
"Starts Sat, 07.11. at 20:45", its day alone where its time is not known (`SportsText.Starts`).

**The face** already told a game on from a result — a red dot and its clock, "ESP 2–1 BEL 40'", against "ESP 2–1 BEL
Final" a few hours after and "SCP 5–0 BODO 17 Mar" as the last played —; its tooltip now says it in words too. Its words
stay the bar's ink: the face's text is made to read on every style's ground (ToneRules), the critical red is not.

No setting was added. The Table has no match of its own to mark.

Words in all 30 languages: `dock.sports.live`, `liveNow`, `tip.live` (`{clock}`), `tip.liveMinutes.one|other`,
`tip.halftime`, `tip.finished`, `tip.finishedToday`, `tip.finishedYesterday`, `tip.finishedDaysAgo.one|other`,
`tip.startsToday`, `tip.startsTomorrow` (`{time}`), `tip.startsOn` (`{day}`, `{time}`), `tip.startsDay` (`{day}`). German
and Dutch write "Live" as English does (`UntranslatedTests.Same`).

Tests: `SportsStateTests` on ESPN's saved answers rewound to a moment of their own (`SavedSports.AsOf`: what had not begun
to come, without a score; what began within two hours on with its minute; the rest as saved) — the Champions League's
second legs on 17 March at 21:10 UTC (`MatchdayLive`), the World Cup's second quarterfinal on 10 July at 19:40 UTC
(`KnockoutLive`, `KnockoutTeamLive`): a row's trail in each state and its shortest; the loser of a result, a shoot-out,
none in a draw or a game on, the three parts of every form; the tooltips' words; the matchday's "Live now" first with
its three games on, then today's result and tomorrow's four, strong; a day gone by quiet; the knockout's played rounds
quiet, the quarterfinals strong with their dot and brought into sight, nothing brought for a knockout played whole; a
followed team's "Live · 40'", its "Results" quiet, a last played's "AET · 17 Mar"; the face's reading on now apart
from its result. `EveryStateDrawn` (sports-state-<ucl-live|worldcup-live|team-live|premier-league|sporting>-<matches|knockout>-<dark|light>-<100|150|225text>.png,
sports-state-faces-<dark|light>.png). The three moments join `SportsCompetitionPictures.Cases`, so every view of them is
laid out whole and says itself in its tooltips at every list width and text size.

By hand: follow the Champions League on a matchday evening: "Live now" over the games on, each "● 55'" in red; today's
results under "Today", the losing side grey; tomorrow's under "Tomorrow". Pick Knockout in its View: the round on now
is what is seen, the rounds played above it grey. Follow a team while it plays: the scoreboard says "● Live · 40'", its
results under a grey "Results", each "Final · 6 Jul". Hover a game: "Live, 40 minutes played", "Finished 3 days ago",
"Starts tomorrow at 23:00".

## 487. A divider's Style lays the open folder out at once; Done leaves the folder you are in open (2026-11-02)

The person (2026-11-02): *"when changing the separator style from grow to only a space or vice versa it does not
immediately update which it should."* And: *"when clicking done in edit mode it should not close the current folder that
you are in."*

**A divider's Style.** Picked in its menu while its folder stood open — Inherited (Space only) to Grow or back (§435,
§482) — it was written to the file and the open folder stayed as it was until something else laid it out: its column not
grown to the folder's room, its two sections not moved apart, the folder no taller. *The root cause:* the open folder
plans again only where its layout's signature changed (`FolderFlyout.Signature`, "everything Build reads"), and a
divider's own Style was not in it, though `Build` reads it (`StyleOf`, `Takes`: Grow takes the room, the folders' look a
gap). A divider whose Style changed is the same widget with a new cell, so only the cards were drawn again
(`FolderChanged`). *Now* each line's term says whether it is a growing divider (`Grows`): Grow and back plan the folder
again at once — the column to all the room (§482) or back to its lines, its two sections that far apart or a gap apart,
the panel's height with them (`LayOut`, `host.Resize`) — at rest and arranged. What a divider inherits, its layout's
style's Folder separators (§478: Line, Space only, None), was in the signature already (`Separators`) and lays it out at
once too.

**Done.** §348 kept the folder open as Done ends edit mode, and the stage's probe holds that it does
(`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.DoneLeavesTheFolderOpenAtRest`). But the stage's desktop never has the input, so it never saw
what the person's does: `EndEdit` handed the keys back to the window that had them before edit mode began (`editReturn`)
wherever a bar being edited had them — a click on a folder's face, on the bar, a menu closed back to the bar leaves them
there — and only then put the folder at rest, which asks for them (`Rest`, `host.Focus`). That window taking the focus is
"another window taking the focus", which closes a folder at rest (`OneFolder`, `FolderCloser.PressElsewhere`). *Now* the
keys go back only where no folder stays open (`OneFolder.KeysBack`); a folder kept open takes them, as a folder opened at
rest has them, and stays where it stood with its dress off, neither closed nor its animation played again (`Rest` lays
it out in place; nothing shows it anew).

**One rule for every end the person asks for.** `LeaveEdit` — Done, and Escape with nothing left to step out of — keeps
the folder open (`EndEdit`'s keepFolder, no longer its caller's choice). Escape still closes the folder first, as a step
of its own (`EditKeys.Escape`: one level out), so its end of edit mode finds none open. A click away ends no edit mode.
Edit mode ending for the displays changing, the session locking or its bar going closes the folder with it, as before.

Tests (red first): `FolderDividerGrowTests.ItsStylePickedWhileTheFolderIsOpenLaysItOutAtOnce` (at rest and arranged: the
row set on a copy of the config and the folder configured from it, as `Dock.OptionPicked` does; Grow: the column the
folder's room, 1016 px, its two sections that far apart, the panel over 400 px taller — red: 86; back: as before; then
its layout's style's Folder separators Line, None, Space only: one section, one, two), `OneFolderTests.TheKeysGoBackOnlyWhereNoFolderStaysOpen`
(red: the keys went back with a folder kept), `AFolderKeptAsEditModeEndsRestsWhereItStands` (LeaveEdit keeps it; EndEdit
asks KeysBack), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.DoneLeavesTheFolderOpenAtRest` (the real dock on two screens, Fly in: Done
with the folder's menu open, with none, with a line's menu open, on its screen's edit bar and the other's — pressed
through the popups' hook first, as the mouse presses it —; the folder at rest where its panel stood, then closed by a
press on the bar's room as any).

By hand: a folder with a divider, in edit mode, its divider's menu › Style › Grow: the column reaches the top of the
screen at once; Inherited (Space only): back at once. Click Done: the folder stays open, at rest, where it stood; a click
on the bar closes it.

## 488. The Top and bottom layout is gone: a layout is one bar (2026-11-02)

The person (2026-11-02): *"the top and bottom layout style should also be removed."* (After §438 took the Dock with two
rows.)

**What went.** The type (`LayoutType.TopBottom`, the file's `"topBottom"`) and everything only it had: its second bar's
size and show (`TaskbarLayout.TopSize`, `TopShow`, the file's `"topSize"`, `"topShow"`), the second row of three sections
(`BarRow`, `BarItem.Row`, the file's `"row"` on every widget) and the slot that paired a row with a section
(`BarPlace`). With one row the slots a type "shows" were always all three, so the machinery that asked went too:
`LayoutTypes.Rows`, `Places` and `Home`, `TaskbarLayout.Rows`, `Places`, `Shows`, `Home`, `EdgeOf`, `Bars`, `RowAt`,
`Step`, `ShowOf`/`SetShowOf`, `SizeOf`/`RawSizeOf`/`SetSizeOf`; the keyboard's way between the two bars (Ctrl+Up/Down,
`Dock.StepRow`, `IslandEdits.Across`) and the "shown" filter on Ctrl+arrow (`IslandEdits.Step`); the licence's "a widget
in a hidden slot does not count" (`LicenseCount`, `LicenseGate.Add`'s place); the row of a pin pinned from a bar
(`Dock.PinApp`), of an add (`AddSpot.Row`, `IslandEdits.Add`/`Put`, `Presets.AddToBar`) and of a renewed layout's pins.
A place in the list is a section and an index, `BarSlot`, everywhere: the two `IslandEdits.Move`s, `MoveGroup`, `Paste`,
`ToList`, `Sections.Put`, `Range` and `Along` take it or a section (`Sections.Of(island)` for an entry's), and
`(BarPlace, int)` is gone from the dock. Layout ▾ (§364's named "Top bar size", "Show top bar", "Bottom bar size", "Show
bottom bar", the `:top` keys, `LayoutRows(…, everyBar)`) has one Size and one Show again; a size typed is offered the
other layouts' bars' sizes (`BarLooks.SizesOffered`). The menu's bar is the display alone (`BarSpot(Display, Name)`).
Their words (`settings.layouts.type.topBottom`, `.size.top`, `.size.bottom`, `.show.top`, `.show.bottom`) left all 30
languages.

**What stayed, and why.** A display still has four edges (`ScreenEdges`, `EdgeBar`): its bar stands on any of them
(`Screen.Edge`), and on hover its three sections are three places along that edge, each a window (`HoverPlaces`,
`Dock.StandingEdges`, `Dock.Shows` with a place). `TaskbarLayout.Edges(screen)` now makes the one bar on the display's
edge, at `BarSize` (its `Size` held to 28–160). `Dock.PopupRoom` keeps a popup off every other bar window of the display
in sight; with one bar that is its own folder's room (`FolderWork`) and, for a Dock, its other docks.

**The Monitor preset** (§472) was a 32-DIP bar along the top with the readings over Karpo's taskbar. It is one Taskbar now,
still Harbor at 48 DIPs: Start, the search, Task view and the desktops at the left; the pins and the open apps in the
middle; at the right the processor, the graphics, the memory, the disk and the network each its figure, then the
clipboard beside the tray and its icons, quick settings, the notifications and show desktop — as a system monitor sits by
the tray. Its line in "Add a layout": "The taskbar with how the PC is doing beside the tray", in every language.

**The file.** `Config.Shape` 51: the type's word and the keys are gone (ConfigWords.txt written again). No migration: a
file that says `"topBottom"` reads as a word this build does not know, which `Config.Repair` makes a Taskbar, every
widget on its one bar in its own section (a top row's after the main row's there); `"row"`, `"topSize"` and `"topShow"`
are read past and leave the file at its next save. The person's config had no Top and bottom (two Taskbar layouts):
nothing to convert; it loads with no repair but the shape's. The stage's catalogue (`scripts/stage/catalog.json`), a
Top and bottom, is a Taskbar now, the top bar's folders in their sections of the one bar.

Tests: `NamedLayoutsTests` (one bar on the display's edge for each type, on all four; a window shows its bar's widgets;
the bar at its size, held; Taskbar to Dock and back moves nothing; a Top and bottom from before reads as a Taskbar, its
top row's widgets on the one bar, the second bar's words gone from the file), `PlacesTests` (kept by section, a "row" read
past), `LayoutPresetsTests.MonitorIsOneTaskbarWithItsReadingsBesideTheTray`, `BarLooksTests` (the Type offers Taskbar
and Dock; one Size and one Show; sizes offered), `LayoutMenuTests`, `EdgeModesTests`, `EditDeckPlanTests`,
`IslandEditsTests`, `PlaceEditTests`, `EditSelectTests`, `SerializationTests` (no `"row"`), `ConfigSchemaTests`; the
pictures (`layout-preset-monitor-*`, `edit-select-*` on a Taskbar on hover, its three places, `edit-inplace-*`,
`side-*`, `top-*`, `places-*`) no longer draw a Top and bottom.

By hand: Layout ▾ › Type offers Taskbar and Dock; Size and Show once. "Add a layout" › Monitor: one bar, the readings
beside the tray.

## 489. One motion for everything: one engine, off or at three speeds; every popup comes in, every swap moves (2026-11-02)

The person: *"in terms of animations, i actually want only one default animation for everything in karpo and it should
also not be customizable. it should be able to be turned off so that there are no animations at all and the speed should
be selectable as well between three levels. go ahead and make sure that everything is animated, transitions between
views, layouts, menus, etc. the transitions in general should be subtle and professional and also clean looking."*

**Where it was** (the audit, every motion and every change without one: `%TEMP%\karpo-coord\motion\motion-audit.md`).
Karpo moved in a dozen ways, each with its times and curves typed where it ran: 83 ms fades in five files, 167 ms glides
in six (`EditLook.MoveMs`, `FolderDrag.MoveMs`, `GapSlideMs`, a menu level's 16 DIP `Slide`), the bar's show and hide
250/167 on a curve of its own, a desktops row's 200 ms on a cubic ease-out, the month's 250 ms glide with a third copy of
the decelerate curve (and a dead `DaySlide` with a fourth), the edit bar's 300 ms flight in from past the screen's edge,
a pressed icon's spring overshooting; folders had six animations to choose from per layout (§446 Slide and Fade, §458 Fly
in, §469 Unfold and Ripple, Off) with a preview that played each on a real folder. Every other popup — menus, flyouts,
the taskbar folder list, tooltips — came up at once (§355: "Opening is not animated") and faded out in 83 ms; a menu's
level, a folder's page, a subfolder, a line's view, another layout on a bar swapped at once.

**The one motion** (`Karpo.Dock\Motion.cs`, the only place a time or a curve is). Windows 11's language: what comes in
decelerates (0, 0, 0, 1), what goes accelerates (0.7, 0, 1, 0.5), a wash or a colour fades straight; whatever moves moves
one short way, 12 DIP; nothing bounces, flies far or grows from nothing. Every surface asks it for its kind:

| Kind | Normal | Curve | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hover | 83 ms | straight | hover and selection washes, colours, the search box's fill, a tooltip coming (a popup's tooltip going too; the bar's goes at once, as Windows' does), launch feedback's fade |
| Press | 83 ms | decelerate | a pressed icon's give (0.9) and its release — no spring, no overshoot |
| Move | 167 ms | decelerate | a block or a line giving way, settling, gliding to its new place or size; tray icons; the desktops line's rows |
| Swap | 167 ms | decelerate | content swapped in place, from 12 DIP along its way; a block added to the bar fading in |
| Open | 200 ms | decelerate | a popup coming in: 12 DIP from its side, fading in |
| Close | 117 ms | accelerate | a popup going back the same way |
| Show / Hide | 250 / 167 ms | decelerate / accelerate | a large surface: a bar out of hiding and back, the edit bar |
| Glide | 250 ms | decelerate | the month's weeks to a month |

Edit mode's marching ants (480 ms a lap) and a signal's runner (2 s) are loops while something is so, not transitions:
the same pace at every speed, none with motion off. Input timing is not motion and stays: a touchpad's quiet before the
weeks settle, hover delays, the launch feedback's 300 ms hold.

**Settings** (⚙ › General, §485's home of Karpo's own ways, under Start with Windows and Show names in the top row; ⚙'s
first level unchanged, so it still never scrolls, R2). **Animations**, a switch, on (`"animations"`, always written).
**Animation speed** — Slower, Normal, Faster, each its own picture (R13), a pick going back (R3, R5) — scaling every time
by one factor: 1.5, 1, ⅔ (`"animationSpeed"`: `"slower"`, `"normal"`, `"faster"`; left out while Normal; a word this
build does not know reads Normal, `Config.Repair`). Off — or Windows' Animation effects off (`UISettings.AnimationsEnabled`,
SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION), whatever Karpo's switch says — nothing moves: every surface is where it ends at once. Both
reach every surface through the look (`Look.Moving`: `Animations` is Windows' and Karpo's together, `Speed` the factor;
`Look.Motion`), which every surface already asked whether to animate. Five strings in every language
(`settings.general.animations.header`, `settings.general.animationSpeed.*`); the glossary (R7): Animations, Animation speed.

**Every popup comes in and goes** (`FlyoutHost`, one plan for all, `PopupMotion.Of`): menus and context menus, every
widget flyout, the quick settings dialog, the taskbar folder list, folders, the edit rail rise 12 DIP from their bar's side
(a submenu from the item it hangs from) fading in over 200 ms and go back over 117; a tooltip (`TipView`,
`PopupEntrance.Tip`) fades where it stands; the edit bar (`PopupEntrance.Bar`) rises and fades over 250 and goes over 167
(§326's flight from past the screen's edge is that rise now). §355's reason for none — DWM can stop every app's
animations, leaving a popup waiting on one unseen — is met as §446 met it for folders: the opening's timer puts the panel
where it ends whether or not DWM ran it (`Arrived`), and its region and hit tests are where it ends from the first frame.
A close as it comes in turns back from where it is (`MotionClock`); a popup shown again while open stands still; a folder
opened for another is there at once; an arranged folder fades where it stands. Window previews fade in as a popup.

**Every swap moves** (`MotionEase.SwapIn`): a menu's level in place (§268), a folder's page opened or closed in its column
(§170: its lines), a subfolder gone into or back in a folder's line (§398, §468: `CellIsland.Swapped`) and in the taskbar
folder list, a line's view picked while it stands (the sports line's Matches, Table, Knockout) or its widget made again in
another style (`FolderFlyout.SwapLine`), another layout shown on a bar (every layer of the bar from the screen's edge, by
`Layout.LayoutId`). In from the end (+1), back from the start (−1), mirrored where Karpo is. Only the offset moves, never
the opacity, so where DWM stopped animations a swap is where it belongs or a few px off it, never unseen. Not swaps: a
showing (a line's first content), anything arranged, live data.

**Folders: one motion, no choice.** §446's Slide, shorter (12 DIP, was 32), is every popup's; Fade, Fly in, Unfold,
Ripple and Off go with their plans and their machinery: `FolderMotion.cs`, `FolderFlight.cs`, `FolderStaging.cs`,
`FolderFlyout.Flight.cs`, `FlyoutHost.Fly`/`BindRims`/`Unfly`, the flight's clock and expressions, the preview
(`FolderPreview.cs`, `Dock.FolderPreview.cs`, `Flyout.Lit`), the row Layout ▾ › Behavior › Folder animation, its seven
strings, `OptionGlyphs.Unfold`/`Groups`, `TaskbarLayout.FolderAnimation`. `EditLook.MoveMs`/`FadeMs`/`Decelerate`,
`FolderDrag.MoveMs`/`Decelerate`, `MarchingAnts.CycleMs` and the dead `DaySlide` went to the engine or away.

**The file.** `"folderAnimation"` leaves every layout and the two Karpo-wide keys come: `Config.Shape` 51, `ConfigWords.txt`
written again. No conversion in Karpo: `%TEMP%\karpo-coord\convert-motion.py in.json out.json` drops each layout's
`"folderAnimation"` and raises `"version"` 50 to 51; the person's file (a copy) converted, its Default layout's `"flyIn"`
dropped, and reads with no repair.

Tests: `MotionTests` (each kind's time and curve; the speeds by one factor; off — Karpo's or Windows' — nothing at all; the
popup plan per entrance, a switch, arranged, the speeds; the side per edge at 100 to 175 %, a submenu's; the curves one
way, decelerate exact; the clock turned back from where it is; a swap told once the way it went and never for a line's
first content; and **NothingButTheEngineNamesATimeOrACurve**: no file of the dock but `Motion.cs` makes an easing or a
spring or times an animation itself — red before: 55 places in 12 files), `MonthScrollTests`, `DayStripTests`,
`EditLookTests`, `DesktopsPresetTests`, `KarpoMenuGeneralTests`, `TopRowNamesTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `MenuRulesTests`,
`ConfigSchemaTests`, `UntranslatedTests`; live `FolderMotionFilmTests` (the one motion's slide, a close as it comes in,
§480's shown-at-once now for it), `FlickerFilmTests`, `RetainedMenuTests`, `MenuToggleTests`, `TipFilmTests`,
`EditChromeFilmTests`, `ArrangedFolderStandsTests`, `EditDeckPlanTests`, `KeptEditBarTests`, `RetainedFolderTests`.
Storyboards (composed from the plan, as §469's: the hidden desktop's compositor skips animations):
`%TEMP%\karpo-coord\motion\motion-<popup-open|popup-close|level-swap>-<slower|normal|faster>.png`.

By hand: ⚙ › General › Animations off: menus, folders, flyouts, tooltips, the edit bar, a bar out of hiding all at once;
on, at Normal: a menu from the bar rises and fades in, a submenu from its row's side, a tooltip fades; a folder rises from
its button and sinks back; a menu's level slides in from the right and back from the left; Animation speed Slower and
Faster, the same, slower and quicker. A folder's line page (a quick settings tile's ">"), a Folder line's subfolder and
back, a sports line's View: each slides in. Display ▾ › another layout: the bar's content rises from the screen's edge.
Edit mode: the edit bar rises and goes. Windows Settings › Accessibility › Visual effects › Animation effects off: nothing
moves whatever ⚙ says.

them to carry the content that the windows native taskbar widget would carry as well."* — *"the windows menus should get
their own top level entry and not be hidden three levels down."* — *"go over the widget groups in the add dialog and make
sure that there are generally speaking not more than 2 levels, only if required up to three but not more."*

**The add list closed over Windows' menu** (§466: a Karpo flyout closes Windows' menu in front). *The root cause:* the
menu is closed by an Escape Karpo sends it (`WindowsPanels.Dismiss`, run by `CloseFor` as the add list opens). In edit
mode Karpo's own low-level keyboard hook is in (`EditFollowHook`, Escape leaves edit mode wherever the keys are), and it
heard that Escape as the person's: it took it for leaving edit mode — the add list closing with edit mode — and kept it
from the menu, which stayed open. Worse, the dock waited for the menu to give up the foreground in a plain `Sleep`; a
low-level hook is called through its thread's sent messages, so the Escape reached no window for the whole wait and then
went to the add list opened meanwhile, which closes on Escape. Outside edit mode no hook of the dock's thread hears keys,
which is why a folder or a menu opened over Windows' menu never showed it. *Now* the Escape carries Karpo's mark
(`TaskbarKeys.Ours`, `WindowsPanels.EscapeTaps`), edit mode's hook lets Karpo's own keys by (`FollowGesture.Key`'s
`ours`), and the wait runs the thread's sent messages (`MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx` with `QS_SENDMESSAGE`, `PeekMessage`
`PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE`), so the hook answers at once and the Escape reaches the menu before the flyout opens. Whether
Windows' menu also hands the focus back to an app as it goes (which would close any Karpo flyout on `WA_INACTIVE`) was not
checked: no test opens Windows' UI.

**Edit mode closes Windows' menus.** As it comes in, before its chrome shows, every open one of them closes the way a
Karpo flyout closes them (`WindowsPanels.ForEditMode` → `CloseFor`: Search and Start where they show, the notifications,
quick settings, the quick link menu and the Widgets board where one is in front, each by Escape), and the keys go back at
its end to none of them (`editReturn`). Not from a dock on a config of its own (a test, `--smoke`).

**Windows' own wear their Karpo folder's faces.** §474 had three of §466's entries wear faces; the other six (the quick
link menu, sound output, Wi-Fi networks, cast, clipboard history, the emoji panel) were one glyph in a button's well,
drawn bigger than a face's icon (the scene's 20 DIP button glyph), cast's another glyph than the cast face's, and all
nine drew their style's Taskbar widgets where a folder's face draws its Folder buttons. Now every one of Windows' menus
wears the faces of the Karpo folder that stands for it (`WindowsFaces.Of`), drawn by `FolderIsland` as that folder's are:

| Entry | Faces | Karpo's folder |
|---|---|---|
| `windowsQuickSettings` | the network, the volume, the battery (on a PC with one) | Quick settings |
| `windowsNotifications` | the time over the date, the bell | Notifications and calendar |
| `widgetsBoard` | the weather | Weather |
| `windowsSound` | the volume | Sound |
| `windowsNetworks` | the network | Wi-Fi |
| `windowsCast` | cast | Cast |
| `windowsClipboard` | the clipboard | Clipboard history |
| `quickLink`, `emojiPanel` | the icon face of their own glyph | (none) |

Worn as a folder's face is: its style's **Folder buttons** (`WidgetLooks.PartOf`), so cards, highlight, outline and
pattern are the face's. What stays Windows' is their content: the time and the date in Windows' formats, the battery's
percentage as Windows' setting says (§485), the weather's conditions on the Widgets button. The sound page's button
takes the wheel, as the volume face does. `BarEntries.WindowsMenu` (the glyph entry) is gone; the scene's glyph buttons
are the pen menu, the touch keyboard, the virtual touchpad, the Snipping Tool and Settings. Quick settings' button is lit
over its pages' while quick settings is in front and no button opened it (`WindowsMenus.IsPage`).

**The add list: two levels.** The list's top (Popular's picks, Browse's subjects) is the first level, a subject's submenu
the second; no subject holds a folder any more. Before (the bar's page; a folder's in brackets where it differs):

    Browse › Time and calendar › … › [Calendar › Calendar, Today's date, Next meeting, Calendar actions]
            Weather and news › … › [Sunrise and sunset › 7]
            Music and sound
            Connections › Network & internet, Wi-Fi › 2 [3], Bluetooth › 3 [3], [VPN › 3], [Mobile hotspot › 3], …
            Quick settings
            Battery and power › … › [Power buttons › 6]
            Screen and sharing › …, Accessibility › 6 [7], …, [Nearby sharing › 3]
            System info › … › [Performance details › 5], [Screen time › 3]
            Notes and messages, Files and tools
            Start and taskbar › Windows menus › Start button, Search, Task view, Widgets and the eight (12), Apps, …
            Keyboard and touch › Keyboard layout, Touch keyboard, Virtual touchpad, Pen menu

After (`AddTree.Browse`), thirteen subjects:

    Browse › Time and calendar   (bar 11 · folder 10: the clock's run | the calendar's run)
             Weather and news    (10 · 15: weather, air, tides, quakes, the sun's | news, markets, sports)
             Music and sound     (8 · 11)
             Connections         (10 · 13: network, Wi-Fi, VPN | Bluetooth | hotspot, airplane mode)
             Quick settings      (19 · 19, as before)
             Battery and power   (5 · 12: battery and power | sleep … lock)
             Screen and sharing  (7 · 13: brightness … rotation lock | cast, project, nearby sharing)
             Accessibility       (6 · 7)
             System info         (9 · 17: readings | details | processes … game mode, screen time)
             Notes and messages  (8 · 7)
             Files and tools     (9 · 10)
             Start and taskbar   (10 · 6: Start button, Search, Task view, Apps, Tray icons, Status icons, Show
                                  desktop, Virtual desktops, Taskbar layouts, Keyboard layout)
             Windows menus       (12 · none: Widgets, Quick link menu, Notifications, Quick settings, Sound output,
                                  Wi-Fi networks, Cast panel, Clipboard panel, Emoji panel | Touch keyboard, Virtual
                                  touchpad, Pen menu)

A third level is allowed only where `AddTreeTests.ThirdLevelAllowed` names it, with why: none. What were folders are runs
between lines; a folder parted by lines holds up to nineteen rows in runs of twelve at most, one without twelve; Browse
thirteen (Accessibility and Windows menus became subjects, Keyboard and touch went into Start and taskbar). Windows menus
wears the Windows glyph, no icon twice among the subjects. Start's three stay in Start and taskbar, where its name says
(and where a folder's page keeps Task view); Windows' input panels join Windows' menus, as Windows' taskbar opens them
too. The eleven folders' titles (`core.addTree.{calendar,sun,wifi,bluetooth,vpn,hotspot,nearby,powerButtons,screenTime,
performanceDetails,input}.title`) left the 30 string files. The search finds the same widgets: each says the subject it
is in ("Connections", "Battery and power", "System info"), and the runs' widgets keep their own words (the sun's "sun",
the power buttons' "power button", the details' "details"). The R8 exception for Windows' "Bluetooth & devices" moved
with it (`Connections › Bluetooth & devices`).

Tests (red first): `WindowsSearchTests.TheEscapeThatClosesWindowsMenuForAFlyoutIsNotThePersons` (stand-in panels whose
dismiss feeds the real taps to edit mode's gesture: nothing kept, edit mode not left; a person's Escape still is),
`KarposOwnEscapeIsNeverEditModes`, `EditModeComingInClosesWindowsMenus`; `EditFollowHookTests.KarposOwnEscapeIsLetBy`;
`WindowsFacesTests.EveryWindowsMenuWearsTheFacesOfItsKarpoFolder` (faces as the preset's, Folder buttons, no glyph
