Karpo folder's, dark and light, 100 and 150 %; KARPO_UI_TESTS); `AddTreeTests.NothingIsDeeperThanTwoLevels`,
`WindowsMenusIsASubjectOfItsOwn`, `EveryFolderIsShortShallowAndNeverOfOneRow`, `EachPageKeepsWhatItHasOfASubject`;
`AddListTests`, `AddListSearchTests`, `PremadeWidgetsTests`, `WindowsButtonsTests`, `InputButtonsTests`,
`TypedRegistryTests`, `MenuRulesTests`. No shortcut is sent and no Windows UI is opened. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`windows-beside-karpo-<windows|graphite|paper>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png` (`SceneTreeTests.WindowsOwnBesideKarposSheets`),
`add-list-windows-menus-<dark|light>.png`, `add-list-system-info-<dark|light>.png` (`AddListPictures.SubjectsSheet`).

By hand: open quick settings (Win+A), enter edit mode: quick settings closes. Open quick settings again, click a "+" of
the bar: the add list opens, quick settings closes, the add list stays; pick a widget. In the Windows layout, the sound,
Wi-Fi, cast and clipboard buttons look as Karpo's Sound, Wi-Fi, Cast and Clipboard folders' faces, at the same size; a
style's Folder buttons colours reach them. The add list: Windows menus is a row of Browse; no submenu opens another.

## 491. One launcher: whatever Karpo opens outside itself closes what of Karpo's is open first (2026-11-02)

The person (2026-11-02): *"as soon as something opens an external program like the settings for example or a website or
something like that it should close the current folder that is open. of course there are some exceptions to this like
windows native menus etc. but i image you can decide yourself on this."*

**The rule.** Everything Karpo hands Windows to open goes through one launcher, `Karpo.Dock\Launch.cs`, and before it
hands anything over, everything of Karpo's that is open closes (`Dock.LeaveForLaunch`, `Dock.Leave.cs`): the open folder,
a menu or a flyout (⚙ included), quick settings, a folder pin's list, the window list. Windows' taskbar does the same with
what it starts. Then the launch: the right to come to the front handed on (`AllowSetForegroundWindow(ASFW_ANY)`, once,
in the launcher, where three places did it each before) and the shell asked. Closing first is what keeps the focus sane:
a folder closing hands the keys back to the window it had them from only while it still has them
(`FlyoutHost.Close(restore)`), so what is launched takes them after and never loses them to the folder.

Before, a folder closed for a launch only where the code happened to close it: a line's click (the folder rule, §15:
the folder goes, then the dock opens) and a widget menu's pick at rest (`HandsAway`, `FolderAfterMenu`). Everything else
left it standing until the launched program took the focus, if it did — a quick-settings line that opens its Settings
page where Windows will not let it switch (night light, the setting toggles, a page switch, nearby sharing, the mobile
hotspot, energy saver, VPN, do not disturb, spatial sound), a quick page's links, a sign-in's browser, an arranged
folder's "Open file location", and from the Karpo menu: About's sites, region settings.

**Edit mode.** A launch closes the folder arranged too (`FolderCloser.Launch`, which `OneFolder.Closes` answers true for in
both modes, as Escape and edit mode ending); edit mode itself stays. Arranging keeps a folder open through what happens
on the bar; a program coming up over it is not that.

**The launcher's ways** (each `Launch.*`, each closing first): `Open` (a target with a verb, a program with parameters:
pages, links, ms-settings:, mailto:, tel:, apps by `shell:AppsFolder`, files), `Aside` (the same off the dock's thread,
with a fallback: a meeting's Join, an event; was `MeetingJoin.Launch`'s own thread), `Elevated` (Ctrl+Shift+click, "Run
as administrator"), `With` / `WithApp` (files dropped on a program or a store app), `Properties`, `Select` ("Open file
location"), `Explorer` (a folder in File Explorer always), `Jump` and `Packaged` (a jump list's line and task; were
`JumpLists.Invoke`'s own ShellExecute and thread), `Program` (Karpo's own Wi-Fi dialog process), `Toast` (a notification's
activation). Deleted: `Items.Open`, `OpenWith`, `OpenElevated`, `OpenWithApp`, `Properties`, `ShowInFolder`,
`FolderReader.InExplorer`, `JumpLists.Activate`, the toast platform's own `ActivateApplication` and `ShellExecuteEx`,
`MicrosoftAuth`'s `Process.Start` (the dock now hands it `MicrosoftAuth.Browser` = `Launch.Open`). The dock's private
`Launch` (open once the press has shown) is `LaunchLater`, and hands to `Launch.Open` / `Launch.Elevated`.

**What reached the shell, and now reaches the launcher** (the audit): the bar's pins, apps and sites (`Dock.Pins.cs`,
`Item.Open`), dropped files (`Dock.Pins.cs`), the bar's menu's shortcuts and places (`Dock.BarMenu.cs`), Start's quick
links and Task Manager (`Dock.cs`), a widget menu's acts (`Dock.OpenFromMenu`: open, Properties, select, Explorer, run as
administrator), Windows' buttons' apps (Settings, the Snipping Tool, its Store page: `WindowsButtons`, `Dock.OpenWindowsButton`),
quick settings' links (`Dock.QuickClosed`, `QuickPageTile`, `ActionsTile`, `IndicatorsIsland`), the services' fall-backs
to Settings (`NightLight`, `SettingToggles`, `Switches` ×4, `Vpn` ×2, `Spatial` ×2, `DoNotDisturb`, `DarkMode`,
`Assistive`'s magnifier, `WifiProperties`), ⚙'s sites and pages (`KarpoServices.Open` → `LaunchLater`) and its backup's
"Show the file" (`Dock.SettingsBackup.cs`), the lines' clicks (`RssIsland`, `SportsTile`, `MailIsland`, `ContactsLine`,
`QuakesLine`, `CameraLine`, `MarketIsland`, `FolderIsland.Markets`, `TimeSearch`, `WeatherLineTile`, `NotebookTile`,
`ClipboardLine`'s links, `ProcessesLine`, `PerformanceIsland`'s Task Manager, `SecurityIsland`, `FolderContents`'s
files and folders, `DriveWatch`'s drives, `MeetingJoin` and `EventLinks`), jump lists (`JumpLists.Invoke`), a
notification's app (`NotificationPartTile` → `Launch.Toast`), the Wi-Fi dialog (`WifiProperties.InAProcessOfItsOwn`) and a
Microsoft sign-in's browser (`MicrosoftAuth.Browse`).

**Not a launch, so nothing closes for it:**

- Windows' own menus (§466). Those opened by their keys (quick settings Win+A, notifications Win+N, Win+X, sound output,
  clipboard history, emoji, cast, the Widgets board) never reach the launcher; the few that open by an address do, as
  everything handed to the shell does, but close nothing (`Launch.IsWindowsPanel`: the Wi-Fi list
  `ms-availablenetworks:`, the pen menu, the virtual touchpad, the touch keyboard's `TabTip.exe`). They come one at a
  time by their own rule (`WindowsMenus`, §466, §490). Settings (`ms-settings:`), the Snipping Tool (`ms-screenclip:`,
  whose snip wants every folder off the screen anyway) and the Store are apps: theirs is a launch.
- Task view, a new desktop, Show desktop, the power buttons: Windows' own, no program started (the widget menu's
  `HandsAway` still closes the folder for the ones picked there).
- What stays in Karpo: a toggle, media transport, volume, a copy to the clipboard, typing, a refresh, a sports view
  changed, a subfolder's contents beside the folder.
- A notification's background activation (a "Like", a reply: `ToastActivation.Closes` false): it shows nothing, and
  closes nothing.
- What starts nothing the person sees: the guard starting the dock again and the dock its guard (`DockLauncher.cs`,
  `Dock.Guard.cs`), the scheduled task's hidden `schtasks.exe` (`StartupTask.cs`), a favicon or a feed fetched.

**Off the dock's thread** (a meeting's fallback, the Wi-Fi dialog's thread, a sign-in's browser, a jump list task's
fallback) the closing is posted to the dock (`Launch.WM_KARPO_LEAVE`, kept through a modal loop like the other posts,
`Dock.Deferrable`): the dock's windows are never touched off its thread, and a folder closing then gives the focus back
only where it still has it. `Aside`, `Packaged` and `Toast` close on the dock's thread before their own threads start, and
those threads call the shell directly (`Launch.Shell`, which only the launcher and the toast's roads name).

Tests (`LaunchTests`, Windows stood in for by `Launch.Stand()`, per flow — nothing is opened):
`EveryLaunchClosesWhatIsOpenFirst` (all twelve ways: "leave" then the launch, once), `TheCallerHearsWhetherItOpened`,
`WindowsOwnPanelsCloseNothing`, `WindowsAppsAreLaunches`, `AToastBroughtForwardLeavesOneInTheBackgroundDoesNot`,
`ALaunchClosesTheFolderArrangedOrNot`, `TheDocksClosingRunsOnItsThreadOnly`, and the corpus test
`NothingButTheLauncherStartsAnything` (no ShellExecute, Process.Start, app activation, CreateProcess, WinRT Launcher or
SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems in Karpo.Dock, Karpo.Core or Karpo.Accounts outside `Launch.cs`, each exception with its
reason); `OneFolderTests.WhatClosesTheOpenFolder` (a launch, arranged and not).

By hand: open a folder with a quick-settings line whose Settings page opens (night light before it has read), click it:
the folder closes and Settings comes to the front with the keys. Right-click a file in an arranged folder, "Open file
location": the folder closes, edit mode stays, Explorer has the keys. Open ⚙ › About, a site: the menu closes, the browser
comes up. Open the Wi-Fi list from a Windows networks button over an open folder: Windows' list opens by its own rule.

## 492. A folder's contents are a line of a folder alone: their buttons on the taskbar and the list from the bar are gone (2026-11-03)

The person: the folder contents taskbar widget is *"a remnant that is actually out of date. remove it after
confirmation"*; confirmed as the taskbar button that opens a pop-up list of a folder's files. Since §380 a folder's
contents stood on the taskbar too (`BarKind.FolderContents`): a button per item of the folder (`Dock.FolderRows.cs`,
"Show titles" saying each name), whose subfolders opened a list of their items from the bar (`PinFolderFlyout`, going
in in place since §398, its own folder's height since §468, kept between showings since §363). All of it went.

**Gone:** the bar's entry (`BarKind.FolderContents`, its `BarEntries` row; the taskbar's add list no longer offers
it), `Dock.FolderRows.cs` (`FolderRows`, `FolderRows.MostButtons`, `FolderRowButton`, `WM_KARPO_FOLDER_ROWS`, a
tile's `Entry` and `Owner`), `Dock.FolderPins.cs` (opening the list, a folder row's menu `Topic.FolderRow` with its
"Open in File Explorer", the list's place among the islands' popups, what closes for a launch, §491),
`Drives\PinFolderFlyout.cs` with its level swap (§489), `Drives\DriveWidgets.cs` (`DriveEntryRow`, its last user the
list), `PanelContent.Kept` (only the list set it), `BarKind.IsPinned` (a pin is one button again), "Show titles"
(`PinOptions.ShowTitles`, the `PinShowTitles` row, `settings.pin.titles.header` in all 30 languages), and the tests of
the list and the row (`PinFolderFlyoutTests`, `FolderRowTests`, `WindowsPinSafetyTests.ASubfoldersButtonOpeningItsListHasNoTooltip`).

**Kept:** a folder's contents as a line of a Karpo folder's list (`ListKind.FolderContents`, `FolderContentsLine`,
`FolderContentsView`), its navigation (`PinFolderNavigation`, `PinFolders`), the walk in and back (`FolderTrail`) and
the reading (`FolderReader`, `FolderSource`, `FolderWatch`), `BackHead`; a pin to a folder on the bar, which opens it in
File Explorer as every pin opens what it points at; `FlyoutHost.ShowBeside`/`BesideX`, which the menus' submenus use.

**The file.** `"kind": "folderContents"` on a bar is a word this build does not know: the entry is dropped as the file
is read, its neighbours where they were, and the file is written back once (`Config.Repair` says it changed); the same
word on a line of a folder's list reads as the line. `"showTitles"` is a word no build reads. `Config.Shape` 53. The
person's own file has two folder contents, both lines of a folder (Repositories, Documents) and none on a bar: nothing
to convert.

Tests: `FolderContentsButtonsRemovedTests` (`TheBarHasNoFolderContents`: no entry, not in the bar's add list, the line
still in the list's, no `ShowTitles`, no string; `ABarsFolderContentsAreDroppedAndAFoldersLineStays`: a bar's dropped
and written back once, a folder's line on the same bar kept with its folder and navigation, round-tripped);
`PinFolderSettingsTests`, `OptionRowsTests.APinsRowsAreItsPagesAndWriteWhatItWrites` and `PinTargetMenuTests` on the
line alone; `TypedRegistryTests` (`folderContents` a line only); `ConfigWords.txt`.

By hand: the add list on the taskbar has no Folder contents under Files; in a folder's list it has. A bar from a file
with one shows the entries beside it and no gap.

## 493. Game mode in the toggles row, and every switch Karpo flips with it (2026-11-03)

The person: *"game mode on and off should go into the toggle widget, see if you forgot another toggle as well"*. Game
mode was a toggle widget of its own since §117's "Game mode, color filters and mono audio", but the toggles row did not
offer it: fifteen toggles at the largest text were more than the six rows a new line had then, and the row was to be
reconsidered first. It never was, and nearby sharing, keep awake (§269) and dark mode (§403) joined the row since without
that question, so the row now offers everything it should.

**The rule** (`TogglesRowSwitchesTests.EveryWidgetThatFlipsIsAToggleOfTheRow`): every widget whose click flips what it
stands for (`WidgetInfo.Flips`) is a toggle of the row too, once, its own switch behind both (`Toggles.All`,
`ToggleSwitches.For` → `QuickSwitches.For`, the same `SwitchData` key "switch:GameMode"). There is no second
implementation: a row's game mode is switched through the Settings handler and followed in `GameBar`
`AutoGameModeEnabled` as the widget is (`SettingToggle`), and the magnifier, the narrator and sticky keys through the
accessibility tools (`AssistiveSwitch`). A widget added later that flips something fails the test until the row has it.

**The audit**, every on/off Karpo can switch (`QuickSwitch`) against the row:

| Switch | In the row | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode, mobile hotspot, energy saver, night light, do not disturb, VPN, rotation lock, spatial sound, sound, microphone, nearby sharing, keep awake, dark mode | already | — |
| **game mode, color filters, mono audio, magnifier, narrator, sticky keys** | **added** | each a toggle widget (`Flips`) the row lacked; color filters and mono audio are tiles of Windows' quick settings' accessibility page, the magnifier, the narrator and sticky keys its switches too |
| live captions, accessibility, cast, project | no | not a switch: Windows says no app whether they are on, and a click presses a shortcut or opens a page (§117) |
| location, mobile data, camera and microphone privacy, HDR, transparency, focus | no | Karpo has no switch for them; a toggle is one existing switch, not a new one |

They are offered in the row's picker (Toggles shown ▸ the rest, after dark mode, in that order), named and drawn as their
widgets are ("Game mode", the gamepad; the "on/off" stays the add list's), lit while on. A new row's six are unchanged
(`Toggles.Default`, Windows' first row and do not disturb), and so is Windows' quick settings preset's row. In a row, color
filters turn on in grayscale: the filter is a widget's card option (`SwitchOptions.ColorFilter`), and a row has no card per
toggle, as spatial sound's format and keep awake's time there are their defaults too.

The file: six new words of `"toggles": { "shown": [...] }` — `gameMode`, `colorFilters`, `monoAudio`, `magnifier`,
`narrator`, `stickyKeys` — so the shape is raised by one (`Config.Shape`, `ConfigWords.txt`); an older Karpo leaves such a
file alone.

Tests: `TogglesRowSwitchesTests` — the rule above; each new toggle by its file word is its widget's switch, glyph, name
and source, round-trips and is not on a new row; a row of game mode, sticky keys and the magnifier, clicked, writes
`AutoGameModeEnabled=0` through a made-up handler and turns the made-up sticky keys and magnifier on (nothing on this PC
read or changed). And `TogglesAndActionsTests`, `OptionRowsTests`, `OptionMenuTests`, `MenuRulesTests`,
`KeyboardSweepTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`. Pictured in `list-form-toggles-<dark|light>.png` ("Every toggle, wrapped", 21
of them, six rows at 225 % text, and "Game mode and the accessibility switches").

By hand: a toggles row's menu ▸ Toggles shown: game mode, color filters, mono audio, magnifier, narrator and sticky keys
are offered; add game mode, click it: Settings ▸ Gaming ▸ Game mode follows, and the game mode widget on the bar too.

## 494. A markets widget in another currency; an amount owned shows its worth first (2026-11-03)

The person: *"for the markets widget you should be able to override the currency in which the stock for example is
shown, it should then lookup the conversion in the background of course and do the currency conversion for you"* and
*"when i enter the amount owned in the markets widget it should actually show the total amount instead of the single
stock price. the places of the two values should basically be swapped."*

**The setting** (`MarketOptions.Currency`, `"currency"` in a `market` record, line and face alike; shape 53). A share's
and a coin's menu has **Currency** (`MarketRows.Currency`, Scope, after Amount owned): "As listed (USD)" — the listing's
currency as its search named it, "As listed" before anything does — or any currency the rates reach (`Currencies.Codes`,
the converter's list), searched by code or by name in Karpo's language or English (`MarketRows.CurrencyFinder`, ICU's
names): as listed first, ticked where nothing is chosen, then the region's, the world's most traded and the rest
(`Currencies.Ordered`). As listed is not written; a code nobody offers reads as listed (`MarketMoney.Kept`). A rate has
no such row: its figure is a rate between the two currencies it tracks (`MarketOptions.ShownIn` is empty for it). One
home: each markets line and face tracks one symbol, so the currency is that item's; no folder-wide default (it would be
a second place saying the same, R15).

**The rate** (`MarketExchange`, `Karpo.Dock\Markets`). One more question to the same store — the listed currency in the
shown one over a day, `"currency:USDCHF 1d"`, by a rate's routes (Yahoo direct, inverse, through the dollar, then the
ECB) — so it is fetched in the background, kept in `markets.json`, asked again on the widget's interval and shared with
any widget asking the same pair; the store wakes the widget when it comes (`MarketStore.Use`'s `wakes`). The listed
currency is the price's once one has come, else what the search named (`MarketMoney.Listed`), so the rate is asked
beside the first price. Drawing never waits: **until a rate has come the figures stand as listed**, in their own
currency; a rate of another pair is never used.

**The conversion** (`MarketReading.Of(…, rate)`, `MarketQuote.Times`). Every figure is the listed one times the rate —
the price, the closes, each chart point with its open, high and low — so the chart, the candles and the last point read
in the shown currency and the change in per cent is the same. London's pence, Johannesburg's cents and Tel Aviv's
agorot are hundredths of their currency (`MarketMoney.Whole`): the pound's rate, a hundredth of it. A price shown in
another currency is written to that currency's minor unit (`MarketMoney.Places`: 512.00 CHF, 96,152 JPY, 1.234 KWD) and
under one with as many figures as it needs (0.3360 CHF); a sum of money too (`MarketHoldings.Figure`, `Money`), as
listed or not. The widget shows no change in money and no day range: the percentage is its only other figure, and it
stays.

**An amount owned: its worth first.** With an amount owned the main figure is what it is worth (the amount times the
price, in the shown currency — "5,120.00 CHF"), and the price of one moves to where the worth stood
(`MarketHoldings.Each`: "10 shares × 512.00 CHF" with room, "512.00 CHF" with less) — the worth on the line's first row
with its currency, the price of one at the third row's end or in what-it-is's place. The face never offered an amount
owned; it shows whatever the reading's main figure is. Without an amount owned nothing changes.

**Hovering** (`MarketReading.ExchangeTip`): a line shown in another currency says its main figure in both and the rate,
"512.00 CHF (640.00 USD × 0.8000)", then with an amount owned "10 shares × 512.00 CHF" (a stale price's words after
them, §77); the face's screen-reader words add the same. Shown as listed, a line says no more than it shows.

Strings (all 30 files): `settings.widget.market.currency.header`, `.listed`, `.listedAny`, `.placeholder`, `.notFound`.

Tests: `MarketCurrencyTests` (a quote's code as a whole currency; the factor or none; each currency's decimals; what the

## 495. Brightness on several displays: one errand at a time per display, the newest level, confirmed by a read back (2026-11-03)

The person (2026-11-03): *"sometimes when chaning the brightness fast not all of my displays can keep up, sometimes one
of the two will then just stay at a lower or higher brightness, i know this is probably not really our fault but try to
mitigate this in a reliable way, not just something that plasters over or glues it together somehow."*

**Why a display stayed behind.** The worker already sent each display only its newest level, one display after
another. But for every write it read the display back *at once*, and believed the answer whatever it said: a monitor
rounds and may refuse, so "it says 61" was taken for "it took 61". DDC/CI (VESA's DDC/CI 1.1) has the host wait 50 ms
after a Set VCP Feature before its next message; a monitor sent one sooner may drop it without a word — `SetVCPFeature`
says it went, the monitor never applies it. So during a fast drag the read back came inside the rest, and the next write
came right after that read: the monitor dropped the drag's last level, the read back said the level before, the worker
took that for the monitor's own rounding and forgot the level asked. Nothing ever sent it again. A write that failed
outright (`SetVCPFeature` false: a monitor waking, a handle gone stale after a dock blip) was forgotten the same way, and
a display whose first probe missed was "no way" until the displays changed.

**The design** (`ScreenWrites`, pure; `Brightness` drives it on its one worker thread):

- *Asking records, nothing more.* The slider, the wheel and the keys call `Brightness.Set`, which records the level per
  display and wakes the worker. The slider shows the level asked (`Brightness.Asked`) until the display has it.
- *One errand at a time per display, the newest level.* A display with a write or a read on its way is sent nothing
  more; when it comes back, the display rests (`IScreenMachine.Gap`: 50 ms for a DDC/CI monitor, none for a panel set
  through WMI), and then it is sent the newest level asked. Every level in between is skipped. The errand whose rest is
  over first goes first, so a fast panel is never held behind a slow monitor's rest. An errand's news counts only while
  it is its display's errand on its way (by identity): a late or repeated report changes nothing.
- *Confirmed, not hoped.* Once nothing was asked or written to a display for 300 ms, it is read back. The level asked,
  or what the display shows for it (`IScreenMachine.ShowsFor`: a monitor whose luminance runs to 20 shows 37 as 35; a
  panel whose WMI levels are tens shows 37 as 30 or 40, whichever its driver takes): done. Anything else: sent again
  after 200 ms, then 400, then 800 — four writes in all for one level asked. No guessing at a display's steps from its
  answers: two dropped writes in a row would look like a step. No answer to the read back: read again (200, 400, 800 ms),
  never written again since it took the level, and after three the level asked stands.
- *Bounded, and said.* A display that refuses four writes, or answers another level after four, or never answers, is
  left alone for that level and said once in karpo.log (`brightness: \\.\DISPLAY2 asked 37 4 times, still at 20`); not
  again until it takes a level. A new level asked starts afresh. The slider then shows what the display last said.
- *Stale handles.* A refused write or an unanswered read forgets that one display's way in (`IScreenMachine.Forget(screen)`),
  so the next try opens its physical monitor afresh. `ScreenMachine` also keeps a floor under every DDC/CI command — never
  within 50 ms of the last to the same monitor (`Rested`, by HMONITOR, so a handle opened again is the same wire) — for
  what `ScreenWrites` does not see: the probe that reopens a handle right before a write.
- *Looks stay out of the way.* A display being got to a level is not read for a look (the pointer, the widget coming
  into view, Windows' brightness news): its own read back is what it shows. A look at any other waits out its rest.

**Timings and why.** 50 ms rest: the DDC/CI standard's own figure; a monitor that needs more is caught by the read back,
which comes in the quiet. 300 ms quiet before the read back: long past any monitor's rest and a panel's fade, short enough
that a display left behind is put right before the person looks for it. 200 ms doubling: a monitor waking or busy gets
1.4 s across the three retries, and a drag's end costs at most four writes per display, never a loop.

Tests (`ScreenWritesTests`, a made-up clock and made-up displays — slow, needing a rest, dropping what comes too soon or
at random, refusing, never answering): `AFastDragEndsWithEveryDisplayAtItsLastLevel` (a panel and a monitor, a level every
8 ms: both end at the last, nothing inside the monitor's rest), `AMonitorThatNeedsMoreRestIsCaughtByTheReadBack` (the
person's case), `DroppedWritesNeverLeaveADisplayStaleWithoutAWord` (200 drags, a third of writes dropped: each display at
the last level or said), `ALateOutcomeCannotWin`, `ADroppedWriteIsReadBackAndSentAgain`, `ADisplaysOwnStepIsWhatItTook`,
`ADisplayThatKeepsRefusingIsSaidOnceAndLeftAlone`, `ADisplayThatNeverAnswersKeepsTheLevelAsked`,
`NothingGoesBeforeTheRestOrTheQuiet`, `DisplaysFoundAgainForgetTheGoneAndSendAgain`; `BrightnessTests` through the worker:
`ADroppedWriteIsReadBackAndSentAgain`, `ADisplayThatKeepsRefusingIsSaidAndLeftAlone` (its handle forgotten each try),
`ADisplaysStepsAroundALevel` (`ScreenMachine.Between`, `Raw`, `Percent`).

By hand: with the laptop panel and an external monitor, drag the brightness slider fast back and forth for a few seconds
and let go: within about half a second both displays are at the slider's level (check the monitor's own OSD). Spin the
wheel over the bar's slider quickly: the same. Switch the monitor's input away and back, or unplug and replug it, then
drag: it follows. Turn DDC/CI off in the monitor's menu while Karpo runs, then drag: the panel follows, and karpo.log has
one line for the monitor.

## 496. Days ahead: the agenda lists as many days as it is set to (2026-11-03)

The person (2026-11-03): *"for the agenda you should be able to set how many days into the future it should show
events."*

**Where it was.** Since 2026-10-05 the agenda listed a fixed week, today and the six days after
(`CalendarIsland.AgendaDays`, a constant 7), every event of each, scrolling where the line holds fewer. It had been a
setting before ("Show events for", `daysAhead`, a day to a month), taken out then on the person's word that a calendar
should list what its view shows; the agenda's view now has a length of its own again, the person's to set.

**Now.** The agenda's menu has **Days ahead** (`OptionRows.CalendarDaysAhead`, what of it it shows, `OptionSlot.Scope`):
a stepper with its unit (R3) — "− 7 days +" — from **1** (today alone) to **60**, a week where nobody set it, so every
agenda shows what it showed before. Today counts as the first day: 7 is today and the six after, as it always was; the
agenda lists every event from now to the midnight that ends its last day (`CalendarIsland.Upcoming`, `Agenda`), an
event of several days under each of its days within them and none after. The stepper is §456's: every number of its
range in its unit (`OptionUnit.Days`, "1 day", "60 days"), so its buttons stand still as it steps; held, it steps on.
A day picked in the folder's month is still that one day's list.

**Only the agenda.** The day's events (`events`) show one day — the folder's day or today — and the day, week, month
and year views show the days their view names; a number of days ahead means nothing there, so they have no such row
(the record is the widget's, kept across its styles, `WidgetStyles.Keeps`, so a style changed and changed back keeps
it).

**The data is there.** The calendars are read, and kept in calendar-cache.json, from last month to the start of the
thirteenth month ahead (`PimCache.Window`), far past 60 days on any day; and asking the store for a range widens what
is read (`AccountCalendars.Want`), so a line asking for more than has been read would still get it. The most is 60
rather than a year so that a list a person scrolls stays a list, and stays well inside what is read without reading
more: nothing new is fetched for it.

**The file.** `calendar.daysAhead` on the agenda's line, a whole number held to 1–60 (`CalendarOptions.KeptDaysAhead`);
absent, or 7, is a week and is not written. Shape 54. "Days ahead" joins the glossary (R7). Words in 30 languages
(`settings.widget.calendar.daysAhead.*`, its value a count of days, ".one"/".other").

Tests (`AgendaDaysAheadTests`, a stand-in calendar and a fixed now, no server):
`TheAgendaListsTheDaysItIsSetToAndNoneAfter` (1, 7, 14, 23 and 60 days: the event past the last day out, the one on it
in, the store asked from today's midnight to the horizon's and no further), `AnEventLongerThanTheDaysIsListedUnderTheDaysWithinThemAlone`,
`TheWindowReadHoldsTheMostDaysAheadOnEveryDay` (`PimCache.Window` on every day of three years, any zone),
`AnAccountsEventFarAheadIsThereForTheLargestAskingLine` (a stand-in account's event 55 days ahead: listed by an agenda
of 60, not by one of a week), `TheFileKeepsTheDaysAheadHeldToItsRange` (round trip, clamped, a week not written),
`TheRowIsAStepperOfDaysThatWritesTheOption` (the row, its range and unit, "+" writes 8, "−" back writes none, no row on
the day's events or the day view); `OptionRowsTests` (the option has its row, and the row writes it), `RepairTests`
(an older file's 99 held to 60, no change counted), `CalendarAgendaTests` (a week where nobody set it).

## 497. Compact rows say their detail at the end; now playing is two lines as the clock is; Windows' glyph buttons wear a face's icon (2026-11-03)

The person (2026-11-03): *"sunrise widget and sunset widget and other widgets in this category should also show the
more detailed information in the compact view as well. i think it could fit on the right side still. (e.g. in how much
time the event is.)"* — *"the now playing widget in the taskbar widgets should also be two rows like the default time and
date taskbar folder face"* — *"the snipping tool taskbar widget icon seems too big"*.

**A row's detail (`RowSpec.Detail`), one rule of the kit.** What a row says of time — how soon, how much is left, till
when — is its detail. `LineRow.Draw` places it: under the name as the caption where the row is three cells tall and has
no caption of its own (where it has one, that one says it); on one row at the row's end, before the reading, in the
Body's size and the secondary ink, on the name's line, ending a gap short of the reading. It stands there only where the
name keeps all of its words beside it: where the row is short the detail is the first thing left out, the name and the
reading kept. A row with a detail is a captioned row's height (`LineRow.Height(style, row)`). Worn by:

| Widget | One row (Compact) says at its end | Its taller form under its name |
|---|---|---|
| Sunrise, Sunset | "in 16 h 56 min" | the same |
| Daylight | "5 h 2 min left" / its change since yesterday | the same |
| Solar noon | the sun's height, "42°" | the same |
| Tides (one row) | "High in 3 h 13 min" | which way, the next turn, its height and how soon |
| Alarm (set or snoozed) | "Rings in 6 h 22 min" / "Snoozed until 7:10" | its caption ("Rings in … · Today") |

Dawn and dusk have no note, so nothing more; the sun's arc and day bar on one row already name the next event with how
soon ("Sunset in 3 h 10 min"). The sun's times drew their note only where the row held a caption (`Caption = fits ?
note : null`); the tides' and the alarm's one row left theirs out.

**Now playing on the bar: the clock's two lines.** The now-playing face set its title over its artist only where two
lines fit at the bar's main text size with 2 px of air (`MediaIsland.TwoLines`: a 44 DIP bar up), while the time-and-date
face steps down the text's sizes (main, secondary, small) with 1 px — so on the person's 42 DIP bar the clock was two
lines and now playing one. Now both take their lines from one rule, `DateTimeFaceDrawing.TwoLines` (the clock's plan,
lifted out): the same size, the same lines' height, the block in the middle of the bar, both lines in the text's ink as
the clock's; the title over the artist, or over the app it plays in where the track has no artist; one line ("title ·
artist") where the clock keeps one; the art or the note where it was. 36 DIP bars and up at 100 % text are two lines.

**Windows' glyph buttons at a face's icon size.** *The root cause:* the scene drew every glyph button — search, Task
view and the five of `BarEntries.IsWindowsButton` (the Snipping Tool, Settings, the pen menu, the touch keyboard, the
virtual touchpad) — at a Start-row button's 20 DIP in a 24 DIP box (`Scene.ButtonGlyphDip`), scaled with the bar, where a
face draws its icon at the taskbar's own icons' size (`Fit.Glyph`: 16 DIP on a 48 DIP bar); §490 moved Windows' menus to
faces but left the five on the glyph. Now those five draw at `Scene.FaceGlyph` (`Fit.SystemIconFor` of the bar's cell, the
very size an icon face's glyph is) in a box their own size, as Show desktop's already did; a missing Snipping Tool's
warning badge sits on that box. Start, search and Task view keep Windows' own taskbar's sizes.

Tests (red first): `RowDetailTests` (the kit: the detail at one row's end and under a taller row's name, left out first
on a short row; the sun's compact times say their full form's caption at the end; the tides' one row its next turn; a
compact alarm when it rings), `SceneTreeTests.AGlyphButtonsIconIsAFacesIcon` (the Snipping Tool's and Settings' sprite
is a face's icon box at 42, 48 and 64 DIP), `MediaSizeTests.TwoLinesWhereTheClocksTwoLinesAre` (two lines exactly where
the clock has them, at its size and height, the person's 42 DIP among them), `TheTitleStandsOverTheArtistWhereTwoLinesFit`
(the artist a clock's line under the title; no artist: title over app). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`compact-details-<dark|light>.png` (`RowDetailTests.CompactDetailsSheet`), `bar-glyphs-<dark|light>-<42|48>-<100|150>.png`
(`SceneTreeTests.GlyphButtonsBesideFacesSheets`), `media-bars-*.png`, `windows-buttons.png`.

By hand: set Sunrise to Compact in a folder: "in … h … min" stands before its time. On a 42 DIP bar the media folder's
face is the title over the artist beside the clock's time over its date, the same size; the Snipping Tool and Settings
stand at the clipboard face's icon size.

## 498. A folder's contents in File Explorer's views: large icons, medium icons, list, details, tiles (2026-11-04)

The person (2026-11-03): *"the folder contents widget should also get different styles like grid, details etc.
(similar to the ones in the file explorer)"*.

**Where it was.** A folder's contents line (§380, `FolderContentsLine`, `FolderContentsView`) showed its items one
way: a row each, the kind's icon, the name and, where the line had room, the date, a subfolder's chevron.

**Now.** The line's menu has **View** (`OptionRows.PinView`, Look): File Explorer's own views in its View menu's order
and words, each its own glyph (R3, R13; `OptionGlyphs.FolderViews`): **Large icons**, **Medium icons**, **List**,
**Details**, **Tiles** (`PinFolderView`, `PinFolders.Views`). List is what every line was and stays the default.

  * **List**: unchanged.
  * **Details**: under the folder's row a row of column names (Name, Date modified, Type, Size) and a hairline, both
    staying while the items scroll (`IListScroll.ScrollHead`, `FolderContentsView.Head`); a compact row an item
    (`LineRow.Compact`): its 16-DIP icon, its name, and as many of the columns as the width keeps beside a name of at
    least 120 DIP (the date first, then the size, then the type), across in Explorer's order, the size against the
    trailing gutter. A medium folder shows Name, Date modified and Size; a wide one all four. The date is the region's
    short date and time; the size Explorer's ("673 KB"), none for a folder; the type the shell's name for the kind
    ("Microsoft Excel Worksheet", "File folder"), else "PNG File" from the extension, else "File".
  * **Tiles**: a 48-DIP picture beside three lines: the name, the type, the size (a folder its type alone); as many
    tiles across as 220 DIP each go into the width (one in a medium folder, two in a wide, three in the widest).
  * **Medium icons** and **Large icons**: a grid of 48- and 96-DIP pictures, the name under each in two lines at most,
    centred, as many across as 84- and 124-DIP cells go into the width (four and two in a medium folder).

One column (list, details, a narrow line of tiles) lights its items as bands edge to edge (§425); more than one lights
a cell's rounded plate, as Explorer does, the cells touching so every pixel of the grid is an item's; the keys' ring
(§470) goes round the plate. A name cut short says itself whole as the tooltip. One layout (`FolderBoard`) is still
what is drawn and what a press, the hover sweep and the ring are tested against, in every view.

**Everything else as it was, in every view.** A click opens the item, a subfolder going in in place where the line's
navigation says so (§398), the back head and Backspace going back; the right click is the line's menu with the folder shown's "Open in File
Explorer"; the line is as tall
as its own folder's items laid out in its view at every level (§468), scrolling under its head where it is held
shorter (§461), the item the keys came to brought into sight (in a grid, its row of cells).

**The keys.** Up and Down walk the items; in a grid (more than one across, `FolderContentsView.Grid`) Up and Down go to
the item above and under, Down into a shorter last row its last item, and Left and Right walk the items (the other way
round where mirrored); past either end the folder's keys move on (§471). Outside a grid Left (Right mirrored) goes back
as before; Backspace goes back in every view.

**Thumbnails.** A picture or a video (jpg, png, gif, webp, heic, mp4, mov and the like, `FolderThumbnails.Shows`) in
tiles and icons wears the shell's own thumbnail (`IShellItemImageFactory`, thumbnail only, `Items.Thumbnail`), its
kind's icon until it comes. Never asked on the dock's thread: a cell drawn asks (`FolderThumbnails.Of`), and the reads
go one after another on the folder source's run (a thread of its own, COM up), the newest wanted first, at most 64
waiting; the line is drawn again as each comes. Only the cells drawn ask, so a folder of thousands of photos reads the
dozen it shows. What is read is kept, its file's time in the key, up to 16 MB, the longest unseen let go first; a file
with none is kept as an answer and never asked again.

**What is read.** A view asks for its icons at its size (twice its DIP, so any scale is a picture scaled down) and, for
details and tiles, the kinds' type names, one question of the shell a kind, no disk touched (`Items.TypeName`,
`FolderReader.Types`); files' sizes come with the listing. Changing the view reads the folder again for it, what it
shows staying until the read comes back.

**The file.** `pin.view` on a folder's contents line: `"largeIcons"`, `"mediumIcons"`, `"details"`, `"tiles"`; absent
is the list, which is not written. A word this build does not know reads as the list; a pin never carries one
(`WidgetItem.Normalize`). Shape 57. Words in 30 languages (`settings.pin.view.*`, `dock.folder.details.*`,
`dock.folder.type.*`).

Tests: `FolderViewsTests` (UI; `EachViewLaysOutItsItems`, `TheKeysWalkAGridInTwoDimensions`,
`AViewReadsItsIconsAtItsSizeAndItsTypes`, `ThumbnailsAreReadOffTheDocksThreadAndKept`,
`AViewScrollsUnderItsHeadAndKeepsItsRootsHeight`, `EveryViewIsPictured`: folder-views-*.png, each theme at 100 and
150 %); `PinFolderSettingsTests.TheViewsAreExplorersAndTheFileSaysOneOnlyWhereChosen`;
`OptionRowsTests.APinsRowsAreItsPagesAndWriteWhatItWrites`; `ConfigWords.txt`.

## 499. One part for everything on the bar: the Folder buttons merged into the Taskbar widgets; a font changed is drawn everywhere at once (2026-11-04) — the font a value of every look since §507 (2026-11-05): a widget's its own, the menus' their layout's Widgets in folders'

The person (2026-11-03): *"folder buttons and taskbar widgets should generally be combined in the style settings and not
have separate settings for both of them."* And: *"changing the font does not change anything."*

**Where it was.** §459 gave a style five parts, two of them for the cards on the bar: **Taskbar widgets** (a widget's
card) and **Folder buttons** (a folder's face — the tray's, the clock's, quick settings' — and, since §490, Windows' own
menus' faces). Each had its own colours and pattern (§462), its own level in a style's editor and its own resolution
(`WidgetLooks.PartOf`, `PartSpec.Part`, `Look.Part(style, part)`), so a bar's group of widgets and folders wore two sets
of colours, and a patterned group was not one sheet across a folder's face.

**One part.** `StylePart.FolderButtons` is gone: the **Taskbar widgets** dress everything on the bar, each on its card —
every widget, every folder's face, Windows' own menus — as the layout's style and as each one's own (`Look.Part(own)`,
`Scene.LookOf`; a line in a folder still wears Widgets in folders). A style has four parts: **Taskbar**, **Taskbar
widgets**, **Folder panel** (an outline, §464), **Widgets in folders**. Its editor has those four levels and no other
(`BarLooks.EditorRows`); a widget's Appearance and a folder's **Face style** offer the same swatches (the style's Taskbar
widgets), the Face style still a style of the folder's own, its Flyout style unchanged. A group's pattern is one part's,
so a group of widgets and folders is one sheet (§462). `WidgetLooks.PartOf`, `PartSpec.Part` and every path that chose
between the two went with the part; nothing special-cases a folder's face's colours any more.

**Ours, merged.** Graphite, Paper and Harbor had the same colours in both parts: nothing changes on their bars. Bloom's
folder buttons were a berry of their own (#F7CFDE / #5C1E47) beside peach widget cards (#FFF3EA / #31173A) that barely
stood off its peach bar (#FFE4D6); merged, every card on Bloom's bar is the berry, its text #4A1530 / #FFE3EF and accent
#B0204F / #FF7AA8 — the part that gave Bloom its character, and the one standing clearer off the bar. Text is 4.5:1 and
the accent 3:1 on it in both modes (`StyleTests.OursReadAsDesignedInBothModes`).

**The font: why nothing changed.** Karpo's text is measured and drawn in one text style, `Gfx.Typeface`. It was set once,
when the dock started (`Dock`'s constructor), from the style the default layout wore — and never again: a font picked in
a style's editor was saved and the bars were built again (a font is no colour, so not `Dock.Recolour`), but every bar,
folder and menu was measured and drawn in the font the dock had started with. And had it been set, the bar's kept
elements, a menu's kept rows and the edit bar's buttons were kept by signatures without the font, so a font alone would
have redrawn nothing. The person changed a font; nothing changed until Karpo was started again.

**Now.** The font is part of the look the dock reads: `Look.Typeface`, set by `Look.Configured` (`Dock.ReadLook`) from
`Styles.KarposText(config)`. A font changed is another look, so `Dock.Rebuild` sets `gfx.Typeface = look.Typeface` before
anything is built; the bar's kept elements (`Scene.Element.Typeface`), a menu's rows (`Flyout.MenuSig`), the edit bar's
buttons (`EditDeck.ButtonSig`) and the tooltip's words are kept by font, so all of them are measured and drawn again in it
at once, and open folders and menus are dressed again as for any look. The measuring caches were already keyed by font
(§459).

**Which font is in force.** One for all of Karpo: the font and weight of the style the **default layout** wears
(`Styles.KarposText`, `KarposTextId`), on every bar of every layout, every folder and every menu. Each bar in its own
layout's style's font was weighed and not done: `Gfx` measures with one typeface, and much is measured and drawn outside
any one bar's build — a menu's row lit or opened, the tooltip, ⚙'s menus, the edit bar, a folder's line updating on its
timer —, so a font per layout would need a typeface carried through every one of those paths (or a Gfx per layout), and a
path that missed it would draw one bar's text in another's font; one font also keeps every row and card on the kit's one
ramp (§388). A widget or a folder wearing another style takes its colours, not its font, as before. So that a font
picked is never silently not used: in a style's editor the **Font** and **Weight** rows of every style the default
layout does not wear say on their second line *"Not in use: Karpo's text is in the font of Follow Windows"* (the name of
the style that is; `settings.appearance.styles.fontNotWorn`). A choice row's second line (`OptionRow.Detail`) was never
drawn (`OptionMenu`); it is now, as on every other kind of row.

**The file.** `appearance.styles[].light|dark.folderButtons` is gone; a file that has one reads it as nothing and writes
it no more (no migration). Shape 57. The person's own file is converted once with
`karpo-coord\convert-styles-merge.py in.json out.json`: a mode's `folderButtons` moves whole to its `widgets` where the
mode has none, and is dropped where it has one (the Taskbar widgets win), each key that said something else reported as a
conflict; a mode, or an override of ours, left saying nothing is taken out. The person's file (shape 52) had no
`folderButtons` anywhere: converted, it is the same file at shape 57, read with no repair.

Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.folderButtons` deleted; `settings.appearance.styles.fontNotWorn` new; 30 languages.

Tests: `StyleTests.OnePartDressesEverythingOnTheBar` (four parts; a widget, a folder and a Windows menu dressed by the
layout's style's Taskbar widgets, then by their own's; no `folderButtons` written, one read as nothing),
`StyleTests.KarposTextIsTheDefaultLayoutsAndAChangeOfItIsAnotherLook` (Follow Windows' font changed is another look on
every layout; another style's font changes none; the default layout put in Paper, Paper's font and weight are Karpo's),
`StyleMenuTests.OnePartOnTheBarAndTheFontInForceSaid` (four levels in every style's editor; the note on every other
style's Font and Weight, drawn on the menu's row, none on the style in force), `StyleMenuTests` (a face's and a widget's
swatches alike), `StyleTests.EachIsDrawnInWhatItWears`, `WindowsFacesTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests` (shape 57, the words).
Live (`KARPO_UI_TESTS=1`): `SceneTreeTests.AFontChangedIsDrawnAgainEverywhere` — a real bar with a folder open over it
and the style's editor beside it, the default layout's bar and another layout's in Graphite; Follow Windows' font changed
to Georgia as the person changed it, the look read and the Gfx set as the dock does, the bar, folder and menu updated
where they stand: every line drawn again is in Georgia, as many as before, none left in Segoe UI Variable, and Georgia
measured as itself. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `font-change-<default|other>-<before|after>.png`, and §459's, §462's and
§464's style and pattern pictures with the one part.

## 500. Cut-off words say themselves whole; the selection's shortcuts act on all of it, through an open menu too; the top row is icons alone again (2026-11-03)

The person (2026-11-03): *"when hovering over text that is partially hidden (like when i search for vanguard ftse all
world etfs for example) i would like the tooltip to show the text after hovering for a while over it."* — *"when
selecting multiple widgets ctrl x does not work. maybe other shortcuts wont work too."* — *"remove the text under the
menu row icons again, it should also not be configurable to show again."* — *"when the context menu is open i should
still be able to perform the same keyboard shortcuts like cut copy etc."*

**Cut-off words, one rule** (`Karpo.Dock\CutWords.cs`). A line is cut where DirectWrite trimmed it at the room it was
given, its ellipsis drawn (`CutWords.Trimmed`: the first line's `isTrimmed`); nothing else decides it, so no widget says
it of itself. Two ways in, both the kit's:

- **Painted lines** (a folder's lines, the bar's faces) go through the kit's two places that draw a line,
  `TextLine.Draw` and `PopupPaint`'s text (one line, and `Wrapped`'s lines, whose last ends in an ellipsis where the whole
  did not fit). While a host paints a surface the pointer can rest on it listens (`CutWords.While`): every line drawn cut
  is remembered with its whole words and its box in the painter's coordinates (`CutRun`). The folder keeps each line's
  (`FolderFlyout.cutRuns`, by its widget), the bar each cell's as it is painted whole (`CellIsland.CutAt`); the pointer's
  point is looked up in them (`CutWords.At`, the last drawn on top). A mirrored line's box is its unmirrored one, as the
  pointer is mirrored back into it (`FolderFlyout.CardSpace`).
- **A menu's rows** (`Flyout`) draw their words once and keep them, so they ask the rule as a row is laid out
  (`Gfx.Cuts`): the row's words, and what it is set to, cut short are kept on the row (`Row.Cut`) — a search's results
  among them, the markets' *"Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF…"*.

The tooltip is the host's own — the menu's, the folder's, the bar's — after Windows' hover time, as their buttons' are.
Where a part has a tooltip of its own (an icon button's name and shortcut, a status icon's, a line's own) it keeps it,
the whole words on its first line above (`CutWords.Said`). The bar has no tooltips on its faces otherwise (§367); the
cut words are the second exception after the status icons. In an arranged folder the cut words show too.

**The selection's shortcuts act on all of it** (`EditKeys.OfTheSelection`: Delete, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+A,
Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y). They acted on the widget the bar's focus was on, which a press leaves there: after a lasso or a
Ctrl+click that selected others, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C and Delete took that one alone. Now the keys are on
`EditSelection.KeysOn`: the widget they walked to (every selected one where it is one of them), else every selected
widget, else the one pressed. A press on the dim gives that display's bar the keys, so a lasso's selection is in their
reach. One path does them all, `Dock.SelectionAct`: the bar's keys, an arranged folder's (one
`FolderFlyoutAction.Selection` carrying its `EditKeyAct`), a menu's Cut and Remove, a pin's Remove, and a key a menu passes
on. The menu's Copy keeps its own (a copy of the selection on the pointer and the clipboard, §220); Ctrl+C on the bar puts
the selection on the clipboard with the marching ants, as before.

**Through an open menu.** A menu open in edit mode hands the selection's shortcuts it has no row for (Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z,
Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+A, and Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Delete in a menu without those buttons) to the dock and closes, as a row's choice
closes it (`Flyout.PassesKey`, `FlyoutEventKind.PassedKey`); the dock gives the key to the folder standing open arranged,
else the bar with the keys (`Dock.KeyFromMenu`). A row's own shortcut still chooses its row; a field keeps its keys; at
rest a menu keeps every key.

**The top row is icons alone again.** §481's names under the top row's icons, `Flyout.ButtonNames`, `NamedWidth` and the
56 DIP row are gone, and with them **⚙ › General › Show names in the top row** and `topRowNames` (`Config.TopRowNames`):
the buttons are their 40 DIP squares, their names and shortcuts in their tooltips, with nothing to turn them on again. A
file's `topRowNames` is read past and left out when written. Shape 57 (`Config.Shape`, `ConfigWords.txt` written again).
Its words in 30 languages are gone; `TransferSummary` no longer names it. R2's room is the 40 DIP row's again.

Tests: `CutWordsTests` (the tooltip's words; the cut line under a point; a line painted cut through `PopupPaint` and
`TextLine` heard with its box, one that fits or has no room to be cut at not; a menu's row cut says its words whole and
an icon button keeps its own; a markets line's Vanguard company cut in a folder's list heard whole; a bar face remembers
what it drew cut by its cell), `SelectionKeysTests` (the seven shortcuts; the keys on the selection, not the widget last
pressed; Ctrl+X with several selected cuts them all; every way to the acts is one; an open menu passes them on),
`EditHistoryTests`, `FolderEditClickTests`, `FolderLineRemoveTests`, `KarpoMenuGeneralTests.TheTopRowHasNoNamesAndNoSwitchForThem`,
`MenuRulesTests`, `MenuLookTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`, `WidgetItemTests`.

## 501. A member's gap between the widgets of a group; the air's day runs left to right (2026-11-04) — each widget its own card, no group card, since §512 (2026-11-05); no groups, the one widget's gap (`Layout.WidgetGap`), since §515 (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-04): *"give the individual taskbar widgets some space as well between them."* and *"the graph on
the air quality widget goes from right to left in time but should go from left to right in time."*

**A member's gap** (`Layout.MemberGap`, 4 DIP: Windows 11's room between two of its taskbar buttons' plates, scaling
with the icon as the groups' gap does, never under 2 px — 4 px at 100 %, 5 at 125 %, 6 at 150 %, 8 at 200 %; 6 DIP
since §506, 6, 9 and 12 px at 100, 150 and 200 % on the 48-DIP bar). It is the
room between any two widgets that stand together, which until now stood flush:
- two members of a group on an islands bar (§54, `Layout.Between` for `Together`);
- two widgets of one dock's panel (the floating look, `Connected`), which was one flush band;
- two app buttons of one part — the open apps, a pin's windows, "…" after the last (`Layout.TileGap`, 0 before) — so a
  pin and its running app still take the same room, as §54 holds (`AppButtonTests.RunningAppsKeepTheRoomPinsKeep`).

The groups' gap (6 DIP, `PartGap`; 14 since §506) stays between groups, beside a separator (none since §511) and between docks, so a group still reads as
one; the tray's icons and the status icons stay touching inside their one widget (Windows' own, the person 2026-10-08).

*(§512: no more. Every widget wears its own card in its own rectangle, its background, outline and pattern its own; a
group reads as one by its gaps alone, and a card pattern still runs on through it, drawn inside each card. The member's
gap stays. What follows of the one card and its pieces is gone.)*

*(§515: no groups on the bar at all. The member's gap is the one gap between any two neighbours of a section
(`Layout.WidgetGap`, `MemberGap` before), a bare corner and a search box too; the groups' gap is gone (`PartGap`,
`IslandGapDip`), 14 DIP stand only between two sections (`Layout.SectionGap`); a card's pattern is a sheet of its own.)*

**Groups keep their one card** (§54, §311): the person's word there was that a run of widgets with nothing between them
is one group on one card. Each member's piece of that card now runs on over the member's gap after it to the next
member's card (`Layout.CardPiece`, which Scene's card pass places), so the card is still one with no seam and the bar's
own background shows nowhere inside a group (§464's cut-out follows the pieces); only the plates under the pointer, the
widgets' content and their pressed shrink stand apart — and, where the style draws no card, each widget's plate at rest
(§506), under its group's card piece. A widget with a card or an outline of its own (§311) runs on into
nobody, as before: its card is its own and the gap beside it is the bar's.

**Patterns** (§462): a group is still one sheet, laid from its first card's corner (`Layout.GroupStart`); the pieces now
cover the gaps, so the sheet runs on through them unbroken.

**The pointer** (§160, the person: *"the clickable area of the widget should actually go all the way out ... to the next
widget of course"*): a gap belongs to the widgets either side of it, each up to its middle, as every gap on the bar
already did; only the drawn plate stands apart. **Edit mode**: the "Add" line inside a group stands in the gap's
middle, and at a group's end half a member's gap out, where the new member's gap will be (`Layout.InsertionRect`); a
carried block's drop slots are the widgets' middles, as before.

**The air's day** (`AirReading.HoursOf`, `AirQualityTile.Hours`). The real answer was checked: Open-Meteo lists the
hours earliest first from the place's midnight, in its own time (`utc_offset_seconds`), and Karpo read them in that
order; nothing mirrored them. What ran backwards was the axis: the bars were the next 24 hours from now, "Now" first, so
each hour every bar moved one place to the left and the day ran from right to left. They are now the place's day on the
weather's own axis (DayGraph, midnight to midnight): a bar an hour where its hour of the day is, the hours gone quiet,
the hour now whole and ringed with "Now" under it, a time under every sixth hour where that leaves it room. An hour keeps
its place all day and now moves on from left to right, as the weather graph's mark does. An answer of another day has
none of today's hours and draws none (the line keeps its rows above).

No config change.

Tests: `WidgetGroupTests` (`AGroupsMembersStandFourDipApart` at 100, 125, 150 and 200 % in both looks, since §506
`AGroupsMembersStandSixDipApartAndGroupsFourteen`;
`AGroupsCardRunsOnOverItsGaps` on all four edges; the pins and the open apps a member's gap apart; the Add line in the
gap), `SceneTreeTests.AGroupsCardRunsOnAcrossItsMembersAndStopsAtItsEnds` (on the real tree each piece runs on over its
gap and meets the next), `IslandCardsTests`, `BarStyleTests`, `FloatingBarTests`, `AppButtonTests`, `AppOverflowTests`;
`AirQualityTests.TheDayRunsLeftToRightAndNowMovesOnToTheRight` (Zürich's and New York's answers through the place's day:
the bars the same 24 hours from its midnight, rising to the right, now 0, 6, 13, 18, 23), `AReadingSaysTheIndexItsLevelAndThePlacesDay`.
Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `SceneTreeTests.BarGapSheets`, `bar-gap-<dark|light>-<100|150>-<plain|dots>-<rest|hover>.png`
(Start, two pins and three open apps, a spacer, a group of three widgets, a divider and a widget alone, on cards of their
own colour, bare and dotted, a group's middle widget lit); `app-group-*`; `air-lines-*` (the day at twenty past two: the
morning quiet, now ringed, the rest to come).


## 502. A divider carried shows its line; the wheel over a stepper steps it (2026-11-04) — a ghost shows the room it will take, no line, since §505 (2026-11-05); no bar separator since §511 (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-03): *"when pasting a divider on the taskbar there is no proper preview, it just moves an empty
space around"*, and *"scrolling over the rows height widget should actually change the value too."*

**A separator's ghost was empty.** Where a carried block would land the bar shows a blue ghost (`Scene.ShowGhost`),
and it was the carried block's rectangle (`Layout.BlockRect`) with nothing on it. A separator's block is its line and
the room either side, a few px, or none at all where Appearance gives it no room; in edit mode the separator is drawn
as a line in the middle of a wider zone it is taken hold of by (`Layout.GrabRect`). So a separator pasted, added or
dragged showed a thin empty ghost sliding along the bar, never the line it is. A folder's divider was worse: lifted,
it was its plate alone, its rule hidden (`FolderFlyout.Raise`), and its ghost the room it takes.

**Now one drawing for both.** Where a separator's line stands in edit mode is the layout's (`Layout.EditLine`, moved
from the scene, and `Layout.InkRect`, the one painter's line, `SeparatorInk.Ink`, §307): the bar draws its separators
from it (`Scene.ComposeSeparators`), and where a carried block would land (`Layout.Landing`, one carried here or
several together — pasted copies follow together, `Dock.EditSelect.Paste`) says the lines of the separators among it
there (`Landed.Inks`), which the ghost shows over it in the separators' colour; a block dragged along its own bar
shows its own line moved with the ghost. The ghost is the size edit mode draws the block at (`Layout.GrabRect`: a
widget's block as before, a separator's zone), and so is what the carry window shows of it, held by its middle
(`Dock.Follow`, `GrabIn`). In a folder a divider lifted takes its rule with it on its carrier, where it stands on its
card (`FolderPlan.Inks`), and back to its place when it lands; its ghost — round its grab (`FolderPlan.Grab`) — shows
its rule where it would land. Whatever the separators' style: a line, room alone or nothing, as edit mode draws every
separator as a line. A divider of None (§416) was not lifted at all: its card takes no room, its plate's outline
came out smaller than nothing, the compositor refused it, and the folder showed its "landing" bar alone; its plate is
held to nothing now (`FolderFlyout.Raise`), and it is carried as the others are. A widget's ghost is as it was.

**The wheel over a stepper steps it.** It scrolled the menu, or did nothing in one that does not scroll. Now the wheel
over a stepper — its "−", its value or its "+" (`Flyout.StepperWheel`) — sends what its buttons send: up its "+",
down its "−", the same Adjust, so the same limits and the same undo as a press, and the buttons stand still as ever
(§456). A notch is a step (`Flyout.WheelNotch`, WHEEL_DELTA): a fine wheel's or a touchpad's small turns add up to one,
a turn the other way starts again, and one message steps once at most. At its limit the wheel does nothing there, and
the menu does not scroll under it. Every stepper — the height's rows, every number's, time's and length's — but not
AM/PM's switch, which a turn would flip back and forth. Anywhere else in the menu the wheel scrolls as before.
A line's menu stands its height rows still at its foot (§276); scrolled, the foot's rows had their bounds moved with
the scroll but not their stepper's buttons (`Flyout.PlaceContent`), so a press on "−" or "+" of a scrolled menu, and
the wheel over them, missed. A row standing still moves whole now (`Row.Shift`, its buttons and tools with it).

Tests: `SeparatorGhostTests` (new; Line, Space and None, along the bottom, the top and the left, 100 % and 150 %: a
separator carried here lands as the line a bar with it there draws, inside its ghost, the ghost its grab; several
together a line for each separator; a widget none; at rest a spacer draws none), `SceneTreeTests`
`ACarriedSeparatorsGhostShowsItsLine` and `ASeparatorOfferedOrPastedWithOthersShowsItsLine` (the real scene: dragged,
offered, carried together; a widget's ghost has none, nothing carried none), `DividerCarryTests` (new; a real folder,
a divider pasted in and carried, each style: its rule on it, its ghost's rule the folder's; put down, none; pictures
divider-carry-<style>.png), `StepperWheelTests` (new: `ANotchIsAStep`; `TheWheelOverTheHeightStepsIt` at 100 % and
150 %, over its value and either button, the buttons still, half notches, its limit; `ElsewhereTheWheelStillScrolls`, a
menu too long for its room with the height's rows at its foot, scrolled: the wheel and a press on its "+" step it;
red first: neither did); `SeparatorMarkTests` (`Layout.EditLine`), `StepperSlotTests`.


## 503. Now playing on the bar is one of three widths (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"the now playing widget on the taskbar should have three fixed widths"*.

**It sized itself to its words.** The now-playing face was as long as its title and artist read now (§244), up to
about three cells of the bar's thickness (`MediaIsland.Column`), past which they were cut; "Hey" was a short face, a
long title a long one, and the bar moved as tracks changed.

**Now its width is a choice of three** (`NowPlayingFace.Width`, the face's Style row, as the meeting's, the air's and
the earthquakes' widths are): Narrow 128 DIP, Medium 192 DIP (the default), Wide 256 DIP (`NowPlayingFace.Dips`),
times the scale and the text's, so a larger text keeps the same characters. Beside Windows' own taskbar widgets — its
weather about 140 DIP, its clock about 80 — Narrow is a short title with its art, Medium a title and its artist, Wide a
long title. The width holds the art, where it is shown, and the words; whatever plays, playing, paused or nothing, the
face is that long (`MediaIsland.FaceLength`), so the bar never moves for a track. Words past their room are cut with
an ellipsis and say themselves whole in the bar's tooltip, the kit's one rule (`CutWords`, §500). Down a bar on its
side it is the art alone, as before. Its choices are named as a folder's list widths are ("Narrow", "Medium", "Wide",
the option's `Words`), in every language those are; Shift+Left and Right in edit mode step it, as every face's width
choice (`EditResize`). The words' column and the words' own length (`Column`, `FaceWords`, `IdleWords`) went.

In the file: the face's option `width`, `"narrow"`, `"medium"` or `"wide"`; none is Medium.

Tests: `MediaSizeTests` (`AWidthChoiceIsItsDips`; `ItIsItsWidthWhateverPlays`: 28, 48 and 72 DIP bars at 100 % and
150 % text, each width, the art on and off, nothing playing, a short track and a long one, one length, the long words
inside it, Narrow < Medium < Wide; side bars the art alone), `MediaPresetTests.TheFaceIsItsWidthWhateverPlays` (the
preset's folder at 150 %).


## 504. Screen time has a face (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"screen time should also have a folder face"*.

**The screen-time face** (`FolderFaces.ScreenTime`, `screenTime`; `ScreenTimeFaceDrawing`): the screen-time glyph and
how long this PC was used today, "3 h 42 min", in the screen-time line's words for a day's total
(`ScreenTimeText.Duration`). Across a bar the glyph and the words as they read (§244); down a bar on its side the glyph
over them, at the largest size the widest total ("88 h 88 min") fits across the bar, as the sun face sets its time.
It reads the one tracker every screen-time widget reads (`ScreenTimeTracker`), which counts from the dock's start
whether anything shows it or not, so a folder without a screen-time line wears it as well as one with; always
today's, whatever day the folder's lines show. Nothing ticks for it but the dock's minute, on which its Reading moves
with the total. To a screen reader "Screen time — 3 h 42 min".

It has no options, and no source row (§477): the faces that inherit their source from the folder's first line of their
kind (news, drive, sports) do so because a line's source is a setting — a feed, a drive, a team. A screen-time line
has none to inherit; there is one count, this PC's.

In the face gallery it stands with the system's faces (readings, battery, power), found by the screen-time widget's
words. The ready-made screen-time folder wears it (`Presets`, `screenTimeGroup`); a folder made before keeps its icon.

In the file: the face kind `screenTime`; config shape 61 (the now-playing width with it, §503).

Tests: `ScreenTimeFaceTests` (new: today's total from a stand-in fortnight, not yesterday's; nothing counted today
"0 min"; the ready-made folder wears it, the gallery lists it with the system's; drawn at 100 % and 150 %, across a bar
and down one: the glyph and the words inside the cell, the words after or under the glyph, "5 min" a shorter face than
"3 h 42 min" and a new Reading), `FaceWidthTests.AShortReadingAndALongOneDifferByTheirWords` (its "5 min" and
"3 h 42 min" in place of now playing's two tracks, which are one width now), `FaceGalleryTests` (the system's group),
`ConfigSchemaTests` (shape 61).

## 505. A separator is empty space: no line, no dot, no look, no setting (2026-11-05) — the bar's separator gone, a folder's divider alone, since §511 (2026-11-05)

The person: *"remove the different spacer styles. the spacers should always just be empty space and not a line or dot or
anything. remove all the settings that are related to this as well."*

**Replaces** what a separator drew — §246's line by default, §307's and §405's Line, Space only and None per surface,
§416's None in a folder, §478's choice in every style (its Taskbar's **Taskbar separators**, its Widgets in folders'
**Folder separators**) — and what §502 drew on a carried separator's ghost. Every separator, on a bar (the file's
"separator") and in a folder's list (the file's "divider"), is empty space, the same everywhere, and nothing sets how it
looks: it has no look.

**How much room** — one width per surface, nobody's setting:

| Surface | Room | Was |
|---|---|---|
| A bar | 8 DIPs either side of its middle, each in whole px (`Layout.SeparatorSpaceDip`, `Layout.SeparatorSpace`): 16 DIPs, added to the one ordinary gap it stands in | Space only's (Line's was the line alone) |
| A floating dock | none of its own: it splits the dock, the room between two docks its gap (`split` no longer adds a style's room to it) | the same under Line, the default |
| A folder's list | 3 DIPs either side (`FolderFlyout.SeparatorSpaceDip`, `SeparatorRoom`): 6 DIPs, splitting the list into two cards; two lists stand as far apart (`FolderPlan.ListGap`) | Space only's, the default (§78) |

What is a size and not a look stays: a folder's divider is still **Fixed** or **Grow** (§435, §482). Its Style row reads
**Fixed** (was "Inherited (Space only)", the look it inherited) and **Grow**; Fixed is still nothing written,
Grow `"divider": { "style": "grow" }` as before. It now stands at the divider's menu's foot under its rule, where another
widget's Appearance stands (R16). A bar's separator has nothing to set: its menu is its buttons alone (Cut, Copy, Remove),
and neither menu links to **Layout ▾** any more (§478's Layout ↗ led to the style that drew it). R16 holds for every menu
with rows; a menu of its buttons alone has no bottom to align an entry at.

**At rest nothing is drawn.** `Layout.EditLine`, `InkRect` are empty at rest; the bar composes a separator's sprite only
in edit mode (`Scene.ComposeSeparators`); a folder's `FolderPlan.Inks` are empty at rest and its dividers' marks hidden.
`LineStyle`, `SeparatorShape`, `SeparatorStyle`, `SeparatorStyles`, `SurfaceStyle.DefaultSeparators`,
`Styled.TaskbarSeparators|FolderSeparators|SeparatorsOf`, `ItemStyle.TaskbarSeparators|FolderSeparators` and its indexer,
`Styles.WriteSeparators|SeparatorsOverrideOf|DefaultSeparatorsOf`, `StyleParts.SeparatorsOf`,
`BarLooks.StyleSeparatorsRow|SeparatorsRow`, `Layout.Separators|LineRect|LineSpace|LineThickness` and the per-part
`lineSpaces`, `FolderIsland.Separators`, `FolderFlyout.Build`'s `separators`, `GrowStyle`, `Splits`, `ListGap`,
`LeastGapDip`, `SeparatorInk.InFolder` and the None and Line branches they fed are gone.

**Edit mode** still shows every separator so it can be found and taken hold of — edit mode's mark alone: on a bar a line
across it in the middle of its room (`Layout.EditLine`, a placed separator's colour and thickness; a floating dock's in
the middle of its marker over the seam), taken hold of over its room and 4 DIPs either side (`GrabRect`); in a folder a
rule two hairlines thick across its gap, taken hold of over a grab at least 13 DIPs tall. Entering edit mode moves
nothing.
*(§524: a folder's spacer is its whole room striped, the stripes moving, in place of the rule.)*

**A ghost is the room it will take.** Where a carried block would land — dragged along its bar, offered from another
surface, pasted with others — the bar's ghost is its block there (`Layout.Landing` → `BlockRect`; was `GrabRect`), for a
separator its 16 DIPs of empty space, nothing on it (`Landed.Inks`, `Scene.GhostInk`, `GhostInksShown` gone). A folder's
ghost is the lines' cards (`GroupRoom`, was their grabs), for a divider its 6 DIPs (`GhostInks`, `GroupInks` gone). The
divider lifted still carries its rule on its carrier (§502): what is carried is edit mode's, not a ghost.

**The file** (shape 61, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no migration code):

```
appearance.styles[].taskbarSeparators   gone ("line" | "space" | "none"; not read, not written)
appearance.styles[].folderSeparators    gone (likewise)
…divider.style "inherited"              now "fixed" (never written: only "grow" is)
```

An entry of ours in `appearance.styles` that said nothing but those keys says nothing now, and is dropped as the file is
read (`Appearance.Normalize`).

Strings: gone `settings.appearance.taskbarSeparators.header`, `settings.appearance.folderSeparators.header`,
`settings.appearance.line.header`, `settings.appearance.separatorStyle.space`, `settings.appearance.outlines.inherited`
(every language); the divider's Fixed is `dock.edit.height.fixedHeight` ("Fixed", a line height's). Changed in every
language: `core.widget.separator.blurb` "Empty space between widgets", `core.widget.divider.blurb` "Empty space between two
lines of a folder".

Tests: `SeparatorSpaceTests` (was `SeparatorLineTests`: its room and no cell at three scales, one gap and its room, a dock's
none, alike, `NothingIsDrawnButEditModesMark` on islands and a dock at rest and arranged, the grab zone);
`SeparatorGhostTests` (rewritten: one carried, several, a widget, each lands as its block; at rest nothing);
`SceneTreeTests.NoBarDrawsALineAtRest` (was `…NobodyPlaced`: no line-shaped sprite on a bar at rest, 4 heights × 2 looks ×
2 themes × 4 edges × 2 scales), `ACarriedSeparatorsGhostIsItsRoom`, `ASeparatorOfferedOrPastedWithOthersShowsTheRoomItTakes`,
`SeparatorSpaceSheets` (pictures `separator-space-…`, was `separator-style-…`); `WidgetGroupTests` (a separator's room
added to the gap; a dock's marker); `DockGroupsTests.ADocksSeparatorIsTheGapBetweenTwoDocks`; `SeparatorMarkTests`;
`DividerStyleRowTests` (Fixed or Grow, its whole menu in every layout; a bar's separator no rows);
`FolderSeparatorTests` (6 DIPs, two lists as far apart, `TheOpenFolderDrawsNothingForItsSeparatorsAtRest`);
`FolderFlushTests`, `FolderDividerGrowTests`, `ListFolderTests`, `DividerCarryTests` (its ghost its room, no rule on it);
`AppearanceTests.AStyleSaysNothingOfSeparators` (the old keys read as nothing, not written back; an override of ours of
them alone dropped); `StyleMenuTests.NoPartHoldsSeparators`, `AnEditorIsTheSameForEveryStyle`, `StyleTests`,
`MenuRulesTests` (R16 as above), `ConfigSchemaTests`. Gone with what they held: `StyleSeparatorsTests`, `LineRowsTests`,
`StyleSeparatorPictures`, `FlatBarOffscreenTests.SeparatorPictures`, `DividerEditLookTests`' None test,
`FolderSeparatorTests`' Line, None and per-layout style tests.

By hand: the bar at rest shows room between its groups and nothing in it; edit mode shows each separator's line;
dragging one shows a blue ghost as wide as the room it will take. ⚙ › Styles › a style › Taskbar and Widgets in folders end
in their colours. A divider's menu: Style (Fixed, Grow) at its foot; a bar separator's: its buttons.

## 506. Plates at rest: every widget a soft plate of its own where the style draws no card; faces 5, buttons 6, groups 14 DIP apart (2026-11-05) — a plate wherever no background is set (an outline alone keeps it), no group card, since §512 (2026-11-05); no groups, every two widgets 6 DIP apart, since §515 (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05), of a bar in Follow Windows with Contours on the Taskbar: *"it is kind of hard to differentiate
between the groups ... give me a few options and let me choose"*. The faces on one folder's button stood about 7 DIP
apart and two buttons about 16, the plates there were none at rest, and the right end of the bar read as one strip.
Five looks were drawn on that bar (plates, group cards, spacing alone, pills, outlines); the person chose the first,
the plates. The study (`LooksStudy`, its pictures and switch) is gone; its numbers are the constants below.

**A plate at rest** (`Scene.RestPlate`, `Scene.RestPlateAlpha`). On a bar of cards (the islands look, `Layout.Cards`)
every widget and every folder's button whose style sets no card colour and no card outline of its own wears a soft
plate: its text's colour at 9 % (the person, 2026-11-05: "make the plates a little bit more visible"; 6 % first, about Windows' hover), its card's rectangle
(`Layout.CardRect`, else its block) rounded all round in the cards' corners (`Layout.CardRadius`) — its own, never run
on into its neighbour, so each widget stands apart. It is drawn as the highlight is, over the bar: no hole is cut in
the bar for it (§464's cut-out is filled cards' alone) and the bar's pattern runs on under it. It stands under the part's
piece of its group's card (§501), which is drawn as ever and wears the card's pattern where the style has one (§462).
- **The style's colours win**: a card colour (any, 0 % too) or a card outline, the bar's or a widget's own (§311,
  §405), is that card, as ever, and no plate. Nor in high contrast, on a connected or floating bar, a search box
  (its own plate, §325), a bare corner, or a separator (none since §511).
- **Arranged** (edit mode) there is none: edit mode's wash is the block's surface (§246), not a second one over a plate.

**One surface, drawn stronger** (the person's §464: *"no stacked surfaces"*). Where the pointer lights a widget whole
— a folder's button, a widget lit as its card, Start, Task View — the highlight lays nothing over its plate
(`Scene.ShadeOf` is clear there); the plate itself takes the shade (`Scene.LightPlates`, `PlateShade`): the rest
colour with the highlight's shade laid in (`FolderFlyout.Blend`), hovered or pressed (pressed fainter than hovered, as
Windows' are, both stronger than at rest), over Windows' brush transition. A folder standing open (§376) is the plate
with the open plate's fill laid in, the open plate drawing only its edge over it; lit too, the lift over the focused
plate (`HoverOnActive`) is laid in on that. A button within a widget — a tray icon, a status icon, an app button —
lights its own cell over the widget's plate as it lit its cell over the card. The keys' focus rectangle goes round what
the pointer lights, in its corners (`Scene.LitShape`, shared with `Dress`), so round a widget's plate in the plate's
corners, where it went round the item in the highlight's softer ones.

**The rhythm**:
- **faces on one button** 5 DIP apart (`FolderIsland.Between`, `FaceGapDip`; about two fifths of a glyph before, 10
  DIP on the 48-DIP bar). A notification icon is a face (§275): the tray's step is its icon and this, 21 DIP on the
  48-DIP bar (24 before);
- **a button's ends** never under 8 DIP (`FolderIsland.Ends`, `EndsDip`; 6 before): the faces stand inside their plate
  with room round them;
- **two widgets of a group** 6 DIP apart (`Layout.MemberGapDip`, §501's member's gap; 4 before), app buttons too;
- **two groups** 14 DIP apart (`Layout.IslandGapDip`; 6 before).
The gaps scale with the icon as ever (`U`, never over their DIP): on the person's 42-DIP bar at 150 % faces and buttons
stand 8 px apart and groups 19.
