*(§515: no groups. Every two widgets of a section 6 DIP apart (`Layout.WidgetGapDip`), a bare corner and a search box too;
14 DIP (`Layout.SectionGapDip`) is the least room between two sections alone.)*

**Kept**: §160, a click in a gap is the nearest widget's, each up to the gap's middle — the plates are drawn apart, the
room to a click is not. §501, a group is one card, its pieces running on over the member's gaps, its pattern one sheet:
where the style draws a card, as before; where it draws none, the group's unfilled pieces are still placed (a card
pattern of the style's runs on over the gaps), and the plates stand apart under them.

No config change.

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.AWidgetWithNoCardWearsAPlateThatLightsStronger` (new; dark and light: each widget its plate in its
card's rectangle at 9 %, no hole cut; hovered and pressed the plate stronger and the highlight clear, its neighbour at
rest, back at rest when the pointer goes; open stronger with the open plate's fill clear, open and lit stronger still;
arranged, none), `AStylesCardWinsOverThePlate` (new), `ThePersonsBarWearsRestPlates` (new; the person's bar's end: every
folder its plate, the buttons a member's gap apart, faces no further apart than buttons, groups more than twice that);
`WidgetGroupTests.AGroupsMembersStandSixDipApartAndGroupsFourteen`, `TrayCellsTests` (the tray's step), `FaceWidthTests`,
`FaceSlackTests`, `FolderFacesTests`, `MediaRowTests` (the ends), `StatusIconColourTests`, `BarMenuTests`,
`SeparatorLineTests` (the gaps). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `rest-plate-<rest|hover|pressed|open|edit>-<dark|light>.png`,
`rest-plate-card-dark.png`, `rest-plates-<100|150>.png`, `rest-plates-150-<hover|open>.png`.

## 507. No styles: a look is values, the layout's in four sections, every widget's its own over them; the painter copies a look (2026-11-05) — one set in both modes, no "Different in dark mode", each palette light and dark since §509 (2026-11-05) — one look, Karpo's Appearance, no layout's or widget's own, since §567 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-05, an interview): *"the styles are too complicated. styles should not exist anymore, everywhere where
we use styles there should be the values to configure yourself again. for the widgets there should be a styles painter /
copier with which i can copy the styles to other widgets."*

**Replaces** the styles of §459 (a named style, ours four and Follow Windows overridden, the person's made, copied, named
and deleted), §464's style a layout wears and a widget's, a folder's Face style and Flyout style, §467's ⚙ › Styles and
every style's editor, §485's "Styles ↗" under each choice of a style, and §499's one font for all of Karpo. Nothing of
them is left: no list, no picker, no override, no copy, rename or delete, no link (`Styles`, `Styled`, `ItemStyle`,
`StyleColours`, `StylePartColours`, `Appearance`, `Worn`, `WidgetLooks`, `FolderSides`, `KarpoMenu.Styles`,
`BarLooks.StyleRow|StylesLevel|EditorRows|PartRows|PatternRow`, `OptionLink.Styles`, `EditEntry.Styles`,
`OptionRow.ChoiceLink`, `OptionPlace.Together`, `KarpoServices.Dark`, `Dock.ShowMadeStyle` are gone).

**A look** (`LookValues`, Karpo.Core\Looks.cs) is values: a background, an outline, a text and an accent colour (each
Windows' own while unset, a colour with its opacity, or None — §459's `Paint`), a pattern (§462), a font and a weight
(§459's `TextStyle`, its ramp `Weights` and `Families` as ever), one set used in both modes — or, with **Different in
dark mode** on, a second set (`Dark`) drawn while Windows is dark. Turned on, the dark set is made of the one set as it
is, so nothing changes until one of them is; turned off, it is gone. *(§509: no second set, no Different in dark mode:
one set in both modes; `LookColours` folded into `LookValues`, `LookSet` gone.)*

**The layout holds the default look** (`TaskbarLayout.Looks`, `LayoutLooks`), in four sections (`LookPart`, §459's parts):

| Section | Values | What it dresses |
|---|---|---|
| Taskbar | background, outline, pattern | the bar |
| Taskbar widgets | background, outline, text, accent, pattern, font, weight | every card on the bar: a widget's, a folder's face, Windows' own menus' faces (§490) |
| Folder panel | outline | an open folder's outline (§464: it has no panel); §514 **Flyouts**, every flyout a widget opens |
| Widgets in folders | background, outline, text, accent, pattern, font, weight | a folder's lines, and every menu and flyout of Karpo's (§464), their font too |

A section's value left unset is Windows' own (Follow Windows' look, as it was). **Every widget has a look of its own**
(`WidgetItem.Look`): a widget on the bar, a folder's face and a widget in a folder, with the values of the section it is
of (`Looks.PartOf`: a line's Widgets in folders, everything on a bar the Taskbar widgets), a folder's face the outline of
its open flyout besides (`LookColours.FlyoutOutline`, over the Folder panel's). A separator and a divider have none
(§505). **One resolver** (`Looks.Over`): the widget's value, else its layout's section's, else Windows' own — value by
value, the font and the weight too (`Looks.Item`, `Looks.FlyoutOutline`). Nothing of a folder's own reaches its lines.
"A card colour is set" (§506's plates) is the part's background as resolved: its own or its section's.

**Fonts per scope.** The font is a value like a colour, so text is measured and drawn in the font of what it belongs to:
`Gfx.Typeface` is put on for each while it is measured or drawn (`Gfx.Wearing`, a scope that puts the one before back) — a
widget's in its look's (`Look.Part` and `Look.Line` carry it; `CellIsland` wears its `IslandStyle`'s or `TileStyle`'s
look's font in every way in: measuring, drawing, redrawing on its timers, hit-testing; `Layout.Measure` measures each part
in its own), the bar's own text (an app's label) in its layout's Taskbar widgets' (`Scene.Update`, `Layout.Measure`), a
menu's in its layout's Widgets in folders' (`Look.MenuTypeface`, `Flyout.Open`; a widget's own menu stays in it, not in
the widget's font), a folder's chrome in the same. What no scope wears — Karpo's own chrome, the edit bar, the tooltip —
is in the default layout's menus' font (`Look.Configured`, set on the Gfx by `Dock.Rebuild`). Every cache of a measure or
a surface was already keyed by the font in force (§499), so a font changed anywhere is measured and drawn again where it
shows, and a widget's look changed is another look (`Look`'s `Typeface` and `MenuTypeface`).

**Menus.**
- **Layout ▾ › Look ›** (`LookRows.LayoutRow`, between the bar's rows and Behavior, where Style stood): **Taskbar ›**,
  **Taskbar widgets ›**, **Folder panel ›**, **Widgets in folders ›**, each the look editor; ruled off **Apply palette**;
  its foot **Reset all** (the layout's look cleared: Windows' own throughout). The right click on the bar has it too (R15).
- **The look editor** (`LookRows.Editor`, the one builder for every look): Font, Weight (where the section has text);
  its colours (`OptionPickers.Paints`: what an unset value comes to first, "Default" for a section, "Layout" for a widget,
  its swatch), Pattern, a folder's face's **Flyout outline**; ruled off **Different in dark mode**; with it on, ruled off,
  "Dark background" and the rest; a widget's ruled off **Reset all**, last (R11: the one name of a reset). *(§509: no
  Different in dark mode and no dark rows; each colour's swatch in its row's icon's place.)* An unset choice
  says what it comes to: a section's "Default (Segoe UI Variable)", a widget's "Layout (Sitka)".
- **A widget's Look ›** (`LookRows.WidgetRow`, `OptionMenu.LookRows`) stands where Appearance stood, at its menu's foot
  under Height. A folder's is the same in both its menus (§481), its face's and Folder ▾'s: its face's values and its
  flyout's outline, which shows while the folder stands open; it is their foot (R16). A separator's and a divider's menu
  have none.
- **R1**: the layout's Look › goes a level deeper than three (a section's colour's picker is its fourth): the person
  allowed it (`MenuRulesTests.DeepAllowed`: "Layout ▾ › Look" and the bar's right click's, §467's "⚙ › Styles" gone;
  `Allowed` empty). A widget's Look › is within three.

**The painter** (Karpo.Dock\Dock.EditLooks.cs). **Copy look** and **Paste look** are buttons of every widget's edit-mode
menu's top row after Copy (Segoe Fluent's Brush and Paste; none on a separator), Paste look greyed while no look is
copied, and the keys **Ctrl+Shift+C** and **Ctrl+Shift+V** (`EditKeyAct.CopyLook|PasteLook`, `MenuChord.CopyLook|PasteLook`,
which now say and match Shift: Ctrl+Shift+C is no Ctrl+C). They are the selection's acts (`EditKeys.OfTheSelection`,
`Dock.SelectionAct`): on the bar, in a folder standing open arranged, and through an open menu, which hands them on as
Ctrl+V (§500). Copy look copies the widget it is on — the menu's, the one the keys walked to, else the one last clicked —:
its own values alone (`Looks.Copy`: both sets — §509: its one set —, font, weight, patterns, a face's flyout outline), nothing of its layout's.
Paste look puts it on the widget it is on, or every selected widget where it is one of them (as Delete acts): each one's
look replaced whole, what the copy does not say back to the layout's (`Looks.Paste`); bar ↔ folder alike, a flyout outline
from a folder's face to a folder's face alone. One change (`Dock.PastedLook` → `Dock.Apply`), one step of edit mode's
history to undo.

**The palettes** (`LookPalettes`): §459's four designed looks — Graphite, Paper, Harbor, Bloom, with §464's cards and
§499's Bloom, unchanged — are palettes now. **Apply palette** writes one's values into the layout's four sections once —
both modes, its fonts and weights — replacing what they said (`LookPalettes.Apply`); nothing links back: a value changed
after is the layout's, and the choice ticks the palette only while the sections say exactly its values ("Custom"
otherwise). Follow Windows is Reset all. A layout preset (§472) is made in its palette's values (`LayoutPreset.Palette`).
*(§509: each palette is two, its light one and its dark one, each one set; "both modes" no more.)*

**The file** (shape 63, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no reading of the old shape — the person's file is converted
once by the coordinator):

```
appearance                       gone (styles, their overrides: not read, not written)
layouts[].style                  gone
layouts[].looks                  new: { taskbar?, widgets?, folderPanel?, folderWidgets? }, each a look
islands[..].appearance           gone (a widget's, a folder's face's style)
islands[..].panelAppearance      gone (a folder's Flyout style)
islands[..].look                 new: a widget's, a face's, a line's own look (a folder's lines' too)
a look                           { font?, weight?, background?, outline?, text?, accent?, pattern?, flyoutOutline?, dark? }
                                 colours "#RRGGBB" | "#AARRGGBB" | "none"; pattern a §462 word or "none"; font, weight §459's;
                                 dark { background?, outline?, text?, accent?, pattern?, flyoutOutline? }, there (even {})
                                 while Different in dark mode is on (§509: gone, shape 64); flyoutOutline a folder's face's alone; each section
                                 only what it has (taskbar: background, outline, pattern; folderPanel: outline)
```

Strings: new `settings.look.header|layoutOf|darkMode|applyPalette|custom|flyoutOutline|darkFlyoutOutline`,
`dock.menu.copyLook|pasteLook`, `dock.keys.shift`; gone `settings.appearance.theme.windows`, `settings.nav.appearance`,
`settings.appearance.styles.header|add|newName|newNameNumbered|copyName|deleteConfirm|fontNotWorn|darkColours|mixed|
faceStyle|flyoutStyle|layoutStyle|layoutStyleOf|noOutline`; 30 languages ("Shift" a cap's name, as "Ctrl").

Tests: `LookTests` (new: the resolver, value by value, the dock's fonts per scope; a folder's flyout outline; what each
section has; Different in dark mode; the file; the palettes read as designed and are written in once, Reset all; Paste
replaces with the source's own values; bar ↔ folder and the flyout outline folder to folder; a selection pasted as one
change, one undo; the painter's keys and buttons), `AppearanceTests` (the bar's opacity its Taskbar section's; the file
keeps each layout's looks and no appearance; the menus wear their layout's lines), `PatternTests` (a pattern a look's
value), `LayoutPresetsTests` (a preset's palette), `BarLooksTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `MenuPickersTests` (the colour
picker over a section), `MenuRulesTests` (`OnlyTheLayoutsLookMayGoDeeperThanThreeLevels`, the corpus's sections dark),
`FolderMenuSidesTests` (Look › in both of a folder's menus, the one setting there twice), `KarpoMenuTests`,
`LinkRowsTests`, `EditEntriesTests`, `ConfigCoverageTests` (`layouts.looks` the layout's), `WidgetButtonsTests`,
`RestMenusTests`, `BarMenuTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `MenuLookTests` (the top row), `ConfigResetTests`,
`SettingsBackupTests` (a layouts reset resets its look), `TransferTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`, `UntranslatedTests`,
`SettingsWordsUsedTests`. Gone with the styles: `StyleTests`, `StyleMenuTests`, `StyleLooks` (now `LookShorthand`).
Live (`KARPO_UI_TESTS=1`): `KeyboardSweepTests` (every line walked, the fonts per scope in), `SceneTreeTests`'
`AFontChangedIsDrawnAgainEverywhere` (a layout's sections' font changed: its bar, folder and Look › drawn again in it),
`PalettesOnABarWithAFolderAndAMenu`, `OnlyTheFolderPanelOutlined`, `TheLookEditor`, `AFontAt225PercentText`,
`EveryColourPickedReachesItsSurfacesLive`, the pattern pictures. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `look-<palette>-<look>.png`,
`look-panel-outline-<look>.png`, `look-editor-<look>.png`, `look-text-225.png`, `look-<palette>-contours-<look>.png`.

By hand: edit mode, Layout ▾ › Look › Apply palette › Harbor: the bar navy, its widgets in Bahnschrift, the menus too.
Right-click a widget › Look › Font › Georgia: that widget alone in Georgia, its menu not. Ctrl+Shift+C on it, select three
others (one a folder's line), Ctrl+Shift+V: all three in Georgia, their own colours gone; Ctrl+Z: all three back. A
folder's Look › Flyout outline › a colour: its open flyout outlined in it, other folders not. Look › Taskbar widgets ›
Different in dark mode, Dark background: switch Windows to dark: the cards that colour. *(§509: gone; a colour set is
the same in both modes.)*

## 508. WhatsApp's count that stayed: Windows held it, and Karpo showed what Windows held (2026-11-05)

The person: *"the notification count on whatsapp is stuck right now."* Measured read-only on this PC (WhatsApp
2.2641.101.0, closed to the tray): Windows' `wpndatabase.db` polled every 250 ms and its WAL's old page images read for
the badge rows' history, a folder watch beside it, the running Karpo's WhatsApp pins as a screen reader hears them and as
they are drawn, and, new here, **Windows' own log of its notification platform**
(`Microsoft-Windows-PushNotification-Platform/Operational`), which names every badge set (3053), every badge cleared
(3056), every push that woke an app's background task (2033) and every time toasts were taken away (3055), to the
millisecond.

**What happened.** 11:11:40 WhatsApp set its badge to 1 (a message, two toasts). 11:12:45 Karpo started and read the 1.
11:19:28 a push woke WhatsApp's background task — by every sign the message read elsewhere — and 1.6 s later toasts were
taken away (3055). The badge was not: Windows held the 1 until 11:29:41, ten more minutes, when WhatsApp cleared it.
Only WhatsApp's page sets or clears its count (§372); closed to the tray it is suspended, and a background task woken by
a push does not touch the badge. The log shows it is how WhatsApp behaves, not a moment's accident: of its badges since
11-04 13:01, six stood 18 minutes to three hours. Windows' notification platform delivered that 1 and took it back only
at 11:29:41, so Windows' own taskbar is handed exactly what Karpo showed.

**What Karpo did.** It followed the store every time it could be watched: five sets and clears while the person chatted,
each heard by the watch and none left on the pin; at 11:38, with Windows holding none, both pins said "Pinned" and drew
no badge (WhatsApp had also set and cleared one 5 ms apart, 11:35:11.557 and .562, and nothing stayed). Nothing in
Karpo keeps a count Windows has dropped: the badge is the app's newest row, read again at every write the folder watch
hears; no toast is counted per app.

**Changed:** nothing in the dock. A count WhatsApp itself leaves standing can't be told from one still meant, and
guessing (taking toasts that went as a read count) would be wrong for every app whose count is not its toasts' (Mail,
To Do). Added a test that the store's watch keeps up with a writer like Windows' own — one connection that stays open in
WAL mode, as Windows' service writes, which the earlier tests' writers did not — through a set and clear 0 to 420 ms
apart: `NotificationStoreTests.ABadgeClearedRightAfterItWasSetGoesUnderAWriterThatStaysOpen` (green before and after; a
guard, not a fix). `NotificationStoreTests` and `NotificationStoreThreadTests` green.

By hand: when the count stays, open WhatsApp's window — the page runs and the count goes, on Karpo's pin within half a
second. To never see a count that is no longer meant, set WhatsApp's "Show taskbar badge" (its notification settings) to
show only while the app is open: it clears the badge as the window closes to the tray, where nothing would keep it right.
To see who held a count, Event Viewer › Applications and Services Logs › Microsoft › Windows › PushNotification-Platform ›
Operational: 3053 "badge … is being delivered" and 3056 "Badge Notification are being cleared" for the app.

## 509. One set in both modes: no "Different in dark mode", each palette a light and a dark one; a colour's swatch where its row's icon stands (2026-11-05) — unset said "Default (…)" with what it comes to since §518 (2026-11-05) — every colour a dark and a light half again, the palettes families again, since §568 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-05): *"remove the dark and light mode difference. the app itself should still have dark and light mode
but the styles should not make this distinction. there should be presets for light and dark mode that you can apply but
there should not be any automatic switching."* And: *"the selected colors should be shown on the left side in the menus,
where others display icons and other stuff."*

**One set.** A look (`LookValues`: a layout's section's, a widget's own) is one set of values, drawn the same while Windows
is light and while it is dark. §507's **Different in dark mode**, its dark set (`LookValues.Dark`, `LookColours`, the
`dark` of the file), its rows ("Dark background", "Dark outline", "Dark text", "Dark accent", "Dark pattern", "Dark
flyout outline"), `Looks.WriteDark`, the painter's copying of the dark set and every resolver's `dark` (`Looks.Over`,
`Item`, `FlyoutOutline`, `WritePaint`, `WritePattern`, `WriteFlyoutOutline`; `LookSet` and its `In`) are gone:
`Looks.Of` is a layout's `LookPaints`, one. Nothing the person set switches with the mode. **What is left unset** is
Windows' own and still follows Windows' mode (`Look.Windows`, `ToneRules.Dress`): the app keeps its light and dark mode —
an unset bar, unset menus, Karpo's own chrome with nothing set are Windows' of the mode. (As §459 ever had it, what is
derived from a set colour — a menu's text, a pattern's ink — is read on that colour, not on the mode.)

**The palettes, light and dark.** Each of §507's four designed palettes is two (`LookPalette(Family, Dark, Design)`, one
`LookPaints` each, the very colour sets §459 designed for each mode): **Apply palette ›** lists *Graphite light, Graphite
dark, Paper light, Paper dark, Harbor light, Harbor dark, Bloom light, Bloom dark* (`settings.look.paletteLight|
paletteDark`, "{name} light", 30 languages), each its swatch. Picked, its one set is written into the layout's four
sections once (`LookPalettes.Apply`), no link and nothing switching; "Custom" where the sections say no palette's values,
Reset all Windows' own, as before. Ids `graphite-light`, `graphite-dark`, … (`LookPalettes.IdOf`); the layout presets
(§472) are Focus in Graphite dark, Planner in Paper light, Monitor in Harbor dark. Every palette reads — text 4.5:1, accent
3:1, its patterns whole — in both of Windows' modes, as either may be applied in either (LookTests, PatternTests).

**A colour's swatch where its row's icon stands.** Every colour row (`OptionRowKind.Color`: a look's background, outline,
text, accent and flyout outline, and a calendar's colour, §338) shows the colour in force in its icon's slot, the kit's
icon size (`MenuPickers.Swatch`), through the one painter of a row's swatch (`Flyout.DrawTile`, a tile not a cell — §429's
style swatches were drawn there already):
- **set** — the colour, over a checker of the quieter text's colour where it is see-through, so its opacity reads;
- **unset** — what it comes to (its layout's, Windows' own of the mode, a calendar's Automatic), quieter: smaller, inset
  3/16 of the slot each side (`FlyoutTile.Quiet`); empty where Windows decides it as it draws (its accent, which the
  menu's rows do not know), slashed where it comes to None;
- **None** — empty, its rim and a slash from corner to corner in the quieter text's colour (`FlyoutTile.Slashed`).

At the row's end, in words (§228's value; what a screen reader says after the row's name): the colour's name where it is
one of the row's (a calendar's "Blue"), else its value ("#1E3A5F", "#1E3A5F, 80%"); "None"; unset, greyed, what the unset
choice is called ("Layout", "Default", "Automatic") — `MenuPickers.Said`. §228 to §507 had the swatch at the row's end and
no icon. A choice whose choices are swatches shows the chosen one's in its icon's place too (`OptionMenu.Rows`): a look's
**Pattern** its pattern on its card, **Apply palette** the palette worn (its own icon while Custom).

**The file** (shape 64, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no reading of shape 63's `dark`: a file that has one reads as
without):

```
layouts[].looks.<section>.dark   gone
islands[..].look.dark            gone (a widget's, a face's, a line's)
```

Strings: new `settings.look.paletteLight|paletteDark`; gone `settings.look.darkMode|darkFlyoutOutline`,
`settings.appearance.styles.darkBackground|darkOutline|darkText|darkAccent|darkPattern`.

Tests: `LookTests` (`ASetValueIsTheSameInBothModesAndUnsetFollowsTheMode` new, in place of `DifferentInDarkModeIsASecondSet`;
the palettes light and dark, read in both modes, named; Apply palette lists all eight and writes one set), `PatternTests`,
`AppearanceTests` (the file's `dark` read as nothing), `MenuPickersTests` (a colour row's swatch: set, unset quiet, None
slashed, see-through; its words), `LayoutPresetsTests`, `BarLooksTests`, `DividerStyleRowTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`;
the pictures' palettes by their new ids. Picture: `look-editor-<light|dark>.png` (SceneTreeTests' `TheLookEditor`).

By hand: Layout ▾ › Look › Apply palette › Harbor dark, Windows light: the bar navy, and it stays navy when Windows turns
dark and back. Look › Taskbar widgets: Background's row starts with a small quiet swatch and says "Default"; pick a colour:
the swatch full size, its value at the row's end; Opacity 50 %: the checker shows through it; None: a slashed square.

## 510. Windows' search box keeps the same room either end: as long as its magnifier and words (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"the windows search box somehow has a different spacing left and right."* The box (Windows'
search button with Show the search box, `SearchPill`) was Windows' 220 DIPs long on the 48-DIP bar (SearchBoxButtonExtent)
whatever it held: the magnifier 11 DIPs in, "Search" 37 in, and after the words some 140 DIPs of empty box. Windows fills
that room with its search highlight's picture; Karpo has none, so the box read as lopsided. Its gaps to its neighbours were
even (a group's gap either side) and are unchanged.

**The box is as long as what it holds** (`SearchPill.Length`): the words 37 DIPs in, then the same 11 DIPs after them as
before the magnifier (`SearchPill.EndDip`, Windows' SearchBoxIconMargin; the far end kept 16, SearchBoxTextMargin, before),
never over Windows' 220. In proportion on every bar as before (the 48-DIP bar's 38.4-DIP card). The words are measured as
they are drawn (`SearchPill.WordsPx`: `TextLine.Lay` in the layout's font and text size, `Layout.Measure`), so another
language's placeholder or another font sizes the box to it; a longer one than 220 DIPs takes is cut as before. "Search" in
Segoe UI Variable makes it about 91 DIPs on the 48-DIP bar. The plate, its highlight, the keyboard's ring and the press are
the box's slot as ever (`Layout.SearchBoxed`), so they follow it. A vertical bar still shows the icon alone.

No config change.

## 511. No separator on the bar: groups are sections, a floating bar's docks are its sections (2026-11-05) — no groups at all since §515 (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"for the taskbar widgets remove the spacer widget completely."*

**Gone** is the bar's separator — the file's `"separator"` island, `BarKind.Separator`, the add list's "Separator" in
Popular for a bar, its catalogue entry (`WidgetInfos.Separator`) — with everything that was its alone: its room
(`Layout.SeparatorSpaceDip`, `SeparatorSpace`), edit mode's mark and grab zone (`Layout.EditLine`, `InkRect`, `GrabRect`,
`SeparatorGrabDip`, `SeparatorUnder`, `Scene.MarkFor`, `SeparatorMark`, `MarkBrushes`, `ComposeSeparators`), a floating
bar's marker over the seam (`Layout.markers`, `Parted`, `SpacerBetween`, `split`), the gap shared round it (`LineSide`),
the one kind outside cells (`WidgetSize.Line`, `WidgetSize.InCells`, `BarKind.InCells`), the one kind with no card
(`Scene.WearsCard`), its chosen colour on the bar (`Scene.Tokens.Separator`, `ChosenSeparator`), the bar's half of the
painter (`SeparatorInk.ForPlaced`, `Thickness`, `SeparatorLook`; `Ink` lies across a folder's list alone), its menus, its
place in the licence's free kinds, and its words in every language. It can no longer be added, pasted, carried or read.
**A folder's divider stays** (the file's `"divider"`, `ListKind.Divider`): Fixed or Grow (§435), empty space, its rule in
edit mode (§505); `SeparatorInk.Hairline` is the panel's hairline (was `ForPanel(scale).Thickness`), and the divider's
glyph is its own.

**Groups.** A group is a run of a section's widgets with nothing between them (§54) — and now nothing placed parts a run:
a section's widgets are one group, a member's gap (6 DIP, §506) apart on one card. A group ends at its section's end, and
beside a part that stands apart: a bare corner (§302) and a search box (§325); between two groups, two sections' or
beside one standing apart, the groups' gap (14 DIP). The rule is `Layout.Together` (both `Groupable`, on a bar of cards)
and `Between` (a member's gap in a group and on a floating bar, the groups' gap else), nothing else. Faces on one button
stay 5 DIP apart (§506).
*(§515: no groups at all. `Together`, `Groupable`, `Between`, `Joined` and `GroupStart` are gone; every two neighbours of
a section stand a widget's gap apart, a bare corner and a search box too, and 14 DIP stand between sections alone.)*

**A floating bar** (`BarStyle.Floating`, §71): a section that holds a widget is one dock, and nothing splits it (§81's
separator did; its two docks a section were `Layout.Panels()`, `DockPanel`). So a floating bar's docks are its sections'
panels: `Layout.SectionPanels()` is the one answer — three, by section, empty for a section that holds nothing — and the
scene shows a panel for each that is not empty (`Scene.ShowPanels`, by section), the carried block's landing
(`Landed.Panels`) too. Its widgets a member's gap apart inside, the room between two docks 8 DIP at least, a press
between two docks the desktop's (`PanelReach`); a widget reaches to its dock's ends (`Layout.Reach`, its neighbours its
section's).

**The presets** (§174, §472): a new bar has no separator after the tray nor before the clock (`Sections.DefaultLayout`:
the tray, the input buttons, the status icons, the keyboard, quick settings, the clock, show desktop, one group); the
layout of every ready-made folder (`PresetLayout`) none before the system icons. Where they stood the groups' gap does not
stand: the end is one section and so one group, its widgets a member's gap apart.

**The file** (shape 65, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no migration code):

```
layouts[].islands[].kind "separator"   gone: a kind this build does not know, and the reader drops the entry
```

Strings: gone `core.widget.separator.title|blurb|keywords` (every language). The divider's own words
(`core.widget.divider.*`, "Separator") are unchanged.

Tests: `DockGroupsTests` (rewritten: each section one dock, its widgets a member's gap apart, an empty section none, a
press between two docks the desktop's, edit mode moves nothing, a block carried to another section joins its dock);
`AddListTests.TheTaskbarsAddListOffersNoSeparator` (new: no "separator" or "divider" among the bar's picks, no row named
as the divider, no widget "separator" in the catalogue; the divider a list's); `LayoutPresetsTests.NoPresetPlacesASeparator`
(new: every preset, a new config's first layout and the layout of every ready-made folder, written, say "separator"
nowhere); `LookTests` (a file's `"separator"` island is dropped as it is read); `WidgetGroupTests` (`ABareCornerEndsTheGroup`,
`AnotherSectionsWidgetPartsNothing`, the card's pieces and edit mode without separators); `SeparatorInkTests` (rewritten:
the divider's mark strong in both looks, the panel's hairline, the painter across a list); `IslandCardsTests`,
`WidgetReachTests`, `BarMenuTests`, `NarratorTests`, `TaskbarKeysTests`, `DefaultsTests`, `DefaultBarTests`,
`InputButtonsTests`, `PresetLayoutTests`, `SectionsTests`, `ResetTests`, `LicensingTests`, `TypedRegistryTests`,

`SeparatorSpaceTests`, `SeparatorGhostTests`, `SeparatorMarkTests`, `SceneTreeTests`' `SeparatorSpaceSheets`,
`EditMarkSheets`, `DockGroupSheets`, `ASeparatorIsDressedAsItsGrabZoneInEditMode`, `ACarriedSeparatorsGhostIsItsRoom`,

`DividerStyleRowTests.ABarsSeparatorHasNone`, `IslandCardsTests`' exception list.

## 512. Every look value changes the surface it names: each widget its own card, the Taskbar's outline on every bar (2026-11-05) — a card pattern a sheet of its own, no groups, since §515 (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"the widgets outline is not correct, the outline goes around the group and not the individual
widgets, same for the background color. the taskbar outline also does not do anything on the normal taskbar. stuff like
this should not be. every style setting should be properly checked so that it changes the correct thing."*

**Each widget its own card** (`Layout.Plate`, `Scene.ComposeCards`). Every widget, folder button and Windows button on the
bar (Start, Task view, search, the pins' and the open apps' parts) wears its own card in its own rectangle — its card's room,
else its block, the very rectangle and corners of its plate at rest (§506) and of its highlight — with its own background,
outline and pattern as its look resolves them (`Looks.Over`: its own values over the layout's Taskbar widgets, `TokensOf`).
Never one card round a group: §501's group card, its pieces run on over the member's gaps (`Layout.CardPiece`,
`Layout.Joined(part, alone)`), the square seams and their clips (`Scene.PlaceCard`'s bleed, `Rounded.Sides`, the cut's
square-ended holes, `Hole.Lead|Trail`) are gone. A group reads as one by its gaps alone (§506: buttons 6, groups 14 DIP);
the member's gap is the bar's. The same on every kind of bar: docked at any edge and floating (where the layout's Taskbar
widgets used to dress nothing but a widget with values of its own, `Scene.Carded`, `OwnCard`, `OwnOutline` gone).

**A card pattern** is drawn inside each card, one sheet per group (`Layout.GroupStart`: the group's first member; on a
floating bar its dock, its section, §511): it runs on from one member's card to the next as one sheet would,
the gaps the bar's, and the next group starts its own (the person's §462 rule, *"continuous between widgets inside the same
group but not between groups"*). A search box wears it too, a sheet of its own.
*(§515: on the bar every card is a sheet of its own, laid from its own corner; `Layout.GroupStart` is gone. A folder's lines
keep §462's one sheet per section.)*

**Plates at rest** (§506) wherever no background is set, its own or its section's, on a bar of cards: an outline alone
keeps the plate (it took it away before) and is drawn round it. Under the pointer and pressed it is still the one plate
drawn stronger, never a second surface.

**The Taskbar's outline** is drawn on a docked bar too, 1 DIP on its edge facing the desktop (a bottom bar's top, a side
bar's inner edge; the others are the screen's) where one is set — Windows' own docked bar has none, so unset none is
drawn; high contrast's border always. A floating bar's docks wear it round them, as before. A bar whose background is None
or 0 % (Clear) keeps its pattern and its outline (it drew neither).

**The menus' outline** is their Widgets in folders' (with its background, text, accent and font, as the section's table
says): the Folder panel's outline is an open folder's alone (it outlined every menu and flyout of Karpo's besides). *(§514: the Folder panel is the Flyouts, the outline of every flyout a widget opens — an open folder and a widget's
flyout alike; a widget's flyout is no menu.)*

| Setting | Changes | Leaves as it was |
|---|---|---|
| Taskbar › Background | the bar (docked strip, floating docks), the gaps between cards | the cards' own backgrounds, outlines |
| Taskbar › Outline | the bar's edge facing the desktop (docked); round each dock (floating) | every card, the bar's room |
| Taskbar › Pattern | the bar's room, under the plates at rest, not under a card with a background | the cards |
| Taskbar › Pattern color (§513) | the ink of the bar's pattern | the cards, their patterns |
| Taskbar widgets › Background | every widget's card, each in its rectangle (its plate at rest gone) | the gaps, the bar, its edge |
| Taskbar widgets › Outline | every widget's card's outline, all four sides | the gaps, the cards' insides (plates kept), the bar |
| Taskbar widgets › Text | the widgets' text and glyphs, the plates at rest (of the text), the app buttons' labels | the bar, the gaps |
| Taskbar widgets › Accent | what is on or chosen on the bar: a switch's on, the focused app's pill | the bar, the cards |
| Taskbar widgets › Pattern | inside every card, one sheet per group (a sheet each since §515) | the gaps, the bar |
| Taskbar widgets › Pattern color (§513) | the ink of the pattern inside every card | the gaps, the bar, its pattern, the lines |
| Taskbar widgets › Font, Weight | the bar's text (widgets, faces, app labels), measured again | the bar, the cards |
| Flyouts › Outline (§514; was Folder panel) | every flyout a widget opens: an open folder, the tray's and the app buttons' overflow, a widget's list | the menus, the lines |
| Widgets in folders › Background, Outline | a folder's lines' cards; every menu's panel and its outline; a widget's open flyout's panel (§514: not its outline) | the bar, every open flyout's outline |
| Widgets in folders › Text, Accent, Font, Weight | a folder's lines; every menu's and flyout's rows | the bar |
| Widgets in folders › Pattern | inside a folder's lines, one sheet per section (§462) | the bar, the menus |
| Widgets in folders › Pattern color (§513) | the ink of the pattern inside a folder's lines | the bar, the cards on it |
| A widget's own value | that widget alone, over its section's | every other widget |
| A widget's Flyout outline (a folder's face, the tray: what opens a flyout, §514) | that widget's open flyout's outline, over the Flyouts' | other widgets' flyouts, the menus |

No config change.

and right and floating, drawn with nothing set and with each value set in turn; the pixels of every card's four sides,

## 513. A pattern on every card, in a colour of its own: Pattern color, after Pattern (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"you should be able to set a background pattern for the folder widgets as well and also for the
taskbar widgets. the background pattern color should also be able to be set."*

**What was there.** Checked first, on the real trees at 150 %, docked and floating, with Windows' transparency and without,
with no background set (a pattern then drawn on the card's rectangle, over its plate at rest, §506; on the lines over the
folder's own ground), with a background, and on the person's own cards (background None, outlined in white, on Contours):
a pattern is settable and shows on exactly its surfaces in all five places — Layout ▾ › Look › Taskbar widgets › Pattern
(every card on the bar: widgets, Windows' buttons, folders' faces), Widgets in folders › Pattern (every line of an open
folder), a bar widget's own Look › Pattern, a folder face's own, a line's own. Nothing was missing in the drawing or the
rows. What was missing is what the person asked second: the pattern's ink was always its text's, at the pattern's low
strength (§462: 4.5 to 16 %, 70 % of that light on dark), so on a dark bar a pattern of Windows' own white was easy not to
see and could not be any other colour.

**Pattern color** (`Tone.PatternColor`, a look's colour like its background, outline, text and accent; the file's
`patternColor`, "#RRGGBB" or "#AARRGGBB"). Wherever a look has a pattern — the Taskbar, the Taskbar widgets, the Widgets in
folders, every widget's own look; not the Folder panel — it has its colour (`LookParts.TonesOf`). It resolves as every
value does (`Looks.Over`: the widget's, else its layout's section's, else Windows' own), is copied and pasted by the painter
with the rest of a look (`Looks.Copy`, `Looks.Paste`), held to what a section may say (`LookValues.Normalize`), written out
of a palette (`LookValues.Of`; no palette says one).
- **Unset**: as before — the pattern in its text's ink at the pattern's strength (`ToneRules.PatternOf(Pattern, Argb)`), made
  fainter where a text would read worse over it (§462).
- **Set**: the pattern is drawn in that colour as said (`ToneRules.PatternOf(PartPaints, Argb)`), its opacity the pattern's
  at a fully covered pixel — no strength laid over it, no cap (`PatternPaint.Fill` caps only what a swatch's boost adds) —
  and never made fainter: the person's colour, as a background is. The text is still made as readable as it can be over it
  (`ToneRules.Dress`).
- **Only its own surface**: the Taskbar widgets' colour is the ink of the cards' pattern, not the bar's; the Taskbar's the
  bar's alone (the bar's pattern took the cards' text colour where that read on it, and still does while its own is unset);
  the Widgets in folders' the lines' alone; a widget's own its card alone. With no pattern in force it draws nothing.
- **One painter**: `PatternLayer` draws every pattern, the bar's, each card's and each line's, its ink whatever the look
  resolved — no second path for a colour said.

**The row** (`LookRows.Editor`): **Pattern color** stands right after Pattern, a colour row as the others (`OptionPickers.Paints`:
its swatch in its icon's place, §509; the recent colours and the grid of the text's colours; the opacity stepped by ten),
while a pattern is in force on that look — its own or the one it comes to — and not while none is (a pattern set to None,
or none anywhere under it), as a row of what is not there would set nothing. Unset it says what it comes to: a section's
"Default", a widget's "Layout", the swatch the ink the pattern is drawn in now (its text's, faint; its layout's colour). A
colour picked keeps the opacity in force, so a first pick is as quiet as the pattern was; the stepper takes it up.

**The file** (shape 66, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no reading of an older shape):

```
a look                           { …, pattern?, patternColor?, flyoutOutline?, … }   patternColor new: "#RRGGBB" | "#AARRGGBB"
                                 a section without a pattern (the Folder panel) drops it; a value that does not read, unset
```

Strings: new `settings.look.patternColor` ("Pattern color"), 30 languages.

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.APatternAndItsColourShowOnTheCardsTheyAreSetOn` (new, `PatternSurfacePictures.cs`: the §512 bar, docked
at the bottom and the left, floating, and at the bottom with transparency; each card's inside read against the picture it
is set over: the Taskbar widgets' pattern changes every card with no background, with one and on the person's None cards,
a widget's own and a face's own that card alone, the bar's room and the gaps kept; each pattern colour changes the same
cards' insides towards its red and nothing else; the Taskbar's colour the bar's room alone; the Widgets in folders'
nothing on the bar; a colour with no pattern nothing. Red before: every colour setting, *"widgets-pattern-colour: s0's

## 514. A widget's flyout and an open folder are one thing: one look section, Flyouts, and one "Open flyouts" (2026-11-05)

The person (2026-11-05): *"open widget flyouts and open folders should be the same setting and not treated differently."*

What a widget on the bar opens on a click — a folder, or a flyout of Karpo's (a widget's list: the status icons' arrow;
the tray's overflow; the app buttons' "…") — is one thing, an open **flyout**, set once wherever a setting says how one
looks or behaves. A menu (a right click's, edit mode's, Look ›…) is no flyout and keeps the Widgets in folders' look (§512).

**One behaviour setting.** Layout ▾ › Behavior had *Open widget flyouts* (the taskbar's `look.openOnHover`, §334, §345) and
*Open folders* (the folders' `folders.openOnHover`, §346, §405) — and since every widget's flyout became a folder's line
(the dock's one table, `Dock.Flyouts`, names the folder alone) the first one opened nothing at all. Now one row, **Open
flyouts** (On click, On hover), the layout's `TaskbarLayout.OpenOnHover`: Behavior's row, and the folder room's right click
the same row (`BarLooks.Hover`, `HoverRow`). The dock's rest opens whatever the widget opens by the one switch and the one
table its click opens it by (`WidgetHover.Opens(layout, …)`, `DockWindow.OpensOnHover`, `Dock.OpenHoverFlyout`: the folder's
branch and the flyout's are one). Gone: `SurfaceLook`, `Surface`, `SurfaceLooks`, `Config.LookOf`, `OptionPlace.LookOf`,
`TaskbarLayout.Look`, `TaskbarLayout.Folders`, `BarLooks.FolderHoverRow`, `FoldersHover`, `WriteOpenOnHover`,
`SurfaceName`; the string `dock.folders.openOnHover`.

**One look section.** Layout ▾ › Look's **Folder panel** is **Flyouts** (`LookPart.Flyouts`): its outline is round every
flyout a widget opens, an open folder and a widget's flyout alike (`Look.Flyout(LookValues?)`, the one dressing of an open
flyout: no ground — it stands over the desktop, not on the bar, so it is drawn in Windows' mode as a folder was —; what is in
it the Widgets in folders, its background a widget's flyout's rows', its font the menus'). It has its outline alone, as the
Folder panel had: a folder has no panel to fill (§464), a widget's flyout's rows wear the Widgets in folders' background as a
folder's lines do. **A widget's own Flyout outline** (`LookValues.FlyoutOutline`, Look › › Flyout outline) is on every widget
whose click opens a flyout (`Looks.OpensFlyout`: its entry's `BarClick.Flyout` — a folder's face and the tray), over the
Flyouts' (`Looks.FlyoutOutline(layout, own)`); the painter carries it from one such widget to another (§507). A widget's flyout
is drawn on a taskbar flyout's surface as a folder is (`Flyout.Taskbar` → `FlyoutHost.Taskbar`, set per showing; Windows'
own overflow and quick settings are taskbar flyouts): `Dock.ShownIn` gives a flyout whose light-dismiss role is Flyout
(`RoleOf`: Island, Overflow, AppOverflow) `DockWindow.FlyoutLook(hit)`, every menu its window's look.

| What | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Open on hover | two switches: the widgets' flyouts' (`layouts[].look.openOnHover`, opened nothing since the table held folders alone) and the folders' (`layouts[].folders.openOnHover`) | one: `layouts[].openOnHover`, "Open flyouts", in Behavior and the folder room's menu |
| Outline | a folder: the Folder panel's, its face's own over it; a widget's flyout: the Widgets in folders' (a menu's) | both: the Flyouts', the widget's own Flyout outline over it (a folder's face, the tray) |
| Surface | a folder: a taskbar flyout's, bare; a widget's flyout: a menu's (WinUI's #2C2C2C dark, its rim over the material, a shadow) | both a taskbar flyout's (#242424 dark, the rim outside, a shadow only with transparency effects); a folder still bare, its lines its cards |
| Light or dark | a folder: Windows' mode; a widget's flyout: the bar's ground's (a dark bar made it dark) | both Windows' mode, their text made readable on what they are |
| Background, text, font | the Widgets in folders' for both | unchanged |
| Corner radius | 8 DIP both (`FlyoutHost.Wear`) | unchanged |
| Placement | both 12 DIP off the bar, 12 in from the work area's ends, centred on the widget; a folder's own Align (§385) a folder's option | unchanged: Align is the folder's own (a widget's flyout has no such option; Automatic is centred) |
| Coming in, going | one Motion engine, `PopupMotion.Of` (§489) for both | unchanged |
| Its own click again | closes either (`OneFolder.Closes(OwnButton)`, §430 `Openers`) | unchanged |
| Click outside, Escape | both close, each by its own light dismiss (`LightDismiss`'s Flyout role, `OneFolder`) | unchanged |
| Something launched | both close as it goes (`FlyoutHost.Close(restore)`) | unchanged |
| Keys, screen reader | each its content's: a folder's lines (Pane, a Button or Group a line), a flyout's rows (List, Menu) | unchanged: what is in them differs, not what they are |
| Edit mode | a folder opens arranged (§212); a widget's flyout does not open (its click is its menu) | unchanged |
| Height | each as tall as what it holds, scrolling past the work area | unchanged |

Left as they are: the status icons' arrow and the tray's chevron open on a click alone: a rest asks the kind whether it opens
a flyout, never the widget (`Click` does things), and both are cells of a widget whose other cells do something else.

**The file** (shape 67, `ConfigWords.txt` written again; no reading of the old shape — the person's file is converted once by
the coordinator):

```
layouts[].look                       gone ({ "openOnHover" }: the widgets' flyouts on hover)
layouts[].folders                    gone ({ "openOnHover" }: the folders on hover)
layouts[].openOnHover                new: true where what the widgets open opens on hover (either of the two above on)
layouts[].looks.folderPanel          now layouts[].looks.flyouts (the same values: { outline })
islands[..].look.flyoutOutline       unchanged; now also on the tray (any widget whose click opens a flyout)
```

Strings: new `settings.look.flyouts` (Flyouts); `settings.general.hoverFlyouts.header` says "Open flyouts" (was "Open widget
flyouts"); gone `settings.appearance.styles.folderPanel`, `dock.folders.openOnHover`; 30 languages.

Tests: `LookTests.AFlyoutsOutlineIsItsWidgetsElseTheFlyoutsSections` (in place of `AFoldersFlyoutOutlineIsItsFacesElseThePanelsAlone`:
a folder's face and the tray, each its own over the section's, Look ›'s Flyout outline on both and on nothing else),

## 515. No groups on the bar: every widget stands alone, a widget's gap from the next; the pictures taken whole (2026-11-05) — the gap the layout's Spacing (None, Small, Large), since §533 (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-05): *"every widget is just its own group / group should not really exist anymore for the taskbar
itself."*

**One gap.** Every two neighbours of a section stand a widget's gap apart (`Layout.WidgetGap`, 6 DIP: §501's and §506's
member's gap, `MemberGap` before; 6, 9 and 12 px at 100, 150 and 200 %), whatever they are — a bare corner (§302) and a
search box (§325) too, which stood the groups' 14 DIP from their neighbours. 14 DIP (`Layout.SectionGapDip`, was
`IslandGapDip`) is now the least room between two sections alone (`Layout.SectionGap`; the tests read `PartGap` before),
and edit mode's room for a section's "+". The sections are laid out and split as before; a floating bar's dock is its
section (§511). Inside one widget nothing changed: the tray's icons and the status icons touch, an app part's buttons
stand a widget's gap apart (`TileGap`). The keys move from widget to widget as before.

**A card's pattern** on the bar is a sheet of its own, laid from its card's corner (`Scene.Card` is handed no sheet); the
bar's own pattern is one sheet as ever, and a folder's lines keep one sheet per section (§462).

**Gone**: `Layout.Together`, `Groupable`, `Between`, `Joined`, `GroupStart` and `PartGap`; edit mode's Add line past a
section's last widget or before its first stands half a widget's gap out on every bar (it stood a few px out on a
floating bar and beside a part that stood apart).

**Crisp outlines.** A card's outline was seen smeared over two px in the pictures, and the cards drifting off where
`Layout.Plate` puts them, up to 3 px at the bar's far end. The bar was right: every card stands on whole px
(`IslandCardsTests.EveryCardStandsOnWholePixels`; the stroke half a px in, `EditLook.Stroke`). The pictures were not:
`PrintWindow` with `PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT` gives a window an odd number of px tall back resampled (a 1-px line drawn at
1500 px came back at 1501.4 in a 255-px-tall window, at 1503.5 at 129 px, at 1506.5 at 73; exactly at 1500 at 72, 128,
200 and 1080 px), and the 48-DIP bar's window at 150 % is 255 px tall. `WindowShots.Save` takes such a window one px
taller, the row past its foot empty, and stands it back after; `ACardOutlineRunsAllTheWayRound` no longer allows for "a
card on a half px".

No config change.

Tests: `WidgetGapTests` (was `WidgetGroupTests`: neighbours a widget's gap apart along every edge and floating; 6 DIP and
sections 14; each widget its own card; a bare corner and a search box as every widget; sections apart; the pins and the
open apps; the Add line in the gap, floating too), `IslandCardsTests` (every two neighbours a widget's gap; new
`EveryCardStandsOnWholePixels`: every plate in each section, every edge, 100 to 250 %, both looks), `BarStyleTests`,

## 516. The tray icons a tad wider: Windows' own 24-DIP slot again (2026-11-05)

The person: *"the tray icons should be just a tad more wide."* §506 had stepped a tray icon by its picture and the
faces' 5 DIP (`FolderIsland.Between`), a 21-DIP cell on the 48-DIP bar. A tray cell now has its own room between two
icons, `Layout.TrayGapDip` = 8: a 16-DIP icon in Windows 11's own 24-DIP slot, still never longer than the bar's
thickness. The icons still touch (no gap between cells); only each cell is wider. `TrayCellsTests`

## 517. Sections: the edit bar's menus side by side, one page each under headings; no forced foot; no look painter (2026-11-05) — a panel since §520 (2026-11-06) — its levels (Formats, Public holidays, Online, Karpo Pro, Back up and reset) sections of the page since §588, levels again since §594 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-05), choosing from the settings-menu study's four designs (its pictures in `docs\menu-study\`, gone with it): *"1.
sections. and additionally there does not have to be an entry all the way on the bottom as well. only if it makes sense in
terms of content."*; *"the settings in the topbar should actually be split so that it does not necessarily resemble a
breadcrumb anymore. it should be split into more logical groups like display settings (currently already done), taskbar
settings, etc... right now the split just does not make a lot of sense."*; *"remove the copy paste look functionality."*

**The edit bar** (`Dock.EditDeck.cs`, `EditDeckPlan`) is no breadcrumb any more: its menus stand side by side, no › between
them, each a drop-down with its glyph, its word and its chevron, the same words whatever the display and the layout are
called (§423), what they are of their caption on hover:

    ⠿ [⚙ Karpo ▾] | [🖥 Display ▾] [▭ Taskbar ▾] [🎨 Look ▾] [📁 Folder ▾] [🕑 Widget ▾]   [⊗ 3] [+ Add] | [↶] [↷] | [✓ Done]

| Button | Holds | Caption |
|---|---|---|
| ⚙ Karpo ▾ (accent, §366) | Karpo's own, app-wide (`KarpoMenu.Rows`) | Settings |
| Display ▾ | this display: where its bar stands, which layout it shows, the layouts, what new displays show (`LooksScope.Display`) | the display's name |
| Taskbar ▾ | the shown layout's bar: type, size, showing, behaviour (`LooksScope.Taskbar`) | the layout's name |
| Look ▾ | the shown layout's look: a palette, its four sections, Reset all (`LooksScope.Look`) | the layout's name |
| Folder ▾ | the folder open arranged: its own menu (§335, §481) | Folder |
| Widget ▾ | the widget selected alone: its menu (§352) | Widget |

Taskbar ▾ and Look ▾ are not there on a display that shows None, Folder ▾ and Widget ▾ only while they apply (§352); the
menus keep the room of all five at their widest (`EditDeckPlan.MenuMostDip`), so nothing after them moves. ⚙ says "Karpo"
now (§335 to §513 an icon alone). Undo and Redo stay icon-only. A screen reader finds the edit bar as a tool bar, its buttons
in the order they stand (`EditDeckPlan.Order`), each by its words (`EditDeck.NameOf`), its caption its help, greyed where it
cannot be pressed; Invoke does what a click does (`EditDeck.Invoked`, `DeckAccess`, `Dock.DeckAct`). §352's Layout ▾ is split
into Taskbar ▾ and Look ▾. Each setting's home is whose it is: Position stays Display ▾'s (§348: *"taskbar position should be
kept in the screen settings"* — it is set for this display, whichever layout it shows; `ConfigCoverageTests` holds that no
menu sets two levels' settings), Taskbar ▾ is the shown layout's bar alone.

**Every menu one page under small headings in a fixed order** (the Sections design), every row icon · name · what it is set to
· chevron:

    ⚙ Karpo ▾           General      Start with Windows · Animations · Animation speed · Language · Formats ›  (Follow Windows)
                        Services     Accounts › (its first) · Public holidays › (its first) · Online › (15 min)
                        Karpo        Karpo Pro › (Free version) · Back up and reset › · About Karpo › (version)
                        ─ Quit Karpo                                                    (foot)
    Display ▾           New displays   Layout (Default)
                        This display   Position (icons) · ✓ Default · Work · None ─ Add a layout
    Taskbar ▾           Bar            Type · Size (stepper) · Show
                        Behavior       Combine buttons · Window previews · Show windows from · Open flyouts
    Look ▾              Apply palette (Custom) ─ Taskbar · Taskbar widgets · Flyouts · Widgets in folders (Default/Custom) ─ Reset all
      a section, a widget's Look ›    Text: Font · Weight · Text color   Colors: Background · Outline · Accent color · Pattern
                                      (and Pattern color (§513), a Flyout outline (§514)); a widget's ─ Reset all

General › (§485) opened onto ⚙'s page; Behavior › (§400) onto Taskbar ▾'s; Look › (§507) onto Look ▾ itself, so a section's
colour's picker is a third level and R1 has no exception left (`DeepAllowed` gone). ⚙ has no "Settings" over it any more (its
button says what it is, as Display ▾'s and Taskbar ▾'s, §423). The bar's right click in edit mode is Taskbar ▾'s rows and, ruled
off, "Look ↗" and "Display ↗" (R15); an arranged folder room's Open flyouts (§514) and "Look ↗" (§423's "Layout ↗" foot). A
`OptionLink.Look` (`EditEntry.LookSettings`) lands on Look ▾; Win+Alt+Enter on Taskbar ▾.

**Values on level rows** (`OptionMenu.ValueOf`, R4): a row opening a level says what it holds — the person's own things their
first (or that there are none), a level its builder's summary (`OptionRow.Summary`, `GroupSummary`): Formats "Follow Windows" or
"Custom", Online the update interval, Karpo Pro the licence, About Karpo the version, Look ▾'s sections and a widget's Look ›
"Default"/"Layout" or "Custom", the status icons and the tray's icons how many show. A level of acts and ways out alone (Back
up and reset) says nothing.

**Words.** New in all 30 languages: `dock.edit.karpo` (Karpo), `dock.edit.taskbar` (each language's own "Taskbar"),
`settings.sections.services`, `.newDisplays`, `.thisDisplay`, `.bar`, `.text`, `.colors`. "New displays show" is the row
"Layout" under its heading "New displays".

**Size to content** (`Flyout.FitsContent`, `FitWidth`): the edit bar's menus and the bar's and a folder room's right clicks
are as tall as their rows and as wide as their widest row needs, every level's — its words and its value whole — from
320 DIP up to the work area (§230's one width and §288's one height stay a widget's menu's). The study cut "Language and regi…"
at ⚙'s 440 DIP and 320.

**No forced foot** (R16, §423's "the root menus always have an entry aligned at the bottom", gone): a row stands still at a
menu's foot only by its content —
- ⚙'s **Quit Karpo**: it ends the app, so it ends the menu (§409: "quit karpo should be all the way on the bottom and sticky");
- a widget's **Height** (its rows) or **Size**, and its **Look ›**: the widget's box — how tall and how it looks —, the same rows
  in every widget's menu, so in the same place in every one (§276, §311, §314).

Gone with it: Display ▾'s "Add a layout" as its foot (right under the layouts now), Layout ▾'s Behavior › foot, the folder
room's "Layout ↗" foot, the right click's "Display ↗" foot, a divider's Style at its menu's foot (a row of its own, §435), and a
folder's Look › in its panel's menu besides its face's (§481): it is the face's menu's alone, as every widget's look is in its
own menu.

**Copy look and Paste look are gone** (§507's painter): the widget menu's top row is Cut, Copy and Remove; Ctrl+Shift+C and
Ctrl+Shift+V do nothing in edit mode; `Dock.EditLooks.cs`, `Looks.Copy`, `Looks.Paste`, `MenuChord.CopyLook`/`PasteLook`,
`EditKeyAct.CopyLook`/`PasteLook` and `dock.menu.copyLook`/`pasteLook` in every language. Look › and its Reset all stay.

`docs\menu-study\`.

**Rules** (`MenuRulesTests`, the allowances empty): R1 no exception; R2 an edit bar's or a right click's menu within a
1920×1080 display's at 150 % under its bar and the edit bar (594 DIP), a widget's within its one height; R4 a setting says its
value and a level what it holds where it holds anything set or to read, a level of acts nothing; R10 a heading over its
section's rows, never last, never over a rule or a heading (§411 to §513 no headings); R15 the right click Taskbar ▾'s rows,
Look ↗ and Display ↗; R16 a foot only by content (above); R17 the headings' fixed order (⚙ General, Services, Karpo; Display ▾
New displays, This display; Taskbar ▾ Bar, Behavior; a look's Text over Colors); R18 every setting one home among ⚙, Display ▾,
Taskbar ▾ and Look ▾, the right clicks' settings each one of theirs (`EverySettingHasOneHome`).

No config change.

(default) in brackets etc. it should always just say it like this: Default (Value) if it is the default value."*

**One form.** Every row whose value is unset says so in one way, `settings.value.default` "Default ({value})" (30
languages, each its `defaultOf`'s words): at its end, to a screen reader, and as its picker's first entry. The value is
what the row draws now — its layout's section's on a widget's look, Windows' own on a section's, Windows' language,
region, formats —; a set value says itself alone. Where Windows decides it as it draws, it says what it is:
`settings.value.windowsAccent` "Windows accent", else `settings.value.windows` "Windows' own".

| row | was | now |

| a section's colour (Look › Taskbar widgets › Background …) | "Default", greyed | "Default (#202020)", "Default (None)", "Default (Windows accent)" |
| a widget's colour, flyout outline, pattern color | "Layout", greyed | "Default (#1E3A5F, 50%)" |
| a section's font, weight, pattern | "Default (Segoe UI Variable)" in the picker, "Segoe UI Variable" at the end | "Default (Segoe UI Variable)" both |
| a widget's font, weight, pattern | "Layout (Contours)" in the picker, "Contours" at the end | "Default (Contours)" both |

| an icon's cross (§306) | "Default" | "Default (Folder)", a pin's and a feed's "Default (Its own icon)" |
| ⚙ › Language | "Windows default (Deutsch)", "Follow Windows" at the end | "Default (Deutsch)" both |
| ⚙ › Formats: short and long date, time | "Follow Windows (22/09/2026)", "Follow Windows" at the end | "Default (22/05/2026)" both |
| ⚙ › Formats: first day, temperature, sizes | "Follow Windows", "As Windows shows them (KB, MB, GB)" | "Default (Monday)", "Default (Celsius (°C))", "Default (KB, MB, GB)" |
| a holiday calendar's country | "As in Windows (Switzerland)" | "Default (Switzerland)" |
| Look ▾'s sections, ⚙ › Formats › at their end (§517) | "Default", "Follow Windows" | "Default (Windows' own)" |
| a widget's Look › at its end (§517) | "Layout" | "Default (Layout)" |

The one formatter is `S.SettingsValueDefault`; the colour's value `OptionPickers.Unset` (`Paints`' `unset` argument gone,
