## 519. A widget carried in edit mode lands on any display: one drop for every surface of every display (2026-11-06)

The person (2026-11-06): *"i just noticed that dragging and dropping widgets across displays does not work but this
should obviously work in all the places and for all the widget types"*.

**Why it didn't.** Since edit mode became every place of a display (§7's places, 2026-10-07) a carried block was
offered only to the surfaces of its own display: `Dock.BarOffer` and `Dock.GroupOffer` asked the windows with
`window.Id == from.Id`, so a bar on another display was never the nearest and never showed a ghost, and the release
landed the block back on its own display. It was on purpose — "a block is measured at its own display's scale" — and
the drop itself could not have done otherwise: `Dock.MoveIsland` and `Dock.MoveGroup` moved a widget only along the list
its key's owner named, never from one layout's list into another's.

**Now one drop for every surface.**
- **Where it goes.** Every bar and place of every display is a surface it may land on (`Dock.DropSurfaces`, the one
  carried from first, which keeps a tie); the one it goes to is the nearest of the display the pointer is over, however
  much nearer another display's is across the seam, and over a display with none, or between displays, the nearest of
  all (`Dock.NearestSurface`, `EditDrops.Nearest`'s new `screens`, each surface's `DockWindow.ScreenBounds`). One widget
  (`BarOffer`), several selected carried together (`GroupOffer`, `ShowGroupCarry`) and a widget following the pointer
  — picked in the add list, copied, pasted (Dock.EditFollow.cs) — all ask it.
- **Its ghost at the other display's scale.** What a bar measured of the block it carries (`Layout.Carry`: its cells,
  its app buttons' labels, a tray's icons) now says the scale it was measured at (`Layout.Carried.Scale`); the bar it is
  over lays itself out with it in its own px (`Carried.At`, in `Layout.With`), so on a display at 200 % the ghost is as
  wide as that display draws the widget itself, a group's too.
- **The move.** The one drop of edit mode is `Dock.MoveIslands(keys, on, slot)` → `IslandEdits.MoveTo(config, keys,
  owner, slot)`: along its bar, to another surface of its display, or to any surface of another display alike. A widget
  of another layout leaves that layout's list for the one the display it was let go on shows — itself, with its id (an
  id is unique across every layout, `Config.Repair`) and its folder's lines; two displays showing one layout share the
  list, so the move is along it. The slot is the window's (`DockWindow.ListSlot`, now one for one widget and several,
  finding what moves by its id whichever display's key names it). A move into another layout asks the licence as an add
  does (`LicenseAllows`); refused, everything stays. What was selected stays selected under its new key
  (`EditSelection.Rename`), so its menu opens again where it landed.
- **Every kind.** Whatever a bar holds moves so: the tray, Start, the app buttons, a folder's face with its lines, a pin
  (a pin dragged at rest takes the same `MoveIslands`).

**As on one display.** A folder's line stays in its folder, and nothing moves between the bar and a folder (2026-10-09,
`Partners`): a block over an open folder is refused there with the folder's sentence, on any display; one folder stands
open at a time, and an arranged folder has edit mode to itself (§212), so there is no drop from one folder into
another. A folder's divider is a line of its folder. Cut and paste already crossed displays (Ctrl+V puts the widgets
into the display under the pointer, `Paste`); what follows the pointer after a paste now lands on any display too.

Deleted: `Dock.MoveIsland`, `Dock.MoveGroup`, `DockWindow.ListSlotGroup` (one `MoveIslands`, one `ListSlot`), and
`BarOffer`'s and `GroupOffer`'s own surface lists and nearest-surface calls. No config change, no strings.

Tests: `CrossDisplayDropTests` (new: a widget, every kind, a folder with its lines and several together moved to another
display's layout, the same layout's one list, the move on its own display unchanged; the display under the pointer
before a nearer surface of another; the ghost at the other display's scale, alone and together; the selection under its
new keys), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AFolderDraggedOntoTheOtherScreensBarMovesToItsLayout` (new, the real dock on two
made-up screens at 150 % and 100 %, each its own layout: a folder's face dragged from the first's bar onto the second's
is in the second's layout and on its bar; fails with the drop kept to its display), `EditDropsTests`,
`IslandEditsTests`, `EditSelectTests`, `EditSelectionTests`, `SelectionKeysTests`, `PlaceEditTests`, `LayoutEditTests`,
`BarAddTests`, `AdoptDragTests`, `EditEntriesTests`, `EmptyRoomSceneTests`, `SelectedFlyoutTests`, `WidgetCopiesTests`,
`DropLandingTests`, `FolderAddCarryTests`, `FolderCarryTests`, `ArrangedFolderStandsTests`.

By hand, with two displays at two scales showing two layouts: in edit mode drag a widget, the tray and a folder's face
from one display's bar onto the other's (the ghost there at its size, the block landing there and gone from the first);
onto a place along the other display's edge; select two and drag them across; pick a widget in the add list on one
display and click it down on the other; Ctrl+X on one, Ctrl+V with the pointer on the other and click.

## 520. The settings panel: the edit bar folds out into one panel, a page for each of its menus (2026-11-06) — the bar its header row folded too, one width, a Layouts page, every setting its proper control, a popup under its control, since §521 (2026-11-07) — a widget's and a folder's page a header card over groups that say what they are set to since §529 (2026-11-07) — in Windows' own look, never the layout's, since §526 (2026-11-07) — Accounts a page of their own, every colour a colour button, since §535 (2026-11-07) — its shell one system, one grid and one rhythm, since §548 (2026-11-07) — the edit bar a command bar of its pages, each opening a flyout of its own, no fold and no side list, since §575 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-06), picking design 1 of the panel study (its pictures in `docs\panel-study\`, gone with it) and then
its recommendation: *"the topbar should be extentible so that it folds out when you click it. i just think that it is not
so clear if all the settings are hidden in the submenus ... open a bigger panel that you can design freely."*; *"even
closer to how win11 does it"*, *"a little more compact"*, *"a clean design ... similar or same sizes of texts or
elements"*, *"connect the topbar with the panel"*; and of the recommendation: *"i like how it looks. build it like that
now."*

**The bar and the panel are one surface** (`EditDeck`, Dock.EditDeck.cs; its layout `PanelLayout`, SettingsPanel.Layout.cs;
its drawing `PanelPainter`, SettingsPanel.Paint.cs). Folded, the edit bar was a pill until §521 (since: the panel's header
row alone, 760 DIP wide, the search box in it) — its buttons have no fill and no rim, as a title bar's, Done the one accent
button:

    ⠿ [⚙ Settings ⌄]  [⊗ 2 errors]  [+ Add]  [✓ Done]

The errors only while there are any (§394). No Undo nor Redo buttons: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y stay (EditFollowHook). Settings ⌄
folds it out, its chevron flipping: the bar becomes the panel's header row across its whole width, one rim round both, no
gap — grip, Settings ⌃ and the errors at its start, the search box in its middle (as Windows 11 apps centre theirs in the
title bar), Add then Done at its end — and under it the side list and the page:

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ ⠿ ⚙ Settings ⌃          [ Search settings            🔍 ]        + Add  ✓ Done │
    │ ⚙ Karpo           Look                                                        │
    │ 🖥 Display        [🎨 Apply palette                       Custom          ⌄ ] │
    │ ▭ Taskbar         [▭ Taskbar             Default (Windows' own)          ⌄ ] │
    │ ▌🎨 Look           [⊞ Taskbar widgets                                      ⌃ ] │
    │                     Font                [Default (Segoe UI Variable)   ⌄]     │
    │ (📁 Folder)         Text color          [□ Default (#FFFFFF)           ⌄]     │
    │ (🕑 Widget)         …                                                          │
    │ ⏻ Quit Karpo                                                                  │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

**Its pages are the edit bar's menus, side by side as pages of one panel** (§520 decision 1; §521 Layouts a page of its own after Display). The side list holds Karpo
(⚙ Karpo ▾, `KarpoMenu.Rows`), Display (Display ▾, `LooksScope.Display`: Position, §348), Taskbar (`LooksScope.Taskbar`) and
Look (`LooksScope.Look`) — no Taskbar nor Look on a display that shows None —, and Folder while a folder stands open
arranged (its panel's settings, `FolderSide.Panel`), Widget while one widget alone is selected (its settings, its Cut, Copy
and Remove at its title's end). Quit Karpo, ⚙'s foot row, is the side list's footer item (§545: General's last row; the footer says what is placed against the licence). One source of settings: a page is
what its menu's builder says (`Dock.SettingsItems`, `Dock.LooksItems`, `OptionMenu.Settings`, `Dock.WidgetRowsFor`), and
each menu row is read as a control (`PanelRows`, SettingsPanel.cs):

| Menu row | Control |
|---|---|
| a toggle's | a toggle switch, 40 × 20, "On"/"Off" 12 before it |
| a stepper's | a number box, − and + inside it |
| a few choices in the row (`FlyoutControl.Segments`); a choice of two or three short ones that is set | a segmented control, equal segments, the chosen raised |
| a choice of one (`PickOne`) | a dropdown: its choices in a popup under it, a ComboBox's list |
| a colour (its swatch, its picker among its choices, §523) | the dropdown with its 16 DIP swatch in it; the swatches and Karpo's colour picker in the popup |
| a level holding a text field | a text box: the field in the popup (§521: typed in place; a search's a dropdown of its field over its finds) |
| a level of rows | an inline expander: its rows inset in its card, 1 DIP lines between, no headings, no icons |
| a row of small buttons (an account's) | its buttons at the row's end: Sign in again, Remove |
| a link (`Opens`) | where it leads at its end, "Karpo › Accounts" (`PanelRows.LeadOf`, `EditEntries.Landing`) |
| a row that acts | a card with a chevron (§521: a button at its end) |

What a control does is what its row did: the page keeps the menu it was (a `Pending`, its picks) and its control sends its
row's id to `Chosen`, the one way every menu row is picked (`Dock.PanelActed`); a dropdown, a colour, a text box and a
button with a level of its own open that level in a popup under it — the very rows, picked by the page's own handler — and a
choice made closes it (`Pending.Drops`, `Dock.PanelDropped`); a colour of one's own is mixed in the popup itself (§523;
§520 to §522 Windows' dialog, `MenuBrowse`). A link opens the page that owns its setting at its row (`Dock.PanelLinked`). A shut expander
says at its end what it is set to, or the accounts it holds; open, its rows say it. Every unset value reads "Default
(Value)" (§518).

**It follows the selection** (§520 decision 3; `PanelMemory`). In edit mode a click on a widget, a folder's face or a line of
the folder open selects it, and nothing pops up (§407 to §519 its menu beside it, §386 Folder ▾'s from the edit bar); the
panel open shows its page; the folder opened, its page; the selection gone, the page shown before. A right click keeps its
menu beside the widget (Cut, Copy, Remove, its settings); the bar's own right click opens the panel on its Taskbar page (§411
to §519 Taskbar ▾'s rows and "Look ↗", "Display ↗"); a folder room's keeps its menu. Settings opens on the last page used —
the selection's where there is one —, and the last page and the expanders open are remembered for the run of the app, in
memory only. Edit mode always starts folded (§537: open, since). Every display's edit bar folds out its own panel, one open at a time (opening
one folds the other, `Dock.panelOn`); its Display page is its display. Every way in from outside lands on a page, at its row,
lit a moment (`OpenEditMenu` → `Dock.OpenPanel`, §340): Win+Alt+Enter the Taskbar page, a face's "Manage accounts" Karpo ›
Accounts, a second start Karpo, a "Look" link the Look page.

**It stays open** until Settings ⌃, Escape or Done: clicks on bars, widgets and the dim, drags and Add leave it open. Escape
goes from the inside out (`EditKeys.Escape`): what is carried, the marching ants, an open dropdown or picker (it closes on
its own Escape), the search's words, the panel, an open folder, edit mode.

**The search** is the header's box, the caret in it as the panel opens (`MenuTextField`, the one text box of Karpo's).
Typing lists the settings of every page whose name holds it, inside the expanders too, those that start with it first, case
and accents not counting (`PanelSearch`): each its page's icon, its name and where it is ("Look › Taskbar widgets"), in a
list under the box (over it at the display's foot). A pick goes to its page, opens the expanders it is in, scrolls to it and
lights it a moment; its words go. Up, Down and Enter walk and pick the list.

**One size, hung from the bar** (§520 decisions 5 and 9). 760 DIP wide, 70 % of the work area tall, whatever the page; a long
page scrolls under the header by the wheel, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End and the keys' focus, a thin indicator at its edge.
It hangs from where the bar hangs: down from a bar at the display's top, its header the bar; up from one at the bottom, its
header its foot (`PanelLayout.HeadAtFoot`), centred on it; the grip drags both (§395). It unfolds out of the bar and folds
back into it as a popup comes in (`FlyoutHost.Unfold`: a clip the compositor runs, nothing drawn again while it moves; the
fold-back ends on the bar's own timer, as a popup's entrance does, DWM being free not to run it). Its content is one surface
drawn whole as what it shows changes — a page, a control, the pointer over another thing — and shown in the commit that
brings it, so no picture between two is seen.

**Metrics** (DIP; at 150 % every one lands on whole pixels; `PanelMetrics`; §548 made them one system — the page from
196, its title a Title 28, its groups 24 apart, the header on the side list's columns —, §548's table the one that holds):

- Type: WinUI's ramp, four styles only — Body 14 for every name, side item and control's words; Body Strong 14 for a
  section's heading; Caption 12 for every second line and every value at a row's end; Subtitle 20 for a page's title.
- Bar: 32 tall buttons; folded 4 round them (40 tall), open 8 (the header 48). Glyphs 16, chevrons 12.
- Side list: 184 wide; items 36 tall, 40 apart, 4 in from its sides, 4 corners; the shown one the subtle fill and the 3 × 16
  accent pill; icons 16 at 16, words at 48.
- Page: from 192 to 16 off the panel's edge; its title row 36 tall, level with the first side item.
- Cards: 48 tall for one line, 60 for two (Body over Caption), 4 apart, 1 DIP rim, 4 corners, 16 padding; icon 16 at 16,
  name at 48; a heading 16 over its group and 8 under it. Mica-like ground, cards a step lighter (CardBackground).
- Controls: every value control 240 × 32 (dropdown, colour, number box, segmented control, text box); every chevron 20 in
  from the control column's end; toggles 40 × 20; buttons 32 tall.
- Search: 320 × 32 in the header's middle; suggestions 36 tall in a list with 8 corners, 4 off the box.

**A screen reader** (§520 decision 11; `DeckUia`, Accessibility\DeckUia.cs) finds the folded bar a tool bar, the open panel a
pane: the header's buttons and the search, the side list a list (each page an item, the one shown selected:
SelectionItem), Quit Karpo, and the page — its title's buttons, each section a group under its heading's name, each control
by its row's name: a toggle that toggles, a number box a range set by its value, a dropdown and an expander that expand and
collapse (ExpandCollapse), a segment that is selected, the rest buttons. A greyed row is in the tree, said to be off (the
menus left greyed rows out). UI Automation's ExpandCollapse and SelectionItem are Karpo's own providers now (Uia.cs). The
keys: Tab and Shift+Tab from the header to the side list (its shown item) to the page's controls; Up and Down in the side
list from page to page; Space and Enter act; F6 and Ctrl+E to the search.

**Rules** (MenuRulesTests, SettingsPanelTests): every setting has one page for its home (R18); the pages' headings in their
one order (R17); a row at a page's foot only by what it is (R16); and R19, every control of every page of every settings
menu Karpo has, every expander open, of its one size class (the person: *"try to use similar or same sizes of texts or
elements"*). The keyboard sweep's rule holds on the panel: whatever a click reaches is a stop of the keys. R15 (the bar's
right click as Taskbar ▾'s rows) went with the right click's menu; R2 is a menu's, a page scrolls.

**Deleted:** the edit bar's drop-down menus and their plumbing — `Dock.DeckLooks`, `Dock.ShowSettingsMenu`,
`Dock.OpenCrumb`, `Dock.CrumbMenu`, `Dock.WidgetCrumbMenu`, `Dock.CrumbSettings`, `LooksMenu(DockWindow)`, `EditMenu` and
`EditEntries.ScopeOf`, `LooksScope.All` and its rows (the right click's whole), `EditDeckPlan`'s parts, widths, `MenuMostDip`,
`For`, `Order`, `Shows`, `ActionAt`, `PartOf`, the kept buttons and the tooltips of the edit bar, the Undo and Redo buttons
(`MenuChord.Undo`, `MenuChord.Redo`, "dock.edit.undo", "dock.edit.redo"), the click's menu beside a widget or a line in edit
mode (`EditActivate`'s and `LineClicked`'s `BesideMenu`/`LineMenu`). Kept: the right clicks' menus, the menus at rest, the
pickers, and `EditDeckPlan.Place`, `Within`, `Offset`. New words in every language: "Search settings", "No settings found".
No config change.

Type names: `PanelPage`, `PanelRow`, `PanelRowKind`, `PanelPageView`, `SettingsContent`, `PanelRows`, `PanelSearch`,
`PanelFound`, `PanelMemory` (SettingsPanel.cs); `PanelMetrics`, `PanelLayout`, `PanelInput`, `PanelHit`, `PanelHitKind`,
`PanelPart`, `PanelLine`, `PanelBlock`, `IPanelText` (SettingsPanel.Layout.cs); `PanelPainter`, `PanelMarks`,
`GfxPanelText` (SettingsPanel.Paint.cs); `DeckUia`; `Dock.PanelOf`, `PanelActed`, `PanelPopup`, `PanelLinked`, `OpenPanel`,
`FoldPanel` (Dock.SettingsPanel.cs).

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests` (new: every menu row a control once, each kind its control, keys and paths, the search inside the
expanders, what it remembers and follows, one size, the person's metrics, every control one size, what is hit is what the
keys reach, the keys reach whatever a click reaches, the panel hung from the bar, Escape from the inside out),
`EditDeckClickTests` (new, the real window: folded buttons, the grip's drag, open controls doing their rows', the search and
the keys, its tree), `MenuRulesTests` (R19; R15 gone), `NarratorTests` (ExpandCollapse, SelectionItem),
`ArrangedFolderStandsTests` (a click selects and the panel follows; the panel over an arranged folder; a palette and the type
set on their pages), `MenuToggleTests` (a dropdown toggled by its box), `EditEntriesTests`, `EditClickTests`, `BarLooksTests`,
`KarpoMenuTests`, `EditBarFolderPictures`, `EditDeckPlanTests`, `EditDeckMoveTests`. Pictures: `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets`
(panel-folded-, panel-look-, panel-karpo-, panel-widget-, panel-search-dark.png and their light ones, to KARPO_PNG_DIR; the
repository keeps no edit-mode pictures).

By hand: edit mode, Settings: the panel unfolds under the bar, the caret in its search; type "pat", pick Pattern › Look ›
Taskbar widgets; flip Animations on the Karpo page; open Accounts; pick a palette from Look's dropdown, a colour of one's own;
click a widget on the bar (its page), open a folder (its page), click a line (its page), click the dim (the page before);
Escape: the search's words, the panel, the folder, edit mode; with a bar along the top, the edit bar at the bottom: the panel
opens up from it; Narrator on the side list and an expander.

## 521. The settings panel, pass two: a popup under its control; Layouts a page of its own; one width folded and open; every setting its proper control (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"layouts should get their own separate entry in the settings."*; *"the edit bar should be the
same width if it is open or closed the settings."*; *"this was just pass one now, now go ahead and check all the settings
and make sure that they are implemented with the proper controlls. (e.g. dropdowns, also think about how many items are
realistically there etc., and other components as well.)"*; and *"the dropdowns also appear at the wrong location."*

### The popups at the wrong place

**What was wrong.** A dropdown of the panel (and a colour's swatches, a field's box, a button's level) opened far from its
control: on a 2560 × 1440 display at 150 %, Language's list stood at y 1026 to 1944 — under the whole panel and past the
display's foot — for a box at y 450 to 498, and 60 px left of it (PanelPopupPlaceTests, before the fix). Three causes:

1. **It was moved off the panel itself.** Every popup that is no Tool host and opens downward keeps clear of the edit bars
   (`FlyoutHost.Avoided`, `ClearOf`, §359: a top bar's popups open where the edit bar stands). Open, the edit bar *is* the
   panel, so a dropdown hanging under its box overlapped it and was pushed past its whole height.
2. **It hung as a bar's flyout.** `Dock.PanelPopup` gave the control's centre as the anchor and the bar's edge as its edge:
   the list was centred on the box, as wide as its rows, not flush with the box's left.
3. **Up or down by the display's halves**, not by the room: a box in the upper half always opened down, a long list then
   clamped to the work area's foot over its own box.

**The fix: one rule, a ComboBox's** (`PopupPlace.Of`, FlyoutHost.cs; pure): the control's rect on the screen, the popup's
size and the work area give the popup's rect — directly under the control, WinUI's 4 DIP of air off it, flush with its left
edge; over it where the room under it is short of the popup and the room over it is not (else the roomier side, the far end
what gives); pushed in only where it would run past the work area's side. A placement that has a control
(`FlyoutPlacement.Control`) is placed by it alone: never moved off an edit bar, never flipped by `Roomiest`, its room the
roomier side's (`PopupPlace.Room`), its shadow's room and its slide by the side it took. The popup is at least as wide as
its control (`Flyout`, the list's width). Every popup the panel opens goes through it (`Dock.PanelPopup` hands the
control's rect, `Pending.Control`); the box is `EditDeck.OnScreen` — the panel where it stands now (moved by its grip too),
the page as scrolled, an expander's inset rows as a card's — in the screen px of the control's own display, the work area
and scale that display's.

Tests: `PopupPlaceTests` (under, over, neither, the sides, whichever way the panel opened, a placement with a control at 150
and 100 %, the control's rect scrolled and inset); `PanelPopupPlaceTests` (the real dock on a stage: a dropdown on a page as
it opens, scrolled, inset in an expander, low by an edit bar at the display's foot — over its box —, with the panel opening
up, and on a second display at 100 %: each popup's panel directly under or over its box, flush with its left, at least as
wide).


### One width, folded and open

The person: *"the edit bar should be the same width if it is open or closed the settings."* Folded, the edit bar is the
panel's header row alone (`PanelLayout`, folded): 760 DIP wide and 48 tall, the same things in the same places — the grip,
Settings ⌄ and the errors at its start, the search box centred, Add and Done at its end:

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ ⠿ ⚙ Settings ⌄  ⊗ 2 errors   [ Search settings          🔍 ]        + Add  ✓ Done │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Opening grows the panel down from it (up from it at the display's foot), and nothing in the row moves (`PanelLayout.Parts`,
one for both; the fold's clip runs from the header's height, `FlyoutHost.Unfold`). The search box shows folded too: a
press on it folds the panel out with the caret in it, its suggestions as one types (`EditDeck`: the folded search's hit is
Settings'). The box is 320 DIP where the buttons either side leave it that, centred, and narrower where they don't (the
errors). On a display too narrow for 760 DIP the bar and the panel are its width as one (`PanelLayout.WidthOf`, with
`EditDeckPlan.Widest`). `PanelMetrics.FoldPad` is gone: the row is 8 round its buttons folded as open.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests.TheBarIsOneWidthFoldedAndOpen` (the same parts at the same rects, the search folded, at the
foot, narrow), `EditDeckMoveTests` (one width with errors or none), `EditDeckClickTests` (the folded search folds out;
open, the panel's sides the bar's), `SceneTreeTests.EditedDisplay` (folded 760 × 48).


### Layouts, a page of their own

The person: *"layouts should get their own separate entry in the settings."* The side list is Karpo, Display, **Layouts**,
Taskbar, Look (and Folder, Widget while there is one); Layouts is there on a display that shows None too (`PanelOf`).

- **The Layouts page** (`LooksScope.Layouts`, `BarLooks.LayoutsRows`): the layouts as the person's own things, in their
  order — each an expander (`PanelRows`: one of the person's things with rows of its own is an expander, its buttons at its
  head's end; §520 dropped its rows): its name (a text box), its icon, Duplicate inset in it, its Delete a button at its
  head's end (asked first; greyed on the last layout, saying why), "This display" under the name of the one this display
  shows. Under them "Add a layout", the presets (§472).
- **The Display page** keeps this display's own alone (`BarLooks.DisplayRows`): under "New displays" their Layout; under
  "This display" its Layout — a dropdown of the layouts and None (`BarLooks.Shown`, `DisplayLayoutChoice`; None where Karpo
  may be hidden here, or is) — and Position (§348). "Show on this display", a layout's own row since §336, is that dropdown
  now; the None row among the layouts (§366) its last choice.
- **Two rows of one name**, Layout under "New displays" and under "This display", are two: a row's key holds its section's
  heading ("Display/This display/Layout", `PanelRows.Of`, `PanelRows.Find`).
- **A choice that grows** (`OptionRow.Grows`, `FlyoutItem.Grows`: the layouts a display shows, new displays' layout) is a
  dropdown however few there are now; a fixed two or three short ones a segmented control whatever is set (§520 made it
  one only while set: a row changed its control with its value).
- **Ways in**: the Layouts face's "Layout settings" and the layouts line's "Add" land on the Layouts page
  (`EditEntry.LayoutSettings`, `AddLayout`); a "Display" link on the Display page (`EditEntry.DisplaySettings`).
- **R18** holds with five pages (`MenuRulesTests.EverySettingHasOneHome`); R17's order has Layouts with no headings; the
  search says "Layouts › Work" for a layout's rows. ConfigCoverage counts the Display and Layouts pages as the one level
  they were (Display ▾): what a layout made, copied or deleted does to the displays is theirs.

Deleted: `BarLooks.Layouts` (the Things row inline in Display ▾), `HereRow`, `NoneRow`, the None thing,
`BarLooksTests.ALayoutsRowOpensItsLevelAsAFacesRowDoes` and the bar-layouts picture (a menu that is no more).

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests.LayoutsHaveAPageOfTheirOwn`, `BarLooksTests.TheLayoutsPageHoldsEachLayoutAsAnExpanderOfItsOwnRows`,
`TheBarsRowsAreCutFourWays`, `TheLayoutsPageGreysWhatCannotBeDone`, `EditEntriesTests`, `LayoutPresetsTests`,
`LayoutsPresetTests`, `ConfigCoverageTests`, `MenuRulesTests`, `EditDeckClickTests` (five side items).

**In numbers** (the table's 4 030 rows over every page of the corpus, `PanelControlsTests`): 283 rows that act became
buttons (265 of them a page's or a widget's Look's Reset all); 24 lines of text became text boxes in place (18 names and
labels, an amount owned, a camera's address, two forms' address and password — the forms' fields had been cards that did
nothing at all); every number row (`OptionRowKind.Number`: a bar's Size, Days ahead, the volume slider's length, a market's
Years, a countdown's minutes) takes a number typed, 4 of them on the corpus' pages; each layout became an expander (its
level had been dropped); 2 dropdowns that grow (a display's layout, new displays') no longer turn segmented with two
layouts; the 214 rows of a fixed two or three short choices are segmented whatever is set (§520 made them a dropdown while
left to their default). The rest — 1 108 dropdowns, 1 167 colours, 158 switches, 361 expanders, 55 rows of the person's
things, 30 links, 6 notes — kept their control: it was the right one.

**What was built**:

- **A text box in place** (`PanelRowKind.Text`, `PanelHitKind.Text`; `EditDeck`'s `editing`): a click puts Karpo's one text
  box (`MenuTextField`, masked for a password) in the row's 240 × 32 box with its words all chosen; Enter keeps them,
  a press elsewhere or Tab keeps them too, Escape puts back what it said (`EditKeys`' step: `ClearSearch` first ends the
  typing). Kept, its words go as its field's (`EditDeckAction.Type`, `Dock.PanelTyped` → `FieldKept`, the very path a
  menu's field takes). A screen reader finds an Edit.
- **A number typed** (`PanelHitKind.Number`): the number box's value is a text box too; what is typed is held to the row's
  range and steps (`OptionUnits.Typed`: "48 px", "1000" → its most, "-5" → its least, words → nothing), set as a step sets it
  (`FieldPicks.KeepRow`). Every number row has its typed field now (`OptionMenu`), the menus' too.
- **A button** (`PanelRowKind.Action`): a row that acts says what it does before its button, the button its name
  (`PanelLayout.ActionWide`: its words, 120 to 240 DIP wide, 32 tall), one line tall; asked first where it asks, as before.
  A row with nothing to say before it is the button alone, no icon either.
- **A way to add one** (`OptionRow.Adds` → `FlyoutItem.Adds`: Add a layout, Add a country, Add a face, Add a toggle) is a
  button with a chevron, its list under it — never an empty dropdown with no value. A search's list opens with the caret in
  its field; a button's list is as wide as a value's box at least.
- **The person's things with rows of their own** (`PanelRows`): an expander, their buttons at its head's end.
- **A control's list** (`FlyoutPlacement.Control`, `Flyout`; a list of rows to pick, `Flyout.PlainList` — a colour's picker
  of §523 keeps its own height and its keys): about ten rows tall and scrolling (`Flyout.ComboRows`), at
  least as wide as its box, opening with its chosen row lit and in sight, a letter typed lighting the row it starts and
  typed again the next (`Flyout.Jump`), Up, Down, Enter and Escape as every menu. A search's list is its field over its
  finds: the filtered long list (zones, places, symbols, currencies, teams, a pin's target).
- **The model says** what the panel cannot see: `OptionRow.Grows` / `FlyoutItem.Grows` (a choice among things there are
  as many of as there are), `OptionRow.Least`, `Most`, `Step`, `Unit` (a number typed); nothing is special-cased in the panel.

R19 holds with the new kinds (`MenuRulesTests.EveryControlIsOfItsSizeClass`: a text box 240 × 32, a row's button 32 tall and
120 to 240 wide, a number box's value its 240 less − and +).

**Left as they are, and why**: Karpo's font choice is its curated seven (StyleFont), not every installed family, so it is
a dropdown with no filter; making it every family is a change of the config's words, not of a control. A choice popup
grows no filter of its own: every list that is realistically long is a search already (zones ~140, places, currencies,
symbols, teams), and the language list (31) scrolls as the person asked. A holiday country's region (a thing with one
choice) stays a row with its buttons, its choice in its own menu. A folder line's Rows and Max rows, and a time's hours
and minutes, keep − and + alone: their steps are their values. No date or time pickers: the panel has no date value, and
a time's hours and minutes are its steppers. The popups keep the flyouts' 8 DIP corners and their own row height, as
every menu of Karpo's; the panel's type ramp is theirs already.

Tests: `PanelControlsTests` (the control of every row of every page, the audit table; a number typed held to its range; a
number box takes a number typed; on the real window a text box and a number box typed in place, Enter, Escape, a press
elsewhere; a control's list opening at its choice, ten rows tall, a letter typed), `SettingsPanelTests` (every control one
size, with the new kinds), `MenuRulesTests` (R19), `OptionFieldsTests.EachWidgetHasItsFields` and
`OwnedLevelsTests.TheAccountsAreAddedSignedInToAgainAndRemovedInSettingsAlone` (stale since §494 and §517: the market's
currency field is wanted, and a level of the person's things says its first at its end — the tests were fixed, not the
product).

Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR; the repository keeps none): `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` (panel-layouts-,
panel-display-, panel-text-, panel-number-, panel-things-, panel-backup-dark.png beside §520's) and
`PanelPopupPlaceTests.PanelPopupPictures` (popup-under-, popup-scrolled-, popup-long-, popup-up-dark.png: the real dock's
windows on a stage, laid over a backdrop of a colour nothing draws).

## 522. A click on what opened a menu closes it on a busy dock too (2026-11-07)

`MenuToggleTests.EveryOpenerOnTheBarTogglesItsPopup` failed now and then on a loaded machine (the whole UI run): the
Start button's right click again (`rest-right-start`), or the bar's (`rest-right-bar`), left the quick links or the bar's
menu open: *"clicked again, it is open still — closed and opened again in the one click"*.

**Why.** The popups' hook leaves a press on a bar or an edit bar to it (`IsBar` → `FlyoutHost.PressesHandledBy`) only while
the dock is not busy; busy as it hears the press (inside a handler that pumps sent messages, as a wait on the dock's STA
thread does), it closes the popup itself (§430). The bar's press, handled after, then found nothing open, so nothing told it
that it had closed its own thing's popup: the press was not used up, and its release opened the menu again. §430's rule
(a press knows what the hook closed for it, `FlyoutHost.Heard` and the popup dismissed since) was asked by a folder's
window alone (`FolderMessage`).

**Now** every window's press asks it, at its point on the screen (`Dock.Pressing(…, screen)`, the point no longer optional;
`ScreenOf`): a bar's (`PressedOn` counts that popup as one its press closed, so `LightDismiss.Consumes` uses the press up
as if the bar had closed it), an edit bar's (`DeckPressed`) and a folder's alike. Nothing else changes: with the dock not
busy the hook still leaves the press to the bar, which closes the popup itself.

No config change.

Tests: `EditBarFolderPictures.EveryPressKnowsWhatTheHookClosedForIt` (new: every press site passes its screen point, the bar's
counts the hook's), `TheToggleIsTheDocksOwnPress`; `MenuToggleTests` (by a run with `IsBar` made to answer no for every
press, so the hook closed every popup first: red before on every toggle of the bar, `rest-folder`, the faces,
`rest-right-folder`, `rest-right-bar`, `rest-right-start`; green after).

## 523. One colour picker, Karpo's own: the custom colour mixed in the picker itself (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"improve the color picker, the custom color should be integrated into the normal color picker."*

**Until now** a colour row — a Look value on a page of the settings panel (§520), a widget's own colours, a folder face's
(a calendar's, an inbox's, the holidays') — opened a level of its "Default (…)", the recent colours and the grid, and
"Custom color…", which shut the menu and opened Windows' own colour dialog (`ChooseColorW`, §224): another window, no
alpha, its own look, the menu shown again after it. An opacity stepped by tens stood under the swatches (§459).

**Now one picker, one level, the same for every colour** (`MenuPickers.Mixer`, `Flyout.Mixer.cs`). Its rows, top to bottom:

    ✓ Default (#202020)
      None                                   (a background's and an outline's)
      ■ ■ ■                                  recent colours, the one in force ringed
      ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■                        the page's grid, 8 to a line
    ─────────────────────────────────────
      [            spectrum            ]     128 DIP tall
      [======== hue ===========○=======]     a rainbow, 12 DIP track in a 32 DIP row
      [▒▒▒▒▒▒ opacity ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒○▒▒▒▒▒▒▒]     where the value takes an alpha
      [■] [ #1E3A5FCC                   ]    the hex box, its swatch the colour it says

- **Default (…)** is the unset value, ticked while it is; picked, it clears the value (§518's words).
- **The swatches** as before (§411: groups ruled off, no headings), the one in force ringed; a swatch picked keeps the
  opacity in force and goes back to the row it opened from (§392).
- **The spectrum** is the hue in force, white across it from its left and black up from its bottom: saturation across, value
  up (`ColorMix.Spectrum`). **The hue** slider is the rainbow, 0° to 360°. **The opacity** slider runs from none to the
  colour whole over §509's checker, and stands only where the value takes an alpha (`OptionRow.Alpha`: a look's colours,
  "#1E3A5F, 80%"; not a calendar's or an account's colour, which are "#RRGGBB"). A white ring with a dark hairline either
  side says where the colour stands on each, on every colour.
- **The hex box** is a line of text (`FlyoutField.Hex`): "#RRGGBB", "#RRGGBBAA" for a see-through colour where the value
  takes an alpha (the web's order, the alpha last); typed with or without "#", either case (`ColorMix.ParseHex`; a value
  without alpha keeps none typed). Its swatch, 32 DIP square before it, shows what its words say as they are typed.
- **Sizes**: on the 4 DIP grid; 4 DIP corners; the spectrum, the tracks and the hex box start and end where the swatches'
  lines do (4 DIP in from a row's fill); the sliders' and the hex box's rows 32 DIP; words Body 14 in the box, nothing else
  written. The spectrum and the sliders read left to right in every language (not mirrored).

**Always shown, no "More" expander.** Windows' Settings › Personalization › Colors hides its custom colours behind "View
colors", a dialog. Here the picker is a level of its own already, opened for the one colour: hiding the spectrum again
behind an expander would be one more click and one more state (open or shut, remembered or not) for the same thing; shown,
the spectrum and the hex box always say the colour in force, nothing about a colour is hidden (the person's §520 point
about settings hidden in submenus), and there is nothing to keep. The popup grows by the custom area (≈ 230 DIP); a
configuration menu's level scrolls in its one height (§288) as before.

**Live, then kept.** A press on the spectrum or a track puts the colour where it went and holds it; the colour follows the
pointer anywhere, held at the edges. Each colour is said as it changes (`FlyoutEventKind.Mix`): the dock wears it on the
bars and the widgets a moment — the config as it would be, applied and not saved, no step of the undo, the menu not shown
again under the pointer (`Dock.mixLooking`). Let go (`MixKept`), it is set on the config the drag began on, saved as one
change, one step of the undo, and the first of the recent colours (opaque, as they all are; `OptionRow.SetColor`'s
`kept`). The keys: Tab and the arrows walk onto the spectrum and the sliders as onto any row; on the spectrum the four
arrows move its point a step, Page Up and Page Down the value ten; on a slider Left and Right a step, Page Up and Page Down
ten, Home and End its ends, Up and Down on to the next row. Each step is worn a moment; the colour is kept once the keys
leave the picker's rows, by Enter or Space, or as the menu closes. Escape while a colour is being mixed puts back the one
before (`MixUndone`: the config the mix began on, nothing saved). The hex box keeps on Enter or as it is left (§332's rule
for a line of text) and puts back on Escape; kept, its colour goes through the same write (`FieldPicks.KeepRow`) and stays
on the picker's level. A grey has no hue of its own: the hue the slider stood at is kept while the menu is open
(`Flyout.mixHeld`), so the ring stays where it was. A calendar's or an account's colour is the service's own: it is written
as it is let go, never while dragged.

**A screen reader** finds the hue and the opacity sliders as ranges it can set (0 to 360, 0 to 100; set, the colour is kept
at once), the spectrum a slider saying its colour, the hex box a value it reads and sets (ValuePattern, new in Uia.cs: every
menu line of text is one now), and the swatches a list, the colour in force its selected item.

**Same picker everywhere.** One builder (`MenuPickers.Rows` → `Tiles` + `Mixer`), one drawing (`Flyout.Mixer.cs`), one dock
handler for every menu kind (`Dock.MenuMixed`, `RowOfPick`: a widget's, a bar's looks', ⚙'s), so the settings panel's colour
dropdowns (§520: its popup is the very level), a widget's colours in its menu and a folder face's colours (an account's
calendar, the holidays' — a tool's level, §452) are the one picker. The panel knows a colour row by its picker
(`PanelRows`: a level holding a `FlyoutMix`, one line changed in SettingsPanel.cs).

**Deleted:** "Custom color…" and its string `dock.edit.customColor` (30 languages); Windows' colour dialog (`Dock.MixColor`,
`ChooseColorW`) and the colour half of `Dock.MenuBrowse` (a pin's target alone now, its bar-looks and ⚙ branches gone with
it); the opacity stepper of the colour level and `OptionRow.Opacity`, `SetOpacity`, `OptionPickers.OpacityStep` and its
`OptionMenu.ApplyRow` case. New words in every language: "Color spectrum", "Hue", "Hex" (`dock.edit.colorSpectrum`,
`colorHue`, `colorHex`; Opacity is `settings.appearance.styles.opacity`). No config change.

Type names: `ColorMix`, `Hsv`, `MixPart` (Karpo.Core\ColorMix.cs); `FlyoutMix`, `Flyout.Mixer.cs` (`Mixing`, `MixLook`,
`MixBox`, `MixPoint`, `MixKey`, `MixShow`), `FlyoutEventKind.Mix`, `MixKept`, `MixUndone`, `FlyoutEvent.Color`,
`FlyoutField.Hex`, `OptionPickKind.Mix`, `OptionRow.Alpha`, `OptionRow.SetColor(colour, kept)`; `Dock.MenuMixed`,
`MixDone`, `RowOfPick` (Dock.MenuPickers.cs); `UiaPattern.Value`, `UiaNode.Value`, `UiaAct.SetText`, `Uia.TakeText`.

Tests: `ColorMixTests` (new: hex written and typed, with and without alpha, and what is no colour; hue, saturation and value
round trips over Windows' colours, the greys and a spread; the spectrum's and a slider's point to colour and back, held at
the edges; the keys' steps; an opacity and its alpha), `MenuPickersTests` (`ThePickersRowsMixTheColourInForce`,
`AColourMixedIsRememberedOnceKeptAndDefaultClearsIt`, `AHexTypedIsKeptAsTheColourItSays`,
`EveryColourRowOpensTheOnePicker` over the whole menu corpus; on a real menu `AColoursPickerMixesOnARealMenu`: the spectrum
pressed and dragged past its corner, the hue stepped and put back by Escape, the opacity to none kept as the keys leave for
the hex box, a colour typed and Enter, a screen reader's hue, the tree), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.
AColourIsMixedInTheSettingsPanel` (the real dock on a config copy: Look page, a colour's dropdown, a drag in its spectrum and
a hex typed land in the file), `LookTests`, `AccountFormTests`, `KarpoMenuTests`, `MenuRulesTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`,
`NarratorTests`. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `color-picker-look-dark.png`, `color-picker-look-light.png` (the Look page's
Taskbar widgets › Background picker as the panel's popup shows it, at 150 %).

By hand: edit mode › Settings › Look › Taskbar widgets › Background: drag in the spectrum (the bars recolour as it moves),
let go (Ctrl+Z puts it back in one step); the hue and the opacity by the keys; Escape while stepping; type "#1E3A5F80" and
Enter; a widget's own colour in its right-click menu; Karpo › Accounts › a calendar's colour (no opacity); Narrator on the
sliders and the hex box.

## 524. A spacer in edit mode is its room striped, the stripes moving, not a line (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the spacers between groups should be a moving stripe pattern and not the line."*

**Replaces** §307's mark in edit mode, kept by §505 (the person, 2026-10-11: *"the spacers / dividers in edit mode should
just show up as a vertical bar / horizontal bar"*): a folder's spacer (the file's `"divider"`) arranged wore a rule two
hairlines thick across its gap, inset by a row's gutter. Now its **whole room** is a band of thin diagonal stripes, slowly
moving along it, so it shows both that the room is a spacer to take hold of and how much room it takes: a **Fixed**
spacer its fixed room (6 DIPs, `FolderFlyout.SeparatorRoom`), a **Grow** spacer all the room it grows to (§435, §482). At
rest nothing changes: a spacer is empty room and nothing is drawn (§505). It is still taken hold of over its grab, at
least 13 DIPs tall (`FolderPlan.Grabs`); nothing moves as the folder is arranged.

**Only the folder's.** Every other spacer or gap between groups was checked: the bar has no separator since §511 (its
mark and grab zone went with it) and a floating bar's docks are its sections with nothing drawn between them; the add list
offers the divider as a row with its glyph, and the settings panel's pages draw no spacer (their 1 DIP lines are the rows
of an expander, not a gap between groups). So the folder's spacer was the one line, and every spacer now looks the same.

**The look** (`SpacerStripes`): stripes 1.5 DIPs wide, 4.5 DIPs apart along the band, at 45°, in the folder's text
(`FlyoutTheme.Text`) at 22 % of its alpha; under the pointer and selected 50 % (`InkOf`). The band's corner is a card's
4 DIPs (at most half the band), clipped to it; nothing of a plate's or a card's look. In high contrast the stripes are the
text itself and the selected ring says the rest. The selected ring and the marching ants stand round it as round any line.

**How, retained** (§357, the flicker rewrite's rule): one stroke and no surface. A line along the band, stroked 1 thick
and dashed (1.5 on, 4.5 off), laid in a space of DIPs along the band and of the band's height across it, then leant: its
dashes are the stripes, its thickness the band's height (`SpacerStripes.LayOf`: the line reaches a whole number of
stripes past both ends, so the band is striped edge to edge, and starts a whole number of stripes before its foot, so a
band that grows keeps its stripes where they were). The stripes move by the compositor alone on the marching ants' own
loop (`MarchingAnts.Loop`, `MarchingAnts.March`: one StrokeDashOffset key-framed through a stripe and its gap, linear,
over four of the ants' laps, forever; the ants now take theirs from the same two). Nothing is drawn again while they move,
as the folder is laid out again or as a Grow spacer grows; a hover or a selection swaps the stroke's brush (`Wear`, two
brushes the folder keeps for its life, coloured again with its look, `Dress`).

**When they move** (`FolderFlyout.MoveBands`, part of `ShowStates`, beside `ShowAnts`): while the folder is arranged and
shows the band, and no line is carried, gives way or glides (`Resting`, the ants' own rule); not with Karpo's Animations
off (`Look.Animations`: the stripes stand still); and the folder closed stops them (`StillKept`, which now stops the ants'
march too). A spacer carried keeps its stripes on its carrier (§502), standing still.

**Deleted:** the rule and its ink — `SeparatorInk.Ink`, `SeparatorInk.ColorOf`, `SeparatorInk.Strong`,
`FolderFlyout.DividerRule`, `FolderPlan.Inks` (now `FolderPlan.Bands`, the band's room), the folder's `markInk` and
`dividerMarks` (now `bands`), the line's `Mark`, `MarkBox`, `MarkShape` (now `Line.Band`), and the colour no painter
read any more: `Palette.Separator`, `ToneRules.SeparatorOf`, `SeparatorDark`, `SeparatorLight`. `SeparatorInk` keeps
the panel's hairline alone. The offscreen list sheets (`ListFormPictures.Panel`) draw no rule: arranged, a spacer is the
compositor's. No config change, no strings.

Type names: `SpacerStripes` (SpacerStripes.cs: `LayOf`, `Laid`, `InkOf`, `Lay`, `Wear`, `Move`, `StripeDip`, `GapDip`,
`PeriodDip`, `Lean`, `CornerDip`, `RestAlpha`, `StrongAlpha`, `Laps`); `MarchingAnts.Loop`, `MarchingAnts.March`;
`FolderPlan.Bands`; `FolderFlyout.MoveBands`, `Resting`, and for tests `Stripes`, `BandsMove`.

Tests: `SpacerStripesTests` (new: the band is the spacer's whole room, Fixed and Grow, nothing for another line or at
rest; the stripes across the whole band at five sizes and scales; a growing band's stripes in place; their colour,
stronger, high contrast; and the real folder at 150 % in both looks — the stripes where the bands are, stronger hovered and
selected, moving arranged, still while a line is carried and while the lines glide home, moving again at rest, still with
Animations off and once closed, none at rest; pictures `spacer-stripes-<dark|light>-150-<edit|hover|selected|rest>.png`
to KARPO_PNG_DIR, laid over Windows' desktop of the mode, as the folder has no panel), `FolderSeparatorTests` (the band
its card arranged; the real folder's stripes where the plan has them), `FolderDividerGrowTests`, `DividerCarryTests`
(carried, its stripes on its carrier and still), `SeparatorInkTests` (the hairline alone), `BarColorThemeTests`. Gone:
`DividerEditLookTests` (the rule across the gap), `SeparatorInkTests`' strong colour and painter tests,
`SceneTreeTests.EveryColourPickedReachesItsSurfacesLive`'s divider colour.

By hand: edit mode, open a folder with a Fixed and a Grow spacer: each its room striped, the stripes moving slowly; the
pointer over one, it is stronger; click it, stronger in its ring; drag a line, every stripe stands still until the lines
come to rest; Karpo › Animations off, the stripes stand; Done, the spacers are empty room again.

## 525. The settings panel's popups toggle as a ComboBox's: clicked again they close, another opens in one click (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the toggleing with dropdowns should properly work as well."*

**What was wrong** (PanelPopupToggleTests, before the fix). A dropdown clicked open and clicked again closed and opened again
(`ooo…`, never closed) — Add on the open panel the same; F4, Alt+Down, Space and Enter after the click opened nothing; the
search's suggestions stayed under it through a click on a side item. One cause for the first: §520 gave the open panel the
activation from a click (WM_MOUSEACTIVATE), so the menu that had the keys closed as it lost them, before the press reached
the edit bar. `DeckPressed` then found nothing open, took the press for a fresh one, and its release opened the popup
again. A click on another control or a toggle went through, by luck: the activation closed the first, the press acted.

**The fix: §522's rule, for the activation too.** Since §522 every press, the edit bar's too (`DeckPressed`), asks
`Dock.Pressing` at its point on the screen what closed for it before it got there — heard by the hook at that point,
dismissed since — and counts that popup as one it closed. The hook hears the press, and posts it, before the click's
activation closes the menu, so the rule does not ask what closed it: a popup the activation closed is one the press closed
as much as one the busy dock's hook closed. Nothing new in the code for it; `PanelPopupToggleTests` hold it, with the
activation as Windows gives it. So whoever closed it (the hook, the bar, the activation), a press on the thing whose popup
it was only closes it; on anything else it closes it and goes on — another dropdown opens in the one click, a toggle
toggles, a side item shows its page, Settings ⌃ folds. The Add list and the errors' list go the same way.

**The keys, as a ComboBox's.** A press on a thing of the panel gives it the keys (no ring), so a dropdown closed by Escape
has them; F4, Alt+Down and Alt+Up open it, as Space and Enter do, and close it again from its popup
(`LightDismiss.TogglesDrop`; not Alt+F4), the keys back on it. The search loses the keys to a press elsewhere, and its
suggestions show only while it has them (`PanelInput.Suggests`); its words stay. The dropdown's chevron does not turn: a
ComboBox's doesn't. Settings ⌄/⌃ shows the fold.

Tests: `PanelPopupToggleTests` (the stage dock, the click's activation as Windows gives it: a dropdown clicked twice, from
one dropdown to another, a toggle, a side item and Settings ⌃ clicked with one open, Add twice and from a dropdown, the keys);
`EditDeckClickTests.APressTakesTheKeysAndADropdownOpensByItsKeys`; `LightDismissTests` (F4, Alt with an arrow);
`EditBarFolderPictures.TheToggleIsTheDocksOwnPress` and `EveryPressKnowsWhatTheHookClosedForIt` (§522's wiring, the edit
bar's press at its point).

## 526. The settings wear Windows' own look, never the person's (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the settings should never take the style of the user, they should always take the style that
we have for it (in our case the base windows 11 based style.)"*

**What leaked.** The edit bar and its panel were shown in the look of the layout their display shows (`Dock.LookOn`), so
`FlyoutTheme.For` laid the layout's Widgets in folders' background (`Palette.Flyout`), its outline (`FlyoutOutline`) and
its text (`PanelText`: the text and the highlight of what lights) over Windows' tokens; a dark bar's light ground made the
whole panel light on a dark Windows; the Taskbar widgets' accent took the place of Windows' (the toggles, Done, the side
list's mark, the selection band). Every popup of edit mode — the panel's dropdowns, colours and boxes, the add list, the
errors, a widget's and the bar's menu, a confirmation — was shown in its bar's look (`ShownIn`), the same values over it, in
the layout's menus' font. And what wears no font of its own is drawn in Karpo's chrome's (`Gfx.Typeface`, the default
layout's menus', §499): the panel, its search, the sections' edit bars' tooltips, a menu's field typed in after it opened.

**One look for the settings: `Dock.SettingsLook`.** Windows' look as the dock reads it (`ReadLook`) with no layout's look
over it (`SettingsLookOf`: `Wearing(null)`): Windows' mode, its accent, high contrast and its system colours, transparency
effects, its text size, and Karpo's own motion (General › Animation speed is no look); no colour, no outline, no text
colour, Segoe UI Variable. Chosen in three places, each the one for what it serves: the edit bar and its panel and the
selection band (`ChromeModels`), the sections' edit bars and their tips (`RailModels`), and every popup (`ShownIn`): a
menu in edit mode, or a widget's settings asked for at rest (§340, `Pending.Configuration`), wears it. What wears it wears
its font too: the panel is measured and drawn in its look's (`EditDeck.Wearing`), a menu is in its look's whatever it
hears (`Flyout.Message`, as `Open` was), a tip in its look's (`TipView`, its words kept by their font too). The swatches
and pictures on the pages are what they show, the person's colours: content, not the panel's look.

**What keeps the person's look (decided).** Out of edit mode everything is the person's taskbar: the bar's own right
click, a widget's acts, an app's jump list, the tray's menus, every flyout a click opens (a folder, a widget's list, the
overflows), in edit mode too — what a bar opens is the bar's. In edit mode every menu is editing (the bar's right click
is its looks, a widget's its settings), so all of them wear the settings' look. A layout's accent once put on a look is not
taken off again: `SettingsLookOf` is of Windows' look alone, never of a layout's.

Tests: `SettingsLookTests` (a default layout odd in every part — its menus' background, outline, text and font, the
flyouts' outline, its widgets' accent and font, a ground of the other mode —: the settings' tokens Windows' own, a menu's,
a taskbar flyout's, a folder's and the text boxes', light and dark, transparency on and off, high contrast's system
colours, Segoe UI Variable); `SettingsWornTests` (the stage dock: the edit bar, its panel open, and a dropdown of the Karpo
page and the Look page drawn in the same tokens and font with that layout as with a plain one — before the fix they were
the layout's magenta, lime and orange, Georgia and Cascadia Mono); `AppearanceTests.NoPopupIsShownInTheDocksBareLook` (the
three places choose `SettingsLook`).

## 527. A click on a folder in edit mode selects it and opens it; its face closes it; no "Open" (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"when i click on a folder in edit mode it still does not open it, it only opens the settings, but
it should toggle open the folder too"*; before: *"a folder should be opened again by clicking on it in edit mode, remove the
separate open folder action."*

**Why it did not open.** Nothing swallowed the click: no press rule (§522), no activation of the panel (§525) and no
dismissal of the folder by the panel. The click did what it was told: since §481 a click on a folder's face was any widget's
click, and since §520 that only selects (`EditClicks.OnClick` → `Menu`, `Dock.EditActivate` → `EditPick`), the panel
following to the Widget page. The folder opened by two other ways alone: its face's "Open" (`CMD_OPEN_FOLDER`, on the
Widget page of the panel and the right click's menu) and a double-click's second (`Dock.ClickedAgain`, the time of the last
click, a branch in `Dock.PressedOn` for the press that closed a menu).

**Now one rule.** `EditClicks.OnClick(kind, closedItsMenu)` says `None` (its press closed the widget's menu), `Select`, or
`Open` for a folder; `Dock.EditActivate` — the one path of the pointer's release, Space, Enter and Narrator's Invoke —
selects, and for `Open` opens the folder arranged in place (`OpenArranged`); the panel follows to its Folder page. Closing
was already there: with a folder open the bars are locked (§212), a press on its face closes it (`EditClicks.OnLocked`,
§252), a press on another folder's face closes it and that click opens the other (§289). So a click toggles, a double-click
is two clicks (open, closed), a drag only carries (the release past the threshold never reaches `EditActivate`), and Ctrl or
Shift held changes the selection alone. Enter and Space on a face open it; Escape closes it (the keys are the folder's
while it is open, §212). A widget's fault on the bar selects it (`Dock.ShowWidget` → `EditPick`) and opens nothing.

**Gone:** "Open" in a folder's top row (`WidgetButtons`' and `WidgetRowsFor`'s `open`, `CMD_OPEN_FOLDER`; 5008 is free),
`Dock.OpenFolderEditing`, `lastClick`, `ClickedAgain`, the double-click branch in `PressedOn`, `EditClickAct.Menu`. The words
stay: "Open" is a drive's own act (Dock.WidgetMenus.cs).

The stage's `stage-edit.json` says what is selected (`"Selected"`, by key), for the probes. The probes open folders by one
click now (`ArrangedFolderStandsTests`, `MenuToggleTests`; their `DoubleClick` gone).

No config change.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AClickOnAFolderSelectsItAndTogglesItOpen` (new, the stage dock, the panel open: a click
selects and opens, the Folder page; again closes, still selected, the panel open; another folder's face in one click; Enter;
a drag opens nothing; red before), `MenuToggleTests.EveryOpenerInEditModeTogglesItsMenu` (`edit-folder`,
`edit-folder-to-folder`: as the mouse does it, the hook first, the panel open), `EditClickTests` (the rule, the locked bar's
clicks, a double-click two clicks, the dock's one path, what is gone), `FolderMenuSidesTests`, `MenuSidesTests` (no "Open").

## 528. Several widgets selected: the settings they have in common, set on them all (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"i should be able to select multiple widgets and edit their common properties like look together.
this should be implemented generically so that i could also select mutliple of the same widget and change their propertier
together."*; and later the same day: *"when i select multiple widgets it still does not show me the combination of the
settings. did you implement this already? also for taskbar based widgets?"* It was not: with several selected the panel's
Widget page was gone (§520 showed it for one widget alone), and a right click on one of them showed that one's settings.

**One page of the one row model** (`OptionRows.Common`, Karpo.Core\OptionRows.Common.cs). With two or more widgets
selected — of a bar, of any display, or one folder's lines (`EditScope`) — the panel's Widget page is theirs: the rows every
one of them has, read from the very rows each one's own page has (`OptionRows.Of`, `LookRows.WidgetRow`), nothing a kind
says of its own:

- **The same setting** is a row of one key in every widget's rows, of one kind and one shape: a choice of the same choices
  (its "Default (…)", §518, may say something else in each — a widget of another layout comes to another default — and
  says "Default (Mixed)" where they differ), a colour's or an icon's tiles the same past their first, a number in one unit
  (within the range every one takes), a search of one field, a link to one place. A level's rows are the rows of it they all
  have; none in common, no level. The person's own things (a line's notes, the accounts), a list put in order and a note
  are no setting several widgets share. So two clocks share their whole page; a clock and the weather, or Start and Search,
  the whole look (Look ›: font, weight, every colour, pattern, Reset all) and whatever else both read by one key and one
  shape — a Style of other choices under the same key is another setting, and is not on the page.
- **Its value** is theirs where they agree. Where they do not it is mixed (`OptionRow.Mixed`, `FlyoutItem.Mixed`): a
  toggle neither on nor off — its rim, a dash for its knob, "Mixed" before it, Indeterminate to a screen reader; a
  dropdown and a segmented control of no choice saying "Mixed"; a number box empty, "Mixed" its placeholder; a colour's
  swatch a dash, "Mixed" its words; a text, a time, an icon "Mixed".
- **Setting it sets every one**: each widget's own row's write called in turn (`Set`, `SetText`, `Pick`, `SetColor`). A
  toggle mixed or off turns them all on; a step steps them all to the first's value stepped; a number typed, a choice, a
  colour (dragged in its picker too, §523), a text and Reset all are the same for all. Every one is written into one copy
  of the file and saved once (`Dock.OptionPicked`, `FieldKept`, `RowOfPick`): one step of the undo, Ctrl+Z puts them all
  back.

The page is titled "3 widgets", or "3 × Clock" where they are of one kind (new words `dock.edit.selectedKind` and
`settings.value.mixed`, in every language), its side item the same; Cut, Copy and Remove at its title's end act on them
all, as they did. It follows the selection live: a Ctrl+click, a Shift+click or a drag adding one or taking one out shows
the page of the selection as it is now; down to one, that one's own page. It stands on the panel open, whatever display
each of them is on. A right click on one of several selected shows the same rows in its menu (§253: its menu acts on
them all).

**One way for one and for several** (`OptionTarget`: a widget, what its rows choose from, where its pickers read and
write). `OptionMenu.Settings`, `Row`, `Apply`, `AskOf` and `FieldPicks.Keep` take the widgets a page is of; for one, its
own rows exactly as before, for several, their rows in common. `Pending.Targets` carries the several from the page into
its popups. **Deleted:** `Dock.OptionRowsFor` (every widget's, folder's and line's settings are `OptionMenu.Settings` over
`Dock.TargetsOf`) and the panel's separate builder of the one widget's page. A folder's faces are its own: with a folder
among the several, its side gives only its look (a folder and the tray share the flyout's outline too). A line's height
(§432) is the one line's alone. No config change.

Kinds: every `BarKind` — the taskbar's own (Start, Search, Task view, the widgets board, the apps, the tray, the
indicators, Show desktop, Windows' menus and panels, every quick switch, a pin, a folder) — and every `ListKind` of a
folder, each paired with another, have the look in common and every row of it sets (`CommonSettingsTests`).

Tests: `CommonSettingsTests` (two of a kind share their whole page; two kinds the look and none of one's own; a value
apart is mixed; a toggle mixed turns them all on; a number mixed typed for all; one config, one step of the undo, Reset all
resets all; every kind paired); `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.TwoWidgetsSelectedShowTheirSettingsInCommon` (the stage dock:
Start and Search selected by a drag, the panel on "2 widgets", a font picked there in the file for both). Pictures:
`SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-same- (two clocks, a switch mixed) and panel-several- (a clock and the weather,
the look open, its font mixed), dark and light.

## 529. A widget's page: a header card, groups that say what they are set to, rows under their choice, the look folded; the folder's one page (2026-11-07) — each value of a default marked set here or inherited, its source named, since §541 (2026-11-07) — the look never folded, every value in its place, since §555 (2026-11-07) — a nested row's guide line gone, its divider as far in as its name, since §564 (2026-11-08) — on a well of its own under its choice, since §565 (2026-11-08) — each level of its menu a group of its own, a group of one setting its row alone, the folder's When it opens gone, a nested row a row of its card, since §588 (2026-11-09) — the levels again, a level alone in What it shows the group itself, a group of one setting a group again, the folder's Alignment under Folder and a nested row a row of its card kept, since §594 (2026-11-09) — plain sections, What it shows and Size, a heading each, no group but a folder's faces, since §645 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07), of the flow study's three concepts for the widget page (a study branch, its README and pictures
drawn by Karpo's code; nothing of it is in the product): *"header of the 3rd one, but the main body content of the second
one"*. So a widget's and a folder's page of the settings panel (§520) open with concept 3's header card, and their body is
concept 2's: groups whose heads are sentences, rows nested under the choice they follow, the look's inherited values
folded. The rows are still the menus' own (`PanelRows.Of`, the same keys: a popup, the search, a link find them as before);
the page only lays them out (Karpo.Dock\SettingsPanel.Widget.cs).

**The header card** (`PanelHeader`, `PanelLayout.LayHeader`, `PanelPainter.Header`): a card as every card (1 DIP rim, 4 DIP
corners), 80 DIP tall: the widget's icon on a 48 DIP tile 16 in (several selected: their icons side by side on one wider
tile, the first in the text's ink), its name in Subtitle 20 ("Calendar"; §528's "3 × Clock", "3 widgets"), where it stands
in Caption under it (`PanelRows.PlaceOf`: "On the taskbar", "In a folder on the taskbar", "On a dock", "In a folder on a
dock"), and Cut, Copy and Remove as a command bar's 32 DIP icon buttons 4 apart at its end — no fill nor rim till the pointer
is on one, each saying its name in a tooltip (the edit bar has a `TipView` now; `PanelLayout.TipOf`) and to a screen
reader. Widgets of several kinds had a line under it, "Select one alone to change what it shows", and a button for each
selecting it alone; since §550 (2026-11-07) they have none: the card is the same for any selection.
Pages without a header (Karpo, Display, …) keep their title row.

**Groups, each head a sentence** (`PanelGroups.Grouped`, `PanelRowKind.Group`): a widget's rows are What it shows (its
own), Height or Size (a folder line's), Look (its look) — one card each, its head the group's icon, its name in Body Strong
and under it in Caption what it is set to (`PanelSentences`), open unless shut (its key marked, `PanelGroups.Mark`; the
memory keeps the shut ones; a search's pick in it opens it again). The sentence is written from the group's rows' values,
so it follows them as they change:

| Kind × group | Sentence |
|---|---|
| a calendar, its agenda | "An agenda of the next 7 days, from every account" (from Show from: "every account", or the one shown) |
| a calendar, another style | "Month, from every account" |
| a clock | "The time in UTC+1", "…, to the second" with its seconds on |
| a weather | "The weather in Zürich" |
| a pin | "Opens Documents" |
| a line's height | "Grows with its content, up to 12 rows", "Always 6 rows tall", "Fills the room the folder leaves" |
| a look | "The layout's look", "The layout's look, its own: Accent color, Weight" |
| a folder's faces | "Its faces: Clock, Icon" |

A kind with nothing to say for a group (a battery's What it shows, a size, a folder's When it opens) has its title alone:
no filler. Several selected (`PanelGroups.Page`'s `each`: each one's own menu): the one sentence where they all say it,
else how they split by the group's first choice ("2 × Compact, 1 × Full"), else the title alone. A sentence too long for
its line is cut with an ellipsis, whole in its tooltip and to a screen reader (`UiaNode.Help`). Every sentence is a string
of Karpo's in all 30 languages (`dock.panel.*`).

**A row under the choice it follows** (`OptionRow.Under` → `FlyoutItem.Setting`/`Under` → `PanelRows.Nest`): the model
says which row only matters after which — an agenda's Days ahead after its Style, a clock's Show seconds after its Style, a
line's Rows/Max rows after its Height (`LineHeightRows`), the accounts' line after Show from (`OptionRows.GroupKey`) — and
the panel stands it in its choice's card, 24 DIP further in (`PanelMetrics.Nest`), a guide line beside it, wherever the two
stood in the menu's order. A row whose choice is not there stays where it is. Nothing is hidden that the menus did not
hide. The search finds a nested row where its choice is; menus show them where they were.

**Show from's accounts a line of words** (`PanelRowKind.Words`): "Ada Lovelace, Contoso, Switzerland" and "Manage
accounts" in the accent at its end, nested under Show from: one row, `OptionAccountRows.Into` (`OptionLink.Accounts` with
its words as `Summary`); "Manage accounts" opens §535's Accounts page. The calendar's own "Public holidays" link is gone
(§351 to §528 two link rows): its countries are named in the line; the calendars themselves, each with §535's colour
button, stay under Services on the Karpo page.

**The look folded** (`PanelGroups.Folded`, `OptionRow.Default` → `FlyoutItem.Default`/`Own`/`Reset`): a widget's look lists
only the values set on it, each saying under its name where it would go back to ("Set here · layout: Windows accent", in
the accent) with a reset — a 32 DIP icon button before its control (`PanelHitKind.Reset`, its first choice's pick:
"Default (…)", §518). The values left to the layout fold into one expander, "6 more from the layout", saying what they
come to ("Segoe UI Variable, Regular, #FFFFFF, …"); opened, each is there to set, and Reset all. §536's preview stays at the look's top, outside the fold. Any row of a default
(a layout's section's on the Look page too) has its reset where it is set. A colour's control is §535's colour button at
the row's end, its reset (or a mixed one's chevron) right before it, and what it is set to ("#E6E6E6", "Default (#FFFFFF)")
before that, all in the value column: the painter draws the control's own cells apart from the reset's
(`PanelPainter.Control`), so a reset never stands in for the control nor its words over it.

**Mixed opens into each one's** (on §528's `OptionRows.Common`): a mixed row keeps each widget's own row
(`OptionRow.Each` → `FlyoutItem.Theirs` → `PanelRow.Theirs`), each named for its widget (`IslandEdits.Header`, two of one
name "Clock (1)", "Clock (2)"). Shut, the row says how they split ("1 × #E6E6E6, 2 × Default (#FFFFFF)"); a chevron
button before its control (`PanelHitKind.Each`) opens each one's own under it, each its own value and its own reset, set
on that one alone (`OptionPick.Target`: `OptionMenu.Apply`/`Row` act on that target only).

**The folder's one page** (`PanelGroups.FolderPage`): a folder selected alone shows the Folder page, as one open arranged
does — no face page of its own. Its header (Folder, where it stands, Cut, Copy, Remove; §527: a click opens it, no Open),
On the bar (each face with its Remove at its end and its settings nested under it, `FlyoutItem.Nests`; Add a face), When
it opens (Alignment), Look (folded). A row of more segments than fit side by side (`PanelRows.SegmentsMost`, 3: a folder's
alignment, a display's position) is a dropdown in the panel (`PanelRows.ChoicesOf`); menus keep their icon buttons (R3).

Metrics as §520/§521: Body 14, Body Strong 14, Caption 12, Subtitle 20; cards 48/60 DIP, 4 apart; controls 240 × 32; icon
buttons 32 × 32; toggles 40 × 20. No config change (Config.Shape as it was).

**Deleted:** the calendar's Public holidays link rows (`OptionHolidays.Into`), the widget page of a folder's face side,
the panel's flat widget page.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests` (the header, several, where it stands; nesting from the model, a row whose choice is not there,
the nested line's place, the search; the accounts' line; groups and their sentences following their values, a kind with
nothing to say, several splitting, a group shut and opened by a search, a sentence cut short whole in its tooltip; the look
folded, a reset back to the default, a mixed value opened into each one's with its own reset acting on it alone; the
folder's page; two or three segmented, four a dropdown; every `BarKind` and `ListKind`: its page builds with its header,
loses no row of its menu nor a setting of its own, its sentences fit or are whole in their tooltip), `SettingsPanelTests`,
`PanelControlsTests`, `HolidaysTests`, `LinkRowsTests`. Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.WidgetPageSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-529-calendar-, -clock-, -kinds- (a clock, the weather, a pin: the picks, their text colour mixed and
opened), -pins- (three pins of a folder), -folder-, each dark and light.

**Not done:** several selected have no Height or Size group (§528 keeps a line's height the one line's), so three pins
can't say "2 × Compact, 1 × Full" for their size; kinds beyond a calendar, a clock, a weather and a pin say their group's
title alone for What it shows.

## 532. The taskbar's right-click menu is the person's again: one for Karpo, on the Karpo page (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the right click context menu of the taskbar should be editable in the settings again. it should
be scoped on a global level"*. It was fixed from 2026-10-12 ("taskbar menu customization should not be possible anymore")
to here; the model had kept its kinds and its drawing (`BarMenus.Lines`, `Tidy`), so this builds the editing again in
today's settings panel; nothing of the settings app's page (8ceaad8) comes back.

**Where it is kept.** `"barMenu"` at the file's top (`Config.BarMenu`): one menu for Karpo as a whole, no layout's and no
display's. Absent, it is the default (`BarMenus.Default`, the fixed menu exactly: Edit, the layouts under no heading, Task
Manager the very last). Every change goes through `BarMenus.Change` — on a copy, repaired, and **out of the file again
where it is the default once more** — so no file holds an unchanged default; `Config.Repair` takes a typed-in default out
too. `BarMenus.Repair`: unknown kinds and actions go, a built-in row's second showing goes, ids unique, at most 100, words
trimmed, a heading's at most 60; a shortcut still to choose stays (the menu draws nothing of it). Shape 69 (§533 took 68). No migration:
there is no file of another shape to read.

**Where it is edited: the Karpo page, a section "Taskbar menu"** (`KarpoMenu.BarMenu.cs`) between General and Services —
a handful of rows, as the Layouts page's layouts, not enough for a side item of its own:

- each entry a row in the menu's order (the person's own things, `OptionOwned`, inline): its name and icon as the menu
  draws it; at its end **↑ Move earlier**, **↓ Move later** and **Remove**. A shortcut and a heading are expanders of their
  own rows: a shortcut's **Target** (a pin's, its kinds App, Folder with Browse…, File with Browse…, Website, Settings page:
  `OptionFields.OfTarget`, the pin's own rows keyed apart per entry), **Name** (the name Windows gives it its placeholder),
  **Arguments**; a heading's **Name**.
- **Add an entry**: a button, its list the built-in rows the menu has not, as Windows names them (Task Manager, File
  Explorer, Run, Terminal, Device Manager, …; Karpo's Edit, Layouts, Show desktop, Quit Karpo), then Separator, Heading and
  Shortcut. What is picked lands at the menu's end.
- **Reset to default**: a button, asked first, greyed while the menu is the default (R11 lets it keep this name: a list of
  the person's put back as it came, no look's values).

Each change is a setting as any other of the page: saved at once, one step of edit mode's undo (`Dock.Apply`).

**Reordering.** The panel drags nothing (§520 dropped every grip), so a thing put in order — the taskbar menu's entries,
and with them the Layouts page's layouts, which could not be reordered in the panel at all — has **Move earlier and Move
later as icon buttons** (`FlyoutTool.Iconic`: a 32 × 32 square, its glyph, its name what a screen reader says) before its
Remove: `OptionMenu.OwnedLevel` gives them to every thing with a move, greyed at either end; a menu keeps its grip as well.
Two rows of one name in one place are keyed apart ("…/Separator #2", `PanelRows.Of`, `Find`).

**Edit stays (decided).** The other ways into edit mode — Win+Alt+Enter on a bar's button, starting Karpo again, dragging
a widget — are not found by looking, and this menu is changed in edit mode's own panel. So "Edit" has **no Remove**; under
its name it says why ("Always in the menu: it's the way into edit mode", `BarMenus.Required`, `WhyNotRemove`). It moves as
any other, and a list typed into the file without it gets it back first.

**Quit Karpo** (`BarMenuAction.QuitKarpo`, "quitKarpo"): addable, in no default — where Quit lives is still the person's
to decide; putting it in the default is one line of `BarMenus.Default`. Chosen, it is the panel's own Quit Karpo
(`Dock.QuitAsked`: `KarpoMenu.Quit`'s question in Windows' dialog, then the host's marked close), once the menu has gone.

Words: ten new `settings.barMenu.*`, in all thirty languages; Move earlier and Move later are `dock.edit.faceEarlier` and
`faceLater`, Separator and Heading the widgets' own, Quit Karpo About's.

Tests: `BarMenuModelTests` (no file: the default, nothing written; a menu of every kind read back as written; changed back
into the default, out of the file; Edit always there; the file's list repaired; added at the end once; Quit addable and in
no default), `BarMenuLinesTests.ThePersonsOwnMenuIsTidiedAsItIsDrawn`, `BarMenuRowsTests.QuitKarpoAsksFirstThenQuits` (a
fake dialog: no, nothing; yes, the way out once), `BarMenuPanelTests` (the section; Add, Move earlier and Remove change the
