menu the bar draws, each undone back to the default and out of the file; a shortcut's and a heading's rows typed in place;
Reset to default), `KarpoMenuTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (R11, R17 with the new heading), `BarLooksTests` and
`SettingsPanelTests` (the layouts' ↑ ↓), `EditDeckClickTests` (Accounts brought into sight under the new section),
`ConfigSchemaTests` (shape 69).

Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-barmenu-dark/light.png (the
default), panel-barmenu-own-dark/light.png (the person's own, its shortcut open); `BarMenuPictures` bar-menu-own-*.png (a
heading over File Explorer, Terminal and a shortcut, the layouts, Quit Karpo, Task Manager).

## 533. Spacing: the room between the widgets, the layout's choice of three; no thin bar flush by itself (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"you should be able to choose the spacing of the widgets on the taskbar, just three modes, none, a
little and more. you decide how they are named. the automatic switch to no space when the taskbar is small should not happen
anymore."*

**Before.** One gap between every two widgets of a section (`Layout.WidgetGap`, §515): 6 DIP on the 48-DIP bar, shrinking
with the icon (`U`: a 16-DIP icon on a bar under 40 DIP gave 4 DIP), never under 2 px; the app buttons of a part the same
(`TileGap`); 14 DIP the least room between two sections (`SectionGap`). And §123's switch: an islands bar under 36 DIP
(`Config.ThinHeight`, so the offered 32) was flush by itself (`Layout.FlushFor`) — its cards across the whole bar, no room off
the screen's edge or its ends, every card, plate, box and ring square — whatever anybody wanted. That was the "no space".

**Now.** A layout's **Spacing** (`TaskbarLayout.Spacing`, `WidgetSpacing`; the file's `"spacing"`, `"none"` / `"small"` /
`"large"`, Small left out), on the Taskbar page under Bar after Size, a segmented control (§521: three short words):
- **None** — no gap: the widgets touch, and an islands bar is flush (§123's look: cards edge to edge and square, no room
  off the edge or the ends), at **every** height. A dock's widgets touch in its panel; a dock is never flush (its panel is
  what stands apart, as ever).
- **Small** (the default, a new layout's and one whose file says nothing) — §515's 6 DIP, 9 and 12 px at 150 and 200 %.
- **Large** — 12 DIP, twice Small: on the bar's 2-DIP grid (the icons are, `Config.IconDips`), 18 and 24 px at 150 and
  200 %, still under the 14 DIP between two sections, so a section still reads as one run and two sections as two.

Each scales with the icon as before (`U`, between a third of its DIP and its DIP: Small 4, Large 8 on a 32-DIP bar at 100 %),
which is the bar's proportion, not a switch: nothing turns to no space by itself any more. `Layout.FlushFor` asks the
spacing alone; `Thin` (the text, the cell's text, the grip, the desktop buttons) still follows the room, a second question.
So a 32-DIP bar spaced Small keeps 3 px of room off the bar and its corners, its cell 26 px rather than 32 (Windows' search box
no longer fits it; on a 28-DIP bar a tray cell is square, its step the cell's side).

**Scope**: the layout's, as its Size, Show and Combine are (`BarLooks.BarRows`); a bar is laid out with its layout
(`Config.WithEdge`; `Config.BarSpacing` reads it without making a layout). A copy takes its source's (`CopyAs`). **Between
sections** nothing changes: 14 DIP at least, in every spacing (a None bar's sections still stand apart; edit mode's room for
a section's "+" is that too). **Everything else follows the one gap**: the blocks and cards, the pointer's reach in the gap
(§160: each neighbour's to its middle; on None's seam the one or the other), a drop's slot and edit mode's Add line (in the
gap's middle, past a section's last where the next one's gap will be), an app part's buttons (`TileGap`), a dock's panel.
No migration: an unknown word reads as Small (`Repair`, as Combine's).

Config shape 68 (`spacing` on a layout; `ConfigWords.txt`). New words: "Spacing", "None", "Small", "Large", in every language.

Tests: `WidgetSpacingTests` (new: each spacing's gap at 28, 32, 48 and 80 DIP, 100 and 150 %, bottom and left; a dock's; only
None flush, at every height, edge and scale, Small and Large never; the room and the spacing two questions; the pointer, a
drop's slot and the Add line in every spacing's gap; edit mode moves nothing; app buttons; absent is Small; written and read
back; an unknown word; the Taskbar page's row after Size and its pick; the panel's segmented control), `BarStyleTests` (the
thin-bar flush tests gone, the islands look at 28 and 32 too), `BarFormTests` (a thin bar's room), `TrayCellsTests`,
`WindowsSearchTests` (the 32-DIP bar shows the icon), `BarLooksTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`; on the real
scene `SceneTreeTests.AFlushBarsPlatesAreSquare` (None square at 32 and 48, Small and Large round), `BarHitsWhereItDrawsTests`
(the 32-DIP bars None at 100 %, Small at 150 %), `EndPadTests`, `IslandCardsTests`. Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`):
`bar-spacing-<none|small|large>-<32|48>-<dark|light>.png` at 150 % (`SceneTreeTests.BarSpacingSheets`).

By hand: Taskbar › Bar › Spacing › None: the widgets touch, square, edge to edge; Large: twice the room; size the bar to 32:
Small keeps its room and corners.

## 531. "+ Add"'s list hangs from the button, as every popup of the edit bar does (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the add widget button still opens the dropdown at the wrong place."*

**What was wrong.** §521 put every popup of the panel on one rule (`PopupPlace.Of`), but "+ Add" and the errors'
indicator were not popups of the panel to it: they kept the bar's flyout path. `EditDeck.AnchorOf` gave the middle of the
button's inner side, `EditDeck.ListEdge` the side the edit bar stands at, and the add list (`Dock.ShowAddList` through
`DeckAdd`, `FolderAdd`, `BeginAdd`, `AddInFolder`, `Pending.Edge`) and the errors' list (`ShowFaults`) were placed as a bar's
flyout: centred on the button, 12 DIP off it, and — panel open — moved off the edit bar by `FlyoutHost.ClearOf`, which
counts the open panel as an edit bar, so the list stood under the whole panel. On a 2560 × 1440 display at 150 % the
button at x −961..−850, y 24..72: its list at x −1269..−543, y 1038..1914, past the panel's foot and the display's
(PanelPopupPlaceTests, before the fix); folded it was centred under the button, 18 px off it, and ran 167 px past the
edit bar's right end. And §521's gap: an Add button at a card's end (Add a country) hung its list flush with its left, past
the panel's right edge.

**The fix: one way to a control's popup.** `EditDeckEvent.Box` (`EditDeck.OnScreen`) is what "+ Add", the errors'
indicator and a page's control hand the dock; `Dock.DeckControlOf` makes it a `DeckControl` — the box, what it stands in
(the edit bar folded, the panel open), that display's work area and scale — and `Pending.From` carries it to the flyout
(`FlyoutPlacement.Control`, `.Within`), for the add list (also into a folder standing open), the errors' list and every
dropdown alike. `Flyout.Show` gives a control's popup WinUI's 4 DIP of air (`PopupPlace.GapDip`) and no bar's edge.
`PopupPlace.Of` keeps a popup inside the sides of what its control stands in: flush with the control's left where that
fits, else flush with its right — WinUI's BottomEdgeAlignedLeft, then BottomEdgeAlignedRight, as a flyout of a button at
a window's end — pushed in only where it would still pass the work area. So "+ Add"'s list hangs from the button flush with
its right, inside the edit bar's width, folded or open, under an edit bar at the top and over one at the foot; Add a country's
flush with its button's right, inside the panel.

What only the edit bar's Add and errors used went: `EditDeck.AnchorOf`, `EditDeck.ListEdge`, the `edge` parameters of
`DeckAdd`, `FolderAdd`, `BeginAdd`, `AddInFolder` and `ShowAddList`, and `PanelPopup`'s own `Edge`, `Work`, `Scale` and
`Gap`. A ComboBox's ten rows, its width and its type-to-jump are a list's (`Flyout.ComboList`): the add list's columns,
hanging from "+ Add", keep their own height and their search.

**Every opener of an add list, and its path.** The edit bar's "+ Add" (folded and open, onto the bar or into the folder open
arranged) and the errors' indicator: `DeckControl` → `PopupPlace`. A page's Add buttons — Add a layout, Add a face, Add a
country, Add a toggle, Add a mail / CalDAV account (`OptionRow.Adds`, `PanelHitKind.Pop`): `Dock.PanelPopup` → the same.
Add a Microsoft account is an act, no popup. A bar's "+" (`AddAtPlus`), the bar's menu's "Add a widget here" and a folder
column's "+" are popups of a bar or a folder, hung from their bar as Windows' taskbar flyouts are, and stay so.

Tests: `PanelPopupPlaceTests.TheAddListOpensUnderTheAddButton` (the stage dock, the bar at the display's foot and top, the
panel open and folded: under or over the button, its 4 DIP of air, flush with its left where that keeps it in the edit bar
and on the work area, else with its right, all on the work area — red before: centred, 12 DIP off, under the whole panel)
and `…OnASecondDisplayAtAnotherScale` (100 %, folded and open); `PanelPopupPlaceTests.Check` holds the dropdowns to the same
rule; `PopupPlaceTests.FlushWithItsRightWhereItsLeftWouldPassWhatItStandsIn`; `SceneTreeTests.TheEditBarsAddListOpensAwayFromIt`
(the list hung from the button, as tall and as wide as a bar's "+" has it: red with a ComboBox's ten rows). Pictures:
`PanelPopupPlaceTests.TheAddListPictures` (add-open, add-folded, add-up) and `PanelPopupPictures`' popup-long (Add a country
flush with its button's right).

## 537. Edit mode opens with its settings panel open (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"when opening edit mode the settings should be open as a default."*

**Every way in, one place.** Edit mode begins in `Dock.BeginEdit` alone, and it opens the settings panel there (`panelOn`,
`panelOpening`) — always, no setting for it. The ways in all go through it: the bar's own menu's "Edit"; a widget dragged at
rest past the threshold (`BeginEditFromDrag`) and a line dragged in a folder open at rest (`BeginEditFromFolderDrag`);
Copy or Cut at rest (`BeginEditFor`); a folder face's "Edit folder"; and every way in from outside (`OpenEditMenu`:
Win+Alt+Enter, a second start, "Manage accounts", "Get Karpo Pro", a link).

**Where.** On the display edit mode was begun on: the bar right clicked, the bar the drag began on; a way from outside on
its bar's display, else the main display's (`OpenEditMenu` hands its display to `BeginEdit`: a display that shows None has
no bar of its own). One panel open at a time, as before.

**On which page.** The one `PanelMemory.Opening` gives as the panel folds out (§520): the page shown last, Karpo the first
time; the selection's where one is (a drag's widget). A way in from outside opens on its own page: the page is chosen
before edit mode begins, so the first frame already shows it, then `OpenPanel` lands at its row.

**No frame folded first.** The panel is set before the arrange, so the dim, the bars' edit dress and the panel open come in
one commit (§359), not the folded bar and a jump to the panel a frame later.

**Folding and leaving, as they were.** Settings ⌃ folds it and edit mode stays; it folds out again on the page it showed.
Escape goes from the inside out as §520 has it: with the panel open, the first Escape folds it (its search's words first,
where any), the next leaves edit mode. Done leaves at once. Edit mode ended, the panel goes with it (`EndEdit`), and the
next edit mode opens it again.

Tests: `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.EditFromTheBarsMenuOpensTheSettingsPanel` (the stage dock on two screens: "Edit" from the
bar's menu on the screen that is not the main one opens edit mode with the panel open on that screen, on Karpo; the Look
page shown, Settings folds it, edit mode stays, Escape leaves; "Edit" again: open on Look; Escape folds it, edit mode
staying, the next Escape leaves). The tests that enter by a second start already fold the panel before what they test.

## 536. Every look has its preview: a sample of what it styles, drawn by Karpo's own painters, at the top of its level (2026-11-07) — a widget's, a folder's and a line's own look none since §562 (2026-11-08) — every sample in dark and light, a slanted line between them, since §582 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07): *"for all the elements where you can edit the style you should show a preview of one of the
elements as well so that a user can see the style / look change directly."*

**Where.** Every level of rows that edits a look says which (`LookShown`, on `OptionRow.Shows`, set in one place:
`LookRows`): the Look page's four sections (`LayoutRows`) and a widget's, a folder's and a line's own Look (`WidgetRow`).
The panel puts its preview at that level's top, over the rows that set it (`PanelRows.PreviewOf`, a row of its own kind,
`PanelRowKind.Preview`): one call site, so a page that lays its look out otherwise (§529) takes it with the level. A menu
shows nothing of it. A divider, which has no look, has no preview.

**What it draws (`LookPreview.SampleOf`, one rule, no row of its own).**

| Look                       | Sample | What                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Taskbar, Taskbar widgets   | Bar    | a piece of the layout's bar (its kind, its size up to 64 DIP): Start, Task view, a folder wearing the clock |
| Widgets in folders         | Lines  | a folder's lines: a compact clock and a calendar                                      |
| Flyouts                    | Open   | a folder open over its face on a piece of the bar, its panel's foot and outline in sight |
| a widget on the bar        | Bar    | the widget itself                                                                     |
| a line                     | Lines  | the line itself                                                                       |
| a folder                   | Open   | its face on the bar, its panel open over it with its first two lines                  |

The bar is the very bar the layout's bars are: a `Layout` of the sample's widgets and a `Scene` (a scene stands inside
another tree now, `Scene(Gfx, ContainerVisual)`), each widget its own island. The lines are drawn as the open folder draws
them: `FolderFlyout`'s plan and painters (`PaintListLine`, `PaintContent`), each line's card in `InkOf`'s colour, its
pattern, its own outline, the flyout's rim round each section. Each in the look's values as they are now, over Windows'
own (`Look.Wearing`), still — and so in what Karpo makes of them (a text colour that would not read on its ground is
darkened as the bar darkens it, `ToneRules`).

**Stand-ins (`LookStand`).** Nothing of this PC's or the network's: the clock stands still at 9:41 today (`Clock.Still`,
on the drawing thread for the moment a sample is made), a calendar shows made-up events of no account (a team meeting at
10:00, lunch at 12:30, localized). A widget whose content is this PC's or an account's (the weather, the mail, the tray,
the open apps, a pin…) is not drawn itself: a stand-in wearing its look takes its place (`LookPreview.DrawsItself`: the
bar's own buttons, folders wearing the clock, the date, an icon, a timer…; lines of the clock, the calendar's views,
headings, timers, power buttons).

**On what.** The sample's room is the card's whole width less 16 DIP a side, under the Caption "Preview": 136 DIP of lines,
128 of an open folder, a bar's thickness and 12 over and under it; its ground a quiet checker, which shows what of a look
is see-through; its corners 4 DIP.

**Drawn once a look (`LookPreviews`).** A sample is visuals of its own in a layer over the panel's one surface, cut to the
page: the surface draws the Caption and the room, the layer the sample where the room is as the page is scrolled, in the
same commit. Its key is every value it is drawn from — the layout's look, its bar's kind and size, the widget's settings,
Windows' look, the scale, the room's size, the day (`LookShown.Values`, `LookPreview.KeyOf`) —, worked out once a look
(the rows are made again at every change, so a new `LookShown` is a new look); the same key, the same sample kept: a
scroll, the pointer, the page shown again draw nothing. A value changed draws its one sample again. A colour being mixed
(§523) is tried on a config of its own (`Dock.MenuMixed`, `Apply(next, save: false)`), whose rows the panel is made of
again: its preview shows the colour tried while it is dragged. Under the search's suggestions a sample gives way to them.
Edit mode ended, the samples and their widgets go.

**To a screen reader** a preview is an image named for what it shows ("Preview of Taskbar widgets", "Preview of Clock"),
nothing to press, no stop of the keys.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests` (every level that edits a look has its preview at its top and nowhere else; each look's sample;
a value changed another key, the layout's name the same; a colour mixed on the trial config reaches the preview, the config
it began on untouched; every widget's sample itself or a stand-in in its look, never one that reads this PC; the stand-ins'
clock and calendar, put back after; the preview an image, no control, no stop, not found by the search);
`SceneTreeTests.LookPreviewSheets` (the Look page's four sections, a clock's, a calendar's and a folder's Look, odd values,
dark and light: preview-*.png); `SceneTreeTests.ALookChangedDrawsItsPreviewAgainOnceAndNothingElseDoes` (the pointer and a
scroll draw nothing again; a value changed draws once, another picture).

## 534. Lock the taskbar; a bar not locked dragged to another edge of its display (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"you should be able to lock the taskbar, on the right click menu."* and *"you should be able to
drag and drop the taskbar to move it to the different edges of the screen."*

**One setting, Windows' words.** `lockTaskbar` (`Config.LockTaskbar`), Karpo's, every bar's alike as Windows' lock is
every taskbar's: on in a new config and in a file that does not say, as Windows ships its taskbar locked. Two homes write
the one value: the bar's right click, "Lock the taskbar" right under "Edit" (`BarMenuAction.LockTaskbar`, the two rows
about the bar itself; ticked while locked, a click turns it) in the default menu — a built-in row of §532's, so a menu
of the person's own has it where they put it from the Karpo page's Taskbar menu, and not until they do —, and the
settings panel's Taskbar page, a switch under "Bar" after the bar's own rows (`BarMoves.LockRow`). Windows' own wording in every language Karpo speaks ("Taskleiste
fixieren", "Verrouiller la barre des tâches", "タスク バーを固定する" …). Config shape 70.

**What the lock locks (decided): the bar's place and size, at rest; never edit mode.** As Windows' lock stops the taskbar
being moved or resized: locked, the grip along a bar's inner edge drags nothing and shows no resize cursor
(`BarMoves.Grips`), and a press on the bar's empty room is only a press (`BarMoves.Carries`). The grip band is still the
bar's room for its menu, so a bar its widgets cover end to end keeps a place to right-click (2026-10-04: the band runs the
bar's whole length so it is the bar on every bar). Edit mode is not locked: it is the way to arrange the bar on purpose, its grip drags the height
whatever the lock says, and a widget dragged at rest still turns edit mode on. Nothing else is locked.

**Dragged to an edge.** Unlocked, a press on the bar's own room (`HitKind.Panel`: between the sections, never a widget
nor the room a widget reaches over) holds the mouse. Short of the system's drag threshold (SM_CXDRAG, SM_CYDRAG, a move of
more than either, as every drag of Karpo's) it stays a press, its release the click it always was, a right click its
menu. Past it the bar is carried (`BarMove`): the pressed look, the tooltip and what was open go, and the strip it would
stand in on the edge nearest the pointer shows in the accent, as the selection rectangle is drawn (the one pointer
window, `EditBand`), the bar's thickness along the whole edge; nothing shows while that is the edge it stands on. The
edge snaps over as the pointer crosses into another edge's part of the display: the nearest edge in px of the screen
(`BarMoves.Nearest`), the same at any scale; at a corner the edge it stands on stays, else the first of bottom, top,
left, right. All four edges: Karpo lays a bar out along any of them. The release writes the edge where the Display
page's Position writes it (`BarLooks.WriteEdge`, then `Apply`: saved, the bar made again on its new edge, the strip it
holds with it). Escape (heard by the drag's timer, or by the bar where it has the keys), a right press or the mouse lost
leave it where it stood. Not undoable outside edit mode, as no setting is: dragged back, or Position.

**Not in edit mode (decided).** A press on the empty room in edit mode draws the selection rectangle (§144), so the bar
is not dragged to an edge there; the Display page's Position moves it.

**Each display its own edge.** Where a bar stands is its display's (`Screen.Edge`, §348): a bar carried over another
display stays on its own, on the edge of its own display nearest the pointer (the pointer held to its display). Moving a
bar to another display is no edge of this model.

Tests: `BarMovesTests` (the nearest edge from pointer positions, corners, a display left of the main one and pointers
over other displays, the same at 100 %, 150 % and 200 %; the landing strip; the drag threshold, each axis its own; what
the lock stops at rest and leaves to edit mode; locked by default and in a file without it; the setting round-tripped;
the menu's row ticked with the setting and its command the dock's; the page's switch the same setting; the drop writes
Position's edge); `BarMoveTests` (the stage dock: unlocked, the bar pressed on its room and carried up shows its
landing at the top and stands there, the file saying so; locked, nothing shows and it stays; Escape mid-drag takes the
landing away and leaves it at the bottom); the bar menu's tests with the new row (`BarMenuLinesTests`,
`BarMenuModelTests`, `BarMenuRowsTests`, `BarMenuTests`, `DockMenusLanguageTests`) and the Taskbar page's
(`BarLooksTests.TheBarsRowsAreCutFourWays`).

## 535. Accounts a page of their own; every colour a colour button that shows its colour (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"accounts should get their complete own section."* And: *"right now it is just a color button,
but the button should show the color, it does not actually have to show the color itself."*

**Where the accounts were.** §335 to §534 they were one row of the Karpo page, "Accounts" under Services (`KarpoMenu.Rows`,
`OptionAccountRows.Row`, an OptionRowKind.Things level), on the panel an expander whose rows were the accounts and the ways
to add one. "Manage accounts" landed there (`EditEntries`: Karpo, `OptionAccountRows.Accounts`).

**The Accounts page.** A side item of its own right after Karpo (`PanelPage.Accounts`, the accounts' glyph): the accounts
are Karpo's as a whole, as its page is, and stand on every display, None or not. Its rows are `KarpoMenu.Accounts`
(`OptionAccountRows.Page`), built and picked as the Karpo page's are (`SettingsItems`, `SettingsMenu.Page`,
`KarpoMenu.Of(KarpoPage)`: one way for both pages, the row a pick finds its row in by the page it came from):

    Your accounts
      me@outlook.com              ˅   an expander: its kinds' headings, a switch per calendar, inbox, book and list with
        Microsoft account                its count, its colour button before its switch; Sign in again, Remove (asked
                                         first) at its head's end
      me@example.com      Remove      one with nothing synced yet: a row with its buttons
      (No account yet)                a note, for none
    Add an account
      Add a Microsoft account         a button, what it gives said before it
      Add a mail account          ˅   its form: the address, the password, the server set by hand, Test and Add
      Add a CalDAV account        ˅   the same

The things stand on the page itself (`OptionRow.Inline`, as the Layouts page's layouts, §521), no "Accounts" expander over
them. Nothing about accounts is left on the Karpo page; Services is Public holidays and Online. "Manage accounts" (a
widget's, a face's, an account's error, `OptionLink.Accounts`) lands on the page itself and says so at its end
("Accounts"), its help "Opens Accounts in Accounts" as Display's says Display's. The search finds the accounts' rows there
("Accounts › me@outlook.com"). There is no account-wide setting yet.

**A form's words stay while the page does.** A form's words and its password went with any menu closing (§338); on the
panel a popup is a menu, so picking a mail form's Security wiped the form being filled. A popup of the panel
(`Pending.Drops`) wipes nothing; the form goes as the panel folds or edit mode ends (`MenuAccountsClosed`). A form's try
answered shows the panel again (`MenuAccountsChanged`), as it showed a menu standing open.

**Colour buttons.** A colour on the panel was two things: a colour row a 240-wide dropdown with a 16-DIP swatch in it, and
a thing's colour (an account's calendar's, a holiday calendar's: `OptionMenu.ColourTool`, a `FlyoutTool` with a `Swatch`)
a button of words, "Color", the colour nowhere — and an account's calendar's switch was not drawn at all (a row of buttons
with a switch, `FlyoutControl.Tools.Switch`, was read as its buttons alone). Now every colour is one control, the
Community Toolkit's ColorPickerButton: a button 68 × 32 whose start is the colour itself, a swatch 32 × 20 inset 6, rimmed
so it shows on a card of its own colour, over a checker where it is see-through, Windows' own (accent and base, half and
half) where it is left to Windows, a slash for none; its chevron after it; its popup the §523 picker. A colour row says
what it is set to before it ("Default (Blue)", "Automatic"), in the 240 every value control has, so the default reads in
words and the colour it comes to in the button. A thing's colour button has no words (its tooltip and a screen reader say
"Color"). An account's calendar's row is its colour button, then its switch at its end (`PanelRow.Switches`), a click on
the switch its flip. One painter for every swatch of the panel (`PanelPainter.Swatch`), the colour drawn from the row's own
(`PanelSwatch.Of`: a colour row's tile, a tool's `Swatch`).

Tests: `AccountsPageTests` (the side item after Karpo; the page's rows; every key the accounts' rows have sent by a control
of the page, none by the Karpo page; the search; an account's calendar's button showing its Automatic and its picked colour,
68 × 32, its switch's pick; every colour of every page a colour button); `KarpoMenuTests.TheAccountsAreEveryAccount`,
`OwnedLevelsTests`, `AccountFormTests`, `EditEntriesTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`, `MenuRulesTests` and
`ConfigCoverageTests` held to the page. Pictures: `panel-accounts-{dark,light}.png` (a Microsoft account open, its
calendars' colour buttons and switches), `panel-colours-{dark,light}.png` (the Look page's Taskbar colours).

## 538. An app's icon follows the bar past 24 DIP: half its height (2026-11-07)

The person, looking at the Store's pictures of a 72-DIP bar: "the icons just dont have a good size when the bar is that
zoomed in ... as if you didnt zoom in and then took a screenshot that you would have cropped", and asked that apps and
widgets both grow with the bar.

**Why it looked cut out.** `Config.IconDips` made Start's, the pins' and the open apps' icon half the bar on a 2-DIP grid
but held it between 16 and 24 DIP, so from a 48-DIP bar up it stood still while everything else on the bar grew: the
cells and their text (`CellTextDips`, in proportion to the cell), a widget's glyph (`Fit.SystemIcon`, a third of the
cell, Windows' 16 DIP on its 48-DIP bar). On a 72-DIP bar the apps were a third of it beside widgets that had grown.

**Now.** Half the bar, on a 2-DIP grid, 16 DIP at least, up to the tallest bar's 80 (`Config.MaxHeight` / 2): 24 on 48,
36 on 72, 48 on 96. The buttons' measures were always in proportion to the icon (`UnitFor`: the 40-DIP highlight of a
24-DIP icon, the 44-DIP cell), so they grow with it as the comment said they would. Widgets already followed the bar; the
tray's icons keep their own bound (`TrayIconPx`, a step under the pins).

Tests: `CellGridTests.TheIconSizeAlwaysFollowsTheBar` (half the bar, 16 at least, at every height) and
`ATallBarsAppIconsKeepGrowing` (36 DIP on a 72-DIP bar, 80 on the tallest).

## 539. The envelope in the middle of its button, its count over the end (2026-11-07)

The person: "the email face / taskbar widget looks like it is off center (with the count), this should not be".

A face with a count (the mail's envelope, the bell where it shows its count) keeps the room of its widest count, "99+",
after its glyph whatever it shows (§276, `FaceSize.Trail`), and `FolderIsland.FaceBoxes` centred the faces together with
that room, so the envelope stood half the room left of its button's middle. The faces are centred without the last
face's trail now: a lone envelope is the button's middle, and its count stands out over the button's end, which holds it
(`GlyphBadge.Place` keeps the pill inside the cell), as an app's badge stands on its icon. The button's length is what
it was (`Along` still counts every trail), so nothing on the bar moves.

Tests: `FaceCentringTests.TheEnvelopeIsInTheMiddleOfItsCellBesideItsCount` (the envelope's box in the cell's middle
within half a pixel, bars of 32 to 72 DIP, at 100 and 150 %).

## 540. Windows' notifications kept off the bars (2026-11-07) — every panel of Windows' since §580 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the windows notifications on the main screen overlap the taskbar. is this something that would
be fixable?"*

**What was seen**, read-only on the user's PC (26300, both displays 3840x2160 at 150 %, Karpo's bar on the right of the
main display and at the bottom of the other): the work area ended at 3777 (the bar's 63 px held, `rcWork`), Explorer's
taskbar auto-hidden (`ABM_GETSTATE` 1) and hidden, as §465 has it. A notification that came while a WinEvent hook listened:
its window, a `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow` of ShellExperienceHost.exe titled "New notification", went from below the screen
to 3246,1848..3840,2160 (flush in the display's corner, 594x312 with Windows' 12 DIP gaps inside it, over the bar), stayed
6.5 s, was cloaked and moved below the screen again, and was gone a while later. No `EVENT_OBJECT_SHOW`: it is shown by
moving it. A second one 2.5 min later: the same window, placed in four steps within 2 ms (no height, 65 px, 312 px reaching
below the screen, then the corner); each step is read as the window is when heard, so mostly one move follows.

**Why.** Windows places it by Explorer's taskbar, never by the work area: the strings of its host
(`Windows.UI.ActionCenter.dll`) name `WindowsUdk.UI.Shell.TaskbarLayout`, which Explorer serves over the shell's own channel,
with a `TaskbarLocationFallback`. An auto-hidden taskbar holds nothing, so the window stands in the corner; a Karpo bar there
is only an appbar, which that channel never hears of. Nothing an app can say makes Explorer's taskbar match the bar: Windows
11's taskbar has no edge but the bottom, a taskbar not auto-hidden takes its strip of the screen from the windows, and the
channel is Explorer's (no way in short of injecting into it). `ABM_GETTASKBARPOS`, which Karpo's tray passes on, is not what
the host reads.

**Now** (`ShellPopups`, Karpo.Dock): every top-level CoreWindow of ShellExperienceHost that reaches into a strip the work area
leaves out is moved off it by the strip's thickness, so Windows' own gap to the screen's end is its gap to the bar
(`ShellPopupPlace.Clear`): left of a bar at the right, above one at the bottom, both where both are; nothing for a bar at the
top or the left, a bar that hides (it holds nothing), a window off the screen (a notification gone below it is never pulled
back), or one larger than the work area. Pixels throughout, so any scale; any display, though notifications come on the main
one. The same rule takes the notification centre and the calendar (Win+N, the same host; not seen live) where they stand
on a bar. Heard by out-of-context WinEvent hooks scoped to that one process (`EVENT_OBJECT_LOCATIONCHANGE`, `_SHOW`,
`_UNCLOAKED`); the host is found by its process at a reconcile, again where it ended (at most every 5 s while none runs). The
move is `SWP_ASYNCWINDOWPOS`, never waiting on the host, and counted: six per window in 10 s (`ShellPopupMoves`), so a host
that put it back each time would be let be, never fought. Each move is a line of appbar.log. Never from a dock on a config of
its own (a test, `--smoke`) or beside a made-up display. No config change.

**Not covered.** Quick settings (Win+A, ShellHost.exe's `ControlCenterWindow`), the volume and brightness indicator and
Explorer's own menus are other hosts, not looked at live here; where one of them stands on a bar it is left as Windows puts it.
An app's own notification window (Teams, Chrome's) is the app's.

Tests: `ShellPopupsTests` (the measured window on a bar at the right and at the bottom, at 150 % and 100 %; bars at the top and
left move nothing; both edges; Windows' gap kept; a window clear already, off the screen, over the whole screen, a tall flyout
stopping at the work area's top; a display left of the main one with a bar on its left; six moves in 10 s per window). No
test moves a real window.

By hand: with Karpo's bar at the right or the bottom of the main display, start a 5 second timer in Windows' Clock app (or wait
for a mail or chat): its notification comes beside the bar, not over it, and appbar.log has a line *"Windows' popup ... moved
off the bars to ..."*. With the bar at the top, the notification stands in the corner as before. Win+N with the bar at the
right: the notifications and calendar stand left of it, not over it.

## 543. The taskbar menu a page of its own, after Taskbar (2026-11-07) — the Taskbar page's last section since §553 (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"taskbar menu should get its own configuration section."* §532 put the editing of the taskbar's
right-click menu on the Karpo page, a section "Taskbar menu" between General and Services ("a handful of rows, not enough for
a side item of its own"). Now it is a side item of its own, as §535 made the accounts one.

**Where it stands: right after Taskbar.** The side list is Karpo, Accounts, Display, Layouts, Taskbar, **Taskbar menu**, Look
(then Folder and Widget while there is one). It is about the taskbar, so it stands by Taskbar rather than with the other
pages of Karpo as a whole; it is still Karpo's one menu (`Config.BarMenu`, no layout's, no display's), so unlike Taskbar it is
on every display's panel, a display that shows None too, where it follows Layouts (Taskbar and Look are not there). Its
glyph is Segoe Fluent Icons' BulletedList (U+E8FD, `OptionGlyphs.BarMenu`): rows each a mark and a name, as a menu's rows are
an icon and a name; the font has no context-menu glyph of its own, and List (U+EA37) reads as lines of text.

**The page.** `PanelPage.BarMenu`, its rows `KarpoMenu.Of(KarpoPage.BarMenu)` = `KarpoMenu.BarMenu`, built and picked as the
Karpo and Accounts pages are (`SettingsItems`, `SettingsMenu.Page`: one way for the three pages, a pick finds its row by the
page it came from; `Dock.PanelOf` adds it between `Looks(Taskbar)` and `Looks(Look)`). Everything of §532 moved whole: the
entries in the menu's order on the page itself (`OptionRow.Inline`) with ↑ ↓ and Remove, a shortcut's and a heading's rows
opening to their fields, Add an entry, Reset to default. No heading over them: the page's title says it. Its words are the
section's ("Taskbar menu", `settings.barMenu.header`, in every language already); nothing new to translate.

Nothing of it is left on the Karpo page (General, Services, Karpo, Quit); `KarpoMenu.BarMenuHeading` is gone. The search
finds its rows there ("Taskbar menu › Notes"). Nothing linked to the old section (no `OptionLink`, no `EditEntry` landed
there), so nothing needed pointing elsewhere. No config change (shape stays), no migration.

Tests: `BarMenuPanelTests` (the side item right after Taskbar, its glyph, no heading on it, the dock's order in
`Dock.PanelOf`; every key of the menu's rows — each entry's move and Remove, a shortcut's and a heading's fields, Add, Reset —
sent by a control of the page, none by the Karpo page nor a row of it there; the search; add, move and remove still change the
menu the bar draws and are undone back to the default; a shortcut and a heading typed in place; Reset), `KarpoMenuTests`
(the Karpo page's sections without it; `PanelOf` builds the page the Karpo way), `KarpoMenuGeneralTests`, `MenuRulesTests`
("Taskbar menu page" a page of the corpus, R17 no headings, R18 its own home), `SettingsPanelTests` (the side list's order,
the keys reaching its side item), `EditEntriesTests`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.
SettingsPanelSheets` panel-barmenu-dark/light.png (the default), panel-barmenu-own-dark/light.png (the person's own, its
shortcut open), now of the new page.

## 542. Explorer's taskbar draws nothing when it shows itself (2026-11-07)

The finding (a read-only watch on the user's PC, 26300, both displays 3840x2160 at 150 %, 60 Hz; Karpo's bar on the
right of the main display and at the bottom of the other, left of it): Explorer showed its `Shell_TrayWnd` and
`Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd` again and again, and Karpo's hook (§89) hid them within a few ms — 159 shows and hides in 16 min.

**What was seen** (out-of-context WinEvent hooks on Explorer, `DWMWA_CLOAKED`, `DwmGetCompositionTimingInfo`):

- In bursts, each burst once more 5.0 s later (a timer of Explorer's), then quiet for 10 s to a minute: 57 shows in
  4.4 min while the person worked. Each show is Explorer laying its taskbar out — `EVENT_OBJECT_REORDER` on `Shell_TrayWnd`
  and a move of its `TrayNotifyWnd` (the notification area's width), often a name change in its XAML just before; or the
  desktop's `WorkerW`, `Start` and `MSTaskListWClass` moved (a work area); or a settings change and the bars' setpos.
  Explorer re-asserts its window as shown whenever it lays it out. Nothing of Karpo's asks it to: the icon calls the tray
  passes on reach Explorer just the same without Karpo, and the pointer stood still through the idle bursts.
- Shown 1–17 ms (4.8 ms on average), never cloaked (`DWMWA_CLOAKED` 0), topmost and raised over Karpo's bar
  (`WS_EX_TOPMOST`, the reorder). DWM composed a frame during every show, and 17 of 57 crossed a vblank: drawn on the
  screen. On the main display the auto-hidden taskbar stands at 0,2158..3840,2230, a 2 px sliver; on the second it
  stands where an unhidden one does, -3840,2088..0,2160 — all 72 px over Karpo's 63 px bar. That is the flicker. At
  Karpo's start Explorer showed them for 300–500 ms; after a display or scale change 130–240 ms (docs/resilience.md).

**Why the hook alone can't help.** Explorer's re-show can't be stopped from outside: it is Explorer's own `SetWindowPos`
on its own window, and a hook only answers it. Cloaking another process's window is refused
(`DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_CLOAK)`: `E_ACCESSDENIED`, tried on a test window of another process); a move is undone at
the next layout.

**Now** (Karpo.Dock\Taskbar.cs, `Surfaces.OtherAppBlank`): every taskbar window of Explorer's has an empty window region
while Karpo hides it — set before it is hidden (`Cover`), and on any taskbar window that shows without one (the hook: a
display's taskbar Explorer made anew); the reconcile covers again where a window has none (`Taskbar.Off`: *"has a window
that would draw again: blanked and hidden"*; once per window, so a refused region never loops). DWM draws a window only
inside its region and input goes by it too, so a show draws nothing and takes no press; the region stays through
Explorer's own moves and shows (Explorer sets none: `GetWindowRgn` said none on both). The hook still hides it, so
nothing else changes: the windows hidden as before, auto-hide as before (§465). Putting the taskbar back (`PutBack`:
a quit, the crash handler, the guard) gives each window its own region again before showing it.

**Not covered.** A dock and its guard ended together leave the taskbar auto-hidden, hidden and now blank too, until Karpo
starts again or Explorer restarts (hidden until then before, §465's table). The churn stays: Explorer shows, Karpo
hides, a few ms of their time per burst, nothing in sight.

Tests: `TaskbarStateTests.ATaskbarWindowWithoutItsBlankRegionIsCoveredAgain` (`Taskbar.Off`),
`TaskbarBarsTests.ABlankedWindowHasAnEmptyRegionAndPutBackNone` (a window of the test's own, never shown);
`RawWindowCallsTests` counts the new call, and §540's `SetWindowPos`, which stood outside Surfaces and failed the rule
(`Surfaces.OtherAppMove` now). Karpo.Resilience reads the region (`WindowSeen.Blank`, `InSight`): a taskbar visible but
blank is not in sight, and `dock-killed` asks for one shown and drawn.

By hand: with the bar at the bottom of the second display, watch its bottom edge for a minute while working (open and
close an app with a notification icon): no flash of Windows' taskbar over the bar. Quit Karpo: Windows' taskbar there
and drawn, not auto-hidden; start Karpo again: gone.

## 545. Quit Karpo in General; the side list's footer says what is placed against the licence (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"quit karpo should be removed. where it is right now there should be a element that shows how many
layouts and widgets are already placed and the limit on them depending on pro or basic version."* Asked where Quit goes then
(the footer was the one way out in the app: no tray icon, the bar's menu has no Quit by default, §532), *"quit karpo should go
into the general settings."*

**Quit Karpo, General's last row.** `KarpoMenu.Rows` puts `KarpoMenu.Quit` under General after Formats, a row that acts as every
other: on the panel a card saying what it does ("Closes the dock and gives the taskbar back", its `Why`) before its button
"Quit Karpo" (§521: an act a button, its words the row's name). Pressed, Windows' dialog asks first, as it did (its
`DeleteQuestion`, `Dock.SettingsPicked`), then the host's marked close (`DockHost.QuitBy.Menu`). Gone with the footer item: the
foot row (`OptionRow.Foot` and OptionMenu's handling of it, ⚙'s rule over it, `KarpoMenu.QuitRow + "-"`), `SettingsContent.Quit`,
`PanelHitKind.Quit` and its rect, paint and UI Automation node. The bar's menu's own Quit Karpo (§532) is the same row, as before.
The way out by hand is now *Edit › Karpo › General › Quit Karpo* (store/README.md still says *Edit › gear › Quit Karpo*).

**The footer, where Quit stood.** `LicenseView.Footer(status, config, shown)`, Core's and pure: the licence as the dock has it
(`StoreLicense.Status`), the widgets of the layout the panel's display shows counted as `LicenseGate` counts them
(`LicenseCount.Widgets`, per layout: a folder once, pins and Windows' own buttons free), the layouts `Config.Layouts`' count.

    ─────────────────────────────          (a rule, 16 in)
    Widgets               7 of 20          Caption 12: the name, the value at the end (TextSecondary)
    ━━━━━━━──────────────────────          a ProgressBar: 1 DIP track, 3 DIP rounded bar, 24 tall, 12 apart
    Layouts               1 of 2
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━───────────────
    Get Karpo Pro                          a HyperlinkButton in the accent, 32 tall, 8 off the body's foot

- **The free version** (also "checking" and an unreachable Store, which the limits hold as free): a meter for the widgets and
  one for the layouts, the bar in the accent under the limit, Windows' caution (SystemFillColorCaution) at it, critical past it
  (a copy over its limits keeps what it has, §138), full from the limit on; high contrast the accent alone. **Get Karpo Pro**
  (`S.CoreLicenseGetPro`, the add list's words) leads where the add list's and a refusal's lead (`EditEntry.GetPro`: Karpo ›
  Karpo Pro, `OpenPanel`): no Store asked by the footer itself.
- **Pro** (and a developer build): what this copy is (`LicenseView.Title`: "Karpo Pro", "Developer build") in Body Strong over
  "12 widgets · 3 layouts" in Caption; no meter, no link.
- A display that shows None has no layout's widgets to say: the layouts alone.
- **Live.** The footer is built with the panel's pages (`Dock.PanelOf`), so a widget added or a layout made shows at once; the
  licence changing (the Store's answer, a purchase, Restore a purchase) raises `StoreLicense.Changed` on the Store's thread,
  posted to the dock's, which draws the open panel again (`Dock.LicenseChanged`).
- **To a screen reader** each meter a progress bar named "Widgets: 7 of 20" (`dock.edit.usage.said`), Pro's line a text, Get
  Karpo Pro a link (UIA's Hyperlink, Invoke). The keys stop on the link after the side list (`PanelLayout.Stops`); the meters
  are read, never a stop.

New words (every language): `dock.edit.usage.widgets` "Widgets", `dock.edit.usage.layouts.one/other` "1 layout" / "3 layouts",
`dock.edit.usage.said` "{name}: {value}"; "Layouts", "7 of 20", "12 widgets", "Get Karpo Pro" and "Karpo Pro" were Karpo's
already. No config change.

Tests: `LicenseViewTests` (the free version below, at and over each limit: the meters, their fill, what is said; the counts
LicenseGate's — a meter under its limit exactly where the gate allows one more; Pro's and a developer build's line; a display
showing None; the footer following a widget added, a layout made, the licence come to Pro), `SettingsPanelTests` (Quit Karpo
General's last, an Action, once on the page, its button a stop of the keys, done as the dock does it: asked first — a fake —,
quitting only on yes; the footer's metrics; the meters progress bars named "Widgets: 7 of 20", Get Karpo Pro a link the keys
reach; Pro's line, no link), `KarpoMenuTests` and `KarpoMenuGeneralTests` (Quit in General, nothing at the foot), `MenuRulesTests`
(R12: Quit General's last). Pictured (`SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): every panel scene with the free
footer, panel-general-{dark,light} (General, Quit Karpo its last), panel-usage-limit-dark (20 of 20, 3 of 2), panel-usage-pro-dark.

## 546. A background's opacity is drawn without transparency effects too; a chosen one never follows Windows' mode (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the background of the taskbar changed with the dark / light mode but it should not. also the
opacity of the taskbar does not work."*

**What was seen**, read-only on the person's PC: Windows' transparency effects are off (`EnableTransparency` 0), Windows'
mode dark (`SystemUsesLightTheme` 0, `AppsUseLightTheme` 0). The default layout's Taskbar had been Graphite dark's
`#E01B1C1F` (88 %) until 00:13 (config.before-qa-2026-11-07.json); at 12:43 it said `{"pattern": "grid"}` — no background,
so Windows' own — the Taskbar widgets' background, outline and text gone with it, their accent kept. No path of Karpo's
was found that drops a value chosen: a layout's section is written by its Look rows (`Looks.WritePaint`, the mixer's
`SetColor` on a copy of the config, kept as one change or the copy put back), Apply palette and Reset all only; §528's
several-widgets writes are widgets', Repair holds a look to what it may say (`LookValues.Normalize`) and keeps every
colour that reads.

**The opacity.** §405 made every see-through surface solid without Windows' transparency effects (`SurfaceStyle.Made`
Opaque, the bar's colour drawn without its alpha; a card's and a folder's line's the same): on this PC the opacity slider
of the colour picker (§523), its hex box's alpha and a palette's 88 % did nothing at all. Now a colour chosen is at its
opacity whether the blur is there or not: with transparency effects it stands on the blur (Acrylic), without them it is
laid straight over the desktop (`Material.Translucent`, new, never in the file) — a bar, a widget's card (`Scene.Theme`'s
`CardFill`, which `DressCards` frosts only with the effects) and a folder's line (`FolderFlyout.LineFill`). Windows' own,
nothing chosen, is Windows' taskbar: its 70 % over the blur with the effects, solid without them, as Windows draws its own.

**The mode.** Windows' own ground follows Windows' mode (`SystemUsesLightTheme`, which Windows' taskbar follows; not the
apps' mode): #1C1C1C dark and #EEEEEE light solid, #202020 and #F3F3F3 at 70 % over the blur — what the person's bar showed
once its background was unset. A colour chosen is painted the same in both modes (it always was). What is derived from
it did not always stay: a ground half opaque or more read dark or light as laid over Windows' surface of the mode
(`ToneRules.Dress`), so an orange at 50 % read dark over #202020 and light over #F3F3F3 and its text, highlight and
pattern's ink went white in the one mode and black in the other. Now it reads as its own colour: the same in both. Under
half opaque the desktop is most of what shows, and the bar reads in Windows' mode as before. A see-through card of a
widget's own still has its text made readable over Windows' surface of the mode in the desktop's place (§464).

Not done, for the person to decide: Windows' own ground in one mode always (say "Default (dark)"), for a bar that keeps
its look when Windows' mode changes without a colour being chosen.

Tests: `BarGroundTests` (a chosen ground and all derived from it the same in both modes, an orange at 50 % among them; its
opacity drawn with and without the effects; opaque solid; Windows' own per mode and effects; a colour set through the
Taskbar's Background row read back from the file at its alpha and painted so; a see-through card and line keep their
alpha), `AppearanceTests.AnOpacityIsHowASurfaceIsMade`, `WindowsOwnIsMadeAsWindowsDoes`,
`BarColorThemeTests.TheMaterialSettlesAgainstWhatWindowsAllows`, and the pictures
`SceneTreeTests.TheBarsGroundIsItsColourAtItsOpacityInBothModes` (UI: the real scene over bands of blue and gold drawn in
its own window's tree, transparency effects off; bar-ground-graphite-88, -orange-50 and -windows, dark and light, each pixel
of the ground the colour at its alpha over the band under it).

## 541. A value set here, or inherited: one mark, its source named, everywhere a value has a default (2026-11-07) — its source a screen reader's alone, every value one line, since §566 (2026-11-08); no value set here or inherited at all since §574 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-07): *"it should be way more visible if a look is overwritten in the widgets settings for example, or if
it is just an inherited look. / property"*. Until now a widget's own look value said "Set here · layout: Windows accent" in
the accent under its name and the rest folded into "6 more from the layout"; nothing said where an inherited value came
from, and the Look page's layout values (Windows' defaults under them) said nothing at all.

**The row model says it** (Karpo.Core\OptionSources.cs). Every row with a default (`OptionRow.Default`, §518/§529) has an
origin (`OptionRow.Origin`: `Inherited` at its first choice "Default (…)", `Overridden` at any other, `Mixed` for several
widgets apart, §528) and a source (`OptionRow.From`, `OptionSource`): a widget's look from its layout's section — Taskbar
widgets for what stands on a bar, Widgets in folders for a folder's line, the Flyouts for a flyout outline —, a layout's
section from Windows. The look editor (`LookRows.Editor`) gives both; several widgets' one row (`OptionRows.Common`) the
source they agree on, or "the layout" as a whole for its sections apart (a clock on the bar and one in a folder). A menu row
carries them (`FlyoutItem.Origin`, `From`; `FlyoutItem.Own` gone), the panel reads them (`PanelRow.Origin`, `Held`,
`ResetTip`; `PanelRow.Source` gone) and draws them in one place (`PanelPainter.One` and `Control`), whatever the kind.

**Drawn so, in Windows' own tokens only:**

| | Overridden (set here) | Inherited |
|---|---|---|
| its start | a 3 × 24 DIP pill in AccentFillColorDefault, 4 in (NavigationView's selection pill) | nothing |
| its name | Body Strong | Body |
| under it | "Set here", Caption Strong in the accent | "From the layout's Taskbar widgets", "From Windows", Caption in TextFillColorSecondary |
| its value | TextFillColorPrimary (a dropdown's, a colour's words, a number's, a text's) | TextFillColorSecondary |
| its reset | the 32 DIP icon button right before its control; its tooltip "Reset to Windows accent (from the layout's Taskbar widgets)" | none |

A mixed row says how many of its widgets set it where some do and some don't ("1 set here, 2 from the layout"), else how
their values split as before; opened, each one's own row (§529) is drawn as above, so which override and which inherit
reads at a glance. A screen reader hears it: each control's description its "Set here" / "From …" (`UiaNode.Help`), the
reset's name what it puts back and from where.

**Counts.** A widget's (and a folder's) Look group head says how many are set here: "2 set here, 5 from the layout", "All
from the layout", several apart "0 set here, 6 from the layout, 1 mixed" (`PanelSentences.Counts`, `OptionSource.Counts`;
with several selected the look group keeps these counts of them all, not §529's split of its first choice). The fold stays,
"5 more from the layout", its summary of what they come to in TextFillColorSecondary; opened, each row says where it comes
from. On the Look page each section's summary is the same count from Windows ("2 set here, 5 from Windows", "All from
Windows") in place of "Default (Windows' own)" / "Custom"; its rows drawn as above. "The layout's look" and "The layout's
look, its own: …" (`dock.panel.look.layout`, `.own`) and "Set here · layout: …" (`dock.panel.look.setHere`) are gone.

**Set, it moves out of the fold; reset, back in (decided).** The page is the model's: a value set is listed above the fold at
once, a value reset goes back into it. So the page doesn't jump under the eye, the panel keeps the row acted on where it
stood (`EditDeck.anchor`): as the content is made again (`EditDeck.Show`), the row last acted on in sight — a dropdown, a
colour, a reset, by the pointer or the keys — is found in the new layout (or, folded away, the head of the fold it went into,
`EditDeck.Showing`) and the page scrolled by as much as it moved, within its scroll; nothing else scrolls. The keys stay with
it: a control gone with the content (a reset, gone once its value is its default's) hands them to its row's first control,
or to the fold's head where the fold is shut (`EditDeck.Open`).

New words, every language: `settings.value.setHere`, `settings.from.{windows,layout,layoutPart}`,
`settings.resetTo.{windows,layout,layoutPart}`, `settings.counts.{layout,windows}.{some,mixed,none}` — each a whole sentence
per source, so no language composes "from" with a name it would have to inflect. No config change.

Tests: `ValueOriginTests` (a bar widget's look from Taskbar widgets, a folder line's from Widgets in folders, a folder's
flyout outline from the Flyouts, a layout's from Windows; set flips it to overridden, its reset back, a layout's too; several
apart mixed, each one's own its own; sources of one kind "the layout"; the counts; the panel: "Set here" and its reset and
tooltip, "From …" and no reset, the group's count, a value set leaving the fold and its reset bringing it back, a mixed row's
widgets each saying theirs and the row its count, the Look page's sections' counts and rows, the reset's tooltip and a screen
reader's words), `ValueOriginDeckTests.AValueSetOrResetStaysWhereItStoodAndKeepsTheKeys` (the real panel: a colour picked
out of the fold stays where it stood; Enter on its reset, the keys on its colour's button; the fold shut, on its head),
`WidgetPageTests` (§529's look tests on the new words). Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.ValueOriginSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-541-clock- (two set here, the rest opened), -calendar- (none set), -mixed- (three clocks, one font its
own, opened into each), -look- (the Look page, a font and an accent set on the layout), each dark and light.

**Not done:** other "Default (…)" choices that are no look — a folder face's source from its line (`FaceSources`), Karpo's
formats from Windows' region (`FormatChoices`), an account's automatic colours (`PartColours`) — carry no `Default` in the
row model, so they show no mark; given one each and an `OptionSource` of their own, they would be drawn the same.

## 544. The settings in Windows' own colours, exactly (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the style of the settings are not yet like the win11 styles"*, and asked what was meant: *"with
the styles i mean the colors dont match what windows has"*.

**What was off.** §526 put the panel in Windows' tokens, but the ones of a flyout, and the ground was none of them: the
panel's ground (`PanelPainter.Ground`) was a blue "Mica" picked off one wallpaper, #1D212A dark and #ECF0F6 light, so every
translucent token on it (cards, controls, the side list) came out blue too. Besides it: a switch that is off was a ring of
TextFillColorSecondary on nothing, under the pointer SubtleFillColorSecondary; a control's rim one flat
ControlStrokeColorDefault, no elevation edge; a text box's rim a dropdown's, no bottom line; a disabled control the rest
fill; an open expander's rows on the card's own fill, apart by DividerStrokeColorDefault; a card under the pointer the card
with a subtle plate over it; the expander's and a link's chevron Secondary; a segment not chosen Secondary; Done no rim; a
link the accent fill, at 80 % under the pointer; the focus ring one ring; the error icon's glyph black at 90 %; the swatches'
rims a hand-picked white at 31 % or black at 25 %; the search's list and the swatches' base the solid colours typed again
rather than their tokens; tooltips a flyout's acrylic.

**Mica, decided: its fallback.** Windows' Settings wears Mica (`DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE` = `DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW`), and Mica
shows only on the active window: inactive, with transparency effects off or where Mica can't be drawn, Windows draws
SolidBackgroundFillColorBase in its place. The panel is a Tool popup (`FlyoutHost`: `WS_POPUP` with `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` and
`WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP`, its content a composition surface): it never takes the activation (the keys come to it through
the dock), so Mica on it would always be Mica's inactive fallback, and a frameless popup without a redirection surface has no
frame for DWM to put a system backdrop behind. So the ground is the fallback itself, `FlyoutTheme.Ground` =
SolidBackgroundFillColorBase, #202020 / #F3F3F3: what the Settings window shows the moment it is not the active one. No tint
sampled off a wallpaper anywhere.

**One source.** `FlyoutTheme` holds every WinUI token the settings surface and its popups draw with (new: `Ground`,
`LayerAlt`, `CardBackgroundSecondary`, `ControlFillDisabled`, `ControlFillInputActive`, `ControlStrokeSecondary`,
`AccentStroke`, `AccentStrokeBottom`, `ControlStrongStroke`, `ControlStrongStrokeDisabled`, `ControlAltFillHover`,
`ControlAltFillPressed`, `AccentDisabled`, `AccentText`, `AccentTextHover`, `AccentTextPressed`, `TextOnAccentSecondary`,
`TextOnAccentDisabled`, `TextInverse`, `Critical`, `Caution`, `ToolTip`), each for dark, light and high contrast (the system colours: the
window's, its text, the highlight, grey text, the hyperlink colour). Quick settings' `QuickTheme` takes its copies of them from
it instead of typing them again (its own HotLight gone). The accent shades are the system's (UISettings): AccentFillColorDefault
is SystemAccentColorLight2 dark and Dark1 light, as it was; `Look` reads AccentLight3 and AccentDark3 too now, for the links.

Sources: microsoft-ui-xaml `winui3/release/1.6-stable`, `src/controls/dev/CommonStyles/Common_themeresources_any.xaml` (the
colours), the controls' `*_themeresources.xaml` (ToggleSwitch, TextBox, Button, ComboBox, NavigationView, Expander, ScrollBar,
ToolTip, ContentDialog, RadioButton, AcrylicBrush), `src/dxaml/xcp/dxaml/themes/generic.xaml` (SystemChromeMediumLowColor);
the Community Toolkit (CommunityToolkit/Windows `main`): `SettingsCard.xaml`, `SettingsExpander.xaml`, `Segmented`,
`ColorPickerButton.xaml`.

**What each thing is now** (`PanelPainter`, every state):

  Secondary pressed.

  then and ControlStrokeColorDefault pressed; a disabled card ControlFillColorDisabled in ControlStrokeColorDefault. An open
  expander (SettingsExpander): its rows on CardBackgroundFillColorSecondary (ExpanderContentBackground), each a card's fill over
  it, apart by CardStrokeColorDefault (an item's top border). The expander's, a group's and a link's chevron Primary.
- *Buttons* (Button: the page's, a row's, a tool's, the colour button): ControlFillColorDefault / Secondary / Tertiary /
  Disabled in ControlElevationBorderBrush (ControlStrokeColorDefault pressed and disabled), words Primary / Secondary pressed /

  pressed), words TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary, Secondary pressed.
- *Dropdowns* (ComboBox): a button's fills and rim, words Primary / Secondary pressed / Disabled, chevron Secondary. *Text and
  number boxes* (TextBox): ControlFillColorDefault, Secondary under the pointer, Disabled, in TextControlElevationBorderBrush;

- *Switches* (ToggleSwitch): off ControlAltFillColorSecondary, Tertiary under the pointer, Quarternary pressed, nothing disabled,

  Secondary / Tertiary / AccentFillColorDisabled, its knob TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary (Disabled). §528's mixed switch as off,
  a dash for its knob. A menu's switch and radio (Flyout.Controls) off: ControlAltFillColorSecondary in
  ControlStrongStrokeColorDefault (a layout's text colour stands in for that stroke as for the text, §396).
- *Segments* (the Toolkit's Segmented): its track ControlAltFillColorSecondary in ControlStrokeColorDefault; the chosen one
  ControlFillColorDefault in ControlElevationBorderBrush; the others SubtleFillColorSecondary under the pointer, Tertiary

- *Links* (§529's words; a value of its own): AccentTextFillColorPrimary, Secondary under the pointer, Tertiary pressed.
- *Colour buttons* (§535, the Toolkit's ColorPickerButton): a Button; the swatch's rim ButtonBorderBrush
  (ControlElevationBorderBrush), the base under a see-through colour the ground; the chevron TextFillColorSecondary, Tertiary
  under the pointer.
- *Focus*: both rings of WinUI's focus visual, 2 DIP of FocusStrokeColorOuter outside 1 DIP of FocusStrokeColorInner (its
  margin −3: the ring 1 DIP further out than before, the one size this changes).
- *Errors*: an InfoBar's error icon, SystemFillColorCritical, its glyph TextFillColorInverse.
- *The search's list* (AutoSuggestBox): a flyout's, AcrylicInAppFillColorDefault's fallback in SurfaceStrokeColorFlyout.

Not changed: the sizes (but the focus ring's); the preview's backdrop (§536, a stand-in desktop: content); the colour picker's

widgets of several kinds selected, a line "Select one alone to change what it shows" and a button for each, selecting it
alone. Gone, and all only it used: its string (`dock.panel.pickOne`, every language), `PanelHeader.Picks` and `PanelPick`
(`PanelRows.HeaderOf` takes each widget's glyph and name), `PanelLayout.Picks`/`PicksLead`, `PanelHitKind.Pick`,
