## 548. The settings panel's shell as one system: one spacing ramp, one column grid, one type ramp (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the settings window just does not look that well designed over all (i am talking about the
shell), it does not look like it comes from one go. go ahead and adjust the elements, spacing, and other stuff as well to
make it look coherent."* — on top of the asks for this panel since §520: as close to Windows 11's Settings as it can be, a
little more compact, clean, nothing drawn that isn't needed, the same sizes for the same things, the edit bar and the panel
one surface, the search centred in the header. The shell is the frame and the structure — the header row folded and open,
the side list and its footer, the page's head (title or §529's header card), its headings, cards, expanders, nested rows,
§536's previews, §541's marks, the scroll —, not what the rows say. The colours are §544's (Windows' tokens); this is the
geometry.

### The audit (before)

Rendered folded and open, Karpo, Accounts, Taskbar, Look, a widget's page, a folder's page, the search, the panel at the
display's foot, dark and light (`SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets`, `WidgetPageSheets`, `ValueOriginSheets`). Measured
against Windows 11's own guidance (learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/design: *Content layout and spacing* — 8 between
buttons, 8 between a control and its header, 12 between a control and its label, 12 between content areas, 16 between a
surface and its edge text, controls in an expander indented 48 and right-aligned; *Geometry* — 8 for windows and flyouts,
4 for in-page elements, 0 where straight edges meet; *Typography* — Caption 12/16, Body 14/20, Body Strong 14/20, Subtitle
20/28, Title 28/36, Semibold for titles) and the controls Windows builds its Settings with (WinUI's NavigationView: items 36
tall with a 4,2 margin, a 40 DIP icon box, 16 DIP icons, words at 48, a 3 × 16 selection pill; the Community Toolkit's
SettingsCard: 16 padding, 1 DIP rim, ControlCornerRadius, 4 between cards; the WinUI Gallery's settings page: a Title over
sections whose Body Strong headings stand 30 under the card before and 6 over their cards).

What doesn't come from one go:

1. **No common left edge between the header and what is under it.** The grip's dots stand at 13 to 23, Settings' gear at 44,
   its word at 68; under them the side list's icons stand at 16 to 32 and its words at 48 — nothing of the header lines up
   with the column it heads. At the right Done ends 8 from the panel's edge, the page's cards 16 from it.
2. **Two icons before one word.** "⠿ ⚙ Settings ⌄": the grip and the gear side by side; the gear says again what the word
   says (and the side list's Karpo wears the same gear).
3. **Unequal gutters round the page.** The page starts 8 after the side list (192), the selection's plate ends at 180, so 12
   of air on its left, 16 on its right; the header's 8, the footer's 16, the cards' 16: five insets for one panel.
4. **No rhythm between sections.** Card to card 4; a card to the next heading 16 (4 + 12); a heading to its cards 8; the title
   to the first heading 8, so "Taskbar" and "Bar" stand on each other; the header card to the first card 12; the page's foot
   12. Windows: 4 between cards, 30 + 6 round a heading.
5. **The page title is no title.** Subtitle 20, the same size as a widget's name in its header card and a step under
   Windows' Title 28: the page's name, a widget's name and a section read as one level.
6. **Chevrons in three places.** A dropdown's and an expander's 20 in from their end, a colour button's 15, a button with a
   list's ("Add a country") and Settings' 18: down a column of rows they zigzag.
7. **Words before a control at two distances.** "On"/"Off" and "Mixed" 12 before their control; a colour's value, an
   expander's summary, a row's value 8; Windows says 12 between a control and its label.
8. **Buttons at two distances.** The header's 4 apart, a row's 8; a reset 4 before its control.
9. **Two pills for one mark.** The side list's selection 3 × 16; §541's "set here" — *NavigationView's selection pill*, it
   says — 3 × 24.
10. **A row that acts reads greyed.** Its words (the card's header: "Closes the dock and gives the taskbar back") in the
    secondary ink where every other card's header has the primary; only a greyed row should look so.
11. **Numbers twice.** The header card's text block nudged by hand (its name 2 DIP up), its tile's glyph 24 and 20 by number,
    its gap 12 a value of its own; the painter adding offsets that are the layout's (`P(12)`, `P(36)`, `P(20)` …), so a
    change in one place leaves the other drawn where it was.

What is coherent already and stays: one ground for the header and the panel, one rim and one shadow round both (the header
row *is* the folded bar, the same 48 DIP, nothing in it moving as it opens, §521); the 8/4 radii; 1 DIP rims; the 48/60
rows, 32 controls, 240 values (§520/§521's compact sizes — Windows' SettingsCard is 68 tall, the person asked for more
compact); the side list's 36/40 items, icons at 16, words at 48 (NavigationView's own); a card's icon at 16, name at 48, an
expander's rows at 48 (Windows: indent 48); the 16 DIP icons (the Toolkit's 20 would want the 68 DIP card).

### The system (`PanelMetrics`, one place per value)

| Token | DIP | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **Spacing ramp** | 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 | nothing else |
| `Tight` | 4 | card to card; side items (2 + 2); icon buttons of a command bar (the header card's); a plate in from the side list's sides |
| `Gap` | 8 | button to button (the header's, a row's); a heading to its cards; the header round its 32 DIP controls; the body's top to its first item and to the page's head |
| `Label` | 12 | words to their control (On/Off, Mixed, a value, a summary); a button's padding |
| `Gutter` | 16 | a card's padding; the page's gutters (the selection's plate to the page, the page to the panel's edge); Done to the panel's edge; the footer's inset; the page's foot |
| `Group` | 24 | one group to the next: the page's head (title or header card) to its first group, a card to the next heading |
| **Columns** (x from the panel's start) | | |
| icon column | 16 – 32 (centre 24) | the side list's icons, the grip's dots |
| word column | 48 | the side list's words, the header's "Settings" |
| page | 196 – (W − 16) | the side list's 184 less its plate's 4, then a gutter; Done ends at W − 16 too |
| in a card | 16 / 48 / +24 / end − 16 | its icon / its name and an expander's rows / each step nested / its control's end |
| chevron | 20 in from its control's end | every chevron: a dropdown's, a colour button's (72 wide), a button with a list's, an expander's, a link's, Settings' |
| **Rows** (y) | | |
| header | 48 = 8 + 32 + 8 | folded and open |
| first side item, page head | header + 8 | level with each other |
| side item | 36, pitch 40 | NavigationView |
| title row | 36 | Title 28/36 |
| heading | 20 | Body Strong 14/20 |
| card | 48 one line, 60 two | Body over Caption |
| header card | 80 = 16 + 48 + 16 | its name (Subtitle) and place (Caption) centred on its tile |
| **Type** | Caption 12/16 · Body 14/20 · Body Strong 14/20 · Subtitle 20/28 · Title 28/36 | Title the page's name; Subtitle a header card's name; Body Strong headings, a group's head, a value set here; Caption every second line and value |
| **Radii** | 8 · 4 · 2 | 8 the panel and its popups; 4 every card, control, button, plate, tile; 2 a swatch; a pill fully round |
| **Strokes** | 1 DIP (whole px) | every rim and divider; the focus ring 2, 2 outside |
| **Pill** | 3 × 16 | the side list's selection and §541's set here, one |
| **Controls** | 32 tall | value controls 240; a colour button 72; a switch 40 × 20; an action button 120 – 240; Done at least 80; an icon button 32 square; the search 320 |
| **Icons** | 16, chevrons 12 | everywhere; the header card's tile 48, its glyph 24 (20 several) |

### What changed

**The grid and the rhythm** (`PanelMetrics`, `PanelLayout`). Every space of the layout is a token of the ramp; what is
built of them says so (`Head = Gap + Control + Gap`, `NavPitch = NavItem + Tight`, `PageLeft = Side − Tight + Gutter`,
`HeaderTall = Gutter + HeaderTile + Gutter`, `ColourWide` from its swatch, gap and chevron). `HeadPad`, `CardGap`, `Pad`,
`HeaderGap`, `HeldMark`, `HeldMarkIn` and `Grip` are gone into them.

- The header: the grip a 32 DIP square in the icon column, its dots' middle 24 in as every side icon's; "Settings ⌄" right
  after it, its words at 48 as the side items', no gear; the buttons 8 apart; Done ending 16 off the edge, where the cards
  end. Folded the same (§521).
- The page: from 196 to 16 off the edge — 16 of air either side of the cards, the selection's plate to them and them to
  the edge. Its head 8 under the header, level with the first side item: a title in **Title 28** (Segoe UI Variable Display
  Semibold) in a 36 DIP row, or the header card. Then each group 24 after what is before it (the head, the last card of the
  group before), its heading 8 over its cards, cards 4 apart, a gutter under the last (`PanelLayout.LayPage`).
- The header card: its name and place one block (a Subtitle line of 28 over a Caption line of 16) centred on its tile, its icon buttons
  centred on it too.
- A name runs to a gutter before its control column (`PanelLayout.NameRoom`, the painter's and the tooltip's one rule);
  `ControlLeft` is the column's start itself; `ControlEnd`, `ValueBox` and `IconX` are the layout's, the painter takes them.

**One style per thing** (`PanelPainter`): every chevron 20 in from its control's end (`Chevron`) — a dropdown's, an
expander's, a link's, a button with a list's (was 18), a colour button's (was 15; the button 72 wide, was 68) and
Settings'; every word said before a control 12 off it (`Label`: a colour's value, an expander's summary, a row's value, a
link's, an action's, as "On"/"Off" and "Mixed" were); a reset or a mixed row's button 8 before its control (was 4); one
pill (`Pill`: 3 × 16, fully round) for the side list's page shown and §541's set here (was 3 × 24); a row that acts says
what it does in the header's ink (it read greyed); every corner `Corner`, `InnerCorner`, `Overlay` or `SwatchCorner`; the
search's suggestions a side item's row (icon at 16, name at 48, plate 4 in). What stays a control's own geometry is §544's
(the focus visual's rings, the elevation borders, a switch's knob).

No config change, no new words.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests.EverySpaceIsAStepOfOneRamp` (the ramp, what adds up of it, the type ramp, a colour button's
chevron), `HeaderSideListAndPageShareTheirEdges` (the grip and Settings on the side list's columns, Done with the cards,
equal gutters, the head level with the first side item — at the top and at the foot, a page and a widget's),
`EveryPageKeepsOneRhythm` (24 / 8 / 4 and the foot on every page, a header card's text and buttons on its tile's middle);
`ItStandsAsThePersonPickedIt`, `EveryControlIsOneSize`, `AccountsPageTests` and `EditDeckMoveTests` on the new positions.
Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): §520's, §529's and §541's sheets, and `panel-taskbar-` (the Taskbar page as it
opens) besides.

## 552. A folder's faces each a section of their own (2026-11-07) — under the heading Faces, the folder's own under Folder, since §563 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the folder faces should have their own sections"*. §529's Folder page held them in one group,
On the bar ("Its faces: Clock, Icon"), each face a row with its Remove and its settings nested under it.

**The page now** (`PanelGroups.FolderPage`, `FaceOf`), top to bottom under its header:

- **each face a section** (a group, `PanelRowKind.Group`), in the faces' order: its head the face's name as the menu says it
  (`Dock.TitleOf`: "Clock", "Clock · Tokyo") with its icon, as every group's head wears its glyph; its rows the face's
  settings — the very rows §529 nested under its row, by the same keys (`Folder/Clock/Time zone`), so a popup, a search, a
  link find them as before — now plain rows of the section; its sentence what it shows where its kind says it
  (`PanelSentences.Shows`), else its name alone. Its key is the face row's marked a group's (`Folder/~Clock`, a second clock
  `Folder/~Clock #2`), so it folds and opens as any group (default open, PanelMemory keeps the shut ones).
- **Remove at the section's head's end**, before its chevron (`PanelLayout.Controls`: a group's head takes its row's buttons
  as an expander's does; greyed for a folder's one face). A text button "Remove": §551's icon-button rule had not landed;
  turning it into the trash icon with its tooltip is that rule's one change (`FlyoutTool.Iconic`). A face with nothing to set
  is a head alone: no chevron, nothing to fold.
- **Add a face**, a button of its own right under the last face, before When it opens.
- When it opens (Alignment), Look (folded) as they were.

**Decided.** The "Its faces: …" sentence went with its group: each face's head names it now, so it said nothing more
(`dock.panel.group.faces`, `dock.panel.folder.faces` gone from every language). Order stays as it is: the panel drags
nothing (§532), a face is still put in order from its menu's grip. A section's head is a heading to a screen reader
(`UiaNode.Heading`, HeadingLevel 2; every group's head, a widget's page's too), its Remove "Remove · Clock". No config
change.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests.EachFaceIsASectionOfItsOwnInTheFacesOrder` (one face and three: a section each in order, its name,
icon and Remove, its rows' keys those nested under its row before, each once; Add a face after them; a face's setting found
under its section, shut and opened by the pick), `AFacesSectionHasItsRemoveAtItsHeadAndIsAHeading`,
`AFoldersPageHoldsItsFacesAlignmentAndLook`, `EveryKindsPage…` (a face's row its section). Pictures: `WidgetPageSheets`'
panel-529-folder-dark/-light (a clock face and an icon face).

## 547. The taskbar never follows Windows' mode: Karpo's own look under the person's, the wallpaper blurred under the bar (2026-11-07) — Windows' mode followed again, Karpo's own of each mode, since §568 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-07): *"the taskbar should always ignore windows dark or light mode. the taskbars appearance should only
depend on the values that ive set. thats it."* — *"the default background of the widgets on the taskbar should not be opaque
at all, it should be a solid background color."* (by default a widget on the bar has a solid, fully opaque card) — *"the
taskbar itself should be a little transparent and should show the desktop background image a little blurred behind it.
(if possible) how blurry the background is should be changeable."*

**What keyed off Windows before.** The dock read Windows' look (`Dock.ReadLook`: `SystemUsesLightTheme`, the accent and its
shades through `UISettings`, `ColorPrevalence`, transparency effects, high contrast, text size, animations) and every bar
wore it in its layout's look (`Look.Wearing`). Everything a layout left unset was Windows' own of the mode (§459, §509,
§546): the bar's ground (#1C1C1C / #EEEEEE solid, #202020 / #F3F3F3 at 70 % over DWM's blur), the text and its quieter
shades, the highlight, the menus and flyouts (`FlyoutTheme.Windows`: #2C2C2C / #F9F9F9, the taskbar flyouts #242424), a
folder's lines, the tooltips, Karpo's menus for the tray and the jump lists, the window previews (`Preview.Palette`), the
glyph variants and Windows' logo (`look.Dark`); the accent everywhere (`Look.Accent`, AccentLight2 / AccentDark1, the bar in
AccentDark2 with "Show accent color on Start and taskbar"); DWM's host backdrop under a see-through bar and card
(`Material.Acrylic`, `Rounded.Frost`) where transparency effects were on; and the swatches of what is unset in the look
rows (`OptionPlace.Dark` was Windows' mode). A mode or accent change rebuilt every bar.

**Karpo's own look (`KarpoLook`, Karpo.Core\SurfaceLook.cs), fixed.** `Look.Wearing(layout)` lays the layout's values over
Karpo's own (`Looks.Of`, over `KarpoLook.Paints`) on `Look.KarpoBase()`: Windows' look with its mode, accent, accent on the
bar and transparency effects replaced — what is left unset is drawn in the dark mode (`KarpoLook.Dark`), in Windows 11's
default blue #0078D4 (#60CDFF on a ground that reads dark, #005FB8 on a light one, AccentDark2 #004C87; §544's text
shades #99EBFF and #003E92), no accent on the
bar, never DWM's blur (`Glass` off). Its values, today's dark ones:

| | Karpo's own | was (dark) |
|---|---|---|
| the bar (Taskbar › Background) | #202020 at 85 % (`#D9202020`), over the wallpaper blurred | #1C1C1C solid without effects, #202020 at 70 % over DWM's blur with them |
| a widget's card (Taskbar widgets › Background) | #2B2B2B solid — Windows 11's dark card (CardBackgroundFillColorDefault, white at 5.12 %) over #202020, made opaque | none |
| text, highlight, outlines, pattern ink | Windows 11's dark: white, its steps; no outline | the mode's |
| menus, flyouts, a folder's lines, tooltips | solid: #2C2C2C menus, #242424 taskbar flyouts and lines, no shadow | acrylic over DWM's blur with effects |
| the Background blur | 30 % | — |

The flyouts and a folder's lines stay solid (decided): they open over windows, not over the wallpaper, and a solid surface
reads over any window; a colour the person gives them keeps its own opacity over the desktop (§546). A ground the person
sets reads in its own mode as before (§546), so a light bar has its glyphs, Windows' logo and the accent's shade for a light
ground; Windows' mode never decides it.

**What still follows Windows, and why.** High contrast (accessibility: Windows asks every app to draw its system colours,
and Karpo does, over every look); Windows' text size and its animation effects (no look either); the settings — the edit
bar, its panel, every popup of edit mode — which wear Windows' own look (§526, `Dock.SettingsLookOf`, now `Look.Plain()`);
and what Windows draws itself in Karpo's process: the shell's context menus, dialogs and scroll bars (`Menu.Theme`, the
process's preferred app mode), and the tray icons apps hand over for their own idea of the mode.

**No re-render on a mode change.** `Dock.LookChanged` compares the taskbar Windows' looks make (`Wearing(null)`, Karpo's
base): where only the mode, the accent, "Show accent color" or transparency effects changed and edit mode is not on,
nothing of the taskbar is built or drawn again — the look is kept for the settings, Windows' own menus follow its mode,
and a widget's settings standing open at rest (§340) are shown again in it.

**The wallpaper under the bar, blurred by Karpo** (Karpo.Core\Wallpapers.cs, Karpo.Dock\WallpaperStrips.cs,
Dock.Wallpaper.cs). DWM's own blur needs Windows' transparency effects (off on this PC) and has no amount, so Karpo draws
it itself, whatever the effects:

1. **Read** each display's desktop through IDesktopWallpaper — its picture (`GetWallpaper` per display; where it says none,
   `SPI_GETDESKWALLPAPER`: a slideshow's or Spotlight's picture as Windows last wrote it), the fit (`GetPosition`) and the
   desktop's colour (`GetBackgroundColor`) —, with the file's write time; when the dock starts, on `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`
   `SPI_SETDESKWALLPAPER` and on a change of displays. Only read; nothing is ever set. A solid colour desktop is its colour.
2. **Map** the bar's strip — its panel's rectangle on the screen and a margin round it the blur reads, three standard
   deviations of the most blur (100 px at 100 %) — to the picture exactly as Windows lays it out (`Wallpapers.Plan`, pure):
   Fill (cover, centred), Fit (all of it, centred, the colour round it), Stretch, Tile (its own size from the display's own
   corner), Center (its own size, centred) and Span (Fill over the rectangle round every display, each its part). Windows
   draws a wallpaper in the display's own pixels, never scaled by its DPI: the scale is the bar's size and the blur's radius.
   Past the display's edge (a bar on a screen's edge) the margin is the display's edge drawn out, not black.
3. **Compose** that strip off the dock's thread (`WallpaperStrips.Compose`): the colour, then each piece decoded by WIC at the
   size Windows draws it (a scaler, only the rows and columns under the strip copied), laid over the colour; posted back
   (`WM_KARPO_WALLPAPER`).
4. **Blur** it on the GPU, Direct2D's Gaussian blur (hard border, the margin all it reads past the bar), into a composition
   surface the bar's size (`WallpaperStrips.Blurred`), which the bar shows under its see-through ground (`Scene.Wallpaper`, a
   surface brush under the panel's colour — and under the cards' holes, so a see-through card stands on it too, §464).

Kept per bar by what it is made of (`WallpaperKey`: the picture and its write time, fit and colour; the display and the
rectangle round them all; the bar's rectangle; the margin, of the scale): composed again only when one of those changes —
another picture, a slideshow's next, another display or arrangement, another DPI, the bar taller, moved to another edge —,
blurred again only when the amount does (a colour change, `Recolour`, re-blurs without composing). A bar keeps what it
showed until its new strip comes. Nothing runs per frame or at rest: one composed strip (the bar and its margin, some 3 MB
for a 2560 px bar at 100 %) and one surface per bar. A bar not see-through — solid, or None (0 %), which is nothing at all
over the desktop — draws no wallpaper. Every kind of bar shows the wallpaper of its display under its own rectangle
(decided): docked, floating (each dock the part under it; a dock covering its shadow now casts it), a place or a bar shown
over the windows — over a window too: the bar is the person's look of the desktop wherever it stands. A place or a bar over the windows
whose background is None shows the wallpaper blurred with no colour over it (`HoverPlaces.Dressed`: Translucent where it
was DWM's blur or solid). Not done: a slideshow
that Windows advances without a `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` is caught at the next one; Spotlight's picture is the one Windows last
wrote (`SPI_GETDESKWALLPAPER`); the settings panel's look samples (§536) show the bar's colour over the panel, not the
wallpaper.

DWM's host backdrop is gone from the bar: `Scene.Backdrop`, `Rounded.Frostable`/`Frost` and the bar windows'
`DWMWA_USE_HOSTBACKDROPBRUSH` (the settings' popups keep theirs, §526).

**Background blur** (the person's "how blurry the background is should be changeable"): on the Taskbar page's look, the
layout's Taskbar section, right after its Background — "Background blur", a number 0 to 100 % in steps of 5 (the settings
panel's slider), Karpo's own 30 %. Each percent is a DIP of the Gaussian's radius, its standard deviation a third of it
(`KarpoLook.Sigma`: 30 % is σ 10 px at 100 %, 15 px at 150 %; 0 the wallpaper sharp). Greyed, "Only where the background is
see-through", while the bar is solid or None. In the file the Taskbar's look's `"blur"` (0 to 100, held so; absent Karpo's
30, set to 30 again it is absent; any other section's dropped): **config shape 71**, ConfigWords.txt written again. No
migration: an older file has none, which is Karpo's own.

**The words.** A layout's look unset is Karpo's own now, not Windows': "Default (Karpo's own)" (`settings.value.karpo`), its
rows "From Karpo" (`settings.from.karpo`, `settings.resetTo.karpo`, `settings.counts.karpo.{some,mixed,none}`, which
replace the `.windows` ones), an unset colour's "Default (#202020, 85%)", "Default (#2B2B2B)", "Default (#60CDFF)" (the
accent its hex: `settings.value.windowsAccent` gone); `settings.look.blur`, `settings.look.blurWhy`; every language.

Tests: `TaskbarModeFreeTests` (the taskbar's every token — the bar, a widget's own values over it, a flyout, a folder's line,
the menus, quick settings — the same for Windows dark and light, Windows' blue and an orange, the accent on the bar on and
off, transparency effects on and off, nothing set and Paper light applied with a flyout outline; Karpo's own values; a light
ground in Karpo's light shade; high contrast still wins; the settings still follow Windows), `BarBlurSettingTests` (the row
after the Background, its range and default, written and read back and held, unset at 30, greyed where not see-through,
the bar's alone, a palette leaving it Karpo's, σ of the setting), `WallpaperLayoutTests` (fill, fit, stretch, tile, center,
span, several displays left of and above the primary one, 150 %, a bar on each edge, the margin, the edge drawn out, a strip
made again only when what it is of changes), and the updated `BarGroundTests` (nothing chosen: Karpo's own in every mode),
`AppearanceTests`, `LookTests`, `MenuPickersTests`, `ValueOriginTests`, `SettingsLookTests`, `ConfigResetTests` and the
persistence tests' default opacity (85). Pictures (`SceneTreeTests`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): bar-wallpaper-blur0-,
-blur30-, -blur100- (the default bar over a test wallpaper made by the test, its strip composed and blurred as the dock does)
and folder-547-, menu-547- (an open folder, a widget's menu), each dark and light, pixel for pixel the same; bar-ground-karpo-
(§546's picture, nothing chosen now Karpo's #202020 at 85 % in both modes).

## 553. The taskbar menu folded into the Taskbar page (2026-11-07) — no section, an expander, Behavior's last row, since §585 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07): *"taskbar menu should be folded into taskbar configuration page."* §543 gave the editing of the
taskbar's right-click menu a side item of its own, "Taskbar menu", right after Taskbar. Now it is no page: it is a section of
the Taskbar page.

**Where it stands: the Taskbar page's last section.** The page is Bar (Type, Size, Spacing, Show, Lock the taskbar),
Behavior (combine, previews, desktops, flyouts on hover), then **Taskbar menu**: the bar's own settings first, as the page
has always opened, and the menu after them, as the menu is what a right click on that bar shows. The side list is Karpo,
Accounts, Display, Layouts, Taskbar, Look again (then Folder and Widget while there is one). The section is §543's page whole
under a heading: the entries in the menu's order (Move earlier, Move later, Remove; a shortcut's and a heading's rows opening
to their fields), Add an entry, Reset to default.

**Every layout's.** The Taskbar page is the shown layout's; the menu is Karpo's one (`Config.BarMenu`, no layout's, no
display's), as Lock the taskbar above it is every bar's. So the heading has a caption under it, *"The same on every layout"*
(`settings.barMenu.everyLayout`, in all 30 languages): a heading's `OptionRow.Detail`, carried to its `FlyoutItem.Detail`
and drawn by the settings panel under the heading in Caption, secondary text (the heading's block 16 taller where it has
one). No other heading has one yet.

**A display that shows None.** It has no Taskbar page (no layout there), so no taskbar menu either. That is what the menu
itself does: it is a right click on a Karpo bar (`ShowBarMenu`, a `DockWindow`'s), and a display that shows None has none —
Windows' own taskbar stands there with Windows' own menu. The menu is edited on the panel of any display with a layout, the
same one menu wherever it is changed. With every display at None there is no Karpo bar and so no menu to edit.

**How.** The Taskbar page's rows are `Dock.LooksOf(Taskbar)`: `BarLooks.Rows` of the scope, then
`KarpoMenu.BarMenuSection` (its heading, then §532's `KarpoMenu.BarMenu`). The page is built (`LooksItems`) and a pick finds
its row (`LooksRow`) from that one list, so the menu's rows are set by the looks' handler as the bar's are (`LooksPicked`
asks Reset's question first; `LooksKept` keeps a typed name or arguments), what a shortcut may open given by
`BarMenuServices` (`TargetLooks.Choices`). A shortcut's Browse… is now asked before the looks' handler takes a pick
(`OptionPicked`), so Windows' open dialog comes on the Taskbar page as it did on §543's. Gone: `PanelPage.BarMenu` with its
side name and glyph (`OptionGlyphs.BarMenu`), `KarpoPage.BarMenu` and its case in `KarpoMenu.Of`, the page's `Add` in
`Dock.PanelOf` (its loop over the looks' pages back), and `KarpoServices.Targets` given to the Karpo pages. Nothing linked to
the old page (no `OptionLink`, no `EditEntry` landed there). No config change, no migration.

**The search.** A row under one of its page's headings is found there: its place says the heading after the page
(*"Taskbar › Taskbar menu › Notes"*; *"Taskbar › Bar"* for Size and for Bar's Lock the taskbar, so it reads apart from the
menu's entry of that name). A heading that names its page is not said twice (the Karpo page's Karpo). Only a page's own
headings count, not those inside an expander.

**§551** (the live preview of the menu at the top of the Taskbar menu page, the entries dragged and dropped) had not landed
when this was made; on landing, its preview goes at the section's top, under the heading, and its list is the section's.

Tests: `BarMenuPanelTests` (no side item; the Taskbar page's headings Bar, Behavior, Taskbar menu, the last with its caption;
the dock building the page and finding a pick through `LooksOf`, the page left out on a display with no layout; every key of
the menu's rows sent by a control of the Taskbar page, none by the Karpo page; the search's places; add, move and remove
still change the menu the bar draws and are undone; a shortcut and a heading typed in place; Reset; Browse before the looks'
handler), `LayoutMenuTests` (the Taskbar page's rows in order, the section last), `MenuRulesTests` (R17 the Taskbar page's
three headings; R18 the menu's settings at home there), `SettingsPanelTests`, `EditDeckClickTests` (the side list without
it), `ConfigCoverageTests` ("barMenu" written by a row of the Taskbar page), `KarpoMenuGeneralTests`, `BarLooksTests`,
`AccountsPageTests` (its search place under "Your accounts"), `EditEntriesTests`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR):
`SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-barmenu-dark/light.png (the Taskbar page at its Taskbar menu section, the default),
panel-barmenu-own-dark/light.png (the person's own, its shortcut open).

## 554. Public holidays on the panel: a calendar's region its dropdown nested under it, a search's pick closing its popup, Show from following a region (2026-11-07) — a row of Public holidays' card right after its country, no well, since §594 (2026-11-09) — in its country's row, before its colour button, since §609 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07): *"adding and changing properties of public holidays like region and stuff just does not work
properly at all. go ahead and fix the issues there"*. Each control of the holidays (Karpo › Services › Public holidays) was
driven as the panel lays it out and the dock picks it, and on the real dock (`Karpo.exe --stage`):

- **A calendar's region could not be picked.** §411 (R1) folded a thing of one choice into its row: the row opened the
  choice's choices themselves (`PickOne`). The settings panel read such a row with buttons (its colour, Remove) as a row of
  buttons alone (`PanelRowKind.Item`): its regions were nowhere. Now a thing of one choice is no fold: its choice is its own
  row, and the panel stands it nested under the thing (`FlyoutItem.Nests`, §529's way with a folder's face), a step in,
  "Region" and its dropdown saying "Zürich" or "Whole country"; a country without regions (France) has its buttons alone. The
  region is said there only, no more under the country's name too (`OptionThing.Summary`). A screen reader names a row nested
  under a thing for it, as its buttons are: "Region · Switzerland" (`DeckUia`). Menu rule R1 counts such a nested row at its
  thing's depth.
- **Add a country's popup stayed open after a country was picked**: a choice closed a panel popup only when it set a value
  (`OptionPickKind.Set`); a search's find is kept through its field (`Field`), so the list stayed, and the next click added one
  more country. A search's find picked is a choice now (`Dock.ChoiceMade`): Add a country's, a time zone's, any search popup's
  close on it, as a ComboBox's list does. Words typed into a field still keep it.
- **"Show from" lost a calendar whose region changed**: a widget's pick of the holidays is keyed by the calendar's region, else
  its country (`WidgetSources.Holidays`, §455); a region set made it another key, and a calendar widget that had picked
  Switzerland showed none of it as Zürich. Setting the region now carries every widget's pick to the new key

- **Windows' region's calendar and its country listed twice**: "Default (Switzerland)" and Switzerland are one calendar

  taken off a pinned one made the pair again. Adding and setting a region now compare the country shown

Two calendars of one country with different regions (Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Innerrhoden) stay allowed, each its row and

asks nothing, and the tests answer from saved replies (`HolidayAnswers`).

**The Look page in two sections** (Karpo.Core\Looks.cs `LookSection`, `LookSections`; LookRows.LayoutRows). The layout's four

| Section | Its parts, in order (each a group in the card) | Its preview (§536) |

| its name (and icon) | TextFillColorSecondary | TextFillColorPrimary, Body (regular) |
| its value (a dropdown's, a colour's words, a number's, a text's) | TextFillColorSecondary | TextFillColorPrimary |

## 557. Ejecting a drive ejects it; Karpo lets go of a drive Windows asks for (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"ejecting a flash drive in karpo does not work"*.

**Where Karpo offers an eject.** Every one goes through `DriveWatch.Eject`: the removable devices' line, each device's
Eject button (`RemovableIsland.Cards.cs`, §91); the Eject row of a widget's menu for a removable Drive widget, a drive's
line, each device of the removable devices' line and the Drive preset's face (`Dock.WidgetMenus.cs`, `WidgetAct.Eject` →
`MenuVerbs.Eject` → `Dock.OpenFromMenu`). The tray's "Safely Remove Hardware and Eject Media" is Explorer's own icon
(hotplug), which Karpo's tray only shows and hands its clicks to; its eject is Windows', and was stopped by the same
handles as Explorer's (below).

**Why nothing happened.** The eject was `ShellExecuteEx(root, "eject")` without `SEE_MASK_INVOKEIDLIST`. "eject" is no
verb of the registry's (`HKCR\Drive\shell` has none): it is a verb of the drive's own menu in File Explorer, as
"properties" is, and ShellExecuteEx finds those only when told to ask the item's menu. Without it the call fails with
ERROR_NO_ASSOCIATION (1155) — measured on this PC with "properties" on C:\, the same kind of verb, SEE_MASK_FLAG_NO_UI:
`ok=False err=1155`, while the drive's menu itself lists Eject. Karpo dropped the answer, so the log said nothing and no
eject was ever attempted (Kernel-PnP has no veto for the stick either).

**What would have stopped it next.** Two handles of Karpo's on the stick. The disk graph (`DiskSampler`, a Performance
widget reading Disk — the person has one) kept `\\.\PhysicalDriveN` open for every disk between samples, the stick's
included; and a folder's contents line on a drive (a folder pin or a drive's contents, `FolderWatch`) keeps a
FileSystemWatcher's handle open on its folder. Windows does not eject a device something holds open ("This device is
currently in use"), whoever asks — Karpo, Explorer, the tray.

**Now.**

* `Launch.Eject` (a `LaunchKind` of its own): the shell's Eject asked of the drive's menu. `Launch.Shell.Mask` is the one
  rule for the item's own verbs, `ItemVerbs` (properties, eject) asked with `SEE_MASK_INVOKEIDLIST` — Properties' own
  `invokeList` flag is gone into it. It runs on an STA thread of its own (`SEE_MASK_NOASYNC`, so the verb has run when the
  thread ends): the eject waits for every window it tells to answer, the dock's host among them, and the dock's thread
  must be free to. Nothing opens, so nothing of Karpo's closes: a folder showing the removable devices stays open and the
  device leaves its line when Windows says it went (the host's `DBT_DEVICEREMOVECOMPLETE` → `RefreshIslands`, as before).
  Windows says how it went, as for Explorer's Eject: its "Safe to remove hardware", or its own message why not. A shell
  that would not run it at all is written to karpo.log ("Drives: ejecting E:\: …").
* The disk graph opens a disk for its query and closes it after (`DiskSampler.Reading`); it keeps disk numbers and
  counters, no handle.
* `DriveHolds`: every `FolderWatch` on Windows' own folders (`FolderSource.Holds`; a test's source has none) is held by
  its volume ("E:\"), and each volume held is registered once with the dock's host (`WindowNotices`:
  RegisterDeviceNotification, `DBT_DEVTYP_HANDLE`, on a handle to the root). Before the device goes, and before the
  volume is locked or dismounted (`DBT_DEVICEQUERYREMOVE`, `GUID_IO_VOLUME_LOCK`, `GUID_IO_VOLUME_DISMOUNT`), every watch
  on it lets go of its watcher (`FolderWatch.Release`) and the registration's handle closes, its registration kept; the
  question is answered yes. A removal that fails, a lock that fails or ends, a dismount that fails
  (`DBT_DEVICEQUERYREMOVEFAILED`, `GUID_IO_VOLUME_LOCK_FAILED`, `…UNLOCK`, `…DISMOUNT_FAILED`, `…MOUNT`) takes them back
  (`FolderWatch.Resume`, which reads the folder again) and registers anew; one that went (`DBT_DEVICEREMOVEPENDING`,
  `…REMOVECOMPLETE`, pulled out unasked too) ends the registration and leaves them let go of until a device arrives
  (`DBT_DEVICEARRIVAL`) and their folder is there again. A watch started while its drive is away waits the same way. The
  host hears these whatever the dock is doing (`WndProc`, before the busy check, beside energy saver's): Windows waits
  for the answer, and a menu open must not make it a veto. Never registered from a dock on a config of its own.

No setting, no config change, no new words (Windows says the outcome). The veto's own words are Windows': Karpo does not
call `CM_Request_Device_Eject` itself, whose answer names a device rather than the program holding it.

Tests: `DriveHoldsTests` (the item's verbs asked of its menu, the eject's thread waiting; an eject the shell's, closing
nothing; a drive's Eject through the launcher; a folder's volume by its root; what each change asks; Windows' message read
for its registration; one registration for all a volume's folders, ended with the last; let go when asked, the question
answered only for what is held; a failed removal taking back, re-registering and reading again; a drive gone — asked or
pulled — taken back on its arrival only once it is there; a watch started while its drive is away; registered only while
there is a window; a test's source holding nothing; a watch ended never started again; the disk graph keeping no handle),
`LaunchTests`, `RemovableCardTests`, `FolderMenuDriveTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `FolderReadingTests`,
`FolderContentsLineTests`, `DiskActivityTests`.

**Check by hand.** Plug in a stick, open the folder with the removable devices and press its Eject (or Eject in the
stick's right-click menu): Windows says "Safe to remove hardware" and the stick leaves the line. With a folder pin on the
stick shown and a Disk performance widget on the bar, the same; and Explorer's Eject and the tray's Safely Remove work
while Karpo shows the stick's folder. With a file of the stick open in another program, Windows says the device is in
use, and the stick stays listed.

## 551. The taskbar menu previewed at its page's top; every list dragged into order, no arrows; a thing's own actions icon buttons (2026-11-07)

The person (2026-11-07): *"taskbar menu should show a preview and it should also be DnD and not arrows, remove the arrows."*
and *"use icons for remove or delete for example and not just the text, apply this to similar buttons too."*

**The preview.** The Taskbar page's section Taskbar menu (§553: the menu folded into the Taskbar page while this was made)
opens with the menu itself, as a right click on this display's bar shows it now: one preview row, §536's mechanism, right
under the section's heading, over the entries. The section's heading says which look it shows (`KarpoMenu.BarMenuSection`:
the heading's `OptionRow.Shows`, carried as a heading item's `FlyoutItem.Shows`), and `PanelRows.Of` puts the preview under
a heading that shows one, as it puts a level's at the level's top: one way a sample comes onto a page. A sample of a kind of its
own (`LookSample.Menu`, `LookShown.Menu` the entries): its rows the bar's very rows (`LookPreview.MenuOf` = `Dock.BarRows` of
the person's entries, `Dock.LayoutRows` — the layouts' names, the display's ticked —, Lock the taskbar ticked while locked),
laid by a menu's own measures (`MenuMetrics`: Explorer's 28 DIP fills 32 apart, 5 in, 3 over and under, 9 a rule, the icon at
16 and the words at 44 — the constants `Flyout` now lays its list menus by, unchanged), drawn in the tokens a menu of the bar
wears (`FlyoutTheme.For` of the bar's look: the layout's, Windows' own under it, never the settings' look), its plate the
material's tint over the checker (what is see-through shows), its rim, its glyphs — Explorer's two-colour pictures where it has
one, as the menu draws them —, its ticks, rules and headings, in the menu's font. A shortcut by its own name and glyph: the
shell is not asked (nothing of this PC's, §536). Its key is every entry, the layouts, which is shown, the lock and the look
(`LookShown.Values`): an entry added, moved, removed or renamed draws it again, once; a scroll draws nothing. A screen reader
calls it "Preview of Taskbar menu". The look is the layout the display shows (`Config.ActiveLayout`), the Taskbar page's.

**Dragged into order (decided: rows making room, as WinUI's ListView reorders).** §532 gave every list put in order Move
earlier and Move later buttons (↑ ↓) because the panel dragged nothing; they are gone, with their two strings in all thirty
languages. Every row whose menu row has a grip that may move (`PanelRow.Drags`: a `FlyoutItem.Reorder` group's, one of two or
more) is dragged among its own: the **taskbar menu's entries** (Edit too: it moves, it is never removed), the **layouts**, a
**folder's faces** (Folder page: §552's sections, each face's group head its face's row still, its grip and its move) and a
**toggles line's toggles** (its widget page) — the last two had no way to be put in order in the panel at all. Each has a **handle** at its start, always shown (a grip's six dots, the menus' own
`PopupPaint.Gripper`, quieter until the pointer is on its row; its icon and name 12 DIP further in), a stop of the keys before
its other controls, its tooltip "Drag to move, or press Ctrl+Up or Ctrl+Down". A press on the handle, the row's name or an
expander's head and a move past the system's drag distance lifts the row (with what is shown under it: an open layout's rows,
a face's settings) onto a raised card under the pointer; the rows it passes make room (`PanelReorder.DropAt`: after every row
whose middle its middle is past; `Shift`: by its height and the gap after it); near the page's top or foot (40 DIP) the page
scrolls under it. Let go, it is moved there — one change through the row's own move, as a menu's grip moves it
(`OptionMenu.Moved` → `Dock.PanelMoved` → `OptionPicked`: `BarMenus.Change`, `BarLooks.MoveLayout`, a face's, a toggle's),
saved, one step of the undo; where it stood, nothing. Escape (edit mode's hook: the carried row goes back first), a right press
or the pointer lost put it back. Let go before the drag distance, a press is the click it was (an expander still opens).

**From the keys: Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down** on any control of such a row (its handle, its Remove) move it a place. Not Alt+Up and
Alt+Down: those open the control's popup, as WinUI's ComboBox (§525); Windows' lists have no reorder keys of their own (Start's
pins take Alt+Shift+arrows), and Karpo's menus already move a row put in order by Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down (§226; the grip's
tooltip says so in every language). The keys stay on the same control of the moved row; a screen reader is told it moved, its
handle named "Drag to move, or press Ctrl+Up or Ctrl+Down · File Explorer", its status where it stands ("3 of 7",
`dock.panel.position`, new, in all thirty languages).

**Icon buttons (the rule).** What acts on *one thing of a list* is a 32 × 32 icon button at its row's end, a command bar's
(WinUI's subtle button: no fill nor rim until the pointer is on it, SubtleFillColorSecondary / Tertiary), 4 DIP apart, its
name its tooltip and what a screen reader says (with its row's: "Remove · File Explorer"); greyed, its tooltip why (the last
layout's Delete, a copy past the licence). What *makes* something or acts on *a page or a section as a whole* — Add a layout,
Add an entry, Add a face, Reset to default, Reset all, Quit Karpo, Get Karpo Pro, Test connection, a form's Add — stays a
button of words. A value's own reset (§529, §541) was an icon button already, and stays; a widget's header's Cut, Copy and
Remove (§529) too; confirmations are as they were. Changed: the taskbar menu's Remove, a layout's Delete, an account's Remove
and Sign in again, a holiday calendar's Remove, a face's Remove, a toggle's Remove, a note's or a list's Rename and Delete
(`FlyoutTool.Iconic` is gone: every row tool but a colour button is an icon button). **A layout's Duplicate** was a row of its
own in its expander, a button with no words beside it; it is an action of the layout itself now (`OptionThing.Acts`, which an
account's Sign in again became too: `Again` generalised), an icon button (Explorer's Copy, U+E8C8) before its Delete, in a
menu and in the panel alike.

No config change, no migration.

Tests: `PanelReorderTests` (where a row lands from the pointer, the rows making room, Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down never past an end,
"3 of 6"; every list put in order with handles — the taskbar menu's six, the layouts, a folder's faces, a toggles line's —, the
handle first, a stop, its tooltip, its UI Automation name and status; no ↑ ↓ button on any page and no faceEarlier/faceLater
string; the real window: a press let go a click, a drag over Edit one move to the top, Escape and a right press put it back,
nothing sent; Ctrl+Down on a row's control a move, Ctrl+Up on the first nothing), `PanelReorderStageTests` (the real dock,
--stage: Task Manager dragged over Edit is the first entry the bar's menu draws; Ctrl+Z puts the default back, out of the file),
`BarMenuPanelTests` (no ↑ ↓, Remove an icon, every entry dragged; a drag a step of the undo; the preview under the section's
heading, the display's layout's, the bar's own rows, its height Explorer's, another key as an entry is added, moved and removed and as the bar's look changes),
`PanelControlsTests.AThingsOwnActionsAreIconButtonsAndAPagesAreWords`, `BarLooksTests` and `SettingsPanelTests` (a layout's
Duplicate its act; its tools), `AccountsPageTests` (every key sent, a move by a drag), `KarpoMenuTests`, `WidgetPageTests` (a
face's section its handle first), `LookPreviewTests` (a section's preview right under its heading, one a look). Also: the
search engines' logos decoded one at a time, under a lock (`Dock.EnginePicture`): the tests build pages on several threads,
which corrupted its cache, and two decodes at once came out none. Pictures
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-barmenu-*.png (the preview in sight),
panel-barmenu-drag-dark/light.png (File Explorer carried down, the rows making room), panel-layouts, panel-accounts,
panel-things, panel-widget.

## 556. A look's Font is its family and its weight as one: every weight of every family on this PC, in its own face (2026-11-07) — its weight a dropdown of its own beside its family since §638 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-07): *"font and weight should also be combined into one setting"*.

**One row.** Every look that holds text — a layout's Taskbar widgets and Widgets in folders, a widget's, a folder's face's,
a line's own — has one **Font** row and no Weight row (`LookRows.FontRow`). It is a choice like every other (§518, §541):
its first choice says what it comes to unset, "Default (Segoe UI Variable Text · Regular)" for a section (Karpo's own),
"Default (Sitka Text · Regular)" for a widget whose layout's section is in Sitka; then every font there is. Picked, it
writes one value; its reset, the first choice, unsets it; several widgets selected that wear fonts apart say "Mixed" and
open into each one's (§528, §529). It inherits **whole**: a widget's font unset is its section's family *and* weight, set
it is its own family and weight both — §459 to §555 let a widget set a weight over its section's font.

**Every family on this PC, each with the weights it really has.** §521 left the font a curated seven ("making it every
family is a change of the config's words, not of a control"). The control is a font picker now, so it lists this PC's
families: `SystemFonts.Read` (Karpo.Dock) asks DirectWrite's system collection — the one Gfx lays every line out of — for
each family's English name and the weights of its upright, normal-width faces that are its own (no weight DirectWrite
would simulate); a family that cannot write a Latin "a" is left out (Marlett, Wingdings, Segoe Fluent Icons: their words
would be boxes). Read once, when the first Font row is built (`InstalledFonts.All`, Karpo.Core), again after Windows says
the fonts changed (`WM_FONTCHANGE` → `InstalledFonts.Forget`). Here: 180 families, 317 fonts, read in 80 ms; the list
opens in 80 to 190 ms. With no reader set — the tests — the families Karpo offered before, with Windows 11's weights
(`InstalledFonts.Shipped`). A weight is named as OpenType names the one nearest it — Thin, Extra light, Light, Semilight,
Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold, Extra bold, Black, Extra black (`TextStyles.WeightName`), in every language Karpo speaks.

**The control** (a ComboBox, as Windows 11's Fonts settings and WinUI's font pickers): the box says the font in force in
that font — "Georgia · Bold" in Georgia Bold (`FlyoutValue.Face`, `PanelRow.ValueFace`; §520's `FontOf`, which guessed a
family from the words, is gone). Its list hangs under it (§521) with a filter at its top, "Search fonts", pinned while
the rest scroll; the default on its own first, then each family under its heading — the heading in that family —, each
of its weights a row of the weight's name drawn in that weight (`OptionRow.ChoiceFaces` → `OptionMenu.FontChoices`,
`FlyoutItem.Face`, worn while the row is measured and drawn; a text surface is kept by its face too, `DrawnKey.Face`). It
opens with the keys in its filter and the font in force ticked and in sight (`Flyout.ChosenTileInView`, an icon picker's
tile's rule, now a filtered list's row's too), ten rows tall as a ComboBox's list and its filter over them
(`Flyout.FilteredList`). The filter finds a font by its family and its weight both ("georgia bold", "bold"); §556 has a
filter keep a heading over the rows it leaves under it (a family over its weights) — §249 dropped every heading. A long
choice list still grows no filter of its own (§521): this one is a picker, and says so with its own.

Why a grouped list, not two pickers (a family, then its weights): one value, one pick, one place it is said; a family's
weights are a handful, shown at once under it; the filter covers the length.

**The file.** One value, `"font": "Family/Weight"`, the weight DirectWrite's 1 to 999 (`TextStyle.Text`, `TextStyle.Parse`):
`"Sitka Text/600"`. A family alone reads as Regular; nothing, or a weight alone, unset. `LookValues.Weight` and the
`StyleFont`/`StyleWeight` words are gone, and with them §459's family fallbacks (Sitka → Georgia, Cascadia Mono →
Consolas): a family this PC has not is kept as said, listed among the choices where it would stand and ticked, and drawn in
Karpo's own family at its weight (`Gfx.TextFamily`). `TextStyle`'s `default` is Karpo's own, Segoe UI Variable Text at
400 — the default font, as before. The kit's two weights stand on the font's (`TextStyle.Weights`): its body at its weight,
its strong one two steps over (Regular 400 and 600, Light 300 and 500, as ever) and one from Semibold on (600 and 700, as
ever; Bold 700 and 800). The palettes say "Sitka Text/400", "Bahnschrift/400", "Segoe UI Variable Text/600" (Bloom).
Config.Shape 73; ConfigWords.txt written again (no `LookValues.weight`, no `StyleFont`/`StyleWeight`). No migration (Karpo is
newly published): the person's own config.json said no font and no weight anywhere; a one-off script converts a file of the old
words (outside the repository). store/config.json's six old words written in the new form.

**R14**: a font's value is its family's name, as long as the family calls itself (`MenuRulesTests`: a value in a face
counts not toward the 20 characters).

Tests: `LookTests.EveryLookOfTextHasOneFontRowOfEveryFamilysWeights` (one Font row per scope, none on the Taskbar and the
Flyouts, no Weight row; its choices and faces), `AFontPickedIsOneValueInheritedWhole` (one value written and read back,
"Default (…)" unsets; a widget unset its section's family and weight, set its own, its section's later change not
reaching it), `AFontIsReadInItsOneFormAndOneNotInstalledIsKept`, the resolver's, the file's and the palettes' tests in the
new form; `CommonSettingsTests` (Mixed, a pick on them all), `ValueOriginTests` (the Font set here, its reset and tooltip),
`AppearanceTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (R6 "Search fonts", R14), `ConfigSchemaTests`, `LookPreviewTests` (a card's six rows),
`PanelPopupPlaceTests` (the real dock: the Font's list under its box; its lowest dropdown in sight the Font again, no
Weight under it, so its list is closed first, and a colour's narrower button is no dropdown there). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.TheFontListPictures` — font-list-dark/light.png (this PC's families, a clock's Georgia Bold
ticked and in sight), font-list-filtered-dark.png ("bold"), font-widget-dark/light.png (the clock's page, its Font box and
its preview in Georgia Bold, PaintWatch seeing Georgia at 700); and a family not installed laid out in Karpo's own.

## 559. A colour's picker hangs off its button, never over it; Escape closes it (2026-11-07)

Found by a test (2026-11-07): a colour's picker opened from a §535 colour button low on the display stood over its own
button — at 150 % on the stage's display, the picker -1288,663..-758,1201 over the button -866,879..-758,927.

**What it was.** Not the place a picker is given: every popup of the panel is placed by `PopupPlace.Of` (§521, §531) on
every showing and every growth (`FlyoutHost.Arrange`, which `Show`, `Fit` and `Resize` all go through), and the picker is
laid out against `PopupPlace.Room`. The picker did not close. A control's popup opened with the keys in its first field
(`Flyout.Show`, for a search's list and §556's filter), and a colour's picker has one: §523's hex box, under its swatches and
its mixer. Escape went to the box, which only put its words back, so the picker stood open, hung from where its button had
been; the page wheeled, another button came where the picker was, and a click on it landed on the picker — whose rows a
click changes, and which was then shown again, taller, still off the first button.

**Now.** A control's popup opens with the keys in a field only where that is what it is for (`Flyout.FieldOnOpening`): a
search's or a filter's field, wherever it stands, or a line's field that leads the popup (a text box's, a number's), as
WinUI puts the keys on a flyout's first control. A colour's picker opens with no field holding them — its hex box takes them
by a click or Tab, as before — and Escape closes it, as it closes every popup of the panel.

**And never over its control, whatever it asks.** `PopupPlace.Of` pushed a popup taller than either side's room back onto
the work area, over its control (`PopupPlaceTests` held it so). It now takes the roomier side and is no taller than that
side's room; what it shows scrolls in it, as the menus lay themselves out against that room already (`FlyoutPlacement.Room`),
and `FlyoutHost.Arrange` sizes the panel to the rect it is given. Only a control with no room on either side (as tall as the
work area) has its popup pushed over it.

Tests: `PopupPlaceTests.RoomOnNeitherSideTakesTheRoomierAndNeverCoversItsControl` (the roomier side, its room's height, off
its control wherever it stands); `MenuPickersTests.AColoursPickerFromItsButtonHangsOffItAndEscapeClosesIt` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1:
a real picker from a button low on a 150 % display, directly over it, no field with the keys, Escape closing it);
`PanelPopupPlaceTests.AColoursPickerHangsFromItsButton` (the real dock, the bar at the display's foot and at its top, and
`…OnASecondDisplayAtAnotherScale`: the Look page wheeled a notch at a time, the highest and the lowest colour button in sight
at each, its picker directly under or over it); `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AColourIsMixedInTheSettingsPanel` reaches
Background through §549's Taskbar section and its Taskbar widgets group, and holds its picker off its button.

## 558. The bar's Background blur a value of a default as every other (2026-11-07) — a value as any, no default, since §574 (2026-11-08)

§547's "Background blur" had no default in the row model (`OptionRow.Default` null), so §541's rule passed it by: never
muted, never "From Karpo", no reset, not in its group's counts. It now joins the rule: its default Karpo's own 30 %
(`Default` "30%", `From` Karpo). A number has no first choice to be unset at, so a number of a default says the value it
comes to unset (`OptionRow.DefaultValue`, Karpo's 30): at it the row is inherited (`OptionRow.Origin`; the setting is unset
there, 30 set again is absent from the file, §547), at any other set here. Its reset is a Set of that value
(`OptionRow.ResetValue`, the pick `OptionMenu.Rows` makes for it), "Reset to 30% (from Karpo)"; a choice's and a colour's
are as before (their first choice, 0). No config change.

Tests: `ValueOriginTests.TheBarsBackgroundBlurIsInheritedFromKarpoAsEveryLookValue` (unset muted "From Karpo", no reset,
the Bar group "All from Karpo"; set here its reset and its tooltip, counted; the reset unset again, nothing in the file;
30 set again inherited); `BarBlurSettingTests` on §549's section.

## 560. A line's own pattern and outline changed show at once (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-08): "when changing the pattern of a widget it does not apply immediately."

**What it was.** A widget's own look changed in the settings panel is saved and the bars are laid out again (`Dock.Apply`),
so a widget on the bar wears its new pattern at once: the scene lays each card out again and its pattern layer redraws on
any change (`Scene.Card`, `PatternLayer.Show`). A line of a folder standing open did not. The folder takes its new settings
(`FolderIsland.Configure`) and decides by its layout's signature whether to plan again; a look is no part of that signature,
so with the same widgets it only drew each line's content again (`FolderFlyout.DrawCards`) and set its colours
(`ShowStates`: its background, its outline's colour). A line's pattern and the shape of its own outline are placed with the
rest of the showing (`FolderFlyout.DrawNow`) and nowhere else, so they stayed as they were until something laid the folder
out again — a line come or gone, the folder shut and opened.

**Now.** The same widgets with new settings are dressed as a showing dresses them (`Draw`): their content, their colours,
their patterns and their outlines' shapes, one path. Nothing is planned or made again: the plan stays, every visual is set
where it already stands, a pattern redrawn only where it changed (`PatternLayer.Show`), a line gliding left alone
(`PlaceLines`). The other values of a line's look were on screen at once already — its background, text, accent and font
with its content and its colours — and so were the bar's widgets', the layout's sections' (`FolderFlyout.Relook`) and the
previews' (§536: rows made again, another key).

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.ALinesPatternAndOutlineChangedWhileItsFolderStandsOpenShowAtOnce` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1: a folder open,
its first line's own pattern and outline set, `Configure`: the plan the same, the line's pattern layer showing the pattern and
its outline drawn round it; failed before); `SceneTreeTests.AWidgetsPatternChangedShowsOnItsCardAtOnce` (a widget's card on
the bar, at rest and arranged, a guard).

## 561. The taskbar menu shows its layouts with only one too (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-08): "in the right click taskbar menu layouts should also show even if only one layout is present."

§366 left a lone layout out of the bar's right-click menu: "a lone layout ticked against itself is noise". It now shows: the
menu's Layouts entry is every layout, a lone one too, ticked — ruled off as several are, under no heading (§366). The rule
went from the two places that held it (`Dock.LayoutRows`, `BarMenus.Lines`), so the menu, its preview at the top of the
Taskbar page's "Taskbar menu" section (§551, §553) and a heading the person put over the layouts all show the one. A click on
it does what a click on the layout shown always did: nothing changes.

The layouts' line (`LayoutsLine`) keeps its rule, now its own (`Switchers.Layouts`): below two there is nothing to choose,
and its Status says so with its "Add" (§404).

Tests: `BarMenuTests.OneLayoutIsARowOfItsOwnTicked`, `…TheBarsMenuKeepsItsOneLayoutInASectionOfItsOwn`;
`BarMenuLinesTests.TheMenuWithOneLayoutShowsItTicked`, `…TheLayoutsUnderAHeadingGoWithItWhereNoneIsOffered`;
`BarMenuPanelTests.ThePageShowsTheMenuAsTheBarDrawsItAtItsTop` (a new config's one layout in the preview, ticked);
`SwitcherTests.OneLayoutOffersNoRows` (the line's rule, unchanged).

## 562. A widget's own look has no preview (2026-11-08) — no widget's own look at all since §567 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-08): *"in the widget look configuration section there should not be a preview"*. §536 put a sample at
the top of every level that edits a look, a widget's own among them; §555 kept it first in a widget's Look group.

**What changed.** A thing's own look — a widget's on the bar, a folder line's, a folder's (one builder for the three,
`LookRows.WidgetRow`) — says no look it shows (`OptionRow.Shows` null), so the panel puts no preview in its Look group, on
a widget's page, on the page of several selected, and on a folder's page alike: the group is its values in the menu's
order and Reset all last (§555), nothing over them. The widget itself, on the bar or in its folder, shows what is set. The
previews of a layout's look stay as they were: the Look page's two sections (§549, Taskbar and Folders and flyouts) and the
Taskbar page's taskbar menu (§551).

**Deleted** with the only thing that asked for them: `LookShown.Item` (and its widget's settings in `LookShown.Values`),
`LookSample.Lines` (a line's own sample) and `LookPreview.LinesDip`, `LookPreview.DrawsItself` and its three lists of the
kinds a sample could draw itself (`BarDrawn`, `FacesDrawn`, `LinesDrawn`), a widget's copy or a stand-in wearing its look
(`BarItemsOf`, `LinesOf`); what is left of a sample is a section's: the bar's stand-ins, a clock folder opened over a clock
and a calendar (`LookPreview.BarItemsOf`, `PanelOf`). No string is gone ("Preview of …" still names a section's), no
config change.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests.AWidgetsOwnLookHasNoPreview` (every widget kind's page with a Look: none in it, its values there;
a clock, a calendar, a folder, Start, a pin; a folder's page), `EveryLevelThatEditsALookHasItsPreviewAtItsTopAndNowhereElse`,
`EachLookPicksItsSampleByOneRule` and `ASampleStandsInForThisPcAndTheNetwork` on the sections alone;
`WidgetPageTests.TheLookShowsEveryValueInItsPlaceSetOrInherited` (no preview, Reset all last). Pictures
(`SceneTreeTests.LookPreviewSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): preview-taskbar-, preview-folders- (the widget
scenes gone); `FontListPictures`' font-widget- its Font's box alone.

## 563. A folder's page in two sections under their headings: Faces, Folder (2026-11-08) — Folder's rows straight under its heading, no group When it opens, since §588 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"the folder configuration should also get section headers"*. The Karpo, Display, Taskbar and Look
pages stand their cards under a page's section headings (Body Strong, §548: 24 after what is before, 8 over its cards); the
Folder page (§529, §552) was its cards alone — each face's section, Add a face, When it opens, Look — one run of cards with
nothing saying which are the faces and which the folder's own.

**The page now** (`PanelGroups.FolderPage`), under its header card:

| Heading | Its cards |
|---|---|
| **Faces** | each face a section of its own as §552 has it (its handle, icon, name, Remove; its settings its rows), in the faces' order; Add a face |
| **Folder** | When it opens (Alignment); Look (§555's every value in its place, §562 no preview) |

A heading is a page's heading as any page's (`PanelRowKind.Heading`, keyed `Folder/Faces`, `Folder/Folder`), laid in §548's
one rhythm (`PanelLayout.LayPage`); a section with no cards has none. The groups keep their keys (`Folder/~Clock`,
`Folder/~When it opens`, `Folder/~Look`), so the memory of the shut ones, a popup, a link and the search find them as
before; the search's way to a face's setting says its heading now ("Folder › Faces › Clock"), as a Taskbar page's says its
section's. To a screen reader each heading is the group its cards are in (`DeckUia`'s sections), a face's head still a
heading of level 2 (§552). Two strings, `dock.panel.section.faces` ("Faces") and `dock.panel.section.folder` ("Folder"), in
all 30 languages, each language's word for a face as its Add a face and Search faces say it. A widget's page is as it was:
its groups (What it shows, Height, Look) are its sections, one kind of thing. No config change.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests.AFoldersPageHoldsItsFacesAlignmentAndLook` (the two headings and their cards in order),
`EachFaceIsASectionOfItsOwnInTheFacesOrder` (under Faces; Add a face, then Folder and When it opens; the search's way through
Faces), `AFacesSectionHasItsRemoveAtItsHeadAndIsAHeading`, `EveryKindsPage…` (a folder's two headings, a widget's none),
`UntranslatedTests` (fr's "Faces", pl's, id's, ms's and ro's "Folder" the same as English on purpose). Pictures
(`SceneTreeTests.WidgetPageSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-529-folder- and panel-529-folder-look-, dark
and light.

## 564. A row nested under a choice: no bar on its left, its divider as far in as its name (2026-11-08) — on a well, no divider of its own, since §565 (2026-11-08) — a row of its card as any, since §588 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"i dont like the third level of the configuration with the bar shown on the left side, change the
design of this level so that it has no bar on the left side."*

**What it was.** The panel's third level: a card's head (a group, an expander), its rows, and under a row the rows that
only matter after its choice (§529: an agenda's Days ahead under Style, a line's Max rows under Height, the accounts' line
under Show from, a holiday calendar's region under it, §554) or a mixed row's widgets' own values (§529, opened). Each such
row stood 24 DIP further in (`PanelMetrics.Nest`) with a 2 DIP rounded bar in TextFillColorTertiary down its left, 6 in from
the name over it, 8 short of its top and foot (`PanelPainter.One`, `GuideWide`, `GuideIn`), and a divider over it the card's
whole width as every row's.

**What it is now — Windows 11 Settings' own idiom.** No bar anywhere. A nested row keeps its step in (its name 24 DIP further
in than its choice's, its control in the value column as every row's), and the divider over it starts where its name does
(`PanelLayout.DividerX`: the card's edge for a row of its card's level, the name's x for a nested one), as Windows ruled
the items of a list inset under what they belong to: the choice and the rows that follow it read as one block in the card,
ruled off from the next row of the card's level by a divider the card's whole width again. The same rule where a row is
carried (§551). Fills, heights, the type and every other measure are §548's tokens as before; nothing new is drawn.

**Deleted:** the guide line's drawing and its two metrics (`PanelMetrics.GuideWide`, `GuideIn`). No config change, no
string.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests.ANestedRowIsLaidInItsChoicesCardAStepInItsDividerAsFarIn` (a step in; its divider at its name, its
choice's at the card's edge, the next row of the card's level ruled whole), `HolidaysPanelTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`,
`MenuRulesTests`. Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.WidgetPageSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-529-calendar- (Days
ahead, the accounts' line, Max rows), -kinds- (a mixed text colour opened into each one's), dark and light.

## 565. A row nested under a choice stands on a well: the third level reads as one (2026-11-08) — no well, no third level, since §588 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"the third level should be designed in a way that you can actually tell that it is the third
level."* §564 took the bar off a nested row's left and started its divider at its name; what was left was a 24 DIP step
in, and a row 24 DIP in under a row reads as a row cut short, not as a level under it.

**What it is now — WinUI's track, in the card.** The rows nested under a choice (§529: an agenda's Days ahead under
Style, a line's Max rows under Height, the accounts' line under Show from, a holiday calendar's region, §554), and a mixed
row's widgets' own rows opened under it, stand together on a *well* (`PanelLayout.NestedRuns`, `WellOf`;
`PanelPainter.Wells`): each run of nested lines in a card one recessed surface, in a track's tokens as WinUI sets a
segmented control's segments or a switch's knob in one — ControlAltFillColorSecondary (#19000000 dark, #06000000 light:
darker than the card in either mode) in ControlStrokeColorDefault, §548's 4 DIP corners. It starts where its choice's name
starts (the nested names a step, 24 DIP, in from its edge, as before), ends a tight space (4) past the controls' end, and
stands a tight space in from the run's top and foot, so the card's own fill shows round it: a block under its choice, the
choice's own row and the next row of the card's level outside it. Its controls stay in the card's value column, 4 off the
well's rim, as a track holds its segments. One surface: no divider in a well nor over it; the next row of the card's
level is ruled off the card's whole width as every row. A row lifted to be put in order (§551) carries its well with it.

**Decided.** Recessed, not raised: a lighter plate (CardBackgroundFillColorDefault, SubtleFillColorSecondary) read as a
row under the pointer in dark and as nothing in light; ControlAltFillColorSecondary is darker in both, the one thing
WinUI draws sunk into a surface. The block keeps the value column: its right end past the controls, not at them, so
a nested value never stands 4 DIP left of the one over it. No new metric: the well is `Nest`, `Tight` and `Corner`.

**Deleted:** `PanelLayout.DividerX` (§564's divider at a nested name): a nested line has no divider. No config change,
no string.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests.ANestedRowIsLaidInItsChoicesCardAStepInOnAWell` (a step in; one run, its well from its choice's
name to a tight space past the controls, a tight space in, its controls inside; its choice on none),
`AMixedValueOpensIntoEachOnesOwnEachWithItsReset` (each one's own one run under it), `HolidaysPanelTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`,
`PanelReorderTests`. Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.WidgetPageSheets`, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-529-calendar-
(the accounts' line, Days ahead, Max rows each on a well), -kinds- (a mixed text colour opened into each one's, the three
on one well), dark and light.

(set and reset, the page laid the same line for line), `ValueOriginDeckTests` (the real panel). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
