## 569. A count Windows' taskbar showed and Karpo did not: the writes the folder watch never hears (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-08): *"karpo did not update the notification count for whatsapp again but the windows taskbar did.
and after restarting it did too."* Unlike §508, where Windows itself held the count, this time Windows had the new count
and Karpo did not.

**What happened.** From Windows' own log (`PushNotification-Platform/Operational`), the store (a copy, read-only)
and Karpo's logs: 19:31:43.309 a push woke WhatsApp's background task (2033), and 19:31:44.251 WhatsApp set its badge to
1 (3053) — row 80102, `<badge value="1"/>`, arrival 19:31:44.247, its toast 80104 at .386, the store's write-ahead log
last written 19:31:44.394. The Karpo running since 18:52:44 never showed it. The person quit it at 19:33:12 (the edit
bar's Quit Karpo), Explorer's taskbar showed the 1 meanwhile, and the next Karpo, the same build (Karpo.exe of 18:51),
showed it from its first read at 19:33:46. karpo.log has no line of the store in between: nothing was thrown.

**Why: the folder watch is not told of every write.** The store read Windows' `wpndatabase.db` when, and only when, a
`FileSystemWatcher` on its folder heard a write (§198). Measured read-only on this PC: a folder watch on Windows'
notification folder, its event queue proved by a file of its own in another folder, beside a poll of the database's and
its log's size and last write. At 19:49:50.512 Windows wrote its log (1,652,152 to 1,726,312 bytes) and the watch heard
nothing; at 20:01:47.548 To Do set its badge (3053), the log grew to 1,837,552 bytes that millisecond, and again the
watch heard nothing, then or in the minutes after. The same on a made-up database: one connection that stays open in WAL mode, a commit every 1.5 s. At
`synchronous=NORMAL`, SQLite's usual for WAL, which does not flush a commit, the watch heard the first two commits of
six and none of the four after them; at `FULL`, which flushes every commit, it heard all six. NTFS tells a folder watch
of a write as it brings the file's entry in its folder up to date, which a flush does and a write left in the cache
does not, or not soon. §372 and §508 checked the watch with writers that flushed (§508's test at `FULL`), so they
always heard it. A write the watch missed stayed missed until the next one it heard, or a restart; and WhatsApp writes
its badge seldom, so its 1 stood.

A second way to the same thing, not seen today but certain if it happens: .NET stops a `FileSystemWatcher` for good at
any error other than an overflow (`EnableRaisingEvents` turns false and nothing more is said), and the store, on that
error, read once and never watched again, nor wrote the error down. Every later write would go unheard until a restart.

**Now** (`NotificationStore`): the watch is how a write is heard at once, no longer what says one was made; the files'
own size and last write are (`WpnStamp`).

- Every read takes them as it begins. Every 5 s (`CheckMs`) while the store is used — a bar with app buttons, or the
  bell — they are looked at again: two file attributes, nothing opened, no read. Changed for over a second
  (`HeardWithinMs`, past the 400 ms a heard write waits at most) with no read since is a write no read took
  (`Unheard`, `Finds`), and it is read then: a count the watch missed shows within about six seconds.
- A watch found stopped is made again, at the check and at its own error (`Rewatch`, `Lost`); an overflow is only read
  after, as .NET keeps that watch going.
- A read that failed on the way (Windows held the database and the copy failed too) took no write, so the check reads
  again until one succeeds. That is §198's retry, which tried five times a second apart and then waited for the next
  write: one rule now (`RetryAfter`, `Retries`, `RetryMs` deleted).
- karpo.log says so: a write the watch did not hear, a watch found stopped (at most a line every ten minutes, with how
  many there were), and the watch's own errors. The next count that stays can be told from Windows' own (§508's log)
  from the files.

Unchanged: a heard write is read 150 ms after its burst settles and never later than 400 ms after its first write
(§198); a read is the store's newest rows, never what Karpo showed last.

Proven and guarded: the unheard write is proven — on the live store (a write of Windows' the watch did not hear) and
on a made-up one, and `ABadgeSetUnderAWriterThatDoesNotFlushIsReadThoughTheWatchNeverHearsIt` fails without the check
(the count stays at 1 after the 5 is written). Which of Windows' writes went unheard at 19:31:44 can't be shown after
the fact, but nothing else in the path to the button failed (no line in karpo.log, the row in the store, the same
build showing it at once after the restart). The stopped watch is guarded, not seen: nothing ever wrote it down.

Tests: `NotificationStoreTests.ABadgeSetUnderAWriterThatDoesNotFlushIsReadThoughTheWatchNeverHearsIt` (a writer that
stays open at `NORMAL`: 1, 2, 3, 1, 5 each shown; red without the check),
`AWatchThatStoppedIsStartedAgainAndTheWriteItMissedIsRead` (the watch left as .NET leaves it after an error: the write
read, the watch made again; red before), `AWriteNoReadTookIsReadOnceTheWatchHadItsTimeToHearIt` (`Unheard`: nothing
written, written just now, written a second ago, the log rewritten in place, the database written),
`TheCheckReadsWhatNoReadTookAndLeavesAReadOnItsWayAlone` (`Finds`, in place of `AReadThatFailedOnTheWayIsTriedAgainAFewTimes`);
the rest of `NotificationStoreTests`, `NotificationStoreThreadTests`, `StoreSignalThreadTests`, and with
KARPO_UI_TESTS=1 `NotificationsPresetTests`, `BadgeSizeTests` green. By hand: with WhatsApp closed to the tray, have a
message sent to you: its pin shows the count within half a second as before, or within six seconds where Windows' write
went unheard, and karpo.log then says "a write to Windows' list the watch did not hear".

## 567. One look, Karpo's: the Appearance; no widget's, folder's, line's or layout's own (2026-11-08) — no Reset all, no value set here or inherited, since §574 (2026-11-08)

The person (2026-11-08): *"you should not be able to set widget level or folder level looks anymore. remove that feature
completely. just one global look configuration. (rename it to Appearance) also not on folder level."*

**One look.** Karpo has one look, its **Appearance** (`Config.Appearance`, the file's top-level `"appearance"`; the type
`Appearance`, §507's `LayoutLooks` renamed): the four sections as ever (`LookPart`: Taskbar, Taskbar widgets, Flyouts,
Widgets in folders), each value over Karpo's own (§547, `KarpoLook.Paints`) — one resolver, `Looks.Of(config)`. Every bar
of every layout wears it, and every menu, flyout and tooltip opened from one (`Look.Wearing(Config)` /
`Wearing(Appearance?)`, the dock's `TaskbarLook`); the font Karpo's own chrome is in is its Widgets in folders'
(`Looks.MenuText(config)`).

**Removed, not hidden** (nothing reads them, nothing writes them):

- a layout's look: `TaskbarLayout.Looks` and its copy and repair, `Looks.Of(TaskbarLayout)`, a layout preset's palette
  (`LayoutPreset.Palette`: Focus, Planner and Monitor are made in no palette now; a layout added changes nothing of the
  Appearance), a layouts reset resetting the look (the Appearance is kept with every other setting);
- a widget's, a folder face's and a line's own look: `WidgetItem.Look` (the file's `"look"`) and its normalising, a folder's
  face's and the tray's Flyout outline (`LookValues.FlyoutOutline`, `Looks.WriteFlyoutOutline`, `LookSlot.Flyout`,
  `settings.look.flyoutOutline`), `Looks.Own|OwnOf|Has|PartOf|Item|OpensFlyout|FlyoutOutline|Reset`, `PartSpec.Own`,
  `Look.Part` and `Look.Line` (and the scene's per-part looks and tokens, `Scene.LookOf(part)`, `Apart`, `partLooks`,
  `partTokens`, `TokensOf`, `Swatched.Part`; the folder's per-line looks, `LineLook`, `LineStyleOf`, `FolderFlyout.Worn`),
  `Look.Flyout(LookValues?)` now `Look.Flyout()` (outlined by the Flyouts alone);
- the widget page's and the folder page's Look group (`PanelGroups.LookOf`, `PanelSentences.Look`), a widget's menu's
  Look › at its foot (`OptionMenu.LookRows|LookRowsOf`, `LookRows.WidgetRow|WidgetKey`, the editor's `ofWidget` and its
  Reset all), several widgets' look in common (§528's look rows, `OptionPlace.Colors`);
- where a default comes from as anything but Karpo: `OptionSource`, `OptionSourceKind`, `OptionRow.From`,
  `FlyoutItem.From`, `OptionOrigin.Mixed` (only a look's rows had a default, and none is several widgets' now): the words are
  `OptionOrigins` (Karpo.Core\OptionOrigins.cs, was OptionSources.cs): "From Karpo", "Reset to … (from Karpo)", "N set
  here, M from Karpo", "All from Karpo"; strings gone `settings.from.layout|layoutPart`, `settings.resetTo.layout|layoutPart`,
  `settings.counts.layout.some|mixed|none`, `settings.counts.karpo.mixed`.

**Appearance, the page.** §520's Look page is the **Appearance** page (`PanelPage.Appearance`, `LooksScope.Appearance`,
`EditEntry.AppearanceSettings`, `OptionLink.Appearance`; `settings.look.header` is `settings.appearance.header`,
"Appearance" in every language — Windows' own word, "Darstellung", "Apparence", …). Its content is §549's as it was: Apply
palette; Taskbar (Bar, Taskbar widgets) and Folders and flyouts (Flyouts, Widgets in folders), each its preview (§536) and
its parts' groups; the bar's Background blur (§547, §558); Reset all. Each value of a default says set here or inherited
as §541, §549, §555 and §566 have it, from Karpo alone. It stands on every display — a display showing None has it too, the
Appearance being Karpo's as a whole (its previews on the bar of the layout the display would show). Its rows are keyed
`Appearance.<section>.<value>` (`LookRows.Key`; §507 to §566 `LayoutLook.`). Apply palette writes into the Appearance.

**The file** (shape 74, ConfigWords.txt written again; no migration, a file's old keys simply not read):

```
appearance                       new: { taskbar?, widgets?, flyouts?, folderWidgets? }, each a look of §507 (no flyoutOutline)
layouts[].looks                  gone
islands[..].look                 gone (a widget's, a face's, a line's)
```

Tests: `LookTests` (the one resolver; `ThereIsOneAppearanceAndNoOtherLevel`: every layout's bar wears it, an old file's
layout looks and widget looks not read; the file; palettes written into the Appearance; fonts and patterns per section),
`ValueOriginTests` (every value from Karpo, counts and resets; `NoWidgetFolderOrLineHasALookOfItsOwn`), `AppearanceTests`
(`TheFileKeepsTheAppearance`), `WidgetPageTests`, `CommonSettingsTests` (several widgets: no look in common; a mixed value
and one pick on them all by a clock's seconds), `ConfigCoverageTests` (the Appearance written by the Appearance page, at
Karpo's level), `ConfigResetTests` and `SettingsBackupTests` (a layouts reset keeps it), `TransferTests`, `LayoutPresetsTests`,
`FolderMenuSidesTests`, `InlineMenuTests` (a line's foot its Height alone), `PatternChangeTests` (§560 by the Appearance),
`FolderOutlineTests` and the pictures that dressed one widget (`FolderFaceLookPictures`, `StackPictures`, `LookPictures`,
`LookSurfacePictures`, `PatternSurfacePictures`, `WidgetLookPictures`, `FontListPictures`' font-appearance-) by the
Appearance; gone `ValueOriginTests`' layout and mixed origins, `LookPreviewTests.AWidgetsOwnLookHasNoPreview`,
`WidgetLookPictures.AStylesOutlineRunsRoundItsWidgetAmongPlainOnes`, `FolderOutlineTests.AnOutlineOfItsOwnRunsRoundItsLineAmongPlainOnes`,
`LookPictures.AWidgetsLookSaysDefaultForWhatIsUnset`.

By hand: edit mode, the side list's Appearance; Taskbar widgets › Background a colour: every widget of every bar that colour,
on every display; a widget's page has no Look group, a folder's none either; another layout shown: the same look.

## 568. Dark and light again: every Appearance colour a pair, the taskbar in Windows' mode (2026-11-08) — no default, no reset of a half, since §574 (2026-11-08); its two buttons as wide as one dropdown, the second one opening its picker, since §577 (2026-11-09); its previews in both modes since §582 (2026-11-09); its page in one mode, one button a colour, since §613 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"dark and light mode should be merged together again and the dark and light mode setting of the
operating system should be respected on the taskbar again. in the settings this should be done by having two color
selectors for dark and light in the same row."*

**Replaces** §509's one set in both modes and §547's taskbar that never followed Windows' mode. §547 stays for the rest:
the taskbar takes nothing of Windows' accent (Karpo's blue #0078D4), of "Show accent color on Start and taskbar" or of its
transparency effects (Karpo blurs the wallpaper itself); high contrast still wins; the settings still wear Windows' own (§526).

**A colour is a pair.** Every colour of the Appearance (§567) — each section's background, outline, text, accent and pattern
colour — holds one for Windows' dark mode and one for its light mode (`ColorPair { Dark, Light }`), each set or left to
Karpo's own of its mode on its own. The font, the pattern and the bar's Background blur stay one each, in both modes.
`LookValues[tone, dark]` reads and writes a half; `Looks.WritePaint(slot, tone, dark, paint)` sets one half, the other as it
was; a pair with neither half said is gone.

**The one resolver, of a mode.** `Looks.Of(config, dark)` / `Looks.Of(appearance, dark)`: each section's values of that
mode over Karpo's own of it (`KarpoLook.Paints(dark)`). The taskbar wears the mode Windows is in: `Look.KarpoBase` keeps
Windows' mode now (§547 replaced it with Karpo's dark), and `Look.Wearing` reads the Appearance's half of it. A mode changed
is another taskbar look, so `Dock.LookChanged` builds and draws every bar, folder and menu again in it, live (§547 kept the
taskbar as it was on a mode change); an accent or transparency effects changed alone still rebuild nothing. Previews (§536)
are drawn in Windows' mode as the panel shows them (their key holds Windows' look, so a mode changed is another picture).

**Karpo's own of each mode** (`KarpoLook`):

| | dark (§547, as it was) | light (new) |
|---|---|---|
| the bar (Taskbar › Background) | #202020 at 85 % (`#D9202020`) over the wallpaper blurred | #F3F3F3 at 85 % (`#D9F3F3F3`) — Windows 11's light taskbar — over the wallpaper blurred |
| a widget's card (Taskbar widgets › Background) | #2B2B2B solid | #FBFBFB solid — Windows 11's light card (CardBackgroundFillColorDefault, white at 70 %) over #F3F3F3, made opaque |
| the accent | #0078D4, its shade for a dark ground #60CDFF | #0078D4, its shade for a light ground #005FB8 |
| text, outlines, menus, flyouts, lines | Windows 11's dark: white, no outline, #2C2C2C menus, #242424 taskbar flyouts, solid | Windows 11's light: dark text, no outline, Windows' light flyout surfaces, solid |
| the Background blur | 30 % | 30 % (one in both) |

**The palettes, a family each again.** With a pair per colour a palette needs no mode of its own: §509's eight palettes
are §507's four again (`LookPalette(Id, Light, Dark)`: Graphite, Paper, Harbor, Bloom), each its light design and its dark
one as §509 drew them, one font in both. Apply palette writes both designs into the Appearance at once, each mode's colours
in their half. Ids `graphite`, `paper`, `harbor`, `bloom` (`LookPalettes.IdOf` gone); strings
`settings.look.paletteLight|paletteDark` gone, each palette named by its family.

**The page: two colour buttons in one row.** The editor makes every colour two rows, its light mode's and its dark mode's
(`OptionRow.Dark`, keys `Appearance.<section>.<tone>.light|.dark`, `LookRows.ColourKey`); each its own tiles in its mode's
palette, its own "Default (…)" (Karpo's own of its mode), its own picker and its own write. The settings panel stands the
dark one beside the light one in the light one's row (`PanelRow.Pair`, `PanelRows.Of`): at the row's end two colour buttons
(`PanelMetrics.ModeColourWide`, 88 DIP: a colour button with its mode's glyph 12 DIP before its swatch — Segoe Fluent's Sun
for Light, Moon for Dark, as Windows' Settings' "Choose your mode"), the dark one last; each its reset (the row's §541 reset,
32 DIP) right before its own button while that half is set here, the reset's room kept while it is not, so setting or
resetting a half moves nothing (`PanelMetrics.PairRoom`, 264 DIP from the controls' end; no words of the value before
them). The row reads set here (§549: drawn as any row) where either half is, muted where both are inherited
(`PanelRow.Origin`; `PanelRow.Own` each half's); a group's and a section's counts count each half (§541: "5 set here, 5 from
Karpo"). Each button opens its own half's picker (its own key); to a screen reader each is "Background · Light" and
"Background · Dark", each reset "Reset to #FBFBFB (from Karpo) · Background · Light" (`settings.appearance.light|dark`,
"Light", "Dark", every language as Windows' own words: "Hell"/"Dunkel", "Clair"/"Sombre", …).

**The file** (shape 74 still — raised once with §567, nothing released between; ConfigWords.txt unchanged, the pair a
converter's: `ColorPairConverter`, which reads anything that is no object, a colour alone too, as nothing):

```
appearance.<section>.<colour>    { "dark"?: "#RRGGBB" | "#AARRGGBB" | "none", "light"?: … }  — each half left out unset
  <section>                      taskbar | widgets | flyouts | folderWidgets
  <colour>                       background | outline | text | accent | patternColor  (as §507 says which a section has)
appearance.<section>.font        "Family/Weight"   (one)
appearance.<section>.pattern     a §462 word | "none" (one)
appearance.taskbar.blur          0 to 100 (one)
```

Tests: `TaskbarModeTests` (was `TaskbarModeFreeTests`: in one mode the taskbar the same whatever Windows' accent, accent on

## 570. The Appearance page in four sections again: Bar, Taskbar widgets, Flyouts, Widgets in folders (2026-11-08) — no counts at a section's head, no Reset all, since §574 (2026-11-08); two sections again since §577 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"split taskbar widgets and bar again, same with the lower section too."*

**Replaces** §549's two sections (Taskbar: Bar and Taskbar widgets; Folders and flyouts: Flyouts and Widgets in folders),
each one card of two groups under one preview. The Appearance page (§567) is:

| Row | What it is | Its preview (§536) |
|---|---|---|
| Apply palette | as §568 | |
| Bar | a section: Background (a pair, §568), Background blur, Outline, Pattern, Pattern color | Bar: the bar and the widgets on it |
| Taskbar widgets | a section: Font, Text color, Background, Outline, Accent color, Pattern, Pattern color | Bar: the bar, its widgets' cards in their look |
| Flyouts | a section: Outline | Open: a folder open over its face, its outline round its lines |
| Widgets in folders | a section: the same seven as Taskbar widgets | Lines: the folder's lines alone, as the open folder draws them (a clock and a calendar) |
| Reset all | as §567 | |

Each section is a card of its own, as before §549 (`LookRows.Rows`: one level a section, `LookParts.All` in its order,
`LookParts.Name` and `Glyph` its head, its key `Appearance.<section>`, `LookRows.SectionKey(part)`): its head its name, its
icon and its own counts at its end ("5 set here, 5 from Karpo", "All from Karpo"; §541, each half of a pair counted, §568);
open, its preview at its top and its editor's rows under it. Every value says set here or inherited as §549, §555, §566 and
§568 have it; nothing of a row changes but its place: its key is its section's ("Appearance/Taskbar widgets/Colors/Background":
§517's Text and Colors headings name the place, as the panel draws no heading inside a card), the search's way to it its
section alone. A preview is named for its section ("Preview of Widgets in folders"). The edit bar's Look ▾ has the four
sections as its levels again (R1: three levels).

**Undone, not layered** — what only the combined form needed is gone: `LookSection`, `LookSections` (its parts, names and
icons), `LookRows.SectionKey(LookSection)`, `LookRows.PartHeading` / `IsPartHeading` (a part's heading in a section),
`PanelGroups.Parts` (a part a group in its section's card, its count at the group's head), `PanelRows.PlaceOf` (a group the
place of its rows, keyed with `~`), `LookPreview.SampleOf`'s section rule; the string `settings.look.folders` ("Folders and
flyouts") in every language. §536's Lines sample is back (`LookSample.Lines`, `LookPreview.LinesDip` 136 DIP: the lines in
the middle of the room, as §562 had dropped it), the Widgets in folders'; Open stays the Flyouts'. The file is as it was:
four sections (`Appearance`), no config change.

and icons, one preview each of its own section, no group on the page, every editor row once in its section's place, each

Open, Lines; the Lines room; its name), `ALookValueChangedIsAnotherPictureAnythingElseTheSame` per section;
`ValueOriginTests` (four levels; a section's counts its own values alone, the others "All from Karpo";
`ASetValueIsPaintedWithoutAMark` with Taskbar widgets open), `PopupPlaceTests`, `BarBlurSettingTests`, `BarGroundTests`,
`LayoutMenuTests` (Look ▾'s four sections), and the tests that open a section by its key (`PanelPopupPlaceTests`,

appearance-sections-<dark|light>.png (every section shut, each its count) and appearance-sections-open-<dark|light>.png
(every section open on a display 3000 DIP tall, each its own preview); `LookPreviewSheets`,

## 571. A preview's room holds the folder's lines whole: measured, not guessed (2026-11-08)

The Widgets in folders' preview (§570's Lines sample) cut its calendar at the foot: "Today" showed, its event under it was
cut off. **Cause:** the sample's room was a guessed constant, `LookPreview.LinesDip` 136 DIP, from §536 when the sample was
one line; §570 brought it back with two, a compact clock and a calendar (its header, "Today" and two events, "Tomorrow" and
one), which the open folder lays out about 300 DIP tall — and taller again at a bigger Windows text size, so no constant
could hold them. The Flyouts' Open sample had the same flaw: `OpenDip` 128 DIP held the bar and the foot of the folder open
over it, its top and its first lines cut off at the room's top edge.

**Fix, at the root:** a sample's room holds what it draws, whole, as the Bar's (its thickness) and the Menu's
(`MenuSample.Plan`) always did. A folder's lines are as tall as the very plan the sample draws: `LookPreviews.Laid` opens the
stand-in folder and lays it out as the open folder does (`FolderFlyout.Natural` and `Build`) — one plan, measured and drawn
alike —, and `LookPreviews.LinesDip(gfx, shows, windows, scale)` measures it (its height in DIP, rounded up) under
`LookStand`. The plan needs the widgets and a device (the lines' heights are their islands' `ListHeight`), so the panel's
layout, which is pure, asks for it through its measurer: `IPanelText.LinesDip(shows, scale)` beside `Width` —
`GfxPanelText(gfx, windows)` in production (the dock hands it Windows' look, as it hands `LookPreviews.Place`), a stand-in
in a test (`SettingsPanelTests.Words.Lines`, 280 DIP). Measured once a look: a `ConditionalWeakTable` by the rows'
`LookShown` (the rows are made again at every change, so a new one is a new look), again only for another Windows' look or
scale (the sample's key without its size); a scroll, the pointer, the page shown again measure nothing. Nothing measured
(an error): 0, the room the checker, as a sample not drawn.

`LookPreview.BoxDip(shows, measure, scale)` (and `TallDip`):

| Sample | Its room (DIP) |
|---|---|
| Bar | the bar's thickness, 12 over and under it (as before) |
| Menu | the menu's plan, 12 over and under it (as before) |
| Lines | the folder's lines, 12 over and under them, in the middle |
| Open | 12 over the folder, its lines, the 8 gap down to its face's bar, the bar, the 8 under it: the folder open whole |

**Gone:** `LookPreview.LinesDip` and `OpenDip`; the Lines sample's fallback for lines taller than their room (they never
are). The Open sample shows the folder whole now, its outline all round (§536's "its panel's foot showing" undone): that
outline is what the Flyouts section edits. A sample's folder is let go one way (`LookPreviews.Close`), measured or drawn.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests.ASamplesRoomHoldsTheFoldersLinesWhole` (the rule for Lines and Open at three heights of lines, the
panel's line and its room as tall; a bar's room holds no lines), `APreviewIsAnImageNothingToPressOrStopOn` and
`BarMenuPanelTests` through the measurer; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `SceneTreeTests.LookPreviewSheets` (every section's
sample: a folder's lines drawn wholly inside its room, `LookPreviews.Rooms`),
`AFoldersLinesStandWholeInTheirRoomAtEveryTextSize` (Widgets in folders and Flyouts at 100 % and 150 % Windows text: whole
both times, the room taller at 150 %; preview-<lines|flyouts>-text<100|150>-dark.png), `AppearanceSectionsSheets` (every
section open now on a display 3800 DIP tall, the page taller by the two whole folders).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Widgets in folders: the clock and the calendar whole, "Tomorrow" and its meeting in sight;
Flyouts: the folder open whole over its face; Windows' text size up, both rooms grow with it.

## 572. The weather shows no day and night: its graph's shaded night and the sun's hairlines gone (2026-11-08)

The person, 2026-11-08: *"day night should not be displayed on the weather widget anymore."* What the weather showed as
day and night: its Next hours (`ListKind.WeatherHours`, the weather's Hourly style, `WeatherHoursTile`) laid today's curve
over a faint fill from midnight to sunrise and from sunset to midnight, and a hairline at sunrise and at sunset (the day's
graph, `DayGraph.Shades` and `Marks`, from §80's flyout; "One gutter" kept the night "to the edges, because when it is
dark is information"). No setting governed it, and no words said it: it was the graph's only split of the day into day and night.

**Gone, at the root:** the weather was the graph's one user of a shade and a crossing (the stock's chart is its own), so
`DayGraph` has neither any more — `Shades`, `Marks`, `Shade` and `Cross`; `WeatherHoursTile` fills no night; the reading
carries no sun (`WeatherReading.Sunrise`, `Sunset`, `WeatherWindow.Sun`); the answer is read without it
(`ForecastDays.Sunrise`, `Sunset`) and the request no longer asks Open-Meteo for `sunrise,sunset`. No setting, no string,
nothing in the file: nothing to convert. A forecast cached before still reads (the sun's times in it are passed over).

**Kept, the other things that follow day and night** (not a display of day and night, and not asked about): the conditions'
glyph and words, now's and each hour's, are Open-Meteo's `is_day`'s — a moon and "Clear" or "Mostly clear" at night, a sun
and "Sunny" or "Mostly sunny" by day (`WeatherCodes.Describe`). The sun widget (§368, §404) shows the sun's day as it did.

Tests: `WeatherReadingTests.OneRequestAskedPerPlaceCarriesTheHoursAndTheWeek` (the request asks no sunrise and no sunset;
it failed first), the reading's tests without the sun's (`TheSunIsTakenFromTheDayItBelongsTo`,
`ADayWithNoSunriseOrNoSunsetIsMarkedWithNeither` gone with what they held); UI: `ListGutterTests`, `WeatherTargetsTests`,
`CalendarWeatherFolderTests` draw the hours as before.

By hand: a folder with the weather's Next hours, a place set: the curve, the hours, their glyphs and now's mark, nothing
shaded before sunrise or after sunset and no line at either.

## 573. A line's Height on its page of the settings panel acts: the panel's one handler knows the height rows (2026-11-08)

The person, 2026-11-08: *"height of the weather widget cannot be changed. it does not update when i click it."* In edit
mode, a folder line selected (the weather's, and any other's), its page of the settings panel shows its Height (§529: the
segments Automatic, Fixed, Fill and the Rows' stepper under them, on their well since §565); a press on a segment or on the
stepper's − and + changed nothing, in the file or on the page.

**Cause:** a line's height rows are not settings of the widget's (`OptionMenu`'s picks, ids from 10000) but rows of their
own (`LineHeightRows`, ids 5870 to 5879). In the line's menu their press comes as an adjustment (`FlyoutEventKind.Adjust`)
and `Dock.MenuAdjusted` acted them. The panel sends every control's press through the one handler of a menu's picks
(`PanelActed` › `Dock.Chosen`, §520), and `Chosen` never knew the height rows: the press fell through every branch and did
nothing. Not the weather's alone: every folder line's Height and Rows, and §432's Size of a sized line, since the panel came
(§520).

**Fix, at the root:** one function acts a line's height rows, whoever asks — `Dock.LineHeightActed(what, id)`: §432 a sized
line's size picked (`LineHeightRows.ActSize`), else the mode picked or the rows stepped (`LineHeightRows.For` › `Act`),
saved at once as every change is (`ChangeWidget`). `MenuAdjusted` calls it and shows the menu's Height or Size as it is now;
`Chosen` calls it after the widget's own picks, and the panel shows its page again from the config (`StirChrome`), the
segment and the stepper saying the height now. The two copies of the size's and the height's branches in `MenuAdjusted` are
that one function.

Tests (UI, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.ALinesHeightIsSetInTheSettingsPanel` — a weather line (no place,
nothing fetched) in a folder open arranged, selected, its page open: Fixed pressed is fixed in the file, a row more on the
Rows' stepper a cell more, Fill pressed fill (it failed before: the file kept `{"fixed":false,"cells":16}`).

By hand: edit mode, a folder open, a weather line selected, Settings: Height › Fixed, the Rows' +, Fill — the line resizes
behind the panel each time and the segment moves with it; the same for a clock, a calendar and a sized line's Size.

## 574. The Appearance's values are settings, nothing above them: no "from Karpo", no default, no reset; Apply palette presets them (2026-11-08) — a palette worn and kept, no Apply palette, since §577 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"the appearance says something like "x from karpo" or something like that, there should not be an
additional appearance level above. it should just be the settings that can also be preset with the apply preset option."*
Since §541 every Appearance value was either inherited from Karpo (muted, its first choice "Default (#…)", "From Karpo" to a
screen reader, no reset) or set here (as any row, its reset beside it); each section's head counted them ("5 set here, 5
from Karpo", "All from Karpo"), the bar's Background blur had Karpo's 30 % as its default (§558), and Reset all stood at the
page's foot.

**Replaces** §541's origin, §549's muting, §555's "set here or inherited", §558's default of the blur, §566's screen reader
words, §567's Reset all, §568's per-half default and reset, §570's counts at a section's head.

**What a value is now.** Every Appearance value is a setting with a value, nothing else. Its row shows the value in force —
`Looks.Of(config, dark)`: the file's value, and where the file says none Karpo's palette's (`KarpoLook.Paints`); a colour
Karpo decides as it draws (its text, its accent) shown as the colour it draws, an outline it draws none of as None. No
"Default (…)" in any of its choices: a colour's tiles are None (a background's, an outline's), the recent colours, the grid
(`OptionPickers.Paints(place, tone, key, title, shown, write, dark)`); the Font's every weight of every family installed, the
one in force ticked; the Pattern's None and the patterns; the Background blur a number, 30 a value as any (written as 30).
A pick is written as it is, Karpo's own value too.

**Apply palette presets them.** Karpo's own is a palette, the first (`LookPalettes.KarpoId`, its designs
`KarpoLook.Paints(false|true)`, named "Karpo" in every language: `settings.look.paletteKarpo`), then Graphite, Paper,
Harbor, Bloom. A new config wears Karpo's (the file's absent values are Karpo's palette's — the default, not a layer shown).
Applied, a palette writes all its values into the four sections at once (`LookPalettes.Apply`). The row shows the palette
whose values the Appearance comes to exactly, in both modes (`LookPalettes.Worn`: `Looks.Of` of the config against
`Looks.Of` of the palette written out, light and dark), else "Custom" — so a file that says Karpo's values and one that
leaves them out both wear Karpo. The way back to Karpo's own is applying Karpo: no Reset all, no reset of a value.

**The panel draws every value as any row.** No section's head says anything of its values (no counts; §517's R4 holds a
section of the Appearance to its preview, `MenuRulesTests`); no name or value muted (`PanelPainter.NameInk`: the text's ink,
the disabled one greyed); no reset; to a screen reader no "Set here" / "From Karpo" (`UiaNode.Help` a group's sentence or
a description alone). A colour of both modes is still one row of two colour buttons, the sun's and the moon's (§568), now 8
apart with nothing between them (`PanelMetrics.PairRoom` 184 DIP: two 88s and a gap).

**Deleted, the origin machinery whole** (the Appearance was its last user — §567 took every other value of a default):
Karpo.Core\OptionOrigins.cs (`OptionOrigin`, `OptionOrigins`, `OptionRow.Origin`, `DefaultValue`, `ResetValue`),
`OptionRow.Default`, `OptionRow.Inherited`, `OptionPickers.Unset`, `LookRows.ResetAllRow`, `LookPalettes.Clear`,
`LookPalettes.Same`, `FlyoutItem.Default|Origin|Reset`, `PanelRow.Origin|Own|Overridden|Inherited|Held|ResetTip|Reset`,
`PanelHitKind.Reset` (its layout, paint, tooltip, UIA and act), `PanelSentences.Counts`, `OptionMenu`'s reset pick and a
font's "Default (…)" alone at its list's top. The other "Default (…)" choices (Karpo's formats, an account's Automatic
colour, a folder face's source, an icon's cross) never had a `Default` in the row model and are as they were. Strings gone in
every language: `settings.value.setHere`, `settings.value.karpo`, `settings.from.karpo`, `settings.resetTo.karpo`,
`settings.counts.karpo.some|none`, `dock.panel.reset`; new `settings.look.paletteKarpo` ("Karpo", a name).

**The file:** no change, shape 74. An absent value is Karpo's palette's, as before; no migration.

Tests: `AppearanceValuesTests` (no "Default (…)", no reset, no counts, every value the one in force, Karpo's own of each
mode; a pick written as it is, Karpo's own too, Karpo still worn; Custom after another value; a palette applied worn, Karpo
applied the way back; the panel: no section value, every name the text's ink, the pair's two buttons 8 apart, a screen
reader's names by mode and no origin help; the strings gone), `LookTests` (Karpo the first palette; the palette applied and
Karpo applied back; the pattern colour the ink it is drawn in; the font's choices without a default; Karpo's font picked
written), `BarBlurSettingTests` (30 written as 30, Karpo worn), `MenuPickersTests` (None first, no "Default (…)", the colour
in force said as any value), `SettingsPanelTests.EveryControlIsOneSize` (the pair 8 apart, 184 DIP), `LookPreviewTests`,
`LayoutMenuTests`, `PatternTests`, `MenuRulesTests`; `ValueOriginTests`, `ValueOriginDeckTests` and `ValueOriginPictures`
gone with what they held. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.AppearanceSectionsSheets` and
`AppearancePairSheets`, appearance-sections[-open]-<dark|light>.png and appearance-page|preview-<dark|light>.png.

By hand: edit mode › Appearance: Apply palette says Karpo; Taskbar widgets: every value plain, no reset, no count on the
section's head; a background picked: Apply palette says Custom; Apply palette › Karpo: Karpo's own again, it says Karpo.

## 575. The edit bar a command bar of the settings' pages, each opening a flyout of its own; no fold, no side list; "+ Add"'s list in the pages' look (2026-11-08) — no search, every flyout centred under its entry, since §578 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-08): *"change once more how the edit bar looks like, today there is basically just one extend and close.
i want to change it so that all the individual menus that we have right now are basically in the edit bar and then they
open a flyout individually with their settings in it. all of the menu entries we have on the sidemenu get promoted to menu
entries on the topbar, the topbar is not extendible anymore and there is no sidemenu too. the add menu should also be
adjusted so its style aligns with the style of the other settings pages."*

**The bar** (`PanelLayout`, SettingsPanel.Layout.cs; `EditDeck`, Dock.EditDeck.cs) is one 48 DIP row, as wide as what it
holds, centred where §296 has it — WinUI's command bar, its buttons a glyph and a word, no fill and no rim until the pointer
is on one, Done the one accent button:

    ⠿ [⚙ Karpo] [@ Accounts] [🖥 Display] [▤ Layouts] [▭ Taskbar] [🎨 Appearance]  [ Search settings 🔍 ]  [⊗ 2 errors] [📁 Folder] [🕑 Clock] [+ Add] [✓ Done]

- **An entry for each page the side list held**, in its order: Karpo, Accounts, Display, Layouts, Taskbar, Appearance —
  what that display shows (no Taskbar on one that shows None, `Dock.PanelOf`). 4 DIP apart (§548's `Tight`, a command bar's),
  a gutter before and after the search box (320 × 32), the errors 8 after it (§394), then **the selection's entries** — the
  folder open arranged or selected (`PanelPage.Folder`, "Folder"), the widget selected (`PanelPage.Widget`, named for it:
  "Clock", "2 × Clock", "3 widgets") —, Add, Done ending a gutter in. The grip first (§395).
- **The entry open is selected**: SubtleFillColorSecondary under it (Tertiary under the pointer) and §548's one pill, 16 × 3 in
  the accent, at its foot, as WinUI's SelectorBar marks its item.
- **Too wide for its display** (`EditDeckPlan.Widest`): the search narrows first, to 160 DIP at the least
  (`PanelMetrics.SearchLeast`); narrower still, the pages' entries show their icon alone, 40 DIP, their words their tooltip
  and a screen reader's.

**A flyout for each entry** (`EditDeck`'s second FlyoutHost, the edit bar's stratum, hung from its entry by §521's one rule,
`PopupPlace.Of`: under it, 4 DIP off it, flush with its left — with its right where flush with its left it would pass the
bar's side, as "+ Add"'s does — over it from an edit bar at the display's foot, inside the work area). It holds exactly that
page: the same rows, cards, controls, header card, previews and popups as the panel's page had — 580 DIP wide (a gutter, the
page's 548 DIP of cards, a gutter; `PanelMetrics.FlyoutWide`), as tall as its page and no taller than the room on its side
(and a popup's most, 70 % of the work area), scrolling past it by the wheel, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End and the keys'
focus, a thin indicator at its edge. No title: the entry names the page; a widget's and a folder's keep their header card.

- **One open at a time**, on one display (`Dock.panelOn`, `PanelMemory.Page`): another entry switches it; the open one
  clicked again, Escape (`EditEscape.CloseFlyout`, after the search's words and before an open folder), or a press anywhere
  but the edit bar and its flyout (the dim, a bar, a folder, another display's edit bar: `Dock.Pressing`, `DeckPressed`,
  `ShadeMessage`) closes it. Nothing opens as edit mode begins (§537 to §574 its panel did) but a selection's.
- **The selection's**: a widget selected (several as one, §528), or a folder opened or selected, brings its entry onto the bar
  of the display it stands on and opens its flyout (`PanelMemory.Follow`: once a selection, so a flyout closed while it stands
  stays closed); the selection gone, its entry goes and its flyout with it. A way in from outside opens its page's flyout at
  its row (`OpenEditMenu` → `Dock.OpenPanel`): a second start Karpo's, Win+Alt+Enter Taskbar's, "Manage accounts" Accounts', the
  bar's right click Taskbar's.
- **The search** stays on the bar; typing lists its finds in the flyout under the box, in place of the flyout open
  (`PanelLayout.Finding`), each a card's row: its page's icon, its name, where it is. Up, Down and Enter walk and pick them;
  a pick opens the owning entry's flyout at its row, its expanders open, the row lit a moment (`EditDeck.Land`). Only the bar in
  use builds its pages whole (`Dock.PanelOf`'s `full`); another display's builds its entries alone until its search or an
  entry is used (`EditDeckAction.Search`, `Open`).

**"+ Add"'s list is a page as every other** (`PanelPage.Add`, `Dock.AddOf`, `PanelRows.Picks`): Add is an entry that opens it
in the same flyout — the same ground, cards, type ramp and spacing tokens, its icons in the card's icon column — the add
tree's sections (Popular, Browse) its headings, each folder of the tree an expander of its rows, each widget a card the whole
of which a click adds (`PanelRowKind.Pick`, its row's command; greyed with why, §545's licence rows too). Its own search, the
settings' search box across the flyout's top (`PanelHitKind.Filter`), has the keys as it opens: what is typed lists the
widgets that match, flat, each saying where it is (`AddList.Results`); Enter adds the one that matches; Down goes into the
list. Its behaviour is the list's: onto the display's bar, or into the folder open arranged there (§298), the pick carried on
the pointer (`AddSpot.Follows`, `Dock.AddChosen`), the flyout closing as it is picked. The bars' and the folders' "+" keep the
add list hung from them (§531's other openers), its place known.

**Keys and a screen reader** (`DeckUia`): the bar is a tool bar — each entry, and Add, a button that expands and collapses
(its flyout open or not), the search an edit —; the flyout a pane named for its page, its sections groups, each control as
§520 has it; the finds a list. Tab and Shift+Tab walk the bar's things and then the flyout's; Left and Right go along the
bar; Enter and Space open an entry (its flyout); Down from an open entry goes into its flyout; F6 and Ctrl+E to the search;
Escape closes the flyout.

**The stage map** (Dock.Stage.cs) names an entry "Nav:<page>" as the side items were, so the probes click "Nav:Appearance"
as before; "Add:" is Add; "Page" is the flyout of the page open, "Flyout" whatever it shows; "Found:<key>#n" a find.

**Deleted**: the fold — Settings ⌄ / ⌃ (`PanelHitKind.Fold`, `EditDeckAction.Fold`, `EditDeck.Unfolded`, its fold-back timer,
`FlyoutHost.Unfold` and `Unfolded`), the panel's header row and body (`PanelLayout.HeadRow`, `Body`, `HeadAtFoot`, `AtFoot`,
`WidthOf`, `BarOf`, the one 760 DIP width), §537's panel open by default (`panelOpening`, `PanelMemory.Opening`, `Chose`,
`General` and its stack of pages before), the side list (`PanelLayout.Nav`, `PanelPainter.Nav`, its metrics `Side`, `NavItem`,
`NavPitch`, `PageLeft`, `PageRight`), §545's side-list footer (`LicenseView.Footer`, `LicenseUsage`, `LicenseMeter`,
`LicenseFill`, `PanelHitKind.GetPro`, `Usage`, `EditDeckAction.GetPro`, the meters' metrics and "dock.edit.usage.*" in every

## 576. Every "+" opens the one add page, hung from it; the edit bar stands still; a click lost, the selection clicked again, the samples cut (2026-11-09) — the bar one width, the add page centred on its "+", since §578 (2026-11-09)

Loose ends §575 left, each fixed where it starts.

**Every "+" opens the add page** (`Dock.AddAtPlus`, `AddInFolder`, `OpenAdd`). The bars' "+" and a folder column's "+"
opened §531's add list as a menu of its own; only the edit bar's Add opened §575's page. Now each opens that page on its
display's edit bar, its flyout hung from the "+" itself (`EditDeckModel.From`, `PopupPlace`: under it or over it as the room
says, flush with it), adding where that "+" adds — at once at its end of its section, or at the column's place — its place
marked meanwhile (`Adding`: the spot, the bar's line). The same "+" pressed again closes it (`addClosed`, §430's rule). Add's
entry on the bar is not marked open while a "+" hangs the page (`PanelInput.Hung`). The page goes however it goes, and the
place with it (`ReconcileChrome` ends the adding). Deleted: `ShowAddList`, `BeginAdd`, `FolderFlyout.PlusOnScreen`, the add
list's menu layout (`FlyoutLayout.Library`, its columns and newspaper keys), the menu's own search (`Flyout.Search.cs`),
`AddList.Title`, `AddList.Said` and their words in every language (`dock.add.toFolder`, `toTaskbar`, `noMatch`, `matches.*`).

**The edit bar stands still** (`PanelLayout.Steady`, `EditDeckPlan.Place`'s `steady`). Selecting a widget put its entry on
the centred bar and the whole bar moved half its width. The bar is centred by its width without the selection's entries,
so its pages' entries and the search keep their place and the selection's come and go at its right, as a command bar's
contextual commands do; pushed back inside only where it would pass the display's side.

**The widget selected, clicked again** (`PanelMemory.Picked` from `EditPick`; `Dock.OnItsWidget`). A press on a bar closed
the flyout open, and the selection being the one followed already, nothing opened it again. A widget picked — clicked, the
one selected too — is followed afresh: its flyout opens; and a press on the widget whose flyout stands open leaves it open.

**A click lost after a flyout came in** (`DockWindow.Pointed`). Windows posted the bar a `WM_MOUSELEAVE` between the
pointer's move and the press (a window shown under a pointer it tracks elsewhere): the hover ended, `HitAt` said nothing,
and the press on a folder's face read as one on the bar's room — the selection cleared, no folder opened. A press is the
pointer on the bar: it begins the hover itself. `RunSettings`' 800 ms pause before the face's click is gone. The stage probes
print the isolated `local\karpo.log` they meant to.

**The looks' samples cut to the flyout** (`LookPreviews.Cut`). The samples' layer was the bar's size (48 DIP tall), and its
inset clip cut every sample below the flyout's first 48 DIP away: the Taskbar page's menu a blank grey box, the
Appearance's previews too. It is the flyout's page now.

**"lockTaskbar" last in the file** (`[JsonPropertyOrder(1)]`). BarMoves.cs compiles before Config.cs, so the lock went above
"version". The round-trip test's file is the one this build writes: no §549 "animations", §534's lock last.

**A colour typed in the picker** (`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AColourIsMixedInTheSettingsPanel`): not reproduced on this
build — alone, with its class and beside other probes; left as it is.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests` (`TheSelectionClickedAgainOpensItsFlyout`, `TheBarsSteadyWidthLeavesTheSelectionOut`, Add not
marked while hung), `EditDeckPlanTests.TheSelectionsEntryMovesNothingBeforeIt`, `LookPreviewTests.EveryPreviewInAFlyoutStandsInsideItsCut`,
`WidgetItemTests.TheFileReadsAndWritesBackByteForByte`, `FolderColumnsTests` (the "+" a column's add page hangs from),
`MenuToggleTests` (each bar's and a column's "+" toggles the add page, hung from it), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.RunSettings`
(no pause; the widget clicked again). Pictures: `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-plus- (the add page from a bar's
"+"), panel-widget-, panel-taskbar- (its menu drawn).

## 579. About Karpo a section with its logos; the Display page every display connected, this one first; the Default layout the Layouts page's (2026-11-09) — one page, Displays and layouts, each display an expander in Windows' order, this one marked, not first, since §585 (2026-11-09) — the Default layout a badge in the list and a switch in each layout's expander, no dropdown, since §595 (2026-11-09) — About Karpo without Open-Meteo since §630 (2026-11-09)

expander: its rows inner rows, which the panel draws without an icon, so the logos §339 gave them (Karpo's, Lometics') never

three lines over one another. It is a section of the Karpo page of its own now, under its heading About Karpo

**The Default layout** (BarLooks.Default, `DefaultRow`, `WriteDefault`). What displays Karpo has not seen yet show is the

off on them), as New displays' Layout was on the Display page. The layout it names is marked in the list: "Default layout"
under its name, "This display · Default layout" where this display shows it too; none while it says None. A layout deleted
sends its displays to the default layout (its question says so).

`settings.sections.newDisplays` and `settings.displays.newDisplays.header`; `settings.layouts.deleteConfirm` now "Its displays
switch to the default layout.".

## 577. A palette worn, each keeping its own values, a designed one's reset; the Appearance in two sections again; a colour pair as wide as one dropdown, its second button opening its picker (2026-11-09) — its sections page sections, nothing folded, a palette holding the person's edits marked, since §583 (2026-11-09); one preview over four tabs since §592 (2026-11-09); the reset in Palette's row, before its dropdown, since §610 (2026-11-09); the reset asked first since §634 (2026-11-09)

**A palette worn** (`LookPalettes`, Karpo.Core\Looks.cs). The Appearance wears one palette: Karpo's own (the default, what a
new config wears), Graphite, Paper, Harbor, Bloom — `LookPalettes.All`, Karpo's designs as §568 has them — or **Custom**

wearing Paper and Graphite again finds Graphite's values as they were. Custom with no values yet is Karpo's own.

**The page** (`LookRows.Rows`):

| Row | What it is |
|---|---|
| Palette | a dropdown of the six, each its swatch as it is drawn now (its values with it), the one worn chosen; a pick wears it at once (`LookPalettes.Wear`), nothing else written |

No confirmation: edit mode's undo has it |
| Taskbar | a section: the Bar's rows and the Taskbar widgets', each part a group in its card, one preview (the Bar sample) |
| Folders and flyouts | a section: the Flyouts' row and the Widgets in folders', each part a group, one preview (the Open sample) |

The Reset's words are the taskbar menu's (`settings.look.reset` = `settings.barMenu.reset`'s in every language, §532), the

## 578. The edit bar one width, no search; every flyout centred under its entry; the add page's widgets tiles; a row that only acts its button alone; every dropdown its choice's icon (2026-11-09) — no empty state in the slot, every flyout 12 DIP off the bar with a beak, since §584 (2026-11-09) — no slot, the selection's entries as any other in a room kept for them, since §596 (2026-11-09)

**Every flyout centred under its entry** (`PopupPlace.Of`'s `centred`, `FlyoutPlacement.Centred`). §521's one rule hung a
control's popup flush with its left (WinUI's ComboBox); an edit bar entry's flyout, and §576's add page hung from a "+",
now stands centred on what it hangs from — under it, 4 DIP off, or over it from an edit bar at the display's foot — pushed in

## 580. Windows' panels kept off a bar at the side: Start, Search, quick settings, the notification centre, the Widgets board, the quick link menu (2026-11-09) — Start down to the work area's end since §591, hung from Karpo's Start button since §601 (2026-11-09) — Start's rules superseded by §666 (2026-11-12)

The person: *"when the taskbar is on the side the start menu overlaps it. is this fixable? if yes fix it for all the
flyouts, not just the start menu"*

**Why.** Windows places every panel of its own by Explorer's taskbar, never by the work area (§540): Windows 11's taskbar has
no edge but the bottom, and the panels hear of it over the shell's own channel (`WindowsUdk.UI.Shell.TaskbarLayout`), which
nothing an app says through `SHAppBarMessage` reaches. With Explorer's taskbar auto-hidden and hidden while Karpo runs (§465),
each stands where it would over a bottom taskbar: Start and Search at the display's left (`TaskbarAl` 0, the person's) or in
its middle, the Widgets board and the quick link menu (Win+X) against its left end, quick settings, the notifications, the
notification centre and the calendar against its right end. Karpo's bar down a side holds its strip (`ABE_LEFT`/`ABE_RIGHT`,
§146) and the work area leaves it out, which no panel reads; so a bar at the left was under Start, Search, the Widgets board
and Win+X, one at the right under quick settings and the notification centre. Windhawk's vertical taskbar mod, which moves
Explorer's own taskbar to a side, has to move the same windows for the same reason, from inside each host process (read, its
source: Start's host and Search's moved along as they are uncloaked, quick settings' and the notification centre's as they are
placed); Karpo moves them from outside, as §540 moves the notifications.

**Seen** on the user's PC (26300, 150 %; read-only, a WinEvent hook that listened while the person used Start; nothing opened
or moved by it): on the display with the bar at its left (work area from -3777 of -3840..0), Start's host, a CoreWindow of
StartMenuExperienceHost, at -3840,0..0,2088 — as wide as the display, short of the hidden taskbar's 72 px — uncloaked as Start
opened, placed again by Windows some 200 ms later and as it closed, and, while Start stood open for minutes, a burst of four
moves every three to five seconds, each ending where it stood; Search's host over it, Start's search box, at
-3840,825..-2553,2160, flush with the display's left. Explorer's menus (`Xaml_WindowedPopupClass`) are shown below the screen
and moved up 5 ms later.

**Now** (`ShellPopups`, Karpo.Dock): §540's one mover for ShellExperienceHost's windows takes every panel's. Which window is
which panel is `WindowsPanels.PanelOfWindow`, the one answer that closes them for a flyout of Karpo's; each panel's process is
hooked (`ShellPopups.Hosts`: ShellExperienceHost, ShellHost, StartMenuExperienceHost, SearchHost, WidgetBoard, and the Explorer
whose taskbar it is), out of context, nothing injected: shown, uncloaked and — but for Explorer, whose process holds every folder
window — moved. Where a panel goes is `ShellPopupPlace.For`, pure:

- **A panel of its own size** (quick settings, the notifications and the notification centre, the Widgets board, Win+X,
  Search's window and Start's search box) that reaches into a strip a bar holds is moved off it by the strip's thickness,
  Windows' own gap to the screen's end kept to the bar (`Clear`, §540's). A window past the screen's end where no bar stands
  is still coming in, and stays (it was pulled in before).
- **Start's host, as wide as the display** (and Search's, should it be one), has Start inside it at Windows' alignment, so its
  rectangle says nothing of where Start is: it stands at the display's left, and further in by the left strip's thickness where
  Windows stands Start at the left (`Wide`, `TaskbarAl` 0, read as it is placed). Centred, Start is in the middle of the display,
  which no bar at a side reaches, and the host stays where Windows put it. Measured from the display, never from where the host
  stands, so it moves once however often it is heard, and back where the bar went. The search box, flush with the display's
  left, goes as far by `Clear`, and stays on Start. No size is changed (the mod's note: resizing Start's host glitched).
- **Never fought** (`ShellPopupMoves`): twelve moves per window in ten seconds (six before; Start's host is placed by Windows up
  to three times an opening), and a window its host puts back where it stood before Karpo moved it is moved again twice while it
  shows, then let be until it shows again (`PutBacks`). Whether Start's bursts while open are Windows putting its host back
  could not be told from outside (they end where Windows had it either way): the mod moves Start's host once, as it is uncloaked,
  and nothing after, which says they leave its place alone; should they not, Start steps aside, back at most twice, and then
  stands over the bar until it is opened again — never a flicker every few seconds.

**Karpo's own flyouts** were looked through for the same (every path that places a window of Karpo's): they hang from the bar's
inner side inside the work area less every other bar in sight (`FlyoutPlacement`, `DockWindow.WorkArea`/`FolderWork`), so
none opens over a bar at the side. Two leaks closed: the room a flyout's panel keeps round it for its shadow, which takes the
pointer, ran 12 DIP past the work area where the panel was pushed against its end (24 DIP of room, 12 of margin), over a bar
standing there — the right one of a Top and bottom on a side — and is now cut to the room it was placed in
(`FlyoutHost.RoomInside`, the window list's too, `Preview`); a folder's tips were kept in the bare work area, which holds a bar
over the windows, and now keep to the folder's own room.

**Not done, and why.** Clipboard history (Win+V) and the emoji panel (Win+.) stand in TextInputHost's window, the size of the
screen, at the caret or the screen's corner: their place is inside a window that never moves, so there is nothing to move, and
WindowsPanels does not know them. The volume and brightness indicator is no panel of these hosts. Start can't be placed before
it shows from outside its process (the mod does it before the uncloak, from inside): Karpo hears it a few ms after, so Start may
be seen to step aside as it opens, and where Windows puts it back 200 ms in, a second step — to be looked at on the real PC. A
bar at the top or the bottom is as before: Windows' panels stand over a bottom taskbar's place, a bottom bar's own, and none
was asked of. Found and left (edit mode and hover bars, others' work now): a hover bar's own strip in `WorkArea` (a menu with no
room anywhere may fall back over it), the edit bar dragged over a hover bar, `ClearOf` taking the edit bar to be at the top.

Tests: `ShellPopupsTests` (Start at the left beside a bar at the left, by its thickness, at 150 % and 100 %, on the user's other
display with the measured host and search box; centred, or with the bar at the right, it stays; moved once however often heard,
and back where the bar went; between bars at both sides; off the display; Search's host as Start's; quick settings and the
notification centre left of a bar at the right; the Widgets board, Win+X and Search right of one at the left; a panel away from
the bar, a non-Start window as wide as the display stays; an Explorer menu below the screen with no bar there; every panel's
process hooked; put back twice a showing, then let be; twelve moves in ten seconds), `PopupRoomTests` (`AFlyoutsRoomStopsAtTheBarBesideIt`,
`AFlyoutsRoomIsWholeInTheMiddleAndNoneWhereItRunsPast`). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.SideBarSheets`
(a folder beside a bar at the left and at the right). No test moves a real window.

By hand, with Karpo's bar at the left of a display and Windows' taskbar aligned left: Start (Karpo's button, and the Windows key)
opens right of the bar, its search box on it, typing in it searches there; leave it open half a minute — it does not step back over the bar; open and close it four times quickly — it stays beside
the bar each time; watch whether it steps aside once as it opens, or twice. Search (Win+S), the Widgets board (Win+W) and Win+X
right of the bar. With the bar at the right: quick settings (Win+A, then its sound and Wi-Fi pages, which resize it), the
notification centre and calendar (Win+N) left of it. Move the bar to the bottom: Start back where Windows puts it. appbar.log has
a line *"Windows' Start ... moved off the bars to ..."* per move.

## 582. Every preview in dark and light: one sample twice, a slanted line through its middle (2026-11-09) — one mode again, the taskbar's, over the desktop's picture, since §613 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the previews should show dark and light mode, it should be done with a tilted vertical line in the
center"*.

**Replaces** §568's previews drawn in the mode Windows is in. Every colour of the Appearance is a pair (§568), so a sample in
one mode showed half of what the page sets; now every look preview — the Appearance's Taskbar and Folders and flyouts (§577),
the Taskbar page's menu (§551, which wears the bar's look and so its mode) — shows both, whichever mode Windows is in.

**One sample, twice, cut by a slanted line** (`LookPreviews.Make`, the one drawing path every preview takes). The sample is
drawn whole once in Windows' dark mode and once in its light one (`LookPreview.ModesOf`: Windows' look with its mode set,
`Look.Wearing` then reading each colour pair's half of it, Karpo's own of that mode where a half is unset), each its own
checker (§536's dark or light greys), each in a visual the room's size. Each is clipped to its side of a line through the
room's middle that leans 1 across for 5 down (about 11° off upright, `LookPreview.Slant`), its top right of the middle, its foot
left: the **dark mode on the left, the light one on the right** (chosen; the pair's buttons stand light then dark, §568, but a
picture reads left to right and dark first is the mode Karpo was born in, §547). Not two half-width samples: each half is the full sample, the line only hides
what is past it. The clip is a rectangle geometry of the half, reaching well past the room (`LookPreview.HalfOf`), sheared onto
the line by the clip's transform (`LookPreview.SlantOf`, a shear about the room's middle) — no path geometry, which would need a
Direct2D geometry source. Over both, the line itself: a hairline (1 DIP, whole px) of grey #8A8A8A that reads on either side,
a Composition line run past the room's top and foot so the room's rounded corners, not its square ends, end it
(`LookPreview.DividerOf`). The room's rounded clip (§536) cuts both halves and the line.

**Live as before.** A half of a pair changed is another key (§536: the Appearance is in it), so its preview is drawn again,
once, both sides — its side shows the change, the other side stays as it was. A scroll and the pointer draw nothing. A mode
changed in Windows still is another key (Windows' look is in it); the picture is the same, drawn again once, as before.

**High contrast**: Windows' one look, whole, no line — its system colours win over both modes (§547), so there is nothing
to split.

**Nothing else moves**: the room's height, the Caption, the cut to the flyout (§576), the stand-ins, the screen reader's name
("Preview of Taskbar") are as they were; no config, no string.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests.ASampleIsDrawnInBothModesDarkFirstEachWearingItsHalf` (dark then light whatever Windows' mode, each
its half of a pair; high contrast one look), `TheModesAreSplitByALeaningLineThroughTheRoomsMiddle` (the line through the
middle, its top right, its foot left, about 11°; the two sheared halves cover the room once, the dark one exactly left of
the line). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `SceneTreeTests.ALookChangedDrawsItsPreviewAgainOnceAndNothingElseDoes` (now on the Taskbar
section, its "widgets" scene gone with §577: both modes drawn, the left a good deal darker; the light half of the bar's
background alone changed, drawn once again, the right side changed, the left not one px); `LookPreviewSheets`
(preview-taskbar|folders-dark|light.png, the odd values now a different colour each mode), `SettingsPanelSheets`
panel-barmenu-dark|light.png (the menu split too).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Taskbar: the preview's left the bar in dark mode, its right in light, a grey line leaning
between them; set the sun button of Bar › Background to a red: the right side red at once, the left as it was; the moon
button: the left. Taskbar › Taskbar menu: the menu dark left, light right.

## 581. The taskbar menu Windows 11's by default: the layouts, Task Manager, Taskbar settings, the last edit mode on the Taskbar page (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the default right click menu on the taskbar should be like in windows: task manager and taskbar
settings (the taskbar settings should open edit mode.) and the layout selector should be also there."*

**The default** (`BarMenus.Default`). Before: Edit, Lock the taskbar, a rule, the layouts, a rule, Task Manager (§366,
§534). Now: the layouts (every one, a lone one too, ticked, under no heading: §366, §561), a rule, then Windows 11's two rows
in Windows' order, **Task Manager** and **Taskbar settings** — the last nearest a bottom bar, where Windows has it. Windows
11's menu has nothing else, so "Lock the taskbar" left the default: the lock stays the Taskbar page's switch under Bar, and
the row is in Add an entry's list for whoever wants it back. Every built-in row that was addable still is; Quit Karpo is
still in no default.

**Taskbar settings** (`BarMenuAction.TaskbarSettings`, written `"taskbarSettings"`). It is §366's "Edit" renamed and sent
further: Windows' words (`core.barMenu.taskbarSettings`, in every language the words Windows uses for its own taskbar
settings, as `core.link.taskbar` has them; Ukrainian "Параметри панелі завдань", Windows' own) and Windows' gear (E713, which
menus draw as Explorer's two-colour Options picture). Chosen, it does what Win+Alt+Enter on a bar's button does
(`EditEntry.TaskbarSettings`, `OpenEditMenuLater` once the menu has gone): edit mode on that bar's display, the edit bar's
Taskbar page open under its entry — the menu itself, Lock the taskbar and the rest a click away. Its command is
`CMD_TASKBAR_SETTINGS` (5000, `CMD_EDIT_LAYOUT` before). It is the menu's required row (`BarMenus.Required`): never removed
(why said under its name), put back first where a hand edit lost it. Gone: `Dock.EditItem`, "Edit"'s pencil in this menu
(`core.barMenu.edit` stays: the edit bar's toolbar name for UI Automation), and `Dock.BarRows(layouts, locked)`'s `locked`.

**A right click on Show desktop** still offers its floor's "Taskbar settings" (Dock.MenuFloor.cs), which opens Windows'
taskbar settings (ms-settings:taskbar), Show desktop having no page of its own: the same words for two places. Left as it is.

**The file: shape 76.** `"editTaskbar"` is no word of the file any more; `"taskbarSettings"` is. The default is never written,
so a file without `"barMenu"` takes the new default as it is. A file with the person's own menu keeps it: converted by hand,
each `{ "kind": "action", "action": "editTaskbar" }` in `"barMenu"` becomes `"action": "taskbarSettings"` (its id and place
kept), and `"version"` 76. Not converted, the unknown row goes and Taskbar settings is put first (`BarMenus.Repair`).

**PanelPopupPlaceTests' scrolled dropdown.** `ADropdownOpensUnderItsControl` and `…WithThePanelOpeningUp` failed since §579:
closed, the Karpo page's only dropdowns are Language and Animations at its top, and About Karpo as a section of its own
made the page tall enough that six notches of the wheel scroll both out of sight with none to come in (the probe saw them at
264 and 342 px, its viewport from 434). Not a bug of the dropdowns: the probe now opens General's date and time formats,
whose rows are dropdowns, and wheels one notch (`Probe.FormatsScrolled`); its failure says which dropdowns it saw.

Tests: `BarMenuModelTests` (the default, Windows' names and glyphs, Lock and Quit addable and in no default, Taskbar settings
always in the menu, the hand-typed default read as none, the repair), `BarMenuLinesTests`, `BarMenuRowsTests` (the default's
rows, commands and glyphs; Karpo's rows keep their commands moved), `BarMenuTests.TheBarsMenuIsWindowsTaskManagerAndTaskbarSettings`,
`BarMovesTests` (the lock's tick on a menu that has it added), `BarMenuPanelTests`, `LayoutMenuTests`, `MenuWordingTests`,
`DockMenusLanguageTests` (German: Task-Manager, Taskleisteneinstellungen), `EditEntriesTests.TheDockGoesEachWay` (the row's
command opens `EditEntry.TaskbarSettings` on its bar), `PanelReorderTests`, `PanelReorderStageTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`
(ConfigWords.txt at shape 76), `PanelPopupPlaceTests`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `BarMenuPictures.TheMenuSheets`
bar-menu-one-layout-, bar-menu-layouts-, bar-menu-own- (dark and light, 100 and 150 %).

By hand: a right click on the bar's room: the layouts, a rule, Task Manager, Taskbar settings; Taskbar settings: edit mode,
the Taskbar page open; its section: Taskbar settings with no Remove, Lock the taskbar in Add an entry's list.

## 587. Every dropdown one width: its list its box's, never as wide as what it lists (2026-11-09) — a colour's picker 400 DIP since §613 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the dropdowns sometimes change their width with their contents and then never change back. the
dropdowns generally should have a fixed width"*.

**Why it grew and stayed.** The panel's popups (`Dock.PanelPopup`) were shown `FitsContent` (§517's edit bar menus): as wide
as their widest row — every level under it too — up to the work area, past §521's "at least as wide as its box". And that
width (`Flyout.fitWidth`) was the widest of every layout of one showing, `MathF.Max` of the last: a Refresh (a step, a
switch, §356), a level opened in it and a search's finds coming in as one types each laid it out again, never narrower. So a
time zone's search opened 591 DIP wide, a place's grew as its finds came and kept the widest find's width when fewer came;
107 of the corpus' 404 popups were wider than their box (a colour filter's 339 DIP, a weather Style's 407, a status icon's
"Show behind the arrow" 245).

**Now** (`Flyout.Open`, the one rule every control's popup takes): a control's popup — a dropdown's list, a colour's picker,
a way to add one's list, a button's level, the errors' list — is one width whatever its rows say, as WinUI's ComboBox list is
its box's: a value's box's 240 DIP (`PanelMetrics.ControlWide`). A row longer than that is cut with an ellipsis and said whole
in its tooltip (Flyout's CutWords, as before). `FitsContent` is no control popup's: §517's fit stays the folder room's right
click's alone.

**A search's popup the same width too** (the person, 2026-11-09: "the dropdowns should all have the same width") — a field
with a finder over its finds (a time zone, a place, a symbol, a currency, a team or league, a feed's address, a folder or a
pin's target): its box's 240 like every other, a long find cut, whole in its tooltip; the same before anything is typed and
as its finds change. No exception anywhere: the font list (§556) fits the 240.

**The closed box** was one width already (§548, 240 × 32); its value cut short now says itself whole in its tooltip
(`PanelLayout.ValueRoom`, the room the painter cuts its words to — 12 in, after its choice's icon where it wears one, §578, to
its chevron's room — and `TipOf`); a screen reader reads it whole as before (its status).

`PanelRows.PopupOf`: the rows a control's popup shows (a button's level, the row's own level, §529 a row of more segments
than fit), the dock's and the tests' one place.

Tests: `DropdownWidthTests` — `ADropdownsListIsItsBoxsWidthWhateverItsChoicesSay` (a list of a long choice its box's width,
the choice cut and whole in its tooltip; refreshed for short ones, again for long ones, opened afresh: always 240; failed
before, 869 px for 360), `EveryPopupOfThePanelIsOneWidth` (every popup of every page of the corpus, every expander open, as
the dock finds it: 240, a search's 360; failed before: 107 of 404), `ASearchsPopupIsItsOwnFixedWidth` (a time zone's, as
letters are typed), `ADropdownsValueCutShortInItsBoxIsWholeInItsTooltip`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR):
`SceneTreeTests.DropdownWidthSheets` — dropdown-long-closed-, dropdown-long-open-, dropdown-short-open-dark|light.png (a colour
filters widget's Filter set to "Red-green (green weak, deuteranopia)", cut in its box and in its list, then to "Inverted" and
opened again: the same width).

By hand: edit mode › a colour filters widget › Filter: the list as wide as its box, the long choices cut, a tooltip on the box
saying it whole; a clock's Time zone: 360 wide, typing "zur" does not change it; any weather's Place: type a name, its finds
come, its width stays.

## 583. The Appearance's sections page sections, nothing folded; a palette holding the person's edits marked "Changed" (2026-11-09) — no sections, one preview over four tabs, since §592 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"in the style dropdown show if a style has custom user configuration inside it."*; *"the
appearance settings should not actually have expansion sections, they should have normal sections"*.

**Replaces** §577's two sections as expanders (Taskbar and Folders and flyouts each a level, a card shut until opened, its
preview at its top inside it) and its parts as groups a head folds (open unless shut). §577 stays for the rest: the palette
worn, each keeping its own values, a designed one's reset, the two sections and their parts, one preview a section.

**Page sections** (`LookRows.Rows`). Under Palette and Reset to default the page is two sections as the Karpo, Display and
Taskbar pages have theirs: each **a heading** (`OptionRowKind.Heading`, keyed `Appearance.section.taskbar|folders` as before,
its look in `Shows`), **its one preview right under it** (`PanelRows.Of` puts a heading's preview under it, §551's one way,
now the Appearance's too: "Appearance/Taskbar/#preview"), then **each part a card always open** — its name and icon at its
head (Semibold, as a group's), its editor's rows in it, no chevron, nothing to press. Nothing on the page folds and nothing
needs opening: a link, a search or a landing finds every row where it stands.

|---|---|
| Taskbar | its preview (the Bar sample); Bar's card; Taskbar widgets' card |
| Folders and flyouts | its preview (the Open sample); Flyouts' card; Widgets in folders' card |

a page's rows, a part ending at the next heading or preview; `PanelRow.Folds`: a group with rows and not fixed). A fixed
group stands open whatever the memory holds (`PanelLayout.Opens`); its head has no control (no Head hit, so nothing lights,
nothing takes the keys, a click on it does nothing), no chevron and no chevron's room; to a screen reader it is a group's
heading (level 2) over its rows, nothing to expand, not focusable (`DeckUia`, its rect its line's; `EditDeck.Act` does
nothing on it). Keys: a part's rows `Appearance/~Taskbar widgets/Font` (§577's place of its rows, the section's level gone
from it), its card `Appearance/~Taskbar widgets`.

**Gone with the expanders**: an expander's preview at its top (`PanelRows.One`'s `Shows` branch: no level shows a look now —
the taskbar menu's and the Appearance's are headings'), `OptionMenu`'s `Shows` on a level, `LookSections.Glyph` (a page
heading has no icon), the ruled-off line between the reset and the sections. `OptionRow.Shows` / `FlyoutItem.Shows` are a
heading's alone.

**"Changed"** (`OptionRow.ChoiceMarks`, the Palette row's: `LookPalettes.Changed` of each palette). A palette whose values
draw it otherwise than designed in either mode is marked: in Palette's list its word "Changed" at its row's end (a choice's
`FlyoutItem.Value`, said quieter as a value is, before its tick), and, the palette worn, in the row's box after its name in
the secondary text colour (`PanelRow.ValueMark`, the chosen choice's mark; the name's room shrinks for it, the mark at most
half the box), and to a screen reader the box's status "Graphite, Changed". Custom is marked once its values change Karpo's
own (its design), so not while it holds none; a value said that is the design's own changes nothing and marks nothing (as
§577's reset is greyed then); the reset takes the mark away; a palette not worn keeps its mark. New string
`settings.look.changed` ("Changed") in every language, agreeing with "palette" where a language marks gender (fr
"Modifiée", it "Modificata", pl "Zmieniona", pt-BR "Alterada", ro "Modificată", ru "Изменена"; es "Con cambios").

No config change (shape 75).

shows a look stands over its preview), `LayoutMenuTests`, `BarBlurSettingTests`, `BarGroundTests`, `PopupPlaceTests`,
`SettingsPanelTests`, the Localization tests. UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `SceneTreeTests.AppearancePaletteSheets`
(appearance-palette-<dark|light>.png, the whole page, Graphite worn and changed, "Changed" in its box;
appearance-palette-list-<dark|light>.png, Palette's list open, Graphite and Paper marked), `AppearanceSectionsSheets`
(appearance-sections-<dark|light>.png, the whole page, nothing folds), `AppearancePairSheets`; the stage tests that opened
