## 586. The add page counts what the layout has; keep awake keeps the screen on too (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"in the add widgets menu show how many widgets from which type are already placed and also sum this
up over the sections itself. that way the user is able to see immediately what he has"*; *"i used keep awake last time and it
did not work i believe, the screen still went dark after a certain time. keep awake should also keep the screen awake"*.

### The add page's counts

    Battery and power                                   4  ⌄
    [⚡ Energy saver on/off ] [☕ Keep awake on/off   2] [▭ Volume              1]

- **A tile its widget's count**, at its end: the number in Caption, TextFillColorSecondary (TextFillColorDisabled greyed), as an
  expander's value is drawn (§544), 12 in from the tile's end; the name cut short 8 before it (`PanelLayout.PlacedWide`,
  `NameRoom`). A widget Popular or Quick settings shows again says the same as its home.
- **A folder of the tree the sum of its widgets**, each kind once however often the folder shows it, at its head's end while
  shut — an expander's value, its one rule (§544: shut, what it holds; open, its tiles say it). Popular and Browse, the two
  section headings, say nothing: Browse's would be every widget of the layout, Popular's a sum of things shown again.
- **None, nothing.** No "0", no dimmed number: a tile that says nothing has none on the layout — the page stays as calm as it
  was for a person who has placed little.
- **What a number is**: its tooltip and its screen reader's status, "On this layout: 2" (`dock.add.placed`, the one new key, in
  all 30 languages; `PanelLayout.TipOf` for a tile's `Act` and a folder's `Head`, `DeckUia`'s `Status`).
- **The words typed** list the matches as tiles with their counts too (`AddList.Results` keeps them).

**What is counted, decided: the layout the page adds into** — its bar and every folder on it (`Folders.All`) — not the whole
file. The page adds into one layout, the one its display shows (`Dock.AddOf`: `config.IslandsFor(window.Screen.Id)`); a clock
of a layout no display shows, or of another display's, is no clock the person sees there, and counting it would say "2" beside
a bar holding one. A widget is counted by its kind (`WidgetInfo.Id`, the file's word, which every catalogue row's id is),
wherever it stands: a keep awake on the bar and one as a folder's line are two keep awakes, on the bar's page and on a
folder's.

**Not counted: a premade widget's tile and a ready-made folder's.** The file keeps no trace of what a widget or a folder was
made from — a "Clock actions" placed is an Actions widget with two slots set, a Quick panel a folder — so neither tile can
know; the widget's own tile counts it (Actions says 1). A folder of the tree sums neither.

**Where** (one place, pure): `AddCounts` (Karpo.Core\AddCounts.cs) — `Placed(islands)`, a layout's kinds counted; `Of(row,
placed)`, a tile's or a folder's number. `AddList.Rows(…, placed)` sets `FlyoutItem.Placed` on each row; `PanelRows.Picks`
makes it the tile's and the folder's `PanelRow.Value`; `PanelPainter.Control` draws a tile's. No config change.

### Keep awake keeps the screen on, always

**Why it did not work.** §269 kept the screen on only where the widget's "Keep the screen on" (`SwitchOptions.AwakeScreen`)
said so — off unless chosen — and two ways on never read it at all: a toggles row's toggle (`KeepAwakeSwitch.Act()`, no
options) and a length picked from the menu at rest while off with no widget at hand. So the power request held
`PowerRequestSystemRequired` alone: the PC was kept from sleeping while Windows' display timeout darkened its screen, which is
what the person saw. (On a PC with Modern Standby a dark screen is the standby itself, so there it would not have kept the PC
awake either; this PC sleeps in S3.) The request's own life was sound: it belongs to a handle, not a thread, is held by the
switch the dock's `SwitchData` keeps from its start, and is let go only when turned off, at its time's end, when the config
loses the last widget for it, or with Karpo — nothing let it go behind the person's back.

**Now one request, both parts, always** (`PowerRequest.Hold()`): `PowerCreateRequest` with Karpo's reason once, then
`PowerRequestSystemRequired` and `PowerRequestDisplayRequired`; held again it asks nothing; a part Windows refuses lets the
whole go (cleared, its handle closed) and keep awake stays off saying so — never the PC kept awake behind a dark screen.
`powercfg /requests` lists Karpo.exe under DISPLAY and SYSTEM with "Keep awake is on in Karpo" whenever it is on.

**Deleted**: "Keep the screen on" — its edit-mode row (`OptionRows.AwakeScreen`), its row in the menu at rest
(`WidgetAct.AwakeScreen`, `MenuKeeps`), `KeepAwake.Screen` and `KeepScreen`, `Turn`'s `keepScreen`, `IAwakeRequest.Hold`'s
`screen`, `SwitchIsland.Options`, and the keys `dock.quick.keepAwake.screen` and `.screenNote` in every language;
`dock.quick.keepAwake.note` now says the screen ("Keeps this PC from going to sleep by itself, and its screen on.", the
screen note's words in each language). The menu at rest is the lengths, a rule, Power & battery settings.

**Windows' four calls behind a seam** (`IPowerCalls`: create, set, clear, close; `WindowsPower` the real ones), so the tests
run the request's whole life on calls of their own and no test sets a real power request any more — §269's
`TheRealRequestIsLetGo`, which held one for a few milliseconds, is gone.

**The file**: shape **76** (ConfigWords.txt written again; no migration). `"awakeScreen"` is gone from a widget's `"switch"`;
a file of shape 75 is converted by deleting every `"awakeScreen"` member and setting `"version": 76` — nothing else changes,
and the screen is kept on whatever it said.

Tests: `AddCountsTests` — `TheLayoutsWidgetsAreCountedByKindOnTheBarAndInItsFolders`, `ATileCountsItsKindAndAFolderSumsItsKindsOnce`
(Again the same; a premade and a preset nothing; a folder's kinds once), `TheAddPageSaysTheCountsOnItsTilesAndFolders` (the
rows' `Placed`, each folder its tree's sum, the tiles' and heads' values, the search's tiles, nothing without counts).
`KeepAwakeTests` — `EveryWayOnKeepsTheScreenOnToo` (the regression: a click with options or none, a length from the menu),
`TheRequestIsMadeOnceAndLetGoWhole`, `APartRefusedLetsTheWholeRequestGo`, `TheMenuAtRestOffersTheLengths`, `EditModeSetsHowLong`,
the rest on the new seam; `WidgetMenuTests`, `MenuKeepsTests`, `OptionRowsTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests` follow. Pictures
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets`): panel-add-counts-, panel-add-counts-open- (a counted layout,
`SceneTreeTests.Counted`: Start, Search, Task view, the apps, the tray, the volume, Wi-Fi, keep awake twice, a folder of two
clocks and the weather), dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › Add: a tile of a widget on the bar says how many, a shut folder its sum, nothing where none; hover one:
"On this layout: 2"; add one more and open Add again: one more. Keep awake: click it, run `powercfg /requests` in an
elevated prompt — Karpo.exe under DISPLAY and under SYSTEM, "Keep awake is on in Karpo"; leave the PC past its screen timeout:
the screen stays on; click it again: nothing of Karpo's listed. From a toggles row's toggle and from a length in its menu: the
same.

## 585. Displays and layouts one page, every display an expander in Windows' one order, this one marked; the taskbar menu an expander of Behavior (2026-11-09) — the page called Layouts since §624 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"merge display settings together with layout settings"*; *"the displays should actually be ordered
the same way everywhere but the one that is the one on which the flyout is shown should be highlighted or marked."*; *"the
displays should get the expansion section for their settings too."*; *"taskbar menu should only get an expansion section with
the configuration inside there but not a full own section"*.

**One page, Displays and layouts** (`PanelPage.Layouts`, `LooksScope.Layouts`, `BarLooks.LayoutsRows`). The edit bar is Karpo,
Accounts, **Displays and layouts**, Taskbar, Appearance (§575's Display and Layouts, two entries, one now; the monitor its
icon). The name says both halves of what it holds, in the order it holds them — a person comes to it first to set what a
display shows, and the layouts are what a display shows —; "Layouts" alone would hide where a bar's position and a display's
None went, "Displays" alone the layouts. The one entry is narrower than the two were, so the bar narrows too. Two sections:

    Displays
      🖥 Two                                   ⌄       Windows' order: the primary first, then left to right
      🖥 One  This display                     ⌄       the display the flyout is shown on, marked, not moved
          Layout     [ Default ⌄ ]
          Position   [ Bottom ⌄ ]
    Layouts
      Default layout  Shown on new displays   [ Work ⌄ ]
      ⠿ ▦ Default  This display              ⧉ 🗑 ⌄
      ⠿ ▦ Work  Default layout               ⧉ 🗑 ⌄
      + Add a layout ⌄

- **One order everywhere** (`BarLooks.DisplaysOf`): every display connected, each once, in `BarSpot.Connected`'s order —
  `Monitors.List`', the order the dock arranges displays in (the primary first, then left to right, then top to
  bottom) —, the same list whichever display's flyout shows it. §579 put the flyout's own first: undone. A display Windows has
  not listed (a page of one display, a test's) stands first.
- **This one marked**: "This display" under its name (`OptionThing.Summary`), as the layout it shows is marked "This display"
  in the Layouts section (§521) — the one mark for the one thing.
- **Each display an expander** (`BarLooks.DisplayThing`): one of the page's things (`OptionOwned` with no Add, `Inline`, as the
  layouts are), its name and the monitor, its own rows in it — Layout (§521's dropdown of the layouts and None) and Position
  (§348). No handle, no Delete, no rename: the displays are Windows', not the person's to order. Its rows keep §579's keys
  (`LayoutShown:<id>`, `BarPosition:<id>`), so a pick sets that display alone as before; two displays of one name are two
  expanders (the panel keys the second "… #2", §532).
- **Under Layouts** what §579 had on the Layouts page: the Default layout first, then the layouts, Add a layout.
- The headings, Displays (`settings.sections.displays`, new) and Layouts, are the page's two (R17 in `MenuRulesTests`).

**The taskbar menu an expander** (`KarpoMenu.BarMenu`). §553 made it the Taskbar page's last section under its own heading; it
is one expander now, **Behavior's last row** — what a right click on the bar does is how the bar behaves — "Taskbar menu"
with "The same on every layout" under its name (§553's heading caption, now the row's line), the menu icon (Segoe Fluent
Icons' GlobalNavigationButton, `OptionGlyphs.Menu`: the bar's own Taskbar icon is Type's, R13). In it, as before: §551's
preview of the menu at its top, the entries dragged into order, Add an entry, Reset to default — §578's buttons alone, each in
its line where the rows' names start, as a foot in an expander is. The row is a `Things` row no longer `Inline`; the menus
(`OptionMenu.Rows`) now carry a things row's `Detail` and `Shows` onto its item, as a level's already did, so the panel's
expander has its line and its preview (`PanelRows.One`: an expander that shows a look has its preview first). The search finds
an entry under it: *"Taskbar › Behavior › Taskbar menu › Notes"*. Its entries were not changed here.

**Deleted**: `PanelPage.Display`, `LooksScope.Display`, `BarLooks.DisplayRows`, `DisplayHeading` (each display's heading),
`DisplayLinkRow` and `OptionLink.Display` (§411's "Display ↗", which no row made since §520), `EditEntry.DisplaySettings`,
`KarpoMenu.BarMenuSection` and `BarMenuHeading`; `dock.edit.display` in every language (its words were the Display entry's and
the link's). New in all thirty: `dock.edit.displaysAndLayouts` ("Displays and layouts"), `settings.sections.displays`
("Displays").

**The file:** no change, shape 75: nothing of the page was ever kept.

Tests: `BarLooksTests` (`TheDisplaysAreInOneOrderEverywhereThisOneMarked`: Windows' order from every display, the mark on the
one shown on, never moved, one not listed first, each an expander of its Layout and Position with nothing to delete or move,
another display's set alone, two of one name keyed apart, the page's two headings; `TheBarsRowsAreCutThreeWays`; the layouts
and the Default layout under Layouts), `SettingsPanelTests.DisplaysAndLayoutsAreOnePage` (the entry's words and icon, the
page's rows, kinds and keys, a landing opening a display's expander), `SettingsPanelTests.ARowThatOnlyActsIsItsButtonAlone`
(Add a layout on the page; Add an entry and Reset to default in the expander), `BarMenuPanelTests.TheTaskbarMenuIsAnExpanderOfBehavior`
(no section, Behavior's last row, its line, its preview first, Reset last) and the rest of the file on the expander's rows,
`KarpoMenuGeneralTests` (Behavior ends with it), `LayoutMenuTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (R17: Displays, Layouts; Bar, Behavior),
`ConfigCoverageTests`, `EditEntriesTests`, `PanelReorderTests`, `EditDeckClickTests` (five entries; the tree's names),
`PanelControlsTests`, `PanelPopupToggleTests`, `PanelReorderStageTests` (the expander opened by its head before the drag).
Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.PagesSheets` — pages-displays- (two displays, Two first, One
marked; the layouts), pages-display-open- (Two's expander open), pages-taskbar-menu- (the Taskbar page, the expander open),
dark and light; `SettingsPanelSheets` panel-display-, panel-barmenu-*.

By hand: two displays; edit mode on the second (not the primary): Displays and layouts lists the primary first, then this one
with "This display" under it; on the primary the same order, the mark on the primary. Open the other display's expander, set
its Layout: its bar changes, this one's not. Taskbar: Behavior's last row Taskbar menu, closed; opened: the preview, the
entries, Add an entry, Reset to default.

## 584. Nothing in the edit bar's slot with nothing selected; every entry's flyout 12 DIP off the bar, its beak pointing at its entry (2026-11-09) — no slot, the room kept for the selection's entries, since §596 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"there should not be a placeholder shown "Widget" in the topbar"*, *"the topbar flyouts should
have a little distance to the topbar and also an angle that points to the button"*.

**The selection's slot empty** (`SettingsPanel.Paint.cs`'s `Bar`). §578's empty state — Segoe Fluent Icons' SelectAll and
"Widget" in TextFillColorDisabled — is gone: with no widget selected and no folder open or selected nothing is drawn in the
slot. Its 192 DIP stay kept (`PanelLayout.Selection`), so the bar is still one width whatever is selected (§578, the person
asked for that too); nothing there was pressed, a stop of the keys nor a screen reader's element before, and nothing is now.
Deleted: `PanelLayout.NothingSelected`, `PanelGlyphs.Selection`. "dock.menu.widget" stays: a widget's own entry and its
menus still say it.

**A gap from the bar** (`EditDeck.HungFrom`, `Beak.GapDip`). An entry's flyout hung from the entry itself (32 DIP tall,
8 in from the bar's 48), 4 DIP under it: it stood 4 DIP over the bar. It hangs from the entry's column across the whole bar
now — the entry's sides, the bar's top and foot — 12 DIP off the bar's edge, as Windows 11's flyouts stand 12 off the
taskbar; over the bar from an edit bar at the display's foot alike. The add page a "+" hangs keeps its "+" as what it hangs
from, 12 off it.

**A beak** (`Beak`, FlyoutHost.cs; `FlyoutPlacement.Beak`, which was §578's `Centred`). A popup placed with it — an edit bar
entry's flyout, the add page of a "+" (`Dock.EditDeck.Open`, the one place) — wears a triangle of its own outline out of the
side facing what it hangs from: 8 DIP out, its sides at 45° (16 across its foot; WinUI's TeachingTip's tail), in the gap,
4 DIP of air left before the bar. Its tip stands over the middle of what it hangs from (`Beak.TipAt`): in the panel's middle
where the panel is centred on it, and where the panel was pushed in at the work area's side, along it to stay over the entry
— never nearer an end than the corner's 8 and its half foot, so its foot stays on the straight of the side. Out of the top
from an edit bar at the top, out of the foot (pointing down) from one at the foot: the side follows the side PopupPlace took
(`Beak.Triangle`).

- **One outline, in the shared chrome** (`FlyoutHost.PlacePanels`, `Beaked`; `CutPath.Beaked`). The panel's rounded
  rectangle and the beak are one Direct2D path (clockwise; the corners its arcs), handed to composition through §464's
  geometry source. The plate is clipped to it, so the beak is the panel's material (acrylic or solid, the same tint); the rim
  strokes it (its line's middle half a rim in, the tip √2 as far), so one rim runs round both; the shadow's caster is cut to it,
  so the beak casts as the panel does, cut on the bar's side by as much as its shadow would spill past the room there (the beak
  stands that much nearer). The plate, the rim and the caster reach over the beak; the content's clip, the panel's hit tests
  and its size are the panel's, as before. Paths are made once per size, beak and rim (`PanelChrome.BeakMadeFor`), never set
  to null (§476); where Direct2D makes none the panel keeps its rounded rectangle. A folder's pieces and every other popup are
  as they were: only a placement with `Beak` has one.
- **Pictures** (`EditPlacePictures.EditedDisplay`): the flyout's window is cut out with its beak and laid over the dim by its
  alpha, its rounded corners and the beak's sides on the dim rather than on black.

Tests: `PopupPlaceTests.TheBeaksTipIsOverItsEntrysMiddle` (centred; pushed in at either side of the work area, still over
the entry; kept off the corners; a narrow panel's middle), `TheBeakPointsUpFromTheTopAndDownFromTheFoot` (its points in the
outline's order, flipped on the foot, inset by a rim at 45°); `SettingsPanelTests.AFlyoutHangsFromItsEntry` (from the entry's
column across the bar, 12 DIP off the bar's edge, centred, the tip over the entry and 4 DIP short of the bar, up and down),
`TheBarIsOneWidthWhateverIsSelected` (nothing in the slot, the width unchanged); `EditDeckClickTests.AnEntryOpensItsFlyoutAnotherSwitchesItItselfClosesIt`
(the real windows: 12 DIP under the bar, the beak out of the top over the entry); `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` (every
flyout's beak over its entry, out of the foot from an edit bar at the foot; panel-edge-: a display 1280 DIP wide, the Karpo
flyout pushed in at its left, its beak still over Karpo); the stage's probe `PanelPopupPlaceTests.TheAddListOpensUnderTheAddButton…`
(Add's flyout 12 DIP off the edit bar, centred on Add). `PanelPopupPlaceTests.ADropdownOpensUnderItsControl` and
`…WithThePanelOpeningUp` fail as they did before this change ("no dropdown in sight" on the scrolled Karpo page): left to the
pages' rework.

By hand: edit mode — the bar, nothing in the slot right of Appearance, the bar as wide as with a widget selected; Appearance:
its flyout 12 DIP under the bar, a beak up to the entry's middle, the same material and rim round both, its shadow under the
beak too; Karpo on a narrow display: the flyout against the display's left, the beak over Karpo; the taskbar at the top (the
edit bar at the foot): the flyout over the bar, its beak pointing down; a bar's "+": the add page under it, its beak at it.

## 589. Add a face closes on its face; a side bar's alignment reads Top, Center, Bottom; Spacing a number of pixels (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when adding a face the add face dropdown does not close after adding"*; *"when the taskbar is
shown on a side the alignment options dont read correctly anymore, left right and center dont make sense anymore in that
context"*; *"spacing should be a pixel value that i can change not just the three states"*.

**Add a face closes.** Why it stayed: a popup of the panel (§520) closed on `Dock.ChoiceMade`, which asked the pick's
kind — a `Set`, or a `Field` with a find (§554) — a second rule beside the flyout's own for a level of one choice (§392,
§411 R5: a ticked row, or a row with no control on a level with no ticks, an Add's). Add a face's faces are `AddFace`
picks and Add a toggle's toggles `Flip`s, so neither kind closed it; the menus went back as they should, the panel's
popup stayed. Now there is one rule: the flyout says whether the pick it heard last was the one choice of its level
(`Flyout.OneChoice`, `TakeChoseOne`: on any level, the popup's own rows too; a search's find and a line's suggestion
picked are one), and the dock closes the popup on that (`Dock.PanelDropped`). `ChoiceMade` is gone. Every "add"
dropdown — Add a face, Add a toggle, Add a country (§554) — closes on its pick; a switch, a stepper, words typed keep it.

**Along a side bar.** A folder's Alignment (§385) on a bar on a display's left or right edge says **Automatic, Top,
Center, Bottom** — in its row, its dropdown, a menu, the screen reader's names — where it said Left, Center, Right. The
value is the same (`FolderAlign.Left` is the work area's start, a side bar's top; §385 said so), so nothing in the file
changes and a layout moved from the bottom to the left keeps its folders where they were. The words are the edges'
(`core.edge.top`, `core.edge.bottom`, in every language already); no new string. Which bar: the one the widget stands on
(`OptionPlace.Side`, set by `Dock.PickerPlace` from its display's bar, `Layout.Vertical`). **The glyphs**: Segoe Fluent
Icons has no top, middle and bottom (none of its glyphs is Word's three turned, checked against every glyph's outline),
so Word's three are drawn a quarter turn clockwise — Left's lines hang from the top, Right's stand on the bottom
(`OptionGlyphs.AlignTop`, `AlignMiddle`, `AlignBottom` = `Turned(…)`: the glyph and a word joiner, which draws as nothing
anywhere that does not ask). The two places glyphs are drawn turn it about its middle (`PopupPaint.Centred`, the panel's;
`Gfx.RedrawGlyph`, the menus'), `Mirror.Quarter` on top of the transform in force.

**Spacing a number.** §533's three words are gone: `TaskbarLayout.Spacing` is an `int`, the room between two widgets in
**DIPs** — as `Size` is, so it is the same room at every display scale and scales with the bar's icon as §533's gaps did
(`U`, never under a third of itself) — from **0 to 24** (`Config.LeastSpacing`, `MostSpacing`; 24 half Windows' 48-DIP
bar), **6** where nobody chose (`Config.DefaultSpacing`, §515's gap), always written (`"spacing": 6`; a file without it
reads 6). The Taskbar page's Spacing, after Size, is the panel's number box (− value +, a pixel a step, a number typed
too), said in px as Size is (Windows' Settings says DIPs as px). **0** is §533's None: the widgets touch, an islands bar
flush (`Layout.FlushFor`). New: a spacing wider than the room between two sections (14 DIP) widens that too, so two
sections never stand closer than two widgets. A number past the range in a hand-edited file is held to it (`Repair`, as
a size is). Gone: `WidgetSpacing`, `BarLooks.Spacings`, `SpacingName`, `Layout.WidgetGapDips`, the "None", "Small" and
"Large" strings in every language.

**The file: shape 77.** Converted by hand, each layout's `"spacing"`: `"none"` → `0`; `"small"`, or none at all → `6`
(or left out); `"large"` → `12`; and `"version"` 77. Not converted, a word where a number belongs does not read.

Tests: `OneChoiceTests.AnAddsRowIsOneChoiceOfItsList` (every face of Add a face, every toggle of Add a toggle, a ticked
choice; not a Find field, a switch, a stepper), `AFacePickedInAddAFacesPopupIsAChoiceMade` (UI: a real flyout of the
popup's rows, a face clicked a choice taken once, a switch none); `HolidaysPanelTests` (ChoiceMade's test gone; the
search's close is `HolidaysPanelUiTests`'). `FolderAlignTests.OnASideBarItsAlignmentReadsTopCenterBottom` (names, turned
glyphs, the same values; the quarter turn's matrix). `WidgetSpacingTests` (rewritten: gaps of 0, 3, 6, 12, 20 and 24 at
28 to 80 DIP and 100 and 150 %; the section gap never under the widget gap; only 0 flush; the pointer, a drop and the Add
line in the gap; app buttons; absent is 6; written and read back; held to the range; the Taskbar page's number row and
the panel's number box), `FlushBarPlates`, `BarHitsWhereItDrawsTests`, `BarFormTests`, `ConfigSchemaTests`
(ConfigWords.txt at shape 77). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.SideAlignmentAndSpacingSheets`
align-side-<dark|light>.png (a left bar, a folder's page, Alignment's dropdown open: Automatic, Top, Center, Bottom),
spacing-number-<dark|light>.png (the Taskbar page, Spacing − 6 px +); `BarSpacingSheets`
bar-spacing-<0|6|12|20>-<32|48>-<dark|light>.png.

By hand: a folder selected, Add a face, a face: the list closes, the face added. Display › the bar on the left; the
folder's Alignment: Top, Center, Bottom, their lines standing. Taskbar › Spacing: + and − a pixel at a time, 0 the widgets
touching.

## 588. Every setting at first sight: no level to open on a widget's page or the Karpo page, no group of one setting, no well (2026-11-09) — its levels back, but for the third level, the tray's icons and the folder's Alignment, since §594 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the tray icons have two levels in their configuration so you have to actually expand to
configure. generally speaking i want all the settings visible on the first go."* — *"i dont like that the public holidays
region configurations have a different (darker) background"* — *"the folder configuration has too many levels that are
actually not needed, (e.g. the alignment is burried two levels deep although it is the only configuration there.)"*

**The rule.** A setting is seen as its page opens: no click deeper than the page to reach it, and no head over a single
setting. What stays a level of its own is a list of the person's things, each an entry (a layout, an account, a folder's
face, a holiday calendar with a region), and a form that adds one.

**A widget's page** (`PanelGroups.Grouped`). Each level of the widget's menu — the tray's icons, the status icons, Show
from, a timer's or focus's Length, an alarm's Time and Repeat on — is a group of its own after What it shows, open, its
head the level's name and icon, its sentence what the level said at its end ("2 shown", "All", "5 min", "07:00",
"Never"), its rows the level's and those nested under it (Show from's accounts' line). Before, a level was an expander
inside What it shows, shut. Its item is the level's still (`OptionRows.GroupKey`: a mixed group's split, the search, a
landing), its key a group's (`PanelGroups.KeyOf`), its rows keyed as they were, so a popup, the search and a link find
them. Menus keep their levels: a widget's right click in edit mode is a menu, which can't show everything; only the
panel lays them open. **A group of one setting is that setting alone**, a card of its own on the page (§529 put every row
in a group): a line's Size, a switch's Show name, a month's Style, a weather's Place, a pen's Show. A group of two or more
stays a group with its sentence (What it shows, Height with its Max rows).

**A folder's page** (`PanelGroups.FolderPage`). Under the heading Folder its panel's rows stand straight, each a card:
Alignment is one card under Folder (§529's group When it opens, which held it alone, is gone, and its string with it).
Each face stays a group of its own under Faces (§552), its Remove at its head.

**One of the person's things with settings of its own is a group** (`PanelRows.One`, its `Nests` case). §552 made a
folder's face a group on the folder's page alone (`PanelGroups.FaceOf`); the panel reads every such thing so now —
its head its name, icon and buttons (§551 its handle where it moves), its settings its rows, keyed as they were, its group
key its row's marked (`Folder/~Clock`). `FaceOf` is gone; a holiday calendar with a region is the same.

**No third level** (`PanelLayout.Inside`, `PanelLine`). A row nested under a choice (§529: an agenda's Days ahead under
Style, a line's Max rows under Height, a clock's Show seconds, the accounts' line under Show from) and a mixed row's
widgets' own rows opened under it are rows of the card as any: right after their choice, their name where every row's
name is, ruled off by the card's divider. §529 to §564 they stood a step (24 DIP) in, §565 on a darker well — the person
saw it as a different background, and with the levels laid open there is no level for it to tell. The nesting itself
stays (`PanelRows.Nest`): a row still stands right after the choice it follows, wherever the menu had it.

**The Karpo page** (`KarpoMenu.Rows`). §517's levels are sections of the page, each its heading, its rows on the page:
General (Start with Windows, Animations, Language, Quit Karpo — Quit General's last still, §545), Formats, Public holidays,
Online, Karpo Pro, Back up and reset, About Karpo (§579). The headings Services and Karpo held nothing but those levels
and went with them (`ServicesHeading`, `KarpoHeading`, and the string "Services"). The rows lost their `OptionRow.Group`
(Formats, Online, Karpo Pro, Back up and reset); what a level said at its end ("Default (Windows' own)", "15 min", "Free
version") is what its rows say. **Public holidays**: the calendars on the page itself (`OptionRow.Inline`, as the layouts
are on theirs), a calendar with a region a card of its own — its name, its colour button and Remove at its head, its
Region a dropdown in it, no darker well —, one without a card of its buttons, Add a country a button under them. To a
screen reader a row of a thing's card is named for it as before ("Region · Switzerland", `DeckUia`: the card's head now,
not the line a step out). "Get Karpo Pro" lands on the licence's row of its section, as before; "Public holidays" on Add a
country (`EditEntries.Landing`: `OptionHolidays.Calendars` was the level's row); a landing at a section's heading scrolls
to it (`EditDeck.Land`: a heading is a block, no line).

**Kept, and why.** Each layout (the Layouts page) and each display (another change of today): the person's entries,
asked for as expanders. The Taskbar page's Taskbar menu (another change of today). An account on the Accounts page: an
entry of the person's, its calendars and mail its rows. Add a mail account and Add a CalDAV account: forms that add an
account, not settings; shut, the page is the accounts. The Appearance page's sections (another change of today). A
folder of the add page (§575): a browse of the catalogue. A mixed value's "each one's" (§529): a chevron that opens each
widget's own value, on demand by its nature. A group's head can still be shut (§529), each open as the page opens.

**Rules** (MenuRulesTests). R13 and R11 read a page's sections each as a level of its own (`Sections`): an icon may stand
once in each section (Formats' Reset all and Back up's Reset all settings, Online's Weather and About's Open-Meteo), Reset
all last in its section, Back up and reset's resets their own names as before. R17's Karpo page order is General, Formats,
Public holidays, Online, Karpo Pro, Back up and reset, About Karpo.

**Deleted:** the well (`PanelLayout.NestedRuns`, `WellOf`, `PanelPainter.Wells`), the step in (`PanelMetrics.Nest`,
`PanelLine.Indent`), `PanelGroups.FaceOf`, `KarpoMenu.ServicesHeading` and `KarpoHeading`, Backup's `GlyphRestore`, the
strings `dock.panel.group.opens` and `settings.sections.services` in every language. No config change (Config.Shape 76 as
it was): the page only lays its rows out.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests` (`ANestedRowIsAPlainRowOfItsChoicesCardRightAfterIt`; Show from a group of its own, its sentence;
every kind's page: no expander, no group of one but a face's, every row of its menu on the page by its key or its level's
group; a folder's Alignment under Folder; each face's group the panel's own; a mixed value's own rows right after it),
`HolidaysPanelTests` (Switzerland a card, its Region in it as far in as its head's name, France a card of its buttons, the

(`EachLandingIsARowOfItsPage`), `MenuRulesTests`. UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `HolidaysPanelUiTests`, `PanelPopupPlaceTests`
(the holidays' and the formats' rows on the page, nothing opened). Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.FlatPageSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR):

## 591. Windows' taskbar waits at the bottom while Karpo runs and comes back on Karpo's edge; Start no longer a taskbar too high (2026-11-09) — no move on quit since §600 (2026-11-09); Start's rule superseded by §666 (2026-11-12)

The person: *"the windows taskbar is still not shown where the karpo bar is shown"*; *"the start menu is also too high up as
if there was an invisible taskbar at the bottom (when the taskbar is shown left or right)"*. Since Experimental build
26300.8493 (2026-05-15) Windows 11's taskbar stands on any edge (Settings › Personalization › Taskbar › Taskbar
behaviors), one edge for every display; §540 and §580 were written as if it had none but the bottom.

**How this Windows keeps and applies it** (26300.9711, read from its own files, read-only; nothing set or restarted):

- The setting is Settings' `SystemSettings_DesktopTaskbar_Lo`, registered under
  `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemSettings\SettingId` (type List) with its handler, `SettingsHandlers_DesktopTaskbar.dll`.
- The value: `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced`, `TaskbarLocation`, a DWORD of ABE_*'s
  numbers — 0 left, 1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom; none is the bottom (the user's PC has none: bottom). Explorer's `Taskbar.dll`
  reads it beside `TaskbarAl` and `TaskbarSize`. StuckRects3's edge byte (still 3) is not it.
- Applied live by the handler's setter (read from its code): it writes that value, then
  `SendMessageW(FindWindow("Shell_TrayWnd"), WM_USER + 0x1CA, 6, value)` — a private message to Explorer's taskbar, the
  setting's number and its value; no broadcast, no Explorer restart. (While Karpo runs, `FindWindow` finds Karpo's tray
  window first, which passes private taskbar messages on to Explorer's.)
- The policy `DisableTaskbarPosition` (`Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer`, machine or user; Taskbar.admx: *"the
  taskbar is moved to the bottom of the screen and the taskbar position setting is grayed out"*).
- **Auto-hide works only at the bottom.** Microsoft's notes for 26300.8493: *"Auto-hidden taskbar and touch optimized
  taskbar are not yet supported"* in the other positions, said again for 26300.9032 (2026-07-31); Settings: *"This setting
  is only available when the taskbar is at the bottom"*; reports through October (26300.9711): it stays in sight there,
  the switch on or not.

Sources: Microsoft Learn, *Experimental Preview Build 26300.8493* release notes; Windows Insider Blog, *Improving Windows
quality: Making Taskbar and Start more personal* (2026-05-15) and *Announcing new builds for 31 July 2026*;
`C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions\Taskbar.admx`; the strings and code of `SettingsHandlers_DesktopTaskbar.dll` and `Taskbar.dll`.

**Why not on Karpo's edge while Karpo runs**, as asked first. Karpo hides Explorer's taskbar by auto-hiding it (§465): a
taskbar that can't auto-hide holds its strip of the screen however hidden its windows are (`Taskbar.HoldsStrip`), and the
shell puts every appbar on its edge beside it — the bar on the left would stand beside an empty 72 px strip, and on every
other display Explorer's taskbar would hold the same edge too. So while Karpo runs Windows' taskbar stands at the bottom,
auto-hidden, and goes to Karpo's edge as Karpo lets go of it (not since §600: it stays at the bottom). Should Windows auto-hide it elsewhere one day,
`TaskbarPosition.Parked` is the one thing to change.

**Now** (`TaskbarPosition`, `Taskbar`, Karpo.Dock):

- **The takeover** (`Taskbar.TakeOver`): Windows' taskbar moved to the bottom (where it stands elsewhere), then auto-hidden.
  The trace: *"took over from Explorer's taskbar in N ms; Windows' taskbar moved to the bottom"*.
- **Every put-back** (`Taskbar.PutBack`: a quit, the session ending, an exception, the guard): auto-hide off, then shown.
  *Until §600 it was also moved to the edge of Karpo's bar on the primary display (`TaskbarPosition.For`,
  `Taskbar.Wanted`, `TaskbarPosition.Saved`); removed — Windows has one edge for every display, so it stood on that edge
  on all of them.* Now it is shown at the bottom, where it waited.
- **Moved as Settings moves it** (`TaskbarPosition.Move`): `TaskbarLocation` written, then Explorer's own taskbar told
  (`WM_USER + 0x1CA`, 6, the value; 2 s at most, never waiting on a hung Explorer). Only where it stands elsewhere;
  a refused value or an Explorer that did not answer is said (*"... from its next start"*).
- **Only where Windows has the edges**: Settings registers the position setting, and no policy holds it (`Offered`) — no
  build number guessed. Never on a dock of a config of its own (a test, `--smoke`) nor a stage (`LiveTaskbarPosition`).
- **Windows' settings while Karpo runs**: the person moving Windows' taskbar to a side there sees it go back to the bottom
  at the next reconcile (`Rehide`: *"... not auto-hidden at the bottom (a new Explorer, Windows' settings): there and
  auto-hidden again"*).

**Start no longer a taskbar too high** (`ShellPopupPlace`). With Windows' taskbar at the bottom, every panel is still placed
by it (§540, §580). Start's host ends where the hidden taskbar begins (seen: 2088 of 2160): with no bar at the bottom
Start stood 72 px (48 DIP) above where it belongs, and over a bottom bar thicker than the taskbar. Now the host ends at the
work area's end (`Wide`, `Drop`): down by the taskbar where nothing holds the bottom, up off a thicker bar, unmoved for a
gap under half a taskbar (Karpo's 63 px against 72: not worth a step as Start opens). Start's search box — SearchHost's
window from Start's top to the screen's end — goes down or up as far (`OnStart`), the thickness read from Explorer's hidden
taskbar windows (`TaskbarThickness`: 0,2158..3840,2230 on the main display, -3840,2088..0,2160 on the other); before, a bar
at the bottom took the box up by the whole bar, off Start. Measured from the display, so moved once, as before.

**What of §580 stays, and why.** All of it: while Karpo runs Windows' taskbar is at the bottom of every display, so Windows
still places Start, Search, the Widgets board and Win+X against a bottom taskbar's left end or middle, and quick settings,
the notification centre and the notifications against its right end, over a bar at the side; `ShellPopups` still moves
them off. Nothing became unneeded. Not changed: quick settings and the notification centre were not seen to stand a taskbar
high (notifications stand flush in the corner, §540), so only Start and its search box go down.

Tests: `TaskbarPositionTests` (ABE_* numbers both ways, none and unknown the bottom; no position setting or a policy: nothing
read, written or told; written then told; not where it stands; a refused value not told, an unheard one said; the primary
display's edge, None there, None everywhere, a new display; a test's run never touches the live store),
`TaskbarStateTests` (the takeover moves to the bottom before auto-hiding; at the bottom or with no edges nothing moved;
put back: auto-hide off, moved, shown, in that order; no edge leaves it; moved off the bottom while Karpo runs goes back),
`BarKeeperTests` (`BarWorld` now has Explorer's edge, auto-hiding only at the bottom: Windows' taskbar on the left with the
bar there — no empty strip while Karpo runs, back on the left after a quit and after a crash; moved to the right in
Windows' settings while Karpo runs — back at the bottom, every bar's strip whole), `ShellPopupsTests` (Start and its
search box down to the screen's end beside a bar at the left or the right, at the left or centred; moved once; a bar at
the bottom as thick, a little thinner, thicker; no thickness known; the thickness from the measured windows). No test
reads or writes this PC's registry or moves a window.

By hand (Windows' taskbar on the bottom in Windows' settings first; Karpo's bar on the left of the main display):

1. Quit Karpo: Windows' taskbar comes up on the **left** (it may be seen to move there from the bottom), not auto-hidden;
   karpo.log / appbar.log: *"Explorer's taskbar shown again, auto-hide off; Windows' taskbar moved to the left"*. Settings
   › Taskbar behaviors says Left. Windows' Start opens beside it.
2. Start Karpo: Windows' taskbar goes to the bottom and out of sight within a moment; appbar.log *"...; Windows' taskbar
   moved to the bottom"*; the bar holds the left edge with nothing beside it; maximized windows touch the bar.
3. With Karpo running: Start (Windows key) on the main display and on the other: its bottom where the screen ends (or
   just above a bar at the bottom), not 72 px higher; type in its search box: the results stand on Start, not above it.
4. With Karpo running, set Windows' taskbar to Right in Settings: within a moment it is back at the bottom, hidden, and
   appbar.log says so.
5. End Karpo.exe in Task Manager (the dock): the guard puts Windows' taskbar on the left, shown; Karpo comes back and it
   goes to the bottom again.
6. Karpo's bar at the bottom: quit and start: Windows' taskbar never moves.

## 595. The default layout a badge in the list; each layout's expander a switch making it the default (2026-11-09) — always one default, its Set as default a button greyed on the default, no None, since §636 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"default layout should not be a dropdown but should be a badge in the layout list and then when
expanding a layout you should be able to make it the default one"*.

**Replaces** §579's Default layout row (the Layouts section's first row, a dropdown of the layouts and None, "Shown on new
displays" under it) and its mark ("Default layout" under the default's name, "This display · Default layout" with the
other). §579 stays for what the default is: the layout displays Karpo has not seen yet show, or None (§344, Karpo off on
them); `defaultLayoutId` and `newDisplaysHidden` as they were.

    Layouts
      ⠿ ▦ Default  This display              ⧉ 🗑 ⌄
      ⠿ ▦ Work (Default)                     ⧉ 🗑 ⌃
          Name             [ Work         ]
          Icon             [ ▦          ⌄ ]
          Default layout                     On ●
          Shown on new displays
      + Add a layout ⌄

- **The badge** (`OptionThing.Badge`, `FlyoutItem.Badge`, `PanelRow.Badge`; BarLooks.Thing): the default layout wears
  "Default" after its name, on its name's line, whatever this display shows; "This display" stays the line under the
  shown one's name, so the two marks never share a line again. Drawn as WinUI's InfoBadge would hold a word
  (`PanelPainter.Badge`): a pill 20 DIP tall, fully round, AccentFillColorDefault, its word in Caption 12,
  TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary, 8 in from either end, 8 after the name (`PanelMetrics.BadgeTall`, `BadgeInset`); the name is
  cut short for it, the badge at most half the room; greyed AccentFillColorDisabled under TextOnAccentFillColorDisabled. To
  a screen reader the expander's head says it as its status ("Default"). No layout is badged while new displays show None.
- **The switch** (`BarLooks.DefaultSwitch`, keyed `DefaultLayout:<id>`, each layout's expander's last row after Name and
  Icon): "Default layout", "Shown on new displays" under it, on for the default alone. Turned on, the default moves there
  (`WriteDefault(id)`), the badge with it; turned off on the default, new displays show None (`WriteDefault(null)`), every
  switch off, the default's id kept; a switch that is off turned off changes nothing. Why a switch, not a "Make default"
  button: a button cannot be undone on the default, so None would need a row of its own again; Windows' Settings makes a
  thing the one in force by a switch where there may be none. The words are §579's two, the badge the one new word.
- **A toggle row says its detail** (`OptionMenu`'s Toggle: `Why ?? Detail`): until now a toggle's second line was only why
  it was held (`OptionRow.Why`), its `Detail` dropped; no other toggle sets one.

**Deleted**: `BarLooks.Default` (the dropdown row) and the joined mark. **Words** (every language): new
`settings.layouts.default.badge` ("Default"; de "Standard", fr "Par défaut", es "Predeterminado", it "Predefinito", pl
"Domyślny", ru "По умолчанию", ja "既定", zh-Hans "默认"…); `settings.layouts.default.header` and `.description` now the
switch's; none gone.

**The file:** no change, shape 78.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.TheDefaultLayoutIsBadgedAndMadeSoInItsExpander` (no Default layout row; the switch's kind, words and
detail, in the menu too; the badge and the switches following the default as it moves; the badge the default's whatever
this display shows; off on another nothing; off on the default None, nothing badged, the id kept, a new display off; on
again anywhere), `TheLayoutsPageHoldsEachLayoutAsAnExpanderOfItsOwnRows`, `TheBarsRowsAreCutThreeWays`,
`TheLayoutsPageGreysWhatCannotBeDone` (each expander three rows, the badge and "This display" on the panel's rows, the
switch's second line), `SettingsPanelTests.DisplaysAndLayoutsAreOnePage`, `LayoutMenuTests`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.PagesSheets` — pages-displays- (Work badged), new pages-layout-open- (Work's expander open,
its switch on), dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › Displays and layouts: the default layout's name followed by an accent pill "Default". Open another
layout: Default layout, off; turn it on: the pill moves to it, the other's switch off. Turn it off: no pill anywhere; plug
in a display Karpo has not seen: no bar on it. Turn one on again: the next new display shows it.

## 600. No way Karpo ends moves Windows' taskbar: shown again where it waited, at the bottom (2026-11-09)

The person, on §591's put-back to Karpo's edge: *"dont do this then. because it moves it to the right on all screens."*
Windows' taskbar has one edge for every display (§591): moved to the right of the main display's bar, it stood on the right
of every display, beside bars at the bottom there.

**Removed**: the move on a put-back. `Taskbar.PutBack` is auto-hide off, then shown, as before §591 (`Back` again, no
`Put`); `Taskbar.Restore()` takes no edge; `Taskbar.Wanted`, `TaskbarPosition.For`, `TaskbarPosition.Saved` (the guard's
read of the file) and `TaskbarPosition.ShownOn` deleted, Dock.Arrange's displays-shown rule back inline where it is used.

**Kept**: the takeover moves Windows' taskbar to the bottom before auto-hiding it (it auto-hides only there), and `Rehide`
sends it back there if moved while Karpo runs. That also repairs what a build of §591 leaves behind at its last quit (the
taskbar on Karpo's edge, `TaskbarLocation` 0, 1 or 2): the next start parks it at the bottom, and there it stays once Karpo
ends. Start placed down to the work area's end (§591) stays.

it: auto-hide off and shown only, at the bottom, left or right as it stands), `TaskbarPositionTests` (TaskbarLocation 0, 1,
2 parked: 3 written and told; the primary display's edge tests deleted), `BarKeeperTests` (Windows' taskbar on the left,
right or top: at the bottom while Karpo runs, still at the bottom after a quit and after a crash).

By hand: Karpo's bar on the right of the main display; quit Karpo: Windows' taskbar comes up at the bottom of every
display, not on the right; karpo.log *"Explorer's taskbar shown again, auto-hide off"*, nothing about a move.

## 594. The levels back, the third level gone: §588 undone but for the region's well, the tray's icons and the folder's Alignment (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), of §588: *"you overdid the menu levels thing. for example the online stuff or the import export
etc. they should have been kept in the extendable sections. i basically just did not like the third level. but not that i
did not like any level. revert this"*. What §588 answered stays answered: *"the tray icons have two levels in their
configuration so you have to actually expand to configure"*, the public holidays' regions on *"a different (darker)
background"*, and the folder's alignment *"burried two levels deep although it is the only configuration there"*.

**The rule.** A page may hold a level the person opens (the second level: an expander, a group); nothing stands a level
inside that one (the third: a row nested under a choice a step in on a well, §529, §564, §565). And no level is made only
to hold what is all there is: a level alone in its card is the card; a section's heading names its rows itself.

**Each of §588's flattenings, decided** (§588's commits reverted whole, then the keepers put back):

| §588 made | Level it removed | §594 |
|---|---|---|
| The Karpo page's Formats ›, Public holidays ›, Online ›, Karpo Pro ›, Back up and reset › sections of the page; the headings Services and Karpo gone | second | back: expanders under General, Services and Karpo as §517 had them, `settings.sections.services` in every language again |
| A widget menu's levels (Show from, a timer's or focus's Length, an alarm's Time and Repeat on) groups of their own, open | second (an expander in What it shows) | back: expanders in What it shows, shut |

## 601. Start hangs from Karpo's Start button (2026-11-09) — Windows' gap kept to the screen's top and the bar since §640 (2026-11-09); superseded by §666 (2026-11-12)

The person: *"is it possible to move the start to the start button on karpo? right now the start appears on the bottom
for example although the start button is shown on the top. is this possible?"*

**What decides where Start stands.** Windows lays Start out by its own taskbar's edge: since 26300.8493 that edge can be
any of four (§591), and the redesigned Start has an opening and closing animation for each edge (Windhawk's *Taskbar on
top* mod hands Start the edge it should animate from, `GetStartMenuTaskbarEdge`). While Karpo runs Windows' taskbar
stays at the bottom, the one edge it can auto-hide on (§591), so Start is always laid out over a bottom taskbar: in a host
window as wide as the display, ending where that taskbar begins, Start at the host's foot, at its left (`TaskbarAl` 0) or
its middle. Telling Windows the taskbar is at the top would need it there and not hidden: the empty 72 px strip §591
turned down.

**What can be done from outside.** The mods that put Start at the top (*Taskbar on top*, *Vertical taskbar*, read: their
source) run inside StartMenuExperienceHost and change Start's XAML (`FrameRoot`'s vertical alignment and margins in the
redesigned Start, `StartSizingFrame`'s `Canvas.Top` in the old one), moving the host only to the work area's edge; they
note that resizing the host glitched. Karpo injects nothing, so it can only move the host — which §580 and §591 already
do — by as far as it takes Start to stand where it should. That needs Start's own rectangle inside the host:

- Read-only on the user's PC (26300, 150 %): with Start closed, neither StartMenuExperienceHost nor SearchHost has a
  top-level window at all (`EnumWindows`, 15:37), so nothing of Start can be read or placed before it opens. A passive
  watcher (25 min: the two processes' windows polled, Start's UI Automation tree read once a showing) saw no opening
  while it ran: Start's panel rectangle was **not** read through UI Automation.
- What is known: Start's search box, SearchHost's window, shows with Start a few ms after the host (appbar.log
  15:30:46.522/.526, 15:30:51.238/.242), at 0,825..1287,2160 — from Start's top to the screen's end, Start's width with
  Windows' gaps, flush with the display's left where Windows stands Start 12 DIP in. So Start's outer rectangle is the
  box's width from the box's top to the host's end, and placing it flush against the bar keeps Windows' own gaps.
- Moving the host is kept: every opening in appbar.log since §580 has one move of the host, none put back by Windows.

**Now** (`ShellPopupPlace.StartShift`, `Hung`, Karpo.Dock\ShellPopups.cs; `Dock.StartButtonOn`, `DockWindow.StartButton`):

- **Which button.** The Start button of Karpo's that opened Start (pressed in the last 5 s, on that display); else, for the
  Windows key or Start opened another way, the first standing bar's on the display Start opens on, the display's main bar
  first. A bar that slides in counts only when its button was pressed. No Start button there: as before.
- **Where.** Start's outer rectangle against the bar's inner side (under a bar at the top, above one at the bottom, beside
  one at a side), centred on the button along the bar — Windows' left-aligned look where the button is at the bar's
  start, its centred look where it is in the middle — kept inside the work area. Along the bar a step of under half a
  taskbar is not taken where Start is clear of the bars already, so a bar at the bottom with its button at the left, or
  centred where Windows centres Start, leaves it where §591 put it.
- **How.** The host and the box go by the same step, each measured from where Windows puts it on the display, so each is
  moved once however often it is heard, and back when the bar goes. The box's size is kept per display from its showing
  with Start (`ShellPopups.boxes`); the host, heard first, goes by the last one, and on the first opening on a display by
  §591 until the box shows, then on. When the box shows, the host is placed again.
- **One display.** The host must keep more of itself on its display than on any other (else Windows takes it to be on
  that one): where a step along the bar would not — Start aligned left by Windows, a button far right on a display with
  another to its right — Start goes only across, against the bar; where neither would, §591's rule.
- **As before** where nothing is known: no hidden taskbar along the bottom, no box seen yet, a host the size of the display,
  Search's own host, a Start larger than the work area. The log line says *"moved for Karpo's Start button to"*.

**Not done, and why.** Start's opening animation is the bottom edge's (it rises), whichever bar it hangs from: only
Start's own process can choose another. Karpo hears the host a few ms after it is uncloaked and moves it then, so Start may
be seen starting at the bottom and jumping to the button (under a top bar that is some 760 px at 150 %) — §580's step, much
longer. Under a bar at the top the gap between it and Start is the box's own margin, assumed Windows' 12 DIP. The host
stands partly above the display (at 150 %, -762..1326), where nothing is drawn. Search on its own (Win+S) is not hung from
Karpo's Search button: it is placed as §580 has it.

Tests: `ShellPopupsTests` (`UnderABarAtTheTopStartHangsFromItsStartButton`: host 762 px up, box at the work area's top,
moved once, measured from the display after §591's step; `AlongTheBarStartIsCentredOnTheButton`: middle, right end,
Windows centring, a pixel off no step; `OnABarAtTheBottomStartGoesAlongToTheButton`: the button at the left stays, further
in goes along, a thicker bar up; `BesideABarAtASideStartHangsFromItsStartButton`: left bar button at the top, right bar at
the foot and halfway; `StartsHostKeepsMostOfItselfOnItsOwnDisplay`: the other display's far button only up, a display above;
`AtAHundredPercentStartHangsInItsOwnPixels`; `WhereNothingIsKnownStartGoesByTheBarsAsBefore`), 44 in all; no test moves a
window.

By hand (Windows' Start with search box as usual; appbar.log open):

1. Karpo's bar at the top of the main display, its Start button at its left: press it. Start opens under the bar at the
   left, 12 DIP below it, not at the bottom; appbar.log *"Windows' Start ... moved for Karpo's Start button to 0,-762"* and
   the search box's line. Watch the opening: does Start flash at the bottom first, and how badly? Type: the results stand
   on Start. Click an app, and click outside Start: it closes. Leave it open 30 s: it does not go back to the bottom.
2. The Windows key with the pointer on the other display: Start under that display's top bar, if it has one with a Start
   button, else as before.
3. Move the Start button to the middle of the top bar: Start centred under it. With Windows' taskbar alignment Center too.
4. Bar at the left with Start at its top: Start beside the bar at the top; at the right with Start at the foot: beside
   it at the bottom.
5. Bar at the bottom, Start button at the left: no change from before; button moved to the middle: Start above it.
6. Note whether Start's closing animation plays where it stands, and whether its gap to the top bar looks like Windows'.

## 592. The Appearance page one preview over four tabs: Bar, Taskbar widgets, Flyouts, Widgets in folders; an expander that shows a look its preview first again (2026-11-09) — the reset in Palette's row since §610 (2026-11-09); its preview on the desktop, more widgets, in the taskbar's mode, a Mode over Palette, since §613 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), looking at the Appearance page: *"actually for the appearance settings page i want only one
preview now, then there should be tabs underneath for the four different sections / groups of styles that you can
change."*

**First, merge fallout**: §583 and §585 were made side by side. §583 deleted `PanelRows.One`'s branch that put a look's
preview at the top of an expander (the Appearance's sections had been expanders); §585 made the taskbar menu an expander of
Behavior that carries its `Shows` (OptionMenu passes a things row's `Detail` and `Shows` onto its item) and relied on that
branch. Merged, the expander kept its look and lost its preview: `BarMenuPanelTests.TheTaskbarMenuIsAnExpanderOfBehavior`
(its first row an Item), `ThePageShowsTheMenuAsTheBarDrawsItAtItsTop` and `LookPreviewTests.EveryPreviewInAFlyoutStandsInsideItsCut`
(no preview on the Taskbar page) failed. Fixed in one place: every expander's rows are made by one local of `PanelRows.One`
(`Level`), the preview first where its item shows a look — the tools' expander and the plain one alike.

**Replaces** §577's and §583's two sections (Taskbar: Bar, Taskbar widgets; Folders and flyouts: Flyouts, Widgets in
folders), each a heading with a preview of its own and each part a card always open. Now:

    Palette                      [ Karpo  Changed ⌄ ]
    Changes to Karpo             [ Reset to default ]
    Preview  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐    the whole look, dark | light
             │      clock and calendar, open     │
             │  ⊞ ⧉ 09:41 ───────────────────────│
             └───────────────────────────────────┘
    Bar   Taskbar widgets   Flyouts   Widgets in folders      the tabs, the chosen one's pill under it
          ▬▬
    the chosen tab's rows, each a card of the page

- **One preview, the whole look** (`LookSample.Whole`, which was §536's Bar and Open): the bar's stand-ins — Start, Task
  view, a folder wearing the clock, each on its card — and that folder open over its face, its lines (a clock, a calendar)
  drawn as the open folder draws them, its outline the Flyouts'. Every part of the four shows in it, so any tab's change
  shows. §582's slanted line splits it dark | light as before; the open folder is centred over its face (`Bar` returns the
  folder's card, not the first). Its room is §571's Open room. A screen reader calls it "Preview of Appearance". The part the
  chosen tab edits is not highlighted in it (left out: the preview would be drawn again at every tab).
- **Tabs, WinUI's SelectorBar** (`PanelTabs`, `PanelRowKind.Tabs`/`Tab`): each part is a `Level` row of `LookRows.Rows`
  keyed `Appearance.<part>.tab` (`LookRows.IsTab`), its editor's rows its level (its own Text and Colors headings left out,
  as §583 left them: the tab names them). The panel makes a run of them one strip, the look they show (each tab's `Shows`,
  the one `LookShown`) previewed right over it (`Appearance/#preview`); the strip `Appearance/#tabs`, each tab
  `Appearance/@<part>` (`PanelTabs.Mark`), its rows in it (`Appearance/@Taskbar widgets/Font`). Laid out (`PanelLayout`):
  the strip on the page's ground, no card, 40 DIP tall (`PanelMetrics.Tabs`), 8 under the preview and 8 over the chosen
  tab's rows, which are laid as the page's own cards, 4 apart; the others' rows are nowhere. Each tab its words and 12 either
  side, from the cards' start, 4 apart (narrowed alike, cut short with their whole words in the tooltip, where a language's
  are too long). Drawn (`PanelPainter.Tabs`): no fill until the pointer is on one (Subtle fills), the chosen one's words
  Body Strong in the text's ink with the accent pill (16 × 3) at its foot, the others' TextFillColorSecondary.
- **The tab chosen remembered**: an open key of `PanelMemory` (`Open`: a tab's key chooses it and lets go of the others of
  its strip), the first where none is — for the run of the app, as the expanders open are, so closing the flyout and opening
  it again keeps it. A landing on a row of a tab chooses that tab (`PanelRows.PathTo` gives the tab, not the strip).
- **Keys**: of a strip only the chosen tab is a stop of Tab; Left and Right choose the tab before and after (mirrored right to
  left, held at the ends), Home and End the first and the last, the keys going with the choice (`EditDeck.Key`). A click
  chooses (`PanelHitKind.Tab`, no id: its strip's place says which). The stage map lists every tab, for a probe to press.
- **Screen reader** (`DeckUia`): the strip a tab list (`UiaRole.Tab`) named for its page, its tabs tab items (`TabItem`),
  each SelectionItem, the chosen one selected; Select on another chooses it.

**Deleted**: `LookSection`, `LookSections`, `LookRows.SectionKey(LookSection)`, `PartHeading`/`IsPartHeading`,
`PanelGroups.Parts`, `PanelRow.Fixed` (and its branches in the layout, the hits, the screen reader and EditDeck.Act), `PanelRows.PlaceOf`,
`LookPreview.BarItemsOf`, `LookSample.Bar`/`Open`, `LookShown.Part` (one look, the whole), and the string
`settings.look.folders` ("Folders and flyouts") in all thirty languages. No new string: the tabs are the parts' names.

**The file:** no change, shape 78 where it landed: nothing of the page is kept but the tab chosen, in memory.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests.TheAppearancePageIsOnePreviewOverFourTabs` (the page's rows Palette, Reset, Preview, Tabs; each tab
keyed, its glyph, its editor's rows in order, keyed in it, a landing's path the tab; laid out with none and with each
chosen: the strip after the preview, the chosen tab's rows alone after it as page cards; the tabs side by side, a click on
one finds it, the chosen one the only stop; to a screen reader a tab list named Appearance of four tab items, the chosen
selected), `TheTabChosenIsRememberedOneAStrip` (PanelMemory), `EveryLevelThatEditsALookHasItsPreviewAtItsTopAndNowhereElse`
(an expander's preview first in it; a strip's right over it), `EachLookPicksItsSampleByOneRule` (Whole, Menu),
`ASamplesRoomHoldsTheFoldersLinesWhole`, `APreviewIsAnImageNothingToPressOrStopOn`; `AppearanceValuesTests` (each tab
chosen in turn for its colour pairs); `SettingsPanelTests` (`EveryPageKeepsOneRhythm` 8 round a strip,
`TheKeysReachWhateverAClickReaches` a tab not chosen by the arrows, `EveryMenuRowIsAControlOnce`); `PanelControlsTests`,
`MenuRulesTests` (no heading on the Appearance page; a strip 40 tall), `LayoutMenuTests`, `BarBlurSettingTests`,
`BarGroundTests`, `PopupPlaceTests`. UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `EditDeckClickTests.TheAppearanceTabsAreChosenByAClickTheArrowsAndAScreenReader`
(the real windows: a click, Tab onto the chosen one alone, Right, Left, Home, End, kept over closing and opening, a screen
reader's Select); pictures `SceneTreeTests.AppearanceTabsSheets` (appearance-tab-<n>-<part>-<dark|light>.png), `LookPreviewSheets`
(preview-whole-), `AFoldersLinesStandWholeInTheirRoomAtEveryTextSize`, `ALookChangedDrawsItsPreviewAgainOnceAndNothingElseDoes`,
`AppearancePairSheets`, `AppearancePaletteSheets`, `PagesSheets` (pages-taskbar-menu-: the expander, its preview first);
the stage probes that open an Appearance row choose its tab first (`PanelPopupPlaceTests`, `SettingsWornTests`,
`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.RunColorPicker`).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance: Palette, Reset to default, one preview (the bar, its widgets, the clock folder open over
its face; dark left, light right), then Bar · Taskbar widgets · Flyouts · Widgets in folders, Bar chosen with its pill; click
Widgets in folders: its rows; close the flyout and open it again: still Widgets in folders; Tab to the strip, Left: Flyouts,

## 596. The selection's entries as any other: the folder's and the widget's side by side, each as wide as its words, in a room kept for them (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"folder and the widget/s that are selected should be independent items in the topbar just like
the other items are. right now they have some fixed width or something like that but they should be displayed the same way
the others are."* — with §578's *"the top edit bar should not change width"* and §584's *"there should not be a placeholder
shown"* still standing.

**No slot** (`PanelLayout.Lay`, `Fit`; `PanelMetrics.SelectionWide`). §578's 192 DIP slot gave one entry its whole width
(its glyph and words from its start) and, with a folder too, the folder's entry its icon alone and the widget's the rest:
neither looked like Karpo, Accounts or Appearance beside it. Now each is an entry of the bar as those are — its icon, 8, its
words, 12 round them, centred, no fill nor rim until the pointer is on it, the entry open marked by the fill and the pill —,
as wide as its words (`ButtonWide`), the folder's ("Folder") then the widget's ("Calendar", "2 × Clock", "3 widgets": §528's
one entry for several, as before), 4 apart, from the start of a room kept for them:

    ⠿ [⚙ Karpo] [@ Accounts] [🖥 Displays and layouts] [▭ Taskbar] [🎨 Appearance]  [📁 Folder] [🗓 Calendar]            [⊗] [+ Add] [✓ Done]

- **The room**, 256 DIP, a gutter after the pages' entries and before the errors' room, kept whatever is selected, so the bar
  is one width (§578): what the entries leave of it is empty — nothing drawn, nothing pressed, no stop of the keys, no element
  of a screen reader's (§584). 256 holds the folder's entry and a widget's of some fourteen letters ("2 × Performance") whole
  in English at Segoe UI Variable's 14; one alone up to some twenty-five.
- **Too long for it** (`Fit`): the last entry, the widget's, cut short at its end less 12 with an ellipsis, its name whole in
  its tooltip (`TipOf`, as §578); never under a name's 40 DIP — there the folder's shows its icon alone (its words its
  tooltip) and the widget's what that leaves, then both their icons.
- **A narrow display**: the pages' entries their icons first (§575), then the room narrows (never under two icons), the
  selection's entries fitting it as above.
- **One way to paint an entry** (`SettingsPanel.Paint.cs`'s `Words`): a button's glyph and words centred in it, from its
  start and cut short where it is narrower than they are. Deleted: the selection's own case (`PanelHitKind.Nav when … Widget
  or Folder` → `GlyphAndWords` across the slot).
- Each opens its own flyout as any entry does, hung from its own column with its beak over its middle (§584, `HungFrom`);
  the keys go along them (Left, Right) after Appearance; a screen reader finds each a button that expands, named its words.

No config, no new words.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests` (`TheBarIsACommandBarOfThePages`: the folder's and the widget's two entries at their words'
widths from the room's start, a screen reader's two buttons; `TheBarIsOneWidthWhateverIsSelected`: one width with nothing,
a widget, a folder, both, several, errors, a flyout open, each one alone its words' width, the rest of the room no hit, a long
name cut at the room's end and whole in its tooltip, the folder's whole beside it; `TheSelectionsEntriesFitTheirRoom`: the
order things give way; `TheBarNarrowsOnANarrowDisplay`: the folder's its icon first; `AFlyoutHangsFromItsEntry`: the
folder's and the widget's flyouts each from its own entry, the beak over it, up and down); `EditDeckClickTests.TheKeysFindTheirWay`
(the arrows onto Folder and the widget's entry); `SceneTreeTests.SelectionSheets` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR):
selection-none-, -widget-, -folder-, -both-, -both-folder-, -several-, dark and light, and selection-widths.txt — the bar
1728 px (1152 DIP at 150 %) in every one, Folder 131 px, Calendar 154 px, "2 × Clock" 160 px.

By hand: edit mode — nothing right of Appearance; a widget clicked: "Calendar" right of Appearance as Appearance stands, its
flyout's beak under it, the bar where it stood, no wider; a widget in a folder: Folder and Calendar, two entries; Folder
