## 590. The weather and the air quality in widgets of fixed content: the current weather, the hourly and the daily forecast, the air's index, pollutants, pollen and day; a few sizes, no rows (2026-11-09) — the current weather's Full no header, its place a caption under the hero, since §607 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"right now a widget like the weather one does show progressively more content depending on its
size. i want to change that for the weather widget but also other widgets like the air quality one: these widgets should
be broken down into smaller ones that always show the same amount of data, e.g. the weather one would be broken down into
current weather, daily forecast and day graph or something like that, those should get their own style variations and can
be placed individually (bring back the graph version for the todays weather and also bring a graph version for a multi day
forecast one as well). same for other widgets that have a similar behaviour. those widgets then should also not have the
size given in rows but just a few different sizes that make sense"*.

**What showed more as it grew.** The weather's Today (`WeatherNow`, §401) had a Height in rows: one row its kit row; from
five cells a header over a hero; from nine the next hours across under it; from eleven a day ahead a row more each two
cells. Its Daily (`WeatherDays`) showed as many of the seven days as its rows held. The air quality (§210) had six tiers:
its row, from two rows the index's scale, from four its pollutants, from five its pollen, from six the place's day.

**The widgets now** (Microsoft Weather's words: Current weather, Hourly forecast, Daily forecast; the air's Pollutants,
Pollen, Air quality forecast). Each says the same at each of its sizes — Compact the smaller arrangement of it, Full the
larger — and nothing more where its line is taller; its line is its size's form, whole cells (§432, §442), never rows:

| Widget (file `kind`, `style`) | Says | Compact | Full |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current weather (`weatherNow`) | the place, the conditions' glyph and words, the temperature, what it feels like with the day's high and low | the kit's row with its caption (3 cells) | a header (the place, the reading's age or why none is newer) over a hero (6) |
| Hourly forecast · Graph (`hourlyForecast`, first; form `weatherHours`) | today's curve midnight to midnight, the hours' times, glyphs, temperatures and chances, now marked | the flyout's 64-DIP band, as it always stood (7); new lines start here | the band half as tall again, 96 DIP (9) |
| Hourly forecast · List (`"style": "list"`, form `weatherHoursList`) | the next five hours past midnight where it comes (`WeatherReading.Next`), each its time, glyph, temperature | the glyph beside the temperature (3) | the glyph large over it (5) |
| Daily forecast · List (`dailyForecast`, first; form `weatherDays`) | the seven days, each its name, glyph, chance of rain, low and high | a column a day across the line (6) | a row a day, its range on the week's scale (14) |
| Daily forecast · Graph (`"style": "graph"`, form `weatherDaysGraph`) | the same seven days | a column a day, its name and glyph over the highs' and the lows' curves, each figure at its point, the chance under them, on a 64-DIP band (7) | the same on 96 DIP (9) |
| Air quality (`airQuality`) | the level, the index, the place and the index's name | the kit's row with its caption (3) | the same over the index's scale, a mark where it stands (5) |
| Pollutants (`airPollutants`) | PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂ in µg/m³ | two columns (5) | a row each (8) |
| Pollen (`airPollen`) | the six plants' grains per m³, always all six in one order, 0 where none (`AirReading.Plants`); outside Europe its Status: "No pollen forecast for this place" | three columns (5) | a row each (12) |
| Air quality forecast (`airForecast`) | the place's day, a bar an hour in its level's colour, now marked (§501) | bars 28 DIP tall (4) | 64 DIP (6) |

The graph of today is the weather flyout's own (§80, `DayGraph`), which the Hourly style had kept: it is the Hourly
forecast's first style. The week's graph is new (`WeatherDaysGraphTile`): the high's curve in the accent, the low's in the
secondary ink, both the monotone cubic of `WeatherCurve` (§80's "no overshoot"), drawn by `DayGraph.Smooth`, which the
day's line now draws through too; a day's two points on the scale the week shares (`DayRow.From`, `To`), the band keeping
a figure's line clear over the highest high and under the lowest low (`WeatherDaysGraphTile.Points`). The forecast's
columns (`WeatherColumns`) stand between the gutters, each its plate and its target (§131): a click searches the weather
(on that day for a day), a hover says the hour or the day in full. The air's four are one class (`AirQualityTile`, its
kind its part) on one store, as before; its index's choice is on the index's line and the day's.

**Placed on their own.** The add page's Weather and news has the weather's ready-made folder and its three widgets, a
line, the air's ready-made folder and its four, a line, then the tides, the earthquakes and the sun (`AddTree`; its runs
apart so the shelf's twenty rows read, §490's cap one more). Each goes into any folder by itself, a folder on any bar; the
bar's own are the folders' faces — the weather's Simple, Detailed, Forecast and Conditions, the air's index —, unchanged.
The ready-made folders: the weather's the current weather, the hourly graph (Compact) and the daily list (Full); Today's
the same three; the air's the index (Full), the pollutants and the pollen (Compact) and the day (Full).

**Deleted.** The weather's styled widget `weather` and its styles `now`, `hourly`, `daily` (`WidgetStyles.Weather`, its
words in every language); the Height of the current weather, the daily forecast and the air quality, and what a height
drew: `WeatherPartTile.Ahead` (the hours across and the days under the hero), the hero's captions dropped as the line
shrank, the days fitted to the rows (`WeatherDaysTile.Rows`' fit, `fits`), the hours' graph giving up its glyphs and then
its words (`DayGraph.Bare`, `WeatherHoursTile.Fill`'s fallbacks), `WeatherNote.Height`, the air's tiers (`AirPlan`,
`AirQualityTile.Plan`, `PollutantColumns`, the day's bars 28 to 64 DIP as the room allowed) and the tests and pictures of
them (`AutomaticHeightTests.TheWeeksWeatherIsAsTallAsItsDays`, `AirQualityPictures.TheLineDrawsWhatItsHeightHolds`,
air-lines-*.png). New words: the five kinds', the two forecasts', their styles' and the pollen's Status in all 30
languages; the current weather is "Current weather" (was "Conditions"), the forms "Hourly graph", "Hourly list", "Daily
list", "Daily graph".

**The file.** `Config.Shape` 79 (77 as made; landed after §589's 77 and the 78 of the tip it landed on). No migration: "weather" is no word this build reads (a line of it is dropped as any
unknown kind); the person's own file is converted once (`artifacts\weather-split\convert-weather-split.py`, cells as the
file keeps them): a current weather fixed at four cells or fewer → `weatherNow` Compact, else Full; fixed at nine or more
→ an `hourlyForecast` (List, Full) after it, eleven or more → a `dailyForecast` (Full) after that; `hourly` →
`hourlyForecast` Compact; `daily` → `dailyForecast`, Compact where fixed at six or fewer, else Full; `airQuality` → Compact
at three cells or fewer or automatic, else Full, from eight `airPollutants`, from ten `airPollen` (a place in Europe),
from twelve (ten elsewhere) `airForecast` after it; fill as the largest. A split line keeps its place and id; the new
ones follow it in its list, each with a copy of its place. The person's layouts (`PersonsLayouts.json`) converted so.

Tests: `WeatherSplitTests` (every kind, style and size read and written back word for word; no height; "weather" read as
nothing; two sizes each, Compact the smaller; the next five hours past midnight; the six plants in one order; the daily
graph's points inside its band; the add page's runs), UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `WeatherSplitLinesTests`
(`EachSizeSaysTheSameAndATallerLineNoMore`: each kind's words and figures the same at Compact and at Full, the current
weather's age apart, and none more drawn twice as tall; `ItsHeightIsItsSizesWhateverTheForecastSays`), `SizedLinesTests`
(the split kinds' Compact is no row: `LineSizeTests.Split`), `LineStyleTests` (the columns' kinds are grids), and the
tests the split made stale. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `weather-split-weather-<dark|light>.png`,
`weather-split-air-<dark|light>.png`, `weather-split-*-text225-dark.png` (each widget a folder of its Compact over its
Full); `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets` panel-add-weather-, panel-add-weather-bar- (the add page's Weather and news, a
folder's and the bar's).

By hand: Add › Weather and news: Current weather, Hourly forecast, Daily forecast, Air quality, Pollutants, Pollen, Air
quality forecast; one in a folder; its page: Style (the forecasts' Graph or List) and Size (Compact, Full), no Height;
each size the same words; the folder taller, the line no different.

## 599. A row that only acts at its line's end, where the value controls end; its list under it flush with its right, one width (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the button like add layout is currently aligned on the left side in the settings, they should be
aligned on the right side. the dropdowns from these menus should also have a fixed width like all the others."*

**At the end** (`PanelLayout.Foots`, `FootAt`). §578 set a row that only acts — Add a layout, the taskbar menu's Add an entry
and Reset to default, a folder's Add a face, a toggles line's Add, Add a country, Formats' Reset all — from its line's start:
on a page from the cards' start, in an expander's card its glyph where the rows' names start. Now each ends where the value
controls end (`ControlEnd`: 16 in from a card's end): on a page a run of them in order along one line, 8 apart, the last
ending 16 in from the cards' end, the next line where the room ends, each line ending there too; in an expander's card each
at its line's end, never further in than where the rows' names start. Their look is §578's (a hyperlink button's).

**Their lists.** Why they looked apart from every other dropdown: §587's one width was theirs already (`Flyout.Open`: every
popup hung from a control is a value's box's 240 DIP, the button's alike — `DropdownWidthTests` finds none wider or
narrower), but a button narrower than its list stood at the line's start and its list hung flush with its left
(§521), so the list ran 100 DIP and more past its button into the cards' middle, its right edge nowhere any other list's is —
a list as wide as what it lists, to the eye. At the line's end the same rule (§531: flush with the control's right where
flush with its left would pass the side of what it stands in) hangs it flush with its button's right: its right edge is
every dropdown's list's and box's, under its button, over it with no room under it, inside the work area. Nothing changed in
the rule; nothing special-cased.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests.ARowThatOnlyActsIsItsButtonAlone` (Add a layout ending 16 in from the cards' end; Add an entry and
Reset to default each at its line's end), `EveryControlIsOneSize` (every page, every expander open: an inset one at its
line's end, a page's run ending where a card's controls end), `EveryPageKeepsOneRhythm`;
`DropdownWidthTests.EveryFootButtonsListIsOneWidthUnderItsButtonFlushWithItsRight` (UI: every row that only acts' list on
every page the dock builds and every page of the corpus — Add a layout, Add an entry, Add a face, Add a toggle, Add a
country among them — hung from its button where the panel lays it out: 240 DIP, under it, flush with its right);
`PanelPopupPlaceTests` (the real dock: every control's popup checked a value's box's width now;
`AFootButtonsListIsOneWidthUnderItsButton`: Add a layout's and Add an entry's lists flush with their buttons' right).
Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.FootRightSheets` footright-layout-, footright-barmenu-,
footright-country-<dark|light>.png (Add a layout's list open; the taskbar menu's Add an entry open over Reset to default; Add
a country's search open).

By hand: edit mode › Displays and layouts: Add a layout at the right under the layouts, its chevron under the Default
layout's; its list under it, its right edge the dropdown's above. Taskbar › Behavior › Taskbar menu: Add an entry and Reset
to default at the right; Add an entry's list flush with its right. Karpo › Public holidays › Add a country: the same.

## 602. Every app button its own card: the open apps the Spacing apart, as the pins are (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the apps that are not pinned and shown in the apps widget should have the same space as the
other pins have to each other."*

**Why they differed.** Not the room: since §515 the layout keeps every two app buttons a widget's gap apart
(`Layout.TileGap` is `WidgetGap`, §589's Spacing), pin to pin, the last pin to the first open app and open app to open app
alike (`WidgetGapTests.PinsAndTheOpenAppsStandAsEveryWidget`). The drawing: a card and a plate at rest (§506, §512) were
one a part, over the part's whole block. A pin is a part of one button, so it stood on its own plate with the bar between
it and the next; the Apps widget is one part of every open app, so its one plate ran under all its buttons and filled the
gaps between them in — the open apps read as one block, the pins as separate buttons. That is §54's "one card" over the
open apps, left standing when §512 and §515 gave every widget its own card and the buttons their gap back. No divider
between the pins and the open apps is in the design log, and none was drawn: nothing to keep.

**Now**: every app button wears its own card and its own plate at rest, over its own cell — a pin's, each open app's in
the Apps widget, each window's of a pin whose windows are not combined, a labelled button as long as it is, and "…" —, so
every two of them stand the Spacing apart with the bar between them, on every edge, at every bar size and Spacing. One
place says it: `Layout.Plates(part)`, a part of buttons its cells (`TileCell`, `OverflowCell`), every other part its one
`Plate` as before. The scene draws a part's cards and plates from it (`Scene.ComposeCards`, `RestPlate` taking the
rectangle; a part's plates at rest one list, lit together, `LightPlates`). A pin's card is where it was; the Apps widget's
first button's card keeps the part's key (`card:<key>`), the others `card:<key>#<n>`. The hover still lights the
button's own cell, the focused app's plate and the running indicator stay inside it. Edit mode is untouched: a part is
still selected, carried and washed as one block. No setting, no file change.

Tests: `AppsGapTests` (the layout's plates: two pins and three open apps, each plate its button's cell, every two the
Spacing apart and the widget after them too — along the bottom, the top, the left and the right, at 32, 48 and 80 DIP,
Spacing 0, 3, 6, 12 and 24, at 100 and 150 %; a window each with titles, a pin's two windows among them; "…" its own plate
the gap after the last button shown; a widget one plate), `SceneTreeTests.EveryAppButtonWearsACardOfItsOwn` (renamed from
`AnAppGroupWearsOneCardAndLightsEachButtonOnIt`: a card over every button's cell, none over the Apps widget's block; the
hover on a pin's and an open app's own cell), `SceneTreeTests.AppsGapSheets` (the plates at rest on the real tree: one a
button, each its cell, the gap apart). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR, `AppsGapSheets`):
appsgap-<bottom|bottom-labels|left>-<6|12>-<dark|light>.png — Start, two pins (the second running), three open apps (the
first focused), a widget, at 150 %; `AppGroupSheets`' app-group-*.png now show a plate a button.

By hand: two apps pinned, three others open: the open apps' plates stand apart as the pins' do; Taskbar › Spacing 0 to
24: the open apps' gaps follow the pins'; the bar on the left: the same down the side; Combine taskbar buttons › Never:
each window's labelled button its own plate.

## 598. The faces of words down a side bar: more rows, never cut; the date keeps its month and year (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the screen time face does not show nicely when the taskbar is shown on the side and not so wide. it should
not overflow like it does right now."*; *"same with the datetime face. at some point the month and year does not show
anymore which should not be."*

**What it was** (`artifacts/sidefaces/before/`; every Size 32 to 160 DIP probed, at 100 and 150 %, 100 and 150 % text): two
rules of §162 that each face kept by hand gave way on a narrow bar, and the ladder's floor followed the text size.

- **One line, cut where it does not fit.** The screen time, the sun, the tides and the sports faces sized their one line
  with `VerticalFit.Across`, which steps down the ladder and, where even 9 DIP is too wide, takes 9 DIP and lets the line
  cut: the screen time read "13 h…" or "13 h 4…" from the thinnest bar up to 56 DIP at 100 % text and to 84 DIP with 150 %
  text. The sun's and tides' "18∶45" and the sports' "2–1" were cut the same way on the thinnest bar.
- **Saying less before saying it smaller.** The date down a side bar (`DateText.Stacked`, the time and date's and the
  calendar's) never had its year, and where "28.12." did not fit at the cell's small text it became the day alone: "28"
  under the time on a 42-DIP bar, the person's (63 px at 150 %).
- **A floor scaled by Windows' text size.** The ladder ended at 9 DIP *of the text scale*, so with 150 % text the battery's
  "100%", the focus's "25m" and the input indicator's code were cut on bars up to 40 DIP.

**One rule now** (`VerticalFit.Rows`). A text down a side bar has forms, fewest rows first; each is set at the largest size
of the ladder at which all its rows fit the room a line has (from templates, never the reading: §12.2); the first form is
taken that is at least two thirds as large as the largest any form reaches (`FewerRowsShare`), and no smaller than 9 DIP
of the text size. So "3 h" over "42 min" at 10 DIP rather than a word a row at 14; "28.12" over "2026" under a time at 20
DIP rather than "28.12.2026" at 12. Nothing is left out: where no form fits that well, the one that fits largest. The ladder
(`VerticalFit.Ladder`) ends with 11, 10 and 9 DIP of plain text, taken only where nothing above fits, so a large text size
on a thin bar sets a row smaller instead of cutting it. A face is as long as the rows it reads now (§244,
`SideRows.LengthOf`): "42 min" one row, "3 h 42 min" two, at one size.

- **A reading** (`VerticalFit.Phrase`): whole; a row per figure with its words (`Groups`: "3 h" | "42 min", "3 Std." |
  "42 Min."); a word a row; its parts (`Parts`, which now also splits a score's dash: "2" | "1"; a wordless total "3" |
  "小时"). Screen time, sun (its time, a polar day's "24 h"), tides (a time; a height "1.25" always whole, as its parts would
  read as two numbers), sports (a score, a kick-off's time, a day).
- **A date** (`DateText.SideForms`, `SideDate`): the region's short date on a row ("28.12.2026"); without its year over the
  year ("28.12" | "2026"; the year first where the region writes it first: "2026" | "12/28"); a field a row ("28" | "12" |
  "2026", `Nls.ShortDateFields`, each as the pattern writes it); where a chosen pattern names the month, the fields with its
  number last ("28" | "Dezember" | "2026", then "28" | "12" | "2026"). Measured on the 28th of every month where the date
  has a name in it, else on one. The time and date says its year, as Windows' clock and the face across a bar do, never
  larger than its time; the calendar says it where it does across a bar (the short date, not the day and the date), the
  day's name over it (`SideNames`: "Mon", else "Mo").
- **Unchanged**: the clock's rows (§162), the input indicator's and the stock's plans, the quakes' "8.8" (one figure; it
  fits). Weather and air were left alone (§590 is splitting them); they read through `VerticalFit.Across` too, and nothing
  of theirs was cut in the probe (without a reading).

Checked at every Size, 100/150 %, 100/150 % text: every face in `FaceDrawings` in English, the screen time and the calendar
in German and Russian too. Fixed: screen time, time and date, calendar (both forms), sun, tides, sports, battery, focus,
input indicator.

Tests: `SideFaceFitTests` — every face inside its cell, as wide as the bar, nothing cut (`PaintWatch.Trimmed`) at every
Size 32–160 in steps of 4; the date's day, month and year in its rows in en-US, de-DE, ru-RU, fi-FI and ja-JP and with a
pattern naming the month (`Nls.Region`, a test's region), every row inside the room; the person's 42-DIP bar at 150 %;
`Rows` over totals in three languages, a score and times; how a reading groups and splits; the date's forms per region;
the ladder's plain-text floor. `ScreenTimeFaceTests` takes the total's rows. Pictures: `SideFaceSheets`
(side-<dark|light>-<100|150>[-text150].png), before and after in `artifacts/sidefaces/`.

## 593. The add page at the edit bar's top, as wide; the pick under the pointer a ghost where it goes; its click puts it there (2026-11-09) — no line with nothing under the pointer, an empty ghost from the page's opening, since §617 (2026-11-09); the ghost whole, no wash over a pick, since §625 (2026-11-09); full of samples, not the person's own place, since §635 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when clicking add for a taskbar widget it shows a blue line, it should show a blue rectangle that
looks like a ghost preview of the new widget. when i hover over the widget that i want to add it should actually display it in
the location. when i then click to add it it should actually add it"*; then *"actually i have an even better idea now: right
now when i click add it shows the menu right where the mouse or the button was, i want the add menu to be shown on the top in
the same width as the edit bar all the time, now when i hover over a group or widget to add it should show the whole group and
widget on the taskbar as a ghost preview. when i click it should place it there and it should also open the folder (if it was a
folder widget that was placed of course)"*; *"same behaviour should be implemented for the widgets placed inside the folder."*

**The add page at the top, the bar's width** (`EditDeck.Open`, `PanelLayout`). Whatever opens it — the edit bar's Add, a bar's
"+", a folder column's "+" — the add page hangs from the whole edit bar: 12 DIP off it (§584's gap; over it from an edit bar at
the display's foot), exactly as wide, flush with its sides, no beak (there is no one entry to point at: a "+" far down on a bar
opens it as often as Add does). Add's entry is marked open whatever opened it. Its tiles fill the width: as many as 200 DIP each
fit (`PanelMetrics.TileLeast`; §578's three at most across 548 DIP gone with `TilesMost`), five across a 1920 DIP display's bar.
Adding into an open folder, which takes the display's height under the edit bar (§329), it stops short of the folder's lists and
their buttons, a line's room past them for the ghost coming in (`FolderFlyout.ContentOnScreen`, taken as the page opens:
`addingClear`, `EditDeckModel.Clear`) — so the column's "+" that opened it stays to be pressed again and the ghost stays in
sight —, where that leaves it 200 DIP (`EditDeck.AddLeastDip`: its search and two rows of tiles); over the folder else.
Deleted: §576's hanging from the "+" — `EditDeckModel.From`, `Placement.From`, `EditDeck.Show`'s `from`, `PanelInput.Hung` and
Add's entry unmarked while hung, `EditDeck.Same`. The "+" pressed is kept as `Adding.Plus` only for §430's rule: the same "+"
pressed again closes the page.

**Every add has a place** (`Dock.AddAt`, `AddSpot`). A "+" adds where it stands, as before. The edit bar's own Add, with no "+"
pressed, decided: **into the folder open arranged on its display, where that folder adds** (`FolderFlyout.AddPlace`: its first
list not full, its end away from the bar; §298), **else at the bar's last "+"** — the end section's, before its first widget,
where a taskbar keeps what it shows beside the clock (the bottom section's on a bar at the side) — on the display's bar, or on
its first surface that has a "+" where the bar has none. A place known, the pick goes in at once (§297): nothing follows the
pointer from the add page any more. Deleted: `AddSpot.Follows`, `AddChosen`'s bar path (`NearestSlot`, `Follow`) and its folder
carry (`CarryInto`) — both stay for a copied or pasted widget —, `AddOf`'s three cases (one now: the place it was opened for).

**The ghost** (Dock.AddGhost.cs; `AddList.Into`, `AddGhost`). The tile under the pointer, else the one the keys are on (a widget
or a ready-made group, not greyed; a folder's head of the add tree is none: `EditDeck.Proposing`, `PickOf`), is put in at the
page's place in a copy of the config, the config itself untouched. The bars and the open folder are built from that copy
(`Dock.Seen`: `DockWindow.Items`, `PlacedIslands`): the ghost's island made as any widget's is (`SyncIslands`), each bar of that
list laid out again (`DockWindow.Build`), a folder configured again (`FolderIsland.Configure`, its `Changed`). So the ghost is the
widget at its real size and look where it goes, the bar laid out as it will stand, its neighbours gliding aside as for a carried
block (the retained scene, §358); a group is its whole folder face. On top, the ghost's own look:
- **On a bar** (`EditView.Ghost`, `Scene.Apply`): the part's drawing at `EditLook.GhostOpacity` (55 %), fading in to it (a new
  part's own fade-in skipped for it, `AnimateEdit`), the blue ghost of a carried block round it (`ShowGhost`: the accent's wash
  in an accent outline) — "a blue rectangle that looks like a ghost preview".
- **In an open folder** (`FolderFlyout.Ghost`): the line, card and all, at the same 55 %, the folder's carried-line ghost
  (`ghostVisual`) round its card.

**Nothing written.** No save, no step of the undo, the add page's counts (§586) still the config's: the copy is the ghost's
alone, gone with the pointer off the tile, the page closed (`EndAdding` → `Unghost`), edit mode ended, or the config changed
under it by anything else (a ghost made of another config is none: `Ghost` compares its `Base`). Its data sources are not
started (`DataSources` follows the config): a weather ghost shows what an unread weather widget does until it is added — a
hover reads nothing from far away (since §635 it shows the samples instead). A widget whose island opens something of this PC as it is made opens it for the ghost too,
and closes it again as the ghost goes.

**The place with nothing under the pointer**, decided: the slim marker stays — the bar's blue line (`Layout.InsertionRect`,
`AddSlotOn`, its "+" drawn pressed) and in a folder the accent bar across its list a carried line's landing draws
(`FolderFlyout.AddingAt`, `MarkFor`). A ghost outline with no widget chosen would have no size to open the bar by, and the bar
would jump twice, once for the outline and again for the widget; the line takes no room. It goes while a ghost stands.

**The click** (`PanelActed`, `AddChosen`, `Ghosted`) puts in that very copy (`TakeGhost`, `placing`): the same ids, so the
widget the ghost laid out is the widget put in — its island kept, nothing made again, nothing moving; it only fades up to whole.
One `Apply`, one step of the undo, the focus on it (§297). A folder put on the bar is picked and opens at once, arranged, as a click on its face does (`EditPick`, `OpenArranged`; a
widget stays as it went in); a folder's line is picked, as before. Where the licence refuses (§545) the bars go back to the
config.

**The stage map** (Dock.Stage.cs) says "Ghost": its key, and where it stands on a bar or among the open folder's lines.

Tests: `AddListTests.AGhostIsThePickPutInACopy` (the config untouched, the ghost's list the one adding at once makes but for the
new id, a group's folder its machine read for it alone, a folder's column, nothing for another command or type),
`APlaceTakesThePickAtOnce`; `SettingsPanelTests` (`TheAddListIsAPageOfItsOwn`: as wide as the bar, Add marked whatever opened it;
`TheAddPagesWidgetsAreTilesSideBySide`: as many as 200 DIP fit); `EditBarFolderPictures` (the Add's place, no `Follows`; the
pick applied, no folder closed). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `EditDeckClickTests.AnEntryOpensItsFlyoutAnotherSwitchesItItselfClosesIt`
(hung from the whole bar; a tile under the pointer its pick, a folder's head none, the pointer gone none),
`AddGhostStageTests.TheAddPagesPickStandsWhereItGoesAndItsClickPutsItThere` (the real windows: the edit bar's Add's ghost on the
bar, the file unchanged, gone with the pointer; clicked, in the file, Ctrl+Z out; a bar's last "+": the world clock clicked, its
folder open; its column's "+": a clock a ghost among its lines, then in the file), `PanelPopupPlaceTests.TheAddListOpensUnderTheAddButton…`
(`CheckAdd`: 12 DIP off the edit bar, as wide, on either display), `MenuToggleTests` (each "+"'s and Add's page as wide as the
edit bar, never on its "+"), `FolderColumnsTests.EveryColumnsPlusOpensTheAddList…`, `SceneTreeTests.SettingsPanelSheets`
(panel-add-, panel-plus-: `HungFromTheBar`). Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.AddGhostSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): addghost-page- (the page
at the top, the place's line), -widget- (Keep awake's ghost), -group- (the world clock's), -folder- (a clock's among the world
clock's lines), -placed- (the world clock put in, its folder open), each dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › Add: the page under the edit bar, as wide; Keep awake under the pointer: a faint Keep awake in a blue box
before the tray, the end section stepping aside; off it: gone, the line back; clicked: there, solid. A bar's "+" › World clock
clicked: its folder open. Its column's "+": a clock under the pointer in the folder, faint; clicked: in. Ctrl+Z: out again.

## 608. A divider between Appearance and the selection's entries (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"add a little divider between appearance and folder"*.

**The divider** (`PanelLayout.Divider`, `PanelMetrics.DividerTall`; drawn in `SettingsPanel.Paint.cs`'s `Bar`): a command
bar's AppBarSeparator — a hairline (1 px, `PanelLayout.Hair`, the one the painter's rims use too) 20 DIP tall in the bar's
middle, in DividerStrokeColorDefault, 8 after the last page's entry and 8 before the selection's room (§596), where §596's
gutter of 16 stood:

    ⠿ [⚙ Karpo] … [🎨 Appearance] | [📁 Folder] [🗓 Calendar]            [⊗] [+ Add] [✓ Done]

- **Only with something selected**: with nothing in the room (§584) a divider would set apart nothing; `Divider` is empty
  then. Where it stands never changes: its hairline is taken from the room (256 DIP less a hairline), so the entries, the
  room, Add and Done stand where they stood and the bar stays one width (§578) whether it shows or not.
- **Not a control**: no part of `Header` — nothing to press, no stop of the keys, no element of a screen reader's; a point on
  it is no hit.
- **A narrow display**: the same with the pages' entries their icons alone; the room never under two icons and the hairline.

No config, no new words.

Tests: `SettingsPanelTests` (`TheBarIsACommandBarOfThePages`: 8, the hairline 20 DIP tall in the middle, 8, the room 256 DIP
less it; `TheBarIsOneWidthWhateverIsSelected`: the divider none with nothing selected (with errors or not), else right after
Appearance's entry and before the first of the selection's, 8 either side, one place in every state, no part on it, no hit;
`TheBarNarrowsOnANarrowDisplay`: the same with icons alone, none with nothing); `EditDeckMoveTests`;
`SceneTreeTests.SelectionSheets` (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): the divider in every picture with a selection, none in
selection-none-; the bar 1728 px in every one, as before.

By hand: edit mode — nothing right of Appearance; a widget clicked: a faint line between Appearance and its entry, nothing
else moving.

## 604. A row as tall as its words: every second line wrapped and shown whole; three UI tests of the tip made true again (2026-11-09)

The bug, seen in several pictures of the Karpo page: Karpo Pro's "What counts as a widget" drew its name over its own words.
Its note says four lines (`settings.license.counts.*`, joined by line breaks under the name), and its row was laid out for
two. **Root cause**: a line's height came from what kind of row it was, never from its words — `PanelLayout.Tall` gave 48
for one line and 60 for any row with a second line (§548), whatever that line said; the painter drew the second line as one
Caption line centred 16 DIP under the name, so four lines of it (64 DIP, centred on that one line) ran up over the name and
down past the card. A description too long for its room was cut short instead (a group's sentence whole only in a tooltip,
§529), the add page's tiles and a heading's caption the same: one line, whatever was to say.

**Now** a row is as tall as its words, measured, in the one place that lays the panel out:

- `IPanelText.Tall(text, px, width)`: how tall words stand wrapped at a width, every line, their own line breaks kept
  (`GfxPanelText`: DirectWrite's, `PopupPaint.WrappedTall`; the tests' `SettingsPanelTests.Words` wraps at spaces as a
  stand-in).
- `PanelLayout.Tall(row, left, w)`: a row with a second line — a description, a group's sentence, a mixed row's split, a
  note's words — 12 + its name's Body line (20) + its second line wrapped at the room its words have in that row
  (`NameRoom`, up to its control column) + 12; at least 60, so one line is as before. `SecondTall(line)`, and
  `WordsAt(line)`: the name's and the second line's rects, centred in the line, which the painter draws in
  (`PopupPaint.Wrapped`, no most). A heading's caption the same (`CaptionTall`). The add page's tiles as tall as the most
  any of them says (8 + 20 + its lines + 8, at least 52), all of a run alike.
- Nothing is cut any more in a second line, so a group's sentence needs no tooltip: `TipOf`'s case for it is gone.
- A name stays one Body line, cut at its room as before; a row that acts says what it does in one line before its button
  (cut, as before).

No config change; no string changed. At the corpus's fresh config three rows grow: Karpo Pro's state ("Free version", its
note in two lines at the flyout's width), "What counts as a widget" (its four lines: 108 DIP), and the add page's tiles
where "Rotation lock on/off" says why it is greyed in two lines.

Tests: `RowTextFitTests` (new, test-first: every page — Karpo, Accounts, Displays and layouts, Taskbar, Appearance, a
folder's, a widget's, several widgets', the add page, every bar kind's and line kind's page — every expander open, each tab
chosen, at 100, 125, 150, 175, 200 and 250 %: no name breaks a line, every second line's measured lines and the name inside

(`ASentenceTooLongForItsLineWrapsWhole`, was `ASentenceCutShortIsWholeInItsTooltip`; every kind's sentences whole),
`MenuRulesTests.EveryControlIsOfItsSizeClass` (R19: 48, 60, or 60 and 16 more a line), `SettingsPanelTests`,
`LookPreviewTests`. Picture (`SceneTreeTests.RowTextFitSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-604-karpo-pro-<100|150>-<dark|light>.png,
the Karpo page landed on Karpo Pro.

## 609. A holiday calendar's region in its row: its dropdown before the calendar's colour button and Remove (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"region selector for public holidays should be on the same line as the color selector"*.

**One row** (Karpo › Services › Public holidays). A country with regions is one row: its name, then at the line's end its
region's dropdown, 8 DIP before its colour button, the colour 4 before Remove, Remove ending where every control of the page
ends (16 in, §548). §554 to §608 the region was a row of its own under the country (§594: a row of the card, no well). The
dropdown keeps §587's one width, 240 DIP, so its list hangs flush under it as every list does and every region of the card
stands in one column; a country without regions (France) has its colour button and Remove alone, where the other's stand,
so the buttons are one column too. The dropdown does not end where a value's box ends (the buttons take that place): the
grid it keeps is the card's own, the buttons at the end, the dropdowns one column before them.

**The one mechanism, a row's pair** (`PanelRow.Pair`). §568 stood a colour's dark half in its light half's line: a second row,
its own item, key and value, whose control stands in the line. The region is that: the thing's row (`PanelRowKind.Item`, its
buttons) holds its one choice as its pair (`PanelRows.One`; `FlyoutItem.Beside`, a thing of one choice, which `OptionMenu`
sets where it set `Nests` — `Nests` is a folder's face's alone again). Its control is a dropdown before the buttons
(`PanelLayout.Controls`), drawn by the one dropdown painter every choice row now uses (`PanelPainter.Dropdown`); its key is
the region's as before ("…/Public holidays/Switzerland/Region"), so the dock opens and sets it as it did (`PanelRows.Find`,
`PanelLayout.Row`), `LineOf` finds it in the country's line as it finds a dark half, and `PathTo` lands on either. A dropdown's
words cut in its box are whole in its tooltip, read from the row the control is of (`ValueRoom` of a row, `TipOf` by `Row`).

**Where the name would not stand whole** — a long name (Bosnia and Herzegovina) on the flyout's 580 DIP, or any on a narrow
display's flyout — the region stands a line of its own right under its country, §594's way (`LayPage`, `Whole`: the name
measured, a gutter off the controls). Nothing ever runs over a name, and no line grows taller. Switzerland, the United
States, the United Kingdom stand beside at 580.

**The keys and a screen reader**: the region, the colour, Remove, as they stand (`Stops`: the controls in order); stacked,
the country's buttons, then its region. A screen reader hears "Region · Switzerland" (a combo box, its value Zürich), "Color ·
Switzerland", "Remove · Switzerland" as before: the region named for the row it is the pair of (`PanelLayout.HolderOf`), in
its line or under it, saying its own value (`DeckUia.Tree`: a pair's control its own row's value, §568's dark half's too).
§554's naming by the last thing with rows nested under it is gone with those rows.

No config change; nothing written differently.

Tests: `HolidaysPanelTests.ACalendarsRegionIsItsDropdownInItsRow` (Switzerland one 48 DIP line, its controls the region's 240 ×
32 dropdown 8 before the colour button, Remove at the controls' end; no region line in the card; France's buttons where
Switzerland's are; each name whole; the keys region, colour, Remove; the screen reader's names and Zürich; the popup, Bern
picked), `ARegionStandsUnderItsCountryWhereItsNameWouldNotStandWhole` (Bosnia and Herzegovina at 580 DIP, Switzerland and it at
420: the region a 48 DIP line right under, as far in, the country's buttons alone, the keys on to it, named for its country),
`AddRegionColourOffAndRemove`; `KarpoMenuTests.EachPublicHolidayCalendarHasItsOwnColour`,
`HolidaysTests.TheMenuListsTheCalendarsInALevelOfTheirOwn` (`Beside`); `MenuRulesTests` (R1: a thing's choice in its row no
level; R19 `EveryControlIsOfItsSizeClass`: the region a value's 240 × 32); `PanelControlsTests`; `DropdownWidthTests`
(`ValueRoom` of a row). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `HolidaysPanelUiTests` (Germany's region, in its row, typed to Bayern),
`PanelPopupPlaceTests`, `EditDeckClickTests`. Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.HolidaysPanelSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR):
panel-holidays-<dark|light>.png (Switzerland with Zürich in its row, France), panel-holidays-region-<dark|light>.png (its
dropdown open, hung from its box).

By hand: edit mode › Karpo › Services › Public holidays: Switzerland, its region's dropdown, its colour, its bin on one line;
France's colour and bin under Switzerland's; Tab from the region to its colour to its bin.

## 607. The weather's place a caption, never its heading: under the current weather's hero, after it the reading's age (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the weather widget should not show the location all the way at the top. it should display it
smaller somewhere else."*

**What stood at the top.** The current weather's Full (§590) was a Header — the place's pin, the place in the Body strong,
the reading's age at the trailing gutter — over the Hero. In a weather folder (the face's flyout) that made the place the
first and the boldest words of the whole folder, over the temperature it is about.

**Now** (Windows 11's weather says where it is the same way: small, in the secondary ink, after the weather). The place is
never a heading on any weather or air line; it is a caption — the Caption's 12, the secondary ink — leading its caption
line, what else that line says after it with the kit's dot (`PlaceLabel`, the one place the weather's and the air's lines
say it):

| Widget | Size | The place |
|---|---|---|
| Current weather (`weatherNow`) | Compact | the row's caption under the conditions, "Zürich · Feels like 15° · High 18° · Low 8°" (unchanged) |
| Current weather | Full | no header: the Hero (glyph, temperature, conditions beside it, what it feels like under it), then the place a caption line under it, the age after it: "Zürich · 15 min ago" (`PlaceLabel.Foot`) |
| Air quality (`airQuality`) | both | the row's caption under "Air quality", "Zürich · European AQI" (unchanged) |

The hourly and daily forecasts and the air's pollutants, pollen and day say no place, as before. The age follows the place
only where the place still reads whole beside it — the place wins, as on the header — and keeps its ink (the critical red
when the reading is stale, why none is newer where it failed). Nothing is cut or dropped: each size says what it said
(§590's fixed content), the Full the same words less the pin, which was a picture.

**Its size.** Full is the hero with two captions (`LineHero.Height(…, 2)`), five cells where the header over the hero was
six (`ListWidgets`: `Cells = 5`, Full 5); Compact unchanged at three. No file change: a line's size is its word, not its
cells (§590), so nobody's file is touched.

**Deleted.** The Full header (`LineRow` with the pin, the strong place and the age at its end) and its fit of the age;
`ListHeightOffscreenTests.FixedContentIsNeverClippedAtTheLargestText`, whose one case, the current weather's 222 px at
225 % text over the 200 it was cut at, is now 168 px and cut by nothing (`ThePlaceIsACaptionUnderWhatTheLineSays` holds
every weather and air line inside its line at 225 %).

Tests: `WeatherRowsTests.ThePlaceIsACaptionUnderTheHeroItsAgeAfterIt` (was `TheAgeStandsAtTheHeadersEndAlone`: the place
the Caption's height, under the hero and every other piece, the age after it on its line, none without a place, none where
the place would not read whole), UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `WeatherSplitLinesTests.ThePlaceIsACaptionUnderWhatTheLineSays`
(the current weather and the air quality at both sizes at 100, 150 and 225 % text: the place said once, the Caption's
height, something larger over it, nothing outside the line), `EachSizeSaysTheSameAndATallerLineNoMore` (unchanged: each
size the same words), `SizedLinesTests` (Full five whole cells), `ListGutterTests` (the current weather ends free of the
trailing gutter), `PlacesAnatomyTests.TheWeatherIsAHeroOverItsPlace` (was `TheWeatherIsAHeaderOverAHero`: nothing over the
Hero, nothing in the Body strong, the last line a Caption at the text edge) and `TheAirQualityIsARow` (its Compact, the row
with its caption, the place a Caption at the text edge; it still measured the one row §590 took away). Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR, `WeatherSplitLinesTests.WeatherSplitPictures`): `artifacts\weatherplace\before\`
and `after\` — weather-split-weather-, weather-split-air- (dark, light, text225-dark): every weather and air kind, Compact
over Full.
