## 615. A CalDAV calendar asked for every series, whatever its time: a server that matches a series by its first occurrence alone misses none (2026-11-09) — no query by time at all since §616: every object kept whole (2026-11-09)

The person, told a CalDAV read asks for the objects with something in the window and expands series itself (2026-11-09):
*"yeah but if a caldav server does not calcualte that we miss that event"*.

**What could be missed**: RFC 4791 §9.9 has a calendar-query's time-range match a recurring event by its instances, so a
yearly birthday begun in 2016 comes back for November 2026. A server that gets recurrence wrong — exceptions, RDATE, BYxxx
rules, zones, a DTSTART long ago — or matches only the object's own DTSTART and DTEND leaves it out, and Karpo, which
expands what it is given (`ICalendar`, its `RecurrenceTests`), had nothing to expand.

**Now** (`DavReader.SeriesAsync`): after a calendar's window (the time-range query, its halving on a 507 as before), the
calendar is asked, once a read, for every series whatever its time — two calendar-queries, no time-range:

    <c:calendar-query xmlns:d="DAV:" xmlns:c="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:caldav">
      <d:prop><d:getetag/><c:calendar-data/></d:prop>
      <c:filter><c:comp-filter name="VCALENDAR"><c:comp-filter name="VEVENT">
        <c:prop-filter name="RRULE"/>
      </c:comp-filter></c:comp-filter></c:filter>
    </c:calendar-query>

and the same with `<c:prop-filter name="RDATE"/>` (a comp-filter's prop-filters must all match, so one query cannot ask for
either). A series' overrides (RECURRENCE-ID) are in its own resource and come with it. The answers are merged with the
window's by href, each object once, and the dock's expansion decides what falls in the window, as it always did. Series are
few, so the window stays the main query; what a series query brings that has nothing in the window expands to nothing.

**A server that will not**: one that refuses those queries (a 4xx or 5xx: a filter it does not take), cuts one short (a
507, whole or among its answers — what came is kept) or does not answer in time keeps today's read: the calendar its
window's objects, not failed, not marked incomplete, nothing in the sync report — it is no fault the person can mend. The
read then asks no other calendar for its series, so such a server costs one request a read, never a timeout a calendar. A
sign-in refused is the account's, as for any request.

No config change; nothing kept differently (the cache keeps occurrences, `PimCache.Keep`).

Tests: `DavTests.ASeriesTheServerLeavesOutOfTheWindowIsStillShown` (a fake server matching a time-range by DTSTART/DTEND
alone: a 2016 birthday on the 14th, a 2015 lunch's RDATE on the 25th, a weekly standup, a one-off, in November 2026; three
REPORTs a calendar), `AnObjectBothAnswersGiveIsKeptOnce`, `AServerThatRefusesTheSeriesQueryIsReadByItsWindow` (400, 501,
507: the window's objects, nothing failed or incomplete, one series query in the read),
`TheSeriesQueryAsksForEveryObjectWithTheRuleWhateverItsTime`; the 507 tests' fake answers the series queries with none.

## 606. A ready-made group's ghost opens its folder too; the Appearance marks the mode Windows is in (2026-11-09) — the mode a setting, the page in one mode, no marks, since §613 (2026-11-09); the ghost folder whole since §625 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when placing a folder group it should show the folder contents as ghost preview as well not only
the faces on the taskbar."*; *"in the styles it should be marked which style is currently active (dark or light.)"*

**The group's folder open as a ghost** (Dock.AddGhost.cs: `GhostFolder`, `UnghostFolder`, `GhostTaken`). §593's ghost of a
ready-made group was its face on the bar alone; the click then opened its folder. Now, while the group's tile is under the
pointer (or the keys), the folder the ghost put on the bar also stands open from that face, exactly as the click opens it:
the folder's own view (`FolderView`, the one `ShowFolder` will show), arranged, placed off the ghost's face by the folder's
own Alignment, its lines the group's — all made of the ghost's copy of the config, through the folder's own layout, nothing
drawn by hand. It is opened as a look (`FlyoutHost.Previewing`): the add page keeps the keys and its search. It wears the
ghost's look (`FolderFlyout.Ghosted`): the whole folder — panels, lines, its "+" and width buttons — at
`EditLook.GhostOpacity` (55 %, `FlyoutHost.Opacity`, a visual over its coming in and going), the ghost of a carried line
(the accent's wash in the accent's outline) round its lists, and nothing of it takes the pointer (`PassesThrough`; the dock
asks a kept view too, `FolderPassesThrough`). Off the tile, another pick, the page closed, edit mode ended, the config
changed under it: the view is let go of at once, before the ghost's island goes (`Reghost`, `Unghost`). Nothing written,
as §593: no save, no undo step, no selection changed (it is no open folder: `openFolders`, the edit bar's Folder page and
the bar's lock know nothing of it).

**The click** opens the folder as before (`AddChosen` → `OpenArranged` → `ShowFolder`), which now finds the ghost's view
standing (`GhostTaken`): that very window shown again — not closed and opened — whole, the focus taken as a folder opening
takes it (`FlyoutHost.Own`: a look made a showing of its own). So it does not move or blink; it only goes from faint to
whole.

**Another folder open**, decided: one folder at a time, so the click closes it (`ShowFolder`'s rule). While the ghost stands
it steps aside (`FolderFlyout.Aside`: out of sight, nothing of it to press) and is back exactly as it was once the ghost
goes; the click closes it for real. (Adding a group always adds onto a bar: a folder open arranged on the same bar hides
that bar's "+" and the edit bar's Add then adds into the folder, so this is another display's folder, or another surface's.)

**Not done, decided**: the add page keeps its height while a group is under the pointer. It hangs from the edit bar's top
and can reach over the ghost's folder (the folder's top under it, as the page stands over any arranged folder, §329): a
page that shortened for the ghost would move its tiles' room under the pointer, lose the hover and grow again.

**The mode Windows is in, marked** (`LookPreview.ModeOf`, `ModesOver`; `PanelPainter.Preview`, `ColourButton`;
`PanelLayout.NowDotUnder`, `NowDotBefore`; `PanelMetrics.NowDot`). The mode is the panel's theme's — Windows' own look as
the dock reads it (`Dock.SettingsLookOf`), the very mode the bars wear the halves of (§568) — so it follows Windows live,
the panel drawn again as Windows' look changes, as before. Chosen, the Windows 11 way of saying "this one is in use" without
new words:
- **Over the preview**: in its Caption line, over the middle of each half's top edge (left and right of the slanted line's
  top, §582), the mode's name — Windows' own words, "Dark", "Light" (`settings.appearance.dark|light`) — the one Windows is
  in now in the text's ink, Semibold, the accent's dot (5 DIP, an InfoBadge's) before it, the other TextFillColorSecondary;
  kept clear of "Preview". Naming both halves says what the split is; the dot says which one is on. Not dimming the other
  half: the preview is there to show its colours as they are.
- **On each colour pair**: the button of Windows' mode its sun or moon in the accent (AccentFillColorDefault, legible on
  either ground), the accent's dot under it level with its swatch's foot; the other button as before.
- **A screen reader**: that half's name "Background · Dark, active" (`dock.uia.active`), the preview "Preview of Appearance
  · Dark, active" (`DeckUia.Things`'s `now`, from `EditDeck.AccessTree`).
- **High contrast**: Windows' one look, neither mode — nothing named, nothing marked.
The Taskbar page's menu preview, split the same way, is marked the same way. No new string, no config change.

Tests: `AppearanceModeNowTests` — `TheModeMarkedIsTheOneWindowsLooksIn` (the injected theme's mode, none in high contrast),
`EachModesNameStandsOverItsHalf`, `AScreenReaderHearsWhichModeIsActive` (each mode injected in turn: the pair's half and the
preview "…, active", the other not; none in high contrast); UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheMarksFollowTheModeWindowsIsIn` (the page
painted in each injected mode: the accent's dot under that mode's button of every pair in sight and not the other's; the
accent over that half alone in the Caption line; pictures appearance-now-dark|light.png). `AddGhostStageTests.TheAddPagesPickStandsWhereItGoesAndItsClickPutsItThere`
(the real windows: the world clock under the keys: "GhostFolder" on the stage map, its key the ghost's, standing somewhere,
55 % shown, its "GhostLine"s the group's, no "Folder" open, the file unchanged; the page closed: all of it gone, the file
unchanged; again and clicked: in the file, the "Folder" open whole where the ghost's stood, no ghost). Pictures
`SceneTreeTests.AddGhostSheets` addghost-group- (the face's ghost and its folder open over it, faint, the outline round it;
`Ghosted`, 55 %) and -placed- (whole), each dark and light. The stage map gains "GhostFolder", "GhostLine", "Aside", and the
"Folder" entry's index says how much of it shows (hundredths).

By hand: edit mode › a bar's "+" › World clock under the pointer: its face faint in a blue box on the bar and its folder
open over it, faint, its clocks in it; off the tile: both gone; clicked: the folder there, whole, where it stood. Edit mode
› Appearance: "● Dark  Light" over the preview's halves (in dark mode), every pair's moon blue with a dot under it; switch
Windows to light: "Light" marked, the suns.

## 611. An hour's and a day's hover band reaches the line's edges: the forecasts' targets the kit's items, on the whole line a sized form stands in (2026-11-09) — every band across a line as wide as the others, the first and the last no wider, since §632 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the weather widgets like the graph or the daily forecast when hovering dont show the hover area
properly. according to our design guidelines it should span to the top and bottom and left and right with no padding
there."* The guideline is §428's (and §436's): what an item lights is a band of its line, edge to edge and top to foot,
touching the next; what it shows keeps its own padding inside.

**Why it did not.** The forecast lines (§590: the hourly Graph and List, the daily List and Graph) each lit a plate of their
own (`WeatherLineTile.Plate`): rounded, and inset three ways — the columns stood from gutter to gutter
(`WeatherColumns.Of`), an hour's plate was its column of the graph inside the graph's housing (`DayGraph.ColumnOf`, the
panel's pad round it), a day's row at Full stood half a panel gutter in, under 4 DIP of air, 1 px short top and bottom.
And under all of them, shared: a sized line (§432, §442) draws and is hit in its form alone, in the middle of its whole
cells (`CellIsland.Scrolled`), so the room over and under the form — up to half a cell either side — was nobody's, unlit and
dead, whatever a line lit inside its form. The tests never saw it: they drew a line at the height it asks for, never at the
cells the folder gives it.

**Now.**
- **The line a form stands in** (`CellIsland.LineAround`): a sized line's form box grown back to its whole cells (the same
  half-of-what-is-left `Scrolled` takes, `Over`), any other line's box as it is. What an item's band reaches; what the line
  shows still keeps to the form.
- **Items across a line** (`LineItem.Across`): bands at the items' middles, each the line's whole height, the first from its
  leading edge, the last to its trailing one, neighbours meeting halfway. **Down a line** (`LineItem.Down`): a count of
  bands as tall as each other, the first from the top, the last to the foot. `LineItem.At`: the band under a point.
- **The forecast lines' one answer** (`WeatherLineTile.Bands`): an hour's or a day's band, which `CardTarget`, `CardTip` (its
  part) and the light (`WeatherLineTile.Light`: `LineItem.Light`, square, the line's clip rounding a corner; the keys' ring
  just inside the band) all ask; the subclasses say only where their items stand. The hourly Graph's bands at its points
  (`DayGraph.CentreOf`), its point's ring kept; the hourly List's, the daily List's at Compact and the daily Graph's at their
  columns' middles (`WeatherColumns.Bands`); the daily List at Full a week of rows filling the line, each day's row of words
  in its band's middle on the gutter, as the flyout placed it.
- **A split switch** (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the mobile hotspot at Full: `SwitchIsland`) is the same case, found by the rule
  below: its page's part, the whole line but its switch, lit the form alone, 3 px short of the line's top and foot at 150 %; it
  lights `LineAround` now.
- **Gone**: `WeatherLineTile.Plate`, `WeatherColumns.At`, `WeatherDaysTile.Places`/`PlateOf`/`DayRows`, the hours' `PlateOf`,
  `DayGraph.PointAt` and `ColumnOf`.
- **Unchanged**: the current weather is one thing to press, lit whole by the folder (§379); the air's four press nothing
  (§590) and light nothing.

**The rule, held for every kind** (`LineHoverRuleTests.AnItemLightsItsLineToItsEdges`): every kind a list holds, at every
size it offers, in a folder at the height the open folder gives it; each target lit under the pointer lights where it
takes the pointer, square, and every side of it is the line's edge, the next item's, or against something drawn between
them (a heading, an axis, a row with nothing to do) — but the room under the last of a list, which §436 leaves unlit. A
control keeps its plate (where it takes the pointer or what it lights no taller than 48 DIP and short of half the line's
width, or no wider and short of half its height: a button, a stepper, a slider lighting its thumb, a notification's ×), the calendar's month, day and week grids theirs (§428's "not the month's days"),
a line the folder lights whole is the folder's. Red first on the tip it landed on, every forecast line at both sizes, e.g.
*"WeatherDays Full 540×420: item 1 lights 6-534 × 10-63: a rounded plate, 4 of its corners unlit"*, *"… 10 px of the line
unlit past its top, nothing drawn in it"*, and the hourly graph's hours 20 px short of the line's left edge, 14 of its top.

**The clock and the pin did not light** (`LineHoverRuleTests.OnTheScreenOnlyAWholeLineLights`): not this. The test worked
its points out as if the panel stood centred in the folder's window, which it no longer does (the window reaches past the
panel, `FolderOffscreenTests.Point`): the pointer landed beside the lines and lit none. It reads them off the panel where it
stands now (`LineClickTests.Client`); the folder lit the clock and the pin all along.

No config, no new words.

Tests: `LineHoverRuleTests` (`AnItemLightsItsLineToItsEdges`, new; `OnTheScreenOnlyAWholeLineLights`, its points off the
panel), `WeatherTargetsTests` (`EachDayIsATargetAndItsClickSearchesThatDay`: every point of the line a day, the first at its
top, the last at its foot, the same day at either edge; `EachHourIsATarget`: over the graph the hour under the pointer, the
first and the last at the line's ends). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR; `LineHoverRuleTests.TheWeatherHoveredPictures`):
weather-hover-<kind>-<dark|light>.png, each weather and air kind a folder of its sizes, an item in the middle of each lit;
before and after in `artifacts\weatherhover\`.

By hand: a folder with the hourly graph and the daily forecast (List, Full; Graph): an hour under the pointer lights its
slice of the line from the top to the foot, the first hour from the line's left edge; a day's row lights the line's width,
the first from its top, the last to its foot; the keys' ring inside the band.

## 616. A CalDAV calendar kept whole and synced with sync-collection: every year shown, a quiet calendar one request (2026-11-09)

The person approved the plan (2026-11-09, `artifacts\caldav-full-sync-plan.md`, every decision its default): Karpo keeps
a full copy of each CalDAV calendar and updates it with `sync-collection` (RFC 6578), so any date, past or future, shows
without a read, and a quiet calendar costs one small request an interval. Microsoft accounts are as they were.

**Before**: a calendar-query with a time-range, the fourteen months of the store's window, asked again in halves when cut
short, and since §615 two more queries for every series whatever its time; the events of the window kept in
calendar-cache.json as occurrences. A view looking further widened the window and read every account again.

**Now** (`Karpo.Accounts\Dav\CalendarSync.cs`, `Karpo.Dock\Pim\CalendarMirror.cs`; docs\accounts.md, "CalDAV" and
"Offline"):

- **The reader keeps nothing; the dock holds the cursor.** `ICalendarSync.SyncCalendarsAsync` (Reading.cs) gets, per
  calendar, each object's href and etag, the sync token and the tag of the last whole sync; it answers what to put in
  (href, etag, the object as kept) and what to take out, and the token and tag to keep. `IAccountReader`, the Microsoft
  and IMAP readers are unchanged; `DavReader.CalendarsAsync` answers every calendar whole, for a caller that keeps
  nothing (the dock never asks so).
- **The gate**: the home's one PROPFIND asks each calendar's `sync-token`, `getctag` and `supported-report-set` too; a
  ctag (else sync-token) unchanged is nothing to do.
- **sync-collection**, Depth 0, getetag only: changed (an etag differs or is new) and gone (404); no token, the whole
  listing compared by etag (what is held and not listed taken out only after the last page). Pages (a 507 for the
  calendar itself) asked with each token given, 1000 at most, stopped when the token does not move; the calendar is then
  not all there and nothing is taken out. A token refused (403, 409, 410, `valid-sync-token`) is let go once for the
  whole listing. A server without it (not among its reports, or 400/403/405/501 to it): PROPFIND Depth 1 etags.
- **Fetched** in calendar-multigets of a hundred, two at a time; a multiget cut short halves (`DavReader.MultigetAsync`,
  the address books' halving made one). **The token is kept only when every change came.** hrefs are one key however a
  server escapes them (`DavClient.Key`). Once a day the whole listing is compared, for a server that loses deletions.
  429/503 fail the account (retried as any failure). At most 50,000 objects a calendar; past it, "not all shown".
- **What is kept** (`KeptICalendar`): the rows' fields, zones and series; the notes only as their meeting's link; no
  attendees, alarms, attachments. A version number: a mirror of another is downloaded again whole. The recurrence and
  meeting tests parse every iCalendar of theirs through `Kept.Parse`, which holds the kept form to the raw one's
  occurrences over five ranges in four zones.
- **On disk**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\calendar-mirror\<account id>\<hash>.bin`, a JSON header and the objects' JSON
  deflated, DPAPI for this user (`Karpo.CalendarMirror.v1`), DurableFile with its `.bak`; token and objects one file. A
  file that does not read is its `.bak`, else deleted and downloaded again; a held one written at the next sync. Deleted
  with its calendar turned off (downloaded again when on) or no longer listed, and with its account (a sweep at the start
  for one removed while the dock was not running). calendar-cache.json keeps Microsoft accounts only; a DAV account an
  older file holds is ignored.
- **In memory** (`EventIndex`): each object parsed once, with the UTC span it can have events in (a day wider each side;
  an UNTIL's last, a COUNT counted once up to 1000, else open); a view expands only the objects near it. A parsed event
  keeps its meeting's link and lets go of its notes; RDATE and EXDATE lists only where there are some; a feed's
  VTIMEZONEs built only for a TZID nobody knows; a plain yearly rule walks no year's days. The kept text stays deflated.
- **The store** (`AccountCalendars`): a CalDAV account has no window — only its interval makes it due, a view of 2040
  reads nothing. Changes are parsed and written on the pool, then merged under the lock. A first download is written and
  shown every 1,000 objects. A start takes the mirrors in before its first read: an account whose calendars were all
  whole and synced less than the interval ago reads nothing.

Gone: `DavReader.EventsAsync` (the time-range query and its six halvings), `Query`, §615's `SeriesAsync` and `Series`,
`PimCache.Keep`'s expansion of CalDAV objects, `ICalendar.Occurrences`. No migration: a calendar-cache.json of before is
read for its Microsoft accounts; the CalDAV calendars download once.

Measured (`CalDavScaleTests`, 10,000 generated objects, alone): a first sync against the fake server 1.5 s (100
multigets), parsing 0.2 s, 8.3 MB held (0.7 MB of it the deflated text), a month 0.6 ms, a year 2.1 ms, the file 0.75 MB
written in 24 ms and read in 234 ms.

Tests: `DavSyncTests` on `FakeCalDav` (first sync in multigets of a hundred, Depth 0; a quiet calendar one PROPFIND, by
ctag or sync-token; a delta; pages, and pages that do not move; a pruned token; no sync-collection by its report set and
by 400/403/405/501; multigets cut short; the token kept only when all came; a calendar refused alone; 429 the account's;
a calendar off asks nothing; hrefs escaped two ways; lost deletions caught by the daily comparison; steps of a first
download; a stateless read whole); `KeptICalendarTests` (what is kept and what goes, the equivalence, the notes as their
link; the link kept whether the lines end CRLF or LF, the test object's ends set explicitly: a raw literal takes its
file's, and turning a CRLF checkout's into CRLF again made CR CR LF, a blank line that broke the folded notes — a test
bug, the parsers were right); `CalendarMirrorTests`; `CalDavStoreTests` (2010, 2035 and the 2016 birthday in 2026 offline with no read; a restart
in the interval and a view of 2040 read nothing; no CalDAV in calendar-cache.json; a change reaching the view and the file;
a calendar off and on; an account removed; a first download cut off resuming; a held file written later);
`CalDavScaleTests` (the index shows what every object shows; the budgets above); `DavTests.ASeriesWhateverItsTimeIsHeldAndShown`
(§615's birthday, lunch and standup, now with no query by time at all).

By hand: an account on a real CalDAV server (Nextcloud, Fastmail, iCloud): the first sync's line in karpo.log
(`Karpo: CalDAV sync: … objects in …`), the mirror's files and their size under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo\calendar-mirror`;
a year view of 2015 and of 2030 showing their events with no read; a restart reading nothing for the interval; an event
changed on the phone showing at the next interval.

## 612. Edit mode's dress one state: the Appearance shows the taskbar as out of edit mode; edit mode and the preview come and go by the motion (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when i open the appearance settings it should not highlight the widgets in any special way
anymore, it should not show the add buttons again, etc. it should basically show the appearance of the taskbar how it would
appear in normal mode. it should also remove the darker tint from the background. the transition should be a smooth
animation if animations are enabled."* — *"additionally the transition into edit mode and out of edit mode should also be
animated if enabled in settings."*

**One state** (`EditDress`, Karpo.Dock\EditDress.cs): what edit mode puts on the bars, the folders open and the display —
**None** out of edit mode, **Edit** in it, **Preview** while the Appearance page's flyout is open (`EditDresses.Of`: edit
mode on and `PanelMemory.Page` Appearance). Only Edit wears the dress (`Worn`): the dim, the blocks' outlines and washes, the
selection's ring and the focus rectangle, the "+" and the empty rooms, a face with nothing to show on the bar (`CellIsland.Arranged`),
a section's edit bar, an arranged folder's guide lines, "+" and spread window. Preview is drawn as None, edit mode on all the
same: the edit bar and its flyout stay, the selection is kept (its entry on the bar), the keys are edit mode's; the dim's
window stays, clear, so a click beside the bars is still one on the dim (it closes the flyout, §575, and the dress comes
back). Another page, the flyout closed (its entry, Escape, a click elsewhere), and the dress is back.

- **The bars** are laid out in the dress the dock last laid (`Dock.laidDress`, set by `Rebuild`; `DockWindow.Lay`'s layout
  arranged only where it is Edit). As the frame ends (`PresentChrome`, after the chrome is reconciled — the selection followed
  may have opened or closed a page), a dress other than the one laid lays every bar and folder out again in it, in that frame,
  and the chrome again where the sections moved: the dim, the bars and the folders change in one commit (§359). Edit mode's
  start and end lay out their own (`BeginEdit`, `EndEdit`), as before.
- **The dim** (`EditChromeModel.Dimmed`, `EditShade.Show(bounds, dimmed, motion)`, `Hide(motion)`) is dimmed in Edit, clear in
  Preview; the sections' edit bars none in Preview.
- **A folder open arranged** (`FolderFlyout.Dress`): plain in Preview — arranged still, drawn as at rest: its plan not an
  editing one (no guide lines, no "+", no ring), its window the panel's, not spread to the display; nothing of edit mode's
  state let go of (the selection, the clipboard) but a line carried, put back. `Rest` and `Arrange` start it dressed.

**The transitions, by the one motion** (§489; none with Animations Off or Windows' Animation effects off, `Look.Motion`):

| What | Coming in (Edit) | Going (Preview, None) |
|---|---|---|
| the dim | fades in, a large surface's Show (250 ms, decelerate) | fades out, its Hide (167 ms, accelerate); at None its window goes once it has (`Surfaces.Hide(…, afterMs)`) |
| a bar's marks (outline, wash, ring, empty rooms) | fade in (as before) | fade out where they stand, the Hide (`Scene.FadeOut`), let go of at the first update after (`LetFadedGo`); their brushes and the "+"'s looks kept until then |
| the "+" | fade in with the marks (were there at once) | fade out with them |
| the blocks | glide aside to make room (§358, as before) | glide together under the fading marks |
| the edit bar | rises and fades in (§489, as before) | as before |
| an arranged folder's lines | glide from where they showed (`Settle`) | the same |

Turned back half way (Appearance and away again), the dim fades back from where it stands (`MotionClock`), the marks fade in
anew over those still fading out. No timer of edit mode's own: the dim's window waits in the window table for its fade
(`WindowTable.Hide`'s `afterMs`, as a destroy's fade, on the table's one wake), the bar's faded marks are let go of by the next
update.

**Deleted / replaced**: `EditShade.Show(bounds)`, `Hide()` (now with their dress and motion); the "+" no longer stand at once
as edit mode begins (`ThePlusesComeAtOnceAsEditModeBegins` is `ThePlusesComeAndGoWithEditModeByTheMotion`: still at once with
motion off). No config change, no new words.

Tests: `EditDressTests.TheDressIsEditModesButWhileTheAppearanceIsOpen`; `WindowTableTests.AHideWaitsForItsFadeAndAShowingCallsItOff`;
UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `EditDressTests.TheAppearanceShowsTheBarsAsOutOfEditModeAndAnotherPageDressesThemAgain` (the real dock
on the stage: Appearance — every bar laid out as before edit mode, its widgets where they stood, no "+", the dim clear, the edit
bar and the flyout there; Taskbar — dressed again; Appearance closed — dressed again; stage-edit.json's `Dress`, `Dressed`,
`Dim`, `FolderDressed`), `RetainedBarTests.ThePlusesComeAndGoWithEditModeByTheMotion` (off: every frame before or end; on: on
the straight way, frames between), `TheDressFadesInAndOutByTheMotion`, `EditChromeFilmTests.TheDimFadesByTheMotionAndIsClearInTheAppearancesPreview`,
`AnArrangedFolderIsPlainInTheAppearancesPreview`. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.DressSheets`
(dress-edit-taskbar-, dress-preview-appearance-, dark and light), the films' strips film-dress-dim-on/-preview/-off,
film-bar-adds-on-animated/-off-animated.

By hand: edit mode — the dim, the outlines and the "+" fade in, the widgets glide apart; Appearance — they fade out and the
widgets glide together, the desktop clear, the edit bar and the Appearance flyout there; change a colour — the bar shows it
at once; Taskbar — the dress fades back; Done — it all fades out. ⚙ › General › Animations Off: each at once.

## 617. The add page's place an empty ghost from its opening, no line; a ready-made folder's ghost opens with its lines, the air quality's and the weather's too (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when adding a widget it still first shows just a blue line, this should not be. it should from teh
beginning show an empty blue rectangle. it also does not show the folder contents as a preview when adding the air quality for
example (then it should also show the contents of the folder with the air qualtiy widgets inside too.)"*

**The empty ghost** (Dock.AddGhost.cs; `AddList.Empty`, `AddGhost.Empty`). §593 decided the slim line while nothing is under
the pointer: an outline with no widget chosen "would have no size". It has one now: one standard room — one cell on a bar,
one line in a folder's column (task view's room, the one widget that is a single button on either; none of its drawing is
shown) — put in at the page's place in a copy of the config exactly as a pick's ghost is, so it goes through the one ghost
path: the bars and the folder built from that copy (`Seen`), the neighbours making room, gliding as for a carried block, the
blue ghost of a carried block round it (`EditView.GhostEmpty`: the part's drawing at 0, its outline alone; in a folder
`FolderFlyout.GhostEmpty`, the line and its card at 0, the carried line's ghost round it). It stands from the page's opening
(`OpenPanel` → `GhostOf(…, 0)`) whatever opened it — the edit bar's Add, a bar's "+", a folder column's "+" —; a tile under
the pointer or the keys turns it into that pick's ghost; off every tile it is back (the one standing kept: the bar does not
move again for it); the page closed, edit mode ended, it goes as any ghost (`EndAdding` → `Unghost`).

**No double jump.** The outline is one shape that moves: on a bar the ghost's rectangle glides and now grows (or shrinks) from
the empty room into the pick's (`Scene.ShowGhost`: `Slide` and `GrowFrom`, its visual's size too), in a folder its box
reshapes from the one line into the other (`FolderFlyout.Reshape`, the outline drawn in the panel's whole visual); with
Animations off both stand at once. The empty part's drawing is at 0 from its making, a pick's fades in to 55 % as before.

**Nothing written, nothing to press.** No save, no undo step, the counts the config's (§586). It is no pick: a click on the
page takes nothing of it (`TakeGhost`: a pick's ghost only; the empty one goes as the page closes), and a press on a ghost's
part on the bar, empty or a pick's, is a press on the bar's room (`EditPressed`): it is in no config to be carried or
selected. The stage map's "Ghost" says which (its index 1 for the empty one).

**Deleted**: §593's line — `Dock.AddSlotOn`, `EditView.Insert` in edit mode (the bar's `insertLine`, its "+" drawn pressed for
the add's place in `ShowAdds`), `FolderFlyout.AddingAt` and its accent bar across the list. `Layout.InsertionRect` stays for
files dragged over a bar at rest (`Scene.Drag`'s `dragLine`), where the bar has no room to show the new pin's cell.

**A ready-made folder's ghost opens with its lines.** On the tip this was taken from, §606 (installed after the person's
report) already does this for every ready-made group, the air quality's and the weather's as much as the world clock's:
`GhostFolder` asks only whether the ghost put a folder on a bar (its island a `FolderIsland` that is a folder), and a preset's
pick is put in as one folder with its lines (`AddList.Add(…, Preset, …)` → `Presets.AddToBar`), so no pick needs telling
apart. What the person saw was the build before §606: a group's ghost its face alone. Nothing more to fix; held by tests for
the presets the person named (their folders tall enough to reach under the page, the tile still the page's).

Tests: `AddListTests.TheEmptyGhostIsOneRoomPutInACopy` (one cell in the "+"'s section, the very list a pick at that place
makes but for its id, one line in a folder's column, the config untouched, nothing for a folder gone),
`APresetsGhostIsItsFolderWithItsLines` (air quality, weather: their folder with the preset's lines). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1):
`AddGhostStageTests.TheAddPagesPickStandsWhereItGoesAndItsClickPutsItThere` (the empty ghost on the bar as the edit bar's Add
and a bar's "+" open the page, one line among the folder's as its column's "+" does, nothing written),
`APresetsGhostOpensItsFolderWithItsLines` (a bar's "+": the empty ghost; the air quality, then the weather under the keys:
"GhostFolder" of the ghost's key, its "GhostLine"s the preset's four and three, the tile still the page's; closed: nothing of
it; the file unchanged throughout). `BarAddPictures` (no "+"
pressed for the add's place), `SceneTreeTests.AddGhostSheets`: addghost-page- (the empty ghost on the bar), -air- (the air
quality's face and its folder, faint), -folder-empty- (the empty line in the world clock's column), each dark and light;
`AddButtonPictures`' add-buttons-open- gone with the line.

By hand: edit mode › Add: an empty blue box at once before the tray, the end section stepping aside; Keep awake under the
pointer: the box grows into a faint Keep awake; off it: the empty box again; Escape: gone. A bar's "+" › Air quality under the
pointer: its face faint in the box and its folder open over it, faint, its four lines in it. A folder column's "+": an empty
box one line tall at the column's end.

## 620. A ready-made group down a side bar is one list: its lists one under the other; three heights of its own (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when the taskbar is on the side some premade configurations of widgets in the folders are in two
columns but this does not really look nice when the taskbar is shown on the side. the premade groups should therefore have a
different layout depending on if the taskbar is placed on the top and bottom or left and right."*

**The rule** (`Preset.ItemsFor`, `Preset.Stacked`, `Preset.WidthsFor`). A preset lists its lines once, as before, its lists
side by side by `PresetItem.NewList`. On a top or a bottom bar it is that. Down a left or a right bar it is one list: its lists
one under the other in their order, left to right, a divider where one ended and the next began (two lists were two cards,
and one list keeps them two), as wide as the widest of them (Markets and news Wide, Power & battery Medium). A folder opened
beside a side bar has the screen's whole height less a margin at each end (§173's room) and little of its width to spare, so
one column is what fits there; two side by side were what fitted over a bottom bar.

**Where it is decided**: the add page's pick, its ghost and its click alike (`AddList.Into` → `AddList.Add` →
`Presets.AddToBar`/`Folder`/`Lists`/`ItemsOn`, each taking the bar's `Edge`), the edge read from the place's display
(`Config.ScreenOf(owner).Edge`), so the ghost shows exactly what the click puts in (§593: the click puts in the ghost's very
copy). A new bar's own folders (`Config.FirstLayout`) and the layout of every ready-made folder are made for the bottom, as
before: a layout has no edge of its own. Stored as any folder: its `lists`, one here; no config change.

**Overrides, decided after checking every preset on a side bar** (`PresetItem.SideHeight`: a line's height in the one list,
where its height across was given only so two lists end level). Ten presets have more than one list (System, Clock and
calendar, Today, Media center, Network & internet, Bluetooth & devices, Inbox, Notes & to-do, Markets and news, Power &
battery); every other is one list already and the same on every edge. Of the ten, three needed one:
- **Clock and calendar**: the stopwatch its one row (two cells), as the clock's; three rows were to end the clock's list level
  with the calendar's. Stacked as it was, the calendar's footer was left out beside a 1440p side bar at 150 %.
- **Today**: the day's events six rows (12 cells), as the calendar's; ten were to end level with the weather's three views.
  As it was, the daily forecast was left out.
- **Markets and news**: the feed as tall as two shares (12 cells); as tall as the four was to end level with them. As it was,
  the feed was left out.

The other seven are the rule alone. Heights at 150 % with every growing line at its most, beside a 1440p side bar (936 DIP of
room): System 730, Clock and calendar 866, Today 906, Media center 772, Network & internet 818, Bluetooth & devices 852,
Inbox 726, Notes & to-do 806, Markets and news 726, Power & battery 546; none leaves anything out. Beside a 1080p side bar at
150 % (696 DIP) most give way at their foot, as across they do over a 1080p bottom bar: the combined groups are made for a
1440p screen at 150 % (`CombinedPresetTests`).

**Not done, decided**: a folder already placed is not arranged again when its bar moves to another edge. It is the person's
folder from the moment it is placed (they may have changed its lists), and nothing marks it as a preset's.

Tests: `PresetSideTests.EveryPresetIsArrangedForTheEdgeItsBarStandsOn` (every preset placed by the add page on the bottom,
the top, the left and the right, laptop and desktop: across as the recipe, at its widths; down a side one list, the lists
across joined by dividers, each line as across but the three overrides, as wide as the widest; what the ghost puts in is
`Presets.Folder` for that edge, line for line; the config untouched; only those three presets have a side height); UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `EachPresetOpenedFromALeftAndABottomBar` (every preset's folder planned from a bottom and a left bar of a
1440p display at 150 % by `FolderFlyout.Build` with the placement's room; each of more than one list stands whole down the
side bar; pictures `presetside-<id>.png`, from a bottom bar beside from a left bar, dark, and `presetside-heights.txt`).
`CombinedPresetTests` shares its stand-ins with it (`WithStandIns`, `Opened`, `AtTheirMost`).

By hand: a display's bar on the left › edit mode › "+" › Clock and calendar under the pointer: its ghost's folder one column,
the clock over the calendar; clicked: the same folder, placed. On a bottom bar: two columns, as before.

## 605. The volume's line its page's beside its controls, the level its air before the ">"; the brightness's button Windows' light or dark; an opened row one item with what it offers (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the volume slider widget should similar as the bluetooth widget when i click anywhere it should go
into the sound settings, except for the areas that are with other buttons. make sure that the buttons are properly spaced
and have the proper spacing on the side as well."*; *"the screen brigtness selector should have the toggle brigth and dark
mode on the side instead of the brightness icon."*; *"in the bluetooth submenu when i open a device it should show a line on
the left as a selection indicator and when hovering it should light up the whole background and not leave out the area
where the connect button is. the same should be done for the wifi and other similar widgets too."*

**What Bluetooth's click opens, and the volume's now.** A click on the Bluetooth line anywhere but its switch opens its page
in the folder's column, Karpo's own (§170's `IslandView.Page`, `SwitchIsland.PageTarget`), not Windows' Settings. The
volume's line in a folder (`SoundPartTile`, the sound panel's volume row) had its ">" to the same kind of page — the outputs,
the input, spatial sound and the mixer — and a click beside its controls did nothing. Now anywhere on it but the speaker's
button and the slider is the ">"'s target (`PageBeside`): its corners, the level, the output's name, the air between them; its
click opens the sound page. Under the pointer there, and pressed, the whole line lights as the Bluetooth line's page part does
(the subtle hover and pressed fills, edge to edge, `RowPress`); on the button or the slider that control lights itself and the
line does not. The keys' stop is the ">" itself, ringed round it (`CellIsland.StopBox`, which `LineFocus` takes for a target answered
over more than its control): a ring round the whole line would stand over the slider, where Enter and a click would differ. On a page itself the
volume has no ">" and its room does nothing. On the bar the volume slider has no room beside its speaker and its track; it is
unchanged.

**The spacing.** The volume's level stood 9 DIP from its ">" — at the edge of the button round the ">", not of its glyph.
What stands before a line's ">" now ends `SwitchIsland.ChevronAirDip` (14 DIP) before its glyph, as a switch's line's words
do (`SliderLine.PageWordsEnd`, `SwitchIsland.WordsEnd`), at every size: the level in the one-row and the two-row forms, the
output's name in all three. The ">"'s glyph stays on the trailing gutter, the speaker's button on the icon column; the
brightness's level, with no ">", on the trailing gutter.

**The brightness's button is Windows' mode** (`BrightnessIsland`). Where the sun stood, on the bar and as a line: a sun while
Windows is light, a moon (Segoe's QuietHours) while it is dark, and a click switches it — the apps and Windows together, told
to every window, as the dark mode widget does (§403), through the one switch every dark mode button reads
(`QuickSwitch.DarkMode`'s `SwitchData`, now the brightness's source too: `SourceKinds.KeyOf`). In a folder it is the line's
button (`ModeTarget`), named "Dark mode" and told as its switch ("Dark mode: off" and what a click does: `CardTip`, which
Narrator reads), a stop of the folder's keys before the slider's. On the bar, where a widget's click is one for the whole cell,
it is a button of its own beside the slider: a press on it is taken (`ISliderIsland.Press`, `OnMode`) and switches the mode
where the release comes still on it; the track stays the slider's, and the widget's click is still nothing. In the short form
the button is the widget. Where this PC has no brightness to set, the widget is greyed whole, its button with it (§247).

**An opened row is one item with what it offers** (`ListRow.Open`, `Below`, `PageLayout.Opened`). A Bluetooth device opened
onto Disconnect or Connect and Remove device, a network onto its key or Connect, a cable onto its facts and Properties stood
on a card (`Backdrop` of `BackdropKind.Card`) behind a row whose band was its own row's: the pointer lit the row alone, the
card under the buttons stayed as it was, and nothing said which was open. Now the opened row's band runs down past all it
offers (`Below`), the list's width; what it offers stands over it and takes the pointer first. Under the pointer anywhere on it
but a button the whole item lights — behind the buttons too —, on a button the button alone; a click there is the row's, as on
its name: it closes. It is drawn chosen: WinUI's selected fill and the accent pill on its leading edge, in the middle of the
whole item. Every page that opens a row in place goes through `Opened` — Bluetooth, Wi-Fi's networks and cables, in a folder
and in a flyout alike —; the sound lines' devices open nothing and keep the pill of the one in use. Deleted: the card,
`BackdropKind.Card`, `PageLayout.Card`.

No setting, no file change, no strings (the button's name and tooltip are the dark mode widget's).

Tests: `QuickSliderLineTests` — `BesideItsControlsTheVolumesLineOpensItsPage` (every size: the corners, the level and the ">"
the page's target, its click the page; the button and the slider their own; lit whole beside them, not on them; on the page no
">"), `WhatStandsBeforeTheChevronKeepsTheSwitchesAir` (every size at 100 and 150 %, 100 and 225 % text: the ">" on the
trailing gutter, the speaker on the icon column, the level and the name 14 DIP before the ">"'s glyph, the brightness's level
on the gutter), `TheBrightnessesButtonSwitchesWindowsLightAndDark` (a made-up switch: the sun, "Dark mode: off", its click
switching it, the moon, "Dark mode: on"; the slider's target the slider's, the room nothing; its stops the button and the
slider), `OnTheBarTheModesButtonSwitchesOnItsRelease` (a press and a release on it switch it, a release off it nothing, the
track the slider's); `QuickPageLineTests.AnOpenedRowIsOneItemWithWhatItOffers` (the headset, a network, a cable: open, its
band past its buttons; beside a button and at its foot the row lit, on it the button; its pill drawn in the middle of the
whole item; closed, a row again); `BrightnessWidgetTests.TheBarsSliderSetsEveryDisplayTogether` takes the press on the sun.
No test reaches this PC's mode (`QuickSwitches.Source`; an isolated run's switch is a sample). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1,
KARPO_PNG_DIR): `QuickSliderLineTests.QuickSliderSheets` qs-sliders-<dark|light>.png (the two lines in each size, Windows dark
on the dark sheet and light on the light one, then the volume's room and the mode's button under the pointer),
`QuickPageLineTests.OpenedRowSheets` qs-<bluetooth|wifi>-<dark|light>.png (opened at rest, beside its button, on it, a closed
row under the pointer).

By hand: quick settings › the volume's line: a click on its corner opens the sound page; on the speaker it mutes; the line

## 610. The palette's reset in Palette's row, before its dropdown (2026-11-09)

## 610. The palette's reset in Palette's row, before its dropdown (2026-11-09) — a value's reset the same pair, any control's, since §613 (2026-11-09) — the palette's reset asked first in Windows' dialog since §634 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"reset to default in appearance should be shown on the same line as the apply style dropdown."*

**Replaces** §577's row of its own under Palette (its words "Changes to Graphite", its button Reset to default). §577 stays
for the rest: a designed palette's reset, greyed while the palette is drawn as designed in both modes, none for Custom;
pressed, the palette's values go, every other palette's kept, no confirmation (edit mode's undo has it).

    Palette                    [ Reset to default ]  [ ▣ Graphite  Changed ⌄ ]
    Preview  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
             …

**One way two controls share a line** (`OptionRow.Beside` → `FlyoutItem.Beside`; `PanelRows.Of`). §568 stood a colour's
dark half beside its light half by a rule of its own (a dark colour right after a light one became its `PanelRow.Pair`).
Now one rule: a row marked Beside is the pair of the row before it, in that row's line — the colour's dark half
(`LookRows.Editor` marks it) and the palette worn's reset (`LookRows.Rows`). A menu shows it where it is. The pair keeps
its own item, key and state; what is a control's asks the row it is (`PanelRow.Own(key)`): a click on a greyed one finds
nothing (`PanelLayout.HitIn`), its greyed look, a screen reader's Enabled. `LineOf` and `RectOf` found a pair's line by its
key already (§577).

**Where it stands** (`PanelLayout.Controls`, `ControlLeft`, `BesideWide`). Palette's dropdown where every value's box is
(240 × 32, 16 in from the card's end), in line with every other row's control; the reset 8 before it, 32 tall, its words'
button (`ActionWide`: its words and 12 either side, 120 to 240). The keys reach it first, as it reads (`Stops`), then the
dropdown. Where the row's name would no longer stand whole before it a gutter off — a flyout narrowed by its display, a
language's longer words (es "Restablecer valores predeterminados") — it is its icon alone (Reset, a 32 DIP square): never
over the name, whose room ends a gutter before the control column (`NameRoom` by `ControlLeft`).

**Its name.** "Reset to default" does not say which palette: its tooltip and its name to a screen reader are the whole
"Reset Graphite to default" (`TipOf`; `DeckUia`; the reset row's Detail, which no line draws now). Its status and help
are none (the dropdown's "Graphite, Changed" stays the dropdown's). Drawn by the one button of a row that acts
(`PanelPainter.Act`: a Button, its words in its middle, or its icon where it is a square), greyed with its own row.

**Strings**: `settings.look.resetDetail` ("Changes to {palette}") gone with the row's words; `settings.look.resetPalette`
("Reset {palette} to default") in every language, no pronoun (de "{palette} auf Standard zurücksetzen", fr "Rétablir les
valeurs par défaut de {palette}"). No config change.

**Landed after §606 and §609** (made side by side). §609 had already called its thing of one choice `FlyoutItem.Beside`
— set on the holiday calendar's row, meaning "my level's one choice stands in my line" —, while §610's `Beside` is set on the
row that stands beside. One name, two meanings, and merged as they were the calendar's row (marked) would have become the pair
of the row before it. One meaning now: **`Beside` marks the row that stands beside; its holder is the row before it, or,
alone in its level, the thing whose level it is** (`OptionMenu` marks the calendar's region, not the calendar;
`PanelRows.One` takes a thing's one-row level whose row is Beside as its pair). Everything after that is `PanelRow.Pair`
alone: `Own(key)` the row a control is (a greyed reset, a region's own state), `HolderOf` whose line a pair stands in (the
screen reader names a region for its calendar, "Region · Switzerland", only where the holder is a thing's row), a pair's own
value its status, a reset's Help none (its whole name is its name). The ten languages added since §610 was written (am, fil,
gu, ha, kn, ml, my, pa, sw, yo) have `settings.look.resetPalette` too.

Tests: `AppearanceValuesTests.ThePalettesResetStandsInItsRowBeforeTheDropdown` (no Action row on the page; Palette's
controls the reset then the dropdown, the dropdown the value box, the reset 8 before it as wide as its words, the control
column's start, the name whole before it; greyed: a click finds nothing, a stop all the same before the dropdown, a screen
reader's "Reset Karpo to default", off, no status nor help; Graphite changed: a click finds it, its tooltip and name
Graphite's, its pick the reset, applied: Graphite as designed, greyed; 450 DIP wide: its icon alone, 32 × 32, the name
whole; Custom: the dropdown alone), `LookPreviewTests.TheAppearancePageIsOnePreviewOverFourTabs` (Palette, Preview, Tabs;
the reset Palette's pair), `SettingsPanelTests.EveryControlIsOneSize` (a dropdown's box where every value's is, a button
beside it 8 before it, 120–240 × 32, the control column's start), `PanelControlsTests.AThingsOwnActionsAreIconButtonsAndAPagesAreWords`
(a button beside a dropdown its whole name its tooltip), `PopupPlaceTests.TheControlsRectFollowsTheScrollAndTheExpanders`
(a head row's own control), `AppearanceValuesTests.EachHalfOfAColourPairOpensItsOwnPickerUnderItsOwnButton` (the colour
pairs alone), `LookTests.EachPaletteKeepsItsOwnValuesAndADesignedOneResetsToItsDesign` (its Detail, Beside). UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.PaletteResetSheets` palettereset-<changed|unchanged|custom>-<dark|light>.png
(Graphite changed: the reset in force; Graphite as designed: greyed; Custom: the dropdown alone), `AppearancePaletteSheets`.

By hand: edit mode › Appearance: Palette's row [Reset to default] [Karpo ⌄], the reset greyed; a background picked: Karpo
"Changed", the reset in force, its tooltip "Reset Karpo to default"; pressed: Karpo as designed, the reset greyed; Palette ›
Custom: the dropdown alone; Tab from the flyout's start: the reset, then Palette.

## 613. The Appearance in one mode: the taskbar's mode a setting (System, Dark, Light), a value's reset beside it, a wider and shorter colour picker, the preview on the desktop (2026-11-09) — the picker in two columns, its swatches beside its mixer, one line of recent colours and two of presets, since §627 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the appearance should actually only show for dark or light mode including all the settings. you
can switch between those with a switcher at the top, either dark light or system."* — asked whether that is a real setting
or a view: *"this is a real setting. default is from system."*; *"the color selector should be wider but not as tall
anymore."* (the colour's picker, its popup); *"you should be able to reset individual properties to the style default"*;
*"the appearance preview should show more widgets in the folder and it should show them centered. it should also show more
widgets on the taskbar, it should also show the background image of the desktop and it should show a light and dark mode
icon on the top left and right."*

**First, §610 landed** on §606 and §609 (made side by side; see §610's last paragraph): one meaning of `Beside`, the row
that stands beside its holder — the row before it, or alone in a thing's level the thing (a holiday calendar's region) —, and
`PanelRow.Pair` the one mechanism after it. This entry's resets are that pair too.

**Replaces** §568's page of two colour buttons a row (each mode's half side by side), §582's preview of both modes cut by a
slanted line and §606's marks of the mode Windows is in (its name over each half of the preview, the accent's dot under a
pair's button, "…, active" to a screen reader). §568 stays for the model: every colour of the Appearance a pair, both halves
kept in the file and in every palette's values; §577's palettes, each keeping its own values; §592's one preview over four
tabs.

### The taskbar's mode, a setting

`Appearance.Mode` (`TaskbarMode`: `System`, `Dark`, `Light`; the file's `"appearance": { "mode": "dark" | "light" }`, left out
for System). **System is the default**: Karpo's taskbar in the mode Windows is in, live as it changes (§568 as it was).
**Dark** or **Light** pins Karpo's taskbar to that mode whatever Windows is in — as Windows 11's "Choose your default Windows
mode" pins its own taskbar and Start while apps follow "Choose your default app mode". One resolver: `Looks.Dark(appearance,
windows)`; `Look.KarpoBase(dark)` takes it (`Look.Wearing(Appearance)`), so every bar, its widgets, every folder, every menu
and flyout opened from the taskbar wears that half of every colour pair, and Karpo's own defaults of that mode
(`KarpoLook.Paints(dark)`). High contrast still wins over any mode (§547). `Dock.LookChanged` compares the taskbar as the
Appearance has it (`Wearing(config)`): with a pinned mode, Windows' mode turned rebuilds nothing of the taskbar — only the
settings follow it.

**Decided: the settings panel keeps following Windows.** The panel (the edit bar's flyouts, the settings page) is Karpo's
settings app, not part of the taskbar; Windows' Settings follows the app mode, not the taskbar's. So the panel wears Windows'
own look (§526, `Dock.SettingsLookOf`) whatever the Mode says — a pinned Light taskbar edited from a dark panel shows its
light values in a dark panel, its preview light. The alternative (the panel in the taskbar's mode) would make the Mode a
second app-wide theme switch, which the person did not ask for.

**The page's switcher** (`LookRows.ModeRow`, the page's first row): "Mode" with a segmented control of three, **Dark ·
Light · System** (the person's order; Windows' own words, `settings.appearance.dark|light`, new `settings.appearance.system`
and `settings.appearance.mode` in every language). A pick writes `appearance.mode` and the whole page is made again in that
mode. R3 lets this one segmented choice be words for no place or direction (`MenuRulesTests.Places` holds "Mode": the switcher
the person asked for).

### The page in one mode

Everything under the switcher is of the mode in force (`LookRows.Rows(config, layout, windows)`: `Looks.Dark` of the
Appearance's Mode and Windows' mode; System shows the mode Windows is in now): Palette's swatches, each colour's value, its
picker's tiles (that mode's palette, `ColorPalette.For(tone, dark)`), the pattern's swatches, the Background blur's greying,
the preview. **One row a colour, one colour button** (§535's, at the controls' end), keyed for its tone alone
(`Appearance.widgets.background`; §568's `.light|.dark` keys gone); a pick writes the half of the mode shown
(`Looks.WritePaint(slot, tone, dark, …)`), the other half kept. The font, the pattern and the blur were one in both modes
already.

**Deleted with the pairs**: `OptionRow.Dark`, `FlyoutItem.Dark`, `PanelMetrics.ModeColourWide`, `PairRoom`, `NowDot`,
`PanelLayout.NowDotUnder|NowDotBefore`, the pair's case of `PanelLayout.Controls|ControlLeft` and `PanelPainter.Control`,
`ColourButton`'s mode glyph and dot, `DeckUia`'s `ModeName`, `Now` and the `now` of `Things`/`Tree`, `LookPreview.ModeOf`,
`ModesOver`, `ModesOf`, `Slant`, `SlantOf`, `HalfOf`, `DividerOf`, `DarkAt`, `Divider`, `Backdrop`, `CheckDip` and the checker,
`LookPreviews.Divide`; tests `AppearanceModeNowTests` (§606) whole, `LookPreviewTests.ASampleIsDrawnInBothModesDarkFirst…`,
`TheModesAreSplitByALeaningLine…`, `AppearanceValuesTests.EachHalfOfAColourPair…`, `SceneTreeTests.AppearancePairSheets`.
`dock.uia.active` stays (the edit bar's entries use it).

### A value's reset

Each value of the editor (`LookRows.Editor`) — a colour, the font, the pattern, its colour, the blur — that the palette worn's
design draws otherwise **in the mode shown** has a reset right after it (`LookRows.ResetOf`, keyed `<row>.reset`), standing
beside its control (`Beside`): pressed, the value is unset in the palette's values, so the design's is drawn again
(`Looks.WritePaint(…, null)`, `WriteFont(null)`, `WritePattern(null)`, `WriteBlur(null)`), and the reset goes. None while the
value is the design's — a value said that equals it changes nothing (as §577's palette reset is greyed then). It compares what
is drawn (`Looks.Of(config, dark)[part]` against `LookPalette.Drawn(dark)[part]`), so the other mode's half of a colour has
its reset only on the page of that mode.

**Custom, decided**: its resets go back to Karpo's own. Custom's design *is* Karpo's (§577: "Custom, the person's own, whose
design is Karpo's"), so unsetting a value there draws Karpo's; no special case, the same rule. Custom still has no palette
reset (§577: its values are never wiped as a whole); one value at a time, undoable, is not that.

**On the panel**: an icon button, Windows' subtle one (`OptionRow.Subtle` → `FlyoutItem.Subtle`; no fill until the pointer is
on it, the Reset glyph in the text's ink), a 32 DIP square 8 before its control, in the value's line — the control stays where
it stands without it, nothing moves when it comes or goes. `PanelPainter.IconButton` is now the one icon button (a thing's
own actions, §551, and this). Its whole name is its tooltip and what a screen reader says: "Reset Background to default"
(new `settings.look.resetValue`, "Reset {setting} to default", in every language); its status and help none. The keys reach
it before its control, as it reads. A colour's reset stands inside the value column (where a colour's words stand, §535);
a dropdown's and a number's before the column (`ControlLeft` from it).

**One pair, laid generically** (§610 made it for Palette's dropdown alone): any row's `Pair` that is an Action is laid 8
before the row's leftmost control (`PanelLayout.Controls`), drawn first and greyed by its own row (`PanelPainter.Control`,
`Act`), hit by its own state (`HitIn`, `Own`), its width `BesideWide` — a subtle one its square, the palette's its words where
the name stays whole. A button beside never stacks under its row (§609's stacking is a dropdown's).

### The colour picker, wider and less tall

A colour's picker — its swatches, its recent colours, its mixer (§523) — is the one popup wider than a value's box:
**400 DIP** (`PanelMetrics.PickerWide`; §587's 240 for every other control's popup, a search's 360). Explicitly the
exception: fixed whatever its rows say, as every popup is, and only it (`Flyout`'s popup rule: a level holding a mix or
colour swatches). Its swatches stand **twelve to a line** (`MenuPickers.SwatchesAcross`, Windows' eight until now; a
settings menu of 320 holds nine), so its grid is about half as many lines, and its spectrum is **96 DIP** tall
(`Flyout.SpectrumDip`, 128 until now), as wide as the swatches. Hung from its button by §531's rule: flush with its right
where flush with its left would pass the panel's side.

### The preview

Drawn **once, in the mode the taskbar is in** (`LookPreviews.Make`: the Appearance worn over Windows' look,
`Look.Wearing(config)`, its Mode read there), every value of that mode; nothing split.

- **On the desktop**: the desktop's own picture under it — the one of the display the panel stands on, as §547 reads it for
  the bars (`IDesktopWallpaper`, only read; `EditDeck.Wallpaper` from `Dock.WallpaperOn`) —, filling the room as Windows'
  Fill does (`WallpaperStrips.Compose` at the room's size), sharp; under the bar the strip blurred as the Taskbar's Blur says
  (`WallpaperStrips.Blurred`, `Scene.Wallpaper`, the dock's own path). Composed once a room (`LookPreviews.composed`): a value
  changed draws the sample again without reading the file again. No picture readable (none set, a solid colour, the stage):
  a quiet gradient of the mode (`LookPreview.Ground|GroundFoot`). The picture is part of the sample's key, so another
  wallpaper is another picture.
- **More on the bar**: Start, search, Task view, Settings and the Snipping Tool in its middle, as Windows 11's centred
  taskbar; the folder wearing the clock at its end, where Windows' clock stands. Each is a button Karpo draws itself — still
  nothing of this PC's (§536).
- **More in the folder, centred**: a compact clock, a compact world clock (Tokyo, the same still moment) and a calendar (its
  made-up events, `LookStand`), the folder open in the room's middle (§592 opened it over its face, at the bar's middle
  then), standing off the bar as a folder does. Tried and left out: the month's grid, which made the preview about 480 DIP
  tall and pushed the tabs and every value under it out of sight on a 1080 display at 150 % (the stage tests that choose a
  tab found it below the flyout's foot).
- **The mode's icon, reinterpreted**: the person asked for "a light and dark mode icon on the top left and right", written
  when the preview showed both modes split. With one mode a preview there is one mode to say, so one icon: **its sun or moon
  in a round badge at the room's top right** (28 DIP, 8 in, the mode's flyout ground, `LookPreview.BadgeOf`), the mode the
  sample is drawn in. None in high contrast (neither mode). The badge says what the switcher chose without a word.
- The room's height still holds the folder's lines whole (§571, measured with the new stand-ins). A screen reader still
  hears "Preview of Appearance" (§606's "· Dark, active" gone).

The Taskbar page's menu preview (§551) is drawn the same way: once, in the taskbar's mode, over the desktop.

### The file

**Shape 80** (`Config.Shape`, `ConfigWords.txt` written again: `property Appearance.mode`, `enum TaskbarMode: "dark" |
"light" | "system"`). **The conversion rule: none but the version** — a file of shape 79 has no `appearance.mode` and reads
as System, which is what it meant; nothing else of the file changed. A word this build does not know reads as System
(`Appearance.Normalized`). No migration code.

```
appearance.mode          "dark" | "light"; left out for System (Windows' mode)
appearance.palette       as §577
appearance.palettes      as §577, each colour still { dark?, light? } (§568)
```

Tests: `AppearanceModeTests` (new) — `TheModeIsARealSettingWindowsByDefault` (the switcher Dark, Light, System, System
chosen, nothing in the file; Light written, read back, worn whatever Windows is in; System again empties the Appearance; an
unknown word System; a file of 79 System; shape 80), `TheTaskbarWearsTheModeTheAppearanceSays` (each mode × Windows' each:
the taskbar's mode and its half; only System another taskbar when Windows turns; high contrast), `ThePageShowsAndWritesTheModeInForceAlone`
(no `.dark|.light` key; the light card with Light pinned under a dark Windows; a mix writes the light half alone; one button
a colour), `AValueOtherThanItsPalettesHasItsResetBesideIt` (Graphite: a colour, the font, the pattern, the blur each its
reset after it, Beside and Subtle, named; none in the other mode; pressed: the design's, gone; Custom back to Karpo's),
`AValuesResetIsAnIconButtonBeforeItsControl` (32 × 32, 8 before the colour button, the button where it was, the name whole,
a click, the keys first, tooltip and screen reader "Reset Background to default", applied through the menu's pick).
`AppearanceValuesTests` (no value's reset on a fresh config; each value of the mode shown; one colour button;
`EveryColourOpensItsPickerUnderItsButton` in each mode, a reset's place too; the palette's reset under Mode),
`LookPreviewTests` (`ASampleIsDrawnInTheTaskbarsModeWearingItsHalf`, `TheModesBadgeStandsAtTheRoomsTopRight`; Mode, Palette,
Preview, Tabs; the new stand-ins), `LookTests` (the pattern colour one row after the pattern's reset), `BarBlurSettingTests`,
`BarGroundTests`, `AppearanceTests`, `MenuPickersTests` (nine to a 320 DIP line, twelve to the picker's 400),
`MenuRulesTests` (R3 Mode; R19 a reset 32 × 32), `LayoutMenuTests`, `UntranslatedTests` (de "System", fr/id "Mode", fil both),
`ConfigSchemaTests`; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `DropdownWidthTests.EveryPopupOfThePanelIsOneWidth` (a colour's picker 400),
`PanelPopupPlaceTests` (colours' pickers 400), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.AColourIsMixedInTheSettingsPanel` (one button, the
picker 400), `LookPreviewPictures.ALookChangedDrawsItsPreviewAgainOnceAndNothingElseDoes` (one mode; the other half changed
draws again, nothing seen; Mode Light: the light bar), `SceneTreeTests.AppearancePaletteSheets` (one button a colour);
pictures (`SceneTreeTests.AppearanceModeSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR, over a test dusk wallpaper made by the test):
appearance613-page-<system|dark|light>-<dark|light>.png (the whole page, Mode as named, Windows as named last),
appearance613-reset-<dark|light>.png (Background's reset beside it), appearance613-picker-<dark|light>.png (its picker
open, 400 DIP), appearance613-preview-<dark|light>.png (the preview: the desktop, the bar's widgets, the folder centred,
the badge).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance: "Mode [Dark | Light | System]" first, System chosen; Light: the bars, their widgets and an
open folder light at once whatever Windows is in, the page's values the light ones, the preview light with a sun top right;
Windows switched to dark (Settings › Personalization › Colors): the taskbar stays light, the panel turns dark. Taskbar
