## 614. The air quality searched on a click; the edit bar's first entry General (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"i should also be able to click on the air quality widget to do a search for it."* and *"the edit
bar should not show karpo as entry but General as entry"*.

**The air quality's click.** A weather line's click searches the weather at its place with the app's one engine
(`SearchUrls.Weather`, "weather Zürich, Switzerland"), and a clock's the time where it stands (§377); the air's lines did
nothing (`CellAct.Nothing`). Now each of the air's four (§590: `airQuality`, `airPollutants`, `airPollen`, `airForecast`) acts
(`CellAct.Action`), lights whole, and its click searches "air quality" and its place (`SearchUrls.Air`,
`widget.air.search` / `widget.air.searchHere` in all 30 languages, "Luftqualität {place}", "{place} 大気質", "calidad del aire
en {place}"; the device's location the query alone, which the engine places itself; `PlaceNames.Whole`, as the weather's).
The engine is Online › Search engine; Online's Weather site (§322) is not used: of its four sites only weather.com and
meteoblue have an air quality page at all, and a click of the weather is a search too, so the air's follows the weather's
click, not its menu's "Open forecast" (which keeps opening the weather site's air quality page). The line chooses the search
and forwards (`IslandView.App`); the dock opens it once the folder has gone (`IOpensOnceGone`, `Dock.FolderForward`) through
`Launch.Open`, which closes whatever of Karpo's is open first (§491), with the line's press shown as every whole line's. A
line not set up is its "Set up" as before; "Refresh" stays its menu's.

**The bar's air face is unchanged:** a folder wearing the air quality face opens its folder on a click, as the weather's faces
do and as the bar's clock does (§377): the ready-made air folder holds the four lines, and with flyouts opening on a click (the
default) a search there would leave no way into it. The markets' face searching (§263) is that face's own exception.

**General.** The edit bar's first entry (§575) said "Karpo"; Windows Settings calls the page of what holds for the whole system
"General" (Privacy & security › General), and so does the page's own first section. The entry, its page's title and its screen reader name (`PanelRows.SideOf(PanelPage.Karpo)`, which
`Dock.SettingsPanel` now takes as the title too), and a link's lead to it (`PanelRows.LeadOf`: "General › Public holidays";
`OptionLinks.Opens`: "Opens Public holidays in General") are `settings.general.header`, already in all 30 languages in
Windows' word ("Allgemein", "Général", "全般", "常规"). The page's section of Karpo Pro and Back up and reset is still "Karpo",
its string `settings.sections.karpo` beside Services (was `dock.edit.karpo`, now gone). The gear stays its glyph, Settings'
own, which a page of app-wide settings is. `PanelPage.Karpo`, `KarpoPage.Karpo` and the rows' keys ("Karpo/…") are no words
anybody sees, and stay. No config change.

Tests: `AirSearchTests` (the address with Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, a custom engine and a broken one, a place and the
device's; the four act; UI: each of the four at a place forwards, lights whole and opens once, one with no place opens
nothing), `LineHoverRuleTests` (the four light whole), `LineClickTests` (the air quality's click forwards and the folder
goes), `GeneralPageTests` (the entry, the title, the glyph; the Karpo section kept; the holidays link's lead and Narrator's
words), `EditDeckClickTests.ItsTreesSayWhatEachThingIs` (the entries and the pane named General), `KarpoMenuTests`,
`MenuRulesTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`, `HolidaysPanelTests`, `StringsTests`. Pictures (`SettingsPanelPictures.SelectionSheets`,
KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): selection-none-<dark|light>.png, the edit bar with General first.

By hand: edit mode: the first entry reads General, its page opens under it; a widget's Public holidays link says "General ›
Public holidays". Out of edit mode open the air folder and click each line: the browser searches "air quality" and the place
with the engine chosen in General › Online, and the folder has gone.

## 619. An app's button clicked again and again does what Windows 11's does, every time (2026-11-09)

The person, 2026-11-09: "in the app widget, when i click the icon again and again it does not behave the same way that
windows does it natively. fix this completely." Windows 11's rules, as its taskbar has them, and where Karpo was off.

**Windows' rules** (sources: Microsoft's keyboard shortcuts page and the ITaskbarList docs; the taskband's code as ReactOS
reimplements it, `taskswnd.cpp` HandleTaskItemClick / ActivateTask; Windows XP's taskband, which judged the button active
"at LDown"; what Windows 11's shell DLLs import — `twinui.pcshell.dll`, which switches to a window for the taskbar and
Alt+Tab, imports SwitchToThisWindow, GetLastActivePopup, IsHungAppWindow and ShowWindowAsync; and the Windhawk mods that
hook `CTaskBand::SwitchTo(ITaskItem*, BOOL noMinimize)` in Taskbar.dll):
- The **active button** is the taskbar's own state — the button of the window last activated (HSHELL_WINDOWACTIVATED,
  _RUDEAPPACTIVATED; a dialog stands for its owner; ActivateTab/SetActiveAlt mark one until the next activation) — read
  as the button goes down, never what the press itself changes. A minimized window is never it.
- **One window, its button active** → minimized: WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_MINIMIZE posted, the app's own minimizing and the
  system's animation with it; a hung app's without asking (ShowWindowAsync), its ghost going; a window without a minimize
  button stays.
- **One window, not active** (behind others, minimized, or nothing in front) → switched to (SwitchToThisWindow): a
  minimized one restored by SC_RESTORE, back as it was (maximized, if it was), then brought to the foreground — its last
  active popup where that is shown and enabled (a modal dialog gets the keys). Clicked again, it minimizes: the clicks
  toggle without end.
- **Several windows** (combined): a plain click shows their thumbnails, nothing brought forward, a click again puts them
  away; Ctrl+click (or every click with LastActiveClick 1) walks them — none active, the most recent; one active, the
  next; Shift+click and a middle click start another; Ctrl+Shift+click one as administrator; Shift+right-click the
  window's menu, the group's for several. Uncombined, each button is a button of one window.
- **Elsewhere**: a window on another desktop (listed with "All desktops") switches there first; an app above Karpo (UIPI)
  is restored and minimized without asking, as nothing Karpo posts reaches it.

**What was off, and the root of it**:
1. **The active plate and the click disagreed on a minimized window.** Minimizing the last window leaves it the
   foreground one where nothing else takes the activation (Explorer's taskbar, which would, is hidden; the old
   `AMinimizedWindowIsNeverTheOneInFront` test was written for it), and no activation says so: the button stayed lit while the window was down, and the click (which rightly restores) did the opposite of
   what the plate said. `AppClicks.ActiveButton` is now the one rule for both, and never a minimized window; `FrontWatch`
   hears EVENT_SYSTEM_MINIMIZESTART/_END (`WM_KARPO_MINIMIZED`, kept for after a modal loop) and the plates are read again.
2. **An app's own mark stuck across its other windows.** ActivateTab/SetActiveAlt ended only when another *process* came
   forward, so a mark one window made outlived every other window of the same process coming to the front — and every
   store app's frame belongs to one process, ApplicationFrameHost: while it held, the button of the window in front did
   not minimize it, and the marked one's minimized a window behind. (Which apps mark is not known; the rule was wrong for
   any that does.) It now ends with the next activated window whose button is another one
   (`AppSignals.ActiveAltEnds(button, listed, sameApp)`), as Windows' taskbar moves its active button; the marked window
   itself, its dialog, or a window of the same app with no button (its full screen) keep it.
3. **Read at the release, not the press.** The click was decided by the foreground at the button's release, after the
   press had closed Karpo's popups (handing the focus back) and whatever time the dock took. The active button is now kept
   as the press goes down on an app's button (`Dock.FrontAtPress`, `FrontForClick`), as Windows' taskbar does.
4. **Restored behind the app's back.** A minimized window was restored by ShowWindowAsync(SW_RESTORE) whatever the app; it
   is now asked, as Windows asks it (`Apps.Restore`: SC_RESTORE through `Apps.Command`), the way minimizing always was, and
   done without the app only where it is hung (`IsHungAppWindow`, new), disabled (5.) or above Karpo (`Apps.Asks`). A hung app's minimize
   used to be posted and wait for the app to answer; it is done at once now. "Restore all windows" goes through the same
   restore.
5. **A modal dialog's owner never minimized or came back from its button.** Measured on a hidden desktop: a disabled
   window's DefWindowProc let a posted SC_RESTORE go by (the window stayed minimized), and SC_MINIMIZE goes the same way
   of the system commands: Notepad under Save As would stay as it was. A
   disabled window is minimized and restored without asking (`Apps.Asks(above, hung, disabled)`); and since the restore
   activates the owner and its dialog was hidden while it was down, the dialog (`WindowOwners.ModalOf`: its last active
   popup, enabled, over the owner it disabled) is shown and activated by its own thread after the restore
   (`Surfaces.ActivateOther`, SetWindowPos with SWP_ASYNCWINDOWPOS and the activation, queued behind the restore;
   ShowWindowAsync SW_SHOW was tried and does not activate a window the restore already showed).
One activation (`Apps.Activate` → `SwitchTo`), one restore, one minimize, one active-button rule: the bar's buttons, the
pins in folders, the window list's cards, Win+N and Win+Ctrl+N, the window menus and a drag resting on a button all go
through them.

**Not done, decided**: the minimize animation flies towards where Explorer's (hidden) taskbar keeps the button, not to
Karpo's: its target is the answer to HSHELL_GETMINRECT, which only a WH_SHELL hook gives (a DLL in every process), and
Karpo injects nothing.

Tests: `AppToggleTests` — `TheForegroundWindowsButtonIsTheActiveOne`, `AMinimizedWindowIsNeverTheActiveButton`,
`KarposOwnWindowStandsForTheAppBeforeIt`, `AnAppsOwnMarkIsTheActiveButton`, `TenClicksToggleTheWindow` (5 worlds: another
window takes the foreground, the minimized one keeps it, none has it; a popup of Karpo's holding the focus),
`AWindowBehindAnotherComesForwardFirst`, `ACommandIsAskedOnlyOfAnAppThatCanAnswer` (5),
`AnAppsMarkEndsWithTheNextWindowWithAButtonOfItsOwn`; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1), on a hidden desktop with the test's own
windows: `TenRealClicksMinimizeAndRestoreAMaximizedWindow`, `ARealWindowBehindAnotherComesForward`,
`RestoreAllBringsEachBackAsItWas`, `TheModalDialogOfAWindowBroughtForwardGetsTheKeys` (the dialog the target; the disabled
owner minimized and switched to: back, its dialog shown and active), and `AMinimizedOwnersModalDialogGetsTheKeysBack`.
`AppButtonRulesTests.AnAppsActiveMarkLastsUntilAnotherAppComesForward` takes the new signature.

By hand: a maximized Notepad's button clicked ten times: down, back maximized, down…, its plate dark while it is down even
with nothing else open; two Notepads combined: a click shows both, again hides them, Ctrl+click walks them, Shift+click
and a middle click open a third; Notepad's Save As open: its button minimizes Notepad with it and brings both back, Save As
with the keys; Calculator and Settings both open (store apps): each one's button minimizes it when it is in front; a
window on another desktop ("All desktops"): its button switches there.

## 621. The add page's ghost outlines each widget it holds, never the whole pick: each app button, each line of a ghost folder (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the ghost blue lines when placing are outlining the outside of the combined widgets, they should
outline each widget individually"*

**What was one outline.** §606's ghost of a ready-made group opened its folder faint with the ghost's outline round the whole
panel (`FolderFlyout.ShowStates`: a rectangle from 0, 0 to the plan's size); and the bar's ghost (`Scene.ShowGhost`) was one
rectangle, the part's block, whatever it held — the open apps under the pointer, three buttons each on its own card since
§602, wore one outline round all three.

**Now one rectangle a card**, each in the shape of the card it rounds, the gaps between them clear:
- **On a bar** (`Layout.GhostRects`): a part wearing several cards (`Layout.Plates`: the app buttons, each its own) gets one
  ghost rectangle each; a part of one card keeps its block's one outline, as a carried block's, unchanged. The blue ghost is a
  visual as big as the bar holding a rectangle (wash and outline, one sprite) per card (`Scene.Ghosts`, made as first asked
  for, the spare ones blank), as the empty blocks are (`ShowEmpty`). A carried block's ghost, a block landing from another
  surface and several carried together pass their one rectangle the same way.
- **In a folder** (`FolderFlyout.ShowGhosts`): the ghost folder's outline round each line's card as its list shows it
  (`Shown`), one each; the add page's ghost among a folder's lines its one line, as before. The ghost's visual holds one more
  rounded rectangle for each line past the first (`ghostMore`), blank while a carried line's ghost (the first alone) stands.
  A ghost folder's outlines stand over its lines (`Ghosted` moves them above the lines' layer, back under once it is whole):
  under them every line's own card hid all of each but the folder's edge, where the one line of a folder's add (its card
  faint, §593) shows them through. Over the lines, as the bar's ghost stands over its parts, at the folder's 55 %.

**The morph, one rule for both** (`EditLook.GhostFrom`): each rectangle grows from its own where the ghost stood as many, else
from the room all of the last took (`EditLook.Around`), else (none stood) it is put where it goes. So §617's empty ghost — one
rectangle — splits into the pick's several, gliding and growing out of it, and several gather into one again; with
Animations off all stand at once. Nothing else changed: the stage map, the 55 %, the click (§593); no config change.

**Not done, decided**: a folder face on the bar showing several faces is one button on one card (§506: faces on one button
read as one), so a ready-made group's face keeps one outline on the bar; its lines are what the folder outlines one by one.
Several blocks carried together keep one ghost round the room they land in (`GroupLanding`): the report is of the add page's
ghost, and that one is the gap the carry opens.

Tests: `GhostOutlineTests` — `APickOfSeveralCardsIsOutlinedCardByCard` (the open apps' three buttons: three rectangles, each
its button's card, apart, none the block), `ASingleWidgetKeepsItsBlocksOneOutline`, `ARectangleGrowsFromItsOwnElseFromTheRoomAllTook`.
UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `SceneTreeTests.TheAddGhostOutlinesEachCardOfItsPick` (the real scene: the empty ghost one block, the
open apps three at their plates, a single widget one again, none once edit ends); `SceneTreeTests.AddGhostSheets` (the world
clock's and the air quality's ghost folders: an outline at each line's card, `FolderFlyout.AddGhostsShown`; a clock's line in
a folder: one, at a line's card; new -apps-: the open apps under the pointer, an outline round each button). Pictures
addghost-group-, -air-, -apps-, each dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › a bar's "+" › World clock under the pointer: its face in one blue box on the bar, its folder open faint
with a blue box round the clock and round each city's line. Start and taskbar › Apps under the pointer: a blue box round each
open app's button, the gaps between them clear; off the tile: the one empty box again, the three gathering into it.

## 618. Eight more palettes: see-through, patterned, light first, dark first, high contrast, the accent forward (2026-11-09) — no palette's folder lines outlined, the folder's border its own, since §624 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"add some more styles. the newly added styles should also incorporate stuff like transparency,
patterns. dark backgrounds, light background. high contrast etc."*

**Data alone** (`LookPalettes.All`, Karpo.Core\Looks.cs, the one place palettes are defined). Nothing of the model was
missing: a palette's design is a `LookPaints` in each mode, and `PartPaints` already says a background with its opacity, an
outline, a text, an accent, a pattern and its colour, the font and the bar's blur (§547, §513, §556). Three helpers for
writing them down: `Ground(background, pattern, ink, blur, outline)`, `Card(…, outline)`, `Rimmed(outline)` (the Flyouts
outlined). No config change, no migration: a palette is code, the file names the one worn and keeps each one's values under
its id (§577), and these are new ids — `daylight`, `midnight`, `contrast`, `acrylic`, `glacier`, `ember`, `blueprint`, `moss`.
A file that names one read by an older build reads as Karpo's own (`Appearance.Normalized`, as before).

| Palette | Idea | Dark | Light |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Daylight** | light first: bright white, hairline rims | bar #2B2D31 95 %, cards #383A40, text #F2F3F5, accent #4CC2FF | bar #FFFFFF 95 %, cards #FFFFFF rimmed black 10 %, text #1A1A1A, accent #0067C0 |
| **Midnight** | dark first: true black, stars of dots on the bar | bar #000000 opaque, dots white 18 %, cards #121214 rimmed white 12 %, text #ECECF1, accent #A99BFF | bar #E8E6F0 95 %, dots #2A2540 15 %, cards #F6F5FA, text #1E1B2E, accent #5A40D0 |
| **Contrast** | high contrast: black and white, every card, line and flyout outlined, semibold | all #000000, outlines and text #FFFFFF, accent #FFE500 | all #FFFFFF, outlines and text #000000, accent #0037C8 |
| **Acrylic** | see-through: Windows' greys, the bar half clear, blur 80 | bar #202020 50 %, cards #2C2C2C 75 % rimmed white 12 %, lines 88 %, text #FFFFFF, accent #60CDFF | bar #F3F3F3 60 %, cards #FFFFFF 75 % rimmed black 10 %, lines 88 %, text #1B1B1B, accent #005FB8 |
| **Glacier** | see-through and cool: icy blue, frosted grain on the bar, blur 60, white rims | bar #0D1B26 60 %, grain #CFEAFF 12 %, cards #16283A 80 %, text #E3F2FC, accent #7FD4FF | bar #DDEBF5 60 %, grain #0B2236 12 %, cards #F2F8FC 80 % rimmed white 60 %, text #0B2236, accent #0A6B9C |
| **Ember** | warm, the accent forward: the cards on the bar burnt orange, semibold | bar #1A1210, cards #7A2E12, text #FFE9DC, accent #FFB077 | bar #FBE6D8, cards #B23F14, text #FFFFFF, accent #FFE0B8; lines #FFF8F3, text #3D1A0C |
| **Blueprint** | patterned: navy and blue, a grid on the bar and its cards, Bahnschrift | bar #0B2545, grid #7CC4FF 18 %, cards #13315C, text #E8F1FF, accent #7CC4FF | bar #DCE8F7, grid #1D5FC2 18 %, cards #EEF4FC, text #0B2545, accent #1D5FC2 |
| **Moss** | patterned: forest greens, contours on the bar and its cards | bar #14201A, contours #9CCB9A 20 %, cards #1E2E25, text #E4F0E2, accent #8FD18A | bar #E3EBDD, contours #2F5233 18 %, cards #F2F6EE, text #1E3322, accent #3B7A35 |

The cards' patterns are drawn in their text's ink at the pattern's strength (§462, made fainter where a text would read
worse), the bar's in its own colour (§513). One font, pattern and blur in both modes, as every palette (`LookValues.Of`).

**Dark backgrounds and light ones, decided: every palette follows the Mode.** A palette dark in both modes (or light in
both) was weighed and left out: §613 made the taskbar's mode a real setting, so "always dark" is any palette with Mode Dark.
A palette that ignored the Mode would make the switcher lie (Light chosen, the bar still dark) and its Light page would edit
values nobody sees as light. So each palette's light bar reads light and its dark one dark (`LookTests`), and the request is
met within that: Daylight is designed light first (pure white, its dark half a soft charcoal rather than black), Midnight
dark first (true black for OLED, its light half a dim lavender grey), and Ember puts dark cards on a light bar.

**Contrast is Karpo's look, not Windows' high contrast**, which still wins over every palette as it did (§547: Karpo draws
Windows' system colours, `Look.Colors.IsAutomatic`).

**Readable over any desktop.** A card with a background of its own stands on the desktop (§464), so a see-through card was
checked over Windows' own surface, a black wallpaper and a white one: every text at least 4.5:1, every accent 3:1, on the
cards and on the lines, in both modes, for every designed palette (Acrylic's cards are 75 % for that: at 70 % its dark accent
over a white wallpaper came to 2.95:1). Contrast's text 21:1, its accent 4.5:1 or more. Karpo draws each text and accent as
designed: none needed mixing to read (`ToneRules.Dress`).

**The Palette dropdown, in groups** (`LookPalettes.Choices`): Karpo · Graphite, Daylight, Midnight, Contrast (the neutrals) ·
Acrylic, Glacier (see-through) · Paper, Harbor, Bloom, Ember (the colours) · Blueprint, Moss (the patterned) · Custom last.
Graphite stays second; Paper, Harbor and Bloom moved after the see-through ones. Fourteen choices: the list scrolls.

**Names**, new `settings.look.palette<Name>` in all 40 languages (Daylight, Midnight, Contrast, Acrylic — Windows' own
material's name —, Glacier, Ember, Blueprint, Moss). None the same as English: fr "Givre" for Glacier, nl "Contrastrijk",
ro "Contrast ridicat", vi "Kính mờ" for Acrylic.

Tests: `PaletteTests` (new) — `EachNewPaletteIsWholeInBothModes` (every section's every colour said in each mode, a bar's
pattern its colour, font, pattern and blur one in both, drawn as designed over Karpo's own, names their own),
`EveryTextReadsOverAnyWallpaper` (all twelve designed: Windows' surface, black, white; drawn unmixed), `EachIsWhatItWasMadeFor`
(see-through bars ≤ 60 % and blurred over Karpo's 30; the patterns; Midnight's black; Daylight's white; Contrast's black and
white, 7:1 and outlines; Ember's cards; Windows' high contrast over each), `EachPaletteWornIsKeptInTheFile` (each of the
fourteen worn, the file, read back, a value kept under its id, its reset), `ThePaletteDropdownListsThemInOrder`.
`LookTests.ThePalettesReadAsDesignedInBothModes` (thirteen, the first four still unlined, each design its own),
`AppearanceValuesTests` (the list's marks over fourteen), `PatternTests.PalettesReadOverEveryPattern` (the new ones over every
pattern), `HoverFilmTests`, `Localization`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.PaletteGallerySheets`,
palette-<id>-<dark|light>.png (the Appearance's preview of each palette over a test wallpaper, cut from the flyout's own
window: the display's picture lays a flyout over what is under it taking pure black for clear room, which turned Contrast's
and Midnight's black into the wallpaper) and palette-sheet.png (a row a palette, dark then light);
`AppearancePaletteSheets` appearance-palette-list-<dark|light>.png (the dropdown, fourteen, scrolling).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Palette: the order above; Acrylic: the wallpaper through the bar, blurred, and through the
cards; Glacier: grain on the bar; Blueprint: a grid on the bar and every card; Contrast: white outlines on black; Mode Light:
Midnight a lavender grey with dark dots, Daylight white.

## 603. Every widget that grew by tiers in widgets of fixed content: the performance graphs, screen time today and its history, the tides now and the tide graph, the sun's arc, the sports score and its lists; screen time's bars always (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), on §590's proposals for the widgets that still showed more as their line grew: *"split all of
them. also remove the are chart option from the screen time, it should always show the bar chart and not the area
chart"*.

**What showed more as it grew.** A performance graph (§9, §97) was four drawings by its height: one row (the figure with
the history behind it), the compact line (the second reading and a band), the whole widget (the figure large, two facts
beside it, the graph behind) and, from 160 DIP, the flyout's minute. The screen time total (§69) was a row, the row with
the daily average, then the day's name with its steps over the total large and the fortnight's bars (or, chosen, an
area); the tides (§236) a row, its caption, then the day's curve; the sun's arc (§368) the next event on a row, then the
picture over its strip with a countdown; the sports line (§239, §369, §479) a row, then the scoreboard and, scrolling, the
league's other matches, the matches to come and played, or the table or the knockout its View chose (§484).

**The widgets now.** Each says the same at each of its sizes — Compact the smaller arrangement of it, Full the larger —
and nothing more where its line is taller; its line is its size's form, whole cells (§432, §442), never rows. The lists
that only show more of one list (mail, the feeds, the agenda, the sports' lists below) keep their Height.

| Widget (file `kind`) | Says | Compact | Full |
|---|---|---|---|
| Performance · Graph (`performance`, a reading) | the glyph, the reading's name, its figure, its second reading (the busiest moment of the processor and the graphics, the memory in use of all there is, the disk's read and write, the network's down and up), the history | the name and the figure on the list's row, the second reading under the name, the graph a band under them edge to edge, 28 DIP at least (5 cells) | the flyout's top (§97): the name as full as it fits, the figure large and written out with what the graph's top stands for at its row's end, the second reading under it, the last minute on its quarters' hairlines, 56 DIP at least, how far back it reaches and "0" under it (9) — the scale, the span and the "0" the only words Full adds, the axes' |
| Performance · Numbers (`"style": "figure"`) | the same, no graph | the row and the second reading (5) | the name, the figure large, the second reading (9) |
| Screen time today (`screenTime`) | the day's name, its total and the daily average; an app picked, the app's time and the day's total it is part of | the kit's row: the glyph, the day, the total at the trailing gutter, the average as its caption (3) | the day's name strong with ‹ › at the trailing gutter over the total in the Hero, the average beside it, under it where the width leaves no room (5) |
| Screen time history (`screenTimeHistory`) | the fortnight's bars ending at the day shown, split by the top apps and the rest, the legend under them, the day shown marked; a day lit under the pointer and shown by a click, a piece saying its app | a 40-DIP band (4) | a 100-DIP band (7) |
| Tides now (`tides`) | "Tides", the height now, which way the sea goes, the next turn with its height and how soon | the kit's row, the turn its detail before the height (2) | the same row, the turn its caption under the name (3) |
| Tide graph (`tideGraph`) | the curve from three hours ago to a day on, its area filled, now marked, each high's and low's time by it | a 36-DIP band and its times (4) | 76 DIP (6) |
| Sunrise and sunset · Arc (`sun`, first style) | the sun's path, the place in its corner, the sunrise, the daylight and the sunset under the points they name; no countdown | the picture 56 DIP over the strip (4) | 96 DIP (6) |
| Score (`sports`) | a team's match now, last or next, or a league's lead match: the sides, the score or the kick-off, the clock or how it ended, the competition and the round, leg or outcome | the kit's row with its caption: the live dot or the logo, the score or "vs …", the clock at the end; the competition and the round under it (3) | the scoreboard: the competition and the clock over the two sides with their logos about the score, the round under it (5) |
| Fixtures and results (`sportsFixtures`) | a team's: on now under "Live now", the league's other matches on now, then Coming up and Results; a league's: its round's days | a list, as tall as it has up to its Height, scrolling (§371, §479) | |
| Table (`sportsTable`) | every group, as §479 | a list | |
| Knockout (`sportsKnockout`) | every round, the one being played brought into sight | a list | |

A competition with no table or no knockout says so on one row ("No table for this competition", "No knockout for this
competition"); a team followed has no knockout of its own to read, which says the same. A click on a row opens it on ESPN,
as before; every sports kind follows what its line follows, and the sports face finds its team on any of the four.

**Screen time's bars always.** The area went with its option: `ScreenTimeOptions`, `ScreenTimeGraph`, the line's
`"screenTime"` options, `WidgetOptionsKind.ScreenTime`, the Style row of the total and its two words in every language; the
history draws its bars at both sizes, and today draws no graph at all. Channels: today steps the folder's day (publishes
Day) and follows the day and the app picked and pointed at; the history publishes the day, the day pointed at and the app
picked and pointed at, which the ring and the apps follow, as the total's bars did.

**Placed on their own.** The add page's Weather and news: the tides' ready-made folder, the tides now and the tide graph,
then the earthquakes and the sun; the news and the markets, a line, the sports' ready-made folder, the score, its fixtures
and results, its table and its knockout (§490's cap twenty-four rows on the list's page, its runs still twelve at most).
System: the screen time's folder, today, its history, the ring and the apps. The ready-made folders: the tides now over
the tide graph; the score over its fixtures and results; screen time today over its history, the ring and the apps; a
reading's own preset its graph Full over its details (§97); System's readings and the network's in Connectivity and the
network hub Compact. The bar's faces — the graphs', screen time's, the tides', the sun's, the score's — are unchanged.

**Deleted.** The tiers: `PerformanceIsland`'s one-row, compact and whole-widget lines, `Details()`, `ProcessorFacts()`,
`Average()`, `MinutePlanned` and its probing (`MinuteLeastDips`, `LineGraphDips`) and the words only the whole widget said
(`widget.performance.average`, `.down`, `.up`, `.read`, `.write`); the screen time total's tiers, its sparkline, its fades
and its pressable area; `TidePlan`, the tides' height plan and `CurveLeast`; the arc's one-row form, its small picture and
its countdown, `SunTile.Floor` and the height-probed plan (the day bar's two forms are its sizes' now); the sports' View
(`SportsOptions.View`, the View row, `OptionGlyphs.SportsViews`, `SportsStore.ViewsOf`, the page-change motion, the words
`dock.sports.matches`, `settings.widget.sports.view.*`) and the score's scrolling. With no chart that stretches left,
`ListWidget.MostCells` (§432), `LineHeight.MostOf` and the folder's cap on a Fill chart (`FillMost`) went; tests of them
went too (`AChartThatStretchesStopsWhereItsInformationIsWhole`, `ACappedFillChartLeavesTheRestToTheGrowingDivider`,
`AChartThatStretchesStepsToItsMostRows`, `TidesPictures.TheLineDrawsWhatItsHeightHolds`, `SportsViewRowTests`).
`Presets.SystemCells` and `ReadingGraphCells` are sizes. New words: the five new kinds' and today's, the tides now's and
the score's new names and blurbs, the lists' two statuses, in all 30 languages.

**The file.** `Config.Shape` 81 (80 was §613's by the time it landed). No migration: a height on a sized line reads as
where its kind starts, an area or a view as nothing; the person's own file is converted once (`artifacts\tier-split\convert-tier-split.py`, cells as the file keeps
them, two a row; "fill" the largest; no height where a new line started):

- `performance` (any reading, graph or figure): Full where fixed at 8 cells or more or fill (where the old line drew the
  minute), else Compact.
- `screenTime`: Compact where fixed at 3 cells or fewer, else Full; at 4 cells or more, fill or no height, a
  `screenTimeHistory` right after it, Full at 8 or more, fill or no height, else Compact; its `"screenTime"` options go.
- `tides`: Compact where fixed at 2 cells, else Full; at 6 or more, automatic, fill or no height, a `tideGraph` after it,
  Full at 7 or more (automatic, fill, no height too), else Compact.
- `sun` (style `arc` or none): Compact where fixed at 4 cells or fewer, else Full; `dayBar` untouched.
- `sports` with `"view": "table"` → `sportsTable`, `"knockout"` → `sportsKnockout`, the height kept; else `sports`, Compact
  where fixed at 3 cells or fewer, else Full, and at 8 or more, automatic, fill or no height a `sportsFixtures` after it with
  the line's height; `"view"` goes from every sports line.

A split line keeps its place, id and options; the new one follows it in its list with a new id and a copy of its place or
what it follows. The person's layouts (`PersonsLayouts.json`) converted so: System's four-cell graphs Compact, the
readings' ten-cell graphs Full, the screen time's eight cells Full with a history Full.

and one the file says is dropped as it is read (`Appearance.Normalized` holds each section to what it may say, as for any word
it may not). Where a palette wants a border in a folder it is the folder's: the Flyouts' outline, round the open folder (§514).
The Taskbar widgets keep their Outline.

## 625. The add page's ghost whole, as it will stand; what edit mode shows off its bar on its own ground, light in light mode (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the ghost preview is a little opaque, this should not be the case."*; *"when having the light
system some colors are not actually updated like the ghost preview background color for example. (or when dragging a
widget)"*

**Read as**: "opaque" the faint ghost — see-through, 55 % (§593's `EditLook.GhostOpacity`) —, not the wash too strong: the
person wants the ghost to look real. The pictures in both modes said the same thing as the second report.

**The root cause, one for both reports.** Every edit visual's colour already came from the taskbar's look — the mode
Karpo's Appearance says, Windows' by default (§613, `Look.Wearing`) — and was dyed again with every update
(`Scene.EditBrushes.Dye`, `FolderFlyout.Dress`): checked one by one below, nothing kept a dark colour or a stale brush. What
stayed dark in light mode was *what showed through*: three things of edit mode stood without a ground of their own, so the
display's dim under them — black at 50 % in every mode, by design (§297, `EditShade.Ink`) — was their background:
- **the carried block** (`Dock.EditCarry`): the carry window draws the lifted block's own visuals, and a widget has no ground
  of its own — it stands on its bar's. Carried off the bar, a light bar's dark text and 3.5 % black wash stood on the dim:
  a dark, see-through block (the pictures' capture, flattening on black, even came back blank — why `EditSelectSheets`
  drew its carried group in dark alone);
- **the ghost folder** (§606) and **a ghost line** (§593) at 55 %: their light panels and cards half the dim, grey;
- **the empty ghost's line in a folder** (§617): its card at 0 with its line, a hole in the folder to the dim — black in
  light mode (`addghost-folder-empty-light.png` showed it).
In dark mode each looked right only because dark on black is what dark looks like.

**So**, no special case of light mode — what stands off its ground takes one:
- **A carried block takes its bar's ground with it** (`Scene.Ground`, `Unground`, `liftPlates`): lifted in edit mode, a
  rounded plate of the block's size and edit corner under it, in the bar's own colour (`EditBrushes.Ground`, the tokens'
  `Base`, dyed with every update as the other edit brushes; none on a Clear bar, whose widgets stand on the desktop), the
  lifted shadow under that — as a folder's lifted line has worn its folder's ground all along (`MakeRaised`'s plate,
  `theme.Base`). Several carried together each on its own. Taken from under it as it is let go.
- **The add page's ghost whole** (`Scene.Apply`, `FolderFlyout.Faint`, `ShowStates`): a pick's ghost on the bar, a ghost
  folder and a ghost line in a folder are drawn at 1, exactly as they will stand — still fading in by the motion, a new
  part's way. `EditLook.GhostOpacity` deleted. The empty ghost keeps nothing of its widget drawn, but **a ghost line keeps
  its card**: the room on its folder's ground, as the bar's empty ghost stands on the bar's.
- **No wash over a pick** (`Scene.ShowGhost(…, wash)`, `FolderFlyout.ShowMoreGhosts(…, wash)`), decided: the accent's wash
  over a whole widget tinted it blue, which is not how it will look; the blue outline round each card (§621) says "not yet
  placed". The wash stays where nothing is in the room yet: the empty ghost (§617) and a carried block's or line's gap.
- **A ghost line's outline over its line** (`FolderFlyout.OverTheLines`): §621 put the ghost folder's over its lines; a
  single ghost line's stood under them, seen through its faint card. Whole now, its card hid it, so the add page's ghost —
  a folder or a line — stands over the lines; a carried line's gap under them, as before.

**Every edit visual checked** (each in the taskbar's look, dyed again with every update and so following the mode as it
turns — Windows' with System, the Appearance's pinned one else):
- on the bar (`Scene`, `EditBrushes`): a block's wash, its outline and the brighter one under the pointer, the hover wash,
  the selected ring, the focus rectangle's two rings, the marching ants (made again for another accent), a part with
  nothing to show's glyph (`TertiaryText`, its colour in its key), the empty sections' rooms and the empty ghost, the blue
  ghost's wash and outline (a carried block's landing, a group's, the add page's), a folder dropped onto's outline, the "+"
  buttons (painted again for another accent), the lifted shadow (made again for another opacity), and now the carried
  block's ground;
- in an open folder (`FolderFlyout.Dress`, again for another theme): the carried line's ghost and its landing bar, the
  selected ring, the focus rectangle, the guide lines, a spacer's stripes, the lifted line's plate and shadow, the "+" and
  width buttons;
- the add page's ghosts: the bar's part and the folder are the widget's and folder's own, made of the ghost's copy in the
  taskbar's look (`DockWindow.Look`);
- by decision not the taskbar's (§526, §613: Karpo's settings follow Windows): the edit bar and its panel, the sections'
  edit bars (`EditRail`), the selection rectangle's accent (`EditBand`); and the dim, black in every mode (§297).

**Not done, decided**: a line carried out of its folder where nothing would take it stays at `CarriedOutOpacity` (60 %),
the dim through its plate: that faintness is the message "nothing takes it here".

No config change, no new words.

Tests: UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `SceneTreeTests.TheEditVisualsWearTheTaskbarsModeAndFollowItAsItTurns` (one scene, the mode
injected — Windows dark, Windows light, Mode Light under a dark Windows, Mode Dark under a light one —: a carried block on
its bar's ground of that mode, the empty ghost's wash that mode's accent and none of its drawing, a pick's ghost whole, its

`SceneTreeTests.AddGhostSheets` (the ghost folder whole). Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): addghost-* (whole, the empty line on

## 623. A backdrop over every display while a folder is open: the Flyouts' "Background while a folder is open", none by default (2026-11-09) — in the Appearance's preview too since §634 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"it should be possible to actually set a background for the whole screen when a folder is open.
that way you can darken everything else when a folder is open for example. this background should be applied to all the
screens when the folder is open."*

**The setting.** A colour of the Appearance's **Flyouts** tab, after their outline: **Background while a folder is open**
(`Tone.Backdrop`, `LookParts.TonesOf(Flyouts)` = Outline, Backdrop; new `settings.look.backdrop` in all 40 languages). The
Flyouts are where the folder's own look already lives (§514: the outline of an open folder is theirs), and the backdrop is
part of how an open folder shows — not the bar's, not a card's. Like every colour of the Appearance it is a pair (§568), the
page showing and writing the half of the taskbar's mode (§613), kept with the palette worn (§577), with its reset beside it
when it differs from the palette's design (§613). **None by default**: Karpo's own and every palette's design leave it
unset, which draws nothing — nothing changes for anyone who does not set it. No palette was given one: each is a look of
the bar and its cards; a screen darkened is a choice of the person's, not of a design.

- Its swatches: the dark neutrals first (black first: "darken everything else"), then the light ones, then Windows'
  colours (`ColorPalette.For(Backdrop)`); "None" first, as an outline's.
- Picked from none, a swatch comes at **half its opacity** (`ToneNames.BackdropAlpha`, 0x80 — the dim Windows and edit mode
  lay behind what wants the attention), never an opaque screen at once; over a colour in force it keeps that one's opacity
  (as every colour pick does, §459); the mixer sets any opacity.
- Unset, "none" or a colour with no alpha: no backdrop (`PartPaints.BackdropColor` null).

**When it stands** (`FolderBackdrop.Of`, pure): a folder open, **out of edit mode** and out of high contrast, a colour said.
Edit mode has its own dim (§612), which already darkens every display; a backdrop under or instead of it would be a second
colour for one job, so it stands down there — a folder kept open as edit mode ends (§348) gets its backdrop as the dim
fades out. High contrast draws Windows' system colours alone (§547), so none.

**Where** (Dock.Backdrop.cs): **over every display** — all of them, the folder's and the others — under Karpo's bars and the
folder, over every other app: the edit dim's stratum (`Stratum.Dim`; ZPlan: other apps < the dims < the bars < a folder at
rest). It **is edit mode's dim's layer** (`EditShade`): one full-screen window a display, now tinted (`EditShade.Tint`) and
titled for what it is (`EditShade.BackdropTitle`), kept for the dock's life once made, a display gone its window with it.
No parallel implementation: the same window, the same fade, the same clear-until-committed showing (§359).

**Reconciled once a frame** (`PresentBackdrop`, from `PresentChrome`, the frame's ending): from what the frame left — a
folder opened, closed, switched for another, edit mode begun or ended, a display come or gone, the colour changed — one
path for all of them; nothing done where nothing changed (the colour and the displays it was laid on, compared).

**The motion**: it fades in and out with the folder by the taskbar's one motion (§489, §612: a large surface's Show and
Hide, 250 ms in, 167 out at Normal), its window out of sight once it has faded; at once with Animations Off or Windows'
animation effects off. A folder switched for another (§446) leaves it standing.

**A press on it** closes the folder, as a press anywhere outside it does (the popups' hook: a window of Karpo's, the folder
closes and gives the focus back, LightDismiss), and its own window closes it too should the hook have been taken away
(Windows drops a slow low-level hook without a word). The press goes no further: the backdrop is the window under the
pointer, so nothing under it hears it — no click through to the app behind. It **never takes the activation**
(WS_EX_NOACTIVATE, MA_NOACTIVATE): the folder keeps the keys while it is open.

**Do not disturb**: a layer over a whole display is an app in full screen to Windows, whose rule turns do not disturb on
for it (found with edit mode's dim, 2026-10-08): while the backdrop stands it is told so as the dim is — one `TellDims` for both (it was two calls in the chrome's
reconcile), so a dim going and a backdrop coming in one frame tell nothing.

### The file

**Shape 82** (`Config.Shape`; `ConfigWords.txt` written again: `property LookValues.backdrop`). **The conversion rule: none
but the version** — a file of shape 81 has no backdrop, which reads as none, what it meant; nothing else of the file
changed. A backdrop said in another section than the Flyouts is not kept (`LookValues.Normalize`), a word that does not read
neither. No migration code.

```
appearance.palettes.<id>.flyouts.backdrop   { "dark"?: "#AARRGGBB" | "none", "light"?: … }; left out: none
```

Tests: `FolderBackdropTests` — `TheBackdropIsAFlyoutsColourNoneByDefault` (Flyouts' tones Outline, Backdrop, no other
section's; none in every palette's design in both modes; the Flyouts tab's rows Outline then the backdrop, "None" chosen;
black picked at half; its reset named; another colour keeps the opacity; the file's pair in its half, read back unchanged;
"none" kept; reset: nothing left; a backdrop said on a card dropped, an unreadable half dropped),
`AFileOfShape81ReadsWithNoBackdrop`, `TheBackdropStandsOnlyWhileAFolderIsOpenAtRest` (FolderBackdrop.Of: closed, edit mode,
high contrast, unset, None, clear); UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheBackdropFadesInAndOutWithTheFolderByTheMotion` (the layer
tinted, under the bar under the folder; frames between with animations on, its window gone once faded; every frame the
before or the end with them off), `TheBackdropCoversEveryDisplayWhileAFolderIsOpenAndAClickOnItClosesIt` (animations on and
off; the real dock, two displays at 150 % and 100 %: none at first; opened at rest, one on each display, whole, half black,
faded or at once as the motion says, the folder Popup over the bar over the backdrop; its face again: gone; opened again, a
click on the other display's backdrop — the window under it the backdrop's — closes the folder, nothing of Karpo's left
there; opened again and edit mode begun: the folder stays, no backdrop, the dims dimmed). stage-edit.json's new
`FolderOpen` (each folder open, at rest too) and `Backdrop` (each display's layer: laid or going, its colour, faded or at
once, in sight, where). `AppearanceModeTests` holds a shape of 80 or more, not 80. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR):
film-backdrop-open-on/-close-on/-open-off/-close-off (a test colour a capture can see).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Flyouts › Background while a folder is open: pick black — half black; Done; open a folder:
every display darkens under the bar and the folder, fading in; the keys still move in the folder; click the darkened desktop
(on any display): the folder closes, nothing behind it clicked; open another folder from the first: the backdrop stays.
Edit mode with a folder open: the edit dim, no backdrop. ⚙ › General › Animations Off: it comes and goes at once. Reset (↺
beside it): none again, folders open as before.

## 631. The languages searched: Language a search over every language, by any of its names or its code (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"you should be able to search the languages"*.

§521 left Language a plain dropdown ("the language list (31) scrolls as the person asked"); 41 rows now, and a panel popup
grows no filter of its own (§279's is an inline level's). **Now** the row is a search, as a time zone's is: no new mechanism,
the one every searchable popup uses (`OptionRowKind.Search`, an `OptionFinder`: `KarpoMenu.LanguageFinder`). On the panel
it stays a dropdown (§521: a search is a dropdown whose list is its field over its finds), its box saying the language in
force ("Default (English)", "Deutsch") as before.

- **Its list**: the field ("Search languages") over Windows default and every language in its own words, in their order, the
  one in force ticked; at each one's end its name in the language Karpo speaks where that is not its own ("Deutsch …
  German"). §587's one width, 240 DIP; the keys in the field as it opens (§559).
- **What finds a language** (`Languages.Rank`, `Languages.Words`): its own name, its English name, its name in the language
  Karpo speaks now, and its code ("de", "pt-BR") — every word typed found among them, accents and capitals aside
  (`CatalogueSearch`'s fold: "francais", "TURKCE", "tieng viet"). Best first: the code typed ("en" is English, not French
  or Bengali), then a name starting so, then a name holding it. Nothing found says "No matches".
- **The keys** as every search's: Enter picks the first find, Down goes into them, Escape puts the words back (every
  language listed again), then lets the keys go, then closes. A pick sets `language` as before (null for Windows default);
  the one in force sets nothing.
- **The names** (`core.language.name.<code>`, the code's dash dropped: `zhHans`, `ptBR`; `Languages.NameIn`): every
  language's name in each of the 40, CLDR's (Windows' own ICU), capitalised as a list item; English's "Bengali" and
  "Swahili" for ICU's "Bangla" and "Kiswahili". Many are English's words in other languages too (Hindi, Tamil, Hausa):
  names, so `UntranslatedTests` lets the prefix through. New words: those 40 × 40, and "Search languages" in all 40.

No config change.

Tests: `LanguageSearchTests` — `ALanguageIsFoundFirstByItsNamesAndItsCode` (own name, English name, code any case,
accents and capitals: 21 cases), `ALanguageIsFoundByItsNameInTheLanguageKarpoSpeaks` (French's "allemand", German's
"franzosisch"; the name at a find's end), `TheCodeTypedComesFirstThenANameStartingSo`, `APickWritesTheCodeTheDefaultNone`,
`EveryLanguageNamesEveryLanguage`; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheLanguagePopupIsSearchedAndEnterPicksTheFirstFind` (the
General page's popup as the dock opens it: 240 DIP before and after typing, the keys in the field, French ticked, Escape
back to every language, "germ" → Deutsch first, Enter kept and written as the dock writes it). `KarpoMenuGeneralTests`
read the search's finds where they read the choices. `UntranslatedTests`.

By hand: edit mode › General › Language: the list opens with the caret in its field; type "germ", "deu", "de", "allemand"
(Karpo in French), "francais": the language first; Enter: Karpo speaks it.

## 630. About Karpo is Karpo and Lometics alone, Lometics' line where it is; the edit bar no longer moves (2026-11-09) — Lometics GmbH its name over its line, no town, its site a button beside it, since §638 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"remove open meteo callout in the about section. rewrite the lometics description."*; *"the topbar
should not be movable anymore. remove that feature"*.

### About Karpo

**Open-Meteo's row is gone** (`KarpoMenu.WeatherDataRow`, `WeatherSite`): the section is Karpo (its logo, its version) and
Lometics GmbH (its mark, its site its button), nothing else (§579's third row, §339's credit).

**Lometics' line** (`settings.about.maker.description`) was "Independent software studio in St. Gallen, Switzerland": a
claim nothing in the repo backs, and a city that is not the company's — store/README.md gives its address as Gaiserau 39,
9056 Gais, Switzerland. Now one line of what is known: **"The company behind Karpo, based in Gais,
Switzerland"**, in all 40 languages, Karpo's name as it is, the town's name as each language writes it (Gais, Гайс, 盖斯).

**Open-Meteo's credit stays, where its data is set.** Its data is CC BY 4.0, which asks for the credit; About was the only
place in Karpo that gave it. It now stands under the Place of every widget and face whose data is Open-Meteo's — the
current weather, the hourly and daily forecasts (and their list and graph), the air quality (and its pollutants, pollen,
day), the tides (and their graph); the folder faces weather, air quality, tides — as the row's second line, the words it
had in About: "Weather data from Open-Meteo.com" (`settings.widget.weather.source`, `OptionFields.Credit`). The sun's and
the earthquakes' places have none (computed; another source). `OptionMenu` hands a search row's `Detail` to its item, which
the page draws under its name (`PanelRow.Second`), as any dropdown's description.

### The edit bar stands still

§395's grip and drag and §402's place kept per display for the edit session are gone: the bar stands at its own spot always
(`EditDeckPlan.Place`: centred, across from the display's bars, §296 — at the top with a bar at the bottom, the sides or
none; at the bottom under a bar at the top, its flyouts opening up, §584). It never had a keyboard move; its place was
never in the file (`Dock.deckMoves`, memory alone), so **no config change, no shape change, no conversion**.

**Deleted**: `PanelHitKind.Grip` (its part at the bar's start, its paint, its skip in the keys' stops and in the screen
reader's tree), `EditDeckAction.Moved` and `EditDeckEvent.Anchor`, `EditDeckAt`, `EditDeckRoom.Moved`,
`EditDeckPlan.Within`, `Offset` and `Dragged`, `EditDeck`'s drag (`dragging`, `Drag`, `Screen`), `Dock.DeckLeft` and
`deckMoves`, `dock.edit.move` ("Drag to move") in 40 languages. The bar is the grip and its gap (32 + 4 DIP)
narrower; its first entry a gutter in. `EditDeckRoom.Work` stays: the flyouts hang within it.

Tests: `KarpoMenuProTests` (About two rows, one site), `KarpoMenuTests`, `OptionFieldsTests.OpenMeteosCreditStandsUnderThePlaceOfItsDataAlone`
(every Open-Meteo line and face credited, the sun's and the earthquakes' not, the menu's item and the page's row carrying

## 622. A choice of the Appearance tried on while the pointer or the keys rest on it: the palette, a font, a pattern, a colour's swatch, worn by every bar and the page's preview till it is picked or left (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when hovering over an entry in the palette it should apply it / preview it with the whole taskbar
and also in the preview itself. the hovering should also work in other selectors like the font selector or color
selectors."*

**One mechanism: a copy of the config worn a moment** (Karpo.Dock\Dock.TryOn.cs). §523's mix already wore each colour of a
drag on the bars without saving it (`Dock.mixLooking`, the config the mix began on in `mixing.From`); that state is now the
dock's one: `wornOver`, the person's config while a copy is worn, `config` the copy. `Wear(next)` is `Apply(next, save:
false)` — the one look path, which builds again only what changed — with the open menu left standing under the pointer
(`MenuAgain` does nothing while a copy is worn). `Settle()` takes the copy off (`config` the person's again), and
`ShowSettled()` shows that config where nothing was applied since (`shownStale`). The mix's `MenuMixed`/`MixDone` wear and
settle through it; `mixLooking` and `mixing.From` are gone.

- **What is tried on** (`LookRows.TriedOn(key)`): a choice set (a `Set` pick) of any row of the Appearance — its keys start
  "Appearance.": Palette, each part's Font and Pattern, every colour's swatches and its "Default (…)" (and Mode, where it is
  ever a list). Nothing else's: a widget's own choices are not looks of the taskbar. One rule, no list of controls.
- **The menu tells where it rests** (`Flyout.TellsHover`, set by the dock on a menu holding such a pick): every change of the
  row lit — by the pointer or by the keys, one state (`SetHot`) — restarts a 50 ms timer (`Flyout.HoverMs`), and as it
  ticks the menu says `FlyoutEventKind.Hover` with the row, 0 for none (off every row, the pointer gone, `WM_MOUSELEAVE`).
  Sweeping through a list tells only where it stops. `Hover` was the thumbnail strip's, told and heard by nobody
  (`stripShowing` deleted).
- **The dock** (`TryOn`): the choice set on a copy of the person's config (`RowOfPick`, `OptionMenu.ApplyRow` — what a pick
  does, on a copy) and worn: every bar, every folder open, the Appearance page's values, its reset buttons, Palette's box and
  its one preview (§592) as the pick would show them. A row that is no such choice, or whose choice changes nothing (the
  one in force), wears the person's config again.
- **Anything done in the menu takes it off first** (`Dock.Settles`: Invoke, Adjust, Dismissed, Context, PassedKey,
  Reorder): settled before the event is handled, so a pick is made on the person's config — one change, one step of the
  undo, written once —, and shown again after it where it applied nothing. The menu closing however it closes
  (`FlyoutClosed`) takes it off too. `Apply` with a save settles first, whatever asked for it; `SaveConfig`,
  `SaveConfigAgain`, `FlushConfig` and the file read again (`ConfigChanged`, `ReadConfigSoon`) use the person's config
  (`Persons`), never the copy; a change of the file's own takes the copy off. Nothing is written while a copy is worn.
- **No flicker of its own**: wearing, taking off and the pick go through the one look path in the frame they happen in; a
  pick of the choice already worn applies the same look again. No new motion: the look changes as any look change does
  (none of its own with Animations Off or on); the list stays as it stands.

**Decided**: the page's values follow what is worn (Palette's box says the palette under the pointer, a value's reset comes
and goes) — the page is the taskbar as it would be, as Windows' own ComboBox shows the item the keys are on in its box.

Tests: `HoverTryOnTests` — `EveryChoiceOfTheAppearanceIsTriedOnAndNothingElse` (Palette, each part's font, pattern and
first colour a Set pick tried on; resets no Set; a pin's choices none), `WhatIsDoneInAMenuTakesAChoiceTriedOnOff`; UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `AMenuTellsTheRowThePointerOrTheKeysRestOn` (a real menu of Palette's choices: the pointer's row told as
the timer ticks, 0 once it leaves, the keys' row; a menu not telling, nothing). `HoverTryOnStageTests` (the real dock on the
stage, stage-edit.json's new "Worn": the Appearance worn, 1 while a copy is): `APaletteRestedOnIsWornTillItIsPicked` (the
palette the keys come to worn, the file untouched; the pointer gone, Escape: the person's look; Enter: written, one undo
back), `AFontAndAColoursSwatchRestedOnAreWornToo` (Taskbar widgets' Font, its Background's swatches; the list closed by
F4: back; a swatch's Enter written, one undo back). On the stage the keys walk the lists: a pointer posted to a window on a
desktop of its own is gone from it at once (the real one is elsewhere), which drives the leaving. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR,
`HoverTryOnPictures`): hover-palette-dark.png (Bloom lit, the bar and the preview in it), hover-font-dark.png (a font
lit, the page's value and preview in it).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Palette ▾: the pointer down the list — the taskbar, an open folder and the preview take
each palette as it stops; off the list, the look you had; a click keeps it, Ctrl+Z once undoes it. Taskbar widgets › Font ▾:
the bar's words in each font the pointer rests on. Background's picker: each swatch on the bar as the pointer rests on it;
the spectrum dragged as before. Up and Down in a list do the same as the pointer. Escape or a click elsewhere: back.

## 628. Add a layout a page of its own: a tile for each preset picturing its bar, Blank first, its way back at its top (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when adding a layout it should not open a dropdown but should open a new page where you also have
a preview of the different layout presets. there should also be one that starts just blank"*.

**Replaces** §472's and §599's "Add a layout" dropdown (the presets as a choice, a pick in its list: the row's `Choices`,
`ChoiceGlyphs`, `ChoiceDetails`). §472 stays for what a preset is and makes; §599 for where the button stands (at the line's
end).

    Displays and layouts                       Add a layout (the same flyout, its content replaced)
      …                                          ← Add a layout
      ⠿ ▦ Work                ⧉ 🗑 ⌄           ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    + Add a layout ›            │ ░░░░░░ desktop ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                                                │ ▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭ the preset's bar ▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭▭ │
                                                │ ▭ Blank                                  │
                                                │   An empty taskbar to fill as you like   │
                                                └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                  then Windows, Karpo, Focus, Planner, Monitor alike

**Decided: the flyout's content replaced, a way back at its top** — not a page of its own on the edit bar, not a dialog. The
Layouts entry's flyout shows the Add a layout page in place of the Layouts page, as Windows 11's quick settings show the
Wi-Fi list in place of their tiles: one plate across the flyout's top the whole of which goes back (as Karpo's own
`BackHead`: the back arrow, the page's title in Body Strong), standing as the tiles scroll under it. The edit bar keeps one
entry for both (the rename of "Displays and layouts" to "Layouts", §624, changes nothing here), selected while either page
shows; the flyout hangs from it and stays where it stands as the page changes (`PanelRows.EntryOf`: a page under another's
entry; `IsUnder`). An entry of its own on the bar would be an entry for one step of a task; a sub-page with a back arrow is
Windows' own way one level down in a flyout.

**A link, not a list** (`BarLooks.AddRow` an `OptionRowKind.Link`, new `OptionLink.AddLayout` → `EditEntry.AddLayout` →
`PanelPage.AddLayout`): Add a layout leads to a page as every link leads to the page that owns a setting, so it is one more
`OptionLink` — the dock's one way to land on a page (`PanelLinked`, `EditEntries.Landing`) — and the layouts line's "Add"
(§485) lands there too. Still a way to add one (`Adds`): its button alone at the line's end (§578, §599), its chevron pointing
on (ChevronRight, mirrored) where a list's points down; its hit a `Link`. Greyed past the licence's layouts, why under it,
leading nowhere (`OptionMenu.LinkItem`: any link greyed so).

**The page** (`LooksScope.AddLayout`, `BarLooks.AddLayoutRows`; built only while it shows, `Dock.PanelOf`): each preset
(`LayoutPresets.All`, **Blank first**, then Windows, Karpo, Focus, Planner, Monitor) a row that acts — its name, its icon,
its line under it — carrying the layout it makes as the look it shows (`OptionRow.Shows`, `LookShown.Itself`). One rule makes
it a tile: an action that pictures what it makes is a `Pick` (`PanelRows.One`), the add page's tile (§578), its picture over
its words (`PanelRow.Picture`, `PanelLayout.PictureOf`, `WordsOf`). Pictured tiles as wide as 400 DIP fit
(`PanelMetrics.PictureTileLeast`): one to a line across a page's 548 DIP — a bar is wide and low; two across would draw a 48
DIP bar 9 DIP tall.

**The picture is the real bar** (`LookSample.Itself`, `LookPreviews.Bar`): the preset's own layout laid out by `Layout` and
drawn by `Scene`, each widget its own island, as the Appearance's preview (§613) draws its stand-ins — across a desktop of
1280 by 144 DIP (a 1080p display at 150 %, `LookPreview.ItselfWideDip|TallDip`) at the scale that makes it the tile's width
(about 0.4: the widgets' own drawing at that size, crisp, not a picture shrunk). In the taskbar's mode and the Appearance's
values (`Look.Wearing`), over the desktop's picture (§613) or the mode's gradient, no mode badge. Its pins their apps' own
buttons, the shell's icons (`Item.Resolve`, in `Bar` for any sample with pins); no open app; the clock at 9:41
(`LookStand`). Drawn once a look and only moved as the page scrolls; its key the layout's widgets (kind, section, a pin's
target, a folder's face), not their ids, so the same preset made again is the same picture (`LookShown.Values`).

**What is pictured is what is made**: the page reads this PC once as it opens (`LayoutMachine`: its pins, its pen and touch,
Windows' taskbar; `Dock.presetMachine`, read again only as the page opens afresh) and the tiles and a pick are both made of
it (`AddShown(…, machine)`).

**Blank** (`LayoutPresets.Blank`; `core.layoutPreset.blank.title|blurb` in every language, "Blank", "An empty taskbar to
fill as you like"): a taskbar of the default size with nothing on it, the Taskbar glyph its icon; its layout named "Blank"
("Blank 2" after it) as every preset names its own — no special case. Its picture the empty bar's ground.

**A pick** (`Dock.PanelActed`): the layout made and shown on this display — `LooksPicked`, one `Apply`, one step of the undo
—, then the flyout is the Layouts page again at the new layout, its expander open and lit a moment (`OpenPanel`'s `nth`: the
level's *n*th thing, `OptionMenu.OwnedLevel`'s pick), where it is named and made the default.

**Keys and a screen reader**: the way back is the flyout's first stop (`PanelHitKind.Back`), then each tile in order (Enter,
Space). Backspace and Alt+Left go back, as in Windows' Settings and File Explorer. The page opened by the keys has them on
its way back; a pick by the keys lands them on the new layout's head. A screen reader: the way back a button, "Back, Add a
layout", at the pane's head (as `BackHead` says it); each tile a button named for its preset, its line its help.

**Deleted**: the Add a layout row's preset choice (`Choices`, `ChoiceGlyphs`, `ChoiceDetails`, its `Set` by index),
footright-layout-* (`SceneTreeTests.FootRightSheets`), `PanelPopupPlaceTests`' foot-layout check, Add a layout among
`DropdownWidthTests`' foot lists, `LayoutPresetsTests.AddALayoutListsThePresetsAndGoesBackToTheNewRowLit` (the menu's level),
`EditLanding(Layouts, AddRow)`.

**The file:** no change, shape 81: nothing of the page is kept; a Blank layout is a layout with no islands.

Tests: `AddLayoutPageTests` (new: every preset a pictured tile, Blank first; a pick makes exactly the pictured layout, Blank
an empty one, nothing else changed; a picture's key its widgets, not their ids; Add a layout a link to the page, under the
Layouts entry; its way back at its top, the tiles one to a line, picture over words, the whole tile its pick; Back the first
stop then each tile, "Back, Add a layout", each tile a button, its line its help; past the licence every tile greyed),
`LayoutPresetsTests` (Blank first, valid and empty; a pick by its tile; past the licence), `BarLooksTests`,
`LayoutsPresetTests` (the line's Add lands on the page), `EditEntriesTests`, `LinkRowsTests`, `SettingsPanelTests`,
`PanelControlsTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (R19: a pictured tile's size class), `MenuCorpus` (the page, for a laptop). UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `AddLayoutStageTests` (the real dock: Add a layout opens the page, no list; Back and Backspace return,
nothing made; Blank clicked: in the file, the Layouts page at it, its expander open; Ctrl+Z: out, one step),
`DropdownWidthTests`, `PanelPopupPlaceTests.AFootButtonsListIsOneWidthUnderItsButton`, `SceneTreeTests.FootRightSheets`.
Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.AddLayoutSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): addlayout-page-<dark|light>.png (the page, each preset's bar),
addlayout-link-<dark|light>.png (the Layouts page, Add a layout › at its foot).

By hand: edit mode › Displays and layouts: "Add a layout ›" at the right under the layouts; clicked: the same flyout shows

"←", or Backspace: the layouts again. Planner clicked: a Planner layout on this display, the Layouts page open at it; Ctrl+Z:

## 632. Every item across a line as wide as the others: the line in equal bands, edge to edge, each item in its band's middle (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the items in the hourly forecast should all have the same width. (right now the ones on the
edge are wider). this should be fixed for other widgets too if applicable."*

**Why they were not.** §611 cut an item's band round where its content stood: neighbours met halfway between their
middles, and the first and the last stretched out to the line's edges (`LineItem.Across(line, centres)`). The content stood
in from the edges — the forecasts' columns from gutter to gutter (`WeatherColumns.Of`), the hourly graph's hours on an axis
pulled in by the panel's pad and half its widest label (`DayGraph.Axis`, the weather flyout's rule) — so the end bands took
that inset on top of their share: at 300 px the hourly graph's hours were 32, 10, 10, …, 10, 32 px wide, the first and the
last three times the others; the hourly List's and the daily lines' end columns a gutter wider.

**Now, one rule** (`LineItem.Across(line, count)`): a line's width in as many equal bands as it has items, the first from
its leading edge, the last to its trailing one, each the line's whole height, on whole px (a px apart at most by rounding).
§611 holds: every band reaches the line's edges or its neighbour. What an item shows stands **in its band's middle**, so the
items stand as evenly apart as their bands are wide.
- **The forecasts' columns are their bands** (`WeatherColumns.Of` = `LineItem.Across` at the form's height): the hourly List,
  the daily List at Compact and the daily Graph draw each hour's or day's words, glyph and points in the middle of the band
  that lights. `WeatherColumns.Bands` gone; each tile asks `LineItem.Across` for its bands.
- **The hourly Graph in equal slices** (`DayGraph.Axis`, `Slices`, `SliceOf`): the graph runs the line's whole width, the day
  cut in a slice a whole hour from midnight to midnight (25, both midnights their own), every hour's point in its slice's
  middle; an hour's band is its slice. What the graph writes keeps to the list's gutter (`DayGraph.Gutter`): a label, glyph
  or value that would cross it is not written and the rhythm carries on either side — so the two midnights, a half slice
  from the edges, go unwritten (their hours still light and say themselves in the tooltip). **Gone**: the graph's panel axis
  (pulled in by `PanelPadDip` and half the widest label), unused since the weather flyout went; `DayGraph.CentreOf`; the
  nullable gutter and its two ways across.
- The daily List at Full is rows down the line (`LineItem.Down`), already as tall as each other.

**Every other widget checked**, by the rule test over every kind at every size and by reading their layout: none lays
bands across a line but the forecasts. Already one width and unchanged: the air's pollutants and pollen columns and its
day's bars (equal columns between the insets; the line pressed whole, §614), screen time's history bars (14 equal slots),
the folder's app grid (`FolderContentsView`, equal cells between its insets), the toggles and the actions rows (buttons,
their own plates, §428), the calendar's month, week and day grids (§428's own), the tide graph, the sun's arc and day bar
and the performance graphs (pressed whole), the sports lists, desktops and layouts (rows down).

No config, no new words.

Tests: `WeatherTargetsTests.EveryHourAndDayIsAsWideAsTheOthers` (new; the hourly Graph and List and the daily Graph at
Compact and Full, the daily List at Compact, 300, 360 and 517 px: every point of the line's middle an item's, in order, the
widths a px apart at most; red on the tip: *"hourly graph Compact 300 px: its items 32, 10, 10, …, 10, 32 px wide"*);
`LineHoverRuleTests.AnItemLightsItsLineToItsEdges` holds it for every kind: the items lighting a line top to foot are one
width. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR; `LineHoverRuleTests.TheItemsHoveredPictures`, was
`TheWeatherHoveredPictures`): item-hover-<kind>-<first|middle|last>-<dark|light>.png for the four forecasts in columns,
each a folder of its sizes; before and after in `artifacts\equalbands\`.

By hand: a folder with the hourly graph, the hourly List and the daily Graph: the first and the last hour or day light a band
as wide as the middle one's; the hours' times, glyphs and figures stand evenly apart, each in its band's middle.

## 627. A colour's picker in two columns: its swatches beside its mixer, one line of recent colours, two of presets; the bar's blur held to the file and the bars (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the color selector should have a maximum of one line of recent colors and two lines of color
presets."* — *"the design should be not row wise but column wise."* — *"the blurr factor cannot be changed"*.

### The picker in columns

**Read as**: the picker's parts side by side rather than one under another (§523, §613 stacked the swatches over the mixer,
twelve to a line, 400 DIP wide and about 350 DIP tall at Karpo's own Background). Two columns in the one 400 DIP popup
(`PanelMetrics.PickerWide`, §613's exception kept): **the swatches first, at the left** — None (or an account colour's
"Default (…)", §518), one line of recent colours, ruled off, two lines of presets —, **the mixer beside them** — the spectrum,
the hue, the opacity where the value takes one, the hex box. Weighed: the mixer at the left (the parent's first reading).
Left out because the swatches are the picker's quick choices and its first rows already: the keys' order (Tab, a screen
reader's) and the row the picker opens on (the swatch in force, §249's `ChosenTileInView`) stay where they were, and the
columns read left to right in that same order. The level is as tall as its taller column, the mixer's: about 220 DIP.

**Six to a line** (`ColorPalette.Columns`, `MenuPickers.SwatchesAcross`; Windows' grid's eight before §613, §613's twelve).
Weighed: eight (Windows' accent grid, the palettes' own columns) — a column of eight 32 DIP cells leaves the mixer 122 DIP,
and its hex box no room for "#RRGGBBAA" beside its swatch; six leaves it about 190, the spectrum as wide, the hex box whole.
Outlook's twelve calendar colours (`PartColours`, an account's) are two lines of six already.

**The caps are the data's, not the drawing's** — nothing is cut off where it is drawn:

- **Recent colours: one line**, six (`ColorPalette.MostRecent = Columns`, eight until now), newest first, the oldest dropped as
  a seventh is mixed (`Remember`); a file of more (an older build's eight) shows its newest six (`Recent`). No conversion: the
  file's list is a list of the newest, and the next colour mixed writes six.
- **Presets: two lines**, twelve each (`ColorPalette.For`, `Lines`):
  - a background, of the mode shown: six neutrals (Windows' own taskbar's #202020 / #F3F3F3 among them) over six tints, one hue
    each — blue, teal, green, brown, red, purple, §405's richer row (its deep row reads as black at a swatch's size; olive and
    plum left out) —, dark ones in the dark mode, pale in the light;
  - an accent: twelve of Windows' 48 round the wheel — red, orange, gold, green, mint, teal; blue (Windows' own, #0078D4),
    indigo, purple, orchid, pink, grey;
  - a text, an outline, a pattern's colour: the other mode's six neutrals over six of Windows' colours (red, orange, gold,
    green, blue, purple).
  §405's 24 backgrounds and Windows' 48 (`ColorPalette.WindowsColors`, public until now) went; Windows' blue, what a picker
  mixes from where nothing is set, is `ColorPalette.Blue`. Every other colour is the mixer's.

**One mechanism, any level** (`Flyout.Columns.cs`): a separator marked `Column` (`FlyoutItem.Column`) starts a column — the
picker's rule between its swatches and its mixer is one now (`MenuPickers.Rows`). `Flyout.Lanes` gives each row its column: one
of tiles as wide as a line of them (`Across` cells of `TileCellDip`), the rest sharing what is left, a rule's room
(`MenuMetrics.Rule`) between, a hairline down its middle the level's height. Every row fills its column as a row fills the menu
(its fill, its words' room, a rule inside it, `TileSpots` and `TileFill` in its column's room); the level is as tall as its
tallest column; a row reaches the pointer to the menu's side only from an outer column. A level in columns is the picker's
width wherever it opens (a submenu's too, not only the panel's popup).

**The keys**: Tab and Shift+Tab through the rows in their order — down the swatches, on into the mixer. Up and Down stay in
their column (a row of another column is never "the row below"); past its end Down goes on to the next column's first row, Up
back to the one before's last (`AcrossColumns`; onto a line of swatches, its first, §240) — in the picker the spectrum, the
mixer's first row, keeps its four arrows to move its point (§523), so the way back is Shift+Tab. Left and Right are the mixer's
own on its rows (§523) and walk a line of swatches, as before.

### The bar's blur: not reproduced

Probed in the real dock (`ArrangedFolderStandsTests.TheBarsBlurIsSetInTheSettingsPanel`, `Karpo.exe --stage` on a desktop of
its own): Appearance › Bar › Background blur's + a step more, + again with its reset (§613's Pair) beside it, − a step less, 15
and 100 typed in its box and Enter, its reset — each in the file at once, in the palette worn's values, and **each on every
bar**: the strip of the wallpaper under it blurred again at that blur's sigma at its display's scale. Karpo's own palette as
Windows is, Acrylic (its own 80) pinned Light, Glacier (60) pinned Dark on two displays at 150 % and 100 %. The model
(`BarBlurSettingTests`), the number box and its steps (§521), the reset's pair, the one-mode page (§613), the dock's rebuild and
its blur of the strip (§547, `DockWindow.Wallpaper`) and the preview's (its sample keyed by the whole Appearance) all hold. No
root cause found in the code; nothing changed for it.

What the person most likely saw: the blur barely shows. Karpo's own bar is #202020 / #F3F3F3 at **85 %** (§547): 15 % of the
wallpaper comes through, and from Karpo's 30 % (sigma 10 DIP, 15 px at 150 %) a 48 DIP strip is already smooth, so a step of 5
moves it by 1.7 DIP of sigma — nothing a person sees, on a photo spanned over two 4K displays least of all. The blur is plain
only on a see-through palette (Acrylic 50 %, Glacier 60 %) or a Background whose opacity is lowered, or from 30 % down towards
0. Greyed with why (§547) where the Background is solid (Midnight's dark half, Contrast). Open for the person: whether the
control did nothing (the number stayed) or the bar did not change; a coarser step, a curve that spends more of the range below
30 %, or Karpo's own bar less opaque would make it visible — each a decision of the look, not a fix.

**For the stage** (tests only, never the person's): a stage run shows a test's own picture on every display where its config's
folder holds `stage-wallpaper.bmp` (`Stage.Wallpaper`; `WallpaperStrips.Read` untouched), and `stage-map.json` says, per bar,
how blurred it shows it ("Wallpaper", its index the sigma in hundredths of a px).

### Tests

`MenuPickersTests.APickerHasOneLineOfRecentColoursAndTwoOfPresets` (every tone and mode twelve presets, once each, opaque;
six recent, newest first, a file's eight read as six; every Appearance colour row and an account's: at most six recent, twelve
presets), `ThePickersSwatchesStandInAColumnBesideItsMixer` (`Lanes`: the swatches' column six cells wide from the inset, the
mixer's the rest after a rule, 180–200 DIP; every swatch six to a line, the recent ones one line, the presets two),
`TheTilesStandInLinesAcrossTheMenu` (a colour's six whatever the room); UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1)
`ThePickerStandsInColumnsOnARealMenu` (hung as the panel hangs it, 400 DIP; the columns side by side from the top, three lines
of swatches, shorter than stacked; Tab through every row in order, Down line by line and on into the spectrum, which keeps
its own Up; pictures `picker627-<dark|light>.png`), `ArrangedFolderStandsTests.TheBarsBlurIsSetInTheSettingsPanel`
(three cases, above), `AColoursPickerMixesOnARealMenu`, `ThePickersActOnARealMenuAndThePicturesAreDrawn`,
`AppearanceModePictures.AppearanceModeSheets`, `DropdownWidthTests.EveryPopupOfThePanelIsOneWidth`.

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Taskbar widgets › Background's colour button: the picker hangs under it, the swatches at the
