left (None, your recent colours on one line, two lines of backgrounds), the spectrum, hue, opacity and hex box at the right; a
hairline between. Mix a seventh colour: the oldest recent one goes. Tab from the first swatch: every swatch, then the spectrum.
Bar › Background blur: + and − change the number and the file; lower the Background's opacity to see the blur.

## 636. One of the layouts is always the default: Set as default a button, greyed on the default; no None for new displays (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"one of the layouts always has to be the default one"*.

**Replaces** §595's switch (on for the default, off on the default leaving None) and §344's None for new displays
(`Config.NewDisplaysHidden`). §595 stays for the badge ("Default" after the default's name) and for where the control
stands (each layout's expander, its last row after Name and Icon); §579 for what the default is: what a display Karpo has
not seen yet shows.

    Layouts
      ⠿ ▦ Home (Default)  This display        ⧉ 🗑 ⌃
          Name             [ Home         ]
          Icon             [ ▦          ⌄ ]
          ▭ Shown on new displays   [ Set as default ]   (greyed: it is the default)
      ⠿ ▦ Work                                ⧉ 🗑 ⌃
          …
          ▭ Shown on new displays   [ Set as default ]

**Decided: a button, not a switch that cannot be turned off.** A switch says on or off is the person's to choose; one held
on and greyed reads as a setting someone else locked (Windows greys a switch so where a policy holds it). One of several
always being the one is what Windows' Settings sets by a button: Printers and scanners' "Set as default", Sound's "Set as
default device", Default apps' "Set default" — pressed on another, the default moves; on the one that is, there is nothing
to do, so it is greyed. §595 chose the switch because a button could not undo the default and None would need a row of its
own; with no None that case is gone.

- **The row** (`BarLooks.DefaultButton`, keyed `DefaultLayout:<id>` as before; an `OptionRowKind.Action` with words): the
  panel draws it as every row that acts and says something (§521, the palette's Reset to default): its card, "Shown on new
  displays" (`settings.layouts.default.description`) before the button "Set as default" (new
  `settings.layouts.default.set`). Greyed on the default; the badge on its expander's head says why. A menu (the edit
  bar's flyouts) shows it as an action, its words under its name. A screen reader: "Set as default, button", its help the
  words.
- **Writing it** (`BarLooks.WriteDefault(config, id)`): a layout's id only, no null; false for the default itself or no such
  layout. The default moves, never goes.
- **Deleting the default** (`Config.DeleteLayout`, as it was): the first layout left becomes it, the displays that showed the
  deleted one show that; the last layout is never deleted (§333).
- **Repair** (`Config.RepairLayouts`, as it was): a file naming no default, an empty one, or one that is gone gets the first
  layout — validation, not migration.
- **A new display** (`Config.NewScreen`): always the default layout, Karpo on. Hiding Karpo on one display — that display's
  own Layout None (`DisplayLayoutChoice`, `Screen.Enabled`, `settings.displays.none`, §309, §366) — is a display's choice,
  not the default's, and stays.

**Deleted**: `Config.NewDisplaysHidden`, `WriteDefault(config, null)`, the switch (`DefaultSwitch`), the layouts reset's and
the backup summary's `newDisplaysHidden`. **Words** (every language): new `settings.layouts.default.set` ("Set as default";
de "Als Standard festlegen", fr "Définir par défaut", es "Establecer como predeterminado", ja "既定に設定", zh-Hans "设为默认"…);
`settings.layouts.default.header` stays the backup summary's name of the setting; none gone.

**The file:** no shape change, 82. `newDisplaysHidden` is no longer read or written; ConfigWords.txt loses it (a property
taken away needs no new shape: an older build reading the newer file reads it absent as false — new displays show the
default, the same). A file saying `true` reads it as a word this build does not know: new displays show the default layout,
and the next save drops it. No conversion needed; Repair holds the default to a layout.

Tests: `BarLooksTests.ThereIsAlwaysOneDefaultLayoutMovedByItsButton` (the row's kind, words and button, in the menu too;
greyed on the default alone; pressed on another the default and the badge move, pressed on the default or for a layout that
is gone nothing; a new display shows it, Karpo on; the default deleted on the page: the first left badged, its button
greyed; one badge always), `TheLayoutsPageHoldsEachLayoutAsAnExpanderOfItsOwnRows`, `TheLayoutsPageGreysWhatCannotBeDone`
(each expander's last row an Action card, not a foot, greyed on the default),
`NamedLayoutsTests.ThereIsAlwaysExactlyOneDefaultLayout` (replaces `NewDisplaysMayShowNone`: no default, null, empty or
unknown repaired to the first, with `"newDisplaysHidden": true` a new display shown the default with Karpo on and the word
not written back; one that exists kept; the default deleted: the first left, its displays with it),
`SettingsPanelTests.TheLayoutsPageHoldsTheDisplaysAndTheLayouts`, `ConfigSchemaTests`. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR):
`SceneTreeTests.PagesSheets` — pages-layout-open- (Work's expander open, its Set as default), dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › Layouts: open the default layout: "Shown on new displays", Set as default greyed. Open another: Set as
default; pressed: the "Default" pill moves to it, its button greyed, the other's not. Delete the default: the first layout
left wears the pill. Plug in a display Karpo has not seen: the default layout's bar on it.

## 629. The add page see-through where its ghost stands behind it, and there alone (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), answering §617's question (A: the ghost folder over the page, clicks passing through; B: a shorter
page): *"the add widget modal should be semi transparent in case the ghost preview is directly behind it. but it should only
be semi transparent for the ghost preview and not for everything actually."*

**Where** (`SeeThroughPlan.Of`). The ghost's own rectangles — §621's, one a widget on a bar (`Layout.GhostRects`), one a
line of a ghost folder or of the folder the page adds into (`FolderFlyout.ShowGhosts`, `AddGhostsShown`) — where they run
under the add page: each one's part in the page, in its own rounded shape (its corners' radius the ghost's outline's, never
more than its half). Outside them not a px of the page changes; the gaps between a ghost folder's lines stay the page's.

**How** (SeeThrough.cs: `SeeThroughView`; `EditDeck.SeeThrough`, `Dock.SeeGhosts`, `GhostSight`). Not the page's window made
see-through — that would show the desktop and every window behind the ghost's own faintness — but the ghost drawn in the
page: the page's ground is a sprite of its own now (`PanelPainter.PaintFlyout(…, ground: false)`, the same
`FlyoutTheme.Ground`), under the page's drawing, and between the two a picture of each window the ghost stands in — a visual
surface of its tree, the very visuals, as a carried block's (`EditCarry`): the bar's scene, the folder's popup
(`FlyoutHost.Whole`) — cut to each of the ghost's rectangles, at `EditLook.SeeThrough` (50 %) over the ground. So the page's
ground thins to the ghost there while its tiles, their cards and their words stay over it whole and readable; nothing but
the ghost shows. Live: the ghost's fading in and out, gliding and growing (§617, §621) is the picture's, at once with
Animations off; the pieces follow the ghost as it changes (`Reghost`, `UnghostFolder`, `Unghost`, and a folder's ghost
moving: `FolderFlyout.GhostsMoved`), and are let go of before a ghost's folder is (no picture of a window gone). The ghost and
its picture change in the same commit, so nothing blinks.

**Input unchanged.** The pieces are pictures in the page; what the page takes is its layout's. A tile, an expander's head,
anything over the ghost takes the pointer and the click as before — §606's reason the page keeps its height holds, and B (a
shorter page) is not done. A (the folder over the page) is not done either: its lines would cover the page's tiles.

In practice the ghost under the page is a folder's: a ready-made group's ghost folder opened from a bar, reaching up under
the page (the air quality's, the world clock's), or the line coming into a folder the page stands over where too little room
is left beside it (§593 `AddLeastDip`). A bar's ghost is never under the page as it is placed (it keeps clear of the bars),
but would be seen through the same way. The stage map says "SeeThrough", a piece each, by its display. No config change, no
new words.

Tests: `SeeThroughPlanTests` (the ghost's rectangles ∩ the page alone: one wholly under it, one half, one beside it none; a
ghost outside the page or touching its edge none; each sight mapped from its own window; corners never rounder than a
rectangle's half). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `SceneTreeTests.TheAddPageShowsItsGhostThroughItselfThereAlone` (the air quality's
ghost folder under a bar's "+"'s page, and a clock's line among the world clock's lines under a page over the folder: the
pieces the page shows equal the ghost's rectangles ∩ the page; the page captured without and with the ghost: outside the
pieces not a px changed beyond the compositor's one step of rounding at the page's corners, inside the ghost there; a tile
over it the page's pick under the pointer, an expander's head over it opening and closing on a click);
`AddGhostStageTests.TheAddPageShowsItsGhostThroughItselfAsItGoes` (the real windows: a bar's "+"'s whole page, the keys along
Popular's first tiles: at each the "SeeThrough" pieces inside the ghost's lines ∩ the page, there alone, none for a ghost on
the bar, the page still the window at each piece; closed: none, the file unchanged) and `APresetsGhostOpensItsFolderWithItsLines`
(none while the empty ghost stands, the same rule for the air quality and the weather, none once closed). Pictures
seethrough-air-, seethrough-line- (and each -off, -on: the page alone), dark and light; `AddGhostSheets`' addghost-group-,
-air-, -folder-, -folder-empty- with the page showing its ghost as the dock has it.

By hand: edit mode › a bar's "+" › Air quality under the pointer: where its folder's top lines run under the page they show
through it, half, the page's rows over them; the rest of the page as before; off the tile: gone with the ghost.

## 633. A settings popup drawn as the settings pages are; the right-click menus as they were (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"i feel like the dropdowns for the settings dont completely match the style of the settings pages.
there are also other dropdowns in the right click menus, those you should not touch. but make the style of the ones that open
on the topbar settings pages more similar to the settings pages themselve."*

**What differed.** A control's popup (`Dock.PanelPopup`, the errors' list: `Flyout.Show` with its `control`) has been one width
since §587, but it was laid out and drawn as a right-click menu, Explorer's (§178, `MenuMetrics`). Side by side with its page
(`panel-dropdown-animations-`, `panel-search-language-`, `footright-country-`, `font-list-`):

1. **Rows of another rhythm**: 28 DIP plates 32 apart, where the page's controls are 32 and its cards 4 apart.
2. **Other columns**: plates 5 in, the icon 16 in and the words 44 in, where a page's card has its icon at 16 and its name
   at 48 (§548's columns).
3. **The choice ticked at the end** (a check mark in the far slot, the slot kept on every row), where WinUI's ComboBox marks
   its selected item with the 3 × 16 accent pill at its start on its plate in the subtle fill — the pages' own pill (§548).
4. **Explorer's two-colour pictures** in place of the pages' glyphs (Animations' Off a blue ✕), where the pages draw every
   glyph in the text's ink.
5. **Explorer's light rim in the dark** (#3B3B3B, `FlyoutHost.MenuRim`), where the page's flyout wears the theme's
   (SurfaceStrokeColorFlyout, the ComboBox dropdown's own).
6. **Headings a menu's**: Caption 12 semibold in the quieter ink (the font list's families), where a page's heading is
   Body Strong 14 in the text's.
7. **Values in the words' size**: a language's English name, a country's code at 14, where a page says a value at a row's
   end in Caption 12.
8. **A level's chevron** in the quieter ink, where a page's link chevron is in the text's.
9. **The scroll indicator** 2 DIP in from the edge, where the page's stands a tight space (4) in.
10. **The search box** 28 tall in a 28 DIP row, where a page's text box is a control's 32.

What matched already and stays: the surface (WinUI's flyout, the ComboBox dropdown's own: AcrylicInAppFillColorDefault, its
solid fallback without transparency), the 8 DIP corners (OverlayCornerRadius) and the shadow, the 4 DIP plates, the hover and
pressed fills (SubtleFillColorSecondary, Tertiary), the text's inks and Segoe UI Variable (§526's settings look), the search
box itself (the page's own `MenuTextField`), §587's one width, §521's ten rows.

**Now one branch: the settings popup** (`Flyout`'s `popup`, kept as `settingsStyle`). A control's popup reads its measures
from `PanelMetrics.Popup`, a `RowMetrics` of the pages' tokens, where every other list reads `RowMetrics.Menu` (MenuMetrics,
unchanged): plates a control's 32 (`Control`), 4 apart (`Tight`), 4 in from the sides, the top and the foot (`Tight`); the icon
at 16 (`IconAt`), the words at 48 (`NameAt`; 16 without icons); 12 at a plate's end (`Label`), so its end stands a gutter in
and a level's chevron 20 in (`ChevronIn`), in the text's ink; a rule a gap's row (`Gap`); a heading a control's row in Body
Strong (`Body`, semibold, the text's ink); a value in `Caption`. The choice in force: its plate in the subtle fill
(`SubtleHover`; none in high contrast, where that is the highlight) and the pill (`PillWide` × `PillTall`, the accent) at
its start, upright in its middle; no tick and no tick's
slot (a list with several ticked, Add a country's, marks each so). The pages' glyphs (no `ExplorerPicture`), the theme's rim
(`MenuRim` off), the scroll indicator `Tight` in. No number of its own: `PanelMetrics.Popup` names the pages' tokens.

**The right-click menus** — the bar's, a widget's, an app's jump list, the folders', every menu not hung from a control —
keep Explorer's look: their pictures before and after are the same to the pixel (`BarMenuPictures.TheMenuSheets`,
`ExplorerMenuPictures`: 36 sheets).

No config change.

Tests: `SettingsPopupStyleTests` — `ASettingsPopupLaysItsRowsAsThePagesDo` (three choices with icons hung from a box, dark and
light: plates 32 tall, 4 in, 36 apart, the icon at 16 and the words at 48, the choice's pill 3 × 16 at its plate's start and
no tick, no Explorer picture, not Explorer's rim; the same rows as a right-click menu: 28 tall, 5 in, 32 apart, the words at
44, the tick at the far end, Explorer's pictures and rim), `AMenusMeasuresAreExplorersStill`; `DropdownWidthTests` and
`MenuRulesTests` as before. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.SettingsSearchPopupSheets` (new:
panel-search-language-dark|light.png, General's Language open), `DropdownIconSheets`, `DropdownWidthSheets`, `FootRightSheets`,
`TheFontListPictures`.

By hand: edit mode › General › Animations: the rows as tall as the page's controls, the icons and words in the page's columns,
Normal on a lit plate with the accent pill at its start, no tick; Language: its box 32 tall, the English names in Caption;
Appearance › a Font: the families' headings Body Strong. Right-click the bar, a widget, an app: as before.

## 634. The open folder's backdrop in the Appearance's preview; the palette's reset asked first in Windows' dialog; a pattern picked from a grid of the patterns (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the background while a folder is open preview does not properly show."*; *"reset to default for
the style should show a system confirmation modal"*; *"the pattern selector should actually not be a dropdown but a grid of
the patterns where you can select the pattern you want."*

### The backdrop in the preview

**Why it did not show.** §623 laid the backdrop live alone (`Dock.PresentBackdrop`, its `EditShade` windows over every
display); the Appearance's preview (`LookPreviews.Draw`, §592/§613: the desktop's picture, the bar, the folder open) never drew
it. The colour picked, a swatch rested on, its reset: the preview's key changed (the Appearance's values are its words), so it
was drawn again — without it, the same picture.

**Now** the whole look's sample lays it as the dock does: the folder in the preview stands open at rest, so its backdrop is
`LookPreview.BackdropOf(look)` = `FolderBackdrop.Of(folderOpen: true, editing: false, high contrast, look.Worn.Flyouts)` — the
one rule, in the look the sample is drawn in (the taskbar's mode, §613; a copy worn by a choice rested on, §622) —: a sprite
of its colour over the whole room, **over the desktop's picture, under the bar and the folder** (drawn after the wallpaper,
before the bar). The bar draws its own blurred strip of the desktop under its see-through ground (§547, as live), so the
backdrop shows round it and not through it; the mode's badge stays on top. None (unset, None, high contrast): nothing, as
before. `Shown.Backdrop` for the tests (`LookPreviews.Backdrops`).

### The palette's reset asks

**Replaces** §577's and §610's "no confirmation (edit mode's undo has it)" for the palette worn's reset. Pressed, Windows' own
question first, a task dialog (`TaskDialogs`, TaskDialogIndirect, comctl32 v6), as every question of the settings already is
(a layout's delete, Quit Karpo, an account removed): the warning icon, **"Reset Graphite?"**, **"Your changes to Graphite will
be lost."**, buttons **Reset** and **Cancel**, Cancel the default (Escape and the close button too). Windows' wording: the
question in the main instruction, what happens in the content, the button the verb. Reset: the palette as designed, one
change, one step of the undo, as before. Cancel: nothing. **A value's own reset** (§613, the small ↺ beside a value) asks
nothing: one value, its undo one step.

- **Its words** (`LookRows.Rows`: the reset row's `Ask`, a `DeleteQuestion`): new `settings.look.resetTitle` ("Reset
  {palette}?"), `settings.look.resetConfirm` ("Your changes to {palette} will be lost."), `settings.look.resetButton`
  ("Reset", each language's word of `settings.barMenu.resetButton`), in all 40 languages.
- **One path for every settings row's question** (`Dock.GoesAhead`, `Dock.Ask`; `LooksPicked`, `SettingsPicked` and a widget
  page's `OptionPicked` had each their own `DeleteAsk.Ask`): an enabled action that asks goes ahead only on yes; anything else
  at once. The question is **modal to the settings flyout** standing open (`EditDeck.FlyoutHwnd`; else the bar or the folder,
  as before), so it stands over it and the flyout takes no input meanwhile.
- **The flyout survives it.** While a question stands (`Dock.asking`), `ClosePanel` does nothing: a press on the edit dim
  around the dialog (the dim is no window the dialog disables) is no click elsewhere. Answered, the flyout has the keys again
  (`SetForegroundWindow` on it).
- **Tests never show it**: `GoesAhead` takes the asking as a function; the tests answer.

### The pattern a grid

**Replaces** §462's and §513's Pattern dropdown (its list of names, each with its small swatch, `OptionMenu`'s choice list for
a row with `ChoiceSwatches`). Palette keeps its list.

    Pattern                        [ ▦ Dots            ⌄ ]       the closed control: the chosen one's swatch, its name
                                   ┌─────────────────────┐
                                   │ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐   │       None, Dots, Grid
                                   │ │ ╱ │ │:::│ │###│   │       Lines, Crosshatch, Waves
                                   │ └───┘ └───┘ └───┘   │       Checks, Contours, Grain
                                   │  …three lines…      │
                                   └─────────────────────┘

- **The row** (`OptionRow.Tiled`, set by `LookRows.PatternRow`): its choices a grid of tiles. `OptionMenu` makes each choice a
  tile (`OptionMenu.TileOf`: a `FlyoutTile` of its `LookSwatch`), the row as any choice's — the chosen one's small swatch in
  its icon's place, its name at its end — so the panel's control is a dropdown's box as before (`PanelRowKind.Choice`), the
  swatch beside the name, opening its popup under it (`PanelPopup`).
- **Each tile** the section's card wearing that pattern, as `Looks.PatternSwatch` has it (the bar itself for the Taskbar):
  its colour, its rim, the pattern **as the card draws it** (`PatternPaint.Fill` at the display's scale, its own strength, in
  the pattern colour — the actual pattern, not the row swatch's stronger, smaller sheet); **None** the card bare, slashed.
  60 DIP square in a 72 DIP cell of its own (`MenuPickers.LookTileDip`, `LookCellDip`), three to a line
  (`LookTilesAcross`): None and the eight patterns three lines of three.
- **The popup** is the colour picker's shell (`Flyout`'s tiles: `TileSpots`, `TileFill`, `DrawTile`; the lit ring; the keys)
  at the width every popup of the panel has, **a value's box's 240 DIP** (`PanelMetrics.ControlWide`; the 400 DIP exception
  stays the colour picker's — its rule asks for colour swatches, `CellDip` 0), fixed whatever it holds; three lines of
  72 DIP: **240 × 223 DIP** with the popup's padding.
- **The one in force** ringed in the accent, 2 DIP off its tile (an icon tile's colour; a colour swatch's ring stays the words'
  colour). **Lit** (pointer or keys) a ring hard round it in the secondary text's colour, as a swatch.
- **The keys**: the arrows across the grid — Left and Right along a line, Up and Down to the tile above or below —, Enter
  or Space picks, Escape closes; a pick closes the popup (`Flyout.OneChoice`, as a swatch's).
- **Hover try-on** (§622): each tile is a Set pick of an Appearance row, so the one the pointer or the keys rest on is worn by
  every bar and the preview until it is picked or left; nothing new.
- **Names**: each tile's name ("Dots") its tooltip (`Flyout.TipsTile`: a look's tile as an icon's) and what a screen reader
  says, as every row of a menu.
- Nothing of the list was the pattern's own: the pattern no longer goes through it. No config change.

Tests: `LookPreviewTests.TheFolderBackdropIsInThePreviewAsItStandsLive` (none by default; set: in the look and another
picture; the light half unset: none in light; Mode Dark: shown; high contrast: none; a swatch tried on a copy: the preview of
the copy lays it, the person's config untouched); `AppearanceValuesTests.ThePalettesResetAsksFirstAValuesDoesNot` (yes, no:
the question's words, Reset only on yes; a value's reset asks nothing); `PatternGridTests` — `ThePatternOpensAGridOfEveryPatternAndNone`
(every part with a pattern: a Choice, its swatch and name; None then the eight, tiles alone, each the card's colour, rim and
pattern, None slashed, the chosen ticked, each a Set pick, tipped; three by three in 240 DIP),
`ATilePickedWritesThePatternAndIsTriedOn` (each tile tried on a copy, the person's untouched; picked, written), UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheGridIsWalkedByTheArrowsAndToldWhereItRests` (a real popup hung from a box: 240 DIP wide, three
columns, three lines; Right, Down, Left, Up; each told as Hover; the pointer's tile told and named in its tooltip);
`MenuPickersTests.EveryColourRowOpensTheOnePicker` (a look's tiles are no colour's swatches). Pictures
(`SceneTreeTests.PatternGridSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): patterngrid-open-<dark|light>.png (Taskbar Widgets' Pattern open, Dots
ringed), patterngrid-backdrop-<dark|light>.png (the preview, the desktop darkened by a half black backdrop under the bar and
the folder).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Flyouts › Background while a folder is open: black — the preview's desktop darkens round the
open folder, the bar and the folder as they were; rest the pointer on other swatches: the preview follows. Palette: Graphite,
change a colour, press Reset to default: Windows' dialog "Reset Graphite?" over the settings flyout; click the dimmed desktop
beside it: nothing closes; Cancel: the change stays, the flyout has the keys; again, Reset: Graphite as designed, Ctrl+Z
brings the change back. A value's ↺: no question. Taskbar Widgets › Pattern: a grid of nine tiles, Dots ringed when worn;
the arrows walk it, the bars wear the tile they rest on; Enter picks it and closes.

## 635. The add page's ghost full of samples: a place that certainly has the data, built in, no network, no account (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"for the tides widget there is "no tidal data here". i dont want the widgets to take the current
place for just the ghost preview, for the ghost preview they should take a place that certainly has the data to show
available."*

**What it was.** §593's ghost was the pick put into a copy of the config and made by the ordinary factory, so a data widget
was made as a new one is: its place this PC's location (`WeatherOptions.New`), its store the dock's. Its data sources were not
started (`DataSources` follows the config), but the island itself registered with its store and asked (a face's `FollowTides`,
`Watch`; a line's first look): a hover fetched the tides of the person's own inland location and drew "No tide data here,
pick a coastal place"; a sports or news ghost drew "No team yet" / "No feed yet" and "Set up"; a markets line "No symbol
yet"; the mail and contacts the person's real accounts.

**Decided: built-in samples, not a sample place fetched live.** A fetch on hover is slow, can fail (offline, a service's
limit) and still shows "Getting the tides…" first; it would also send the person's hovering to the services. The samples are
made up and shipped in the exe (`Karpo.Dock\Samples\`, one `Samples` class), worded as each service answers and read by the
widget's own parser, made against the clock now so they are always current, there the moment the ghost stands:

- weather: Zürich's conditions, 48 hours and a week (`Samples.Weather`, `WeatherSource`);
- air quality, pollutants, pollen, the day's index: Zürich's, birch and ragweed in the air (`Air`, `AirSource`);
- tides now and the tide graph: Brest's sea, a high and a low every 12 h 25 min (`Tides`, `TideSource`);
- the sun (arc, sunrise, sunset, daylight, solar noon; its face): Zürich's position (`Zurich`), no position of this PC asked;
- earthquakes: a week of eight round Zürich, this PC said to be there (`Quakes`);
- sports (score, fixtures, table, knockout; its face): Barcelona in LALIGA, 2–1 against Real Madrid in the 67th minute, its
  results and fixtures, the table (`SportsTeam`, `Sports`, `SportsSource`); no logo asked;
- markets (a share, a rate, a coin, any range; the converter; the face): a store whose every answer is settled the moment it
  is asked (`Markets`, `Quote`; `MarketStore`'s new `settled`), the ready-made groups' shares by name, any other symbol a price
  of its own; a session on now;
- news (a line, a news face's own feed): six headlines, two unseen (`Feeds`; `RssStore`'s new `settled`), no picture, no
  site's icon;
- calendar (agenda, events, day/week/year views, month), next meeting (line and face): a week of meetings round now, the next
  25 minutes ahead with its Join (`Calendars`, `Calendar`);
- mail (line and face): five messages, three unread (`Inbox`, `Mail`); contacts: five people (`People`, `Contacts`); no
  account, the stores filled as a read leaves them (`Answered`), nothing due.

Not given samples, because they show this PC and the placed widget will show the same: the performance graphs, sound,
media, battery, drives, notifications, clipboard, screen time, the notebook's to-do and notes, the switches; and the camera,
whose picture is a stream the person names (it stays "Pick a camera…").

A widget that follows nothing yet (sports, news, markets) follows the samples' team, feed or share while it is a ghost
(`SportsTile.Configure`, `FolderIsland.Followed`, `RssIsland.Configure`, `MarketIsland.Configure`), and a widget showing the
samples never wants setting up (`CellIsland.Unset`).

**How a ghost shows them** (one rule, no kind special-cased in the dock). The dock names the ghost's key as it lays out from
the ghost's copy (`Dock.SyncIslands`: `Samples.Ghost`, the empty ghost none); the one factory makes that widget and everything
inside it — a ready-made group's lines, a news face's own feed, a ghost line in an open folder — under `Samples.Show(key)`
(`Islands.Make`). What is made then reads the samples from its making on, through the seams the tests already had: a face's
stand (`FolderIsland` `WeatherStand`, `AirStand`, `TidesStand`, `QuakeStand`, `SportsStand`, its mail, its markets), a line's
`Source` (weather, air, tides, sports, quakes) or `Stand` (sun), the store a widget takes (`MarketIsland.Made`,
`RssIsland.Made`, `CalendarLines.Store`, `MailIsland.Store`, `ContactsLine.StoreNow`). It remembers so (`CellIsland.Sampled`).

**The ghost put in reads the person's own.** §593's click kept the ghost's island; one showing the samples is now made again
instead, from the config (`Samples.Outlived`: made showing them, no ghost's now) — on a bar by `SyncIslands` (as a kind changed
under one key is), in a folder by `FolderIsland.Configure`. Same ids, same place; it reads its place, its store, its accounts
at once. The ghost folder's view taken by the click (§606 `GhostTaken`) shows the new island.

**The Appearance's preview and a layout's tile** (`LookStand`, §536, §628) show the samples too (`Samples.Show()`): a layout
preset's weather or news is Zürich's and the samples' headlines; the preview's own calendar of two events at its still clock
stays (`Samples.PreviewCalendar`, moved from `LookStand.Calendar`).

**One copy.** The tests' saved weather, air and tides (`Karpo.Tests\Forecasts\SavedWeather|SavedAir|SavedTides`) ask the
samples' (their generators moved into `Samples.Forecasts.cs`, the same values, every test's pictures the same); `--stage`'s
made-up calendar and inbox (`Stage.Samples`) are the samples'. `HardCodedEnglishTests` reads the samples' files as Stage.cs:
names and made-up data, not Karpo's words.

**Nothing written**, no config change, no network, no account, no location asked.

Tests: `GhostSamplesTests` — `TheGhostAndWhatIsInsideItShowTheSamples` (the key and its lines, not a key that only starts the
same; scopes nest), `EveryForecastSampleIsFullNow`, `AMarketSampleAnswersAnythingAtOnce`, `EveryAccountSampleIsFullNow`; UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `EveryDataBackedGhostIsDrawnFull` (every ready-made group holding such a widget, its face and lines, and
each such list widget alone, made as the ghost: drawn without a word of any empty state — getting, set up, no data here, no
team, no feed, no symbol, no events, inbox empty, can't be reached —, none wanting setting up, all made showing the samples,
the tides' store asked nothing), `TheGhostPutInIsMadeAgainAndReadsThePersonsOwn` (the tides group: the samples' sea as ghost;
put in, outlived, made again reading the store, its line no source; a ghost line in an open folder made again on Configure).
Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.GhostSampleSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): ghostdata-tides|air|sports|weather-dark.png.

By hand: edit mode › Add › Weather and news › hover Tides: the faint face (the next high or low) and its folder with Brest's height and
curve, whatever this PC's place; click: the widget placed reads your own place (inland: "No tide data here"). Hover Sports
scores: BAR 2–1 RMA 67'; News: six headlines.

## 637. A layout switch morphs: the bar becomes the other one — a taskbar shrinks into a dock, a dock grows into a taskbar — its widgets gliding, the rest fading, by the one motion (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"switching between layouts should have a very nice animation. optimize the animation also to look
smooth if it transitions from one style to another. (e.g. dock to normal taskbar etc)"*

**One mechanism** (`BarMorph`, Karpo.Dock\BarMorph.cs; the scene's side Scene.Morph.cs). Whenever a bar's window is laid out as
another bar — another layout shown on its display (the bar's menu, the layouts' line, the Layouts page), the shown layout made
another type — and motion is on, `DockWindow.Lay` keeps the scene as it stood, untouched, as the morph's **leaving picture**
and lays a **new scene** out over it in the same window (`NewScene`, the window's host; R2: the window stands still, it is
the edge's most thickness). Both are told one plan made from what each shows (`BarPicture`: every placed widget by key,
kind and block; the grounds — a strip, or a dock's panels by section):

| What | The new bar (`MorphIn`) | The old bar (`MorphOut`, under it) |
|---|---|---|
| a widget on both — the same id, else the next of its kind along the bar | glides from the old one's place at its size (centre and the smaller side's scale, held to ½–2×) to its own, fading in over the first half | glides to the new one's place and size, fading out from 40 % to 80 % — never a frame with neither |
| a widget on one only | fades in from 92 % size once the glides are under way (25 %–100 %: a large surface's Show, 250 ms) | fades out to 92 % size in the first half (a large surface's Hide, 167 ms, accelerate) |
| the ground | each new ground starts as the old ones that go to it together, else the nearest old one (a strip splits into three docks, three docks merge into a strip, a dock goes to the nearest dock); its corners round or square on the way; fades in over the first half | each old ground goes to the new ones it went to, gone by three quarters |

A strip is morphed by a rounded clip over its panel (offset, size, corner radius); a dock's panels by their own shapes —
material, hairline, shadow — so nothing is stretched. The ground's cut round the cards (§464) is off while the cards move
and back once they stand. All of it on Windows' decelerate in one time: `MotionKind.Morph`, **333 ms** at Normal (Fluent's
point-to-point third of a second; 500 Slower, 222 Faster), the one kind longer than 250.

**Its end** is the compositor's: the animations are started in a scoped batch whose end (heard on the dock's queue) puts
everything the new scene animated where it ends and lets the old scene go (`Morphing.End`) — no timer. Laid out again
first (any update of the bar), the window going, or another switch: it ends there, at once, and a switch starts from where
the bar stands.

**The window and the work area**: the window kept for every switch that shows on the same edge the same way (a taskbar and a
dock both holding their strip, or over the windows: `Dock.StandingEdges` alike); while a morph runs its region is its whole
frame (the old and the new both seen), the bar's own again at its end. The strip held changes **once**:
`BarMorph.HoldsNow` — a bar growing (a 48 DIP taskbar into a dock that floats 8 DIP up) holds its new strip only once it has
grown into it, the windows moving once onto a bar already there, no desktop strip showing while it grows; one shrinking lets
go at the start, the windows moving once under a bar that then shrinks off them.

**Another window** (the display's edge another, or a way of showing that has another window: a bar coming in on hover): the
display's old bar goes as a bar into hiding goes (`GoByMotion`: Scene.Present, Hide, its window destroyed once it has,
`Surfaces.Destroy(…, afterMs)`), the new one comes as a bar out of hiding (`ComeByMotion`: Show), in the same commit; a display
gone or new, at once.

**Widgets the bars no longer show** are let go of once no bar morphs past them (`Dock.lingering`, `MorphsOver`): the leaving
bar shows them fading from what they drew. Every display's morph starts in the one arrange, one commit: together.

**Off** (⚙ › General › Animations Off, or Windows' Animation effects off): no morph, no new scene — the bar laid out again in
place at once, as before (§358).

**Deleted / replaced**: §489's layout swap (`Scene.SwapIn`, `swapMade`: the new content slid 12 DIP up from the edge);
`MotionKind.Swap` no longer names a layout. No config change.

**Numbers** (`BarMorphFilmTests.TwoFourKDisplaysAt150PercentSwitchTogether`, two 3840 × 2160 displays at 144 DPI, both bars
switched in one frame, ten rounds taskbar ⇄ dock): the dock's thread per switch of both, median 9.6–14 ms (most 28 ms, once
97 ms on a loaded run), every morph over 390–440 ms after the switch (333 ms and the commit). The morph itself runs in DWM, not
on the dock's thread; DWM's counters (`DwmGetCompositionTimingInfo`) said no frame missed, dropped or late — but a hidden
desktop's windows are not composed to the screen, so that says little: watch it on the screen.

Tests: `BarMorphTests` (the same widget glides, else the next of its kind, the rest fade; a strip splits and docks merge,
radius on the way; a glide's scale; 333/500/222/0 ms and each step's curve and share; never a frame with neither; the work area
changes once growing or shrinking, against BarWorld's shell; layouts that show alike keep the window), `MotionTests`. UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `BarMorphFilmTests` (films: taskbar → dock → taskbar, the same window and a new scene, the plan's glides,
frames between for about the time, none going back, no jump; motion off every frame the before or the end, the scene the same;
islands → flush taskbar and back; a bar moving edge, one of the two always in sight; the 4K numbers), `LayoutSwitchStageTests`
(the real dock, Karpo.exe --stage: the layout switched in its file and back — every bar window the same all along, the region
its whole frame from ~150 ms and the bar's own again at ~550 ms), `RetainedBarTests` (the harness's host, two scenes at once).
Films (KARPO_PNG_DIR): film-layout-taskbar-to-dock, -dock-to-taskbar, -islands-to-flush, -flush-to-islands,
-edge-bottom-to-left, -taskbar-to-dock-off, -edge-bottom-to-left-off (.png strips, .txt frame numbers), layout-morph-4k.txt.

By hand: right click the bar › another layout: the widgets glide to their places in the new one, the others fade, the ground
shrinks into the dock's panels (or grows out of them), about a third of a second, no flash, maximized windows moving once;
both displays together; Layouts page › the shown layout's type Dock: the same; ⚙ › General › Animations Slower: half a second;
Off, or Windows' Settings › Accessibility › Visual effects › Animation effects off: at once. Display edge Left: the bottom bar
sinks away as the left one slides in.

## 639. Mail folders synced per account, through to the mail widget (2026-11-09) — Show from offers every folder by account, a pick syncing it, since §644 (2026-11-09)

The person: *"you should also be able to sync other folders than just the inbox for example. this change should be put
through all the way to the email widget as well."*

**Where it was** (§455). Karpo listed each account's mail folders, but read a folder only while some mail line's "Show
from" picked it: the dock gathered the union of every mail line's picks from the config (`WidgetSources.Folders`) and
handed it to the store (`MailStore.Want`), which asked each reader for those beside the inbox. ⚙ › Accounts showed the
inbox alone; a folder's sync was a side effect of a widget.

**Now: the Accounts page syncs a folder, a widget picks among what is synced** — as every other part of an account.

- **⚙ › Accounts › an account › Mail**: the inbox, then every other folder as the last read listed them, each a switch with
  the folder glyph, **off until turned on** (`Account.On`, the one kind of part that is; `SyncKeys.OffUntilOn`). Its row
  says its counts when read ("512 messages · 1 unread"), off its unread where the account gave it with the list ("Not
  synced · 3 unread"), else "Not synced"; no swatch — on the bar it wears its inbox's colour. The inbox may be off with a
  folder on (`Account.SyncsMail`); with every mail part off the account's mail is not read and its heading says so.
- **Readers** (`IAccountReader.MailAsync(count)` — the folders argument gone): the inbox unless turned off, every other
  folder listed, each turned on read the same way as the inbox (Graph `/me/mailFolders/{id}/messages?$top=30&$select=…&$orderby=
  receivedDateTime desc`; IMAP STATUS, EXAMINE, FETCH of the newest 30). Graph lists `mailFolders` and each folder's
  `childFolders` to 4 deep with `unreadItemCount`/`totalItemCount` (`MailFolder.Unread`, `.Total`); IMAP lists in one LIST
  with the special uses (RFC 6154): drafts, sent, archive, junk, trash first, by their own names ("Sent Mail", not "[Gmail]
  / Sent Mail"), then the rest in the server's order, \All and \Flagged last (`ImapReader.Listed`); counts with the list
  only where the server has LIST-STATUS — never a STATUS per folder just to list it. Read-only, no bodies: what rows show.
- **The store** (`MailStore`): reads every account with any mail part on, keeps each folder turned on beside its inbox
  (`Sync.Boxes`, by id, with its name), tells the report every folder with its counts and whether it is synced
  (`SyncPart.Folders`, `SyncItem.Off`), caches each synced folder's newest 30 with its name (`MailCacheFolder.Name`), so
  it is there offline. A part turned off shows nowhere, a line that picked it too, not even what the cache kept. A folder
  turned on is read at once (accounts.json's change is a change of `AccountSet.Shape`). `Want`, `Asked` and
  `WidgetSources.Folders` are gone.
- **The mail widget**: "Show from" (§455) offers each account's inbox (on by default) and the folders it syncs (off until
  picked) — nothing else (`SourceParts.Of`; since §644 every folder, those not synced saying so, a pick turning one on). A line of more than one folder, not inboxes alone, lists their newest merged
  by date (`MailStore.Merged`, as before) and names each row's folder at its end, before when it came ("Archive · 40m",
  `MailItem.Folder`, `MailIsland.Stamp`); a line of one folder or of inboxes alone names none. Its unread count is of
  what it picked; so is the **mail face's badge** now: the folder's face counts what its first mail line shows
  (`FolderIsland.MailShows`, `MailFaceDrawing.Look`), every inbox where that line picked nothing — §455 kept the
  inboxes'. A row opens its message as before (Graph's webLink, the message itself whatever its folder).

**Config.** accounts.json, per account: `"on": ["mail:<folder id>", …]` beside `"off"`, left out when empty — Graph's
folder id, IMAP's full name. config.json is unchanged: a mail widget's `sources` already keep `"<address>|mail"` and
`"<address>|mail:<folder id>"` (§455), and nothing written is every synced inbox. Conversion of the person's files: an
account with no `on` syncs its inbox alone, as today; a widget with no `sources` shows every synced inbox, as today; for
each `"<address>|mail:<id>"` in any mail widget's `sources`, add `"mail:<id>"` to the `on` of the account of that address,
or that widget shows nothing of the folder until it is turned on on the Accounts page.

Strings: none new (`settings.accounts.sync.off`, `.unread`, `.pair` and `core.accounts.inbox` say it all).

Tests: `SyncChoiceTests.AFolderIsOffUntilTurnedOnAndKeptInTheFileAsOn` (defaults, `on` as a patch and gone when empty,
the shape the dock hears, inbox off with a folder on), `.AMicrosoftAccountListsItsFoldersAndReadsThoseTurnedOn` (children
two deep, names under their parents, counts with the list, only the folders on read, the inbox off listed and not read),
`.AnImapServersFoldersAreListedBySpecialUse`; `AccountSyncRowsTests.AnAccountsMailFoldersAreRowsOffUntilTurnedOn`;
`WidgetSourcesTests.AMailLineLimitedToAFolderShowsThatFoldersMessages`, `.AFolderIsReadWhereTurnedOnAndOfferedToShowFromSayingWhetherItIsSynced` (§644's name),
`.ALineOfSeveralFoldersNamesEachRowsFolderAndTheBadgeCountsWhatItShows`; `OfflineCacheTests.TheFoldersSyncedAreThereAtTheNextStartWithoutAConnection`;
UI `MailFolderPictures.TheAccountsFoldersTheShowFromAndTheLine` (`mailfolders-account-<dark|light>.png`,
`mailfolders-showfrom-<dark|light>.png`, `mailfolders-line-<dark|light>.png`).

By hand, with a Microsoft account: edit bar › ⚙ › Accounts › the account › Mail: Inbox on, the other folders listed with
their unread, off; turn Archive on — "Not synced yet", then its counts a moment later. A mail line's menu › Show from:
Inbox and Archive; turn Archive on — the line merges the two by date, each row "Inbox · 4m" / "Archive · 40m", the head's
count and the folder's badge the two's unread. Turn Archive off on the account: it leaves the line at once.

## 638. A font's weight its own dropdown beside its family; Lometics GmbH its name over its line, no town; an account shut says everything synced of it (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"font weight should be selectable individually but on the same row. not combined into one
dropdown"*; *"the about should show the name Lometics GmbH as title over the description from where we are. remove the exact
location gais."*; *"the accounts when collapsed should show the amount of items totally synced."*

### The Font: its family and its weight, two dropdowns in one line

**Replaces** §556's one choice of every weight of every family (its families as headings, each weight a row). §556 stays for
the rest: this PC's families as DirectWrite has them (`SystemFonts`, `InstalledFonts`), a family or weight not installed kept
as said and listed where it would stand, the file's one value `"font": "Family/Weight"` (no config change, nothing written
differently), the kit's two weights on the font's.

    Font   [↺] [ Georgia                 ⌄ ] [ Bold      ⌄ ]
                 a filter, every family        the family's weights,
                 in the face it comes to       each in itself

- **The family** (`LookRows.FontRow`): every family installed (`TextStyles.Families`), under §556's filter ("Search fonts"),
  each drawn in the font a pick of it comes to — the weight in force where the family has it, else **its nearest**
  (`TextStyles.In`: of two as near the heavier past Medium, the lighter below, as CSS matches a weight). Picked: that font,
  one value (Semibold Segoe → Georgia Bold; Light → Georgia Regular; Sitka keeps Semibold).
- **The weight** (`LookRows.WeightRow`, "Font weight", in every language): the weights the family has
  (`TextStyles.Weights`), named as OpenType names them and each drawn in itself, a dropdown however few (`Grows`: Georgia's two
  are no segmented control), no filter (a handful). Picked: the family kept. No glyph of its own (R13: it stands in the
  family's line).
- **Both tried on** (§622): their keys are the Appearance's ("Appearance.widgets.font", ".weight"), so resting on a family or
  a weight wears it on every bar and the preview.
- **One reset** for the font (§613), after both: "Reset Font to default".

**The one pair, a pair of a pair** (`PanelRow.Pair`). A row marked Beside stands beside the row before it (§610); the reset
comes after the weight, so the weight — the family's pair — holds it in turn: `Pairs` (the chain), `Button` (the one that
acts, wherever in it), `With` (`PanelRows.Of`), `Own`, `LineOf`, `PathTo`, the layout's holders and rows go through the
chain. Nothing special for fonts in the panel: a Choice whose pair is a Choice lays both (`PanelLayout.Controls`), the
painter draws each control's dropdown (`row.Own(hit.Key)`).

**Where they stand, decided**: not as wide as one control together, as §577's colour pair was. A family's name needs the
one dropdown width (a 116 DIP half would cut "Segoe UI Variable Text" to a few letters, §587 keeps it in the box's 240), and
its list is §556's, searched, 240 wide; so the **family keeps the one width (240 DIP)** and the **weight is a box of its own,
140 DIP** (`PanelMetrics.PairWide`: "Extra black" in Black and its chevron), at the line's end where every control ends, the
family 8 before it, the reset 8 before that — §609's grid (the controls end at the card's end, a dropdown one column before
what follows it). Family first, as a font is said ("Georgia Bold", the box said "Georgia · Bold" until now). At 580 DIP "Font"
and its reset, family and weight fit (German "Schriftart" too); where the name would not stand whole (a narrow display's
flyout), the weight stands a line of its own right under it with the reset (§609's stacking), the family alone in the value
column. A dropdown's words are cut to its own box (`ValueRoom` by the box's width), whole in its tooltip; its list keeps the
one popup width (240, §587), hung flush with the box's right where its left would pass the flyout (§531). The keys: the
reset, the family, the weight; a screen reader hears "Font" and "Font weight", each a combo box saying its value.

Deleted: `TextStyles.All`, `TextStyles.Name`; the family headings of `OptionMenu.FontChoices` (a font's list is its rows, a
filter over a family's). Strings: `settings.appearance.styles.weight` in all 40 languages.

### About: Lometics GmbH over its line

§579 to §637 Lometics' row was a row that acts (§521: what it does said before its button, the button its name), so its line
"The company behind Karpo, …" stood as its name and "Lometics GmbH" was the button. Now it is a **note as Karpo's is**: its
mark, **"Lometics GmbH"** over **"The company behind Karpo, based in Switzerland"** (`settings.about.maker.description`, all 40
languages; no town — Gais gone), and its site a button **beside** it (`KarpoMenu.MakerSiteRow`, Beside: the one pair), its
words where it leads, **"lometics.com"** (not-ui, no translation), at the controls' end; its glyph Link (R13: Online has the
globe). A button of words beside a note has the room to the controls' end (`BesideWide`); its tooltip only where it is its
icon alone (`TipOf`).

### An account shut says everything synced of it

`AccountSyncRows.Holds`: each kind the account gives, in the card's order — the events of its calendars, the contacts of its
books, the messages of its inbox, the open tasks of its lists —, each the **sum of the parts whose row shows a count** (synced,
read, no problem of its own; a part turned off, not yet read or failing alone left out), the kind's plural
(`settings.accounts.sync.events` and its neighbours, `.one`/`.other`), joined as a part's own words are ("·",
`settings.accounts.sync.pair`): **"57 events · 312 contacts · 1,234 messages · 8 open tasks"**. A kind not given or not counted
yet is left out; nothing counted, nothing said. It comes with the account (`OptionAccount.Holds`, `OptionThing.Holds`, the
thing's item's value), so it is said again whenever a sync finishes and the page is built again.

On the panel it is the **expander head's value while it is shut** (§521: "shut, what it is set to; nothing while open: its
rows say it"), in Caption 12 before its buttons, cut at the value column's 240; the name and its address never run under it
(`ControlLeft` counts it). A screen reader hears it as the head's status. R14 leaves a thing's counts whole (as many as the
kinds it gives).

**Counts written as the region writes them.** The dock's .NET culture is the invariant one (`InvariantGlobalization`), so
"N0" would group every count with a comma whatever the region; every `{count:int}` of Karpo's words now goes through
`RegionFormats.Count` (Windows' `GetNumberFormatEx`, its decimals cut off): "1,234", "1.234", "1’234", India's "1,23,456"
(`StringsGenerator.Interpolated`; a `{count}` that is words, "99+", stays as it is). A part's own count says "1’234
messages" too.

### Tests

`LookTests.EverySectionOfTextHasItsFontsFamilyAndItsWeightBesideIt`, `AFamilyPickedKeepsItsWeightOrTakesTheNearestAndAWeightKeepsItsFamily`,
`AFontPickedIsOneValue`, `AFontIsReadInItsOneFormAndOneNotInstalledIsKept` (a family and a weight not installed kept, ticked);
`FontPairTests.TheFamilyAndItsWeightAreTwoDropdownsInOneLine` (240 and 140 DIP, 8 apart, at the controls' end; no line of its
own; values in their faces; the weight's room; the keys; the screen reader; no filter over the weights; Bold picked through
the menu's pick), `AChangedFontHasOneResetBeforeItsFamilyAndANarrowFlyoutStacksTheWeight`; `HoverTryOnTests` (the weight
tried on), `PopupPlaceTests`, `MenuRulesTests` (R13, R14). `AboutPanelTests.LometicsIsItsNameOverItsLineItsSiteAButtonBesideIt`,
`KarpoMenuProTests`, `KarpoMenuTests`, `PanelControlsTests`. `AccountSyncRowsTests.WhatIsSyncedOfAnAccountIsSummedKindByKind`,
`ACountIsWrittenAsTheRegionWritesAWholeNumber`, `AccountsPageTests.AnAccountShutSaysEverythingSyncedOfItAtItsHeadsEnd`.
UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.FontWeightSheets` — fontweight-row-<dark|light>.png (Taskbar widgets'
Font in Georgia Bold, the weight's list open), fontweight-family-, fontweight-about-, fontweight-accounts-; `TheFontListPictures`
(the family list, "geo" filtered).

By hand: edit mode › Appearance › Taskbar Widgets: Font, [Segoe UI Variable Text ⌄] [Regular ⌄]; Semibold, then Georgia:
Bold; the weight's list Regular and Bold, each in itself; rest on one: the bar wears it. ⚙ General › About Karpo: Lometics
GmbH, under it "The company behind Karpo, based in Switzerland", [lometics.com] at the end. Accounts: a synced account shut
says its events, contacts, messages, tasks at its head's end; opened, its rows say them.

## 643. A ghost not set up yet shown set up: this PC's own where it has one, else made up; put in as it is (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"also widgets like the drive one show no drive choosen yet, in preview it should just choose one best
effort or even make one up so that the user can see how the widget looks configured. this should be done for all the widgets
where this is currently an issue."*

**What it was.** §635 gave the widgets of data from far away or the accounts their samples; a widget that wants a field of its
own before it shows anything (WidgetSetup.Needs) was still a ghost of a widget not set up. Built as the dock builds its ghost,
every ready-made group and every list widget alone, these said so: the drive and the network drive "No drive chosen" / "Not set"
(and the drive's and network drive's groups' folder contents "No folder" under them), a folder's contents "Choose a folder in its
settings", a pin "Choose what to pin" with the warning badge (on the bar too), the camera "Connecting…" with no name (§635's
"Pick a camera…"). The notebook's note and to-do, empty on a PC with nothing in them, said "Click to write…" and showed an empty
list. Toggles and actions, the alarm, the timers and the clock come with their own defaults and were already full; the heading
says "Heading" by design.

**Decided: the ghost shown set up, from one table; put in as it is.** The ghost (§593) is shown from a copy of its own copy of the
config, whose empty settings are filled in (`AddGhost.Shown`, made by `AddList.Into`; `Dock.Seen` builds the bars and folders
from it); what the click puts in is `AddGhost.Config`, without them. The table is `Samples.Dress` (`Karpo.Dock\Samples\Samples.Defaults.cs`),
this PC's own where it has an obvious one, else made up:

| kind | the ghost's |
| --- | --- |
| drive | this PC's system drive (C:), read as the placed widget reads it |
| network drive | a made-up share, `\\nas\media`, 3.6 TB with 1.5 TB free, drawn from the samples (`Samples.DriveOf`) |
| folder contents | the Documents folder, read as the placed line reads it |
| a drive's group's folder contents | the drive's root, as the group's one question gives it (`DriveTargets.SpreadContents`, §119) |
| the network drive's group's | the made-up share's made-up listing: films, music, photos… (`Samples.Folders`) |
| pin (a line, and on the bar) | File Explorer (`shell:AppsFolder\Microsoft.Windows.Explorer`) |
| camera | "Lake Zürich", a lake under mountains at dusk drawn in the exe, a snapshot of a minute ago (`Samples.Camera`) |
| note | the notebook's note; where it is empty, a made-up one, "Weekend" (`Samples.Note`) |
| to-do | the notebook's list; where it holds nothing, four made-up tasks, one due today, one starred, one done (`Samples.Tasks`) |
| news, markets, sports, weather | §635's: the samples' feed, share, team and place, as the widget is made |

The note and the to-do read the samples where the notebook gives nothing while they are made showing them (`CellIsland.Sampled`,
`NoteTile.Note`, `TodoTile.List`); a drive line's drive this PC does not give, or the share's, is the samples' and never asked
(`DriveIsland.Read`); a folder's contents read the made-up share through the samples (`FolderContentsLine`, `PinItems` names it);
a camera made showing the samples shows their picture and never opens a stream (`CameraLine.Source`). No address of the camera
is asked (camera.example.com), no share's name looked up.

**Put in, a new one.** The widget placed is made again from the config (§635's `Samples.Outlived`) and wants what a new one wants:
the drive its drive, the pin its target, the camera its stream, and says so on its line, whose Set up opens its menu at
the field (§228). Not the ghost's: a pin to
File Explorer or a made-up camera put in would be something the person did not pick, and the drive's group asks its one question
anyway; the ghost shows how it looks once set up, the click leaves it to be set up.

Not given a default because they are this PC's state, not a setting, and the placed widget shows the same (§635): nothing copied,
no notifications, nothing playing, no screen time yet, no laps, nothing plugged in. A new empty folder is a folder with nothing in
it.

**Nothing written**: the copy is the ghost's alone, the notebook's samples are never saved, no config change, no network.

Tests: `GhostSamplesTests` — `EveryPickIsShownSetUpAndPutInAsItIs` (every pick of the add page, on a bar and into a folder: its
`Shown` wanting no field but §635's, its `Config` the pick as it is, the config untouched), `AGhostIsSetUpWithThisPcsOwnElseMadeUp`
(each default, the groups' contents, a setting already there kept); UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `EveryGhostIsDrawnSetUp` (every
ready-made group and every list widget alone, dressed and made as the ghost: no word of a widget not set up, none wanting setting
up; the share and the camera the samples', no stream opened; put in, the drive's group wants its drive). Pictures
(`SceneTreeTests.GhostSampleSheets`, KARPO_PNG_DIR): ghostset-drive|networkdrive|notebook|lines|pin-dark.png.

By hand: edit mode › Add › Files and tools › hover Drive: the drive's group with C: and its root's folders; Network drive: media
(\\nas) and its folders; click: the drive placed asks for its drive. In a folder, hover Camera: the lake.

## 640. Start hung from Karpo's Start button keeps Windows' gap to the screen's top and to the bar (2026-11-09) — superseded by §666 (2026-11-12)

The person: *"the start appears too high now"*.

**Seen** (read-only, 2026-11-09; nothing opened, moved or set). The bars, read through UI Automation: one on the right of the
main display (3777..3840, work area 0,0..3777,2160) and one on the left of the other (-3840..-3777), 63 px each, Start the
first button of each, at their top (3783,6..3834,57 and -3834,6..-3783,57). Every opening in appbar.log since §601 was hung:
on the main display *"Windows' Start 0,72..3840,2160 moved for Karpo's Start button to 2490,-825"* and *"Windows' Search
0,825..1287,2160 moved for Karpo's Start button to 2490,0"* (21:06:57; the host as Windows had it, 0,0..3840,2088, the same
at 20:26:55), on the other *"-3777,72..63,2160 moved ... to -3777,-825"* (16:21, 18:16, 20:06) with the box at -3777,0. The
numbers are §601's own: nothing doubled (§591's drop is measured from the display, not added to the hang), the box's size
the same at every showing (1287x1335), both displays 150 %. A passive watcher (28 min; StartMenuExperienceHost's and
SearchHost's windows polled, UI Automation once a showing) saw no opening, so Start's own rectangle was again not read.

**Why too high.** §601 took Start's outer rectangle to be the search box's width from the box's top to the host's end, with
Windows' gaps on all four sides, and put that rectangle flush against the bar and the work area. The box has the gap on two
sides only: it reaches from the display's left and the screen's end — the corner Windows' taskbar starts from, the box
going down over the taskbar's 72 px, past Start's foot — to Start's right and Start's top. Its near sides are the
display's (Start stands 12 DIP in from the left and 12 above the host's end, §580/§591), its far sides Start's own. So hung
from a button at the top of a side bar Start stood flush with the screen's top — the box at y 0 — and, beside the bar at
the right, against the bar; under a bar at the top it would touch the bar. With the bar at the left or the bottom the
rectangle's gap was the right one, which is why §601's tests and §591 looked right.

**Now** (`ShellPopupPlace.StartShift`): Start itself is placed — from the box's top to a gap above where Windows ends the
host, from a gap in from where Windows puts the box's left to the box's right — a gap (`StartGapDip`, 12 DIP, by the
display's DPI, `StartGap`; 18 px at 150 %) from the bar's inner side and inside the work area less the gap all round, centred
on the button along the bar as before. Host and box go by as much as Start does. For the user: the main display's host to
2472,-807 and the box to 2472,18 (Start 18 px under the screen's top, 18 px off the bar), the other display's to -3777,-807
and -3777,18. Unchanged: a bar at the left (63 in, as before), a bar at the bottom with the button at its left (no step), a
thicker bottom bar (48 up), every §580/§591 rule.

**Not known.** Start's own rectangle inside its host was never read; the box's top and right as Start's edges is read off the
box's shape (its near sides are the display's, not Start's plus a margin: its foot is the screen's end, 90 px under Start).
Should the box hold a margin above Start after all, Start now stands 24 DIP under the top instead of 12 — look on the PC.
Centred Start (TaskbarAl 1) keeps §601's guess of a box centred on the display.

Tests: `ShellPopupsTests` — `BesideTheUsersSideBarsStartKeepsWindowsGapToTheTopAndTheBar` (the user's bars and buttons, the
host and box as appbar.log heard them: Windows', §591's, where the build before left them; both displays),
`WindowsGapIsTwelveDipsInTheDisplaysPixels` (96, 120, 144, 192 DPI), §601's tests with the gap (under a top bar the host
744 px up, the box 18 px under it; along the bar Start's own 1269 px centred; the right end, beside a side bar, halfway down,
the other display, 100 %), 46 in all.

By hand (appbar.log open):

1. Press Karpo's Start button on the main display (bar at the right): Start opens at the top right, a small gap under the
   screen's top and a small gap left of the bar, as wide as Windows' gap at the screen's left when Karpo is not running;
   appbar.log *"... moved for Karpo's Start button to 2472,-807"* and the box's *"... to 2472,18"*. Type: the results stand
   on Start.
2. The Windows key with the pointer on the other display: Start right of its left bar, the same gap under the top.
3. If Start's top gap looks twice Windows' own (about 24 DIP against the 12 at the bar), say so: the box holds a margin above
   Start, and only the right side's gap is wanted.

## 645. A widget's page in plain sections, as the other pages: What it shows and Size, a heading each, every row a card (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the widget settings should have normal sections like the other settings pages not just the expanding
sections. for all widgets."*

**Where it was** (§529, §594). A widget's page was its header card over groups: What it shows and Height (or Size), each
one card under a head with an icon and a sentence of what it was set to ("An agenda of the next 7 days, from every
account", "Grows with its content, up to 12 rows"), its rows inside, a chevron to shut it. The General, Taskbar and
Appearance pages are headings over cards, so a widget's page read as another kind of page.

**Now** (`PanelGroups.Page`, `Sections`, Karpo.Dock\SettingsPanel.Widget.cs). Every widget's and line's page, every kind:
the header card (§529) at its top, then plain sections as the other pages have them — a heading, 8 DIP over its first
card and 24 after the section before, its rows each a card of their own, always open; nothing at the page's top folds. A
row nested under a choice (Days ahead under Style, Show seconds, Max rows under Height, Show from's accounts' line) is a
row of its choice's card, as before (§594).

| Section | Holds |
|---|---|
| What it shows (`dock.panel.group.shows`) | the widget's own rows; §594 the one level it holds where that is all (the tray's icons, the status icons): that level's name the heading, its rows the section's |
| Size (`dock.edit.size.title`) | a folder line's Height with its Max rows, or a sized line's Size |

A heading's key is its page's and its name, marked (`PanelGroups.HeadingOf`: "Widget/§Size"), never a row's of one name
("Widget/Size"). To a screen reader each section is a group named for its heading, its controls in it in the page's
order (`DeckUia.Tree`, as on every page); a widget's page has no group head's heading now. A landing (`EditDeck.Land`) on a
row of a section opens nothing (`PanelRows.PathTo`: an empty path); on a row in a level, that level.

**Expanders kept, and why** (the second level the person kept in §594; no third):

- A widget menu's levels inside What it shows, shut: **Show from** (a list of sources: accounts, calendars, mail
  folders), a timer's or focus's **Length**, an alarm's **Time** and **Repeat on** — optional, list-like, each saying what
  it holds at its end.
- **A folder's faces** (§552) on the folder's page: each a group under Faces with its handle, its Remove and its settings —
  a list of the person's things, as the Layouts page's layouts and the Accounts page's accounts. The folder's page was in
  sections already (§563) and is unchanged.
- A mixed value's **each one's** (§529) with several selected: opened on demand by its nature.

**Deleted.** The groups of a widget's page (`PanelGroups.Grouped`, `LevelOf`, `Group`) — `PanelRowKind.Group` is a
folder's face's alone now —; the sentences only a widget's groups said: the height's (`PanelSentences.Height`,
`dock.panel.height.auto`, `.fixed`, `.fill` in every language) and several selected's split of a group
(`PanelSentences.Split`, `PanelGroups.Page`'s `each` and the dock's menu of each one's that fed it). A mixed row still says
how its widgets split under its name (`PanelSentences.SplitOf`), a face's head what it shows (`PanelSentences.Shows`). No
config change.

Tests: `WidgetPageTests` (`AWidgetsPageIsPlainSectionsEachRowACard`: a calendar's headings What it shows and Size, no
group, every row once by its key, each heading a block with no line and no stop, its first card 8 under it, cards 4 apart,
24 to the next heading; `ATraysIconsAreItsPagesSection`; `ALandingInASectionOpensNothingButItsLevel`, a weather's Size
heading and Size row two keys; `ASectionIsAGroupNamedForItsHeadingToAScreenReader`; `WhatItShowsFollowsItsValues`;
`EveryKindsPageIsSectionsLosesNoRowAndLandsOnEach` over every `BarKind` and `ListKind`: a heading first, no group but a
folder's faces, What it shows then Size, no expander alone in a section, no row lost nor twice, every row landed on laid),
`MenuRulesTests.EveryWidgetsPageIsItsSectionsInOrderOfTheirSizes` (R17's order and R19's sizes on every widget's page,
every expander open), `SettingsPanelTests`, `PanelControlsTests`. Pictures (`SceneTreeTests.WidgetSectionsSheets`,
KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): panel-645-clock-, -calendar-, -weather-, -tray-, -folder-, each dark and light.

By hand: edit mode › a clock: What it shows (Time zone, Style with Show seconds, Name) and Size (Size), each a heading over
cards, nothing to shut. A calendar line: Show from shut in What it shows, Height and Max rows under Size. A tray icons
widget: Tray icons over a card per icon. A folder: Faces and Folder as before.

## 644. A mail widget picks its accounts and their folders: Show from by account, every folder, a pick syncing it (2026-11-09)

The person: *"for the mail widget you should also be able to select which accounts and from the account which folders
you want to show in the widget itself. e.g. inbox from two accounts or similar."*

**Where it was** (§455, §639). A mail line's Show from offered each account's inbox and only the folders turned on in
⚙ › Accounts, each account under a heading. In the menu that read; on the widget's settings page the heading went (a
card's expander leaves headings out, `PanelLayout.Inside`), so two accounts' "Inbox" stood one under the other with
nothing to tell them apart. A folder not synced was not there at all: to show it the person had to know to go to
⚙ › Accounts first.

**Now** — one list for the menu's Show from level and the settings page's Show from expander alike (`WidgetSources.Into`,
`SourceParts.Of`):

- **Each account a line over its parts**: its name, its address under it where the name is another, and on a mail line
  the colour its rows wear on the bar (its inbox's, `SourceColours`, the one the mail store paints) in its icon's place
  (`OptionRow.Swatch`). A line to read (`OptionRowKind.Note`), nothing to pick — in the menu a row, on the page a row of
  Show from's card, so no third level (§594). One account, no line (§445). Calendars and contacts get the same line
  (their headings went on the page too); their parts wear colours of their own, so no swatch there.
- **Every folder of every account**: the inbox first, then every other folder as the account's last read listed it
  (IMAP: its special folders first, §639; Graph: as Graph lists them, a folder's folders after it, "Inbox / Projects").
  One not synced is offered too, off, saying "Not synced" at its end (`SourcePart.Sync`, `SourceSync.Off`); an inbox
  turned off in ⚙ › Accounts the same.
- **Picking one not synced syncs it** (`WidgetSources.Pick`, `SourcePart.SyncOn`): accounts.json's `"on"` gets
  `"mail:<id>"` (an inbox comes off `"off"`) through `AccountBook.SetSynced`, the one way ⚙ › Accounts' switch writes it;
  the dock hears the file and reads at once (§639). Until the read lands the row says "Syncing…" (`SourceSync.Reading`:
  on in accounts.json, off in sync-report.json); the page is built again when the store tells the report
  (`Dock.HearAccountParts`), and the row then says nothing more.
- **Unpicking never turns a sync off.** Another widget may show that folder (a second mail line, the mail face's line),
  and ⚙ › Accounts is the one place a part's sync is turned off — Show from's "Manage accounts" goes there. A widget's
  "stop syncing" would make one widget's pick reach every other's, the coupling §639 removed. A folder synced and shown
  nowhere costs one read of its newest 30 per interval; the Accounts page lists it on.
- **Several accounts at once**: a line picks any parts of any accounts — both inboxes, one account's inbox and another's
  Archive —, merged by date as §639 has it, each row naming its folder where more than inboxes are shown. A new line
  shows every account's inbox, as ever, and nothing is written while the picks are that (`WidgetSources.Turn`).
  **No "All accounts' inboxes" row**: it is the default, and Show from says so at its end ("All inboxes"); as a switch it
  would mean nothing off, and as an action it would stand among switches against the menu rules. Back to every inbox is
  one switch per account, and nothing is written then.
- The menu's swatch survives a group's one-icon rule (§411 R13: a group whose rows wear one glyph shows none; a swatch is
  each row's own). On the page a line of a card draws an icon only where it is its own colour; a switch says its words
  before "On"/"Off" (`PanelLayout.SummaryWide`), as the menu's row does at its end.

**Config.** Unchanged: accounts.json's `"on"`/`"off"` stay the one record of what is synced (§639), a mail widget's
`sources` (`"<address>|mail"`, `"<address>|mail:<folder id>"`) what it picked (§455). Nothing to convert.

Strings: `dock.menu.showFrom.syncing` ("Syncing…") in every language; "Not synced" is `settings.accounts.sync.off`.

Tests: `MailShowFromTests.ShowFromListsEveryAccountsFoldersUnderItsLine` (two accounts' every folder, those not synced
off and saying so, each account's line with its address and its inbox's colour, the one its messages wear),
`.SeveralAccountsInboxesAndFoldersArePickedTogether` (both inboxes by default, nothing written; an archive beside both;
one inbox off; the file's round trip; back to the defaults, nothing written), `.PickingAFolderNotSyncedTurnsItsSyncOnAndItIsRead`
(accounts.json in the test's folder: picked, `"on"` written, "Syncing…", read once the store hears it, then shown;
unpicked, its sync stays), `.AnInboxTurnedOffIsOfferedAndPickingItSyncsItAgain`, `.TheWidgetsPageGroupsShowFromByAccount`
(the page's expander: each account a row, its address under it, its swatch, its parts after it, laid in order);
`WidgetSourcesTests` and `MailFolderPictures` as §639 left them, every folder offered now. UI
`SceneTreeTests.MailPickSheets` (`mailpick-page-<dark|light>.png`: the mail widget's page, Show from landed on;
`mailpick-menu-<dark|light>.png`: its menu's Show from).

By hand, with two accounts: edit mode › a mail line › What it shows › Show from: each account's line (name, address,
colour), its Inbox on, its folders off, those not synced saying "Not synced". Turn on the work account's Receipts:
"Syncing…", a moment later nothing more, the line merging both inboxes and Receipts by date; ⚙ › Accounts › the work
account › Mail: Receipts on. Turn Receipts off in Show from: it leaves the line, still on in ⚙ › Accounts.

## 646. An account's mail folders a page of their own: one row, Mail folders, in its expander; no third level (2026-11-09)

The person: *"the email folder selector to select which folders to sync should be under an additional menu so that the
account is not that long when extended"*.

**Where it was** (§639): ⚙ › Accounts › an account's expander held, under Mail, the inbox and then every folder its mailbox
lists, each a switch — an expander as long as the mailbox has folders.

**Now: the mail one row, its folders a page under the Accounts entry** (§628's sub-page, as Add a layout's):

    me@outlook.com                 ⟳ 🗑 ⌃          ← Mail folders · me@outlook.com
      Work        56 events [■⌄]  On ●            ✉ Inbox      1234 messages [■⌄]  On ●
      Home        Not synced[■⌄]  Off ○           🗀 Archive    512 messages · 1 unread  On ●
      Mail folders   Inbox and 1 more synced ›    🗀 Receipts   Not synced · 3 unread    Off ○

- **The row** (`OptionAccountRows.Parts`): the mail group (`OptionAccountGroup.Folders`, its words) is one link,
  `OptionLink.MailFolders` keyed `AccountsFolders.<account id>`, the folder glyph, what is synced at its end
  (`AccountSyncRows.Synced`: "Inbox synced", "Inbox and 2 more synced", the inbox off "2 folders synced", none "Not
  synced"), a chevron. A link to a page under its own (`OptionLinks.Under`: Add a layout, Mail folders) says what it holds at
  its end as an expander does (`OptionMenu.LinkItem`, `PanelRows.One`); one elsewhere says it as a line of words (§529).
  Calendars, contacts and task lists stay in the expander.
- **The page** (`PanelPage.MailFolders`, under the Accounts entry: `PanelRows.EntryOf`; `Dock.MailFoldersItems`): the link's
  own level — the inbox (its colour button) and every folder, each a switch with its counts, as §639 has them. Being the
  link's level, a pick there finds its switch among the Accounts page's rows (`OptionRows.Flat`, `SettingsRow`) and is set as
  every account switch is (accounts.json's `on`/`off`). Its way back at its top, "Mail folders · <the account>" (the account by
  its name, else its address; `OptionAccountRows.FoldersTitle`).
- **Back** (the arrow, Backspace, Alt+Left) lands on the link it was opened by (`Dock.linkedBy`, `PanelRows.BackTo`), its
  account's expander open, not lit, the keys on it where they were in use — the one rule for every page under another's
  entry, Add a layout's back too.
- **A switch's value**: a plain toggle's value is drawn before its On/Off (`PanelPainter`, `PanelRowKind.Toggle`), as a thing's
  switch's was: a folder wears no colour, so is no thing's row, and §639's folders' counts were never drawn on the panel.

No third level: the page is one level down in the same flyout, its rows switches. Forms typed on the Accounts page stay while
its Mail folders show (`MenuAccountsClosed` by entry).

**Deleted**: the folders' switches in the account's expander.

**The file**: no change (accounts.json's `on`/`off` as §639).

Strings (all 40 languages): `settings.accounts.mailFolders` "Mail folders", `.mailFoldersInbox` "Inbox synced",
`.mailFoldersInboxAnd.one|other` "Inbox and {count} more synced", `.mailFoldersSynced.one|other` "{count} folder(s) synced".

Tests: `MailFoldersPageTests` (new: the expander holds one Mail folders row, glyph, words, link, no folder switch on the page;
the page lists the inbox and every folder with counts and the inbox's colour, a folder turned on writes `"on"` in an
accounts.json of the test's own, the mail's keys sent there and not on the Accounts page; under the Accounts entry, back
first, "Back, Mail folders · me@outlook.com", each folder a toggle; back lands on the link in its account's expander; UI:
Enter on the link, the keys on Back, Tab to Inbox, Backspace to the link, expander open, in sight),
`AccountSyncRowsTests.TheMailFoldersLinkSaysWhatIsSynced`, `AccountsPageTests`, `EditEntriesTests`, `AddLayoutPageTests`
(EntryOf). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, `SceneTreeTests.MailFolderPageSheets`): mailfolderpage-account-<dark|light>.png,
mailfolderpage-page-<dark|light>.png; `MailFolderPictures`' mailfolders-account-* now the page's level.

By hand: edit bar › Accounts › an account: under Work and Home, "Mail folders  Inbox synced ›"; click: "← Mail folders ·
the account", Inbox and every folder; turn Archive on: "Not synced yet", then its counts; ← (or Backspace): the Accounts
page, the account still open, its row "Inbox and 1 more synced".

## 641. Start (beta): a ready-made group that is Windows 11's Start, made of five Beta widgets — search, pinned apps, All apps, Recommended, account and power (2026-11-09) — four, the search box gone, since §653 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"create a widget group that looks like the start. for this you can also create new widgets to achieve
the look and features that the start has. (mark them as beta in the add) … make those widgets / groups feature rich. first
study what win11 has for features in these areas and then go ahead and implement them and also see how you can improve on them
too."*

### What Windows 11's Start has, and what Karpo's does

Read from Microsoft's own pages (support.microsoft.com, "See what's on the Start menu", "Customize the Start menu"; the Windows
Insider blog's 2025 Start, builds 26120.4250/26200.5641 of June 2025, Canary 27965 of 2025-10-08, Release Preview
26100.7015/26200.7015 of 2025-10-21; learn.microsoft.com for the APIs named below).

| Windows 11's Start (25H2, 2025's redesign) | Karpo's Start (beta) |
|---|---|
