| Search box at the top (opens Windows Search) | *(Removed in §653.)* **Start search** line: typing narrows the apps of every Start line in the folder at once (the folder's `search` channel); Enter opens the best match, which the box names at its end ("→ Paint"); Escape clears it first |
| Search matches the start of a word | Fuzzy and folded: a name's start, a word's start, the words' initials ("vsc"), anywhere, letters in order; no case, no accents (`StartSearch`) *(removed in §653)* |
| Pinned: a grid (6 across), 3 lines (Layout: more pins / default / more recommendations), "Show all" | **Pinned apps** line: a grid as wide as its list (3–8 across, 6 in Wide), Compact one line, Full three, more scroll under "Pinned" |
| Pin to Start / Unpin from Start / Move to front (right click) | The same rows; Pin to Start from All apps and Recommended pins to the pinned apps beside them |
| Pins reordered by dragging; Alt+Shift+arrows | A tile dragged onto another place (an accent bar where it goes); Ctrl+Shift+arrows (Alt goes to Windows' own menus) |
| Folders of pins (drag one onto another) | Not built — a Karpo folder of pins is the way (see "Left for later") |
| Default pins from the OEM's layout (start2.bin, not readable) | This PC's usual Windows apps in Start's own order, those it has (`StartPins.Usual`), until a pin is changed |
| Recommended: recent files, new apps, (websites, tips), on or off in Settings | **Recommended** line: files opened lately (Windows' Recent folder) and apps first seen in the last week, newest first, two across; Compact one line, Full three; files / new apps each a switch on its page |
| A file's "when": "15m ago", "Yesterday at …" | The time today, the day and time this week, else the date — the region's own formats (Nls), no new words |
| All (2025: on the same page as Pinned, scrolling); views Category (folders of ≥ 3, auto-sorted), Grid, List; Start remembers the view | **All apps** line beside the others (a list of its own, as tall as they are — no scrolling of the whole folder needed); views Category, Grid, List, its button a menu ("Category ⌄"), the view kept in the line |
| Categories from the Store's metadata | From the name against a table of the apps people have (Productivity, Creativity, Social, Entertainment, Games, Utilities & Tools, Other); fewer than three fold into Other, as Windows' |
| "Recently added" at the top of All | The same, in every view, while an app is new (first seen by Karpo within 7 days) |
| A–Z list with letter headers; the letter index | Letter heads (& # A–Z, folded); no letter jump yet |
| Right click: Open, Run as administrator, Open file location, Uninstall, App settings, Share, Rate | Open, Run as administrator and Open file location (desktop apps), Pin/Unpin, Move to front, Uninstall (Settings' Installed apps, Windows' one way) |
| Jump lists on a pinned app's right click | Not in Start's menus yet (JumpLists.cs is the bar's; see "Left for later") |
| Account button: picture and name; Change account settings, Lock, Sign out, other users / Switch user | **Account and power** line: the account's picture in its circle (its initials where there is none), its name; Change account settings, Lock, Sign out, Switch user |
| Power: Sleep, Hibernate (if on), Shut down, Restart; "Update and restart / shut down" while updates wait, the orange dot | The same, Sleep and Hibernate where Windows' power menu offers them, the update rows and the orange dot while a restart is due |
| Folders next to power (Settings, File Explorer, Documents, Downloads, Music, Pictures, Videos, Network, Personal folder) | The same nine, Settings and File Explorer by default, each a switch on its page |
| Phone Link companion panel | Not built (a Phone Link widget is no part of this group) |
| Keyboard: arrows, Enter, Escape, type to search at once | The box has the keys as the folder opens *(no box since §653)*; every tile, row, button is a stop of the folder's keys (arrows, Tab, Enter, Menu key); Ctrl+Shift+arrows move a pin |
| What is opened most | Frecency (Firefox's weighing): among matches as good, what is opened most and latest first; Karpo's own record on this PC (`start.tsv`) *(the weighing removed with the search in §653; the record stays)* |

### The group

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐
    │ [🔍 Search                      → Paint] │ │ All apps            Category⌄│
    │ Pinned                                    │ │ Recently added               │
    │  ▢    ▢    ▢    ▢    ▢    ▢               │ │   ▢                          │
    │ Edge Word Excel PPT Outlook Copilot        │ │ Productivity                 │
    │  … three lines …                          │ │   ▢  ▢  ▢  ▢                 │
    │ Recommended                               │ │ Games                        │
    │  ▤ Quarterly report.docx  ▤ Budget.xlsx    │ │   …                          │
    │  ▣ Clipchamp  Recently added …            │ │                              │
    │ (AM) Alex Morgan              ⚙  🗀  ⏻•    │ │                              │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘
          Wide (480 DIP)                                  Medium (360 DIP)

`Presets.StartId` ("startGroup"), its face Windows' glyph. Left: `startSearch` (one form, 3 cells), `startPins` Full (16),
`startRecommended` Full (10), `startProfile` (one form, 3) — 32 cells; right: `startApps`, fixed 32 so the two end level. Down a
side bar one list (§620), All apps fixed 20 under the rest. Offered in Start and taskbar's own run after Windows' three
(AddTree), its five widgets after it; a folder's page offers the five. *(Since §653: no `startSearch`; the left 29 cells, All apps
fixed 29, down a side bar 16.)*

### The widgets (new ListKinds, `WidgetOptionsKind.Start`)

| Kind (file word) | Drawing (Karpo.Dock\StartWidgets) | Sizes | Options (`StartOptions`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `startSearch` *(removed in §653)* | StartSearchLine — the quick settings' TextField, publishes `Channels.Search` | one form | none |
| `startPins` | StartAppsLine — tiles; drag and keys reorder | Compact / Full | `pins` (null: the usual ones) |
| `startApps` | StartAppsLine — categories, grid or list | grows (Height) | `view` (null: category) |
| `startRecommended` | StartRecommendedLine | Compact / Full | `files`, `newApps` (null: yes) |
| `startProfile` | StartProfileLine | one form | `places` (null: Settings, File Explorer) |

Each is marked `WidgetInfo.Beta`; a preset holding one is `Preset.Beta`; the add page's tile wears **"Beta"** (§595's badge,
`FlyoutItem.Badge`, `S.DockAddBeta`), kept by the search's results and said to a screen reader after its count. The pins, the
view and the folders are changed through the dock as any edit (`StartEdits.Apply` on a copy, `Dock.Apply`: saved, a step of edit
mode's undo); a menu's change keeps the folder open (`WidgetAct.StartEdit`), an act hands the screen away (`WidgetAct.Start`).
Config: **Shape 83** (the five line kinds, `start` on an item, `StartOptions`, `StartView`, `StartPlace`).

### What it reads (StartStore; tests and pictures StartSamples)

- **Apps**: the shell's Apps folder (FOLDERID_AppsFolder, `shell:AppsFolder`, enumerated with `IShellItem::BindToHandler(BHID_EnumItems)` —
  `InstalledApps`, the pins' picker's), each its parsing name; a path-named app's program from its known folder's GUID.
- **Recent files**: Windows' Recent folder (FOLDERID_Recent), its shortcuts newest first, a local file still there (as §425's).
- **Account**: `GetUserNameExW(NameDisplay)` (secur32), else the user name; the picture Windows keeps for its sign-in screen and
  Start (HKLM `…\AccountPicture\Users\<SID>`, `Image192`…, decoded with WIC). An isolated run (a test, `--smoke`) reads none of it.
- **Power**: what Windows' power menu offers (`QuickLinkMachine`, the power buttons' read); a restart due (`WindowsUpdateRegistry`,
  the status icon's). Commands: `QuickLinks.Power` — Sleep/Hibernate `SetSuspendState`, Shut down/Restart `ExitWindowsEx` with
  `SE_SHUTDOWN_NAME` enabled, Sign out `ExitWindowsEx(EWX_LOGOFF)`, Lock `LockWorkStation`, **new** Switch user
  `WTSDisconnectSession(WTS_CURRENT_SESSION)`, Update and restart / shut down `InitiateShutdownW(SHUTDOWN_INSTALL_UPDATES | …)` —
  through `PowerButtonTile.Run`, which a test stands in for.
- **Opening**: the one launcher (`Launch.Open` of the Apps folder item; `Launch.Elevated`; `Launch.Select`), the folder closing first.
- Read off the dock's thread a minute at most apart, only while a Start line shows (`IStartSource.Refresh`); icons through a 64 px
  `TargetPictures`.

**Ghosts (§635)**: a Start ghost reads the PC's apps (local, no network). §635's `Samples.On` is not in this base; once merged,
`StartSources.Now` takes `new StartSamples()` while it is on — one line.

### Tests

`StartMenuTests` (14): the search (words, initials, folded, letters in order), the order (score, use, a whole name first),
frecency, first sight and its file, letters and categories (folding into Other), the pins and their changes, what a line keeps,
`StartEdits` on a config (pin from All apps, front, move, view, the file), Recommended's list and its "when", a program's path.
`StartGroupTests` (7, one of pictures): the group and its side-bar form; the Beta badges (both pages, the search) and the run;
the grid and what typing narrows in every line; clicks and Enter left for the dock and opened through the launcher's stand-in;
the menus (pinned, All apps, a desktop app's elevate and location), the dock's act rows and the editor; a pin dragged and
clicked, every tile a stop; All apps' views and their menu; the foot's menus and every command into `PowerButtonTile.Runner`.
Registry tests brought along: TypedRegistry, LineSize, Channels, Interaction, PresetSide, PersonsPresets, WidgetMenu,
OptionRows, ConfigWords, Untranslated. Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, KARPO_PNG_DIR): `start-group-<dark|light>.png`,
`start-search-<dark|light>.png` ("pa"), `start-views-<dark|light>.png`. *(The search's tests and picture went in §653.)*

By hand: edit mode › Add › Start and taskbar › **Start (Beta)** onto the bar; click its face: Start opens, the box has the keys;
type "calc", Enter: Calculator opens *(no box since §653)*; right-click a pinned tile › Move to front; drag a tile onto another place; All apps ›
Category ⌄ › List; the power button's menu (with an update waiting: "Update and restart" first, the orange dot).

### Left for later

Folders of pins (a pin dropped onto a pin), jump lists in a pin's menu, the A–Z letter index, Recommended's "Remove from list",
websites and tips, Phone Link's panel, the pins of Windows' own Start (start2.bin is no documented format), Store-based
categories, the account's other users listed in its menu, §635's samples for the ghost (above).

## 647. A folder's style: Cards, as every folder stood, or Attached — its columns on a ground in the bar's colour that adjoins the bar (2026-11-09) — its lines flat on the ground with no cards, its colour the Appearance's, its dividers lines of its outline, since §649 (2026-11-09) — the bar grown out: its ground from edge to edge, flush, in the bar's own paint, its columns a seam apart, since §651 (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"for every folder you should be able to also set a folder style. right now how it is should be
the default one. one other folder style should be that in case of showing the taskbar on the left or right side the whole
columns where the widgets are placed should be filled with a solid background color, or when the tasbar is shown on the
bottom or top that the whole area up the highest or lowest widget is filled with a solid color. do you know what i mean?
and this solid area should connect all the way to the taskbar so that it looks like it is part of it."*

**The setting.** Each folder's page, after its alignment's heading Folder: **Folder style**, a dropdown of **Cards**
(Segoe's Tiles) and **Attached** (the Taskbar glyph) (`FolderOptions.Style`, `FolderStyle`, `FolderStyles`;
`OptionRows.FolderStyle`, slot Look, so before Alignment, which is Placement). Cards is what every folder was and stays
the default. Per folder, as the person asked — not a look of the Appearance (§567: one look; this is how a folder stands,
as its alignment is). New `dock.folder.style.title`, `.cards`, `.attached` in all 40 languages.

**Attached** (`FlyoutHost.Ground`, `GroundOf`, `FolderFlyout.GroundOf`, `AtBar`, `AttachedGround`). The folder's lists
are laid out and drawn exactly as Cards draws them — the same plan, the same panels, the same lines and their own look —;
under them a **ground**:

- **Where.** From the **bar's inner side** — the folder's work area's edge there, which is the bar's panel's inner side
  (`DockWindow.FolderWork`, §287) — to the **gap past the panel's far side** (the 12 DIP a folder stands off the bar:
  the air round the cards is one all round). Down a **side bar** the work area's **whole height**, top to bottom; along a
  **bottom or top bar** the panel's width and the gap either side, and from the bar to the gap past the tallest column
  (shorter ones stand on the bar, §303). Never past the work area: pushed against an end it ends there; it never goes
  under another bar. With several columns the ground is one: the columns stand a separator's room apart (§346), and the
  ground fills that room too. An empty spacer column is ground as well.
- **Adjoining the bar.** Attached, the folder hangs from the bar's inner side itself, not from its face's (`AtBar`): a
  face inset in its island would otherwise leave the cards nearer the bar than the gap. Square everywhere — it is the bar
  grown out, not a popup.
- **Its colour: the bar's, solid** (`AttachedGround`): the Appearance's Taskbar colour (or Windows' own), in Windows' mode
  (or the one the Appearance pins), its base where the bar is opaque, its tint at **full opacity** otherwise. The person
  said "solid"; the bar's see-through over Karpo's blurred wallpaper (§547) would need a blurred strip of its own under
  every folder, and Karpo's own bar is #202020 at 85 % — its ground #202020 reads as the bar. Recoloured live with the bar
  (`Relook`, `FlyoutHost.Wear`). Light mode light, dark dark.
- **The cards keep their look** — the lines' Widgets in folders background and the Flyouts' outline round each list
  (§624) — but **cast no shadow**: they stand on the ground as the bar's widgets stand on the bar. Flat lines on the
  ground were weighed and set aside: a folder's lines are flush with each other and their list's edge (§410), so without
  their card a list would have no edge on a ground of nearly its colour.
- **A press on the ground** is a press on the folder (`FlyoutHost.OnPanel`): it closes nothing, as a press between two
  lines does not. Past it, a press is elsewhere as ever. The window's box is the ground at rest — no room kept for a
  shadow there is none of.
- **Coming and going**: with Animations on, as a **drawer** out of the bar — the whole folder, ground and cards, slides its
  ground's whole depth from behind the bar's edge (the box ends at the bar, so what is still in the bar is out of sight),
  never fading (`FlyoutHost.Drawer`, `Move`); back into it as it closes. With Animations off, there at once. Arranged it
  fades where it stands as every arranged folder does (its guide lines reach the display's edges), on its ground; a switch
  between folders is at once.
- **Set while it stands open** (its page): the folder takes it at once — onto its ground from the bar, or back off its face
  as cards (the layout's signature has the style, `LayOut` hands the host its ground and anchor again).
- **Everything else is the folder's as before**: its alignment along the bar, its widths, edit mode's buttons, slots and
  guide lines (over the ground), the §623 backdrop (under the folder, so under its ground), scaling, light and dark, both
  side edges (on a right bar the first column is still next to the bar, §303).

**The file.** `"style": "attached"` in a folder's options, written only where it is not Cards; a word this build does not
know reads as Cards. **Shape 83** (`Config.Shape`, ConfigWords: `enum FolderStyle`, `property FolderOptions.style`).
**Conversion of the person's file: the version alone** (82 → 83); no folder has a style yet, so every one stays Cards.

Tests: `FolderStyleTests` — `ANewFolderAndAFileWithoutOneAreCardsWhichIsHowEveryFolderStood`,
`TheFileKeepsAStyleOnlyWhereItIsAttached` (round trip, an unknown word), `TheFoldersPageSetsItsStyle`,
`TheGroundAdjoinsTheBarAndReachesTheGapPastTheFarthestWidget` (each edge at 100, 150, 200 %),
`TheGroundNeverRunsPastTheWorkArea`, `AnAttachedFolderHangsFromTheBarsInnerSide`, `ItsDrawerGoesBackIntoTheBarItsWholeDepth`,
`TheGroundIsTheBarsColourSolid`; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheAttachedFolderAdjoinsItsBar` (a real two-column folder on each
edge and scale, its face inset in the bar: the ground from the bar's inner side, the cards the gap off it, every column on
it, a press by the bar the folder's; as Cards where it always stood, on no ground), `ChangedWhileOpenTheFolderTakesItsStyleAtOnce`,
`ItSlidesOutOfTheBarWithAnimationsAndIsThereAtOnceWithout`. Updated for the row: `FolderFacesTests.AFolderHasNoName`,
`FolderMenuSidesTests.AFoldersPanelMenuIsWhatChangesTheFolderOpened`, `WidgetPageTests` (the folder's page),
`ConfigCoverageTests.AFacesRowsWriteTheFaceAndAFoldersRowsTheFolder`, `OptionRowsTests` (the property's row), `ConfigSchemaTests`.
Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.FolderStyleSheets`, the clock preset's folder in two columns at a Taskbar's end
on each edge, Attached and Cards, dark and light: `folderstyle-<attached|cards>-<bottom|left|right|top>-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: a folder's page › Folder style › Attached, with the folder open: it drops onto a ground of the bar's colour that
runs from the bar to just past its farthest line (the whole height on a side bar); click the ground's empty part — it
stays open; close and open it — it slides out of the bar; Animations off — it is there at once; Cards — as before.

## 648. A switch on is its whole button: the accent edge to edge in its plate's corners; Markets and Stocks one ready-made group (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"the toggle button on the taskbar like the microphone on / off have a little space between the
area that is filled and the outer edge, this should not be."*; *"market and stocks group preset should be merged as they
are basically the same."*

**Why there was a gap.** A one-button widget on the bar (`SwitchIsland`: the microphone, sound, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane
mode, night light, keep awake and the rest; `SecurityIsland`'s shield, lit while protected) drew its accent as a square round
the glyph (`SwitchIsland.Pill`: the glyph and 6 px each side, held 2 px inside the cell), corners 4 px. The card, the plate
at rest (§506), the highlight and since §602 `Layout.Plates` are the whole cell, corners `Layout.CardRadius`: between the two
a ring of the plate showed, on every bar size, wider on a tall bar. No ring was drawn round the fill; the fill was smaller.

**Now**: lit, the accent fills the whole cell — which is the button's card, its plate and its highlight — in the plate's own
corners. One number says them: `Layout.PlateRadius`, the cards' corner on a bar of cards, a highlight's (4 DIP grown with the
bar, §376) on a floating dock's panel, none on a flush bar (§533); the scene's cards, rest plates and the open folder's plate
read it (Scene's `CardCorner` and the open plate's own copy of the rule are gone), and `Layout.StyleFor` hands it to the
widget (`IslandStyle.PlateRadius`), so a drawing that fills its cell is that plate exactly. One painter for the one-button
widgets, `SwitchIsland.PaintButton`: the glyph in its square (`GlyphSide`, the old pill's size, which the button's length is
still measured with: nothing moves), its name after it where it shows one — on the accent in the accent's ink (black on dark
mode's light accent, white on light mode's), as the glyph. On its way (SwitchPending) the accent and its ink at 60 % as
before. High contrast: Windows' highlight colour and highlight text, as its quick-settings tile. Down a side bar the same.
In a folder nothing changes: the toggles row's buttons were filled to their edges already, and a switch's line lights to
its edges round the form (§611).

What it costs: the highlight lies under the widgets, so the pointer over a switch that is on no longer shows its plate
round the accent; the tooltip still comes. (Windows' tile lightens its accent under the pointer; a widget on the bar is not
told it is hovered.)

**Markets and Stocks.** The Watchlist ("Stocks", `stocksGroup`: MSFT, AAPL, NVDA and the S&P 500, a markets line each, wide)
and Markets (`stockGroup`, §246: one markets line with no symbol yet under the markets face, "Set up") were the same widget,
once and four times. One group now, **Markets** (`Presets.MarketId`, its id as it was): the four shares at their Full form,
wide, under the S&P 500's ticker (the face Markets and news wears, set: nothing in it asks to be set up), the chart glyph the
person asked for the Watchlist. Each line is the markets widget, so its menu still turns it into a rate or a coin. The add
page's Weather and news shelf lists Markets, the markets widget, Markets and news; the Stocks group and its three strings are
gone from all 40 languages, Markets' blurb is the Watchlist's ("A watchlist of Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA and the S&P 500")
and its keywords hold the Watchlist's and its old name ("stocks", "watchlist", "nvda" find it). Not combined, so §620's side
arrangement has nothing of it; its ghost (§635) shows the samples' four prices and the SPX face. Placed folders are no
presets: a bar keeps whatever it holds. The person's fixture (`PersonsLayouts.json`) holds their Stocks folder as Markets and
no longer the one-line Markets folder; Markets is among what they asked to change since.

Tests: `SceneTreeTests.ASwitchOnFillsItsPlateEdgeToEdge` (new: on a bar of cards, a flush one and a floating dock's, 32, 48
and 72 DIP, bottom and left, 100 and 150 %, dark, light and high contrast: every switch's cell is its card, its style carries
`Layout.PlateRadius`, a switch on has the accent at the middle of all four edges and a rounded corner where the plate has
one, square on a flush bar, one off nothing there; every switch a `SampleSwitch`, none of this PC's), `MarketPresetTests.
ThePresetIsTheSharesUnderTheIndexsTicker` (renamed from `ThePresetIsTheMarketsLineUnderTheTicker`), `PresetsTests`,
`AddListPresetsTests`, `PersonsPresetsTests`, `GraphLeftEdgeTests` on Markets; the tests of one markets line take the preset cut
to its first (`MarketOffscreenTests.OneLineFolder`). Pictures (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `SceneTreeTests.ToggleFillSheets`,
togglefill-<bottom|left>-<32|48>-<dark|light>.png (Start; the microphone, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth off, night light, keep awake on;
airplane mode on with its name) and togglefill-hover-48-<dark|light>.png (the pointer over the microphone);
`MarketPresetTests.MarketsPresetPictures`, markets-preset-<dark|light>.png; `GhostSampleSheets`' ghostdata-markets-dark.png.

By hand: put the microphone switch on the bar, mute it: the accent fills the button to its edges, the corners the card's;
Taskbar › Spacing 0: square, to the bar's edges; the bar on the left: the same; a switch with its name: the name on the
accent too. Edit bar › Add › Weather and news: Markets once, no Stocks; search "stocks": Markets.

## 642. Windows search (beta): Windows' own index, the apps, Settings and answers in a search box, everything found as it is typed (2026-11-09) — a home of sections before anything is typed, the chosen result's pane beside a wide list, the index linked from its page, since §655 (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-09): *"add an additional seach widget that searches windows with the native windows search (mark them
as beta too) … make those widgets / groups feature rich. first study what win11 has for features in these areas and then go
ahead and implement them and also see how you can improve on them too."*

**What Windows 11's search has** (Microsoft's own pages: support "Search indexing in Windows", "Customize the Taskbar in
Windows"; Learn "Querying the index with Windows Search SQL syntax", "CONTAINS predicate", "Literals"; the Policy CSP's
Search; read 2026-11-09), and what Karpo's does:

| Windows 11 | Karpo's Windows search (beta) |
|---|---|
| Results grouped: Best match, then Apps, Settings, Documents, Folders, Photos, Web …; Enter opens the best match | The same groups (Answer, Apps, Settings, Documents, Folders, Photos, Videos, Music, Email, Web), the best match first, Enter opens it |
| Filters as tabs (All, Apps, Documents, Web, Settings, People, Folders, Photos, "…" more), always the same | Chips for All and only the groups that found something, wrapping onto a second line; Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab (Ctrl+→/←) step through every group |
| Typed filters ("documents: tax") | The same, by the English word or the group's name in the language Karpo speaks ("Fotos: Strand") |
| Quick actions in the preview pane: Open, Run as administrator, Open file location, Copy path | On every row under the pointer or the keys (Open file location, Copy as path, Open with; Run as administrator for apps and programs), on the best match always; Ctrl+Enter the location, Ctrl+Shift+Enter as administrator, Ctrl+C the path |
| Recent searches and top apps on the home | Recent searches (a click types one again, Delete or its × forgets it, "Clear search history" all) and the files used lately (Windows' Recent folder) |
| Calculator and unit answers come from Bing (web results) | Worked out on the PC: arithmetic (precedence, %, ^, !, mod, sqrt, sin/cos/tan in degrees, π, e, "15% of 80"), units (length, mass, volume, area, data in Windows' 1,024, time, speed, °C/°F/K), the region's decimal sign; Enter copies the value |
| Web results on by default (Bing), off by a setting or a policy | Off: nothing typed leaves the PC unless the line's "Search the web" is on; then a "Search the web for …" row with the app's engine (§80) |
| Indexer scopes: Classic (libraries, desktop) or Enhanced (the whole PC), Indexing Options' folders | Asks the index as it stands, and says under the results which it is (Classic or Enhanced, read from the indexer's rules) with a link to Searching Windows settings |
| Name prefixes, ranked with Bing | Karpo's own ranking over every source: the whole name, its start, a word's start (after a capital too: "toys", PowerToys), initials ("vsc"), held, letters in order in one word ("ntpd"); apps before pages before folders before files named alike; fresher files first; what was opened from here before, for words starting so, first (it learns) |
| As-you-type, with the web's latency | Apps, pages and answers at once from memory; the index once the typing rests 120 ms, a keystroke cancelling the question before (the command's own ICommand::Cancel) |

**The API.** Windows Search's documented OLE DB provider, `Search.CollatorDSO` (CLSID_CollatorDataSource), with SQL over
`SystemIndex` (`WinSearchQuery.Sql`): each word a prefix of `System.ItemNameDisplay` (and of `System.Search.Contents` from three
letters, "Search inside files", on by default), escaped twice — CONTAINS' doubled `"`, then SQL's doubled `'` —, a filter its
`System.Kind`, every filter but mail held to `SCOPE='file:'`, `ORDER BY System.Search.Rank DESC`, TOP 60. Chosen over
ISearchQueryHelper (it writes the same SQL from AQS, but its text would not be ours to test) and the shell's search folders
(ISearchFolderItemFactory: the shell walks what the index does not cover, slowly, and ranks as it likes). TerraFX has none of
oledb.h's interfaces, so `Karpo.Dock\WinSearch\WindowsIndex.cs` calls them through their tables (`delegate* unmanaged`, as
DesktopControl does): IDBInitialize → IDBCreateSession → IDBCreateCommand → ICommandText → IRowset, an accessor binding the seven
columns (strings by reference, the provider's buffers freed; FILETIME, I8, I4). AOT-safe, nothing held between questions, on a
thread of its own with COM up (DriveReader.Start). On this PC: 60 rows in 60–210 ms. The apps are Start's All apps as the shell
lists them (`InstalledApps`, behind `IWinSearchApps`; §641's `StartStore` reads the same `InstalledApps`, one listing kept a minute for both); Settings' pages are `WindowsPages`
(Karpo's one list, "Display settings" in all 40 languages; ten more now: Installed apps, Default apps, Startup apps, Background,
Mouse, Printers & scanners, Sign-in options, About, Privacy & security, Searching Windows), each with English words of its own
("resolution", "wallpaper", "uninstall") that answer words of three letters or more.

**The widget** (`winSearch`, a line; "Beta" on its add tile, §641's one Beta: `WidgetInfo.Beta`, `dock.add.beta`) and **its group** (`winSearchGroup`, Beta too, as §641's `Preset.Beta` holding a Beta widget): a
folder whose face is Windows 11's search box (`SearchPill`: the magnifier and "Search"; the magnifier alone down a side), its
click opening the folder with the keys in the line. The line is ContactsLine's shape: the box, the chips, then the home or the
results, scrolling under the box, the rows the folder's own items; the best match taller (a larger icon, what it is, when it
changed, its size, its folder) on a control's fill, lit as where Enter lands until the arrows move; the shell's icons read off
the dock's thread. What opens, opens once the folder has gone (Dock.FolderForward → `OpenChosen`, the keys' Enter through the
folder's click on the line, through the one launcher, §491); a copy stays and says "Copied". Its two switches (`winSearch`:
`web`, `contents`) are rows of its menu. The history is this PC's state, `LocalFolder\winsearch.txt` (an isolated run's own),
never config.json. A ghost on the add page or a preview, made showing §635's samples (`CellIsland.Sampled`), lists its sample
(`WinSearchSamples`, "budget": a spreadsheet, two documents, a folder, a picture) and asks nothing. Shape 85 (a line kind, a face
kind, `winSearch` and its two words; after §641's 83 and §647's 84). On the add page: Start and taskbar's run, after Start (beta)'s.

**Limitations.** Mail: classic Outlook's items are found where the index holds them; a `mapi:` address is handed to the shell
and may not open in new Outlook. No People group (Windows' needs an account's directory). No thumbnail in the best match yet.
The scopes are read from the indexer's rules in the registry, not ISearchCrawlScopeManager; a line kept to some folders
(`WinSearchQuery.Sql`'s scopes) is ready in the query but has no row.

Tests: `WinSearchQueryTests` (prefixes in English and German, words, escaping, the SQL, kinds, the file scope, scopes, nothing
asked for apps, settings or the web), `WinSearchRankTests` (name scores, groups by type and address, Start's shortcuts left to the
apps, the best match, the answer first and the web never, each target once, caps, freshness and history, the index's rows, apps,
pages by name and words, sizes), `WinSearchCalcTests` (sums, units, non-answers, the region's marks), `WinSearchEngineTests`
(instant then the index, one question for a word typed fast, a keystroke cancelling and dropping a late answer, the problem said,
the answer and the web's row, late apps, the home, what was opened first, disposed, the history and its file), `WindowsIndexTests`
(the indexer's rules as folders; with KARPO_INDEX_TESTS=1 the real index asked read-only, and a cancel), UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1)
`WinSearchLineTests` (typing, the arrows and Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+Shift+Enter, a row's actions and tooltips, copying, the
chips and Ctrl+Tab, Escape, the home, the ghost's sample, the group and its Beta badges) and the pictures
`winsearch-line-<dark|light>.png`, `winsearch-face-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: edit mode › Add › Taskbar › Windows search (Beta) onto the bar: a search box. Click it: the folder opens with the caret,
the recent searches and files under it. Type "pa": Paint the best match, its actions under it; Down walks; Ctrl+Enter on a file
opens File Explorer at it; "12*(3+4)" says = 84, Enter copies 84; "photos: beach" filters; Escape empties, Escape again closes.
Its menu: Search the web on — a "Search the web for …" row.

## 649. An attached folder's lines flat on its ground, no cards; its colour the Appearance's "Attached folder background"; a divider a line of its outline (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), after hearing §647's plan: *"the widgets inside should not keep their own cards."*, *"the
background should be configurable in the settings."*, *"dividers become an outline of the folder"*.

**Flat on the ground** (`FolderFlyout.Flat` = `FlyoutHost.Grounded`). An attached folder's lines stand on its ground as the
bar's widgets stand on the bar, with nothing of a card left: **no background** (a line's fill clear at rest, no blur of the
desktop under it: `OnCard` false), **no pattern**, **no rim** round a list (`FlyoutHost.Dress`: clear on a ground) and no
room kept inside one (`RimInset` 0), **no corner rounded** (`FolderPlan.Radius` 0, `Build(attached:)`: a list's clip, its
cards' clips, the focus rectangle, a lifted line's plate all square). What lights lights **on the ground**: a line under the
pointer, and every item's band (§611, §632), from the column's edge to its edge. §647's "the cards keep their look" is gone
with it — its fear, a list with no edge on a ground of nearly its colour, is the person's choice now: the column is where
its lines are, the ground round it the air.

- **Its text reads on the ground** (`Look.Flyout(ground)`, `FolderFlyout.Wearing`): the folder's look is dressed with the
  lines' background the ground's colour and no pattern, so the one rule (`ToneRules.Dress`) makes their text and accent
  readable on the ground and their highlight of it — a pale ground in the dark mode gets dark text. Nothing of that card
  is drawn: the ground under them is it. The menus and flyouts opened from the folder are dressed as from any (`Menus`).
- **A widget's own drawing is its own**: the actions line's footer band (Windows' footer, §68) and a graph's plate stay —
  they are what the widget shows, not a card under it.
- Its style set while it stands open (§647) puts the look on at once (`Rewear`, at every layout): onto the ground flat,
  back off its face as cards.

**Its colour** (`Tone.Ground`, the Flyouts' **Attached folder background**, new `settings.look.ground` in all 40
languages). A colour of the Appearance like every other (§568: a pair, the page showing and writing the half of the
taskbar's mode, §613; its reset beside it where it differs from the palette's design; §622 tried on under the pointer —
every bar, every folder open, the page's preview). **In the Flyouts tab, last** — after Outline and Background while a
folder is open: the Flyouts are where the open folder's own look lives (§514 its outline, §623 its backdrop), and the ground
is how an attached folder shows; not the Taskbar's, though it follows the bar by default, since it is the folder's, and only
attached folders have it, so last. **Unset — Karpo's own and every palette's design — it follows the bar** (§647: the bar's
colour, solid, live with it, high contrast's system colour); the row shows that colour, the value in force (§574,
`Looks.Ground`). Said, it is drawn **as said, its opacity its own** (`FolderFlyout.AttachedGround`; never in high
contrast). **No None** (`MayBeNone` false): an attached folder's lines have no card, so a ground of nothing would leave text
on whatever is behind; the reset is the way back to the bar's. Its swatches are the backgrounds (`ColorPalette.For`), as the
bar's: the area is the bar grown out. No palette was given one — each designs a bar, and its ground is that bar's.

**The Appearance's preview** (`LookPreview.GroundOf`): while a ground is said (or tried on) the preview's folder stands
attached — on a ground of that colour from the bar's top to the gap past its lines, the gap either side, its lines flat —:
the one place the page can show the colour, which a folder of cards never shows. Unset, it stands as cards, as every folder
does by default.

**A divider** (`FolderFlyout.RuleOf`, `RuleInk`; a divider's `Line.Rule`). Between two cards a divider was the gap between
their outlines (§505, §624: each card its outline); with no cards it would be nothing. So, attached, **a divider is a line
of the folder's outline**: the Flyouts' Outline colour (Windows' flyout stroke where unset), its weight (`FlyoutHost.Rim`,
a whole px or two), **across its column's whole width, in the middle of its room** (a Grow divider's middle of all it grows
to) on whole px — where the two cards' outlines stood, the one line that parts them. Where the outline is None, the theme's
divider stroke (DividerStrokeColorDefault), so a divider still parts. It moves with its line (in its holder), drag and all;
edit mode's stripes over its room as ever (§524). As cards, nothing of it, as before. *Weighed*: the line out to the ground's
edges (reads as a frame of compartments, but crosses the next column's air and would need its own layer outside the column's
clip); the columns' gaps drawn as outlines too (the person spoke of dividers; a column gap is not one).

### The file

`appearance.palettes.<id>.flyouts.ground   { "dark"?: "#AARRGGBB", "light"?: … }; left out: the bar's colour`

**Shape 85** (`Config.Shape`; `ConfigWords.txt`: `property LookValues.ground`). **The conversion rule: none but the version**
— a file of shape 84 has no ground, which reads as the bar's colour: what every attached folder stood on. Said in another
section it is not kept (`Normalize`), a half that does not read neither. No migration code.

Tests: `AttachedFlatTests` — `TheAttachedGroundIsAFlyoutsColourThatFollowsTheBarByDefault` (the Flyouts' last tone, no
other section's, no None, unset in every palette; the row the bar's colour solid in both modes, the backgrounds' swatches, no
reset; a pick in its half alone, read back unchanged, its reset; reset nothing left; said on the bar dropped, its opacity
kept), `AFileOfShape84ReadsWithTheBarsColour`, `TheGroundsSwatchesAreTriedOn`, `OnItsGroundAFoldersLinesReadOnTheGround`
(the colour said or the bar's, high contrast's own; no pattern, the text 4.5:1 on a pale ground, the menus as ever; a line
clear at rest, no blur, its highlight under the pointer), `ADividerIsALineOfTheOutlineAcrossItsRoom`; UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1)
`AttachedLinesStandFlatOnTheGroundAndLightEdgeToEdge` (left bar 150 %, bottom 100 %, two columns with a divider: as cards
every line on its card, a rim round each, round corners, no rule; attached every fill clear, no rim, radius 0, the rule
across its column in its room's middle; captured: the lines' corners and edges the ground's pixels, the rule the outline over
the ground, a line under the pointer lit at its left and right edge alike, the ground beside it and the line above as at
rest), `TheGroundsColourTriedOnRecoloursTheOpenFolder` (a worn copy relooks the open folder's ground, taken off it is the
bar's again). Updated: `FolderBackdropTests` (the Flyouts' three tones and rows). §647's `FolderStyleTests` hold unchanged.
Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.AttachedFlatSheets` — `attached2-<bar|custom>-<bottom|left>-<dark|light>-150.png`
(the clock preset's folder in two columns, a divider after its first line; the bar's colour, and a dark blue / pale blue
said) and `attached2-appearance-<dark|light>.png` (the Flyouts tab, the preview's folder attached on the colour said).

By hand: a folder › Folder style › Attached, open it: its lines on the ground with no card, no outline, square; point at
one — it lights from the column's edge to its edge; add a Divider to it — a thin line of the outline across the column.
Edit mode › Appearance › Flyouts › Attached folder background: rest on a swatch — the open folder and the preview take it;
pick it; ↺ — the bar's colour again.

## 650. The add page's search has the keys as it opens, whatever opened it (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"when clicking add widget i cannot immeadiately type to find widgets. i first have to click
again."*

**Why.** Opening the add page gave its search the keys only inside the edit bar (`EditDeck.Opening`: the field focused, its
caret blinking); the window with the keyboard focus stayed whatever had it. The edit bar and its flyout are Tool popups
(`FlyoutHost`, `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`), which never take the focus as they show; only a press on the flyout's own controls
(WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, §520) did. A bar's "+" leaves the keys on the bar (`FocusBar`), a folder's "+" on the folder: the letters
typed went there, the caret blinked in a search that heard nothing, and a click on it was what moved the keys.

**Now**: one mechanism, the one a Menu popup already takes the keys by. `FlyoutHost.TakeKeys` hands an open popup's window the
keys once it shows (`Surfaces.Focus`, as a Menu's opening and §606's `Own` do), keeps the window that was in front, and gives
them back to it as it closes while it still has them (`Close`'s restore, a Menu's alone until now; the window in front is a
showing's own, reset as one opens, never kept from the last). The edit bar asks for it once, as a page whose field has the
keys opens (`EditDeck.Opening` marks it, `Open` hands it over after the flyout shows) — so the bar's "+", a folder's "+", the
edit bar's Add by a click or by the keys all leave the first letter in the search. Drawn again while it stands (a hover, the
errors' count, a letter typed) it takes nothing back: a click on another app keeps the keys there. The foreground is Karpo's
at that moment (the click that opened it was Karpo's: a bar's press takes the foreground, `FocusBar`; a folder has it; the
edit bar's Add activates its bar), so Windows' foreground lock allows it. The settings pages' dropdowns (Language and every
240 DIP box) open a Menu popup, which took the keys already, and their long lists' searches are its levels'
(`Flyout.Inline`): nothing to change there.

Tests: `EditDeckClickTests.TheAddPagesSearchHasTheKeysAsItOpens` (UI, KARPO_UI_TESTS=1; new, failing before: another window
has the keys; Taskbar's page leaves them there; Add's click and the dock's answer leave them on the flyout's window, the search
with the caret; each letter sent where the focus is lands in the search; the keys moved away, the page drawn again takes
nothing back; closed and opened again, it takes them again, its search empty).

By hand: edit mode, the "+" at a section's end on the bar: type "clock" at once — the list shows the clocks. The edit bar's
Add, a folder's "+": the same. Escape twice: the page closes and the keys are back on the bar (Tab walks its widgets).

## 651. An attached folder is the bar grown out: its ground from edge to edge, flush, in the bar's own paint; its columns a seam apart; its outline along its far side (2026-11-09) — beside a taskbar alone: a dock's folder is cards, since §656 (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-09), after seeing §647: *"the attached folder style should be better designed. also the background
should always span from edge to edge. in attached mode the widgets themselves should also should not have the card look. you
can redesign the shell around so that it matches the style. they also dont have to have any spacing to the edges anymore
necessarily."* (The card look went in §649.)

**What was wrong** (pictures `artifacts/attached3/before/`): the ground was a box round the folder — the panel's width and
the 12 DIP gap either side along a bottom or top bar, the gap past its far side —, so along a bottom bar it ended in the
middle of the screen while down a side bar it ran top to bottom; the columns stood a separator's room (9 px at 150 %) apart
and 12 DIP off the bar and off the screen's ends, all of it air on the ground; and the ground was the bar's colour *solid*
while the bar is that colour at 85 % over the wallpaper blurred: #202020 against #1F252E dark, #F3F3F3 against #E6ECF3 light —
two surfaces meeting at the bar's edge, not one.

**The design: the bar grown out.** Attached, the folder is the taskbar made deeper for as long as it is open, not a popup
over it — as a drawer slides out of a dock's edge:

- **Edge to edge** (`FlyoutHost.GroundOf`, its gap parameter gone): along the bar the work area's **whole length** — the
  screen's ends, or another bar's inner side; never under it —; across it from the bar's inner side to the columns' far
  side. Down a side bar that was already so (top to bottom); a bottom or top bar is now the same rule turned: the person's
  first ask (§647) was "the whole area up the highest widget", and "always … edge to edge" is that. Its depth is the tallest
  column's; a shorter one stands on the bar (§303) with ground over it.
- **Flush** (`FlyoutPlacement.Flush`: no gap, no margin; `FlyoutHost.Placement` hands it on a ground, so the folder's room,
  `FolderFlyout.Room`, is from the bar itself): the columns stand on the bar's inner side and, against an end, reach it. No air
  between the ground and its edges: what keeps text off an edge is a line's own padding, as on the bar. A line lit runs from
  its column's edge to its edge (§649), which is now the ground's edge where it is one.
- **The bar's own paint** (`FolderFlyout.AttachedGround` = `Scene.GroundOf`, what the bar paints itself in): a see-through
  bar's colour at the bar's opacity, laid on **the wallpaper blurred as under the bar** — the dock composes the strip for the
  ground's rectangle with the bar's own pipeline (§547: `DockWindow.Paper`, `WallpaperStrips.Compose` off the dock's thread,
  then `Blurred` at the bar's Background blur; kept, blurred again only where the amount changes, composed again where the
  ground's rectangle or the wallpaper does) and the host lays it under the colour (`FlyoutHost.Paper`, `Repaper`). Across the
  join the pixels are the bar's: (30,35,43) both sides in the dark picture, (230,236,243) in the light one. Until the strip
  has come — the first opening of a ground of that size —, or with no wallpaper known, the colour is drawn solid, as §647 did.
  An opaque bar's ground is its colour solid; a bar of nothing (0 %) or Windows' acrylic its colour solid (text on nothing
  would not read). A colour said in Flyouts › Attached folder background (§649) is drawn as said, its opacity on the same
  paper. The drawer's slide keeps the paper still on the screen (an expression, `-root.Offset`), so the wallpaper does not
  ride out with it. §647's "solid" was the word for *filled*; the person's aim was "looks like it is part of it".
- **Square**: no corner anywhere — its ends are the screen's or another bar's, its bar side is the bar. Rounding the far
  corners was weighed: with the ground running end to end there are no free corners to round.
- **No shadow, no floating rim** (as §647, §649). **Its outline along its far side only** (`groundEdge`): the Flyouts'
  Outline (Windows' flyout stroke unset; none where it is None), the folder's outline's weight (`Rim`, 1 px at 100 %, 2 at
  150 %), on the one open side of the bar-and-ground silhouette; never on the bar side (no seam) nor at the ends. Drawn over
  the lines, so one lit at the far side stops at it.
- **Columns a seam apart, not air** (`FolderPlan.Seams`, `FlyoutHost.Seams`; `FolderFlyout.SeamOf`): attached, two columns
  stand the outline's weight apart (`ListGap`), and that room is a line in the dividers' ink (§649 `RuleInk`) across the
  ground's **whole depth**, bar to far side — lanes of one surface, as the person's side-bar columns were "whole columns"
  (§647). An empty spacer column is a lane of its own. As Cards the lists stand a separator's room apart as ever.
- **Coming and going**: the drawer of §647, its whole depth now the columns' — nothing of a gap to slide.

**Cards**: nothing changed (its pictures differ from before only in the clock's seconds).

**Settings**: none added. The Appearance's row for the ground still names the bar's colour opaque (`Looks.Ground`): a pick
there is solid; the ground drawn follows the bar's opacity only while unset.

**The Appearance's preview** (`LookPreview`): a said ground stands across the whole room, flush on the bar, its outline
along its top, a seam between columns.

Not done: the Taskbar's own outline (§512, None by default) is drawn on the bar's inner side and so lies between the bar
and the ground when one is set; hiding it under an open attached folder would need the bar to know the folder.

Tests: `FolderStyleTests` — `TheGroundIsTheBarGrownOutFromEdgeToEdge` (each edge at 100, 150, 200 %: the work area's whole
length, from the bar to the panel's far side, the panel flush on the bar, against either end flush with it, as Cards the gap
and margin as ever; replaces `TheGroundAdjoinsTheBarAndReachesTheGapPastTheFarthestWidget`), `TheGroundNeverRunsPastTheWorkArea`
(rewritten), `AttachedColumnsMeetAtASeam` (new: the gap the outline's weight, one seam where the plan has it, high contrast's
2 DIP, cards a separator's room), `TheGroundIsTheBarAsTheBarIsPainted` (replaces `TheGroundIsTheBarsColourSolid`: Scene.GroundOf,
see-through, an opaque bar solid); UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `TheAttachedFolderAdjoinsItsBar` (end to end, flush, one seam of the
outline's weight, dressed solid with no paper, its far side the outline and its seam the dividers' ink, a press on the ground
off the columns the folder's), `ChangedWhileOpenTheFolderTakesItsStyleAtOnce` (flush); `AttachedFlatTests.AttachedLinesStandFlatOnTheGroundAndLightEdgeToEdge`
(the lines' corners the ground a stroke in from the far side, the far side the outline over the ground). Pictures
(KARPO_PNG_DIR, the picture's wallpaper handed as the paper, `SceneTreeTests.Wash`): `SceneTreeTests.AttachedDrawerSheets`,
`attached3-<bottom|left|right|top>-<one|two>-<dark|light>-<100|150>.png`; `FolderStyleSheets` and `AttachedFlatSheets` as before.

By hand: a folder › Folder style › Attached on a bottom bar, open it: one band from the screen's left to its right edge, the
bar's own see-through colour over the same blurred wallpaper, no line where it meets the bar, the columns on the bar and at
the screen's end when the folder is there, a thin line between two columns and along the band's top; on a side bar the same
turned; Animations on — it slides out of the bar, the wallpaper under it still.

## 652. Windows search's sources: one small interface, Karpo's mail, calendars, contacts, notes and itself among Windows'; each row Windows' own icon; one height (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09), of §642's Windows search: *"the windows search should show the native windows or folder icons."*,
*"also the search widget should have a fixed height."*, *"you should also show results from mail and calendar and contacts
etc. generally also show results from our application too. (should be configurable / on offable.) think of a good system
here so that it is extensible as well."*

### Sources (Karpo.Core\WinSearchSource.cs)

Everything the line searches is a **source**, one small interface:

```csharp
public interface IWinSearchSource
{
    string Id { get; }                       // its info's id, the word config.json switches it by
    bool Slow => false;                      // asked once the typing rests, on a thread of its own (the index)
    void Warm(Action came) { }               // get ready as the line shows (list the apps, snapshot Karpo's settings)
    void Forget() { }                        // read again next time
    WinSearchFound Find(WinSearchAsk ask, CancellationToken cancel);   // hits, scored; a problem where it could not answer
}
```

What a source *is* — its name, glyph, the groups (`WinSearchCategory`) its hits are in, and whether it is on by default —
is its `WinSearchSourceInfo` in **one list**, `WinSearchSourceInfos.All`, which is also the order of the "Search in"
switches:

| Id | Source | Groups | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps` | Apps | Apps | Start's apps (`InstalledApps`, §641's listing) |
| `settings` | Windows settings | Settings | `WindowsPages` and their words (§642) |
| `files` | File and folder names | Documents, Folders, Photos, Videos, Music, Email | Windows' index, names (slow) |
| `contents` | Search inside files | Documents, Photos, Videos, Music, Email | Windows' index, names or contents per word of 3+ letters (slow) |
| `mail` | Email | Email | the messages Karpo's accounts synced (`MailStore`), by subject, sender, address, preview |
| `calendar` | Calendar | Events | Karpo's calendars (`CalendarStore`), a month back to a year ahead, by title and place |
| `contacts` | Contacts | People | Karpo's address books (`ContactStore`), matched by the contacts line's own `ContactSearch` |
| `notes` | Notes | Notes | Karpo's notebook (`Notebook`), by title, then by what a note says |
| `karpo` | Karpo's settings, widgets and layouts | Karpo | its settings' pages and General rows (`KarpoMenu.Rows`), every widget to add (`Catalogue`, matched as the add page matches, `CatalogueSearch`), the layouts |
| `calculator` | Calculator and units | Answer | §642's `WinSearchCalc` |
| `web` | Search the web | Web | the app's engine (§80); **off by default** — nothing typed leaves the PC unasked (§642) |

Every other source is on by default; one whose account the person has none of finds nothing. Only what Karpo already
holds in memory is read — nothing is asked of an account or the network for a search. The registry of instances is
`WinSearchSystem.Sources` (Karpo.Dock\WinSearch): `WinSearchSources.Windows(index, apps, …, more: Karpo's)`; a test and
a ghost hand their own.

**To add a source:** an id and its info in `WinSearchSourceInfos.All` (its name in `WinSearchWords.Source` and the 40
languages), a class answering `Find` with hits scored by the one ranking (`WinSearchRank.NameScore`/`Score`), and its
instance in `WinSearchSystem.Sources`. The engine asks it, the results group and rank it, its switch appears under
"Search in" — nothing else changes.

### The engine (WinSearchEngine)

Each keystroke asks every source switched on that answers the filter (a chip, a typed prefix — `calendar:`, `people:`,
`notes:`, `karpo:` are new). The **quick** sources are asked together, at once, **off the dock's thread**, and listed
together (the list does not jump as each answers; until they have, the last results stand); each **slow** one on a
thread of its own once the typing has rested 120 ms, listed with them as it answers. A keystroke cancels the question
before (the index's own Cancel) and drops whatever of it comes late; a source that throws answers nothing. The engine
marks each hit with its source and adds what was opened from here before (the history, by a hit's **Key** — its target
but where several share one: two messages on one inbox's page).

Results are grouped by what they are, as Windows' search groups them — Best match, Apps, Settings, Documents, Folders,
Photos, Videos, Music, Email, **Calendar, Contacts, Notes, Karpo**, Web — ranked within, the best of all on top. A hit
now says what it copies (`Copies`: a path in quotes, an answer, a person's address, a note's text) and what its icon is
(`Icon`).

**What Karpo's own open** is an address of Karpo's (`KarpoTargets`): `karpo:settings/<Page>[/<row>]` opens edit mode on
that page at its row (the one way in from outside, `OpenEditLanding`), `karpo:add/<words>` the add page with its search
saying them (`EditDeck.Search`), `karpo:layout/<n>` switches this display (as the layouts' line), `karpo:note/<id>` opens
the folder on this bar holding a note line that shows it — else the add page at the Note widget. A message opens in its
account's web mail, an event where a calendar line's click opens it (`EventLinks`), a person a mail to them (else a call).

### Native icons

Every row wears **Windows' own icon**: a file's and a folder's its own (its path — special folders theirs), an app's (its
Apps folder address), Settings' pages **Settings' own** (`WinSearchPages.SettingsApp`). Read off the dock's thread and
kept by the one cache Start's lines use — `TargetPictures.Large` (64 px, shared; the line's own second cache deleted) —,
its glyph while it comes (once: then kept) and for a hit with none (an answer, a message, an event). A ghost (§635) reads
no file of this PC: a file's or a folder's icon is its **kind's** (`WinSearchHit.KindIcon`, "kind:.xlsx" →
`Items.KindIcon`, the shell's image list asked by the type alone, `SHGFI_USEFILEATTRIBUTES`); an app's by its Apps folder
id, as Start's samples.

### One height

`ListWidgets`: the line is **Fixed only** (`Grows = false`), 24 cells (twelve rows, 480 DIP — a panel's), the preset's line
`LineHeight.Exactly(24)`; what it finds scrolls under the box, a short list leaves room under it, and a file's
`automatic up to 24` reads as fixed 24. The same on every edge (pictures: the bottom and the left bar).

### Configuration: "Search in"

The widget's page has one plain section **Search in**, a switch per source in the registry's order (the rows are one group,
`OptionRow.Group`, which §594 makes the page's section and the menu's level). They replace §642's two switches (`web`,
`contents`): one mechanism.

    cell.winSearch   { "sources"?: { "<id>": true|false, … } }   // only what differs from its default; none, no record

**Shape 87** (`Config.Shape`; `ConfigWords.txt`: `property WinSearchOptions.sources` for `.web`, `.contents`). **The
conversion rule:** `"winSearch": { "web": true }` → `"winSearch": { "sources": { "web": true } }`;
`"contents": false` → `"sources": { "contents": false }`; `"web": false`/`"contents": true` (defaults) are dropped. An
`automatic` height on a `winSearch` line needs nothing: it reads as fixed. No migration code.

### Samples

A ghost asks made-up sources (`WinSearchSamples`), "team" typed: Microsoft Teams the best match (opened for "team"
before), then Apps, Documents (a .pptx, .docx, .xlsx), Folders, Photos, Email, Calendar (the samples' week's "Team
check-in"), Notes and Karpo's own, every row its icon.

### Strings

New in all 40 languages: `core.winSearch.category.{events,people,notes,karpo}`, `core.winSearch.searchIn`,
`core.winSearch.source.{settings,files,karpo,calculator}`, `core.winSearch.karpoSettings`; a source's other names are its
group's or §642's switches' words.

### Tests

`WinSearchSourcesTests` (12): the registry the one list, every source the dock and the ghost build in it, the defaults;
the switches writing only what differs; "Search in" one toggle a source in order, writing the config and back to none;
a source off never asked, one that throws answering nothing, a chip asking only the sources of its group; grouping and
ranking over several sources, two messages by their keys; mail, people (ContactSearch's order, a number by its digits),
events (the nearest first, the window read), notes (title, then text; the first line), Karpo itself (a page, a widget by
its search words, a layout, every General row); Karpo's addresses read back; the fixed height (kind, preset, a file's
automatic). Updated: `WinSearchEngineTests` (quick sources together off the thread, the index's two sources, the web and
the calculator switched), `WinSearchQueryTests` (the new prefixes), `OptionRowsTests`, `UntranslatedTests` (fr, ro, fil:
Windows' own words). UI: `WinSearchLineTests.AGhostListsItsSamplesGroupedWithIconsAndAsksNothingOfThisPC` (several
sources' groups, only kinds' and apps' icons asked, glyphs while none has come),
`EveryRowWearsWindowsOwnIconItsGlyphWhileItComes` (an app's address, a file's and a folder's path, Settings' app; the
icon in the glyph's place once come). Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `winsearch-line-<dark|light>.png` (now with Karpo's own
and Windows' icons), `SceneTreeTests.WinSearchGroupSheets` — `winsearch2-group-<bottom|left>-<dark|light>-150.png`.

By hand: the search box › type "team": your Teams, files with their own icons, your mail, meetings, notes; "appearance"
— Karpo's Appearance page; Enter on it: edit mode at that page. Its page › Search in › Email off: no mail any more.

## 653. Start (beta) loses its search box: the `startSearch` widget removed whole (2026-11-09)

The person (2026-11-09): *"start search folder widget does not seem to do anything. remove it."*

**Removed.** The Start group's search line (§641) and everything that was only there for it: `WidgetInfos.StartSearch`,
`ListKind.StartSearch` (file word `startSearch`), `WidgetSource.StartSearch`, `StartSearchLine`, its add-list leaf (Start and
taskbar's run is now the group and its four widgets), its rows in Island, `Dock.WidgetMenus` and the registries, the `search`
channel (`Channels.Search`, `StartQuery`) and every line's `Follows` of it, `StartLine.Query`, what the pinned apps, All apps
and Recommended narrowed by it (their "Nothing matches" words, `dock.start.noMatch`), the fuzzy match and its order
(`StartSearch.Score/Rank/Best/Words`, `StartUses.Frecency`), the samples' opening counts that fed that order, and the widget's
three words in all 40 languages. `StartSearch.Fold` was the add page's fold already (`CatalogueSearch.Fold`, called directly
now); `ByName` is `StartApp.ByName`. Windows search (beta, §642, `winSearch`) is a widget of its own and untouched.

**The group.** Pinned apps (Full, 16 cells), Recommended (Full, 10) and the foot (3) — 29 cells — beside All apps fixed 29
(`Presets.StartAppsCells`). Down a side bar one list (§620): All apps under the rest at 16 cells (`StartAppsSideCells`, was
20), so the whole list stands beside a 1440p screen's side bar at 150 % (886 of 936 DIP; `PresetSideTests` failed for
`startGroup` before, All apps left out).

**The file.** No conversion code (memory: no migrations): Config.Shape 86 → 87, ConfigWords written again (`line kind
"startSearch"` gone). A file that still has one — only as a folder's line, `layouts[].islands[].folder.lists[][].island.kind
== "startSearch"` (never a bar item: it was a list line only; it carried no options record) — reads, and the line is dropped

folder and its other lines stay, and the next save leaves it out. `start.tsv` (opening counts and first sightings) is
unchanged; the counts are still kept, nothing reads them now.
