## 654. Beside a dock an attached folder grows top to bottom: its ground the columns' width and the work area's whole height (2026-11-09) — withdrawn in §656

The person (2026-11-09), after seeing §651's pictures of a ground from edge to edge: *"actually, the folders in dock mode
should always grow top to bottom. from side to side it just does not look good."*

**What was wrong** (pictures `artifacts/attached4/before/`): §651's rule is a taskbar's — the bar grown out, its ground along
the bar from end to end. A dock (a Dock layout, `BarStyle.Floating`: panels 8 DIP off the screen's edge, centred) is no
strip from end to end, so along a bottom dock the ground was a band across the whole screen, far wider than the dock it grew
out of, the dock's short panels under one part of it. Down a side dock the same rule already ran top to bottom.

**The rule** (`FlyoutHost.GroundOf`, one branch, `floating`): beside a floating dock, whatever its edge, the ground is **the
work area's whole height, top to bottom, and the columns' own width** — beside a bottom or top dock from the columns' one
edge to their other, edge to edge (the columns flush, a seam between two, as §651), up to the screen's top (or another
bar's side); beside a side dock from the dock's inner side to the columns' far side, which is what §651 drew there:
unchanged. Never past the work area. The folder is told its bar is a dock by the dock (`FolderFlyout.Show(floating:)` from
`Layout.Floating`, at its three showings: opened, shown again on a bar's successor, the add page's ghost) and hands it to its
host (`FlyoutHost.Floating`). No setting, nothing in the file.

**Where it meets the dock**: a dock's folder's work area ends at the dock's inner side (DockWindow.FolderWork, the dock
panel's strip), so the ground's foot is the dock's top (a bottom dock), flush, the columns standing on it: over the dock the
ground and the dock are one surface, the dock's own outline the join. Where the columns reach past the dock's panel (a folder
at a panel's end, two columns) the ground's foot stands on the dock's line beside the panel, a column on a shelf; no line is
drawn there. Weighed and left: running the ground on down past the dock to the screen's edge — the folder's window is
topmost and would take the dock's pointer; and closing its foot with a line, which over the dock would double the dock's.

**Its outline** (`FlyoutHost.GroundEdges`, one rule for both kinds of bar): along every side of the ground open to the screen —
every side not on the work area's edge. Beside a taskbar that is §651's far side alone (its bar side and its ends are the
work area's edges); beside a bottom or top dock the ground's two long sides (its top is the screen's, its foot the dock's
side); beside a side dock its far side; columns pushed against a screen's end draw none on that side. The one line became
four, each shown where its side is open.

**Taskbars**: unchanged (§651). In one case §651 drew a line it should not have: a ground whose columns fill the work area's
whole depth no longer draws its far line along the screen's edge.

**Coming and going**: the drawer of §647, its depth the ground's — beside a bottom dock its whole height, out of the dock.

Not changed: the Appearance's preview (`LookPreview`) shows a sample bar of no kind and draws §651's ground.

Tests: `FolderStyleTests` — `ADocksGroundRunsTopToBottomTheColumnsWide` (new: each edge at 100, 150, 200 %, centred and at
either end: the work area's whole height, the columns' width, flush on the dock's inner side; the same panel beside a taskbar
§651's ground; a panel taller and wider than the room stops at the work area), `TheGroundsOutlineRunsAlongItsOpenSides` (new:
a bottom taskbar its top; a bottom dock its two sides; against the screen's end one; a left dock its far side); UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `OnADockTheAttachedFolderRunsTopToBottom` (new: bottom and left at 150 %, top at 100 %: the ground the
columns' width from the work area's top to its bottom, the columns flush on the dock, a press at its far end the folder's,
one beside it not, one seam). `TheAttachedFolderAdjoinsItsBar` and `AttachedFlatTests` hold unchanged. Pictures
(KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.AttachedDockSheets`, `attached4-dock-<bottom|left>-<one|two>-<dark|light>-150.png`
(`artifacts/attached4/before/`, `after/`).

By hand: a Dock layout along the bottom, a folder in it › Folder style › Attached, open it: a column in the dock's own paint
from the screen's top down to the dock, as wide as the folder's columns, a thin line down its two sides, the columns on the
dock; a Taskbar as §651; a Dock on the left as before, top to bottom.

## 656. A dock's folder is always cards: no Folder style row on a dock, §654 withdrawn (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-09), after §654: *"actually, in dock mode you should not be able to have the folder docked too. then
you dont have the optimize the looks."*

**The rule** (`FolderStyles.Worn`, one place): the style a folder opens in is its own beside a taskbar, **Cards beside a
dock** (a `LayoutType.Dock` layout, the bar's `Layout.Floating`), whatever it says. The dock tells the folder its bar is a
dock at its three showings (`FolderFlyout.Show(dock:)` from `Layout.Floating`: opened, shown again on a bar's successor, the
add page's ghost; the pictures' `FolderFrom` the same), and the folder's one question "attached?" (`FolderFlyout.Attached`)
asks the rule: its ground, its flush placement, its anchor on the bar, its flat lines and its seams all follow from it, so
an Attached folder on a dock is drawn and placed exactly as a folder of cards.

**The row**: on a dock's folder its page has no Folder style row — not greyed, not there (`FolderStyles.Offered`, read by
`OptionRows.FolderRows` from the page's layout, `OptionPlace.Layout`). On a taskbar's it is there as §647.

**The file**: unchanged. The style a folder says is kept as it is: a layout made a Dock and back a Taskbar wears Attached
again, its row back with Attached in force. No shape change, nothing converted.

**The Appearance's preview** (`LookPreview.GroundOf`): the sample bar a dock's (the layout shown a Dock), its folder stands
as cards even where Flyouts › Attached folder background is said; a taskbar's as §649. The background row itself stays — it
is global and taskbars wear it.

**§654 withdrawn**, its code deleted whole: `GroundOf`'s `floating` branch, `FlyoutHost.Floating` and its wiring,
`FlyoutHost.GroundEdges` and its four lines (back to §651's one line along the far side), the dock picture
(`AttachedDockSheets`) and its tests (`ADocksGroundRunsTopToBottomTheColumnsWide`, `TheGroundsOutlineRunsAlongItsOpenSides`,
`OnADockTheAttachedFolderRunsTopToBottom`). The one taskbar detail §654 changed — a ground whose columns fill the work area's
whole depth drew no far line along the screen's edge — is §651's again (the line drawn): `GroundEdges` existed for the dock's
two open sides, and one sprite at the far side is the simpler rule for a taskbar, whose far side is the one open.

Tests: `FolderStyleTests` — `OnADockAFolderIsWornAsCards` (new: Worn and Offered for both kinds), `OnADockTheFoldersPageHasNoStyleRow`
(new: the folder's page as the panel builds it and its option rows, a taskbar's with the row, a dock's without; made a
taskbar again, the row back with Attached in force), `OnADockTheAppearancePreviewsFolderStandsAsCards` (new); UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `OnADockTheAttachedFolderStandsAsCards` (new: bottom at 150 %, left at 100 %: placed where a folder of
cards stands, the same cards, the same gap between its columns, no ground, not flat; opened from a taskbar the same folder
on its ground). `TheAttachedFolderAdjoinsItsBar`, `AttachedFlatTests`, `FolderFacesTests`, `WidgetPageTests` hold unchanged.
Picture (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `SceneTreeTests.AttachedOnADockSheet`, `attached5-dock-bottom-dark-150.png` (`artifacts/attached5/`).

By hand: a Dock layout, a folder in it whose style was Attached on a taskbar: open it — cards off the dock, as every dock's
folder; its page has no Folder style. Switch the layout to a Taskbar: the folder opens attached again, its row back.

## 657. The sun's day bar is always the clock's 24 hours (2026-11-10)

The person: *"sunrise sunset bar should always show 24 h (one full day) but does not do so."*

**The root cause.** The day bar (`SunDayBar`, `ListKind.SunDayBar`, §368) mixed two different days. Its axis was this
PC's calendar day, midnight to midnight in instants (a 23- or 25-hour day that long), but the only marks it put on it
were the sunrise and sunset of *one* solar day of the place — the solar day holding now (`SolarPosition.TimesFor`), which
turns at the place's solar midnight, not this PC's. Where the two did not line up an event fell off the bar, and a
missing event was read as the bar's end (`Rise ?? 0`, `Set ?? 1`):

- Zürich between 00:00 and its solar midnight (00:26 in winter, 01:26 in summer): the solar day was still yesterday's,
  both its events off today's bar, so the **whole bar was lit as daylight**, the dot on it.
- A place in another zone (the person's sun line stands on New York): New York's solar day turns at 05:56 here, so from
  midnight to then the whole bar was lit; Tokyo's daylight crosses this PC's midnight (22:12 to 08:38 here), so only one
  of its two stretches was drawn and its sunrise had no tick.
- The days the clocks change: the axis was 23 or 25 hours, so noon was off the bar's middle and now's dot off its clock
  time (13:30 on March 29 drawn at 54 % of the bar, not 56 %).

**The fix** (`Karpo.Dock\Weather\Sun.cs`). The bar is always one full day of 24 hours: this PC's clock from 00:00 to 24:00
of the day holding now, each instant where its clock time is (`SunDayBar.Share`: its time of day over 24 hours), noon in
the middle on every day. What is lit is wherever the sun is up in those hours: the sunrises and sunsets of every solar
day of the place that touches them (two either side of now's) become marks (`SunMark`), in order; the bar is lit from
00:00 where its first mark is a sunset (with none, as the sun is all day: `SolarPosition.Up`, the upper limb over the
horizon as a sunrise is reckoned), each sunrise opens a stretch and each sunset closes it (`SunDayBarPlan.Lit`: one
stretch, two where the daylight crosses midnight, all of it in polar day, none in polar night). `SunDayBar.Midnight` and
the `PolarState` the plan carried are gone; the plan is now, the lit stretches and the marks.

`SunTile` draws every lit stretch and a tick at every mark; the strip's sunrise and sunset stand under the bar's own first
sunrise and sunset ticks and say *their* times (New York at 03:00 here says today's 12:36 and 22:42 under them, not
yesterday's), the daylight under the longest lit stretch. The one-row (Compact) bar is the same plan, small.

**Where else.** Nothing else reckons a day's span for the sun: the arc is the sun's path from sunrise to sunset (an hour
angle, not a clock); the face on the bar, the times' widgets and the folder's widths read times and how soon, no axis.
No config change, nothing converted.

Tests: `SunTests.TheDayBarIsAlwaysTheClocksTwentyFourHours` (replaces `TheDayBarIsTheLocalDayAndTheDayTheClocksGoForwardIsTwentyThreeHours`;
on W. Europe's clock: Zürich on an ordinary day, at 00:10, on the days the clocks go forward and back; New York at 03:00
here; Tokyo at noon here, its daylight in two; Tromsø in polar summer and winter — now at its clock time over 24 hours,
noon at 0.5, each lit stretch between the right instants, a tick at each sunrise and sunset and no other, now lit where it
is in a stretch), `TheDayBarsDaylightIsTheDaysLengthOfTwentyFourHours` (Tokyo's two stretches together its 10 h 28 min).
UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `SunPictures.TheDayBarIsAlwaysTwentyFourHoursPictured`: sun-dayBar-24h-dark/light.png, the seven
cases at 150 % (`artifacts/sunbar/`).

By hand: a sun line in the Day bar style on a place in another zone (New York): after midnight here the bar is dark until
New York's sunrise in the afternoon, lit to its sunset in the evening, the dot at the clock's time; noon the bar's middle.

## 655. Windows search's home before anything is typed, the chosen result's pane beside a wide list, the index linked from its page, Open with Windows' own dialog (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-09), after using §642's and §652's widget:

1. *"windows indexing settings should not show up on the bottom in the search widget. it should be linked in the configuration."*
2. *"the actions should be shown on the right side if there is enough space. it should be designed in a win11 similar style."*
3. *"even when i have nothing typed in search widget yet it should already show usable contents like recent files, folders, pinned stuff, apps etc whatever. this should be configurable to a high degree and it should also have a responsive design so that on wider columns it still looks good as on narrower ones."*
4. *"open with does not work in the search widget."*

### 1. The index linked from the page; no foot

The foot under the results (Classic or Enhanced, and "Searching Windows" as a link) is gone, and with it everything only it
needed: `WinSearchScopes`, `IWinSearchIndex.Scopes`, `WindowsIndex.Scopes`/`PathOf` and the indexer's rules read from the
registry, the engine's `Scopes`, the `Spot.Indexing` target and the words `dock.winSearch.classic`/`.enhanced` in all 40
languages. The way there is the last row of **Search in** on the widget's page: `WinSearchIndex`, an action row named as
Windows names the page (`WindowsPages.SearchingWindows`, `ms-settings:cortana-windowssearch` — Settings › Privacy & security ›
Searching Windows, where Classic or Enhanced and the excluded folders are chosen), the launch glyph at its start, as Formats'
"Region settings" row opens Windows' own page. The rows have no launcher of their own: the dock hands one in
(`OptionDevices.Open`, `Launch.Open`).

### 2. The pane (Windows 11's preview)

From **560 DIP** wide (`WinSearchLine.Wide`, the breakpoint grown with larger text: 560 × the text scale) the line is split:
its list on the left, the chosen result's **pane** on the right — two fifths of the width, 240 to 360 DIP, the gutter's inset
beyond it (`WinSearchLine.Split`). The split is the width's alone: typing, chips, a pointer or a scroll never move it. The
pane is a card (the control fill, its stroke, 8 DIP corners): the result's icon at 48 DIP in the middle (Windows' own, its
glyph while it comes), its name strong under it (two lines where it does not fit), what it is ("App", "Documents",
"Calendar"), a rule, what is known of it (a file's folder; what it is, when it changed and how big; anything else's line),
a rule, then **its actions, a row each**, glyph and name, lit under the pointer: Open, Run as administrator, Open file
location, Copy as path (an answer's "Copy result", anything else's "Copy"), Open with — those it can have done
(`WinSearchLine.Actions`, `Can`). A copy says "Copied" in its row. A wide line's rows have no buttons of their own and the
best match no strip under it: the pane has them.

**What it shows** (`PaneHit`): the row the keys are on; else the one the pointer was last on — kept as the pointer crosses
to the pane, which stands beside the rows; else the best match, with nothing typed the home's first. Up and Down walk, the
pane follows; Enter opens the row the keys chose (the best match until they move).

**It stays while the list scrolls.** One mechanism for any line: `IListScroll.ScrollAside` — a band at the line's trailing
side under the head that stays, as the head and the foot do (ListScroll.cs). `ListScrolled` has an `Aside`; its `Window`
(what the items show through) ends where the band starts; the band is drawn in the content as it stands unscrolled and a
point in it read there (`ListScrolled.At(point)`, which takes a point now); the scrollbar stands at the window's edge. The
pane reaches the foot of what shows of the line (the height it was last given).

Narrower than 560 DIP: one list, the best match's actions under it, a row's at its end under the pointer or the keys, as
§642 had them. The group's preset is **Extra wide** (640 DIP) now, so a new group opens split; a group already on a bar
keeps its width (its folder's Width menu sets it).

### 3. The home: sections, configurable

Before anything is typed the line shows its **home** (`WinSearchHome`, Karpo.Core\WinSearchHome.cs), sections built as the
sources are (§652): **one registry**, `WinSearchHomeInfos.All` — each section's id, glyph, how its items stand
(`WinSearchHomeLook`: rows, tiles, the searches), how many it shows by default and at most, whether it is shown by default —,
and a small interface per section, `IWinSearchHomeSource` (`Id`, `Warm(came)`, `Forget()`, `List(ask)`; `WinSearchHomeSource`
makes one of functions). The engine lists every section off the dock's thread as the line shows and again whenever one says
it changed, a section that throws listing nothing; the recent searches are the engine's own (its history), a section of the
registry like the others.

| Id | Section | Look | Shown / most | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `searches` | Recent searches | rows, × and "Clear search history" | 4 / 8 | the line's history (§642) |
| `apps` | Top apps | tiles | 6 / 24 | the apps opened most: Karpo's Start's counts (`StartUses`, start.tsv) and the line's history together; an app opened from the line now counts there too |
| `pinned` | Pinned | tiles | 12 / 24 | the pins of the config's Start (beta) pinned apps line (`StartPins.OfConfig`), else this PC's usual ones |
| `files` | Recent files | rows | 6 / 24 | Windows' Recent folder (`StartStore.Files`, Start's Recommended's) |
| `folders` | Recent folders | rows | 4 / 12 | the same folder's shortcuts to folders (`StartStore.Folders`, new) |
| `events` | Coming up | rows | 3 / 12 | Karpo's calendars: not over yet, within 14 days, the soonest first |
| `mail` | Unread mail | rows | 3 / 12 | the messages Karpo synced, unread, the newest first |
| `notes` | Recent notes | rows | 3 / 12, **off by default** | Karpo's notebook, the ones changed last first |

Nothing is read twice: Windows' Recent folder has **one reader** now (`RecentFiles.Items`, files and folders, a minute
kept), the pins' picker and `StartStore` both its; Top apps, Pinned, files and folders read Start (beta)'s source
(`IStartSource`: `StartStore` on the dock, `StartSamples` in a ghost), told when it has read again while the line shows and let
go once it has gone (`WinSearchHomes`); the mail, events and notes rows are made by the line's own sources' (`Hit`,
`Unread`, `Coming`, `Recent` in KarpoSources.cs).

**What a line shows** (`WinSearchHome.For`): its sections in its order, each cut to its count; a thing an earlier section
showed is not shown again (an app pinned and used a lot is one tile); a section with nothing to show is left out; with none at
all, "Type to search apps, settings, files and more."

**Responsive.** Rows as §642's. Tiles as Windows 11's search home's Top apps: each its icon (32 DIP) over its name, as many
across as the list has room for at 88 DIP or more each, three at the least, the list's width shared out evenly — three
across at 280 and 360 DIP and beside a 640 DIP line's pane, six at 559, five beside a 900 DIP line's pane. A wide line's home has the pane too (its
first item), so nothing jumps sideways as typing begins. The line keeps its one height (§652) and scrolls inside.

**The page** (§645's plain sections; `SettingsPanel.Widget.cs`: §594's rule — a level that is all What it shows holds is
the section — grown to several levels and lists put in order, each a section of its own):

- **Search in** — a switch per source (§652), then Searching Windows (above).
- **When nothing is typed** — the toggles widget's ordered list (`OptionRow.Ordered`, `Move`): the sections shown, in
  their order, dragged by their grips (and Ctrl+Up/Down), each taken out by its ×; "Add a section" offers the others. The
  list's words are its own now (`OptionRow.OrderedWords`; the toggles' "Add a toggle" by default).
- **How many each shows** — a number per section shown, 1 to its most.

No third level, no expander hiding one setting.

### 4. Open with

It handed the file to the shell with the "openas" verb, which opens nothing for most files on Windows 11. Now
`Launch.OpenWith(file)` asks **Windows' own Open with dialog**, `SHOpenWithDialog` (TerraFX's binding, blittable, AOT-safe)
with `OPENASINFO { pcszFile, oaifInFlags = OAIF_ALLOW_REGISTRATION | OAIF_EXEC }` — "Always use this app" offered, the file
opened in the app picked —, through the one launcher (§491: what is open of Karpo's closes first). The dialog is modal to
its owner, so it is owned by nothing and runs on an STA thread of its own: the dock's message loop is never held.
`LaunchKind.OpenWith`; `Launched.Flags` says the flags a stand-in sees. The line's acts go through
`WinSearchLine.Launches` (static), the seam the tests stand in for.

### Samples

A ghost (§635) opens on its **home, the samples'**: the samples' searches, Start's sample apps opened most (Edge, Word,
Outlook, Excel, Spotify, Terminal) and pinned, Start's sample week's files and folders (`StartSamples.SampleFolders`, new),
the samples' week's events, mail and note. What is typed into it (a picture's "team") the samples answer, as before; wide,
the pane beside them.

### The file

    cell.winSearch   { "sources"?: {…}, "home"?: ["apps", "files", …], "homeMost"?: { "<id>": n, … } }

`home`: the sections shown, in their order — none written for the default ones in theirs; `homeMost`: a section's count
where it is not its default. Unknown ids dropped, a count held to its section's range. **Shape 89** (`Config.Shape`;
`ConfigWords.txt`: `property WinSearchOptions.home`, `.homeMost`). **The conversion rule:** the version number only
(`"version": 88` → `89`); nothing else in a file changes — a line without `home`/`homeMost` shows the default home. No
migration code.

### Strings

New in all 40 languages: `core.winSearch.home.{apps,pinned,folders,events,mail,notes}`, `core.winSearch.homeShown`,
`.homeCounts`, `.homeAdd`, `.homeEmpty`, `.homeAll`. Reused: `dock.winSearch.recentSearches`, `.recentFiles`, `.copyResult`,
`dock.menu.copy`. Gone: `dock.winSearch.classic`, `.enhanced`.

### Tests

New: `WinSearchHomeTests` (12: the registry the one list the dock's and the ghost's home sources answer; a line's sections
in its order, cut, each thing once; only what differs written and the file's JSON; Top apps; the page's Searching Windows
row opening `ms-settings:cortana-windowssearch`; When nothing is typed an ordered list writing the order, its counts
writing `homeMost` and back to no record; the dock's sections over Start's samples, a config's Start pins, events, unread
mail, notes; Start's source told once and let go; a section that throws; the breakpoint at 100, 150, 200 %),
`WinSearchOpenWithTests` (written first: Open with asks the Open-with seam for the file with
`OAIF_ALLOW_REGISTRATION | OAIF_EXEC`, after "leave"; the other acts where they went), `ListScrollTests.TheSideStaysBesideTheItems`,
`LaunchTests` (the new way out), UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `WinSearchLineTests.TheHomeListsItsSections…`,
`AGhostShowsTheSamplesHome…`, `WideThePaneShowsTheChosenResultAndItsActionsBesideTheList` (the pane follows the keys and
the pointer, keeps it crossing over, its Open with clicked), `ThePaneStandsFromFiveHundredSixtyDip…` (280, 480, 559 one list;
560, 640, 900 split; the split never moves; three tiles across at 280). Brought along: `WinSearchEngineTests`,
`WinSearchSourcesTests`, `WindowsIndexTests` (the rules' test gone with them), `OptionRowsTests`, `WidgetPageTests` (§655's
sections), `SceneTreeTests.WinSearchGroupSheets` (the home checked, then "team"). The two stale lists fixed:
`WidgetMenuTests.EveryLineHasTheMenuItsKindWasGiven` (`ListKind.WinSearch`: none, its acts in the line) and
`ListGutterTests.EveryListKindIsPictured` (a group "Start (beta) and Windows search", their `Held` from the UI run: All
apps' heading and the search box on the gutter to the pixel; Pinned's and Recommended's headings a px or two in at the
largest text, held to nothing; `StoodIn` stands Start's and Windows search's samples in). Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR):
`winsearch3-<narrow|wide>-<home|typed>-<dark|light>.png`, `winsearch-line-<dark|light>.png`,
`winsearch2-group-<bottom|left>-<dark|light>-150.png` (now split, "team" typed), `panel-529-winsearch-<dark|light>.png` (the page).

By hand: edit mode › Add › Windows search (Beta) onto the bar (Extra wide); click it: the recent searches, Top apps and
Pinned as tiles, files, folders, events, unread mail; the pane on the right shows the first. Type "pa": the list on the
left, Paint's pane on the right; Down walks, the pane follows; point at a file and move right onto the pane: its Open with
— Windows' dialog. Narrow the folder to Medium: one list, each row's buttons at its end. Its page: Search in › Searching
Windows settings opens Windows' page; When nothing is typed: drag Recent files to the top, take Unread mail out, Add a
section › Recent notes; How many each shows › Recent files 10.

## 658. All apps lists the apps, the first search no longer freezes the dock, the search's home is filled on a first use (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10), on the published build:

> 1. "all apps does not show anything."
> 2. "when searching for the first time karpo completely freezes for a short time"
> 3. "when nothing is typed in the search it should show more than just coming up events."

Measured first, read only, on this PC (`RealShellTests`, KARPO_REAL_SHELL=1): the shell's Apps folder lists 253 apps in
~300 ms off the dock's thread (`InstalledApps.List`, fine); `StartStore.Shared.Refresh()` read **nothing in 30 s**; the
Recent folder holds **no shortcut at all** (Start_TrackDocs = 0 and File Explorer's ShowRecent = 0: recent items are turned
off on this PC); the index's first question 30–40 ms, Karpo's own rows 30 ms (once, as the line shows), Settings' pages,
the calculator, the contacts, mail and notes a few ms each — no step of a query itself is slow.

### 1 and 3: Start's source never read (the root cause), and no recent items on this PC

**`StartStore` never read Windows.** Its "read a minute ago?" test was `Environment.TickCount64 - readAt < 60 000` with
`readAt` starting at `long.MinValue`: now − MinValue overflows to a negative number, smaller than a minute, so every
`Refresh` returned at once — since §641. Every Start line (All apps, Pinned, Recommended, the account's name and picture)
and §655's home sections over the same source (Top apps, Pinned, Recent files, Recent folders) stood empty; only the
sections over Karpo's own stores (Coming up) showed. Fixed: `readAt` is `long?`, null before the first read. Nothing
AOT-specific: the same under the test runtime.

**Seam:** `StartStore` takes its reads (`StartReads`: the apps, the recent items, the account, Windows Update, the power
menu, the worker and the clock); `StartStore.Shared` hands Windows' own, a test its own.

**No recent items** (the rest of report 3): where Windows' Recent folder points at nothing still there, `RecentFiles.Items`
— the one reader, §655 — takes **what changed last on the Desktop, in Documents and in Downloads**, files and folders
alike, newest first, nothing hidden, no `desktop.ini`, no dot-names, no network place. The pins' picker had this fallback
for files alone (`Newest`, Desktop and Documents); it moved into `Items`, so the picker, Start's Recommended and Windows
search's Recent files and Recent folders share it, and `List` is a plain projection now.

**Top apps on a first use:** nothing was opened from Karpo yet, so no app counted. `WinSearchHomeHits.TopApps` takes
`usual` — the apps Start (beta) pins (the config's pinned line, else this PC's usual pins) — and fills the section after
the apps opened, each once; the home's "each thing once" (`WinSearchHome.For`) leaves Pinned the pins Top apps did not show.

### 2: the first search's icons flooded the dock's queue (the root cause)

Every row asks its icon at every drawing (`TargetPictures.Large.Get(…, Arrived)`), and an icon not read yet **added a
waiter per ask**. The first search lists dozens of rows whose icons were never read (later searches find them kept): each
drawing added one more `Arrived` to every icon still coming, each icon that came called all of them, each call posted a
`WM_KARPO_ISLAND`, each message was a whole redraw, which asked again — the posts grew faster than the dock could draw.
Posted messages are taken before the keys and the mouse: the dock froze until the icons were all in.

- `TargetPictures.Get` keeps a waiter once (a line's `Arrived` is the same delegate at every drawing).
- `Islands.Post` (all of `CellIsland.Wake`/`Post`): **one message waits per island at a time**; the dock's `IslandReady`
  takes it (`Islands.Taken`) before the refresh, so news meanwhile posts again and nothing is missed; `Attach` clears what an
  earlier window of the same handle and token left. Any store's burst of news is one redraw now.

Nothing else of a query runs on the dock's thread: the engine hands every source, the index and the home to the worker
(`WinSearchEngineTests.TheFirstQuestionRunsNothingOnTheCallersThread`). The index's connection is made per question on a
worker and its first open measured 30–40 ms, so nothing is warmed ahead. Not changed, noted: a keystroke's cancel runs the
running question's `ICommand::Cancel` on the dock's thread (the token's callback); the provider documents it as callable
from any thread.

### Tests

New: `StartStoreTests` (the first line shown reads at clocks 0, 12 345 678 and long.MaxValue/2 — red before; a second
asks nothing while one reads; within the minute nothing, after it again), `IslandPostTests` (400 pieces of news of two
islands are two messages; taken, the next posts), `TargetLooksTests.AnAskNeverWaitsForTheReadAndAPictureComingTellsItsLineOnce`
(50 asks while the read holds: told once — 50 before), `TargetLooksTests.WithoutRecentItemsWhatChangedLastStandsIn` (an
empty or missing Recent folder: the newest folders and files of the places, hidden, dot-names and desktop.ini left out; a
shortcut kept: it alone), `WinSearchHomeTests.TopAppsFallBackToThePinnedOnAFirstUse`,
`WinSearchEngineTests.TheFirstQuestionRunsNothingOnTheCallersThread`, `RealShellTests` (KARPO_REAL_SHELL=1, by hand: the
readers and steps above, timed, on this PC). Brought along: `WinSearchHomeTests.TheDocksSectionsReadWhatKarpoAlreadyReads`
(Top apps: Word opened, then Paint pinned), `ChangedElsewhereTests` and `BrightnessWidgetTests` (their stand-in dock takes
each message, as the dock does).

By hand: Start (beta) › All apps lists every app, Recommended its files; Windows search (beta) opened with nothing typed:
Top apps and Pinned as tiles, Recent files and Recent folders (Desktop, Documents and Downloads' newest where recent items
are off), Coming up; the first word typed after a start: the list fills, its icons come, the dock answers the keys throughout.

## 659. Windows search: every row's actions at its end, the best match's too (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10), of §642's and §655's Windows search (beta):

> "for the best match for example it should show the actions on the right like it is done for the other sections as well. this should be done for all the sections"

**One row.** Every result of every section — the best match, Apps, Settings, Documents, Folders, Photos, Videos, Music,
Email, Calendar, Contacts, Notes, Karpo, Web, and the home's rows (Recent files, Recent folders, Coming up, Unread mail,
Recent notes) — is drawn by the one `RowPaint.Hit`, its actions **at its end**: subtle glyph buttons in the middle of its
words, every row's ending at one edge, named by their tooltips. They show while the row is under the pointer or the keys,
or is where Enter lands — the best match until the keys move, so its stand there as the results come, as its strip did.
The best match stays taller (a larger icon, its name strong, what it is and when it changed, its folder) on the control
fill; **nothing stands under it** any more: §642's strip under the best match is gone, and with it the row's `head`, the
strip's height, the buttons' `strong`/dimmed switch and the rows' `wide` switch.

**Which buttons** (`WinSearchLine.RowActs`): a row's actions (`Actions`) but Open — the row itself opens —, in their
order (Run as administrator, Open file location, Copy as path / Copy / Copy result, Open with), as many as stand in half
the row's room for its words. A row Open is all of (a Settings page, Karpo's own, an event, the web's row) has none. An
app: Run as administrator; a file: Open file location, Copy as path, Open with (a program Run as administrator first); a
folder: Open file location, Copy as path; a message and a person: Copy (the address); a note: Copy (its text); an
answer: Copy result. A copy says "Copied" in their place, as before. Before, a row showed the last three of its actions
(a program lost Run as administrator) and the best match all of them, Open first, in a strip under it.

**Narrow and wide alike.** §655's wide rows had no buttons (the pane had them); now they have them too, and the pane
beside the list still names the chosen one's actions, a row each, as Windows' does. A pane's button is a target of its
own (`Target.Pane`): the pointer on it lights it alone, not the row's button for the same act.

**Tiles** (Top apps, Pinned) have none: 88 DIP for an icon and a name leave no room for buttons that would not cover
them, and Windows' Top apps have none either. Their actions are the pane's (wide) and the keys' (Ctrl+Shift+Enter as
administrator).

**The keys** are unchanged: Up and Down walk the rows, the row they are on shows its buttons (the best match's go once it
is no longer where Enter lands), Enter opens, Ctrl+Enter the location, Ctrl+Shift+Enter as administrator, Ctrl+C copies.
No key reached a row's buttons before and none does now: their acts have keys of their own.

Tests: UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `WinSearchLineTests.EveryRowOfEverySectionHasItsActionsAtItsEndTheBestMatchToo` (360 and
700 DIP: the best match's Run as administrator at its end at rest, no piece of it under its words, no Open button; every
row of Apps, Settings, Documents, Folders, Photos, Music, Email, Calendar, Contacts, Notes and Web none at rest and its
actions but Open, in order, at its end under the pointer, beside and in the middle of its words, ending where the best
match's do; a click and a tooltip; the keys' row; wide, the pane's button leaving the row's alone; an answer's Copy; the
home's files and folders rows alike, a tile none) — in place of `ARowUnderThePointerOffersItsActionsAndTheBestMatchAlways`;
`WideThePaneShowsTheChosenResultAndItsActionsBesideTheList` and `ThePaneStandsFromFiveHundredSixtyDip…` (the best
match's button at its end at every width). Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `winsearch3-<narrow|wide>-typed-<dark|light>.png`,
`winsearch-line-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: the search box › type "pa": Paint the best match, its Run as administrator at the right of its row; point at a
document: its three buttons at its end, in line with Paint's; Down: the row under the keys shows its own, Paint's go.

## 660. Size: Fill shows no rows under its Height (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10), of a widget's Size on its page of the settings panel and in its menu:

> "when fill is selected as height there should not be a height property anymore as it is ignored"

**One rule, where the rows are made.** `LineHeightRows.Rows`, the one place a folder line's height rows are built (the
line's menu's foot and, read from that menu, its page's Size section alike), gives the rows' stepper only to the modes that
use the rows: **Automatic** ("Max rows", which the content grows up to) and **Fixed** ("Rows", exactly that tall). Under
**Fill** the Height row stands alone: Fill takes the room its list has left whatever the rows say (§168), so §168 to §659's
greyed "Max rows − 6 rows +" under it is gone. The rows are not dropped: `LineHeight` keeps its cells under Fill as it
always did (`As`), so Automatic or Fixed picked again shows the stepper back at them; nothing in the file changes.
`LineHeightRows.Updated` already put the rows back by the Height row's id, so the menu shows the stepper going and coming
back in place; a step (the stepper's keys, the arranged bar's resize keys) under Fill still asks for nothing.

**The other mode-and-value pairs, checked.** None of them shows a value its choice ignores, so nothing else changed:

- a sized line's Size (Compact, Medium, Full, §432): sizes only, no value under them;
- a folder list's width (Narrow to Widest): presets only, no number;
- a market line's Range and its Years: Years made only under the Years range (`MarketRows`);
- a calendar's Style and its Days ahead: Days ahead is the agenda's own (`WidgetOptionsKind.Calendar`); another style is
  another kind, without it;
- a clock's Style and its Seconds: both styles (clock, time) draw the seconds;
- a volume slider's Direction and Length: every direction is that long;
- a bar's Show (space kept, over the windows, hidden) and its Size and Spacing: every way of showing uses both;
- a folder face's options: shown only while their condition holds already (`FaceOption.When`).

Left as it is, on purpose: the bar's **Background blur** (§547) stands greyed, with why under it, while the background is
solid or None. It follows a colour's opacity, not a mode picked beside it, and says why it does nothing, so the person
knows what to change to make it count.

Tests: `LineHeightRowsTests.UnderFillThereIsNoStepperAndTheRowsComeBack` (Fill: the Height row alone, ticked; Automatic and
Fixed: the stepper, for a calendar and for a kind of Fixed alone; Automatic and Fixed through Fill and back at 6½ rows; no
step under Fill) in place of `UnderFillTheStepperIsGreyedAndStepsNothing`; `TheMenuIsShownAgainWithTheRowsAsTheyAreNow`
(Fill drops the stepper from a shown menu, Fixed puts it back at 7 rows); `WidgetPageTests.UnderFillTheHeightHasNoRows`
(the page: nothing under Height under Fill, Max rows under Automatic, Rows under Fixed, the rows kept through Fill). UI
(KARPO_UI_TESTS=1): `LineHeightRowsTests.TheRowsActAndTheMenuStaysOpen` (under Fill no stepper on screen, back in its place
with Fixed); `SceneTreeTests.WidgetPageSheets`, its new scene `panel-529-calendar-fill-<dark|light>.png`.

By hand: arrange the bar › a folder's calendar line › its page: Size › Height Fill: no Max rows under it; Automatic: Max
rows back at what it was. The line's right-click menu: the same at its foot.

## 661. Windows search's files wear File Explorer's icons, the new widgets' items edge to edge, a person their picture (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10), on the installed build:

> 1. "in the search the file types should actually have the proper icon that they also have in the file explorer."
> 2. "the items in the widgets that were created newly dont go from edge to edge like the other widgets are designed to do."
> 3. "the contacts should show the profile picture in the search if possible / applicable."

### 1. The icons: the index's display path (the root cause), and one size for all

Measured first, read only, on this PC (`RealShellTests`, KARPO_REAL_SHELL=1): the shell's icon for a file (`Items.Icon`,
`IShellItemImageFactory` with `SIIGBF_ICONONLY`) is File Explorer's own — a program's, a shortcut's, a customised folder's —
but **220 of 2,444 files the index answered had no icon at all**. A hit's target was the index's `System.ItemPathDisplay`,
which is the path *as Explorer's address bar writes it*: a known folder by its display name ("C:\Users\Public\**Public
Documents**\…", a phone's "…\S24\**Internal storage**\…"). The shell cannot parse that back, so the icon read gave nothing
and the row wore its group's glyph — and opening it, Open file location and Copy as path were wrong for the same rows.

- **The path of a file of the index is its address's** (`WinSearchRank.PathOf`): `System.ItemUrl`'s "file:C:/Users/Public/
  Documents/x.ini" → "C:\Users\Public\Documents\x.ini" ("file://server/share" a UNC path, "file:///C:/" too); the display
  path only where the address is no file's. The target, the icon, the copy and the folder under the name are all it.
- **Read at the size it is drawn** (`TargetPictures.Sized`, was `Large`: one 64 px picture scaled down for a row and up for
  the pane): the cache is kept by target *and* size, each read at the shell's next size up (`TargetPictures.Bucket`: 16, 20,
  24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256), so a row's icon is the shell's 24-px image at 150 %, a tile's its 48, the pane's its 96
  — as Explorer picks its image by its view. Start's lines ask it the same way (`IStartSource.Icon(target, px, came)`). A
  kind's icon (a ghost's sample, `Items.KindIcon`) takes Windows' small, large or extra-large image list by the size too.
- **One way to wear it** (`WinSearchLine.Wear`): a row, a tile and the pane drew their icon each its own way; now one
  method, the icon's size what it is drawn at.

Rows stay icons, not thumbnails, as Explorer's Details and List views show them (its Medium icons and larger show
thumbnails); the pane's large icon is the icon too. Samples and ghosts keep their kinds' icons and read no file.

### 2. Edge to edge: Start (beta)'s lines and Windows search's tiles and pane

The kit's rule (§428, §436, §611, §632): an item lights a band of its line, square, from edge to edge, touching the next.
`LineHoverRuleTests.AnItemLightsItsLineToItsEdges` holds it over every kind — and failed **111 times** on the new ones,
which nobody had run it over since §641: Start's tiles, rows, recommended files and the account stood a gutter in, each on
a rounded 4-DIP plate (`StartLine.Plate`), and Windows search's Top apps and Pinned tiles 2 px into the list's gutter on
rounded plates, the pane's action rows 6 DIP in on rounded plates. Windows search's rows were already the kit's.

- **A grid is the kit's** (`LineItem.Grid`, new beside `Across` and `Down`): `count` tiles `across` a line's whole width,
  each row of them `LineItem.Across`, the cells as wide as each other, the rows touching; a short last row keeps the others'
  cells, as File Explorer's grid. A cell's words keep inside the gutters at the line's edges (`LineItem.Words`). Start's
  Pinned and All apps (Category, Grid), Recommended (two across) and Windows search's Top apps and Pinned all use it; the
  per-widget tile maths is gone.
- **Rows and the account are bands**: All apps' List rows `LineItem.Down` the line's width, the icon on the gutter; the
  account the band from the line's edge to the first folder button, top to foot, its picture on the gutter (and as large as
  its initials, `Text(32)`, so they stay inside it at any text size). Every item lights through `LineItem.Light`; only the
  folder and power **buttons** keep their own rounded plates, as controls do (`StartLine.Plate(button: true)`). A section's
  heading ("Productivity") stands on the gutter, not 4 DIP in.
- **The pane's actions** are bands of the pane's whole width inside its outline, touching.

The tests now hold the rest exactly: the overlay scrollbar a scrolling line shows under the pointer is no item's light
(masked by `ListScrolled.Thumb`); a heading anywhere across the rows over or under an item parts it from the next (a grid's
tiles under "Pinned", which stands only over the first); beside a grid's short row the room to the edge is whole empty
cells. `ListGutterTests` holds Start's account on the gutter (Icon) and its power button's box on the trailing one (Box).

### 3. A person's picture

The contacts line already keeps everyone's picture (`ContactPhotos`, fetched by `ContactStore` after each read — Graph's
`/contacts/{id}/photo`, CardDAV's PHOTO — on disk and in memory). Windows search now **reuses that cache and fetches
nothing**: a person's hit carries the address of their picture (`ContactPhotos.Address`, "contact-photo:" and the key the
cache keeps it under, a hash of the id and the picture's version); the line's one picture reader
(`WinSearchLine.Picture`) asks the store's memory for it (`ContactStore.Photo(address)`), and `Wear` draws it in a circle
(`PopupPaint.Covered`, as the contacts line's rows) — in the row, the best match and the pane. Without one, or until it
has come, the contacts' glyph, as the contacts line draws a person without a picture.

### Tests

New: `WinSearchRankTests.AFileOfTheIndexIsItsAddresssPathNotItsDisplayPath` (Public Documents, a phone's storage, a plain
path, UNC, "file:///", an empty address; red before), `TargetLooksTests.EachFilesIconIsReadAtTheSizeItIsDrawnAndKeptByTheFileAndTheSize`
(the buckets; 24 and 48 two reads, 22 and 24 one, a path's case aside, two programs two reads),
`LineHoverRuleTests.AGridsTilesSpanTheLineEdgeToEdgeAsWideAsEachOther`, UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1)
`WinSearchLineTests.APersonWearsTheirPictureTheContactsLineKeepsElseTheGlyph` (360 and 700 DIP, the row and the pane; a
person whose picture has not come and one with none the glyph), and opt-in on this PC (KARPO_REAL_SHELL=1, read only)
`RealShellTests.EveryFileWearsItsOwnIconAtTheSizeItIsDrawn` (notepad's and explorer's two pictures, neither the .exe kind's;
Documents not a plain folder's; 24 and 48 px; Public Documents' display path nothing, its address's an icon),
`RealShellTests.TheIndexsFilesAreTheirAddressesPaths`. Now passing for the new kinds:
`LineHoverRuleTests.AnItemLightsItsLineToItsEdges` (the one failure left, SoundVolume Medium's 3 px over its item, is older
than this and not of these lines), `ListGutterTests.EveryLineStandsOnTheGutter` for Start's and Windows search's lines
(the weather's hours' and days' graph ink in the gutter fails there before and after). Brought along: `WinSearchLineTests`,
`StartGroupTests`, the icon stand-ins' size. Pictures (KARPO_PNG_DIR): `winsearch5-real-<narrow|wide>-dark.png` (this PC's
files, opt-in), `winsearch5-person-dark.png` (new: a person's picture in the row, the best match and the pane; one
without the glyph), `start-group-hover-<dark|light>.png` (new: a tile, a file and the account lit), `winsearch3-*` (a Top
apps tile lit at home), `winsearch-line-<dark|light>.png` ("A person, their picture").

By hand: Windows search › type a word that finds files under Public Documents or a linked phone: each wears its own icon,
Open file location opens there. Start (beta) and the search's home: point at the first pinned tile — it lights to the
folder's edge; at a recommended file — half the line, edge to its middle. Search a person with a picture in the contacts
line: their picture in a circle.

## 662. Task Manager's button minimizes and restores it: an app run as administrator is asked as any other (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10):

> "there is a bug: right now when i click the task manager it actually does not maximize or minimize the window as it
> should. i think this has something to do with that the taskmanager is not pinned but in the apps widget. fix this."

**Not the apps widget.** A pinned app's button and an open app's that nothing pins (the apps widget's) are the same tile
and take the same click: `Dock.TileClicked` › `OpenApp` › `AppClicks.Decide` › `Apps.Activate` / `Apps.Minimize`, as do a
pin in a folder, a card, the keys and the window menus. Task Manager differs from the person's pinned apps in another way:
on an administrator's account Windows runs it **as administrator** (high integrity), and Karpo runs at medium.

**The root.** §362 (item 10) and §619 held that Windows (UIPI) drops every message Karpo posts to an app above it, so for
those apps Karpo never asked (`Apps.Above` read the integrity) and did it without asking instead: `ShowWindowAsync`
(`Surfaces.MinimizeOther`, `RestoreOther`). That was not verified against a real elevated window, and it is backwards.
Measured on this PC (Windows 11 26300, a throwaway probe; the rows Karpo stands on are held by `AboveKarpoTests`), a program at low integrity acting on a window at medium integrity, on a hidden
desktop of its own — UIPI is one rule for any lower level and any higher one (Microsoft's Windows Integrity Mechanism
design: a lower process may not send or post messages to a higher one's windows, nor otherwise drive them):

| From below | Result |
|---|---|
| `PostMessage` WM_SYSCOMMAND **SC_MINIMIZE**, **SC_RESTORE**, **SC_CLOSE** | reaches it, and it minimizes, restores (maximized again), closes |
| `PostMessage` WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_MAXIMIZE, WM_CLOSE, WM_USER+1 | refused: FALSE, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED |
| `ShowWindowAsync`, `ShowWindow` (minimize, restore), `SetWindowPlacement` | refused: FALSE, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, nothing happens |
| `CloseWindow`, `OpenIcon` | say TRUE, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, nothing happens |
| `SwitchToThisWindow` | restores it (Windows posts it SC_RESTORE itself) |
| `EndTask(hwnd, FALSE, FALSE)` | reaches it: Windows sends it WM_CLOSE itself (and waits on it) |
| `IsIconic`, `IsWindowVisible`, `GetWindowPlacement` | read as from anywhere |

The same calls from medium integrity (the control) all work. So Windows lets exactly the taskbar's system commands —
minimize, restore, close — through to an app above the caller, which is how Windows' own taskbar (medium integrity too)
minimizes and restores Task Manager; and it refuses exactly what Karpo did for such apps. A refused post says so
(`PostMessage`'s documentation: blocked by UIPI, the last error is 5, access denied), so nothing needs to guess the
integrity first.

**The fix: one path, the post's own answer.** `Apps.Command` asks every app the same way — WM_SYSCOMMAND posted — and
does it without asking (`ShowWindowAsync`) only where the app can't answer (hung, or the window disabled under its modal
dialog: `Apps.Asks(hung, disabled)`, §619) or where Windows refused the post (a maximize to an app above Karpo, a window
gone). `Apps.Close` posts WM_CLOSE and goes through `EndTask` only where Windows refuses that post, rather than where the
integrity said it would. `Apps.Above` and its token reads are gone. So Task Manager's button, a click, Win+N, a window
menu's Minimize and Restore, "Minimize all windows" and "Restore all windows" minimize and restore an app run as
administrator as they do any other; its close (the window menu's, the jump list's Close window) still goes through
`EndTask`, which reaches it from below too (measured above). Left as Windows has
it: a maximize from a window menu (SC_MAXIMIZE) does not reach an app above Karpo, and a hung or disabled one above it
can't be minimized or restored at all — Windows refuses both ways.

Tests: UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1), new `AboveKarpoTests` — a maximized window of the test's own, at medium integrity on a
hidden desktop labelled for low integrity, and this test assembly run as a program at low integrity on it
(`AboveWorker`, `--above-click`, which refuses to count unless it really runs at low integrity) making the click's own
calls: `AWindowAboveTheClickerMinimizesAndComesBackMaximized` (`Apps.Minimize`, `Apps.Restore`, twice; red before the
fix: "round 1: not minimized from below") and `FromBelowTheWindowIsReadButNotMovedWithoutAsking` (ShowWindowAsync refused
with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, the window read). `AppToggleTests.ACommandIsAskedOnlyOfAnAppThatCanAnswer` now without "above";
the rest of `AppToggleTests`, `AppClicksTests`, `AppButtonRulesTests` brought along.

By hand: open Task Manager (it runs as administrator) and click its button: it minimizes; again: it comes back, maximized
if it was, in front. Its button's Shift+right-click menu: Minimize and Restore work; Close closes it. Not checked here
against a real elevated window (the tests cannot elevate): that the window comes to the front after the restore
(`SetForegroundWindow`, which a hidden desktop has no foreground to test).

## 663. Lock the taskbar in the default menu again; a locked bar's widgets are not dragged (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10):

> "locking the taskbar should be shown in the default right click context menu again.
> when the taskbar is locked dragging a widget should not go into edit mode anymore / should not be possible anymore.
> but dragging contents inside of widgets around should still work normally."

**What there was.** The setting never went: §534's `lockTaskbar` (Config.LockTaskbar, `BarMoves`), every bar's alike, on
(locked) in a new config as Windows ships its taskbar, written by the bar's right click (`BarMenuAction.LockTaskbar`, ticked
while locked, `CMD_LOCK_TASKBAR` → `ToggleLock`) and the Taskbar page's switch under Bar. §534 had the row in the default
menu under "Edit"; §581 made the default Windows 11's (the layouts, Task Manager, Taskbar settings) and left the row out,
addable, because Windows 11's menu has none. What the lock locked was the bar's place and height at rest (§534: no carry to
another edge, no grip); a widget dragged at rest still turned edit mode on (2026-10-05, 2026-10-08), locked or not.

**The menu.** `BarMenus.Default` has the row again, where Windows 10's menu had it at its foot: the layouts, a rule, Task
Manager, a rule, **Lock the taskbar** (ticked while locked), **Taskbar settings** (`lock`, `rule-1`; the ids fixed as the
others). No string is new: `core.barMenu.lockTaskbar` is in all 40 languages since §534 ("Taskleiste fixieren", ...). It is
an entry as any other: it can be moved or taken out on the Taskbar page's Taskbar menu, and is offered under Add an entry
only while the menu has it not. Config: no new shape, nothing converted. A file without `barMenu` (the default) shows the
row from now on; a file with the person's own list keeps that list as it is (the default is never written, §532).

**The lock, one gate.** `BarMoves.Arranges(locked, editing)` (§534's `Grips`, renamed and widened): a drag arranges the bar —
its grip drags its height, a widget pressed on it or in its folder is carried — in edit mode always, at rest only where
the bar is not locked. Asked in the two places a press at rest can become a carried widget:

- the bar (`DockWindow.PinPressed`, Dock.Pins.cs): locked, a press on a widget, a face, a pin, a folder's face, the Apps
  widget keeps no `PinDrag`, so past the drag threshold nothing is carried, edit mode is not asked
  (`HandOverToEditMode`), and a release elsewhere is no click. The grip and the cursor over it ask the same gate
  (`Arranges`, was `Grips`).
- a folder open at rest (`FolderFlyout`, WM_MOUSEMOVE): locked (`FolderFlyout.Locked`, the dock's `config.LockTaskbar`),
  a line pressed and carried is neither handed to edit mode (`HandOver` / `ArrangeFromDrag`) nor dragged out of the
  folder (`Dragged` → DragMove/DragDrop); it stays a press, its release on the line a click.

What a widget drags itself is untouched, because it takes the press before the gate is asked: a slider's thumb (volume,
brightness; `SliderPressed` on the bar, `TakePointer`/`holding` in a folder), the tray's icons reordered or sent to the
overflow (`TakesDragItself`, `TrayPress`), a list's scroll (the wheel and the touchpad, `ScrollLine`). Files dropped on
the bar still pin or open, as Windows' locked taskbar still takes a pin. Edit mode is not locked: Taskbar settings (the
menu), Win+Alt+Enter, the folder footer's Edit, and Copy/Paste still open it, and in it every widget is dragged as ever.
The bar's edge-to-edge carry and its grip were locked already (§534), at rest only.

Since a new config is locked, a widget dragged at rest no longer turns edit mode on until the person unticks Lock the
taskbar; the default menu now shows the row that does.

**Tests.** `BarMenuModelTests.TheMenuIsTheLayoutsTaskManagerThenLockAndTaskbarSettings`,
`LockTheTaskbarIsInTheDefaultAndAddableOnceTakenOut`; `BarMovesTests.TheLockStopsMovingAndSizingAtRestOnly` (Arranges),
`TheMenusRowIsTickedWhileLocked` (the default's row, ticked and not, the rule before it); `BarMenuTests
.TheBarsMenuIsWindowsTaskManagerLockAndTaskbarSettings` (its command, glyph, tick). Brought along: `BarMenuLinesTests`,
`BarMenuRowsTests`, `BarMenuPanelTests`, `PanelReorderTests`, `DockMenusLanguageTests` (German). UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1):
`FolderDragEditTests.LockedALineDraggedAtRestStaysWhereItIs` (no edit mode, nothing dragged out; unlocked the same press
is edit mode's), `FolderSliderTests.LockedTheSliderStillFollowsTheDrag`, and on the real dock
`BarMoveTests.LockedAWidgetDraggedIsNoDragUntilTheMenuUnlocksTheBar` (locked: a folder's face dragged 300 px, no edit dim,
