## 665. Join that does nothing says why; nothing Karpo launches fails in silence (2026-11-10)

The person (2026-11-10), on the installed build:

> "when i click the join button on a meeting nothing happens. it should at least show an error message if something does
> not work. (i tried a teams meeting for example)"

### What was found

- **The link is there.** Read only, on this PC (the offline cache decrypted in memory, nothing printed but its shape): the
  meeting with a Join holds `https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/19%3ameeting_…%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b…%7d`, Graph's
  `onlineMeeting.joinUrl` whole (§616 dropped notes only; a Graph event's link was never taken from a body Karpo keeps).
  `MicrosoftReader.Event` and `MeetingLinks.AppUri` give the exact link and `msteams:/l/meetup-join/…`, escaped as it came.
- **The click reaches the Join.** The agenda's, the day's, the views' and the meetings' Join hand the meeting to
  `MeetingJoin` once the folder has gone (UI tests `EventOpenTests`, `JoinEverywhereTests`, passing).
- **The launch is where it died.** `msteams:` on this PC is the new Teams' — a packaged app (`MSTeams_8wekyb3d8bbwe`),
  its protocol's ProgID opened through a `DelegateExecute` handler (`{A56A841F-…}`, the shell's packaged-app activation),
  beside an older `"ms-teams.exe" "%1"` command. `Launch.Aside` called ShellExecuteEx on a thread of its own that **ended
  the moment the call returned**, without `SEE_MASK_NOASYNC` — the flag Microsoft's documentation asks of exactly such a
  caller, because the shell may finish an activation (DDE, a DelegateExecute) after it has returned. On a thread that has
  ended it never finishes; ShellExecuteEx had already said yes, so the fallback to the browser was never tried; and the
  failure, if any, went to `Console.Error`, which a windowed Karpo does not have. Nothing happened, and nothing was said.
  §557's Eject had the flag (its thread ends with the call too); the aside never did. Not verified by launching Teams here
  (no real URL is opened by an agent): the person tries a Teams meeting by hand.

### Now

- **The aside waits** (`Launch.Aside`): `SEE_MASK_NOASYNC`, and `SEE_MASK_FLAG_NO_UI` (`Launch.Shell.Mask(…, waits, quiet)`):
  the app's address, then the page (`Launch.Tried`), and what fails last is said by Karpo. A jump list task's fallback
  (`Launch.Packaged`) waits too.
- **Never silent, in one place** (`Launch.Go` → `Launch.Failed`): every launch that does not open is written to karpo.log
  (its kind, and only a web address's host, another's scheme or a path's name — never a whole address with a meeting's or a
  person's ids) and **said to the person** in Windows' task dialog with the error icon, owned by nothing and on a thread of
  its own (`TaskDialogs.Tell`, the dialog ⚙ › Back up and reset already says a failed export in) — "Couldn't open the
  meeting" for a Join (`dock.meeting.joinFailed`), else "Couldn't open {name}" (`dock.launch.failed`: "Couldn't open
  outlook.office365.com", "Couldn't open a.txt"), with Windows' own reason ("Application not found"). Not twice: where the
  shell shows its own message box (an Open, Run as administrator, a jump list's line, Properties, File Explorer) or a
  caller falls back itself (the Wi-Fi dialog's process → Wi-Fi settings), Karpo only writes it down; a launch the person
  cancelled (UAC's No, ERROR_CANCELLED) is no failure. A file's place, a store app taking files, an aside, an exception:
  Karpo says it. Why a dialog and not the edit bar's errors (§394): those are states that last and show in edit mode only; a
  failed click is said once, there and then, as a failed export is.
- **No link, no Join** (kept, not changed): a meeting with no link Karpo knows has no Join to press (`JoinButton.Of`), nor
  "Join meeting" in its menu, so there is no "no join link" to say. A Teams invitation from another organisation whose link
  is only in its body (Graph's `onlineMeeting` empty, `bodyPreview` text without the link) still has none; the body itself is
  not asked for.

Nothing kept changes: no cache or config shape.

### Tests

New, red first: `MeetingLinksTests.ATeamsMeetingFromGraphJoinsTeamsWithItsExactLink` (a Graph-shaped Teams event: its
`joinUrl` whole; the Join hands the launcher `msteams:` + the link's own text after its host, the link to fall back on, and
"Couldn't open the meeting"; without Teams the link alone), `LaunchTests.ALaunchThatFailsIsSaidToThePerson` (an aside, a
file's place said with the caller's or the launcher's words and Windows' reason; an Open the shell said written down only;
a cancel nothing; what opens nothing), `LaunchTests.AnAsideWaitsForTheShellAndLeavesTheTellingToKarpo` (NOASYNC and
NO_UI asked, neither by a plain Open), `LaunchTests.AnAsideTriesTheAppThenThePageThenSaysWhy`. Passing still:
`LaunchTests`, `MeetingLinksTests`, `DriveHoldsTests`, `MeetingTests`, the localization tests, and UI `EventOpenTests`,
`JoinEverywhereTests`.

By hand: a Teams meeting's Join — Teams opens the meeting (or, where it does not take it, the browser's Teams page); were
neither to open, a "Couldn't open the meeting" dialog says why.

## 664. A pick that acts in place never closes the folder under its menu (2026-11-10)

The person: *"when clicking refresh in the context menu it closed the panel, this should never happen"*.

**Where it was.** What a pick does to the folder its menu stood over was decided twice. The pick itself said (§185,
`HandsAway`: what leaves Karpo closes it at rest, what acts in place does not) — Refresh rightly in place since §451. But
once the menu had gone, `FolderMenuEnded` closed the folder anyway wherever **the folder was not the window in front at
that moment** (`GetForegroundWindow() != folder`), standing in for "something else took the focus while the menu held
it". That stand-in is wrong whenever the folder is not in front for any other reason — the menu still going or never
handing the focus back, none in front a moment, a window of Karpo's own — and then every pick, Refresh, Escape too,
closed the folder. Held on the real dock (Karpo.exe --stage, where no window of the dock's is ever in front): Refresh and
Escape in a feed line's menu at rest closed the folder each time (red: *"Escape on a line's menu closed the folder"*,
*"picking Refresh in a line's menu closed the folder"*). And `HandsAway` listed what stays and called everything else
leaving, so an act added later that acts in place would have closed the folder until someone noticed.

**One rule.** The folder at rest closes after its menu for two things only: the pick left Karpo (`HandsAway`), or **another
program** has the foreground as the menu ends (`Dock.ForegroundTakenFromKarpo`: a window of another process; none in
front, the folder, the menu or any window of Karpo's is not the focus taken). Arranged it stays through everything, as
before. `HandsAway` now lists what leaves — an app, a file, a place or a page opened; Windows' own windows and panels
(Properties, Settings' pages, troubleshooters, Task view, clipboard history, casting, ending a task); Karpo's settings
taking the folder over (Edit folder, Manage accounts, the layouts' settings) — and everything else acts in place.

**Every act, said once** (`WidgetMenuTests.EveryActIsClassifiedAsLeavingOrInPlace`, which replaces
`OnlyWhatOpensSomethingHandsTheScreenAway`): leaving — OpenPlayer, OpenDrive, CalendarApp, ClockApp, OpenApp, Start,
RunAsAdministrator, OpenFileLocation, FileExplorer, OpenInExplorer, OpenWebsite, OpenForecast, OpenMap, ContactEmail,
ContactCall, JoinMeeting, ResourceMonitor, TaskManager, OpenVolumeMixer, OpenSnippingTool, GetSnippingTool, SnipIn3,
SnipIn10, RecordScreen, DriveProperties, FileProperties, WindowsSettings, DateTimeSettings, NotificationSettings,
SoundSettings, TroubleshootSound, DiagnoseNetwork, NetworkSettings, PowerSettings, HotspotSettings, AutoPlaySettings,
WindowsUpdate, StorageSettings, TaskView, NewDesktop, ClipboardHistory, CastConnect, EndTask, EditFolder, ManageAccounts,
LayoutSettings; in place — Refresh, PlayPause, Previous, Next, SeekBack, SeekForward, FollowSession, Shuffle, Repeat,
Mute, MuteMicrophone, ChooseDevice, MuteApp, EnergySaver, DoNotDisturb, WifiRadio, BluetoothRadio, PowerMode, AwakeFor,
StartPause, Stop, Longer, Shorter, Lap, Reset, ClearAll, ClearCompleted, Eject, Disconnect, StartEdit, ContactCopy,
CopyAsPath, CopyLink. A new act fails the test until it is put in one list; the dock's rule is asked for each, the focus
taken or not. The rows every widget has (Cut, Copy, Remove, Close window, End task, Add) and the settings set in a menu
stay in place as before (`PickHandsAway`). Every act is classified as it was: only the default and the focus's stand-in
changed.

**The bar's own widgets.** A right click on a bar closes what is open first (light dismiss, §366), so no folder or flyout
stands behind a bar widget's menu; its picks go through the same `RunAct` and `HandsAway`, and what leaves Karpo goes
through the one launcher (§491).

**The stage** maps a folder's lines at rest (`FolderLine`) and the open menu's rows (`MenuRow`, by id and words) for a test
to right-click a line and pick a row (Dock.Stage.cs).

Tests (red first): UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `MenuPickInPlaceTests.RefreshFromALinesMenuLeavesTheFolderOpen` — the real dock
at rest, a folder of a clock and a feed line whose address is the test's own loopback listener (it hangs up on every read:
nothing leaves the PC): its menu closed by Escape, the folder open; "Refresh" clicked as the mouse clicks it, the menu
gone, the folder open, the feed read again; `MenuPickInPlaceTests.OnlyAnotherProgramInFrontIsTheFocusTaken` (none and one
of this process's windows: not taken; Windows' desktop window: taken); `WidgetMenuTests.EveryActIsClassifiedAsLeavingOrInPlace`.
Brought along green: `FolderMenuTests`, `WidgetMenuTests`, `MenuKeepsTests`, `FaceMenuTests`, `TaskViewTests`,
`HotspotPresetTests`, `RssRegistryTests`, `FeedRulesTests`, `FolderBackdropTests`, `MenuToggleTests`,
`ArrangedFolderStandsTests` (stands, press on the bar, Done at rest).

By hand: open a folder with a weather, news or mail line; right-click the line, pick Refresh — the folder stays open and
the line updates when the read lands; again with Escape and with a switch (Mute on a sound line). Pick "Open website": the
folder closes as the page opens. Open a line's menu and press the Windows key: Start comes up and the folder goes.

## 666. Windows' Start in one place, by one function: hung from Karpo's Start button, measured from its host (2026-11-12)

The person (2026-11-10): *"the native start menu is still placed at wrong locations. fix this once and for all and also
thorouhgly test this"*.

**Replaces** the rules for Start of §580 (moved along by a side bar's strip, `Wide`), §591 (down to the work area's end,
`Drop`, `OnStart`, the hidden taskbar's thickness, `TaskbarThickness`), §601 (hung from the button, `StartShift`, `Hung`,
the per-display box cache) and §640 (Windows' gap off the box's far sides). §580's `Clear` for every other panel, §600 and
§591's taskbar waiting at the bottom stay.

**History.** §580 moved Start's host right of a bar at the left (*"when the taskbar is on the side the start menu overlaps
it"*); §591 moved it down by the hidden taskbar (*"the start menu is also too high up as if there was an invisible taskbar
at the bottom"*); §601 hung it from Karpo's button (*"is it possible to move the start to the start button on karpo?"*);
§640 took a gap off (*"the start appears too high now"*). Each rule corrected the one before from one more reading of
where Windows had put Start's windows, each anchored to the display and Explorer's hidden taskbar, with special cases
(no step under half a taskbar; a host the size of the display; Search's own host) — and each was right for the scene it
was read on and wrong for the next.

**Root causes** (from appbar.log, 2026-11-10/11, read-only; Windhawk's *Taskbar on top* mod, read; nothing opened):

1. **Start's windows were modelled wrong.** §591/§640 took Start's search box (SearchHost's window over Start) to reach
   from Start's top to the screen's end and from the display's left to Start's right. It is Start's frame: Start plus
   Windows' 12 DIP gap all round. appbar.log heard the same 1287x1335 box in two places as Start opened: first against the
   screen's end (*"Windows' Search 0,825..1287,2160"*, 11:26:43.838, 15:55:41.843, 20:16:06.329) and then, settled, against
   the host's end (*"0,753..1287,2088"* under the host 0,0..3840,2088; 11:26:47.191, 11:27:55.283, 16:51:48.129), 72 px apart
   — so its foot is not the screen's, and only its size says anything. Its search field stands centred in it (68 px in from
   its left, 67 from its right at 150 %, read by the pass before this one, not read again). The mod lays the redesigned
   Start's `FrameRoot` out at its host's foot with Windows' margin and moves SearchHost's window only to the work area's top:
   the box goes with Start, as its frame. So Start is 1251x1299 at 150 %, not 1269x1245: hung beside the user's right bar
   to 2472,-807, it stood with its top **36 px above the screen**, its search box 54 px under its own search field, and 36
   px off the bar instead of 18.
2. **Two moves as Start opened.** The box's size was kept per display in memory, lost at every Karpo start; until the box
   showed (4 ms after the host) §580/§591 placed the host, so Start was first sent to the bottom and then hung: *"Windows'
   Start 2472,-807..6312,1281 moved off the bars to 0,72"* then *"0,72..3840,2160 moved for Karpo's Start button to
   2472,-807"* (09:06:38.321/.325, 16:30:21.222/.226, 20:16:06.319/.323, 20:42:22.268/.272, 15:55:41.840/.843). It also
   shows Windows reopening the host where Karpo left it, which a rule anchored to the display sent back to the bottom first.
3. **Quick reopenings ran out of moves.** Twelve moves per window in ten seconds, up to three an opening plus the box's:
   the fifth opening in ten seconds stood where Windows put it.
4. **Stale displays.** The displays Start was kept on were the last arrange's; after a display change before the next
   arrange they were the old ones.

**Can Windows place it right itself?** No, on this Windows. Windows places Start by Explorer's taskbar (the shell's
`TaskbarLayout` channel, §580), which waits at the bottom auto-hidden while Karpo runs because it auto-hides only there
(§591); Start's alignment inside its host is XAML inside StartMenuExperienceHost, reachable only by injecting into it
(the mods' way), which Karpo does not do. So the host is still moved from outside — now by one rule, once.

**Now** (`StartPlacement`, Karpo.Dock\StartPlacement.cs, pure; `ShellPopups.PlaceStart`):

- **Start's size** is its box's less the gap all round (`SizeOfBox`), kept in DIPs from the last box (`StartSize`) for the
  few ms between the host showing and the box showing; before the first box after Karpo starts, nothing moves (Start shows
  where Windows put it until the box comes, 4 ms later, and places both).
- **Where Windows lays Start out in its host** (`InHost`): its frame at the host's foot, at its left (`TaskbarAl` 0) or in
  its middle (1), Start the gap in.
- **Where Start belongs** (`Target`): against the inner side of the bar whose Start button opened it (the one pressed, else
  for the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc the display's main bar's, `Dock.StartButtonOn` as §601), Windows' gap from it (12 DIP,
  `Gap`: 12, 15, 18, 21, 24 px at 100–200 %), centred on the button along the bar, inside the room — the work area less the
  gap all round (`Room`). Windows 11's two looks come from where the button stands: at the bar's start Start stands at that
  end the gap from the screen's end (its left-aligned Start), in the bar's middle in the middle (its centred one). With no
  Start button on the display: where Windows stands it over a taskbar at the work area's end, at its left or in its middle.
- **The host** goes by exactly target − `InHost(host as it stands)` (`Host`): measured from the host where it is, whoever
  put it there, so it moves once however often it is heard, and nothing about Explorer's hidden taskbar, the box's place
  or an earlier opening is read. Never so far that the host stands as much on another display as on its own (Windows would
  take Start to be there, `Keeps`): then as far as it may along the bar, against the bar, else the nearest it may get —
  never outside the room. **The box** goes where Start then stands, less the gap (`Box`). Both moves asynchronous and
  counted as before (`ShellPopupMoves`), the count now from each showing.
- **Heard**: Start's host shown, uncloaked or moved — placed with the box showing over it, or by the kept size; the box
  shown, moved or resized (Start's All view grows it) — host and box placed again by its size, so Start keeps its top
  under a bar at the top as it grows up from the host's foot. Displays and DPIs read as each placement happens
  (`EnumDisplayMonitors`, `GetDpiForMonitor`), never the last arrange's.
- appbar.log: *"Windows' Start … moved for Karpo's Start button to x,y"*, or *"… where Windows stands it over a taskbar at
  the work area's end"*.

For the user (150 %, the bar at the right of the main display, Start its first button): host 2490,-753, box 2490,0, Start
2508,18..3759,1317 — 18 px under the screen's top and 18 px left of the bar; on the other display (bar at its left)
host -3777,-753, Start -3759,18.

**Deleted**: `ShellPopupPlace.For`, `Wide`, `OnStart`, `Hung`, `StartShift`, `Settle`, `Drop`, `TaskbarThickness`,
`StartHang`, `StartGap`, `ShellPopups.boxes`, `TaskbarRects`, the Dock's displays list for it. No config change.

**Tests.** `StartPlacementTests`: the user's scenes as appbar.log heard them (beside the right bar, the other display's
left bar, from where the build before left the host, heard again: nothing); no Start button (§591's case, a bottom bar,
centred); a table — each edge (top, bottom, left, right), the button at the bar's start, middle and end, both of Windows'
alignments, 100, 125, 150, 175 and 200 %, the other display at negative coordinates, a display above at another DPI, a
display beyond the bar (the host held back, Start still at the top, off the bar), a dock floating over the desktop; Windows'
gap at each DPI; Start's size from its box and kept in DIPs; Start growing; reopened from five places the host was left
in; a display changed. Properties over 20 000 drawn scenes (one to three displays in any arrangement, negative
coordinates, mixed DPI, any edge, taskbar or dock, any button, either alignment, any Start that fits, the host anywhere on
its display): Start inside the room (never off its display, never over a reserved strip), never over the bar, the host
kept on its display, the box round Start, placing again moves nothing, Windows' gap to the bar ±1 px and centred on the
button wherever nothing holds it back. `ShellPopupsTests`: the other panels' `Clear` as before;
`StartOpenedQuicklyAgainAndAgainIsPlacedEachTime`. UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `StartPlacementUiTests`: windows of the test's own
on a hidden desktop moved by `ShellPopups.PlaceStart` as Windows' Start's would be — nothing before the box, both once as
it shows, nothing heard again, the host again as Start grows.

**Live** (`Karpo.Resilience`, scenario `start-placement`, by name only — never in `run all`; docs/resilience.md §3): with
Karpo running, it opens Start through each bar's Start button by UI Automation's Invoke (the button's own click; no
pointer moved, no key sent), then three quick reopenings, and with `--keys` by the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc (real
keystrokes); watches Start's host and box every 15 ms until still for 700 ms; reports every place heard before that,
Start's rectangle against `StartPlacement`'s with pixel deltas, the gap to the bar, the display, UI Automation's own
rectangle of Start's panel beside it, and a picture (artifacts\resilience\start-placement\*.bmp); closes Start the way it
opened it. It sets nothing and writes nothing but the report and the pictures.

```powershell
dotnet build Karpo.Resilience -c Release
$h = "Karpo.Resilience\bin\Release\net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0\win-x64\Karpo.Resilience.exe"
& $h run start-placement           # Karpo's Start buttons, every display, and quick reopenings
& $h run start-placement --keys    # and the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc
```

**Not known, not done.** Start's own rectangle inside its host has still not been read while Start was open (nothing here
opens it): the box as Start's frame stands on the two box places in appbar.log, the centred search field and the mod's
source — `start-placement` checks it at its first run (*"§666's model of Start's windows does not hold here"* where the box
is not round Start as Windows lays it out), and UI Automation's panel beside. Start's opening animation is still the
bottom edge's; on the first opening after Karpo starts Start is seen where Windows put it for the 4 ms until its box
shows. Search on its own (Win+S) is placed by `Clear`, not hung from Karpo's Search button.

By hand (appbar.log open): press Karpo's Start button on each display — Start opens beside, under or above the bar, a gap
as wide as Windows' at the screen's top; its search box on Start's own search field; one appbar.log line for the host and
one for the box, no *"moved off the bars"* line for Start before them. Open and close it five times quickly: each in the
same place. Open All: Start grows and stays under a top bar. The Windows key and Ctrl+Esc: Start hung from the
main bar of whichever display Windows opens it on.

## 668. A pin is never lost: its answer from the shell is asked again, its windows held by what it names (2026-11-12)

The person (2026-11-12): *"sometimes the pins are lost, for example the claude one is lost right now. can we fix this?"*

**What was found** (read only: config.json and its 55 backups and kept copies from 2026-10-16 to 2026-11-12, karpo.log,
appbar.log, the AppX deployment log, the installed package, the bars' pixels; nothing opened or changed):

- **The file never lost a pin.** Every backup holds Claude's pin, `shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`, on the
  default layout's start section between Bitwarden and WhatsApp, as widget `1b8fb195` in every one since 2026-11-09 (and in
  the second layout as `4907c76e`). No load, repair, merge or save drops a pin by its target: `Config.Repair` removes only
  kinds this build doesn't know. The loss was the bar's, not the file's.
- **Claude's app is packaged (MSIX), pinned by its app id** — already the most stable identity there is; its windows carry
  the same id (`GetAppIDForWindow` = `Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`), and resolved now the pin is whole: installed, named
  "Claude", key `aumid:claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!claude`, a 32 px icon. It is not a Squirrel app whose program moves on update.
  Windows updated it on 2026-11-11 11:30–11:41 (5.1231.0.0 → 5.1231.2.0, deferred while it ran, then re-registered).
- **A restart brought it back**: the dock started at 2026-11-12 00:39:40; at 00:44 both bars drew Claude's pin, lit, in
  its place.

**Root cause: the dock kept the shell's first answer for a pin for as long as it ran.** `PinItems` resolved a pin once
and kept the answer; a *broken* one (the shell had no item, or `PinTargets.Check` didn't find the package) was forgotten
only by `Keep`, which runs on a settings change. `PinItems.ForgetBroken`, documented as run "when a drive comes", had no
caller. So an answer taken at a moment the shell had none — the Apps folder at a logon, a package while Windows
re-registers it, a drive still coming — stood until the next restart: the pin drawn dimmed with its first letter and a
warning, and, because a broken answer held no identity (`Keys = []`), its app's windows shown among the open apps as if
nothing pinned it. Two more kept the same moment: the bar's pictures (`Icons`) were kept by target alone, so even a pin
that healed kept its broken letter (`Item.PictureKey`, made to tell them apart, was used nowhere); and a whole answer
whose app-id property the shell failed to read once held no app id for the dock's life. The exact moment Claude's pin
went wrong in the dock that ran from 2026-11-11 15:14 is not in any log (nothing logged pins); the update above fell in an
earlier dock's life.

**Now:**

- `PinCache` (Karpo.Dock\PinItems.cs, the dock's one `PinItems.Shared`): a whole answer is kept; a broken one for
  `RetryMs` (5 s), then the next build asks the shell again. `Keep` still forgets the broken at once on a settings change.
  `ForgetBroken` is gone.
- `Items.TargetKeys`: what a target names by itself — an Apps folder target its app id, a program its path. A broken pin
  holds its app's windows by it, and `Item.Resolve` starts from it, so no failed property read costs a pin its app id.
  Matching stays app id first (`Win.Keys`: the window's app id, then its program), so an Electron/Squirrel app pinned by its
  id (`com.squirrel.<app>.<app>`, how `PinApp` pins an app Start has) holds its windows from `app-0.14.10\` and
  `app-0.15.0\` alike.
- `Icons.KeyOf`: a surface is kept by target, `PictureKey` (own picture, broken or whole) and size.
- Pins are still never removed but by the person; no shape change (`Config.Shape` unchanged, nothing to convert).

**Not done, noted.** A pin to a program's path inside a versioned folder (a Squirrel app's `app-1.2.3\claude.exe`, pinned
by dragging the file) still breaks when an update deletes that folder; it shows broken with Locate…, as any moved file.
Pins Karpo makes itself from an open app use its Apps folder id where Start has one, and Windows' own taskbar pins are the
apps' shortcuts, so neither stores such a path.

### Tests

New: `PinIdentityTests` — `APinTheShellCouldNotAnswerYetIsAskedAgainAndHeals` (broken at 0, not asked again before
`RetryMs`, whole at `RetryMs`, never asked again after), `AnAppPinTheShellCannotFindStillHoldsItsWindowsByItsAppId`,
`AnElectronAppsPinHoldsItsWindowsAcrossAnUpdate`, `ATargetNamesItsOwnIdentity`, `ABrokenPinsPictureIsKeptApartFromTheWholeOnes`;
`LoadSaveTests.PinsThisPCCannotOpenSurviveALoadAndASave` (a program in a versioned folder gone, a package not installed, a
drive not there: loaded, saved and loaded again unchanged). `PinCacheTests` forgets through `Keep`.

## 669. A note's lists hang their words: one indent for every block (2026-11-12)

The person: *"in the notes widget the bullet point lists should properly indent the text too. same for the task list.
make sure that the markdown components are layouted nicely, also for the other ones"*.

**Root cause.** Since §321 a note's row was one wrapping DirectWrite layout of the whole line, marks and words, starting at
the note's edge; DirectWrite has no hanging indent, so a wrapped item's second line started under its `-`, its `[ ]`, its
number or its `>`, and nesting was only the width of the item's own two spaces.

**Now** (`NoteLayout`, one mechanism for every block kind; no config, no note format change):

- **A row is two layouts** (`NoteLayout.Part`): its **lead**, the marks before its words (a quote's `>`s, a list's
  indent, marker and box, a heading's `#`s; `NoteLayout.LeadLength`) on one line, and its **body**, the words, wrapping
  in the column the lead ends at. Every wrapped line of a bullet, task, number, quote, quoted item or heading starts
  under its words. A paragraph's line indented two spaces or more under a list's item goes on in that item's column
  (a lazy line at the edge stays at the edge; a paragraph never stands in otherwise).
- **The marks stay text** (§321 holds: every character shows and is a place for the caret), placed by spacing between
  characters (`IDWriteTextLayout1.SetCharacterSpacing`, the room after the character before a mark, so a caret before
  a mark stands at it), never drawn elsewhere: a quote's `>` 10 DIP after its bar, a quote's words a step in per quote
  (`QuoteStep`, the bar's room and a `> `); a list's marker at its parent item's words; a bullet or a box at its
  column's start, its words at least 18 DIP on (`Slot`, so a bullet's and a number's words line up); a **number
  right-aligned** to the widest of its list (the items of its depth and quote up to a line that is not the list's, blank
  lines and indented lines kept), so `9.` and `10.` end together and their words stand in one column.
- **Quotes** have a bar (3 DIP, the strong stroke, rounded) per level down the quote's rows, the `>`s faint after it,
  the words in the secondary ink as before. **Rules** draw a divider line from their faint `---` to the note's edge.
  **Inline code** has room either side of its words (3/14 of the text size) for its plate, so the plate no longer runs
  into its faint backticks. **Headings** have 10 DIP above a first or second level, 6 above the rest (not at the note's
  top), and 2 under. Code blocks as before: Consolas on a plate, 8 DIP in, wrapping inside it.
- **The editor** goes through both layouts: the caret, a click (left of the words on their first line: the lead), a
  task's box (in its lead), a link (in its words), Home and End (the first wrapped line holds the lead), Up and Down,
  the selection and its sliver. The lead and the words share the first baseline whatever their fonts.
- Not done, on purpose: bullet glyphs per level, drawn check boxes and drawn numbers (§321: the marks are the text);
  tables and images are still read as their text (Markdown.cs reads neither).

**Also fixed.** The to-do's ticked check box (`NoteLayout.CheckBox`) had drawn no check mark since 2a3e333d2 (§87's
rewrite): its glyph was an empty string. It is `` again, written as an escape.

**Tests** (UI, `KARPO_UI_TESTS=1`): `NoteLayoutTests` — `AWrappedLineGoesOnUnderItsWords` (bullet, `*`, open and ticked
task, `1.`, `10)`, quote, quoted bullet and number, `#`, `###`, nested quote: words after the marks, every wrapped
line and Home at the words' column), `AParagraphNeverStandsIn`, `ANestedMarkerStandsAtItsParentsWords` (bullets,
tasks, a bullet under a number, a line going on with a number), `ANumberedListsMarkersEndTogether` (8. to 11. end and
start their words together, 9. further in than 10., a list after a paragraph as wide as its own numbers),
`AQuoteAndCodeStandIn` (quote step, bar room, nested quote, a rule in a quote, code and its wrapped line 8 in),
`EveryPlaceIsFoundWhereItsCaretIs` (every place of the showcase note at 160 and 420 px, 100 % and 225 %: its caret
clicked is the place again; Home and End stay on its row), `ATickedBoxHasItsCheckMark`; `NotebookLinesTests` (all 18,
unchanged, pass). Pictures (`KARPO_PNG_DIR`): `notes-showcase-<dark|light>.png` (`TheNotesShowcaseIsPictured`, the
`Showcase` note: narrow and wide, 100 % and 225 % text), and `notes-marks-*`, `notes-note-*`, `notes-todo-*` as before.

By hand: in a note, type a bullet, a task and a numbered item long enough to wrap in a narrow folder: the second line
starts under the words; Tab a child under each: its marker stands under its parent's words; number past 9: the dots
line up; a quote shows its bar; click anywhere in the marks and the words, arrow and Home/End through a wrapped item.

## 667. Windows minimize into their button on Karpo's bar, wherever the bar is (2026-11-12)

The person (2026-11-12): *"the windows dont minimize or maximize to the correct location when the taskbar is shown on the
side for example, they still minimize and maximize to the bottom"*.

**How Windows asks** (measured on this Windows, 26300, 2026-11-12: a probe of our own registering two shell hook windows
on the shown desktop and minimizing and restoring a window of its own with SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE / SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE —
nothing of the person's touched):

- As a window is minimized or restored, Windows sends **`WM_KLUDGEMINRECT` (0x8B)** — wParam the window, lParam a RECT —
  to **every** shell hook window of the desktop (`RegisterShellHookWindow`), one after another **in the order they were
  registered**, waiting about **100 ms** for each (a window answering after 400 ms was passed over; the next one was asked
  ~100 ms after the slow one).
- `DefWindowProc` turns it into the documented question: the registered `SHELLHOOK` message with **`HSHELL_GETMINRECT`**
  (5), lParam a `SHELLHOOKINFO` whose rectangle is **four SHORTs** packed into the first 8 bytes (left, top, right,
  bottom), not the RECT of winuser.h. What the window writes there goes back into the RECT (DefWindowProc returns 0 even
  then).
- The **same RECT goes on** to the next window: the second window saw the first one's answer coming in. So **the last
  window registered that answers decides**; there is no "first TRUE wins".
- Registering a window that is registered already returns FALSE and **moves nothing**; deregistering and registering
  again puts it **last**.
- Coordinates are screen px — physical: what came in to the probe (DPI unaware) was Explorer's
  **479,2158..480,2230**, its hidden taskbar's insertion point *below* the 3840x2160 main display (§465, §591). That is
  the bug, seen.
- `WM_KLUDGEMINRECT` sent by an app (a test) to another process's window is marshalled as Windows' own is: the RECT goes
  in and comes back.
- On a desktop that is not the one shown, nothing is asked as a window minimizes (no shell hook message arrives there at
  all), so the tests ask as Windows asks.

**Sources.** Microsoft: `RegisterShellHookWindow` ("not intended for general use"; the window gets the registered
`SHELLHOOK` message) and the `ShellProc`/`HSHELL_GETMINRECT` entry ("a pointer to a RECT" in the old docs, `SHELLHOOKINFO`
in the newer) — learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-registershellhookwindow,
learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/ms644991(v=vs.85). **ManagedShell** (Cairo Shell's and
RetroBar's library; github.com/cairoshell/ManagedShell, `src/ManagedShell.WindowsTasks/TasksService.cs`, PR #123 "Fix
broken handling of HSHELL_GETMINRECT", merged 2025-01-31, fixing RetroBar issue #254 "Minimize animation does not redirect
to the correct TaskButton rects"): a shell hook window answers `HSHELL.GETMINRECT` with the button's rectangle as a
`ShortRect` of four `short`s in `SHELLHOOKINFO` and `msg.Result = 1`; RetroBar's `TaskButton.Window_GetButtonRect` gives
`PointToScreen` of the button (physical px), the primary display's button where several bars show it. ManagedShell also
calls `SetTaskmanWindow` and does nothing about the order. **ReactOS** (`win32ss/user/ntuser/desktop.c`,
`co_IntShellHookNotify`; `base/shell/explorer/taskswnd.cpp`): posts the shell hook messages to every registered window;
its Explorer leaves `HSHELL_GETMINRECT` unhandled. **Wine** (`dlls/user32/hook.c`): "HSHELL_GETMINRECT Not implemented".
A Stack Overflow answer (question 4998833) changes `lpShellHook->rc` and returns TRUE. None of them says what decides
between two shells; the probe above does.

**Alternatives looked at.** Nothing else sets where a window minimizes to: no `SetProp`, no `ITaskbarList` call (Karpo's
band sees all of them, Taskband.cs), no `DwmSetWindowAttribute` attribute, no `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` field;
`SetWindowPlacement`'s `ptMinPosition` is the iconic position the person never sees, and would be another app's window to
change. `SPI_SETMINIMIZEDMETRICS` (ManagedShell's `SetMinimizedMetrics`) hides minimized windows, which Windows 11 does
anyway. Moving Explorer's hidden taskbar is §600's no.

**Root cause.** Karpo's dock host is a shell hook window (for the window list) but never answered: `WM_KLUDGEMINRECT` went
to `DefWindowProc`, which asked the host again as `HSHELL_GETMINRECT`; busy, the host kept that for later (`Deferrable`),
else took it for one more change to its window list — either way the RECT went on as it came. Explorer's taskbar, waiting
hidden at the bottom, answered before it, with its own button at the bottom.

**Now.**

- **`MinRect`** (Karpo.Dock\MinRect.cs): a hidden window of its own, on a thread of its own (the dock's thread may be busy
  longer than Windows' 100 ms), on the dock's desktop, registered as a shell hook window after the host and Explorer.
  It answers `HSHELL_GETMINRECT` with where the window's button is (`Answer`: the four SHORTs, clamped, TRUE; no answer:
  FALSE, the rectangle as it came). When Explorer's taskbar is made again (TaskbarCreated) it deregisters and registers
  again (`Again`), so it is last once more. The dock host lets `WM_KLUDGEMINRECT` go by (returns 0), so DefWindowProc no
  longer asks it again. Started only by the person's own dock, or by a stage on a desktop of its own (never on the
  person's desktop from a test or --smoke); gone with the dock, leaving Explorer's answer.
- **`WindowButtons`** (Karpo.Dock\WindowButtons.cs): each bar publishes, as it is laid out and as its buttons' windows
  change (`DockWindow.PublishButtons`, from `Lay` and `DeriveTiles`; none for an anchor, none once it goes), its places
  in screen px through `Layout.OnScreen`: every app button with the windows it stands for (`Layout.ItemRect(Hit.Tile)`),
  a folder whose pins have windows open at its button (`BlockRect`; `TilesFor` keeps which windows each folder stands for),
  the buttons the bar had no room for at "…", its display and its panel. Replaced whole; MinRect's thread reads it without
  the dock. `For`: the window, else its first owner with a button (a dialog goes with its app, `WindowOwners.ButtonOf`);
  `Of`: the button on a bar of the window's own display (Windows' `MonitorFromWindow`, which for a minimized window is
  where it will be restored), else on another bar, the main display's first; where no bar shows it, the middle of its
  display's bar — a square as thick as the bar —, else the main one's. No bar: no answer.
- **`Layout.OnScreen`** is now the one conversion of a layout's px to the screen (DockWindow.OnScreen, PanelOnScreen,
  SectionsOnScreen and the tray's rectangles used four copies of it).

No config change.

**Tests.** `WindowButtonsTests`: the user's bar at the right (the button there, not the bottom), every window of a
combined button, two displays (the window's own display's bar, published in either order), its own bar without a button
for it (another bar's, main first), a folder, "…", the bar's middle (side and bottom, unknown display, no bar on the
display, no main bar), no bars (no answer), publishing per bar; the answer as Windows reads it (Explorer's rectangle
replaced, negative coordinates), none (left as it came), clamped to a SHORT. UI (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1) `MinRectUiTests`: the
hook on a hidden desktop asked as Windows asks (`WM_KLUDGEMINRECT` through DefWindowProc): no bars — Explorer's kept; the
button, a dialog's owner's button, the bar's middle; registered again, still the answer; its window gone with it. A real
layout at the right of 3840x2160 at 150 %: each button's place is its `ItemRect` on the screen down the bar, the folder's
its block, forty buttons on a short display — the rest at "…". The stage dock (Karpo.exe --stage on its own desktop): its
own `Karpo.MinRect` window answers, cross-process, with the middle of the bar along the made-up display's bottom (a stage
lists no windows, Apps.Probe, so no button there).

**Not known, not done.** The animation itself was not watched (nothing of the person's was minimized; a hidden desktop
gets no question). Karpo started at sign-in before Explorer's taskband registers would be answered over until Explorer's
TaskbarCreated makes it register again — not seen. A bar that auto-hides answers with where its buttons stand when shown.
A window Windows asks about before its bar has laid out its new button goes to the bar's middle once.

By hand: with the bar at the side, minimize a window from its title bar and restore it from its button — it shrinks into
its button on the side and grows out of it; on the other display likewise into that display's bar; a window of a pinned
app inside a folder into the folder; one Karpo shows no button for into the middle of the bar.

## 670. The Appearance page's pickers inline, as Windows 11's SettingsExpander (2026-11-12)

The person: *"i want the pickers to be inlined. so that the they dont show up as pickers that popoever but bascially as
expandable sections that have the picker inside. do this for all the settings in the appearance configuration section ...
design it leaned on win11 style."* (A first try, c68efe18e, was reverted: words drawn over the spectrum and the sliders,
"Hex" over its own box, "Pale…" cut short, the palettes' pictures lost, a list view's selection bar.)

**Now.** On the Appearance page every dropdown and colour button is a card that opens in place (`PanelRowKind.Picker`,
`SettingsPanel.Picker.cs`): its head the row's icon and name, what it is set to before its chevron — the colour's swatch or
the choice's picture, its words (a font's in its face), open or shut —, a value's reset before that; open, its picker on the
expander's content ground under a hairline, from the head's words' column (48 DIP) to the controls' end:

- **A choice** (Palette, Font): WinUI's RadioButtons, 36 DIP each — radio, the choice's picture, its words, a palette's
  "Changed" after them —, in up to three columns of at least 180 DIP where there are more than six, down the first column
  first. A font's search box across the column over them filters them as it is typed (Escape takes its words, nothing
  reaches the config); at most 18 shown, the one in force among them, "and N more" under them.
- **A font's weight** stands in its family's card, under its own name, a second radio group — no dropdown, no third level.
- **A colour**: Windows' colour grid — 36 DIP swatches, None first (slashed), lines shared out evenly, the one in force
  ringed in the text colour —, then the spectrum (96 DIP) and the hue and opacity on 12 DIP round tracks with a 20 DIP thumb;
  a press and a drag wear the colour (`EditDeckAction.Mix` → `Dock.PanelMixed` → the popup picker's own `MenuMixed`), let go
  it is kept, the pointer lost puts it back. The hex box a row of its own under the picker. Each colour worn rebuilds the
  page and its menu, so the dock tells the mix by its display and page (`Dock.SameMix`), not by its menu (the person,
  2026-11-12: "when dragging to change a color it immeadiately blows up the recent color list with it" — each move was
  taken for a new mix and the one before kept, a recent colour each); only the colour let go becomes a recent colour.
- **A pattern**: 72 DIP tiles of the card it would be drawn on, its name under each, the one in force ringed in the accent.

A screen reader hears each choice as a list item, selected where it is in force, and the spectrum and tracks as sliders
("Hue · Background"). Outside the Appearance page a dropdown still drops.

Tests: `InlinePickerTests` (UI: a head opens and shuts its card; a choice sends its own pick, which set changes the palette;
a drag on the hue track mixes and let go keeps; a font's search filters and Escape clears; every picker's cells inside its
card and apart at 580 and 360 DIP), pictures `InlineAppearanceSheets` (inline670-*.png, every picker open, dark and light).
The Appearance tests that held the popups (`AppearanceValuesTests`, `AppearanceModeTests`, `LookPreviewTests`,
`SettingsPanelTests.EachKindOfRowIsItsControl`, the palette and mode pictures) now hold the inline pickers.

widget still moves by its room and in edit mode.

## §681 Palette pictured on the page; app-button sketches full width (2026-11-12)

The person: "the palettes are not shown with previews anymore. why?". The gate (Dock.Pictures) turned Palette away: its
choices are each a swatch tile and there are more than eight (PicturedMost). The sheet drew pictures only because it handed
its own in. Palette and Mode are now always pictured; the gate is tested with the page's own choices
(ChoicePictureGateTests). And: "for the combine buttons previews they should be shown full width", "same for show windows
from": those two sketches take the picker's whole width, one to a line (LookPreview.FullWide).

## §682 Inline pickers: denser, scrolled, nothing left as a popup (2026-11-12)

The person's list:
- "positions setting should be all four positions in one row": Position's sketches 112 by 70, four to a line.
- "layout should just be a list of layout names": a display's layout its names alone (no sketch).
- "icon selector should show the icons way denser, without title. the preview does not work at the moment": the gallery a
  grid of 40 DIP squares of its glyph (PickerCellKind.Glyph), its search filtering them; its tiles had been drawn as
  colour swatches, their glyph never.
- "the color picker in the accounts should also be inlined somehow", "public holidays should also be moved to the inline
  dropdowns": a dropdown standing beside another's controls (a country's region, Add a country) and a button whose level is
  a picker (an account's calendar's colour, a holiday calendar's: PanelRow.Folded) unfold their picker's body under their
  line (PanelPickers.Inline, PanelLayout.Inside) — no popup.
- "language inline dropdown does not show the languages when opening, only when searching, show two columns as well": a
  lookup that needs no letters lists what it finds for nothing typed before its search answers (PanelFinds.Before), and
  the deck lays out again once a new lookup's search answers at once; its finds in two columns.
- "mail folders should actually be shown like a tree": each folder under its nearest listed parent, a step in
  (FlyoutItem.Indent, PanelMetrics.IndentStep), by its own name (MailTree).
- "animations should get previews as well ... same for the open on click, you could animate those too", "animations should
  go into appearance settings": Animations is the Appearance page's, after Palette; its choices a flyout coming up and going
  over a clicked folder at that speed (BarSketch.Motion, twice a flyout's own time so the speeds read apart), Open flyouts
  the pointer coming onto the folder and clicking or resting before it comes up — played over and over where Karpo moves.
- "generally the inline dropdowns without special contents should be two column ones": a plain list two columns down where
  two fit (three for a long one).
- "in the pallette selector you should show if the palette is changed from its default with a little icon": a pencil after
  a changed palette's name.
- "the inline color selector ... should be more in a column layout": swatches in the left half, the mixer beside them, where
  the body is 420 DIP or wider.
- "the inline selectors should be limited to a maximum height after which they have to scroll": a body at most 400 DIP
  (PickerMetrics.MostTall); past it its cells scroll inside it with the wheel (EditDeck.pickerScrolls), a thin bar at its
  right edge, the page under it never moving; a sample over a tile cut to its band.

The person: "dont make the moving out of a programm in the app widgets pin it to taskbar anymore. it should be like it was

## §684 Hover tries a choice on; every font listed; the taskbar menu's count (2026-11-12)

- "right now it is not possible to browse all the fonts anymore": a picker's list shows every choice (no 18 at most), the
  body scrolled to past its 400 DIP (§682).
- "when hovering over a font for example or color it should also apply it as preview again ... this should be a general

- "mail folders only shows the inbox": §683, the mail cache keeps every folder listed (MailCacheAccount.Listed), so Mail

## §685 An account's parts under their kind (2026-11-12)

The person: "for the accounts it should be more obivous / clearer what belongs to email, calendar, etc. right now everything
is just displayed in the same list". An expander's heading with a glyph of its own (an account's Calendars, Mail, Contacts,

under it to the next a step in (PanelLayout.Grouped). A heading without one stays left out, as before.

## §687 Google accounts (2026-11-12)

The person: "i want to integrate google oauth api into karpo as well. make a new project on google cloud for this and fill
in all the required information. use the company information. then also implement the sync on our side so that users can
login with google directly and give the application consent to access their data." A Google account is a kind of its own
(AccountKind.Google), signed in to in the browser and read through Google's APIs: Calendar, People, Gmail and Google Tasks,
the tasks read and written as To Do's are (docs\accounts.md, "Google").

- **One sign-in for both providers.** What Microsoft's sign-in did by hand — the authorization request with PKCE, the
  loopback port, the state, the code's exchange, the refresh writing a new refresh token back, the access tokens held per
  slot, Forget — is OAuthClient now, a provider its endpoints, client, scopes and what else it asks (OAuthProvider);
  MicrosoftAuth keeps its registration and To Do's token of its own, GoogleAuth its client, its secret (a Desktop client's,
  no secret) and a kind's token refused where its scope was not granted. Graph's request — the bearer, throttling waited
  out, the refusal in Karpo's words — is Rest, Graph and GoogleApi its pagers. The words are one family naming the provider
  (core.accounts.oauth.*).
- **Settings › Accounts** (and a widget's Accounts link): "Add a Google account" beside Microsoft's, "Gmail or Google
  Workspace: calendars, contacts, mail, tasks" under it, the globe its glyph; greyed with "no Google app registration"
  while GoogleAuth.ClientId is empty. A Google account has Sign in again as a Microsoft one has (AccountSignIn.AddAsync,
  SignInAgainAsync for any kind that signs in in the browser, Account.InBrowser).
- **Consent kind by kind.** Google's consent screen lets the person untick a kind: that kind alone waits —
  ConsentException (To Do's TasksConsentException, made general), SyncPart.Consent from every store, "Not synced: Karpo
  needs your permission for Gmail" under its heading with "Reconnect to sync mail" (calendars, contacts, tasks;
  OptionAccountGroup.Kind), the edit bar's errors the same — and the rest is read as ever.
- **Where things open**: an event its htmlLink, a day Google Calendar's day view, a message Gmail's search for its
  Message-ID — the Google CalDAV account's and Gmail IMAP's links, one each (CalendarLinks, MailLinks.Google).
- **The tasks** name their service: "deleted from Google Tasks", "Google Tasks won't list the task lists" (TodoSource.Service,
  TaskStore.Service).
- Not verified by Google yet: the consent screen is in Testing (test users only, refresh tokens for seven days); Gmail's
  read scope is restricted and needs a security assessment before a public release (docs\accounts.md, "Google").
- The client (same day): "Karpo for Windows", a Desktop client in project lometics-karpo of the new Lometics organization
  (lometics.com), its id and secret in GoogleAuth; so "Add a Google account" is offered from this build on. Its project,
  consent screen and who manages it: docs\accounts.md, "Google".

Tests: Accounts\GoogleAuthTests, GoogleReaderTests, GoogleTasksTests; AccountSyncRowsTests
(AGoogleKindNeverGrantedOffersAReconnectForThatKind), AccountRowsTests (AGoogleAccountGivesEverythingFromGoogle),
MailLinksTests, Calendars\EventOpenTests, Edit\FaultsTests, Pim\SyncChoiceStoreTests
(AKindNeverGrantedIsToldAsConsentNotAsAFailure); the accounts' pages list the Google add (AccountsPageTests,
OwnedLevelsTests, KarpoMenuTests).

## §688 A dock keeps the strip its size says (2026-11-12)

The person: "the taskbar and dock even though both are set to 42px size take up a different amount of space, the windows
move. this should not be the case". A floating dock's room is its size less the 8 DIP it floats over (Layout.LiftDip, taken out
of HeightOf and EffectiveHeight): its panel that much thinner, its icon the size's, the strip it keeps (Reserve, ReserveFor)
its size — a taskbar's of the same size — so turning one into the other moves no window.

## §689 The errors a settings page (2026-11-12)

The person: "the errors flyout should be styled the same as the other configuration pages". The edit bar's errors indicator
opens a page of the flyout (PanelPage.Errors), hung from it as a page from its entry, the indicator standing selected while
it is open — no popup list, no entry of its own on the bar. Each error a card: its icon, what failed, why its second line
(FlyoutItem.DetailUnder), since when and a chevron at its end (Dock.FaultItems); followed, what it is of opens (FaultChosen,
as the list's rows did). The popup (ShowFaults, EditDeckAction.Errors) is gone. Along the way: an inline picker's head opens
and shuts with F4, Alt+Down and Alt+Up as a dropdown's list did; Left and Right along the Appearance's tabs never step onto
the reset at their end (§673).

## §690 One set of presets, under a line of recent colours (2026-11-12)

The person: "the colors of the color picker on the side should be fixed, there should be one row that is filled with the most
recent color choices. but other than that the color pickers everywhere should have the same preset colors". Every colour
picker — the Appearance's in every tone and mode, a widget's and a folder's, an account's calendar's, a holiday calendar's —
offers the same twelve presets (ColorPalette.Presets: Windows' red, orange, gold, green, teal, blue; purple, pink, a brown,
grey, the dark and the light taskbar's grounds; named where they have a name, ColorPalette.NameOf), two lines of six. Over them
one line: None or Default where the colour may be unset, then the colours last mixed, as many as the line holds. The inline
picker lays each group from a line of its own (SettingsPanel.Picker.cs, Groups), the first line kept even with nothing in it,
so the presets always stand where they stand. The automatic colours an account's calendars are given are their own still
(PartColours.Palette).

## §691 A colour kept is built (2026-11-12)

The person: "the background color of the taskbar does not update after i clicked multiple colors. it gets hung up". Not
reproduced here. A colour kept (a pick, saved) no longer takes the in-place recolour (Recolour): the bars are built as for any
change; only a colour worn a moment — a mix dragged, a choice tried on under the pointer — is recoloured in place. After a kept
colour, every bar whose scene does not show the look it is to wear (DockWindow.ShowsItsLook, Scene.Shown) is written to
karpo.log ("Look: a bar … did not show the colours just kept") and built again.

## §694 The settings edit the Appearance in its own mode (2026-11-12)

The person: "the taskbar again does not care about the background value. it just shows as white". The dock told the settings
which mode to edit by the mode its taskbar reads in (Look.Dark after dressing), which a solid ground decides by its own
lightness: Midnight's taskbar made white in dark mode read light, so the page edited and wrote the light mode's values and
the dark mode's white — the one the bar wears — could no longer be changed from it. ReadsDark is now the Appearance's own
mode (Dock.ModeOf: its Mode, else Windows'), never the ground's.

## §695 A choice tried on changes no row (2026-11-12)

The person: "the reset button also appears when i am just hovering over a color value. this should obviously also not be".
While a choice is tried on, a page is made of the person's own config — its marks, its values, which values have a reset,
every row as it stands — and only its pictures of the whole look (a LookShown of the person's config: the Appearance's
preview, its tabs' look) show the config worn (TriedOnPreviews). §686's mending of marks row by row (AsChosen) is gone: a
row the worn config adds or takes away (a reset) it could not mend.

## §696 Colours recolour in place; slow changes timed (2026-11-12)

The person: "when changing the color it is very laggy ... it is laggy when changing other settings as well". Timed in karpo.log
("Slow: …", any change or chrome redraw past 50 ms, its steps): every step of a colour dragged or tried on built every bar again,
60 to 80 ms — Dock.OnlyColorsDiffer counted only the recent colours as colours, so no colour of the Appearance ever took the
in-place recolour (Scene.Recolour). It counts them now (every palette's backgrounds, outlines, texts, accents, backdrops,
grounds, and the opacity in them; not a pattern's colour), and a bar takes a colour in place where only its brushes change
(Dock.InPlace): a ground, a card, an outline another colour, each still there or not; never what its widgets draw themselves
(the text, the accent, the highlight) nor a pattern's ink, where it is built again. §691's building of every bar for a colour
kept is undone (what stuck was §694's); its check that every bar shows what was kept stays.

## §697 Only the open page made (2026-11-13)

Timed in karpo.log (§696): of a change's 60 to 150 ms, laying the bars out took about 15; the rest was the edit chrome, which
made the rows of every page of the edit bar — Karpo, Accounts, Layouts, Taskbar, Appearance, each with its pictures — at every
change, though only one page's flyout shows. Dock.PanelOf now makes the rows of the page whose flyout is open alone, every other
an entry; a page is made as its flyout opens (OpenPanel), as on every display but the one in use already. Nothing reads a
page that is not open (SettingsContent.Of: the open one; panelPages: what the open one picks).
While copies are tried on one after another (a colour's swatches hovered, a colour mixed), the open page is made of the
person's config once and kept (Dock.wornPages, keyed by that config, cleared as the copy comes off: Settle): the person's own
does not change under them, only its whole-look previews take each copy (TriedOnPreviews).

## §701 A drag or a morph never held over (2026-11-14)

The person: "when hover a pin it switches the tooltip between the pin and another pin really fast. i also cannot click the
topright area of the screen as it is blocked by something, when i click a pin it also immeadiately goes into edit mode ... it
also opens the application", "the window preview flickers as well". The right bar's window (652 px wide, its edge's most

The person: "the karpo taskbar sometimes clips infront of a fullscreen video for example, this happens when i go into edit

(WinUIDesktopWin32WindowClass) came to the front at 0,0..3840,2159)". Themia keeps its widget windows on the desktop, just

The owner: "dont show quit karpo". The Karpo page's General section loses its last row, Quit Karpo (§545 put it there; §409 to

swap's way). Its words (`settings.about.quit.header`, `.description`, `.button`) stay in every language: that row of the taskbar menu
says them. Autostart, the guard and the uninstall paths do not use the row.

`TheSettingsMenuIsTheSectionsUnderTheirHeadings`; `KarpoMenuGeneralTests.TheSettingsMenuHasTheGeneralSectionFirst`;
`SettingsPanelTests.TheKarpoPageHasNoQuitKarpo` (in place of §545's `QuitKarpoIsGeneralsLastButton`); `MenuRulesTests` R12 (no
Quit Karpo on the Karpo page, in place of "Quit General's last"); `KarpoMenuTests.QuitKarpoAsksThenTakesTheWayOut` and
`BarMenuRowsTests.QuitKarpoAsksFirstThenQuits` keep the row the taskbar menu uses.
## §704 Liquid glass, a palette that is a material (2026-11-15)

The owner: a "Liquid glass" look, Apple's Liquid Glass (iOS 26, macOS Tahoe), the style Themia draws (its SPEC [S-2123],
`Themia.Core\Widgets\LiquidGlass.cs`, `Themia.App\Shell\WidgetCard.Glass.cs`), placed after Glacier. It follows the Mode (§613)
like every palette, and it is a material, not colours alone. The same day: "update Karpo's Liquid glass to the new, modern
iOS 26 look that Themia now has": a clearer tint, a glow at the top edge in place of the sheen over the whole surface, a lens
of three bands inside the rim, the rim's light down the glass, a larger and fainter lift, 24 DIP corners, and a joined set one
glass shape parted by hairlines.

**The hook, one path.** A palette's design is a `LookPaints` in each mode; `LookPaints.Glass` (a `GlassLook`, null for colours
alone) is the material it is drawn in. Only Liquid glass's design has one (`LiquidGlass.Light`, `LiquidGlass.Dark`); it is
carried into what the palette draws (`LookPalette.Drawn`), never a value of the file's — the file names the palette (`liquidGlass`)
and keeps its values as any other's (§577). The dock reads it as `Look.Liquid` (none in high contrast) and `FlyoutTheme.Liquid`.

**Layers, bottom up** (`Karpo.Core\LiquidGlass.cs`, the values Themia's; every stop's offset runs down the whole glass shape):

| Layer | Light | Dark | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lift | #000, edge darkness .10, falling off as (1 − d/40)², 12 DIP down (`GlassLook.Lift`) | edge .24 | a floating bar's panels, which stand on the frosted wallpaper |
| Frost | the wallpaper blurred at 70 (`LookPalettes.GlassBlur`, Karpo's own blur, §547) | same | the bar and its cards |
| Tint | #FFFFFF, 6–70 % | #1C1C1E, 14–78 % | the bar, its cards, a folder's lines, the menus |
| Glow | white 22 DIP deep from the top edge: (0, .16), (.35, .05), (1, 0) | (0, .09), (.35, .03), (1, 0) | over the tint, under the content; no sheen over the rest |
| Lens | three 2-DIP bands from the rim in, weights .34/.18/.08, each times (0, .80), (.12, .40), (.5, .16), (.88, .34), (1, .66) | (0, .60), (.12, .26), (.5, .10), (.88, .22), (1, .46) | over the tint, under the content |
| Content | | | |
| Dividers | 1-DIP hairline #000 at .10, 14 DIP short of the glass's outer edge | #FFF at .12 | between the parts of a joined glass |
| Rim | 1 DIP, white down the glass: (0, .92), (.06, .58), (.3, .16), (.55, .08), (.9, .24), (1, .62) | (0, .56), (.06, .34), (.3, .10), (.55, .05), (.9, .13), (1, .36) | over the content |

Corners 24 DIP (a card's never more than half of it across, a floating panel's likewise; `Layout.GlassCorner`,
`FlyoutTheme.CornerDip`, a folder's pieces `FolderPlan.Radius`). The text Windows' own of the mode (#1A1A1A, #FFFFFF); the accent
the system's (`Look.Wearing` keeps Windows' accent and its shades where every other palette wears Karpo's blue, §547); every
flyout outlined white 30 % / 20 %. No outline of its own on the bar or its cards: the rim is the material's.

**The tint follows what is behind** (`GlassLook.TintOpacity`, pure, `LiquidGlassTests`): the least alpha, from the mode's least,
at which the text reads 4.5:1 on the glass — tint and backdrop mixed in sRGB (`bg = back + (tint − back)·α`), linearised for
the luminance, halved to a hundredth and rounded up —, its most where nothing is known or nothing reads (light glass 6 % over
white, 51 % over black; dark glass 14 % over black, 61 % over white). The backdrop's light: a 32 × 18 grid of the bar's
wallpaper strip (4 × 4 samples a cell), its mean under the bar weighed by coverage (`LiquidGlass.Grid`, `Mean`, `Behind`), read
once a strip as it comes (`DockWindow.Composed`) and told to the scene (`Scene.Backdrop`), which sets the bar's and its cards'
tint in place (`Scene.Glassed`). The design's tint is its most (`GlassLook.Designed`); a colour somebody chose in its place is
drawn as chosen (`GlassLook.Tinted`). The Appearance preview reads its own strip the same way.

**A joined set is one glass shape** (`LiquidGlass.Join`, pure, as Themia's `CardJoins.Bodies`): surfaces that meet — side by
side with the same top and bottom, or one on another with the same sides — are one body; each draws its glow, lens and rim round
the body (cut to its own box: its visual's clip), and a hairline on its side of the seam toward the mate before it (left, else
above), the inset short of the body's outer edges, none where that leaves nothing. In Karpo: a folder's lines that stand on cards
in one piece (`FolderFlyout.Seams`, `SeamsOf`; the pieces between its dividers stay apart, each its panel), and a bar's cards
that meet (an islands bar spaced 0, §533's flush cards; `Scene.ComposeCards` gathers the cards and joins the filled ones).

**Where it is drawn.** The bar (`Scene`): a docked bar's glow over its tint (cut where the cards stand), and along its inner edge
(the others are the screen's) the lens's bands and the rim, each the piece of the light down the bar where it stands
(`Scene.DownTheBar`); a floating bar's panels their glow, lens and rim (`Glaze`) and the lift (the compositor's own soft drop
shadow, blur 40 DIP, 12 down, cast at twice the edge darkness, as a blurred shape is half as dark at its edge; the frost covers
it under the panel); every card its glow and lens (`Rounded.Glazed`), its rim in the rim layer, joined cards as one body
(`Rounded.Joined`, `Divided`). Every flyout, menu and folder (`FlyoutHost`): each panel's glow and lens over its plate, its rim
the glass's; a folder's joined lines their hairlines (`FolderFlyout.PlaceSeam`). The Appearance preview: the bar is the bar; its
folder's lines get the glow and lens between their tint and their drawing, the hairlines and the rim round each piece over it
(`GlassPaint`, Direct2D). Scene.cs's "flat materials only" holds for every other look.

**Approximated or different from Themia's**: the refraction is the lens's stepped bands; the light fixed from above; the blur
the bar's one wallpaper blur; continuous corners circular arcs (all as Themia). Karpo's own: one tint a bar (the mean under the
whole bar, not each card's or each joined set's own box); menus, flyouts and a folder's lines stand on no frost — as Acrylic's
and Glacier's, Karpo blurs only the wallpaper under its bars — so they have their tint at its most and no lift; a folder's glow
and lens lie under its lines' own tint (the folder's panel is bare, §464), faint there; a docked bar has no lift (it stands on
the screen's edge) and its lens and rim only along its inner edge; the lift is a soft drop shadow, not Themia's ten rings (those
were only because Composition shadows did not show in Themia's pictures), and is cut where the bar's window ends; a gradient set
in place does not glide while a card or panel grows.

Tests: `LiquidGlassTests` — `EachModesValuesAreThemias`, `EachLensBandIsTheProfileAtItsWeight`, `TheLiftFallsOffToNothingAtItsBlur`,
`BoxesThatMeetAreOneGlassPartedByHairlines`, `TheTintIsTheLeastThatKeepsTheTextReadable`, `AChosenColourOverridesTheTint`,
`ABackdropsLightIsTheMeanOfItsGridUnderTheBox`, `ThePaletteIsTheMaterial`, `TheDockWearsTheSystemsAccentAndATintThatFollowsTheWallpaper`;
`PaletteTests` (the order, the accent the system's, Liquid glass's folders outlined). Names in 40 languages

## §703 A notification moved off the bar once it is still (2026-11-16)

The person: "the notification just appeared at the wrong place. it shows clipped on the bottom right but half off screen".
appbar.log: "Windows' Notifications 3246,2088..3840,2153 moved off the bars to 3183,2088" and, 2 ms on, "3246,2023..3840,2403
moved off the bars to 3183,2023", then nothing. Windows places a notification in a few steps within a few ms; §540 read each
step as it stood when heard and moved it with that step's top along with the new left. The move is asynchronous
(SWP_ASYNCWINDOWPOS) and landed after Windows' last step, so the notification stood beside the bar with a top from a step on
its way in: reaching below the screen. Heard then, it read as clear of the bar and stayed.

- **ShellPopups.Place**: a panel off the bars is moved only once it has been still for `ShellPopups.SettleMs` (40 ms, the
  dock's POPUPS_SETTLE timer, rearmed by every move heard), read as it then stands and moved once. Start and its search box
  (§666) are placed at once, as before.
- Not covered by a test: the wait is a timer over real windows of Windows' shell; `ShellPopupsTests` keep the placement rule.

By hand: with the bar at the right, start a 5 second timer in Windows' Clock app: the notification comes in Windows' corner
for a blink, then stands wholly on the screen beside the bar; appbar.log has one "moved off the bars" line for it.

## §705 A dock's panels merge into a strip by their own stretches (2026-11-16)

BarMorphFilmTests.ATaskbarMorphsIntoADockAndBack failed for some time: "layout-dock-to-taskbar: a jump of 70 % of the way". Two
things were behind it.

- **The morph (BarMorph.Grounds)**: a dock's panels merging into a strip each grew over the whole strip, the three
  overlapping and in full sight while they did, so the gaps between them shut at once; a strip splitting into panels had each
  panel start as the whole strip. Now each panel ends (a merge), or starts (a split), as its own stretch of the strip: the
  strip cut along the bar at the middles of the gaps between the panels (BarMorph.Share). The panels widen into each other
  and meet. One panel to one ground is unchanged; so is the strip's own start (the panels' hull) and end.
- **The film's measure (FrameFilm.DistanceOverBlack)**: the capture gives a see-through pixel already laid on black, its
  alpha lost, so a ground fading in at a tenth of its strength read as a dark pixel where the purple backdrop was — nearly
  the whole way at once. How far along a morph frame is is now measured with the backdrop read as black, as the frames
  would show over a black desktop, where a tenth of a ground is a tenth of the way.
- Tests: BarMorphTests.AStripSplitsIntoPanelsAndPanelsMergeIntoAStrip (the stretches); the four BarMorphFilmTests pass
  (KARPO_UI_TESTS=1, three runs; the most between two frames 50 %, was 60-70 %).

  and the video keeps its display. Show desktop still gives the display back: it minimizes the video ("its window was
  minimized"), or raises the desktop over it (then it is not under).

  popup is a top-level window of its own (WinUI's popups are), standing over everything; opened from a window under the video
  (Themia's widgets), it leaves the video its display. A window with a caption (a dialog) owned the same way is a window in
  front, as before.

  screen app covers its display from above.
- Tests: BarKeeperTests.ADesktopClickOnTheOtherDisplayLeavesTheVideoItsDisplay,
  AFlyoutOfAWidgetUnderTheVideoLeavesTheVideoItsDisplay (BarWorld windows have an owner); §702's and

## §708 A Chromium video a pixel row short, out of the foreground, is full screen still (2026-11-20)

The person: "karpo is currently moving over my fullscreen video sometimes. the last 5mins like 100 times". appbar.log,
2026-11-20 18:09:02 to 18:12:27, a video full screen in Brave on DISPLAY1: "full screen app gone: its bars come back (its
window left full screen: at 0,0..3840,2159)" thirty-five times, "full screen app in front: brave.exe … at 0,0..3840,2160" half
a second to a second after each. The same line stood in the log once or twice a day before (2026-11-15 20:14, 11-16 20:18,
11-19 15:49).

Chromium does it on purpose (ui/views/win/hwnd_message_handler.cc, PostProcessActivateMessage, `background_fullscreen_hack_`):
a full screen window that loses activation to a window on the same monitor is made one pixel shorter at the bottom, so
that Windows' taskbar no longer counts its thread as full screen; activated again, it takes the whole monitor back. The
window that took the foreground need not be in sight on that display: the desktop (Progman spans every display and is the
primary's, so a click on the other display's desktop or on a Themia widget there, §706), a widget under the video (§702), a
hidden window of a program started in the background. Each of those left the video its display's front (§702, §706), and
then the front no longer covered the display: the bars came back over it.

- **FullscreenApps.StandsBack**, counted by `Fills`: a window of Chromium's class (Chrome_WidgetWin_N: Brave, Chrome, Edge,
  Electron), with no caption, not maximized, at its display's rectangle exactly less the last row, is a full screen app
  still. A window that comes over the video takes the display's front as before, and gives it back when it goes (§707): the
  video is a row short then too, never activated since, and has its display.
- Never by the shape alone: Themia's widget surface is a display less its last row as well (0,0..3840,2159), and no full
  screen app.
- Tests: FullscreenTests.AChromiumFullScreenWindowOutOfTheForegroundIsFullScreenStill,
  OnlyChromiumsOwnRowShortWindowIsFullScreen; BarKeeperTests.AChromiumVideoAPixelShortOutOfTheForegroundKeepsItsDisplay,
  AChromiumVideoAPixelShortAtTheStartHasItsDisplay.

By hand: a video full screen in a Chromium browser on the primary display; click the other display's desktop and widgets,
start a console program in the background: the bars stay away, and appbar.log says nothing. A window opened over the video:
they come back; minimized from the other display: they go.

## §709 The same video in a browser that was maximized (2026-11-20)

The person, an hour after §708 was installed: "karpo again is moving itself over a fullscreen view. fix". appbar.log,
2026-11-20 18:58 to 19:08, the build with §708 running since 18:30: "full screen app gone: its bars come back (its window
left full screen: at 0,0..3840,2159)" over fifty times more, the video "in front" at 0,0..3840,2160 again half a second to a
second to three and a half after each. What took the foreground each time was a window nobody sees: Themia's, rendering its

the two lengths the bars had stood over the video for all evening).

The video's window, read off the screen while it stood full screen: class Chrome_WidgetWin_1, style 170B0000 — no caption,
no sizing frame, and WS_MAXIMIZE; IsZoomed true. Chromium's full screen (ui/views/win/fullscreen_handler.cc) takes
WS_CAPTION and WS_THICKFRAME off the window and leaves the rest of its style as it was, so a browser that was maximized
when its video went full screen — the usual way to watch one — stays zoomed all through, and comes out at -11,-11..3851,2171
with its caption back. §708's StandsBack asked for a window "not maximized", so it never held for this window; its tests
made the row-short window up restored, and it was not tried by hand against the browser as the person keeps it.

  rectangle exactly less the last row. A maximized window that is no full screen app has its caption (`Fills` leaves it
  out), or stands at the work area and past the display's edges, never at the display less one row.
- Tests: FullscreenTests.AMaximizedChromiumWindowGoneFullScreenAndOutOfTheForegroundIsFullScreenStill (and
  OnlyChromiumsOwnRowShortWindowIsFullScreen, which had "a maximized one is not" among its cases);
  BarKeeperTests.AMaximizedBrowsersVideoAPixelShortOutOfTheForegroundKeepsItsDisplay.

Seen on the screen, the fixed build running since 19:16:55 with the video full screen: both of those windows took the
