## §710 The Microsoft Store's package (2026-11-22)

The person: "i want to publish karpo under my personal account then. for now at least. because right now we are under
pressure to publish but are not able to because our mircrosoft store sign up hangs", "you should price it at 5usd", and "the
flow that i want in the end is that microsoft signs the release for me and that a github pipeline autmatically creates the
release for karpo". So Karpo is Partner Center's product "Karpo" of that account (Store ID 9MXKV2VWR2CP, identity
`NathanWalser.Karpo`, publisher `CN=C470EED8-37EC-4C04-9586-6B249062A51A`, shown as "Nathan Walser"), free, with the durable
add-on `karpo-pro` (Store ID 9NT4RFR5R3BN, 4.99 USD) that §138 was written for. A first product reserved as "Karpos" was a
slip of the name and is not this one.

- **The package**: `package\AppxManifest.xml` (the identity, the 40 languages by their listings' tags, the visual elements)
  and `package\Images` (the 72 logos of `node store/compose.mjs --package`, kept in the repository so a build needs no
  browser to draw them). `scripts\package.ps1 -Version 1.0.0` publishes Karpo with `-Channel store`, lays the exe, the
  manifest with that version and the logos in a folder, makes `resources.pri` (which logo is which size) and packs
  `artifacts\package\Karpo_1.0.0_x64.msix`. Unsigned: the Store signs what it publishes. `scripts\publish.ps1` takes
  `-Version` (About Karpo's, 1.0.0 without it) and `-Channel`.
- **The release**: `.github\workflows\release.yml`. A tag `v1.0.1` tests, packs and keeps the package on a GitHub release of
  that name; "Run workflow" does the same for a version typed in, kept on the run. Publishing stays a person's: Partner
  Center › Karpo › Packages, upload, Submit. No secret is held anywhere.
- **`StoreIds.ProAddOn`** is the add-on's Store ID, no placeholder any more.
- **A Store build outside its package is the free version** (`LicenseBasis.StoreMissing`, "The Microsoft Store isn't
  available to this copy of Karpo."). Until now every copy without a package was a developer build, unrestricted: the
  Store's exe copied out of its package, or started some way that lost its identity, would have been Pro for anybody. The
  build is marked (`KarpoChannel=store`, an AssemblyMetadata `scripts\publish.ps1 -Channel store` writes and
  `StoreLicense.Channel` reads); a build of the source has no mark and is what it was, the person's own Karpo among them.
- **Start with Windows** is the package's startup task (`windows.startupTask`, "KarpoStartup") for a packaged copy, in place
  of the Run entry and the logon task, which a package may not keep: the logon task is real, outlives an uninstall (Store
  policy 10.2.7) and, like the Run entry, names an exe whose folder changes with every update. `Dock.SyncStartup` makes the
  task follow the setting (`StartupRegistration.PackagedAct`: enabled where Karpo itself left it off, disabled where it is
  on and the setting is not, never against the person's or the administrator's own switch); the menu's switch reads it as it
  reads a Run entry (`PackagedState`: "turned off in Task Manager" means what it meant); a start by the task has no command
  line, so the dock asks Windows how it was started and adds "--startup" (`PackagedStartup.Arguments`). The rules are
  `Karpo.Core\PackagedStartup.cs`, Windows' side `Karpo.Dock\PackagedStartup.cs`. A copy without a package keeps the Run
  entry and the logon task.
- **The guard starts a packaged dock again by its package** (`DockLauncher.ThroughPackage`, the app's id
  `PackageIdentity.AppUserModelId`) where it started it through Explorer: the exe started by its path from outside the
  package runs without the package.
- **The real registry and the real %APPDATA%** (the manifest's `desktop6:RegistryWriteVirtualization` and
  `FileSystemWriteVirtualization`, both "disabled", with the restricted capability `unvirtualizedResources`, which the
  Store must grant). A package otherwise sees its own copies of both, and so does every program it starts. Karpo writes
  for Windows to read — where Windows' taskbar is parked (TaskbarPosition), which tray icons show (Tray, IsPromoted), night
  light, colour filters, nearby sharing — and starts every app the person clicks; "Open file location" opens Explorer at a
  file Explorer must see. With them off, Karpo's files are where they always were, and outlive an uninstall as any desktop
  app's do. The other capabilities are what Windows asks a packaged app to declare before it may ask the person:
  `userNotificationListener` (the bell), `location` (the weather's place, the Wi-Fi networks' names), `radios`.

**Not done here, and not tried**: the packaged Karpo has not been installed or run. Registering a package needs Developer
Mode on this PC, which is the person's to turn on. Until it has been tried in its package, these are open:

- whether the apps Karpo starts run outside its package's view once the two are disabled (the reason they are disabled);
- whether an uninstall, which runs none of Karpo's code, leaves Windows' taskbar hidden: Windows ends the dock and its guard
  together, and the taskbar comes back only if Windows asks the dock to close first (WM_QUERYENDSESSION, which the dock
  answers by putting it back, Dock.cs);
- whether the guard's restart by the package's id carries its arguments, and whether breaking away from the package's job
  is allowed (if not, every restart takes that road);
- the Store's own answers: the purchase of Pro, its price, and the licence after it (§138 said so too: "can only be tried
  in a packaged build" that is published);
- whether Burmese (my-MM) is a language the Store takes.

A start at sign-in comes later for the Store's copy than for the person's own: Windows starts a package's startup task with
its other startup apps, which is the wait the logon task was made to skip (StartupTask.cs).

- Tests: LicensingTests.AStoreBuildWithoutItsPackageIsTheFreeVersion, TheProAddOnIsARealStoreId, APlaceholderStoreIdMatchesNoLicence;
  PackagedStartupTests (the states by number, the switch's reading, what the dock does, a start by the task, the manifest
  naming what the code asks for, every listing language declared).

## §711 GitHub flow, CI, and a listing that promises nothing that is gone (2026-11-22)

The person: "setup the repository and create instructions for contributers to use github flow where releases are created by
creating tags", and of the Store: "we want the app submitted for review with all the necesary stuff too".

- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: a change is a branch off `master` and a pull request, merged squashed; a release is a tag `vX.Y.Z` on
  `master`. The repository merges squashed and deletes a merged branch. `master` is not locked: GitHub gives a private
  repository branch protection only on a paid plan, and the organisation is on the free one.
- **`.github\workflows\ci.yml`**: every pull request and every push to `master` builds Karpo and runs its tests, in the time
  zone the tests were written in (the runner's is UTC; `WeatherSplitTests` and `TidesTests` read hours as the PC's clock tells
  them, and failed there on the first run).
- **`.github\workflows\release.yml`** has a second job, `store`: the package of a tag handed to the Microsoft Store as an update
  (`msstore publish`, Microsoft's Store Developer CLI) and submitted for certification, where the repository's variable
  `STORE_SUBMIT` is "true" and it holds the Entra application's four secrets. The Store takes an update this way only after
  the first submission was made and published by hand. Not run yet. The first job's trial ("Run workflow", 1.0.0) built,
  smoke-checked and packed the Store's package on a GitHub runner.
- **The listings' "ALWAYS YOUR CHOICE"** began "Hiding the Windows taskbar is a setting you can turn off." in all 40
  languages. There is no such setting since §465 (Karpo hides Windows' taskbar whenever it runs), so the sentence is gone
  from each `store\listing\<lang>.json`; the paragraph goes on from "Quit Karpo any time …".
- **The tests**: eleven of the thirteen that failed on `master` are green again, each by the side that was out of date (five
  in the code, six in the test, by the entry that changed the rule: §631, §637, §655, §687, §689, §696). Two are left, both
  the Windows search widget's menu against the menu rules of §411 (`MenuConventionTests.EveryNumberSaysItsUnit`,
  `MenuRulesTests.EveryMenuKeepsTheRules`): its "How many each shows" counts have no unit, its first level is 402 of 390 DIP
  tall, two of its rows share an icon, a title is a sentence and one is cut off. Mending them means new words in 40 languages
  and a decision about that menu, which nobody has made.

In Partner Center the submission of "Karpo" has its price (free), properties, English listing (the words, nine screenshots,
the hero art and the tile), notes for certification and "don't publish until I select Publish now". Left to the person: the
age ratings' last step (agreeing to IARC's terms), the package's upload, and Submit.

## §712 The repository is `karpo`, its README a pitch, its licence Elastic's (2026-11-22)

The person: "the github karpo-app repo should be renamed to just karpo", "the readme should be more like a sales pitch not
how to setup or contribute, that should be moved into another md file", "it should be published under the elastic licence",
and "make karpo repo public".

- **`LICENSE`** is the Elastic License 2.0, word for word as Elastic publishes it. It lets anybody use, copy and change
  Karpo's source; it forbids offering it to others as a hosted service, and moving, changing, disabling or getting around
  "the license key functionality" and what it protects, which for Karpo is the licence of §138 and §710.
- **`README.md`** says what Karpo is for somebody who might want it, in the Store listing's words (`store\listing\en.json`):
  the day on the taskbar, the widgets, folders, layouts, every screen and edge, privacy, free and Pro. What it said about
  building, checking, where things live and the repository's layout is `docs\development.md`, unchanged; how changes and
  releases are made stays `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **The repository on GitHub** is `lometics/karpo`. The folder it is checked out into on the PC it is made on is still
  `karpo-app` (karpo.app's `npm run shots` reads `../karpo-app`), and GitHub sends the old address on.

A build of the source is still a developer build, which nothing limits (§138). With the source public that is a Karpo Pro
for whoever builds it, and the licence does not forbid it: nothing is got around, the build simply has no limit. Whether a
build of the source should be the free version instead is a decision nobody has made.

## §713 Public, from a clean start: Google's client secret comes in at build time (2026-11-22)

The person, asked how the repository should become public once its history had been read through for what should not be
(one secret, Google's client secret, in `GoogleAuth.cs` and so in every commit since §687; who administers which account
in `docs\accounts.md`; an address in an old `store\README.md`): "Clean it first".

- **Google's client secret is not in the source.** `GoogleAuth.ClientSecret` reads the assembly's mark
  `KarpoGoogleClientSecret`, which `Karpo.Accounts.csproj` writes from the MSBuild property of that name. The property
  comes from `Local.Build.props` beside `Directory.Build.props` on the PC Karpo is made on (`.gitignore` keeps the file out
  of the repository), or from the environment's `KARPO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, which the release workflow fills from the
  repository's secret of that name. Google itself calls a Desktop app a public client that cannot keep a secret, and
  every Karpo that has it carries it; it stays out of the source because the source is public, and because GitHub refuses
  a push that holds one.
- **A build without it offers no Google account** (`GoogleAuth.Offered`: no id is given to the sign-in, which is what
  greys "Add a Google account", `OAuthClient.HasClientId`); everything else is the same. So a fork builds and runs, and CI
  needs no secret. The smoke check says which it is ("accounts: Google sign-in built in" or "left out"), and
  `scripts\package.ps1` refuses to pack the Store's Karpo without it, unless told `-WithoutGoogle`.
- **`docs\accounts.md`** no longer says whose accounts administer the Entra registration and the Google Cloud project, or
  how that organization's access rules are set; what the registrations are, and what they ask for, it says as before.
- **The repository starts again from one commit.** Everything up to here is kept, privately, in `lometics/karpo-history`;
  `lometics/karpo` begins with the tree as it stands, so nothing that was ever committed and taken out again is in it.
  Commits are made as the maker's GitHub address, not a personal one.

Tests: GoogleAuthTests (a Google account offered exactly where the build has the secret; `Offered`).

- **Now that it is public**, `master` is protected (no force push, no deletion; §711 said it could not be while the repository
  was private on the free plan) and GitHub scans every push for secrets and refuses one that holds any. The agents' settings
  for a checkout (`.claude\`) are each PC's own and no longer part of the repository.

## §714 Show desktop leaves the bars where they are (2026-11-22)

The person: "the taskbar does hide when doing win+d, maybe this can be fixed too".

Show desktop (Win+D, Explorer's corner, a three-finger swipe) raises the desktop's window over every window, the
always-on-top ones too. Explorer's taskbar goes up with it; Karpo's bars are Karpo's windows, so they went under it with the
apps and stayed there until the next window came up. Read live on the person's PC, 30 ms after Win+D, top first: Themia's two
surfaces, Progman (the foreground), then both `karpo.dock` windows, still WS_EX_TOPMOST and under it. Karpo's own Show
desktop corner never had this: it puts the bars back itself for 600 ms after its press (`ToggleDesktop`).

- **The rule** (`BarKeeper.DesktopOver`, `DesktopInFront`; `FullscreenApps.IsDesktop`): the desktop (Progman, a WorkerW) has
  the foreground and stands over a bar in the z-order. A click on the wallpaper gives it the foreground where it lies, under
  the bars: nothing.
- **What the dock does** (`Dock.DesktopCameToFront`, on FrontWatch's foreground change): where the rule holds, every bar goes
  back over the desktop as the corner's press does (`KeepAboveDesktop`: shown, the plan's stack applied again; never on a full
  screen app's display), now and at each 80 ms look for the 600 ms the shell may take to raise it (the corner's
  `DESKTOP_RESTORE` timer). One line in appbar.log each time it does: "Show desktop raised the desktop over the bars: they go
  back over it". Nothing is written or moved while the desktop is not over a bar.
- Themia's widgets, lifted for Show desktop, go directly above the desktop and under every other window (its [S-33f]), so the
  bars put back are over them without either program answering the other.
- Tests: `BarKeeperTests.ShowDesktopRaisingTheDesktopOverABarIsSeenAndAClickOnTheWallpaperIsNot`.

## §715 The Store's Karpo, run in its package for the first time: Pro's price (2026-11-22)

The person turned Developer Mode on so that the package could be run before it is handed in ("you can also turn on test
mode"). `Add-AppxPackage -Register artifacts\package\layout\AppxManifest.xml`, started by its package, on the person's PC
with their own settings.

- **One fault, found in karpo.log.** ⚙ › Karpo Pro asked the Store for Pro's price and got none: "license: Pro's price:
  InvalidCastException: Failed to create a CCW for object of type '<>z__ReadOnlySingleElementList`1[System.String]'".
  `GetStoreProductsAsync(["Durable"], [id])` handed Windows a managed collection, which section 10 forbids in the native
  build; a `List<string>` in its place threw the same, as section 10 says it would. A managed build never shows it, and an
  unpackaged Karpo never asks. What is handed over now is a list Windows made (`WindowsStrings.Of`: a `DataPackage`'s
  `FileTypes`, an `IVector<String>` that is filled and never used for anything else).
- **The smoke check asks too, where it can.** In its package (`Karpo.exe --smoke` through the package's alias,
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\Karpo.exe`) it says "store: Pro's price …", having asked as the menu asks. Without
  a package it says nothing of it, as before. Run so on 2026-11-22 it threw nothing and was told no price: the add-on is
  not published yet, so the Store lists none.
- **What held**, each read from the processes, the registry and karpo.log rather than looked at:
  - the dock and its guard both run with the package's identity; the Windows taskbar is hidden while they do;
  - the Store answers: "license: app active False, 0 add-on licence(s), Pro not owned", Free (StoreFree), and a purchase
    begun from the menu ended NotPurchased (the add-on is not published yet);
  - the package's startup task is Enabled after the first start;
  - the dock ended from outside comes back through its package ("started by its package"), with its identity;
  - a program started by ShellExecuteEx from inside the package has no package identity (tried from a PowerShell run in
    the package's context, `Invoke-CommandInDesktopPackage`, which starts things as `Launch` does), so what a person
    opens from the bar is an ordinary app;
  - the package removed while Karpo runs: the dock is told the session is ending, puts the Windows taskbar back and
    ends; the guard tries once more 20 s later, finds no package, and ends. Nothing of Karpo runs afterwards and the
    startup task is gone. The settings in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Karpo` stay, as they are the person's and not the package's.
- **The first version in the Store is 1.0.1.** The package first handed to Partner Center was 1.0.0, built before this
  fault was found. Partner Center takes no second package of the same name and version, and saves no submission without
  a package, so the mended one could not take its place under that number. `v1.0.1` is the tag; the pipeline's package of
  that tag is the one uploaded.
- **Not tried**: a purchase that goes through (there is nothing to buy until the add-on is published), and a start by the
  startup task at sign-in.
